text: Alege Naawen a basi ate Faaro suinummu a pagra, ate wa kan basi ate Izirali demma a cheŋ.

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
text: Ate Naawen a weeni Moosis ayen, <<Zak fi nisaŋa a tuk wen ate legi a jam lik Ejipiti tɛŋka. Legi dii ale di jo nuruma nyiŋ.>>

ref: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
text: Moosis yaa zak nisa a tuk wen ate legi nna kpitɔ a lik Ejipiti a paari daa ŋata.

ref: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
text: Nuru waai an jam nya wa choa yaase wa basi wa jigi a paari daa ŋata. Alege Izirali demma ale bo juijui meena la ku a nya.

ref: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
text: Faaro yaa wi Moosis a weeni wa ayen, <<Ni cheŋ a ga puusi Naawen. Ni nipooma ale ni bisaŋa a baga a cheŋ ale ni kama. Ka ni tin basi ni piisaŋa ale ni duŋsaŋa ŋaaŋ.>>

ref: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
text: Alege Moosis a weeni wa ayen, <<Ku a fɛ ate fi basi ate ti ta ti duŋsaŋa ale juka tiiritaŋa ate ti pai te Naawen, ti Wenni.

ref: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
text: Alege Naawen a basi ate Faaro suinummu a pagra, ate wa kan yaali ayen ba cheŋ.

ref: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
text: Faaro yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Cheŋ du mi niŋ. Seba ate fi kan ŋman jam mi niŋŋa. Dai dii dai ate fi a nya mi nina la fi le kpi.>>

ref: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
text: Moosis yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ase fi le weeni diila, m kan ŋman jam fi niŋ diipo diipo.

ref: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<M le ta ka daanika bunyi a jam Faaro ale Ejipiti zuk. Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa le te ate ni nyini dela cheŋ. Wa dan nye dila wa le yiak ni meena ate ni nyini.

ref: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
text: Weeni Izirali nidoama ale nipooma ayen ba bek ba le Ejipiti dem baai ale moata chaab la a tuesi kpana ale ligmɔniŋ ŋanta a nyini ba jigi.>>

ref: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
text: Naawen a basi kama ate Ejipiti demma a pai badek a te Izirali ate Moosis dek mɛ Faaro nisɔmma ale nuruma jaa zuli wa kama.

ref: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
text: Moosis yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <Yɔk suŋsuŋ m le cheŋ Ejipiti tɛŋka meena.

ref: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
text: Bi kpagi meena Ejipiti tɛŋka po ale kpi, a zaani Faaro bikpagni waai ale wa kali naamu zukpaglika zuk la, a ga paari nipok yɔmawa waai ale a num zom la bikpagni ale niiga bi kpaga mɛ.

ref: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
text: Kaarik nna yegayega le za ku bo Ejipiti a bie a gaam kaarik sii ate ba kaari a nya la, yaase kaari ka choa ale ŋman jam ase dila la.

ref: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
text: Alege Izirali demma po biak mɛ la a kan wosi nuru yaase duŋŋa.> Ate ni miŋ ayen Naawen a nye kama ate pooruŋ a bo Ejipiti ale Izirali suŋsuŋ.

ref: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
text: Fi nisɔmma de meena ale jam mi jigi a koori tɛŋ mi niŋ a weeni ayen, <Ni cheŋ, fi ale fi nuruma meena ale va fu la.> Dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ m le cheŋ.>> Moosis yaa basi Faaro ale suipuurum nna yegayega.

ref: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
text: Naawen a poom weeni Moosis kama ayen, Faaro ale zɛri wa kan wom fu ate m wakinkaglaŋa a tom piisi Ejipiti.>>

ref: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
text: Moosis ale Aaron a tom wakinkaglaŋa de meena kama Faaro niŋ, alege Naawen a basi ate Faaro suinummu a pagra, ate wa kan basi ate Izirali demma a nyini wa tɛŋka po a nyini.

ref: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ale Aaron Ejipiti tɛŋka po ayen,

ref: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
text: <<Chiika de ale ka chim ni piilimka chiik, chiik kaai ale a chim ni benni piilimka chiik la.

ref: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
text: Weeni Izirali demma ayen chiika da pi dai, nuru meena a yaali pabiik a magsi wa dɔkdem, kanyi a magsi yeri meena.

ref: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
text: Nya si zuk a ga paari chiika daa pi ale ŋanaansi dai ku junɔi ate Izirali demma meena ale tɔgri si la.

ref: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
text: Ba yaa pai ziimu gela a sa yeeŋa tuataŋa ganaŋa ale ŋmazuimaŋa juijui ate ba kali a ŋɔbi pabisaŋa lantaŋa la.

ref: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
text: <<Yok kula ba se lammu bolim po a ŋɔbi ale tinaŋ tuasa ale boroborok ate dabinta a ka ku po.

ref: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
text: Ni kan ŋɔbi lammu bein ya yaase ni dik bu ale nyiamoa, alege ni se bu bolim po. Ni se zukku ale naŋsaŋa ale puuka po ŋantaŋa.

ref: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
text: Ni kan tali bu gela a ta paari saluiwa, bu gela a dan tali a paari saluik, ni ju bu.

ref: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
text: Ni ale magsi ni ŋɔbi lammu diila ale nna. Ni pai chiak gbana a bobi ni gattaŋa a paari, abe ni su ni nuesaŋa, abe ni ta ni doaŋa ni nisima po. Ni ŋɔbi bu nwuli. Ku ka Naawen Gaambasika.

ref: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
text: <<Yok kula dek m le va Ejipiti po a nak nuru ale jaabuuri meena ate ba dɛ niŋ a biak la a lɔnsi tɛŋ. Ate m yaa ta buusa boka a jam Ejipiti wenaŋa meena zuk. Mi ale Naawen.

ref: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
text: Ziimu ale bu sak yie ŋaai ate ni bo ŋa po la. M dan nya ziimu m le gaam ni a taam. Biem a kan maa paari ni ase m nin boro a kaasi Ejipiti.

ref: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
text: Daa ŋayopɔi ni ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ale kan ta dabinta la. Da dii dai ale a dɛ niŋ la ni yeeri dabintaŋa ni yeeŋa po a basi. Waai a dan dɛ jaab ate dabinta a boro a nyini piilimka danni a ta ga paari daa ŋayopɔiwa danni, ba yeeri a nyini Izirali po.

ref: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
text: Piilim ka danni ni nye tuilum tigsuŋ ale daa ŋayopɔiwa danni mɛ ni ŋman nye tuilum tigsuŋ. Ni kan tom tuin pagri. Dii nyiini ale magsi ayen ni nye la ale ni dik ŋandiinta a dɛ.

ref: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
text: <<Ni ŋɔbi Boroborok Ate Dabinta A Ka Ku Po La Tigini, dii nyiŋla ka da dila danni ate ni beŋsaŋa meena a nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka. Ni te ŋmarisika de a kasim boro a cheŋ gaŋsa buuri meena zuk.

ref: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
text: Chiik kaai ale a dɛ niŋ la, ni ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ate dabinta a ka ku po, a zaani daa pi ale ŋanaansiwa danni ku junɔi, a ga paari daa pisiye ale dinyi.

ref: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
text: Dabinta a kan bo waai yeri po daa ŋayopɔi. Ate waai a dan dɛ ŋandiinta ate dabinta a bo ti po, wa poom ka Izirali dek denɔ yaase nichaanɔ, ba yeeri wa a nyini Izirali nuruma po.

ref: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
text: Kan dɛ jaab ate ba pai dabinta a nye. Juijui meena ate fi boro la ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ate ba an pai dabinta a nye la.>>

ref: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
text: Ate Moosis yaa tigsi nuruma a yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni cheŋ nwuli a ga luk duŋsa a te ni dɔkdemma a magsi chaab ale Gaambasika.

ref: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
text: Ni pai kpaliok a su ziimu ale bo taasi kpienni po la a pai ziimu gela a sa tuataŋa ganaŋa meena. Ni wanyi mɛ la a kan gaam yenni tuoku a nyini peelim ate ku ga paari saluik.

ref: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
text: Naawen a dan va Ejipiti tɛŋka ayen wa ko Ejipiti demma a lɔnsi, wa le nya ziimu tuataŋa ŋmaaŋa ale ganaŋa ate wa le gaam tua tila, wa kan te kaasirɔwa suik ate wa ko ni lɔnsi.

ref: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
text: Ni dan jo tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen ayen wa te ni a magsi chaab ale wa le puulim la, ni kpesi a va wanni de.

ref: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
text: Ate ni bisaŋa a dan bek ni ayen, <Tigini de kiri ale boa a te ni?>

ref: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
text: Ni yaa weeni ba ayen, <Ka Gaambasika kaabka a te Naawen dii ale gaam Izirali demma yeeŋa a basi ale vari ti yeeŋa a basi wa le jam ko Ejipiti demma a lɔnsi la.> >> Ate nuruma a koori tɛŋ a puusi wa.

ref: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
text: Izirali demma a jam nye ka dii dek ate Naawen a weeni Moosis ale Aaron la.

ref: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
text: Yɔk suŋsuŋ Naawen a ko bi kpaŋŋa meena a dueni, a zaan Faaro bikpagni waai ale wa kali naam zukpaglika zuk la, a ga paari waai ate ba lik likka dɔk po la bikpagni ale duŋsa bi kpaga mɛ.

ref: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
text: Faaro ale wa nisɔmma ale Ejipiti demma yaa yiti yokku a kasim a kaari nna yegayega Ejipiti po diila yeri karo ate waai an kpi ya.

ref: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
text: Yɔkku Faaro yaa wi Moosis ale Aaron a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni yiti. Ni basi m nuruma, fi ale Izirali demma. Ni cheŋ a ga puusi Naawen ase ni ale bek diila.

ref: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
text: Ni ta ni piisaŋa ale ni duŋsaŋa, ase ni ale weeni diila a cheŋ. Abe ni niak mu mɛ.>>

ref: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
text: Ejipiti demma a yaa va nuruma ayen ba nye nwuli a basi tɛŋka. Ba weeni ayen, <<Kan daa di ti meena ale kpi.>>

ref: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
text: Nuruma yaa pai ba boroboroku alege ate ba gum dabinta du, a yaa pai vi ŋmankpala ale taasi tanlaŋ sii ate ba bilisi boroborok du la a pai gatta a pobi.

ref: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
text: Izirali demma yaa nye Moosis ale weeni diila. Ba yaa bek Izirali demma a tuesi kpana ale ligmɔniŋ ale gatta.

ref: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
text: Naawen a basi kama ate Ejipiti demma a ta ŋman teka ale siak teka ale nuruma ate ba te ba jabuui meena ate ba bek a yaali la. Ba yaa vari Ejipiti demma.

ref: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
text: Izirali yaa piilim ba chelimu a nyini Arameses a ga paari Sukkot. Nidoama a jam ka nuruba tusa kobsiyuebi (

ref: of them, not counting women and children.
text: ) a cheŋ naŋta. Nipooba ale bimbaansa an gum du.

ref: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
text: Nuru boari ate ba an chim Izirali dem la ale piisa ale bua ale niiga nna yegayega ale jam maa cheŋ ale ba.

ref: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
text: Ba le ta zom buui a nyini Ejipiti jam la, ba yaa pai nye maasa. Ba an jam nyo dabinta du. Zommu a jam ka dabinta dii nyiŋla ba yiak ba kama ate ba nyini Ejipiti nyini, ba an nya suik a nye ŋandiinta.

ref: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
text: Naawen ale kpesi a nya yokku ayen wa ta ba nyini Ejipiti nyini la nyiŋ, Izirali demma meena a kpesi ate ba a zuli Naawen a magsi ba ŋaaŋsaŋa ale cheen la.

ref: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ale Aaron ayen, <<Ŋmarisika ale nna a magsi Gaambasika. Nichaanɔ a kan dɛ Gaambasika.

ref: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
text: Fi dan ta yɔma wa baga dɛ kama, wa yoanni gebika ŋaaŋnyiŋ,

ref: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
text: <<Waai dan ayen wa ŋɔbi lammu wa be ŋɔbi yenni po. Kan ta lammu a nyini peelimmoa. Kan wɛ kobini dinyi mɛ.

ref: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
text: Izirali demma meena a magsi ba dɛ tigini kama.

ref: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
text: <<Nichaanɔ waai ale maa bo ale ni la a daa yaali ayen wa dɛ Naawen Gaambasika ku a fɛ ate wa gebi nidoama ale bo wa yenni po la yoaŋa. Ate wa yaa maa baga a dɛ ase waai ate ba biak wa tɛŋka po la. Nidoa waai ale kan gebi la a kan dɛ.

ref: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
text: Sinsaŋŋa ka dila degadega ale tɛŋ biik ale nichaanɔ waai ale bo ale ni la.>>

ref: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
text: Izirali demma meena yaa nye dii ate Naawen a weeni Moosis ale Aaron la.

ref: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
text: Dai dila danni dek ate Naawen a ta Izirali demma a nyini Ejipiti nyini a va chaab ale ba ale poori diila.

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
text: <<Gaari ba le liŋ biak jaduok kuui meena a te mu ase tuilum jaab la. Luik meena ale liŋ biak jabuui Izirali demma po la, nuru yaase duŋ ka mi ale soa.>>

ref: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
text: Naawen a dan ta ni a ga jo Keenan demma ale Yit demma ale Amori demma ale Yivi demma ale Jebus demma tɛŋka, tɛŋ kaai ate wa puulim ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa ayen wa te ni la, tɛŋ kaai ale ta biisim ale siita la, ni a teeri tigini de chiika de po.

ref: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
text: Daa ŋayopɔi ni ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ate dabinta a ka ku po la, abe daa ŋayopɔiwa danni ni nye tigi a te Naawen.

ref: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
text: <<Ni ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ate dabinta a ka ku po la daa ŋayopɔiwa po. Jaabuui ale ta dabinta la a kan bo ni suŋsuŋŋa yaase dabinta a bo ni tɛŋ banaŋa.

ref: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
text: Dai dila danni weeni fi nidoabinni ayen, <Mi nye nna ka Naawen ale nye dii a te mi la nyiŋ, diipo ate mi a jam nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka po a nyini la.>

ref: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
text: Kpesi teerika de ale chim ka daana a bo ni nisa po ale teerika ni deeŋa nyiŋ ate Naawen sinsaŋŋa abe bo ni noaŋa po. Ale Naawen a ta ni nyini Ejipiti nyini kama ale wa ni pagrisa.

ref: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
text: Ni be magsi kama ayen ni ta ŋmarisika de diipo ale magsi la, ale ben ben meena po.

ref: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
text: <<Naawen a dan ta ni jam jo Keenan demma tɛŋka a pai ka a te ni, ase wa le puulim a pɛ ale nama ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa la ŋaaŋnyiŋ,

ref: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
text: jabuui ale liŋ a nyini luik po a nyini la ni pai te Naawen. Ni duŋ wuunsa ale liŋ a biak ŋan doa tii la, Naawen ale soa.

ref: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
text: Pai pabiik a da tuesi boniŋ ale liŋ biak kaai la, alege fi dan kan da tuesi ya, wɛ ka ŋinni. Ni da tuesi biik kaai meena ate ba liŋ biak ni bisaŋa po la.

ref: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
text: <<Chum po fi bisaŋa a dan bek fu ayen, <Ka kude kiri ale boa?> Weeni wa ayen, <Naawen ale pai wa pagrimu a ta ti a nyini Ejipiti ale ka yɔntidi tɛŋ po la nyiŋ.

ref: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
text: Faaro ale ta tukpari a zɛri a kan te ti a cheŋ la, ate Naawen yaa ko bi kpaŋŋa Ejipiti po, nuruba ale duŋsa meena. Ka dila ale soa ate mi a nye kaabka ale ŋandoa tii ate ba liŋ biak la ayen m da tuesi ba a basi.>

ref: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
text: Ate ku chim magsa fi nisa nyiŋ ale magsa fi diri nyiŋ ayen Naawen ale ta ti nyini Ejipiti nyini ale wa pagrim.>>

ref: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
text: Faaro ale te nuruma a cheŋ la, Wen an basi ate ba va suik kuui ale va Filistia tɛŋka la. Suik kula abe jam gela kama. Wen jam weeni kama ayen, <<Ba dan tu kpaliŋ, ba le tagri ba popolaŋa a ŋman cheŋ Ejipiti.>>

ref: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
text: Dila Wen yaa ta ba gilim va goa kosikka suiku ale a cheŋ Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku la. Izirali demma a jam basi Ejipiti kama a gomsi badek a magsi kpaliŋ.

ref: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
text: Moosis a jam pai Josefi kobaŋa kama dii nyiŋla Josefi a jam basi kama ate Izirali bisaŋa a pɛ. Wa jam weeni kama ayen, <<Wen za wa sum jam maari ni kama, ate ni yaa pai m kobaŋa dela a ji a ta cheŋ.>>

ref: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
text: Ba le basi Sukkot ŋaaŋ nyiŋla, ba ga kali ka Etam goa kosikka nɔi.

ref: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
text: Ate Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
text: <<Weeni Izirali demma ayen ba cheem ŋaaŋ a ga kali a moata Pi Yayirot, Migdol ale nyakpiemu suŋsuŋ. Ba yaa kali moata nyakpiemu, a tuk Baal Zefon.

ref: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
text: Faaro ale poli ayen, <Izirali demma a tuim kama a cheŋ a gilim goa kosikka suŋsuŋ.>

ref: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
text: M le basi ate Faaro suinummu a pagra, ate wa chali vi ba. Alege m le nya zula a te m dek Faaro ale wa kpaliŋ nyeerisaŋa nyiŋ. Ate Ejipiti demma a seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.>> Ate Izirali demma a nye kude.

ref: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
text: Ba le weeni Ejipiti naawa ayen nuruma a chali kama la, Faaro ale wa nisɔmma yaa tagri ba popolaŋa a weeni ayen, <<Ti tin nye ka sɛ? Ti basi ate Izirali demma a cheŋ alege jɔgi ba tuimaŋa.>>

ref: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
text: Wa yaa gomsi wusum ale toroko a magsi a ta wa kpaliŋ nyeerisaŋa a cheŋ.

ref: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
text: Naawen a basi ate Faaro Ejipiti naawa suinummu a pagra ate wa vi Izirali demma ale jam gɔk santiri a nyini ale suinum pagrisa la ŋaaŋ.

ref: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
text: Ejipiti demma ale Faaro wusumaŋa ale torokoma ale wusum duerisa ale kpaliŋ nyeerisaŋa meena a vi Izirali a ga paari ba, ba le kali a moata nyakpiemu a moata Pi Yayirot a tuk Baal Zefon nyiŋla.

ref: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
text: Faaro ale ga tuak la, Izirali demma yaa zak nya ale Ejipiti demma a gɔk santiri a vi ba. Yɔgsum yaa yik ba ate ba kaari a wi Naawen.

ref: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
text: Ba yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Ka vie ale kan bo Ejipiti ate fi yaa ta ti jam gɔi kosikka po ayen ti kpi yaa? Ka boan le la ate fi nye a ta ti nyini Ejipiti nyini?

ref: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
text: Tama an weeni fu Ejipiti ayen, <Basi tidek ti nyiini, basi ate ti tom a te Ejipiti demma?> Ku ti le zunchoŋ ase ti nin tom a te Ejipiti demma a gaam ti nin kpi gɔnni po!>>

ref: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
text: Moosis yaa tulisi nuruma ayen, <<Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa. Ni zaani giŋgiŋ ate ni ale nya varibasika kaai ate Naawen a za wa ta jam jinla la. Ejipiti demma ate ni a nya ba jinla la ni kan ŋman nya ba.

ref: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
text: Naawen ale kpaliŋ a te ni. Ni tin nye diki.>>

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
text: Ate Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi kaari a wi mi? Weeni Izirali demma ayen ba a cheŋ.

ref: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
text: Zak fi doani a teeri fi nisaŋa nyakpiemu zuk a poori nyiamu ate Izirali demma a va nyakpiemu po tɛŋ kosik zuk a taam.

ref: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
text: M le basi ate Ejipiti demma suiniima a pagra ate ba siŋ a vi ni. Ate m nya zula Faaro ale wa kpaliŋ nyeerisaŋa ale wa wusum duerisaŋa nyiŋ.

ref: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
text: Ate Wen maarɔwa ale dɛ Izirali kpaliŋ nyeerisaŋa niŋ a cheŋ la yaa yeeri wadek a taam ba ŋaaŋ. Chiŋmanni ale a maari ba la a yeeri di dek ba niŋ a taam zaani ba ŋaaŋ,

ref: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
text: a yaa bo Ejipiti kpaliŋ nyeerisaŋa ale Izirali suŋsuŋ. Yɔkku meena chiŋmanni a ta ka legi a jam kauk kunyi ale ta bolim a jam kauk kunkula. Ba waai an moata wa choa yokku meena.

ref: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
text: Ate Moosis yaa teeri wa nisaŋa nyakpiemu zuk, ate yok kula meena Naawen a basi ate kori geŋ va pagrik a fuk nyakpiemu ate ku chim tɛŋ kosik. Ate nyaataŋa a poori,

ref: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
text: ate Izirali demma a cheŋ va nyakpiemu po tɛŋ kosik zuk a taam ate nyiam parik a bo ba juga ale ba gala.

ref: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
text: Yɔkku suŋsuŋ Naawen a yaa nya nyini bolimu ale chiŋmanni a nya Ejipiti kpaliŋ nyeerisaŋa a yaa basi ate butimka a jam.

ref: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
text: Wa nye kama ate ba torokoma wiilima a yeeri ate ba damka a tua. Ate Ejipiti demma a weeni ayen, <<Ni te ti cheŋ abe ti ge Izirali demma. Naawen ale kpaliŋ a maari ba a ta chaab ale Ejipiti.>>

ref: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Teeri fi nisaŋa nyakpiemu zuk ate nyiamu a ŋmani a lik Ejipiti demma ale ba torokoma ale ba wusum duerisaŋa.>>

ref: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
text: Moosis a teeri wa doani nyakpiemu zuk, ate vari ale veenti la nyakpiemu a pilim ŋman bu jigini, Ejipiti demma a chali a cheŋ bu jigi, ate Naawen a chuiri ba a basi nyakpiemu po.

ref: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
text: Nyiamu a chali a ŋmani ŋaaŋ a lik torokoma ale wusum duerisaŋa, Faaro kpaliŋ nyeerisaŋa ale va Izirali demma a siŋ nyakpiemu po la. Ba wanyi mɛ la an vuugi ya.

ref: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
text: Alege Izirali demma a va nyakpiemu tɛŋ kosik zuk ate nyiam pagrik a bo ba juga ate m kala mɛ a bo ba gala.

ref: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
text: Dai dila danni Naawen yaa vari Izirali demma Ejipiti demma nisa po a basi, ate Izirali demma a nya Ejipiti demma ale kpi doa kunkɔŋni la.

ref: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
text: Izirali demma ale nya Naawen ale sak pagrim kpiemu ale Ejipiti demma la, nuruma yaa chali Naawen yɔgsum ale ta mariŋka ale wa ale Moosis wa tomteerɔwa.

ref: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
text: Moosis ale Izirali demma yaa yi yiini de a pak Naawen ayen. <<M le yi yiili a pak Naawen, diila wa zuak ka yegayega. Wusummu ale bu duerɔwa wa yuk basi nyakpiemu po.

ref: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
text: Naawen ka m pagrɔ ale m yiili, wa chim ka m varibasika. Wa ka m Wen, m be le pak wa, m kowa Wen, m be le zak wa yuenni a zaani.

ref: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
text: Naawen ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ, Naawen ale wa yuenni.

ref: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
text: Faaro torokoma ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma wa yuk ba basi nyakpiemu po. Faaro kpagi maŋsaŋa a siŋ ka Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku po.

ref: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
text: Nya liuŋtaŋa a lim ba. Ba siŋ liuŋku po ase tintain la.

ref: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
text: <<Naawen yaa, fi naamu zuaka bo fi juga nisaŋa po. Naawen yaa, fi juga nisaŋa a lik dachiaka nɔi.

ref: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
text: Fi naamu zuaka po, fi yuk baai ale kisi fu la a lɔnsi. Fi basi ate fi suipuurumu ale a de nna pɔkpɔk la a nyini a dɛ baai ale a zɛri fi wie ase wuuk la a basi.

ref: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
text: Fi nyueŋa vuusika a basi ate nyaataŋa a tigsi a vi chaab zuk. Nya tii ale a chali la a zaani giŋgiŋ ase parik la. Nya liuŋtaŋa a nye diki nyakpiemu suŋsuŋ.

ref: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
text: <<Dachiaka yaa nak suinum ayen, <Mi le vi a yik ba m le pai ba ŋantaŋa. M le gomsi a kɔlim ba meena. M le yeeri m gebik woŋka ate m nisaŋa a ko ba meena.>

ref: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
text: Alege fi peeri ale fi vuusumu ate nyakpiemu a lik ba. Ate ba siŋ tɛŋ ase nanlik la nyakpientaŋa po.

ref: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
text: Fi teeri fi juga nisaŋa ate tɛŋka a nɛ ba.

ref: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
text: <<Fi ŋmanteka nyiŋ, fi le dɛ nuru baai ate fi da tuesi la niŋ. Fi pagrimu nyiŋ fi le gani ba ta cheŋ fi tuilum boka jigini.

ref: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
text: Tɛŋsaŋa nuruma ale wom ate ba nyiŋsa a gɔk, yɔgsum ale yik Filistia demma.

ref: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
text: Edom nalimaŋa yɔgsum ale yik ba, Moab niŋdeerɔma nyiŋsa ale kasim a gɔk, Keenan demma ale nyaliŋ a bɛ.

ref: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
text: Yɔgsum ale siŋ ba zuk. Fi nisa pagrimu nyiŋ ba le nye diki ase tintain la, Naawen yaa, ate fi nuruma ate fi da la a ga taamu.

ref: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
text: Fi le ta ba jam jo a vuk ba guuk kuui ate fidek soa la zuk, juijui ate fi Naawen a nye magsi fi boka la, jigi weleŋka ate fi Nyɔnɔwa a nye ale fi nisa la.

ref: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
text: Naawen ale dɛ wa naamu a kasim a cheŋ wuu.>>

ref: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
text: Faaro wusumaŋa ale torokoma ale wusum duerɔma a yaa siŋ nyiamu po, ate Naawen a ta nyakpiemu nyaataŋa a jam lik ba, alege Izirali demma a cheŋ tɛŋ kosik zuk a taam.

ref: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
text: Ate Miriam, Naawen biisiteerɔwa, Aaron tuawa a pai sinyak a nyo nisa po, ate nipooma meena a va wa ale sinyaksa a gɔk.

ref: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
text: Miriam yaa yi yiili a te ba ayen, <<Yi yiili a pak Naawen, diila wa yuenni a zuak kama. Wusum ale bu duerɔ wa yuk a basi nyakpiemu po.>>

ref: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
text: Ate Moosis yaa dɛ Izirali demma niŋ a ta ba nyini Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku jigini ate ba cheŋ a jo Sur Gɔnni po daa ŋata alege ba an nya nyiamoa.

ref: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
text: Ba le jam paari Mara la, ba an baga a nyu nyiamu diila bu tua kama. Dila ale soa ate ba a wi dula jigini ayen Mara la.

ref: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
text: Dila nyiŋ nuruma yaa jaa ŋuuni a ta chaab ale Moosis, a weeni ayen, <<Ti le nyu ka boa?>>

ref: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
text: Moosis yaa kaari wi Naawen, ate Naawen yaa dak diok a sak wa. Moosis yaa pai yuk a basi nyiamu po ate bu tagri a masa. Dula jigini Naawen yaa te ba sinsaga ale chamsi ba a nya.

ref: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
text: Wa weeni ayen, <<Ni dan kpesi a wom Naawen ni Wenni lueluk ale a nye dii ale nala wa nina po la ale kpesi a wom wa sinsaŋŋa ale a va ŋa meena, m kan ta nyiŋtuilaŋa dɛ ŋaai ate m ta jam Ejipiti demma zuk la a jam ni zuwa, diila ka Mi ale Naawen dii ale a tebi ni la.

ref: Later the Israelites came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and
text: Ate ba yaa jam Elim, kauk kuui ate bulisa pi ale siye ale kpinkpatta tiisa pisiyopɔi, ate ba wari kali dula a moata nyiamu.

ref: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
text: Izirali naakuuni meena yaa nyini Elim a jam Sin Gɔi kosikka ale bo Elim ale Sinai suŋsuŋ la. Ku jam ka benni po chi kaai ale a saari siyewa la, ka daa pi ale ŋanu dai ba le basi Ejipiti la ŋaaŋnyiŋ.

ref: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
text: Gɔi kosikka po Izirali demma meena jam a ŋuuni kama a ta chaab ale Moosis ale Aaron.

ref: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
text: Izirali demma yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ku ti le zunchoŋŋa ase Naawen a nin poom ko ti Ejipiti tɛŋka po. Dula ti nyiem kali kama a gilim samɔnsa ale lanta a dɛ ŋandiintaŋa meena ate ti a yaali la, alege fi ta ti jam gɔnni de po ayen nuruma de meena a viiri.>>

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
text: Ate Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<M le basi ate ŋandiinta nyini wenŋmazuk a siŋ a te ni. Nuruma a nyini daa meena a tigsi a zuak a magsi dai dila danni. Suik kude po m le nye ba a nya ase ba le va m sinsaŋŋa ya.

ref: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
text: Daa ŋayuebiwa danni ba tigsi ku paari naŋtuok nɔi buye a ta jam jo a dik daa ŋaye.>>

ref: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
text: Dila la Moosis ale Aaron yaa weeni Izirali demma meena ayen, <<Junɔi ni le seba ayen ka Naawen ale ta ni nyini Ejipiti a nyini.

ref: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
text: Abe saluik ni le nya Naawen zulaŋa, dii nyiŋla wa wom ni le ŋuuni a te wa la kama. Tama ka bana, ate ni ŋuuni a ta chaab ale ti?>>

ref: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
text: Moosis mɛ yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni le seba ayen ka Naawen ale te ni lanta ate ni ŋɔbi junɔinni ale ŋandiinta meena ate ni a yaali saluiku la, dii nyiŋla wa wom ni le a ŋuuni a ta chaab ale wa la kama. Tama ka bana? Ni kan ŋuuni a ta chaab ale ka tama, alege ka Naawen.>>

ref: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
text: Moosis yaa weeni Aaron ayen, <<Weeni Izirali demma meena ayen, <Ni jam Naawen niŋ, diila wa wom ni ŋuunika kama.>>

ref: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
text: Aaron ale boro a biisi a te Izirali demma meena la, ba yaa nya gɔnni geŋka, ate Naawen zulaŋa nyaksi a nyini chiŋmari po a nyini.

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Naawen a weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
text: <<M wom Izirali demma ŋuunika kama. Weeni ba ayen, <Junɔi ba le ŋɔbi lanta, abe saluik ba dɛ ŋandiinta a chak. Ate ni seba ayen Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

ref: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
text: Junɔi dila yeŋsa yaa jam sueri ba boka jigini, ate saluiku maglim yaa lo gilim ba boka jigini.

ref: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
text: Maglimu ale kpaanti la, ŋanta ase ŋmoruk tana la kabsa kabsa yaa doa tɛŋ gɔnni po.

ref: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
text: Izirali demma ale nya ŋantaŋa la, ba yaa bek chaab ayen, <<Ka boa ale nna?>> Diila ba zɛ le ka ŋan baai la. Moosis yaa weeni ba ayen, ka ŋandiin tii ate Naawen a te ni ayen ni dɛ la.

ref: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
text: Naawen abe le weeni diila ale nna. <Waai meena a tigsi a magsi wa le a yaali diila. Pai chin nɔi a magsi nuru meena ale bo viuku po la.

ref: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
text: Izirali demma yaa nye ba le weeni ba diila, ba gela tigsi yega, ba gela tigsi maga.

ref: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
text: Moosis yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Waai a kan tali ŋantaŋa gela ate ku paari chum saluiwa.>>

ref: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
text: Alege ba gela an wom Moosis ale weeni diila, ale tali gela a ta paari saluik, ate nanzue a sueri ba po a nyuŋ. Moosis sui yaa jam a puuri ale ba.

ref: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
text: Saluik meena waai meena a tigsi ka wa le yaali diila, wenbinni a dan a nak ate ku tuila, ŋa nyaliŋ a bɛ.

ref: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
text: Daa ŋayuebiwa danni ba a tigsi ka buye, china ŋaye a magsi nuru yeŋ ate niŋdeerɔma a jam weeni a sak Moosis.

ref: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
text: Moosis yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna. <Chum ka vuusum dai, vuusum dai dii ale ta tuilum a te Naawen. Dila nyiŋ ni sɛ ni le a yaali ayen ni sɛ ŋan baai la abe ni dik ni le a yaali ayen ni dik ŋan baai la. Ŋan baai ale a tali la ni pai zaani ate ku paari saluik.> >>

ref: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
text: Ba yaa pai zaani ate ku paari saluik ase Moosis ale weeni diila alege ba an nyuŋ ya yaase nanzue a jo ba.

ref: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
text: Moosis yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni dɛ jinla, dii nyiŋla jinla ka Vuusum dai a te Naawen. Ni kan nya ŋandiinta tɛŋka jinla.

ref: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
text: Daa ŋayuebi ni tigsi ŋandiintaŋa alege daa ŋayopɔiwa, Vuusum danni, ŋandiinta kan boro.>>

ref: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
text: Alege dila meena nuruma gela a diem nyini kama daa ŋayopɔiwa danni ayen ba tigsi, alege ba an nya jaaboa.

ref: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Nama taa ni zɛri m wieŋa ale m sinsaŋŋa vaka a paari ka dimpo?

ref: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
text: Ni ta ni popola po ayen Naawen a te ni Vuusum danni kama, dila ale soa ate daa ŋayuebiwa danni wa te ni ŋandiinta a magsi daa ŋaye la. Waai meena a bo wa le bo juijui la daa ŋayopɔiwa danni, waai a kan nyini peelim.

ref: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
text: Nuruma yaa vuusi daa ŋayopɔiwa danni.

ref: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
text: Izirali demma a jam a wi wenzuk ŋandiintaŋa ayen, ka manna. Ŋa jam peenti kama ase ŋanta bie la. A masa nna se boroborok faasiŋ ate ba nye ale siita la.

ref: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”

text: <<Ase nuru a dan yik wa lie a da ase tomteerɔ la, wa kan boro fasiyaa ase nidoa tomteerɔba ale ka diila.

ref: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
text: Ase wa dan kan nye ate wa kpagni waai ale lueri wa a te wadek la sui a yɔk ya, ku a fɛ ate wa kowa a da tuesi wa. Wa ka suik a pai wa da a te nichamma, wa ale kan ŋman ta siaka ale wa la nyiŋŋa.

ref: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
text: Ase wa dan lueri wa a te wa biik, ku a fɛ ate wa te wa suik ase lie la.

ref: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
text: Ase wa dan faari nipok wa choa, ku a fɛ ate wa kan mini pok kpagni ŋandiinta ale kɔlima yaase wa kan goa ale wa.

ref: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
text: Ase wa dan kan te nipowa ŋantaŋa de butawa, nipowa a baga a cheŋ fasiyaa kama a kan tuni ligri ku nyiŋŋa.

ref: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
text: Alege wa dan kan potim seba ale nye ya, alege ka Wen ale basi ate ku nye wa chali cheŋ juijui ate mi ale dak la.

ref: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
text: Alege nuru a dan potim seba ale ko waai, ni ta wa a nyini m kuŋkuŋku zuk a nyini a ko wa.

ref: Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
text: <<Nuru waai a dan zu nuru a da, yaase wa ta nuruwa ate ba yik wa, ku a fɛ ate ba ko wa.

ref: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
text: <<Nuru waai a dan ka te wa ko yaase wa ma, ku a fɛ ate ba ko wa.

ref: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
text: nuru waai ale chubi la ba kan nye wa wari ya ase nwala a nin yiti boro a cheŋ ale wa tachekka, ku a fɛ ate nuru waai ale chubi la a tuni waai ale koani la, wa le nye ate wa nya nyiŋyɔgsa a paari.

ref: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
text: alege ba kan dari wa turi ase yɔmawa a nin yiti da dila danni yaase ku daa ŋaye po a boro a cheŋ dii nyiŋla, ka wa ale soa yɔmawa.

ref: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
text: <<Ase nuruba a dan kpaliŋ a nak nipok puuk ate wa biak diipo ale kan magsi la alege a potim nya tuemoa, waai ale nye dila la ku a fɛ ate wa tuni nipowa chorɔwa ale a weeni diila ate buusa boka dɔkku a te suik.

ref: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
text: Alege wa dan nya tuem yega, ni ko wa,

ref: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
text: <<Ase nuru a dan nak nidoa yaase nipok tomteerɔ num a kaasi, ku a fɛ ate wa basi ate tomteerɔwa a cheŋ fasiyaa wa nummu ate wa kpagni a kaasi la nyiŋ,

ref: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
text: <<Ase lalik a dan chub nidoa yaase nipok a ko, ku a fɛ ate ba yuk lalikka ale tintana a ko, ni kan ŋɔbi ka lammu. Alege waai ale soa lalikka la, ni kan nye wa wari ya.

ref: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
text: Alege lalikka a daa chub ate ba kaam ka nyɔnɔwa alege ate wa an yik ka, ate ka ko nidoa yaase nipok, ku a fɛ ate ba yuk lalikka ale ka nyɔnɔwa a ko.

ref: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
text: Alege ku dan magsi wa tunika, wa baga tuni dii ale magsi la kama a vari wa nyuvunni a basi.

ref: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
text: Sinsaŋŋa de dek ale a tom tuima ase lalik a nin chub nidoabili yaase nipokbili.

ref: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
text: <<Ase nuru a dan lak goluk yaase wa tu goluk ale an si ku ate naab yaase boniŋ a lo du,

ref: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
text: golukku nyɔnɔwa ale wa tuni pamini. Ku a fɛ ate wa tuni ku nyɔnɔwa abe wa tanla duŋ kpiuku.

ref: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
text: <<Ase waai lalik kpaaŋ a dan kɔni a waai lalik kpaaŋ ate ka kpi, ku a magsi ka ba yik javukku a da a lab ligraŋa ale duŋ kpiuku a soa ase chaab la a te chaab.

ref: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
text: Alege ba dan seba ayen ka lalikka nyeka ale duŋsa chubika alege ka nyɔnɔwa an yik ka, ku a fɛ ate ka nyɔnɔwa a tuni, wa yik duŋ a tuni duŋka nyiŋ abe wa tanla duŋ kpiuku.

ref: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
text: <<Ase nuru a dan zu lalik kpaaŋ yaase posuk a tɔgri yaase wa pai da, ku a fɛ ate wa tuni niiga ŋanu lalik kpaaŋka nyiŋ abe wa tuni piisa ŋanaansi pa yeoŋku nyiŋ.

ref: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
text: <<Ase nuru a dan ta wa duŋsa a nyini si dɛ wuuk a basi ate duŋsaŋa a jo waai laŋ yaase kaduk po, ku a fɛ ate wa pai wadek laŋ maŋ ale kaduk maŋ a te tuni.

ref: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
text: <<Ase bolim a daa dɛ kapeok ale za yaase laŋ meena waai ale beeri bolimu la, ku a fɛ ate wa tuni.

ref: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
text: <<Ase nuru a dan pai wa kpana yaase ŋanta a te wa vaanchoa ayen wa dueni a te wa, ate ba zu ŋa wa yenni po ate ba dan yik zuewa, ku a fɛ kama ate wa tuni ŋa ku nɔi buye.

ref: But if the thief isn't caught, some judges will decide if you are the guilty one.
text: Alege ba dan kan nya zuewa, yenni nyɔnɔwa a jam buusa boorɔwa niŋ a pagsi wa nɔi ase ka wa ale pai wa vaanchoawa nitalimu yaa daa wa.

ref: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
text: Suik kuui meena po ate nuru a va a ta jaab ase boniŋ yaase lalik kpaaŋ yaase posuk yaase garuk yaase jabuui meena ale bei a bo fi jigi la, ate waai a dan yen wa lo kama, ku a fɛ ate wa tuni a te wa vaanchoawa ku nɔi buye.

ref: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
text: <<Ase nuru a dan pai wa boniŋ yaase lalik kpaaŋ yaase posuk yaa duŋ kaai meena a te wa vaanchoa ayen wa nya a te wa, ate ka kpi yaase ka koani yaa ba yik ka ate waai an nya ya,

ref: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
text: nanpaŋŋa ale bo baai bayema suŋsuŋ la, a nya wanni zuk ale pɛka Naawen niŋ ayen wa vaanchoawa an pai nisa a tiri wa nitalimu. Duŋka nyɔnɔwa ale siak kude ate tutuna a kan boro.

ref: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
text: Alege ba dan zu duŋka fi vaanchoawa jigi, ku a fɛ ate wa tuni ka nyɔnɔwa.

ref: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
text: Be dan ka duŋ waarik ka choa ale yik ka, wa ta lamboanaŋa a jam ate ba nya ate dila ale basi ate wa kan tuni ka nyiŋŋa.

ref: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
text: <<Ase nuru a dan piem duŋ wa vaanchoa jigi ate ka koani yaase ka kpi alege ka nyɔnɔwa an moata, ku a fɛ ate wa tuni.

ref: But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it. Laws for Everyday Life The Lord said:
text: Alege ka nyɔnɔwa a dan moata duŋka, waai ale piem duŋka la a kan tuni jaaboa. Alege wa dan te ka ligra ale tuesi duŋka, wa le te lig dii ale tuesi ka la, a deri magsi duŋka ale bɛ la nyiŋ.

ref: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
text: <<Ase nuru a dan fɛ goa ale nipok kaliak kaai ale kan ta yoŋ la, ku a fɛ ate wa nye a kaa yaali ate wa chim wa pok.

ref: But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
text: Ase nipok kaliaka kowa a dan zɛri an pai wa a te nidoawa, ku a fɛ ate fi diem tuni fi le magsi fi tuni dii a te waai ale kan seba nidoa la.

ref: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
text: <<Kan basi ate chichirik wiirik a vua.

ref: Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
text: <<Nuru waai a dan goa ale duŋ, ku a fɛ ate ni ko wa.

ref: Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
text: <<Waai a dan kaabi wen yoŋ alege daa Naawen ku a fɛ ate ba kaasi wa.

ref: Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
text: <<Ni kan nye nichaanɔ viesiviesiga ate ku jo wa nyiŋŋa, diila nama a jam ka nicham Ejipiti tɛŋka po.

ref: Do not mistreat widows or orphans.
text: <<Ni kan nya pukɔgi yaase kpiŋ a nueri.

ref: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
text: Ni dan nye dila ate ba kaari a te mu, m le wom ba kaarika.

ref: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
text: Mi sui ale puuri ate m ko ni ale gebik. Ni pooma ale chim pukɔga ate ni bisaŋa ale chim kpiŋsa.

ref: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
text: Ase fi dan tuesi fi vaanchoa gattiak ase peemka la, wenbinni ale di siŋka, ta cheŋ ga te wa,

ref: because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
text: dii nyiŋla wa gattiaka meena ale la, ate wa ta a pili wa nyiŋka. Wa le pili ka boa a goa? Ase wa dan kaari a te mi, m le wom, mi ka waai ale ta jiirim.

ref: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
text: <<Kan nye dii ate Wen a kisi la yaase fi ka a te baai ale a nya fi nuruma zuk la.

ref: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
text: <<Kan peri ŋandiinta ale daamu tiiritaŋa ate ni te mi la. <<Ku a fɛ ate ni te mi ni bi kpaŋŋa.

ref: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
text: Ni nye dila dekdega a te mu ni niiŋa ale piisaŋa. Ni basi ate ŋa bo ale ŋa mama a paari daa ŋayopɔi, alege ni pai ŋa a te mi da naanika danni.

ref: You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
text: <<Ni ale chim ka nuru baai ale ta tuilum. Dila nyiŋ ni kan ŋɔbi duŋ waarik ale yik duŋ kaai la lammoa. Ni yuk te baasa.

ref: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
text: <<Kan va nuru boanni a nye a kaasi. Ni daa bo buusa, ni kan basi wensieŋa abe ni va nuru boanni,

ref: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
text: abe ni kan ŋman te jajak buusa boka po.

ref: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
text: <<Ase fi dan nya fi dachiak lalik kpaaŋ yaase wa boniŋ ale ka cheŋ a bɛ, yik ta ga te wa.

ref: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
text: Fi dan nya waai ale kisi fu la boniŋ ale ka ji ŋanta a lo, kan basi ka dula. Seba ate fi maari wa ate ka zaani.

ref: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
text: <<Ku a fɛ ate ni bo wensie buusa a te nuru waai ale jaŋ la.

ref: Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like. Laws for the Sabbath The Lord said:
text: <<Kan namsi nichaanɔ. Nama dek seba nicham chimka ale ka diila kama, diila ni le jam chim ka nicham a bo Ejipiti tɛŋka po.

ref: Plant and harvest your crops for six years,
text: <<Bena ŋayuebi ale a magsi ni pai bori ni tattaŋa a che ni ŋandiintaŋa,

ref: but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
text: alege bena ŋayopɔiwa po ni kan kpa. Ate dila ale basi ate ŋanjaksaŋa ale bo ni po la a nya ŋandiinta a dɛ, ate duŋ waarisa a dɛ bala. Ni kaduksaŋa ale bo yeeŋa po la ni kan kpa, ni yɔna tiisaŋa mɛ ni kan nya si zuwa.

ref: Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
text: <<Ni pai daa ŋayuebi a tom nidek tuima, alege daa ŋayopɔiwa danni ni kan tom, ate dila ale basi ate ni lalik kpaansaŋa ale bonsaŋa ale ni yɔmma ate ba biak ba ni yieŋa po la, ale nichamma a vuusi a nya nyiŋ pagra.

ref: Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names. Three Annual Festivals (Exodus
text: <<Ni kpesi nidek a nye dii meena ate m weeni ni la. Ni kaa wi wen yona yue. Ni kan basi ate waai wom dila ni noaŋa po.

ref: Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
text: <<Kan te mi ziim ase kaabka la ate dabinta a bo bu po. Mi tigini kpapalaŋa tiiritaŋa ku a fɛ ate fi kan basi ate vari veenti ŋa.

ref: Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
text: ate waai a kan biak a kaasi yaase wa chim kirik ni tɛŋka po. M le te ni nyuvuri woŋ.

ref: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
text: <<Ni dɛ Ŋandiinta Tigini Ale Yɔna Ŋaai Ale Dɛ Niŋ a bɛ ni tattaŋa po la. Ni dɛ Ŋandiintaŋa Tigini Benni Kpeglimka Po, ase nama a nin tigsi ni ŋantaŋa ni tattaŋa po a ta jo.

ref: Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
text: <<Buta meena benni po nidoama a magsi ba jam Nyɔnɔwa waai ale ka Naawen la niŋ kama.

ref: Celebrate three festivals each year in my honor.
text: <<Ben meena po ni dɛ tigi buta a te mu.

ref: Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
text: <<Ni dɛ Tigi Dii Ŋandiinta Ate Dabinta a ka ti po la. Ni pai daa ŋayopɔi a dɛ ŋandiin tii ate dabinta a ka ti po la, ase m le weeni ni la. Ni nye kude diipo ate m dak la Abib chiika po ale ka dila po ate ni nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka po a nyini la. Waai a kan jam mi niŋ ale nikotta.

ref: Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. A Promise and a Warning The Lord said:
text: <<Ta ŋandiin tii ale dɛ niŋ a bɛ fi kaduksaŋa po la a jam Naawen fi Wenni yenni po. Be kan dik bu poali ku ma biisim po.>>

ref: I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you.
text: <<Nya mi a tom ka Wen maarɔ ayen wa dɛ ni niŋ a nya ni zuk abe wa ta ni a jam juijui ate m gomsi la.

ref: Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion.
text: Ni zaan nalimnyiini abe ni wom wa le a weeni diila. Ni kan nye tukpari ale wa. Wa kan vɔŋ te ni tukpanni, ayen mi Yuenni ale bo wa po la nyiŋŋa.

ref: My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
text: Mi maarɔwa ale dɛ ni niŋ a ta ni jam Amori ale Yit ale Perizzi ale Keenan ale Yivi ale Jebus demma tɛŋka po, ate mi ale ko ba.

ref: Don't worship their gods or follow their customs. Instead, destroy their idols and shatter their stone images.
text: Ni kan koori tɛŋ ba wenaŋa niŋŋa yaase ni puusi ŋa yaase ni va ŋa nyeelaŋa. Ku a fɛ ate ni kaasi ŋa a bugsi ba tintanaŋa nna bunabuna.

ref: Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong.
text: Ni puusi Naawen ni Wenni, ate wa niauŋku ale bo ni ŋandiintaŋa ale ni nyiamu zuk. M le yiak yuem ni jigi a basi,

ref: But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere.
text: Alege m kan yiak ba ka ben yeŋ po, dii nyiŋla tɛŋka ale doa ate gɔi duŋsa ale bo ka po a gilim ni.

ref: Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
text: Mi ale yiak ba ka maga maga a te ni ate ku paari diipo ate ni le piisi a soa tɛŋka.

ref: I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land.
text: <<Mi ale basi ate ni tɛŋ banni a nyini Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku a ga paari Filistia Nyakpiemu a nyini gɔnni a ta cheŋ ga paari Benni. M le pai nuruma ale bo tɛŋka po la a nyo ni nisima po ate ni yiak ba a basi.

ref: But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods.
text: Ni kan nye nɔiyeŋ ale ba yaase ba wenaŋa.

ref: Don't let them stay in your land. They will trap you into sinning against me and worshiping their gods.
text: Ni kan basi ate ba bo ni tɛŋka po, ni dan basi ate ba boro, ba le basi ate ni nye biem a kaasi mi, dii nyiŋla ba wenaŋa puusika ale chim baruk a te ni.>>

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and
text: Ate wa yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Jueli jam Naawen jigi fi ale Aaron ale Nadab ale Abiyu ale Izirali nisɔm pisiyopɔiwa. Ni yalima ale mi a puusi,

ref: Moses gave the Lord's instructions to the people, and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded!”
text: Moosis ale jam ga weeni nuruma Naawen wieŋa ale wa sinsaŋŋa la, ba jam tulisi ale lueluk yeŋ ayen, <<Dii meena ate Naawen a weeni la ti le nye.>>

ref: Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said. The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel.
text: Moosis yaa ŋmarisi dii meena ate Naawen a weeni la a dueni. Dai dii ale paasaŋ la, saluik yokyokwa wa yaa yiti a sɛ kuŋkuŋ guuku chiak, a feri tintana pi ale ŋaye a sɛ zaŋŋa la, ate ŋa tagri za Izirali buuni pi ale ŋayewa nankula po.

ref: He also sent some young men to burn offerings and to sacrifice bulls as special offerings to the Lord.
text: Ate wa yaa tom Izirali nidoa paalukku, ate ba nye tiirim juka a kaab lalik paalisa ase suiyɔgni tiirita la a te Naawen.

ref: Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar.
text: Moosis yaa pai ziimu geli a nyo kuta china po, ale pai geli ndila a misi basi kuŋkuŋku zuk.

ref: Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
text: Wa yaa pai Nɔiyeŋka Gbaŋka a kariŋ te nuruma. Ate ba tulisi ayen, <<Ti le nye dii meena ate Naawen a weeni la. Ti le siak a te wa.>>

ref: Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
text: Moosis yaa pai ziimu a misi basi nuruma nyiŋ ale weeni ayen, <<Kude ka nɔiyeŋka ziimu ale la ate Naawen a nye ale ni a magsi chaab ale wieŋa de.>>

ref: Moses and Aaron, together with Nadab and Abihu and the
text: Moosis ale Aaron ale Nadab ale Abiyu ale Izirali nisɔm pisiyopɔiwa yaa jueli nya Izirali Wenni.

ref: and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something that looked like a pavement made out of sapphire, and it was as bright as the sky.
text: Wa naŋtaataŋa po a jam a nye ase ka suik ate ba pai tintain sobta a nye la, ku jam ka nna cheri ase chiŋmanni dek la.

ref: Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank. Moses on Mount Sinai
text: Alege Wen sui an jam puuri ale Izirali niŋdeerɔma dɛ. Ba jam nya Wen kama ale jam dɛ ale nyu.

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up on the mountain and stay here for a while. I will give you the two flat stones on which I have written the laws that my people must obey.”
text: Naawen a weeni Moosis ayen, <<Jueli mi jigi guuku zuk a bo dela, ate m pai tintain paglaksaŋa ale m sinsaŋŋa ale m wieŋa ate m ŋmarisi la a te fu a magsi ba sakka.>>

ref: Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
text: Moosis yaa cheŋ ale Josua wa pasaŋdoawa, Moosis a jam jueli ka guuku zuk Wen jigi.

ref: Moses had told the leaders, “Wait here until we come back. Aaron and Hur will be with you, and they can settle any arguments while we are away.”
text: Wa weeni nisɔmma ayen, <<Ni limisi ti dela ate ku paari diipo ate ti le ŋman jam ni jigi la. Aaron ale Yur a bo ale ni kama, nuru waai a dan ta wari, wa cheŋ ba jigi.>>

ref: When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it,
