text: Ate wa ŋman sugri duŋka ponni po ŋantaŋa ale naŋsaŋa a pai vi juka tiirimu zuk a ju dakanni zuk.

ref: Next, Aaron sacrificed the goat for the sins of the people, as he had done with the sacrifice for his own sins.
text: Aaron yaa ta nuruma tiirimu a jam. Wa yaa pai buuku a magsi nuruma biem tiirimu a yaa tɔgri a te magsi biem tiirimu ase wa le liŋ a nye diila.

ref: And so, he burned this sacrifice on the altar in the proper way.
text: Wa yaa ta juka tiirimu a jam te va ku le magsi diila.

ref: He also presented the grain sacrifice and burned a handful of the flour on the altar as part of the morning sacrifice.
text: Wa yaa ta ŋandiinta tiirimu mɛ a jam a nye nisa nɔi a ju dakanni zuk a gum saluiku juka tiirimu po.

ref: Finally, he killed the bull and the ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing on the people. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against the four sides of the altar.
text: Wa tɔgri naamu ale padiaka mɛ ase suiyɔgni tiirim la a te nuruma. Wa bisaŋa yaa pai ziimu a te wa ate wa boori basi kuŋkuŋku kabtaŋa meena.

ref: His sons placed all the fat, as well as the kidneys and the lower part of the liver
text: Ate ba yaa yeeri naamu ale padiaka kpapalaŋa, juiku kpapalaŋa, kpapala ŋaai ale lik la, yiimaŋa ale paŋni kauk kuui ale moata yiimaŋa la,

ref: Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar and lifted up the ribs and the right hind leg to show that these were dedicated to the Lord. This was done just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
text: Aaron yaa zak kuusini ale juga naŋka a sak Naawen ase zak sakka tiirim la a magsi chaab ale Moosis ale weeni diila.

ref: Aaron held out his hand and gave the people his blessing, before coming down from the bronze altar where he had offered the sacrifices.
text: Aaron yaa zak wa nisimaŋa a tuk nuruma nyiŋ a niak ba. Wa pai biem tiirimu ale juka tiirimu ale suiyɔgni tiiritaŋa a te nueri la wa yaa siŋ tɛŋ.

ref: He and Moses went into the sacred tent, and when they came out, they gave the people their blessing. Then the Lord appeared to the people in all of his glory.
text: Moosis ale Aaron yaa jo Tuka Viuku po. Ba ale ŋman nyini la, ba yaa niak nuruma ate Naawen pai wa nyaksika a sak nuruma meena.

ref: The Lord sent fiery flames that burned up everything on the altar, and when everyone saw this, they shouted and fell to their knees to worship the Lord.
text: Bolim yaa nyini Naawen jigi a jam dɛ juka tiirimu ale kpapalaŋa kuŋkuŋku zuk. Ate nuruma meena ale nya dila la, ba yaa nuem ale suipeentik ale koori tɛŋ a te wa zula.

ref: Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to.
text: Aaron nidoabilisaŋa Nadab ale Abiyu yaa pai jabuui ate ba pai a yeeri bolim la a yaa yeeri bolim a pai ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a nyoro. Ba taka bolim chaŋ a jam Naawen niŋ, alege an va wa wanni la.

ref: Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death.
text: Bolim yaa nyini Naawen jigi jam dɛ ba dula Naawen niŋ.

ref: Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said: “I demand respect from my priests, and I will be praised by everyone!” Aaron was speechless.
text: Moosis yaa weeni Aaron ayen, <<Dii ate Naawen a jam biisi a weeni ayen, <Baai ale a jam mi jigi la suŋsuŋ M le sak ayen m ta tuilum, nuruma meena niŋ M le nya zula.> >> Alege Aaron nye diki.

ref: Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.”
text: Moosis yaa wi Misael ale Elzafan Aaron kowa suoku Uzziel nidoabilisaŋa a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni jam dɛ a pai ni suataŋa tuka jigini niŋ a ta nyini peelim.>>

ref: Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire.
text: Ate Moosis yaa weeni Aaron ale wa nidoabili sinsila Eleaza ale Itamar ayen, <<Ni kan basi ni zuisaŋa dila, ni bɛ kan cheeri ni gattaŋa, dan kan daa di ni le kpi ate Naawen sui a puuri ale nuruma meena. Alege fi dɔkdemma ale Izirali demma a baga a kum baai ate Naawen a ko ale bolimu la kama.

ref: But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die. Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
text: Ni kan diem basi Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku dan kan daa di ni le kpi, dii nyiŋla Naawen a bobi ni kama.>> Ba yaa nye Moosis ale weeni ba diila.

ref: The Lord said to Aaron:
text: Naawen yaa weeni Aaron ayen,

ref: When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change.
text: Fi ale fi nidoabilisaŋa a kan nyu da pagriga yaase da buui ale kum ya diipo meena ni a jo Tuka Viuku po la, dan kan daa di ni le kpi ka ŋmarisi kaai ale ka doa a magsi nama ale ni gaŋsa a ta cheŋ.

ref: You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean.
text: Ku a fɛ ate ni gaari tuilum ŋanta a nyini ŋankoa po, abe ni gaari ŋan naliŋsa ale ŋan daŋtisa tɔgatɔga.

ref: You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
text: Sak Izirali demma meena ŋmarisi sii ate Naawen a te Moosis ate wa te ni la.

ref: Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar.
text: Moosis yaa weeni Aaron ale wa nidoabili sii ale tali la, Eleaza ale Itamar ayen, <<Ŋandiinta tiirimu ate ni ju ale bolim te Naawen ate ti tali la, ni dɛ ti kuŋkuŋku tɛŋ ni kan nyo dabinta du. Ka ŋandiin tii ale ŋmasi ta tuilum.

ref: The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place.
text: Ni dɛ ŋandiintaŋa dɛ tuilum jigi, dii nyiŋla ka fi ale fi nidoabilisaŋa charuk ale la tiirim buui ate ba ju ale bolim a te Naawen la po. Naawen ale weeni mi diila ale la.

ref: But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
text: Naŋka ate fi pai te la ale kuusini ale kpapalaŋa ate fi zak sak Naawen la. Ka fi ale fi nidoabilisaŋa daa meena charuk ale la ate Naawen a weeni la.>>

ref: When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said,
text: Moosis ale bek buuk kuui ale ka biem tiirim la wari la, wa yaa nya ayen ba ju ku kama, ate wa sui a puuri ale Aaron nidoabili sii ale tali la, Eleaza ale Itamar a yaa bek ayen,

ref: “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt.
text: <<Ka boa ale soa ate ni an ŋɔbi biem tiirimu duŋka Wen yenni po? Ka tuilum tiirim ate ba pai te ni ayen ni nye biem duisi basika ate nuruma chivieŋa a cheŋ.

ref: Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
text: Ziimu ale kan jo Wen yenni po la, ni ti ŋɔbi buuku ka Wen yenni po ase Naawen ale weeni diila.>>

ref: Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
text: Aaron yaa tulisi Moosis ayen, <<Jinla ba pai ba biem tiirimu ale juka tiirimu a te Naawen, alege wieŋa de chaab a nye mi nya kama. Ase mi dan poom ŋɔbi biem tiirimu duŋka kama jinla Naawen sui ti peenti kama?>>

ref: Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
text: Moosis ale wom nnala la, wa suinni yaa yɔk.

ref: The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
text: Alege ŋan yirin tii meena ale ta naŋsa sinaansi la ba ka kisuk ŋanta a te ni.

ref: Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
text: Nuru waai a dan tiri duŋ kpiuku ku a magsi ka wa sugri wa gattaŋa, wa le daŋ ka wadek a ga paari wen siŋka si ka ŋan daŋtisa a te ni.

ref: Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean.
text: kasilik ale wuri ale baŋ fiisa ale kasoluk ale bunoruk.

ref: Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening.
text: Bade meena ale a cheŋ ba lɔga zuk la a daŋ kama a te ni. Waai a dan tiri jaab kpiuk kula wa daŋ ka wadek a ga a paari wen siŋka.

ref: If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean.
text: Ba wanyi a dan lo liik po jabuui meena ale bo ka po la daŋ kama, ku a fɛ kama ate ni mobi liikka.

ref: If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
text: Ŋandiin tii ate ni a dɛ ate nyiam a bo ti po samɔniŋka po la a daŋ kama, ŋan ŋaasa meena ate ni a nyu ka po la a daŋ kama.

ref: If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed.
text: Jaab kpiuku ale a tiri jabuui meena la jabula a daŋ kama. Ku dan poom tiri daaniŋ yaase samɔniŋ kaai ate ba pai a dik la ba kaasi si. Ba daŋ kama. Ni nya ba ase ba daŋ kama la.

ref: A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean.
text: Alege bulik yaase vili ate ba a ŋari nyiam du la a nala kama, alege waai ale a tiri jakpiuku de wanyi la a daŋ kama.

ref: If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean.
text: Alege jakpiuku a dan lo ŋan buura meena ate ba a bori la po, ŋa nala kama.

ref: But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
text: Nyiam a dan bo bieŋa po ate jakpiuku a lo ŋa po ŋa daŋ kama a te ni.

ref: If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening.
text: << <Alege duŋ sii ate ni a ŋɔbi la kanyi a dan kpi, waai ale tiri jakpiuku la a daŋ kama a ga paari wen siŋka.

ref: If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
text: Waai ale ŋɔbi jakpiuku la a sugri wa gattaŋa kama, wa a daŋ ka wadek a ga paari wen siŋka. Waai ale a pai jakpiuku la ku a fɛ kama ate wa sugri wa gattaŋa abe wa chim waai ale daŋ wadek a ga paari wen siŋka.

ref: Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground.
text: Ni kan ŋɔbi jabuui ale cheŋ tɛŋka zuk la, wa cheŋ wa lɔgni zuk yaase naŋsa sinaansi yaase naŋ boari ku a kisi kama.

ref: If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are.
text: Ni kan daŋ nidek ale ŋantaŋa de. Ni kan basi ate ŋantaŋa de a daŋ ni yaase ni tiri ba a daŋ.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures.
text: Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni. Ni gaari nidek a jam m jigi abe ni ta tuilum, ale mi a ta tuilum kama. Ni be kan chim baai ale daŋ la a ta va chaab ale ŋan baai ale a cheŋ tɛŋka zuk la.

ref: I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
text: Ale ka Mi ale Naawen dii ale ta ni a nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka po a nyini ayen m chim ni Wen. Dila nyiŋla ni ta tuilum ale mi a ta tuilum kama.

ref: I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
text: Ku a fɛ ate ni a gaari ŋan daŋtisa ale naliŋsa baai ale magsi dɛka ale baai ale kan magsi dɛka.> >>

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period.
text: <<Weeni Izirali demma ayen, <Nipok a dan yik lɔgi a biak nidoabili wa daŋ kama a ga paari daa ŋayopɔi, ase wa daa lo chiak wa le daŋ diila.

ref: Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day,
text: Da naanika danni ba gebi biika yɔnni.

ref: Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another
text: Wa abe dan biak nipokbili wa daŋ kama a ga paari daa pi ale ŋanaansi ase diipo ate wa a lo chiak la. Wa limisi a paari daa pisiyuebi ale ŋayuebi ate ziimu a gebiri ate ba nye ate wa nala.

ref: When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin.
text: <<Ase nipowa a dan biak nidoabili yaase nipokbili da ŋaai ate wa cheri nyeka a nueri la, wa ta bein pabiik a jam te Tuka Viuku kaabteerɔwa Tuka Viuku nɔi. Wa maa ta nangbaŋ a jam magsi biem tiirim.

ref: After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl.
text: Wa pai ba te Naawen ate ba nye biem duisi basika te wa, ate ba dan nye nueri abe wa nala. Sinsaŋŋa ale nna a magsi nipok waai ale a biak nidoabili yaase nipokbili la.

ref: If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
text: Wa dan kan ta pabiiga wa ta nangbaŋsa siye a jam ate kanyi a soa juka tiirimu abe m kala a soa biem tiirimu. Suiku de po kaabteerɔwa ale nye biem duisi basika a te wa ate wa nala.> >>

ref: The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
text: Naawen a weeni Moosis ale Aaron ayen,

ref: If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests.
text: <<Nuru waai nyiŋ gbaŋ a dan ta birima yaase koosuk a baga a chim nyiŋ a baŋ tuem buui ale a chɔgsi, ba ta wa jam kaabteerɔwa Aaron yaase wa nidoabilisaŋa waai ale chim kaabteerɔ la jigi.

ref: If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Kaabteerɔwa a kpesi a nya noruku ale bo nyiŋka la, ate zuisaŋa ale bo noruku po la dan peenti ate noruku a limisa a gaam nyiŋ gbaŋka, ka tue buui ale a chɔgsi la. Kaabteerɔwa a dan kpesi nya wa be mooli weeni ayen wa daŋ kama.

ref: But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Alege nyiŋ gbaŋka kauk kula dan peenti alege an limisa alege ate zuisaŋa an peenti ya, kaabteerɔwa a gaari wa ate wa bo wa tɔga a paari daa ŋayopɔi.

ref: If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days.
text: Daa ŋayopɔiwa danni kaabteerɔwa a ŋman kpesi nya. Wa dan nya ale noruku an tagri ya ku be an che ya, wa ŋman basi ate wa bo wa tɔga a paari daa ŋayopɔi.

ref: Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
text: Daa ŋayopɔiwa danni kaabteerɔwa a ŋman kpesi nya wa. Noruku a dan cheŋ ale an che ya, kaabteerɔwa a mooli weeni ayen wa nala kama, ka birima kama ale bo wa nyiŋ ka. Nuruwa yaa sugri wa gattaŋa ate wa nala.

ref: If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Kaabteerɔwa a kpesi nya wa ate birimaŋa a dan tagli nyiŋka, wa mooli weeni ayen wa daŋ kama. Ka tue buui ale a chɔgsi.

ref: Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest.
text: <<Waai a dan ta nyiŋ gbaŋ tue buui ale a chɔgsi, ba ta wa jam kaabteerɔwa jigi.

ref: If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white,
text: Kaabteerɔwa kpesi nya wa, wa nyiŋ ka dan ji a nye peeluk ate zuisaŋa a tagri peenti ale ta noruk,

ref: he will say, “This is leprosy. You are unclean and must stay away from everyone else.”
text: ka tue buui ale bie. Kaabteerɔwa a mooli a weeni ayen wa daŋ kama. Wa kan gaari wa, dii nyiŋla wa poom daŋ kama.

ref: But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.”
text: kaabteerɔwa nya wa ate tuemu dan lik nyiŋka meena wa mooli weeni ayen wa nala. Diila bu meena ale tagri peenti la, wa nala kama.

ref: If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Kaabteerɔwa a dan nya noruku wa mooli weeni ayen wa daŋ kama. Noruku daŋ kama, wa ta ka tue buui ale a chɔgsi.

ref: However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
text: Kaabteerɔwa a kpesi nya ate niraŋa a dan tagri peenti, kaabteerɔwa a mooli a weeni waai ale ta tuemu la ayen wa nala ate wa nala.

ref: If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest.
text: ate juijui ate nirika a nye la a ji ale peenti yaase ku mɔna, wa pai wadek a sak kaabteerɔwa.

ref: If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Kaabteerɔwa a kpesi a nya wa, ate ku dan limisa a gaam nyiŋka ate zuisaŋa a tagri peenti, kaabteerɔwa a mooli weeni ayen wa daŋ kama. Ka tue buui ale a chɔgsi ale piilim nirika jigini a che.

ref: But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Alege kaabteerɔwa a dan kpesi nya ale zuisaŋa an peenti ya ate noruku an limisa a gaam nyiŋka alege luenti, kaabteerɔwa a gaari wa daa ŋayopɔi.

ref: If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.”
text: Ku be da a che nyiŋka, kaabteerɔwa mooli a weeni ayen, wa daŋ kama. Ka tue buui ale a chɔgsi.

ref: But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
text: Alege ku jigini a dan kan tagri ya alege an che ya, ka nirika lauŋ. Kaabteerɔwa a mooli a weeni ayen wa nala.

ref: If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white,
text: <<Ase tuiluk a dan foti waai ate wa nyiŋ gbaŋka a nye mɔnuŋ yaase ku peenti,

ref: a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.”
text: kaabteerɔwa a kpesi nya ku jigini ate dula zuisaŋa a dan peenti ate ku limisa a gaam nyiŋka, ka tue buui ale a chɔgsi la ale boro. Kaabteerɔwa a mooli a weeni ayen wa daŋ kama. Bu ka tue buui ale a chɔgsi.

ref: But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Alege kaabteerɔwa a dan kpesi nya wa ate ku jigini zuisaŋa an peenti ya, ate ku an limisa alege luenti kaabteerɔwa gaari wa ate ku paari dan ŋayopɔi.

ref: On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Daa ŋayopɔiwa danni kaabteerɔwa ŋman kpesi nya wa ate bu daa tagli nyiŋka, kaabteerɔwa mooli weeni ayen wa daŋ kama. Ka tue buui ale a chɔgsi.

ref: However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
text: Alege ku jigini a dan kan tagri ya alege an tagli nyiŋka alege luenti, ka fotika nyiini, kaabteerɔwa mooli weeni ayen wa nala kama. Ka fotika lauŋ nyiini.

ref: If you have a sore on your head or chin,
text: <<Nidoa yaase nipok a dan ta noruk wa zukku po yaase wa teeŋkuruku nyiŋ,

ref: it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: kaabteerɔwa a kpesi nya noruku, ate ku dan siŋ gaam nyiŋka ate zuisaŋa a nye ŋoolisa, kaabteerɔwa mooli weeni ayen wa daŋ kama. Ka zuk yaase teeŋkuruk tue buui ale a zak ale a chɔgsi.

ref: On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Alege kaabteerɔwa a dan kpesi nya noruku ate ku an siŋ gaam nyiŋka ate zui sobsa karo kaabteerɔwa gaari wa, wa tɔga a paari daa ŋayopɔi.

ref: By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep,
text: Daa ŋayopɔiwa danni kaabteerɔwa ŋman kpesi nya noruku ate ku dan kan che ya ate zuisaŋa an nye ŋoolisa ate ku kan nye ase ku siŋ gaam nyiŋka la,

ref: you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days.
text: ba poin wa zukku, ka noruku ale bo juijui la nyiini, abe kaabteerɔwa gaari wa daa ŋayopɔi ŋmana.

ref: By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
text: Daa ŋayopɔiwa danni kaabteerɔwa ŋman nya noruku ate ku dan kan che ya alege an siŋ gaam nyiŋka, kaabteerɔwa a mooli ayen wa nala. Ku a fɛ ate wa sugri wa gattaŋa ate wa nala.

ref: Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.”
text: kaabteerɔwa a kpesi a nya wa ate noruku a dan che kaabteerɔwa a kan yaksi ayen wa nya zui ŋoolisa ku nyɔnɔwa daŋ kama.

ref: If white spots break out on your skin,
text: <<Ase nidoa yaase nipok nyiŋgbaŋ a dan lagsi peela wa nyiŋka,

ref: but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
text: kaabteerɔwa kpesi a nya ba ate kab tila a dan kan potim peenti ya, ka tue buui ale bo nyiŋka a ka wari ya. Kula nyɔnɔwa a nala kama.

ref: There you will present them to me by placing the incense on the coals, so that the place of mercy will be covered with a cloud of smoke. Do this, or you will die right there!
text: Wa le pai ŋan baai nyummu ale masa la a nyo bolimu po Naawen niŋ, ate ŋan baai nyummu ale masa la nyuisaŋa a yiti lik biem duisi basika nanlikka nɔiyeŋ dakanni zuk, ate wa kan kpi.

ref: Next, use a finger to sprinkle some of the blood on the place of mercy, which is on the lid of the sacred chest; then sprinkle blood seven times in front of the chest.
text: Wa le pai lalikka ziimu gela a pai nandub a tiak a misi biem duisi basika nanlikka zuk abe wa ŋman pai nandub a tiak a misi buyopɔi biem duisi basika nanlikka niŋ.

ref: Aaron, you must next sacrifice the goat for the sins of the people, and you must sprinkle its blood inside the most holy place, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
text: <<Wa yaa le tɔgri biem tiirim buuku a te nuruma abe wa pai ziimu garuk panni ŋaaŋ a yaa nye dii dek ate wa nye ale lalikka ziimu la. Wa yaa misi ziimu gela biem duisi basika nanlikka zuk ale ka niŋ.

ref: By doing this, you will take away the sins that make both the most holy place and the people of Israel unclean. Do the same for the sacred tent, which is here among the people.
text: Suiku de po wa le nye biem duisi basika a te jigi dii ale ta tuilum la, Izirali demma daŋtaŋa ale ba tuikpanni nyiŋ, ba biemu a dan poom ka dii ya. Wa le nye dila mɛ a te Tuka Viuku dii nyiŋla ku bo ka ba suŋsuŋ po.

ref: After leaving the tent, you will purify the bronze altar by smearing each of its four corners with some of the blood from the bull and from the goat.
text: <<Wa yaa nyini kuŋkuŋku jigini a nye biem duisi basika a te di. Wa pai lalikka ziimu gela a sa kuŋkuŋku nyiilaŋa.

ref: Use a finger to sprinkle the altar seven times with the blood, and it will be completely clean from the sins of the people.
text: Wa le misi ziimu gela ale wa nandub naŋtuok nɔi buyopɔi a duisi ate ku ta tuilum a nyini daŋ tii ale bo Izirali demma po la.

ref: After you have purified the most holy place, the sacred tent, and the bronze altar, you must bring the live goat to the front of the tent.
text: <<Ase Aaron dan nye biem duisi basika a te jigi dii ale ta tuilum la, ale Tuka Viuku ale kuŋkuŋku a ga nueri, wa yaa ta buuk vuuku a jam niŋ.

ref: There you will lay your hands on its head, while confessing every sin the people have committed, and you will appoint someone to lead the goat into the desert, so that it can take away their sins.
text: Wa pai nisaŋa meena a vi buuk vuku zukku zuk a weeni Izirali biemu ale ba gaasa ale ba tuikpari nyeka a basi ku zuk. Wa pai ku ate waai ale magsi wa ta ku ga basi gɔnni po la.

ref: Finally, this goat that carries the heavy burden of Israel's sins must be released deep in the desert.
text: Buuku ale ku ji ba wabaataŋa meena a ta cheŋ juijui ate nuruba ka la, ate nuruwa yaa basi ku gɔnni po.

ref: Aaron, after this you must go inside the sacred tent, take a bath, put on your regular priestly clothes, and leave there the clothes you put on before entering the most holy place. Then you will come out and offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices for your sins and for the sins of the people.
text: Wa yaa so wa nyiŋka ale nyiam tuilum jigi, abe wa ge jo wadek gattaŋa. Wa yaa nyini a pai juka tiirimu a te magsi wadek abe wa pai juka tiirimu a te a magsi nuruma, a nye biem duisi basika te nuruma ale wadek.

ref: The fat from these sacrifices for sin must be sent up in smoke on the bronze altar.
text: Wa le ju biem tiirimu kpapalaŋa mɛ ka kuŋkuŋku zuk.

ref: The one who led the goat into the desert and sent it off to the demon Azazel must take a bath and wash his clothes before coming back into camp.
text: <<Nuru waai ale ta buuk kuui ale ta biem a cheŋ a ga basi gɔnni po la, a sugri wa gattaŋa abe wa so wa nyiŋka ale nyiam abe wa yaa nya suik a jam nuruma boka jigini.

ref: And whoever does this must take a bath and change clothes before coming back into camp. The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
text: Nuru waai ale a ju ba la ku a fɛ ate wa sugri wa gattaŋa abe wa so wa nyiŋka ale nyiam. Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa yaa jam nuruma jigi.

ref: On the tenth day of the seventh month of each year, you must go without eating to show sorrow for your sins, and no one, including foreigners who live among you, is allowed to work.
text: <<Kude ka ŋmarisi kaai ale magsi ni kasim a va a ta cheŋ. Chiisa siyopɔiwa po ka daa piwa danni ni zɛri nidek ni kan tom tuini. Dan poom ka tɛŋka denɔ yaase nichaanɔ ale bo ale ni waai kan tom tuini.

ref: This is the day on which the sacrifice for the forgiveness of your sins will be made in my presence,
text: Dii nyiŋla danni de, ba le nye biem duisi basika a te ni ate ni nye cheri. Ate Naawen niŋ ni biemu a duisi basi ate ni nye cheri.

ref: and from now on, it must be celebrated each year. Go without eating and make this a day of complete rest just like the Sabbath.
text: Di ka vuusum dai, ate ni zɛri nidek. Ka ŋmarisi kaai ale magsi ni kasim a va.

ref: He will offer these sacrifices for the most holy place, the sacred tent, the bronze altar, all the priests, and for the whole community.
text: Wa nye biem duisi basika a te Wen dɔkku ale Tuka Viuku ale kuŋkuŋku ale kaabteerɔma ale tɛŋka nuruma meena.

ref: You must celebrate this day each year—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness for all the sins of the people of Israel. Moses did exactly as the Lord had commanded.

text: Ate Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

text: <<Biisi ate Aaron ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ale Izirali demma meena a weeni ba ayen, <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna:

ref: Whenever you kill any of your cattle, sheep, or goats as sacrifices to me, you must do it at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you don't, you will be guilty of pouring out blood, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: alege an ta jam Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku nɔi ayen ba nye kaabka a te Naawen viuku niŋ. Nuru wala ba a nya wa a se ka nuru koorik la. Wa ko ka nuru ate ku magsi ba yeeri wa a ta nyini nuruma po a nyini.

ref: but in front of the sacred tent. Then a priest can splatter its blood against the bronze altar and send its fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Kaabteerɔwa yaa le misi ziimu a basi Naawen kaabka kuŋkuŋku tuka viuku nansuiŋku nɔi abe wa yaa ju kpapalaŋa ase nyum buui ale masa la, a te Naawen.

ref: except at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you do, you will no longer belong to my people. Do Not Eat Blood The Lord said:
text: alege an ta jam tuka jigini viuku nansuiŋku nɔi a nye kaabka a te Naawen ba yeeri wa a ta nyini wa nuruma po nyini.

text: Dii nyiŋla nyuvuri ale bo ziimu po ate mi a pai te ni ayen ni nye biem duisi basika a te nidek juka kuŋkuŋku zuk. Ka ziimu ale nye biem duisi basika a te nuru.

ref: That's also why I have forbidden you to eat blood.
text: Dila nyiŋ mi weeni Izirali demma ale nichamma ale bo po la kama ayen ba waai kan dɛ ziimoa.

ref: Even if you should hunt and kill a bird or an animal, you must drain out the blood and cover it with soil.
text: << <Izirali denɔ waai yaase nichaanɔ waai a dan bo ni po a bari a yik duŋ yaase nuim ate ba a ŋɔbi bu, wa tɔgri ziimu a basi tɛŋ a chuiri tanta si bu.

ref: The life of every living creature is in its blood. That's why I have forbidden you to eat blood and why I have warned you that anyone who does will no longer belong to my people.
text: Dii nyiŋla javuk meena nyuvuri a bo ka ziimu po. Dila nyiŋ ate mi weeni Izirali demma ayen, fi an magsi ayen fi dɛ jaab ziimoa. Dii nyiŋla javuk meena nyuvuri ale wa ziimu. Waai ale a dɛ ziimu la ba yeeri wa a ta nyini nuruma po a nyini.

ref: If you happen to find a dead animal and eat it, you must take a bath and wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
text: << <Nuru waai a dan ka tɛŋka denɔ yaase nichaanɔ a ŋɔbi jakpiuk yaase gɔi duŋsa a yik ka. Wa magsi wa sugri wa gattaŋa abe wa so wa nyiŋka ale nyiam wa daŋ kama a ga paari wen siŋka, ate wa nye cheri.

ref: If you don't take a bath, you will suffer for what you did wrong.
text: Alege wa dan kan sugri wa gattaŋa ale m so ya. Wa le diem ta wa kaasuŋku kama.> >>

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: to tell the people of Israel: I am the Lord your God!
text: <<Weeni Izirali demma ayen, <Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

text: Ni a chali m buusaŋa abe ni kpesi a va m ŋmarisika. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

text: << <Waai a kan bobi wa mabiik a goa. Mi ale Naawen.

text: << <Kan goa ale fi biik lie yaase fi liewa lie. Dila ale te fu ka chivie.

text: << <Kan goa ale nipok ale wa lie. Kan goa ale wa biik lie yaase wa lie lie. Ba meena ka wadek mabisa. Dila ka gaasa.

ref: As long as your wife is alive, don't cause trouble for her by taking one of her sisters as a second wife.
text: << <Kan faari fi pok suowa ate ba chim ŋaaŋchaaba. Kan goa ale wa alege ate fi powa a vua.

ref: When a woman is having her monthly period, she is unclean, so don't have sex with her.
text: << <Kan ga nipok jigi ayen fi goa ale wa diipo ate wa a lo chiak a daŋ la.

ref: Don't have sex with another man's wife—that would make you unclean.
text: << <Kan goa ale fi vaanchoa powa a taŋ fi dega.

ref: Don't sacrifice your children on the altar fires to the god Molech. I am the Lord your God, and that would disgrace me.
text: << <Kan pai fi bisa a nye kaabka a te Molek. Ku ale kaasi ka fi Wenni yuei. Mi ale Naawen.

text: << <Kan goa ale nidoa ase ba ale a goa le nipok diila. Ku a kisi kama.

ref: Don't make yourselves unclean by any of these disgusting practices of those nations that I am forcing out of the land for you. They made themselves
text: << <Ni kan taŋ ni dega ale wieŋa de dii ya, dii nyiŋla tɛŋ sii dem ate m za m yiak alege a te nama la a taŋ badek ka dila.

text: Wieŋa de meena ka nuru baai ale liŋ bo tɛŋka po alege nama la, ale nye ate tɛŋka a yaa taŋ.

text: Ni ta mi ale a yaali diila abe ni kan va kisuk wieŋa de ale ba ŋiak wieŋa ate ba a nye alege ate nama a jam la. Ni kan taŋ nidek ale ŋa. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.> >>

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: I am the Lord your God. I am holy, and you must be holy too!
text: <<Biisi ate Izirali demma meena a weeni ba ayen, <Weeni Izirali demma meena ayen, <<Ni abe ta tuilum, dii la Mi Naawen ni Wenni ta tuilum kama.>> > >>

ref: Respect your father and your mother, honor the Sabbath, and don't make idols or images. I am the Lord your God.
text: << <Ni kan cheem va bɔgta yaase ni pai kuta a nye wena a te ni dega. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

ref: When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, be sure to follow my instructions.
text: << <Ni daa kaab suiyɔgni tiirim a te Naawen, ni kaab suik kuui po ate mi ale tuesi ni nyiŋ.

ref: You may eat the meat either on the day of the sacrifice or on the next day, but you must burn anything left over on the third day.
text: Ni ŋɔbi lammu kaabka danni yaase dai dii ale pai a saŋ la. Buui ale a tali daa ŋatawa danni la ni pai ju.

ref: If you eat any of it on the third day, the sacrifice will be disgusting to me, and I will reject it.
text: Bu dan tali daa ŋatawa danni ate ni ŋɔbi bu, ni nye kaasi kama. M kan siagi.

ref: In fact, you will be punished for not respecting what I say is holy, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: Waai dek ale a ŋɔbi la, M le yik wa a dari wa turi ku nyiŋ, dii nyiŋla wa an zuli jabuui ale ta tuilum a te Naawen la. Ku a fɛ ate ba yeeri wa a ta nyini wa nuruma po a nyini.

ref: When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing along the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground.
text: << <Ni dan boro a che yaase ni a ŋari ni kpanni ŋantaŋa ni kan paari kaduksaŋa kpeglimka yaase ni tigsi ŋan baai ale magsi yiisika la.

ref: Don't strip your grapevines clean or gather the grapes that fall off the vines. Leave them for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God.
text: Ni kan cheŋ kadukka po a tulim buye yaase ni gbesi yɔna ate ŋa gela a lo la. Ni basi a te ŋanjaksaŋa ale nichamma. Mi ale Naawen, ni Wenni.

ref: Do not steal or tell lies or cheat others.
text: << <Kan zu. Kan velimu. Kan paasi waai ya.

ref: Do not misuse my name by making promises you don't intend to keep. I am the Lord your God.
text: << <Ni kan pai mi yuenni a pɛ venta pɛka a kaasi ni Wenni yuei ya. Ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Do not steal anything or cheat anyone, and don't fail to pay your workers at the end of each day.
text: << <Kan vari fi vaanchoa jaaboa. Fi dan pai waai ate wa tom te fu kan zɛri wa tuni ka. Kan te vari veenti.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and I command you not to make fun of the deaf or to cause a blind person to stumble.
text: << <Kan ka te tukpara nyɔnɔ yaase fi pai jaab a kasi yeo. Alege ni a chali ni Wenni. Ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Be fair, no matter who is on trial—don't favor either the poor or the rich.
text: << <Ni a bo wensie buusa. Ni kan ŋmani a te ŋanjaksa, yaase ni a zuli nuru kpienta, alege ni a bo ni vaanchaab buusa a magsi.

ref: Don't be a gossip, but never hesitate to speak up in court, especially if your testimony can save someone's life.
text: << <Kan nyiem a kaasi nuruba yue nuruba po. Kan nye dii ale pai fi vaanchoa a nyo daanika po la, ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Don't hold grudges. On the other hand, it's wrong not to correct someone who needs correcting.
text: << <Kan kisi fi mabiik fi suinum po. Toariŋ fi vaanchoa wensie toariŋka ate wa kaasuŋku kan maa chim fi kaasuŋ.

ref: Don't be angry or try to take revenge. I am the Lord, and I command you to love others as much as you love yourself.
text: << <Kan pai biem a tuni waai ya, yaase fi ta chaab ale fi nuruma waai ya. Alege yaali fi vaanchoa ase fi ale a yaali fidek diila. Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Breed your livestock animals only with animals of the same kind, and don't plant two kinds of seed in the same field or wear clothes made of different kinds of material.
text: << <Ni ta m ŋmarisika. Ni kan basi ate duŋsa tɔgatɔga a jueli chaaba. Ni kan pai ŋanbuura tɔgatɔga buye a bori talim yeŋ po. Ni kan jo garuk tii ate ba pai garuk pala ŋaye a baali la.

ref: If a man has sex with a slave woman who is promised in marriage to someone else, he must pay a fine, but they are not to be put to death. After all, she was still a slave at the time.
text: << <Nuru waai a dan goa ale nipokbili waai ale ka yɔma ate ba puulim ayen ba pai te nuru yoŋ, alege ate ba an tuni wa nyiŋla, ku magsi namsika a boro kama alege ba kan ko ba. Dii nyiŋla wa diem ka yɔma.

ref: The man must bring a ram to the entrance of the sacred tent and give it to a priest, who will then offer it as a sacrifice to me, so the man's sins will be forgiven.
text: Padiaka ale magsi nyemagsika tiirimu la, kaabteerɔwa ale nye biem duisi basika a te wa Naawen niŋ, wa le nye biemu la nyiŋ, ate wa nya vɔŋteka.

ref: After you enter the land, you will plant fruit trees, but you are not to eat any fruit from them for the first three years.
text: << <Ni dan jo tɛŋka po a vuk ti sii buuri ale ta yɔna la, ni a kisi si yɔnaŋa. Ni a kisi ate ku paari bena ŋata. Ni kan dɛ.

ref: In the fourth year the fruit must be set apart, as an expression of thanks
text: Bein dii ale a saari ŋanaansiwa la, si yɔnaŋa a ta tuilum kama, ale chim pimpauk tiirim a te Naawen.

ref: to me, the Lord God. Do this, and in the fifth year, those trees will produce an abundant harvest of fruit for you to eat.
text: Alege bein dii ale a saari ŋanuwa la ni yaa dɛ si yɔnaŋa. Suiku de po ni le gbesi piisi. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

ref: Don't eat the blood of any animal. Don't practice any kind of witchcraft.
text: << <Waai a kan ŋɔbi lam ate ziim a bo bu po. Waai a kan tom sampoporinni yaase chichirik wiirisa tuima.

ref: I forbid you to shave any part of your head or beard or to cut and tattoo yourself as a way of worshiping the dead.
text: << <Ni kan gebi ni nyiŋsaŋa a te kpio yaase ni ŋmarisi ni nyiŋsaŋa. Ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Don't let your daughters serve as temple prostitutes—this would bring disgrace both to them and the land.
text: << <Kan valiŋ fi lie a basi ate wa chim nidoa yaaliga. Kan daa di tɛŋka demma ale tulim va bɔgluk yoŋta ate gaasa a sueri tɛŋka po.

ref: I command you to respect the Sabbath and the place where I am worshiped.
text: << <Ni a kpesi m vuusumu daaŋa abe ni a zuli m Tuka Viuku. Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Don't make yourselves disgusting to me by going to people who claim they can talk to the dead.
text: << <Ni kan tulim va sampoporinni yaase ni a gisi chichirik wiirisa. Ba le taŋ ni. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

ref: I command you to show respect for older people and to obey me with fear and trembling.
text: << <Ni dan bo ŋankpagsa suŋsuŋ ni a sak zuli abe ni a chali Wen. Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Don't mistreat any foreigners who live in your land.
text: << <Nichaanɔ a dan bo ni tɛŋka po ale ni, ni kaa nye wa gaasa.

ref: Instead, treat them as well as you treat your own people and love them as much as you love yourself. Remember, you were once foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
text: Nichaanɔwa ale bo ale ni la, ni a nye wa ase tɛŋ biik la. Ni a yaali wa ase nidek la, nama mɛ jam ka nicham Ejipiti tɛŋka. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

ref: Use honest scales and don't cheat when you weigh or measure anything. I am the Lord your God. I rescued you from Egypt,
text: Ni pai ŋanmagsin maŋsa ale dobrim maŋsa ale boorik maŋsa ale chin maŋsa. Mi ale Naawen ni Wen dii ale ta ni nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Naawen yaa biisi ale Moosis ayen,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: Death by stoning is the penalty for any citizens or foreigners in the country who sacrifice their children to the god Molech.
text: <<Weeni Izirali demma ayen, <Nuru waai a dan nyini Izirali yaase nichaanɔ a bo Izirali a pai wa biik a te Molek bɔglukku ba ko wa; tɛŋka nuruma a yuk wa ale tana a ko.

ref: They have disgraced both the place where I am worshiped and my holy name, and so I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people.
text: Mi sui ale puuri ale nuru wala choa kama ate dila ale basi ate m yeeri wa a ta nyini wa nuruma po a nyini; wa le pai wa bisaŋa a te Molek bɔglukku la nyiŋ. Wa taŋ ka m yenni ale kaasi m yuei dii ale ta tuilum la.

ref: but not me. If any of you worship Molech, I will turn against you and your entire family, and I will no longer let you belong to my people.
text: mi dek sui ale puuri ale nuru wala ale wa buuni meena abe m yeeri wa ale wa buuni meena a ta nyini ba nuruma po a nyini. Wa ale baai meena ale taŋ badek a va Molek bɔglukku la.

ref: I will be your enemy if you go to someone who claims to speak with the dead, and I will destroy you from among my people.
text: << <M sui le puuri ale nuru waai ale a tom sampoporinni ale chichirik wiirisa tuima a va bɔgluk yoŋta la, m le yeeri ba a ta nyini wa nuruma po a nyini.

ref: Dedicate yourselves to me and be holy because I am the Lord your God.
text: << <Ni gaari nidek abe ni welema, dii nyiŋla, ka Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

ref: I have chosen you as my people, and I expect you to obey my laws.
text: Ni ta m ŋmarisika abe ni a va ŋa. Mi ale Naawen dii ale basi ate ni welema la.

ref: If you curse your father or mother, you will be put to death, and it will be your own fault.
text: << <Ase ni po wanyi a dan ka te wa ko yaase wa ma, ku a magsi ka ba ko wa. Wa ka te ka wa ko ale wa ma, wa ziimu a va ka wadek.

ref: If any of you men have sex with another man's wife, both you and the woman will be put to death.
text: << <Ase nuru waai a dan goa ale wa vaanchoa pok, baai ale goa ale chaab la, ka kaboŋ nyeerisa. Ba ko ba.

ref: Having sex with one of your father's wives disgraces him. So both you and the woman will be put to death, just as you deserve.
text: << <Nuru a dan goa ale wa ko pok wa pai ka wa kowa a nyo chivie po. Ku a magsi ka ba ko nipowa ale nidoawa, ba ziimu a va ka badek.

ref: It isn't natural to have sex with your daughter-in-law, and both of you will be put to death, just as you deserve.
text: << <Ase nuru waai a dan goa ale wa sampok, ku a magsi ka ba ko ba nɔi bayema. Ba le nye diila ka butima. Ba ziimu a va ka badek.

ref: It's disgusting for men to have sex with one another, and those who do will be put to death, just as they deserve.

text: << <Chiik kaai ale saari siyopɔiwa la ka daa pi ale ŋanuwa danni ni dan tigsi ŋandiintaŋa ni tɛŋka po ni pai daa ŋayopɔi a dɛ Naawen tigini abe dai dii ale piilim la da naanika danni ni vuusi.

ref: I command you and all of your descendants to celebrate this festival during the seventh month of each year.
text: Ni de ku ase tigi la a te Naawen daa ŋayopɔi bein meena po. Ŋmarisika de a magsi ka nama ale ni gaŋsaŋa meena kauk kuui meena ate ni a boro la. Ni dɛ di chiisa siyopɔiwa po.

ref: so future generations will know that I made their ancestors live in shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
text: ate ni buuni po meena a seba ayen m basi ate Izirali demma meena a bo ka viita po m ta ba nyini Ejipiti po a jam basi ka viita po. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.> >>

ref: This is how Moses instructed the people of Israel to celebrate the Lord's festivals.
text: Moosis a jam weeni Izirali demma da ŋaai ate Naawen a te ba la kama.

ref: It's possible to pay the owner for an animal that has been killed, but death is the penalty for murder.
text: Nuru waai a dan ko waai duŋ, wa tuni ka, alege nuru waai a dan ko nurubiik ba ko wa mɛ.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: You must supply the purest olive oil for the lamps in the sacred tent, so they will keep burning.
text: <<Weeni Izirali demma ate ba ta kpaam buui ale nye nna cheri ate ba ŋmiak a ta nyini kpaam tiib yɔna po a magsi bolim zeuŋtaŋa la ate bolimu a kasim a de.

ref: Use your finest flour to bake twelve loaves of bread about two kilograms each,
text: <<Pai zom naliŋ a nye borobotta pi ale tiye. Pai zom chin nɔi a nye boroborok kunyi meena.

ref: then take them into the sacred tent and lay them on the gold table in two rows of six loaves.
text: Dueni ti vuta buye bunyi, tiyuebi bunyi mɛ tiyuebi cheri ligmɔniŋka jazaanimu zuk Naawen niŋ.

ref: Alongside each row put some pure incense that will be sent up by fire in place of the bread as an offering to me.
text: Vuuku kunyi pai ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a dueni du ate ku sak ayen mi ale soa a magsi boroboroku. Ku ka tiirim ate ba ju a te Naawen.

ref: Aaron must lay fresh loaves on the table each Sabbath, and priests in all generations must continue this practice as part of Israel's agreement with me.
text: Boroboroku de a dueni Vuusum dai meena, Izirali demma nyiŋ. Ka nɔiyeŋ kaai ale kasim boro a cheŋ.

ref: This bread will always belong to Aaron and his family; it is very holy because it was offered to me, and it must be eaten in a holy place. Punishment for Cursing the Lord
text: Ka Aaron ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ale soa. Ba dɛ jigi dii ale ta tuilum, dii nyiŋla bu ŋmasi chim ka tuilum juka tiirim buui ale nyini Naawen jigi. Ku kasim ka wa charuk.>>

ref: Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri from the tribe of Dan, had married an Egyptian, and they had a son. One day their son got into a fight with an Israelite man in camp and cursed the name of the Lord. So the young man was dragged off to Moses,
text: Izirali nipowa biika yaa biisi kaasi Naawen Yuenni ate ba yaa ta wa jam Moosis jigi. Wa mawa yuei jam le Selomit. Dibri ale nyini Dan dɔkku po la lie ale wa.

ref: who had him guarded while everyone waited for the Lord to tell them what to do.
text: Ba yaa lik biika tara ale a limisi ayen Naawen a basi ate ba seba wa le a yaali ayen ba nye diila.

ref: Finally, the Lord said to Moses:
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: This man has cursed me! Take him outside the camp and tell the witnesses to lay their hands on his head. Then command the whole community of Israel to stone him to death.
text: <<Ni ta waai ale lɛ la a nyini nuruma boka jigini a nyini cheŋ peelim. Baai meena ale ka seerɔba a wom la a pai ba nisimaŋa a vi wa zukku alege ate nuruma meena a yuk wa ale tana.

ref: And warn the others that everyone else who curses me will die in the same way, whether they are Israelites by birth or foreigners living among you.
text: waai ale a lɛ Naawen yuenni la ku a fɛ ate ba ko wa. Nuruma meena a yuk wa a ko. Wa ka nichaanɔ yoo tɛŋ biik yoo wa dan lɛ Yuenni, ku a fɛ ate ba yuk wa ko.

ref: Death is also the penalty for murder,
text: << <Waai a dan ko nurubiik, ku a fɛ ate ba ko wa mɛ.

ref: but the killing of an animal that belongs to someone else requires only that the animal be replaced.
text: Waai a dan ko waai duŋ ku a fɛ ate wa tuni ku nyɔnɔwa ale duŋ vuk.

ref: Personal injuries to others must be dealt with in keeping with the crime—
text: Nuru waai a dan te wa vaanchoa tuem, wa le nye diila ba nye wa mɛ dila.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and I demand equal justice both for you Israelites and for those foreigners who live among you.
text: Sinsak yenaŋa ate fi a te nichamma ale tɛŋ bisaŋa. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.> >>

ref: When Moses finished speaking, the people did what the Lord had told Moses, and they stoned to death the man who had cursed the Lord.
text: Ate Moosis yaa biisi te Izirali demma ate ba yaa ta waai ale lɛ Naawen la a nyini nuruma boka jigini a yuk ko. Izirali demma yaa nye dii ate Naawen a weeni Moosis.

ref: So when you buy or sell farmland, the price is to be determined by the number of crops it can produce before the next Year of Celebration. Don't try to cheat.
text: Da tɛŋka fi tɛŋka denɔwa jigi a magsi chaab ale Ŋmanpateka Beinni a jam paari diipo ate fi a da la. Wa da te fu a magsi chaab ale bena dii ale tali ate ku paari cheka yaase ŋarika la.

ref: When Moses was on Mount Sinai, the Lord told him
text: Naawen yaa weeni Moosis Sinai Guuku zuk ayen,

ref: This is a year of complete celebration, so don't plant any seed or harvest what your fields or vineyards produce.
text: Bein dii ale a saari pisinu la, ka Ŋmanpateka Bein a te ni. Ni kan bori, ni be kan che yaa ni ŋari ŋan baai ale nyini badek la, yaase tiisaŋa yɔna.

ref: to say to the community of Israel: After you enter the land that I am giving you, it must be allowed to rest one year out of every seven.
text: <<Weeni Izirali demma ayen ba dan jo tɛŋ kaai ate mi ayen m te ba la, tɛŋka dek a duak a vuusi.

ref: You may raise grain and grapes for six years,
text: <Ni bori ni laŋka bena ŋayuebi a che ni ŋantaŋa abe ni yɔrisi kadukka tiisaŋa.

ref: but the seventh year you must let your fields and vineyards rest in honor of me, your Lord.
text: Alege bein dii ale a saari ŋayopɔi la, tɛŋka duak vuusi, Vuusum bein a te Naawen, ni kan bori laŋka yaase ni yɔrisi kadukka tiisaŋa.

ref: This is to be a time of complete rest for your fields and vineyards, so don't harvest anything they produce.
text: Ni kan che yaase ni ŋari ŋan baai ate ni an bori ya yaase ni gbesi ti sii yɔna ate ni an vuk ya. Tɛŋka a duak bein dila a vuusi.

ref: However, you and your slaves and your hired workers, as well as any domestic or wild animals, may eat whatever grows on its own. The Year of Celebration The Lord said to his people:
text: ale ni yeri duŋsaŋa ale gɔi duŋsaŋa. Jaabuui meena ale a bɛ tɛŋka zuk ni baga a dɛ kama.

ref: or uncle or cousin, or some other family member. In fact, if you ever get enough money, you may buy your own freedom
text: Wa ko suok yaase wa ko suok biik yaase wa le waai ale ka zi yem la a baga a da tuesi wa kama. Yaase wa dan nya wadek wa baga a da a tuesi wadek kama.

ref: on the tenth day of the seventh month, which is also the Great Day of Forgiveness, trumpets are to be blown everywhere in the land.
text: Vuusum bena pisinaansi ale neokku po chiisa siyopɔiwa po ka daa pi dai basi ate ba peeri damunsa jigi meena. Vɔŋteka juisika dai ale la, ba peeri damunsaŋa tɛŋka meena.

ref: This fiftieth year is sacred—it is a time of freedom and of celebration when everyone will receive back their original property, and slaves will return home to their families.
text: Bein dii ale a saari pisinu la, ni gaari bein dila a te mu. Ni mooli varibasika a te waai meena tɛŋka meena. Ka Ŋmanpateka Bein ate waai meena a ŋman tuesi wa ŋanta abe yɔm pilim ŋman ba dɔkdem jigi.

ref: During this year, all property must go back to its original owner.
text: << <Ŋmanpateka Bein jaab meena pilim cheŋ wa nyɔnɔwa jigi.

ref: If it is a long time before the next Year of Celebration, the price will be higher, because what is really being sold are the crops that the land can produce.
text: Benaŋa a dan piisi, dak ligraŋa a zuak, alege benaŋa a dan kan piisi ya kan dak zuak, dii nyiŋla wa le pai dii a da a te fu la ka ŋantaŋa ale soa dii du la.

ref: I am the Lord your God, so obey me and don't cheat anyone.
text: Ni kan nye yam a gebi chaab ŋanta. Ni a chali ni Wenni. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

ref: If you obey my laws and teachings, you will live safely in the land and enjoy its abundant crops.
text: Ate tɛŋka a nye ŋandiinta ate ni dɛ a chak abe ni bo du nalimnyiini.

ref: Don't ever worry about what you will eat during the seventh year when you are forbidden to plant or harvest.
text: Ni le bek ayen, <<Ti ti dɛ ka boa bena ŋayopɔiwa po ase ti nin kan bori yaase ti che ŋanta?>>

ref: I will see to it that you harvest enough in the sixth year to last for three years.
text: M le basi ate niauŋ a jam ate bena ŋayuebiwa po ŋantaŋa a nye yega a magsi bena ŋata dɛka.

ref: In the eighth year you will live on what you harvested in the sixth year, but in the ninth year you will eat what you plant and harvest in the eighth year.
text: Ni dan boro a bori bena naanika po, ni le diem a dɛ ka ŋandiin kpaksaŋa. Ni be ni kasim a dɛ ka bala ate ni ga che bena neokku po ŋantaŋa.

ref: No land may be permanently bought or sold. It all belongs to me—it isn't your land, and you only live there for a little while.
text: << <Ni kan deri pai tɛŋka a da ate ka ŋman ka tuesika, dii nyiŋla tɛŋka ka mi ale soa. Ni ka nicham ka po, ni an soa ka.

ref: When property is being sold, the original owner must be given the first chance to buy it.
text: Ni dan pai jaab a boro a da ni te waai ale liŋ soa jaamu la suik ate wade niŋ a da.

ref: If any of you Israelites become so poor that you are forced to sell your property, your closest relative must buy it back,
text: << <Ni tɛŋka waai a dan jaŋ a pai wa ŋantaŋa gela a da, wa mabiik kaai ale moata wa a jam a da tuesi.

ref: if that relative has the money. Later, if you can afford to buy it,
text: Wa dan kan ta waai ate wa a da ate wadek a jam nya a tara wa ŋman da.

ref: you must pay enough to make up for what the present owner will lose on it before the next Year of Celebration, when the property would become yours again.
text: Wa nya jaamu tuilum ale ka dii a magsi bena diila a yaa tuni saari a te waai ate wa pai da te la, a yaa pilim tuesi.

ref: But if you don't have the money to pay the present owner a fair price, you will have to wait until the Year of Celebration, when the property will once again become yours.
text: Alege wa dan kan baga a nya ŋanta a tuni a tuesi wa le pai jabuui da te la a wari ka nuruwa jigi a paari Ŋmanpateka Beinni. Ŋmanpateka Beinni ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa le ta ŋmani ate wa yaa ga tuesi.

ref: If you sell a house in a walled city, you have only one year in which to buy it back.
text: << <Fi yeri dan bo tɛŋka po ate parik a gilim tɛŋka, ate fi pai yenni a da, fi ta ka bein yeŋ dekki ate fi pilim tuesi di.

ref: If you don't buy it back before that year is up, it becomes the permanent property of the one who bought it, and it will not be returned to you in the Year of Celebration.
text: Wa dan kan baga a ŋman tuesi alege ate beinni a nueri, yenni ale bo tɛŋka po ate parisa a gilim ka waai ale da la ale wa bisa ale kasim soa di. Ŋanta Ŋmanpateka Beinni wa kan ta ŋmani.

ref: But a house out in a village may be bought back at any time just like a field. And it must be returned to its original owner in the Year of Celebration.
text: Alege yie ŋaai ale bo tɛŋ kpaŋsa ate parisa an gilim la, ni nya ase ka tɛŋ kaai ale lak doa. Ba ŋman baga a tuesi kama. Se ba ta cheŋ Ŋmanpateka Beinni.

ref: If any Levites own houses inside a walled city, they will always have the right to buy them back.
text: << <Livaima a kasim ta suik kama a da a tuesi ba yeeŋa Livai tɛŋsaŋa po, ate ba soa la.

ref: And any houses that they do not buy back will be returned to them in the Year of Celebration, because these homes are their permanent property among the people of Israel.
text: Livaima ale soa ŋan baai la, ba ŋman baga a da kama. Yie dii ate ba pai a da tɛŋ kaai po ate ba ta la, ba ŋman pai yenni a te Ŋmanpateka Beinni, dii nyiŋla yeeŋa ale bo Livaima tɛŋsaŋa la ka ba ale soa Izirali demma po.

ref: No pastureland owned by the Levi tribe can ever be sold; it is their permanent possession. Help for the Poor The Lord said:
text: Alege tɛŋ sii ale ta wuuk ate ba tɛŋsaŋa a soa la, ba kan pai da, ka ba ale kasim soa dula.

ref: If any of your people become poor and unable to support themselves, you must help them, just as you are supposed to help foreigners who live among you.
text: << <Ni tɛŋka nuru waai a dan wobsa an baga a maari wa dega a bo le ni, ni maari wa ase ni le a maari nichaanɔ yaase waai ale diema ayen wa goa ale ni magadek diila. Ate wa baga a bo le ni.

ref: Don't take advantage of them by charging any kind of interest or selling them food for profit. Instead, honor me by letting them stay where they now live.
text: Ni kan pai ligra a peem a te wa a yaali viila yaase ni pai ŋandiinta a da te wa a yaali nyuenta.

ref: Remember—I am the Lord your God! I rescued you from Egypt and gave you the land of Canaan, so that I would be your God.
text: Mi ale Naawen ni Wen dii ale ta ni nyini Ejipiti a nyini ayen m pai Keenan tɛŋka a te ni abe m chim ni Wen.

ref: Suppose some of your people become so poor that they have to sell themselves and become your slaves.
text: Ni tɛŋka nuru a dan wobsa a pai wadek a da te ni, ni kan basi ate wa a tom ase yɔma la.

ref: Then you must treat them as servants, rather than as slaves. And in the Year of Celebration they are to be set free,
text: Ni a nye ase waai ate ni pai wa ase tuimtomdik la yaase waai ale diem bo ale ni la. Se wa tom a te ni a ga paari Ŋmanpateka Beinni.

ref: so they and their children may return home to their families and property.
text: Ate ni yaa basi wa le wa bisaŋa ate wa ŋman cheŋ wadek dɔkku jigi ale wa kokpieŋsaŋa ŋantaŋa jigi.

ref: I brought them out of Egypt to be my servants, not to be sold as slaves.
text: Dii nyiŋla Izirali demma ka mi yɔm, baai ate mi a ta ba nyini Ejipiti a nyini. Ba kan pai ba a da ase yɔm la.

ref: So obey me, and don't be cruel to the poor.
text: Ni kaa nya ba zuk ale gaasa, alege ni a chali ni Wenni.

ref: You can own them, and even leave them to your children when you die, but do not make slaves of your own people or be cruel to them.
text: Ni baga a pai ba kama a te ni bisaŋa ate ba a soa ba ate ba chim yɔm ba boka po meena, alege ni kaa nya ni Izirali dem chaama zuk ale gaasa.

ref: Even if some of you Israelites become so much in debt that you must sell yourselves to foreigners in your country,
text: << <Ase nichaanɔ yaase waai ale diem bo ale ni la a dan jigsi alege ate ni tɛŋka denɔ a chim jajak a pai wadek a da te nichaanɔwa buuni,

ref: you still have the right to be set free by a relative, such as a brother
text: wa ta suik kama ate ba da a tuesi wa, wa le pai wadek a da la ŋaaŋnyiŋ. Wa mabisaŋa wanyi a baga a da a tuesi wa kama.

ref: The longer the time until then, the more you will have to pay.
text: Be dan ka bena maga ale tali ate ku paari Ŋmanpateka Beinni, wa chiini ŋa a tuni a magsi a yeeri wadek.

ref: And even while you are the slaves of foreigners in your own country, your people must make sure that you are not mistreated.
text: Ba a nye wa ase waai ate ba a pai wa bein, bein la. Ku a fɛ ate ni nya ku zuk ate wa nyɔnɔwa a kaa nya wa zuk ale gaasa.

ref: If you cannot gain your freedom in any of these ways, both you and your children will still be set free in the Year of Celebration.
text: << <Alege ba dan poom kan da tuesi wa suitaŋa de po, wa le bisaŋa ba basi ba Ŋmanpateka Beinni po,

ref: People of Israel, I am the Lord your God, and I brought you out of Egypt to be my own servants.
text: diila Izirali demma ka mi ale soa ba ase m yɔm la. Ba ka m yɔm, baai ate m ta nyini Ejipiti a nyini. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.

ref: Respect the Sabbath and honor the place where I am worshiped, because I am the Lord.
text: << <Ni kpesi a zuli mi Vuusum daaŋa abe ni a zuli m yenni. Mi ale Naawen.

ref: and I will send rain to make your crops grow and your trees produce fruit.
text: m le basi ate ŋmoruk a jam diipo ale magsi ku jam la, ate tɛŋka ŋanborintaŋa a bɛ abe tiisaŋa a yɔni yɔna.

ref: I will bless your country with peace, and you will rest without fear. I will wipe out the dangerous animals and protect you from enemy attacks.
text: << <M le basi ate suiyɔgni a bo tɛŋka po, ate ni doa ale ge waai a kan nye ate yɔgsum a yik ni. M le yeeri gɔi duŋsa tɛŋka po, ate gebik a kan va ni tɛŋka po a taamu.

ref: You will chase and destroy your enemies,
text: Ni le vi ni dachaasa, a ko ale gebik a lɔnsi ni niŋ.

ref: I will treat you with such kindness that your nation will grow strong, and I will also keep my promises to you.
text: << <M le nya ni zuk ale ŋmanteka abe m basi ate ni biak a pusi, abe m ta m nɔiyeŋka ale ni.

ref: I will live among you and never again look on you with disgust.
text: M le pai m viuku a basi ni suŋsuŋ, m be kan kisi ni.

ref: I will walk with you—I will be your God, and you will be my people.
text: M le kasim a cheŋ ni suŋsuŋ, abe m chim ni Wen, abe nama mɛ a chim m nuruba.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and I rescued you from Egypt, so that you would never again be slaves. I have set you free; now walk with your heads held high. Punishment for Disobeying the Lord The Lord said:
text: Mi ka Naawen ni Wenni, waai ale ta ni nyini Ejipiti a nyini ayen ni kan ŋman chim Ejipiti yɔmma. Mi wɛ da tii ale a nye ase niiga daata la kama alege basi ate ni baga a zak ni zuima ŋmai.

ref: If you disobey me and my laws, and if you break our agreement,
text: ale zɛri m ŋmarisika ale kisi m buusaŋa an va m wieŋa meena ale a zuli m nɔiyeŋka,

ref: I will punish you terribly, and you will be ruined. You will be struck with incurable diseases and with fever that leads to blindness and depression. Your enemies will eat the crops you plant,
text: M nin nye ni diila ale nna: M le ta yɔgsum a jam diiri ni. M le ta nyiŋtuila ale nyiŋ toliŋka ate ŋa kaasi ni nyaasim ale kaasi ni boka. Ni le bori kinla, dii nyiŋla ni dachaasaŋa ale dɛ.

ref: and I will turn from you and let you be destroyed by your attackers. You will even run at the very rumor of attack.
text: M le pai m nina a dueni ni zuk ate ni dachaasaŋa a nak dɛ ni. Baai ale kisi ni la ale ba a nya ni zuk ate ni a chali alege waai a kan vi ni.

ref: Then, if you still refuse to obey me, I will punish you seven times for each of your sins,
text: << <Ŋade meena ŋaaŋnyiŋ ni dan kan wom mu, m le namsi ni ni biemu nyiŋ ku nɔi buyopɔi.

ref: until your pride is completely crushed. I will hold back the rain, so the sky above you will be like iron, and the ground beneath your feet will be like copper.
text: M le kaasi ni tukpari kanjantaŋa abe m basi ate wenzukku a nye ase kutuk la, abe tɛŋka a nye ase kutuk mɔnuŋ la.

ref: All of your hard work will be for nothing—and there will be no harvest of grain or fruit.
text: Ni le pai ni pagrim a tom kinla dii nyiŋla ni tɛŋka a kan nye ŋandiinta, yaase tɛŋka tiisaŋa yɔni yɔna.

ref: If you keep rebelling against me, I'll punish you seven times worse, just as your sins deserve!
text: << <Ni dan kasim kisi mi ale zɛri kan wom mu, m le basi ate ni ninammu a piisi ku nɔi buyopɔi a magsi ni biemu.

ref: I'll send wild animals to attack you, and they will gobble up your children and livestock. So few of you will be left that your roads will be deserted.
text: M le basi ate gɔi duŋsa a jam ta chaab ale ni ate si vari ni bisaŋa, abe si kaasi ni niiŋa, a basi ate ni pɔsima ate ni manpalaŋa a wari doa.

ref: If you remain my enemies after this,
text: << <Wieŋa de meena ni dan kaa siak mi sinsaŋŋa alege kasim kisi mu,

ref: I'll remain your enemy and punish you even worse.
text: mi dek le namsi ni ni biemu nyiŋ ku nɔi buyopɔi.

ref: War will break out because you broke our agreement, and if you escape to your walled cities, I'll punish you with horrible diseases, and you will be captured by your enemies.
text: M le ta gebik a jam ni zuk a tuni ni le kaasi nɔiyeŋka la. Ni dan yeeri nidek a jo tɛŋsaŋa po, m le te daanika a jam ni suŋsuŋ, a pai ni nyo ni dachaasaŋa nisa po.

ref: You will have such a shortage of bread, that ten women will be able to bake their bread in the same oven. Each of you will get only a few crumbs, and you will go hungry.
text: Ase m dan gebi ni boroboroku a basi, nipooba pi ale baga a nye ni boroboroku dɔk yeoŋ po. Ba le chari ku a magsi ku dobrim. Ni le ŋɔbi ku alege ni kan chagi.

ref: I'll really get furious and punish you terribly for your sins!
text: m suipuurum po m le kisi ni, ate mi dek namsi ni ni biemu nyiŋ ku nɔi buyopɔi.

ref: In fact, you will be so desperate for food that you will eat your own children.
text: Ni le ŋɔbi ni nidoabilisaŋa ale ni liema nyiŋsaŋa.

ref: I'll destroy your shrines and tear down your incense altars, leaving your dead bodies piled on top of your idols. And you will be disgusting to me.
text: M le kaasi ni bɔgluk kpientaŋa, abe m kaasi ni ŋan baai nyum ale masa la kuŋkuŋtaŋa abe m tigsi ni kpiema a vi bɔgluk tii ale kan ta nyuvuri la zuk, abe m kisi ni.

ref: I'll wipe out your towns and your places of worship and will no longer be pleased with the smell of your sacrifices.
text: M le basi ate ni tɛŋsaŋa a tulim kaasi abe ni tuka jiŋŋa a doa kinla. M niŋ kan bo ni ŋan baai nyum ale masa la tiiritaŋa po.

ref: Your land will become so desolate that even your enemies who settle there will be shocked when they see it.
text: M le basi ate tɛŋka a doa kinla, ate ni dachaasaŋa ale bo dula la ku kan nye ba masimmoa.

ref: After I destroy your towns and ruin your land with war, I'll scatter you among the nations.
text: M le basi ate ni waaŋ tɛŋsaŋa meena abe m yeeri m gebika a vi ni. Ni tɛŋka ale doa kinla, abe ni tɛŋsaŋa a kaasi meena a doa.

ref: While you are prisoners in foreign lands, your own land will enjoy years of rest and refreshment, as it should have done each seventh year when you lived there.
text: Diipo meena ate tɛŋka doa kinla la, tɛŋka ale vuusi vuusum buui ate ka an vuusi Vuusum benaŋa ate ni jam bo ka po la.

ref: In the land of your enemies, you will tremble at the rustle of a leaf, as though it were a sword. And you will become so weak that you will stumble and fall over each other, even when no one is chasing you.
text: Ba le chali a nak chaab ase ba nya gebik a chali a bɛ la, alege waai a kan vi ba. Ni kan baga a zaani ni dachaasaŋa niŋŋa.
