ref: During the first month of Israel's second year in the Sinai Desert, the Lord had told Moses
text: Naawen a jam biisi ale Moosis Sinai Gɔi Kosikka po chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la bena ŋayewa po ate ba jam basi Ejipiti tɛŋka la ŋaaŋnyiŋ. Wa jam weeni ayen,

ref: to say to the people, “Celebrate Passover
text: <<Basi ate Izirali demma a dɛ Gaambasika Tigini diipo ale magsi la.

ref: in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month and do it by following all the regulations.”
text: Ni de di diipo ale magsi la junɔi chiika de daa pi ale ŋanaansiwa danni a ta va di ŋmarisika ale di buusaŋa ale ka diila.>>

ref: Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
text: ate ba nye dila Sinai Gɔi Kosikka po junɔi chiik kaai ale piilim la, ka daa pi ale ŋanaansiwa danni. Izirali demma a jam nye ka dii meena ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis la.

ref: Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron,
text: Alege ba gela an jam bag a dɛ Gaambasika Tigini dai dila danni, dii nyiŋla ba jam taŋ ka badek ale kpio. Ba yaa jam Moosis ale Aaron jigi dai dila danni

ref: “Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
text: a weeni Moosis ayen, <<Tama a taŋ kama dii nyiŋla ti tiri ka kpio, alege ka boa ale a kasi tama ate ti an baga a te Naawen ti tiirimu ale Izirali dem mbala diipo ale magsi la?>>

ref: Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
text: Moosis yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Ni limisi ate m bek Naawen a wom wa le ta dii wa weeni ni la.>>

ref: The Lord then told Moses
text: Ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover.
text: <<Weeni Izirali demma ayen, <Ase ni wanyi yaase ni ŋaaŋbisa a dan daŋ badek ba le tiri kpio la nyiŋ, yaase ba bo nyeerim po, ba diem baga dɛ Naawen Gaambasika Tigini kama.

ref: But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs,
text: Ba magsi ba dɛ tigini ka daa pi ale ŋanaansiwa danni chiisa siyewa po junɔi. Ba a magsi ba ŋɔbi pabiika a gum chaab ale ŋandiin tii ate ba an nyo dabinta du la ale tinaŋ tuasa.

ref: and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
text: Ku a fɛ ate ba kan tali lammu ate vari veenti bu yaase ba ŋɔbi ka kobaŋa. Ase ba daa dɛ Gaambasika Tigini, ku a fɛ ate ba va ŋmarisika meena.

ref: But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
text: Alege nuru waai a dan nala, ale an bo nyeerim po, a zɛri an dɛ Gaambasika Tigini, kula nyɔnɔwa ku a fɛ ate ba yiak wa, wa nuruma po a basi dii nyiŋla wa an te Naawen tiirim diipo ale magsi la. Nuru wala ale nya wa biemu tutuna.

ref: As soon as the sacred tent was set up, a thick cloud appeared and covered it. The cloud was there each day, and during the night, a fire could be seen in it.
text: Ku le jam ka dii a tom du a cheŋ la ale la. Chiŋmanni a jam lik ku kama, tɛŋka a dan sobiri di a nya ase ka bolim la.

ref: whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites.
text: Chiŋmanni a dan bo viuku zuk a paari daa ŋaye yaase chiik yaase ben, Izirali demma a bo ka dula ba kan cheŋ, alege di dan zagri, ba a cheŋ kama.

ref: The Lord told Moses:
text: Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp.
text: <<Kuri kpana a nye damunsa siye a ta peeri a wi naakuuni ate ba a jam jigi yeŋ.

ref: If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: Ase siyewa a dan peeri, naakuuni meena ale tigsi fi niŋ Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku nɔi.

ref: But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
text: Ase kanyi dekki a dan kum, niŋdeerɔma ale yezuimaŋa nyam a yaa le tigsi fi niŋ.

ref: Give a signal on a trumpet when it is time to break camp. The first blast will be the signal for the tribes camped on the east side, and the second blast will be the signal for those on the south.
text: Damuniŋka a dan kum saari buye, baai ale bo yeseoku geŋsa la mɛ ale nyini. Damuniŋka kumsaŋa ale ku sak ayen ku magsika ba nyini a cheŋ.

ref: But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet.
text: Ate fi tigsi tigsuŋku la, peeri damunsaŋa, alege si kumsaŋa a chim ku tɔga ale nyinika kumsaŋa.

ref: The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
text: <<Kaabteerɔwa Aaron nidoabilisaŋa ale magsi ba peeri damunsaŋa. Kude ale chim ka ŋmarisi kaai ale ka beni a te fi ale fi gaŋsaŋa.

ref: Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you.
text: Ase nama a dan cheŋ ni nye kpaliŋ nidek tɛŋka po ale ni dachiak waai ale a namsi ni la, ni peeri ni damunsaŋa. Naawen ni Wenni ale teeri ni wari a vari ni ni dachaasaŋa nisa po a basi.

ref: During the celebration of the New Moon Festival and other religious festivals, sound the trumpets while you offer sacrifices. This will be a reminder that I am the Lord your God. The Israelites Begin Their Journey
text: Ate diipo ate ni mariŋ nidek a dɛ Chiik Paalika tigini la, ni yaa peeri damunsaŋa a basi ni juka ale ni suiyɔgni tiiritaŋa zuk ate ku la chim teerika a te ni, ni Wen niŋ. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.>>

ref: On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on.
text: Daa pisiyewa danni chiisa siyewa, bena ŋayewa po, chiŋmanni a yaa basi viuku ate Naawen Wanni a boro la.

ref: So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert.
text: Ate Izirali demma a yaa basi Sinai Gɔnni a taam dɛ, a ga dɛ ate ku ga paari diipo ate chiŋmanni a ga bo Paran Gɔnni zuk la.

ref: This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
text: Ba yaa jam piilim nyini a cheŋ ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis la.

ref: Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe,
text: Juda nidoabilisaŋa tiktiwa a va chaab ale ba tugurik tommu yueŋa ale dɛ niŋ a nyini, ate Amminadab nidoabinni Naason, a nya tommu zuk.

ref: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe,
text: Zuar nidoabinni Netanel ale jam chim Isaka dɔkku niŋdeerɔ,

ref: and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
text: alege ate Yelon nidoabinni Eliab a chim Zebulun dɔkku niŋdeerɔ.

ref: The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
text: Ate Livaima yaa kpiti viuku, ate Gerson ale Merari kabini a ji nyini a cheŋ.

ref: Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe,
text: Aruben dɔkku ale jam pai a saŋ ale ba tiktiwa a ta va ba ale ka diila. Ka Sedeur nidoabinni Elizur ale jam dɛ ba niŋ.

ref: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe,
text: Zurisaddai nidoabinni Selumiel ale jam dɛ Simeyon dɔkku niŋ,

ref: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
text: alege ate Deuel nidoabinni Eliasaf a chim Gad dɔkku niŋdeerɔ.

ref: Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
text: Koyat kabini a yaa nyini a ji ŋan weleŋsaŋa. Viuku a jam magsi ka ku ti alege jigi ate ba paari du.

ref: Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe,
text: Ɛfraim dɔkku ale jam pai saŋ ale ba tiktiwa a ta va ba ale ka diila. Ka Ammiyud nidoabinni Elisama ale jam dɛ ba niŋ.

ref: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe,
text: Pedazur nidoabinni Gamaliil ale jam dɛ Manasa dɔkku niŋ,

ref: and Abidan son of Gideoni was the leader of the Benjamin tribe.
text: alege ate Abidan nidoabinni Abidan a jam dɛ Benjamin dɔkku niŋ.

ref: Dan and the tribes that camped alongside it were to protect the Israelites against an attack from behind, and so they marched last, carrying their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Dan,
text: Kpeglimka po ase baai ale jam potim a nya labika zuk la, ka Dan dɔkku ale jam wari ŋaaŋ a nyini ale ba tikti wa a ta va ba mɛ ale ka diila. Ammisaddai nidoabinni Ayiezer ale jam dɛ ba mɛ niŋ.

ref: Pagiel son of Ochran was the leader of the Asher tribe,
text: Okran nidoabinni Pagiel ale jam a nya Asɛ dɔkku zuk,

ref: and Ahira son of Enan was the leader of the Naphtali tribe.
text: alege ate Enan nidoabinni Ayira a nya Nafitali dɔkku zuk.

ref: This was the order in which the Israelites marched each time they moved their camp.
text: Izirali demma ale jam labi dii a cheŋ la ale la.

ref: Hobab the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, was there. And Moses said to him, “We're leaving for the place the Lord has promised us. He has said that all will go well for us. So come along, and we will make sure that all goes well for you.”
text: Moosis yaa weeni Areuel nidoabinni Yobab, Midian denɔwa, wa ŋachobwa ayen, <<Ti a yaali ti nyini cheŋ ka juijui ate Naawen a weeni ayen, <M le pai dula a te ni la.> Cheŋ ale ti, tama ale nye fu a magsi, Naawen a puulim ka wamaŋsa ale Izirali demma.>>

ref: “No, I won't go,” Hobab answered. “I'm returning home to be with my own people.”
text: Alege ate wa tulisi ayen, <<Aaya, m kan cheŋŋi. Mi a yaa m ŋman kuli ka m dek tɛŋka ale m nuruma jigi.>>

ref: “Please go with us!” Moses said. “You can be our guide because you know the places to camp in the desert.
text: Alege Moosis a weeni ayen, <<Jenje kan basi ti. Fi seba kauk kuui ale magsi ti tigsi gɔnni de po la kama, fi a baga a chim tama nina kama.

ref: Besides that, if you go, we will give you a share of the good things the Lord gives us.”
text: Fi a dan cheŋ ale ti, tama ale chari ale fu jamaŋ kaai ate Naawen a te tama la.>>

ref: The people of Israel began their journey from Mount Sinai. They traveled three days, and the Levites who carried the sacred chest led the way, so the Lord could show them where to camp.
text: Ate ba yaa basi Naawen guuku ale nyini cheŋ daa ŋata meena. Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale jam dɛ ba niŋ daa ŋatawa meena po a gisi jigi a te ba ayen ba vuusi.

ref: Each day as the Israelites began their journey, Moses would pray, “Our Lord, defeat your enemies and make them run!”
text: Diipo meena nɔiyeŋka dakanni a dan ga nyini, Moosis nyiem jam weeni kama ayen, <<M Naawen, yiti zaani, ate fi dachaasaŋa a waaŋ chaab. Fi dachaasaŋa a chali bɛ fi niŋ.>>

ref: And when they stopped to set up camp, he would pray, “Our Lord, stay close to Israel's thousands and thousands of people.”
text: Ase di dan jam zaani, wa nyiem weeni kama ayen, <<Ŋman jam m Naawen Izirali demma baai ale kan ta chiina la jigi.>>

ref: One day the Israelites started complaining about their troubles. The Lord heard them and became so angry that he destroyed the outer edges of their camp with fire.
text: Nuruma a yaa jam fɔbili a ta va wapagra ŋaai ate ba bo ŋa po la Naawen tue po, ase wa le ga wom ba la, wa sui yaa puuri. Ate bolim a nyini Naawen jigi a dɛ ba alege a kaasi ba boka jigini nakpiaka gela.

ref: When the people begged Moses to help, he prayed, and the fire went out.
text: Ase nuruma ale jam kum te Moosis la, wa yaa puusi a te Naawen ate bolimu a kpi.

ref: They named the place “Burning,” because in his anger the Lord had set their camp on fire. The People Grumble about Being Hungry
text: Ba jam a wi dula jigini ayen ka Tabera, dii nyiŋla bolimu ale nyini Naawen jigi a dɛ ba.

ref: One day some foreigners among the Israelites became greedy for food, and even the Israelites themselves began moaning, “We don't have any meat!
text: Nicham baai ale jam va ba a nyini Ejipiti la, kɔrisa a yaa jam bo ŋandiin yonta jigi, ate Izirali demma a ŋman piilim kum a weeni ayen, <<Ase ti dan poom taka lam a ŋɔbi,

ref: In Egypt we could eat all the fish we wanted, and there were cucumbers, melons, all kinds of onions, and garlic.
text: tama a teeri jumaŋa ate ti jam bo Ejipiti a ŋɔbi ale kan tuni ŋa nyiŋla kama, ti jam maari a dɛ yɔna tɔgatɔga mɛ ale alabasa ale galik kama.

ref: But we're starving out here, and the only food we have is this manna.”
text: Alege yɔgyɔgla de ti jɔk koarisila kama. Tama an ŋman nya jaaboa ka Nyɔnɔwa ŋandiintaŋa nyiini.>>

ref: He prayed: I am your servant, Lord, so why are you doing this to me? What have I done to deserve this? You've made me responsible for all these people,
text: Ate wa bek Naawen ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a ta daanika dɛ a jam fi yɔmawa jigi ya? Ka boa ate mi nye a kaasi fi, ate fi pai nuruma de daanika a seeri mi?

ref: This job is too much for me. How can I take care of all these people by myself?
text: Mi a kan baga a ta nuruma de meena m dega, wanni a ŋmasi pagra a gaam mu kama.

ref: If this is the way you're going to treat me, just kill me now and end my miserable life! Seventy Leaders Are Chosen To Help Moses
text: Fi a daa fi nye mi kan nnala, be ko mu yɔgyɔgla de ase ku nin yɔk fi sui. Kan basi ate mi kpi mi dek kummoa.>>

ref: While I am talking with you there, I will give them some of your authority, so they can share responsibility for my people. You will no longer have to care for them by yourself.
text: M le siŋ jam biisi ale fu dula jigini, mi ale pai Chiik kaai ale bo fi po la, a nyo ba po. Ba le maari fu ate fi baga a nya nuruma zuk, dii le ku basi ate ku kan chim fi nyiini wari ya.

ref: As for the Israelites, I have heard them complaining about not having meat and about being better off in Egypt. So tell them to make themselves acceptable to me, because tomorrow they will have meat.
text: <<Weeni nuruma ayen, <Ni gomsi nidek a magsi chum, ale ni a ni ŋɔbi ka lam, Naawen a wom ni kama diipo ate ni kum ayen, ase tama a dan poom ta ka lam a ŋɔbi, ti jam zunchoŋ kama diipo ate ti jam bo Ejipiti po la. Yɔgyɔgla de Naawen ale te ni lam ate ni ŋɔbi.

ref: . They turned against me and wanted to go back to Egypt. Now they will eat meat until they get sick of it.
text: alege ni le ŋɔbi a paari ka chiik pumi ate ti va ni nyueŋa nyini dii nyiŋla ni zɛri Naawen dii ale bo ale ni la kama a kum wa niŋ a weeni ayen, ka boa ate tama a basi Ejipiti tɛŋka?> >>

ref: grown men are here with me. How can you say there will be enough meat to feed them and their families for a whole month?
text: ) po a cheŋ naŋta, ate fi weeni ayen, <Mi ale te ba lam ate ba ŋɔbi chiika meena.>

ref: Even if we butchered all our sheep and cattle, or caught every fish in the sea, we wouldn't have enough to feed them.”
text: Ba le nya yega ase ba nin poom tɔgri duŋsa a te ba? Ba le chagi ase ba nin yik jumaŋa meena nyakpiemu po a te ba?>>

ref: The Lord answered, “I can do anything! Watch and you'll see my words come true.”
text: Naawen a yaa tulisi Moosis ayen, <<Naawen nisaŋa a ŋmasi gela kama? Fi yaa le nya ase m le weeni diila ale nye wensie a te fu ya.>>

ref: Eldad and Medad were two leaders who had not gone to the tent. But when the Spirit took control of them, they began shouting like prophets right there in camp.
text: Alege nuruba baye, ba yue jam le Eldad ale Medad ale jam tali bo ba boka jigini. Ba jam chiini ba a gum nisɔmma po kama alege ba an jam nyini cheŋ Viuku po. Alege Chiika a diem jam bo ba po kama ate ba biisi Naawen wie.

ref: A boy ran to Moses and told him about Eldad and Medad.
text: Nuru paalik a yaa chali cheŋ Moosis jigi a ga weeni ayen, <<Eldad ale Medad a biisi ka Wen wie ba boka jigini.>>

ref: Joshua was there helping Moses, as he had done since he was young. And he said to Moses, “Sir, you must stop them!”
text: Nun nidoabinni Josua waai ale jam a maari Moosis wa paalimu po la, a yaa biisi ayen, <<Moosis m nyɔnɔwa, kasi ba!>>

ref: But Moses replied, “Are you concerned what this might do to me? I wish the Lord would give his Spirit to all his people so everyone could be a prophet.”
text: Alege Moosis yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi a dɛka nyuri mi nyiŋŋa? Mi a yaali ayen Naawen nuruma meena ate ka biisiteerɔba ate Naawen a pai wa Chiika a nyo ba po.>>

ref: Some time later the Lord sent a strong wind that blew quails in from the sea until Israel's camp was completely surrounded with birds, piled up about a meter high for many kilometers in every direction.
text: Viok a yaa nyini Naawen jigi a ta yeŋsa nyini nyakpiemu geŋsa a jam te ba. Ku ta jam gilim ba boka jigini meena kama ate si vi chaab a jueli paari duna a yalima ase danni po meena chelim la.

ref: The people picked up quails for two days—each person filled at least ten large baskets. Then they spread them out to dry.
text: Dai dila meena ale yok kula ale dai dii ale paasaŋ la meena, nuruma a jam nyini a tigsi ka yeŋsa. Waai an jam tigsi boorisa ate si an paari pi. Ba jam kati si a waaŋ gilim ba boka jigini meena kama.

ref: But before the meat could be eaten, the Lord became angry and sent a deadly disease through the camp.
text: Alege lammu ale diem jam bo ba nyinaŋa po la, alege jigi ate ba nɛ bu la, Naawen sui yaa puuri ale nuruma, ate wa yaa basi ate nyiŋtuila a yik ba.

ref: After they had buried the people who had been so greedy for meat, they called the place “Graves for the Greedy.”
text: Dila nyiŋla ba yaa te dula yuei ayen Kibrot Yattaava dii nyiŋla, dula jigini ate ba gu nuru baai ale dɛ ŋandiin yonta la.

ref: Israel then broke camp and traveled to Hazeroth.
text: A nyini Kibrot Yattaava nuruma a jam cheŋ ka Yazerot a ga bo dula jigini.

ref: and told Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to come to the entrance of the sacred tent.
text: Ate Naawen yaa deri weeni Moosis ale Aaron ale Miriam ayen, <<Ni nyini jam Tuka Viuku po ni nɔi ni tama meena.>> Ate ba nɔi ba tama a yaa nyini.

ref: Then after commanding them to listen carefully, he said: “I, the Lord, speak to prophets in visions and dreams.
text: Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni wom mi wieŋa. Ase Naawen biisiteerɔ a dan bo ni po, m te pai m dek sak wa kama, m le biisi ale wa gɔdaasima po.

ref: He sees me face to face, and everything I say to him is perfectly clear. You have no right to criticize my servant Moses.”
text: Mi a biisi le wa ka wa nina po nalimnyiini, daa sunsuelima, wa a nya mi ase ka mi ale ka diila. Ka boa ate nama a kan chali yɔgsum ale biisi m tomteerɔwa Moosis a kaasi?>>

ref: The Lord became angry with Aaron and Miriam. And after the Lord left
text: Ate Naawen sui yaa puuri ale ba ate wa basi ba.

ref: and the cloud disappeared from over the sacred tent, Miriam's skin turned white with leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her,
text: Ase chiŋmanni ale basi Viuku la, Miriam yaa deri za a peenti nna tektek. Aaron a yaa viriŋ tuk wa a nya ale wa nyiŋka a kaasi,

ref: he said to Moses, “Sir, please don't punish us for doing such a foolish thing.
text: ate wa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Jenje m nyɔnɔ, kan pai tuni ti, tama le nye betta nyeka a tom biem buui la nyiŋŋa.

ref: Moses prayed, “Lord God, please heal her.”
text: Dila nyiŋla Moosis yaa kaari a te Naawen ayen, <<Wen yaa, tebi wa.>>

ref: But the Lord replied, “Miriam would be disgraced for seven days if her father had punished her by spitting in her face. So make her stay outside the camp for seven days, before coming back.”
text: Ate Naawen a yaa tulisi Moosis ayen, <<Ase wa kowa a dan chesi tuntueta a nyo wa ninaŋa po, wa ti le bo chivie po a paari daa ŋayopɔi. Basi ate wa jam ni boka jigini.>>

ref: The people of Israel did not move their camp until Miriam returned seven days later.
text: Dila nyiŋ Miriam yaa jam boka peelim a paari daa ŋayopɔi, nuruma an jam ga jigi ya ate ku paari diipo ate ba ta wa ŋman jam la.

ref: Then they left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran Desert.
text: Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ, nuruma a basi Yazerot kama ale cheŋ ga bo Paran Gɔnni po.

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: In fact, we saw the Nephilim who are the ancestors of the Anakim. They were so big that we felt as small as grasshoppers.”
text: Ti nya Anak ŋaaŋbisaŋa Nefilim demma mɛ a boka dula. Tama a nye ase ka nanchoŋta la tama dek nina po, ti ka dila a te ba.>>

ref: “Choose a leader from each tribe and send them into Canaan to explore the land I am giving you.”
text: <<Tom nuruba ate ba ga kpesi nya Keenan tɛŋka, kaai ate mi ale pai te Izirali demma la. A nyini ba ŋiaka dɔkku po tom ku niŋdeerɔma wanyi meena.>>

ref: So Moses sent twelve tribal leaders from Israel's camp in the Paran Desert
text: Ase Naawen ale weeni la, Moosis yaa tom ba ate ba nyini Paran Gɔnni. Ba meena a jam ka Izirali niŋdeerɔba.

ref: Before Moses sent them into Canaan, he said: After you go through the Southern Desert of Canaan, continue north into the hill country
text: Ase Moosis ale tom ba ayen ba ga kpesi nya Keenan tɛŋka la, wa weeni ayen, <<Ni va Negev tɛŋka po ale tɛŋ kaai ate guuta a bo ka po la.

ref: and find out what those regions are like. Be sure to remember how many people live there, how strong they are,
text: Ni nya ase tɛŋka a nye ase ka se la, nuru baai ale bo ka po la a ta pagrim yaase ba wobsa kama, ba piisi yaase ba an piisi ya.

ref: and if they live in open towns or walled cities. See if the land is good for growing crops and find out what kinds of trees grow there. It's time for grapes to ripen, so try to bring back some of the fruit that grows there.
text: Ka tantaŋa ka sɛ? Poosuk a bo ka po yaase poosuk a ka? Tiisa a bo ka po yaase tiisa ka? Ni nye dii ate ni ale baga a ta tɛŋka tiisaŋa yɔnaŋa gela a jam la.>> Ku jam ka diipo ale magsi yɔn fi gilima ŋaai ale dɛ niŋ a muni la.

text: Alege Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ale Aaron ayen, <<Nama ale kan ta sebchakka mi la ate ni an zuli mi ase weleŋsa nyɔnɔ Izirali demma nina po la nyiŋ, ni kan ta tigsuŋku dɛ a jam tɛŋka ate mi a te ba la po.>>

ref: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
text: Meriba nyaataŋa jam ale nna juijui ate Izirali demma a jam kpaliŋ ale Naawen, dula jigini ate wa jam pai wadek a sak ba ase waai ale ta tuilum la.

ref: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
text: Moosis a yaa tom nuruba ate ba nyini Kades a cheŋ Edom Naawa jigi, a weeni wa ayen, <<Dii ate fi suoku Izirali a weeni la ale nna: fi seba wapagri ŋaai ale jam tama jigi la kama.

ref: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
text: Tama kokpieŋsaŋa a jam cheŋ ka Ejipiti tɛŋka, ti jam bo dula ka ben boari. Ejipiti demma a jam namisi tama ale ti koma kama,

ref: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
text: alege tama ale jam kaari a te Naawen la, wa wom ti kaarika a tom maarɔ ate wa ta ti a nyini Ejipiti po a nyini. Yɔgyɔgla de ti bo ka dela Kades, tɛŋ kaai ale moata fi tɛŋ banni la.

ref: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
text: <<Ti a saalim basi ate ti va fi tɛŋka po a taam. Ti kan jo talim yaase kaduk po yaase ti nyu nyiam vili po. Ti le vaka Naawa Suik Duoku po a taam ti kan viriŋ juga yaase gala ate ti ga nyini fi tɛŋka po a nyini.>>

ref: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
text: Edom a yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ni kan va dela ni dan zɛri ale jam, ti le nyini ale gebisa a siti ni.>>

ref: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
text: Izirali demma a yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ti le va ka suik duoku a taam ase tama yaase ti duŋsaŋa a dan nyu ni nyaataŋa ti le tuni bu nyiŋ. Tama a yaa ti cheŋ ka naŋta a va du a taam wari a karo.>>

ref: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
text: Ba yaa ŋman tulisi ayen, <<Ni kan bag a va dela.>> Edom demma a yaa nyini a tu chaab ale ba ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba nna yegayega.

ref: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
text: Ase Edom demma ale zɛri ayen ba kan va ba tɛŋka po a taam la Izirali demma a yaa cheem va suik yoŋ.

ref: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
text: Izirali naakuuni meena a yaa basi Kades ale jam Yor Guuku.

ref: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
text: <<Aaron kala wa kpi a cheŋ ka wa nuruma jigi. Wa kan jo tɛŋ kaai ate mi a te Izirali demma la dii nyiŋla, ni nɔi niyema a nye kaasi m wanni kama diipo ate ni bo Meriba nyaataŋa jigini la.

text: Yik Aaron ale wa nidoabinni Eleaza a ta ba jueli Yor Guuku zuk.

ref: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
text: Yeeri Aaron gattaŋa a pai ti jo wa nidoabinni Eleaza ale Aaron a kala wa kpi a cheŋ ka wa nuruma jigi. Wa le kpi ka dela.>>

ref: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
text: Moosis yaa nye dii ate Naawen a weeni wa la. Ba yaa jam jueli Yor Guuku zuk alege naakuuni meena.

ref: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
text: Moosis a yaa yeeri Aaron gattaŋa a pai ti jo wa nidoabinni Eleaza. Aaron a yaa jam kpi guuku zuk. Moosis ale Eleaza a yaa nyini guuku zuk a siŋ,

text: ase naakuuni meena ale ga wom ayen Aaron kpi la, Izirali yenni meena a yaa kum wa nyiŋ a paari daa pisita.

ref: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient

text: Ba yaa jam biisi kaasi Wen ale Moosis ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi ta ti nyini Ejipiti po a nyini ayen ti kpi gɔnni dɛ po? Ŋandiinta ka! Nyiam ka! Ti be kan yaali niniga ŋandiintaŋa de!>>

ref: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
text: Izirali demma a yaa jam bo Amori demma tɛŋka po.

text: Ba yaa jam chub wa lɔnsi ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ale wa tugurik tommu meena an tali javuwa. Ale jam tuesi wa tɛŋka a tara.

ref: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel

text: Moab demma a yaa biisi ale Midian nisɔmma ayen, <<Nuru boanni a za ba dɛ ka jabuui meena ale gilim ti la ase naab ale dɛ wuuk meena diila.>> Dila nyiŋla Zippor nidoabinni Belak, waai ale jam ka Moab naab da ŋala po la,

ref: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.

text: Balaam yaa tulisi Wen ayen, <<Zippor nidoabinni Belak, Moab naawa ale tom ba mi jigi,

text: Alege Balaam a yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Ase Belak a dam poom pai wa yenni ate kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a sueri di la a te mi, mi a kan baga a nye wakpien yaase wa fiik a kaasi Naawen m Wenni wanni.

ref: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
text: Balaam yaa yiti saluiku a do wa bonika a va Moab nabisaŋa a cheŋ.

ref: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.

ref: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.

ref: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
text: Naawen maarɔwa a yaa weeni Balaam ayen, <<Cheŋ ale nuruma alege biisi dii ate mi a weeni fu la nyiini.>> Ate Balaam va nabisaŋa a cheŋ Belak jigi.

text: <<Nyɔnɔwa waai ale ka Naawen la, fi piilim boro a sak fi tomteerɔwa fi zuaka ale fi pagrimu ale ka diila kama. A nyini wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk de wen a karo a tom wakpiema ŋaai ate fi a tom la?

ref: The land west of the Jordan is such good land. Please let me cross the Jordan and see the hills and the Lebanon Mountains.”
text: Basi ate m cheŋ a ga nya tɛŋ maŋka ale gaam Jodan a taam la, kaai ale bo guuta zuk la ale Lebanon tɛŋka.>>

ref: But the Lord was angry with me because of you people, and he refused to listen. “That's enough!” he said. “I don't want to hear any more.
text: Alege nama nyiŋ Naawen sui a jam puuri ale mu kama ate wa an wom m puusaŋa. <<Ku magsi ya.>> Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Kan ŋman biisi wanni de wie ale mu.

ref: Climb to the top of Mount Pisgah and look north, south, east, and west. Take a good look, but you are not going to cross the Jordan River.
text: Jueli Pisga guuku zuk a nya yeniŋ geŋ ale yeseoku geŋ ale wiiluk geŋ ale kori geŋsaŋa. Nya tɛŋka ale fidek nimbie dii nyiŋla fi a kan yaali fi gaam Jodan benni a taamu.

ref: Joshua will lead Israel across the Jordan to take the land, so help him be strong and brave and tell him what he must do.”
text: Alege sak Josua abe fi maari a te wa nyiŋbiiri ate wa ale dɛ nuruma dɛ niŋ a ta ba gaam a taam a tuesi tɛŋ kaai ate fi a nya la.>>

ref: After this we stayed in the valley at Beth-Peor.
text: Ate tama a yaa jam bo viaka po a moata Bet Peor.

ref: Israel, listen to these laws and teachings! If you obey them, you will live, and you will go in and take the land that the Lord is giving you. He is the God your ancestors worshiped,
text: Ni wom de, Izirali demma, sinsaŋŋa ate m boro a yaali ayen m sak ni la ale wie ŋaai ate ni a va la. Ni va ŋa ate ni vua ate ni jo tɛŋka po a tuesi ka, kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni kokpieŋsaŋa Wen la ale te ni la.

ref: But all of you that were faithful to the Lord your God are still alive today.
text: Alege nama baai meena ale chiib va Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a diem vua kama jinla.

ref: You must be very careful not to forget the things you have seen God do for you. Keep reminding yourselves, and tell your children and grandchildren as well.
text: Ni kpesi yik nidek, a moata chaab ate ni kan baŋ dii ate ni nya ale ni ninaŋa la yaase ni basi ate ŋa sati a nyini ni suiniimaŋa po a nyini ase ni le diem vua la. Ni pai ŋa a sak ni bisaŋa ale ni ŋaaŋsaŋa mɛ.

ref: Do you remember the day you stood in the Lord's presence at Mount Sinai? The Lord said, “Moses, bring the people of Israel here. I want to speak to them so they will obey me as long as they live, and so they will teach their children to obey me too.”
text: Ni teeri dai dii danni ate ni jam zaani Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋ Yoreb guuku zuk la diipo ate wa weeni mi ayen, <<Tigsi nuruma m niŋ ate ba wom m wieŋa ate ba zamsi ate ba va mi diipo meena ate ba vua a bo tɛŋka po la, abe ba pai ŋa a sak ba bisaŋa.>>

ref: Mount Sinai was surrounded by deep dark clouds, and fire went up to the sky. You came to the foot of the mountain,
text: Ni jam torisi moata kama ale za guuku zuk alege ate ku jam a nyaksi ase bolim la a jueli wenŋmazuk ale chiŋma sobta ate ku jam nye legi,

ref: and the Lord spoke to you from the fire. You could hear him and understand what he was saying, but you couldn't see him.
text: Ate Naawen a yaa jam biisi bolimu po ale ni. Ni wom ka wieŋa nuemka alege ni an jam nya jaaboa ku jam ka lueluk nyiini.

ref: The Lord said he was making an agreement with you, and he told you that your part of the agreement is to obey the Ten Commandments. Then the Lord wrote these Commandments on two flat stones.
text: Wa yaa weeni ni wa nɔiyeŋka, Wie Piika ŋaai ate wa weeni ni ayen ni va ŋa abe ni ŋmarisiŋa a dueni tintain paglaksa siye zuk.

ref: That's when the Lord commanded me to give you the laws and teachings you must obey in the land that you will conquer west of the Jordan River. Don't Worship Idols Moses said to Israel:
text: Ate Naawen a yaa weeni mi dipo ayen m sak ni wa wieŋa ale sinsaŋŋa ate ni va ŋa tɛŋ kaai ate ni a yaali ni gaam Jodan benni a taam soaka la.

ref: When God spoke to you from the fire, he was invisible. So be careful
text: Ni an jam nya wari ya da dii danni ate Naawen a biisi ale ni bolimu po Yoreb guuku zuk la. Dila nyiŋla ni be kpesi nidek nalimnyiini,

ref: not to commit the sin of worshiping idols. Don't make idols to be worshiped, whether they are shaped like men, women,
text: dii ale ku nye ate ni kan taŋ nidek ale bɔgta, yaali ŋan mɛɛnta, baai ale a nye ase nidoa yaase nipok la.

ref: And when you see the sun or moon or stars, don't be tempted to bow down and worship them. The Lord put them there for all the other nations to worship.
text: Ase ni dan zak nya chiŋmaaŋa po a nya wenbinni ale chiika ale chiŋmarisaŋa ale wenŋmazuk ŋantaŋa meena ni kan koori tɛŋ a zuli ŋan baai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a pai te tɛŋ meena tɛŋzuk de la.

ref: The Lord was angry with me because of what you said, and he told me that he would not let me cross the Jordan River into the good land that he is giving you.
text: Naawen sui ale jam puuri ale mu nama nyiŋ, ate wa yaa pɛ ayen m kan gaam Jodan benni a jo wenŋmazuk kuui ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaali wa te ni ate ni ta la.

ref: So I must stay here and die on this side of the Jordan, but you will cross the river and take the land.
text: M le kpi kama tɛŋka de po; m kan gaam Jodan benni a taamu, alege nama boro a yaali ni gaam kama abe le tuesi tɛŋ naliŋka.

ref: The Lord will be angry if you worship other gods, and he can be like a fire destroying everything in its path.
text: Ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a nye ase ka bolim buui ale dɛ la, wa ka Naawen dii ale a dɛ nyuri.

ref: Soon you will cross the Jordan River and settle down in the land. Then in the years to come, you will have children, and they will give you grandchildren. After many years, you might lose your sense of right and wrong and make idols, even though the Lord your God hates them. So I am giving you fair warning today, and I call the earth and the sky as witnesses. If you ever make idols, the Lord will be angry, and you won't have long to live, because the Lord will let you be wiped out.
text: mi ale wi ka wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋ ate ba chim m seerɔba a ta va ni jigi ate daaŋa de po ate nama ale kpi nwuli tɛŋ kaai po ate nama a yaali ni gaam Jodan benni a taam a ta la. Ni kan bo dula a beni ni ale kpi kama.

ref: Only a few of you will survive, and the Lord will force you to leave the land and will scatter you among the nations.
text: Naawen ale kati ni a waaŋ kama nuruma po, ka ni maga ale ni vuuk a bo tɛŋ sii ate Naawen a ta ni a cheŋ la.

ref: There you will have to worship gods made of wood and stone, and these are nothing but idols that can't see or hear or eat or smell.
text: Dula jigini ni yaa ale kaab bɔgluk tii ate nuruba a pai nisa a nye ale daata ale tintana la, tii ale kaa nya yaase ti a wom yaase ti a dɛ yaase ti a wom nyum la.

ref: In all of your troubles, you may finally decide that you want to worship only the Lord. And if you turn back to him and obey him completely, he will again be your God.
text: Ase ni dan bo watuasa po ate wieŋa de meena a nye ni ku kan beni ale ni ale tulim Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la jigi a wom wa.

ref: The Lord your God will have mercy—he won't destroy you or desert you. The Lord will remember his promise, and he will keep the agreement he made with your ancestors.
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ka jiirim Wen. Wa kan zɛri ni yaase wa kaasi ni yaa wa baŋ nɔiyeŋka ate wa nye ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa kaai la.

ref: When the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt, you saw how he fought for you and showed his great power by performing terrifying miracles. You became his people, and at Mount Sinai you heard him talking to you out of fiery flames. And yet you are still alive! Has anything like this ever happened since the time God created humans? No matter where you go or who you ask, you will get the same answer. No one has ever heard of another god even trying to do such things as the Lord your God has done for you.
text: Bɔgluk kuui a diem baga a tuesi tɛŋ a tara a ta va nyenyaka yaase wakperikaliisa yaase wakinkagla yaase zuaka ale nyeka ase wie ŋaai meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a nye ni nimbie po a te ni diipo ate ni jam bo Ejipiti po la?

ref: The Lord wants you to know he is the only true God, and he wants you to obey him. That's why he let you see his mighty miracles and his fierce fire on earth, and why you heard his voice from that fire and from the sky.
text: A nyini wenŋmazuk wa basi ate ni wom wa lueluku ayen wa namsi ni. Tɛŋzuk de sak ni wa bolim kpiemu ale ka diila kama, ate ni wom wa wieŋa bolimu po.

ref: The Lord loved your ancestors and decided that you would be his people. So the Lord used his great power to bring you out of Egypt.
text: Wa ale jam a yaali ni kokpieŋsaŋa ale lueri ba ŋaaŋbisaŋa la nyiŋ ate wa yaa ta ni a nyini Ejipiti po nyini ale wa pagrim kpiemu,

ref: Now you face other nations more powerful than you are, but the Lord has already started forcing them out of their land and giving it to you.
text: ale yiak tɛŋ sii ale pagra a gaam ni la ate si nyini ale ta ni a jam ba tɛŋsaŋa po ayen ni tanla se ku ale ka dii jinla de la.

ref: So remember that the Lord is the only true God, whether in the sky above or on the earth below.
text: Ni be seba, abe le basi ate ku bo ni suiniima po jinla danni ayen, Naawen ka Wen wenŋmazuk po ale tɛŋzuk de mɛ. Waai a ŋman karo.

ref: Today I am explaining his laws and teachings. And if you always obey them, you and your descendants will live long and be successful in the land the Lord is giving you. Safe Towns
text: Ni be ta wa wieŋa ale wa sinsaŋŋa, ŋaai ate mi a te ni jinla de la, ate ku ale cheŋ nalimnyiini ale nama ale ni bisaŋa ate ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate ni ale goa tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a pai a te ni la po a beni.

ref: The Israelites had come from Egypt and were camped east of the Jordan River near Beth-Peor, when Moses gave these laws and teachings. The land around their camp had once belonged to King Sihon of Heshbon. But Moses and the Israelites defeated him
text: ale diipo ate ba jam bo Bet Peor viaka po Jodan kori geŋka la, tɛŋ kaai ate ba a wi ayen Amori la, ate Siyon a jam chim ka naab la waai ale jam a nya Yesbon ate Moosis ale Izirali demma nak yik ba diipo ate ba jam nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la.

ref: and King Og of Bashan, and took their lands. These two Amorite kings had ruled the territory east of the Jordan River
text: Ba jam tuesi wa tɛŋka kama ale Basan Naawa Og tɛŋka, nalima ŋayewa ale jam bo Amori tɛŋsaŋa ale bo Jodan benni kori geŋsa la.

ref: from the town of Aroer on the edge of the Arnon River gorge, north to Mount Hermon.
text: Tɛŋka de a jam zaani ka Aroer a ga nye ban ale Arnon Buboalika a ta ga va Sirion guuku ,

ref: Their land included the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, as far south as the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
text: a ga pai Araba ale bo Jodan benni kori geŋsa la meena a gum du a ta ga paari nyakpiemu ale bo Araba la a ta jueli tuak Pisga.

ref: Moses called together the people of Israel and said: Today I am telling you the laws and teachings that you must follow, so listen carefully.
text: Moosis a tigsi Izirali demma meena a weeni ba ayen. Izirali demma, ni wom sinsaŋŋa ale wieŋa ate mi a weeni jinla de la. Ni zamsi ŋa abe ni seba a chak ayen ni va ŋa kama.

ref: Do not murder.
text: Kan ko nuru.

ref: The Lord our God made an agreement with our nation at Mount Sinai.
text: Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a jam nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale ti Yoreb guuku.

ref: That agreement wasn't only with our ancestors but with us, who are here today.
text: Ku be daa ti koma ate Naawen a jam nye nɔiyeŋka ale ba alege ka tama, baai meena ale vua a bo dela jinla de la.

ref: The Lord himself spoke to you out of the fire,
text: Naawen a jam biisi bolimu po ale ni ka nidek nimbie po guuku zuk.

ref: but you were afraid of the fire and refused to go up the mountain. So I spoke with the Lord for you, then I told you that he had said:
text: Diipo ate mi a jam zaani Naawen ale nama suŋsuŋ a pai wa wanni a te ni la dii nyiŋla ni jam yɔgsa kama ale bolimu ate ni an jueli guuku zuwa. Ate wa yaa weeni ayen.

ref: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
text: <<Mi ale Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la, waai ale ta fu nyini Ejipiti a nyini yɔntidi tɛŋka po a nyini la.

ref: Do not worship any god except me.
text: <<Kan ta wen yona a gum mi po.

ref: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
text: <<Kan nye bɔgluk ate ku a neesi jaab wenŋmazuk yaase tɛŋzuk yaase nyiam po a te fi dega.

ref: Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me and worship idols, I will punish your families for three or four generations.
text: <<Kan koori tɛŋ a zuli ba yaase fi puusi ba, diila mi Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la, ka nyuri Wen, a namsi bimbaansa ba koba biem nyiŋ a ta ga paari ba gaŋ sii ale a saari buta ale bunaansi la baai ale kisi mi la.

ref: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
text: Alege a sak ŋmanteka ale gaŋ sii ale saari tusidi a yaali mi ale ŋman ta m wieŋa la.

ref: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
text: <<Kan wi Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la yuenni kinla, diila Naawen a kan basi waai ale a wi Wa yuenni kinla la.

ref: You have six days when you can do your work,
text: Daa ŋayuebi fi pai tom fi tuimaŋa meena,

ref: but the seventh day of the week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your oxen or donkeys or any other animal, not even those foreigners who live in your towns. And don't make your slaves do any work.
text: alege daa ŋayopɔiwa danni ka Vuusum dai a te Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la. Dai dila danni kan tom tuin yoŋŋoa. Fi dek kan tom yaase fi nidoabili yaase fi lie yaase tomteerɔ yaase dɔklie yaase fi lalik yaase boniŋ yaase fi duŋsaŋa kaai yaase nichaanɔ ale bo ale fi la. Dila ale ku basi ate fi tomteerɔwa ale dɔkliewa a vuusi ase fi la.

ref: When we were gathered at the mountain, the Lord spoke to us in a loud voice from the dark fiery cloud. The Lord gave us these commands, and only these. Then he wrote them on two flat stones and gave them to me. The People Were Afraid (Exodus
text: Sinsaŋŋa de ate Naawen weeni ale lueluk kpioŋ a nyini bolimu po ate tigsuŋku meena ale jam bo guuku zuk la a nyini chiŋmaaŋa ale legini po ale an ŋman gum wari du. Ate wa yaa ŋmarisi ŋa a dueni tintain paglaksa siye zuk a te mu.

ref: When fire blazed from the mountain, and you heard the voice coming from the darkness, your tribal leaders came to me
text: Ase nama ale ga wom lueluku legini po la, alege ate guuku zuk a dɛ ale bolim la, ni buuni po niŋdeerɔma meena a jam jam ka mi jigi.

ref: and said: Today the Lord our God has shown us how powerful and glorious he is. He spoke to us from the fire, and we learned that people can live, even though God speaks to them.
text: Ate ni yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a sak ti wa zulaŋa ale wa pagrimu kama ate tama me a wom wa lueluk bolimu po. Jinla ti nya kama ayen nuru a baga a boro kama ase Wen a nin poom a biisi ale wa.

ref: But we don't want to take a chance on being killed by that terrible fire, and if we keep on hearing the Lord's voice, we will die.
text: Alege yɔgyɔgla de, ka boa ale soa ate tama a kpi? Bolim kpiemu dɛ ale dɛ ti, ate ti kpi ase tama ale a wom Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la lueluku ŋmana.

ref: Has anyone else ever heard the only true God speaking from fire, as we have? And even if they have, would they live to tell about it?
text: Ka nuru wana ale diem wom Wen dii ale vua la lueluk ale ku a biisi bolim po ase tama la ale vua?

ref: I wish they would always worship me with fear and trembling and be this willing to obey me! Then they and their children would always enjoy a successful life.
text: Mi dek a yaali kama ayen ba le chali mu yɔgsum ale ba suiniima meena abe ba ta m sinsaŋŋa diipo meena ate ku ale cheŋ nalimnyiini a te ba ale ba bisaŋa taam wuu!

ref: Now, tell them to return to their tents,
text: <<Cheŋ a ga weeni ba ate ba pilim a ŋman cheŋ ba viitaŋa po.

ref: but you come back here to me. After I tell you my laws and teachings, you will repeat them to the people, so they can obey these laws in the land I am giving them. Moses said:
text: Alege fi bo dela ale mi ate mi ale te fu wieŋa ale sinsaŋŋa meena ate fi ale sak ba ate ba ale va ŋa tɛŋ kaai po ate mi ale te ba la.>>

ref: Follow them, because they make a path that will lead to a long successful life in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
text: Cheŋ kauk kuui meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a weeni ni la, dii ale ku nye ate ni boro ale niaka ate nama a goa tɛŋ kaai ate nama ni tuesi la po a beni.

ref: The Lord told me to give you these laws and teachings, so you can obey them in the land he is giving you. Soon you will cross the Jordan River and take that land.
text: Sinsaŋŋa ale wieŋa de ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a weeni ayen mi a sak ni ate ni kpesi a va ŋa tɛŋ kaai po ate ni za ni gaam Jodan benni a taam ka po la;

ref: Pay attention, Israel! Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he promised to give us this land that is rich with milk and honey. Be careful to obey him, and you will become a successful and powerful nation.
text: Ni wom de Izirali demma, abe ni kpesi nidek ate ni wom dii ale ku nye ate wari meena a cheŋ nalimnyiini ate ni piisi tɛŋ kaai po ate biisim ale siita a boro la, ase Naawen ni kokpieŋsaŋa Wenni ale jam puulim ale ni la.

ref: Listen, Israel! The Lord our God is the only true God!
text: Ni wom de Izirali demma: Naawen ka ti Wen. Naawen ka dinyi.

ref: So love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and strength.
text: Yaali Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la ale fi suinum meena ale fi chiik meena ale fi pagrim meena.

ref: and tell them to your children over and over again. Talk about them all the time, whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning.
text: Ni pai ŋa a te ni bisaŋa. Ni a biisi ŋa wie ase ni ale bo yeri yaase nama a nin bo suitaŋa po a cheŋ yaase ni doa yaase ni yiti.

ref: Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and foreheads to help you obey them.
text: Ni bobi ŋa ni nisimaŋa nyiŋ ase daana la abe ni pai ŋa a mag ni deeŋa nyiŋ.

ref: The Lord promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you this land. Now he will take you there and give you large towns, with good buildings that you didn't build,
text: Ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale ta ni a jam tɛŋka po la wa pɛ kama ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob ayen wa te ni tɛŋ kaai ale zuak ate daa nama ale se ya,

ref: and houses full of good things that you didn't put there. The Lord will give you wells that you didn't have to dig, and vineyards and olive orchards that you didn't have to plant. But when you have eaten so much that you can't eat any more,
text: Yie ŋaai ate ŋanmaŋsa meena a sueri ŋa ale daa nama ale pai ba a nyoro, vili ŋaai ate mama an tu ŋa, tali tii ate nama an bori jaab ti po ate nama a yaa dan dɛ a chak,

ref: don't forget it was the Lord who set you free from slavery and brought you out of Egypt.
text: Ni be kpesi nidek ate ni kan baŋ Naawen, waai ale ta ni a nyini Ejipiti yontini tɛŋka po a nyini la wari ya.

ref: Worship and obey the Lord your God with fear and trembling, and promise that you will be loyal to him.
text: Chali Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la nyiini, puusi te wala nyiini abe fi nye ni pɛka wa yuenni nyiŋ.

ref: Don't have anything to do with gods that are worshiped by the nations around you.
text: Kan va wen yona, nuru baai ale bo ale ni la wenaŋa,

ref: If you worship other gods, the Lord will be furious and wipe you off the face of the earth. The Lord your God is with you,
text: ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, waai ale bo ale ni la, ka nyuri dɛka Wen ate ni dan va wen yona wa sui ale puuri ale ni ate wa le kaasi ni tɛŋka de po.

ref: so don't try to make him prove that he can help you, as you did at Massah.
text: Be kan nye Naawen ni Wenni a nya ase ni ale jam a nye dii Massaya la.

ref: Someday your children will ask, “Why did the Lord give us these laws and teachings?”
text: Chum diipo fi biik a dan bek fu ayen, wieŋa de ale sinsaŋŋa de ate Naawen ti Wenni a te ni la kiri ale boa?>>

ref: Then you will answer: We were slaves of the king of Egypt, but the Lord used his great power and set us free.
text: Weeni wa ayen, <<Tama a jam ka yɔm a te Faaro Ejipiti tɛŋka po, alege Naawen a yeeri ti Ejipiti po a ta nyini ale wa pagrimu.

ref: We saw him perform miracles and make horrible things happen to the king, his officials, and everyone else.
text: Naawen a tom ka wakinkagla ale wakperikaliisa, sii ale zuak a ta va Ejipiti ale Faaro ale wa yenni meena tama nimbie po.

ref: The Lord rescued us from Egypt, so he could bring us into this land, as he had promised our ancestors.
text: Alege wa ta ti a nyini dula kama a jam ayen wa te ti tɛŋ kaai ate wa puulim ale pɛ ale ti kokpieŋsaŋa la.

ref: That's why the Lord our God demands that we obey his laws and worship him with fear and trembling. And if we do, he will protect us and help us be successful.
text: Ase ti dan kpesi tidek a va Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la sinsaŋŋa de meena ase wa ale weeni diila, kula ale chim ti wayɔrisima.>>

ref: So be sure to obey his laws and teachings I am giving you today. The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey (Deuteronomy
text: Dila nyiŋla, ni kpesi nidek a va wieŋa ale sinsaŋŋa ate mi a te ni jinla de la.

ref: When the Lord helps you defeat your enemies, you must destroy them without pity! And don't get trapped into worshiping their gods.
text: Ni ko nuru baai meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a pai te ni la. Ni kan sak jiirim ale ba yaase ni maari a kaab ba bɔgtaŋa ale dila ale chim ka baruk a te ni.

ref: the Lord will force them out of the land. Then you must destroy them without mercy. Don't make any peace treaties with them,
text: Ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaa dan pai ba a nyo ni nisima po ate ni nya pagrim ba zuk ku a magsi kama ayen ni ko ba. Ni kan nye nɔiyeŋ ale ba yaase ni ta jiirim ale ba.

ref: If you do, those people will lead your descendants to worship other gods and to turn their backs on the Lord. That will make him very angry, and he will quickly destroy Israel.
text: ale ba ale basi ate ni bisaŋa a basi mi vaka be ba a kaab bɔgluk yonta, ate Naawen sui a puuri ale ni ate wa ko ni nwuli.

ref: So when you conquer these nations, tear down the altars where they worship their gods. Break up their sacred stones, cut down the poles that they use in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and throw their idols in the fire. The Lord's Chosen People Moses said:
text: Dii ale magsi ni nye bala ale nna: Ni kaasi ba kuŋkuŋtaŋa abe ni ŋɔriŋ ba bɔgluk tintanaŋa, abe ni kaasi Asera nipok bɔglukku abe ni ju ba bɔgtaŋa ale bolim.

ref: Israel, you are the chosen people of the Lord your God. There are many nations on this earth, but he chose only Israel to be his very own.
text: Ale nama ka nuru weleŋsa a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la. Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a lueri ni kama a ta nyini nuruba meena po tɛŋka zuk de ayen wa soa ni ase tuilum nuruba la.

text: Ni a teeri jinla danni ayen daa ni bisaŋa ale jam nya Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la waalika. Wa pagrimu ale wa nisa ale pagra diila, ale wa nisaŋa ale a teeri a tom dii,

ref: when he worked miracles in Egypt, making terrible things happen to the king and all his people.
text: ale wakperikaliisaŋa ate wa tom ale wie ŋaai ate wa tom Ejipiti po ale wa le nye Faaro Ejipiti naawa ale wa tɛŋka meena dii,

ref: And when the Egyptian army chased you in their chariots, you saw the Lord drown them and their horses in the Red Sea. Egypt still suffers from that defeat!
text: wa ale nye Ejipiti tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale ba wusumaŋa ale ŋa torokoma diila, wa jam basi ate ba wari beli Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku po diipo ate ba jam a vi ni la. Ni be nya Naawen ale nye ba diila kama.

ref: You saw what the Lord did for you while you were in the desert, right up to the time you arrived here.
text: Daa ni biisaŋa ale jam nya dii ate wa nye gɔnni po a te ni alege ate nama a jam paari dela jigini la.

ref: And you saw how the Lord made the ground open up in the middle of our camp underneath the tents of Dathan and Abiram, who were swallowed up along with their families, their animals, and their tents.
text: Ni be teeri wa ale jam nye Datan ale Abiram, Eliab bisaŋa ate wa nyini Aruben dɔkku po bisaŋa diila kama. Tɛŋka a jam na kama a lagri ate ba zi du ate ka lik ba ale ba dɔkdemma ale ba viitaŋa ale ŋanvuta meena a basi du.

ref: With your own eyes, you saw the Lord's mighty power do all these things.
text: Ka nidek nina po ate Naawen jam basi ate wakpienni de a nye.

ref: Soon you will cross the Jordan River, and if you obey the laws and teachings I'm giving you today, you will be strong enough to conquer the land
text: Ni be va sinsak ŋaai meena ate mi a te ni jinla de la dii ale ku te ni pagrim ate ni baga a jo tɛŋ kaai ate ni ale lo Jodan benni a jueli a tuesi la,

ref: that the Lord promised your ancestors and their descendants. It's rich with milk and honey, and you will live there and enjoy it for a long time.
text: dii ale ku nye ate ni goa beni tɛŋ kaai po ate Naawen a puulim ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa ayen wa pai a te ba ale ba ŋaaŋbisaŋa la. Siita ale biisim ale bo ka po.

ref: It's better land than you had in Egypt, where you had to struggle just to water your crops.
text: Tɛŋ kaai ate ni a jo ni tuesi la a kan nye ase ka Ejipiti la kauk kuui ate ni basi la, juijui ate ni jam bori ale ji nyiam a zaŋti ase jenvaata talim la.

ref: But the hills and valleys in the promised land are watered by rain from heaven,
text: Alege tɛŋ kaai ate nama a lo Jodan benni a jueli ayen ni tuesi la ka tɛŋ kaai ale ta guuta ale vaasa ate ŋmoruk nyiam a jo ka po.

ref: The Lord your God commands you to love him and to serve him with all your heart and soul. If you obey him,
text: Ni dan chiib va wa sinsaŋŋa ate mi a te ni jinla de la ale a yaali Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la abe ni a va wa ale ni suiniima meena ale ni chiisa meena,

ref: he will send rain at the right seasons, so you will have more than enough food, wine, and olive oil, and there will be plenty of grass for your cattle.
text: Wa le basi ate wuuk a nyini tɛŋka po ate ni duŋsaŋa a dɛ ate nama dek mɛ a dɛ chak.

ref: But watch out! You will be tempted to turn your backs on the Lord. And if you worship other gods,
text: Ni be kpesi nidek ate ni kan basi Naawen abe le va bɔgluk yonta a koori tɛŋ a zuli ti.

ref: the Lord will become angry and keep the rain from falling. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will die and disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
text: Ate Naawen sui a puuri ale ni ate wa basi ate ŋmoruk a kan ni ate ni kan nya ŋandiinta tɛŋka po ate ni kpi nwuli abe ni basi tɛŋ naliŋ kaai ate wa ayen wa pai te ni la.

ref: Memorize these laws and think about them. Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and your foreheads to help you obey them.
text: Ni pai mi wieŋa de a nyo ni suiniimaŋa ale ni popolaŋa po, abe ni bobaŋa a maŋ ni nisaŋa nyiŋ, abe ni pai ŋa a bobi maŋ ni deeŋa nyiŋ.

ref: Teach them to your children. Talk about them all the time—whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning.
text: Ni pai ŋa a sak ni bisaŋa, Ni a biisi ŋa wie ase ni nin diem bo yeri, yaase ni nin bo suik po a cheŋ yaase ni nin doa tɛŋ yaase ni nin yiti goom po.

ref: Write them on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates.
text: Ni ŋmarisiŋa nyo ni yeeŋa tuataŋa nyiŋ ale ni nansuiŋtaŋa meena nyiŋ.

ref: Then you and your descendants will live a long time in the land that the Lord promised your ancestors. Your families will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.
text: Dii ale ku basi ate nama ale ni bisaŋa daaŋa a piisi tɛŋ kaai po ate Naawen pɛ ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa ayen wa pai a te ba la. Ni ale kasim boro ka dila ase diipo meena ate ni zak zuk a nya ale chiŋmaaŋa a diem boro la.

ref: Love the Lord your God faithfully and obey all the laws and teachings I'm giving you today. If you live the way the Lord wants,
text: Ase ni dan chiib a va sinsaŋŋa de meena ate mi a weeni ni la, a yaali Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale a cheŋ wa suitaŋa po ale a va wa nalimnyiini,

ref: he will help you take the land. And even though the nations there are more powerful than you, the Lord will force them to leave when you attack.
text: Naawen ale yiak tɛŋsaŋa de meena nuruma kama a basi a te ni ate nama ale jo bo tɛŋ sii ale zuak ale ŋman pagra a gaam ni la po.

ref: You will capture the land everywhere you go, from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains, and from the Euphrates River west to the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Kauk kuui meena ate nama a pai ni naŋtuok a tabi la ka nama ale soa: Ni tɛŋka ale zuak a ta nyini gɔnni po a ta ga va Lebanon, a ta nyini Yufiretis Benni a ga paari yeniŋ geŋsa nyakpiemu nɔi.

ref: No one will be able to stand up to you. The Lord will make everyone terrified of you, just as he promised.
text: Nuru a kan boro a baga a nye kpaliŋ ale ni. Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ase wa ale puulim dii ale ni la, yɔgsum ale yik tɛŋsaŋa kauk kuui meena ate nama a cheŋ la.

ref: You have a choice—do you want the Lord to bless you, or do you want him to put a curse on you?
text: Ni nya de jinla m pai ka niaka ale kikaasa a dueni ni niŋ.

ref: Today I am giving you his laws, and if you obey him, he will bless you.
text: Nama ale nya niaka ase nama a nin va Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la sinsaŋŋa ate mi a pai a te ni jinla dela;

ref: But if you disobey him and worship those gods that have never done anything for you, the Lord will put a curse on you.
text: Nama abe le nya kikaasa ase nama a nin zɛri Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la sinsaŋŋa ate mi a weeni ayen ni kan ŋmani va bɔgluk yonta tii ate nama a poom zɛ la.

ref: After the Lord your God helps you take the land, you must have a ceremony where you announce his blessings from Mount Gerizim and his curses from Mount Ebal.
text: Ase Naawen dii ale ka nama Wen la ale ta ni a jam tɛŋ kaai po ate ni a jo nna, ku a magsi ayen ni zaani ka Gerizim Guuku zuk a biisi niaka wie abe ni zaani Ebal Guuku zuk mɛ a biisi kikaasa wie.

ref: You know that these two mountains are west of the Jordan River in land now controlled by the Canaanites living in the Jordan River valley. The mountains are west of the road near the sacred trees of Moreh on the other side of Gilgal.
text: Ase nama ale poom seba la, guutaŋa a bo ka Jodan benni ŋmazuk suiku yeniŋ geŋsa kauk kuui ate wenbinni a siŋ la a moata More ti kpieŋsaŋa ale bo Keenan banni la a bo Araba ate ka bo Gilgal po la.

ref: Soon you will cross the Jordan River to conquer the land that the Lord your God is giving you. And when you have settled there,
text: Nama boro ayen ni lo Jodan benni a jueli kama a taam tɛŋ kaai po ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ayen wa pai te ni la. Ase ni dan tuesi ka a bo ka po,

ref: be careful to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
text: ni be seba ayen ni va sinsaŋŋa meena ate mi a weeni jinla de la.

ref: Now I'll tell you the laws and teachings that you have to obey as long as you live. Your ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he is giving you this land.
text: Sinsaŋŋa de ku a magsi ka ni kpesi va ŋa, tɛŋ kaai po ate Naawen dii ale ka ni kokpieŋsaŋa Wen la a te ni ayen ni ta la diipo meena ate nama a diem vua a bo tɛŋka po la.

ref: But the nations that live there worship other gods. So after you capture the land, you must completely destroy their places of worship—on mountains and hills or in the shade of large trees.
text: Ni kaasi nuruma ŋan baai meena ale bo pinaŋa ale guutaŋa zuima ale tiisaŋa kab tii ate ba bɔgtaŋa a boro ate ba a kaab la.

ref: Wherever these nations worship their gods, you must tear down their altars, break their sacred stones, burn the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and smash their idols to pieces. Destroy these places of worship so completely that no one will remember they were ever there.
text: Ni nak ba kuŋkuŋtaŋa a kaasi abe ni saam ba tintanaŋa chaab abe le ju ba bɔgluk kuui ate ba a wi ayen Asera la daataŋa ale bolim. Ni lɔnsi ba bɔgtaŋa tɛŋ ate ti yue a kan ŋman boro.

ref: Don't worship the Lord your God in the way those nations worship their gods.
text: Ni kan puusi Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ba ale a puusi diila.

ref: The Lord has promised that later on he will give Israel more land, and some of you may not be able to travel all the way from your homes to the place of worship each time you are hungry for meat. But the Lord will give you cattle, sheep, and goats, and you can butcher any of those animals at home and eat as much as you want.
text: Ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale lueri kauk kuui ayen ni a nye kaabka la a dan yalima ale ni, ni baga a ko duŋsaŋa ate Naawen a te ni la kama ase mi ale weeni diila. Ni dɛ ni yeeŋa po nama ale baga a dɛ diila.

ref: It is the same as eating the meat from a deer or a gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And in this way, anyone who is unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat.
text: Ni ŋɔbi duŋ sii ate ni a ko la meena ase ni ale a ko gɔi duŋsa diila. Baai ale daŋ la ale baai ale nala la a baga a ŋɔbi kama.

ref: But don't eat the blood. It is the life of the animal, so let it drain out on the ground before you eat the meat.
text: Ni kan dɛ ziimu ni kpiiri bu a basi tɛŋ ase nyiam la.

ref: Do you want the Lord to make you successful? Do you want your children to be successful even after you are gone? Then do what pleases the Lord and don't eat blood.
text: Ni kan dɛ ba ate wari meena ale nye nalimnyiini a te ni ale ni bisaŋa dii nyiŋla ni a yaa ni a nye ka dii ale nala Naawen nimbie po la.

ref: All sacrifices and offerings to the Lord must be taken to the place where he chooses to be worshiped. If you offer a sacrifice to please the Lord, all of its meat must be burned on the altar. You can eat the meat from certain kinds of sacrifices, but you must always pour out the animal's blood on the altar.
text: Ni nye ni juka kaabka Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la kuŋkuŋku zuk. Lammu ale ziimu ni pai ba meena a vi Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la kaabka kuŋkuŋku zuk abe ni ŋɔbi lantaŋa.

ref: If you obey these laws, you will be doing what the Lord your God says is right and good. Then he will help you and your descendants be successful. Worship the Lord in the Right Way Moses said:
text: Ni be chiib kpesi nidek a va wie ŋaai ate mi a te ni la dii ale ku nye ate wari meena a cheŋ nalimnyiini ate nama ale ni bisaŋa ale bo ŋaaŋ la. Dii nyiŋla ni a nye ka dii ale nala la Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la nimbie po.

ref: Israel, as you go into the land and attack the nations that are there, the Lord will get rid of them, and you can have their land.
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la dek ale yik tɛŋ sii ale moata ayen ni jo si po la. Alege ni dan yik ba ate ba nyini ale kali ba tɛŋsaŋa po,

ref: But that's when you must be especially careful not to ask, “How did those nations worship their gods? Shouldn't we worship the Lord in the same way?”
text: ase ni ale kaasi ba a ga nueri la ni be seba ate ni kan bek ayen, <<Tɛŋsaŋa de a nye ka sɛ a kaab ba bɔgtaŋa? Tama mɛ ale nye ka dila.>>

ref: Obey all the laws and teachings I am giving you. Don't add any, and don't take any away.
text: Ni nye dii meena ate mi a weeni la. Ni kan yaali wari a gum du yaase ni yeeri wari a basi.

ref: Someday a prophet may come along who is able to perform miracles or tell what will happen in the future. Then the prophet may say, “Let's start worshiping some new gods—some gods that we know nothing about.”
text: ate wakperikaliika yaase wakinkagli dii ate wa biisi di wie la a nye ate wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni basi ate ti va bɔgluk yonta.>> <<Abe ni basi ate ti a puusi ti.>>

ref: If the prophet says this, don't listen! The Lord your God will be watching to find out whether or not you love him with all your heart and soul.
text: Ku kan magsi ayen ni wom wie ŋaai ate biisiteerɔwa yaase gɔdaasima nyɔnɔwa de a biisi la. Ka Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale a nye ni a nya ase ni a yaali wa ale ni suiniima meena ale ni chiisa meena ya.

ref: You must be completely faithful to the Lord. Worship and obey only the Lord and do this with fear and trembling,
text: Ka Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale la ni va wa abe ni a puusi wa abe ni ta wa sinsaŋŋa nalimnyiini, abe ni tom a te wa abe ni yik wa giŋgiŋ.

ref: After the Lord your God gives you towns to live in, you may hear a rumor about one of the towns.
text: Ase ni dan wom ayen tɛŋ sii ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a pai a te ni ayen ni boro la,

ref: You may hear that some worthless people have talked everyone there into worshiping other gods, even though these gods had never done anything for them.
text: ayen gaasa nyam ale bo ni po a yaa ba ta nuruma tɛŋka po a cheŋ bɛ. Ba le weeni ayen, <<Ni basi ate ti cheŋ a ga kaab bɔgluk yonta.>> ,

ref: You must carefully find out if the rumor is true. Then if the people of that town have actually done such a disgusting thing in your own country,
text: ku a magsi kama ayen ni kpesi a gisi nya nalimnyiini. Ku be dan ka wensie ayen biemu de a bo ni suŋsuŋ,

ref: you must take your swords and kill every one of them, and their livestock too.
text: ku a magsi kama ayen ni ko bala meena ale ba duŋsaŋa meena tɛŋka po.

ref: Gather all the possessions of the people who lived there, and pile them up in the marketplace, without keeping anything for yourself. Set the pile and the whole town on fire, and don't ever rebuild the town. The whole town will be a sacrifice to the Lord your God. Then he won't be angry anymore, and he will have mercy on you and make your nation stronger, just as he promised your ancestors.
text: Ni kan pai ŋan baai ate Naawen ayen ni kaasi ba la a tanla, dii ale ku basi ate wa a basi wa suipuurumu abe wa ta jiirim ale ni la. Wa ale ta jiirim ale ni abe wa basi ate ni piisi ase wa ale puulim ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa la,

ref: That's why you must do what the Lord your God says is right. I am giving you his laws and teachings today, and you must obey them.
text: dii nyiŋla nama va Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la kama ale ta wa wieŋa ate mi a te ni jinla de la ale dii ale nala wa nimbie po la.

ref: Out of all the nations on this earth, the Lord your God chose you to be his own. You belong to the Lord, so don't behave like those who worship other gods. Animals That Can Be Eaten (Leviticus
text: ale nama ka nuru weleŋsa a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la. A ta nyini nuruba meena po tɛŋka de zuk, Naawen a lueri ka nama ayen ni chim wa nuruba.

ref: You can eat any clean bird.
text: Ni baga a ŋɔbi ja yirim buui ale nala la kama.

ref: It is all right to eat meat from any animals that have divided hoofs and also chew the cud.
text: Ni baga a ŋɔbi duŋ sii meena ale ta naŋsaba ŋaai ale poori alege a ŋɔbi a guli la kama.

ref: But don't eat camels, rabbits, and rock badgers. These animals chew the cud but do not have divided hoofs. You must treat them as unclean.
text: Ni kan ni ŋɔbi duŋ yonsa. Ni a ŋɔbi sii ale ta naŋsaba ate ŋa poori ale a ŋɔbi a guli la nyiini. Ni kaa ŋɔbi laalaakomi ale suem ale siseri ya. Duŋsaŋa de a ŋɔbi a guli kama alege si ka naŋsaba; si ka duŋ daŋtisa a te ni.

ref: And don't eat pork, since pigs have divided hoofs, but they do not chew their cud. Don't even touch a dead pig!
text: Deri mɛ daŋ kama; di ta naŋsaba ate ŋa poori alege di kan ŋɔbi a guli. Ni kaa ŋɔbi di lammu yaase ni tiri deri dii ale kpi la.

ref: You can eat any fish that has fins and scales. But there are other creatures that live in the water,
text: Ŋan baai meena ale bo nyiam po a ta pie ale pagta la ni baga a ŋɔbi kama.

ref: and if they do not have fins and scales, you must not eat them. Treat them as unclean.
text: Alege jabuui ale kan ta pie ale pagta la ni kan ŋɔbi ba ale ba ka ŋan baai ale daŋ la.

ref: Swarming insects are unclean, so don't eat them.
text: Ŋan yirin tii ale a nye ase nanjuŋsa la daŋ kama ni kan ŋɔbi ba.

ref: However, you are allowed to eat certain kinds of winged insects.
text: Alege jabuui meena ale ta kinkaŋŋa ale nala la ni a ŋɔbi.

ref: You belong to the Lord your God, so if you happen to find a dead animal, don't eat its meat. You may give it to foreigners who live in your town or sell it to foreigners who are visiting your town. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. Give the Lord Ten Percent of Your Harvest Moses said:
text: Ni kan ŋɔbi ja kpiuwa. Ni baga a pai ja kpiuku a te nichamma ale bo ni tɛŋsaŋa po la kama ate bala a ŋɔbi yaase nama baga a pai ja kpiuku kama a da a te nichamma. Nama ka nuru weleŋsa Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la jigi. Ni be kan dik buli ale ku ma biisimɔ.

ref: People of Israel, every year you must set aside ten percent of your grain harvest.
text: Ni teeri ate ni poori benni po ate ni kpa nya ŋan baai ni talitaŋa po la piika a zaani nakpiak.

ref: Also set aside ten percent of your wine and olive oil, and the first-born of every cow, sheep, and goat. Take these to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, and eat them there. This will teach you to always respect the Lord your God.
text: Ni dɛ ni kpanni ŋantaŋa piika po, da paalimu ale kpaamu ale ni duŋsaŋa ale dɛ niŋ a biak biik sii la Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋ kauk kuui ate wa lueri a te ni ayen ni boro wa yuenni nyiŋla. Dila ale ku basi ate ni a va Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la nalimnyiini.

ref: But suppose you can't carry that ten percent of your harvest to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. If you live too far away, or if the Lord gives you a big harvest,
text: Alege dula jigini a dan yalima, ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale niak ni la, ni dan kan baga a ji ni piika a ta a cheŋ dula dii nyiŋla Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale a yaali wa lueri juijui la ale yalima la nyiŋ,

ref: When you and your family arrive, spend the money on food for a big celebration. Buy cattle, sheep, goats, wine, beer, and if there are any other kinds of food that you want, buy those too.
text: Ni pai ligraŋa a da jabuui ate ni a yaali la: ni da ase ka niiga, piisa ale daam ale da buui ale kum la ale ŋan baai ate nama a yaali la. Nama ale ni yeeŋa demma a dɛ Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋ ale suipeentik.

ref: And since people of the Levi tribe won't own any land for growing crops, remember to ask the Levites to celebrate with you.
text: Ni be kan baŋ Livaima ale bo ni tɛŋka po la wari ya, ale ba ka badek tɛŋa yaase jaaboa.

ref: Every third year, instead of using the ten percent of your harvest for a big celebration, bring it into town and put it in a community storehouse.
text: Bena ŋata meena kpeglim ka po, ni piisaŋa meena ate ni kpa nya la ni ta jam dueni ni tɛŋsaŋa po,

ref: The Levites have no land of their own, so you must give them food from the storehouse. You must also give food to the poor who live in your town, including orphans, widows, and foreigners. If they have enough to eat, then the Lord your God will be pleased and make you successful in everything you do.
text: dii ale ku basi ate Livaima ale nichamma ale kpiŋsaŋa ale pukɔŋŋa baai ale bo ni tɛŋsaŋa po la a jam dɛ chak ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a niak ni nisima tuima meena.

ref: After the Lord your God gives land to each of you, there may be poor Israelites in the town where you live. If there are, then don't be mean and selfish with your money.
text: Ase nuru jak a dan bo ni suataŋa tɛŋka kanyi po, kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaa wa te ni la, ni be kan nye suinum pagrik a ta va ni mabiik jakka de jigiya.

ref: Every seven years you must announce, “The Lord says loans do not need to be paid back.” Then if you have loaned money to another Israelite, you can no longer ask for payment.
text: Fi le magsi fi nye diila ale nna: waai meena ate ba dɛ wa pami la a baŋ wa ale pai dii a te wa Izirali denɔ choawa la. Wa kan ŋman a yiili ayen Izirali yaase wa mabiika ale tuni wa pamini dii nyiŋla Naawen ale te diipo ayen waai a kan ŋman tuesi pami la a paari kama.

ref: This law applies only to loans you have made to other Israelites. Foreigners will still have to pay back what you have loaned them.
text: Fi baga a bek nichamma baai ale ta fi pama la kama alege fi baŋ fi mabisaŋa ale ta fi pamaŋa la wari.

ref: No one in Israel should ever be poor. The Lord your God is giving you this land, and he has promised to make you very successful, if you obey his laws and teachings that I'm giving you today. You will lend money to many nations, but you won't have to borrow. You will rule many nations, but they won't rule you.
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale niak ni kama ase wa ale puulim diila ate nama ale te tɛŋsa yegayega ŋanta abe ni kan tuesi jaab a ta nyini si jigi ya. Nama ale ta pagrim tɛŋsa yega zuk alege si kan ta pagrim nama zuwa.

ref: Instead, be kind and lend them what they need.
text: Ni laari ni nisimaŋa ate ni suoku jajakka de jabuui ate wa a yaali la.

ref: Be careful! Don't say to yourself, “Soon it will be the seventh year, and then I won't be able to get my money back.” It would be horrible for you to think that way and to be so selfish that you refuse to help the poor. They are your relatives, and if you don't help them, they may ask the Lord to decide whether you have done wrong. And he will say that you are guilty.
text: Ni be kan zɛri ayen nama a kan te ba jaaboa, dii nyiŋla diipo ate ni zɛri pama tuesika la moata nyiŋŋa. Ni kan basi ate biem wieŋa de a bo ni popolaŋa po. Ni dan zɛri an te wa jaaboa, wa le kaari a te Naawen ate ni nya ni le nye kaasi la.

ref: You should be happy to give the poor what they need, because then the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
text: Te wa ale suipeentik kan nye butuemmoa ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale niak ni tuima ale dii meena ate ni pai ni nisima a nye la.

ref: But if the animal is lame or blind or has something else wrong with it, you must not sacrifice it to the Lord your God.
text: Ase duŋ kaai a dan kɔni, yaase ka gbariŋ yaase ka yi ni kan pai kala choa a nye kaabka a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la.

ref: And don't just tell them they are free to leave—
text: Ase ni dan a yaali ni basi wa ni kan basi wa kinla, ni te wa ŋanta.

ref: give them sheep and goats and a good supply of grain and wine. The more the Lord has given you, the more you should give them.
text: Ni te wa a ta nyini Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale niak ni ale ŋan baai la. Ni te wa piisa ale zaa ale damasik.

ref: But one of your slaves may say, “I love you and your family, and I would be better off staying with you, so please don't make me leave.”
text: Alege ni tomteerɔma a dan weeni ayen, <<Mi a kan yaali m basi ni.>> Wa ale a yaali fi ale fi dɔkdemma la nyiŋ ate ku a cheŋ nalimnyiini ale fu,

ref: Take the slave to the door of your house and push a sharp metal rod through one earlobe and into the door. Such slaves will belong to you for life, whether they are men or women.
text: ta wa a nyini peelim a vuri wa tueŋa ate wa yaa ale chim fi tomteerɔ taam wuu. Nye nipok baai ale tom a te fu la mɛ dila dekdega.

ref: If the first-born animal of a cow or sheep or goat is a male, it must be given to the Lord. Don't put first-born cattle to work or cut wool from first-born sheep.
text: Ni duŋsaŋa ale dɛ niŋ a biak ŋandoa tii la ni pai a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la. Ni kan basi ate naab bula a tom tuini yaase piisaŋa ale dɛ niŋ a biak ŋaai la ni kan che ŋa kɔbtaŋa.

ref: Instead, each year you must take the first-born of these animals to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped. You and your family will sacrifice them to the Lord and then eat them as part of a sacred meal.
text: Bein meena nama ale ni dɔkdemma a magsi kama ayen ni ko ŋa a ŋɔbi Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋ wa le lueri kauk kuui a te ni la.

ref: You can butcher it where you live, and eat it just like the meat of a deer or gazelle that you kill while hunting. Even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some.
text: Ku a magsi ni ŋɔbi kala ka ni yeeŋa. Baai ale daŋ la ale baai ale nala la a baga a ŋɔbi kama ase ba ale a ŋɔbi gɔi duŋsa diila.

ref: But you must never eat the blood of an animal—let it drain out on the ground.
text: Alege ni kan dɛ ziimoa; ni kpiiri bu a basi tɛŋ ase nyiam la.

ref: People of Israel, you must celebrate Passover in the month of Abib, because one night in that month years ago, the Lord your God rescued you from Egypt.
text: Ni be a teeri Abib Chiika ate ni a dɛ Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la Gaambasika tigini, dii nyiŋla ka Abib Chiika po ate wa ta ni a nyini Ejipiti po a nyini yok.

ref: People of Israel, if you want to enjoy a long and successful life, make sure that everyone is treated with justice in the land the Lord is giving you. Don't Set Up Sacred Poles or Stones Moses said to Israel:
text: Ni va wensie ale ka wensie nyiini ale ŋa basi ate ni vua ate nama ale baga a tuesi tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a za wa pai a te ni la.

ref: Eat thin bread for the next six days. Then on the seventh day, don't do any work. Instead, come together and worship the Lord. The Harvest Festival (Exodus
text: Ni ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ate dabinta a ka ku po la a ta ga paari daa ŋayuebi alege dai dii ale a saari ŋayopɔiwa la ni tigsi chaab a puusi Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la. Ni kan tom tuini dai dila danni.

ref: The Passover sacrifice must be a cow, a sheep, or a goat, and you must offer it at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped.
text: Ni be cheŋ kauk kuui ate Naawen a lueri ayen ni a puusi wa la, a tɔgri duŋka dula jigini a nye kaabka ase Gaambasika la te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la.

ref: It must be offered at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Kill the sacrifice at sunset, the time of day when you left Egypt.
text: Ku a magsi ni nye Gaambasika Tigini kaabka kauk kuui ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a lueri ayen ni puusi wa la. Ku magsi ni nye kaabka ka junɔi ase diipo ate nama a jam basi Ejipiti tɛŋka la.

ref: Then cook it and eat it there at the place of worship, returning to your tents the next morning.
text: Ni be sɛ abe ni ŋɔbi bu kauk kuui ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a lueri ayen ni a puusi wa la, abe ni yaa ŋmani kuli ni yeeŋa chum saluik.

ref: And don't set up a sacred stone! The Lord hates these things.
