text: Abe ni kan feri tintain bɔgluk a zaani a kaabi ku, Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a kisa ŋala kama.

ref: After you have finished the grain harvest and the grape harvest, take your sons and daughters and all your servants to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. The Lord will give you big harvests and make you successful in everything you do. You will be completely happy, so celebrate this festival in honor of the Lord your God. Three Festivals at the Place of Worship (Exodus
text: Ni pai daa ŋayopɔi a nye tigini a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la juijui ate Naawen lueri ayen ni a puusi wa la. Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la dek ale niak ni kpanni ŋantaŋa ale ni ale pai ni nisima a tom tuin dii meena la ate ni sue ale kasim a peenti meena.

ref: When you build the altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God, don't set up a sacred pole for the worship of the goddess Asherah.
text: Ase ni dan sɛ Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la puusika kuŋkuŋku, ni kan ŋman sɛ nipok bɔglukku ate ba a wi ku ayen Asera la a kaab ku.

ref: go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped and celebrate the Harvest Festival in honor of the Lord your God. Bring him an offering as large as you can afford, depending on how big a harvest he has given you. Be sure to take along your sons and daughters and all your servants. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
text: Nama ale ni nidoabilisaŋa ale ni liema ale ni tomteerɔ nidoaba ale nipooba ale Livaima ale nichamma ale bo ni tɛŋsaŋa po la ale kpiŋsaŋa ale pukɔŋŋa meena a nye Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la jiam kauk kuui ate wa lueri ayen ni a puusi wa la.

ref: The bigger the harvest the Lord gives you, the bigger your gift should be. Treat Everyone with Justice Moses said to Israel:
text: Waai meena a ta tiirim a jam a magsi chaab ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale niak wa diila.

ref: Each year there are three festivals when all Israelite men must go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. These are the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters. And don't forget to take along a gift for the Lord.
text: Nidoama meena a jam Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋ naŋtuok nɔi buta bein po juijui ate wa lueri a magsi Boroborok Kuui Ale Kan Ta Dabinta Tigini, ale Bakoa Tigini, ale Viita Tigini la. Nuru waai a kan jam Naawen niŋ ale ni koruta.

ref: If an ox or a sheep has something wrong with it, don't offer it as a sacrifice to the Lord your God—he will be disgusted! Put To Death People Who Worship Idols Moses said to Israel:
text: Ni kan nye kaabka a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale naab buui yaase posuk kuui ale kɔni ya. Naawen a kisi dila kama.

ref: So when you hear that someone in your town is committing this disgusting sin, you must carefully find out if that person really is guilty.
text: ate ni dan ga miŋ dila, ni ŋmasi a gisi di po a nya dan ka wensie ayen kisukku de choa a sum nye kama Izirali tɛŋka po,

ref: But you will need two or three witnesses—one witness isn't enough to prove a person guilty. Get rid of those who are guilty of such evil. Take them outside your town gates and everyone must stone them to death. But the witnesses must be the first to throw stones. Difficult Cases Moses said to Israel:
text: Baai ale weeni ayen wanni ka wensie la ale magsi ba dɛ niŋ a yuk nuruwa ale tintana abe ba ge suik ate waai meena a yuk wa a ko. Ku a magsi kama ayen ni basi ate biemu de a nyini ni po a nyini.

ref: When other Israelites hear about it, they will be afraid and obey the decisions of the court. The King Moses said:
text: Nuruma meena ale wom ate ba a chali yɔgsum, ate waai a kan ŋman nye wa dila choa.

ref: People of Israel, after you capture the land the Lord your God is giving you, and after you settle on it, you will say, “We want a king, just like the nations around us.”
text: Ase ni yaa dan jo tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaa wa pai te ni la a tuesi nueri a yaa kala ka po, ate ni yaa weeni ayen, <<Ti lueri naab ate wa a nya ti zuk ase tɛŋ sii ale kala a gilim ti la ale ta nalima diila.>>

ref: Go ahead and appoint a king, but make sure that he is an Israelite and that he is the one the Lord has chosen.
text: Ni be lueri naab waai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a lueri la. Wa magsi wa nyini ka nidek suataŋa po. Ni kan basi ate nichaanɔ a nya ni zuwa.

ref: And the king must not have a lot of wives—they might tempt him to be unfaithful to the Lord. Finally, the king must not try to get huge amounts of silver and gold.
text: Wa be kan faari nipok boari ya. Wa dan nye dila wa suinummu a kan ŋman bo ale Naawen yaa. Wa be kan tuesi kpana ale ligmɔniŋ yegayega mɛ.

ref: The official copy of God's laws will be kept by the priests of the Levi tribe. So, as soon as anyone becomes king, he must go to the priests and write out a copy of these laws while they watch.
text: Ase wa yaa a dan chim naab a ga nueri, ku magsi kama ayen wa ta Naawen sinsaŋŋa gbaŋka kanyi piilimka po sinsaŋŋa ate kaabteerɔma baai ale ka Livaima a ŋmarisi la.

ref: Each day the king must read and obey these laws, so that he will learn to worship the Lord with fear and trembling
text: Ku a magsi ka kasim a bo ale wa kama ate wa kasim a kariŋ ka diipo meena ate wa diem vua la dii ale ku nye ate wa a zuli Naawen dii ale ka wa Wen la abe wa a va wa wieŋa nalimnyiini la,

ref: and not think that he's better than everyone else. If the king completely obeys the Lord's commands, he and his descendants will rule Israel for many years.
text: abe wa kan wa a nya wadek ase wa zunchoŋŋa ka waai la abe wa kan viriŋ wa gala yaase wa juga ate wa ale wa buuni po ale kasim a dɛ naam Izirali tɛŋka po ate ku beni.

ref: So when I want to speak to them, I will choose one of them to be a prophet like you. I will give my message to that prophet, who will tell the people exactly what I have said.
text: M le te ba ka biisiteerɔ a nyini badek suataŋa po ase fi la, m le pai m wieŋa a nyo wa nɔnni po ate wa ale weeni ba m sinsaŋŋa ate mi a te wa la.

ref: Some Levites may have money from selling family possessions, and others may not. But all Levites serving at the place of worship will receive the same amount of food from the sacrifices and gifts brought by the people. Don't Do Disgusting Things Moses said to Israel:
text: Wa ale kaabteerɔma a magsi ba dɛ a soa si ka chaab la a gum wa dɔkdemma ŋan baai ate wa pai da ligra la po.

ref: The people of the Levi tribe, including the priests, will not receive any land. Instead, they will receive part of the sacrifices that are offered to the Lord,
text: Kaabteerɔma, baai ale ka Livaima la an magsi ayen ba ta ba dek tɛŋ Izirali tɛŋka po. Livai dɔkku meena an magsi ba poom ta jaaboa. Ku a magsi ba soa ka ŋan baai ate ba pai a nye juka kaabka a te Naawen la.

ref: because he has promised to provide for them in this way.
text: Ba an magsi ba ta tɛŋ ba suataŋa jigi ya; Naawen ale ba ŋantaŋa ase wa ale puulim ba la.

ref: When you sacrifice a bull or sheep, the priests will be given the shoulder, the jaws, and the stomach.
text: Diipo meena ni dan nye kaabka ale naab yaase posuk ku a magsi kama ayen ni te kaabteerɔwa ka bɔŋŋa ale tapayaasaŋa ale puuka.

ref: In addition, they will receive the first part of your grain harvest and part of your first batches of wine and olive oil. You must also give them the first wool that is cut from your sheep each year.
text: Ni te ba ni kpanni ŋan baai ale liŋ a bɛ la ni zaaŋa ale da paalimu ale kpaamu ale ni ale dɛ niŋ a che ni piisaŋa kob tii la,

ref: Give these gifts to the priests, because the Lord has chosen them and their descendants out of all the tribes of Israel to be his special servants at the place of worship.
text: ale ka Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale lueri ba ale ba ŋaaŋbisaŋa a ta nyini ni dɔkku po ayen ba zaani a biisi a te Naawen yuenni nyiŋ diipo meena.

ref: Any Levite can leave his hometown, and go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped,
text: Ase Livai denɔ a dan basi wa le bo juijui la ale jam juijui ate Naawen ale lueri ayen ni a puusi wa la,

ref: and then be a special servant of the Lord there, just like all the other Levites.
text: wa ale biisi kama wa Naawen dii ale ka wa Naawen la yuenni nyiŋ ase wa vaanchaab mbala Livaima ale a nye dii Naawen nyiŋla.

ref: Soon you will go into the land that the Lord your God is giving you. The nations that live there do things that are disgusting to the Lord, and you must not follow their example.
text: Ase ni dan jo tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaa wa te ni la, ni kan ni tomsi ba a nye kisita wie ŋaai ate Naawen a kisa alege ate tɛŋ sila a nye la.

ref: Don't sacrifice your son or daughter. And don't try to use any kind of magic or witchcraft to tell fortunes or to cast spells or to talk with spirits of the dead.
text: yaase waai a paasi nuruba, yaase waai a porisi yaase waai a wi chichirisa yaase waai a biisi ale baai ale kpi la.

ref: The Lord is disgusted with anyone who does these things, and that's why he will help you destroy the nations that are in the land.
text: Waai abe a nye wieŋa de la Naawen a kisa ŋa kama. Be ka kisita wieŋa de nyiŋ ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yiak tɛŋsaŋa de meena a basi a te ni la.

ref: Never be guilty of doing any of these disgusting things! A Prophet like Moses Moses said to Israel:
text: Ni kan ta nye kaasuŋ Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋŋa.

ref: You will go in and take the land from nations that practice magic and witchcraft. But the Lord your God won't allow you to do those things.
text: Tɛŋ sii po ate ni za ni tuesi la nuruba ale a va sampoporinni ale sakpaŋni wie. Alege Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a kan yaali ni a nye di la.

ref: Instead, he will choose one of your own people to be a prophet just like me, and you must do what that prophet says.
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale te ni biisiteerɔ ase mi la a ta nyini nidek suataŋa po. Ku a fɛ kama ayen ni a wom wa.

ref: You were asking for a prophet the day you were gathered at Mount Sinai and said to the Lord, “Please don't let us hear your voice or see this terrible fire again—if we do, we will die!”
text: Dii ate ni jam a bek Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la diipo ate ni jam tigsi chaab Yoreb guuku zuk a weeni ayen, <<Mi kan basi ate ti wom Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la lueluku yaase ti nya bolim kpiemu, kan daa di ti ale kpi.

ref: Then the Lord told me: Moses, they have said the right thing.
text: Ate Naawen a yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Ba ale weeni diila a nala kama.

ref: Since the message comes from me, anyone who doesn't obey the message will have to answer to me.
text: Ase nuru waai a dan kan wom m wieŋa ate biisiteerɔwa a biisi m yuenni nyiŋla, m dek ale te wa waalika.

ref: But if I haven't spoken, and a prophet claims to have a message from me, you must kill that prophet, and you must also kill any prophet who claims to have a message from another god. Moses said to Israel:
text: Alege biisiteerɔ waai ale a pai mi yuenni nyiŋ a biisi dii ate mi an weeni wa ayen wa biisi la yaase biisiteerɔ waai ale a biisi bɔgluk yonta yuei nyiŋla, a za wa kpi kama.

ref: You may be asking yourselves, “How can we tell if a prophet's message really comes from the Lord?”
text: Da dii dai ni ale bek nidek ayen, <<Tama ale nye ka sɛ a seba ayen wanni de daa Naawen ale biisi ya?

ref: You will know, because if the Lord says something will happen, it will happen. And if it doesn't, you will know that the prophet was falsely claiming to speak for the Lord. Don't be afraid of any prophet whose message doesn't come from the Lord.
text: Ase biisiteerɔwa a dan biisi wari Naawen yuenni nyiŋ alege ate wanni an nye ya di ka wa dii ate Naawen an biisi ya. Nuru wala a biisi ka wadek wie. Ni kan chali wa yɔgsum.

ref: Israel, the Lord your God has promised that if you obey his laws and teachings I'm giving you, and if you always love him, then he will give you the land he promised your ancestors. When that happens, you must name three more Safe Towns in the new territory.
text: dii nyiŋla ni ale chiibi a va sinsaŋŋa ate mi a weeni ni jinla de ayen ni a yaali Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la abe ni a va wa suitaŋa meena nyiŋ, ni bɛ ŋman lueri tɛŋsa sita a gum du.

ref: Soon you will go into the land and attack the nations. The Lord your God will destroy them and give you their lands, towns, and homes. Then after you are settled,
text: Ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a dan ko nuruma baai tɛŋka ate wa pai a te ni la, ale yiak ba ate ba nyini ni yaa le kali ba tɛŋsaŋa ale ba yeeŋa po.

ref: you must choose three of your towns to be Safe Towns. Divide the land into three regions with one Safe Town near the middle of each, so that a Safe Town can be easily reached from anywhere in your land. Then, if one of you accidentally kills someone, you can run to a Safe Town and find protection from being put to death. But you must not have been angry with the person you killed.
text: Suiku ale nna ase waai a dan kan potim seba ale ko nuru ale chali a cheŋ dula wa vari wa nyuvunni a basi la. Waai a dan kan seba alege ko wa vaanchoa ale ge ku nyɔnɔwa a daa wa dachiaga wa baga a chali a cheŋ tɛŋ sila kanyi kama.

ref: For example, suppose you and a friend go into the forest to cut wood. You are chopping down a tree with an ax, when the ax head slips off the handle, hits your friend, and kills him. You can run to one of the Safe Towns and save your life.
text: Ase nuruba baye a dan cheŋ gɔi ba che daata, ase wa ale boro a che la liaka a ga nak nuruwa a ko, nuru wala a baga a chali a cheŋ tɛŋsaŋa de kanyi po kama a suk a vari wa nyuvunni a basi.

ref: You don't deserve to die, since you did not mean to harm your friend. But he did get killed, and his relatives might be very angry. They might even choose one of the men from their family to track you down and kill you. If it is too far to one of the Safe Towns, the victim's relative might be able to catch you and kill you.
text: Dan kan daa di kotundɔwa ale vi waai ale kan seba ale ko la ale suipuurum, a paari wa, diila suiku a wɔŋa kama, a ko wa, alege ku an poom magsi ayen wa kpi, wa le kan poom kisi wa kama a nyini daam la.

ref: That's why I said there must be three Safe Towns.
text: Dila nyiŋ ate mi a weeni ayen ni lueri tɛŋsa sita a te nidek la.

ref: You will need them, so innocent people won't be killed on your land while they are trying to reach a Safe Town that is too far away. You will be guilty of murder, if innocent people lose their lives because you didn't name enough Safe Towns in the land the Lord your God will give you.
text: Ni nye di la ate nuru baai ale kan nye wari la a kpi ni tɛŋka po, kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaa wa pai a te ni la, ate ku kan daani ni ale ko ba la nyiŋŋa.

ref: But what if you really do commit murder? Suppose one of you hates a neighbor. So you wait in a deserted place, kill the neighbor, and run to a Safe Town.
text: Alege nuru a dan kisa wa vaanchoa a magi a nak wa a ko ale chali cheŋ tɛŋsaŋa de kanyi,

ref: If that happens, the leaders of your town must send messengers to bring you back from the Safe Town. They will hand you over to one of the victim's relatives, who will put you to death.
text: waai ate wa ko la tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma a tom ate ba ta wa jam ate kotundɔwa a ko wa.

ref: Israel, for the good of the whole country, you must kill anyone who murders an innocent person. Never show mercy to a murderer! Property Lines Moses said to Israel:
text: Ni kan sak jiirim ale wa. Ni yeeri biem bula a ta nyini ni po a nyini ate ni kaa ko nuru baai ale kan nye wari la, ate wari meena ale nye niak a te ni.

ref: In the land the Lord is giving you, there are already stones set up to mark the property lines between fields. So don't move those stones. Witnesses Must Tell the Truth Moses said to Israel:
text: Kan voori fi vaanchoawa tɛŋka tintain dii ate ni koma a feri ate di a sak ni ni tɛŋsaŋa banaŋa ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a te ayen ni ta la.

ref: Before you are convicted of a crime, at least two witnesses must be able to testify that you did it.
text: Nuru yeŋ nyiini a kan baga a weeni ayen nuru a kaasi wari ya. Ka nuruba a nin paari baye yaase bata a weeni ayen nuruwa a nye kaasi kama.

ref: If you accuse someone of a crime, but seem to be lying,
text: Ase waai a da a yaali wa daani waai a yaa velim a te wa,

ref: then both you and the accused must be taken to the court at the place where the Lord is worshiped. There the priests and judges will find out if you are lying or telling the truth. If you are lying and the accused is innocent,
text: Boteerɔma a magsi kama ayen ba ŋmasi kpesi nya wanni po ase waai ale weeni wanni la ka velimvendik, a yaa wa velim a te wa vaanchoawa,

ref: then you will be punished without mercy. You will receive the same punishment the accused would have received if found guilty, whether it means losing an eye, a tooth, a hand, a foot, or even your life. Israel, the crime of telling lies in court must be punished. And when people hear what happens to witnesses that lie, everyone else who testifies in court will tell the truth.
text: Ni kan sak jiirimmoa. Waai a dan ko nuru ba le ko wa mɛ a tuni. Waai a dan yeeri nuru num ba le yeeri wa mɛ num a tuni. Waai abe dan voori waai nyin ba le voori wa mɛ nyiini a tuni. Waai mɛ abe dan gebi nuru nisa ba le gebi wa mɛ nisaŋa. Waai a dan gebi nuru naŋ ba le gebi wa mɛ naŋka a tuni.

ref: If you have to go to war, you may find yourselves facing an enemy army that is bigger than yours and that has horses and chariots. But don't be afraid! The Lord your God rescued you from Egypt, and he will help you fight.
text: Ase ni dan cheŋ kpaliŋ ate ni nya ale ni dachaasaŋa a ta wusuma ate ba tugurik tɔŋdɔma mɛ a piisi a gaam nama ale ka diila ni kan chali yɔgsummoa, dii nyiŋla Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la dii ale ta ni nyini Ejipiti nyini la a bo le ni kama.

ref: Before you march into battle, a priest will go to the front of the army
text: Ni daa yaali ni cheŋ kpaliŋ, kaabteerɔwa ale magsi wa jam niŋ a weeni dii ale magsi ni nye la.

ref: and say, “Soldiers of Israel, listen to me! Today when you go into battle, don't be afraid of the enemy, and when you see them, don't panic.
text: Wa le weeni ayen, <<Ni wom Izirali demma, jinla danni ni a cheŋ ni ga nye ka kpaliŋ ale ni dachaasaŋa. Ni kan chali yaase ni a chali yɔgsummoa; ni kan basi ate yɔgsum nye ate ni nyiŋsaŋa a gɔgi.

ref: Then the tribal officials will say to the troops: If any of you have built a new house, but haven't yet moved in, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to live in your new house.
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaŋŋa ale bek ayen, <<Waai ale sɛ yie paali a kan pai di a nyo Naawen nisima po? Basi ate wa kuli yeri dai dii dai wa le kpi kama kpaliŋka po ate waai ale pai di nyo Naawen nisima po.

ref: If any of you have planted a vineyard but haven't had your first grape harvest, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to enjoy your grapes.
text: Waai a boro a ta wa kaduk ale kan dɛ ka ŋanta? Basi ate wa kuli yeri dai dii dai wa le kpi ka kpaliŋ po alege ate waai a dɛ wa kadukka ŋantaŋa.

ref: If any of you are engaged to be married, you may go back home and get married. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to marry the woman you are engaged to.
text: Nuru a baga a puulim ale nipok ayen wa ale faari wa alege an faari wa, wa le kpi ka kpaliŋ po ate nuru yoŋ faari wa.

ref: Finally, if any of you are afraid, you may go home. We don't want you to discourage the other soldiers.
text: Ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaŋŋa mɛ ale weeni gum du ayen, <<Nuru a boro a chali yɔgsummoa? Ni basi ate wa kuli yeri ate wa suataŋa mɛ a kan chali yɔgsummoa.>>

ref: When the officials are finished giving these orders, they will appoint officers to be in command of the army.
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaŋŋa a dan biisi ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma a ga nueri, ba yaa le lueri nuruba ate bala ale dɛ ba niŋ.

ref: Whenever you capture towns in the land the Lord your God is giving you, be sure to kill all the people and animals.
text: Alege tɛŋ sii ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale pai te ate ni bo si po la, ni ko ŋanvutaŋa meena.

ref: He has commanded you to completely wipe out the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
text: Ni ko nuruma meena: Yit demma ale Amori demma ale Keenan demma ale Perizzi demma ale Yivi demma ale Jebus demma ni ko ba meena ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale weeni ayen ni nye diila.

ref: If you allow them to live, they will persuade you to worship their disgusting gods, and you will be unfaithful to the Lord.
text: Ni dan kan nye dila ba le sak ni kama ate nama mɛ maara a tom biem tuima ŋaai ate ba a nye la, a maara a kaab bɔgta. Dila abe basi kama ate ni tom a kaasi Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la.

ref: When you are attacking a town, don't chop down its fruit trees, not even if you have had the town surrounded for a long time. Fruit trees aren't your enemies, and they produce food that you can eat, so don't cut them down.
text: Ase ni dan boro a nye kpaliŋ ale tɛŋ kaai ate ku beni ni kan che tiisaŋa a lɔnsi ale liaga. Dii nyiŋla ni baga a dɛ si yɔnaŋa kama. Ni kan che si a lɔnsi. Tiisaŋa daa ni dachaasaŋa.

ref: You may need wood to make ladders and towers to help you get over the walls and capture the town. But use only trees that you know are not fruit trees.
text: Alege ni baga a che ti sii ale kan ta yɔna ate ni a dɛ la kama a nye ŋanta a nak parisaŋa a wɛ a ta ga paari diipo ate nama ale nak a yik ba la.

ref: Suppose the body of a murder victim is found in a field in the land the Lord your God is giving you, and no one knows who the murderer is.
text: Ase ni dan nya nuru ale wa kpi doa tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a pai a te ni la po ate ni dan kan seba waai ale ko wa la,

ref: The judges and other leaders from the towns around there must find out what town is the closest to where the body was found.
text: ni niŋdeerɔma ale baai ale a bo buusa la a magsi ba nyini ka peelim a magsi a ta nyini kpiewa ale doa juijui la a ta ga paari tɛŋ kaai ale moata la.

ref: The leaders from that town will go to their cattle herds and choose a young cow that has never been put to work.
text: Ate tɛŋ kaai ale moata kpiewa la niŋdeerɔma a lueri naasari dii ate ba an diem pai bu a tom tuini nya la,

ref: They and some of the priests will take this cow to a nearby valley where there is a stream, but no crops. Once they reach the valley, the leaders will break the cow's neck. The priests must be there, because the Lord your God has chosen them to be his special servants at the place of worship. The Lord has chosen them to bless the people in his name and to be judges in all legal cases, whether property or injury is involved.
text: Kaabteerɔwa ale Livaima bisaŋa yaa le nyini jam niŋ, diila Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale lueri ba ayen ba a tom abe ba a mooli niauŋ Naawen yuenni nyiŋ abe ba a nya biisa zuk nuruba a nin ta chaab ale a nak chaab.

ref: and say, “We had no part in this murder, and we don't know who did it.
text: abe ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Tama an ko nuruwa de yaase ti nya dii ale nye la.

ref: From time to time, you men will serve as soldiers and go off to war. The Lord your God will help you defeat your enemies, and you will take many prisoners.
text: Ase ni dan cheŋ ni nye kpaliŋ ale ni dachaasaŋa ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a dan pai ba a nyo ni nisima po ate ni nak yik ba,

ref: One of these prisoners may be a beautiful woman, and you may want to marry her. But first you must bring her into your home, and have her shave her head, cut her nails, get rid of her foreign clothes, and start wearing Israelite clothes. She will mourn a month for her father and mother, then you can marry her.
text: abe ni yeeri kɔlima ŋaai ate wa jo diipo ate ni nya wa kpaliŋka po la dueni nakpiak. Ase wa yaa a dan bo ni yeeŋa po a kum wa nyama nyiŋ a paari chiik pumi ni baga a faari wa kama.

ref: Later on, if you are not happy with the woman, you can divorce her, and she can go free. But you have slept with her as your wife, so you cannot sell her as a slave or make her into your own slave. Rights of a First-Born Son Moses said to Israel:
text: Ase fi dan kan mariŋ wa, basi ate wa cheŋ kauk kuui meena ate wa a yaali la. Kan pai wa a da yaase fi nye wa ase yɔma la, fi le tɔlim kan te wa zula la.

ref: Suppose a man has two wives and loves one more than the other. The first son of either wife is the man's first-born son, even if the boy's mother is the wife the man doesn't love. Later, when the man is near death and is dividing up his property, he must give a double share to his first-born son, simply because he was the first to be born. A Son Who Rebels Moses said to Israel:
text: Wa magsi wa siak kama ayen wa pok waai ate wa kan yaali la biika ale kpagi, wa te wa kpagi charuk. Bi kala ale dɛ niŋ a sak wa kowa pagrimu. Kpagi ale magsi wa soa jabuui meena la, ka wa le soa.

ref: A father and a mother may have a stubborn and rebellious son who refuses to obey them even after he has been punished.
text: Ase nuru a dan ta biik ate wa ta tukpari a kan wom wa kowa ale wa mawa nɔiya, wa kan zuli ba, se ba dari wa turi,

ref: If a son is like that, his parents must drag him to the town gate, where the leaders of the town hold their meetings.
text: wa kowa ale wa mawa a magsi ba ta wa a jam te ka niŋdeerɔma ale bo tɛŋka nansuiŋtaŋa la.

ref: The parents will tell the leaders, “This son of ours is stubborn and never obeys. He spends all his time drinking and partying.”
text: Ba le magsi ba weeni diila ale nna, <<Tama biika de a ta ka tukpari a kan wom ti nɔiya. Wa kan zuli ti. Wa a kaasi ka ligra ale a nyu daam.>>

ref: The men of the town will stone that son to death, because they must get rid of the evil he brought into the community. Everyone in Israel will be afraid when they hear how he was punished. The Body of a Criminal Moses said to Israel:
text: Ate tɛŋka nuruma meena a yaa yuk wa ale tana a ko ku a magsi kama ayen ni yeeri biemu de ni po. Izirali demma meena ale wom dila ate ba yɔgsa.

ref: If a criminal is put to death, and you hang the dead body on a tree,
text: Ase ba dan ko nuru wa biemu nyiŋ a pai wa a yik tiib nyiŋ,

ref: you must not leave it there overnight. Bury it the same day, because the dead body of a criminal hanging on a tree will bring God's curse on the land. The Lord your God is giving this land to you, so don't make it unclean by leaving the bodies of executed criminals on display.
text: ni kan basi ate wa nyiŋka a bo tiimu nyiŋ ate tɛŋka a sobi. Ni gu wa da dila danni dek. Dii nyiŋla waai ate ba pai a yik tiib nyiŋla Naawen a ka te ku nyɔnɔwa kama. Ni kan kaasi tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaali wa te ni ate ni bo ka po la.

ref: If you see a cow or sheep wandering around lost, take the animal back to its owner.
text: Fi dan nya fi suok naab yaase wa posuk a cheŋ bɛ a jam fi jigi kan deri ta, ta cheŋ ga te waai ale soa jaamu la.

ref: If the owner lives too far away, or if you don't know who the owner is, take the animal home with you and take care of it. The owner will come looking for the animal, and then you can give it back.
text: Alege ku nyɔnɔwa a dan yalima ale fu yaase fi zɛ ku nyɔnɔwa, ta duŋka a kuli fi yenni ate ku nyɔnɔwa a dan jam abe fi te wa.

ref: That's what you should do if you find anything that belongs to someone else. Do whatever you can to help, whether you find a cow or sheep or donkey or some clothing.
text: Nye dila dekdega a te fi suok kuui boniŋ yaase wa garuk ale bɛ la mɛ yaase jabuui meena ale bɛ jam fi jigi la. Kan fi peri jaamu.

ref: Oxen and donkeys that carry heavy loads can stumble and fall, and be unable to get up by themselves. So as you walk along the road, help anyone who is trying to get an ox or donkey back on its feet. Don't Pretend To Be the Opposite Sex Moses said to Israel:
text: Ase fi dan nya fi suok boniŋ yaase naab ale bu lo suik po kan gaam duŋka a taamu maari wa ate ni yik ka ate ka yiti zaani.

ref: Women must not pretend to be men, and men must not pretend to be women. The Lord your God is disgusted with people who do that. Don't Take a Mother Bird Moses said to Israel:
text: Nipok an magsi wa a jo nidoa kɔlima yaase nidoa a jo nipok kɔlima, dii nyiŋla Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a kisa dila kama.

ref: If you build a house, make sure to put a low wall around the edge of the flat roof. Then if someone falls off the roof and is killed, it won't be your fault. Laws against Mixing Different Things Moses said to Israel:
text: Ase ni dan se dɔk paaluk, ni se parik a gilim gboŋku ate waai a dan nyini ku zuk a lo abe wari a kan daani ni.

ref: If you plant a vineyard, don't plant any other fruit tree or crop in it. If you do plant something else there, you must bring to the place of worship everything you harvest from the vineyard.
text: Ni kan pai ŋanta baye a bori kaduk yeŋ po; ni dan nye dila daa jabuui ate fi a vuk fi kadukka po la nyiini ale a kaasi yɔnaŋa mɛ a kaasi kama.

ref: Don't hitch an ox and a donkey to your plow at the same time.
text: Ni kan yik naab ale boniŋ a maŋ chaab a kpa.

ref: When you weave cloth for clothing, you can use thread made of flax or wool, but not both together.
text: Ni kan pai ba le pai duŋsa kɔbta ale garuk miisa a gum chaab yɔk kɔlima ŋaai la a jo.

ref: And when you make a coat, sew a tassel on each of the four corners. When a Husband Accuses His Wife Moses said to Israel:
text: Ni dan baali garuk ni basi ate ku ta zuesa ku noaŋa bunaansiwa.

ref: Suppose a man starts hating his wife soon after they are married.
text: Ase nuru a dan faari nipok a goa ale wa ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ a kan ŋma a yaali wa,

ref: He might tell ugly lies about her, and say, “I married this woman, but when we slept together, I found out she wasn't a virgin.”
text: a yaa kisi wa ale te wa yue kaasuŋ, a weeni ayen, <<Mi faari nipowa de kama, alege mi ale goa ale wa a ga nueri la m yaa miŋ ayen ba liŋ goa ale wa a nya kama.>>

ref: If this happens, the bride's father and mother must go to the town gate to show the town leaders the proof that the woman was a virgin.
text: Nipokbinni kowa ale wa mawa a yaa le weeni ayen wa jam ka waai ale kan seba nidoa a nya ya ate tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma a seba ku nɔi po.

ref: Her father will say, “I let my daughter marry this man, but he started hating her
text: Nipokbinni kowa ale weeni niŋdeerɔma ayen, <<Mi pai m liewa a yalisi nuruwa de kama alege ate wa kan yaali wa.

ref: and accusing her of not being a virgin. But he is wrong, because here is proof that she was a virgin!” Then the bride's parents will show them the bed sheet from the woman's wedding night.
text: Wa weeni ayen fi liewa ka waai ale poom seba nidoa la. Ate wa kowa yaa ale weeni ayen dii ale a sak ayen m liewa ka waai ale kan seba nidoa la ale nna. Liewa nyama yaa le lati garuk kuui ate wa duek ku zuk a goa la.>>

ref: The town leaders will beat the man with a whip
text: Ate niŋdeerɔma ale yik nuruwa de a namsi wa.

ref: But if the man was right and there is no proof that his bride was a virgin,
text: Ase nidoawa ale weeni diila a dan sum ka wensie ayen nipokbinni a seba nidoa a nya kama, alege wari a karo a sak ayen wa zɛ nidoa.

ref: the men of the town will take the woman to the door of her father's house and stone her to death. This woman brought evil into your community by sleeping with someone before she got married, and you must get rid of that evil by killing her. Laws about Illegal Sex Moses said:
text: Ba ta wa a nyini wa kowa nansuiŋku nɔi ate tɛŋka nuruma a yuk wa ale tana a ko. Dii nyiŋla wa ta ka chivie a jam Izirali tɛŋka po. Wa jam diem boka wa kowa yenni po ale deri a goa ale nidoaba. Ni yeeri biemu de ni po a basi.

ref: People of Israel, if a man is caught having sex with someone else's wife, you must put them both to death. That way, you will get rid of the evil they have done in Israel.
text: Ase ni dan yik nuru ale wa boro a goa ale nuru pok nidoawa ale nipowa baai ale goa ale chaab la ni ko ba meena. Ni yeeri biemu de Izirali tɛŋka po a basi.

ref: If an engaged woman is raped out in the country, only the man will be put to death.
text: Alege nuru a dan zik nipokbili dii ale gomsi magsi ayen wa yali la gɔi po a fɛ a goa ale wa, nuru waai ale nye dila la ba ko wa.

ref: Do not punish the woman at all; she has done nothing wrong, and certainly nothing deserving death. This crime is like murder,
text: Ni kan nye nipokbinni wari ya, dii nyiŋla wa an nye biem a magsi ni ko wa. Kude a nye ase ka nuru ale nye kpaliŋ ale wa vaanchoa a ko wa diila.

ref: because the woman was alone out in the country when the man attacked her. She screamed, but there was no one to help her.
text: Nuruwa a nya nipokbinni ka gɔnni po, nipokbinni a kaari kama alege waai an moata ayen wa vari wa a basi.

ref: Suppose a woman isn't engaged to be married, and a man forces her to have sex with him. If he is caught,
text: Ase nuru a dan zik nipokbili dii ale kan seba nidoa ale ka waai a gomsi ayen wa yali mɛ la a goa ale wa ate ni nya,

ref: A man must not marry a woman who was married to his father. This would be a disgrace to his father.
text: Nuru an magsi wa faari wa ko powa. Ku an magsi wa goa ale wa ko powa.

ref: If a man's private parts have been crushed or cut off, he cannot fully belong to the Lord's people.
text: Nuru waai ate ba je la yaase ba gebi wa yoari meena la an magsi wa gum Naawen nuruma po.

ref: No one born outside of a legal marriage, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can fully belong to the Lord's people.
text: Waai ate ba an yali alege biak wa la bala buuni po a ta ga paari buui dii ale a saari piika la an magsi ba gum Naawen nuruma po.

ref: No Ammonites or Moabites, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can become part of Israel, the Lord's people.
text: Ammon demma yaase Moab demma yaase ba buuni po waai a ta ga paari buui dii ale saari piika la an magsi ba gum Naawen nuruma po.

ref: This is because when you came out of Egypt, they refused to provide you with food and water. And besides, they hired Balaam to put a curse on you.
text: Dii nyiŋla ba an tu ni suiku po a te ni ŋandiinta ale nyiamoa diipo ate ni jam nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la. Ba gɔnti da ka Balaam, Biio ate wa nyini Petor Araam Nayaraim po la biika ayen wa ka a te ni.

ref: But the Lord your God loves you, so he refused to listen to Balaam and turned Balaam's curse into a blessing.
text: Alege Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a jam zɛri Balaam nɔi kama alege basi ate kikaasaŋa a chim niaka a te ni dii nyiŋla Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaali ni kama.

ref: Don't even think of signing a peace treaty with Moab or Ammon.
text: Ase nama ale diem vua a boro ase tɛŋ la ni kan nye nɔiyeŋ ale tɛŋsaŋa de yaase ni basi ate ba jigsi.

ref: But Edomites are your relatives, and you lived as foreigners in the country of Egypt. Now you must be kind to Edomites and Egyptians
text: Ni nye Edom demma a magsi ale ba ka ni suata. Ni nye Ejipiti demma mɛ a magsi diila ni jam ka nicham ba tɛŋka po.

ref: and let their great-grandchildren become part of Israel, the Lord's people. Keep the Army Camp Acceptable Moses said to Israel:
text: Ba ŋaaŋbisa butawa po ale jam gum Naawen nuruma po kama.

ref: When you men go off to fight your enemies, make sure your camp is acceptable to the Lord.
text: Ni dan tu chaab ayen ni nye kpaliŋ ale ni dachaasaŋa ni basi wa kaasima nye ka.

ref: For example, if something happens at night that makes a man unclean and unfit for worship, he must go outside the camp and stay there
text: Ase ni po nuru wanyi a dan daŋ wa le sam sim yokku la nyiŋ ku a magsi ka wa basi nuruma ale tigsi chaab kauk kuui la abe wa cheŋ jigi yoŋ.

ref: until late afternoon. Then he must take a bath, and at sunset he can go back into camp.
text: Ase wenni a dan baliŋ wa so wadek ate wenni a dan siŋ wa yaa le ŋmani a cheŋ nuruma ale tigsi chaab a bo kauk kuui la.

ref: Set up a place outside the camp to be used as a toilet area.
text: Ni lueri kauk kuui ale kan moata ni tuka jigini la a cheŋ dula a ga gomsi nidek a magsi.

ref: And make sure that you have a small shovel in your equipment. When you go out to the toilet area, use the shovel to dig a hole. Then, after you relieve yourself, bury the waste in the hole.
text: Ase ni da a cheŋ ni ta jaab a magsi goluk tuka. Ate ni yaa dan cheŋ ni basi yaata ni ya tu goluk a lik ti.

ref: You must keep your camp clean of filthy and disgusting things. The Lord is always present in your camp, ready to rescue you and give you victory over your enemies. But if he sees something disgusting in your camp, he may turn around and leave. Runaway Slaves from Other Countries Moses said:
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a cheŋ a gilim ni boka jigini kama a nya ni zuk ale gomsi ayen wa pai ni dachaasaŋa a nyo ni nisima po ni boka jigini a magsi ka weleŋsa a boro dii ale ku nye ate wa kan nya biem ni jigi ya ate dila nye ate wa basi ni.

ref: When runaway slaves from other countries come to Israel and ask for protection, you must not hand them back to their owners.
text: Ase yɔma a dan suk bo ni jigi, ni kan ni pai wa a te wa kpagni.

ref: Instead, you must let them choose which one of your towns they want to live in. Don't be cruel to runaway slaves. Temple Prostitutes Moses said:
text: Ni basi ate wa bo ale ni kauk kuui meena ate wa a yaa la ale tɛŋ kaai dek ate wa a lueri la. Ni kan namsi wa.

ref: People of Israel, don't any of you ever be temple prostitutes.
text: Izirali nidoa yaase nipok a kan chim nidoa yaalik yaase nipok yaalik a bo bɔgta yeri po.

ref: The Lord your God is disgusted with men and women who are prostitutes of any kind, and he will not accept a gift from them, even if it had been promised to him. Interest on Loans Moses said:
text: Ni kan ta nidoa yaalik yaase nipok yaalik ale nya ŋan baai la a jam Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la yenni po ayen ni tuni ni pumpuulima dii nyiŋla, Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a kisi ŋala meena kama.

ref: When you lend money, food, or anything else to another Israelite, you are not allowed to charge interest.
text: Ase fi dan peem ligra yaase ŋandiinta a te fi mabiik ka fi a yiili ayen wa tuni fu a poom gaam dii ate fi a peem a te wa la.

ref: You can charge a foreigner interest. But if you charge other Israelites interest, the Lord your God will not let you be successful in the land you are about to take. Sacred Promises to the Lord Moses said:
text: Fi baga a nye dila nichaanɔ jigi kama alege kan nye dila Izirali denɔ jigi ya. Dila ale ku basi ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a niak ni ale tuin dii meena ate ni a tom tɛŋ kaai po ate ni a tuesi la.

ref: People of Israel, if you make a sacred promise to give a gift to the Lord, then do it as soon as you can. If the Lord has to come looking for the gift you promised, you will be guilty of breaking that promise.
text: Ase ni dan pɛ ayen ni nye wari a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, kan beni abe ni tuni. Ni dan beni Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale bek ni kama dii nyiŋla ku ka biem.

ref: On the other hand, if you never make a sacred promise, you can't be guilty of breaking it.
text: Alege ni dan yeeri nidek pumpuulima po ni an nye kaasi ya.

ref: You must keep whatever promises you make to the Lord. After all, you are the one who chose to make the promises. Eating Someone Else's Produce
text: Alege ni dan nye dila ni be seba ayen ni a tuni kama, diila nidek ale lak ni noaŋa a puulim ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la.

ref: If you go into a vineyard that belongs to someone else, you are allowed to eat as many grapes as you want while you are there. But don't take any with you when you leave.
text: Ase ni dan jo ni mabiik kaduk po ni baga a dɛ ŋan baai meena ate ni a yaali la kama. Alege ni kan tali a nyo busik po a ta kuli.

ref: In the same way, if you are in a grain field that belongs to someone else, you can pick heads of grain and eat the kernels. But don't cut down the stalks of grain and take them with you.
text: Ase ni dan jo ni mabiik zaa laŋ po ni baga a wɛ zaaŋa a ŋɔbi kama alege ni kan che za ŋaai ale za la.

ref: Suppose a woman was divorced by her first husband because he found something disgraceful about her. He wrote out divorce papers, gave them to her, and sent her away.
text: Ase nidoa a dan faari nipok ate ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa an ŋma a yaali wa dii nyiŋla wa nya ka wari wa jigi, ate wa yaa ŋmarisi gbaŋ a nyo wa nisa po a zɛri wa ayen wa nyini yenni po a nyini,

ref: Since she has slept with her second husband, she cannot marry her first husband again. Their marriage would pollute the land that the Lord your God is giving you, and he would be disgusted. Newlyweds Moses said to Israel:
text: Nidoa waai ale liŋ a zɛri nipowa la a ka suik a ŋma a faari wa dii nyiŋla nidoa yoŋ ale goa ale wa la nyiŋ. Dila ka kisuk Naawen nimbie po. Ni kan ta biem a jam tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ni Wen la a yaa wa te ni la po.

ref: If a man and a woman have been married less than one year, he must not be sent off to war or sent away to do forced labor. He must be allowed to stay home for a year and be happy with his wife. Loans Moses said to Israel:
text: Ase nidoa a dan piilim faari nipok ku kan magsi ayen wa cheŋ kpaliŋ po yaase ba tom wa jigiya. Ku a magsi wa wari ka yeri a nye ate nipowa waai ate wa faari la sui a yɔk.

ref: When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that they will pay back the loan. But don't take one or both of their millstones, or else they may starve. They need these stones for grinding grain into flour to make bread. Kidnapping Moses said to Israel:
text: Ase fi dan peem fi ligra a te nuru fi baga a tuesi wa jaab kama a ta dii ale ku nye ate wa tuni ligni a te fu abe wa tuesi wa jaamu la. Alege kan fi tuesi niri yaase ba nie ŋaye wa meena ni dan nye dila ba le kpi ale kɔm. Ba ta nieŋa a num ka zom a nye ŋandiinta.

ref: If you are guilty of kidnapping Israelites and forcing them into slavery, you will be put to death to remove this evil from the community. Skin Diseases Moses said to Israel:
text: Ase ni dan nya nuru ale wa yik wadek suok Izirali demma wanyi a nye wa ase yɔma la ni ko wa. Ni yeeri biem a ta nyini ni po a nyini.

ref: I have told the priests what to do if any of you have leprosy, so do exactly what they say.
text: Gama tuem a dan boro ni kpesi nidek a nye dii ate kaabteerɔma baai ale ka Livaima a weeni ni la. Ku a magsi kama ayen ni va mi ale weeni diila.

ref: And remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam after you left Egypt. Loans Moses said to Israel:
text: Ni a teeri dii ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a jam nye Miriam la diipo ate ni jam nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la.

ref: When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that the money will be paid back. But you must not go into their house to get it.
text: Ase nama a dan peem jaab a te ni mabiik, ni kan cheŋ wa yenni a ga tuesi jabuui ate wa a yaali wa pai a te a puulim la.

ref: Wait outside, and they will bring out the item you have agreed on.
text: Limisi ate nuru waai ale dɛ fi pamini la dek a jam te fu.

ref: Suppose someone is so poor that a coat is the only thing that can be offered as a guarantee on a loan. Don't keep the coat overnight.
text: Ase nuruwa a dan ka jajak kan ga goa ale wa le puulim jaabuui la a tara.

ref: Instead, give it back before sunset, so the owner can keep warm and sleep and ask the Lord to bless you. Then the Lord your God will notice that you have done the right thing. Poor People's Wages Moses said:
text: Pai wa garukku a te wa, alege ate wen siŋ ate wa goa ku zuk ate wa te fi jiam ate ku nye ase wa maŋ la Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la nina po.

ref: If you hire poor people to work for you, don't hold back their pay, whether they are Israelites or foreigners who live in your town.
text: Ni kaa vari ŋanjaksaŋa yaase baai ate ni pai ate ba a tom. Ku nyɔnɔwa a dan poom ka Izirali denɔ yaa wa ka nichaanɔ a bo ni tɛŋsaŋa kanyi po ni kan vari wa.

ref: Pay them their wages at the end of each day, because they live in poverty and need the money to survive. If you don't pay them on time, they will complain about you to the Lord, and he will punish you. The Death Penalty Moses said to Israel:
text: Ni tuni wa danni tutunaŋa ku le magsi ni tuni wa diila abe le ge ate wenni a siŋ. Wa ka jajak wa boro ka ŋanta bala nyiŋ. Kan daa di wa le kaari a te Naawen ate wa namsi ni biem bula nyiŋ.

ref: Parents must not be put to death for crimes committed by their children, and children must not be put to death for crimes committed by their parents. Don't put anyone to death for someone else's crime. Don't Mistreat the Powerless Moses said to Israel:
text: Ko a kan kpi a te biiga biik mɛ abe ka suik a kpi ko nyiŋŋa. Waai meena a kpi ka wadek biem nyiŋ.

ref: Make sure that orphans and foreigners are treated fairly. And if you lend money to a widow and want to keep something of hers to guarantee that she will pay you back, don't take any of her clothes.
text: Ni be kan kasi nichamma ale kpiŋsaŋa ayen ba ka a nye ba yaalika, abe ni kan tuesi pukɔgi garuk a ta ayen wa dɛ pami nyiŋŋa.

ref: You were slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws. Leave Some of Your Harvest for the Poor Moses said to Israel:
text: Ni a teeri ayen ni daam ka yɔm Ejipiti tɛŋka po ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la da tuesi ni a basi. Dila ale soa ate mi a weeni ayen ni a nye kude la.

ref: If you forget to bring in a stack of harvested grain, don't go back in the field to get it. Leave it for the poor, including foreigners, orphans, and widows, and the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
text: Ase ni dan boro a che ni tattaŋa ŋantaŋa, ŋan baai ate ni gaam a basi la ni kan ŋman a cheŋ ba po. Ni basi bala ate nichamma ale kpiŋsaŋa ale pukɔŋŋa ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a niak ni nisima tuimaŋa meena.

ref: When you harvest your olives, don't try to get them all for yourself, but leave some for the poor.
text: Ase ni dan zaŋ kpaam tiisaŋa yɔnaŋa ŋaai ale a wari naŋsaŋa nyiŋla ni basi ba a te nichamma ale kpiŋsaŋa ale pukɔŋŋa.

ref: And when you pick your grapes, go over the vines only once, then let the poor have what is left.
text: Ni dan gbesi ni kaduksaŋa yɔnaŋa, ŋaai ate ni gaam a taam la, ni kan ŋman cheŋ ŋa po. Ni basi ŋala ate nichamma ale kpiŋsaŋa ale pukɔŋŋa.

ref: You lived in poverty as slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws.
text: Ni be kan baŋ ni a le jam ka yɔm Ejipiti tɛŋka po la. Dila ale soa ate mi a weeni kude la.

ref: Suppose you and someone else each accuse the other of doing something wrong, and you go to court, where the judges decide you are guilty. If your punishment is to be beaten with a whip, one of the judges will order you to lie down, and you will receive the number of lashes you deserve.
text: Ase waai ate ba bo a mini la ku dan magsi kama ayen ba nak wa, boteerɔwa ale basi kama ate wa duak tɛŋ ate ba miiri wa wa nimbie po a magsi chaab ale wa kaasuŋku ale ka diila.

ref: Forty lashes is the most that you can be given, because more than that might make other Israelites think you are worthless. Don't Muzzle an Ox Moses said to Israel:
text: Alege ku kan magsi ba miiri wa a gaam pisinaansi. Ba dan miiri wa a gaam di la, ba le valiŋ wa.

ref: Don't muzzle an ox while it is threshing grain. A Son for a Dead Brother Moses said to Israel:
text: Kan kpalimu naab dɛka ase ni nin yik bu a fɔbi za.

ref: Suppose two brothers are living on the same property, when one of them dies without having a son to carry on his name. If this happens, his widow must not marry anyone outside the family. Instead, she must marry her late husband's brother, and their first son will be the legal son of the dead man.
text: Biik kaai ate nipowa a dɛ niŋ a biak la ba pai nidoawa waai ale kpi la yuenni a te wa ate nuruwa yuenni a kan bɛ Izirali tɛŋka po.

ref: But suppose the brother refuses to marry the widow. She must go to a meeting of the town leaders at the town gate and say, “My husband died without having a son to carry on his name. And my husband's brother refuses to marry me so I can have a son.”
text: Alege nuruwa a dan zɛri an faari wa suoku powa, Nipowa a yaa le cheŋ ka tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma jigi a weeni ba ayen, <M chorɔwa suoku a zɛri kama ayen wa kan zak wa suoku yue a zaani Izirali tɛŋka po. Wa kan nye wa suoku ale magsi wa nye dii a te mu la.>

ref: The leaders will call the living brother to the town gate and try to persuade him to marry the widow. But if he doesn't change his mind and marry her,
text: Tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma ale biisi ale wa. Alege wa dan diem a zɛri ayen, <Mi kan yaali ayen wa faari wa.>

ref: she must go over to him while the town leaders watch. She will pull off one of his sandals and spit in his face, while saying, “That's what happens to a man who won't help provide descendants for his dead brother.”
text: Wa suoku pukɔgini a yaa le cheŋ wa jigi niŋdeerɔma nimbie po, a pai wa nuesaŋa dinyi a yaa chesi tintueta a nyo wa nimbidiaka nyiŋ abe wa weeni ayen, <Ku le magsi ayen ba nye waai ale ka a yaali ayen wa suoku a ta bisa la diila ale nna.

ref: From then on, that man's family will be known as “the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off.” When Two Men Fight Moses said to Israel:
text: Izirali demma ale seba nuruwa de ase ka waai nuensa ate ba yeeri la.

ref: If two men are fighting, and the wife of one man tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the other man's private parts,
text: Ase nidoaba baye a dan ta chaab ate nwala powa a dan maari wa a yik nwala kolaŋa,

ref: you must cut off her hand. Don't have any mercy. Be Honest in Business Moses said to Israel:
text: ni gebi wa nisaŋa ni kan sak jiirim ale wa.

ref: If you weigh and measure things honestly, the Lord your God will let you enjoy a long life in the land he is giving you.
text: Ni ta dobrim maŋsa ale ŋanmagsin maŋsa ate ni goa tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ayen wa te ni la a beni.

ref: But the Lord is disgusted with anyone who cheats or is dishonest. Wipe Out Amalek Moses said:
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a kisi nuru waai ale a nye wieŋa de la kama.

ref: People of Israel, do you remember what the Amalekites did to you after you came out of Egypt?
text: Ni teeri dii ate Amalek demma a nye ni la, diipo ate ni jam nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka po a nyini la.

ref: You were tired, and they followed along behind, attacking those who could not keep up with the others. This showed that the Amalekites have no respect for God.
text: Diipo ate ni jam jiak la ba jam tu ni ka suik a ko baai ale jam wobsa a wari bo ŋaaŋ la. Ba kan chali Naawen yaa.

ref: The Lord your God will help you capture the land, and he will give you peace. But when that day comes, you must wipe out Amalek so completely that no one will remember they ever lived.
text: Ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, a dan basi ate ni nya vuusum a ta nyini ni dachaasaŋa meena ale gilim ni la, tɛŋ kaai ate wa le te ni ate ni boro la, ni yeeri Amalek demma tɛŋka zuk. Ni kan baŋ.

ref: The Lord is giving you the land, and soon you will conquer it, settle down,
text: Ni dan jo tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaa wa pai te ni la po a ga kali nueri,

ref: and plant crops. And when you begin harvesting each of your crops, the very first things you pick must be put in a basket. Take them to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped,
text: ni pai ni ale kpa ŋan baai tɛŋ kaai po ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ayen wa te ni la, ŋan baai ale dɛ niŋ a bɛ la ni ta ba cheŋ juijui ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a lueri ayen ni a puusi wa la ale busisa a ga nye wa jiam.

ref: and tell the priest, “Long ago the Lord our God promised our ancestors that he would give us this land. And today, I thank him for keeping his promise and giving me a share of the land.”
text: Abe ni weeni kaabteerɔma ayen, <Mi a weeni fi Naawen dii ale ka mi Wen la jinla de kama ayen m jam tɛŋ kaai po ate fi Naawen a pɛ ayen fi le pai ka a te ti kokpieŋsaŋa la po kama.>

ref: Then, standing there in front of the place of worship, you must pray: My ancestor was homeless, an Aramean who went to live in Egypt. There were only a few in his family then, but they became great and powerful, a nation of many people.
text: Ate ni yaa le weeni Naawen fi Wenni ayen, <M kowa jam ka Araam denɔ a nyiem a cheŋ. Wa jam cheŋ ga bo ka Ejipiti tɛŋka po, ale nuruba maga. Wa jam bo ka dula a yaa jam chim tɛŋ kpieŋ a pagra ale piisi mɛ.

ref: The Egyptians were cruel and had no pity on us. They mistreated our people and forced us into slavery.
text: Alege Ejipiti demma a jam ta ka gaasa ale ti a basi ate ti a nam ale basi ate ti a tom tuim pagra.

ref: We called out for help to you, the Lord God of our ancestors. You heard our cries; you knew we were in trouble and abused.
text: Ate tama a yaa jam kaari a te ti koma Naawen dii ale ka ti kokpieŋsaŋa Naawen la, ate Naawen a wom ti luelutaŋa ale nya tama ale a namu diila.

ref: Then you terrified the Egyptians with your mighty miracles and rescued us from Egypt.
text: Naawen a yaa ta ti a nyini Ejipiti po a nyini ale wadek pagrim. Wa sui ale jam puuri ate wa nye wakperikaliisa ale wakinkagla ale kpazinagsuk wie.

ref: You brought us here and gave us this land rich with milk and honey.
text: Wa ta ti a jam ka dela a pai tɛŋka de a te ti. Tɛŋ kaai ate biisim ale siita a kasim bo ka po a chali.

ref: Now, Lord, I bring to you the best of the crops that you have given me. After you say these things, place the basket in front of the Lord's altar and bow down to worship him.
text: Ate m yaa ta ŋan baai ate mi a kpa tɛŋka po ate fi te mu ate ba dɛ niŋ a bɛ la a jam ayen m te fi Naawen.> Pai busika a zaani Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋ, a koori tɛŋ wa niŋ a puusi wa.

ref: Then you and your family must celebrate by eating a meal at the place of worship to thank the Lord your God for giving you such a good harvest. And remember to invite the Levites and the foreigners who live in your town. Ten Percent of the Harvest Moses said to Israel:
text: Nama ale Livaima ale nichamma yaa le ta suipeentik ale wamaŋ sii meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a nye te ni ale ni yeeŋa demma la nyiŋ.

ref: Every year you are to give ten percent of your harvest to the Lord. But every third year, this ten percent must be given to the poor who live in your town, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. That way, they will have enough to eat.
text: Bena ŋata po meena tuni fi kpanni ŋantaŋa piika po a te Livaima ale nichamma ale kpiŋsaŋa ale pukɔŋŋa ate dila ale basi ate jigi meena baai ale kan ta ŋanta a dɛ ŋandiinta a chak. Ase ni dan nye dila,

ref: Then you must pray: Our Lord and our God, you have said that ten percent of my harvest is sacred. I have obeyed your command and given this to the poor, including the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
text: ni yaa weeni Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ayen, <M pai tuilum ŋan baai ate m yeeri m yenni po a magsi fi la m pai te Livaima ale nichamma ale kpiŋsaŋa ale pukɔŋŋa la a te ba kama a ta va fi ale weeni diila. Mi an zɛri fi ale weeni diila yaase m baŋi dinyi mɛ la.

ref: I have not eaten any of this sacred food while I was in mourning; in fact, I never touched it when I was unclean. And none of it has been offered as a sacrifice to the spirits of the dead. I have done everything exactly as you commanded.
text: Mi an dɛ ŋan baai ate m yeeri a magsi fi la diipo ate mi a kum la, mi abe m pai wanyi mɛ la diipo ate mi daŋ la. Mi abe m pai jaab a te kpio. Mi a wom fi nɔi kama Naawen dii ale ka mi Wen la, m nye dii meena ate fi a weeni ayen m nye la kama.

ref: Our Lord, look down from your temple in heaven and bless us and our land. You promised our ancestors that you would give us this land rich with milk and honey, and you have kept your promise. The Lord Is Your God, and You Are His People Moses said to Israel:
text: Nya ti a nyini wenŋmazuk fi tuilum jigini ate fi boro la abe fi basi ate niaka a nyini wenŋmazuk a jam fi nuruma Izirali demma jigi. Ase fi ale puulim dii ale ti koma ayen fi le te ba tɛŋ kaai ate biisim ale siita a bo ka po la.

ref: Today the Lord your God has commanded you to obey these laws and teachings with all your heart and soul.
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a weeni ni kama jinla de ayen sinsaŋŋa de: Ni kpesi a va ŋa ale ni suiniima meena ale ni chiisa meena.

ref: In response, you have agreed that the Lord will be your God, that you will obey all his laws and teachings, and that you will listen when he speaks to you.
text: Nama a weeni kama jinla de ayen Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale va wa suitaŋa kama abe ni va wa wieŋa ale wa sinsaŋŋa abe ni a wom wa le a weeni diila.

ref: Since you have agreed to obey the Lord, he has agreed that you will be his people and that you will belong to him, just as he promised.
text: Naawen a weeni kama jinla dɛ ayen ni ka wa nuruba ale wa tuilum ŋanta ase wa le puulim dii ale ni la ale weeni ayen ni va wa wieŋa la.

ref: The Lord created all nations, but he will make you more famous than any of them, and you will receive more praise and honor. You will belong only to the Lord your God, just as he promised.
text: Wa le basi ate ni gaam tɛŋsa meena ate wa nye la, ate ni nya yuei ale zula. Ni le chim ka nuru weleŋsa a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ase wa le puulim diila.

ref: Moses stood together with the leaders and told the people of Israel: Obey all the laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
text: Moosis ale Izirali niŋdeerɔma a yaa weeni nuruma ayen, <<Ni ta wieŋa de ŋaai ate mi a weeni ni jinla de la.

ref: At this same place, build an altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God. But don't use stones that have been cut with iron tools.
text: Ni sɛ kuŋkuŋ dula jigini a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la. Ni pai tintana nyiini a sɛ kuŋkuŋku, ni kan pai kutuk a che tintanaŋa.

ref: Look for stones that can be used without being cut. Then offer sacrifices to please the Lord, burning them completely on the altar.
text: Ni pai tintana a sɛ kuŋkuŋ a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la abe ni nye juka kaabka a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la.

ref: Next, offer sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing, and serve the meat at a sacred meal where you will celebrate in honor of the Lord.
text: Ni nye suiyɔgni tiirita kaabka dula abe ni dɛ ale suipeentik Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋ.

ref: Don't forget to write out a copy of these laws on the stone slabs that you are going to set up. Make sure that the writing is easy to read. Curses on Those Who Disobey
text: Abe ni ŋmarisi sinsaŋŋa meena ate ŋa a nya cheri a dueni tintanaŋa de ate ni sɛ la zuk.>>

ref: Moses stood together with the priests and said, “Israel, be quiet and listen to me! Today you have become the people of the Lord your God.
text: Ate Moosis ale kaabteerɔma baai ale ka Livaima la a yaa weeni Izirali demma ayen, <<Ni goori Izirali demma abe ni wom de! Ni yaa ka Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la nuruba.

ref: So you must obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you.”
text: Ni zuli Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la abe le va wa wieŋa ale wa sinsaŋŋa ate mi a te ni jinla de la.>>

ref: That same day, Moses gave them the following instructions:
text: Da dila danni dek Moosis a weeni nuruma ayen,

ref: After you cross the Jordan River, you will go to Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. The tribes of Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin will go up on Mount Gerizim, where they will bless the people of Israel. The tribes of Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali will go up on Mount Ebal where they will agree to the curses.
text: Abe nuruma de dɔkku mɛ po a jueli Ebal Guuku zuk a ka kikaasa. Baai ale magsi ba nye dila la ale Aruben ale Gad ale Asɛ ale Zebulun ale Dan ale Nafitali.

ref: Today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. Always obey them, and the Lord will make Israel the most famous and important nation on earth, and he will bless you in many ways.
text: Niaka de meena ale jam ni jigi ase nama a nin wom Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la nɔi.

ref: The Lord will make your businesses and your farms successful.
text: Ni le nya niaka ni tɛŋ fiisaŋa po abe ni nya niaka tɛŋ kpieŋka dek po mɛ.

ref: You will have many children. You will harvest large crops, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats will produce many young.
text: Ni le nya niaka ni bisaŋa zuk ale ni kpanni ŋantaŋa ale ni duŋsaŋa, naabisa ale pabisa.

ref: You will have plenty of bread to eat.
text: Ni le nya niaka ni busisaŋa ale ni ŋandiintaŋa zuk.

ref: The Lord will make you successful in your daily work.
text: Ni le nya niaka ni le a jo ale a nyini.

ref: The Lord your God is giving you the land, and he will make sure you are successful in everything you do. Your harvests will be so large that your storehouses will be full.
text: Naawen ale niak ni booŋa ale wa dii meena ate ni pai ni nisima a nye la. Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la dek ale niak ni tɛŋ kaai po ate wa ayen wa te ni la.

ref: If you follow and obey the Lord, he will make you his own special people, just as he promised.
text: Naawen ale nye ni ase wadek nuru weleŋsa la, ase wa le puulim ayen ni dan ta Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la wieŋa ale a va wa suitaŋa mɛ la.

ref: Then everyone on earth will know that you belong to the Lord, and they will be afraid of you.
text: Ate nuruma meena tɛŋzuk de ale nya ayen ka Naawen ale wi ni ate dila ale basi ate ba a chali ni yɔgsum.

ref: The Lord will give you a lot of children and make sure that your animals give birth to many young. The Lord promised your ancestors that this land would be yours, and he will make it produce large crops for you.
text: Naawen ale niak ni ale bisa. Ni duŋsaŋa mɛ ale piisi abe ni ta ŋandiinta tɛŋka po ase wa le puulim dii ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa ayen wa te ni la.

ref: The Lord will open the storehouses of the skies where he keeps the rain, and he will send rain on your land at just the right times. He will make you successful in everything you do. You will have plenty of money to lend to other nations, but you won't need to borrow any yourself.
text: Naawen ale lagri wenŋmazukku ŋantaŋa ale bo dɔk kuui po la a basi ate ŋmoruk a ni ni tɛŋka po abe wa niak ni nisa tuima meena. Nama ale te tɛŋsa yegayega ŋanta alege a kan tuesi jaab tɛŋ sila jigi ya.

ref: Obey the laws and teachings that I'm giving you today, and the Lord your God will make Israel a leader among the nations, and not a follower. Israel will be wealthy and powerful, not poor and weak.
text: Naawen ale basi ate ni chim zuima ni kan chim juita. Ase nama a dan wom Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la wieŋa nalimnyiini ŋaai ate mi a te ni jinla de la, nama ale kasim boka ŋmai ni kan siŋ tɛŋa.

ref: and no one will disturb the birds and wild animals while they eat your dead bodies.
text: Ni nyiŋ lantaŋa ale chim ka ŋandiinta a te ŋan yirinta meena ale duŋsaŋa meena tɛŋzuk de ate waai a kan kpaliŋ ayen si ka a dɛ ni nyiŋsaŋa.

ref: Then everyone will look at you and your descendants and realize that the Lord has placed you under a curse.
text: Wieŋa de ale chim sakka ale wakinkagla a te nama ale ni ŋaaŋbisaŋa taam wuu.

ref: Israel, today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. And if you don't obey them all, he will put many curses on you.
text: Alege, ni dan kan wom Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la alege zɛri an va wa wieŋa ale wa ŋmarisika ate mi a te jinla de la nalimnyiini, kikaasaŋa de meena a cheen ka ni jigi.

ref: Your businesses and farms will fail.
text: Naawen ale ka te ni tɛŋ fiisaŋa po ale tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po.

ref: You'll have only a few children, your crops will be small, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats won't produce many young.
text: Naawen ale ka te ni ate ni kan biak bisa a soa dii ya, ni kan nya ŋandiinta ale niiga ale piisa a soa dii ya.

ref: The Lord will make you fail in everything you do.
text: Ni dan bo dɔk Naawen ale ka te ni, ni dan nyini peelim wa le ka a te ni mɛ.

ref: No matter what you try to accomplish, the Lord will confuse you, and you will feel his anger. You won't last long, and you may even meet with disaster, all because you rejected the Lord.
text: Naawen ale basi ate kikaasa a jam ni jigi, butimka ale toariŋka ale jam ni jigi ni ale pai ni nisaŋa a tiri jabuui meena la a ta ga paari diipo ate wa le ko ni nama ale nye dii ale zɛri wa la nyiŋ.

ref: The Lord will let you be defeated by your enemies, and you will scatter in all directions. You will be a horrible sight for the other nations to see,
text: Naawen ale ka te ni ate ni dachaasaŋa a nya pagrim ni zuk. Ni le va ka suik yeoŋ a jam ba jigi alege ni le va ka suik boari a chali, ate jigi meena tɛŋzuk a yaa le chali yɔgsum dii ale nye ni la.

ref: The Lord will make you suffer with diseases that will cause oozing sores or crusty itchy patches on your skin or boils like the ones that are common in Egypt. And there will be no cure for you!
text: Naawen ale basi ate nirisa a moari ni ase wa le jam nye Ejipiti demma diila. Wa le basi ate nira a nye ni nyiŋsaŋa meena abe wa nye ate ni nyiŋsaŋa a ŋarisi abe si a zak ate ni a ŋomisi alege ni kan nya nyiŋyɔgsa.

ref: You will become insane and go blind. The Lord will make you so confused,
text: Naawen ale basi ate ni chim yesiŋsa abe ni chim yeeba ate ni popolaŋa a ka tom tuima.

ref: that even in bright sunshine you will have to feel your way around like a blind person, who cannot tell day from night. For the rest of your life, people will beat and rob you, and no one will be able to stop them.
text: Ni le tigsi chaab jigi yeŋ kantueŋ ase yeeba la ate ni kan nya suiku a cheŋŋi. Ni kan nya niaka ale dii meena ate ni a nye la. Ni le kasim a tu ka ninam abe ba a vari ni alege waai a kan maari ni.

ref: A man will be engaged to a woman, but before they can get married, she will be raped by enemy soldiers. Some of you will build houses, but never get to live in them. If you plant a vineyard, you won't be around long enough to enjoy the first harvest.
text: Ni le puulim kama a yaali ayen ni faari nipok alege ate nuru yoŋ a va kauk a goa le wa. Ni le sɛ yie alege kan goa ŋa po mɛ. Ni le kpa tatta alege ni kan dɛ ti yɔnaŋa.

ref: Your cattle will be killed while you watch, but you won't get to eat any of the meat. Your donkeys and sheep will be stolen from you, and no one will be around to force your enemies to give them back.
text: Ba le togri ni niiŋa nidek nimbie po alege ni kan ŋɔbi ŋa. Ba le tuesi ni bonsaŋa ale fifiok ba kan ŋman pai si a te ni diipo diipo. Ni dachaasaŋa ale tuesi ni piisaŋa alege waai a kan tuesi ŋa a te ni.

ref: Your sons and daughters will be dragged off to a foreign country, while you stand there helpless. And even if you watch for them until you go blind, you will never see them again.
text: Ba le pai ni nidoabilisaŋa ale ni liema a te tɛŋ yoŋ ate ni le yeeri ni ninaŋa a nya a yiili ayen ni le nya ba daa meena ni ale wobsa la nyiŋ ni kan nye wari ya.

ref: You will work hard on your farms, but everything you harvest will be eaten by foreigners, who will mistreat you and abuse you for the rest of your life.
text: Nuru baai ate ni zɛ ba la ale ba dɛ ŋan baai ate ni namu nya ba ni tɛŋka po la ni kan ta jaaboa ka ninam nyiini daaŋa meena.

ref: What you see will be so horrible that you will go insane,
text: Ninam buui ale bu jam ni jigi la ale basi kama ate ni a yesim.

ref: The Lord will let you and your king be taken captive to a country that you and your ancestors have never even heard of, and there you will have to worship idols made of wood and stone.
text: Naawen ale ta ni ale ni naawa a cheŋ ka tɛŋ kaai ate nama yaase ni koma a zɛ ka wie la po. Dula jigini nama ale kaabka bɔgluk yonta, tii ate ba pai daata ale tana a nye ti la.

ref: People of nearby countries will shudder when they see your terrible troubles, but they will still make fun of you.
text: Tɛŋ sii po ate Naawen a yaali wa basi ate ni waaŋ si po la, ku le cha nuruma dii ale nye ni la nyiŋ abe ba nye ni a la.

ref: You will plant a lot of seed, but gather a small harvest, because locusts will eat your crops.
text: Ni le bori ka bie yega alege che maga, dii nyiŋla tintue ale dɛ ni ŋantaŋa.

ref: You will plant vineyards and work hard at taking care of them, but you won't gather any grapes, much less get any wine, because the vines themselves will be eaten by worms.
text: Ni le kpa tatta a che alege ni kan pai yɔnaŋa a nye damasik a nyu yaa ni tigsi yɔnaŋa, dii nyiŋla nanzue ale ŋa dɛ ŋa.

ref: Even if your olive trees grow everywhere in your country, the olives will fall off before they are ready, and there won't be enough olive oil for combing your hair.
text: Ni le ta kpaam tiisa ni tɛŋka meena po alege ni kan pai kpaamu a tom tuini, dii nyiŋla ŋa ni wiiri kama.

ref: Even your children will be taken as prisoners of war.
text: Ni le ta bisa ale lieba alege ni kan bo ale ba dii nyiŋla ba le cheŋ ka yɔntidi po.

ref: Locusts will eat your crops and strip your trees of leaves and fruit.
text: Tintue ale piisi a jam dɛ tiisaŋa ale ni kpari ŋantaŋa meena ni tɛŋka po.

ref: Foreigners in your towns will become wealthy and powerful, while you become poor and powerless.
text: Nichamma ale bo ni tɛŋka po ale ni la ale nya pagrim a gaam ni alege ate nama a jɔk ni pagrimu.

ref: You will be so short of money that you will have to borrow from those foreigners. They will be the leaders in the community, and you will be the followers. More Curses for Disobedience Moses said:
text: Bala ale ta ligra a te ni alege nama a kan ta ligra a te ba. Bala ale chim zuk alege ate nama a chim juik.

ref: Israel, if you don't obey the laws and teachings that the Lord your God is giving you, he will send these curses to chase, attack, and destroy you.
text: Kikaasaŋa de meena ale jam ni jigi. Ba le vi ni a kaasi ni, dii nyiŋla ni le kaa wom Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la nɔi alege an va wa wieŋa ale wa ŋmarisika ate wa te ni la nyiŋ.

ref: If the Lord makes you wealthy, but you don't joyfully worship and honor him,
text: Ni le kan va Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen ale mariŋka ale suipeentik da ŋaai po ate ni nya niaka la nyiŋ,

ref: he will send enemies to attack you and make you their slaves. Then you will live in poverty with nothing to eat, drink, or wear, and your owners will work you to death.
text: Dila nyiŋ nama ale ga tom a te ka dacha sii ate Naawen ayen wa pai ni a nyo ba nisa po la. Kɔm ale nyanyuila ale kasim ta ni, ni le nya jaŋsa nna yegayega ale chaboala mɛ. Ba le namsi ni ka nna yegayega a ta ga paari diipo ate wa le kaasi ni la.

ref: Foreigners who speak a strange language will be sent to attack you without warning, just like an eagle swooping down.
text: Naawen ale basi ate tɛŋ a nyini niŋniŋa a jam nye kpaliŋ ale ni, ba le nye ka nna nwuli ase jiiruk la ni kan miŋ tɛŋ kala biika mɛ,

ref: They won't show any mercy, and they will have no respect for old people or pity for children.
text: tɛŋ kaai ate ni dan nya ka nuruma abe yɔgsum a yik ni la, ba kan zuli ŋankpagsaŋa yaase ba ta jiirim ale bi paalukku.

ref: All over the land that the Lord your God gave you, the enemy army will surround your towns. You may feel safe inside your town walls, but the enemy will tear them down,
text: Ba le nye kpaliŋ ale tɛŋ sii meena ale bo ni tɛŋka po la a ta ga paari diipo ate parik kaai ate ni ta sebchakka la a lo tɛŋ. Ba le tuesi tɛŋka meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaa wa pai te ni la.

ref: while you wait in horror. Finally, you will get so hungry that you will eat the sons and daughters that the Lord gave you.
text: Ninammu ate ni dachaasaŋa a basi ate ni a namu la nyiŋ kɔm ale yik ni ate nama ale yik ni bisaŋa ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a te ni la a ŋɔbi.

ref: Because of hunger, a man who had been gentle and kind will eat his own children and refuse to share the meal with his brother or wife or with his other children.
text: wa poom kan nye bisaŋa lammu ate wa bi sii ale diem tali a boro la kude meena ale nye kama dii nyiŋla ni dachaasaŋa ale basi ate ninammu de a jam ni jigi.

ref: A woman may have grown up in such luxury that she never had to put a foot on the ground. But times will be so bad that she will secretly eat both her newborn baby and the afterbirth, without sharing any with her husband or her other children. Disobedience Brings Destruction Moses said to Israel:
text: Wa le a biak waai ŋaaŋnyiŋ la ale zanni wa le suk a ŋɔbi dii nyiŋla, wa le kan ta jaab a dɛ la, ale ninam buui ate ni dachaasaŋa ale ta jam ni jigi ni tɛŋsaŋa po la.

ref: You must obey everything in The Book of God's Law. Because if you don't respect the Lord,
text: Ni dan kan kpesi a va sinsaŋŋa wieŋa meena, ŋaai ale ŋmarisi gbaŋka de po la, ale zɛri a kan zuli Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la yuenni,

ref: Remember! If the Lord decides to destroy your nation, he can use any disease or disaster, not just the ones written in The Book of God's Law.
text: Naawen ale basi ate nyiŋtuila ale tueta tɔgatɔga a yik ni, ŋaai ale kan maa ŋmarisi a bo sinsaŋŋa gbaŋka de po la a ta ga paari diipo ate ni le kpi la.

ref: There are as many of you now as the stars in the sky, but if you disobey the Lord your God, only a few of you will be left.
text: Nama baai ale piisi ase chiŋmarisaŋa ale bo chiŋmaaŋa po la ni magadega ale tali dii nyiŋla ni ale zɛri an va Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la yaalika la nyiŋ.

ref: The Lord is happy to make you successful and to help your nation grow while you conquer the land. But if you disobey him, he will be just as happy to pull you up by your roots.
text: Ase ku le yɔk Naawen sui ate wa niak ni ale basi ate ni piisi a gum du la, ku le yɔk wa suinni ka dila dekdega ase wa nin kaasi ni. Ba le voori ni kama a ta nyini tɛŋ kaai po ate ni a jo ni tuesi la po.

ref: Those of you that survive will be scattered to every nation on earth, and you will have to worship stone and wood idols that never helped you or your ancestors.
text: Ate Naawen ale basi ate ni waaŋ a bo tɛŋsaŋa meena po a nyini tɛŋka kpeglimka a ta ga paari kauk kunkula. Dula jigini ni yaa le kaab bɔgluk yonta, tii ate ba pai daata ale tana a nye ti la. Tii ate nama yaa ni koma a zɛ ti wie la.

ref: Each morning you will wake up to such terrible sights that you will say, “I wish it were night!” But at night you will be terrified and say, “I wish it were day!”
text: Ni kpaziim ale kasim a nak ate ni le kasim a chali yɔgsum ale wa dii meena ate ni a nya la. Saluik meena ni le kasim a yaali kama ayen ku chim junɔi abe junɔi meena ni kasim a yaali ayen ku chim saluik.

ref: I told you never to go back to Egypt. But now the Lord himself will load you on ships and send you back. Then you will even try to sell yourselves as slaves, but no one will be interested.
text: Naawen ale ta ni ŋman cheŋ Ejipiti ale ŋaaruŋta. Wa le ta ni va suik kuui ate mi a weeni ayen ni kan ŋman nya ku. Ni le yaali ni pai nidek da te ni dachaasaŋa ase yɔm la alege waai a kan da ni.

ref: So Moses finished telling the Israelites what they had to do in order to keep the agreement the Lord was making with them in Moab, which was in addition to the one the Lord had made with them at Mount Sinai. The Third Speech: Israel Must Keep Its Agreement with the Lord The Lord Is Your God
text: Wieŋa de ale nɔiyeŋka wieŋa ate Naawen a weeni Moosis ayen wa nye ale Izirali demma Moab tɛŋka la. Nɔiyeŋ kala a gum chaab ale ka kaai ate wa liŋ jam nye ale ba Yoreb guuku la.

ref: Moses called the nation of Israel together and told them: When you were in Egypt, you saw the Lord perform great miracles that caused trouble for the king, his officials, and everyone else in the country.
text: Ni nya kama ale nidek nina nye nya kaai ale zuak ale wakperikaliisaŋa ale wakinkaglaŋa ate Naawen a nye la kama.

ref: When we first camped here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan attacked, but we defeated them.
text: <<Ase ni dan paari dela jigini, Naab Siyon Yesbon Naawa ale Naab Og Basan Naawa a yaa jam a nye kpaliŋ ale ti, alege ti nak yiak ba.

ref: Then we captured their land and divided it among the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. Keep the Agreement Moses said:
text: Ti jam tuesi ba tɛŋka kama a poori ka a te Aruben ale Gad ale Manasa dɔkku geli.

ref: Israel, the Lord has made an agreement with you, and if you keep your part, you will be successful in everything you do.
text: <<Ni kpesi a va nɔiyeŋ wieŋa de ate dila ale basi ate ni nya niaka dii meena ate ni a nye la po.

ref: Today everyone in our nation is standing here in the Lord's presence, including leaders and officials, parents and children, and even those foreigners who cut wood and carry water for us. We are at this place of worship to promise that we will keep our part of the agreement with the Lord our God.
text: Ni za dela kama ayen ni nye nɔiyeŋ ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, ku ka pumpuulima ŋaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a nye ale ni jinla de ale pɛka,

ref: When we lived in Egypt, you saw the Egyptians worship disgusting idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold. Then as we traveled through other nations, you saw those people worship other disgusting idols.
text: Ni jam nya biem wieŋa ŋaai ate ba jam nye a ta va ba le sɛ daata ale tintana ale kpana ale ligmɔniŋ bɔgta a kaab la kama.

ref: So make sure that everyone in your tribe remains faithful to the Lord and never starts worshiping gods of other nations. If even one of you worships idols, you will be like the root of a plant that produces bitter, poisonous fruit.
text: Ni be a seba a chak ayen nidoa yaase nipok yaase ni dɔkku po jinla de a nye wa suinum po ayen wa kan va Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la abe wa cheŋ a ga a kaab tɛŋ yoŋta bɔgta; ni be kan te suik ate choŋ kula choa a jam ni po.

ref: You may be an Israelite and know all about the Lord's agreement with us, but he won't bless you if you rebel against him. You may think you can get away with it, but you will cause the rest of Israel to be punished along with you.
text: <<Ni be a seba ayen ni po waai a dan wom wieŋa de alege a poli a te wadek ayen wari meena ale nye nalimnyiini a te wa kama ase wa ni poom a nye wadek ale a yaali diila. Kula ale ta kaasuŋ a jam tɛŋka meena zuk.

ref: The Lord will be furious, and instead of forgiving you, he will separate you from the other tribes. Then he will destroy you, by piling on you all the curses in The Book of God's Law, and you will be forgotten forever.
text: Naawen ale yeeri wadek wa nyiini a ta nyini Izirali buuni po a nyini a basi ate kaasuŋ a jam wa jigi a ta va nɔiyeŋka kika sii meena ale ŋmarisi bo sinsaŋŋa gbaŋka de po la.

ref: The Lord will strike your country with diseases and disasters. Your descendants and foreigners from distant countries will see that your land
text: <<Ate chum po ni ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale nichamma baai ale nyini niŋniŋ a jam bo ale ni la ale nya kaasuŋku ale ninam buui ate Naawen a ta jam ni tɛŋka po la.

ref: has become a scorching desert of salt and sulfur, where nothing is planted, nothing sprouts, and nothing grows. It will be as lifeless as the land around the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, after the Lord became angry and destroyed them.
text: Ni tɛŋka a kan nala ate ni a kpa, ka le nye ase ka yesa ale bo ka po la. Ni kan bori Jaab ka po, wuuta a poom kan nyini du mɛ. Ni tɛŋka ale nye ase ka Sodom ale Gomora ale Adma ale Zeboiim tɛŋsaŋa ate Naawen a jam kaasi si meena diipo ate wa suinni a jam puuri ale ba la.

ref: People from other nations will ask, “Why did the Lord destroy this country? Why was he so furious?”
text: Ate tɛŋka meena demma a yaa bek ayen, <Ka boa ate Naawen a nye ba tɛŋka dila? Ka boa ate wa sui a domu?>

ref: And they will be given this answer: Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, but after he brought them out of Egypt and made an agreement with them, they rejected the agreement
