text: <<Tulisaŋa abe nna, <Dii nyiŋla nuruma de a zɛri Naawen, ba koma Wen nɔiyeŋ kaai ate ba nye diipo ate wa jam ta ba a nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka po a nyini la kama.

ref: and decided to worship gods that had never helped them. The Lord had forbidden Israel to worship these gods,
text: Ba jam a kaabka bɔgluk yoŋta ale koori tɛŋ a zuli bɔgluk tii ate ba zɛ, bɔgluk tii ate wa an pai a te ba.

ref: and so he became furious and punished the land with all the curses in The Book of God's Law. Then he pulled up Israel by the roots and tossed them into a foreign country, where they still are today.
text: Naawen suinni a ŋmasi jam a puuri kama, suipuurum bula nyiŋ wa yaa yeeri ba a ta nyini badek tɛŋka po ate a cheŋ tɛŋ yoŋ. Ba bo ka dula jinla de.>

ref: The Lord our God hasn't explained the present or the future, but he has commanded us to obey the laws he gave to us and our descendants.
text: <<Wasusuga meena ka Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la ale soa. Alege wie ŋaai ale kan daa wasusuga la, ka tama ale ti bisaŋa ale soa ŋa taam wuu, dila ale ku basi ate ti a va sinsaŋŋa wieŋa de.>>

ref: I have told you everything the Lord your God will do for you, and I've also told you the curses he will put on you if you reject him. He will scatter you in faraway countries, but when you realize that he is punishing you,
text: <<Mi a te ni ka suik ayen ni lueri a ta nyini niaka ale kikaasa po. Ase wieŋa de meena a dan nye ni alege ate ni dan bo ale tɛŋ sii ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a basi ate ni waaŋ a bo si po la, ni le teeri mi ale weeni ayen ni lueri diila.

ref: Then he will stop punishing you and treat you with kindness. He may have scattered you to the farthest countries on earth, but he will bring you back
text: Ni dan poom a yalima diidii ya, Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale tigsi ni a basi jigi yeŋ a ta ni ŋman jam.

ref: You and your descendants are stubborn, but the Lord will make you willing to obey him and love him with all your heart and soul, and you will enjoy a long life.
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, dek ale te ni ale ni ŋaaŋbisaŋa suiniima ŋaai ate ni a zuli, dii ale ku basi ate ni a yaali Naawen ale ni suiniima meena ale ni chiisa meena ate ni boro.

ref: Then the Lord your God will remove the curses from you and put them on those enemies who hate and attack you.
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, ale tulim kikaasaŋa de meena a te ka ni dachaasaŋa baai ale kisi ni ale a namsi ni la.

ref: You will again obey the laws and teachings of the Lord,
text: Ate nama ale ŋman a zuli Naawen abe ni va wa sinsaŋŋa meena ate mi a te ni jinla de la.

ref: and he will bless you with many children, large herds and flocks, and abundant crops. The Lord will be happy to do good things for you, just as he did for your ancestors.
text: Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale niak ni wa dii meena ate ni a nye la po. Ni bisaŋa ale piisi abe wa niak ni duŋsaŋa mɛ. Ni tattaŋa ale nye ŋandiinta nalimnyiini. Naawen sui ale peenti ate wa basi ate ni jigsi ase wa le jam a basi ate ni koma a jigsi diila.

ref: But you must decide once and for all to worship him with all your heart and soul and to obey everything in The Book of God's Law. Choose Life, Not Death Moses said to Israel:
text: Alege ku a magsi ka ni a wom Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la nɔi abe ni ta wa wieŋa ale wa ŋmarisika ale ŋmarisi a bo wa sinsaŋŋa gbaŋka de po la. Ku a magsi kama ayen ni ŋmani a va Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale ni suiniima meena ale ni chiisa meena.

ref: You know God's laws, and it isn't impossible to obey them.
text: <<Wie ŋaai ate mi a te ni jinla de la vaka an toa yaase ŋa pagra a gaam vaka.

ref: His commands aren't in heaven, so you can't excuse yourselves by saying, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are in heaven, and no one can go up to get them, then bring them down and explain them to us.”
text: Ŋa an bo daa chiŋmaaŋa po ate ni bek ayen, <Ka wana ale wa jueli a ta ŋa a jam ate ti wom abe ti va ŋa?>

ref: And you can't say, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are across the sea, and someone must go across, then bring them back and explain them to us.”
text: Yaa ŋa boka nyakpiemu kauk kunkula ate ti bek ayen ka wana ale wa lo beni a jueli a mooli a sak ti ate ti va ŋa?

ref: No, these commands are nearby and you know them by heart. All you have to do is obey!
text: Aaya, wanni a moata ni kama, a bo ni noa po ale ni suiniima po. Dila nyiŋla ku a magsi kama ayen ni va ŋa.

ref: Today I am giving you a choice. You can choose life and success or death and disaster.
text: <<Ni nya jinla de m te ni ka nyuvuri ale niaka, kum ale kaasuŋ

ref: Now I call the sky and the earth to be witnesses that I am offering you this choice. Will you choose for the Lord to make you prosperous and give you a long life? Or will he put you under a curse and kill you? Choose life!
text: <<Jinla mi a wi ka wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋ ate ba chim mi seerɔba ayen ni lueri nyuvuri ale niaka yaase kum ale kikaasa. Yɔgyɔgla de ni be lueri nyuvuri dii ale ku basi ate nama ale ni bisaŋa a vua.

ref: Be completely faithful to the Lord your God, love him, and do whatever he tells you. The Lord is the only one who can give life, and he will let you live a long time in the land that he promised to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
text: Yaali Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, wom wa lueluku abe ni va wa nalimnyiini. Ale ka wa ale ni nyuvunni, wala ale wa te ni bena piisi tɛŋka ate Naawen puulim ayen wa le te ni koma, Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob la.>>

ref: Moses again spoke to the whole nation of Israel:
text: Ate Moosis a yaa nyini peelim a weeni wieŋa de meena a te Izirali demma ayen,

ref: Be brave and strong! Don't be afraid of the nations on the other side of the Jordan. The Lord your God will always be at your side, and he will never abandon you.
text: Ni pagra abe ni chiib a zaani. Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa yaase ni nyiŋsa a gɔgi ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a cheŋ ale ni kama, wa kan basi ni yaase wa zɛri ni mɛ.>>

ref: Then Moses called Joshua up in front of the crowd and said: Joshua, be brave and strong as you lead these people into their land. The Lord made a promise long ago to Israel's ancestors that this land would someday belong to Israel. That time has now come, and you must divide up the land among the people.
text: Ate Moosis a yaa wi Josua a weeni wa Izirali demma meena niŋ ayen, <<Be a pagra abe fi chiib a zaani, fi ale nuruma ale magsi ni ga jo tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen a puulim ale ba kokpieŋsaŋa ayen wa te ba la, abe fi poori tɛŋka a chari ba ase ba tiirim la.

ref: The Lord will lead you into the land. He will always be with you and help you, so don't ever be afraid of your enemies. Read These Laws
text: Naawen dek a dɛ ka ni niŋ a cheŋ wa le bo ale ni, wa kan basi ni yaase wa zɛri ni. Kan chali yɔgsummoa; kan jɔgi nyiŋbiiri.>>

ref: Moses wrote down all of these laws and teachings and gave them to the priests and the leaders of Israel. The priests were from the Levi tribe, and they carried the sacred chest that belonged to the Lord.
text: Moosis a yaa jam ŋmarisi sinsaŋŋa de a yaa pai ŋa a te kaabteerɔma Livai bisaŋa baai ale a ji Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni la ale Izirali nisɔmma meena.

ref: Moses told these priests and leaders: Each year the Israelites must come together to celebrate the Festival of Shelters at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. You must read these laws and teachings to the people at the festival every seventh year, the year when loans do not need to be repaid.
text: Ase Izirali demma meena a dan jam Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋ kauk kuui ate wa lueri ayen ni a puusi wa la, fi yaa kariŋ sinsaŋŋa de a te ba wom.

ref: Everyone must come—men, women, children, and even the foreigners who live in your towns. And each new generation will listen and learn to worship the Lord their God with fear and trembling and to do exactly what is said in God's Law. Israel Will Reject the Lord
text: Ba bisaŋa baai ale kan seba sinsaŋŋa de la a magsi ba wom abe ba zamsi di ate ba a chali Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la diipo meena ate ni bo tɛŋ kaai po ate ni lo Jodan benni a jueli ka po la.>>

ref: The Lord told Moses, “You will soon die, so bring Joshua to the sacred tent, and I will appoint him the leader of Israel.” Moses and Joshua went to the sacred tent,
text: Naawen a weeni Moosis ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de fi kummu danni a moata kama. Wi Josua a pai fidek a sak wa viuku po, kauk kuui ate mi ale gomsi wa a magsi la,>> ate Moosis ale Josua a yaa ta badek a jam viuku po ba tuka jigini.

ref: and the Lord appeared in a thick cloud right over the entrance to the tent.
text: Ate Naawen a yaa jam viuku po ase chiŋmari la ate chiŋmanni a yaa za viuku nansuiŋku nɔi.

ref: The Lord said: Moses, you will soon die. But Israel is going into a land where other gods are worshiped, and Israel will reject me and start worshiping these gods. The people will break the agreement I made with them,
text: Ate Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Fi a yaa fi cheŋ a ga vuusi ale ka fi koma, ate nuruma de ale cheŋ a ga pai badek a te bɔgluk chaŋsa a se jentirisa la tɛŋ kaai po ate ba a cheŋ ba jo ka po la. Ba le zɛri mu abe ba kaasi nɔiyeŋ kaai ate mi a jam nye ale ba la.

ref: and I will be so furious that I will abandon them and ignore their prayers. I will send disasters and suffering that will nearly wipe them out. Finally, they will realize that the disasters happened because I abandoned them.
text: Dai dila danni m sui ale puuri ale ba ate m zɛri ba; m le viriŋ, m ninaŋa a basi nakpiak abe m kaasi ba. Kaasuŋ ale wa pagrisa ale piisi a jam ni jigi, ate dai dila danni ba le bek ayen, <<Kaasuŋku de ale jam tama jigi la ti Wenni a ka ale ti?

ref: They will pray to me, but I will ignore them because they were evil and started worshiping other gods.
text: Ate m le viriŋ m ninaŋa a basi nakpiak dai dila danni gaasa wie ŋaai ate ba nye a ta va chaab ale bɔgluk yoŋta kaabka la nyiŋ.

ref: I am bringing them into the land that I promised their ancestors. It is a land rich with milk and honey, and the Israelites will have more than enough food to eat. But they will get fat and turn their backs on me and start worshiping other gods. The Israelites will reject me and break the agreement that I made with them.
text: M le ta ba a cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ale jigsi ale poagi a magsi kpari la po, ase m le puulim ale ba kokpieŋsaŋa diila. Dula jigini ba le ta ŋandiin tii meena ate ba a yaali la abe ba boro nalimnyiini wari a kan daani ba. Alege ba le tulim a kaabi bɔgluk yoŋta. Ba le zɛri mu abe ba kaasi nɔiyeŋ kaai ate m nye ale ba la.

ref: When I punish the Israelites and their descendants with suffering and disasters, I will remind them that they know the words to this song, so they have no excuse for not obeying me. I will give them the land that I promised, but I know the way they are going to live later on.
text: Ate kaasuŋ m na yegayega ale jam ba jigi. Alege ba dan lenni yiini dɛ di le teeri ba. Yɔgyɔgla de alege jigi ate mi a poom ta ba a cheŋ tɛŋ kaai po ate mi a puulim ayen m le te ba la, m seba dii ate ba a poli la kama.>>

ref: Moses at once wrote down the words to the song, and he taught it to the Israelites.
text: Dai dila danni dek Moosis a ŋmarisi yiini kama ale sak Izirali demma di lennika.

ref: The Lord told Joshua, “Be brave and strong! I will help you lead the people of Israel into the land that I have promised them.”
text: Ate Naawen a yaa biisi ale Josua Nun biika a weeni wa ayen, <Be pagra abe fi chiib a zaani. Fi ale dɛ Izirali demma niŋ a ta ba jo tɛŋ kaai ate m puulim ayen m te ba la po, m le bo ale fu.>>

ref: Moses wrote down all these laws and teachings in a book,
text: Moosis a jam ŋmarisi Naawen sinsaŋŋa a nyo ka gbaŋ po ale kpesi wadek nalimnyiini an tali wari a basi ya.

ref: then he went to the Levites who carried the sacred chest and said:
text: Moosis le jam nueri la, wa yaa a weeni Livaima baai ale jam a ji Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni la ayen,

ref: This is The Book of God's Law. Keep it beside the sacred chest that holds the agreement the Lord your God made with Israel. This book is proof that you know what the Lord wants you to do.
text: <<Ni pai Naawen sinsaŋŋa de a magi Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la nɔiyeŋka dakanni nyiŋ ate ku le, kasim a bo dula a teeri wa nuruma.

ref: I know how stubborn and rebellious you and the rest of the Israelites are. You have rebelled against the Lord while I have been alive, and it will only get worse after I am gone.
text: Mi a seba tukpari dii ate ba ta la nɔi po kama. Ba jam zɛri Naawen kama diipo ate mi jam vua la, ba be za ba diem a zɛri wa kama mi kummu ŋaaŋnyiŋ.

ref: So call together the leaders and officials of the tribes of Israel. I will bring this book and read every word of it to you, and I will call the sky and the earth as witnesses that all of you know what you are supposed to do.
text: Tigsi ni dɔkku po niŋdeerɔma ale kpaŋŋa meena m niŋ ate m weeni ba wieŋa de; m le wi ka wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋ ate ba chim mi seerɔba mi ale nama suŋsuŋ.

ref: I am going to die soon, and I know that in the future you will stop caring about what is right and what is wrong, and so you will disobey the Lord and stop living the way I told you to live. The Lord will be angry, and terrible things will happen to you. The Song of Moses
text: Mi a seba kama ayen mi kummu ŋaaŋnyiŋ nuruma ale ta ka gaasa abe ba zɛri dii ate mi a sak ba la. Ku be kan beni ba le nya kaasuŋ dii nyiŋla ba le nye ate Naawen sui a puuri, a ta va wie ŋaai ate wa kisa la.>>

ref: Earth and Sky, listen to what I say!
text: Wom wenŋmazuk wa, mi a yaa m biisi kama; wom tɛŋŋa, wieŋa m nɔnni po.

ref: Join with me in praising the wonderful name of the Lord our God.
text: M le mooli Naawen yuenni, ate wa nuruma a weeni wa zuaka ale ka diila.

ref: The Lord is a mighty rock, and he never does wrong. God can always be trusted to bring justice.
text: Wa ka piuŋ wa tuimaŋa kaasuŋ a ka du wa suitaŋa a nye cheri. Naawen dii ale ta wensie la, waai ale kan nye wari a kaasi. Wa ka waai ale ta wayɔrisima ale nye a magsi.

ref: But you lie and cheat and are unfaithful to him. You have disgraced yourselves and are no longer worthy to be his children.
text: Ba an nye dii ate wa a yaali ayen ba nye la; chivie a yik ba kama dii nyiŋla ba ŋman daa wa bisa. Ba ka wabaata nyam ale nuru baai ale kan ta wensie.

ref: Israel, the Lord is your Father, the one who created you, but you repaid him by being foolish.
text: Ka ku le magsi ni nye Naawen diila ale la? Ni ka betta, nuru baai ale kan ta yammoa. Wa daa nama Ko ale ni Nyeerɔ? Daa wa ale nye ni a basi ate ni boro?

ref: that God Most High gave land to every nation. He assigned a guardian angel to each of them,
text: Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La ale a te tɛŋsa ba le magsi ba soa juijui la; Wa le poori nuru bisa la, Wa te ba ka bana a magsi Izirali bisaŋa nɔi ale ka diila.

ref: but the Lord himself takes care of Israel.
text: Naawen nuruma ka wa a le soa, Jekob ŋaaŋbisaŋa ka wadek ale soa.

ref: The Lord was like an eagle teaching its young to fly, always ready to swoop down and catch them on its back.
text: Ase jiiruk ale a sak ku bisa yiri ka dii ale chɔgsi si dii ale ku kinkaŋŋa ate si kan lo tɛŋ diila, Naawen mɛ a nya Izirali demma zuk ka dila ate ba kan lo.

ref: Israel, the Lord led you, and without the aid of a foreign god,
text: Naawen dek wa nyiini ale dɛ wa nuruma niŋ, wa jam kan yaali bɔgluk chaŋsa maarika.

ref: he helped you capture the land. Your fields were rich with grain. Olive trees grew in your stony soil, and honey was found among the rocks.
text: Wa jam basi kama ate ni nya pagrim tɛŋsaŋa zuk. Ni tattaŋa mɛ a jam ta ŋandiinta. Olivi tiisaŋa mɛ a jam a chim tɛŋ kaai ale ta tintana la po, alege basi ate siita a bo pinaŋa po ate ni a dɛ.

ref: Your flocks and herds produced milk and yogurt, and you got choice meat from your sheep and goats that grazed in Bashan. Your wheat was the finest, and you drank the best wine.
text: Ba niiŋa ale ba booŋa a jam a te ba ka biisim nna yegayega; ba jam ta ka pa ŋaai ale bo ŋaai ale naa ŋaai ale chim duŋ maŋsa la. Ba jam maa ta ka za ale daam.

ref: You made God jealous and angry by worshiping disgusting idols and foreign gods.
text: Ba bɔgtaŋa a jam basi kama ate Wen a dɛ nyuri alege ba biemu mɛ a nye ate wa sui a puuri.

ref: You turned away from God, your Creator; you forgot the Mighty Rock, the source of your life.
text: Ba baŋ ba Wen dii ale ka Piuŋ la kama ba varibasidɔ kpioŋku waai ale te ba nyuvuri la.

ref: You were the Lord's children, but you made him angry. Then he rejected you
text: Ase Naawen ale nya kude la wa sui a yaa puuri ate wa zɛri wa bisaŋa ale wa liema.

ref: and said, “You are unfaithful and can't be trusted. So I won't answer your prayers; I'll just watch and see what happens to you.
text: Mi a kan ŋman a maari ni diipo diipo wa ale weeni diila a ni la m le nya dii ale ku nye tukpari nyama ale nuru baai ale kan ta siaka la.

ref: “My people, I will breathe out fire that sends you down to the world of the dead. It will scorch your farmlands and burn deep down under the mountains.
text: M suipuurumu ale nye ase bolim la a dɛ jaab meena tɛŋka zuk bu le paari tɛŋka meena a dɛ jaab meena.

ref: “I wanted to scatter you, so no one would remember that you had ever lived.
text: M weeni kama ayen m ti waaŋ ba kama ale yeeri ba nurubisa suŋsuŋ,

ref: But I dreaded the sound of your enemies saying, ‘We defeated Israel with no help from the Lord.’ ”
text: alege mi chali ka dachaasaŋa suiniima nakka, ba kan miŋi a weeni ayen, ba nya ka pagrim, daa Naawen ale nye nnawa meena.

ref: People of Israel, that's what the Lord has said to you. But you don't have good sense, and you never listen to advice.
text: Izirali tɛŋka demma ka baai ale kan ta popola; ba bola ka yam ale magadek mɛ la.

ref: If you did, you could see where you are headed.
text: Ba an miŋi jabuui nyiŋ ate ba nak a yik ba la; ba kan miŋ wa dii ale nye la.

ref: How could one enemy soldier chase a thousand of Israel's troops? Or how could two of theirs pursue ten thousand of ours? It can only happen if the Lord stops protecting Israel and lets the enemy win.
text: Ka boa ale soa ate nuru yeŋ a baga a nya pagrim nuruba tusidi zuwa yaase nuruba tusa ŋaye (

ref: Even our enemies know that only our God is a Mighty Rock.
text: Ba dachaasaŋa a seba kama ayen badek bɔgtaŋa a wobsa kama, ti an pagra ase Izirali Wenni la.

ref: Our enemies are grapevines rooted in the fields of Sodom and Gomorrah. The grapes they produce are full of bitter poison;
text: Ba dachaasaŋa a bie kama ase Sodom ale Gomora demma la alege a nye ase tiib sii yɔna ale tua ase choŋ la.

ref: their wine is more deadly than cobra venom.
text: Ba a nye ase ka daam ate ba pai waapiik sim a nyoro la.

ref: But the Lord has written a list of their sins and locked it in his vault.
text: Naawen a teeri dii ate ba dachaasaŋa a nye ba la kama; wa a limisi kama ayen di danni a paari ate wa namsi ba.

ref: When only a few of the Lord's people remain, when their strength is gone, and some of them are slaves, the Lord will feel sorry for them and give them justice.
text: Naawen ale bo wa nuruma buusa. Wa le ta jiirim ale ba ase wa nin nya ale ba pagrimu a nueri ya, ate waai an tali ya, baai ale ka yɔm ale baai ale kan daa yɔm la.

ref: But first the Lord will say, “You ran for safety to other gods— couldn't they help you?
text: Ate Naawen a yaa le bek wa nuruma ayen, <Bɔgluk kpieŋ tii ate ni ta siaka ale ti la a boka bɛ?

ref: Don't you understand? I am the only God; there are no others. I am the one who takes life and gives it again. I punished you with suffering. But now I will heal you, and nothing can stop me!
text: Mi dek nyiini ale Naawen. Wen yoŋ a ŋman karo a gum mi po. Mi ale a ko ale a te nyuvuri mɛ. Mi ale a te nuruba tuem mɛ abe le ŋmaa tebi ba mɛ ate waai a karo a zɛri dii ate mi a nye la.

ref: “I make this solemn promise: Just as I live forever,
text: Ase mi ale ka Naawen dii ale vua la, mi zak ka m nisaŋa ale pɛ ayen,

ref: I will take revenge on my hateful enemies. I will sharpen my sword and let it flash like lightning.
text: m le saasi ka m gebika kaai ale a nyaksi la a nye dii ale magsi la. Mi ale nye a tuni m dachaasaŋa ale nye diila abe m namsi baai ale kisi mu la.

ref: My arrows will get drunk on enemy blood; my sword will taste the flesh and the blood of the enemy. It will kill prisoners, and cut off the heads of their leaders.”
text: Mi peeŋa ale feri ba ziimu po abe m gebika mɛ ko baai meena ale a zɛri mu la, baai ale kɔni la ale baai ate ba yik lik likka diina po meena la ale kpi.

ref: Tell the heavens to celebrate and all gods to bow down to the Lord, because he will take revenge on those hateful enemies who killed his people. He will forgive the sins of Israel and purify their land.
text: Tɛŋsa ku a fɛ kama ayen ni pak Naawen ale wa nuruma. Wa nye tuni wa dachaasaŋa ale nye wa diila kama alege a vɔŋ wa nuruma biemu a te ba.>>

ref: Moses spoke the words of the song so that all the Israelites could hear, and Joshua helped him. When Moses had finished,
text: Ase Moosis ale jam sak Naawen nuruma a ga nueri la,

ref: he said, “Always remember this song I have taught you today. And let it be a warning that you must teach your children to obey everything written in The Book of God's Law.
text: Wa weeni ayen, <<Ni seba a chak ayen ni a va sinsaŋŋa de meena ate mi a te ni jinla de la. Ni ŋman pai ŋa a sak ni bisaŋa, dii ale ku basi ate ba va Naawen sinsaŋŋa meena.

ref: The Law isn't empty words. It can give you a long life in the land that you are going to take.” Moses Will See the Land
text: Sinsaŋŋa de a daa sinsak koruta; ŋa ka ni nyuvooŋa. Ni va ŋa ate ni goa a beni tɛŋ kaai ate ni le lo Jodan benni jueli a bo ka po la.>>

ref: Later that day the Lord said to Moses:
text: Da dila danni dek ate Naawen a weeni Moosis ayen,

ref: Go up into the Abarim Mountain range here in Moab across the Jordan River valley from Jericho. And when you reach the top of Mount Nebo, you will be able to see the land of Canaan, which I am giving to Israel.
text: <<Cheŋ Abarim guutaŋa zuk Moab tɛŋka po ate ka le Jeriko a kala a tuk chaab la; jueli Nebo guuku zuk a nya Keenan tɛŋka a te mi a yaali m pai ate Izirali demma la.

ref: Then you will die and be buried on the mountaintop, just as your brother Aaron died and was buried on Mount Hor.
text: Fi ale kpi ka guuk kula zuk ase fi suoku Aaron ale jam Yor Guuku zuk a kpi la,

ref: Both of you were unfaithful to me at Meribah Spring near Kadesh in the Zin Desert. I am God, but there in front of the Israelites, you did not treat me with the honor and respect I deserve.
text: dii nyiŋla ni nɔi niyema a jam ka siaka ale mi Izirali demma niŋŋa. Ni le jam Meriba nyaataŋa jigini ate ku moata Kades Zin gɔnni po la, ni an jam a nye mi ase waai ale ta tuilum la.

ref: So I will give the land to the people of Israel, but you will only get to see it from a distance.
text: Fi le zaani ka niŋ a nya tɛŋka, alege fi kan jo tɛŋ kaai ate mi a yaa m pai te Izirali demma la.>>

ref: Moses was a prophet, and before he died, he blessed the tribes of Israel by saying:
text: Niaka de Moosis Naawen nuruwa a biisi te Izirali demma alege kpi,

ref: The Lord came from Mount Sinai. From Edom, he gave light to his people, and his glory was shining from Mount Paran. Thousands of his warriors were with him, and fire was at his right hand.
text: Naawen a yaa jam Sinai guuku zuk; wa jam a yiti ase wenbinni ale bo Seir tɛŋka zuk diila a yaa jam a nyaksi diipo ate wa nuruma a jam bo Paran guuku zuk la. Maarɔba tusa pi ale jam bo ale wa, ate bolim ŋiak a jam bo wa juga nisaŋa po.

ref: The Lord loves the tribes of Israel, and he protects his people. They listen to his words and worship at his feet. *
text: Naawen a yaali wa nuruma kama ale a kasi baai ate wa soa la. Dila nyiŋ ti a koori ka wa niŋ abe ti wom wa sinsaŋŋa.

ref: I called a meeting of the tribes of Israel and gave you God's Law.
text: Ti le va sinsaŋŋa ŋaai ate Moosis a te la, ti tɛŋka tuilum jaab a magsi ta ka.

ref: Tribe of Reuben, you will live, even though your tribe will always be small.
text: Moosis a yaa jam weeni Aruben ayen, Aruben dɔkku a kan kpi meena, ba an soa diiya alege ba le boro.

ref: The Lord will listen to you, tribe of Judah, as you beg to come safely home. You fought your enemies alone; now the Lord will help you.
text: Juda dɔkku mɛ wa weeni ayen, Naawen a wom ba kaarika abe wa maari ba; basi ate ba ta nɔiyeŋ ale buura m ŋala. Naawen, kpaliŋ a te ba.

ref: Protecting Israel's agreement with the Lord was more important to you than the life of your father or mother, or brothers or sisters, or your own children.
text: Ba jam sak ba yaali kpieŋka ale fu kama a gaam ba nyam ale ba suata ale bisaŋa ate ba ta yaalika ale ba diila. Ba an jam zɛri fi wieŋa. Ba jam ta siaka ale fi nɔiyeŋka kama.

ref: You teach God's laws to Israel, and at the place of worship you offer sacrifices and burn incense.
text: Ba le sak fi nuruma ate ba kan zɛri fi sinsaŋŋa; ba le nye kaabka fi yenni po a te fu.

ref: I pray that the Lord will bless everything you do, and make you strong enough to crush your enemies.
text: Naawen maari ba buuni po ate ba chim abe ba ta pagrim. Ta suipeentik ale dii meena ate ba a nye la. Ko ba dachaasaŋa meena kan basi ate ba ŋman yiti.

ref: Descendants of Joseph, the Lord will bless you with precious water from deep wells and with dew from the sky.
text: Wa weeni Josefi dɔkku mɛ ayen, Naawen a niak ba tɛŋka ale ŋmoruk abe nyiam mɛ a bo tɛŋ a yɔk tɛŋka.

ref: You will have a rich harvest from the slopes of the ancient hills.
text: Ba guutaŋa zuk a kasim a ta ka yɔna ŋaai ate ba a yaali la.

ref: The Lord who appeared in the burning bush wants to give you the best the land can produce, and it will be a princely crown on Joseph's head.
text: Ba tɛŋka a kasim a sueri ale ka ŋan maŋsa meena ale niaka a nyini Naawen jigi, waai ale jam bo bolimu ale a dɛ gɔnni po a biisi la. Niaka de abe jam Josefi dɔkku jigi dii nyiŋla wala ale niŋdeerɔ wa suataŋa zuk.

ref: The armies of Ephraim and Manasseh are majestic and fierce like a bull or a wild ox. They will run their spears through faraway nations.
text: Josefi pagrimu a jam a nye ase ka lalik ale a kpa la ate wa pagra ase ka Ɛfraim dɔkku tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa pi la, alege a nye ase Manasa dɔkku tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa la.

ref: Be happy, Zebulun, as your boats set sail; be happy, Issachar, in your tents.
text: Wa weeni Zebulun dɔkku ayen, Ni ta suipeentik ase nama ale a nyini peelim alege a weeni Isaka dɔkku ayen nama mɛ ale jigsi ni yeeŋa po.

ref: The sea will make you wealthy, and from the sandy beach you will get treasure. So invite the other tribes to celebrate with you and offer sacrifices to God.
text: Ba le wi nuruba ate ba jam guuku zuk ate ba nye kaab maŋ dula jigini. Ba le nya ba ŋanta ka nyakpiemu po ale tintain busuŋ bu po.

ref: Tribe of Gad, the Lord will bless you with more land. So shout his praises! Your tribe is like a lion ripping up its victim.
text: Gad dɔkku mɛ wa weeni ba ayen, Pak Naawen waai ale nye ate Gad dɔkku a piisi la. Gad a bo dula kama ase gbeŋli la ayen wa kaasi.

ref: Your leaders met together and chose the best land for your tribe, but you obeyed the Lord and helped the other tribes.
text: Ba jam lueri ka tɛŋ kaai ale nala la a te badek, Niŋdeerɔma mɛ a jam nya ka tɛŋ maŋ a te ba dɔkku. Ba jam zuli Naawen kama a maari buuri yɔnaŋa.

ref: Tribe of Dan, you are like a lion cub, startled by a snake.
text: Dan dɔkku mɛ wa weeni ba ayen, Fi ka gbeŋ paali; fi nyini ka Basan.

ref: The Lord is pleased with you, people of Naphtali. He will bless you and give you the land to the west and the south.
text: Nafitali dɔkku wa weeni ba mɛ ayen, Naawen a niak fu kama ale wa jiirim maŋka; Ba tɛŋka paari Galili nyakpiemu kama.

ref: The Lord's greatest blessing is for you, tribe of Asher. You will be the favorite of all the other tribes. You will be rich with olive oil
text: Asɛ dɔkku wa weeni ba ayen, Asɛ a nya niaka a gaam buura m ŋala meena kama. Wa nyeka abe masa a te wa suataŋa abe wa tɛŋka po kpaam tiisa a kasim a boro.

ref: and have strong town gates with bronze and iron bolts. Your people will be powerful for as long as they live.
text: Wa tɛŋka a nye ase ka kuta tuok ale lik la ate wa le kasim boro ale suiyɔgni.

ref: Israel, no other god is like ours— the clouds are his chariot as he rides across the skies to come and help us.
text: Wen a karo ase Izirali Wenni la, waai ale nyini wenŋmazuk a maari ni la.

ref: The eternal God is our hiding place; he carries us in his arms. When God tells you to destroy your enemies, he will make them run.
text: Wen ale kasim a maari ni; wa nisaŋa a kasim a maari ni kama. Wa ale yiak ni dachaasaŋa a basi, ni ale weeni ayen ni ko ba meena.

ref: Israel, you will live in safety; your enemies will be gone. The dew will fall from the sky, and you will have plenty of grain and wine.
text: Dila nyiŋ Jekob ŋaaŋbisa ni boro ale suiyɔgni wari a kan daani ni. Tɛŋka ka za ale damasik ale bo ka po, dula jigini maglim ale nyini chiŋmaaŋa po a lo tɛŋka.

ref: The Lord has rescued you and given you more blessings than any other nation. He protects you like a shield and is your majestic sword. Your enemies will bow in fear, and you will trample on their backs.
text: Izirali demma nya suipeentik kaai ate ni ta la! Waai a karo a nye ase nama la. Ni ka tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen a vari basi. Wadek ale ni kasidɔ ale ni maarɔ ale ni gebik a nya ni zuk. Ni dachaasaŋa ale jam a saalim ayen ni ta jiirim ale ba ate ni le ko ba.

ref: Sometime later, Moses left the lowlands of Moab. He went up Mount Pisgah to the peak of Mount Nebo, which is across the Jordan River from Jericho. The Lord showed him all the land as far north as Gilead and the town of Dan.
text: Ate Moosis a yaa jam nyini Moab tɛŋka a ga jueli Nebo guuku ale Pisga guuku ale bo Jeriko kori geŋsa la, dula jigini ate Naawen a pai tɛŋka meena a sak wa. Wa jam nya Gilead tɛŋka a ta ga paari tɛŋ kaai ate ba a wi ayen Dan la;

ref: He let Moses see the territories that would soon belong to the tribes of Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Judah, as far west as the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Nafitali tɛŋka meena ale Ɛfraim ale Manasa ale Juda tɛŋka meena a ta ga paari nyakpiemu yeniŋ geŋsa,

ref: The Lord also showed him the land in the south, from the valley near the town of Jericho, known as The City of Palm Trees, down to the town of Zoar.
text: Juda yeseok geŋka ale Zoar ale Jeriko tɛŋsaŋa tɛŋ kaai ate kpinkpatta a bo ka po la, wa jam nya si meena kama.

ref: The Lord said, “Moses, this is the land I was talking about when I solemnly promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that I would give land to their descendants. I have let you see it, but you will not cross the Jordan and go in.”
text: Ate Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Tɛŋka de ate m puulim ale Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob ayen m le pai ka a te ba ŋaaŋbisaŋa la. Mi basi ate fi a nya ka kama alege m kan basi ate fi jo ka po.

ref: And so, Moses the Lord's servant died there in Moab, just as the Lord had said.
text: Moosis Naawen tomteerɔwa a yaa jam kpi Moab tɛŋka po ase Naawen ale weeni diila.

ref: The people of Israel stayed in the lowlands of Moab, where they mourned and grieved
text: Izirali demma a jam kum wa nyiŋ a paari ka daa pisita Moab tɛŋka po.

ref: Before Moses died, he had placed his hands on Joshua, and the Lord had given Joshua wisdom. The Israelites paid attention to what Joshua said and obeyed the commands that the Lord had given Moses. Moses Was a Great Prophet
text: Josua Nun biika Naawen chiika a yaa jam sueri wa dii nyiŋla Moosis a jam lueri wa kama ayen wa zaani wa nankula po. Ate Izirali demma a yaa va Josua ale ta sinsaŋŋa ate Naawen a jam ta va Moosis zuk a te ba la.

ref: There has never again been a prophet in Israel like Moses. The Lord spoke face to face with him
text: Biisiteerɔ a jam ka Izirali tɛŋka po ase Moosis la, a jam paari jinla. Naawen a jam a nya wa kama ate ba a biisi ale chaab.

ref: and sent him to perform powerful miracles in the presence of the king of Egypt and his entire nation.
text: Biisiteerɔ a jam karo a nye wakinkagla ale wakperikaliisa ase ŋaai ate Naawen a jam basi ate Moosis a nye Ejipiti Naawa ale wa niŋdeerɔma nyiŋ diila Ejipiti tɛŋka po.

ref: No one else has ever had the power to do such great things as Moses did for everyone to see.
text: Biisiteerɔ waai an jam baga a nye wakpiema ŋaai ate Moosis a jam nye a te Izirali demma meena la a nya.

ref: Moses, the Lord's servant, was dead. So the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, who had been the assistant of Moses. The Lord said:
text: Naawen tomteerɔwa Moosis kummu ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate Naawen a yaa weeni Nun nidoabinni Josua waai ale pai a vi Moosis ŋaaŋ la ayen,

ref: My servant Moses is dead. Now you must lead Israel across the Jordan River into the land I'm giving to all of you.
text: <<Moosis m tomteerɔwa a kpi kama. Yɔgyɔgla de fi ale Izirali demma meena a gomsi ate ni lo Jodan Benni a jueli a jo tɛŋ kaai ate mi a yaali m te Izirali demma la po.

ref: Wherever you go, I'll give you that land, as I promised Moses.
text: Mi ale pai kauk kuui meena ate ni pai naŋ a tabi du la ase mi ale puulim ale Moosis diila.

ref: It will reach from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains in the north, and to the northeast as far as the great Euphrates River. It will include the land of the Hittites, and the land from here at the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea on the west.
text: Ni tɛŋka ale zaani ka gɔnni ale bo yeseoku la, a ta ga paari tɛŋ kaai ate ba a wi ka ayen Lebanon ale bo wiilukku geŋsa la a ta ga va Yufiretis beli kpienni ale bo Yit demma tɛŋka po kori geŋsa la a ta ga paari Nyakpiemu ale bo yeniŋ geŋsa la.

ref: Joshua, I will always be with you and help you as I helped Moses, and no one will ever be able to defeat you.
text: Waai a kan boro a baga a zaani ale fu daa ŋaai meena ate fu vua la po. Ase mi ale jam bo ale Moosis diila m le bo ale fu ka dila mɛ. M kan basi fu yaase m zɛri fu.

text: Nuruma ale ga wom damunsaŋa peeri ka la, ba yaa kaari nna zigzig, ate Jeriko tɛŋka parika ale se gilim ka la a yaa deri lo meena a paari tɛŋ. Izirali bisaŋa a yaa deri chali jo tɛŋka po a nak nuruma a vari ka.

ref: After Jericho was destroyed, Joshua warned the people, “Someday a man will rebuild Jericho, but the Lord will put a curse on him, and the man's oldest son will die when he starts to build the town wall. And by the time he finishes the wall and puts gates in it, all his children will be dead.”
text: Va ŋala po Josua a jam pɛ a basi Jeriko tɛŋka nyiŋ ayen, <<Naawen ka te waai ale nye wa popola ayen wa ŋman se Jeriko tɛŋka la. Dai dii danni ate wa a piilim ka nyubini la wa bikpagni kpi. Wa ale a su tɛŋka nansuiŋtaŋa dai dii danni la wa nisa po biika me kpi.>>

ref: The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
text: Naawen a yaa jam bo ale Josua ate wa yuei a yiti tɛŋ kala meena po.

ref: The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
text: Alege Izirali bisaŋa a ta va ŋan baai ale kan magsi ayen ba pai ba la. Achan ate wa kowa a jam chim Karmi la ate Zabdi a chim wa ko kpieŋ ate ba nyini Zera. Juda dɔkku ale la. Ate Naawen sui yaa jam puuri ale ba.

ref: Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset.
text: Josua yaa cheeri wa kɔlimaŋa ale lo tɛŋ Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni niŋ a doa dula a ta ga paari wenbalinni. Izirali nisɔmma mɛ a jam nye ka di la dekdega ale nye paasuk a basi ba zuimaŋa po.

ref: Then Joshua said: Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
text: Ate Josua yaa weeni ayen, <<Aa! Nyɔnɔwa waai ale ka Naawen la, ka boa ale soa ate fi ta nuruma de a lo Jodan benni a jueli ayen fi pai ti a nyo Amori demma nisima po ate ba kaasi ti? Tama a dan poom bo Jodan benni kauk kunkula ku ti le zunchoŋŋa.

ref: I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy.
text: Nyɔnɔ, mi a yaa ayen m weeni ayen ka boa, yɔgyɔgla de dachaasaŋa ale vi Izirali ate ba chali la?

ref: Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
text: Keenan ale nuru mbala tɛŋka po ale wom di la ate ba ale jam gilim ti a basi suŋsuŋ a ko ti ate tama yuei a kan ŋman bo tɛŋka po fi ale nye fi yuei kpienni ka sɛ?>>

ref: The Lord answered: Stop lying there on the ground! Get up!
text: Naawen a yaa weeni Josua ayen, <<Yiti zaani fi pai fi ninaŋa a vuk tɛŋ a nye ka boa?

ref: I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it.
text: Izirali demma nye ka biem ba zɛri m nɔiyeŋka ate nye ale ba la kama, dii ate mi a weeni ba ayen ba tara la. Ba pai ŋan baai ale kan magsi ayen ba pai la kama, ba zu kama ale ŋman velim mɛ ba pai ba a gum ka badek ŋantaŋa po.

ref: What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
text: Dila ale soa ate Izirali demma a kan baga a zaani ale ba dachaasaŋa la. Ba viriŋ ba ŋaaŋ a chali dii nyiŋla ba seba ayen ba ale ko ba kama. Mi a kan ŋman bo ale ni ka nama a nin kaasi ŋan baai ale magsi ni kaasi ba la.

ref: Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
text: Cheŋ ga gaari nuruma a magsi, weeni ba ayen ba gaari badek a magsi chum ale Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Ŋan baai ale kan magsi ayen ni ta la a bo ni po kama, Izirali demma, ni kan baga a zaani ale ni dachaasaŋa ka nama a nin yeeri ba ni po.

ref: “Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come,
text: <<Saluik buuri meena zaani di beŋ di beŋ. Buui dii ate Naawen a lueri la a jam niŋ yeri zuk yeri zuk. Yeri zuk kuui ate Naawen a lueri la a jam niŋ dɔk ku buuri dɔk ku buuri; ate dɔk buuri dii ate Naawen a lueri la nuru yeŋ meena a jam niŋ.

ref: and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
text: Waai ate ti le yik ale ŋanta baai ale kan daa wa ŋanta la ti ale ju wa ale bolim ale ŋan baai meena ate wa soa la. Wa zɛri Naawen nɔiyeŋka kama alege ta chivie a jam Izirali po.>>

ref: Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty.
text: Dai dii ale pai a saŋ la saluik yokyokwa Josua a basi ate Izirali dɔkku a jam niŋ ate ba lueri Juda dɔkku.

ref: Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
text: Josua a yaa basi ate wa dɔkku po yeri meena nidoa a jam niŋ. Ate Achan, ale ka Karmi biika. Karmi Zimri biika. Zimri Zera biika, Zera biika ate wa nyini Juda dɔkku po la a jam.

ref: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
text: Josua a yaa weeni wa ayen m biiga pai pimpauk a te Naawen, Izirali Wenni. Weeni mu fi ale nye diila. Kan suk di m jigi ya.

ref: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
text: Achan yaa tulisa ayen, <<Ka wensie mi nyeka biem a kaasi Naawen, Izirali Wenni. Mi abe le nye diila ale nna.

ref: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
text: Ba yaa yeeri ŋantaŋa a ta nyini viuku po a nyini a yaa ta ba a jam Josua ale Izirali demma meena niŋ a pai ba a dueni Naawen niŋ.

ref: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
text: Ate Josua ale Izirali demma meena a gum chaab a yik Achan Zera biika ale kpanaŋa ale garukku ale ligmɔniŋka ale wa bisaŋa ale wa liema ale wa niiŋa ale wa bonsaŋa ale wa piisaŋa ale ŋan baai meena ate wa ta la a ta ba cheŋ Akor Viaka po.

ref: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
text: Ate Josua a yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi ta kaasuŋ kude a jam ti jigi ya? Naawen ale ta wari a jam fi jigi jinla de.>> A ta Izirali demma meena a yaa yuk wa ale tana a ko, ase ba le yuk naŋta mbala a ko la ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba yaa ju ba ale bolim.

ref: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
text: Achan zuk ba jam tigsi ka pina a ji wa ate ŋa diem boro a ta pai jinla de. Ate Naawen suinni a yaa yɔk. Dila nyiŋ ba a wi dula ayen ka Akor Viak.

ref: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
text: Nama mɛ a yaa basi ni le suk a doa kauk kuui la a jo tɛŋka po. Naawen ni Wenni dek ale pai tɛŋka a nyo ni nisima po.

ref: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
text: Ase ni dan tuesi tɛŋka a ga nueri ni ju ka ale bolim. Ni nye dii ate Naawen a weeni la. Ni ŋmasi kpesi a tara m wieŋa.>>

ref: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
text: Vari ale veenti la saluik yokyokwa, Josua a sak nuruma ate wa ale Izirali niŋdeerɔma a dɛ nuruma niŋ ate ba cheŋ Ai tɛŋka.

ref: They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north.
text: Tugurik tommu meena ale jam bo ale wa la a yaa jam cheŋ tɛŋka po. Ba jam ga boka Ai wiilukku geŋsa ate viak kpieŋ a bo ba ale tɛŋka suŋsuŋ.

ref: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena jam boka ba le magsi ba bo kauk kuui la. Baai ale jam bo yeri la a bo tɛŋka yeseoku geŋ ale baai ale suk bo gɔnni po la a bo tɛŋka yeniŋ geŋsa. Yok kula Josua a yaa jam cheŋŋi viaka po.

ref: So he called out every man in Ai to go after Joshua's troops. They all rushed out to chase the Israelite army, and they left the town gates wide open. Not one man was left in Ai or in Bethel. Joshua let the men of Ai chase him and his army farther and farther away from Ai.
text: Nuru a jam tali a wari Ai yaase Betel tɛŋsaŋa po an nyini peelim a vi Izirali demma. Ba meena a jam basi ba tɛŋka kama alege a saŋ Izirali demma ŋaaŋ.

ref: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
text: Ate Naawen a yaa weeni Josua ayen, <<Yik fi gbaluku ale bo fi nisimaŋa po la ale mi ale pai tɛŋka a nyo ka fi nisa po.>> Josua a yaa pari wa dachoruku a cheŋ Ai tɛŋka.

ref: the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
text: Ase wa le ga nye dela a ga nueri la, nuru baai ale jam suk doa la a yaa jam nye nwuli a jo tɛŋka po. Ba jam jo ka po kama a tuesi ka ale ju ka ale bolim.

ref: When Joshua and his troops saw smoke rising from the town, they knew that the other part of their army had captured it. So they turned and attacked. The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from their town. But they could not escape, because the soldiers they had been chasing had suddenly turned and started fighting.
text: Ase Josua ale Izirali demma meena ale nya ale baai ale jam suk doa a moata tɛŋka la a nak yik Ai tɛŋka ale ju ka ale bolim ate nyuisaŋ a yiti ka po la, ba yaa viriŋ a nye kpaliŋ ale Ai demma.

ref: Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them. The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there.
text: Ase Izirali demma ale jam ko Ai nuru baai meena ale nyini ba nye kpaliŋka ale ba gɔnni po la a ga nueri la, ba le togri waai meena la, Izirali demma meena a yaa ŋman jo Ai tɛŋka po a ko nuru baai meena ale tali bo ka po la.

ref: Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. Those rocks are still there, and the town itself has never been rebuilt. Joshua Reads the Blessings and Curses (Deuteronomy
text: Wa jam pai Ai naawa a yik ka tiib nyiŋ ate wa yiga dula jigini a ta ga paari wenbalinni. Wenni ale siŋ la Josua a yaa weeni ate ba pai wa nyiŋka a ta nyini tiimu zuk a ga dueni tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi. Ba jam pai ka pina a vi ka zuk ate ku doa a paari jinla danni.

ref: Moses had said that everyone in Israel was to go to the valley between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, where they were to be blessed. So everyone went there, including the foreigners, the leaders, officials, and judges. Half of the people stood on one side of the valley, and half on the other side, with the priests from the Levi tribe standing in the middle with the sacred chest. Then in a loud voice, Joshua read the blessings and curses from The Book of the Law of Moses.
text: Wie ŋaai meena ate Moosis a jam weeni Josua la, wa jam an tali dinyi mɛ la a basi ya. Wa jam kariŋa kama ate Izirali demma tigsuŋku meena. Nipooma ale bisaŋa ale nichamma ale baai meena ale jam gum ba po la a jam wom ŋa kama.

ref: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
text: Ase Gibeon demma ale ga wom dii ate Josua a nye Jeriko ale Ai tɛŋsaŋa la,

ref: So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country. The men put worn-out bags on their donkeys and found some old wineskins that had cracked and had been sewn back together.
text: Ba yaa poli ayen ba paasi ba. Ba yaa cheŋ ga yaali ŋandiinta a yaa ji ale ba bonsaŋa ale boorik kpagsa ale daam bunlɔk kpagsa ate ba laŋ ti.

ref: Their sandals were old and patched, and their clothes were worn out. They even took along some dry and crumbly bread.
text: Nuruma a jam su nuesi kpagsa ale jo garuk tii ale cheeri la mɛ. Ŋandiin tii meena ate ba jam ta la a jam ko kama alege koali mɛ.

ref: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
text: Ba yaa jam cheŋ Josua jigi Gilgal tɛŋka po a weeni wa ale Izirali demma ayen, <<Tama a nyini ka tɛŋ kaai ale yalima bi nye nɔiyeŋ ale ti.>>

ref: The Israelites replied, “But maybe you really live near us. We can't make a peace treaty with you if you live nearby.” The Gibeonites said, “If you make a peace treaty with us, we will be your servants.” “Who are you?” Joshua asked. “Where do you come from?” They answered:
text: <<Tama ka ni tomteerɔba>> ba ale weeni Josua diila ni la. Alege Josua a yaa bek ba ayen, <<Nama ka bana nama abe nyini ka be?>>

ref: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
text: Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ni tomteerɔma a nyini ka tɛŋ kaai ale yaalima dii nyiŋla ti wom ayen Naawen ni Wenni wie kama. Tama wom wa le nye dii Ejipiti tɛŋka po la kama,

ref: and what he did to those two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan: King Og of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, and King Sihon of Heshbon.
text: ale dii meena ate wa nye Amori demma nalima ŋayewa ale jam bo Jodan benni kori geŋsa la. Ba jam ka naab Siyon ate wa nyini Yesbon la ale naab Og ate wa mɛ a nyini Basan la waai ale jam a nya Astarot la.

ref: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
text: Ate tama niŋdeerɔma ale baai meena ale bo ti tɛŋka po la yaa weeni ti ayen, <Ti pai ŋanta a ga tu ba suik a weeni ba ayen, <<Tama ka ni tomteerɔba. Ni nye nɔiyeŋ ale ti.>> >

ref: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
text: Ŋandiintaŋa de a kaasi ka suiku po a zaani dai dii danni ate tama a nyini yeeri a cheena nama jigi la. Alege m yɔgla de ni be nya ti le koi ale koali diila.

ref: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
text: Leŋsaŋa de diipo ate ti pai daamu a nyo si po la si jam nala kama, alege nya si le na diila. Ate ti kɔlimaŋa ale ti nuensaŋa a cheeri ti le bo chelimu po ate ku beni la nyiŋ.>>

ref: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
text: Izirali demma a yaa tuesi ŋandiintaŋa alege an beki Naawen a nya ya.

ref: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
text: Josua a yaa jam nye suiyɔgni nɔiyeŋ ale ba ayen ba boro alege ate niŋdeerɔma me a yaa nye pɛka ayen ba le ta nɔiyeŋka ale ba.

ref: A couple of days later, the Israelites found out that these people actually lived in the nearby towns of Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim. So the Israelites left the place where they had camped and arrived at the four towns two days later.
text: Ate Izirali demma a yaa nyini a paari tɛŋsaŋa daa ŋata dai. Tɛŋ sila abe le Gibeon ale Kefira ale Beerot ale Kiriat Jearim.

ref: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
text: Alege Izirali demma an jam nye kpaliŋ ale ba dii nyiŋla niŋdeerɔma a jam nyeka pɛka ale Naawen, Izirali Wenni nyiŋ. Tigsuŋku meena sui a yaa kaasi ale niŋdeerɔma ale nye diila,

ref: but the leaders reminded them, “We promised these people in the name of the Lord God of Israel that we would let them live, so we must not harm them. If we break our promise, God will punish us. We'll let them live, but we'll make them cut wood and carry water for our people.”
text: Ba ŋman weeni gum du ayen, <<Ni basi ba ate ba boro bi ni basi ate ba chim dacheerisa ale nyiaŋadisa ate tigsuŋku meena.>> Niŋdeerɔma ale puulim dii ale ba la a sum jam nye kama.

ref: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
text: Josua a yaa weeni Gibeon demma ayen ka boa ate ni paasi ti ayen, <<Tama a yalima kama ale ni,>> alege a kala moata tama?

ref: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
text: Ni yaa boka kikaasa po. Ni le kasim ka dacheerisa ale nyiaŋadisa mi Wen yenni po.

ref: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
text: Ba yaa tulisi Josua ayen, <<Ku jo fi tomteerɔma tue kama dii ate Naawen ni Wenni a weeni ayen wa tomteerɔwa Moosis ayen wa le pai tɛŋka meena ate ni abe wa yiak ba meena ate ba yaa jigi abe ba te ni suik la. Dila nyiŋ tama yaa jam a chali yɔgsum ti nyuvooŋa nyiŋ dila ale soa ate ti nye dila.

ref: and you are strong enough to do anything to us that you want. We just ask you to do what seems right.”
text: Tama yaa boka fi nisima po. Bi nye ti dii ale nala ate fi la.>>

ref: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
text: Ate Josua a yaa maari ba ate Izirali demma an jam ko ba.

ref: but he did tell the Gibeonites that they would have to be servants of the nation of Israel. They would have to cut firewood and bring it for the priests to use for burning sacrifices on the Lord's altar, wherever the Lord decided the altar would be. The Gibeonites would also have to carry water for the priests. And that is still the work of the Gibeonites.
text: Dai dila danni wa yaa basi ate Gibeon demma a chim dacheerisa ale nyiaŋadisa ate Izirali demma meena Naawen kuŋkuŋku kauk kuui ate Naawen ale lueri la. Ba abe le ka dii a ta jam paari jinla dɛ la abe le la.

ref: King Adonizedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured and destroyed the town of Ai, and then killed its king as he had done at Jericho. He also learned that the Gibeonites had signed a peace treaty with Israel.
text: Adoni Zedek, Jerusalem naawa ale wom ayen Josua a nak yik Ai tɛŋka ale kaasi ka meena alege a nye Ai ale ka naawa ase wa le jam nye Jeriko ale ka naawa diila ate Gibeon demma me a nye nɔiyeŋ ale Izirali demma ale bo ale ba la.

ref: This frightened Adonizedek and his people. They knew that Gibeon was a large town, as big as the towns that had kings, and even bigger than the town of Ai had been. And all of the men of Gibeon were warriors.
text: Wa ale wa nuruma nyiŋsa a yaa jam a gɔk dii nyiŋla Gibeon jam ka tɛŋ maŋ ase tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa kanyi la, ka jam zuak gaam Ai tɛŋka kama ate ka nuruma meena a seba kpaliŋ nyeka.

ref: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
text: Adoni Zedek Jerusalem naawa ayen weeni Yebron naawa Yoyam ale Jarmut naawa Piram ale Lachis naawa Jafia ale Eglon naawa Debir ayen,

ref: “The Gibeonites have signed a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. Come and help me attack Gibeon!”
text: <<Ba jam maari wa ate wa nye kpaliŋ ale Gibeon demma, dii nyiŋla ba nyeka nɔiyeŋ ale Josua ale Izirali demma.>>

ref: the Gibeonites sent a message to the Israelite camp at Gilgal: “Joshua, please come and rescue us! The Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together and are attacking us. We are your servants, so don't let us down. Please hurry!”
text: Ate Gibeon demma a yaa tom weeni Josua ale jam bo Gilgal ayen, <<Kan baŋ fi tomteerɔma wari ya. Jamu nwuli a vari ti a basi maari ti dii nyiŋla Amori demma nalimaŋa meena ale bo guutaŋa zuima la a gum ka chaab ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale ti.>>

ref: “Joshua,” the Lord said, “don't be afraid of the Amorites. They will run away when you attack, and I will help you defeat them.”
text: Naawen a yaa weeni Josua ayen, <<Kan chali ba yɔgsummoa m pai ba a nyo fi nisima po kama. Ba wanyi mɛ la a kan baga a zaani ale fu.>>

ref: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon and made a surprise attack on the Amorite camp.
text: Josua yaa basi Gilgal ale cheŋ yokku meena a ga diiri ba.

ref: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
text: Naawen a yaa basi ate butimka a jam ba po ate Izirali demma a yaa nya pagrim ba zuk Gibeon tɛŋka po. Izirali demma a jam vi ba ka dila suik kuui ale a cheŋ Bet Yoron la po a yaa ga yik ba Azeka ale Makkeda tɛŋsaŋa po.

ref: And while these troops were going down through Beth-Horon Pass, the Lord made huge hailstones fall on them all the way to Azekah. More of the enemy soldiers died from the hail than from the Israelite weapons.
text: Ase Izirali demma ale jam a vi ate ba chali va suiku a nyini Bet Yoron a cheŋ Azeka la, Naawen a yaa basi ate tintain kpiema a lo ba zuk. Tintain kpiemaŋa ale jam ko baai la a piisi gaam baai ate Izirali demma a jam ko la kama.

ref: The Lord was helping the Israelites defeat the Amorites that day. So about noon, Joshua prayed to the Lord loud enough for the Israelites to hear: “Our Lord, make the sun stop in the sky over Gibeon, and the moon stand still over Aijalon Valley.” So the sun and the moon stopped and stood still until Israel defeated its enemies. This poem can be found in The Book of Jashar. The sun stood still and didn't go down for about a whole day.
text: Ate wenbinni a za di kan cheŋŋi chiika me a za ate Izirali demma a nya pagrim ba dachaasaŋa zuk. Ase ku le ŋmarisi Jasar gbaŋka po la. Wenbinni a jam boka wenzuk suŋsuŋ chiŋmaaŋa po a beni ale siŋka ase dai pumi la.

ref: Never before and never since has the Lord done anything like that for someone who prayed. The Lord was really fighting for Israel.
text: Dai a jam karo ase danni dɛ la alege ate kude a nye la. Dai mɛ abe ŋman karo ate wanni de choa a nye ya. Chekki ka Naawen ale jam kpaliŋ a te Izirali demma.

ref: While the enemy soldiers were running from the Israelites, the five enemy kings ran away and hid in a cave near Makkedah.
text: Nalima ŋanuwa de a jam chali a ga suk ka piuŋ vɔrup po Makkeda tɛŋka po.

ref: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
text: Ase Josua ale ga wom ayen nalima ŋanuwa de a jam suk ka piuŋ vɔrup ale jam bo Makkeda tɛŋka po la,

ref: Joshua answered, “Roll some big stones over the mouth of the cave and leave a few soldiers to guard it.
text: wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni bilim piuŋ kpioŋ a lik vɔrumu nɔnni abe ni basi nuruba gela ate ba a limisi bu.

ref: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
text: Alege ni kan basi ni dachaasaŋa vika, ni yik ba suik ni kan basi ate ba paari ba tɛŋsaŋa ale Naawen ni Wenni a pai ba a nyoka ni nisima po.>>

ref: So Joshua and the Israelites almost wiped out the enemy soldiers. Only a few safely reached their walled towns.
text: Josua ale Izirali demma a jam ko ka ba yega ka ba magadek nyiini ale jam chali paari ba tɛŋsaŋa po.

ref: The Israelite army returned to their camp at Makkedah, where Joshua was waiting for them. No one around there dared say anything bad about the Israelites.
text: Ate tugurik tommu meena a yaa jam pilim ŋmani nalimnyiini a cheŋ. Josua ale jam bo Makkeda tɛŋka la jigi.

ref: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
text: Josua a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni lagri vɔrumu nɔnni abe ni ta nalima ŋanuwa a jam te mu.>>

ref: The soldiers opened the entrance to the cave and brought out the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
text: Ba yaa jam ta nalima ŋanuwa a nyini vɔrumu po a nyini. Ba be jam ka Jerusalem ale Yebron ale Yarmuk ale Lachis ale Eglon nalimaŋa.

ref: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
text: Ase ba le ta nalimaŋa de a jam Josua jigi la, wa yaa tigsi Izirali demma meena ale weeni tugurik tommu kpaŋŋa baai ale jam va wa a jam la ayen, <<Ba jam de, ni pai ni naŋsaŋa a tabi nalimaŋa de ŋeeŋa.>> Ba yaa jam niŋ nyiŋ a tabi ba ŋeeŋa.

ref: and Joshua continued, “Don't ever be afraid or discouraged. Be brave and strong. This is what the Lord will do to all your enemies.”
text: Josua a yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa. Ni kan jɔk nyiŋbiiri. Ni pagra abe ni chiib a zaani. Naawen ale wa nye dii ale dachaasa meena ate ni a kpaliŋ ale ba la ale la.>>

ref: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
text: Josua yaa ko nalima ŋanuwa a pari ba nyiŋsaŋa a yik tiisa sinu nyiŋ, ate ba yik tiisaŋa nyiŋ a ta ga paari wenbalinni.

ref: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
text: Vari ale ga veenti la Josua yaa basi ate ba yaa ta ba nyini tiisaŋa zuk a siŋ tɛŋ a pai ba nyo vɔrup buui po ate ba liŋ suk bu po la. Piuŋ kpioŋ ate ba ba jam pa lik vɔrumu nɔnni, ku diem lik du kama a ta jam paari jinla de.

ref: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
text: Josua ale Izirali demma meena a yaa basi Makkeda tɛŋka alege cheŋ Libna tɛŋka a ga nye kpaliŋ ale ba.

ref: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
text: Ate Josua ale Izirali demma meena a yaa ŋman basi Libna alege cheŋ Lachis tɛŋka, a nye kpaliŋ ale ka me.

ref: and the next day the Lord let them capture the town. They killed everyone, as they had done at Libnah.
text: Naawen a jam pai Lachis tɛŋka a te Izirali demma kama ate Josua a nak yik ka daa ŋayewa danni. Tɛŋka demma meena wa jam ko ba kama ase wa le jam nye Libna tɛŋka diila.

ref: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
text: Alege Gezer naawa Yoram a jan jam kama ayen wa maari Lachis alege Josua a jam nak yik ba kama ale ba tugurik tommu nuru vuk a jam tali ya.

ref: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
text: Ate Josua ale Izirali demma meena a yaa jam basi Lachis ale cheŋ Eglon tɛŋka a nye kpaliŋ ale ba.

ref: captured it that same day, then killed everyone, as they had done at Lachish.
text: Ba jam nak yik ba ka dai dila danni dek a tɔgri ba meena ase ba le nye Lachis tɛŋka diila.

ref: They captured the town and the nearby villages, then killed everyone, including the king. They destroyed Hebron in the same way they had destroyed Eglon.
text: Ba jam nak yik tɛŋka kama a tɔgri nuruma ale ka naawa ale tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa meena nuruma. Ba tali nuru vuk a basi ya. Ase ba le jam nye Eglon diila, ba jam ko waai meena tɛŋ kala po kama.

ref: Joshua and the Israelite army turned and attacked Debir.
text: Josua ale Izirali demma meena a yaa ŋman viriŋ a nye kpaliŋ ale Debir tɛŋka.

ref: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
text: Ba jam nya pagrim tɛŋka ale ka naawa ale tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa meena zuk kama ale tɔgri ba meena. Ba jam ko waai meena kama. Ba an jam tali javuk a basi ya. Ba nye Debir tɛŋka ale ka naawa ase ka ba le jam nye Libna ale Yebron tɛŋsaŋa ale si nalimaŋa diila.

ref: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
text: Josua ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma a yaa jam nak yik tɛŋsaŋa meena ale nalim ŋaai meena ale jam bo tɛŋ sii ale bo guutaŋa zuima ale vaasaŋa po ale tɛŋ sii meena ale bo guutaŋa chaasa la. Ba jam ko nuru meena kama ase Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale weeni ayen ba nye diila.

ref: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
text: Josua a jam tɔgri ba ka dila a nyini Kades Barnea a ga paari Gaza ale ŋman zaani Gosen a tɔgri dila a ta ga paari Gibeon tɛŋka.

ref: King Jabin of Hazor heard about Joshua's victories, so he sent messages to many nearby kings and asked them to join him in fighting Israel. He sent these messages to King Jobab of Madon, the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
text: Ase Yazor naawa Jabin ale ga wom kude la wa yaa tom weeni Madon naawa Jobab ale Simron naawa ale Aksap naawa

ref: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
text: ale nalima ŋaai ale bo wiilukku geŋsa guutaŋa zuima la ale Araba ate ka bo Kinneret yeniŋ geŋsa la ale yeniŋ tɛŋsaŋa meena

ref: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
text: ale Keenan demma ale bo kori ale yeniŋ geŋsa la a ta ga paari Amori demma ale Yit demma ale Perizzi demma ale Jebus demma tɛŋsaŋa ale bo guutaŋa zuima la ale Yivi demma ale bo Yermon ate ka bo Mizpa tɛŋka po la.

ref: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
text: Naawen a yaa weeni Josua ayen, <<Kan fi a chali ba yɔgsummoa, dii nyiŋla chum nna po de m le pai ba meena a nyo Izirali demma nisima po. Ni tuesi ba wusumaŋa abe ni ju ba torokoma ale bolim.>>

ref: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
text: Josua ale wa tugurik tommu meena a yaa jam Merom Benni a nye kpaliŋ ale ba,

ref: Up to this time, the king of Hazor had controlled the kingdoms that had joined together to attack Israel, so Joshua led his army back and captured Hazor. They killed its king
text: Va ŋala po mɛ Josua a ŋmani ŋaaŋ a nye kpaliŋ ale Yazor tɛŋka a ko ka naawa, Yazor ale jam chim tɛŋsaŋa de meena tɛŋ kpieŋ.

ref: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
text: Josua a jam tuesi tɛŋka de meena kama, tɛŋ kaai ale bo guuku zuk la ale Negev meena ale Gosen tɛŋka meena ale tɛŋ sii ale bo yeniŋ la ale Araba ale Izirali guutaŋa zuima meena,

ref: The Lord had told Moses that he wanted the towns in this region destroyed and their people killed without mercy. That's why the Lord made the people in the towns stubborn and determined to fight Israel. The only town that signed a peace treaty with Israel was the Hivite town of Gibeon. The Israelite army captured the rest of the towns in battle.
text: Ka Naawen dek ale basi ate ba suiniima a pagra ate ba nye kpaliŋ ale Izirali demma dii le ku nye ate wa ko ba meena ase Naawen ale weeni Moosis diila.

ref: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
text: A nyini va ŋala po Josua a jam ga kaasi Anak tɛŋka ale bo guuku zuk la; a nyini Yebron ale Debir ale Anab a ta nyini tɛŋ sii meena ale bo guuku zuk Izirali ale Juda tɛŋsaŋa po la. Josua a jam kaasi ba kama ale ba tɛŋsaŋa meena

ref: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
text: Anak demma waai an jam tali bo Izirali tɛŋsaŋa po ka Gaza nyiini, Gat ale Asdod demma wanyi mɛ la an jam vua.

ref: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
text: Josua a yaa jam tuesi tɛŋka meena ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila. Wa jam pai ka kama ate Izirali demma ate ba tara a magsi chaab ale ba buuni ale ka diila ate tɛŋka a yaa vuusi ale kpaliŋ.

ref: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
text: Nalimaŋa de ka baai ate Izirali demma a jam nya pagrim ba zuk ale tuesi ba tɛŋsaŋa ale Jodan benni kori geŋsa la, a nyini Arnon Buboalika a ta ga va Yermon Guuku a ta ga va Araba ale bo kori geŋsa la meena.

ref: The first king that Moses and the Israelites defeated was an Amorite, King Sihon of Heshbon. The southern border of his kingdom ran down the middle of the Arnon River gorge, taking in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the gorge. The Jabbok River separated Sihon's kingdom from the Ammonites on the east. Then the Jabbok turned west and became his northern border, so his kingdom included the southern half of the region of Gilead.
text: Siyon Amori demma naawa waai ale jam a nya Yesbon tɛŋka la jam a nya kama a nyini Aroer ale bo Arnon Buboalika la a ta va Jabbok Benaŋka kaai ale nye bain ale Ammon demma tɛŋka la. Gilead tɛŋka geli a jam gum du kama.

ref: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
text: Wa ŋman jam nya ka Araba ale bo kori geŋsa a moata nyakpiemu la a ta ga paari Araba beli dii ate yisiŋa a bo di po la a ta ga paari Bet Jesimot a ta ga churinti a siŋ Pisga ale bo yeseoku la.

ref: Next, Moses and the Israelites defeated King Og of Bashan, who lived in the town of Ashtaroth part of each year and in Edrei the rest of the year. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim.
text: Naab Og ale nyini Basan la ate wa chim Arefa biik baaŋ la waai ale jam ka naab Astarot ale Edrei tɛŋsaŋa po la.

ref: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
text: Wa jam a nya ka tɛŋ sii meena ale bo Yermon Guuku jigini la, Saleka a ga va Basan a ga nye bain ale Gesur ale Maaka ale Gilead tɛŋka kauk ale ŋman nye bain ale naab Siyon tɛŋka Yesbon.

ref: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
text: Naawen tomteerɔwa Moosis ale Izirali demma a jam nak yik ba kama. Ate Naawen tomteerɔwa Moosis a yaa pai ba tɛŋka ate Aruben ale Gad ale Manasa dɔkku geli ayen ba tanla.

ref: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
text: Ase Josua ale jam kpaŋ ate wa benaŋa mɛ a piisi la, Naawen a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi kpaŋ kama alege tɛŋka a diem zuak kama a magsi ni tuesi.

ref: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
text: Manasa dɔkku ale teeri la Aruben ale Gad diina a jam tuesi ka kauk kuui ate Moosis a jam pai te ba ate ku bo Jodan benni kori geŋsa la, ase wa Naawen tomteerɔ ale te ba dula.

ref: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
text: Ku lagri ka dila a ta nyini Aroer ale bo Arnon Buboalika geŋsa la ale ŋman nyini tɛŋ kaai ale bo suŋsuŋsaŋa po la a maa pai guuk labsiku ale bo Medeba la, a ta ga Dibon

ref: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
text: ale tɛŋ sii meena ale bo Naab Siyon tɛŋka a ti ba a wi ayen Amori demma la, waai ale jam a nya Yesbon a ta ga paari Ammon demma tɛŋka banni.

ref: Geshur and Maacah were part of this region, and so was the whole territory that King Og had ruled, that is, Gilead, Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far east as Salecah. Og had lived in Ashtaroth part of each year, and he had lived in Edrei the rest of the year. Og had been one of the last of the Rephaim, but Moses had defeated Sihon and Og and their people and had forced them to leave their land.
text: Dula abe le Og ale bo Basan tɛŋka la meena. Wa ka waai mɛ ale jam a nya Astarot ale Edrei ale ŋman chim Aruben dɔkku po waai ale wari ŋaaŋ a diem vua a boro. Moosis a jam nak yik ba kama ale tuesi ba tɛŋka.

ref: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
text: Alege Izirali demma an jam yiak Gesur ale Maaka a basi ya, ate ba yaa bo ale Izirali demma a ta jam paari jinla danni.

ref: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
text: Alege Livai dɔkku wa an jam te ba jigi ya, ase ba le jam pai ka bolim a nye kaabka tiirim a te Naawen, Izirali Wenni la, dila ale ba ŋanta ase wa le puulim ba la.

ref: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
text: Dii ate Moosis a te Aruben ŋaaŋbisaŋa yezuk meena la ale nna.

ref: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
text: A zaani Aroer a ta ga va Arnon Buboalika, a ta ga va tɛŋ kaai ale bo suŋsuŋka po tɛŋsaŋa ale guuk labsiku ale bo Medeba la meena,

ref: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
text: tɛŋ sii meena ale bo guuk labsiku zuk la ale Naab Siyon ale jam bo Amori demma tɛŋka la, waai ale jam a nya Yesbon la. Moosis a jam nak yik wa ale Midian naawa kama. Evi ale Arekem ale Zur ale Yur ale Areba nabisaŋa a yaa jam nye nɔiyeŋ ale Siyon waai ale jam bo tɛŋka po la.

ref: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
text: Ale baai ale kpi kpaliŋka po la, Izirali demma a jam ko Balaam Biio nidoabinni waai ale jam a porisi la kama.

ref: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
text: Aruben tɛŋka bani a jam kpeglimka Jodan benni nɔi. Tɛŋsaŋa de ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ka Aruben ale wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale soa.

ref: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
text: Dii ate Moosis a jam te Gad ŋaaŋbisaŋa la ale nna:

ref: It included the town of Jazer, and in the Gilead region their territory took in the land and towns as far east as the town of Aroer just west of Rabbah. This was about half of the land that had once belonged to the Ammonites.
text: Jazer tɛŋka ale tɛŋ sii meena ale bo Gilead ale Ammon tɛŋka geli, a ta ga paari Aroer ate ka moata Arabba la,

ref: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
text: ale ŋman nyini Yesbon a cheŋ Aramat Mizpa ale Betonim, a zaani Mayanaim a cheŋ Debir tɛŋka,

ref: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
text: Viaka po mɛ ka Bet Yaram, ale Bet Nimra ale Sukkot ale Zafon ale Naab Siyon ale bo Yesbon tɛŋka ale bo Jodan benni ale bo kori geŋsa la meena kauk kuui meena ale moata Kinneret Nyakpiemu la.

ref: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
text: Tɛŋsaŋa de ale si tɛŋ fiisaŋa ka Gad dɔkku ale jam soa.

ref: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
text: Dii ate Moosis a jam te Manasa dɔkku kauk ale jam tali la ale nna. Dɔkku kauk ale Manasa dɔkku yeri zuk yeri zuk.

ref: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
text: Gilead tɛŋka geli ale Astarot ale Edrei, Naab Og ale bo Basan la tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale la. Si dɛ a jam ka Makir ate wa kowa a chiim Manasa la. Tɛŋka geli ka Makir Manasa biika ale jam soa.

ref: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
text: Moosis ale jam labi tɛŋka dii Jodan benni kori geŋsa kauk kuui ate nuruma a jam boro a yaali ba gaam taam Jeriko tɛŋka la.

ref: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
text: Alege Moosis an jam te Livai dɔkku teŋŋa ase wa le jam a biisi dii ale ba la. Naawen, Izirali Wen a jam le ba tiirim. Wala a jam le waai ate ba a yaali la. Wa le nya ba zuk suita po meena.

ref: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
text: Dai yen ate nuruba gela a nyini Juda tɛŋka a jam Josua jigi Gilgal tɛŋka po. Ba po wanyi jam le Jefunne nidoabinni Kaleb Kenizzi denɔwa a yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Fi seba kama Kades Barnea tɛŋka po Naawen a jam weeni ka fi ale mi wie a sak Wen nuruwa Moosis.

ref: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
text: Nuru baai ale jam va mi cheŋ la a gonti nye kama ate nuruma a chali yɔgsum. Alege mi a jam wom Naawen m Wenni kama.

ref: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
text: Ase mi ale nye dila la, Moosis a yaa puulim ayen mi ale m bisaŋa ale nya ti dɛka jigini tɛŋ kaai po ate m boro a cheŋ la taam wuu, dii nyiŋla fi va Naawen mi Wenni ale ka fi suinum meena.

ref: I'm just as strong today as I was then, and I can still fight as well in battle.
text: Alege jinla de m diem pagra kama ase m le jam ka dii ate Moosis a tom mu la. Mi diem pagra kama a baga a nye kpaliŋ yaase wa dii meena.

ref: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
