text: Yɔgyɔgla de be te mu tɛŋ kaai ale bo guuku zuk ate Naawen a puulim dai dila danni ayen wa le pai ka a te mu ase mi ale jam weeni fu tɛŋka wie la. Tama a weeni fu kama ayen tɛŋ kala demma ka ganduata ale bo ba tɛŋka po a se parik woŋ a gilim ka. Ba jam ka Anak bisa. Dai dii dai Naawen ale bo ale mu ate m yiak ba ate ba nyini tɛŋka po a nyini ase Naawen ale weeni diila.>>

ref: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
text: Josua yaa jam niak Jefunne nidoabinni Kaleb ale te wa Yebron tɛŋka.

ref: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
text: Yebron tɛŋka diem boka Kaleb Jefunne denɔwa ŋaaŋbisaŋa nisima po dii nyiŋla wa jam va Naawen, Izirali Wenni ka nalimnyiini.

ref: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
text: Alege ate kude meena a nye la, Yebron yuei a jam le Kiriat Arba. Arba a jam le Anak demma tɛŋ kpieŋ. Suiyɔgni a yaa le jam bo tɛŋka po.

ref: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
text: Tɛŋka de a jam doa ka dila a ta ga paari Yesa Nyakpiemu,

ref: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
text: a zaani Akrabbim a gilim taam paari Zin. A zaani Kades Barnea a ta ga paari Ayeziron ale Addar a ta cheŋ Karka,

ref: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
text: a ŋman zaani Azmon a va buboalika a nye bain ale Ejipiti beli a ga paari Nyakpiemu la, banni ale kpeglim juijui la a ni la. Bain dii ale bo Juda yeseoku geŋsa la a ni la.

ref: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
text: Kori geŋsa tɛŋ banni jam boka Yesa Nyakpiemu a ga paari Jodan benni nyiamu chali a siŋ du la. Yeseoku me tɛŋ banni a nyini ka dula,

ref: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
text: a ga va Bet Yogla pimpitiŋku ale bo Jodan viaka jigini la. A ŋman zaani a va Boyan Piuŋku. Boyan jam ka Aruben nidoabili.

ref: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
text: Tɛŋbain dii Debir la a taam ga va ka Achor Viaka a ta ga paari Gilgal tɛŋka kauk kuui ale tuk Adummim buboalika nyiŋla. Ka jam va ka dula a ga paari En Sɛmes a taam ga nyini En Arogel.

ref: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
text: A ga va Ben Yinnom Viaka kauk kuui ate Jebus demma tɛŋka Jerusalem a jam bo la. Tɛŋka bani a jam ga va ka guuku zuk yeniŋ geŋsa Yinnom Viaka ale va yeseoku geŋsa me a cheŋ Arefaim Viaka.

ref: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
text: A zaani dula bani a jam cheŋ paari ka Neftoa belaŋa ale tɛŋ sii ale moata Efron guuku la a yaa ba cheŋ Baalaya yaase, Kiriat Jearim.

ref: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
text: A ŋman nyini Baalaya yeniŋ geŋsa a cheŋ Edom tɛŋka ale bo guuku zuk la, a ŋman zaani yeseoku a duŋ Jearim yaase, Kesalon Guuku a siŋ Bet Sɛmes a ga paari Timnaya.

ref: It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea,
text: Tɛŋ banni a ŋman zaan dula Ekron guuku ale bo yeseoku la, a viriŋ va Baalaya Guuku a ta ga paari Jabneel. Tɛŋ banni a jam kpeglim ka nyakpiemu.

ref: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
text: A nyini dula wa yaa ŋman cheŋ ga nye kpaliŋ ale nuru baai ale bo Debir tɛŋka po la. Tɛŋka dɛ ba jam a wi ka ayen ka Kiriat Sefer.

ref: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
text: Ase Naawen ale weeni Josua diila, Juda tɛŋka kauk ba jam pai te ka Kaleb Jefunne biika, wa jam tuesi ka Yebron tɛŋka. Yebron yuei a jam le Kiriat Arba. Anak a jam le ba ko.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
text: Kaleb a jam yiak Anak ŋaaŋbisaŋa kama ate ba nyini tɛŋka po a nyini. Ba buuni abe le Sesai ale Ayiman ale Talmai.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
text: Kaleb a weeni ayen, <<Mi ale pai m liewa Aksa a yalisi nuru waai ale a nya pagrim Kiriat Sefer tɛŋka zuk la.>>

ref: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, and Caleb let him marry Achsah.
text: Kenaz nidoabinni Otniel, Kaleb yuawa a yaa nak yik ka, ate Kaleb a pai wa liewa Aksa a yalisi wa.

ref: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
text: Yalika danni Otniel a yaa weeni liewa ayen wa bek wa kowa ate wa te wa tɛŋ. Wa yaa nyini wa bonika zuk a siŋ, ate Kaleb a yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a yaali?>>

ref: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
text: Ate liewa a tulisi ayen, <<Sak jiirim ale mu, ase fi ale te mu tɛŋ Negev po la, bu te mu bulik kaai ale ta nyiam la mɛ.>> Kaleb yaa te wa bulik sii ale bo pimpitini zuk ale viaka po la.

ref: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
text: Tɛŋ sii ate Juda dɔkku a jam so a ale nna.

ref: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
text: ale Lebaot ale Silyim ale Ain ale Arimmon. Si le tɛŋ sii meena ale jam kala moata si la meena a jam gum chaab a paari ka tɛŋsa pisiye ale neok.

ref: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
text: ale Saaraim ale Aditaim ale Gedera, yaase Gederotaim. Si jam ka tɛŋsa pi ale sinaansi a gum chaab ale sii ale kala moata ba la.

ref: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
text: ale Gederot ale Bet Dagon ale Naama ale Makkeda. Si meena a jam gum chaab ale tɛŋ sii ale kala moata ba la a paari ka pi ale siyuebi.

ref: The fourth region was located in the central part of the lower foothills, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages: Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah.
text: ale Keila ale Akzib ale Maresa. Sila me a jam ka tɛŋsa neok a gum chaab ale tɛŋ sii ale kala moata ba la.

ref: The sixth region was in the southwestern part of the hill country, and it had the following eleven towns with their surrounding villages: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, Dannah, Kiriath-Sannah, which is now called Debir, Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, and Giloh.
text: Gosen ale Yolon a yaa pai Gilo a gum du a nye tɛŋsa pi ale kanyi ale tɛŋ fiik sii meena ale kala moata ba la.

ref: The seventh region was located in the south-central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages: Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth-Tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath-Arba, which is now called Hebron, and Zior.
text: ale Yumta ale Kiriat Arba, yaase Yebron, ale Zior. Si ka tɛŋsa neok a gum chaab ale tɛŋ sii ale kali moata ba la.

ref: The eighth region was located in the southeastern part of the hill country, and it had the following ten towns with their surrounding villages: Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah.
text: ale Keen ale Gibea ale Timnaya. Si me a jam ka tɛŋsa pi ale gu chaab ale tɛŋ sii ale kali moata ba la.

ref: The eleventh region was located in the northern part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following two towns with their surrounding villages: Rabbah, and Kiriath-Baal, which is also called Kiriath-Jearim.
text: Kiriat Baal, yaase Kiriat Jearim, ale Arabba, tɛŋ kpiensa siye ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsa a gilim ba.

ref: The twelfth region was located in the desert along the Dead Sea, and it had the following six towns with their surrounding villages: Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, Salt Town, and En-Gedi. The Jebusites
text: ale Nibsan ale tɛŋ kaai ale ta yesaŋa la ale En Gedi. Si me ka siyuebi a gum chaab ale tɛŋ sii ale kala gilim ba la.

ref: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
text: Alege Juda demma an jam baga a yiak ate Jebus demma baai ale bo Jerusalem po la a nyini ya. Jebus demma a diem boro ale Juda demma kama.

ref: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
text: Ɛfraim dɔkku ale jam bo kabi tii la ale nna: Ba tɛŋka bani a jam nyinika Atarot Addar tɛŋka kori geŋsa a jueli va Bet Yoron tɛŋka.

ref: Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
text: Di jam maa gum chaab ale ka tɛŋ fiik sii ale maa bo Manasa tɛŋka po la alege Ɛfraim demma a soa si la.

ref: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
text: Alege ba an jam a yiak Keenan demma baai ale jam bo Gezer la ate ba nyini ya, ate Keenan demma a bo ale Ɛfraim demma a paari jinla de, Ɛfraim demma jam fɛ ba kama ate ba a tom fifiok tuima.

ref: The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring.
text: Manasa jigini a jam paari ka Asɛ ale Mikmetat Sikiim kori geŋsa. Tɛŋ banni yaa va yeseok geŋsa a ga paari nuru baai ale bo En Tappua la a gum du.

ref: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
text: Manasa ale jam soa Tappua tɛŋka, alege Tappua dek ale jam bo Manasa tɛŋ banni po la ka Ɛfraim demma ale soa.

ref: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
text: Isaka ale Asɛ po, Manasa a jam maa soa ka Bet San ale Ibleam ale nuruma ale bo Dor ale Endor ale Taanak ale Megiddo la a gum chaab ale ba tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale kali gilim ba la. Buta nyɔnɔwa a nyini Nafot po.

ref: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
text: Manasa demma an jam taari lik tɛŋsaŋa de, ate Keenan demma a diem bo dula.

ref: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
text: Alege Izirali demma ale ga nya pagrim la, ba yaa basi ate Keenan demma a tom fifiok tuima ale an yiak ba a basi ya.

ref: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
text: Josefi ŋaaŋbisaŋa yaa weeni Josua ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a te tama charuk yeŋ ale nitalim yeŋ nyiini? Tama a piisi kama dii nyiŋla Naawen a niak ti kama nna yegayega.>>

ref: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
text: Josua a yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ase nama a dan piisi a te Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guuta a bo ka po la a pɔsima a te ni, ni ga che peelim a te nidek Perizzi ale Arefa demma tɛŋsaŋa sagni po a tanla.>>

ref: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
text: Josefi ŋaaŋbisaŋa a yaa tulisi ayen, <<Tɛŋ kaai ate guutaŋa a bo ka po la an soa dii a te tama, Keenan demma meena baai ale bo Bet San ale ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa po la ale baai ale bo Jezreel Viaka po la a ta ka kuta torokoba.>>

ref: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
text: Alege Josua a yaa weeni Josefi yenni demma Ɛfraim ale Manasa ayen, <<Nama a piisi kama ale pagra. Ni kan ta charuk yeŋ dekki

ref: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
text: alege sagni tɛŋka kaai ate guutaŋa a bo ka po la ka nama ale ni soa. Ni che tiisaŋa meena ate ka le lagri a soa diila meena ka nama ale soa. Keenan demma a ta ka kuta torokoba ale pagra, nama baga a yiak ba kama.>>

ref: After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent.
text: Izirali tigsuŋku meena a jam tigsi Siilo tɛŋka a ti Tuka Viuku dula. Izirali demma a jam nya pagrim tɛŋka zuk kama

ref: There were still seven tribes without any land,
text: alege Izirali buuni diina buyopɔi ale jam tali an diem nya charukwa.

ref: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
text: Ase nuruma ale piilim a bo ba suiku po ayen ba kpesi nya tɛŋka la, Josua a jam sak ba kama ayen, <<Ga kpesi nya tɛŋka a ŋmarisi a magsi ka wie, abe ni ŋman jam mi jigi, ate mi ale nak gbaŋsa dela Siilo po Naawen niŋ.>>

ref: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
text: Dila nuruma a yaa basi dula ale cheŋ tɛŋka meena. Ba jam ŋmarisi ka wie a basi ka gbaŋ po, tɛŋ kpieŋ meena wie ba jam ŋmarisi a paari ka buyopɔi ale ŋmani pilim cheŋ Josua jigi Siilo.

ref: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
text: Josua yaa nak gbaŋ Naawen niŋ, dula jigini wa yaa chari tɛŋka a te Izirali diinaŋa labka ale ka diila.

ref: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
text: Gbaŋka yaa jam lo Benjamin dɔkku, yezuk yezuk meena zuk. Ba charuku tɛŋka banni a jam bo ka Juda ale Josefi diinaŋa suŋsuŋka po.

ref: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
text: A nyini wiilukku geŋ tɛŋka banni a piilim nyini ka Jodan benni a churinti va Jeriko wiilukku geŋsa a ga va tɛŋ kaai ate guuta a bo ka po la yeniŋ geŋsa a ga paari Bet Aven gɔnni po.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
text: A nyini guuku ale tuk Bet Yoron la yeseoku geŋ tɛŋ banni a tulim va ka yeseok a cheŋ yeniŋ geŋ a ga vuri nyini Kiriat Baal yaase Kiriat Jearim. Ka de ka Juda demma tɛŋ. Kude a jam ka yeniŋ geŋsa.

ref: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
text: Yeseoku geŋsaŋa a piilim nyini ka Kiriat Jearim nakpiaka yeniŋ geŋ, ate tɛŋ banni a jam nyini bulik sii ale bo Neftoa tɛŋka la.

ref: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
text: Tɛŋ banni a va ka guuku zuk a tuk Bet Yinnom Viaka, Arefaim Viaka wiiluk geŋ. Di zaan dula a va ka Yinnom Viaka yeseok geŋsa Jebus tɛŋ kpieŋka a ga paari En Arogel.

ref: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
text: Di ŋman tulim wiilukku geŋ a va ka En Sɛmes a tom du a cheŋ Gelilot ale tuk Adummim la, a ga va Boyan Piuŋku jigini la. Boyan jam ka Aruben nidoabili.

ref: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
text: Di ga va ka wiilukku geŋ Bet Araba churinti a cheŋ Araba.

ref: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
text: Di jam ga va ka Bet Yogla wiilukku geŋsa churintika a jam nyini Yesa Nyakpiemu wiiluk geŋ, a ga kpeglim Jodan benni nɔi yeseoku geŋ. Kude a jam le yeseoku geŋsa tɛŋ banni.

ref: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
text: Jodan benni ale jam chim kori geŋsa tɛŋ banni. Ŋade a jam le tɛŋ banaŋa a labi Benjamin yezuimaŋa kabitaŋa meena la.

ref: One region of Benjamin's tribal land had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Those towns were Jericho, Beth-Hoglah, Emek-Keziz, Beth-Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Chephar-Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba.
text: Kefar Ammoni ale Ofni ale Geba. Si jam ka tɛŋsa pi ale siye ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsa.

ref: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
text: Gbaŋsa buye po a jam lo ka Simeyon dɔkku yezuk yezuk zuk. Ba charuku a jam bo ka Juda tɛŋka po.

ref: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
text: ale Bet Lebaot ale Saruyen, tɛŋsa pi ale sita ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsa.

ref: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
text: Di ŋman nyini kori geŋsa a cheŋ Gat Yefer ale Et Kazin tɛŋsaŋa, di jam nyini ka Arimmon a viriŋ a duŋ Nea nyiŋ.

ref: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
text: Ain ale Arimmon ale Eter ale Asan si mɛ ka sinaansi ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsa.

ref: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
text: Side meena a gum chaab ale ka tɛŋ fi sii ale gilim ba la a ta ga paari Baalat Beer yaase Arama, ale bo Negev tɛŋka la. Side a jam le Simeyon dɔkku yezuk yezuk charuk la.

ref: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
text: Ba jam pai Simeyon demma charuku a ta nyini Juda charuku po kama dii nyiŋla, Juda charuku a poom zuak gaam ba ale a silim diila kama. Dila Simeyon demma a jam nya ba charuku a nyini ka Juda po.

ref: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
text: A nyini dula tɛŋ banni a cheŋ gilim va ka wiilukku geŋsa a cheŋ Yannaton a ga kpeglim Ipta El Viaka.

ref: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
text: Tɛŋ sii ale jam maa gum du la ale nna. Kattat ale Nayalal ale Simron ale Idala ale Betiliyem. Si jam ka tɛŋ kpieŋsa pi ale siye ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsa.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa a jam le Zebulun dɔkku yezuk yezuk charuk.

ref: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa de ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa a jam ka charuk a te Isaka dɔkku yezuk yezuk.

ref: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
text: Di yaa viriŋ kori geŋsa a duŋ Bet Dagon, a ga paari Zebulun dɔkku ale Ipta El Viaka, a cheŋ wiilukku geŋ a paari Bet Emek ale Neiel, a gaam Kabul basi gala.

ref: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
text: Di jam cheŋ ka Ebron ale Areyob ale Yammon ale Kanaya a ga paari Saidon.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob. Naphtali's Land
text: Tɛŋ banni a jam paari Tabor ale Sayazuma ale Bet Sɛmes a ga kpeglim Jodan benni. Si jam ka tɛŋ kpieŋsa pi ale siyuebi ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsa.

ref: The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa de ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa a jam ka charuk a te Nafitali dɔkku yezuk yezuk.

ref: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
text: Tɛŋsaŋa de ale kaabteerɔwa Eleaza ale Josua Nun nidoabinni ale Izirali dɔkku yezuimaŋa nyama a jam nak gbaŋ Siilo tɛŋka Naawen niŋ, Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku nɔi la. Ba jam labi tɛŋka a te chaab a nueri kama.

ref: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
text: Izirali demma waai yaase nichamma ale bo ale ba la waai a dan kan potim seba ale ko nuru a bag chali ga suk tɛŋsaŋa de po kama ate kotundɔwa a kan ko wa ate ku paari diipo ate tigsuŋku ale nya wanni zuk la.

ref: One day the Lord told Joshua:
text: Naawen a yaa weeni Josua ayen,

ref: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
text: <<Weeni Izirali demma ayen ba lueri tɛŋsa a magsi sukka jigi ase mi ale biisi a ta va Moosis zuk ate wa weeni fu diila,

ref: If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
text: <<Ase wa dan chali paari tɛŋ sila kanyi, wa a magsi ka wa zaani tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi a weeni wa le nye diila a sak tɛŋ kala nisɔmma. Ate ba yaa te wa suik ate wa jo ba tɛŋka po a te wa jigi ate wa boro ale ba.

ref: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
text: Ase kotundɔwa a daa vi wa, ku a fɛ ate ba kan pai waai ate ba a ŋma la a te, dii nyiŋla wa an potim seba ale ko nuruwa.

ref: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
text: Wa a magsi ka wa bo tɛŋ kala po, ka wa nin zaani tigsuŋku niŋ ate ba kpesi nya wa wanni zuk, abe ku paari diipo ate kaabteerɔ kpioŋku waai ale boro alege ate kude nye la kum. Dila wa baga a ŋmani a kuli wadek yenni kama, tɛŋ kaai ate wa jam chali ale ge ka la.>>

ref: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
text: Dila ba yaa jam lueri Kedes ale bo Galili ate ka bo Nafitali ate guutaŋa a bo ka po la ale Sikiim ale bo Ɛfraim ate guutaŋa a bo ka po la ale Kiriat Arba yaase Yebron ate ka bo Juda ate guutaŋa a bo ka po la.

ref: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
text: Jodan benni ale bo Jeriko la kori geŋsa, ba jam lueri ka Bezer ale bo gɔnni po la, tɛŋ kaai ale doa jassi la a nyini Aruben dɔkku po ale Aramot ale bo Gilead po la a nyini Gad dɔkku po ale Golan ale bo Basan po la a nyini Manasa dɔkku po.

ref: While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
text: Siilo ale bo Keenan tɛŋka po la a weeni ba ayen, <<Naawen a jam biisi kama ale Moosis ayen ni te ti tɛŋsa ate si ta wuuk ate tama a bo dula ale ti duŋsaŋa.>>

ref: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
text: Dila ase Naawen ale weeni diila Izirali demma a yaa jam te Livaima tɛŋsaŋa de ase wuuk jigi la a ta nyini ba charuku po.

ref: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
text: Gbaŋ kaai ale dɛ niŋ la a jam lo ka Koyat dɔkku yezuk yezuk zuk. Livaima baai ale ka kaabteerɔwa Aaron ŋaaŋbisa la a jam nya ka tɛŋsa pi ale sita a nyini Juda ale Simeyon ale Benjamin diinaŋa jigi.

ref: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
text: Dila Izirali demma a jam te Livaima ka tɛŋsaŋa de ale si wuuku ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.

ref: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
text: Tɛŋ sii meena ate ba jam te kaabteerɔma, Aaron ŋaaŋbisaŋa la, ka pi ale sita ate si ta wuuk a magsi ba duŋsaŋa dɛka.

ref: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
text: Gerson kabini tɛŋsaŋa meena a jam ka tɛŋsa pi ale sita ale wuuk a magsi ba duŋsaŋa dɛka.

ref: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
text: Dila Naawen a te Izirali demma tɛŋka meena ate wa jam pɛ ayen wa pai te ba kokpieŋsaŋa la, ate ba tuesi a kala dula.

ref: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
text: Naawen a yaa jam te ba vuusum jigi meena, ase wa le jam pɛ dii ale ba kokpieŋsaŋa la. Ba dachaasaŋa an jam baga a zaani ale ba. Naawen a jam pai ba dachaasaŋa meena a te ba kama.

ref: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
text: Naawen an jam gaam pumpuulim maŋsaŋa ŋaai ate wa jam nye ale Izirali yenni demma la a basi ya, wa jam nye ŋa meena kama.

ref: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
text: Ate Josua a tigsi Aruben demma ale Gad demma ale Manasa dɔkku kauk

ref: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
text: ku beni kama yɔgyɔgla de nama an zɛri ni suataŋa, alege ni nye dii ate Naawen ni Wenni weeni la kama.

ref: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
text: Ase Naawen ni Wenni ale basi ate ni suataŋa a vuusi ase wa le jam puulim dii ale ni la, ni ŋmani a kuli ni yeeŋa tɛŋ kaai po ate Naawen tomteerɔwa Moosis a pai te ni ate ka bo Jodan benni kauk m kula la.

ref: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
text: Alege ni abe kpesi nidek a ta wieŋa ale sinsaŋŋa ŋaai ate Naawen tomteerɔwa Moosis a te ni la, ate ni a yaali Naawen ni Wenni, abe ni a va wa suitaŋa meena abe ni va wa wieŋa abe ni chiib va wa nalimnyiini a tom a te wa ale ni suiniima meena ale ni chiisa meena.>>

ref: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
text: Ase Izirali demma ale ga wom ayen ba sɛka kuŋkuŋ Keenan tɛŋ banni ale bo Gelilot a moata Jodan benni Izirali demma geŋka la,

ref: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
text: Izirali tigsuŋku meena a yaa tigsi jigi yeŋ Siilo tɛŋka po ayen ba ga nye kpaliŋ ale ba.

ref: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
text: Dila Izirali demma a yaa jam tom kaabteerɔwa Eleaza nidoabinni Fineyas Gilead tɛŋka, Aruben demma ale Gad demma ale Manasa dɔkku genni jigi.

ref: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
text: Baai ale jam va wa cheŋ la ka nuru zuima pi. Izirali buuni diina piwa meena a jam te ka nuru yeŋ waai ale ka yeri nyɔnɔ Izirali labika yezuimaŋa po la.

ref: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
text: Ase ba le jam cheŋ Gilead tɛŋka po, Aruben dɔkku ale Gad dɔkku ale Manasa dɔkku genni jigi la, ba yaa weeni ba ayen,

ref: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
text: <<Naawen tigsuŋku meena ayen, ku le nye kase ate ni basi siaka ale Izirali Wenni ase nna la la? Ni le nye kase a ŋmani Naawen ŋaaŋ a sɛ kuŋkuŋ a te nidek abe ni zɛri wa?

ref: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
text: A ta jam paari jinla de tama a diem nye cheri a nyini biem bula po, nyiŋtuilaŋa ale a jam Naawen naakuuni po la meena.

ref: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
text: Ate nama a yaali ni basi Naawen vaka? <<Ni dan zɛri Naawen jinla, chum wa sui ale puuri ale Izirali naakuuni meena.

ref: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
text: Ase tɛŋ kaai ate nama a tuesi la a dan taŋ, ni jam Naawen tɛŋka po. Kauk kuui ate Naawen viuku a za la a maa boro ale tama. Alege ni abe kan ni zɛri Naawen yaase tama nɔi abe ni sɛ kuŋkuŋ a te ni dega a ŋman gum Naawen ti Wenni kuŋkuŋku po.

ref: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
text: Ase Zera nidoabinni Achan ale jam kan ta wensie a pai ŋan baai ate Wen ayen ba kaasi la, suipuurum an jam Izirali naakuuni meena jigi ya? Daa wala nyiini ale jam kpi wa biemu nyiŋŋa.>>

ref: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh answered:
text: Ate Aruben dɔkku ale Gad dɔkku ale Manasa dɔkku geli a yaa tulisi Izirali yezuimaŋa nyama ayen,

ref: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
text: <<Tanjaŋini Wen, Naawen! Tanjaŋini Wen, Naawen! Wa ale seba, ale basi ate Izirali a seba. Ase kude a dan ka tukpari yaase zɛrika a te Naawen, kan basi ti jinla de.

ref: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
text: Ase tama a dan sɛ tidek kuŋkuŋ ayen ti basi Naawen vaka, ayen ti nye juka tiirim yaase ŋandiinta tiirim yaase ti nye suiyɔgni tiirita kaabka ku zuk, Naawen dek abe dari ti tue.

ref: We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.” Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord.
text: Naawen a basi ate ka Jodan benni a chim ban a bo tama ale nama Aruben demma ale Gad demma suŋsuŋ po. Ni ka charuk a nyini Naawen jigi ya.> Ni ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale nye ate tama ŋaaŋbisaŋa a basi Naawen yɔgsum chalika.

ref: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
text: <<Dila ale soa ate tama a weeni ayen, <Ni basi ate ti gomsi a sɛ kuŋkuŋ alege daa juka tiirim yaase kaabka kuŋkuŋoa.>

ref: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
text: Kaabteerɔwa Eleaza nidoabinni Fineyas a yaa weeni Aruben ale Gad ale Manasa ayen, <<Jinla de tama seba ayen Naawen a bo le ti kama, dii nyiŋla nama an zɛri wensie ale Naawen vaka kude nyiŋŋa. Yɔgyɔgla de ni vari Izirali demma Naawen nisima po a basi kama.>>

ref: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
text: Kaabteerɔwa Eleaza nidoabinni Fineyas ale niŋdeerɔma a yaa ŋmani cheŋ Keenan tɛŋka ba le ga tu chaab ale Aruben demma ale Gad demma Gilead po, a weeni sak Izirali demma ba ale zɔk diila.

ref: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
text: Ba sue a jam peenti kama ase ba le jam wom dii ale nye la a yaa pak Naawen ku nyiŋ. Ba an jam ŋman biisi kpaliŋ wie ayen ba ga kaasi ba tɛŋka juijui ate Aruben demma ale Gad demma a jam boro la.

ref: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
text: Aruben demma ale Gad demma a jam te kuŋkuŋku ka yuenni de, ayen Seerɔ Tama Suŋsuŋ ayen Naawen ka Wen.

ref: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
text: Ku le jam beni alege ate Naawen a basi ate Izirali demma a nya vuusum a ta nyini ba dachaasaŋa meena ale gilim ba jigi la, Josua a jam kpaŋ kama ate wa benaŋa mɛ a piisi.

ref: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
text: Josua yaa tigsi Izirali demma meena, ba nisɔmma ale niŋdeerɔma ale buusa boorisaŋa ale kpaŋŋa a weeni ba ayen, <<Mi yaa kpaŋ kama ate m benaŋa mɛ a piisi.

ref: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
text: Nama dek a nya dii meena ate Naawen ni Wenni a nye tɛŋsaŋa de meena ni nyiŋla kama, ku jam ka Naawen ni Wenni ale kpaliŋ te ni.

ref: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Naawen ni Wenni dek ale yiak ba a basi te ni, wa le namsi ba a te ni, ate nama ale tuesi ba tɛŋka ase Naawen ni Wenni ale puulim diila.>>

ref: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
text: <<Ni be pagra, abe ni kpesi a siak dii meena ale ŋmarisi Moosis Sinsaŋŋa Gbaŋka po la, abe ni kan viriŋ juga yaase gala.

ref: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
text: Ni kan pai nidek a gum chaab ale tɛŋsaŋa de ale tali a bo ni po la. Ni kan wi ba wenaŋa yue yaase ni a pɛ ŋa nyiŋŋa. Ku a fɛ ate ni kan kaab ŋa yaase ni koori tɛŋ a zuli ŋa.

ref: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
text: Alege ku a magsi ka ni ŋmasi va Naawen ni Wenni ase ni le nye dii a jam paari yɔgyɔgla de la.

ref: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
text: <<Naawen a yiak ka tɛŋ sii ale zuek ale pagra la a basi te ni; a ta jam paari jinla de tɛŋ karo a baga a zaani ale ni.

ref: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
text: Ni wanyi a nya pagrim tusidi zuk, dii nyiŋla ka Naawen ni Wenni ale kpaliŋ a te ni ase wa le puulim diila.

ref: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
text: Dila ni abe kpesi nidek a yaali Naawen ni Wenni.

ref: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
text: ni abe seba chak ayen Naawen ni Wenni a kan ŋman yiak nuruma de a basi te ni. Alege ba le chim ka barukta a te ni, ba le chim finsa a bo ni ŋaaŋsaŋa abe ba chim munsa ni nimbieŋa po a ta ga paari diipo ate nama ale kpi tɛŋ maŋka de po, kaai ate Naawen ni Wenni a te ni la po.

ref: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
text: <<Yɔgyɔgla de mi a yaa moata ka kum. Ni seba kama ale ni suiniima ale ni chiisa meena ayen pumpuulim maŋ sii meena ate Naawen ni Wenni a weeni la wa an jam tali dinyi mɛ la a basi ya.

ref: Yes, when the Lord makes a promise, he does what he has promised. But when he makes a threat, he will also do what he has threatened. The Lord is our God. He gave us this wonderful land and made an agreement with us that we would worship only him. But if you worship other gods, it will make the Lord furious. He will start getting rid of you, and soon not one of you will be left in this good land that he has given you.
text: Ase nama a dan zɛri Naawen ni Wenni nɔiyeŋka, kaai ate wa weeni la ale ga kaab wen yona a koori tɛŋ ŋa niŋ, Naawen sui ale puuri ale ni ate ni le kpi nwuli tɛŋ maŋ kaai ate wa te ni la po.>>

ref: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
text: Josua a yaa jam tigsi Izirali buuni meena Sikiim po. Wa weeni nisɔmma ale niŋdeerɔma ale baai ale a bo buusa la ale kpaŋŋa ate ba ta badek jam Wen niŋ.

ref: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
text: Josua a weeni nuruma meena ayen, <<Dii ate Naawen, Izirali Wenni a weeni la ale nna. Ku beni kama ni kokpieŋsaŋa, a maa gum Tɛra Abrayam ale Nayo kowa a jam gaam Benni a taam kama a kala a kaab wen yona.

ref: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
text: Alege mi Wen a jam yeeri ni kowa Abrayam a ta nyini tɛŋka ale gaam Benaŋka la a ta cheŋ Keenan a te wa ŋaaŋbi boari. Mi te wa Aizik,

ref: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
text: a te Aizik mɛ Jekob ale Iisɔ. Mi yaa pai Seir tɛŋka ale ta guuta la a te Iisɔ, alege Jekob ale wa nidoabilisaŋa a jam cheŋ ka Ejipiti.

ref: Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea.
text: Ase mi ale ta ni koma a nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la, nama a jam paari ka nyakpiemu ate Ejipiti demma a jam a vi ba ale kpaliŋ torokoba ale wusum duerisa a ga paari Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku.

ref: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
text: Alege ba jam kaari a te Naawen a yaali maarika ate wa yaa basi ate legi a bo nama ale Ejipiti demma suŋsuŋ, wa jam basi ate ba wari nyiamu po. Nama nya kama ale nidek nina m le nye Ejipiti demma diila. Ni jam bo gɔnni po ate ku beni kama.

ref: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
text: <<Mi ta ni jam Amori demma tɛŋka po baai ale bo Jodan benni kori geŋsa la. Ba jam kpaliŋ ale ni alege mi pai ba a nyo ka ni nisima po. Mi jam ko ba kama ate ni tuesi ba tɛŋka.

ref: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
text: Ase Zippor nidoabinni Belak, Moab naawa ale jam gomsi ayen wa nye kpaliŋ ale Izirali demma la, wa jam tom weeni ka Biio nidoabinni Balaam ayen wa ka kikaasa a te ni.

ref: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
text: Alege mi an jam wom Balaam ale a weeni diila, wa goanti jam a niak ni kama m jam vari ni a ta nyini wa nisima po a nyini kama.

ref: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
text: <<Ni lo Jodan benni a jueli kama a jam Jeriko tɛŋka po. Ate Jeriko demma a nye kpaliŋ ale ni ase Amori ale Perizzi ale Keenan ale Yit ale Girgas ale Yivi ale Jebus demma ale jam kpaliŋ ale ni dii alege ate mi a jam pai ba a nyo ni nisima po la.

ref: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
text: Mi jam tom zirima ate ŋa de ni niŋ, ŋaai ale jam yiak ba a basi te ni la. Amori demma nalima ŋayewa mɛ a jam boro kama. Nama an jam nye kude ale ka nidek gebik ale tommoa.

ref: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
text: Dila mi te ni ka tɛŋ kaai ate nama an namu ka nyiŋŋa ale tɛŋ kpieŋsa ate nama an sɛ si la, ate ni bo si po a dɛ ŋan baai ate nama an bori ba la.>

ref: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
text: <<Yɔgyɔgla de ni abe a chali Naawen abe ni puusi a te wa ale wensie. Ni yuk wena ŋaai ate ni kokpieŋsaŋa a jam a kaab ate ŋa gaam Benaŋka taam la ale ŋaai ale bo Ejipiti po la abe ni puusi a te Naawen.

ref: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
text: Alege Naawen puusi teka a dan kan nala a te ni, bi lueri a te nidek jinla danni waai ate ni a yaali ni puusi a te la, ka wen ŋaai ate ni kokpieŋsaŋa a jam a kaab ate ŋa gaam Benaŋka a taam la yaase ka Amori demma wenaŋa baai tɛŋka po ate ni boro la. Alege mi ale m yenni demma meena, tama ale puusi a te ka Naawen.>>

ref: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
text: Ate nuruma a yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ku abe yalima ale ti ate tama a zɛri Naawen abe ti kaab wen yona.

ref: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
text: Ku ka Naawen ti Wenni dek ale ta tama ale ti koma a nyini Ejipiti po, a nyini tɛŋ kaai ale ka yɔntidi la po, a tom wakinkaglaŋa de tama dek nina po. Wa jam kasi ti kama ti chelimu meena po ale tɛŋ sii meena po ate tama va si po a taam la.

ref: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
text: Naawen ale yiak tɛŋsaŋa de meena a basi a te ti a maa gum Amori demma baai ale jam bo tɛŋka po la. Tama mɛ ale puusi a te Naawen dii nyiŋla wa ka ti Wen.>>

ref: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
text: Josua a yaa weeni nuruma ayen, <<Nama an baga a puusi a te Naawen ya. Wa ka weleŋsa Naawen. Wa ka nyuri dɛka Wen. Wa kan vɔŋ a te ni, ni tukpanni ale ni biemu nyiŋŋa.

ref: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
text: Ase ni dan zɛri Naawen ale kaab tɛŋ yoŋta wena, wa le basi ate kaasuŋ jam ni jigi ate dila a basi ate ni kpeglim, wa le jam chim Naawen maŋ ate ni la ŋaaŋnyiŋ.>>

ref: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
text: Alege nuruma a yaa weeni Josua ayen, <<Aaya, ti le puusi a te ka Naawen.>>

ref: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
text: Ate Josua a yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nama dek ka seerɔba a te nidek ayen ni a yaali ni puusi a te ka Naawen.>> Ba yaa tulisa ayen, <<Mm ti le weeni diila a ni la.>>

ref: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
text: Josua a yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni yuk ni wen yonaŋa ate ni ta la a basi abe ni pai ni suiniimaŋa a te Naawen, Izirali Wenni.>>

ref: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
text: Ate nuruma a yaa weeni Josua ayen, <<Ti le puusi a te Naawen ti Wenni abe ti a wom wa.>>

ref: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
text: A nyini dai dila danni Josua a jam nye ka nɔiyeŋ pumpuulima a te nuruma, dula jigini Sikiim tɛŋka po wa yaa ŋmarisi sinsaga ale wie te ba.

ref: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
text: Ate Josua yaa jam ŋmarisi wieŋa de meena a nyo Wen sinsaŋŋa gbaŋka po. Wa jam pai ka tintain kpienni a feri kinkaŋ peruk tɛŋ a moata Naawen weleŋsa jigini.

ref: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
text: Wa ya weeni nuruma meena ayen, <<Nya de, tintanni de ale chim ka seerɔ a te ni. Di wom dii meena ate Naawen a weeni ti la kama. Di le chim ka seerɔ a bo mini ni ase ni dan kan ta wensie ale ni Wenni.>>

ref: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
text: Josua a yaa jam basi ate nuruma meena a kuli ba yeeŋa.

ref: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
text: Wieŋa de meena ŋaaŋnyiŋ Naawen tomteerɔwa Nun nidoabinni Josua a yaa kpi. Wa jam taka bena kook ale pi.

ref: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
text: Ate ba yaa gu wa kauk kuui ate wa jam boro la, Timnat Seraya po Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guutaŋa a bo ka po Gaas guuku wiiluk geŋsa.

text: Izirali demma a puusi a te Naawen kama diipo ate Josua ale nisɔmma a jam vua la ale baai ale jam kpiem wa ale nya dii meena ate Naawen a jam nye te Izirali demma la.

ref: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
text: Ate Josefi kobaŋa ŋaai ate Izirali demma a ta nyini Ejipiti a jam la ba yaa jam gu ŋa tɛŋ kala po kaa ate Jekob a jam da ale ligbie kook a nyini Ayaamo nidoabilisaŋa jigi, Sikiim ko a jam le la. Kude a yaa jam chim ka Josefi ŋaaŋbisaŋa nitalim.

ref: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.

ref: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
text: Juda demma a jam siti Jerusalem mɛ a tuesi ka. Ba jam ko tɛŋka demma kama ale juka ale bolim.

ref: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.

text: Ate wa yaa cheŋ Yit demma tɛŋka po, dula jigini wa jam sɛ ka tɛŋ ka yuei jam le Luz, ka yuei diem ale la a ta jam paari jinla danni.

ref: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.

text: Amori demma mɛ a jam a yaali ba nyini Yeres Guuku ale Aijalon ale Saalbim a siŋ kama, alege Josefi yenni pagrimu ale jam gum du la, ba jam fɛ ba mɛ kama a te ba fifiok tuima.

text: Amori demma tɛŋ banni a jam nyini ka Nueoŋ Guuku a ga va Sela a siŋ a cheŋ.

ref: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,

ref: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
text: ale wi jigini yuei ayen Bokim. Dula jigini ba yaa nye kaabka a te Naawen.

text: Diipo meena Izirali demma a dan nyini peelim ba nye kpaliŋ Naawen ale namsi ba ate ba nak dɛ ba ase Wa le pɛ a te ba la. Ba jam bo ka ninam kpiem po.

ref: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
text: Naawen a yaa lueri niŋdeerɔba baai ale vari ba a ta nyini baai ale siti ba la nisima po a basi.

ref: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.

ref: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
text: Alege niŋdeerɔwa a dan kpi, nuruma a nyiem pilim ŋmani kama a ŋmasi tom kaasi a gaam ba kokpieŋsaŋa, a va bɔgluk yoŋta a tom a te ale a puusi ti. Ba jam zɛri ba biem nyeelaŋa ale ba tukpari suitaŋa basika kama.

ref: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,

ref: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
text: Mi a kan ŋman yiak tɛŋsaŋa de kanyi a te ba, sii ate Josua a kpi alege la.

ref: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
text: M le pai si kama a nye Izirali demma a nya ase ba ta Naawen suiku ale a cheŋ ku po ase ba kokpieŋsaŋa la ya.>>

ref: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
text: Naawen a basi tɛŋ sila ayen si tali boro kama, Wa an jam yiak si a basi bunyi dekki a pai si a nyo Josua nisima po.

ref: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
text: Wa nye kude ayen wa sak ba ka Izirali ŋaaŋbisaŋa baai ale kan seba kpaliŋ sii ale liŋ nye la wie.

text: Ba tali boro ayen ba nye ka Izirali demma a nya ase ba le siak te Naawen wieŋa, ŋaai ate wa ta va Moosis zuk a te ba kokpieŋsaŋa la.

ref: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
text: Ba jam a faari ka ba liema ale pai badek liema a yalisi tɛŋ sila bisaŋa ale a va ba bɔgtaŋa.

ref: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
text: Ate Naawen sui a yaa puuri ale Izirali demma ate wa pai ba a nyo Kusan Arisataim, Araam Nayaraim tɛŋka naawa nisima po, waai ate Izirali demma a jam bo wa jigi a paari bena naaniŋ la.

ref: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
text: Alege ase ba le jam kum te Naawen la, Wa yaa yeeri varibasidɔ a ta nyini badek po. Wa yuei ale Otniel Kenaz biik, Kaleb yoa ale nye wa, wala ale jam vari ba a basi.

ref: and Israel was at peace until Othniel died about
text: Tɛŋka a yaa jam nya suiyɔgni bena pisinaansi a paari diipo ate Otniel Kenaz biika a kpi la.

text: Eyud yaa forisi paari wa ase wa le kala wadek wa nyiini wa naam yeri gboŋku zuk la a weeni ayen, <<M ta ka wari a nyini Wen jigi m te fu.>> Ase naawa ale yiti wa zukpaglika zuk la,

text: Mi ale basi dela la, m ta kama yegayega, alege Naawen an ta mi ŋmani ale jaaboa. Ka boa ale soa ate ni a wi mu ayen Naomi. Naawen dii ale zuak la a bo mini mi kama a basi ate ninam a jam mi jigi.>>

ref: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
text: Naomi ale wa sampowa Arut ale nyini Moab tɛŋka a jam diila ale nna. Ba ale jam Betiliyem la ale ŋanta a nye magsi a yaali ka cheka.

ref: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
text: Ku an beniya ate Boazi a nyini Betiliyem a jam a yaa te baai ale a ŋari ŋantaŋa la jiam ale weeni ayen, Naawen a bo ale ba, ate ba mɛ tulisi ayen, <<Naawen abe niak fi mɛ,>>

ref: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
text: Boazi a yaa bek waai ale a nya baai ale a ŋari la zuk ayen, <<Ka wana lie ale nna?>>

ref: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
text: Waai ale a nya ba zuk la a yaa weeni ayen wa nyini ka Moab a va Naomi a jam.

ref: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
text: Wa abe weeni kama ayen, wa a saalim m basi ate wa yiisi a vi baai ale a ŋari la ŋaaŋ. Wa abe jo talimu po kama a tom nyini saluiku a jam paari yɔgyɔgla de. Wa kali vuusi ka maga viuku po.

ref: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
text: Boazi a yaa weeni Arut ayen, <<M lie, wom m le a weeni fu diila kan basi dela abe fi cheŋ talim yoŋ po a yiisi ŋanta. Bo dela ale nipokbili sii ale tom a te mi la.

ref: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
text: Kpesi a nya talim buui ate mi nuruma a tom la abe fi va nipokbilisaŋa. M weeni nuruma kama ayen ba kan nye fu wari ya. Nyanyuila a dan ta fu diipo, nuruma a ŋari nyiam a sueri samɔnsaŋa kama, ga ŋari nyu.>>

ref: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
text: Wa yaa domsi kali a nye wa jiam, wa ale ŋmani te wa ale pai wa nichaanɔwa a chim nuru diila.

ref: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
text: Boazi yaa weeni ayen, <<Ba weeni mu fi ale nye dii meena a te fi ŋianipowa a zaani diipo ate fi chorɔwa a kpi la kama. Ale fi ale basi fi mawa ale fi kowa ale fi tɛŋka ale jam ayen fi bo ale nuru baai ate fi zɛ ba la.

ref: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
text: Naawen ale pilim tuni fu fi ale nye diila, Izirali Wenni ate fi ta fidek a jam su wa kiŋkaŋŋa po la, ale tuni fu dii meena ate fi nye la.

ref: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
text: Arut yaa weeni ayen, <<M be kasim a nya fi ŋmanteka kama. Fi basi ate m sui a yɔk kama ale biisi jiirim biik ale mi, fi tomteerɔwa alege mi an poom soa ale nipokbili sii ale tom a te fu la wanyi mɛ.>>

ref: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
text: Boazi a yaa weeni wa ayen, ku dan paari ŋandiinta dɛka po, wa ga pai boroboroku a lusi damiisiŋka po a ŋɔbi. Wa ale kala ale baai ale a ŋari ŋantaŋa la ba yaa sɛ ŋanta te wa, ate wa ŋɔbi chak ale tali.

ref: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
text: Wa ale yiti ayen wa yiisi la, Boazi a yaa weeni wa nuruma ayen, <<Wa dan poom a tigsi bobaŋa ni basi, ni kan nyo wa chivie po.

ref: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
text: Arut yaa yiisi talimu po a ga paari junɔi. Wa yaa fɔbi ŋantaŋa a nya ase taasi kpienni nɔi la.

ref: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
text: Wa yaa ta kuli yeri ate wa ŋianipowa a nya ŋantaŋa ale soa diila. Wa ŋman pai ŋandiin tii ate wa dɛ ale tali la a te wa.

ref: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
text: Wa ŋianipowa a yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi yiisi ka be jinla? Fi tom ka be? Nuru waai ale seba fi nɔi po la ale nya niaka.>> Arut yaa weeni wa ŋiak nipowa waai jigi ate wa a tom la, <<Nuru waai jigi ate mi tom jinla la ale Boazi.>>

ref: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
text: Naomi a yaa weeni wa sampowa ayen, <<Naawen ale niak wa. Wa an basi jiirim sakka ale ŋanvuta ale kpieba.>> Wa yaa ŋman weeni ayen, <<Nuru wala ka tama dek suok. Wa ka ti da tuesirɔma wanyi.>>

ref: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
text: Arut waai ale nyini Moab la a yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa poom weeni mi kama ayen m bo ale wa tuimtomdɔma ate ba ga ŋari wa ŋantaŋa a nueri.>>

ref: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
text: Naomi a yaa weeni wa sampowa Arut ayen, <<Ku nala kama m lie, ate fi cheŋ ale nipokbilisaŋa dii nyiŋla nuru yoŋ talim po ba baga a nye fu biem kama.>>

ref: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
text: Dila nyiŋ Arut yaa kasim bo ale ka nipokbili sii ale a tom a te Boazi la ate ŋantaŋa ŋarika ga nueri. Arut jam kasim boro ale ka wa ŋianipowa.

ref: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
text: Dai yeŋ ate Naomi, Arut ŋianipowa a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ku an magsi ayen m yaali dɔk a te fu ate ba a nya fi zuwa?

ref: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
text: Boazi waai ate fi bo wa jigi ale nipokbilisaŋa la, daa tama suowa? Jinla yokku wa za wa fɔbi wa ŋantaŋa a yali kama.

ref: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
text: Fi yaa so fi nyiŋka a sa kpa buui nyum ale masa la abe fi jo garuk tii ate fi mariŋ la. Fi dan nye dila fi yaa cheŋ ŋantaŋa yalika jigini alege kan basi ate wa seba ayen fi bo dula, se ka wa nin dɛ nueri.

ref: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
text: Wa yaa bɛ dan so, kpesi nya juijui ate wa doa la. Fi yaa yik jabuui ale lik wa la a zak abe fi ge wa naŋsaŋa a yaa duak. Fi dan nye dila wa yaa le weeni fi le fi nye diila.>>

ref: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
text: Arut yaa weeni ayen, <<M le nye dii meena ate fi weeni la.>>

ref: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
text: Wa yaa cheŋ ŋantaŋa fɔbika jigini a ga nye dii meena ate wa ŋianipowa a weeni wa ayen wa nye la.

ref: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
text: Boazi ale dɛ nueri ate wa nyiŋka a yɔk la, wa yaa ga duak wa ŋantaŋa ale vi chaab zuk dua la jigini kpeglimka. Arut yaa mak cheŋ a ga lagri alege wa naŋsaŋa a yaa duak.

ref: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
text: Yɔkku suŋsuŋ jaab yaa nye ate Boazi nye nna legi, a ga a labri la ale nipok ale dua wa naŋsa po.

ref: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
text: Boazi yaa bek ayen, <<Ka wana?>> Arut yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ka mi Arut fi tomteerɔwa.>> Arut yaa ŋman weeni ayen pai fi garukku kauk a lik mu fi le ka m da tuesirɔ la nyiŋ.

ref: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
text: Boazi yaa weeni ayen, <<M lie, Naawen ale niak fu. Jiirim buui ate fi sak ale mu la a poom gaam fi ale liŋ sak jiirim buui la kama. Fi an chali a vi bimbaan paaluk ŋaaŋŋa, jigsirɔba yaase ŋanjaksa.

ref: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
text: Ku ka wensie ayen m ka da tuesirɔ, alege da tuesirɔ a boro a moata gaam mi.

ref: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
text: Be goa dela yokku de ate chum saluik wa dan da tuesi fu ku nala. Alege wa dan kan da tuesi fu, Naawen boro mi ale da tuesi fu.>>

ref: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
text: Dila la, wa yaa duak wa naŋsa geŋ, a yaa kpabi yiti diipo ate nuru kan nya a miŋ la, a yaa weeni ayen, <<Kan basi ate ba miŋ ayen nipok a jam ŋantaŋa fɔbika jigini.>>

ref: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
text: Boazi yaa ŋman weeni wa ayen, <<Ta garuk kuui ate fi pai a lik fi zukku la a jam lagri.>> Wa ale lagri la, wa yaa pai jaab magsi barli ku nɔi buyuebi a kpiiri nyoro a ji wa ate wa ta kuli.

ref: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
text: ale ŋman weeni wa le magsi barliwa jaamu nɔi buyuebiwa te wa ale weeni ayen, <<Kan kuli fi ŋianipowa jigi ale nikotta>> la.

ref: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
text: Naomi yaa weeni ayen, <<M lie limisi ate fi nya dii meena ale za ku nye la. Nuruwa kan vuusi se ka wanni a nin nye magsi jinla.>>

ref: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
text: Dila la Boazi yaa cheŋ tɛŋka nansuiŋku jigini a ga kala. Ba da tuesirɔwa ate wa poom weeni wa wari la a yaa jam ate Boazi yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M doa jam kali dela.>> Ate wa ga kali.

ref: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
text: Boazi yaa yik tɛŋka nisɔm pi ate ba mɛ kali.

ref: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
text: Wa yaa weeni wa da tuesirɔwa ayen, <<Naomi ale nyini Moab jam la, a pai ti suoku Elimelek tɛŋka a da kama.

ref: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
text: Mi abe a poli ayen ku magsi ka fi seba ku nɔi po. Yɔgyɔgla de fi dan a yaali da nuruma de ale kali la niŋ. Fi dan da a tuesi, da tuesi. Alege fi dan kan da a tuesi, weeni mu ate m seba. Dii la nuru karo ka fi ale fi da tuesi, mi abe le a vi fi ŋaaŋ,>> Ate wa weeni ayen, <<M da tuesi.>>

ref: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
text: Boazi yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ku nala, fi dan da tɛŋka Naomi jigi, se fi da Arut mɛ ale nyini Moab a chim pukɔgini la, ate kpiewa dɔkdemma a diem soa tɛŋka.

ref: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
text: Da tuesirɔwa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ku dan ka dila mi ale pai mi suiku a te ate fi da tuesi dii nyiŋla mi a dan da tuesi ate m poom kpi m dek bisaŋa kan nya tɛŋka. Fi da ale mi kan da a tuesi.>>

ref: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
text: Da tuesirɔwa yaa be le weeni Boazi ayen wa be da la, wa yaa yeeri wa nuensaŋa a te Boazi,

ref: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
text: Boazi yaa weeni niŋdeerɔma ale baai ale bo dula la, <<Ayen nama ka mi seerɔba jinla ayen mi da jaab meena ale bo Naomi jigi ate Elimelek ale wa bisaŋa Kilion ale Malon a soa la kama.

ref: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
text: Dii ale ŋman gum du la, Arut waai ale nyini Moab la, ate wa chorɔwa Malon a kpi ale ge wa la ka mi pok. Kude ale basi ate kpiewa dɔkdemma soa ŋantaŋa abe ba bo badek tɛŋka po ate wa tomini kasim a cheŋ. Nama meena ka mi seerɔba jinla.>>

ref: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
text: Niŋdeerɔma ale nuru mbala ale bo nansuiŋ la ku yaa weeni ayen, <<Tama meena ka seerɔba. Naawen a basi ate fi powa a nye ase Arekel ale Leya ale biak bisa yega ate Jekob la. Fi ale jigsi Efrata buuni po abe fi yuei yiti Betiliyem tɛŋka po.

ref: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
text: Naawen ale wa basi ate nipowa a biak biik sii a te fu la, a nye ase Juda ale Tamara biika Perezi dɔkdemma la.>>

ref: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
text: Nipooma yaa weeni Naomi ayen, <<Pak Naawen ale wa te fu ka ŋaaŋ ayen wa a nya fi zuk. Naawen maari ate biika nya yuei Izirali tɛŋka po.

ref: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
text: Fi sampowa a yaali fu ka nna yegayega, wa be nye gaam bisa bayopɔi ale a nye diila kama. Yɔgyɔgla de wa biak ka ŋaaŋ a ta fu, waai ale wa te fu nyuvuri abe wa yik fu nna ŋmapi ale fi kpaŋsaŋa la.>>

ref: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
text: Naomi yaa tuesi biika a yaa ta wa nna ŋmapi a nya wa zuk.

ref: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
text: Nipok baai ale kali moata ba la yaa te biika yuenni ayen Obed. Ba yaa weeni waai meena ayen ba biak ka biik a te Naomi Obed yaa biak Jese ate Jese a biak Deevid.

ref: Here is a list of the ancestors of David: Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, and Perez.
text: ate Obed a biak Jese ate Jese a biak Deevid.

ref: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
text: Nuru ale jam boro wa yuei ale Elkana. Wa jam nyini ka Arama tɛŋka ate ka bo Zuf, Ɛfraim tɛŋka po, kauk kuui ate guuta a boro la. Wa kowa yuei jam le Jeroyam. Wa kokpieŋka yuei jam le Eliyu. Wa kokpieŋka kowa yuei jam le Toyu. Toyu a jam ka Zuf biik. Elkana ale wa nuruma jam nyini ka Ɛfraim dɔkku po.

ref: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
text: Elkana jam ta ka nipooba baye. Wanyi yuei jam le Yanna, nwala yuei jam le Peninna. Peninna jam ta bisa kama alege Yanna jam ka kirik.

ref: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
text: Bein meena Elkana ale wa dɔkdemma a nyiem basi ba tɛŋka Arama kama alege cheŋ Siilo ayen ba puusi Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La abe ba nye kaabka te wa. Nuru ale jam bo Siilo ate ba a wi wa ayen Eli. Wa jam ka Naawen kaabteerɔ. Eli jam ta ka nidoabilisa baye, Yofni ale Fineyas. Ba mɛ jam ka kaabteerɔba.

ref: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
text: Elkana a dan jam nye kaabka wa nyiem chari wa dɔkdemma lammu kama. Wa le gebi lammu dii a te wa powa Peninna la, wa a gebi ka dila mɛ a te wa bisaŋa ale wa liema.

ref: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
text: Alege Yanna wa nyiem te ka ku nɔi buye dii nyiŋla wa a yaali wa ka nna yegayega, ale Naawen ale diem lik wa bisa biamu la meena.

ref: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
text: Peninna a kasim a nye Yanna ka dila bein meena. Diipo meena ba dan cheŋ Naawen yenni ale bo Siilo la, Peninna a nye Yanna a la kama ate wa kum a zɛri ŋandiinta.

ref: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
text: Kude nyiem dan nye, Elkana yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Yanna, ka boa ale soa ate fi a kum? Ka boa ale soa ate fi a zɛri ŋandiinta dɛka? Ka boa ate fi sui a kaasi? Mi ale yaali fu a soa diila an gaam bisa pi?>>

ref: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
text: Dai yeŋ Elkana ale wa dɔkdemma ale dɛ nueri Siilo po la, Yanna yaa yiti zaani. Eli waai ale ka kaabteerɔ la a jam kali ka zukpaglik zuk Naawen yenni tuoku nɔi peelim.

ref: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
text: Yanna sui ale jam kaasi nna yegayega ate wa puusi a te Naawen ale kasim a kum.

ref: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
text: Wa puusaŋa po wa yaa puulim a weeni ayen, <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, nya m niniga, kan baŋi. Fi dan te fi liewa nidoabili, mi a puulim kama ayen m le pai wa te fu wa boka po meena. Dii ale di sak ayen m pai wa te fu la wa kan che wa zuisaŋa.>>

ref: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
text: Wa le a puusi la, Eli a poli ayen wa nyu ka daam, diila wa nɔngbanvaataŋa ale a choa alege wa an jam puusi ate ku a jueli. Wa jam a puusi ka wa suinummu po.

ref: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
text: Eli yaa weeni Yanna ayen, <<Ka boa ti fi buk daam a jam dela? Basi fi daamu yibaŋa.>>

ref: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
text: Eli yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi baga a cheŋ kama ale suiyɔgni. Izirali Wenni ale nye dii ate fi bek wa la te fu.>>

ref: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
text: Yanna yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi a nye fi jiam. Be kasim poli wamaŋsa a te mu.>> Wa le biisi nueri la wa yaa basi Eli ale ga yaali ŋandiinta dɛ. Wa sui a ŋman jam kaasi ya.

ref: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
text: Vari ale veenti la saluik yokyokwa Elkana ale wa dɔkdemma a yaa yiti a puusi Naawen wa yenni po Siilo ale ŋman kuli ba yenni ale bo Arama la. Elkana yaa goa ale Yanna wa powa, ate Naawen a teeri wa wari.

ref: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ Yanna yaa yik lɔgi a biak nidoabili a te wa yuei ayen Samuel. Wa mawa weeni wadek ayen dii nyiŋla m bek ka Naawen ate wa te mu.

ref: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
text: Ku ŋman jam paari ka diipo ale magsi Elkana ale wa dɔkdemma a cheŋ Siilo a ga nye ben nuerika kaabka ate Naawen. Elkana mɛ poom jam a yaali kama ayen wa ga tuni wa pumpuulimaŋa a te Naawen.

ref: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
text: Yanna an jam va cheŋ ya. Wa jam weeni wa chorɔwa kama ayen, <<M kan va cheŋ yɔgyɔgla. M le limisi ate biika gaari biisiri abe m yaa ta wa cheŋ Wen yenni ale bo Siilo po la a pai wa te Naawen ate wa kasim bo dula.>>

ref: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
text: Wa chorɔwa Elkana yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ku bo ka fi jigi. Nye dii ale nala a te fu la. Wari bo yeri ate biika a gaari biisiri. Naawen a maari fu ate fi ta fi pumpuulimaŋa.>> Yanna yaa wari a nya wa biika zuk.

ref: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
