text: Kude nyiŋ, a nyini dila po a cheŋ baai ale a kaab Dagon la a daa jo wenni yenni po ba kan tabi juijui ate wenni jam lo dua la. Ba nyiem gaam tabi kama taam.

ref: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
text: Naawen jam namsi Asdod demma kama ale baai meena ale bo gilagilawa la. Wa jam basi ate ba nam ka nna yegayega. A basi ate ŋan pagra a moari ba nyiŋsaŋa.

ref: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
text: Asdod demma ale nya dii ale a nye la, ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Ti jɔgi ta nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale ka Izirali demma wen la a ga te ya. Ba wenni a namsi tama ale ti wenni Dagon kama.>>

ref: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
text: Ba yaa tom nuruba ate ba wi Filistia nalima ŋanuwa a bek ba ayen, <<Ti ta Izirali demma Wenni nɔiyeŋka dakanni a ga ka bɛ?>> Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ti ta di cheŋ Gat.>> Ba yaa te di cheŋ Filistia tɛŋka kanyi ate ba wi ayen Gat la.

ref: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
text: Alege ba le te di ga Gat la, Naawen basi ate ninam a paari ba ate ku daani ba nna yegayega. Wa basi ate ba nyiŋsaŋa a moari, bimbaansa ale ŋankpagsa meena.

ref: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
text: Nuruma dula jigini a basi ate di cheŋ Ekron, Filistia tɛŋ mɛ ale la. Alege ba le ta a jo Ekron la, nuruma deri a kaari ayen, <<Ba ta Izirali Wenni nɔiyeŋka dakanni a cheen ka dela ba ko ti ale ti nuruma meena.>>

ref: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
text: Ba yaa wi Filistia nalimaŋa a weeni ayen, <<Ni te di cheŋ Izirali. Ni te di cheŋ di nyama jigi, dan kan daa di di le ko ti meena.>> Dii nyiŋla ku jam a jo ba nyiŋ ka yegayega ate nuruba poom kpi.

ref: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
text: Baai ale kan jam kpi la jam a yuak kama ale ba nyiŋsaŋa ŋanmɔrintaŋa. Nuruma yaa kaari a wi ba wenaŋa.

ref: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
text: Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale bo Filistia paari chiisa siyopɔi la,

ref: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
text: nuruma yaa wi kaabteerɔma ale sampoporisaŋa a weeni ba ayen, <<Ti a ti nye nɔiyeŋka dakanni ka sɛ? Ni weeni ti le ti nye dii ate di cheŋ Izirali la.>>

ref: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
text: Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ti daa yaali ayen ti te nɔiyeŋka dakanni a cheŋ Izirali, ti kan te di cheŋ kinla ti gum nyemagsika tiirim du a saalim ba wenni ti le kaasi la. Ni dan nye dila, wa le tebi ni. Ni dan te tiirimu wa le basi ni namsika.>>

ref: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
text: Filistia demma yaa bek ayen, <<Ti tin ti te ka boan tiirim a magsi ti kaasuŋku?>> Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ti pai ligmɔniŋ a nye ŋanta ase ŋanmɔrinta la banu abe ni pai ligmɔniŋ mɛ a nye dawuita tinu a magsi Filistia nalima ŋanuwa. Dii nyiŋla tuemu a yik ka nama ale nalimaŋa.

ref: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
text: Ni pai ŋanmɔrintaŋa ale dawuitaŋa ale a kaasi tɛŋka la, a te Izirali Wenni a saalim wa. Da dii dai wa le basi tama ale ti wenaŋa ale ti tɛŋka namsika.

ref: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
text: Ni nye tama ale a weeni diila abe ni kan basi ate ni tue a kpari ase Ejipiti demma ale ba naawa la. Wen jam namsi ba ka nna yegayega ate ba yaa siak ate Izirali demma a cheŋ.

ref: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
text: <<Ni be yaali toroko paalik a yaa yaali naa ŋaai ale ta naabisa an diem a dari toroko a nya ya. A yaa bobi toroko a maŋ niiŋa ate ŋa ta cheŋ. Ni gaari ŋa bisaŋa a bobi zaani.

ref: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
text: Ni dan nye dila ni yaa pai Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni a zaani toroko zuk. A yaali dakari mɛ a pai ŋanmɔrintaŋa ale dawuitaŋa ate ni nye la a nyoro a te ase nyemagsika tiirim la. Ni kan te nuru a dari.

ref: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
text: Abe ni a nya ŋa, ŋa daŋ ga paari ŋa dek jigini tuak Bet Sɛmes abe ku sak ayen ka Naawen ale ta ninammu a jam ti zuk. Alege ŋa dan kan ta cheŋ du ti yaa le seba ayen ka ninam kama ale jam ti zuk daa Naawen ale ta jam.>>

ref: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
text: Ba yaa siak sinsaŋŋa de a yaa niiga ŋaye ŋaai ale ta naab bisa a bobi toroko a maŋ ŋa, ale bobi naabisaŋa.

ref: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
text: A yaa pai Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni a zaani toroko zuk. A pai dakari di choa a pai ŋanmɔrintaŋa ale dawuitaŋa ate ba nye la a nyoro.

ref: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
text: Ate niiŋa a cheŋ a duŋ Bet Sɛmes nyiŋ. Ŋa le a cheŋ ale a ŋuuni la ŋa an mobi gala yaase juga. Nalimaŋa yaa va ŋa a ga paari Bet Sɛmes banni.

ref: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
text: Dila po Bet Sɛmes demma a jam boro a che ka za viaka po. Ba le zak zuima nya nɔiyeŋka dakanni la, ba sue yaa jam peenti.

ref: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
text: Filistia nalima ŋanuwa yaa zaani niŋ a nya dii meena ale nye la ate ba yaa ŋman cheŋ Ekron dai dila danni.

ref: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
text: Filistia demma a te ka ŋanmɔrinta banu ate ba nye ale ligmɔniŋ la a magsi ba nyemagsika tiirim. Dinyi meena a magsi ba tɛŋsaŋa Asdod ale Gaza ale Askelon ale Gat ale Ekron.

ref: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
text: Ba jam pai ka ligmɔniŋka mɛ dawuita a magsi chaab ale Filistia tɛŋsaŋa, sii ale sɛ parisa a gilim ale sii ale kan sɛ parisa ate nalima ŋanuwa a nya si zuk la. Piuŋ kpioŋku ate ba pai nɔiyeŋka dakanni a zaani ku zuk Josua talimu po Bet Sɛmes po la a chim ka seerɔ dai dila danni ate dii nye la.

ref: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
text: Bet Sɛmes demma yaa bek chaab ayen, <<Ka wana ale baga a zaani Naawen, Wen weleŋka dɛ niŋŋa? Ti a ti ta dakanni ga te ka wana?>>

ref: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
text: Ba yaa tom nuruba ate ba cheŋ Kiriat Jearim a ga weeni ayen, <<Filistia demma a ta Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni a jam ti jigi kama. Ni jam pai ta cheŋ ni jigini.>>

ref: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
text: Kiriat Jearim demma yaa ga pai Naawen nɔiyeŋ dakanni a ta jam Abinadab yenni. Di jam za ka guuk zuk. Ba yaa jam gaari Abinadab nidoabinni Eleaza ayen wa a nya dakanni zuk.

ref: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
text: Ate Samuel yaa weeni Izirali demma ayen, <<Ni daa yaali ayen ni ŋmani Naawen jigi ale ni suiniima meena ni basi tɛŋ yonsa wena vaka. Abe ni maa basi bɔgluk nipowa ate ba a wi ayen Astarot la. Ni pai nidek a te Naawen abe ni a puusi wa. Ni dan nye dila, wa le vari ni Filistia demma jigi basi.>>

ref: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
text: Izirali demma yaa basi Baal ale Astarot bɔgtaŋa vaka ale va Naawen nyiini.

ref: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
text: Samuel yaa weeni niŋdeerɔma ayen, <<Ni wi Izirali demma meena ate ba tu Mizpa ate m puusi a te ni.>>

ref: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
text: Ba le tu Mizpa la, ba yaa ŋari nyiam a kpiiri a basi ase tiirim la a te Naawen. Da dila danni ba bobi ka nɔi a puusi a weeni ayen, <<Ba tom kaasi Naawen kama.>> Samuel jam le ba niŋdeerɔ Mizpa po.

ref: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
text: Filistia demma yaa wom ayen Izirali demma a tu chaab Mizpa. Nalima ŋanuwa yaa dɛ ba tugurik tɔŋdɔma niŋ ayen ba siti Izirali demma. Izirali demma ale wom ayen Filistia demma a cheen ba jigi la ba yaa chali yɔgsum.

ref: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
text: Ba yaa weeni Samuel ayen, <<Wa kasim puusi a te Naawen ti Wenni ate wa vari ti Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma nisa po basi.>>

ref: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
text: Diipo ate Samuel boro a nye kaabka la, ale Filistia demma a poom cheŋ moata kama ayen ba nye kpaliŋ. Naawen yaa basi ate wenni a na nyigsi Filistia demma, ate ba nyiŋsa a gɔk ate ba a chali.

ref: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
text: Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa chali Mizpa tɛŋka po a vi Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma a ko ba Bet Kar suiku po.

ref: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
text: Izirali tɛŋ sii ale jam bo Ekron ale Gat suŋsuŋ ate Filistia demma jam tuesi soa la, a ŋman jam chim ka Izirali tɛŋsa. Daa dila nyiini Amori demma a jam basi kpaliŋ nyeka ale Izirali kama.

ref: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
text: Samuel kasim a nya Izirali tɛŋka zuk kama ase niŋdeerɔ la wa boka meena po.

ref: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
text: Ben meena wa nyiem nyini ka Arama a gilim va Betel ale Gilgal ale Mizpa a bo Izirali demma buusa jiŋŋa de meena.

ref: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
text: Wa dan nueri wa tuimaŋa wa nyiem ŋman kuli ka wa tɛŋka Arama. Wa jam sɛ ka kaabka kuŋkuŋ dula jigini a te Naawen.

ref: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
text: Wa bikpagni yuei jam le Joel, waai ale pai saŋ la yuei ale Abaija. Ba jam a tom ka Beerseba.

ref: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
text: Izirali nisɔmma yaa jam jigi yeŋ ayen ba nya Samuel Arama tɛŋka.

ref: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
text: Ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de fi kpaŋ kama alege fi bisaŋa a kan va fi nyeka, dila nyiŋ lueri naab ate wa a nya ti zuk ate tama mɛ ta naab ase tɛŋ yonsa la.>>

ref: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
text: Samuel ale wom ayen ba a yaali naab la wa sui an peenti ya. Wa yaa puusi te Naawen ayen wa sak wa.

ref: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
text: Alege Naawen yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nye nuruma ale a yaali diila. Lueri naab a te ba. Fi a poli ayen ba zɛri ka fi, ka mi ate ba zɛri.

ref: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
text: A zaani diipo ate mi ta ba nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka po nyini la, ba kasim a zɛri mi kama alege a va wena. Dila dek ate ba a nye fi mɛ.

ref: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
text: Wom ba le a weeni diila, alege chiib kpaam ba naawa ale za wa yaali ayen ba nye dii te wa la.>>

ref: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
text: Samuel yaa jam weeni Naawen wieŋa meena a te nuru baai ale jam bek a yaali naab la.

ref: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
text: Wa weeni ba ayen, <<Dii ate naab waai a za wa a nya ni zuk la ale nye la ale nna. Wa le basi ate ni bisaŋa a tom a te wa, abe ba a dam kpaliŋ torokoba ale wusuma abe ba chali dɛ kpaliŋ torokoma niŋ a mooli juijui meena ate wa a cheŋ la.

ref: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
text: Wa le tuesi ni laŋsaŋa po ŋan baai ale zunchoŋ la, ale ni kaduksaŋa yɔn maŋsaŋa a te baai ale tom a te wa la.

ref: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
text: Ni kpanni ŋantaŋa ale ni daamu meena piika po wa le yeeri bunyi bunyi a te wa kpaŋŋa ale wa yɔmma.

ref: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
text: Wa le lueri ni nuruma gela nidoaba ale nipooba ate ba a tom wa yenni. Wa le lueri ni naab maŋsaŋa ale ni bon maŋsaŋa a te wadek.

ref: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
text: Daa dila nyiini piisa ale bua meena piik po wa le lueri kunyi. Di kpeglimka meena ni le chim ni naawa yɔm.

ref: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
text: Kula dan nye ni le kum a wi Naawen ayen wa basi ate ni naawa a ta jiirim ale ni. Alege Naawen a kan wom ni. Samuel ale weeni diila ale la.>>

ref: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
text: Ti a yaali ka naab ayen wa a dɛ ti niŋ ate ti a cheŋ kpaliŋsa ate tama mɛ a nye ase tɛŋ yonsa ale ta nalima diila.>>

ref: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
text: Samuel ale wom dii meena ate nuruma weeni la, wa yaa ŋman weeni sak Naawen.

ref: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
text: Ate Naawen yaa tulisi ayen, <<Wom ba le weeni diila abe fi te ba naab.>> Samuel yaa weeni Izirali demma ayen waai meena a kuli.

ref: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
text: Nuru ale jam boro wa yuei ale Kis. Wa nyini ka Benjamin buuni po. Wa jam jigsi kama alege ta yuei. Wa kowa yuei jam le Abiel, wa kokpieŋka yuei jam le Zeror. Wa ko kpieŋ kpieŋka yuei jam le Bekorat. Ba meena jam ka Apia ŋaaŋ tulisa.

ref: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
text: Kis jam ta ka biik wa yuei ale Sɔɔl. Sɔɔl jam diem ka biik a chim duerɔ a nala. Wa jam ka choa. Wa jam wɔŋŋa a gaam waai meena kama.

ref: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
text: Sɔɔl kowa Kis jam ta ka bonsa. Dai yeŋ si yaa cheŋ bɛ. Kis yaa weeni wa biika Sɔɔl ayen, <<Nyiem gisi bonsaŋa. Basi ate tomteerɔ wanyi a va fu.>>

ref: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
text: Sɔɔl yaa cheŋ va Ɛfraim juijui ate guuta a gilim la ale Salisa tɛŋsaŋa alege ba an nya si. Ba cheŋ va Saalim tɛŋka alege si ka dula. A va Benjamin geŋsaŋa meena alege ba an nya si.

ref: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
text: Ba le ŋman cheŋ ga moata Zuf la ate Sɔɔl yaa weeni wa tomteerɔwa ayen, <<Ti dan kuli a zunchoŋŋa dan kan daa di m kowa ale kasim a yiili ti wari kama alege daa bonsaŋa ŋmana.>>

ref: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
text: Tomteerɔwa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Naawen nuru ale bo tɛŋka de. Wa ka waai ate nuruba a zuli. Dii meena ate wa a weeni la ka wensie. Ku nala kama ase ti nin nya wa. Wa baga kama a weeni juijui ate ti a nya si la.>>

ref: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni tomteerɔwa ayen, <<Ti dan ga nya wa ti ti te wa ka boa? Ti abe dɛ ti ŋandiintaŋa meena alege ŋan koruta tara. Ti ka jaaboa a te wa. Ti ta jaaboa?>>

ref: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
text: Tomteerɔwa yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi ta ligbiri. Ti pai dila a te wa ate wa weeni ti juijui ate ti a nya si la.>>

ref: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni wa tomteerɔwa ayen, <<Ku nala ti cheŋ.>> Ate ba yaa cheŋ tɛŋka Wen nuruwa ale bo juijui la.

ref: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
text: Ba le jam a cheŋ jueli guuku a tuak tɛŋka la ba yaa tu nipokbilisa ale ba nyini tɛŋka po a nyini ba ŋari nyiam. Ba yaa bek nipokbilisaŋa ayen, <<Biisiteerɔwa a bo dela?>>

ref: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
text: Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Wa boro. Wa bo tɛŋka po ni niŋ geŋ. Wa jam dela ka jinla ayen wa nye kaabka a te nuruma guuku zuk.

ref: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
text: Ni daa yaali ayen ni nya wa ni kpabi. Wa le nyini tɛŋka po a jueli guuku a dɛ ale nuruma. Nuruma a limisi kama ba kan dɛ se wa nin jam niak kaabka. Ate baai ate ba wi ate ba jam la yaa dɛ. Ni nye nwuli a jo tɛŋka po, dai dii dai ni le nya wa alege ate wa cheŋ.>>

ref: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
text: Sɔɔl ale tomteerɔwa le a jo tɛŋka po la ba yaa nya Samuel a cheŋ guuku kaabka jigi a tu ba.

ref: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
text: Dai dii danni ale pai te dii ate Sɔɔl jam la, Naawen a biisi ale Samuel kama ayen,

ref: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
text: <<Chum nna po de m le tom nuru ate wa nyini Benjamin tɛŋka a jam fi jigi. Kpiiri kpaam a basi wa zukku po ate ku sak ayen wala ate mi lueri ayen wa chim Izirali naab. Wa le vari m nuruma Filistia demma nisa po a basi. M nya m nuruma kama a wom ba le kum a yaali maarika la.>>

ref: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
text: Samuel ale nya Sɔɔl la, Naawen yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nuru waai ate m weeni wa wie la ale nna. Wa le wa a nya m nuruma zuk.>>

ref: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
text: Sɔɔl yaa tu Samuel tɛŋka dek nɔi a yaa bek wa ayen, <<Mi a yaali ka biisiteerɔwa ale bo juijui la.>>

text: <<Mi a ŋma ka m dek m le basi ate Sɔɔl a chim naab la, dii nyiŋla wa basi m vaka kama alege an zuli mu.>> Ate ku yaa daani Samuel ate wa kum yok meena a te Naawen.

ref: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
text: Vari ale veenti la saluik Samuel yaa yiti a cheŋ ayen wa tu Sɔɔl. Alege nuruma yaa weeni Samuel ayen, <<Sɔɔl a cheŋ ka Karmel kauk kuui ate wa se wadek jaab ayen wa nya yuei la. Yɔgyɔgla de wa cheŋ ka Gilgal.>>

ref: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
text: Samuel ale jam Sɔɔl jigi la, Sɔɔl yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen niak fu. Mi va Naawen nɔi kama a nye wa yaalika.>>

ref: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
text: Alege Samuel yaa weeni ayen, <<Ka boa abe le soa ate mi a wom niiga ale piisa kumsa?>>

ref: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa tulisi ayen, <<Tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale tuesi Amalek demma jigi. Niiga ale piisa ŋaai ale nala la ti ta jam ayen ti nye kaabka a te fi Naawen fi Wenni alege duŋ yonsaŋa ti ko kama.>>

ref: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
text: Samuel yaa weeni Sɔɔl ayen, <<Limisi ate m weeni fu Naawen ale weeni mi dii deemwa yokku la.>> Sɔɔl yaa weeni ayen, <<Weeni mu.>>

ref: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
text: Samuel weeni ayen, <<Fi an jam pai fidek a chim nuru, alege yɔgyɔgla de fi chim Izirali buuni niŋdeerɔ. Naawen ale lueri fu ate fi chim naab a nya Izirali zuk.

ref: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
text: A yaa tom fu wari nyiŋ. Wa weeni ayen, <Cheŋ a ga ko Amalek demma ŋanbaataŋa. Nye kpaliŋ ale ba a ko ba meena.>

ref: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
text: Ka boa ale soa ate fi an va Naawen nɔi yaa? Ka boa ale soa ate fi wuuri lueri ŋanmaŋsaŋa? Ka boa ate fi nye dii ate Naawen ayen ku an nala la?>>

ref: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni ayen, <<Alege mi va Naawen nɔi kama? Mi nye Naawen ale weeni ayen mi nye diila kama. Mi ko Amalek demma ka meena ale ta ba naawa Agag jam.

ref: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔma a lueri ka naa maŋsaŋa ale pai maŋsaŋa ayen ti nye kaabka a te Naawen fi Wenni Gilgal tɛŋa po.>>

ref: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
text: Alege Samuel yaa tulisi wa ayen, Ka boa ale a peenti Naawen sui ya, kaabka yaa wa nɔi vaka? Wa nɔi vaka a zunchoŋ fi le pai pada naliŋsa a kaab te wa.

ref: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
text: Kan wom Naawen nɔi a bie ase ka sampoporinni la. Kanjanta a bie ase ka bɔgta kaabka la. Wa zɛri fu kama ase naab la, fi le zɛri wa wanni la nyiŋ.

ref: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni Samuel ayen, <<Mi tom kaasi kama. Mi an va Naawen nɔi ale fi le weeni diila. Mi chali ka nuruma yɔgsum a nye ba le weeni diila.

ref: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
text: Yɔgyɔgla de, mi a saalim fu, vɔŋ a te mu. Va mu a jam dɛ ate ti puusi Naawen.>>

ref: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
text: Alege Samuel a weeni Sɔɔl, <<Mi kan va fu. Fi zɛri Naawen nɔi kama ate wa yaa zɛri fu ase Izirali naab la.

ref: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
text: Samuel ale cheen wa cheŋ la, Sɔɔl yaa yik wa garukku tɛŋka ate ku cheeri.

ref: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
text: Samuel yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Naawen a cheeri Izirali naamu fi jigi kama jinla a pai te nuru yoŋ waai ale zunchoŋ fu.

ref: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
text: Waai a Ale Ka Izirali Zulaŋa La a kan velimu yaase wa tagri wa popola. Wa daa nuru biiga dila nyiŋ wa kan tagri wa popolaŋa.>>

ref: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni ayen, <<M tom kaasi kama. Alege zuli mu ŋankpagsaŋa ale Izirali demma niŋ. Va mu jam ate m puusi Naawen fi Wenni,>>

ref: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
text: Samuel yaa va Sɔɔl a cheŋ, ate Sɔɔl a puusi Naawen.

ref: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
text: Samuel yaa ŋman weeni ayen, <<Ta Amalek demma naawa Agag jam te mu.>> Alege Agag yaa poli ayen wa nyini kum po nyini kama.

ref: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
text: Samuel yaa weeni Agag ayen, Fi gebika basi kama ate maba a jɔg ba bisa. Yɔgyɔgla de fi mawa a kan ta bisa. Samuel yaa che Agag munamuna Naawen niŋ Gilgal tɛŋka po.

ref: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
text: Samuel yaa basi dula ale cheŋ Arama alege ate Sɔɔl mɛ a kuli Gibea.

ref: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
text: Samuel an ŋman jam nya Sɔɔl wa boka po meena alege Sɔɔl wie jam a daani wa kama. Naawen jam a ŋma ka wadek wa le basi ate Sɔɔl a chim Izirali naab la.

ref: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
text: Naawen yaa weeni Samuel ayen, <<Sɔɔl wie ale daani fi a paari ka dimpo? Mi zɛri wa kama, wa ŋman daa Izirali naaba. Pa kpaam a sueri nyiini a cheŋ. Mi a tom fu ka Jese jigi Betiliyem, dii nyiŋla mi lueri ka wa nidoabilisaŋa wanyi ayen wa chim naab.>>

ref: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
text: Alege Samuel yaa weeni ayen, <<M dan cheŋ Sɔɔl ale wom a ko mu.>> Naawen yaa weeni ayen, <<Yaali naab paalik a ta cheŋ. Weeni ayen, <M jam kama ayen m nye kaabka a te Naawen.>

ref: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
text: Wi Jese ate wa jam kaabka jigini. Ate m yaa weeni dii ate fi le nye la. Waai ate mi a dak la, kpiiri kpaamu basi wa zukku po a lueri wa.>>

ref: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
text: Samuel yaa nye dii ate Naawen weeni la. Wa le ga paari Betiliyem la nisɔmma nyiŋsa deri a gɔk. Ba yaa tu wa a bek wa ayen, <<Fidek ti fi cheena?>>

ref: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
text: Samuel yaa weeni ayen, <<Ka m dek. M jam kama ayen m nye kaabka a te Naawen. Ni be gomsi nidek magsi a jam.>> Ate wa yaa poori Jese ale wa bisaŋa a yaa wi ba ayen ba jam kaabka.

ref: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
text: Ba le jam la, Samuel yaa nya Jese biika Eliab a poli ayen Naawen a lueri ka waai ale za nna.

ref: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
text: Alege Naawen yaa weeni Samuel, <<Kan nya Eliab ale ka diila yaase wa le wɔŋŋa la, mi an lueri wa. Naawen kan nya wie ase nuruba ale a nya ŋa diila. Nuruba a nya ka peelim alege Naawen a nya suinummu po.>>

ref: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
text: Jese yaa wi Abinadab a weeni wa ayen wa taam ate Samuel nya wa. Alege Samuel weeni ayen, <<Naawen an lueri nuruwa de mɛ.>>

ref: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
text: Jese a ŋman basi ate Sammaya a taam. Alege Samuel a weeni ayen, <<Aaya, Naawen an lueri wa de.>>

ref: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
text: Jese yaa basi ate wa bisaŋa bayopɔi a taam. Alege Samuel a weeni ayen, <<Naawen an lueri ba de.>>

ref: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
text: Samuel yaa bek Jese, <<Ka fi bisaŋa meena ale nna.>> Jese yaa tulisi ayen, <<M ta bi baaŋ. Wa ta ka piisa nyini a nya.>> Samuel yaa weeni ayen, <<Tom wi wa ate wa jam ti kan kali ka wa nin jam.>>

ref: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
text: Jese yaa tom ate ba ta wa bi baaŋka a jam. Wa jam ka bi kaai ale nala a chim duerɔ. Naawen yaa weeni Samuel ayen, <<Ga bobi wa dii nyiŋla wala ate mi a lueri.>>

ref: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
text: Samuel yaa pai kpaamu ale nyiini a kpiiri basi Jese bi baaŋka zuk po a lueri wa wa suataŋa niŋ. A zaani da dila danni Naawen chiika jam sueri Deevid ale pagrim. Samuel yaa basi dula ale ŋman cheŋ Arama.

ref: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
text: Alege Naawen Chiika yaa basi Sɔɔl ate chiik biok a nyini Naawen jigi a jam namsi Sɔɔl nna yegayega.

ref: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
text: Sɔɔl tomteerɔma yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nya, Naawen basi ate ka chiik biok a daani fu nna yegayega.

ref: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
text: Te ti suik ate ti yaali nuru waai ale baga a nak kpanuŋ. Ate Naawen a dan basi ate chiik biok jam a daani fu, abe wa a nak ate ku zunchoŋ fi jigi.>>

ref: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni wa tomteerɔma ayen, <<Ni gisi ta waai ale baga a nak nalimnyiini a jam te mu.>>

ref: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
text: Tomteerɔma wanyi yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa nya Betiliyem denɔwa Jese. Wala nidoabinni ale a nak kpanuŋ. Wa ka waai ale ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ tuak. Wa biik nala ale chim nuru maŋ ate Naawen mɛ bo ale wa.>>

ref: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa tom wa tomteerɔma a weeni Jese ayen, <<Te ti fi biika Deevid waai ale a nya piisaŋa zuk la a jam.>>

ref: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
text: Jese yaa yaali boroborok ale bunlɔk ale daam ale buuk a vi boniŋ zuk a tom Deevid ate wa cheŋ Sɔɔl jigi.

ref: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
text: Deevid ale cheŋ Sɔɔl jigi la, wa yaa tom a te wa. Sɔɔl jam a yaali Deevid ka nna yegayega a yaa basi ate wa a yik wa kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa.

ref: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa tom weeni Jese ayen, <<Basi ate Deevid a bo ale mu a tom a te mu diila mi a yaali wa ka nna yegayega.>>

ref: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
text: Chiik bioku a dan nyini Naawen jigi jam a daani Sɔɔl, Deevid nyiem pai ka wa kpanuŋku a nak ate chiik bioku a basi Sɔɔl ate ku zunchoŋ wa jigi.

ref: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
text: Filistia demma yaa tigsi ba tugurik tɔŋdɔma a magsi kpaliŋ. Ba jam tu chaab ka Sokoyo ale bo Juda po la. A yaa nye goomu jigini Efes Dammim, Sokoyo ale Azeka suŋsuŋ po.

ref: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
text: Filistia demma a jam soa ka guuk kunyi, Izirali demma mɛ a soa kunyi ate viaka yaa bo suŋsuŋ.

ref: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
text: Filistia demma a jam ta ka ganduok, wa yuei jam le Goliat a nyini Gat. Wa yaa nyini Filistia demma tuka jigini a nyini. Wa jam wɔŋa ase ka anamagib pi ale buta la.

ref: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
text: Wa jam jo ka kuta ŋanta lik wa naŋsaŋa ale ta kuta gbaluk wa ŋaaŋ.

ref: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
text: Wa gbaluku dueku a jam zuak ase ka chib la, ate gbaluku kutukku nɔnni a dobra ase ligbie dobrim kobsiyuebi la. Waai ale jam yik jaab buuni ate wa pai a chɔgsi ŋanta la jam bo ka wa niŋ.

ref: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
text: Goliat yaa nyini zaani a kaari weeni Izirali demma, <<Ka boa ate ni tu ayen ni nye kpaliŋŋa? Mi ka Filistia denɔ nama Sɔɔl tomteerɔba? Ni lueri waai ate wa jam kpaliŋ ale mi.

ref: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
text: Wa dan baga a ko mi tama ale chim ni yɔm. Mi abe dan baga a ko wa nama chim tama tomteerɔba.>>

ref: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
text: Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Jinla mi za a nak nanpaga ale Izirali demma, ni lueri waai ate ti kpaliŋ chaab.>>

ref: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
text: Sɔɔl ale Izirali demma ale wom Filistia denɔwa biika la yɔgsum yaa yik ba nna yegayega.

ref: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
text: Deevid jam ka Jese biik Jese jam ka Efrat denɔ a nyini Betiliyem ale bo Juda po la. Jese a jam ta ka bisa naaniŋ. Sɔɔl daaŋa po Jese a jam kpaŋ kama yɔgla.

ref: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
text: alege Deevid a nyini Sɔɔl jigi a cheŋ Betiliyem a kasim a nya wa kowa piisaŋa ale a ŋmani.

text: Daa pisinaansi meena saluik ale junɔi Goliat a nyiem nyini kama a zaani a nak nanpaga ale Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma.

ref: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
text: Deevid yaa pai wa doani a nyo nisa po ale pisi tana ŋanu beli naŋka po. A yaa pai nyo wa naapeerik foruku po ale pai wa visiŋka. Wa yaa cheŋ ayen wa tu chaab ale ganduoku.

ref: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
text: Jese yaa weeni wa biika Deevid ayen, <<Pa ŋandiintaŋa de boorik genni ale borobotta pi a kpabi ga te fi suataŋa kpaliŋka jigini.

text: Fi suataŋa a bo ale ka Sɔɔl ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma Elaya Viaka po ayen ba kpaliŋ ale Filistia demma.>>

ref: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.

ref: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.

text: Deevid yaa basi ŋandiintaŋa ate nuru waai ale a nya ba ŋandiintaŋa zuk la ale cheŋ kpaliŋka jigini ayen wa puusi wa suataŋa.

ref: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.

ref: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
text: Deevid yaa bek nuru baai ale za moata wala ayen, <<Ba le nye ka boa a te nuru waai ale baga a ko Filistia denɔwa de la a yeeri chivieŋa de Izirali jigiya? Filistia denɔwa de waai ale kaa a te Naawen la ate a poli wa baga a nak nanpaga ale Naawen dii ale vua la tugurik tɔŋdɔma kama yaa?>>

ref: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.

text: Deevid suok kpagni Eliab ale wom Deevid ale a biisi ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma la, wa sui yaa puuri ale Deevid, wa yaa bek Deevid, <<Ka boan ti fi jam dela? ref: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi an baga a ga a nye kpaliŋ ale Filistia denɔwa de. Fi ka biik. Goliat abe nye kpaliŋ a nyini ka wa biik po.>>

ref: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
text: Alege Deevid a weeni Sɔɔl ayen, <<Mi fi tomteerɔwa a nya ka m kowa piisa zuk. Ase gbeŋli yaase piuk a dan jam yik piisaŋa kunyi,

ref: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
text: Mi nyiem vi di kama a vari posuku a basi. Gbeŋli yaase piuk a dan siti mi, mi nyiem yik ka di zukku a nak ko.

ref: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
text: Mi waai ale ka fi tomteerɔ la, a ko gbeŋli ale piuk kama. Filistia denɔwa de bɔgluk kaarika m le ko wa ase ka gbeŋli yaase piuku la, dii nyiŋla wa biisi a kaasi Naawen dii ale vua la tugurik tɔŋdɔma kama.

ref: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
text: Naawen ale vari mi gbeŋli ale piuku jigi a basi la ale vari mi Filistia denɔwa de jigi a basi.>> Sɔɔl yaa weeni Deevid, <<Cheŋ ale Naawen ale bo ale fu.>>

ref: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
text: Sɔɔl yaa pai wadek kɔlimaŋa a jo Deevid. Wa jam pai wa kuta zuk chinni a vuk wa ale pai kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa a jo wa.

ref: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
text: Deevid yaa pai Sɔɔl gebika a cheŋ gilim alege wa an pai ŋan baai ate Sɔɔl a pai jo wa la a nye wari nya ya. Wa yaa weeni Sɔɔl ayen, <<Mi an baga a ta ba a cheŋ, dii nyiŋla mi an pai ba nye wari nya ya.>> Deevid yaa yeeri ŋantaŋa meena.

ref: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
text: Filistia denɔwa yaa cheŋ a ga tu wa. Nuru waai ale jam yik wa jakasimu la a dɛ ka wa niŋ.

ref: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
text: Goliat ale nya Deevid ale wa ka biik ale nala la, wa deri kisi wa.

ref: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
text: Wa yaa weeni Deevid ayen, <<Fi pai mi a chim ka biaga ate fi cheen mi jigi ale doari ya.>> Wa yaa wi ba bɔgtaŋa wie a ka a te Deevid.

ref: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
text: Wa yaa weeni Deevid ayen, <<Jam dela. M le ko fu a te wenzuk nuinsa ale duŋsa.>>

ref: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
text: Alege Deevid yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi cheen ale ka gebik ale gbatta tiye. Mi bɛ cheena ale ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma Wenni yuenni nyiŋ. Fi biisi kaasi Wen dila kama.

ref: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
text: Jinla Naawen dii ale ta pagrim la ale pai fu nyo m nisa po ate m ko fu a gebi fi zukku. Jinla m le ko Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma ate nuinsa ale duŋsa a de ba. Ate tɛŋka meena seba ayen Wen a bo ale Izirali.

ref: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
text: Waai meena ale tigsi dela la ale seba ayen Naawen dii ale ta pagrim la a kan pai daa gebisa ale gbatta a vari wa nuruba a basi. Kpaliŋka ka Naawen ale soa, wa bɛ le pai fu te mu.>>

ref: When Goliath started forward, David ran toward him.
text: Goliat ale torisi moata wa la, Deevid yaa chali nwuli a tu wa.

ref: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
text: Wa yaa yeeri tain wa foruku po, a pai nyo wa visiŋka po a nak. Tintanni yaa ga yik dinni a vuri jo, ate Goliat a lo nyue nyiŋ.

ref: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
text: Deevid a pai ka visiŋ ale tain a nak dɛ Goliat. Wa jam nak kama a ko wa. Wa jam ka gebik wa nisa po.

ref: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
text: Deevid yaa chali ga zaani wa tɛŋ. Wa yaa yeeri Goliat dek gebik ka fook po a gebi wa zukku. Filistia demma ale nya ayen ba ganduok a kpi la, ba deri cheen pai chala choa.

ref: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
text: Izirali ale Juda nuruma yaa kaari zik zik a vi Filistia demma a ga paari viaka ale Ekron tɛŋka nɔi. Filistia demma a jam kpi dua ka nna bilabila Saaraim suiku po a ga paari Gat ale Ekron.

ref: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
text: Izirali demma yaa vi ba pilim ŋmani Filistia demma tuka jigini a pai ba ŋantaŋa.

ref: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
text: Deevid yaa pai Goliat zukku a ta cheŋ Jerusalem. Wa jam pai Goliat kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa a dueni ka wadek viuku po.

ref: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
text: Sɔɔl ale nya Deevid ale wa cheŋ ayen wa tu Goliat la, wa yaa bek Abner, Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni ayen, <<Abner biika nna ko ale wana?>> Abner yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi zɛ.>>

ref: “Then find out!” Saul told him.
text: Naawa yaa weeni ayen, <<Bek wom ase ka wana biik.>>

ref: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa bek wa ayen, <<Biiga, fi ko ale wana?>> Deevid yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi ka fi tomteerɔwa Jese ate wa nyini Betiliyem la biik.>>

ref: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
text: Sɔɔl jam basi ate Deevid bo ale wa kama a nyini dai dila danni a kan siak ate wa a ga wa kowa yenni.

ref: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
text: Sɔɔl biika Jonatan ale Deevid yaa jam nye nɔiyeŋ dii nyiŋla wa jam a yaali Deevid ase ka wadek la.

ref: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
text: Wa jam yeeri wa garukku kama a te Deevid, ale wa kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa ale wa gebika ale wa tommu ale wa chiak gbanni.

ref: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
text: Sɔɔl a jam tom Deevid kama ate wa ga nye kpaliŋ yonsa. Deevid jam nak kama dɛ. Ate Sɔɔl jam basi ate Deevid a chim tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi. Ku jam peenti Sɔɔl kpaŋŋa ale nuruma meena sui kama.

ref: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
text: Deevid ale ko Filistia denɔwa la, wa le nuruma meena ale jam ŋman kuli la, nipooma yaa nyini tɛŋsaŋa meena ale bo Izirali po la a nyini a tu naab Sɔɔl. Ba jam a yi ka yiila ale suipeentik a gɔk ale a yegsi ŋanta ale a nak kpanta.

ref: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
text: Ba le a nak la, ba yaa yi yiila ayen, Sɔɔl ko ka dachaasa tusa, alege Deevid a ko tusa piisa.

ref: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
text: Nipooma yiini a yaa daani Sɔɔl, ate wa sui a puuri. Wa yaa poli, <<Nipooma a weeni ayen Deevid a ko tusa piisa, alege a weeni ayen mi ko ka tusidi nyiini. Dii yaa le tali la ale wa tuesi naamu.>>

ref: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
text: Vari ale veenti la chiik biok yaa nyini Wen jigi a jam jo Sɔɔl, ate wa a porisi wie yenni po. Ate Deevid a jam pai kpanuŋ a nak ase wa nyiem le poom a nye diila. Sɔɔl abe jam ta ka gbaluk nisa po.

ref: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
text: Wa yaa yuk gbaluku ale poli ayen, <<M le yuk wa a maŋ ka siaka.>> Alege Deevid a nyini du nyini buye meena.

ref: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
text: Naawen dii ale ta pagrim la a jam bo le Deevid kama alege basi Sɔɔl. Dila nyiŋ Sɔɔl yaa jam a chali Deevid ka yɔgsum.

ref: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
text: Wa jam nya nakdeka kama ale dii meena dii nyiŋla Naawen a jam bo le wa kama.

ref: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
text: Alege Izirali ale Juda nuruma meena a jam a yaali Deevid ka nna yegayega dii nyiŋla wa jam a dɛ ba niŋ kama nalimnyiini kpaliŋ po.

ref: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni Deevid ayen, <<M lie kpagni Merab ale nna. M le basi ate fi faari wa. Mi a yaali ka fi tin tua abe fi a kpaliŋ Naawen kpaliŋsaŋa.>> Sɔɔl a jam poli kama ayen, <<Mi kan ko Deevid ka Filistia demma ale ba ko wa.>>

ref: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
text: Alege Deevid yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi ka wana? Mi ale nyini dɔkdem baai po la an magsi mi chim naawa chicham biiga.>>

ref: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
text: Ku le jam paari diipo ate Sɔɔl liewa Merab a magsi wa yali Deevid la, Sɔɔl a gɔnti pai wa te Adriel ale nyini Meyola la.

ref: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
text: Sɔɔl liewa wa choawa, Michal a jam yaali Deevid kama. Ba le weeni Sɔɔl la, wa sui jam peenti kama.

ref: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa poli ayen, <<M le basi ate wa yali Deevid. Ate wa yaa chim wa baruk ate Filistia, demma a baga a ko wa.>> Sɔɔl yaa ŋman weeni Deevid nye buye ayen, <<Fi baga a chim m chicham biik kama.>>

ref: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
text: Ba weeni dila meena a te Deevid. Alege Deevid yaa weeni ayen, <<Nama a poli ayen ku ka wa fiik ate fi chim naawa chicham biiga? Mi ka jajak nuruba abe zɛ mu piisi ya.>>

ref: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
text: Sɔɔl tomteerɔma le weeni wa dii ate Deevid a weeni la,

ref: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
text: Sɔɔl yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ni weeni Deevid ayen, <Naawa a kan yaali jaab nipok fiaka nyiŋ a gaam fi ale ko Filistia demma kook a gebi ba yua gbantaŋa ate ku chim tutuna a te wa dachaasaŋa la.> >> Sɔɔl zɔŋŋa jam le Filistia demma a ko Deevid.

ref: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
text: Tomteerɔma ale weeni Deevid wieŋa de la, wa sui yaa peenti ayen wa chim naawa chichambiik. Abe daaŋa a paari la,

ref: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
text: Sɔɔl ale miŋ ayen Naawen dii ale ta pagrim la a bo ale Deevid la ate wa liewa Michal mɛ a yaali wa la,

ref: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
text: yɔgsum yaa ŋmasi ta Sɔɔl nna yegayega ate Deevid yaa kasim chim wa dachiak a cheŋ.

ref: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
text: Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpaŋŋa a jam kasim a cheŋ kpaliŋka ka dila. Ba bɛ le a cheŋ diila Deevid a nya nakdeka mɛ ka dila a gaam Sɔɔl tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpaŋŋa. Deevid yuenni a yaa jam a yiti ate waai meena a sebi wa.

ref: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni wa biika Jonatan ale wa nuruma meena ayen ba ko Deevid, alege Jonatan jam a yaali Deevid ka nna yegayega.

ref: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
text: M le nyini ga za ale m kowa juijui ate fi suk la abe m yaa biisi fi wie ale wa. Dii meena ale boro la m le basi ate fi seba.>>

ref: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
text: Deevid a pai wadek nyuvuri a da ate Naawen basi ate Izirali meena nya nak dekka. Fi nya ku kama ate fi sui jam peenti. Ka boa ate fi le nye Deevid kaasi? Wa an kaasi wari ya. Wari karo a magsi wa ko ka.>>

ref: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
text: Sɔɔl yaa wom Jonatan ale biisi diila a yaa puulim ayen, <<Naawen ale vua la nyiŋ, m kan ko Deevid.>>

ref: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
text: Jonatan yaa wi Deevid a weeni wa dii meena ate Sɔɔl a biisi la. Wa yaa ta Deevid a jam Sɔɔl jigi ate Deevid a ŋman bo le Sɔɔl ase piilimka la.

ref: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
text: Kpaliŋ ale ŋman jam yiti ate Deevid nyini ga kpaliŋka ale Filistia demma. Wa jam nak dɛ ba kama ale ko ba yega ate ba gela a chali.

ref: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
text: Sɔɔl yaa nye nyiŋbiiri ayen wa yuk Deevid a maŋ siaka ale gbaluku ale bo wa nisaŋa po la, alege Deevid yɔk ga nakpiak. Sɔɔl gbaluku jam vuri ka siaka alege ate Deevid chali bɛ yok kula.

ref: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
text: Sɔɔl yaa tom nuruba ayen ba ga Deevid yenni a kpesi nya abe ba ko wa saluiku. Alege Deevid powa Michal yaa kaam wa ayen, <<Yɔkku de se fi chali ti vummu nyiŋ. Fi dan kan chali ya, fi le kpi saluik.>>

ref: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
text: Wa yaa basi ate Deevid va tuokparuk a siŋ chali bɛ.

ref: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
text: Deevid powa Michal yaa pai bɔgluk a dueni gaduokku zuk, a pai buuk kɔbta a lik ku nyiŋka a ŋman pai buuku kɔbta mɛ a dueni zukku geŋ.

ref: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa tom nuruba ayen ba ga yik Deevid, ale ge Michal yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa a yuak kama.>>

ref: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
text: Sɔɔl a ŋman tom nuruma ayen ba ŋman ga nya Deevid, a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni pai wa le gaduokku meena a ta jam ate m ko wa.>>

ref: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
text: Nuruma ale ga jo Deevid dɔkku po la, ba yaa nya bɔgluk ale dua gaduokku zuk ate kɔbta lik ku zukku.

ref: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
text: Sɔɔl yaa weeni Michal ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate fi paasi mu nna? Fi basi ate m dachiaka a nyini ayen wa chali bɛ.>> Michal yaa tulisi Sɔɔl, <<Deevid weeni mi kama ayen m dan kan maa wa ate wa chali bɛ ya, wa le ko mu.>>

ref: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
text: Deevid ale nyini Sɔɔl jigi a chali bɛ la, wa yaa cheŋ Samuel jigi Arama tɛŋka a ga weeni wa dii meena ate Sɔɔl a nye wa la. Deevid ale Samuel yaa cheŋ Naiot a bo dula.

ref: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa wom ayen Deevid a bo ka Naiot ale bo Arama tɛŋka la.

ref: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
text: Wa yaa tom nuruba ayen ba ga yik wa. Alege ba yaa ga zik biisiteerɔba ale ba tigsi za a mooli wie, ate Samuel a dɛ ba niŋ. Naawen chiika yaa jo Sɔɔl nuruma ate ba maari a mooli wieŋa.

ref: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
text: Sɔɔl ale wom dii meena ale nye la, wa yaa tom nuruba yega, alege ba mɛ a maa mooli. Wa ŋman tom nuruba nye buta, alege ba mɛ mooli.

ref: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
text: Sɔɔl dek yaa cheŋ Arama, a paari vili kpienni ale bo Seku la a yaa bek ayen, <<Samuel ale Deevid a bo ka bɛ?>> Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Ba bo ka Naiot ale bo Arama la.>>

ref: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
text: Sɔɔl ale cheŋ Naiot ale bo Arama la, Wen Chiika yaa jo wa. Ate wa yaa mooli a cheŋ a ga paari Naiot ale bo Arama la.

ref: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
text: Wa yaa yeeri wa gattaŋa alege za Samuel niŋ a mooli. Wa duak ka dila yokku ale kantueŋka meena. Dila ale soa ate nuruba a bek ayen, <<Sɔɔl mɛ maa ka biisiteerɔma po wanyi yaa?>>

ref: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
text: Deevid yaa basi Naiot ale bo Arama po la ale chali cheŋ Jonatan jigi. Wa yaa bek Jonatan ayen, <<M nye ka sɛ? M kaasuŋku ale boa? M tin nye ka sɛ a kaasi fi kowa? Ka boa ate wa yaali ayen wa ko mu?>>

ref: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
text: Jonatan yaa tulisi ayen, <<Aaya, fi kan kpi. Nya, mi kowa kan nye wa kpienni yaase wa fiik alege kan weeni mi. Boan le soa ate wa a suk kude mi jigiya? Ku daa wensie.>>

ref: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
text: Alege Deevid yaa pɛ, a weeni ayen, <<Fi kowa seba kama nalimnyiini ayen fi a yaali mi kama. Wa le weeni wadek ayen, <Jonatan an magsi wa seba kan daa di wa sui ale kaasi.> Deevid, Naawen ale vua ate fi mɛ vua la mi an yalima ale kum.>>

ref: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
text: Jonatan yaa weeni Deevid ayen, <<M le nye dii meena ate fi a yaali ayen m nye la.>>

ref: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
text: Deevid yaa weeni ayen, <<Nya, chum ale Chiik Paalika tigini. Ku magsi ka m dɛ ŋandiinta ale naawa, alege basi ate m suk peelim a paari daa ŋata junɔi.

ref: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
text: Fi kowa a dan kan nya mu weeni wa ayen m cheŋ ka Betiliyem. Ben meena ase nna po de la wa dɔkdemma a tigsi ka chaab a nye kaabka.

ref: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
text: Fi kowa dan weeni ayen, <ku nala>, m soa m dek kama. Alege wa sui a dan puuri, fi seba ayen wa le nye mu wari.
