text: Deevid yaa cheŋ Keila a ga nye kpaliŋ ale Filistia demma a tuesi ba niiŋa. Deevid a jam ko Filistia demma ka nna yegayega a vari Keila demma a basi.

ref: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
text: Deevid mɛ yaa wom ayen Sɔɔl a ta ka popola baata zɔga a yaa wa siti wa. Dila nyiŋ wa yaa weeni kaabteerɔwa Abiata ayen ta garuk genni a jam.

ref: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
text: Deevid yaa puusi ayen, <<Naawen, Izirali Wen yaa, mi wom kama ayen Sɔɔl a zɔk kama ayen wa jam kaasi Keila tɛŋka mi nyiŋ.

ref: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
text: Keila tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma ale pai mi a te Sɔɔl? Sɔɔl ale jam Keila ase mi ale wom diila? M Naawenni, Izirali Wen yaa, weeni a sak mi fi tomteerɔwa.>> Naawen yaa tulisi ayen, <<Sɔɔl ale jam.>>

ref: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
text: Deevid yaa ŋman bek ayen, <<Keila niŋdeerɔma ale pai mi ale m nuruma a nyo Sɔɔl nisima po?>> Naawen yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ba le pai te.>>

ref: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
text: Deevid jam suk bo ka pinaŋa po guuk zuk Zif gɔnni po. Sɔɔl jam kasim a gisi Deevid ka daaŋa meena alege Wen an pai Deevid a te wa.

ref: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
text: Deevid ale jam bo Yores Zif gɔnni po la, wa jam wom kama ayen Sɔɔl a cheen wa ko wa.

ref: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
text: Alege Sɔɔl biika Jonatan yaa cheŋ Deevid jigi Yores a te wa nyiŋbiiri ate wa siaka a pagra ale Wen.

ref: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
text: Jonatan yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Kan chali yɔgsum, dii nyiŋla mi kowa kan tiri fu. Fi le chim Izirali naab ate mi pai a vi fu. Mi kowa Sɔɔl dek poom seba kude kama.>>

ref: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
text: Ba nɔi bayewa yaa nye nɔiyeŋ Naawen niŋ. Ate Jonatan yaa kuli alege Deevid a bo Yores tɛŋka.

ref: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
text: Zif demma yaa cheŋ Sɔɔl jigi Gibea tɛŋka a weeni wa ayen, <<Deevid a suk bo ka tama tɛŋka po. Wa bo ka Yores pinaŋa po, Yachila guuku zuk, Jesimon yeseok geŋ.

ref: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
text: Sɔɔl yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Naawen a niak fu fi le ta jiirim ale mu la nyiŋ.

ref: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
text: Cheŋ a ga kpesi nya chak. Nya ase wa bo ka be dek chekki abe fi bek ase ka wana ale nya wa. Mi wom ayen wa seba ka nna yegayega.

ref: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
text: Kpesi bek wom wa sukka jiŋŋa meena abe fi ŋman jam weeni mu wari meena. Ate m yaa cheŋ ale fu. Deevid a dan bo dula dan poom ka m gisi Juda buuni po meena m le nye.>>

ref: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
text: Ba yaa dɛ Sɔɔl niŋ a cheŋ Zif. Yɔgyɔgla de Deevid nuruma jam ga bo ka Maon gɔnni po, Jesimon yeseok geŋ.

ref: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
text: Sɔɔl ale wa nuruma yaa cheŋ ba gisi Deevid, alege Deevid a wom ba wari a yaa cheŋ siŋ piuŋ po Maon gɔnni po. Sɔɔl ale wom la, wa yaa va Deevid naŋsa a jam Maon gɔnni po.

ref: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
text: Sɔɔl a jam sali va ka piuŋku gauŋ nyiŋ alege Deevid ale wa nuruma mɛ a bo gauŋ kunkula. Ba jam a kpabi kama ayen ba chali bɛ Sɔɔl, dii nyiŋla Sɔɔl ale wa nuruma a jam moata ba kama.

ref: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
text: Alege ba yaa tom waai Sɔɔl jigi ate wa weeni ayen, <<Nye nwuli a jam. Filistia demma a jam siti ti tɛŋka kama.>>

ref: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
text: Sɔɔl yaa basi Deevid vi ka ale cheŋ ayen wa tu chaab ale Filistia demma. Dila ale soa ate ba a wi dela ayen piuŋ kuui jigi ate ti chali bɛ ti dachaasaŋa la.

ref: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
text: Deevid yaa basi Maon gɔnni ale cheŋ ga bo En Gedi pinaŋa po.

ref: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
text: Sɔɔl ale nye kpaliŋka ale Filistia demma ale pilim ŋman la, waai yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Deevid a bo ka En Gedi Pinaŋa po.>>

ref: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
text: Sɔɔl yaa jam piisa geruku ale moata manpanni la piuŋ vɔrup ale jam bo dula, ate wa jo ayen wa basi yaata. Deevid ale wa nuruma abe jam boka vɔrup bula dek po niŋniŋŋa.

ref: of Israel's best soldiers out to look for David and his men near Wild Goat Rocks at En-Gedi.
text: ) Izirali tɛŋka meena ate ba ga a gisi Deevid ale wa nuruma, Gɔi Bua Pinaŋa niŋ.

ref: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
text: Nuruma yaa weeni Deevid ayen, <<Jinla ale dai dii dai ate Nyɔnɔwa a biisi di wari la, wa weeni ayen, <M le pai fi dachiaka a te fu. Nye wa fi ale a yaali diila.> >> Deevid yaa mak a kuuk a ga gebi Sɔɔl garukku nɔnni.

ref: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ Deevid ŋman ŋma wadek wa le gebi Sɔɔl garukku nɔnni la.

ref: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
text: Deevid jam biisi ka nna a kasi wa nuruma ate ba an nye Sɔɔl wari ya. Ate Sɔɔl yaa nyini vɔrumu po a nyini a cheŋ.

ref: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
text: Deevid yaa saŋ va nyini a kaari wi ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ naaba.>> Sɔɔl yaa cheen ŋaaŋ nya ate Deevid a koori tɛŋ a zuli wa.

ref: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
text: Wa yaa weeni Sɔɔl ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate fi a wom nuru baai ale a weeni fu ayen, <Deevid a yaa wa ko fu kama la.>

ref: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
text: Ku daa wensie mi nya suik kama magsi m ko fu vɔrumu po. Mi nuruma gela weeni ayen ka m ko fu, alege mi zɛri ale basi fu, dii nyiŋla Naawen ale lueri fu.

ref: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
text: M dek koa, nya mi gebi ka fi garukku nɔnni, alege an ko fu. Yɔgyɔgla de be miŋ a seba ayen mi ka popola baata ale fu. Mi an zɛri fi nɔi ya. Mi an nye fu wari a kaasi ya, alege fi a vi mu ayen fi ko.

ref: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
text: Daam ale weeni ayen, <Nuru baata ale a nye wabaata.> Alege kan te ku daani fu mi kan nye fu wari ya.

ref: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
text: <<Ka mi ate Izirali naawa a vi? Biak kpiukwa, yaase m ka kabik ga.

ref: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
text: Naawen be bo mi ale fi buusa a nya ti waai ale kaasi la. Naawen maa maari mu abe wa sak ayen m nye magsi. Wa bɛ vari mu fi jigi a basi.>>

ref: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
text: A weeni ayen, <<Fi ka nuru maŋ a gaam mi. Fi nye a magsi kama alege mi nye a kaasi.

ref: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
text: Fi weeni mu wamaŋ sii meena ate fi nye la. Naawen a pai mu te fu kama, alege fi an ko mu.

ref: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
text: Nuru a dan nya wa dachiak wa basi ate wa a cheŋ yaa wa kan basi? Naawen ale tuni fu a magsi wamaŋ kaai ate fi nye mu la.

ref: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
text: Mi seba ayen fi le sum chim naab a nya Izirali tɛŋka zuk.

ref: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de puulim ale Naawen ayen fi kan ko m ŋaaŋsaŋa abe fi kan yeeri m yuenni m kowa dɔkdemma po.>>

ref: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
text: Deevid yaa puulim a te Sɔɔl. Ate Sɔɔl yaa ŋman kuli, alege ate Deevid ale wa nuruma a ŋman ga suk guuku zuk.

ref: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
text: Deevid ale jam diem bo gɔnni po la wa yaa wom ayen Nabal a boro a chari wa piisaŋa.

ref: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
text: Ni weeni Nabal ayen, <Fi ale fi dɔkdemma ale baai meena ate fi soa la ale ta nyiŋyɔgsa.

ref: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
text: << <M wom kama ayen fi boro a chari fi piisaŋa. Fi naapeerisaŋa ale jam bo le ti la, ti an nye ba wari ya. Fi piisaŋa ale jam kasim bo Karmel la ti an zu ŋa.

ref: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
text: Bek fi tomteerɔma ba le weeni fu. Ti jam ka suipeentik dai ta jiirim ale m nuruma. Fi le ta jabuui meena la pai te ba ale fi biika Deevid.> >>

ref: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
text: Deevid nuruma ale ga paari du la, ba yaa weeni Nabal Deevid ale weeni ba diila alege a limisi.

ref: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
text: Wa weeni ba ayen, <<Deevid ka wana? Ka wana ale Jese biiga? Jinla tomteerɔba yegayega ale a chali ale a ge ba kpaga.

ref: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
text: Mi ta ŋandiinta ale nyiam kama ale lanta a magsi m tomteerɔma ale a gebi m piisaŋa kɔbtaŋa la. Alege mi kan pai a te nuru baai ate mi zɛ ba.>>

ref: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
text: Deevid nuruma yaa ŋman weeni wa dii meena ate Nabal a weeni la.

ref: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
text: Deevid yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni pai ni gebisaŋa.>> Ba yaa pai ba gebisaŋa, ate wa mɛ a pai wa gebika. Nuruba kobsinaansi ale jam va Deevid cheŋ alege kobsiye wari a nya ba ŋantaŋa.

ref: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de be poli ku wari a nya ti le ti nye diila. Daani kpieŋ ale za ka jam ti kpagni ale wa dɔkdemma zuk. Nabal nyeka tua ka nna yegayega ate nuru an baga a biisi ale wa.>>

ref: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
text: A yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Cheŋ ate mi a vi ni.>> Alege wa an jam weeni wa chorɔwa.

ref: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
text: Abigail yaa do wa boniŋka a ga paari gɔnni po guuku jigini. Dula jigini wa yaa tu Deevid ale wa nuruma a siŋ cheen wa jigi.

ref: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
text: Deevid poom weeni kama ayen, <<Nabal ŋantaŋa ate mi a nya ba zuk gɔnni po la ka koa. Mi nya ŋa zuk kama ate kunyi mɛ la an bɛ ya. Mi nye wa ka nalim alege ate wa pai biem a tuni mi.

ref: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
text: Wen a namsi mi Deevid nna yegayega. Ase mi nin basi ate Nabal nuruma wanyi mɛ la a bɛ alege ate vari a veenti.>>

ref: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
text: Abigail ale ga nya Deevid la, wa yaa kpabi nyini wa boniŋka zuk a siŋ a koori tɛŋ a puusi wa.

ref: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
text: M nyɔnɔ, Nabal ka kiriya. Kan basi ate wa le nye diila a daani fu. Wa yuenni ale ka diila, wadek ka dila. Wa yuenni kiri ale beruk. Wa bɛ sum ka beruk. Alege mi fi tomteerɔwa, nina an tu baai ate fi tom la.

ref: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
text: Mi a saalim, vɔŋ m kaasuŋku a te mu. Naawen ale basi ate fi dɔkdemma a ta nalima yegayega, dii nyiŋla fi ale a kpaliŋ wa kpaliŋsaŋ. Fi le vua la nyiŋ, Kan nye wabiowa.

ref: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
text: Nuru a dan poom a vi fu ayen wa ko, alege Naawen fi Wenni ale yik fu tara ate fi vua. Wa le yuk fi dachaasaŋa nyuvooŋa a basi ase wa le pai tintain a nyo visiŋ po a nak a basi diila.

ref: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
text: Naawen ale yik ŋanmaŋ sii meena ate wa puulim ayen wa te fu la a ta. Wa le basi ate fi chim Izirali niŋdeerɔ.

ref: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
text: Ate fi kan ko nuru baai ale kan seba wari nɔi po la a nya kaasuŋ yaase daanika. Mi a saalim, Naawen a dan nye wamaŋsaŋa de meena a te fu, teeri m wari.>>

ref: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
text: Deevid yaa tulisi Abigail ayen, <<Pak Naawen, Izirali Wenni dii ale tom fu mi jigi la.

ref: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
text: Fi le nya niauŋ fi yammu nyiŋ. Fi kasi mu kama ate mi an ko nuruba yaase m namsi nuruba jinla.

ref: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
text: Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale vua la nyiŋ, wa kasi mu kama ate mi an nye fu wari ya. Fi dan kan kpabi jam tu mu kama nna, Nabal nuruma wanyi mɛ ti kan vua paari chum saluiwa.>>

ref: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
text: Deevid yaa tuesi Abigail tiiritaŋa. Wa weeni Abigail ayen, <<Kuli yeri ale suiyɔgni. M wom fi biika kama, m be le nye fi le weeni diila.>>

ref: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
text: Abigail ale ŋman kuli ga a paari yeri la, Nabal kali kama a dɛ ase naab la. Wa jam nyu ka daam buk ate wa sui a peenti. Wa an jam weeni wa wari alege ate vari a veenti.

ref: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
text: Saluik ate wa daamu a yiinti la, wa powa yaa weeni wa wari meena. Wa le wom la suinum tuem deri yik wa ate wa gbariŋ.

ref: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
text: Daa pi ŋaaŋnyiŋ Naawen yaa ka te Nabal ate wa kpi.

ref: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
text: Abigail yaa koori tɛŋ a weeni ayen, <<Mi ka ni tomteerɔ. Mi gomsi kama ayen m tom a te ni abe m sugri m kpagni tomteerɔwa naŋsa.>>

ref: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
text: Abigail yaa nye nwuli a do boniŋ a va Deevid ale tom baai la ale wa dɔkliema banu a cheŋ. Wa yaa jam chim Deevid pok.

ref: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
text: Deevid jam faari ka Ayinoam mɛ. Wa jam nyini ka Jezreel. Ba noa baye wa jam ka Deevid pooba.

ref: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
text: Sɔɔl liewa Michal jam ka Deevid pok mɛ, alege Sɔɔl a jam pai wa te ka Lais biika Paltiel waai ale nyini Gallim.

ref: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
text: Zif demma yaa cheŋ Sɔɔl jigi Gibea tɛŋka a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Deevid an suk daa Yachila guuku ale tuk Jesimon la zuwa?>>

ref: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
text: Sɔɔl ale wa nuruma yaa tigsi bo suiku ale bo Yachila guuku zuk a tuk Jesimon nyiŋla, alege Deevid a bo gɔnni po. Wa le nya ayen Sɔɔl a va wa a jam dula la,

ref: of Israel's best soldiers and went to look for David there in Ziph Desert.
text: ) ate wa lueri la, ayen ba gisi Deevid dula.

ref: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
text: wa yaa tom nuruba ate ba nyini kpesi nya ayen Sɔɔl a jam kama.

ref: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
text: Ate Deevid yaa cheŋ Sɔɔl ale bo juijui la, wa yaa nya Sɔɔl ale Abner, Ner biika waai ale ka tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi la ale ba doa. Sɔɔl yaa doa ba tigsika jigini ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma a doa gilim wa.

ref: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
text: Deevid yaa bek Ayimelek Yit denɔwa ale Zeruiya biika Abisai waai ale Joab suok la, ayen, <<Ka wana ale wa va mi cheŋ Sɔɔl jigi ba tigsika jigini?>> Abisai yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi le cheŋ ale fu.>>

ref: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
text: Deevid ale Abisai yaa cheŋ tugurik tɔŋdɔma jigi yok a yaa nya Sɔɔl ale wa doa a goa tigsika jigini ate wa gbaluku a chiksi feri za wa zuk geŋsa. Abner ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale jam doa a gilim wa.

ref: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
text: Abisai yaa weeni Deevid ayen, <<Jinla Wen a pai fi dachiaka a nyo fi nisa po kama yɔgyɔgla de basi ate m pai m gbaluku a chubi wa a feri tɛŋ bunyi dekki daa buye.>>

ref: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
text: Alege Deevid a weeni Abisai, <<Kan ko wa. Ka wana ale wa pai nisa a tiri waai ate Naawen a lueri la alege kan nye a kaasi?>>

ref: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
text: Deevid yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen ale boro la nyiŋ, Naawen dek ale wa ko wa. Da dii dai wadek dai ale paari ate wa kpi yaase wa le cheŋ kpaliŋ a ga kpi.

ref: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
text: Alege Naawen a kisi kama ayen mi pai nisa a tiri waai ate wa lueri la. Yɔgyɔgla de pai wa gbaluku ale wa nyiamu leŋka ale moata wa zukku la ate ti cheŋ.>>

text: Abner ale basi dula la, Deevid nuruma ale Joab yaa nyini kpaliŋ sitika po a jam ale ŋanta yegayega ate ba kɔlim. Alege Abner an ŋman jam bo ale Deevid Yebron tɛŋka po, dii nyiŋla Deevid a basi ate wa cheŋ ale ka suiyɔgni.

ref: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
text: Joab ale tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai meena ale bo le wa la ale paari la, ba weeni wa ayen Ner nidoabinni Abner a jam naawa jigi kama ate naawa a basi ate wa cheŋ ale suiyɔgni.

ref: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
text: Joab yaa cheŋ naawa jigi a ga weeni ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi nye? Nya, Abner jam fi jigi kama. Ka boa ate fi a basi ate wa cheŋ? Yɔgyɔgla de wa cheŋ ya.

text: Fi seba Ner nidoabinni Abner a jam kama ayen wa paasi fu abe wa kpesi fi chelimu abe wa nya wari meena ate fi a nye la.>>

ref: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
text: Joab yaa basi Deevid ale tom nuruba ate ba saŋ Abner ŋaaŋ, ate ba ta wa nyini Sira vinni a ŋmani. Alege Deevid a jam zɛ.

ref: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
text: Abner ale pilim ŋmani cheŋ Yebron la, Joab a yaa ta wa cheŋ nakpiak suiku nɔi ase wa a yaali wa biisi ale wa ka wadek wa nyiini la. Dula jigini ate wa ko wa tuni wa suoku Asayel nyiŋ, Joab yaa chubi wa lɔgni ate wa kpi.

ref: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ, ate Deevid a wom kude la, wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi ale mi naamu a zɛ wari nɔi po a magsi chaab ale Ner nidoabinni Abner ziimu Naawen niŋŋa.

text: Wa ziimu a bo Joab ale wa kowa yenni meena zuk. Joab yenni a kan jɔk waai ate wa noruk a chali nyiamoa yaase, wa nyiŋ kaasi yaase waai ale a sali dagbiowa, yaase waai ate ba ko wa lɔnsi ale gebiga yaase, waai ale a silim ŋandiinta.

ref: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.

text: Sɔɔl nidoabinni Jonatan a jam ta ka nidoabili ate wa chim gbaruk, naŋsaŋa meena a jam gbariŋ kama. Wa jam ka bena ŋanu ate Sɔɔl ale Jonatan wie a jan jam Jezreel. text: Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi nyɔnɔwa naawa, fi tomteerɔwa ale toalim ka gbaniŋ la, mi weeni kama ayen, <M le gomsi m boniŋka a do ka, ate m baga a cheŋ ale naawa.> Alege mi tomteerɔwa Ziba a pai mi a da.

ref: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home

text: Nuruma meena yaa lo Jodan jueli. Ate naawa a gbaari Barzillai ale te wa wa niauŋku, ate Barzillai yaa ŋman kuli.

ref: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
text: Izirali nuruma yaa tulisi Juda nuruma ayen, <<Tama charuku ka naŋtuok nɔi pi ale naawa, be daa di nyiini, tama a soa Deevid kama a gaam nama. Ka boa ale soa ate nama a nye ti ale kisi ka? text: Tugurik nuru ale jam boro wa yuei ale Siiba. Wa jam ka Bikri nidoabili a nyini Benjamin buuni a bo dula jigini. Wa yaa peeri damuniŋka a kaari weeni ayen, <<Tama ka wari a nye ale Deevid, ti ka wari ale Jese nidoabinni. Waai meena ale wa viuk, Izirali demma.>>

ref: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
text: Dila nyiŋ Izirali nuruma yaa basi Deevid ale va Siiba, Bikri nidoabinni. Alege Juda nuruma a za ale ba naawa a zaani Jodan a ga paari Jerusalem.

ref: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. text: Deevid ale ŋman cheŋ wa yenni Jerusalem la, wa yaa ta nɔŋta piwa ate wa basi ayen ba a nya naab yenni zuk la a basi ba yeri po ayen limisidɔba a nya ba zuk. Wa jam a nya ba zuk kama, alege an duak ale ba. Ba jam pai ba a basi ka jigi a ta ga paari ba kum. Ba jam boro ase ka pukɔga la.

ref: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
text: Alege Amasa ale cheŋ ayen wa wi Juda la, wa jam beni kama a gaam naawa ale te wa daa diila.

ref: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
text: Deevid yaa weeni Abisai ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de Bikri nidoabinni Siiba ale nye ti biem a gaam Absalom ale nye diila. Pai fi kpagni nuruma a vi wa, dan kan daa di wa le nya tɛŋ pagrisa a chali abe wa ge ti.>>

ref: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
text: Joab nuruma ale Keret nuruma ale Pelet nuruma ale tugurik tɔŋdɔ pagrisaŋa meena a yaa nyini ate Abisai a nya ba zuk. Ba gɔk ka santiri a nyini ayen ba vi Bikri nidoabinni Siiba.

ref: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.

ref: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.

ref: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
text: Amasa an jam a kpesi gebika ale bo Joab nisa po la, ate Joab a pai ka a lu feri wa lɔgni, ate wa nyuetaŋa a nyini lo tɛŋ. Wa an ŋman jam chub wa alege ate Amasa a kpi. Joab ale wa suoku Abisai yaa vi Siiba Bikri nidoabinni.

ref: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”

ref: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
text: Amasa yaa jam dua ziimu po a labinti manpanni suŋsuŋ, ate nuruwa nya ayen tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena a jam zimsi ka dula. Wa le miŋ ayen waai meena ale jam Amasa jigi la a wari za kama la, wa yaa vuuri wa a ta nyini manpanni po a jo laŋ po a pai garuk a pili wa.

ref: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
text: Ba le yeeri Amasa manpanni po la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, nuruma meena a yaa cheŋ ale Joab ayen ba vi Siiba Bikri nidoabinni.

ref: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
text: Siiba yaa va Izirali yezuimaŋa meena po a ga paari Abel Bet Maaka ale va Beri demma tɛŋka po meena, baai ale tigsi chaab a va wa.

ref: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena ale bo ale Joab la yaa gilim Siiba ale bo Abel Bet Maaka po la. Ba sɛ bimbimi a ta jueli tɛŋka po, ate di zaani a ta chaab ale peelim ŋanpagrisaŋa. Alege ate ba a nak parika ayen ka siŋ tɛŋ.

ref: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
text: Yam nipok yaa wi nyini tɛŋka po ayen, <<Wom! Wom! Weeni Joab ayen wa jam de ate m biisi ale wa.>>

text: Wa yaa cheŋ a duŋ nipowa nyiŋ, ate nipowa a bek wa ayen, <<Fi ka Joab?>> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ka mi ale Joab.>> Nipowa yaa weeni ayen, <<Wom fi tomteerɔwa ale ta dii ayen wa weeni la. >> Joab yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi a wom.>>

ref: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
text: Wa yaa gum du biisi a cheŋ ayen, <<Dila powa ba jam a weeni kama ayen, <Nya fi tulisaŋa a nyini Abel,> ate wari meena a nueri.

text: Tama ale suiyɔgni ale wensie nyam Izirali tɛŋka po. Ni a nye ni kaasi tɛŋ kaai ale ka ma Izirali tɛŋka po la kama. Ka boa ale soa ate nama a yaali ayen ni nɛ Naawen nitalimu?>>

ref: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
text: Joab yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ku yalima ale mi ate mi nɛ yaase mi kaasi tɛŋka.

ref: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
text: Ku daa di. Nuru ate ba a wi ayen Siiba, wa ka Bikri nidoabili a nyini Ɛfraim ate guuta a bo ka po la, ale zak nisa a ta chaab ale naawa, a ta chaab ale Deevid. Pai nuru yeŋka de a te ate mi yeeri m dek tɛŋka po.>> Nipowa yaa weeni Joab ayen, <<Ba le yuk wa zukku a te a nyini parika jigini.>>

ref: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
text: Nipowa yaa ta wa yammu sinsaŋŋa a cheŋ nuruma meena jigi, ate ba gebi Bikri nidoabinni Siiba zukku a yuk a te Joab. Wa yaa peeri damuniŋka, ate wa nuruma a waaŋ tɛŋka po ate waai meena a kuli wa yeri. Ate Joab a ŋman cheŋ naawa jigi Jerusalem.

ref: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
text: Joab ale jam a nya Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena zuk. Jeyoiada nidoabinni Benaya ale jam a nya Keret ale Pelet demma zuk.

ref: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
text: Adoniram ale jam a nya fifiok tuimaŋa zuk, Ayilud nidoabinni Jeyosafat ale jam chim teerɔwa.

ref: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
text: Seva ale jam chim gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa, Zadok ale Abiata ale jam chim kaabteerɔba.

ref: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
text: Ate Ira, Jair denɔwa a chim Deevid kaabteerɔ.

ref: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
text: Naawen yaa wi Gibeon demma a biisi ale ba. Gibeon demma jam maa daa Izirali demma po alege ka Amori dem baai ale jam vuuk la. Izirali demma jam pɛ kama ayen ba kan ko ba, alege Sɔɔl ale wa nyiŋ zeentika ale jam Izirali ale Juda la a jam yaali ayen wa ko ka ba meena.

ref: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”

ref: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.

ref: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
text: Naawa an jam nye Jonatan nidoabinni Mefiboset waai ale ka Sɔɔl ŋaaŋ la wari ya, dii nyiŋla pɛka ale jam pɛ Naawen niŋ a bo Deevid ale Jonatan suŋsuŋ.

ref: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
text: Wa yaa pai ba a te Gibeon demma, baai ale ko ba ale nyati ba guuku zuk Naawen niŋ la. Bayopɔiwa meena jam lo ale ka chaab. Ba jam ko ba ka cheka wenni piilimka daaŋa. Dila po barli cheka a jaa piilim kama.

ref: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
text: Aiaya liewa Arizpaya yaa pai garuk zaksik a pati piuŋ zuk a te wadek. A zaani cheka wenni a ga paari diipo ate ŋmoruk a kuri ba nyiŋsaŋa la, wa an te ti wenzuk nuinsa yaase kantueŋŋa yaase gɔi duŋsa a tiri si yowa.

ref: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. text: wa jam cheŋ ga pai Sɔɔl ale wa nidoabinni Jonatan kobaŋa Jabes Gilead demma jigi. Ba jam suk pai ŋa kama a nyini nuru boari tuka jigi a bo Bet San po. Dula ate Filistia demma a pai ba a saŋ miisa nyiŋ ba le nak Sɔɔl a lɔnsi Gilboa la ŋaaŋnyiŋ.

text: Ba yaa gu Sɔɔl kobaŋa ale wa nidoabinni Jonatan Sɔɔl kowa Kis vɔrumu po Zela tɛŋka ale bo Benjamin po la, ale nye dii meena ate naawa a weeni la. Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Wen yaa jam tulisi puusa tɛŋka nyiŋ.

ref: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.

ref: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
text: Kpaliŋ yaa ŋman jam bo Filistia demma ale Izirali demma suŋsuŋ. Deevid yaa cheŋ ale wa nuruma ayen wa kpaliŋ ale Filistia demma a yaa jiak.

ref: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
text: Ate Isbi Benob, Arafa ŋaaŋbisaŋa wanyi, waai kuta gbaluk zuk ale jam a nye ase ligbie dobrim kobsita ale jam gomsi wadek ale gebik paalik, a yaa weeni ayen wa le ko Deevid.

ref: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
text: Alege Abisai, Zeruiya nidoabinni a jam vari Deevid a basi. Wa nak Filistia denɔwa a lɔnsi a ko. Ate Deevid nuruma a yaa pɛ a te wa ayen, <<Fi kan ŋman nyini va tama a cheŋ kpaliŋ diipo diipo, ate Izirali zeuŋku a kan kpimsi.>>

ref: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.

ref: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
text: Kpaliŋ ka choa ale Filistia demma ale jam nye Gob po, ate Jaare Oregim nidoabinni Elhanan ale nyini Betiliyem la a ko Gitti denɔwa Goliat waai gbaluk duok ale jam a nye ase chib la.

ref: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
text: Wa le jam nye Izirali a la la, Simeaya nidoabinni Jonatan, Deevid suoku a yaa ko wa.

ref: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
text: Bade banaansiwa jam ka Arafa ŋaaŋbisa a bo Gat tɛŋka, ate Deevid ale wa nuruma jam ko ba.

ref: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
text: Deevid yaa pai wieŋa de a yi yiili a te Naawen diipo ate Naawen a vari wa wa dachaasaŋa meena ale Sɔɔl nisima po a basi la.

text: Izirali naawa yaa na ayen, <<Boa! Naawen a wi tama nalima ŋatawa a ta ti a jam jigi yeŋ ayen wa pai ti a te ka Moab yaa?>>

ref: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
text: Alege Jeyosafat a jam bek ayen, <<Naawen biisiteerɔ a ka dela ayen ti va wa zuk a miŋ ku kiri a nyini Naawen jigi ya?>> Izirali naawa kpagi yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ɛlaisa ale ka Safat nidoabili la a bo dela. Wa jam ka Elaja tomteerɔ.>>

ref: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
text: Jeyosafat yaa jam weeni ayen, <<Naawen wanni a bo ale wa kama.>> Ate Izirali naawa ale Jeyosafat ale Edom naawa a yaa jam cheŋ wa jigi.

ref: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
text: Ɛlaisa yaa jam weeni Izirali naawa ayen, <<Tama ale nye tidek ka sɛ? Cheŋ fi kowa biisiteerɔma ale fi mawa biisiteerɔma jigi.>> Izirali naawa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Aaya, dii nyiŋla ka Naawen ale wi tama nalima ŋatawa ayen wa pai ti a nyo Moab nisa po.>>

ref: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
text: Ɛlaisa yaa jam weeni ayen, <<Ase Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale vua la, waai ate mi tom a te la, ase mi a dan kan ta zula a te Jeyosafat ale ka Juda naab la, m ti kan zak a nya fu yaase m poom miŋ fu.

ref: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
text: Alege ni ta waai ale a nak kpanuŋ la a jam te mu.>> Ase kpanuŋ nagrɔwa ale jam boro a nak la, ate Naawen nisa a yaa jam Ɛlaisa zuk,

ref: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
text: ate wa weeni ayen, <<Naawen ale a weeni diila ale nna, ayen ni tu gola woŋta a sueri viaka po.

ref: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
text: Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna ayen, fi a kan nya viok yaase ŋmoruwa, alege viaka de ale sueri ale nyiam, ate fi ale fi niiga ale fi duŋ yonsaŋa ale nyu nyiam.

ref: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
text: Nya kude ka moali Naawen nina po. Wa ale pai Moab a nyo ni nisa po.

ref: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
text: Ni ale nya pagrim tɛŋ pagrik ale tɛŋ kpieŋ meena zuk. Ni ale che tiib maŋsa meena a lɔnsi tɛŋ, abe ni si bulisa meena, abe ni pai tana a kaasi tɛŋ maŋsaŋa meena.>>

ref: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
text: Vanni ale veenti la, a moata diipo ate ba a nye kaabka la, nyiam ale jam nyini Edom tɛŋka geŋsaŋa a jam sueri tɛŋka!

ref: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de Moab demma a jam wom kama ayen nalimaŋa a jam kama ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale ba. Ate nuru meena, bi paalukku ale ŋankpagsa ale baga a yik kpaliŋ kɔlima la, ba jam wi ba kama a ta ba ga zaani tɛŋka banni.

ref: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
text: Ba ale jam yiti saluik yokyokku la, wenbinni a jam a nyaksi nyiamu zuk kama. Moab demma ale jam gaam suiku a za la jigi, ku jam muni ka nna gbaŋgbaŋ ase ziim la.

ref: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
text: Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Ziim ale la. Da dii dai nalim ŋala a nye ka kpaliŋ a tɔgri chaab. Yɔgyɔgla de ka Moab ale ba kɔlim ba ŋantaŋa.>>

ref: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
text: Alege Moab demma ale jam cheŋ Izirali bo ka jigini la, Izirali demma a yiti kama a kpaliŋ ale ba ate ba chali be. Ate Izirali demma a fɛ jo tɛŋka po a yik Moab demma a tɔgri.

ref: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
text: Ba jam kaasi tɛŋsaŋa kama, ate nuru meena a yuk tana a basi tɛŋ maŋ meena zuk ate tanaŋa a ga lik ka. Ba jam si bulisaŋa meena kama ale che tiib maŋ meena a lɔnsi. Ka Kir Yareset nyiini ale jam tali ate ka tanaŋa a doa si jigini, alege nuruba ale jam ta visiŋsa a gilim ka ale siti ka mɛ.

ref: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
text: Ate wa pai bi kaai ate wa dɛ niŋ a biak la, waai ate wa dan kan boro wa tagri wa zuk a chim naab la, a nye kaabka tɛŋka parika zuk. Ba sueŋa a jam a puuri ale Izirali ka nna yegayega. Izirali demma yaa jam pai basi ale ŋman cheŋ badek tɛŋka po.

ref: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
text: Nuru wanyi ale jam maa bo Wen biisiteerɔma tigsuŋku po la pok yaa jam kum sak Ɛlaisa ayen, <<Fi tomteerɔwa m chorɔwa a kpi kama, fi abe seba kama ayen wa jam a zuli Naawen kama. Alege wa ale ta waai pami la a cheen kama ayen wa pai m nidoabilisa bayewa ase yɔm la.>>

ref: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
text: Ɛlaisa yaa tulisi wa ayen, << M nye se a maari fu? Weeni a sak mu, ka boa ate fi ta bo fi yenni po?>> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi tomteerɔwa a ka jaaboa, ka kpaam nna maga.>>

ref: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
text: Ɛlaisa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Cheŋ fi ale moata baai la a weeni ba ate ba te fu samɔn koruta. Kan tuesi maga.

ref: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
text: Fi yaa jo dɔkku po a lik fidek ale fi nidoabilisaŋa du, boori kpaamu a nyo samɔnsaŋa meena po, ate kanyi meena a dan ga sueri pai zaani nakpiak.>>

ref: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
text: Wa yaa jam cheŋ ga jo dɔkku po lik wa tuoku ale wa nidoabilisaŋa. Ba jam ta samɔnsaŋa kama a ga te wa ate wa kasim jam a kpiiri kpaamu.

ref: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
text: Samɔnsaŋa meena ale jam sueri la, wa yaa weeni wa nidoabinni ayen, <<Ta ka choa a jam te mu.>> Alege wa tulisi wa kama ayen, <<Samɔniŋ an tali ya.>> Ate kpaamu yaa gebiri.

ref: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
text: Wa yaa cheŋ ga weeni sak Wen nuruwa ate wa weeni wa ayen, <<Cheŋ ga pai kpaamu a da tuni fi pamaŋa. Dii ale tali la, fi ale fi nidoabilisaŋa abe pai a dɛ.>>

ref: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
text: Dai yeŋ ate Ɛlaisa a jam cheŋ Sunem. Ate nipok waai ale jigsi la jam bo dula. Nipowa yaa weeni Ɛlaisa ayen wa te ate wa te wa ŋandiinta. Ate diipo meena ate wa a va dula la, wa nyiem zaani dula kama a dɛ.

ref: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
text: Wa yaa weeni sak wa chorɔwa ayen, <<Mi seba kama ayen nuru waai ale kasim a jam ti jigi la ka Wen nuru weleŋ.

ref: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
text: Basi ate ti nye dɔk fiik ti yenni zuk a pai gaduok ale jazaanim ale zukpaglik ale zeuŋ a te wa. Ate wa dan jam ti jigi diipo meena wa bo dula.>>

ref: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
text: Dai yeŋ ate Ɛlaisa a jam, wa yaa cheŋ wa dɔkku po a ga duak dula.

ref: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
text: Ɛlaisa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Weeni wa ayen, <Fi jo ninammu de po meena a te ka tama. Yɔgyɔgla de ti le nye ka boa a te fu? Ti weeni naawa yaase tugurik tɔŋdɔma ate wa maari fu?> >> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<M bo ale ka m nuruma.>>

ref: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
text: Ɛlaisa yaa bek ayen, <<Te le nye ka boa a te wa?>> Geyazi yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa ka nidoabili ya. Wa chorɔwa mɛ a kpaŋ kama.>>

ref: “Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
text: Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ayen, <<Wi wa.>> Ate wa wi wa, ate wa jam zaani nansuiŋku nɔi.

ref: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
text: Ɛlaisa weeni ayen, <<Bali nna po de, fi ale ta nidoabili fi nisa po.>> Wa yaa zɛri wa ale weeni wa diila ale ayen, <<Aaya, m nyɔnɔ, kan paasi fi tomteerɔwa, Wen nuroa.>>

ref: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
text: Alege nipowa a jam yik lɔgi kama ate ben dii ale paasaŋ la dila po dek wa biak nidoabili ase Ɛlaisa ale jam weeni la.

ref: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
text: Nidoabinni yaa chim, ate dai yeŋ wa yaa cheŋ wa kowa jigi, juijui ate nuruba a boro a pisi ŋan baai ate ba kpa la.

ref: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
text: Wa yaa weeni wa kowa ayen, <<M zuk! M zuk!>> Wa kowa yaa weeni wa tomteerɔma wanyi ayen, <<Pai wa ga te wa mawa.>>

ref: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
text: Tomteerɔwa ale ta wa a ga te wa mawa la nidoabinni yaa kali wa mawa naŋsa zuk a ga paari kantueŋ, ate wa yaa kpi.

ref: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
text: Wa yaa ta wa cheŋ ga dueni Wen nuruwa gaduokku zuk, a yaa kpari tuoku ale cheŋ nyini.

ref: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
text: Wa yaa wi wa chorɔwa ayen, <<Mi a saalim ayen fi te ate fi tomteerɔma wanyi ta boniŋ a jam te mu ate m cheŋ Wen nuruwa jigi nwuli abe m ŋman jam.>>

ref: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
text: Wa yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boan wari ate fi a cheŋ wa jigi jinla? Ku daa Chiik Paalik yaase Vuusum Dai ya. Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Jaab meena a magsi kama.>>

ref: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.”
text: Wa yaa gomsi bonika ale weeni wa tomteerɔwa ayen, <<De niŋ. Kan a cheŋ maga maga ka mi nin weeni fu.>>

ref: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
text: Ate wa yaa jam cheŋ paari Karmel Guuku juijui ate Wen nuruwa a boro la. Wa ale jam zaani niŋ a nya wa la, Wen nuruwa yaa weeni wa tomteerɔwa Geyazi ayen, <<Nya, Sunem denɔwa ale nna.

ref: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
text: Chali a ga tu wa abe fi bek wa ayen, <Nalim a bo ni meena jigi ya? Nalim a bo fi chorɔwa jigi ya? Nalim a bo fi nidoabinni jigi ya?> >> Sunem denɔwa yaa weeni ayen, <<Nalim a bo waai meena jigi kama.>>

ref: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
text: Wa ale ga paari Wen nuruwa guuku zuk la, wa yaa yik wa naŋsaŋa a tara Geyazi yaa nyini ayen wa tusi wa a basi, alege Wen nuruwa a weeni wa ayen, <<Basi wa. Wa sui ale kaasi, alege Naawen a pai suk mi kama ale an weeni wari a sak mi.>>

ref: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
text: Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, mi weeni fu ayen mi a yaali nidoabili ya? Mi weeni fu ayen, kan basi ate m ta yiila.>>

ref: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
text: Ɛlaisa yaa weeni Geyazi ayen, <<Yik fi garukku a basi fi chiak gbainni po, abe fi pai m dachekka a nyo fi nisa po a chali. Fi dan zik waai suiku po, kan puusi wa, waai abe dan puusi fu, kan tulisi wa. Pai m dachekka a vi nidoabinni ninaŋa zuk.>>

ref: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
text: Alege biika mawa a weeni ayen, <<Ase Naawen ale vua la, ate fi mɛ a vua la, m kan basi fu.>> Ate wa jam yiti a va wa a cheŋ.

ref: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
text: Geyazi a jam de ka niŋ a ga pai dachekka a vi biika ninaŋa zuk, alege chiok a kan choa yaase wa poom tulisi. Ate Geyazi a pilim ŋmani a ga tu Ɛlaisa suik a weeni sak wa ayen, <<Nidoabinni an yiti ya.>>

ref: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
text: Ɛlaisa ale ga paari yenni la, wa nya ka biika ale kpi doa wa gaduokku zuk.

ref: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
text: Wa yaa cheŋ jo ale kpari tuoku ate ba nɔi bayewa nyiini a boro, ate Ɛlaisa puusi te Naawen.

ref: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
text: Ate wa yaa jueli gaduokku zuk a yaa duak biika zuk, a pai wa nɔnni a tuk wa nɔnni, ale pai wa ninaŋa a tuk wa ninaŋa ale pai wa nisaŋa a yik wa nisaŋa. Ase wa ale jam neenti a basi wa nyiŋla, biika nyiŋka yaa tuila.

ref: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
text: Ɛlaisa yaa viriŋ a cheŋ ŋaaŋnyiŋ ale niŋ nyiŋ dɔkku po ale ŋman jueli gaduokku zuk a neenti a ŋman basi wa nyiŋ. Biika yaa chesim buyopɔi ale lak wa nina.

ref: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
text: Ɛlaisa yaa weeni Geyazi ayen, <<Wi Sunem denɔwa. >> Ate wa ga wi wa. Wa ale jam la, wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Pai fi biika.>>

ref: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
text: Wa yaa cheŋ jo, a yaa lo wa naŋsa tɛŋ a yaa koori tɛŋ. Wa yaa jam pai wa biika ta cheŋ nyini peelim.

ref: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
text: Ɛlaisa yaa ŋmani cheŋ Gilgal ate kom a jam bo tɛŋ kala po. Wen biisiteerɔma ale jam tigsi a boro a tu wa la, wa yaa weeni wa tomteerɔwa ayen, <<Pai samɔn kpieŋ a dik jenta a te nuruma de.>>

ref: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
text: Ba wanyi yaa cheŋ tattaŋa po ayen wa yaali jenvaata, ate wa yaa nya tiib ale zuak. Wa yaa yaali bu yɔnaŋa a sueri wa garukku po. Wa ale jam paari la, wa yaa gebi ŋa a nyo jenta samɔniŋka po. Waai mɛ a poom zɛ ba ale ka ŋan baai la.

ref: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
text: Ba jam nye jentaŋa kama a te nuruma, alege ba ale jam boro ayen ba dɛ la, ba kaari ayen, <<Wen nuroa, kum ale bo samɔniŋka po.>> Ate ba an jam baga a dɛ ya.

ref: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
text: Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni ta zom a jam.>> Wa yaa pai nyo samɔniŋ po ale weeni ayen, <<Ni nye a te nuruma ate ba dɛ.>> Ate jaab a jam ka samɔniŋka po a daani.

ref: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
text: Ate wa nye te ba ate ba dɛ ale tali ŋa gela a zaani, a magsi chaab ale Naawen wanni ale weeni diila.

ref: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de Naaman a jam ka Araam naawa tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi. Wa jam ka nuru kpioŋ wa kpagni nina po ate ba a te wa zula nna yegayega. Wa nyiŋ ate Naawen a pai nakdeka a te Araam. Wa jam ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ, a ta suinum pagrik, alege wa jam ka gami.

ref: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de nuruba ale jam nyini Araam a cheŋ ga yik nipokbili a nyini Izirali a jam ate wa boro a tom a te Naaman powa.

ref: When Naaman told the king what the girl had said,
text: Naaman yaa cheŋ wa kpagni jigi a ga weeni wa nipokbinni ale weeni diila.

ref: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
text: Araam naawa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ku nala kama be cheŋ, m le te gbaŋ ate ka cheŋ Izirali naawa jigi.>> Ate Naaman yaa jam pai kpana boorik dobrim pi ale ligmɔniŋ ligbie dobrim tusa ŋayuebi (

ref: pieces of silver and some new clothes?”
text: ) ale gatta joka pi a yaa cheŋ.

ref: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
text: Gbaŋka ate wa jam ŋmarisi ayen wa ta ga te naawa la a jam a weeni kama ayen, <<M va ka gbaŋka de zuk a tom m tomteerɔwa Naaman fi jigi ayen, fi tebi wa gama tuemu.>>

ref: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
text: Ɛlaisa yaa tom nuru ayen wa ga weeni wa ayen, <<Cheŋ ga so fidek naŋtuok nɔi buyopɔi Jodan benni po, ate fi nyiŋka ale ŋman nye ka denni ate fi nala.

ref: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
text: Izirali naawa ale ga karim gbaŋka la, wa yaa dari wa garuk woŋku a cheeri ale sui kaasuŋ weeni ayen, <<Mi ka Wen yaa? Mi baga a ko a ŋman baga ta nyuvuri a jamu? Ka boan nyiŋ ate nuru wade a tom a waai m jigi ayen m tebi wa gama tuemoa? Nya wa ale a nye ayen wa nye tugurik ale mu la.>>

ref: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
text: Wen nuruwa Ɛlaisa ale jam wom ayen Izirali naawa a dari wa garuk woŋku a cheeri ale sui kaasuŋ la, wa yaa tom ayen ba ga weeni wa ayen, <<Ka boan nyiŋ ate fi dari fi garuk woŋku a cheeri? Te ate nuruwa a jam mi jigi ate wa ale seba ayen Wen biisiteerɔ a bo Izirali.>>

ref: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
text: Ate Naaman a jam cheŋ ale wa wusumaŋa ale torokoma a ga zaani Ɛlaisa yenni tuoku nɔi.

ref: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
text: Alege Naaman jam basi wa kama ale suipuurum ale weeni ayen, <<Mi poli kama ayen wa le nyini ka peelim a tu mu a zaani a wi Naawen dii ale ka wa Wen la yuenni, abe wa pai wa nisa a vi m niraŋa zuk a tebi m gama tuemu.

ref: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”

ref: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
text: Wa yaa cheŋ siŋ Jodan benni po a musi du naŋtuok nɔi buyopɔi ase Wen nuruwa ale weeni wa diila, ate wa nyiŋka a ŋman nye ka ale ka diila, a nala nna se nidoabili paalik nyiŋla.
