text: Ate Jeyoayaz nidoabinni Jeyoas ŋman jam nya nakdeka a nyini Yazael nidoabinni Ben Yadad jigi tɛŋ sii ate wa nye tugurik a vari si a nyini wa kowa Jeyoayaz jigi la. Joas a jam nya nakdeka wa zuk a paari ka ku naŋtuok nɔi buta, ate wa ŋman tuesi Izirali demma tɛŋsaŋa.

ref: Jeroboam extended the boundaries of Israel from Lebo-Hamath in the north to the Dead Sea in the south, just as the Lord had promised his servant Jonah son of Amittai, who was a prophet from Gath-Hepher.
text: Wa la ale jam ŋman tuesi Izirali tɛŋsaŋa a nyini Yamat ta cheŋ ga paari Araba nyakpiemu a magsi chaab ale Naawen wanni, Izirali Wenni a jam biisi a va wa tomteerɔwa Jona ale ka Amittai nidoabili la, biisiteerɔ waai ale nyini Gat Yefer.

ref: Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah in the second year of Jehoash's rule in Israel.
text: Jeyoayaz Izirali naawa nidoabinni Joas ale jam de wa naamu a paari bena ŋaye la, ate Joas Juda naawa nidoabinni Amaziya a piilim wa naamu dɛka.

ref: He disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po, wa abe an jam pai Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam wabaataŋa a basi ya, tii ate wa jam choa Izirali ate ba nye la.

ref: Jeroboam died and was buried, and his son Zechariah became king.
text: Jeroboam a jam kpi a vuusi ale ka wa koma Izirali nalimaŋa. Ate wa nidoabinni Zakaria a tagri wa a chim naab.

ref: Amaziah followed the example of his father Joash by obeying the Lord and doing right. But he was not as faithful as his ancestor David.
text: Amaziya a jam nye ka dii ale nala la Naawen niŋ, alege daa dii ate wa kowa Deevid a jam nye la. Jaab meena po wa jam va ka wa kowa Joas ale jam nye diila.

ref: Amaziah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
text: Alege wa an jam kaasi ba kaabka jiŋŋa guutaŋa zuima. Nuruma a jam kasim boro kama a nye kaabka ale a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la.

ref: As soon as Amaziah had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father.
text: Naab Amaziya ale jam kali paari la, wa yaa jam ko kpaga ŋaai ale ko wa kowa naawa la.

ref: But the children of those officers were not killed. The Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished, not their parents or children.
text: Alege wa an ko baai ale ko wa kowa la nidoabilisaŋa dii nyiŋla wa jam va ka dii ale ŋmarisi Moosis Sinsaŋŋa Gbaŋka po ate Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Ba kan ko koba ba bisa nyiŋŋa, yaase ba ko bisa ba koba nyiŋŋa. Waai meena abe kpi wadek wabaata nyiŋ.>>

ref: While Amaziah was king, he killed
text: Wa ale jam nya nakdeka Edom demma tusa pi (

ref: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. Go ahead and celebrate—but stay at home. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
text: Fi nya nakdeka Edom zuk kama, ate yɔgyɔgla de kayerinni yaa jo fu. Te ate fi nina a sueri ale fi nakdeka, abe fi kali yeri. Ka boa ale soa ate fi a bek daanika a te fidek ale Juda mɛ?>>

ref: Edomite soldiers in Salt Valley. He captured the town of Sela and renamed it Joktheel, which is still its name.
text: ) Yesa Viaka po ale nak yik Sela kpaliŋ po ate ba a wi ka ayen Jokteel, yuei dila ate ka ta a jam paari jinla de.

ref: One day, Amaziah sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
text: Amaziya yaa jam tom nuruba ayen ba cheŋ Jeyoayaz nidoabinni Jeyoas jigi, ate wa ko kpieŋ a chim Jeyu la, Izirali naawa jigi ale nampaŋŋa de ayen, <<Jam, te ate ti pai nina a tu chaab.>>

ref: Jehoash sent back this reply: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon announced that his son was going to marry the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
text: Alege Izirali naawa Jeyoas a jam tulisi Juda naawa Amaziya ayen, <<Muŋ ale bo Lebanon a te tomtomiŋ Lebanon nyunyoŋ ayen, <Pai fi liewa ate m nidoabinni a faari wa.> Ate Lebanon gɔi duŋ yaa jam tabi muŋka a kaasi.

ref: But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash and his troops marched to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
text: Alege Amaziya a kan wom, dila Izirali naawa Jeyoas a yaa siti wa. Jeyoas ale Juda naawa Amaziya a yaa jam tu chaab ka Bet Sɛmes Juda po.

ref: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
text: Izirali a jam nak yiak Juda kama, ate nuru meena a chali kuli wa yeri.

ref: He took the gold and silver, as well as everything of value from the Lord's temple and the king's treasury. He took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
text: Wa jam pai ka ligmɔniŋka meena ale kpanaŋa meena ale ŋantaŋa meena ale bo Naawen yenni po ale tuilum ŋantaŋa ale bo naab yenni po la. Wa jam maa yik ka nuruba a ŋman cheŋ Samaria.

ref: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he defeated King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Dan ka Jeyoas naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii meena ate wa jam nye la a maa gum wa tugurika ate wa nye ale Juda naawa Amaziya la, ŋala a ŋmarisi doa Izirali nalimaŋa gbaŋka po kama.

ref: After his death the people of Judah made his son Azariah king, even though he was only
text: Ate nuruma meena a pai Azariya, waai ale jam ta bena pi ale ŋayuebi la, ate wa chim naab a tagri wa kowa Amaziya.

ref: Azariah was the one who later recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath. King Jeroboam the Second of Israel
text: Wa ale ŋman jam sɛ Elat ale pai ka a te Juda Amaziya ale vuusi ale wa koma la ŋaaŋnyiŋ.

ref: Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in the fifteenth year of Amaziah's rule in Judah. Jeroboam ruled
text: Juda naawa Joas nidoabinni Amaziya bena pi ale ŋanuwa po, ate Izirali naawa Jeyoas nidoabinni Jeroboam a jam chim Samaria naab, ate wa kali wa naamu zuk a paari bena pisinaansi ale dinyi.

ref: The Lord helped Jeroboam do this because he had seen how terribly the Israelites were suffering, whether slave or free, and no one was left to help them.
text: Naawen a nya Izirali sui kaasuŋku ale ka diila kama, yɔm ale baai ale soa badek meena a jam a nam kama. Waai karo a maari ba.

ref: And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
text: Naawen abe le weeni ayen wa kan yeeri Izirali yuenni a nyini wenŋmazuk a basi la, wa jam pai ka Joas nidoabinni Jeroboam nisa a vari ba a basi.

ref: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Dan ka Jeroboam naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii meena ate wa nye la ale wa tugurik tɔŋka nakdeka ale wa ale ŋman tuesi Damasikus ale Yamat a te Izirali la, ate Yaudi a jam soa la, ŋala a ŋmarisi a doa Izirali nalima gbaŋka po kama.

ref: Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Pekah of Israel
text: Dan ka Pekayia naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii meena ate wa jam nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi doa ka Izirali nalima gbaŋka po.

ref: Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
text: Juda naawa Azariya bena pisinuwa po, ate Menayem nidoabinni Pekayia a chim Izirali naab Samaria po, wa abe jam de naamu ka bena ŋaye.

ref: Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
text: Wa jam nye ka dii ale nala Naawen nina po, ase wa kowa Amaziya ale jam nye diila.

ref: But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
text: Alege wa an jam kaasi ba kaabka jiŋŋa guutaŋa zuima. Nuruma a jam kasim a nye ka kaabka ale a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la.

ref: The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
text: Naawen a jam namsi naawa ale ka gama tuem a ga paari wa kummu danni, ate wa bo yeri dii ale gaari za di dek di nyiini. Naawa nidoabinni Jotam ale jam a nya naab yenni ale nuruma ale bo tɛŋka po la zuk.

ref: Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
text: Dan ka Azariya naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii meena ate wa nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi doa Juda nalima gbaŋka po kama.

ref: Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king. King Zechariah of Israel
text: Azariya a jam kpi kama a vuusi ale wa koma ate ba gu wa a moata ba Deevid Tɛŋka po. Ate wa nidoabinni Jotam a tagri wa a chim naab.

ref: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria.
text: Juda naawa Azariya bena pisita ale naanika po, ate Jeroboam nidoabinni Zakaria a chim Izirali naab Samaria po. Wa a jam de naamu a paari ka chiisa siyuebi.

ref: Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king.
text: Jabes nidoabinni Sallum a jam zok ka biem a ta va Zakaria zuk. Wa ga siti wa ka nuruma niŋ, a ko wa a yaa tagri wa a chim naab.

ref: So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family. Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Shallum of Israel
text: Dila Naawen wanni ale jam weeni Jeyu diila yaa chim wensie ayen, <<Fi ŋaaŋbisa ale kali Izirali naam zukpaglika zuk a ga paari gaŋsa bunaansiwa po.>>

ref: Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king,
text: Juda naawa Yuzaya bena pisita ale neokku po, ate Jabes nidoabinni Sallum a chim naab, wa abe jam chim naab Samaria po ka chiik yeŋ.

ref: Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria.
text: Juda naawa Azariya bena pisita ale neokku po, ate Gadi nidoabinni Menayem a chim Izirali naab, wa be jam de wa naamu a paari ka bena pi Samaria po.

ref: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po. Wa naamu vaaŋa po meena wa an jam basi Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam wabaataŋa, tii ate wa jam choa Izirali ate ba nye la.

ref: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
text: Ate Assiria naawa Pul a jam fɛ jo tɛŋka po, ate Menayem a jam te wa kpana boorisa dobrim tusidi ayen wa nya maarika ate ku te wa pagrim tɛŋka zuk.

ref: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
text: Wa jam nye ka dii ale nala la, Naawen nina po ase wa kowa Yuzaya ale jam nye diila.

ref: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
text: Dan ka Menayem naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii meena ate wa nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi doa ka Izirali nalima gbaŋka po.

ref: Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king. King Pekahiah of Israel
text: Menayem a jam kpi kama a vuusi ale wa koma. Ate wa nidoabinni Pekayia a tagri wa a chim naab.

ref: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
text: Pekayia a jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po. Wa an jam basi Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam wabaataŋa, tii ate wa jam choa Izirali ate ba nye la.

ref: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
text: Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po. Wa an jam basi Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam wabaataŋa, tii ate wa jam choa Izirali ate ba nye la.

ref: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
text: Izirali naawa Peka vaaŋa po, Assiria naawa Tiglat Pileser a jam yik ka Ijon ale Abel Bet Maaka ale Janoa ale Kedes ale Yazor. Wa jam pai Gilead ale Galili ale tɛŋsaŋa meena ale bo Nafitali la kama ale yiak nuruma ate ba cheŋ Assiria.

ref: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
text: Ate Elaya nidoabinni Yoseya a jam ta biem zɔga a ta va Aremaliya nidoabinni Peka zuk. Wa jam siti wa kama a ko wa, a yaa tagri wa a chim naab Yuzaya nidoabinni Jotam bena pisiyewa po.

ref: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
text: Dan ka Peka naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii meena ate wa nye la, ŋala ŋmarisi doa ka Izirali nalima gbaŋka po.

ref: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
text: Izirali naawa Aremaliya nidoabinni Peka bena ŋayewa po, ate Juda naawa Yuzaya nidoabinni Jotam a piilim chim naab.

ref: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
text: Alege wa an jam kaasi ba tangbanaŋa bo ka jiŋŋa. Nuruma jam kasim a nye ka kaabka ale a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la. Jotam a ŋman jam sɛ Naawen yenni ŋmazuk nansuiŋku.

ref: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
text: Dan ka Jotam naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii meena ate wa nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi doa ka Juda nalima gbaŋka po.

ref: During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah.
text: Da ŋala po Naawen a piilim tom ka Araam naawa Arezin ale Aremaliya nidoabinni Peka ate ba ta chaab ale Juda.

ref: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
text: Jotam a kpi kama a vuusi ale wa koma ate ba gu wa ale ba Deevid Tɛŋka po, wa kowa tɛŋka. Wa nidoabinni Ayazi yaa tagri wa chim naab.

ref: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
text: Aremaliya nidoabinni Peka bena pi ale ŋayopɔiwa po, ate Juda naawa Jotam nidoabinni Ayazi a chim naab.

ref: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
text: Ayazi jam kpi kama a vuusi ale wa koma ate ba gu wa ale ba Deevid Tɛŋka po. Ate wa nidoabinni Azekaya a tagri wa a chim naab.

ref: and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
text: Wa jam va ka Izirali nalimaŋa suitaŋa a poom pai wa nidoabili a basi bolim po a nye kaabka ale va kisita suitaŋa ate tɛŋ sii a nye ate Naawen a yiak ba Izirali demma niŋ la.

ref: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
text: Wa jam nye ka kaabka ale ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la tangbanaŋa jiŋŋa ale guutaŋa zuima ale tiib buui ale teeri la meena tɛŋ.

ref: While Ahaz was ruling Judah, the king of Edom recaptured the town of Elath from Judah and forced out the people of Judah. Edomites then moved into Elath, and they still live there. About the same time, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel marched to Jerusalem and attacked, but they could not capture it.
text: Va ŋala po Araam naawa Arezin a ŋman jam tuesi Elat kama a te Araam a ta va wa ale yiak Juda nidoama a basi la nyiŋ. Edom demma yaa cheŋ Elat a ga bo dula a jam paari jinla de.

ref: Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.”
text: Ayazi yaa tom nuruba Assiria naawa Tiglat Pileser jigi ayen, <<Mi ka fi tomteerɔ ale waai ate fi gaam la. Jam a vari mu a nyini Araam ale Izirali nalimaŋa nisa po a basi, baai ale a siti mu la.>>

ref: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
text: Ate Ayazi yaa pai kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka ale bo Naawen yenni po la, a ta ga te Assiria naawa ase tiirim la.

ref: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
text: Assiria naawa a yaa siak a ga siti Damasikus a nya nakdeka ka zuk. Wa yaa basi ate baai ale bo ka po la a ŋman cheŋ Kir ale bo Arezin la.

ref: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
text: Ate naab Ayazi yaa cheŋ Damasikus ayen wa tu Assiria naawa Tiglat Pileser. Wa yaa nya kuŋkuŋ Damasikus po a daani ku ale ka diila a ta ga te kaabteerɔwa Yuraya ale ku jaab meena ayen wa nye ku choa.

ref: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
text: Dila kaabteerɔwa Yuraya yaa sɛ kuŋkuŋku magsi chaab ale dii meena ate naab Ayazi a tom nyini Damasikus la a nueri alege ate naab Ayazi a ŋmani.

ref: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
text: Ase naawa ale ŋman nyini Damasikus a nya kuŋkuŋku la, wa yaa cheŋ paari ku a ta tiirita a ga vi ku zuk.

ref: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
text: Wa jam nye ka juka tiirim ale ŋandiinta tiirim ale kpiiri wa nyuka tiirim ale misi wa suiyɔgni tiirita ziimu tiiritaŋa ku zuk.

ref: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
text: Kutuk mɔnuŋ kuŋkuŋku ale za Naawen niŋ la, wa ta nyini ka yenni niŋ kuŋkuŋ paalukku ale Naawen yenni suŋsuŋ. A yaa pai ku a dueni kuŋkuŋ paalukku wiiluk geŋsa.

ref: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
text: Naab Ayazi yaa weeni wieŋa de a te kaabteerɔwa Yuraya ayen, <<Kuŋkuŋ kuui ale paala a zuak la zuk, nye saluik juka tiirimu ale junɔi ŋanbie tiirimu ale naawa juka tiirimu ale wa ŋanbie tiirimu ale nuruma meena ale bo tɛŋka po la juka tiirimu ale ba ŋanbie tiirimu ale ba nyuka tiirimu. Misi juka tiiritaŋa ale kaabka ziitaŋa a basi kuŋkuŋku zuk. Alege m le pai kutuk mɔnuŋ kuŋkuŋku a gisi m le m nye diila.>>

ref: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
text: Naab Ayazi yaa pai jabuui ale a lik kauk kunkula la, a yaa yeeri chinaŋa a nyini ŋan zaani tii ate fi baga a pai la. Wa yaa yeeri nyakpiemu a nyini kutuk mɔnuŋ lalisaŋa ale a maari bu la, a yaa pai bu a zaani tana zuk.

ref: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
text: Wa jam pai Vuusum danni viuku ate ba ti zaani Naawen yenni la ale lik naab yenni nansuiŋku ale bo Naawen yenni peelimmu la, ayen ku maari Assiria naawa.

ref: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
text: Dan ka Ayazi naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii ate wa nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi doa ka Juda nalima gbaŋka po.

ref: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
text: Juda naawa Ayazi bena pi ale ŋayewa po, ate Elaya nidoabinni Yoseya yaa chim Izirali naab Samaria po. Wa de naamu a paari ka bena neok.

ref: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
text: Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po, alege ku an nye ase Izirali nalimaŋa baai ale de wa niŋ la.

ref: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
text: Assiria naawa Salmaneser yaa jam ayen wa siti Yoseya waai ate Salmaneser a ta pagrim wa zuk la a yaa tuni ligra a te wa bein meena.

ref: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
text: Alege Assiria naawa a jam miŋ kama ayen Yoseya ka bumbobrɔ, dii nyiŋla wa tom ka nuruba ate ba cheŋ Ejipiti naawa So jigi, ase bein meena ate wa jam a nye diila. Dila yaa basi ate Salmaneser a yik wa a ta ga lik.

ref: Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years,
text: Assiria naawa yaa fɛ jo tɛŋka meena ale gɔk santiri a jueli Samaria zuk ale gilim tɛŋka meena bena ŋata.

ref: before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
text: Yoseya bena neokku po, ate Assiria naawa a jam nak yik Samaria ale basi ate Izirali demma a ŋman cheŋ Assiria. Wa jam te ba kali ka Yala ale bo Gozan po la, Yabor Benni ale Miidi tɛŋsaŋa po.

ref: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
text: Dii nyiŋ ate kude meena a nye la ka Izirali demma ale nye biem a kaasi Naawen ba Wenni, dii ale ta ba nyini Ejipiti po la, a nyini Ejipiti naawa Faaro nisa po la. Ba jam a puusi ka wen yona,

ref: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
text: ale a nye dii ate tɛŋ sii ate Naawen a yiak ba nina po la nyeelaŋa ale dii dek ate Izirali nalimaŋa a ta jam sak ba la.

ref: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
text: Izirali demma a jam suk nye ka dii ale kan nala ale Naawen dii ale ka ba Wen la. A zaani ba gbirima diinaŋa a ga paari parik pagrisaŋa tɛŋsaŋa ba sɛ ka tangbana a te badek ba tɛŋsaŋa po meena.

ref: Lotan was the father of Hori and Homam; Lotan's sister was Timna.
text: Lotan nidoabilisaŋa jam le Yori ale Yomam. Timna jam ka Lotan toa.

ref: Shobal was the father of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon was the father of Aiah and Anah.
text: Sobal nidoabilisaŋa jam le Alian ale Manahat ale Ebal ale Sefi ale Onam. Zibeon nidoabilisaŋa jam le Aiaya ale Anaya.

ref: Anah was the father of Dishon and the grandfather of Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
text: Anaya nidoabili jam le Dison. Dison nidoabilisa jam le Yamran ale Esban ale Itran ale Cheran.

ref: Ezer was the father of Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan was the father of Uz and Aran.
text: Ezer nidoabilisaŋa jam le Bilyan ale Zaavan ale Jakan. Disan mɛ nidoabilisa jam le Uz ale Aran.

ref: After Jobab's death, Husham from the land of Teman became king.
text: Jobab ale jam kpi la, Yusam ale nyini Tema demma tɛŋka la ale jam zaani wa nankula po a chim naab.

ref: After Husham's death, Hadad son of Bedad became king and ruled from Avith. Earlier, Bedad had defeated the Midianites in the territory of Moab.
text: Yusam ale kpi la, Bedad nidoabinni Yadad ate wa jam nak dɛ Midian tɛŋka ale bo Moab po la ale dɛ naamu. Wa tɛŋka ba jam te ka yuei ayen ka Avit.

ref: After Hadad's death, Samlah from Masrekah became king;
text: Yadad ale kpi la, Samla ale nyini Masreka la ale dɛ naamu.

ref: after Samlah's death, Shaul from the town of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River became king;
text: Samla ale jam kpi la, Sɛyaul ale nyini Areyobot ale bo Benni nɔi la ale jam chim naab.

ref: and after Shaul's death, Baal Hanan son of Achbor became king.
text: Sɛyaul ale jam kpi la, Achbor nidoabinni Baal Yanan ale jam chim naab.

ref: After Baal Hanan's death, Hadad ruled from Pai. His wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab.
text: Baal Yanan ale jam kpi la, Yadad ale jam chim naab. Wa tɛŋ kpieŋka yuei jam le Pai, wa powa yuei jam le Meyetabel a chim Matred lie ate Matred a chim Mezayab lie.

ref: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
text: Oyolibama ale Elaya ale Pinon ale

ref: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
text: Kenaz ale Teman ale Mibzar ale

ref: Jacob was the father of twelve sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
text: Dan ale Josefi ale Benjamin ale Nafitali ale Gad ale Asɛ.

ref: Judah and his Canaanite wife Bathshua had three sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah. But the Lord had Er put to death, because he disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
text: Juda nidoabilisaŋa jam le Ɛri ale Onan ale Sɛla. Bade batama ka Keenan tɛŋka lie Bat Sɛyua ale jam biak ba a te wa. Juda nidoabili kpagni Ɛri a jam ta ka gaasa Naawen nimbie po ate Naawen a ko wa.

ref: Judah and his daughter-in-law Tamar also had two sons: Perez and Zerah.
text: Tamara Juda sampowa jam biak ka Perezi ale Zera. Juda nidoabilisaŋa meena jam ka banu.

ref: Perez was the father of Hezron and Hamul.
text: Perezi nidoabilisaŋa jam le Ayeziron ale Yamul.

ref: Zerah was the father of Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda.
text: Zera nidoabilisaŋa jam le Zimri ale Etan ale Yeman ale Kalkol ale Darda. Ba meena ka banu.

ref: Achan, who was a descendant of Zerah and the son of Carmi, caused trouble for Israel, because he kept for himself things that belonged only to the Lord.
text: Karmi nidoabili ale Achar, waai ale jam ta daanika a jam Izirali zuk ta va kisuk ŋantaŋa ate ba ayen ba kan tiri la.

ref: Ethan's son was Azariah. The Ancestors of King David
text: Etan nidoabili jam le Azariya.

ref: Hezron was the father of Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.
text: Ayeziron nidoabilisaŋa jam le Jerameel ale Aram ale Chelubai.

ref: Ram was the father of Amminadab and the grandfather of Nahshon, a tribal leader of Judah.
text: Aram jam ka Amminadab ko, Amminadab jam ka Nayson ko Juda nuruma niŋdeerɔ.

ref: Nahshon's descendants included Salma, Boaz,
text: Nayson jam ka Salimon ko, Salimon jam ka Boazi ko,

ref: Jesse also had two daughters: Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah was the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
text: Ba toama jam le Zeruiya ale Abigail. Zeruiya nidoabilisaŋa batawa jam le Abisai ale Joab ale Asayel.

ref: Abigail's husband was Jether, who was a descendant of Ishmael, and their son was Amasa. The Descendants of Hezron
text: Abigail jam ka Amasa ma waai ko ale jam ka Jeter Ismael denɔ la.

ref: Hezron's son Caleb married Azubah, and their daughter was Jerioth, the mother of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
text: Ayeziron nidoabinni Kaleb jam ta ka nidoabilisa ale wa powa Azuba ale wa pok wa choawa Jeriot. Azuba nidoabilisaŋa jam le Jeser ale Sobab ale Ardon.

ref: After the death of Azubah, Caleb married Ephrath. Their son Hur
text: Azuba ale jam kpi la, Kaleb a jam faari ka Efrat ate wa mɛ a biak Yur.

ref: was the father of Uri and the grandfather of Bezalel.
text: Yur jam ka Uri ko, Uri jam ka Bezalel ko.

ref: After the death of Hezron, Caleb married Ephrath, his father's wife. Their son was Ashhur, who later settled the town of Tekoa. The Descendants of Jerahmeel
text: Ayeziron ale jam kpi Kaleb Efrata po la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Abaija Ayeziron powa a jam biak ka Asur Tekoa kowa.

ref: Jerahmeel, Hezron's oldest son, was the father of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
text: Ayeziron nidoabili kpagni jam le Jerameel. Jerameel nidoabilisaŋa jam le Aram ale Bunaya ale Oren ale Ozem ale Ayija. Aram jam le Jerameel nidoabili kpagni.

ref: Jerahmeel had a second wife, Atarah, who gave birth to Onam.
text: Jerameel jam ta ka nipok wa choa, wa yuei jam le Ataraya. Wa jam ka Onam ma.

ref: Ram was the father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
text: Jerameel nidoabili kpagni Aram a jam ta ka nidoabilisa, bala abe le Maaz ale Jamin ale Eker.

ref: Onam was the father of Shammai and Jada. Shammai was the father of Nadab and Abishur.
text: Onam nidoabilisaŋa jam le Sammai ale Jada. Sammai mɛ nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Nadab ale Abisur.

ref: Abishur married Abihail, and their two sons were Ahban and Molid.
text: Abisur powa yuei a jam le Abiyail, wala ale jam biak Aban ale Molid.

ref: Nadab was the father of Seled and Appaim. Seled had no children;
text: Nadab mɛ nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Seled ale Appaim. Seled an jam biak bisa ale kpi ya.

ref: Appaim's son was Ishi, the father of Sheshan and the grandfather of Ahlai.
text: Appaim nidoabili jam le Isi. Isi a jam ka Sesan ko ate Sesan a jam chim Alai ko.

ref: Jada was the father of Jether and Jonathan. Jether had no children,
text: Jada Sammai suoku nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Jeter ale Jonatan. Jeter an jam biak bisa ale kpi ya.

ref: but Jonathan had two sons: Peleth and Zaza.
text: Jonatan nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Pelet ale Zaza. Bade a jam le Jerameel ŋaaŋbisaŋa.

ref: Sheshan had no sons, and so he let one of his daughters marry Jarha, his Egyptian slave. Their son was Attai,
text: Sesan a jam pa ka wa lie a yalisi wa tomteerɔwa Jarha, ate wa biak Attai.

ref: the father of Nathan and the grandfather of Zabad.
text: Attai jam ka Natan ko, Natan jam ka Zabad ko,

ref: Zabad's descendants included Ephlal, Obed, Jehu, Azariah, Helez, Eleasah, Sismai, Shallum, Jekamiah, and Elishama. The Descendants of Caleb
text: Sallum jam ka Jekamia ko, Jekamia jam ka Elisama ko.

ref: and Hebron's four sons, Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
text: Yebron mɛ nidoabilisaŋa jam le Koora ale Tappua ale Arekem ale Sɛma.

ref: Shema was the father of Raham and the grandfather of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai,
text: Sɛma jam ka Arayam ko, Arayam jam ka Jorkeam ko. Arekem jam ka Sammai ko.

ref: the grandfather of Maon, and the great-grandfather of Bethzur.
text: Sammai jam ka Maon ko, Maon jam ka Bet Zur ko.

ref: Ephah was one of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran named his son after his brother Gazez.
text: Kaleb pokbinni Efa jam ka Yaran ale Moza ale Gazez ma. Yaran jam ka Gazez ko.

ref: Ephah was the daughter of Jahdai, who was also the father of Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, and Shaaph.
text: Jadai nidoabilisaŋa jam le Aregem ale Jotam ale Gesan ale Pelet ale Efa ale Saaf.

ref: Maacah was another of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Sheber and Tirhanah.
text: Kaleb pokbinni Maaka jam ka Seber ale Tirana ma.

ref: Later, they had two more sons: Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
text: Wa ale jam maa biak Saaf Madmanna kowa ale Seva Makbena kowa ale Gibeya. Kaleb lie jam le Aksaya.

ref: Shobal, who settled the town of Kiriath-Jearim, was the ancestor of Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth clan,
text: Sobal Kiriat Jearim kowa ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam le Yaroe ale Manahat demma geli ale

ref: and the clans that lived near Kiriath-Jearim; they were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The Zorathites and the Eshtaolites were descendants of the Mishraites.
text: Kiriat Jearim yezuimaŋa. Bala ale Itri demma ale Puti demma ale Sumat demma ale Misra demma. Ŋaaŋbisaŋa de po ale Zorat demma ale Estaol demma a nyini la.

ref: Salma settled the town of Bethlehem and was the ancestor of the Netophathites, the people of Atroth-Bethjoab, half of the Manahathite clan, and the Zorites.
text: Salma ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam le Betiliyem ale Netofat demma ale Atrot Bet Joab ale Manahat demma geli ale Zor demma buuraŋa ale

ref: Salma was also the ancestor of the clans in Jabez that kept the court and government records; they were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These clans were the descendants of Hammath the Kenite, who was also the ancestor of the Rechabites.
text: gbaŋ ŋmarisidoama yezuimaŋa baai ale bo Jabez la. Bala abe le Tirat demma ale Simeat demma ale Sukat demma. Bade ale Ken demma waai ale nyini Yammat, Arekab kowa yenni la.

ref: more sons. His wife Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel gave birth to Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon.
text: Jotam nidoabili jam le Ayazi, Ayazi nidoabili jam le Azekaya, Azekaya nidoabili jam le Manasa.

ref: David's other sons included Ibhar, Elishua, Eliphelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
text: Elisama ale Eliada ale Elifelet. Ba meena jam ka neok.

ref: David's other wives also gave birth to sons. Tamar was his daughter. The Descendants of King Solomon
text: Bade meena jam ka Deevid bisa, wa pokbinni nidoabilisaŋa a maa karo. Tamara jam ka ba toa.

ref: Solomon's descendants included the following kings: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah, Azariah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, and Josiah and his four sons, Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Jehoahaz.
text: Josia nidoabilisaŋa a jam le nna. Wa nidoabili kpagni a jam le Joyanan a paasaŋ Jeyoiakim batawa po jam ka Zedekia ate Sallum a saari banaansi.

ref: Jehoiachin, who was taken to Babylon as a prisoner, had seven sons: Shealtiel,
text: Jekonaya ate ba jam nak yik la nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Sealtiel ale

ref: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
text: Malkiram ale Pedaiya ale Senazzar ale Jekamia ale Yosama ale Nedabia.

ref: Pedaiah had two sons: Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel was the father of Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister.
text: Pedaiya nidoabilisaŋa mɛ a jam le Zerubabel ale Simei. Zerubabel nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Mesullam ale Yanania, ba tua a jam le Selomit.

ref: He also had five other sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushabhesed.
text: Zerubabel mɛ a jam ta ka bi yoŋta banu. Bala abe le Yasuba ale Oyel ale Berekiya ale Yasadia ale Jusab Yesed.

ref: the father of Shemaiah and the grandfather of Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
text: Sekania nidoabili a jam le Sɛmaiya. Sɛmaiya nidoabilisa mɛ a jam le Yattus ale Igal ale Baria ale Nearia ale Safat. Ba meena a jam ka nidoabilisa bayuebi.

ref: Neariah was the father of Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
text: Nearia nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Elioenai ale Yizkia ale Azrikam. Ba meena jam ka bata.

ref: Elioenai was the father of Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
text: Elioenai nidoabilisaŋa mɛ a jam le Yodavia ale Eliasib ale Pelaiya ale Akkub ale Joyanan ale Delaiya ale Anani. Ba meena jam ka bayopɔi.

ref: Judah was the father of five sons: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
text: Juda nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Perezi ale Ayeziron ale Karmi ale Yur ale Sobal.

ref: Shobal was the father of Reaiah, the grandfather of Jahath, and the great-grandfather of Ahumai and Lahad. These men all belonged to the Zorathite clan.
text: Sobal nidoabinni Areaiya a jam ka Jayat ko, Jayat jam ka Ayumai ale Layud ko. Bade jam le Zorat yezuimaŋa.

ref: Ashhur, who settled the town of Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah.
text: Tekoa kowa Asur a jam ta ka nipooba baye, Yela ale Naaraya.

ref: daughters. But his brothers did not have as many children, so the Simeon tribe was smaller than the Judah tribe.
text: Naaraya a jam biak ka Ayuzzam ale Yefer ale Temeni ale Yaayastari a te wa. Naaraya ŋaaŋbisaŋa le la.

ref: Ashhur and Helah were the parents of Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
text: Yela nidoabilisaŋa a jam le nna. Zeret ale Zoyar ale Etnan ale

ref: Koz, the father of Anub and Zobebah, was also the ancestor of the clans of Aharhel, the son of Harum.
text: Koz waai ale jam biak Anub ale Yazzobeba ale Ayaryel Yarum nidoabinni yezuimaŋa.

ref: Jabez was a man who got his name because of the pain he caused his mother during birth. But he was still the most respected son in his family.
text: Jabez a jam ta zula a gaam wa suataŋa kama. Ate wa mawa a jam te wa yuei ayen Jabez, di kiri ale, <<Mi biak wa ale ka nyiŋdomma.>>

ref: One day he prayed to Israel's God, “Please bless me and give me a lot of land. Be with me so I will be safe from harm.” And God did just what Jabez had asked.
text: Jabez yaa jam puusi a weeni Izirali Wenni ayen, <<Fi a niak mu a basi ate m tɛŋka a lagri a gum du, basi ate fi nisaŋa a bo ale mu, abe fi kasi mu ate wari a kan paari mu ate dila ale basi ate mi nye fasiyaa ale nyiŋdomma.>> Ate Wen a tulisi wa puusaŋa.

ref: Chelub was the brother of Shuhah and the father of Mehir. Later, Mehir had a son, Eshton,
text: Suyaya suoku Chelub a jam ka Meyir ko, Meyir jam ka Eston ko.

ref: whose three sons were Bethrapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. It was Tehinnah who settled the town of Nahash. These men and their families lived in the town of Recah.
text: Eston jam ka Bet Arafa ale Pasea ale Teyinna ko. Teyinna a jam ka nuru baai ale nyini Nayas tɛŋka la ko. Nuruma de a nyini ka Areka.

ref: Kenaz was the father of Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel had two sons: Hathath and Meonothai,
text: Kenaz nidoabilisa a jam le Otniel ale Seraiya. Otniel mɛ nidoabilisa a jam le Yatat ale Meonotai.

ref: who was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, who settled a place called “Valley of Crafts” because the people who lived there were experts in making things.
text: Meonotai a jam ka Ofra ko. Seraiya a jam ka Joab ko, wa mɛ jam ka Ge Yarasim ko. Ba yuei a jam le la dii nyiŋla ba jam ka yɔgrɔba.

ref: Caleb son of Jephunneh had three sons: Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah was the father of Kenaz.
text: Jefunne nidoabili a jam le Kaleb. Kaleb mɛ nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Iru ale Elaya ale Naam. Elaya nidoabili a jam le Kenaz.

ref: A man named Hodiah was married to the sister of Naham. Hodiah's descendants included Keilah of the Garmite clan and Eshtemoa of the Maacathite clan.
text: Yodia powa jam ka Nayam ko lie. Yodia powa nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Estemoa ale Keila kowa. Keila a jam nyini ka Garm demma po, ate Estemoa a jam nyini Maaka demma po.

ref: Shimon was the father of Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. Ishi was the father of Zoheth and Benzoheth.
text: Sɛyɛmon nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Amnon ale Arinnaya ale Ben Yanan ale Tilon. Isi ŋaaŋbisaŋa jam le Zoyet ale Ben Zoyet.

ref: The members of these clans were the potters who lived in the towns of Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king. The Descendants of Simeon
text: Ba jam ka mɛɛrɔba a bo Netaim ale Gedera tɛŋsaŋa po. Ba jam bo ka dula a tom a te naawa.

ref: Simeon had five sons: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
text: Simeyon ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam le Nemuel ale Jamin ale Jarib ale Zera ale Sɛyaul.

ref: The descendants of Shaul included his son Shallum, his grandson Mibsam, and his great-grandson Mishma.
text: Sɛyaul jam ka Sallum ko, Sallum jam le Mibsam ko. Mibsam nidoabili a jam le Misma.

ref: The descendants of Mishma included his son Hammuel, his grandson Zaccur, and his great-grandson Shimei.
text: Misma nidoabili a jam le Yammuel. Yammuel nidoabili a jam le Zakkur. Zakkur mɛ nidoabili a jam le Simei.

ref: Before David became king, the people of the Simeon tribe lived in the following towns: Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-Shual, Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad, Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazarsusim, Bethbiri, and Shaaraim.
text: Bet Markabot ale Yazar Susim ale Bet Biri ale Saaraim tɛŋsaŋa. Ba jam bo ka tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa de po ate ku paari diipo ate Deevid a chim naab la.

ref: They also lived in the five villages of Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan,
text: Tɛŋ kpaŋsa sinuwa ale jam moata tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa de la a jam le Etam ale Ain ale Arimmon ale Token ale Asan.

ref: as well as in the nearby villages as far as the town of Baal. These are the places where Simeon's descendants had settled, according to their own family records.
text: Tɛŋ kpaŋsa si chaab ale jam maa boro a yalima a paari Baalat. Dela ale ba jam boro la. Ate ba yaa jam ŋmarisi ba dɔkdemma ŋiak wie a dueni.

ref: As their families and clans became larger, the people of Simeon had the following leaders: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah, Joel, Jehu, Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah, and Ziza.
text: Nidoama yueŋa ale ŋmarisi ŋmazukku la a jam ka niŋdeerɔba ba yezuimaŋa po. Ba dɔkdemma a jam ŋmasi piisi kama,

ref: When the people needed more pastureland for their flocks and herds, they looked as far as the eastern side of the valley where the town of Gerar is located,
text: ate ba yaa jam nyini Gedor tɛŋka nakpiak viaka kori geŋsa ayen ba gisi wuyɔgsuk a te ba duŋsaŋa.

ref: and they found a lot of good pastureland that was quiet and undisturbed. This had once belonged to the Hamites,
text: Ba yaa jam nya wuuk maŋ ate ku piisi, tɛŋka a jam ta peelim nna jalɔ a ta suiyɔgni nna chim. Yɛm demma gela ale jam liŋ bo dula.

ref: Reuben was the oldest son of Jacob, but he lost his rights as the first-born son because he slept with one of his father's wives. The honor of the first-born son was then given to Joseph,
text: Izirali nidoabili kpagni Aruben nidoabilisaŋa ale nna: Wa ale jam chim nidoabili kpagni, alege wa ale taŋ wa kowa powa la nyiŋ, wa biam kpaŋtaŋa yaa cheŋ Izirali nidoabinni Josefi nidoabilisaŋa jigi. Dila nyiŋ wa yuenni a ka dɔkdemma po ase wa ka nidoabi kpagi la.

ref: Reuben had four sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
text: Izirali nidoabili kpagni Aruben nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Yanok ale Pallu ale Ayeziron ale Karmi.

ref: The descendants of Joel included Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, Baal, and Beerah, a leader of the Reuben tribe. Later, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria took Beerah away as prisoner.
text: Beeraya jam ka Baal nidoabili. Beeraya a jam ka Aruben dɔkku buuni niŋdeerɔ, waai ate Assiria naawa Tilgat Pilneser a jam nak yik la.

ref: The family records also include Jeiel, who was a clan leader, Zechariah, and Bela son of Azaz and grandson of Shema of the Joel clan. They lived in the territory around the town of Aroer, as far north as Nebo and Baal-Meon,
text: ale Azaz nidoabinni Bela, Azaz mɛ jam ka Sɛma nidoabili, Sɛma jam ka Joel nidoabili. Ba jam boka Aroer kabini a va dula meena a cheŋ Nebo ale Baal Meon.

ref: and as far east as the desert just west of the Euphrates River. They needed this much land because they owned too many cattle to keep them all in Gilead.
text: Nuruma a jam bo ka kori geŋsa a yalima a paari sagni ale bo Yufiretis Benaŋka la, dii nyiŋla ba duŋsaŋa a jam piisi kama Gilead tɛŋka po.

ref: When Saul was king, the Reuben tribe attacked and defeated the Hagrites, then took over their land east of Gilead. The Descendants of Gad
text: Sɔɔl naamu vaaŋa po ba jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale Yagri demma a nak yik ba. Ba jam tuesi Yagri demma boka jigini kama a kala ka meena po ale bo Gilead kori geŋka la.

ref: The tribe of Gad lived in the region of Bashan, north of the Reuben tribe. Gad's territory extended all the way to the town of Salecah.
text: Gad dɔkku ale jam paasaŋ ba a bo Basan a ta ga paari Saleka.

ref: Some of the clan leaders were Joel, Shapham, Janai, and Shaphat.
text: Joel a jam le kpagi a pasaŋ Safam ale Janai ale Safat Basan po.

ref: Ahi, the son of Abdiel and the grandson of Guni, was the leader of their clan.
text: Ayi jam ka Abdiel nidoabili, Abdiel jam ka Guni nidoabili. Ayi a jam le ba dɔkdemma niŋdeerɔ.

ref: The people of Gad lived in the towns in the regions of Bashan and Gilead, as well as in the pastureland of Sharon.
text: Gad demma a jam boka Gilead tɛŋka ale bo Basan po la ale ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale wuuk a bo Saaron po a lagri a cheŋ la.

ref: Their family records were written when Jotham was king of Judah and Jeroboam was king of Israel.
text: Ŋade meena a jam bo ka gaŋka wieŋa ale jam ŋmarisi doa diipo ate Juda naawa Jotam ale Izirali naawa Jeroboam a dɛ ba naataŋa la.

ref: They fought against the Hagrites and the tribes of Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
text: Ba jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale Yagri ale Jetur ale Nafis ale Nodab demma.

ref: Whenever these soldiers went to war against their enemies, they prayed to God and trusted him to help. That's why the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh defeated the Hagrites and their allies.
text: Manasa ale Aruben diinaŋa buuni a jam puusi kama a te Naawen diipo ate kpaliŋka a nye la ayen wa maari ba. Wa yaa maari ba dii nyiŋla ba jam ta ka sebchakka ale wa. Wa yaa jam pai Yagri ale baai meena ale jam gum wa po la a nyo ba nisima po.

The ancestor of the family of Barzillai had married the daughter of Barzillai from Gilead and had taken his wife's family name. But the records of these three families could not be found, and none of them were allowed to serve as priests.
text: Bade a jam gisi ba yueŋa kama alege ba an nya ŋa ate ba yaa yeeri ba a ta nyini kaabteerɔma po a nyini ase baai ale kan welema la.

ref: In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until we find out if you really are priests.”
text: Niŋdeerɔwa a weeni ba ayen ba kan dɛ tuilum ŋandiintaŋa ba basi ate kaabteerɔwa a pai ŋanti baai ate ba a wi ayen Urim ale Tummim la a nye.

ref: When the people came to where the Lord's temple had been in Jerusalem, some of the family leaders gave gifts so it could be rebuilt in the same place.
text: Ase ba ale ga paari Naawen yenni ale bo Jerusalem la, yeeŋa nyama kpaŋŋa gela a yaa te tiirim a magsi chaab ale Naawen yenni sɛka.

ref: Everyone returned to the towns from which their families had come, including the priests, the Levites, the musicians, the temple guards, and the workers.
text: Kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale yilendisaŋa, baai ale a nya nansuiŋtaŋa zuk la ale baai ale a tom Naawen yenni po la a jam boka badek tɛŋsaŋa po, a gum chaab ale nuruba gela, alege ate Izirali dem mbala meena a bo badek tɛŋsaŋa po.

ref: During the seventh month of the year, the Israelites who had settled in their towns went to Jerusalem.
text: Ase chiisa siyopɔiwa ale paari la ate Izirali demma a jam bo ba tɛŋsaŋa po la, nuruma a jam tigsi ka chaab ase nuru yeŋ la Jerusalem po.

ref: The priest Joshua son of Jozadak, together with the other priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives rebuilt the altar of Israel's God. Then they were able to offer sacrifices there by following the instructions God had given to Moses, the man of God.
text: Ate Jozadak nidoabinni Jesua ale wa kaabteerɔ chaama ale Sealtiel nidoabinni Zerubabel ale wa vaanchaama a yaa piilim a boro a sɛ Izirali Wenni kuŋkuŋku kuui ate ba ale nye juka kaabka ku zuk la, a ta magsi chaab ale dii ale ŋmarisi Moosis Wen nuruwa Sinsaŋŋa po la.

ref: And they built the altar where it had stood before, even though they were afraid of the people who were already living around there. Then every morning and evening they burned sacrifices and offerings to the Lord.
text: Ba a jam a chali yɔgsum ase nuruma ale jam za a gilim ba la, alege ba sɛ kuŋkuŋ, kama nyubini zuk ale nye juka kaabka ku zuk a te Naawen ba jam nye kaabka ka saluik ale junɔi meena.

ref: The people followed the rules for celebrating the Festival of Shelters and offered the proper sacrifices each day.
text: A ta vaanchaab ale dii ale ŋmarisi la, ba jam a dɛ Viitaŋa Tigini ale ŋanti baai ale magsi ayen ba pai a nye juka kaabka la dai meena po la.

ref: They offered sacrifices to please the Lord, sacrifices at each New Moon Festival, and sacrifices at the rest of the Lord's festivals. Every offering the people had brought voluntarily was also presented to the Lord.
text: Ku la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, ba jam te ba ale magsi ba te dii a magsi juka kaabka, ale Chiik Paalik kaabka ale kaab weleŋ kaai meena ate ba lueri a te Naawen, ale baai meena ate ba ta jam ase tiirim la a te Naawen.

ref: Although work on the temple itself had not yet begun, the people started offering sacrifices on the Lord's altar on the first day of the seventh month of that year. The Rebuilding of the Temple Begins
text: Chiisa siyopɔiwa po ka dai dii ale dɛ niŋka la ba piilim a nye juka kaabka a te Naawen, alege dila po wa ba an diem a jam sɛ Naawen yenni nyubini.

ref: King Cyrus of Persia had said the Israelites could have cedar trees brought from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. So they sent grain, wine, and olive oil to the cities of Tyre and Sidon as payment for these trees, and they gave money to the stoneworkers and carpenters.
text: Ba yaa jam te seerɔma ale danagrɔba ligra ale te Saidon ale Taaya demma ŋandiinta ale nyuka ale kpaam, dii ale ku basi ate ba ta nyunyoŋ daata a va Lebanon nyakpiemu po a yaa va Jopa, ase Persia naawa Sairus ale weeni diila.

ref: During the second month of the second year after the people had returned from Babylonia, they started rebuilding the Lord's temple. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jozadak, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned started working. Every Levite over
text: Chiik kaai ale saari siyewa la bena ŋayewa po ba ale jam ŋman nya nyiŋbiiri Naawen yenni Jerusalem po la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Sealtiel nidoabinni Zerubabel ale Jozadak nidoabinni Jesua ale ba suataŋa kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale baai meena ale nyini yɔntini po a cheŋ Jerusalem la a piilim tomka, ba lueri baai ate ba a wi ba ayen Livaima la ate ba bena a paari pisiye ale tali la ate bala a nya Naawen yenni sɛka zuk.

ref: The Levites in charge of the whole project were Joshua and his sons and relatives and Kadmiel and his sons from the family of Hodaviah. The family of Henadad worked along with them.
text: Jesua ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ale wa suataŋa ale Kadmiel ale wa nidoabilisaŋa baai ale jam ka Yodavia ŋaaŋbisa la, ale Yenadad nidoabilisaŋa ale ba nidoabilisaŋa ale ba suataŋa baai ale jam ka Livaiba la meena a gum chaab a jaa nya baai ale jam boro a tom Naawen yenni tuimaŋa la zuk.

ref: When the builders had finished laying the foundation of the temple, the priests put on their robes and blew trumpets in honor of the Lord, while the Levites from the family of Asaph praised God with cymbals. All of them followed the instructions given years before by King David.
text: Ase seerɔma ale dueni Naawen yenni nyubini la, kaabteerɔma pai ba gattaŋa ale ba damunsaŋa ale Livaima. Asaf nidoabilisaŋa ale la. Ba ale ba dalinkinkeŋsa, a piilim a pak Naawen ase Izirali Naawa Deevid ale weeni diila.

ref: They praised the Lord and gave thanks as they took turns singing: “The Lord is good! His faithful love for Israel will last forever.” Everyone started shouting and praising the Lord because work on the foundation of the temple had begun.
text: Ba yaa jam lenni yiila a pak Naawen ale weeni ayen, <<Wa nala, wa ŋmanteka ale Izirali demma boro ka dila taam wuu.>> Ate nuruma meena a yaa nuemu nna yegayega a pak Naawen, dii nyiŋla ba jam dueni Naawen yenni nyubini kama.

ref: Many of the older priests and Levites and the heads of families wept bitterly because they remembered seeing the first temple years before. But others were so happy that they celebrated with joyful shouts.
text: Alege kaabteerɔ kpagsaŋa ale Livaima yeeŋa nyama yega ale ga wom la, Baai ale jam a nya Naawen yekpakka la, a yaa jam kumu ate ku jueli nna yegayega ase ba ale nya ale ba ŋman pilim dueni Naawen yenni nyubini la, alege ba yega mɛ jam kasim a nuem kama ale suipeentik.

ref: Their shouting and crying were so noisy that it all sounded alike and could be heard a long way off.
text: Waai an jam baga a poori suipeentik nuemka ale kumsaŋa dii nyiŋla nuruma a jam a nuem ka nna yegayega. Ate nuemka a jam a wom nna niŋniŋa.

ref: The enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people had come back to rebuild the temple of the Lord God of Israel.
text: Ase Juda ale Benjamin dachaasaŋa ale wom ayen ba boro a sɛ Naawen, Izirali Wen yenni la,

ref: So they went to Zerubbabel and to the family leaders and said, “Let us help! Ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here, we have worshiped your God and offered sacrifices to him.”
text: ba yaa jam Zerubabel ale yeeŋa nyama jigi a weeni ba ayen, <<Basi ate tama a maari ni ate ni sɛ, ase nama la, tama a gisi ni Wenni ale a nye kaabka a te wa a ta nyini Assiria naawa Esayaddon daaŋa po, waai ale ta tama a jam dela la.>>

ref: But Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the family leaders answered, “You cannot take part in building a temple for the Lord our God! We will build it ourselves, just as King Cyrus of Persia commanded us.”
text: Alege Zerubabel ale Jesua ale Izirali yeeŋa nyama meena a tulisi ba ayen, <<Nama a ka wari a nye ale tama a ta va chaab ale Naawen yenni sɛka. Tama nyiini ale sɛ a te Naawen, Izirali Wenni, ase Naab Sairus, Persia Naawa ale weeni diila.>>

ref: Then the neighboring people began to do everything possible to frighten the Jews and to make them stop building.
text: Ate nuru baai ale gilim ba la a yaa jaa a nye ayen Juda demma a jɔk nyiŋbiiri abe ba nye ate ba a chali yɔgsum ate ba kan baga a sɛ.

ref: During the time that Cyrus was king and even until Darius became king, they kept bribing government officials to slow down the work. Trouble Rebuilding Jerusalem
text: Ba yaa da sagrɔba ayen ba tom a kaasi ba ale a poli ba nye dii Persia naawa Sairus naamu daaŋa po a ta ga paari Persia naawa Darius daaŋa po la.

ref: In the first year that Xerxes was king, the neighboring people brought written charges against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
text: A ta nyini piilimka diipo ate Ayasuerus a dɛ wa naamu la, ba yaa velim a te Juda ale Jerusalem demma.

ref: Later, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their advisors got together and wrote a letter to Artaxerxes when he was king of Persia. It was written in Aramaic and had to be translated.
text: Ate diipo ate Artasaset a chim Persia Naab la, Bislam ale Mitredat ale Tabeel ale ba ŋaaŋviirɔma meena a yaa jam ŋmarisi gbaŋ a te Artasaset. Ba jam ŋmarisi gbaŋka ale ka bi kaai ate ba a wi ayen Araam demma biik la.

ref: This letter said: Your Majesty King Artaxerxes, we are your servants from everywhere in Western Province, and we send you our greetings.
text: Gbaŋka ate ba jam a tom a te wa la ale nna. Ka tama fi tomteerɔma, nuru baai ale nyini Yufiretis Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala la ale ŋmarisi gbaŋka de a te Naab Artasaset:

ref: You should know that the Jews who left your country have moved back to Jerusalem and are now rebuilding that rebellious city. In fact, they have almost finished rebuilding the walls and repairing the foundations.
text: Naawa a magsi ayen wa sebi kama ayen Juuma baai ale nyini fi jigi a jam tama jigi la a cheŋ ka Jerusalem a ŋman pilim boro a sɛ tukpari ale gaasa tɛŋka. Ba ŋaan gomsi nyubini ale parisaŋa a magsi kama.

ref: You should also know that if the walls are completed and the city is rebuilt, the Jews won't pay any kind of taxes, and there will be less money in your treasury.
text: A ŋman gum du, naawa a magsi ayen wa sebi kama ayen ba dan se tɛŋka ale ka parisaŋa, lampoo a kan ŋman tuni, ate naa yeri wieŋa ale a kan nye nalimnyiini.

ref: We are telling you this, because you have done so much for us, and we want everyone to respect you.
text: Ase tama ale bo ka naab yenni po la ku kan magsi ayen ti ka a te wa zula, ti nya wanni de kama ate tama a yaali ti weeni a sak naawa,

ref: If you look up the official records of your ancestors, you will find that Jerusalem has constantly rebelled and has led others to rebel against kings and provinces. That's why the city was destroyed in the first place.
text: ate dila ale basi ate wa kpesi nya gbaŋ sii po ate fi kokpieŋsaŋa a ŋmarisi la po. Ase fi a dan nye dila, fi ale nya ayen a nyini dila po wa tɛŋka de ka tukpari tɛŋ ale kasim a yaali wie a te nalima ale tɛŋka niŋdeerɔwa. Ka nuruma nyeka a jam toa kama ale fi ale dɛ ba niŋ. Dila ale soa ate tɛŋka a kaasi la.

ref: If Jerusalem is rebuilt and its walls completed, you will no longer have control over Western Province.
text: Ti weeni naawa kama ayen ase ba dan sɛ tɛŋka ale ka parisaŋa, fi kan nya jaaboa a ta nyini Yufiretis Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala ŋmana.

ref: King Artaxerxes answered: Greetings to Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and to your advisors in Samaria and other parts of Western Province.
text: Ate Naawa a yaa tom a tulisi ayen: ate fi kpagni ale Simsai gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa ale mbala meena ale ba vaanchaama ale bo Samaria ale Yufiretis Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala geŋsa la: Mi a puusi ni.

ref: I had the old records checked. It is true that for years Jerusalem has rebelled and caused trouble for other kings and nations.
text: Mi te ka suik ate ba gisi, ale nya mɛ ayen tɛŋka de a nyini dila po wa ba gomsi kama ayen ba zɛri nalimaŋa ale ba weeni diila, dula ka tukpari ale baai ale nye ate nuruba a zɛri kpaga nɔi.

ref: And powerful kings have ruled Western Province from Jerusalem and have collected all kinds of taxes.
text: Jerusalem jam ta ka nalima ŋaai ale pagra ate ba a nya Yufiretis Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala zuk ale lampoo ale tiiritaŋa meena ka ba ale jaa a tuesi.

ref: I want you to command the people to stop rebuilding the city until I give further notice.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de be weeni nuruma de ate ba basi tomka, ate kula ale nye ate ba basi sɛka a ga paari diipo ate m le te ba suik la.

ref: Do this at once, so that no harm will come to the kingdom.
text: Bi kpesi fidek ate fi kan zɛri wanni de. Kan basi ate nyinyigsaŋa de a chim a gum du, a kaasi naamu wie.

ref: As soon as this letter was read, Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and their advisors went to Jerusalem and forced everyone to stop rebuilding the city. Work on the Temple Starts Again
text: Ase ba ale ga kariŋ Naab Artasaset gbaŋka ate wa ŋmarisi la a te Areyum ale Simsai gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa ale ba vaanchaama a wom la, ba nye nwuli a cheŋ Juuma ale bo Jerusalem la a ga fɛ ba ayen ba basi tuini.

ref: The Jews were forced to stop work on the temple and were not able to do any more building until the year after Darius became king of Persia.
text: Naawen yenni tuini Jerusalem po a jam doa ka dila a ta ga paari bena ŋayewa po ate Persia naawa Darius a dɛ wa naamu la.

ref: Then the Lord God of Israel told the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to speak in his name to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. And they did.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de Naawen biisiteerɔwa Aggai ale biisiteerɔwa Zakaria, Iddo ŋaaŋbiika, a jam mooli te Juuma ale bo Juda ale Jerusalem po la Izirali Wenni yuei nyiŋ, waai ale a nya ba la.

ref: So Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the priest urged the people to start working on the temple again, and God's prophets encouraged them.
text: Ate Sealtiel nidoabinni Zerubabel ale Jozadak nidoabinni Jesua a yaa piilim tuima a boro a sɛ Naawen yenni Jerusalem po. Ate Naawen biisiteerɔma a jam maa boro ale ba, a maari ba.

ref: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and his assistant Shethar Bozenai got together with some of their officials. Then they went to Jerusalem and said to the people, “Who told you to rebuild this temple?
text: A nyini dila po wa Yufiretis Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala zuk niŋdeerɔwa Tattenai ale Setar Bozenai ale ba vaanchaama a jam cheŋ ba jigi a bek ayen, <<Ka wana ale te ni suiku de ayen ni ŋman pilim sɛ Naawen yenni abe ni zak di a zaani?>>

ref: But God was looking after the Jewish leaders. So the governor and his group decided not to make the people stop working on the temple until they could report to Darius and get his advice.
text: Alege ba Wenni nina a jam bo Juuma nisɔmma zuk kama, alege ba an basi tomka a ta ga paari diipo ate tontomiŋka a jam paari Darius ate wa yaa ŋmarisi tulisi ba.

ref: which said: King Darius, we wish you the best!
text: Wie ŋaai ate ba jam tom a te wa la ale nna. Naab Darius tama a puusi fu.

ref: We went to Judah, where the temple of the great God is being built with huge stones and wooden beams set in the walls. Everyone is working hard, and the building is going up quickly.
text: Naawa a magsi ayen wa seba ayen tama cheŋ Juda tɛŋka po kama, ale Naawen Kpienni yenni. Nuruma a boro a pai tintain kpiema a sɛ ale pai tapaga a vi parika zuk. Tuini a cheŋ kama nalimnyiini ase di ale magsi di cheŋ diila.

ref: We asked those in charge to tell us who gave them permission to rebuild the temple.
text: Tama a yaa bek niŋdeerɔma ayen, <<Ka wana ale te nama suik ayen ni ŋman pilim sɛ Naawen yenni?>>

ref: We also asked for the names of their leaders, so that we could write them down for you.
text: Ti be ŋman pilim bek ba kama ayen ba yue ale boa? Dii ale ku nye ate tama ŋmarisi ba niŋdeerɔma yueŋa ate ti weeni ba wie a sak fu.

ref: They claimed to be servants of the God who rules heaven and earth. And they said they were rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago by one of Israel's greatest kings.
text: Dii ate ba tulisi ti la ale nna: <<Ti ka wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk Wenni tomteerɔba, ate tama ŋman pilim boro a sɛ Naawen yenni dii ate ba poom a liŋ jam sɛ di bena ŋaai ale taam la, dii ate Izirali naab kpioŋku a jam sɛ di tuk la.

ref: We were told that their people had made God angry, and he let them be captured by Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king who took them away as captives to Babylonia. Nebuchadnezzar tore down their temple,
text: Alege ti koma ale nye ate wenŋmazuk Wenni sui a puuri la, wa yaa pai ba a nyo Nebukadnezzar Kaldiya denɔwa nisima po, Babilon Naawa ale la, waai ale kaasi Wen yenni de alege ta nuruma a cheŋ Babilon tɛŋka.

ref: Sheshbazzar then went to Jerusalem and laid the foundation for the temple, and the work is still going on.
text: Ate Sesbazzar wade a yaa jam dueni Wen yenni nyubini Jerusalem po. A nyini da di la danni a ta jam paari jinla ba diem boro a sɛ di kama ba an diem nueri ya.>>

ref: Your Majesty, please order someone to look up the old records in Babylonia and find out if King Cyrus really did give orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem. We will do whatever you think we should.
text: Nya kude dan yɔk naawa sui, basi ate ti gisi a ta nyini naab yeri ŋiak wieŋa po a ta nyini Babilon po ate ti nya ase Naab Sairus a sum jam te ka suik ayen ba ŋman pilim sɛ Wen yenni Jerusalem po ya. Basi ate Naawa a weeni ti wa popolaŋa ale ka dii a ta va wanni de la.

ref: King Darius ordered someone to go through the old records kept in Babylonia.
text: Naab Darius a yaa basi ate ba gisi Babilon po dɔkku po ate ba jam a dueni ŋanta du la.

ref: Finally, a scroll was found in Ecbatana, the capital of Media Province, and it said: This official record will show
text: Ba yaa yaali jabuui ate ba jam ŋmarisi yueŋa a dueni wa zuk la Ekbatana tɛŋka ate ka bo Miidi po la, dii ate ba jam ŋmarisi la abe le nna:

ref: that in the first year Cyrus was king, he gave orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem, so that sacrifices and offerings could be presented there. It is to be built
text: Naab Sairus ale dɛ wa naamu bein diila, Naawa a yaa weeni wari ale fifiok a ta va Wen yenni Jerusalem po: Ni pilim a sɛ Wen yenni ase jigi la a magsi kaabka, abe ni dueni nyubini. Ku woglimmu a magsi ku paari ku naŋtuok nɔi pineok,

ref: with one row of wooden beams for each three rows of large stones. The royal treasury will pay for everything.
text: abe ni pai tintain kpiema a sɛ paari kaarima ŋata abe le pai tapaga a sɛ kaarinni dinyi a gum du. Pamini ka waai ale a nya ligraŋa zuk naab yeri la ale wa tuni.

ref: Then the gold and silver things that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple and brought to Babylonia are to be returned to their proper places. King Darius Orders the Work To Continue
text: Ligmɔniŋka ale kpanaŋa ale jam bo Wen yenni po la, ŋaai ate Nebukadnezzar a jam pai a ta nyini Wen yenni ale bo Jerusalem po la a ta jam Babilon, a magsi ba ŋman ŋmani kama a cheŋ ba jigini Wen yenni Jerusalem po. Ba magsi ba bo ka Wen yenni po.

ref: King Darius sent this message: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and Shethar Bozenai, you and your advisors must stay away from the temple.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de, Tattenai, niŋdeerɔ waai ale a nya Yufiretis Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala zuk la, ale Setar Bozenai ale fi, ba kpaga ŋaai ale bo tɛŋka po la, a yaa jam bo ba tɔga.

ref: Let the Jewish governor and leaders rebuild it where it stood before. And stop slowing them down!
text: Ni kan basi ate ni niŋ a bo ale Wen yenni tuimaŋa po. Ni basi ate Juuma niŋdeerɔwa ale Juuma nisɔmma a pilim sɛ Wen yenni de a zaani di jigini.

ref: Starting at once, I am ordering you to help the leaders by paying their expenses from the tax money collected in Western Province.
text: Alege m ŋman weeni ni, ni le ni nye dii a te Juuma nisɔmma a magsi chaab ale Wen yenni sɛka la. Nuruma de tuimaŋa ligra meena a tuni a nyini naam ligraŋa po, a nyini Yufiretis Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala lampoowa po ate tuini kan wari.

ref: And don't fail to let the priests in Jerusalem have whatever they need each day so they can offer sacrifices to the God of heaven. Give them young bulls, rams, sheep, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and olive oil.
text: Jabuui meena ate ba a yaali la, lalik paalisa ale padaasa ale padabilisa a magsi juka tiirim a te wenŋmazuk Wenni ale ŋanbie ale yesa ale daam ale kpaam ase kaabteerɔma ale bo Jerusalem la a nin bek a yaali. Ku a fɛ ate ni te daa meena ni kan zɛri,

ref: I want them to be able to offer pleasing sacrifices to God and to pray for me and my family.
text: ate ba nye kaab sii ale a peenti wenŋmazuk Wenni sui abe ba puusi ate wari meena a nye nalimnyiini a te naawa ale wa nidoabilisaŋa.

ref: If any of you don't obey this order, a wooden beam will be taken from your house and sharpened on one end. Then it will be driven through your body, and your house will be torn down and turned into a garbage dump.
text: A ŋman gum du, m weeni kama ayen waai a dan zɛri wanni de ba ale yeeri ka chib wa yenni po a peesi bu a pai chub wa ko ate wa yenni ale chim tampoi ate ba kpiiri yaata a basi du.

ref: I ask the God who is worshiped in Jerusalem to destroy any king or nation who tries either to change what I have said or to tear down his temple. I, Darius, give these orders, and I expect them to be followed carefully. The Temple Is Dedicated
text: Wen, waai ale basi ate wa Yuenni a bo dula la, abe yeeri naab waai yaase nuru waai ale zak nisa ayen wa tagri wanni yaase wa kaasi Wen yenni de Jerusalem po la a basi. Mi Darius a te suik kama ayen ni kpesi a nye kude.

ref: With great success the Jewish leaders continued working on the temple, while Haggai and Zechariah encouraged them by their preaching. And so, the temple was completed at the command of the God of Israel and by the orders of kings Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes of Persia.
text: Dila nyiŋ Juuma nisɔmma a yaa pii nyiŋ ase ba ale a nya niaka a ta nyini Wen wanni ate biisiteerɔma Aggai ale Iddo ŋaaŋbiika Zakaria a jaa a biisi a te ba la jigi. Ba jam nueri Wen yenni kama a ta va chaab ale Izirali Wenni ale Persia nalimaŋa Sairus ale Darius ale Artasaset ale jam weeni diila.

ref: On the third day of the month of Adar in the sixth year of the rule of Darius, the temple was finished.
text: Ba jam sɛ Wen yenni a nueri ka Adar chiika ka daa ŋata danni, bena ŋayuebiwa po ate Darius a jam de wa naamu la.

ref: The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned from exile were happy and celebrated as they dedicated God's temple.
text: Ate Izirali nuruma ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale baai ale ŋman jam la a yaa jam de Wen yenni teka tigini ale suipeentik.

ref: One hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs were offered as sacrifices at the dedication. Also twelve goats were sacrificed as sin offerings for the twelve tribes of Israel.
text: Ba ale jam pai yenni a boro a nyo Wen nisima po la ba teka lalisa kook, padaasa kobsiye ale padabilisa kobsinaansi ayen ba pai a nye biem vɔŋteka kaabka a te Izirali meena, budukta pi ale tiye, ale ba jam te ayen ba pai kunyi kunyi a te Izirali buura pi ale buyewa meena.

ref: Then the priests and Levites were assigned their duties in God's temple in Jerusalem, according to the instructions Moses had written. The Passover
text: Ate ba yaa poori kaabteerɔma ba tɔga Livaima mɛ ba tɔga a magsi chaab ale Wen tuimaŋa Jerusalem po, a ta magsi chaab ale dii ale ŋmarisi Moosis gbaŋka po la.

ref: Everyone who had returned from exile celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
text: Chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la ka daa pi ale ŋanaansiwa danni baai ale nyini yontini po a kuli la a dɛ Gaambasika Tigini kama.

ref: The priests and Levites had gone through a ceremony to make themselves acceptable to lead in worship. Then some of them killed Passover lambs for those who had returned, including the other priests and themselves.
text: Kaabteerɔma ale Livaima a gomsi badek kama a nala. Livaima a yaa tɔgri Gaambasika pabiika a te baai meena ale nyini yontini po a jam la, ale ba suataŋa kaabteerɔma ale badek.

ref: The sacrifices were eaten by the Israelites who had returned and by the neighboring people who had given up the sinful customs of other nations in order to worship the Lord God of Israel.
text: Ate Izirali demma baai ale nyini yontini po a jam la a yaa dɛ ale baai meena ale poori badek a ta nyini baai ale kan daa Juuba la daŋta wie po ayen ba gisi Naawen, Izirali Wenni la.

ref: For seven days they celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread. Everyone was happy because the Lord God of Israel had made sure that the king of Assyria would be kind to them and help them build the temple.
text: Daa ŋayopɔi ba kasim a jam pai a ŋɔbi ka boroborok kuui ate ba an nyo dabinta ku po la tigini, dii nyiŋla Naawen a basi ate ka ba sue a peenti a ta va wa ale tagri Assiria Naawa popolaŋa la, ate wa maari ba ate ba tom Wen yenni Izirali Wenni tuini la.

ref: Much later, when Artaxerxes was king of Persia, Ezra came to Jerusalem from Babylonia. Ezra was the son of Seraiah and the grandson of Azariah. His other ancestors were Hilkiah, Shallum, Zadok, Ahitub, Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth, Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki, Abishua, Phinehas, Eleazar, and Aaron, the high priest. Ezra was an expert in the Law that the Lord God of Israel had given to Moses, and the Lord made sure that the king gave Ezra everything he asked for.
text: Ezra wade a jam nyini ka Babilon jam. Wa jam ka sagrɔ waai ale seba Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ŋaai ate Naawen, Izirali Wenni a jam te la. Naawa a jam te wa jaabuuri meena ate wa bek la kama, dii nyiŋla Naawen wa Wenni nisa a jam bo wa zuk kama.

ref: Other Jews, including priests, Levites, musicians, the temple guards, and servants, came to Jerusalem with Ezra. This happened during the seventh year that Artaxerxes was king.
text: Izirali demma gela ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale yilendisaŋa ale baai ale a nya nansuiŋtaŋa zuk la ale baai ale jam a tom Wen yenni po la, meena a yaa jam Jerusalem po bena ŋayopɔiwa po ate Naab Artasaset a jam dɛ wa naamu la.

ref: God helped Ezra, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month of that seventh year, after leaving Babylonia on the first day of the first month.
text: Wa yaa jam piilim wa chelimu a basi Babilon tɛŋka piilimka chiika da dii ale dɛ niŋka la danni, a yaa paari Jerusalem tɛŋka chiik kaai ale saari sinuwa la ka piilimka danni, wa Wenni ni sii ale a niak la ale bo ale wa la nyiŋ.

ref: Ezra was a priest and an expert in the laws and commands that the Lord had given to Israel. One day King Artaxerxes gave Ezra a letter which said:
text: Gbaŋ kaai ate Naab Artasaset a ŋmarisi a te Ezra waai ale ka kaabteerɔ ale sagrɔ la, wa ka nuru waai ale zamsi wie a magsi chaab ale Izirali Naawen buusaŋa ale wa wieŋa.

ref: Greetings from the great King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and expert in the teachings of the God of heaven.
text: Nalima meena naawa Artasaset a puusi kaabteerɔwa Ezra waai ale ŋman chim sagrɔ a sak wenŋmazuk Wenni wieŋa la mi a puusi fu.

ref: Any of the people of Israel or their priests or Levites in my kingdom may go with you to Jerusalem if they want to. My seven advisors and I agree that you may go to Jerusalem and Judah to find out if the laws of your God are being obeyed.
text: Naawa a tom fu kama ale wa nuruba bayopɔi baai ale a sak wa wie la ayen ni ga kpesi nya Juda ale Jerusalem a ta va ni Wenni wieŋa ale bo fi nisaŋa po la.

ref: When you go, take the silver and gold that I and my advisors are freely giving to the God of Israel, whose temple is in Jerusalem.
text: Ku abe magsi kama ayen fi pai naawa ale baai ale a sak wa wie la ale jam pai kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka a te Izirali Wenni ale bo Jerusalem po la,

ref: Take the silver and gold that you collect from everywhere in Babylonia. Also take the gifts that your own people and priests have so willingly contributed for the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
text: a gum chaab ale kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka meena ate ni nya a nyini Babilon tɛŋka la, ale tiirim tii meena ate nuruma ale kaabteerɔma a te Wen yenni Jerusalem po la.

ref: Use the money carefully to buy the best bulls, rams, lambs, grain, and wine. Then sacrifice them on the altar at God's temple in Jerusalem.
text: Pai ligraŋa de a da lalisa ale padaasa ale padabilisa ale ŋandiinta tiirim ale nyuka tiirim a yaa pai ba a nye kaabka Wen yenni po kuŋkuŋku zuk a te ni Wenni ale bo Jerusalem la.

ref: If any silver or gold is left, you and your people may use it for whatever pleases your God.
text: Fi ale fi suataŋa Juuma a baga a pai kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka ale tali la meena a nye nama ale a yaali diila, kama a ta va ni Wenni ale a yaali diila.

ref: Give your God the other articles that have been contributed for use in his temple.
text: Pai ŋanti baai ate ba pai te ni a magsi chaab ale jiam teka Wen yenni po la a te Jerusalem Wenni.

ref: If you need to get anything else for the temple, you may have the money you need from the royal treasury.
text: Jaabuuri meena ale magsi wa bo Wen yenni po ate ni nya ale baga a nye la ni pai naam ligraŋa a nye.

ref: Ezra, you are a priest and an expert in the laws of the God of heaven, and I order all treasurers in Western Province to do their very best to help you.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de mi, Naab Artasaset, a weeni baai meena ale a nya ligra zuk ate ba bo Yufiretis Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala geŋsa la kama ayen Ezra kaabteerɔwa wenŋmazuk Wen Sinsaŋŋa sagrɔwa a dan bek ni jabuui ate wa a yaali la ni te wa,

ref: They must provide whatever the God of heaven demands for his temple, so that he won't be angry with me and with the kings who rule after me.
text: Jaabuuri meena ate wenŋmazuk Wenni a weeni la, basi ate ku abe nye nalimnyiini a magsi chaab ale wenŋmazuk Wen yenni. Ka boa ale a bo naawa ale wa nidoabilisaŋa suŋsuŋŋa?

ref: We want you to know that no priests, Levites, musicians, guards, temple servants, or any other temple workers will have to pay any kind of taxes.
text: Ku magsi kama ayen fi seba ayen fi ka suik a pai lampoo tunika a ji kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale yilendisaŋa ale baai ale a limisi nansuiŋtaŋa la ale baai ale a tom Wen yenni po la ale tomteerɔma ba chaama a tom tuima Wen yenni de po.

ref: Ezra, use the wisdom God has given you and choose officials and leaders to govern the people of Western Province. These leaders should know God's laws and have them taught to anyone who doesn't know them.
text: Fi Ezra, a ta magsi chaab ale fi Wenni yammu, buui ate fi ta la, lueri boteerɔba ate ba a biisi wensie a te nuru baai meena ale bo Yufiretis Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala zuk geŋka la, baai meena ale seba Wen wieŋa la, abe fi sak waai ale kan sebi ŋa la.

ref: Everyone who fails to obey God's Law or the king's law will be punished without pity. They will either be executed or put in prison or forced to leave their country, or have all they own taken away. Ezra Praises God
text: Waai ale ka a zuli fi Wenni wieŋa ale naawa nɔi la, ku a magsi wa tu ka kum waalika yaase ba yiak wa a basi yaase ba tuesi wa ŋantaŋa meena yaase ba yik wa a lik.

ref: Because King Artaxerxes was so kind, Ezra said: Praise the Lord God of our ancestors! He made sure that the king honored the Lord's temple in Jerusalem.
text: Pimpauk a cheŋ Naawen jigi, tama koma Wenni, waai ale pai nyo naawa suinummu po ayen wa ta zula a jam wa yenni ale bo Jerusalem tɛŋka po la suiku de po,

ref: God has told the king, his advisors, and his powerful officials to treat me with kindness. The Lord God has helped me, and I have been able to bring many Jewish leaders back to Jerusalem.
text: ale waai ale basi ate wa ŋmanteka a jam mi jigi naawa ale wa nisɔmma ale naawa nuru baai meena ale ta pagrim la niŋ. Dii nyiŋla Naawen m Wenni nisaŋa a jam bo m zuk kama, m jam nye ka nyiŋbiiri ale tigsi Izirali tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma meena ayen ba cheŋ ale mu.

ref: Artaxerxes was king of Persia when I led the following chiefs of the family groups from Babylonia to Jerusalem:
text: Baai ale jam dɛ ba dɔkdemma niŋ la ale baai yue ale jam ŋmarisi ate ba va mi a nyini Babilon a jam diipo ate Artasaset a chim naab la ale nna:

ref: Gershom of the Phinehas family; Daniel of the Ithamar family; Hattush son of Shecaniah of the David family; Zechariah and
text: Utai ale Zakkur ate ba nyini Bivai buuni po la a jam ka nidoaba pisiyopɔi.

ref: I said to the priests: You belong to the Lord, the God of your ancestors, and these things also belong to him. The silver and gold were willingly given as gifts to the Lord.
text: Mi yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nama ale ŋantaŋa a ta tuilum kama a te Naawen. Kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka ka tiirim a te Naawen ni koma Wenni.

ref: I brought everyone together by the river that flows to the town of Ahava where we camped for three days. Not one Levite could be found among the people and priests.
text: Mi yaa tigsi ba a ta moata buboali kaai ale chali va Ayava benaŋka la jigini, ti jam bo dula a paari ka daa ŋata. Mi ale kpesi a nya nuruma ale kaabteerɔma po la mi an jam nya Livai denɔ ba po.

ref: So I sent for the leaders Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. I also sent for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were very wise counselors.
text: M yaa weeni Ɛlieza ale Ariel ale Sɛmaiya ale Elnatan ale Jarib ale Elnatan ale Natan ale Zakaria ale Mesullam baai ale ka niŋdeerɔba la ale Joiarib ale Elnatan baai zamsika ale zuak la,

ref: Then I sent them to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, and I told them to ask him and his temple workers to send people to serve in God's temple.
text: a yaa tom ba Iddo jigi wa la ale chim Kasifia tɛŋka kpagi. M weeni ba ale ba weeni Iddo ale wa nuruma, baai ale a tom Wen yenni po ate di bo Kasifia po la dii ale magsi ba nye la kama dila ale ku basi ate ba niŋ a bo ale ti Wen yenni jigi.

ref: God was kind to us and caused them to send a skillful man named Sherebiah, who was a Levite from the family of Mahli. Eighteen of his relatives came with him.
text: Ti Wen nisaŋa ale bo ti zuk la, ba yaa ta Serebia, nuru maŋ, wa jam ka Livai a nyini Mayali buuni po. Wa ale wa bisaŋa ale wa suataŋa a jam ka pi ale naaniŋ.

ref: We were also sent Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from the family of Merari along with
text: Yasabia ale Jesaiya ale nyini Merari buuni po la ale wa suataŋa ale wa suataŋa bisaŋa a jam ka nuruba pisiye.

ref: Beside the Ahava River, I asked the people to go without eating and to pray. We humbled ourselves and asked God to bring us and our children safely to Jerusalem with all of our possessions.
text: Ayava benaŋka nɔi, m yaa weeni ayen ti bobi nɔi, dii ale ku basi ate tama a zɛri tidek ti Wenni niŋ abe ti bek wa ate wa nya tama ale ti bisaŋa chelimu zuk ale ŋanti baai ate ti ta la zuk.

ref: So we went without food and asked God himself to protect us, and he answered our prayers. The Gifts for the Temple
text: Dila nyiŋ ti yaa bobi nɔi a bek ti Wenni nya kude ate wa yaa tulisi ti puusaŋa.

ref: I chose twelve of the leading priests—Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their relatives.
