text: Ate mi yaa lueri kaabteerɔba pi ale baye a gum chaab ale Serebia ale Yasabia ale ba suataŋa pi,

ref: Then I weighed the gifts that had been given for God's temple, and I divided them among the twelve priests I had chosen. There were gifts of silver and gold, as well as the articles that the king, his advisors and officials, and the people of Israel had contributed. In all there were:
text: ale ligmɔniŋ taasa pisiye ale a magsi chaab ale boorik dobrim bunaansi la ale kutuk mɔnuŋ ŋantomta baye ale salisi a nala la a ta tuilum ase ligmɔniŋ la.

ref: Be sure to guard them and keep them safe until you reach Jerusalem. Then weigh them inside God's temple in the presence of the chief priests, the Levites, and the heads of the Israelite families.
text: Ni kpesi a nya ba zuk nalimnyiini a ta ga paari diipo ate nama ale pai ba a nyo Naawen yenni ale bo Jerusalem po la, kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale Izirali demma niŋdeerɔma nisima po.>>

ref: The priests and Levites then took charge of the gifts that had been weighed, so they could take them to the temple of our God in Jerusalem. The Return to Jerusalem
text: Ate kaabteerɔma ale Livaima a yaa tuesi kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka ale ŋan baai meena ale magsi ayen ba pai a ta cheŋ ti Wen yenni ale bo Jerusalem la po.

ref: On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River and started for Jerusalem. Our God watched over us, and as we traveled along, he kept our enemies from ambushing us.
text: Chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la ka daa pi ale ŋayewa danni tama a yaa basi Ayava buboalika ayen ti cheŋ Jerusalem. Ti Wenni nisima a jam bo ti zuk kama ate wa a kasi ti a ta a nyini dachaasa nisima po ale baai ale a vari nuruba la jigi suiku po a basi.

ref: After arriving in Jerusalem, we rested for three days.
text: Ti yaa jam paari Jerusalem, dula jigini ti yaa vuusi da ŋata.

ref: Then on the fourth day we went to God's temple, where the silver, the gold, and the other things were weighed and given to the priest Meremoth son of Uriah. With him were Eleazar son of Phinehas and the two Levites, Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
text: Daa ŋanaansiwa danni, ti Wen yenni po, tama yaa pai kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a nyo Yuraya nidoabinni Meremot kaabteerɔwa nisima po. Fineyas nidoabinni Eleaza a jam maa bo dula kama ale wa, Livaima Jesua nidoabinni Jozabad ale Binnui nidoabinni Noadiya mɛ a jam maa boro.

ref: Some of those who had returned took the king's orders to the governors and officials in Western Province. Then the officials did what they could for the people and for the temple of God.
text: Ba jam pai naawa ale weeni diila a sak niŋdeerɔwa waai ale a nya Benni Kunkɔŋ Kinkala zuk la kama, waai ale jam a maari nuruma ale Wen yenni la.

ref: Later the Jewish leaders came to me and said: Many Israelites, including priests and Levites, are living just like the people around them. They are even guilty of some of the horrible sins of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
text: Wieŋa de meena ale jam nye la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, niŋdeerɔma a yaa jam a weeni mi ayen, <<Izirali demma, a gum chaab ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima, an jam poori ba dega a ta nyini tuim kaasima ŋaai ate Keenan demma ale Yit demma ale Perizzi demma ale Jebus demma ale Ammon demma ale Moab demma ale Ejipiti demma ale Amori demma jam a tom la.

ref: Some Israelite men have married foreign women and have let their sons do the same thing. Our own officials and leaders were the first to commit this disgusting sin, and now God's holy people are mixed with foreigners.
text: Ba jam faari tɛŋ sila liema gela kama a te badek ale ba nidoabilisaŋa, ale pai baai ale gaari badek la a gum chaab ale tɛŋ sila nuruma. Niŋdeerɔma ale kpaŋŋa ale jam a dɛ niŋ a sak nye kaasuŋku.

ref: This news made me so angry that I ripped my clothes and tore hair from my head and beard. Then I just sat in shock
text: Ase mi ale ga wom nya kude la, m yaa dari m gattaŋa a cheeri ale dari m zukku zuisaŋa ale m teeŋka a vɔssi alege kali tɛŋ ale daanika.

ref: until the time for the evening sacrifice. Many of our people were greatly concerned and gathered around me, because the God of Israel had warned us to stay away from foreigners. Ezra's Prayer
text: Ate baai nyiŋsa ale a gɔk Izirali Wenni wieŋa nyiŋla a yaa tigsi a gilim mu nuruma de ale kan ta siaka la nyiŋ. Mi jam kala kama ale daanika a ta ga paari diipo ate ba nye junɔinni kaabka la.

ref: At the time of the evening sacrifice, I was still sitting there in sorrow with my clothes all torn. So I got down on my knees, then lifted my arms,
text: Ase ku ale ga paari junɔinni kaabka la, mi yaa yiti zaani ale m gattaŋa tii ale cheeri la, a kpi duna tɛŋ a zak nisa a te Naawen m Wenni

ref: and prayed: I am much too ashamed to face you, Lord God. Our sins and our guilt have swept over us like a flood that reaches up to the heavens.
text: a puusi ayen, <<M Wen yaa, chivie ale ta mu nna yegayega ate mi an baga a zak mi ninaŋa a nya fi m Wenni, dii nyiŋla tama biemu a zuak ka nna yegayega alege ate ti kaasuŋku mɛ a jueli paari wenŋmazuk.

ref: Since the time of our ancestors, all of us have sinned. That's why we, our kings, and our priests have often been defeated by other kings. They have killed some of us and made slaves of others; they have taken our possessions and made us ashamed, just as we are today.
text: A nyini ti kokpieŋsaŋa daaŋa po a ta jam paari jinla, ti biemu a kasim zuak kama. Alege ti biemu nyiŋ, tama ale ti nalimaŋa ale ti kaabteerɔma a yaa jo ti dachaasaŋa ale ba nalimaŋa nisima po ase ku ale ka dii jinla nna.

ref: But for now, Lord God, you have shown great kindness to us. You made us truly happy by letting some of us settle in this sacred place and by helping us in our time of slavery.
text: <<Alege yɔgyɔgla de, ku an bola beni ya, Naawen ti Wenni a ta jiirim ale ti kama ale baai ale tali a vua la ale pai ti a basi jigi maŋ wa yenni po, dila nyiŋ ti Wenni a te ti ka bolim buui ale basi ate tama ninaŋa a nya ale vari ti a ta nyini yɔntidi po a nyini.

ref: We are slaves, but you have never turned your back on us. You love us, and because of you, the kings of Persia have helped us. It's as though you have given us new life! You let us rebuild your temple and live safely in Judah and Jerusalem.
text: Tama ka yɔm, alege tama Wenni an zɛri ti a basi ya. Wa jam sak wa ŋmanteka ale ti kama Persia nalimaŋa niŋ: Wa jam te ti ka nyuvuri paalik ayen tama a ŋman pilim sɛ ti Wen yenni, ale te ti parik ate ka kasi Juda ale Jerusalem meena.

ref: Our God, what can we say now? Even after all this, we have disobeyed the commands
text: <<Alege yɔgyɔgla de, ti Wen yaa, tama a yaali ti weeni ayen ka boa kude ŋaaŋ nyiŋŋa? Tama an zuli buusaŋa,

ref: that were given to us by your servants the prophets. They said the land you are giving us is full of sinful and wicked people, who never stop doing disgusting things.
text: ate fi pai a te ti a ta va fi tomteerɔma ale ka biisiteerɔba la zuk diipo ate fi a weeni ayen, <Tɛŋ kaai ate nama a yaali ni ga bo ka po la ka nuruma a kaasi tɛŋka a basi kama. A ta va ba kaasuŋku nyeka ba meena a yaa jam kaasi.

ref: And we were warned not to let our daughters and sons marry their sons and daughters. Your prophets also told us never to help those foreigners or even let them live in peace. You wanted us to become strong and to enjoy the good things in the land, then someday to leave it to our children forever.
text: Dila nyiŋ nama a kan pai ni liema a yalisi ba bisaŋa yaase ni a faari ba liema a te ni bisaŋa. Ni poom kan nye wari ate ku a sak ayen nama a yaali ni dɛ ka doata ale ba diipo diipo, dila ale ku basi ate ni pagra abe ni dɛ tɛŋka ŋanmaŋsaŋa abe ni tali a te ni bisaŋa ate ba ale kasim a boro taam wuu.>

ref: You punished us because of our terrible sins. But you did not punish us nearly as much as we deserve, and you have brought some of us back home.
text: <<Dii ale nye ti la ka ti biemu ale ti wakaasimaŋa nyiŋ, alege, tama Wenni, fi an poom a namsi ti ase tama biemu ale ka diila, alege a te tama jigi maŋ ase nna la la.

ref: Why should we disobey your commands again by letting our sons and daughters marry these foreigners who do such disgusting things? That would make you angry enough to destroy us all!
text: Tama a ŋman magsi ayen ti ŋman pilim a tom kaasi fi buusaŋa abe ti ga faari baai ale tom a kaasi fi la? Fi sui a kan puuri ale tama ate fi kaasi ti, ate fi kan tali nuruba magadek yaase javuk mɛ la?

ref: Lord God of Israel, you have been more than fair by letting a few of us survive. But once again, our sins have made us ashamed to face you.
text: Naawen yaa, Izirali Wenni, fi ka waai ale ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ. Fi a tali ti a basi kama. Dila nyiŋla tama a bo ka fi niŋ ale ti kaasuŋku, kula nyiŋ ale soa ate tama wanyi mɛ la an baga a zaani fi niŋ la.>>

ref: While Ezra was down on his knees in front of God's temple, praying with tears in his eyes and confessing the sins of the people of Israel, a large number of men, women, and children gathered around him and cried bitterly.
text: Ase Ezra ale jam a puusi ale a weeni kaasuŋku ale a kum alege lo tɛŋ Wen yenni po la, Izirali demma nuru boari nidoaba ale nipooba ale bisa a yaa jam gilim wa. Ba mɛ a jam a kum kama.

ref: Shecaniah son of Jehiel from the family of Elam said: Ezra, we have disobeyed God by marrying these foreign women. But there is still hope for the people of Israel,
text: Ate Jeyiel nidoabinni Sekania, ate wa nyini Iilam buuni po la, a yaa weeni Ezra ayen, <<Tama a jam ka siaka ale ti Wenni ate tama a yaa jaa faari nipok yonta a ta nyini nuru baai ale jam kala moata ti la. Alege kude meena po, Izirali a diem ta yiila kama.

ref: if we follow your advice and the advice of others who truly respect the laws of God. We must promise God that we will divorce our foreign wives and send them away, together with their children.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de, ni basi ate ti nye nɔiyeŋ ti Wenni niŋ ate wa basi ate nipooma de ale ba bisaŋa a cheŋ, a ta va m nyɔnɔwa sinsaŋŋa ale baai ale a chali ti Wenni buusaŋa la nyiŋ. Basi ate ku nye a magsi chaab ale Sinsaŋŋa.

ref: Ezra, it's up to you to do something! We will support whatever you do. So be brave!
text: Yiti zaani. Wanni de a bo ka fi nisima po. Ti ale maari fu, pii nyiŋ a nye di.>>

ref: Ezra stood up and made the chief priests, the Levites, and everyone else in Israel swear that they would follow the advice of Shecaniah.
text: Dila nyiŋ Ezra a yaa zaani a basi ate Izirali kaabteerɔma baai ale dɛ niŋka la ale Livaima ale Izirali demma meena ayen ba pɛ ayen ba ale nye dii ate ba a zɔk ale chaab la. Ate ba yaa jam pɛ.

ref: Then Ezra left God's temple and went to spend the night in the living quarters of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He felt sorry because of what the people had done, and he did not eat or drink a thing.
text: Ate Ezra a yaa ŋmani wa an jo Wen yenni po alege cheŋ ga jo Eliasib nidoabinni Jeyoyanan dɔkku po. Ase wa ale jam dula la, wa an jam dɛ jaaboa yaase wa nyu nyiam mɛ, dii nyiŋla wa jam kasim a kum kama baai ale nyini yɔntini po a jam la ale jam kan ta wensie la nyiŋ.

ref: The officials and leaders sent a message to all who had returned from Babylonia and were now living in Jerusalem and Judah. This message told them to meet in Jerusalem within three days, or else they would lose everything they owned and would no longer be considered part of the people that had returned from Babylonia.
text: Nuru waai a dan zɛri ate ku paari daa ŋata alege ate wa an jam ya wa le jɔk ŋan baai ate wa ta la a ta va kpaŋŋa ale nisɔmma ale zɔk diila, abe ba yiak wa baai ale ŋmani la tigsuŋku po.

ref: Three days later, on the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone from Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem and sat in the temple courtyard. It was a serious meeting, and they sat there, trembling in the rain.
text: Daa ŋatawa po Juda ale Benjamin demma meena a yaa jam tigsi chaab Jerusalem po. A nyini chiik kaai ale a saari neokku la ka daa pisiyewa danni, nuruma meena a yaa jam tigsi gigiluk a kala Wen yenni po, ŋmoruk ale jam a ni ale ba bo dula jigini ba tuka nyiŋ.

ref: Ezra the priest stood up and said: You have broken God's Law by marrying foreign women, and you have made the whole nation guilty!
text: Ate Ezra waai ale ka kaabteerɔ la a yaa yiti zaani ale weeni ba ayen, <<Nama a ka wensie. Nama a faari ka tɛŋ yonsa lieba, a gum Izirali kaasuŋku po.

ref: Now you must confess your sins to the Lord God of your ancestors and obey him. Divorce your foreign wives and don't have anything to do with the rest of the foreigners who live around here.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ni weeni ni kaasuŋku a te Naawen, ni koma Wenni jigi, abe ni a nye wa yaalika. Ni poori nidek a nyini nuru baai ale gilim ni la po a nyini abe ni basi tɛŋ yonsaŋa liema ate ni faari la.>>

ref: Everyone in the crowd shouted: You're right! We will do what you say.
text: Ate tigsuŋku meena a yaa tulisi ate ku jueli ayen, <<Fi ta wensie kama! Tama ale nye ase fi ale weeni diila.

ref: But there are so many of us, and we can't just stay out here in this downpour. A lot of us have sinned by marrying foreign women, and the matter can't be settled in only a day or two.
text: Alege nuruba yegayega ale bo dela ku be ŋman chim ka ŋmoruk nika vari dila nyiŋla tama a kan baga a zaani peelimmoa. Daa dila nyiini, ti kan baga a pai dai yeŋ yaase daa ŋaye nya wanni de zuwa, dii nyiŋla tama biemu a zuak ka nna yegayega.

ref: Why can't our officials stay on in Jerusalem and take care of this for us? Let everyone who has sinned in this way meet here at a certain time with leaders and judges from their own towns. If we take care of this problem, God will surely stop being so terribly angry with us.
text: Basi ate ti kpaŋŋa a tom a te tigsuŋku meena. Basi ate ti tɛŋka po waai meena ale faari tɛŋ yoŋ nipok la a jam ba le dak diipo la ale niŋdeerɔma ale baai ale a bo buusa la wanyi meena a nyini tɛŋ meena a va jam, a ta ga paari diipo ate tama Wenni suipuurumu a ta va wanni de zuk ale basi ti la.>>

ref: Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were the only ones who objected, except for the two Levites, Meshullam and Shabbethai.
text: Ka Asayel nidoabinni Jonatan ale Tikva nidoabinni Jazeya, bala nyiini ale Mesullam ale Livaiwa Sabbetai, ale maari ba ate ba zɛri nya kude.

ref: Everyone else who had returned from exile agreed with the plan. So Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of the families, and he listed their names. They started looking into the matter on the first day of the tenth month,
text: Ate baai ale nyini yɔntini po a jam la a yaa nye dii ale magsi ba nye la. Kaabteerɔwa Ezra yaa lueri nuruba baai ale ka yie nyam la, nuru yeŋ a ta nyini buuri meena po, ale ŋmarisi ba meena yueŋa. Chiisa piwa ka piilimka danni ba yaa kali ayen ba kpesi wanni zuk.

ref: and they did not finish until the first day of the first month of the next year. The Men Who Had Foreign Wives
text: A ta nyini chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la ka piilimka danni ba yaa jam tu chaab ale baai meena ale faari tɛŋ yonsa lieba la a nueri.

ref: Here is a list of the priests who had agreed to divorce their foreign wives and to sacrifice a ram as a sin offering: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah from the family of Joshua son of Jozadak and his brothers;
text: Ba a jam pɛ kama ayen ba yiak ba pooma alege waai meena a te padiak ayen ba nye kaabka ba kaasuŋ ku nyiŋ.

ref: Hanani and Zebadiah from the family of Immer;
text: A nyini Immer ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Yanani ale Zebadia.

ref: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah from the family of Harim;
text: A nyini Yarim ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Maaseiya ale Elaja ale Sɛmaiya ale Jeyiel ale Yuzaya.

ref: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah from the family of Pashhur.
text: A nyini Pasur ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Elioenai ale Maaseiya ale Ismael ale Netanel ale Jozabad ale Elasa.

ref: Those Levites who had foreign wives were: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah , Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
text: Livaima po a jam ka Jozabad ale Simei ale Kelaiya, Kelaiya yuei di choa a jam le Kelita, ale Petayia ale Juda ale Ɛlieza.

ref: Eliashib, the musician, had a foreign wife. These temple guards had foreign wives: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
text: A nyini yilendisaŋa po a jam ka Eliasib. A nyini nansuiŋ limisidɔma po a jam ka Sallum ale Telem ale Uri.

ref: Here is a list of the others from Israel who had foreign wives: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Hashabiah, and Benaiah from the family of Parosh;
text: Izirali demma po a jam ka Paros ŋaaŋbisaŋa. Ŋaaŋbisaŋa de jam ka Aramiya ale Izzia ale Malkija ale Mijamin ale Eleaza ale Malkija ale Benaya.

ref: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah from the family of Elam;
text: A nyini Iilam ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Mattania ale Zakaria ale Jeyiel ale Abdi ale Jeremot ale Elaja.

ref: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza from the family of Zattu;
text: A nyini Zattu ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Elioenai ale Eliasib ale Mattania ale Jeremot ale Zabad ale Aziza.

ref: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai from the family of Bebai;
text: A nyini Bebai ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Jeyoyanan ale Yanania ale Zabbai ale Atlai.

ref: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth from the family of Bani;
text: A nyini Bani ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Mesullam ale Malluk ale Adaiya ale Jasub ale Seal ale Jeremot.

ref: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh from the family of Pahath Moab;
text: A nyini Payat Moab ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Adna ale Chelal ale Benaya ale Maaseiya ale Mattania ale Bezalel ale Binnui ale Manasa.

ref: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei from the family of Hashum;
text: A nyini Yasum ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Mattenai ale Mattatta ale Zabad ale Elifelet ale Jeremai ale Manasa ale Simei.

ref: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah from the family of Nebo.
text: A nyini Nebo ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a jam ka Jeiel ale Mattitia ale Zabad ale Zebina ale Jaddai ale Joel ale Benaya.

ref: These men divorced their foreign wives, then sent them and their children away.
text: Bade meena a jam faari ka tɛŋ yonsa lieba, ate ba gela ale ba pooma a ta bisa.

ref: I am Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and in this book I tell what I have done. During the month of Chislev in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes ruled Persia, I was in his fortress city of Susa,
text: Yakalia nidoabinni Neyemia wieŋa ale nna: Kislev chiika, bena pisiye wa po, diipo ate mi bo Susa tɛŋka po jigi pagrika la,

ref: when my brother Hanani came with some men from Judah. So I asked them about the Jews who had escaped from being captives in Babylonia. I also asked them about the city of Jerusalem.
text: Yanani m suataŋa wanyi ale nuruba ba chaab ale jam nyini Juda a jam ate mi a bek ba Juda dem baai ale tali a vua la ale Jerusalem mɛ wie.

ref: They told me, “Those captives who have come back are having all kinds of troubles. They are terribly disgraced, Jerusalem's walls are broken down, and its gates have been burned.”
text: Ba yaa weeni mu ayen, <<Baai ale nyini yɔntini po a nyini la a bo ka daanika ale chivie po. Jerusalem parika a lo kama ate bolim a dɛ tuataŋa meena.

ref: When I heard this, I sat down on the ground and cried. Then for several days, I mourned; I went without eating to show my sorrow, and I prayed:
text: Mi ale ga wom wieŋa de meena la, mi jam kali ka tɛŋ a kum. Da boari mi kasim jam a kum kama ale a bobi nɔi ale a puusi wenŋmazuk Wenni niŋ.

ref: Lord God of heaven, you are great and fearsome. And you faithfully keep your promises to everyone who loves you and obeys your commands.
text: Ate mi yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen, wenŋmazuk Wen yaa, fi ka Wen kpien, waai ate ba a chali yɔgsum la waai ale ta wa nɔiyeŋka ale wa ŋmanteka ale baai ale a yaali wa ale a wom wa ale wa wieŋa la.

ref: I am your servant, so please have mercy on me and answer the prayer that I make day and night for these people of Israel who serve you. I, my family, and the rest of your people have sinned
text: Basi ate fi tuinni nye a wuli, abe fi ninaŋa a lagri ate fi wom puusa ŋaai ate fi tomteerɔwa yok ale kantueŋ a ta va fi nuruma Izirali demma jigi la. Mi a biisi ka tama Izirali demma biemu ale m kowa yenni biem buui ate tama a nye kaasi fu la.

ref: by choosing to disobey you and the laws and teachings you gave to your servant Moses.
text: Tama nye ka gaasa a ta va fi jigi. Tama an wom fi wieŋa ale ŋmarisika ale buusaŋa ate fi a pai a te fi tomteerɔwa Moosis la.

ref: Please remember the promise you made to Moses. You told him that if we were unfaithful, you would scatter us among foreign nations.
text: <<Teeri fi sinsaŋŋa ate fi a te fi tomteerɔwa Moosis ayen, ni dan kan ta wensie, mi ale kati ni waaŋ tɛŋka meena la.

ref: But you also said that no matter how far away we were, we could turn to you and start obeying your laws. Then you would bring us back to the place where you have chosen to be worshiped.
text: Alege ni dan ŋmani mi jigi ale wom m wieŋa ni nuru baai ale bo yontini po la a dan poom bo niŋniŋa mi ale tigsi ba dula jigini a ta ba a jam mi ale lueri kauk kuui ayen m boro m yuenni nyiŋla.

ref: Our Lord, I am praying for your servants—those you rescued by your great strength and mighty power.
text: <<Ba ka fi tomteerɔba ale fi nuruba, baai ate fi a da tuesi ba ale fi pagrim kpiemu ale fi ni pagrisaŋa la.

ref: Please answer my prayer and the prayer of your other servants who gladly honor your name. When I serve the king his wine today, make him pleased with me and let him do what I ask.
text: M Nyɔnɔ, wom fi tomteerɔwa puusaŋa ale fi tomteerɔma puusaŋa baai ale a zuli fi yuenni la. Te fi tomteerɔwa nyeboka jinla abe fi te wa ŋmanteka nuruwa de niŋ.>> Mi ka waai a daam ale a te Susa naawa daam la.

ref: During the month of Nisan in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king, I served him his wine, as I had done before. But this was the first time I had ever looked depressed.
text: Nisan chiika po ate Artasaset a jam dɛ wa naamu a paari bena pisiye wa la, ba jam ta ka daam a jam ayen m pai a te Naawa. Mi an diem kaasi nina wa niŋ a nya ya.

ref: So the king said, “Why do you look so sad? You're not sick. Something must be bothering you.” Even though I was frightened,
text: Naawa a yaa bek mi ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a kaasi nina alege fi kan yuagi? Nya kude a daa jaaboa alege ka sui kaasuŋ.>> Mi a chali ka yɔgsum,

ref: I answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! I feel sad because the city where my ancestors are buried is in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”
text: alege mi a yaa weeni Naawa ayen, <<Naabaa boro taam wuu! Boa ate mi a kan kaasi nina? Ase m tɛŋka kauk kuui ate ba gu m koma la parisaŋa ale lo ate bolim a dɛ tuataŋa a kaasi la?>>

ref: The king asked, “What do you want me to do?” I prayed to the God who rules from heaven.
text: Naawa a yaa bek mu ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a yaali?>> Ate mi a yaa puusi a te wenŋmazuk Wenni,

ref: Then I told the king, “Sir, if it's all right with you, please send me back to Judah, so that I can rebuild the city where my ancestors are buried.”
text: ale tulisi Naawa ayen, <<Ase ku dan yɔk naawa sui ate fi tomteerɔwa a nya suik a nyini fi jigi, be basi ate mi cheŋ m tɛŋka Juda kauk kuui ate ba gu m koma la, dii ale ku nye ate mi a pilim sɛ parisaŋa la.>>

ref: The queen was sitting beside the king when he asked me, “How long will it take, and when will you be back?” The king agreed to let me go, and I told him when I would return.
text: Ate naawa ale wa powa ale kala wa gauŋ la a bek mu ayen, <<Fi ale paari ka disa po, ka disa po ate fi ale ŋmani?>> Ku jam nye Naawa masim ayen wa basi ate m cheŋ, mi yaa te diipo ate mi ale pilim ŋmani la.

ref: Then I asked, “Your Majesty, would you be willing to give me letters to the governors of the provinces west of the Euphrates River, so that I can travel safely to Judah?
text: Mi yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ase ku dan peenti Naawa sui wa ŋmarisi gbaŋ a te mu ate mi a ta ga te waai ale a nya Yufiretis zuk la, ate ba te mu suik ate m paari Juda.

ref: I will need timber to rebuild the gates of the fortress near the temple and more timber to construct the city wall and to build a place for me to live. And so, I would appreciate a letter to Asaph, who is in charge of the royal forest.” God was good to me, and the king did everything I asked.
text: Abe wa te mu gbaŋ ate m pai a te Asaf, waai ale a nya Naawa tiisaŋa zuk la ate wa te mu daata ate m nye a su tɛŋka jigi pagrika tuataŋa ale moata Wen yenni la ale parisaŋa tuataŋa ale kauk kuui ate mi a cheŋ m boro la?>> Ase m Wenni nisaŋa ale bo m zuk la, Naawa a te mu suik.

ref: The king sent some army officers and cavalry troops along with me, and as I traveled through the Western Provinces, I gave the letters to the governors.
text: Dila mi yaa cheŋ kpaŋŋa ale a nya benni la jigi a pai Naawa gbaŋka a te ba. Naawa a jam tom ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpaga ate ba do wusuma a va mu.

ref: But when Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about what had happened, they became very angry, because they didn't want anyone to help the people of Israel. Nehemiah Inspects the Wall of Jerusalem
text: Ase Yoron denɔwa Sanballat ale Ammon demma niŋdeerɔwa Tobiya ale wom kude la, ku yaa daani ba dii nyiŋla, waai ale jam ayen wa nya Izirali demma nyeboka.

ref: I got up during the night and left my house. I took some men with me, without telling anyone what I thought God wanted me to do for the city. The only animal I took was the donkey I rode on.
text: mi yaa nyini yokku ale nidoaba maga. Mi an weeni waai dii ate m Wenni a pai nyo m suinni po ayen m nye a te Jerusalem la. M jam ka boniŋ ka choa ka kaai ate m jam do la nyiini.

ref: I went through Valley Gate on the west, then south past Dragon Spring, before coming to Garbage Gate. As I rode along, I took a good look at the crumbled walls of the city and the gates that had been torn down and burned.
text: Yɔkku po mi yaa nyini va Viaka Nansuiŋku a ga paari Piuk Vinni ale Tampoi Nansuiŋku a kpesi a nya Jerusalem parisaŋa ale lo la, ate bolim mɛ a dɛ tuataŋa diila.

ref: On the east side of the city, I headed north to Fountain Gate and King's Pool, but then the trail became too narrow for my donkey.
text: M ŋman va Bulik Nansuiŋku ale Naawa Mɔgni alege suik a karo ate m boniŋka a taamu.

ref: So I went down to Kidron Valley and looked at the wall from there. Then before daylight I returned to the city through Valley Gate.
text: Mi yaa va viaka po yokku a kpesi nya parisaŋa, kpeglimka po, mi yaa pilim ŋmani a va ka Viaka Nansuiŋku geŋsa a jo.

ref: None of the city officials knew what I had in mind. And I had not even told any of the Jews—not the priests, the leaders, the officials, or any other Jews who would be helping in the work.
text: Tɛŋka kpaŋŋa a jam zɛ mi ale cheŋ juijui la yaase dii ate mi a nye la. Dii nyiŋla mi an diem weeni Juuma yaase kaabteerɔma yaase kpaŋŋa ale baai ale ba tom tuimaŋa la wari ya.

ref: But when I got back, I said to them, “Jerusalem is truly in a mess! The gates have been torn down and burned, and everything is in ruins. We must rebuild the city wall so that we can again take pride in our city.”
text: Mi yaa weeni ba, <<Ni nya ti ale bo daani kaai po la kama. Jerusalem parisaŋa a lo kama ate bolim a dɛ tuataŋa. Ni jam ate tama a pilim a sɛ Jerusalem parisaŋa, ate tama a kan kasim bo chivie po.>>

ref: Then I told them how kind God had been and what the king had said. Immediately, they replied, “Let's start building now!” So they got everything ready.
text: M weeni ba m Wenni nisaŋa ale bo m zuk diila, ale Naawa ale weeni mu diila. Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Basi ate tama a piilim sɛka,>> ate ba yaa nye nyiŋbiiri ale tuin maŋka de.

ref: When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab heard about our plans, they started insulting us and saying, “Just look at you! Do you plan to rebuild the walls of the city and rebel against the king?”
text: Alege Yoron denɔwa Sanballat ale Ammon demma niŋdeerɔwa Tobiya ale Arab denɔwa Gesem ale ga wom la ba yaa nye ti a la. Ba yaa bek ayen, <<Ka boa ale la ate nama a nye? Nama ŋman pilim a nye ka tukpari ale Naawa?>>

ref: I answered, “We are servants of the God who rules from heaven, and he will make our work succeed. So we will start rebuilding Jerusalem, but you have no right to any of its property, because you have had no part in its history.”
text: Mi yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Wenŋmazuk Wenni ale te ti nyeboka. Tama wa tomteerɔma ale piilim sɛka, alege dan ka nama, ni ka charuk Jerusalem po yaase suik kuui ya yaase ni ta ŋiak suik ku choa.>>

ref: These are the people who helped rebuild the wall and gates of Jerusalem: The high priest Eliashib and the other priests rebuilt Sheep Gate and hung its doors. Then they dedicated Sheep Gate and the section of the wall as far as Hundred Tower and Hananel Tower.
text: Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Eliasib ale wa kaabteerɔ chaama yaa cheŋ ba tom abe ba pilim sɛ Piisa Nansuiŋku. Ba yaa gaari ku a su tuata. Ba jam sɛ parika kama ate ka yalima a paari Kook Yewɔŋku dii ate ba pai nyo Naawen nisa po a yalima a paari Yananel Yewɔŋku la.

ref: The people of Jericho rebuilt the next section of the wall, and Zaccur son of Imri rebuilt the section after that.
text: Jeriko demma a sɛ tom du ate Imri nidoabinni Zakkur mɛ a sɛ tom bala jigini.

ref: The family of Hassenaah built Fish Gate. They put the beams in place and hung the doors, then they added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
text: Yassenaa nidoabilisaŋa ale jam pilim sɛ Juma Nansuiŋku. Ba vi chibsa du ale su tuataŋa a pai kuta a kpi maŋ laarisaŋa.

ref: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, completed the next section of the wall. Meshullam, son of Berechiah and grandson of Meshezabel, rebuilt the next section, and Zadok son of Baana rebuilt the section beside that.
text: Yuraya nidoabinni Meremot, Yakkoz ŋaaŋka ale sɛ kauk kunkula. Berekiya nidoabinni Mesullam ate wa kokpieŋka a chim Mesezabel la mɛ ale jam sɛ tom du, ate Baana nidoabinni Zadok a sɛ tom wa ale sɛ a zaani kauk kuui la.

ref: The next section was to be repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their town leaders refused to do the hard work they were assigned.
text: Kauk kuui ale pai a vi la ka Tekoa demma ale sɛ, alege ba kpaŋŋa jam zɛri tuim ŋaai ate baai ale jam a nya ba zuk la a te ba la kama.

ref: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah restored Ancient Gate. They put the beams in place, hung the doors, and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
text: Jesana Nansuiŋku ka Pasea nidoabinni Joiada ale Besodeiya nidoabinni Mesullam ale jam sɛ, bala ale sɛ a vi ku chibsaŋa du, a su tuata ale a pai kuta a kpi maŋ laarisaŋa.

ref: Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and the men from Gibeon and Mizpah rebuilt the next section of the wall. This section reached as far as the house of the governor of West Euphrates Province.
text: A nyini bala jigini, nuruba ale nyini Gibeon ale Mizpa a tom. Bala jam le Melatia ale nyini Gibeon ale Jadon ale nyini Meronot la. Jiŋŋa de ka kpagi dii ale jam a nya tɛŋ kaai ale moata Benni la ale jam a nya ŋa zuk.

ref: Uzziel son of Harhaiah the goldsmith rebuilt the next section. Hananiah the perfume maker rebuilt the section next after that, and it went as far as Broad Wall.
text: Yaryaiya nidoabinni Uzziel choabiika wanyi ale jam sɛ tom bala jigini. Ate Yanania baai ale a nye kpasaam la wanyi a sɛ tom dula. Bala a jam sɛ ka dila a ta nyini Jerusalem parika a ta ga paari Labisim Parika.

ref: Rephaiah son of Hur ruled half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall.
text: Yur nidoabinni Arefaiya, waai ale a nya Jerusalem tɛŋ kpieŋka kauk la ale jam sɛ kauk kunkula.

ref: The section after that was close to the home of Jedaiah son of Harumaph, and he rebuilt it. Hattush son of Hashabneiah constructed the next section of the wall.
text: A tom dula, Jedaya ate wa kowa a nye Yarumaf la ale jam sɛ a tuk wa yenni, ate Yasabneya nidoabinni Yattus a sɛ tom.

ref: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath Moab rebuilt the section after that, and they also built Oven Tower.
text: Yarim nidoabinni Malkija ale Payat Moab nidoabinni Yassub mɛ ale sɛ gela ale Boroborok Nyeka Yewɔŋku.

ref: Shallum son of Hallohesh ruled the other half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. Shallum's daughters also worked with him.
text: Sallum ate wa kowa a chim Yalloyes waai ale a nya Jerusalem tɛŋka kauk la, wa liema a maari wa ate wa mɛ a sɛ kabta.

ref: Hanun and the people who lived in the town of Zanoah rebuilt Valley Gate. They hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. They also rebuilt the wall for
text: Viaka Nansuiŋku ka Yanun ale baai ale bo Zanoaya la ale sɛ. Ba ŋman sɛ ka kama a su tuata a pai kuta a kpi maŋ laarisaŋa. Ba ŋman sɛ parika kauk ate ka woglimmu a paari anamagib kobsinu a ta ga paari Tampoi Nansuiŋku.

ref: Malchijah son of Rechab ruled the district of Beth-Haccherem, and he rebuilt Garbage Gate. He hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
text: Tampoi Nansuiŋku ka Arekab nidoabinni Malkija waai ale jam a nya Bet Yakkerem tɛŋka la ale sɛ. Wa ŋman sɛ kama ale su tuata a pai kuta a kpi maŋ laarisaŋa.

ref: Shallum son of Colhozeh ruled the district of Mizpah, and he rebuilt Fountain Gate. He put a cover over the gateway, then hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. He also rebuilt the wall at Shelah Pool. This section was next to the king's garden and went as far as the stairs leading down from David's City.
text: Bulik Nansuiŋku ka Kol Yoze nidoabinni Sallum waai ale a nya Mizpa tɛŋka zuk la ale jam sɛ. Wa mɛ a sɛ ku kama a pili ku ale su tuata a pai kuta a kpi maŋ laarisaŋa. Wa ŋman sɛ Sɛla Beli Gilini jigini parika ale moata Naawa Talimu la a ta ga paari tiilaŋa ale nyini Deevid tɛŋka a siŋ la.

ref: Nehemiah son of Azbuk ruled half of the district of Beth-Zur, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. It went as far as the royal cemetery, the artificial pool, and the army barracks. Levites Who Worked on the Wall
text: A nyini wala jigini, ka Azbuk nidoabinni Neyemia waai ale a nya Bet Zur tɛŋka geli la ale sɛ a tuk chaab ale Deevid boosuku ale bo kauk kuui la a ta ga paari mɔgni ale Nuru Pagrisaŋa Yenni.

ref: The Levites who worked on the next sections of the wall were Rehum son of Bani; Hashabiah, who ruled half of the district of Keilah and did this work for his district;
text: A nyini wala jigini, ka Livaima ate Bani nidoabinni Areyum a jam a nya ba zuk la ale sɛ. A nyini wa mɛ jigini, Yasabia waai ale jam a nya Keila tɛŋka la ale sɛ a magsi wa tɛŋka demma.

ref: Binnui son of Henadad, who ruled the other half of the district of Keilah;
text: A nyini wala jigini, dula ba suataŋa ate Yenadad nidoabinni Binnui a jam a nya ba zuk la ale sɛ. Wa ale jam a nya Keila tɛŋka kauk.

ref: Ezer son of Jeshua, who ruled Mizpah, rebuilt the section of the wall that was in front of the armory and reached to the corner of the wall;
text: Jesua nidoabinni Ezer, Mizpa tɛŋka kpagni, mɛ ale jam sɛ tuk chaab ale kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa ale bo kauk kuui la.

ref: Baruch son of Zabbai eagerly rebuilt the section of the wall that went all the way to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest;
text: Zabbai nidoabinni Baruk a jam sɛ a ta nyini kauk kuui ate ba va a jo kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Eliasib nansuiŋku.

ref: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, built up to the far end of Eliashib's house. Priests Who Worked on the Wall
text: A ŋman nyini dula, ka Yuraya nidoabinni Meremot ate Yakkoz a chim wa kokpieŋ la ale sɛ dula a ta nyini Eliasib yenni nansuiŋku a ta ga paari ku kpeglimka.

ref: Here is a list of the priests who worked on the wall: Priests from the region around Jerusalem rebuilt the next section of the wall.
text: A nyini wala jigini, kaabteerɔ baai ale bo tɛŋ sii ale gilim la ale sɛ.

ref: Benjamin and Hasshub rebuilt the wall in front of their own houses. Azariah, who was the son of Maaseiah and the grandson of Ananiah, rebuilt the section in front of his house.
text: A nyini bala jigini, Benjamin ale Yassub ale gomsi ba yeniŋka geŋsa parika a ta zaani bala jigini mɛ, ka Maaseiya nidoabinni Azariya ate Anania a chim wa kokpieŋ la ale gomsi parika ale bo wa yenni gauŋ la.

ref: Binnui son of Henadad rebuilt the section of the wall from Azariah's house to the corner of the wall.
text: Yenadad nidoabinni Binnui ale sɛ kabta a ta nyini Azariya yenni gugottaŋa po.

ref: Palal son of Uzai rebuilt the next section, which began at the corner of the wall and the tower of the upper palace near the court of the guard. Pedaiah son of Parosh rebuilt the next section of the wall.
text: Uzai nidoabinni Palal mɛ a sɛ tuk ka Naawa yewɔŋku ale moata limisidɔma dabiaka la. A nyini wala jigini, Paros nidoabinni Pedaiya

ref: He stopped at a place near the Water Gate on the east and the tower guarding the temple. This was close to a section in the city called Ophel, where the temple workers lived. Other Builders Who Worked on the Wall
text: ale Naawen yenni po tuimtomdisaŋa ale bo Ofel guuku zuk la a sɛ tuk chaab ale Nyiamu Nansuiŋku a tuak kori geŋsa ale yewɔŋku.

ref: Zadok son of Immer rebuilt the wall in front of his house. Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, who looked after the East Gate, rebuilt the section after that.
text: A nyini bala jigini, Immer nidoabinni Zadok a jam sɛ magsi chaab ale ka wa yenni. A nyini wala jigini, Sekania nidoabinni Sɛmaiya ate wa a nya Kori Nansuiŋku la a sɛ.

ref: Hananiah and Hanun rebuilt the next section, which was the second section for them. Meshullam son of Berechiah rebuilt the next section, which happened to be in front of his house.
text: A nyini wala jigini, Selemia nidoabinni Yanania ale Zalaf nidoabinni Yanun ale saari bayuebiwa la ale sɛ dula. A nyini bala jigini, ka Berekiya nidoabinni Mesullam ale sɛ kabi tii ale tuk wa yenni la.

ref: Malchijah, a goldsmith, rebuilt the next section, as far as the house used by the temple workers and merchants. This area was across from Gathering Gate, near the room on top of the wall at the northeast corner.
text: A nyini wala jigini, choabiika wanyi ate ba a wi ayen Malkija la ale sɛ a ta nyini baai ale tom Naawen yenni po la yeeŋa a ta ga paari geruŋdɔma yeeŋa ale tuk kpesi Nyaka Nansuiŋku a ta ga paari dɔk kuui ale bo gugoruku ŋmazuk la.

ref: The goldsmiths and merchants rebuilt the last section of the wall, which went from the corner room all the way to Sheep Gate.
text: A nyini dɔk kuui ale bo gugoruku ŋmazuk la ale Piisa Nansuiŋku suŋsuŋ la choabisaŋa ale geruŋdɔma ale jam sɛ parika.

ref: When Sanballat, the governor of Samaria, heard that we were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, he became angry and started insulting our people.
text: Ase Sanballat ale wom ayen ti ŋman pilim boro a sɛ parika la, wa sui yaa jam puuri. Wa jam nye Juuma a la kama

ref: In front of his friends and the Samaritan army he said, “What is this feeble bunch of Jews trying to do? Are they going to rebuild the wall and offer sacrifices all in one day? Do they think they can make something out of this pile of scorched stones?”
text: wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ale Samaria tugurik tɔŋdɔma niŋ. Wa weeni ba ayen, <<Ka boa ate Juu wobsisaŋa de a nye? Ba ale sɛ ba parika? Ba ale nye kaabka? Ba ale baga a pai dai yeŋ a nueri? Ba ale baga a tigsi tintanaŋa ale duak a yiti guuku nna ate bolimu a dɛ ŋa la?>>

ref: Tobiah from Ammon was standing beside Sanballat and said, “Look at the wall they are building! Why, even a fox could knock over this pile of stones.”
text: Ammon denɔwa Tobiya ale jam za wa gauŋ la mɛ a weeni ayen, <<Ba ale a sɛ jabuui la suemkparuk a dan jueli ka zuk, ku ale lɔnsi ba tintanaŋa parika.>>

ref: But I prayed, “Our God, these people hate us and have wished horrible things for us. Please answer our prayers and make their insults fall on them! Let them be the ones to be dragged away as prisoners of war.
text: Wom ti, ti Wenni ale ba kisi ti kama. Tulim ba leetaŋa a basi badek zuk. Te ba ta badek a cheŋ yɔntidi po.

ref: Don't forgive the mean and evil way they have insulted the builders.”
text: Kan lik ba kaasuŋku yaase fi duisi ba biemu a basi, dii nyiŋla ba lɛ baai ale a sɛ la kama.

ref: The people worked hard, and we built the walls of Jerusalem halfway up again.
text: Ti sɛ parika a paari ka suŋsuŋsa po, nuruma mɛ a jam tom kama ale ba sue meena.

ref: But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people from the city of Ashdod saw the walls going up and the holes being repaired. So they became angry
text: Alege Sanballat ale Tobiya ale Arab demma ale Ammon demma ale Asdod demma ale ga wom ale ba boro a sɛ Jerusalem parika ate paaŋa a lik la, ba sue yaa a kasim jam a puuri.

ref: and decided to stir up trouble, and to fight against the people of Jerusalem.
text: Ba meena a jam tigsi ka chaab ayen ba jam a nye kpaliŋ ale Jerusalem a ta daanika a jam ka po.

ref: But we kept on praying to our God, and we also stationed guards day and night.
text: Alege tama a puusi a te ti Wenni ale basi ate limisidɔ a limisi kantueŋ ale yok ayen ti tu chaab ale ba.

ref: Meanwhile, the people of Judah were singing a sorrowful song: “So much rubble for us to haul! Worn out and weary, will we ever finish this wall?”
text: Dila nyiŋla Juda nuruma a weeni ayen, <<Tuimtomdisaŋa a jiak kama ate guuraŋa a zuak ate tama an ŋman baga a sɛ parika.>>

ref: Our enemies were saying, “Before those Jews know what has happened, we will sneak up and kill them and put an end to their work.”
text: Ti dachaasaŋa a ŋman weeni ayen, <<Alege jigi ate ba seba yaase ba nya ti la, ti ale bo dula ale ba. Ti ale ko ba abe tuini mɛ a kpeglim dula.>>

ref: On at least ten different occasions, the Jews living near our enemies warned us against attacks from every side,
text: Juuma baai ale jam moata ba la a jam weeni ti ku wari naŋtuok nɔi pi ayen kauk kuui meena ate nama a tulim la, ba ale siti ti.>>

ref: and so I sent people to guard the wall at its lowest places and where there were still holes in it. I placed them according to families, and they stood guard with swords and spears and with bows and arrows.
text: Dila nyiŋ mi yaa basi ate nuruma gela a za parika kauk kuui ale gela la jigini ate ba a nya ba, m jam poori ba kama ase ba dɔkdemma ale ka diila ale gebisa ale gbatta ale tima.

ref: Then I looked things over and told the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don't be afraid of your enemies! The Lord is great and fearsome. So think of him and fight for your relatives and children, your wives and homes!”
text: Ase mi ale jam nya wari meena zuk a ga nueri la, m yaa yiti zaani ale weeni kpaŋŋa ale niŋdeerɔma ale nuru mbala meena ayen, <<Ni kan chali ba yɔgsummoa. Ni teeri Nyɔnɔwa waai ale zuak ale nala la, abe ni kpaliŋ a te ni suataŋa ale ni nidoabilisaŋa, ale ni liema ale ni pooma ale ni yeeŋa.>>

ref: Our enemies found out that we knew about their plot against us, but God kept them from doing what they had planned. So we went back to work on the wall.
text: Ase ti dachaasaŋa ale wom ayen tama a seba ba ale a poli diila nɔi po kama la, ate Wen a basi ate ba yɔgsa. Tama meena a ŋman cheŋ parika jigi waai meena a cheŋ wa tuini jigi.

ref: From then on, I let half of the young men work while the other half stood guard. They wore armor and had spears and shields, as well as bows and arrows. The leaders helped the workers
text: A nyini dai dila danni m nuruma gela ale a tom tuimaŋa, alege geli mɛ a gomsi magsi ale gbatta ale ŋanchɔgsinta ale tima ale kuusidi jachɔgsim. Kpaŋŋa meena a yaa jam za Juda demma baai ale jam a sɛ parika la ŋaaŋ,

ref: who were rebuilding the wall. Everyone who hauled building materials kept one hand free to carry a weapon.
text: baai ale jam a tom tuimaŋa la a jaa a ji ale ka ni yeŋsa alege m sila a ta kpaliŋ kɔlima,

ref: Even the workers who were rebuilding the wall strapped on a sword. The worker who was to blow the signal trumpet stayed with me.
text: seerɔ meena a jam su ka gebik wa gauŋ ale a tom. Alege nuru waai ale a peeri damuniŋka la a za ale mi.

ref: I told the people and their officials and leaders, “Our work is so spread out, that we are a long way from one another.
text: Ate mi yaa weeni kpaŋŋa ale niŋdeerɔma ale nuruma meena ayen, <<Tuini a zuak kama ale lagri ate tama a waaŋ bo parika meena a yalima ale chaab.

ref: If you hear the sound of the trumpet, come quickly and gather around me. Our God will help us fight.”
text: Diipo meena ni dan wom ale damuniŋka a peeri, ni jam ti Wenni ale kpaliŋ a te ti.>>

ref: Every day from dawn to dark, half of the workers rebuilt the walls, while the rest stood guard with their spears.
text: Dila ti yaa tom a cheŋ ate nuruma gela a ta gbatta a nyini saluik a ta ga paari diipo ate chiŋmarisaŋa a pusi la.

ref: I asked the men in charge and their workers to stay inside Jerusalem and stand guard at night. So they guarded the city at night and worked during the day.
text: A nyini dipo m ŋman weeni nuruma ayen, <<Basi ate nuru meena ale wa maarɔ a bo Jerusalem tɛŋka po yok ate ba baga a nya ti zuk yok ase limisidɔba la abe tuimtomdisa kantueŋ.>>

ref: I even slept in my work clothes at night; my relatives, the workers, and the guards slept in theirs as well. And we always kept our weapons close by.
text: Mi yaase m suataŋa yaase m nuruma yaase limisidɔma ale bo ale mi la an yeeri ti gattaŋa waai meena a ta wa kpaliŋ kɔlima kama ase wa nin poom a cheŋ nyiam ŋarika.

ref: Some of the men and their wives complained about the Jews in power
text: Yɔgyɔgla de nuruma ale ba pooma a yaa kaari nna tuotuowa a ta chaab ale ba suataŋa Juuma.

ref: and said, “We have large families, and it takes a lot of grain merely to keep us alive.”
text: Ba gela a jam a weeni ayen, <<Tama ale ti nidoabilisaŋa ale ti liema a piisi kama, ku a fɛ ayen ti ta ŋanbie a dɛ ate ti vua.>>

ref: Others said, “During the famine we even had to mortgage our fields, vineyards, and homes to them in order to buy grain.”
text: Ba gela a weeni ayen, <<Tama pai ti laŋsaŋa ale ti kaduksaŋa ale ti yeeŋa a dueni te ayen ti nya ŋanbie kɔmmu wenni.>>

ref: Then others said, “We had to borrow money from those in power to pay the government tax on our fields and vineyards.
text: Ba gela mɛ a diem a weeni ayen, <<Tama a peem ka ligra ayen ti tuni naawa lampoowa a magsi ti laŋsaŋa ale ti kaduksaŋa.

ref: We are Jews just as they are, and our children are as good as theirs. But we still have to sell our children as slaves, and some of our daughters have already been raped. We are completely helpless; our fields and vineyards have even been taken from us.”
text: Ti nyiŋsaŋa ale ba nyiŋsaŋa ka bunyi ti ziimu mɛ a nye ase ka ti suataŋa Juuma la, ti nidoabilisaŋa mɛ a nye ase ba nidoabilisaŋa la alege ti pai ti nidoabilisaŋa ale ti liema a te ase yɔm la. Ti liema gela a poom ŋaam bo ka yɔntidi po alege ti wobsa, dii nyiŋla ti laŋsaŋa ale ti kaduksaŋa ka ti suataŋa ale soa.>>

ref: When I heard their complaints and their charges, I became very angry.
text: Ase mi ale ga wom kaarika dɛ ale ba ale a biisi diila mi sui a yaa puuri.

ref: So I thought it over and said to the leaders and officials, “How can you charge your own people interest?” Then I called a public meeting and accused the leaders
text: Ase mi ale poli ku zuk la mi yaa toariŋ kpaŋŋa. M weeni ba ayen, <<Nama a tuesi ka viila yegayega nidek nuruma jigi.>> Mi yaa wi tukpieŋ ayen m nye ale ba.

ref: by saying, “We have tried to buy back all of our people who were sold into exile. But here you are, selling more of them for us to buy back!” The officials and leaders did not say a word, because they knew this was true.
text: Ate mi a weeni ba ayen, <<Ku dan poom ka dii ya ti da tuesi Juuma ti suataŋa ate ba pai a da te baai ale kan daa Izirali dem la kama. Yɔgyɔgla de nama a pai ni suataŋa a da kama ayen ba pilim a pai ba da a te ti,>> ba yaa jam sina dii nyiŋla ba an jam nya wari a weeni ya.

ref: I continued, “What you have done is wrong! We must honor our God by the way we live, so the Gentiles can't find fault with us.
text: Dila mi yaa tom du ayen, <<Dii ate nama a nye la an nala. Nama a magsi ayen ni a chali Wen ate ti dachaasaŋa baai ale kan daa Juuba la a kan biisi ti a kaasi.

ref: My relatives, my friends, and I are also lending money and grain, but we must no longer demand payment in return.
text: Mi ale m suataŋa ale m nuruma a te nuruma ka ligra ale ŋanbie. Alege ni basi ate ni viilaŋa yegayega wa a kpeglim!

ref: Now give back the fields, vineyards, olive orchards, and houses you have taken and also the interest you have been paid.”
text: Ŋman pilim pai ba kaduksaŋa ale ba tattaŋa a te ba nwuli, kpaam tiisaŋa ale yeeŋa ale viilaŋa yegayega yaalika ale ligraŋa ale ba ŋanbieŋa ale ba dapaalimu ale ba kpaamu ni pai a te ba.>>

ref: The leaders answered, “We will do whatever you say and return their property, without asking to be repaid.” So I made the leaders promise in front of the priests to give back the property.
text: Ba ale tulisi diila ale la, <<Ti ale ŋman pai te ba. Ti kan ŋman a yaali jaaboa a nyini ba jigi ya. Ti le nye ase fi ale weeni ti la.>> Ate mi yaa wi kaabteerɔma ale kpaŋŋa ayen ba nye pɛka a ase ba ale puulim ba nye diila.

ref: Then I emptied my pockets and said, “If you don't keep your promise, that's what God will do to you. He will empty out everything you own, even taking away your houses.” The people answered, “We will keep our promise.” Then they praised the Lord and did as they had promised. Nehemiah Is Generous
text: Mi mɛ a kpaanti ŋan baai ale bo m garukku po la a basi ale weeni ayen, <<Wen mɛ a za wa kpaanti baai ale zɛri an ta wa wieŋa ale wa pumpuulimaŋa la a ta nyini wa yenni po a basi kama. Dila nuru wala ba kpaanti wa a basi. Ate tigsuŋku meena a weeni ayen, <<Ku be nye dila,>> ale a pak Naawen. Ate nuruma a nye ase ba ale puulim diila.

ref: I was governor of Judah from the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king until the thirty-second year. And during these entire twelve years, my relatives and I refused to accept the food that I was allowed.
text: Naab Artasaset ale dɛ wa naamu paari bena pisiyewa po la, ase mi ate wa jam lueri ayen m chim Juda tɛŋka kpagi la, ate ku paari wa bena pisita ale ŋayewa la, bena pi ale ŋaye mi yaase m suataŋa an jam dɛ ŋandiin tii ate kpagni a soa la.

ref: Each governor before me had been a burden to the people by making them pay for his food and wine and by demanding forty silver coins a day. Even their officials had been a burden to the people. But I respected God, and I didn't think it was right to be so hard on them.
text: Alege kpaga ŋaai ale jam a dɛ mi niŋ la a pai ka jibta a ji nuruma ale tuesi ligbie ale paari pisinaansi ale ŋandiinta ale daam. Ba ŋaaŋviirɔma mɛ a jam nye nuruma ka dila. Alege mi ale a zuli Wen la, mi an nye dila.

ref: I spent all my time getting the wall rebuilt and did not buy any property. Everyone working for me did the same thing.
text: Ase ku ale magsi ayen m pai m dek a te tuini a ta vachaab ale parika la, m nuruma meena a jam tigsi kama ayen ba tom, ti an jam da tɛŋŋa.

ref: Each day one ox, six of the best sheep, and lots of chickens were prepared. Then every ten days, a large supply of wine was brought in. I knew what a heavy burden this would have been for the people, and so I did not ask for my food allowance as governor.
text: Daa meena naab ale piisa ŋayuebi ale kpesa ale ba gomsi a magsi mu. Daa pi meena po, daam nna yegayega tɔgatɔga ale ba a te mu. Nya kude meena po, mi an yaali ŋandiin tii ate kpagni a soa la, dii nyiŋla ba ale jam a yaali diila a dobra kama a te nuruma.

ref: I pray that God will bless me for everything I have done for my people.
text: M Wen yaa, teeri mu ale ŋmanteka, mi ale nye dii meena a te nuruma de la nyiŋ.

ref: Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and our other enemies learned that I had completely rebuilt the wall. All I lacked was hanging the doors in the gates.
text: Ase tomtomiŋka ale jam paari Sanballat ale Tobiya ale Arab denɔwa Gesem ale ti dachaasaŋa meena ayen mi a ŋman pilim a sɛ parika ate pari a karo la, a ta ga paari diipo ate mi an diem a su tuataŋa du la,

ref: Then Sanballat and Geshem sent a message, asking me to meet with them in one of the villages in Ono Valley. I knew they were planning to harm me in some way.
text: Sanballat ale Gesem a tom ka tomtomiŋ ka dɛ a te mi ayen m jam ate mi ale ba a tu chaab tɛŋ fiisaŋa kanyi po, Ono tɛŋka ale la. Ba jam a yaali ba ko mu kama.

ref: So I sent messengers to tell them, “My work is too important to stop now and go there. I can't afford to slow down the work just to visit with you.”
text: Mi a yaa tom nuruba ba jigi ale tulisaŋa dɛ: <<M ta ka tuim kpienni dela m kan baga a jam. Mi ale nye ka sɛ a basi tuini abe m siŋ a jam nama jigi yaa?>>

ref: They invited me four times, but each time I refused to go.
text: Ku naŋtuok nɔi bunaansi, ate ba tom ate mi mɛ a tulisi ba dila dekdega a paari bunaansi.

ref: which said: A rumor is going around among the nations that you and the other Jews are rebuilding the wall and planning to rebel, because you want to be their king. And Geshem says it's true!
text: Wa ale ŋmarisi diila ale nna: <<Ba a weeni tɛŋsaŋa meena kama ate Gesem ayen ku ka wensie fi ale Juuma a gomsi kama ayen ni nye kpaliŋ, dila ale soa ate nama a ŋman boro a sɛ parika la. Ase ti ale wom diila fi a yaali fi chim ka Naab,

ref: You even have prophets in Jerusalem, claiming you are now the king of Judah. You know the Persian king will hear about this, so let's get together and talk it over.
text: fi abe poom a lueri ka biisiteerɔba ayen ba mooli fi wie Jerusalem po: Naab a bo Juda kama! Yɔgyɔgla de tomtomiŋka ale paari Naawa. Dila nyiŋ jam ate tama a biisi magsi chaab.>>

ref: I sent a message back to Sanballat, saying, “None of this is true! You are making it all up.”
text: Mi yaa tom a tulisi wa ayen, <<Wari an nye ase fi ale a weeni diila, ka fidek ale a poli dila fi zukku po.>>

ref: Our enemies were trying to frighten us and to keep us from our work. But I asked God to give me strength.
text: Ba meena a yaali ba nyigsi ti kama a poli ayen, <<Ba ale jɔk nyiŋbiiri ale tuimaŋa tomka ate ŋa kan nueri.>> Alege mi a puusi kama ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de basi ate m nyiŋka a pagra.>>

ref: One day I went to visit Shemaiah. He wasn't supposed to leave his house, but he said, “Let's hurry to the holy place of the temple and hide there. We will lock the temple doors, because your enemies are planning to kill you tonight.”
text: Dai yeŋ mi yaa cheŋ Delaiya nidoabinni Sɛmaiya ate wa kokpieŋ a chim Meyetabel yenni waai ate ba jam lik wa basi wa yenni po la. Wa a weeni ayen, <<Basi ate ti tu chaab Wen yenni po abe ti lik tuataŋa, dii nyiŋla nuruba ale cheena ayen ba ko fu, yok ba cheena ayen ba ko fu.>>

ref: I answered, “Why should someone like me have to run and hide in the temple to save my life? I won't go!”
text: Alege m tulisi wa ayen, <<Nuru ase mi choa la a chali nyini? Yaase mi la a jo Wen yenni po a suk? M kan cheŋŋi!

ref: Suddenly I realized that God had not given Shemaiah this message. But Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him to trick me
text: Mi a miŋ kama ayen Wen an tom wa, alege wa a nye dila ka Tobiya ale Sanballat ale da wa.

ref: and to frighten me into doing something wrong, because they wanted to ruin my good name.
text: Ba da wa kama ayen wa nye dila ate mi a nye biem ase mi a nin nye dila, ate ba yaa ale kaasi mi yuei a ta mi a siŋ tɛŋ.

ref: Then I asked God to punish Tobiah and Sanballat for what they had done. I prayed that God would punish the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who, together with her, had tried to frighten me. The Work Is Finished
text: Teeri Tobiya ale Sanballat, Naawen yaa, ba ale nye diila nyiŋ. Teeri nipok biisiteerɔwa Noadiya ale biisiteerɔma meena baai ale a yaali ayen ba nye ate mi nyiŋ a gɔk la.

ref: On the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, the wall was completely rebuilt. It had taken
text: Ba jam sɛ parika a nuerika Elul chiika ka daa pisiye ale ŋanu dai, daa pisinu ale ŋaye ate ba pai a sɛ ka.

ref: When our enemies in the surrounding nations learned that the work was finished, they felt helpless, because they knew that our God had helped us rebuild the wall.

ref: After this, the Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah went among the people, explaining the meaning of what Ezra had read.

ref: The people started crying when God's Law was read to them. Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who had been teaching the people all said, “This is a special day for the Lord your God. So don't be sad and don't cry!”
text: Kpagni Neyemia ale kaabteerɔwa ale gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Ezra ale Livaima baai ale jam a sak nuruma la yaa weeni ba meena ayen, <<Danni de a welema kama a te Naawen ni Wenni. Ni kan kaari yaase ni kum.>> Diila nuruma meena a jam a kum kama ase ba ale jam wom Sinsaŋŋa wieŋa la.

ref: Nehemiah told the people, “Enjoy your good food and wine and share some with those who didn't have anything to bring. Don't be sad! This is a special day for the Lord, and he will make you happy and strong.”
text: Wa weeni ayen, <<Ni cheŋ a ga dɛ nidek ale a yaali ŋandiin tii ale damasik kaai la abe ni tom gela a te baai ale kan ta jaab la. Danni de ka dai weleŋ a te Nyɔnɔwa. Ni kan te ni sue a kaasi ale Naawen mariŋka ka ni pagrim.>>

ref: The Levites encouraged the people by saying, “This is a sacred day, so don't worry or mourn!”
text: Livaima yaa nye ate nuruma meena a goori ale weeni ayen, <<Ni zaan ŋmam ale danni de ka dai weleŋ. Ni kan te ni sue a kaasi.>>

ref: When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them. Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
text: Ate nuruma meena yaa jam cheŋ a ga dɛ ale nyu ale tom ŋandiinta a te ale a dɛ tigini ale mariŋka nna yegayega dii nyiŋla ba yaa miŋ wieŋa ate ba sak ba la kama.

ref: On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law
text: Chiika daa ŋayewa danni, yieŋa nyama meena a gum chaab ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima yaa tigsi gilim gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Ezra ayen ba pai ba popola a basi Sinsaŋŋa wieŋa jigi.

ref: that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year.
text: Ba yaa jam nya ale ku ŋmarisi Sinsaŋŋa po, dii ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis ayen Izirali demma a jam magsi ba bo ka kusuŋta po chiisa siyopɔiwa tigini vaaŋa po abe

ref: They also learned that they were to go into the woods and gather branches of leafy trees such as olives, myrtles, and palms for making these shelters.
text: ba a mooli wieŋa de ate ŋa waaŋ ba tɛŋsaŋa meena ale Jerusalem po, <<Ni cheŋ guuta tɛŋka meena po a ta naŋsa a nyini kpaam tiisa ale gɔi kpaam tiisa ale puuta tiisa ale kpinkpatta tiisa ale yɔgsum tiisa a ti kusuŋta ase ku ale ŋmarisi diila.

ref: So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate.
text: Dila nuruma yaa cheŋ ga ta tiisa naŋsa a jam a ti kusuŋta a te badek badek yieŋa zuk ale ba dabaasaŋa po ale Wen yenni dabaasaŋa po ale Nyiam Nansuiŋku nɔi peelimmu po ate kunyi a bo Ɛfraim Nansuiŋku.

ref: Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
text: Tigsuŋku meena ale nyini yɔntini po a ŋmani la a jam ti ka kusuŋta a bo ti po. A nyini Nun nidoabinni Josua daaŋa po a ta ga paari dai dila danni, Izirali demma an jam dɛ tigini ase nnala la. Ba mariŋka a jam ŋmasi zuak kama.

ref: On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
text: Daa meena a nyini piilimka danni a ga paari kpeglimka, Ezra a jam kariŋ a nyini ka Wen Sinsaŋŋa Gbaŋka po. Ba jam dɛ tigini ka daa ŋayopɔi, daa naanika danni a ta va buusa ale ka diila, ba jam tigsi ka chaab.

ref: On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, the people of Israel went without eating, and they dressed in sackcloth and threw dirt on their heads to show their sorrow.
text: Chiik kala dek daa pisiye ale ŋanaansiwa danni, Izirali demma a jam tigsi ka jigi yeŋ a bobi nɔi a jo boorisa gatta a nye tanta a basi ba zuimaŋa po.

ref: They refused to let foreigners join them, as they met to confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors.
text: Baai ale ka Izirali buuni po la a jam gaari ka badek a ta nyini nichamma po. Ba jam zaani ka ba jiŋŋa a biisi ba biemu ale ba koma gaasaŋa wie.

ref: For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
text: Ba jam zaani ka ba ale bo juijui la a kariŋ a ta nyini Naawen ba Wenni Sinsaŋŋa Gbaŋka po a paari baŋsa buta ale pai baŋsa buta a weeni ba biemu ale a puusi Naawen ba Wenni.

ref: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God.
text: Ŋmazukku jam ka Livaima ale za, Jesua ale Bani ale Kadmiel ale Sebania ale Bunni ale Serebia ale Bani ale Kenani, baai ale jam za du a kaari a wi Naawen ba Wenni la.

ref: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said: “Stand and shout praises to your Lord, the eternal God! Praise his wonderful name, though he is greater than words can express.” The People Pray
text: Ate Livaima Jesua ale Kadmiel ale Bani ale Yasabneya ale Serebia ale Yodia ale Sebania ale Petayia a yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni yiti zaani a pak Naawen ni Wenni waai ale boro taam wuu la! Niauŋ a bo fi zula yuenni po, di abe nya pimpauk a gaam niauŋ ale pimpauk meena.

ref: You alone are the Lord, Creator of the heavens and all the stars, Creator of the earth and those who live on it, Creator of the ocean and all its creatures. You are the source of life, praised by the stars that fill the heavens.
text: Fi nyiini ale Naawen. Fi ale nye wenŋmazukku, poom ka ŋmazuk kuui ale yalima la ale ŋan baai meena ale bo ku po la ale tɛŋzuk de ale jaab meena ale bo ka po la ale nyakpiemu ale jaab meena ale bo bu po la. Fi ale te jaab meena nyuvuri ate ŋan boanni wenŋmazuk a puusi fu.

ref: You are the Lord our God, the one who chose Abram— you brought him from Ur in Babylonia and named him Abraham.
text: <<Naawen yaa, fi waai ale ka Wen la, ale jam lueri Abram a ta wa nyini Ur ale bo Kaldiya po la a nyini a te wa yuei ayen Abrayam.

ref: Because he was faithful, you made an agreement to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites and Hittites, of the Amorites and Perizzites, and of the Jebusites and Girgashites. Now you have kept your promise, just as you always do.
text: Fi jam nya ale wa suinummu a ta ka wensie ale fu, ate fi nye nɔiyeŋ ale wa ayen fi te wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa Keenan ale Yit ale Amori ale Perizzi ale Jebus ale Girgas demma tɛŋsaŋa. Fi ta fi puulimka kama dii nyiŋla fi ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ.

ref: When our ancestors were in Egypt, you saw their suffering; when they were at the Red Sea, you heard their cry for help.
text: <<Fi nya ti kokpieŋsaŋa ninammu Ejipiti po kama, fi wom ba kaarika kama Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku nɔi.

ref: You knew that the King of Egypt and his officials and his nation had mistreated your people. So you worked fearsome miracles against the Egyptians and earned a reputation that still remains.
text: Fi jam tom ka wakinkagla ale wakperikaliisa a siti Faaro ale wa kpaŋŋa ale nuruma meena tɛŋka po, dii nyiŋla fi jam seba kayerinni dii ate Ejipiti demma a jam nye le ba la kama. Fi jam nye ka yuei a te fidek, dii ale boro a paari jinla de la.

ref: You divided the deep sea, and your people walked through on dry land. But you tossed their enemies in, and they sank down like a heavy stone.
text: Fi jam labi nyakpiemu buye a te ba, ate dila a te ba suik ate ba cheŋ tɛŋ kosik zuk a taam, alege fi jam basi ate baai ale a vi ba la a wari liuŋku po ase tintain ale lo nyakpiem po diila.

ref: Each day you led your people with a thick cloud, and at night you showed the way with a flaming fire.
text: Danni po fi jam dɛ ba niŋ ale ka chiŋmari la ale de ba niŋ yokku po ase bolim la ate bu a nya suiku ate ba jam a yaali ba va la.

ref: At Sinai you came down from heaven, and you gave your people good laws and teachings that are fair and honest.
text: <<Fi jam siŋ jam Sinai guuku zuk kama a biisi nyini wenŋmazuk ale ba. Fi jam te ba ka buusa ŋaai ale ka chekki, ale sinsak ŋaai ale ka wensie, ale ŋmarisika, ale wie ŋaai ale ka wamaŋsa la.

ref: You commanded them to respect your holy Sabbath, and you instructed your servant Moses to teach them your laws.
text: Fi jam basi ate ba seba fi tuilum Vuusum Danni kama a te ba wieŋa ale buusa ale sinsaŋŋa a nyini fi tomteerɔwa Moosis jigi.

ref: When they were hungry, you sent bread from heaven, and when they were thirsty, you let water flow from a rock. Then you commanded them to capture the land that you had solemnly promised. *
text: Ba kɔmmu po fi jam te ba ŋandiinta a nyini wenŋmazuk, nyanyuilaŋa ale jam ta ba la fi te ba nyiam a nyini piuŋ po, fi weeni ba ayen ba jo a tuesi tɛŋka ale jam zak nisa ŋmai a pɛ ayen fi te ba la.

ref: Our stubborn ancestors refused to obey— they forgot about the miracles you had worked for them, and they were determined to return to Egypt and become slaves again.
text: <<Alege bala, tama kokpieŋsaŋa a jam ta ka kayerinni ale tukpari ale an siak a te fi wieŋa.

ref: not even when they made an idol shaped like a calf and insulted you by claiming, “This is the god who rescued us from Egypt.”
text: poom ka diipo ate ba jam mɛ naabiik a te badek ale weeni ayen, <Ni wenni ale nna, dii ale ta ni a nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la,> yaase ba le jam potim seba ale nye kisuk wanni la.

ref: Because of your great mercy, you never abandoned them in the desert. And you always guided them with a cloud by day and a fire at night.
text: <<Fi jiirim kpiemu nyiŋ fi an banti ba a basi gɔnni po. Danni po chiŋmanni an basi ba ganika suiku po yaase bolimu a basi nyaksika suik kuui po ate ba jam a yaali ba va la.

ref: Your gentle Spirit instructed them, and you gave them manna to eat and water to drink.
text: Fi jam basi ate fi Chiik maŋka a sak ba. Fi an jam peri fi ŋandiintaŋa ba noaŋa po ale te ba nyiam ba nyanyuilaŋa nyiŋ.

ref: You took good care of them, and for forty years they never lacked a thing. Their clothes didn't wear out, and their feet were never swollen.
text: Bena pisinaansi fi jam ta ba ka dila gɔnni po, ba an jam a silim jaaboa, ba gattaŋa an jam cheeri ya yaase ba naŋsaŋa a zak ji ya.

ref: You let them conquer kings and take their land, including King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan.
text: <<Fi jam te ba naata ale tɛŋ kpieŋsa, a pai niŋniŋ tɛŋsa a te ba. Ba jam tuesi naab Siyon tɛŋka Yesbon ale naab Og tɛŋka Basan kama.

ref: You brought them into the land that you had promised their ancestors, and you blessed their nation with people that outnumbered the stars in the sky.
text: Fi nye ate ba nidoabilisaŋa a piisi kama ase wenzuk chiŋmarisaŋa la, ale ta ba jam jo tɛŋka po ate fi weeni ba koma ayen ba jo a tuesi a ta.

ref: They captured strong cities and rich farmland; they took furnished houses, as well as cisterns, vineyards, olive orchards, and numerous fruit trees. They ate till they were satisfied, and they celebrated your abundant blessings.
text: Ba jam nak yik tɛŋ pagrisa ale tɛŋ kaai ale ta poosuk. Ba tuesi yie ŋaai ate ŋan maŋsa tɔgatɔga a sueri ŋa la ale vila ŋaai ale poom tu ale kaduksa ale kpaam tiisa ale yɔna tiisa ale piisi. Ba dɛ chak ate ba nyiŋsa a nala. Ba jam a dɛ ka masim fi nye maŋka ale zuak la po.

ref: In spite of this, they rebelled and disobeyed your laws. They killed your prophets, who warned them to turn back to you, and they cursed your name.
text: <<Alege ba jam ta ka tukpari ale zɛri fi, ba jam pai fi sinsaŋŋa a basi ka ba ŋaaŋsa. Ba jam ko fi biisiteerɔma baai ale jam a sak ba ayen ba tulim ba a te fi la kama, ba jam nye ka kisuk wari.

ref: So you handed them over to their enemies, who treated them terribly. But in their sufferings, they begged you to help. From heaven you listened to their prayers and because of your great mercy, you sent leaders to rescue them.
text: Dila fi yaa pai ba a nyo ba dachaasaŋa nisima po baai ale jam namsi ba. Alege ba ale jam namsi ba la ba yaa kaari a te fi. A nyini wenŋmazuk fi wom ba, fi jiirim kpiemu nyiŋ fi jam te ba varibasidɔba, baai ale jam vari ba ba dachaasaŋa nisa po a basi.

ref: But when they were at peace, they would turn against you, and you would hand them over to their enemies. Then they would beg for help, and because you are merciful, you rescued them over and over again.
text: <<Alege ba ale jam nya vuusum la ba ŋman jam nye ka biem fi nina po. Fi yaa banti ba a te ba dachaasaŋa ate ba jam a nya ba zuk. Ba ŋman jam kaari kama a te fi a wom nyini wenŋmazuk, fi jiirim kpiemu nyiŋ ate fi ŋman vari ba a basi.

ref: For years, you were patient, and your Spirit warned them with messages spoken by your prophets. Still they refused to listen, and you handed them over to their enemies.
text: Bena nna yega ate fi kasim jam a ŋmagli ale ba. Fi pai fi Chiika a ta va fi biisiteerɔma zuk a kaam ba. Dila meena ba an jam diem wom ya dila fi yaa pai ba a te nuru baai ale kali moata ba la.

ref: But you are merciful and kind, and so you never forgot them or let them be destroyed.
text: Alege fi jiirim kpiemu nyiŋ fi an jam basi ate ba kpeglim ya yaase fi banti ba, diila fi ka ŋmanteka ale jiirim Wen.

ref: Our God, you are powerful, fearsome, and faithful, always true to your word. So please keep in mind the terrible sufferings of our people, kings, leaders, priests, and prophets, from the time Assyria ruled until this very day.
text: <<Yɔgyɔgla de, ti Wen yaa, Wen kpien dii ale zuak ate ba a chali fu la, waai ale va wa nɔiyeŋka ale wa ŋmanteka la, kan basi ate wa pagraŋa de meena a nya suik fi nina po. Wapagra ŋaai ale jam tama ale ti nalimaŋa ale ti niŋdeerɔma ale ti kaabteerɔma ale ti biisiteerɔma ale ti koma ale fi nuruma meena zuk a nyini Assiria nalimaŋa daaŋa po a jam paari jinla de la.

ref: Our kings and leaders, our priests and ancestors have never obeyed your commands or heeded your warnings.
text: Ti nalimaŋa ale ti nisɔmma ale ti kaabteerɔma ale ti koma an jam va fi sinsaŋŋa, ba niŋ jam ka fi wieŋa yaase kaamka ate fi a te ba la po.

ref: You blessed them with a kingdom and with an abundance of rich, fertile land, but they refused to worship you or turn from their evil.
text: Poom daa ba ale jam bo ba naamu po a dɛ fi wamaŋsa masimu tɛŋka ale lak nna jalɔ ale poak ate fi a te ba la, ba an jam tom a te fi yaase ba basi ba biem suitaŋa.

ref: Its plentiful harvest is taken by kings you placed over us because of our sins. Our suffering is unbearable, because they do as they wish to us and our livestock. The People Make an Agreement
text: Tama biem nyiŋ, ŋan cheenta yega a cheŋ ka nalimaŋa ate fi a te ba nya ti zuk la jigi. Ba jam a nya ka ti nyiŋsaŋa ale niiŋa ase ba ale a yaali diila. Tama a bo ka wapagrisa po nna yega.

ref: And so, a firm agreement was made that had the official approval of the leaders, the Levites, and priests.
text: Kude meena ate ti nya la nyiŋ, tama a nye ka nɔiyeŋ kaai ale a bobi ti la, a ŋmarisi ka a dueni ale ti niŋdeerɔma ale ti Livaima ale ti kaabteerɔma a yaa ŋmarisi ba yueŋa.>>
