text: Bade meena yaa gum ba suataŋa ale ba kpaŋŋa po, a ka kikaasa a pɛ ayen ba Wen Sinsaŋŋa ate ba wom a ta va Wen tomteerɔwa Moosis jigi la ayen ba kpesi a va Naawen ti Nyɔnɔwa wieŋa ale buusaŋa ale ŋmarisika.

ref: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
text: Ase tɛŋ sii ale moata la nuruma a dan ta ŋanta yaase ŋandiinta jam ayen ba da Vuusumu Danni yaase tuilum dai yoŋ ti kan da a nyini ba jigi ya. Bena ŋayopɔi po meena ti kan kpa abe ti baŋ nuruba ale ta ti pama la wie.

ref: Once a year we will each donate a small amount of silver to the temple of our God.
text: <<Ti ŋman piilim a nye ti le wom wie ŋaai ayen ti pai ligbie ŋata a magsi ti Wen yenni tuini la.

ref: This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
text: Kude a magsika jazaanimu zuk boroboroku ale magsi daa meena ŋandiinta tiiritaŋa ale juka tiiritaŋa ale Vuusum Daaŋa tiiritaŋa ale Chiik Paalik tiŋŋa ale tik ŋaai ate ba lueri la ale tuilum tiiritaŋa ale biem tiiritaŋa a nye biem duisi basika a te Izirali demma ale tuini meena ti Wen yenni po.

ref: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
text: <<Tama baai kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale nuruma a nak ka gbaŋ ayen ti miŋ diipo ate waai meena dɔkdem ale ta jam ti Wen yenni diipo ale magsi benni po ayen ti cheesi daata a magsi juka Naawen ti Wenni kuŋkuŋku zuk, ase ku le ŋmarisi Sinsaŋŋa po la.

ref: Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
text: <<Ti jam ŋman siak ayen ti le ta ŋandiin tii ale dɛ niŋ a bɛ la ale tiib meena yɔna a jam Naawen yenni bein meena po.

ref: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
text: <<Ase ku le ŋmarisi dii Sinsaŋŋa po la, ti le ta ti nidoabilisaŋa ate ti a dɛ niŋ a biak la ale ti niiŋa ale dɛ niŋ a biak ŋaai la ale ti duŋ buulimu ale dɛ niŋ a biak sii la ale ti piisaŋa ale dɛ niŋ a biak ŋaai la a jam ti Wen yenni po, a te kaabteerɔma ale a tom dula la.

ref: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
text: <<Ti le ta jam Wen yenni ŋanta duenika jigini a te kaabteerɔwa ti le dɛ niŋ a ta ti zommu ale ti ŋanbie tiiritaŋa ale ti tiisaŋa meena yɔnaŋa ale ti dapaalimu ale kpaamu. Abe ti labi ti kpanni ŋantaŋa pi a pai bunyi a te Livaima dii nyiŋla ka Livaima ale a tuesi tɛŋ sii meena ate ti boro a tom la.

ref: A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom,
text: Kaabteerɔ waai ale nyini Aaron buuni po la ale magsi wa va Livaima ase ba nin ba tuesi piika, ka Livaima abe le ba ta piika a jam ti Wen yenni po, ŋanta dueni ka dɔkku po.

ref: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.
text: Izirali demma a maa gum Livaima du ale ta ba ŋandiinta cheesuŋku ale ba dapaalimu ale kpaamu a jam ŋanta duenika diinaŋa po juijui ate Wen yenni ŋantaŋa a doa la ale juijui ate kaabteerɔ baai a tom la ale nansuiŋ limisidɔma ale yilendisaŋa a boro la. Ti kan banti ti Wen yenni a basi.>>

ref: The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de nuruma niŋdeerɔma yaa kali Jerusalem po ate nuru mbala a nak gbaŋ a yeeri nuru yeŋ a ta nyini nuruba pi po ayen wa maa bo tuilum tɛŋka Jerusalem po abe neokku ale tali la a bo badek tɛŋsaŋa po.

ref: Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
text: Nuruma a yaa pak nidoama meena ale siak ayen ba bo Jerusalem po la.

ref: Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families. The Judah Tribe
text: Baai ale jam a dɛ tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa niŋ a kala Jerusalem po la ale nna. Izirali demma gela ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale baai ale a tom Wen yenni po la ale Solomon tomteerɔma ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam bo ka Juda tɛŋsaŋa po waai meena a bo wadek jigi tɛŋsaŋa po,

ref: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command. Priests
text: Zikri nidoabinni Joel a jam chim ka ba kpagi ate Yassenuya nidoabinni Juda a jaa a nya ka tɛŋka labi kinkala zuk.

ref: Four priests settled in Jerusalem. The first was Jedaiah; he was the son of Joiarib and the uncle of Jachin.
text: Baai ale chim kaabteerɔma ŋaaŋbisa a jam kali la ale nna: Jedaya ale Joiarib nidoabinni ale Jakin,

ref: The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest.
text: ale Seraiya waai kowa a jam le Yilkia ate wa mɛ ko a nye Mesullam ate wa mɛ ko a nye Zadok ate wa mɛ ko a nye Meraiot ate wa mɛ ko a nye Wen yenni nyaarɔwa Ayitub

ref: Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
text: ale Livaima kpaga ŋaye Sabbetai ale Jozabad baai ale a nya Wen yenni tuimaŋa zuk peelim

ref: Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant. Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
text: ale Mattania waai kowa a jam le Mika ate wa mɛ ko a nye Zabdi ate wa mɛ ko a nye Asaf waai ale a dɛ nuruma niŋ ate ba a nye Naawen jiam ale puusa la ale Bakbukia waai ale pai a vi wa ŋaaŋviirɔma la ale Abda waai kowa ale nye Sammua ate wa mɛ ko a nye Galal ate wa mɛ ko a nye Jedutun.

ref: The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah.
text: Izirali dem mbala ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima, a jam bo ka Juda tɛŋsaŋa meena, waai meena a bo wa ŋiak tɛŋzuk.

ref: But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
text: Baai ale jam bo Wen yenni po a tom la a jam bo ka Ofel guuku zuk ate Ziya ale Gispa a nya ba zuk.

ref: Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services,
text: Jerusalem tɛŋka po Livaima kpagni a jam le Uzzi waai kowa a jam le Bani ate wa mɛ ko a nye Yasabia ate wa mɛ ko a nye Mattania ate wa mɛ ko a nye Mika. Uzzi wa dɛ a jam ka Asaf ŋaaŋbisaŋa po baai ale jam chim yilendisa ale jam a nya Wen yenni tuimaŋa zuk.

ref: though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
text: Yilendisaŋa a jam bo ka Naawa nisa po, wa ale jam a weeni ba dii ale magsi ba nye la.

ref: The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe. The People in the Other Towns and Villages
text: Mesezabel nidoabinni Petayia waai ale ka Juda nidoabinni Zera ŋaaŋbisaŋa wanyi la ale jam chim kpagi a nya wa ŋaai meena ale a nye ale nuruma la.

ref: Some of the people of Judah lived in the following towns near their farms: Kiriath-Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel,
text: Dan ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale si laŋsaŋa, Juda nuruma gela ale jam bo Kiriat Arba ale ka gilagila tɛŋsaŋa, ale bo Dibon ale ka gilagilawa, ale Jekabzeel ale ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa,

ref: Enrimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
text: En Arimmon ale Zoraya ale Jarmut

ref: Zanoah, Adullam, Lachish, and Azekah. In fact, they settled the towns from Beersheba in the south to Hinnom Valley in the north.
text: ale Zanoaya ale Adullam ale ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale Lachis ale ka laŋsaŋa ale Azeka ale ka gilagila tɛŋsaŋa. Ba jam bo ka Beerseba tɛŋka a ta ga paari Yinnom Viaka.

ref: The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages,
text: Benjamin ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale nyini Geba la a jam bo ka Mikmas ale Aija ale Betel gilagila tɛŋsaŋa

ref: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
text: ale Anatot ale Nob ale Anania

ref: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
text: ale Yazor ale Arama ale Gittaim

ref: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
text: ale Yadid ale Zeboim ale Neballat

ref: Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley.
text: ale Lod ale Ono ale Yɔgdɔma Viaka.

ref: Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
text: Juda Livaima beŋsaŋa gela a jam bo ka Benjamin.

ref: Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
text: Kaabteerɔma ale Livaima baai ale jam va Sealtiel nidoabinni Zerubabel ale Jesua a ŋmani la ale nna: Seraiya ale Jeremaya ale Ezra

ref: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
text: ale Amariya ale Malluk ale Yattus

ref: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
text: ale Sekania ale Areyum ale Meremot

ref: Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
text: ale Iddo ale Ginneton ale Abaija

ref: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
text: ale Mijamin ale Moadia ale Bilga

ref: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
text: ale Sɛmaiya ale Joiarib ale Jedaya

ref: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
text: ale Sallu ale Amok ale Yilkia ale Jedaya. Ba de ale jam chim kaabteerɔma ale ba ŋaaŋviirɔma niŋdeerɔba Jesua daaŋa po.

ref: The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise,
text: Livaima ale nna: Jesua ale Binnui ale Kadmiel ale Serebia ale Juda ale Mattania waai ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ale jam a dɛ jiam teka yiilaŋa niŋ.

ref: while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses. Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
text: Bakbukia ale Unni ale baai ale a vi ba ŋaaŋ la a zaani a tuk ba tama tuka po.

ref: Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada.
text: Jesua ale jam biak Joiakim ate Joiakim a jam biak Eliasib ate Eliasib a jam biak Joiada

ref: Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua. Leaders of the Priestly Clans
text: ate Joiada a jam biak Jonatan ate Jonatan mɛ a jam biak Jaddua.

ref: When Joiakim was high priest, the following priests were leaders of their clans: Meraiah of the Seraiah clan, Hananiah of Jeremiah,
text: Joiakim daaŋa po ate baai a jam dɛ kaabteerɔma dɔkdemma niŋ la ale nna: Seraiya dɔkdemma po jam ka Meraia. Jeremaya dɔkdemma po jam ka Yanania.

ref: Meshullam of Ezra, Jehohanan of Amariah,
text: Ezra dɔkdemma po jam ka Mesullam. Amariya dɔkdemma po jam ka Jeyoyanan.

ref: Jonathan of Malluchi, Joseph of Shebaniah,
text: Malluk dɔkdemma po jam ka Jonatan. Sebania dɔkdemma po jam ka Josefi.

ref: Adna of Harim, Helkai of Meraioth,
text: Yarim dɔkdemma po jam ka Adna. Meraiot dɔkdemma po jam ka Yelkai.

ref: Zechariah of Iddo, Meshullam of Ginnethon,
text: Iddo dɔkdemma po jam ka Zakaria. Ginneton dɔkdemma po jam ka Mesullam.

ref: Shammua of Bilgah, Jehonathan of Shemaiah,
text: Bilga dɔkdemma po jam ka Sammua. Sɛmaiya dɔkdemma po jam ka Jeyonatan.

ref: Mattenai of Joiarib, Uzzi of Jedaiah,
text: Joiarib dɔkdemma po jam ka Mattenai. Jedaya dɔkdemma po jam ka Uzzi.

ref: Kallai of Sallai, Eber of Amok,
text: Sallu dɔkdemma po jam ka Kallai. Amok dɔkdemma po jam ka Eber.

ref: Hashabiah of Hilkiah, and Nethanel of Jedaiah. The Priestly and Levite Families
text: Yilkia dɔkdemma po jam ka Yasabia. Jedaya dɔkdemma po jam ka Netanel.

ref: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
text: Eliasib ale Joiada ale Joyanan ale Jaddua ale kaabteerɔma daaŋa po, Livaima dɔkdemma yie nyama a jam ŋmarisi kama Persia naawa Darius daaŋa po.

ref: However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
text: Yieŋa nyama niŋdeerɔma ale jam bo Livaima ŋaaŋbisaŋa po la a ga paari Eliasib nidoabinni Joyanan daaŋa po la a jam ŋmarisi doa wie gbaŋka po kama.

ref: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
text: Livaima niŋdeerɔma jam le Yasabia ale Serebia ale Kadmiel nidoabinni Jesua ale ba ŋaaŋviirɔma, baai ale jam za a tuk ba ayen ba, te pimpauk ale jiam, kauk kunyi ale jam a tulisi m kula ase Deevid Naawen nuruwa ale jam biisi diila.

ref: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
text: Mattania ale Bakbukia ale Obadia ale Mesullam ale Talmon ale Akkub jam le nansuiŋ limisidɔ baai ale jam a limisi ŋanta duenika diinaŋa ale bo nansuiŋtaŋa.

ref: All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest. Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
text: Ba jam tom ka Jesua nidoabinni Joiakim ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Jozadak la daaŋa po ale kpagni Neyemia ale kaabteerɔwa ale ŋmarisidoawa Ezra daaŋa po kama.

ref: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
text: Ba le jam pai Jerusalem parika a nyo Wen nisa po la, ba jam wi Livaima kama a nyini juijui ate ba boro la a ta jam Jerusalem po ayen ba dɛ masim ale yiila ale jiam teka ale sinyaara ale kpanta ale bagansa.

ref: The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth.
text: ale Bet Gilgal ale Geba ale Azmavet diila yilendisaŋa a jam sɛ ka tɛŋ kpaŋsa a te badek a gilim Jerusalem.

ref: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
text: Ase kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale jam gomsi badek nna cheri ase ba ale magsi ba nye diila, ba jam maa nye ate nuruma a nye ka cheri ale nansuiŋtaŋa ale parika.

ref: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
text: Mi jam basi ate Juda niŋdeerɔma a jueli ka parika zuk. Mi jam lueri ka yilendɔ boari buye ayen ba te jiam. Yilendisaŋa bunyi ale jam bo parika zuk juga geŋsa a tuk Tamponni Nansuiŋku

ref: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them.
text: Yosaya ale Juda niŋdeerɔma geli ale jam va ba a gum chaab ale

ref: Then came the priests Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
text: Azariya ale Ezra ale Mesullam ale

ref: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
text: Juda ale Benjamin ale Sɛmaiya ale Jeremaya ale

ref: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
text: ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma Sɛmaiya ale Azarel ale Milalai ale Gilalai ale Maai ale Netanel ale Juda ale Yanani ale ŋannaginta tii ate Wen nuruwa Deevid a jam magsi sak ba la. Ŋmarisidoawa Ezra ale jam de ba niŋ.

ref: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
text: Bulik Nansuiŋku ba jam tom du kama a va Deevid Tɛŋka tiilaŋa a jueli parika jigini a gaam Deevid yenni taam cheŋ Nyiamu Nansuiŋku kori geŋsa.

ref: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
text: Yilendisa buyewa po a jam tuk kauk yoŋ. Mi jam va ba kama a jueli parika zuk a gum chaab ale nuruma geli, a ga gaam Boroborok Sɛka Yewɔŋku la a taam paari Parik Labsuku

ref: Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard,
text: a va Ɛfraim Nansuiŋku ŋmazuk ale Jesana Nansuiŋku ale Juma Nansuiŋku ale Yananel Yewɔŋku ale Kook Yewɔŋku a ta ga paari Piisa Nansuiŋku. Limisidɔma Nansuiŋku ate ba yaa ga zaani.

ref: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
text: Yilendisa buyewa ale jam lenni a te jiamu la yaa zaani ba jiŋŋa Wen yenni po, dila a te mi mɛ a jam nye a gum chaab ale kpaŋŋa geli ale

ref: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
text: kaabteerɔma de Eliakim ale Maaseiya ale Miniamin ale Mikaiya ale Elioenai ale Zakaria ale Yanania ale ba damunsa, a maa gum ba po jam ka

ref: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
text: Maaseiya ale Sɛmaiya ale Eleaza ale Uzzi ale Jeyoyanan ale Malkija ale Iilam ale Ezer. Yilendisaŋa ka Jezrayia ale jam a nya ba zuk.

ref: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
text: Dai dila danni ba jam nye ka kaab kpieŋ, a dɛ masim dii nyiŋla Wen a te ba ka suipeentik nna yegayega. Nipooma ale bimbaansaŋa mɛ a jam dɛ ka masim. Masimu dɛka nuemka Jerusalem po a jam cheŋ ka nna niŋniŋŋa.

ref: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
text: Dila powa ba jam lueri ka nidoaba ayen ba a nya ŋanta duenika diina zuk ate ba cheesika ŋantaŋa ale ŋandiin tii ale dɛ niŋ a bɛ la ale ba piika a duak du la. A nyini tattaŋa ale gilim ba tɛŋsaŋa la po, ba a magsi ba ta jam ŋanta duenika diinaŋa po ka Sinsaŋŋa ale weeni ayen ba te kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale a tom la. Diila Juda sui a jam peenti ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima tuimaŋa kama.

ref: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
text: Ba jam a tom ba Wenni tuimaŋa kama ale a tom cheri nyeka tuimaŋa ase yilendisaŋa ale nansuiŋ limisidɔma ale jam a nye dii a ta va Deevid ale wa nidoabinni Solomon ale jam weeni diila.

ref: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
text: Dipowa, Deevid ale Asaf daaŋa po, niŋdeerɔba ale jam boro a nya yilendisaŋa ale Wen pimpauk ale jiam teka zuk.

ref: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
text: Dila Zerubabel ale Neyemia daaŋa po, Izirali demma meena a jam a cheesi ba danni po cheesuŋku kama a te yilendisaŋa ale nansuiŋ limisidɔma. Ba jam pai cheesuŋku kauk mɛ kama a magsi Livaima ate Livaima mɛ a pai dii ale magsi ku cheŋ Aaron ŋaaŋbisaŋa jigi la a te ba.

ref: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
text: Dai dila danni ba jam kariŋ Moosis gbaŋka kama ate ku jueli ate nuruma a wom, dula jigini ba jam nya kama ale ku ŋmarisi ayen Ammon denɔ yaase Moab denɔ an magsi wa bo Wen tigsuŋku po,

ref: This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing.
text: dii nyiŋla ba an jam te Izirali demma ŋandiinta ale nyiamoa alege daa Balaam ayen wa ka te ba. Ti Wen yaa tulim kikaasaŋa ate si chim niauŋ.

ref: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
text: Ase nuruma ale jam wom sinsaŋŋa de la, ba yaa yeeri nuru baai meena ale ka nicham la Izirali buuni po a basi.

ref: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
text: Alege ate kude nye la, kaabteerɔwa Eliasib ale jam a nya ŋanta duenika jigini zuk Wen yenni po. Ka Tobiya ale jam chim wa ŋaaŋviirɔ,

ref: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
text: Eliasib jam te wa ka dɔk kpioŋ, kuui ate ba jam pai ŋandiinta tiirita ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a dueni ku po ale Wen yenni ŋanta ba jam maa pa ka ŋanbieŋa ate ba lab pi a pai bunyi a te Wen la ale dapaalimu ale kpaamu piika ate ba jam magsi sak Livaima ale yilendisaŋa ale nansuiŋ limisidɔma la ale cheesuŋku ale magsi kaabteerɔma la.

ref: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
text: Alege kude meena ale jam a nye la, mi jam ka Jerusalem po, mi jam ŋmani cheŋ ka Babilon naawa Artasaset jigi diipo ate wade wa naamu a paari bena pisita ale ŋayewa la. Daa maga ale taam la mi jam bek wa ate wa te mu suik

ref: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
text: ate m ŋman jam Jerusalem po. Dila mi jam miŋ biem buui ate Eliasib a nye a pai dɔk te Tobiya Wen yenni dabiaka po la.

ref: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
text: Mi sui a jam puuri ka nna yegayega ate mi kɔlim Tobiya yenni meena kɔlimaŋa dɔkku po a yuk basi peelim.

ref: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
text: Mi yaa te suik ayen ba nye ate diinaŋa a welema, dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ mi yaa ŋman pai Wen yenni ŋantaŋa a zaani du ale ŋandiinta tiiritaŋa ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la.

ref: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
text: Mi jam miŋ kama mɛ ayen ŋandiin tii ale magsi Livaima la an jo ba nisa ate Livaima meena ale yilendisaŋa ale magsi ba tom tuini la yaa ŋman cheŋ badek kaduksaŋa po.

ref: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
text: Dila mi yaa toariŋ kpaŋŋa a bek ba ayen, <<Ka boa ate ni banti Wen yenni a basi?>> Mi yaa wi ba jigi yeŋ ate ba cheŋ ba le magsi ba bo juijui la.

ref: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
text: Juda demma meena yaa ta ba ŋan bieŋa piika ale dapaalimu piika ale kpaamu piika a jam ŋanta duenika jigini diinaŋa po.

ref: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
text: Mi basi ate ka kaabteerɔwa Selemia ale gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Zadok ale Livai denɔ wa yuei jam le Pedaiya ate bala a nya ŋandiinta duenika diinaŋa ale basi ate Yanan ate wa ko a jam nye Zakkur ate wa kokpieŋ mɛ a jam nye Mattania la ale chim ba ŋaaŋviirɔ. Mi nye dila ka ba wensieŋa nyiŋ. Ba ale jam a chari ŋanta a te ba suataŋa.

ref: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
text: Teeri mu kude nyiŋ m Wen yaa, abe fi kan duisi dii ate mi a nye ale wensie a te m Wen yenni ale di tuimaŋa la a basi.

ref: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
text: Da ŋala po mi jam nya Juda nidoaba ale ba bo daam ŋmiaka jigini a tom Vuusum Danni ale ta ŋandiinta jam bobi a ji bonsa a gum chaab ale daam ale yɔna ale kinkama ale ŋan yonta buuri meena. Ba jam ta bade meena a cheen ka Jerusalem Vuusum Danni. Dila nyiŋ mi yaa kaam ayen ba kan pai ŋandiinta a da dai dila danni.

ref: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
text: Nuruba ale nyini Taaya tɛŋka a jam bo Jerusalem po la a jam ta ka juma ale geruŋ ŋanta buuri meena bo Jerusalem po a da Vuusumu Danni a te Juda nuruma.

ref: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
text: Mi yaa toariŋ Juda kpaŋŋa ale weeni ba ayen, <<Ka boan jaab gaasa ale la ate ni nye a valiŋ Vuusum Danni?

ref: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
text: Ni kokpieŋsaŋa an jam nye daa wieŋa de dek ate ti Wenni a ta kaasuŋku jam tama ale tɛŋka de zuwa? Yɔgyɔgla de nama a nye ate ka suipuurum yega a jam Izirali zuk a ta va nama ale a valiŋ Vuusum Danni la.>>

ref: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
text: Ase junɔi yisuŋta ale jam tulim bo Jerusalem nansuiŋtaŋa ale ge ate Vuusum Danni a jam la, mi jam weeni kama ayen ba lik tuataŋa abe ba kan lak ti ate Vuusum Danni a ga taam. Mi jam basi ate ka mi dek nidoama gela a za nansuiŋtaŋa ate dila ale basi ate waai kan ji ŋanta a ta jam Vuusum Danni.

ref: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
text: Bunyi yaase buye daarɔma ale geruŋdɔma ale ta jaab meena la a nyiem jam goa ka Jerusalem peelim yokku.

ref: But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath.
text: Alege mi jam kaam ba kama ayen ka boa ate nama a goa parika kiri yokku? Ni dan ŋman nye dila m le yik ni.>> A nyini dai dila danni ba an ŋman jam vuusum danni.

ref: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
text: Mi yaa weeni Livaima ayen ba gomsi badek a nye cheri a ga limisi nansuiŋtaŋa a gaari Vuusum Danni. Be teeri mu kude mɛ nyiŋ m Wen yaa, a sak jiirim ale mu a ta va fi ŋmanteka.

ref: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
text: Da ŋala po mi jam nya ale Juda nidoaba a faari Asdod ale Ammon ale Moab tɛŋsaŋa lieba.

ref: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
text: Ba bisaŋa geli ale jam a biisi Asdod tɛŋka biika yaase nuru mbala biisaŋa ale zɛ ba ale ba nye dii a biisi Juda biika la.

ref: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
text: Mi yaa jam toariŋ ale ka kikaasa a te ba. Mi jam nak nidoama gela kama ale dari ba zuisaŋa a vɔssi. Mi jam basi kama ate ba nye pɛka Wen yuenni nyiŋ ayen, <<Ni kan pai ni liema a yalisi ba nidoabilisaŋa yaase ni faari ba liema a te ni nidoabilisaŋa yaase ni dega.

ref: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
text: Tama a kan wom yɔgyɔgla de ayen nama mɛ a nye gaasaŋa de meena a ka wensie ale ti Wenni a faari tɛŋ yonsa lieba!>>

ref: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
text: Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Eliasib nidoabinni Joiada nidoabilisaŋa wanyi jam ka Yoron denɔwa Sanballat chicham biik. Mi jam yiak wa kama m jigi.

ref: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
text: Teeri ba wari m Wen yaa, dii nyiŋla ba taŋ kaabteerɔ tuini ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima nɔiyeŋka kama.

ref: Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites.
text: Dila mi yaa nye ate kaabteerɔma ale Livaima a nye cheri a nyini dii meena ale ka wachaŋ la po ale te ba tuima waai meena ale wa le magsi wa nye dii.

ref: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
text: Mi jam maa basi ate Izirali demma cheesi ka daata mɛ daaŋa gela a magsi yɔn ŋaai ale dɛ niŋ a bɛ la. Teeri mu ale ŋmanteka m Wen yaa.

ref: King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled
text: Da ŋala po, Naab Ayasuerus a jam kali wa naam zukpaglika zuk ka Susa tɛŋka jigi pagrika a nya tɛŋka zuk.

ref: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
text: Wa yaa le nya tɛŋka zuk a ga paari bena ŋata la, wa yaa nye tigi a te wa nisɔmma ale wa tomteerɔma: Persia ale Miidi kpaŋŋa ale nisɔmma meena yaa jam maa boro.

ref: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
text: Ase daaŋa de ale jam taam la, naawa yaa nye tigi a te nuru baai meena ale jam bo Susa tɛŋka po la, ŋankpagsa ale bimbaansa. Daa ŋayopɔi ate wa pai a nye dila wa yenni po.

ref: The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
text: Dula ba jam pai ka garuk pala peeta ale garuk pala sobta a yaa pai mi mɔnta ale mi peeta a tuiri a yik kpana baŋsa nyiŋ a yik ŋan baai ate ba pai tana sɛ chɔgsi yenni a zaani la. Wa zukpaglik woŋsaŋa jam ka kpana ale ligmɔniŋ ate ba pai nye. Wa dɔkku tɛŋka mɛ a jam ŋmirisi kama ale mɔnuŋ ale peeluk ale sobluk ale tintain ŋaai ale a nyaksi la.

ref: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
text: Ate ba yaa jam te ba daam ale ligmɔniŋ beerisa tɔgatɔga. Naawa yenni daamu mɛ a jam zuak kama a magsi chaab ale naawa pagrimu ale ka diila.

ref: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ naawa powa Vasti yaa jam nye tigi a te nipooma, naamu yenni po, dii ate Naab Ayasuerus soa la.

ref: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
text: A nyini daa ŋayopɔiwa danni, naawa yaa jam nyu daam a buk. Wa yaa weeni Meyuman ale Bizta ale Yarbona ale Bigta ale Abagta ale Zetar ale Karkas, tomteerɔba bayopɔi baai ale jam a tom a te Naab Ayasuerus la,

ref: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
text: ayen ba ta naawa powa Vasti a jam wa niŋ ale wa naam zutɔkka ate wa sak nuruma ale kpaŋŋa ale wa nala kama a magsi ayen ba a nya.

ref: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
text: Alege naawa powa Vasti yaa jam zɛri an cheŋ naawa jigi ya, ase wa ale jam tom wa tomteerɔma ayen ba wi wa la, dila nyiŋ naawa sui yaa jam puuri ate wa suinni kasim jam a dɛ.

ref: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ baai ale jam a vi wa la ale Karsena ale Setar ale Admata ale Tarsis ale Meres ale Marsena ale Memukan. Persia ale Miidi kpaga ŋayopɔiwa de ale baai ale jam baga a paari wa ale wie ale ŋman chim baai ale maa de naamu niŋ la.

ref: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
text: Ka boa ate ti le nye m powa Vasti a magsi chaab ale tɛŋka kisukku? Wa an jam nye Naab Ayasuerus ale weeni wa nisɔmma ayen ba weeni wa ate wa nye diila.

ref: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
text: Ate Memukan yaa tulisi naawa ale wa nisɔmma niŋ ayen, naawa powa Vasti an nye kaasi daa naawa nyiini alege ka nisɔmma ale nuruma meena ale bo Naab Ayasuerus tɛŋka po la.

ref: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
text: Nye kaai ate nipowa a nye la, a sak nipooma kama ayen ba a zɛri ba chorɔba noa ba nimbie po, ayen Naab Ayasuerus ale jam wi wa powa Vasti ayen wa jam la wa an jam cheŋ ya.

ref: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
text: Danni de dek Persia ale Miidi tɛŋsaŋa kpaŋŋa pooma baai ale wom dii ate nipowa a nye la, ba mɛ ale zɛri, waai meena zula teka kama ale suipuurum.

ref: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
text: Ase Naawa a daa yaali, wa te wari a nyini wadek jigi dii ate naawa dek an baga a tagri la ate ba ŋmarisi di a gum Persia ale Miidi tɛŋsaŋa wieŋa po ate ku weeni ayen Vasti naawa powa a kan ŋman bo Naab Ayasuerus jigi ya, abe naawa a pai wa boka jigini a te waai ale zunchoŋ wa la.

ref: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
text: Ate naawa wieŋa, ŋaai ate wa a yaali ayen wa nye la, yaa dan nyini wa tɛŋka po meena, nipooma meena a yaa le te ba chorɔma zula, baai ale pagi ale baai ale kan pagi la.

ref: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
text: Ate wa yaa tom gbaŋsa a te nalima meena, tɛŋ meena ale tɛŋ buuri a ta va dii ate wa ŋmarisi la, a te biik meena ale nuru meena ayen wa nya wa yeri zuk, abe ba basi ate nuru meena a seba a ta nyini ba tɛŋka biika po.

ref: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
text: Wieŋa de ŋaaŋnyiŋ ase Naab Ayasuerus suinni ale jam yɔk la, wa yaa teeri Vasti wie ale dii ate wa nye la, ale wa dii ale jam nye a ta va wa ale nye diila.

ref: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
text: Naawa tomteerɔma baai ale a tom a te wa la, weeni ayen naawa basi ate ba gisi nipok paalisa baai ale kan seba nidoa la a ta jam te naawa.

ref: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
text: Abe ni basi ate naawa a lueri nuruba tɛŋ fi sii meena ale bo wa tɛŋka po la ate ba yaa tigsi paalik sii meena ale kan seba nidoa la a ta jam jigi yeŋ Susa tɛŋka jigi pagrika, nipooma yenni po. Ni basi ate ba bo Yegai naawa yɔmawa waai ale a nya nipooma zuk la jigi abe ni tebi ba nalim tebika.

ref: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
text: Abe ni basi ate nipok bi dii ate naawa mariŋ la a chim naawa pok, daa Vasti ŋmana. Ate naawa yaa mariŋ wanni de, a yaa nye di.

ref: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de Susa naab yenni po, Juuma wanyi ale jam boro wa yuei jam ale Mordekai wa jam ka Jair nidoabili, Jair kowa mɛ ale Simei, Simei kowa ale Kis a nyini Benjamin buuni po.

ref: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
text: Wa jam ka baai ate ba jam nak yik a ta nyini Jerusalem tɛŋka ate ka bo Juda po la wanyi, ale ka naawa ate ba a wi ayen Jekonaya la. Ka Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar ale jam yik ba a ta cheŋ.

ref: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
text: Ate Mordekai yaa jam a nya Yadassa zuk, Ester ale la, wa jam ka wa kowa suok lie. Dii nyiŋla wa jam ka koa yaa si ma. Nipowa yaa jam magsi ale nala, wa kowa ale wa mawa a jam kpi kama ate Mordekai yaa pai wa ase wadek lie la.

ref: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
text: Ase ku yaa ale jam paari diipo ate nipok paalisa yega a tigsi wa wanni nyiŋla, ba yaa tigsi lieba nna yegayega a basi jigi yeŋ Susa naab yenni po ate Yegai a nya ba zuk, Ester mɛ jam maa bo naawa yenni po kama Yegai jigi.

ref: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
text: Ester a yaa yɔk wa sui, ate wa yaa nye nwuli a te wa ŋan baai ale ba nye ate wa nala la, ale ŋandiin yonta, ale pai wa a basi jigi maŋ naab yenni po. A lueri nipooba bayopɔi a ta nyini naawa yenni po ayen ba ga tom a te wa.

ref: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
text: Ester an jam basi ate ba seba wa nuruma yaase wa buuni, dii nyiŋla, Mordekai ale weeni wa ayen wa kan basi ate ba seba.

ref: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
text: Ase ku yaa ale paari diipo ayen liema meena a cheŋ Naab Ayasuerus jigi la, ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ku magsi ayen wa pai ka chiisa pi ale siye a gomsi nala a magsi chaab ale nipok ale magsi ayen wa nye diila. Da ŋala po ale ba pai a gomsi badek a nueri, chiisa siyuebi, ba pai sa kpaam, abe chiisa siyuebi ba sa kpa masik, ale wie ŋaai ale ŋa nye ate lie meena a nala la.

ref: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
text: Lie meena ale magsi ayen wa cheŋ naawa jigi diila ale nna, jabuui meena ate wa a yaali la, ba te wa ate wa ta nyini nipooma yenni po a cheŋ naawa yenni.

ref: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
text: Junɔi wa yaa cheŋ naawa jigi abe wa ŋman pilim ŋman saluik a cheŋ nipooma yie woŋku ale saari ŋayewa la, naawa tomteerɔwa Saasgaz jigi waai ale a nya nɔŋtaŋa zuk la. Wa kan ŋman cheŋ naawa jigi ya, ka wa sui nin peenti ate wa wi yuei ayen wa jam.

ref: Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
text: Ba yaa jam ta Ester a ga te Naab Ayasuerus wa yenni po, chiisa piika po, Tebet chiika ale la, wa ale dɛ wa naamu a ta a ga paari bena ŋayopɔi wa po la.

ref: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
text: Ate naawa a yaali Ester a gaam nipok mbala meena, wa yaa jam nya niaka ale nyemagsika a gaam mbala meena, ate wa pai naam zutɔkka a vuk wa, a nye wa wa pok. Ku an ŋman magsi ayen ku chim Vasti.

ref: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
text: Ate naawa yaa nye tigi kpienni Ester nyiŋ a te nabisaŋa ale wa tomteerɔma meena, wa jam mooli ka vuusum dai a te tɛŋsaŋa meena ale chari tiirita tɛŋka meena a magsi chaab ale naawa pagrimu ale jam ka diila.

ref: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
text: Baai ale kan seba nidoaba la a yaa jam tigsi jigi yeŋ, ku naŋtuok nɔi buyewa po Mordekai mɛ a jam kala ka naawa tuoku nɔi.

ref: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
text: Ester an diem jam weeni ba wa nuruma yaase wa buuni ale ka baai la, ase Mordekai ale weeni wa ayen wa kan weeni la, wa diem kasim jam va ka Mordekai nɔnni ase wa ale jam weeni wa ayen wa nye diila.

ref: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
text: Da ŋala po, ase Mordekai ale jam kala naawa tuoku nɔi la, naawa limisidɔba baye Bigtana ale Teres, baai ale jam a limisi tuoku la sue yaa puuri ate ba a zɔk ayen ba ko Naab Ayasuerus.

ref: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
text: Ate Mordekai wom ate wa mɛ yaa weeni sak Ester naawa powa, ate Ester mɛ a yaa weeni sak naawa ayen ka Mordekai ale weeni sak wa.

ref: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
text: Ase ba ale jam kpesi nya ayen wanni ka wensie la, ba yaa bobi limisidɔma de bayewa a yik tiib nyiŋ ate ba kpi. Ate ba yaa ŋmarisi wie ŋaai ale nye la a nyo ba ŋiak gbaŋsaŋa po naawa nimbie.

ref: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
text: Wieŋa de ŋaaŋnyiŋ Naab Ayasuerus yaa gum kpaŋta du a te Yammedata nidoabinni Yaman ate wa nyini Agag buuni po la ate wa jueli kali kalik kaai jigi ale gaam naabisa meena kalisa jiga la.

ref: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
text: Ate naawa tomteerɔma meena, baai ale jam bo naawa tuoku nɔi la koori a zuli Yaman. Ka naawa ale te ba suik ayen ba nye dila. Alege Mordekai an jam koori ya alege ka wa zuli wa.

ref: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
