ref: The words of a bad woman are like a deep pit; if you make the Lord angry, you will fall right in.
text: Nipok kaasuŋ nɔi ka baruk pagrik. Baai ate Naawen sui a puuri ale ba la a lɔ ka ku po.

ref: All children are foolish, but firm correction will make them change.
text: Biik suinum po a sueri ale ka betta, alege ka turi darika ale a yeeri dila a nyini wa po.

ref: Cheat the poor to make profit or give gifts to the rich— either way you lose. Thirty Wise Sayings
text: Nuru waai ale a namsi ŋanjaksa ayen wa jigsi yaase wa a te jigsirɔba tiirita la ale kpeglim ale jaŋsa.

ref: Here are some sayings of people with wisdom, so listen carefully as I teach.
text: Lak fi tunni a wom yam nyam wieŋa, abe fi basi ate fi suinummu a ta m miŋka.

ref: You will be glad that you know these sayings and can recite them.
text: Diila ŋa nala ayen fi ta wieŋa de fi suinum po, abe ŋa kasim bo fi nɔi po.

ref: I am teaching them today, so that you may trust the Lord.
text: Jinla danni de po, mi nye kama ate fi a miŋ yam nyama kiri, ate fi ale ta mariŋka ale Naawen.

ref: You can trust them completely to give you the right words for those in charge of you. –
text: Suiku de po, fi ale miŋ wensie ate baai ale tom fu la, fi ale ga weeni ba fi ale nya diila.

ref: Don't take advantage of the poor or cheat them in court.
text: Kan vari jajak ŋanta ayen wa jaŋ nyiŋŋa, yaase fi vari waai ale a silim a jam bo buusa dɔkku po la.

ref: The Lord is their defender, and what you do to them, he will do to you. –
text: Naawen ale tuesi ba biisaŋa a biisi a te ba, abe wa kɔni waai ale kɔni ba la.

ref: Don't make friends with anyone who has a bad temper.
text: Kan dɛ doata ale suipuurum nuruba yaase fi a nye wari ale nuru baai sue ale kpabi a puuri la,

ref: You might turn out like them and get caught in a trap. –
text: dan kan daa di fi ale zamsi wa suitaŋa a ta fidek a ga jo baruk po.

ref: If you don't have the money, you might lose your bed. –
text: Fi kan jam baga a tuni, ba ale poom a pai fi gaduokku a nyini fi jigi.

ref: Don't move a boundary marker set up by your ancestors. –
text: Ni kan yeeri banaŋa ate ni kokpieŋsaŋa a dueni la ate ni baga a zu ni vaanchaama nitalimu.

ref: If you do your job well, you will work for a ruler and never be a slave.
text: Fi nya nuru baai ale seba tuima la a nya ya? Ba ale tom a te ka nalima alege daa nuruba kinla.

ref: Don't accept an invitation to eat a selfish person's food, no matter how good it is.
text: Kan dɛ ŋandiinta ale butuem nyama. Kan te fi kɔrisa a bo ale ba ŋantaŋa.

ref: When you are invited to eat with a king, use your best manners.
text: Fi dan boro a dɛ ale niŋdeerɔ, kpesi nya ba ale pai jabuui a zaani fi niŋ la.

ref: Don't go and stuff yourself! That would be just the same as cutting your throat.
text: Fi dan ka waai ale baga a dɛ, pai gebik a tiik fi tutɔk.

ref: Don't be greedy for all of that fancy food! It may not be so tasty. –
text: Kan basi ate fi popola meena a bo ŋandiin maŋsaŋa jigi ya, da dii dai wa a yaali wa nye fu nya kama.

ref: People like that take note of how much you eat. They say, “Take all you want!” But they don't mean it.
text: Butuem nyam nyiem kasim a poli ka ŋandiinta nyaka wari ale toa diila ate ku a daani ba. Ba le weeni fu ayen a dɛ abe fi a nyu alege ba suinummu po ku daa dila.

ref: Your money flies away before you know it, just like an eagle suddenly taking off. –
text: Jigsika a muriŋ a bɛ ka nna yilibi ase nina kamsika la. Diila ku ale tom ka kinkaŋŋa a yaa yiti jueli wen ase jiiruk la.

ref: Each bite will come back up, and all your kind words will be wasted. –
text: Fi ale chiiri mag kaai ate fi dɛ la a basi ate fi jiirim wieŋa a kan ta kiri.

ref: Don't talk to fools— they will make fun of you. –
text: Kan biisi wari a basi beruk tue po dii nyiŋla, wa ale yuk fi yam wieŋa a basi.

ref: Don't move a boundary marker or take the land that belongs to orphans.
text: Kan zu niwoba yaase kpiŋsa tɛŋsa a yeeri ba kokpieŋsaŋa banaŋa.

ref: Listen to me, my children! Be wise and have enough sense to follow the right path.
text: Wom de m biiga, ate fi ta yam, ate fi suinummu a va suiku.

ref: Don't be a heavy drinker or stuff yourself with food.
text: Kan bo ale danyuirisa yaase baai ale baga a dɛ la,

ref: It will make you feel drowsy, and you will end up poor with only rags to wear. –
text: diila ba bo ka ba suik po a cheŋ jaŋsa po, ate goom yegayega ale chim garuchaasa a lik ba.

ref: Pay attention to your father, and don't neglect your mother when she grows old.
text: A wom fi kowa waai ale te fu nyuvuri la, abe fi kan zɛri fi mawa ase wa nin jam kpaŋmu.

ref: Invest in truth and wisdom, discipline and good sense, and don't part with them.
text: Tuesi wensie abe fi kan pai ŋa a da. Be ŋman tuesi yam ale waalika ale wensie buusa boka.

ref: Make your parents proud, especially your mother. –
text: Te fi kowa ale fi mawa masim. Te waai ale biak fu la sui a peenti.

ref: My son, pay close attention, and gladly follow my example.
text: M biiga te mu fi suinummu, abe fi basi ate fi ninaŋa a kpesi nya m suitaŋa.

ref: they are waiting to attack you like a gang of robbers with victim after victim. –
text: Wa suk kama ale a limisi ase zue la, a yaali ayen wa nye ate nidoaba yegayega a kan chim wensie nuruba.

ref: Who is always in trouble? Who argues and fights? Who has cuts and bruises? Whose eyes are red?
text: Ka wana ale ta nyiŋdomma? Ka wana ale ta suipuurummoa? Ka wana ale kasim a fɔbili? Ka wana ale ta mula alege zɛ ku kiri ya? Ka wana nimbie ale muni ya?

ref: Everyone who stays up late, having just one more drink.
text: Ka baai ale a kali daam zuk a beni la. Baai ale a lam da paalisa a nya la.

ref: Don't even look at that colorful stuff bubbling up in the glass! It goes down so easily,
text: Kaa nya daamoa, a nya bu ale muni dii ya, bu ale a tɔŋ chiima beerika po dii ya, bu ale nyu a siŋ dii ya.

ref: You will see weird things, and your mind will play tricks on you.
text: Fi ale nya ŋanchaŋsa ate fi ale weeni yesiŋsa wie.

ref: You will feel tossed about like someone trying to sleep on a ship in a storm.
text: Fi ale nye ase waai ale doa nyakpiemu suŋsuŋ, ate fi kpari maŋ diok woŋ ate ba pai ti zaani ŋaaruŋ zuk diila.

ref: You will be bruised all over, without even remembering how it all happened. And you will lie awake asking, “When will morning come, so I can drink some more?”
text: Ate fi ale weeni ayen, <<Ba nak mu kama, alege ku an jo m nyiŋŋa. Mi a poom zɛ diipo ate ba nak mi la. Mi ale yiti ka dimpo ate m ŋman gisi daam bu choa?>>

ref: Don't let evil people worry you or make you jealous.
text: Kan te wabanyeerisa wie a daani fu. Kaa dɛ nyuri ale gaasa nyama.

ref: Don't be jealous of crooks or want to be their friends.
text: Kan dɛ nyuri ale nuru baata yaase fi poom yaali ayen fi bo ale ba.

ref: All they think about and talk about is violence and cruelty. –
text: Diila ba a zɔk ka wɔkwɔk ba suiniimaŋa po, ate ba wieŋa a siti kpaliŋ.

ref: They will soon be gone like the flame of a lamp that burns out. –
text: Diila nuru baata a ka chum. Gaasa nyama bolimu ale kpi.

ref: Use wisdom and understanding to establish your home;
text: Yam ate ba pai a sɛ yeri ale a ta pagrim a nyini yam maŋ po.

ref: let good sense fill the rooms with priceless treasures. –
text: A nyini yam wie miŋka ate bu diinaŋa a sueri le jigsika ale ŋan baai ale ta dobrim.

ref: My children, you must respect the Lord and the king, and you must not make friends with anyone who rebels against either of them.
text: M biiga, a chali Naawen ale Naawa. Kan pai fidek a gum tukpari nyam po,

ref: Battles are won by listening to advice and making a lot of plans. –
text: Dila nyiŋ kan cheŋ kpaliŋ alege ate ba an sak fu dii ate fi ale nye la. Nakdeka a nyini ka sagrɔba jigi.

ref: Who knows what sudden disaster the Lord or a ruler might bring? More Sayings That Make Good Sense
text: diila kaasuŋ ale kpabi a jam ba zuk. Ka wana ale seba namsi kaai choa ale nyini Naawen ale Naawa jigi a cheen ba zuk la?

ref: Wisdom is too much for fools! Their advice is no good. –
text: Yam a ka kiri a te betta. A bo niŋdeerɔba tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi ba ka wari a weeni.

ref: Here are some more sayings that make good sense: When you judge, you must be fair.
text: Yam wie gela ale nna ŋmana: Ku an nala ase fi nin boro a bo buusa ate fi luk a sak jiirim ale baai ate fi a yaali la.

ref: Everyone hates senseless fools who think up ways to sin. –
text: Beruk popola ka biem. Waai meena a kisi waai ale nye nuruba a la la kama.

ref: If you let the guilty go free, people of all nations will hate and curse you.
text: Boteerɔ waai ale a weeni gaasa nyɔnɔwa ayen, <<Fi zɛ wari nɔi po la,>> nuruba yegayega ale ka kikaasa a te wa, ate tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale biisi zɛri wa.

ref: Don't give up and be helpless in times of trouble. –
text: Ase ku dan jam miri fu, fi pagrimu an soa dii ya.

ref: But if you punish the guilty, things will go well for you, and you will prosper.
text: Alege ku ale cheŋ nalimnyiini a te baai ale basi ate waai ale nye kaasi la a siak wa kaasuŋku la kama. Niaka ale bo ba zuk.

ref: Don't say, “I didn't know it!” God can read your mind. He watches each of us and knows our thoughts. And God will pay us back for what we do. –
text: Kan yaali wari a weeni ayen, <<Nya tama jam zɛ.>> Diila Naawen a miŋ suiniima meena kiri kama, wa abe a nya fu kama. Waai ale a nya fi chiika zuk la a seba ayen fi seba kama. Wa le tuni nuru meena a magsi wa nyeka ale ka diila kama.

ref: Giving an honest answer is a sign of true friendship.
text: Wensie tulisika a nye ase ka doaba ale a gbaari chaab diila.

ref: Honey is good for you, my children, and it tastes sweet.
text: M biiga, a dɛ siita ale ku nala kama, ate samparimaŋa lamka a masa.

ref: Get your fields ready and plant your crops before starting a home.
text: Nye fi zɔŋŋa abe fi gomsi fi tɛŋka abe fi ge piilim fi yenni sɛka.

ref: Don't be a cruel person who attacks good people and hurts their families.
text: Kan gu doa nuru maŋ yeri po ayen fi nye wa biem, be kan ga yik nuru maŋka wa yenni po.

ref: Even if good people fall seven times, they will get back up. But when trouble strikes the wicked, that's the end of them. –
text: Nuru maŋsa ale sati lɔ naŋtuok nɔi buyopɔi, alege ba ale ŋman yiti. Alege kaasuŋ bunyi nyiini ale te ate gaasa nyam a muriŋ bɛ.

ref: Don't accuse anyone who isn't guilty. Don't ever tell a lie
text: Kan biisi kaasi fi vaanchaab alege ate ba an nye fu wari ya. Kan velim a te ba.

ref: Don't be happy to see your enemies trip and fall down.
text: Kaa dɛ masim ase fi dachaasa nin lɔ. Kan te fi sui a peenti ase ba nin nak naŋŋa.

ref: The Lord will find out and be unhappy. Then he will stop being angry with them. –
text: Diila Naawen sui a kan peenti ale fu, ate wa ale yeeri wa suipuurumu a nyini ba zuk.

ref: I once walked by the field and the vineyard of a lazy fool.
text: Mi va ka nyiŋworuk nyɔnɔ laŋ po a taam, nuru waai ale kan ta wadek yam a bo wa kaduk po la.

ref: Thorns and weeds were everywhere, and the stone wall had fallen down.
text: Mi jam nya ka muŋsa ale chim ka po, ate wuuta a lik ka, ate ka parisaŋa a lɔ.

ref: When I saw this, it taught me a lesson:
text: Ate mi ale nya ale poli ka wari la, mi yaa zamsi wanni de:

ref: Sleep a little. Doze a little. Fold your hands and twiddle your thumbs.
text: Goom nna maga ale goajɔgsika nna maga ale nisa gurumka nna maga ayen fi vuusi,

ref: Here are some more of Solomon's proverbs. They were copied by the officials of King Hezekiah of Judah.
text: Yam wie ale nna ate Solomon a weeni ate ŋmarisidoama baai ale bo Naab Azekaya buusa boka yenni po a bo Juda tɛŋka po la a ŋmarisi.

ref: God is praised for being mysterious; rulers are praised for explaining mysteries.
text: Ku ka Naawen suik ate wa lik wie, ku ka naawa suik ate wa lak ŋa.

ref: Who can fully understand the thoughts of a ruler? They reach beyond the sky and go deep in the earth.
text: Ase wenŋmazuk ale yalima ate tɛŋzuk a limisa diila, ku ka dila ale nalima suiniima fi kan seba dii ale boro la.

ref: Silver must be purified before it can be used to make something of value.
text: Ase nuruba a dan yeeri yaataŋa a nyini kpana po, tuimtomdɔwa ale pai ku a nye wamaŋsa.

ref: Evil people must be removed before anyone can rule with justice.
text: Yiak gaasa nyɔnɔwa ate wa nyini naawa dabiaka po a nyini, ate wa dɛ naamu a nyini wensie po.

ref: Don't try to seem important in the court of a ruler.
text: Kan te nuruba a nya ase fi ale naawa ka bunyi la, yaase fi ga zaani nuru kpienta boka jigi ya.

ref: It's better for the ruler to give you a high position than for you to be embarrassed in front of royal officials. Be sure you are right
text: Fi dan limisi ate ba wi fu, a zunchoŋŋa ase fi ale cheŋ fidek ate ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba zɛri fu nuru boari suŋsuŋ po ale chivie. Fi ale nya jaab la nyiŋ,

ref: When you and someone else can't get along, don't gossip about it.
text: Weeni fi wanni a sak fi ale waai ale ta chaab la nyiini. Kan weeni a sak waai ya,

ref: Others will find out, and your reputation will then be ruined.
text: dan kan daa di nuruba ale wi fu ayen bumbobrɔ ate fi ale jɔk fi zula.

ref: The right word at the right time is like precious gold set in silver.
text: Fi dan biisi wamaŋ diipo ale magsi la, ku nala kama ase ligmɔniŋ ale ŋmirisi kpana chin po la.

ref: Listening to good advice is worth much more than jewelry made of gold.
text: Yam kaamka ate waai ale wa wom la a ta dobrim ase ka ligmɔniŋ tukpana yaase ligmɔniŋ baŋsa la.

ref: A messenger you can trust is just as refreshing as cool water in summer.
text: Tintomdɔ waai ate ba a mariŋ wa la a nye ase ka wenkarik ŋmoruk la. Wa a te wa kpagni nyiŋbiiri.

ref: Patience and gentle talk can convince a ruler and overcome any problem.
text: Chichiiba a baga a tagri niŋdeerɔ popola kama, fi be dan seba biik wari meena ka moali.

ref: Eating too much honey can make you sick.
text: Fi a yaali siita? Kan de ti yega, ti le basi ate fi yuak.

ref: Don't visit friends too often, or they will get tired of it and start hating you.
text: Kan kasim a cheŋ fi mabiik jigi daa meena. Wa nyue ale kasim a nyuŋ ale fu.

ref: Telling lies about friends is like attacking them with clubs and swords and sharp arrows.
text: Nuru waai ale a biisi venta wie a te wa vaanchoa la, a nye ase ka kpaliŋ tigsuŋ la, yaase gebik woŋ la, yaase pein la.

ref: If your enemies are hungry, give them something to eat. And if they are thirsty, give them something to drink.
text: Kɔm a dan ta fi dachiak te wa ŋandiinta ate wa dɛ. Nyanyuila a abe dan ta wa, te wa nyiam ate wa nyu.

ref: This will be the same as piling burning coals on their heads. And the Lord will reward you.
text: Fi pai ka bolim kaala a vi wa zuk, ate Naawen ale te fu tutuna.

ref: As surely as rain blows in from the north, anger is caused by cruel words.
text: Wiilukku geŋsa vioku ta ka ŋmoruk a jam ate bumbobrɔ a ta suipuurum a jam.

ref: It's better to stay outside on the roof of your house than to live inside with a nagging wife.
text: Fi bo gboŋ zuk gugoruk po, a zunchoŋŋa ale fi le bo yeri naliŋ po ate nipok tugurik tɔŋdɔba a bo di po.

ref: Good news from far away refreshes like cold water when you are thirsty.
text: Ase nya yɔgsik ale ka dii a te nyanyuila ale ta waai la, ku ka dila ase fi nin wom wapaala maŋsa a ta nyini niŋniŋŋa.

ref: When a good person gives in to the wicked, it's like dumping garbage in a stream of clear water.
text: Ase wayɔrisima nyama a dan siak a te gaasa nyama, ku a nye ase ka bulik nyiam daŋka yaase bulik nyiam poatika la.

ref: Losing self-control leaves you as helpless as a city without a wall.
text: Nuru waai ale kan bag wadek a yik la a nye ase ka tɛŋ kpieŋ ale kan ta pagrim diila.

ref: Expecting snow in summer and rain in the dry season makes more sense than honoring a fool.
text: Ase ŋmoruk nika ale kan ta kiri fanɔi vaari po la, dila mɛ ate zula a ka kiri a te beruwa.

ref: A curse you don't deserve will take wings and fly away like a sparrow or a swallow.
text: Kikaasa kan jam fi zuwa nin ka fi mɛ nin magsi dila, ŋa ale nye ase ka nuim ale bo wen ale kan zi diila.

ref: Horses and donkeys must be beaten and bridled— and so must fools.
text: Fiŋ ka wusum ale soa, a pai miik a dari boniŋ mɛ ate doari a soa beruk ŋaaŋ.

ref: But if you answer any fools, show how foolish they are, so they won't feel smart.
text: Tulisi beruk a magsi chaab ale wa betta, dan kan daa di wa ale pai wadek a chim ka yam nyɔnɔ.

ref: Sending a message by a fool is like chopping off your foot just to spite yourself.
text: A waai ale pai tomtomiŋ a te beruk la, a che ka wadek naŋsa ale a gisi daanika a te wadek.

ref: A fool with words of wisdom is like an athlete with legs that can't move.
text: Ase gbaniŋ naŋsa, ale kan ta kiri diila, wamagsini ka dila a te beruk.

ref: Are you going to honor a fool? Why not shoot a slingshot with the rock tied tight?
text: Ase waai ale pai tain a nyo visiŋ po la a nye ase ka waai ale pai zula a te beruk la.

ref: A thornbush waved around in the hand of a drunkard is no worse than a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
text: Ase muŋ ale a lu danyuirik diila. Wamagsini ka dila a bo beruk nɔi po.

ref: It's no smarter to shoot arrows at every passerby than it is to hire a bunch of worthless nobodies.
text: Tuima nyɔnɔ waai ale a pai beruk yaase waai ale za a nya tuimaŋa la a nye ase ka tɔŋdɔ ale tɔŋ a basi dula.

ref: Dogs return to eat their vomit, just as fools repeat their foolishness.
text: Ase biak ale ŋman a lak ka chichiita diila, ku ka dila ate beruk kuui nyiem ale ŋman a tom wa betta la.

ref: There is more hope for a fool than for someone who says, “I'm really smart!”
text: Waai ale a poli ayen wa ta yam la, alege ka bu la, betta a gaam wa kama.

ref: A door turns on its hinges, but a lazy person just turns over in bed.
text: Ase kuta ale a yik tuok ate ku a lik ale a lak diila, dila mɛ ate nyiŋworuk nyɔnɔwa gaduokku a yik wa a tara.

ref: Some of us are so lazy that we won't lift a hand to feed ourselves.
text: Nuruba gela nyiŋ wɔrukku a nye kama ate ba nisa nɔi ta juelika a toa a te ba.

ref: A lazy person says, “I am smarter than everyone else.”
text: Nyiŋworuk nyam a poli ayen ba seba gaam yam nyam bayopɔi kama.

ref: It's better to take hold of a mad dog by the ears than to take part in someone else's argument.
text: Fi ta fidek a jo a waai wari po a nak nanpaga ku nyiŋ alege ate ku an nya fu la, ku ka betta ase fi ale ga yik biak turi diila.

ref: It's no crazier to shoot sharp and flaming arrows
text: Ku a nye ase ka yesiŋ ale a tɔŋ tom diila.

ref: than to cheat someone and say, “I was only fooling!”
text: Ka waai ale a weeni venta wie a sak wa doa ale weeni ayen, <<Mi poom a diini kama.>>

ref: Where there is no fuel a fire goes out; where there is no gossip arguments come to an end.
text: Daata a dan kan boro bolim a kpi kama, ŋaaŋzum mɛ a dan kan boro kpaliŋ a kan boro.

ref: Troublemakers start trouble, just as sparks and fuel start a fire.
text: Kpaliŋ nyeerɔ a piilim kpaliŋ ka nna se bolim a nyiem ale chɔgsi kaala yaase daata diila.

ref: There is nothing so delicious as the taste of gossip! It melts in your mouth.
text: Ŋaaŋzum nyɔnɔ wie a nye a ase ka ŋandiin masa ale a siŋ a waai poi po diila.

ref: Hiding hateful thoughts behind smooth talk is like coating a clay pot with a cheap glaze.
text: Gaasa nyɔnɔ ale biisi wamasik a lik wa suinum ase ba ale pai jabuui ale a nyaksi a nye yak liik nyiŋ diila.

ref: The pleasant talk of an enemy hides more evil plans
text: Nuruba ale weeni wie ŋaai ale masa la a lirim ba biem popolaŋa, alege ba a paasi fu kama.

ref: If you dig a pit, you will fall in; if you start a stone rolling, it will roll back on you.
text: Fi dan bari baruk ayen ku yik nuruba, ku ale cheem yik ka fidek. Fi abe dan bilim piuŋ ayen ku bilim a ji a waai zuk, ku ale cheem bilim a ji ka fidek.

ref: Watch out for anyone who tells lies and flatters— they are out to get you.
text: Giŋgeluŋ kuui ale a velim la a kisa baai ale a nye wa wari la kama, ate venta pimpaga a ka kiri ya.

ref: Don't brag about tomorrow! Each day brings its own surprises.
text: Kan nak kuusidi chum nyiŋŋa, fi zɛ danni ale ta ka dii cheen la.

ref: Don't brag about yourself— let others praise you.
text: Kan pak fi dega, basi ate nuru yoŋta a nye dila.

ref: Stones and sand are heavy, but trouble caused by a fool is a much heavier load.
text: Tana a dobra kama ate tanta a dobra gaam di ate beruk ale a daani diila a dobra a gaam ŋala meena.

ref: An angry person is dangerous, but a jealous person is even worse.
text: Suipuurum a bie kama ale ŋman a kaasi tuima alege nyuri a pagra a gaam ŋa kama.

ref: A truly good friend will openly correct you.
text: Fi dan toariŋ nuruwa nimbie po a zunchoŋŋa fi le suk a yaali wa.

ref: You can trust a friend who corrects you, but kisses from an enemy are nothing but lies.
text: Fi doa a dan te fu tuem a zunchoŋŋa fi dachiak ale a gbaari fu.

ref: If you have had enough to eat, honey doesn't taste good, but if you are really hungry, you will eat anything.
text: Fi dan dɛ chak siita mɛ an poom masa a te fu, alege kom a dan ta fu jabuui ale toa la a masa kama.

ref: When you are far from home, you feel like a bird without a nest.
text: Ase nuim ale a nyini bu tuk po a cheŋ diila, nidoa waai ale a basi wa yeri la mɛ ka dila.

ref: The sweet smell of incense can make you feel good, but true friendship is better still.
text: Kpaam ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a basi ate ka fi sui a peenti, doa masim a nyini ka wa sinsak maŋsa jigi.

ref: Don't desert an old friend of your family or visit your relatives when you are in trouble. A friend nearby is better than relatives far away.
text: Kan baŋ fi doa yaase fi kowa doa wari ya. Ate diipo ate fi a silim la, fi kan bek mabiik ayen wa maari fu. Fi dan cheŋ waai ale moata fu la jigi a zunchoŋ fi le cheŋ fi mabiik waai ale yalima la jigi.

ref: My child, show good sense! Then I will be happy and able to answer anyone who criticizes me.
text: M biiga, be ta yam, abe fi nye ate m sui a peenti. Ate m baga a tulisi baai ale kan biisi mu a magsi la.

ref: You deserve to lose your coat if you loan it to someone to guarantee payment for the debt of a stranger.
text: Waai a dan chim beruk ayen wa zaani ate nichaanɔ a tuesi pami jaab, wa magsi wa pai ka wadek nitalim a zaani a magsi pamini tuesika.

ref: A loud greeting early in the morning is the same as a curse.
text: Fi dan tue na puusi waai ale moata fu la saluik yokyokwa, ku a nye ase ka kikaasa la.

ref: The steady dripping of rain and the nagging of a wife are one and the same.
text: Nipok kpaliŋ kpaliŋdɔ nyeka a puuri ka sui ase ŋmoruk kuui ale kasim a minisi a kan vɔssi la.

ref: Just as iron sharpens iron, friends sharpen the minds of each other.
text: Ase ba le pai kuta a saasi chaab diila, nuruba mɛ a maari chaab ka dila.

ref: Take care of a tree, and you will eat its fruit; look after your master, and you will be praised.
text: Ase tuimtomdɔ waai ale a nya tiib zuk a baga a dɛ bu yɔna diila, dila mɛ ate tuimtomdɔ waai ale a nye wa kpagi ale a yaali diila ale nya wa tutuna.

ref: You see your face in a mirror and your thoughts in the minds of others.
text: Ase nuru ale a nya wa nimbidiaka nyiam po diila, dila mɛ ate wa suinummu a dak wa a sak.

ref: Death and the grave are never satisfied, and neither are humans.
text: Ase Kum ale Kaasuŋ ale kaa chak diila, dila mɛ ate nuru a kan chak ale ŋanta.

ref: Gold and silver are tested in a red-hot furnace, but we are tested by praise.
text: Bolim ate ba pai chamsi kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a nya, alege ba chamsi nuru a nya ale ka pimpauk.

ref: No matter how hard you beat a fool, you can't pound out the foolishness.
text: Fi dan poom a nak beruk ase ba ale a kuri zaa diila, wa kan basi wa bettaŋa.

ref: You should take good care of your sheep and goats,
text: Seba fi piisaŋa ale ka diila a chak, abe fi te ate fi suinum a bo fi niiŋa zuk nyaasim.

ref: After the hay is cut and the new growth appears and the harvest is over,
text: Ate ba dan ŋari wuuta, ate ŋan bulaŋa ate ba bori laŋsaŋa bo la a nyini, ate ba tigsi guuta wuutaŋa a ta jo dueni,

ref: you can sell lambs and goats to buy clothes and land.
text: ni piisaŋa ale te kɔbta a magsi gatta, ate ni booŋa ale tuni laŋsaŋa nyiŋ.

ref: From the milk of the goats, you can make enough cheese to feed your family and all your servants.
text: Ate ni ale nya booŋa biisim yega ate ku paari ni ale ni dɔkdem ale ni tomteerɔma nipokbilisaŋa.

ref: Wicked people run away when no one chases them, but those who live right are as brave as lions.
text: Gaasa nyɔnɔwa a chali kama alege ate waai an poom a vi wa, alege wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa suinummu a pagra kama nna se gbeŋli la.

ref: In time of civil war there are many leaders, but a sensible leader restores law and order.
text: Tɛŋ nuruba nyeela a dan kan nala, niŋdeerɔma a jɔk ba naamu kama. Alege yam ale sebika niŋdeerɔba a ta ka zaana nalimnyiini.

ref: When someone poor takes over and mistreats the poor, it's like a heavy rain destroying the crops.
text: Nuru jak waai ale a namsi jajak la, a nye ase ka ŋmoruk ale ni kaasi ŋankpaanta diila.

ref: Criminals don't know what justice means, but all who respect the Lord understand it completely.
text: Nuru baata a kan miŋ wensie kiri ya, alege baai ale a gisi Naawen la a miŋ ku kiri ka nalimnyiini.

ref: It's better to be poor and live right, than to be rich and dishonest.
text: Jajak a dan a cheŋ wa wensie suik po, ku gaam jigsirɔ ale va venta suik po.

ref: It makes good sense to obey the Law of God, but you disgrace your parents if you make friends with worthless nobodies.
text: Nuru paalisa baai ale a nye tuewomma a te sinsaŋŋa la, ka yam nyam. Baai ale a va doa baai ale waara la a ta ka chivie a jam ba nyam zuk.

ref: If you make money by charging high interest rates, you will lose it all to someone who cares for the poor.
text: Waai ale a gebi ligra a nya nyuenta la ale jɔk ŋa. Ku kpeglim ka ŋa le jo ka waai ale ta jiirim ale ŋanjaksa la nisima po.

ref: God cannot stand the prayers of anyone who disobeys his Law.
text: Waai ale lik turi a kan wom sinsaŋŋa la, kula nyɔnɔ puusa ka leeta a te Naawen.

ref: By leading good people to sin, you dig a pit for yourself, but all who live right will have a bright future.
text: Baai ale a paasi nuru maŋsa a ta ba a jo biem po la ale lɔ ka badek baruk po, alege baai ale za dekki la ale nya ŋan maŋsa.

ref: The rich think highly of themselves, but anyone poor and sensible sees right through them.
text: Jigsirɔ ale poli ayen wa ta yam ka wadek nina po, alege waai ale jaŋ ale ta miŋ chakka la a seba dii ale nala la kama.

ref: When an honest person wins, it's time to celebrate; when crooks are in control, it's best to hide.
text: Ase Wen nuruma a dan nya nyeboka, waai meena sue a peenti kama. Alege gaasa nyam a dan nya pagrim nuruba ale jo ŋooma vie.

ref: If you don't confess your sins, you will be a failure. But God will be merciful if you confess your sins and give them up.
text: Nuru baai ale a lik ba wabaata la a kan nya ba dega, alege ba dan weeni ale basi ŋa ba ale nya jiirim.

ref: The Lord blesses everyone who is afraid to do evil, but if you are cruel, you will end up in trouble.
text: Niauŋ a bo ale waai ale a chali Naawen diipo meena la jigi, alege waai ale ta tukpari la ale jo ninam po.

ref: A ruler who mistreats the poor is like a roaring lion or a bear hunting for food.
text: Niŋdeerɔ biok a nye ase ka gbeŋli yaase gɔi biak ale waara diila nuru waai ale jaŋ la jigi.

ref: A heartless leader is a fool, but anyone who refuses to get rich by cheating others will live a long time.
text: Niŋdeerɔ waai ale kan ta miŋka la a namsi ka wa nuruba, alege waai ale kaa yaali venta ŋanta la daaŋa ale wɔŋa.

ref: Don't give help to murderers! Make them stay on the run for as long as they live.
text: Nuru koorik popola a ta wa a daani ka dila a ga a paari wa kum. Kan nya wa zuwa.

ref: Honesty will keep you safe, but everyone who is crooked will suddenly fall.
text: Waai ale a cheŋ wensie suik la ale nya varibasika, alege waai ale kan va wensie po la ale deri lɔ tɛŋ.

ref: Work hard, and you will have a lot of food; waste time, and you will have a lot of trouble.
text: Tuimtomdɔ waai ale ta nyiŋbiiri a kpa la a ta ŋandiinta ka nna yegayega, alege nuru waai ale a va wie kayaata la ale kpeglim ale ka jaŋsa.

ref: God blesses his loyal people, but punishes all who want to get rich quick.
text: Wensie nuru ale nya niauŋ yegayega, alege nuru waai ale a yaali ayen wa kpabi a jigsi la ale ga jo ka daanika po.

ref: It isn't right to be unfair, but some people can be bribed with only a piece of bread.
text: Fi daa sak lukka ku an nala, alege dɛka nyiŋ nuru a bag nye a kaasi kama.

ref: Don't be selfish and eager to get rich— you will end up worse off than you can imagine.
text: Nuru baai ale a yaali de gaamka la a yaali kama ayen ba kpabi a jigsi, alege zɛ ayen ba a cheŋ tuak ka jaŋsa po.

ref: If you cheat your parents and don't think it's wrong, you are a common thief.
text: Waai ale a zu wa ko ale wa ma alege a weeni ayen, <<Kaasuŋ boa ale bo nya kude po?>> Wa ale nuru koorik ka bunyi.

ref: Selfish people cause trouble, but you will live a full life if you trust the Lord.
text: De gaamka nyɔnɔ a siti ka kpaliŋ, alege waai ale ta sebchakka ale Naawen la ale nya wadek kama.

ref: Only fools would trust what they alone think, but if you live by wisdom, you will do all right.
text: A waai ale ta sebchakka ale wadek popola la ka beruk, alege waai ale a cheŋ yam po la a nya varibasika kama.

ref: Giving to the poor will keep you from poverty, but if you close your eyes to their needs, everyone will curse you.
text: Nuru waai ale a te ŋanjaksa ŋanta la, a kan silim jaaboa, alege waai ale kan cheem a nya ba la ale nya kikaasa yegayega.

ref: When crooks are in control, everyone tries to hide, but when they lose power, good people are everywhere.
text: Gaasa nyam a dan bo pagrim po, nuruba a suk kama. Ba dan ta chaab ale kaasuŋ Wen nuruma a piisi kama.

ref: If you keep being stubborn after many warnings, you will suddenly discover you have gone too far.
text: Nuru waai ale kaa wom sinsaga la ale deri kpi kama wa tukpanni nyiŋ ale kan nyini du a nyini.

ref: When justice rules a nation, everyone is glad; when injustice rules, everyone groans.
text: Wen nuruma a dan bo pagrim po, nuruma a de ka masim. Alege gaasa nyama a dan bo pagrim po nuruma a kum kama.

ref: If you love wisdom your parents will be glad, but chasing after bad women will cost you everything.
text: Waai ale a yaali yam la a nye ate ka wa ko sui a peenti, alege waai ale a yaali nipooba la, a nueri ka wa nitalim.

ref: An honest ruler makes the nation strong; a ruler who takes bribes will bring it to ruin.
text: Naab waai ale chekki la a yik wa tɛŋka a zaani kama, alege waai ale te ate ba pai ŋanta a da wa la a lɔnsi ka kama.

ref: Flattery is nothing less than setting a trap.
text: Baai ale ta nɔi masim la a bari ka nuruba.

ref: Your sins will catch you, but everyone who lives right will sing and celebrate.
text: Wabaata nyam bari yik nuru baata kama, alege ku kan yik wayɔrisima nyama ate ba nyiem yaa nye masim nuemka.

ref: The wicked don't care about the rights of the poor, but good people do.
text: Wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa a seba dii ale magsi jajakka la kama, alege gaasa nyɔnɔwa niŋ a poom karo ayen wa miŋ wari ya.

ref: Sneering at others is a spark that sets a city on fire; using good sense can put out the flames of anger.
text: Baai ale a la nuruba la a nye kama ate tɛŋ a chɔgsi bolim, alege baai ale ta yam la a kpimsi ka suipuurum.

ref: Be wise and don't sue a fool. You won't get satisfaction, because all the fool will do is sneer and shout.
text: Ase yam nyɔnɔ a dan ta nanpaga ale beruk, beruku a biisi a basi kama ale a la, ate chim nyeka a kan boro.

ref: Don't be a fool and quickly lose your temper— be sensible and patient.
text: Beruk a sak wa suipuurum ka nna nwuli alege yam nyɔnɔ a yik wadek kama.

ref: A ruler who listens to lies will have corrupt officials.
text: Niŋdeerɔ a daa wom venta wie, wa ŋaaŋviirɔma meena a chim ka gaasa nyam.

ref: The poor and all who abuse them must each depend on God for light.
text: Ŋanjaksaŋa ale ba namsidɔma meena ka Naawen ale basi ate ba a nya.

ref: Kings who are fair to the poor will rule a long time.
text: Naab waai ale a bo ŋanjaksa wensie buusa bo ka la, wa naam zukpaglika ale boro taam wuu.

ref: Correct your children, and they will be wise; children out of control disgrace their mothers.
text: Biik waalika a te wa ka yam, alege biik kaai ate ba a basi wa la a ta ka chivie a jam a te wa ma.

ref: Crime increases when crooks are in power, but law-abiding citizens will see them fall.
text: Ase gaasa nyam a dan bo pagrim po, biem a piisi kama. Alege Wen nuruma ale boro a nya ba lueta.

ref: If you correct your children, they will bring you peace and happiness.
text: Te fi biika waalika, ate wa ale basi ate fi vuusi. Wa ale te ate fi chiika a dɛ masim.

ref: Without guidance from God law and order disappear, but God blesses everyone who obeys his Law.
text: Juijui ate Naawen wanni a ka la, nuruma a nye a kaasi kama, alege waai ale ta sinsaŋŋa la ale nya niauŋ.

ref: Even when servants are smart, it takes more than words to make them obey.
text: Biik nyiini a kan tagri tomteerɔ, wa dan poom miŋ fi ale a weeni diila, wa kan nye.

ref: There is more hope for a fool than for someone who speaks without thinking.
text: Beruk a ta yiila a gaam a waai ale a biisi ale kan poli la kama.

ref: Slaves that you treat kindly from their childhood will cause you sorrow.
text: Fi daa poagi fi tomteerɔ wa ale yiri a zɛri fi nɔi.

ref: A person with a quick temper stirs up arguments and commits a lot of sins.
text: Waai sui ale kpabi a puuri la, a kpabi a nye ka kpaliŋ ale a nye wie ŋaai ale bie la.

ref: If you take part in a crime you are your worst enemy, because even under oath you can't tell the truth.
text: Fi dan maari zue, fi a nye ka fidek. Ba ale namsi fu ase fi ale weeni kaasuŋ kuui ale nye la, alege kikaasa ale bo fi zuk ase fi a nin kan weeni ya.

ref: Don't fall into the trap of being a coward— trust the Lord, and you will be safe.
text: Nurubiik yɔgsum chala ka baruk barika, alege waai ale ta sebchakka ale Naawen la a nya boka dek jigi kama.

ref: Many try to make friends with a ruler, but justice comes from the Lord.
text: Nuruba yegayega a zak a nya ka kpaga, alege nuru a nya wensie boteka a nyini ka Naawen jigi.

ref: Good people and criminals can't stand each other.
text: Wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ a kisi gaasa nyɔnɔwa kama, ate gaasa nyɔnɔwa mɛ a kisa wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa.

ref: These are the sayings and the message of Agur son of Jakeh. Someone cries out to God, “I am completely worn out! How can I last?
text: Jakey biika Agur wieŋa ale nna. M Wen yaa m jiak kama. M dek Wen yaa, m sum a jiak kama ate pagrim a ka m po.

ref: I am far too stupid to be considered human.
text: M ka beruk, ate m ka m dek yam mɛ.

ref: I never was wise, and I don't understand what God is like.”
text: Mi an zamsi yam yaase m seba Waai Ale Welema la wari ya.

ref: Has anyone gone up to heaven and come back down? Has anyone grabbed hold of the wind? Has anyone wrapped up the sea or marked out boundaries for the earth? If you know of any who have done such things, then tell me their names and their children's names.
text: Ka wana ale jueli wenŋmazuk ale siŋ ya? Ka wana ale baga a gum vioku a ta wa nisima po? Ka wana ale baga a kpamsi nyaataŋa a nyo wa garuk po? Ka wana ale nye tɛŋka kpeglimka meena? Wa yue ale boa, wa biika mɛ yue ale boa. Weeni a sak mu ase fi a nin seba.

ref: Everything God says is true— and it's a shield for all who come to him for safety.
text: Naawen wari meena ka wensie. Wa chim ka ligrɔ a te baai ale a jam wa jigi ayen wa a nya ba zuk la.

ref: Don't change what God has said! He will correct you and show that you are a liar.
text: Kan yaali wari a gum wa wieŋa po, fi dan nye dila fi ka velimvendik, wa le toariŋ fu.

ref: There are two things, Lord, I want you to do for me before I die:
text: M Naawen ya, mi a yaali ka wie ŋaye ayen fi nye a te mu. Basi ate m nya ŋa abe m ge a kpi.

ref: Make me absolutely honest and don't let me be too poor or too rich. Give me just what I need.
text: Dii ale a dɛ niŋ la ale maari mu ate m kan velim. Dii ale a saari buye la ale kan te m jaŋ yaase m jigsi. Te ate mi a nya a magsi ate m kan silimu.

ref: If I have too much to eat, I might forget about you; if I don't have enough, I might steal and disgrace your name.
text: Dii nyiŋla m dan jigsi, m le zɛri fu abe m weeni ayen, <<Ka wana ale Naawen?>> Ate m dan jaŋ, da dii dai m le cheŋ ga zu ate ku ta leeta a jam Naawen yuei weleŋka jigi.

ref: Don't tell a slave owner something bad about one of the slaves. That slave will curse you, and you will be in trouble.
text: Kan weeni tomteerɔ kaasuŋ a sak wa kpagi ya. Wa ale ka a te fu ate ku ale sum a va fu.

ref: Some people curse their father and even their mother;
text: Nuruba gela a ka a te ba koba kama ale kan nye ba maba jiamoa.

ref: others think they are perfect, but they are stained by sin.
text: Ba nye cheri ka badek nimbie po, alege ba daŋ kama ale an poom sugri ba dega.

ref: Some people are stuck-up and act like snobs;
text: Ba a poli kama ayen ba ka nuru maŋsa, alege ba daa jaaboa.

ref: The world of the dead and a childless wife, the thirsty earth and a flaming fire.
text: Boosuku ale kirika ale tɛŋ kaai ale kaa jo nyiamoa ale bolim ŋiak.

ref: Don't make fun of your father or disobey your mother— crows will peck out your eyes, and buzzards will eat the rest of you.
text: Numbiri dii ale a nye ko a la la ale a zɛri ma sinsaga la, tagaarutaŋa ale bo viaka po la ale yeeri bu ate duinsa a dɛ.

ref: There are three or four things I cannot understand:
text: Ŋanta bata ale cha mi. Aaya, ŋanta banaansi ate mi a kan miŋ ku kiri ya.

ref: An unfaithful wife says, “Sleeping with another man is as natural as eating.”
text: Nipok kaboŋ nyeerik ale dɛ nidoa kama, a yaa duisi wa nɔnni ale weeni ayen, <<Kaasuŋ boa ale bo nya kude po?>>

ref: There are three or four things that make the earth tremble and are unbearable:
text: Wie ŋata ale basi ate tɛŋka a choa, aaya, ŋanaansi ale kan baga a zaani.

ref: A slave who becomes king, a fool who eats too much,
text: Ase yɔma a nin chim naab, ate beruk puuk a sueri ale ŋandiinta,

ref: a hateful woman who finds a husband, and a slave who takes the place of the woman who owns her.
text: nipok waai nyeka ale toa la a nyiem yaa jam nya chorɔ a yali, ate dɔklie nyiem yaa jam tagri wa kpagni.

ref: On this earth four things are small but very wise:
text: Wie ŋanaansi ale fiisa a bo tɛŋzuk de alege a ta yam nna yegayega.

ref: Ants, who seem to be feeble, but store up food all summer long;
text: Nankeriŋsa, si ka pagrimoa, alege si a dueni ŋandiinta fanɔi wen.

ref: badgers, who seem to be weak, but live among the rocks;
text: Suensa, ka pagrimoa alege si a nye si yieŋa ka pina po.

ref: locusts, who have no king, but march like an army;
text: Tintue ŋa ka naaba alege ŋa a va ka chaab.

ref: lizards, which can be caught in your hand, but sneak into palaces.
text: Baŋsa, si yikka an toa, alege si bo nalima yie po.

ref: Those fearless lions who rule the jungle,
text: Gbeŋli ale ka duŋsaŋa naab la, ate di kan viriŋ ayen wari nyiŋla,

ref: those proud roosters, those mountain goats, and those rulers who have no enemies.
text: ale kpadiak ale buduk ale naab waai ale de wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma niŋ la.

ref: If you are foolishly bragging or planning something evil, then stop it now!
text: Ase fi dan chim beruk ale ta kanjanta yaase fi nye biem, kan nak kuusidi dila nyiŋŋa, pai fi nisaŋa a lik fi nɔnni ale chivie.

ref: If you churn milk you get butter; if you pound on your nose, you get blood— and if you stay angry, you get in trouble.
text: Ase ba ale a nak biisim ate bu a goa diila, ale a tak nyue ate ziim a nyini diila, ka dila ate fi dan nye ate nuruba sue a puuri wɔkwɔk a jam la.

ref: These are the sayings that King Lemuel of Massa was taught by his mother.
text: Naab Lemuel ale weeni bi sii ate wa mawa a sak la ale nna.

ref: My son Lemuel, you were born in answer to my prayers, so listen carefully.
text: <<M dek biiga, m dek popo biiga, m bek ka Naawen ate wa pai fu a te mu.

ref: Don't waste your life chasing after women! This has ruined many kings.
text: Kan pai fi pagrim a te nipooba, baai ale a kaasi nalima.

ref: Kings and leaders should not get drunk or even want to drink.
text: Lemuel, ku an nala ayen nalima a nyu daamoa, yaase kpaga a nyu da pagrisa.

ref: Beer and wine are only for the dying or for those who have lost all hope.
text: Pai da pagrik a te waai ale cheŋ a bɛ la, abe fi te waai chiik ale bo daanika po la daam.

ref: Let them drink and forget how poor and miserable they feel.
text: Basi ate ba nyu a baŋ ba jaŋsaŋa abe ba kan ŋman teeri ba daanika.

ref: But you must defend those who are helpless and have no hope.
text: Biisi a te baai ale kan baga a biisi a te badek la. Tom wensie tuima a te baai ale bo daanika po la.

ref: Be fair and give justice to the poor and homeless. In Praise of a Good Wife
text: Wensie, be biisi a te ŋanjaksa ale baai ale kan ta maarika la, abe fi basi ate wensie buusa boka a tom tuima.

ref: A truly good wife is the most precious treasure a man can find!
text: Ka wana ale wa nya nipok maŋŋa ate wa baga wie a nye? Wa gaam tintain munta.

ref: She is good to him every day of her life,
text: Wa boka po meena, wa ta ka ŋandiinta a jam a te wa alege daa daanika.

ref: and with her own hands she gladly makes clothes.
text: Wa gisi a nya ka duŋ kɔbta ale bɔkta a pai a tom wa tuima.

ref: She is like a sailing ship that brings food from across the sea.
text: Wa a nye ase ka geruŋdɔ ŋaaruŋ ale a cheŋ niŋniŋ a ta ŋandiinta a jam la.

ref: She gets up before daylight to prepare food for her family and for her servants.
text: Wa a yiri kama alege ate vanni a veenti a dik ŋandiinta a te wa dɔkdem ale a gomsi danni tuima a te wa dɔkliema.

ref: She knows how to buy land and how to plant a vineyard,
text: Wa a nya laŋ a da kama. Wa pai wa tutunaŋa a bori ŋanta wa kadukka po.

ref: and she always works hard.
text: Wa pagra kama ale ta nyiŋbiiri ale tuima tomka.

ref: and she helps the poor and the needy.
text: Wa a teeri wa nisa a maari ŋanjaksa ale baai ale a silim la.

ref: Her family has warm clothing, and so she doesn't worry when it snows.
text: Wa kpaziim a kan nak ale ŋoota wen ya dii nyiŋla wa ta ŋoota gatta kama a te wa dɔkdemma.

ref: Her husband is a well-known and respected leader in the city.
text: Tɛŋka nansuiŋtaŋa demma a seba wa chorɔwa kama, juijui ate wa a kali ale tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma la.

ref: She makes clothes to sell to the shop owners.
text: Wa a nye ka gatta ale chiak gbana a da a te geruŋdɔba.

ref: She is strong and graceful, as well as cheerful about the future.
text: Pagrim ale zula a bo wa po ate wa kpaziim a kan nak ale chum wie.

ref: Her words are sensible, and her advice is thoughtful.
text: Wa dan biisi, yam a bo wa biika po kama ale a te sinsaga ale jiirim.

ref: She takes good care of her family and is never lazy.
text: Wa a kpesi a nya wa yenni po ŋanta meena ale ka wari a nye ale nyiŋ wɔrukwa.

ref: Her children praise her, and with great pride her husband says,
text: Wa bisaŋa a yiti a wi wa ayen suipeentik nyɔnɔ. Wa chorɔwa mɛ a pak wa.

ref: Charm can be deceiving, and beauty fades away, but a woman who honors the Lord deserves to be praised.
text: Nyeela maŋsa a baga chim pimpaasima kama, nalim mɛ ka kinla, alege nipok waai ale a chali Naawen la ale magsi pakka.

ref: Show her respect— praise her in public for what she has done.
text: Tuni wa ale nye dii meena la nyiŋ. Te wa tuimaŋa nyiŋ nuru meena a pak wa.

ref: When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
text: Deevid ale jam ka naab a bo Jerusalem la nidoabinni Sagrɔwa wieŋa ale nna: Sagrɔwa ayen,

ref: Nothing makes sense! Everything is nonsense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense!
text: <<Ku ka kiri ya! Ku ka kiri ya! Ku din bola ka kiri ya! Jaab meena a ka kiri ya.>>

ref: What is there to show for all of our hard work here on this earth?
text: Nuru ale nya ka boa a nyini wa ninammu meena po dii ate wa nam tɛŋzuk de la?

ref: People come, and people go, but still the world never changes.
text: Gaŋsa a jam kama ate gaŋsa a cheŋ, alege tɛŋzuk de a boro kama taam wuu.

ref: The sun comes up, the sun goes down; it hurries right back to where it started from.
text: Wenbinni a pusi kama, wenbinni abe a siŋ kama, ale kpabi a ŋmani a cheŋ di pusika jigini.

ref: The wind blows south, the wind blows north; round and round it blows over and over again.
text: Vioku a fuk a cheŋ yeseoku ale tulim a cheŋ wiilukku geŋsa a gilim a gilim ku le poom liŋ va juijui la.

ref: All rivers empty into the sea, but it never spills over; one by one the rivers return to their source.
text: Buboalisa meena chali a siŋ ka nyakpiemu po, alege nyakpiemu diem kan sueri. Buboalisaŋa ale nyini juijui la, dula jigini ate si ŋmani a cheŋ.

ref: All of life is far more boring than words could ever say. Our eyes and our ears are never satisfied with what we see and hear.
text: Wari meena a ta ka jianta ate waai a kan baga a biisi ŋa wari ya. Numbinni a nya ka dila a kan jiagi, tunni mɛ a wom ka dila di kan jiagi.

ref: Everything that happens has happened before; nothing is new, nothing under the sun.
text: Dii ale liŋ boro la ale pilim boro dii ale liŋ nye la ale ŋman pilim nye. Wari a ka tɛŋzuk de a chim wapaali.

ref: Someone might say, “Here is something new!” But it happened before, long before we were born.
text: Wari a boro ate waai ale baga ayen, <<Nya wanni de ka wapaali?>> Di poom liŋ bo dela kama ate ku beni, alege ate tama a jam.

ref: No one who lived in the past is remembered anymore, and everyone yet to be born will be forgotten too. It Is Senseless To Be Wise
text: Ba kan ŋman teeri nuru kpagsa wari ya, ate baai mɛ ale diem cheena la baai ale paasaŋ ba la a kan teeri ba wari ya.

ref: I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel.
text: Mi, sagrɔwa jam ka naab a nya Izirali zuk Jerusalem po.

ref: With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do.
text: Mi jam yik ka m dek a zamsi ale kpesi ayen m gisi ale yam a nya dii meena ale nye tɛŋzuk la. Ka boan jib doabrita ate Naawen a pai ji nuru biiga!

ref: I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
text: Mi nya wie ŋaai meena ale jam nye tɛŋzuk de la kama, ŋa meena ka kiri ya ŋa a nye ase ka fi le a vi viok diila.

ref: If something is crooked, it can't be made straight; if something isn't there, it can't be counted.
text: Jabuui ale goaliŋ la a ka teentika, jabuui ale kan karo la ba kan chiini.

ref: I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.”
text: Mi yaa weeni m dek ayen, <<Nya m chim kama ale ta yam a gaam waai meena ale nya Jerusalem zuk ale ge te mi la. Mi nya ka yam ale sebika yega.>>

ref: Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
text: Mi yaa poli ayen m miŋ yam ale yesiŋsa ale berinni kiri, alege mi yaa miŋ ayen kude mɛ a nye ase fi le a vi viok diila.

ref: The more you know, the more you hurt; the more you understand, the more you suffer.
text: Yam yega a ta ka niniga cheena. Fi dan ta sebika yega, fi a nya ka niniga yega.

ref: Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do?
text: Mi yaa weeni ayen, <<Laata! Ku ka betta. Masim dɛka a ta ka boan cheena?>>

ref: I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
text: Mi yaa piilim a te m dek nyiŋbiiri ale daam nyuka ale kpari maŋ berinni ate m popolaŋa a diem a gani mu ale yam. Mi jam a yaali ayen m nya ka dii ale ka wamaŋ ayen nuruba a nye tɛŋzuk de daa magadek ate ba vua la po.

ref: I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards.
text: Mi yaa nye wakpiema nna yegayega: Mi jam sɛ ka yie a te m dek ale bori kaduksa yega.

ref: I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees.
text: Mi lɔ ka tatta ale peelim nna jalɔ ale vuk yɔna tiisa ti po.

ref: And I had pools where I could get water for the trees.
text: Mi jam nye gola ate nyiam a bo ŋa po a zaŋti ti sii ale a busim la.

ref: I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem.
text: Mi jam ta ka nidoa yɔm ale nipok yɔm ale ta yɔm ba chaab ate ba biak ba m yenni po. Mi jam ta ka duŋ boari ale duŋ buulim a gaam waai meena ale jam bo Jerusalem po a ta diila.

ref: Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
text: Mi jam maa ta ka kpana ale ligmɔniŋ ale ligra a nyini nalima ale tɛŋsa jigi. Mi jam ta ka nidoa yilendisa ale nipok yilendisa ale nipooba boka jigi, nidoa suinum mariŋka jigini.

ref: I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise.
text: Mi jam ta ka yuei a poom gaam baai meena ale liŋ bo Jerusalem po ale ge mi la. M yammu ale jam maari mu nnala meena.

ref: Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble. Wisdom Comes from God
text: Alege mi ale kpesi nya dii meena ate mi nisaŋa a nye la ale mi ale nam a nye diila, wari meena jam ka kiri ya, ku ka viok chali vika nyuenta ka tɛŋzuk de.

ref: I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity.
text: Mi yaa tulim m popolaŋa a basi yam ale yesiŋsa ale berinni jigi. Ka boa ate waai ale za naawa nankula po la ale ŋman nye a gaam nnala, dii ale poom liŋ nye la?

ref: And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
text: Mi yaa nya ale yam a zunchoŋ berinni kama, ase bolim ale zunchoŋ legi diila.

ref: Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
text: Yam nyam a nya ba le a cheŋ juijui la kama alege betta a bo ka legini po a gilim. Mi nya dila, yam nyam ale betta nyam kpeglimka ka bunyi.

ref: Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense.
text: Mi yaa poli m suinum po ayen dii ale nye beruku la ale nye mi mɛ kama. Dila ka boan tiirim ale boro ase fi nin ta yammoa?>> Mi weeni midek ayen, <<Fi dan ta yam mɛ ku ka kiri ya.>>

ref: Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all.
text: Mi kisa jaab meena ate mi nam nya tɛŋzuk de la kama, dii nyiŋla ku a fɛ ate m basi a te waai ale wa boro mi ŋaaŋnyiŋ la.

ref: Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
text: Nuru yoŋ ale wa soa ŋan baai ate mi nam tɛŋzuk de a nya la, mi abe zɛ ase wa le ta yam yaase wa ka beruwa. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya.

ref: I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed.
text: Dila nyiŋ mi suinum yaa piilim a kaasi dii meena ate m nam nye tɛŋzuk de la.

ref: When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong.
text: Nuru ale tom wa tuini ale yam ale sebika ale wa le seba diila, a basi ŋan baai meena ate wa soa la a te waai ale kan tom ba nyiŋla. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya ale chim zubiok.

ref: What do we really gain from all of our hard work?
text: Nuru ale nya ka boa wa tuimaŋa ale wa ninammu nyiŋ tɛŋzuk de?

ref: Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
text: Wa daaŋa meena, wa tuini meena ka nyiŋdomma ale niniga, yokku po wa popolaŋa kan vuusi. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya.

ref: The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us,
text: Wamaŋ kaai ate nuru ale nye la ale wa dɛ abe wa nyu abe wa dɛ masim wa tuini nyiŋ. Mi nya dila kama kude a poom nyini ka Wen jigi.

ref: and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do.
text: Dan kan daa wala, ka wana ale baga a dɛ yaase wa nya masimmoa?

ref: If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: Ate nuru waai ale nye ate wa sui a yɔk la, Wen a te ka yam ale sebika ale suipeentik, alege wabanyeerika, wa basi kama ate wa tigsi ale su wa paaruŋku a zaani ate wa pai ba a te waai ale nye ate Wen sui a peenti la. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya, ku a nye ase ka fi le chali a vi viok diila.

ref: Everything on earth has its own time and its own season.
text: Dai ale boro a te wari meena, ate vari a boro a te tuini meena tɛŋzuk de.

ref: There is a time for birth and death, planting and reaping,
text: Biam dai a boro kama, ate kum dai a boro. Borik dai a boro kama ate voorika dai mɛ a boro.

ref: There is also a time for love and hate, for war and peace. What God Has Given Us To Do
text: Yaalika dai a boro kama ate kisika dai a boro. Kpaliŋ dai a boro kama ate suiyɔgni dai mɛ a boro.

ref: What do we gain by all our hard work?
text: Ka boa ate tuimtomdɔwa ale nya wa ninammu nyiŋŋa?

ref: I have seen what difficult things God demands of us.
text: Mi nya gigelika ate Wen a pai ji nurubiik la kama.

ref: God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future.
text: Wen a nye wari meena kama ate di nala diipo ale magsi la. Wa nye kama mɛ ate wenŋmazuk wie a bo nurubisa suiniima po alege ba kan miŋ Wen ale nye dii a nyini piilimka a ga paari kpeglimka.

ref: because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do.
text: Wen a yaali kama ayen ba a dɛ abe ba nyu a ta suipeentik ba tuimaŋa po, dii ale ka tiirim a nyini Wen jigi la.

ref: Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
text: Mi seba ayen Wen ale a nye diila ale boro kama taam wuu. Ba kan pai wari a gum du ba be kan yeeri wari a ta a nyini du. Wen a nye dila kama ayen nurubiik a zuli wa.

ref: Everything that happens has happened before, and all that will be has already been— God does everything over and over again. The Future Is Known Only to God
text: Dii ale a nye yɔgyɔgla de la a liŋ nye nya kama, dii abe le kali di nye chum po la a liŋ nye kama. Wen ale basi ate dii ale nye dipo la a ŋman pilim nye.

ref: Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice.
text: Mi nya ka wari dichoa tɛŋzuk de. Buusa boka jigini gaasa ale boro. Nyemagsika jigini gaasa ale boro.

ref: So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good.
text: Mi yaa weeni m dek ayen, Wen a gomsi ka dai a magsi wari meena ale nyeela meena, ate dila ale basi ate wa bo nuru maŋsa ale nuru baata meena buusa.

ref: All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth.
text: Ba meena a cheŋ ka jigi yeŋ, ba meena a nyini ka tanta po, tantaŋa po abe le ba meena ale wari du.

ref: Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth?
text: Ka wana ale seba a chak ase nuru chiik a jueli ka Wen jigi ate duŋ chiik a siŋ tɛŋŋa?>>

ref: I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful.
text: Mi yaa ŋman nya namsi kaai meena ale bo tɛŋzuk de la. Mi nya baai ate ba a namsi la ninyaataŋa alege ba ka maarɔ, pagrimu a jam bo ka ba namsidɔma jigi, ba jam ka maarɔ.

ref: I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living.
text: Mi yaa weeni ayen kpiema, baai ale ŋaam kpi la a ta suipeentik a gaam ŋanvutaŋa baai ale diem vua la.

ref: But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
text: Alege ba le kan diem biak baai la a zunchoŋ ba nɔi buyewa kama ba an diem nya biem buui ale nye tɛŋzuk de la.

ref: Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: Ate mi yaa nya ninam ale dii meena ate nuru a nye la ka wa ninŋmaarima ale wa vaanchoa la nyiŋ. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya, ku a nye ase ka fi le chali a vi viok diila.

ref: Yet a very little food eaten in peace is better than twice as much earned from overwork and chasing the wind.
text: Ku zunchoŋ ate fi nina a sueri ale magadekka ate fi ta la. Kan daa di fi le kasim a nam kama fi nya yega, dila abe a nye ase ka fi le chali a vi viok diila.

ref: Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense.
text: Mi ŋman nya ka wari ale di ka kiri tɛŋzuk de.

ref: For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life! It Is Better To Have a Friend
text: Nuru ale jam boro wadek wa nyiini, wa ka nidoabili yaase suokwa. Wa ninammu a ka kpeglimka, dila meena wa nina an sueri ale wa paaruŋku. Wa yaa bek ayen, <<Ka wana ate mi a nam a te, ka boa ate mi a zɛri masim dɛka?>> Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya. Ninam kayiok.

ref: You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn.
text: Nuruba baye a zunchoŋ wanyi kama, dii nyiŋla ba ale nya ka yega ba le a tom ale chaab la nyiŋ.

ref: If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble.
text: Wanyi a dan lo tɛŋ, wa doawa ale maari wa ate wa yiti. Alege ta niniga ale waai ale lo ale ka nuru ate wa a maari wa ate wa a yiti la.

ref: If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night.
text: Baye a dan doa ale chaab ba nyiŋsa a toliŋ kama. Alege nuru yeŋ nyiŋ ale nye ka sɛ a toliŋŋi?

ref: Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
text: Ba le baga a nya pagrim wanyi zuk, alege nuruba baye a baga a zɛri badek nyiŋ kama. Miisa sita a dan mɛliŋ chaab si gebika toa kama.

ref: You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice.
text: Bi kaai ale jaŋ ale ta yam la a zunchoŋ naab waai ale pak ale kan wom sinsaga la kama.

ref: Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king.
text: Dai dii dai bi paaluk ale nyini likka dɔk a jam dɛ naam yaase ba biak wa jaŋsa po wa naamu po.

ref: I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone.
text: Mi nya ale baai meena ale boro ale a cheŋ tɛŋzuk de la a va ka bi paalukku, waai ale tagri za naawa nankula po la.

ref: His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: Nuru baai ale jam dɛ wa niŋ la a ka kpeglimka. Alege baai ale jam ŋaaŋnyiŋ la sue an peenti ale waai ale za naawa nankula po la. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya, ku a nye ase ka fi ale chali a vi viok diila.

ref: Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship.
text: Kpesi fidek ase fi nin cheŋ fi puusi Wen yenni po. Fi dan wom chak zunchoŋ fi le nye betta kaabka ale poom zɛ ayen fi nye kaasi kama.

ref: Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much.
text: Kan te ate fi nɔi a valima abe fi kpesi fidek fi ale a biisi dii a te Wen la. Wen a bo ka wenŋmazuk ate fi bo tɛŋzuk de, dila biisi magadega.

ref: If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
text: Fi daa poli yegayega ku ta ka gɔdaasima a jam, ka betta ale a biisi wie yega.

ref: God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God.
text: Ase fi dan puulim a te Wen, kan beni ale nyeka. Wen sui kan peenti ale betta, nye fi le puulim diila.

ref: It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it.
text: Fi dan kan puulim ya ku zunchoŋ fi le puulim ale kan nye fi ale puulim diila.

ref: Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
text: Kan basi ate fi nɔnni a ta fu jo biem po, abe fi kan ta chaab ale biisiteerɔwa Wen yenni po ayen, <<Mi ale puulim diila m nye bɛ kama.>> Fi dan nye dila Wen sui ale puuri ale fu ate wa kaasi jaab meena ate fi nam nya la.

ref: Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
text: Gɔdaasima yegayega ale wie yegayega biisika a ka kiri ya. Dila a zuli Wen.

ref: Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do.
text: Fi dan nya ale ba a namsi ŋanjaksa tɛŋ kpieŋ po, ate nyemagsika ale wensie a karo, kan te wa ŋala a cha fu, ale ka kpagi kpien nina ale bo wa zuk, ŋayema zuk ka kpagi kpiema ale diem boro.

ref: And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
text: Tɛŋka ŋantaŋa ka ba ale soa ba meena, naawa dek a nya nyuenta ka dula.

ref: If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense.
text: Waai ale a yaali ligra la a kan ta ligra yega, waai ale a yaali jigsika la jigsika a kan paari wa. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya.

ref: The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you.
text: Ase ŋanta ale a piisi diila, ba dɛɛrɔma mɛ a piisi ka dila. Be ka boan jaab nyuenta a te ba nyɔnɔwa, ka wa pai nina a nya ba?

ref: If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
text: Tuimtomdɔ goom a masa kama, wa dɛ maga yaase wa dɛ yega wa a goa kama alege nuru waai ale jigsi la ŋantaŋa a kan te wa suik ate wa a goa.

ref: I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good.
text: Mi nya ka biem ate bu a daani tɛŋzuk de, paaruŋ ka biem a te ku nyɔnɔwa

ref: Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children.
text: yaase paaruŋ a va ka suik yoŋ a muriŋ a be dila wa dan ta nidoabili jaab karo tali a te wa.

ref: They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work.
text: Chaboala ate nuru a nyini wa ma popo a nyini, wa be pilim a cheŋ ka dila dek. Wa kan pai jaab a nyini wa gigelika nyiŋŋa a nyo wa nisaŋa po a cheŋ.

ref: That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind.
text: Kude mɛ ka biem ale ta daanika tɛŋzuk de. Ase nuru ale jam diila, dila dek ate wa a ŋmani, ka boan nyuenta ate wa nya, wa nam a te ka vioku?

ref: Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
text: Wa daaŋa meena po wa a dɛ kama legini po ale ninam kayiok ale nyiŋ wula ale suipuurum.

ref: What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do.
text: Mi yaa nya ayen ku nala kama ale chim wamaŋ ayen nuru a dɛ abe wa a nyu a chak wa gigelika ale wa ninammu nyiŋ tɛŋzuk de daa magadega ate Wen a te wa la, ka wa charuk ale la.

ref: Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you.
text: Alege Wen a dan te nuru jigsika ale ŋanta ale maari wa ate wa a dɛ ba ale masim, ate wa tuesi wa paaruŋku ale ta suipeentik, kude ka Wen tiirim.

ref: God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
text: Wa nyiem kan poli wa daaŋa ale gela diila wari ya, dii nyiŋla Wen a basi kama ate wa nina a muni ate wa sui a peenti.

ref: There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth.
text: Mi nya ka biem bu choa tɛŋzuk de ate bu dobra nna zaŋzaŋ nurubiik zuk.

ref: You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial.
text: Dai dii dai nuru ale ta bimbaansa kook ale goa ben boari, wa dan poom goa beni dii ya, wa dan kan dɛ masim wa jigsika nyiŋŋa ate ba an gu wa nalimnyiini, mi a weeni kama ayen biluak kpiuk a zunchoŋ wa kama.

ref: That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you,
text: Ka an poom nya wenbinni yaase ka seba wari ya, ka nya vuusum a gaam nuru wala kama.

ref: We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied.
text: Nurubiik a nam ka wa nɔnni nyiŋ, alege wa nɔi masimu a kan kpi.

ref: We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right.
text: Ka boan jaab zunchoŋ ate yam nyɔnɔ a ta gaam beruwa? Ka boan nyuenta ate jaŋsa nyɔnɔ ale nya ase wa nin seba wadek yikka nuruba niŋŋa?

ref: It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: Fi dan nya jabuui ate fi ta la a zunchoŋŋa fi ale a yaali yega. Ŋanta yaalika yega a ka kiri ya, ku a nye ase ka fi le chali a vi viok diila.

ref: Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us.
text: Jabuui meena ale boro la a poom ŋaam ta yuei kama, nuru abe le ta jabuui la ba poom seba kama, nuru a kan nak nanpaga ale waai ale pagra gaam wa la.

ref: The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk?
text: Wieŋa a dan piisi, ŋa kiri a gela kama, dila abe le te ka wana nyuenta?

ref: Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
text: Ka wana ale seba dii ale nala a te nuru wa boka po, daa magdega ale kan ta kiri la ate wa a taam ase yisuŋ la? Ka wana ale baga a weeni wa dii ale ku nye tɛŋzuk de wa nin cheŋ ga nueri ŋaaŋ nyiŋŋa?

ref: A good reputation at the time of death is better than loving care at the time of birth.
text: Yuei maŋ a gaam kpa buui nyum ale masa la kama, ate kum dai a zunchoŋ biam dai.

ref: It's better to go to a funeral than to attend a feast; funerals remind us that we all must die.
text: Fi dan cheŋ kuub a zunchoŋ dɛka tigi kama diila nuru meena a za wa kpi kama. Javuk meena abe a poli kude wari.

ref: Choose sorrow over laughter because a sad face may hide a happy heart.
text: Niniga a zunchoŋ laata kama, dii nyiŋla nimbie kaasika ka wamaŋ a te suinummu.

ref: Correction from someone wise is better by far than praise from fools.
text: Yam nyɔnɔ a dan toariŋ fu a zunchoŋ beruk ale a pak fu.

ref: Foolish laughter is stupid. It sounds like thorns crackling in a fire.
text: Beruk laata a nye ase ka munsa ale bo bolim po a parisi diila. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya.

ref: Something completed is better than something just begun; patience is better than too much pride.
text: Wari kpeglimka a zunchoŋ di piilimka kama ate chichiiba a zunchoŋ kanjanta.

ref: Only fools get angry quickly and hold a grudge.
text: Kan basi ate fi sui a kpabi a puuri. Ka betta sue ale kpabi a puuri.

ref: It isn't wise to ask, “Why is everything worse than it used to be?”
text: Kan begi ayen ka boa ate dila po wa a zunchoŋ daaŋa de?>> Yam a ka ku po ase fi nin bek beŋŋa de.

ref: Wisdom will protect you just like money; knowledge with good sense will lead you to life.
text: Yam a nye ase ka ligra la ba meena a maari kama. Alege yam a zunchoŋ kama, dii nyiŋla bu a vari waai ale ta bu la a basi kama.

ref: Think of what God has done! If God makes something crooked, can you make it straight?
text: Nya Wen ale nye diila. Ka wana ale baga a teenti jabuui ate wa nye ate wa goaliŋ la?

ref: When times are good, you should be cheerful; when times are bad, think about what it means. God makes them both to keep us from knowing what will happen next. Some of Life's Questions
text: Ase daaŋa po ku dan masa, ta suipeentik, ale daaŋa po ku dan kan masa, a teeri, Wen a nye dinyiwa ase ka ndila la, dila nyiŋ nuru a kan baga a miŋ wa chum po wari ya.

ref: I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper.
text: Mi bo kaai ale kan ta kiri la po mi nya ŋade buyewa kama, wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ a kpi ka wa wayɔrisimaŋa po ate gaasa nyɔnɔ a goa a beni ale wa gaasaŋa.

ref: So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart!
text: Kan ŋmasi chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ a gaam taam yaase fi ta yam a gaam taam, boa ate fi a kaasi fi dega?

ref: Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool.
text: Kan ŋmasi ta gaasa, abe fi kan chim beruwa, boa ate fi a kpi ale ge fi daa an paari yaa?

ref: Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
text: Ku nala kama ate fi yik wanyi abe fi kan basi ate wanyiwa a cheŋ. Waai ale a chali Wen la ale ta ba meena.

ref: Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
text: Yam a basi ate nuru a ta ka pagrim a gaam tɛŋ kpieŋ niŋdeerɔba pi.

ref: No one in this world always does right.
text: Wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ a ka tɛŋzuk de a nye dii ale magsi la a kan nye wabaata.

ref: Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you.
text: Kan fi wom wari meena ate nuruba a weeni la, fi le wom ale fidek tomteerɔ a boro ka a te fu.

ref: I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me.
text: Ŋade meena mi chamsi nya kama ale yam ale weeni ayen, <<Mi ale kpesi kama a nye ate m ta yam,>> alege kude a gaam m pagrim.

ref: The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep.
text: Yam ale ka dii meena la, bu zunchoŋ kama ale zuak, ka wana ale baga a nya bu?

ref: So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
text: Dila mi yaa tuliŋ m popola a basi miŋ chakka jigi ayen m kpesi gisi nya yam ale kperisa wie kiri abe m miŋ ayen ku ka koansa ase fi nin ta gaasa, ku abe a nye ase ka yesiŋsa la ase fi nin chim beruk.

ref: Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for.
text: Mi nya ayen nipooba gela a bie gaam kum kama ate wa wari a pagra ase baruk la, ba yaalika a nye ase ka ŋmiak la, ate ba nisaŋa a bobi nidoaba a tara ase chɔrima la. Nidoa waai ale nye ate Naawen sui a yɔk la ale nya varibasika ba jigi, alege wabanyeerika ba le yik wa giŋgiŋ.

ref: With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together,
text: Sagrɔwa ayen, <<Dii ate mi nya la ale nna. Mi pai ŋade meena a gum ka chaab ayen m nya kperisa meena kiri.

ref: but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman.
text: Ase m le diem boro a gisi la, mi nya ka nidoa yeŋ tusini ate mi nya la po ale wa ta wensie alege daa nipok yeŋ ba po ale wa ta wensie.

ref: I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
text: Kude nyiini ate mi nya ale Wen a nye nurubiik ayen wa ta wensie alege ba yaa va suita yega a gisi kperisa wie.>>

ref: Who is smart enough to explain everything? Wisdom makes you cheerful and gives you a smile. Obey the King
text: Ka wana ale a nye ase yam nyɔnɔwa la? Ka wana ale baga a weeni wie kiri yaa? Yam a ta ka suipeentik a jam ale a nye ate waai sui ale kaasi la sui a peenti.

ref: If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise.
text: Mi weeni ayen, siak a te naawa ale weeni diila, dii nyiŋla fi nye ka pɛka Wen niŋ.

ref: The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?”
text: Ase naawa ale a weeni dii ale gaam wari meena la, ka wana ale wa weeni wa ayen, <<Boa ale la ate fi a nye?>>

ref: If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it.
text: Waai ale siak a te naawa ale weeni diila ale vari wadek a basi. Waai ale ta yam la a nye wamaŋ ka diipo ale magsi la.

ref: Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything,
text: Dai ale boro a te wari meena ale fi le a nye diila. Alege nuru niniga a duŋ wa a basi ka tɛŋ.

ref: We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil.
text: Nuru a ka pagrim vioku zuwa a baga a ta ku, ku ka dila mɛ ate nuru waai a ka pagrim wa kum dai ya. Ase ba le kan basi nuru ate wa cheŋ kpaliŋ dai la, ku ka dila gaasa a kan basi baai ale a zamsi gaasa la.

ref: I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another? Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
text: Ŋade meena mi jam nya kama, ase mi ale pai m popola a basi wari meena zuk tɛŋzuk de la. Nuruma gela a ta pagrim kama tɛŋka zuk ate nuruba gela a nam ba nisa po.

ref: I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense.
text: Mi yaa ŋman nya gaasa nyama guka, baai le nyini jigi weleŋka a cheŋ a nya pimpauk tɛŋka po la. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya.

ref: When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime.
text: Ase ba dan kan kpabi a namsi gaasa nyama, ku le basi ayen ka nuruba a ŋmasi a kaasi wie.

ref: They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying: Everyone who lives right and respects God will prosper,
text: Dai dii dai gaasa nyɔnɔ ale kaasi wie a paari ka kook ale diem goa beni, mi seba ayen ku ale zunchoŋ a te nuru baai ale a chali Wen la, baai ale tom a te Wen la.

ref: but no one who sins and rejects God will prosper or live very long.
text: Gaasa nyam ale kaa chali Wen la, ku kan cheŋ nalimnyiini ale ba ba daaŋa mɛ a kan woŋŋa ase yisuŋ la.

ref: There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens.
text: Wari di choa ale boro a ka kiri tɛŋzuk de, nuru maŋsa a nya ka dii ale kan nala la ate nuru baata a nya dii ale nala la. Mi yaa weeni ayen kude mɛ a ka kiri ya.

ref: So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
text: Dila nyiŋ ate mi yaa weeni ayen fi dan dɛ masim fi boka po, dii ale zunchoŋ tɛŋzuk de a te nuru la ale fi a dɛ abe fi a nyu abe fi dɛ masim fi boka po. Ate mariŋka ale bo wa jigi wa tuini meena po da ŋaai meena ate Wen a te wa tɛŋzuk de la.

ref: Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world.
text: Ase mi ale nye m popola ayen m seba yam abe m kpesi nya nurubiik ninammu tɛŋzuk de la, ate wa kan goa yok ale kantueŋ la.

ref: I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
text: Mi yaa nya dii meena ate Wen a nye la. Waai an baga a miŋ dii ale a nye tɛŋzuk de la. Wa dan poom a yaali wa nye dii meena wa kan miŋ di kiri ya. Yam nyɔnɔ a dan poom sak ayen wa seba, wa kan baga a miŋi.

ref: I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad.
text: Mi yaa poli kude meena zuk a yaa weeni ayen nuru maŋsa ale yam nyam ale dii meena ate ba a nye la a bo ka Wen nisa po, alege nuru a zɛ ase ka yaalika yaase ka kisika ale a limisi ba.

ref: But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
text: Wayɔrisima ale gaasa nyam, nuru maŋsa ale nuru baata, baai ale nala ale baai ale daŋ, baai ale a nye kaabka ale baai ale kaa nye kaabka la ba meena ka wayeŋ. Ase ku le ka dii a te nuru maŋ la ku ka dila a te wabanyeerik, ase ku le ka dii a te baai ale a pɛ la, ku ka dila a te baai ale a chali yɔgsum ale pɛka la.

ref: It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die.
text: Biem ale nna wari meena po a nye tɛŋzuk de la. Wayeŋka ale a nye nurubisa suiniimaŋa po la ka gaasa ale sueri ate yesiŋsa nyeela a sueri ba popolaŋa po ale diem boro, kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba le gum kpiema po.

ref: As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
text: Waai ale vua la a ta yiila kama, ba kaai ale vua la a zunchoŋ gbeŋ kpiuk kama.

ref: We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten.
text: Diila ŋanvutaŋa a seba kama ayen ba le kpi alege ŋankpiuktaŋa a zɛ dila, ba ka tutuna a gum du ba poom baŋ ba wari kama.

ref: Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
text: Ba yaalika ale ba kisika ale ba nyuri dɛka a muriŋ bɛ kama, ba ŋman ka wari a nye ale dii meena ale a nye tɛŋzuk de la.

ref: So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do.
text: Cheŋ, dɛ fi ŋandiintaŋa ale suipeentik abe fi nyu fi daamu ale suipeentik ale ka yɔgyɔgla de ate Wen nina a sueri ale dii ate fi nye la.

ref: Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best.
text: Kasim a jo garuk peeta a kpiiri kpaam fi zukku po.

ref: Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth.
text: Kasim a dɛ masim ale fi powa waai ate fi a yaali la fi vum daaŋa po da ŋaai meena ale kan ta kiri ate Wen a te ti tɛŋzuk de la po. Ale ka fi charuk ale la fi boka po tɛŋzuk de ate fi a tuilum a nam la.

ref: Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
text: Dii meena ate fi nisa a baga a nye la, nye ale fi pagrim meena ale boosuku po, juijui ate fi a cheŋ la tomka yaase zɔkka yaase miŋ chakka yaase yam a ka dula.
