ref: Here is something else I have learned: The fastest runners and the greatest heroes don't always win races and battles. Wisdom, intelligence, and skill don't always make you healthy, rich, or popular. We each have our own share of misfortune.
text: Mi ŋman nya ka wari di choa tɛŋzuk de, chalaŋa daa waai ale a kpabi la ale soa, yaase kpaliŋka waai ale pagra la ale soa, yaase ŋandiinta a jam yam nyɔnɔ jigi ya, yaase jigsika a paari sebrɔ jigi ya, yaase ŋmanteka a cheŋ zamsidɔ jigi ya, alege wie a paari ba meena kama.

ref: None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap. Better To Be Wise than Foolish
text: Nuru waai zɛ dii ale cheena wa zuk danni po la. Ase juma ate ŋmiak a yik diila yaase baruk ale a yik nuinsa diila dila dek ate biem a bari a yik nuruba.

ref: Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me.
text: Mi ŋman nya ka yam daana ŋa chaab tɛŋzuk de ate ku nye mi masim nna yega.

ref: It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls.
text: Tɛŋ fiik ale jam boro ale nuruba nna magadega ka po. Ate naab waai ale pagra a jam wa nye kpaliŋ ale ka, wa te wa tugurik tom boanni a ga gilim ka.

ref: But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten.
text: Nuru jak ale jam bo tɛŋka po alege ta yam, wa jam vari tɛŋka a basi kama ale wa yammu. Alege waai an jam ŋman teeri nuru jakka de wari ya.

ref: So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
text: Mi weeni ayen, <<Yam a gaam pagrim kama.>> Alege nuru jakka de yammu ba jam baŋ kama an ŋmaa teeri wa wieŋa.

ref: Words of wisdom spoken softly make much more sense than the shouts of a ruler to a crowd of fools.
text: Yam nyɔnɔ waai wie ale kaa nuem la a magsi womka kama a gaam beruk kuui ale nuem la.

ref: Wisdom is more powerful than weapons, yet one mistake can destroy all the good you have done.
text: Yam a zunchoŋ tugurik ŋanta kama, alege wabanyeerik yeŋ a kaasi ka ŋan maŋ boari.

ref: A few dead flies in perfume make all of it stink, and a little foolishness outweighs a lot of wisdom.
text: Ase nanjuŋ kpiita ale basi ate kpaam a nyuŋ diila, ku ka dila ate berinni magadega a kaasi yam ale zula.

ref: Sensible thoughts lead you to do right; foolish thoughts lead you to do wrong.
text: Yam nyɔnɔ a ta ka wensie alege beruk suinum a nye ka wakaasima.

ref: Fools show their stupidity by the way they live; it's easy to see they have no sense.
text: Ase beruk a dan bo suik po, wa diem a silim ka yam ale a sak waai meena ayen wa ka beruk.

ref: Don't give up your job when your boss gets angry. If you stay calm, you'll be forgiven.
text: Ase kpagi sui a dan puuri ale fu kan basi fi tuimaŋa, fi dan nye diki wanni a kpi kama.

ref: they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
text: Mi nya yɔm kama ale ba do wusuma alege ate nabisa a cheŋ naŋta ase yɔm la.

ref: If you dig a pit, you might fall in; if you break down a wall, a snake might bite you.
text: Nuru waai ale a tu goluk la ale lo ku po, waai mɛ ale wɛ parik a jo la, waab ale dom wa.

ref: You could even get hurt by chiseling a stone or chopping a log.
text: Waai ale a mobi tana la dai dii dai ŋa le kɔni wa, waai mɛ ale a mobi daata la ti baga a kɔni wa kama.

ref: If you don't sharpen your ax, it will be harder to use; if you are wise, you'll know what to do.
text: Ase liak a dan gbiri ate ka nɔnni an saasi ya, pagrim yega ale a nyini alege yam a basi ate tuini a chim ka moali.

ref: The power to charm a snake does you no good if it bites you anyway.
text: Ase waab a dan dom baliŋdɔ alege ate wa baliŋ bu, baliŋdɔwa a ka kiri ya.

ref: If you talk sensibly, you will have friends; if you talk foolishly, you will destroy yourself.
text: Wie yam nyɔnɔ nɔi po a ta ka ŋmanteka nna yega alege beruk dek nɔi po wie ale a dɛ wa.

ref: Fools begin with nonsense, and their stupid chatter ends with disaster.
text: Piilimka wa wieŋa ka berinni, kpeglimka ŋa ka gaasa ale yesiŋsa nyeka.

ref: They never tire of talking, but none of us really know what the future will bring.
text: Wa kasim biisi ka wie a gum du. Waai zɛ dii ale cheen la, ka wana ale wa weeni wa dii ale di nye wa dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ la?

ref: Fools wear themselves out— they don't know enough to find their way home.
text: Beruk tuima a nye ate wa a jiak kama wa zɛ suik a cheŋ tɛŋka po.

ref: A country is in for trouble when its ruler is childish, and its leaders party all day long.
text: Ku ka kikaasa a te nama baai naab ale jam ka tomteerɔ la ale baai nabisa ale a dɛ saluik meena la.

ref: Some people are too lazy to fix a leaky roof— then the house collapses.
text: Nuru a dan ta nyiŋworuk wa yenni ate wa pili la ale piilim latika. Wa dan kan pili di yenni a yuli kama.

ref: Eating and drinking make you feel happy, and money can buy everything you need.
text: Tigi a ta ka laata a jam ate daam a basi ate suipeentik a boro alege ka ligri ale a nye wari meena.

ref: Don't let yourself think about cursing the king; don't curse the rich, not even in secret. A little bird might hear and tell everything.
text: Kan nye naab a la fi popolaŋa po yaase fi ka te jigsirɔ fi goom dɔk po, dii nyiŋla dai dii dai nuim ale bo vioku po a wom fi wieŋa, nuimmu ale ta fi le weeni diila a ga biisi sak.

ref: Be generous, and someday you will be rewarded.
text: Yuk fi boroboroku a basi nyaata po, diila da boari ŋaaŋnyiŋ fi le ŋman nya ku.

ref: Share what you have with seven or eight others, because you never know when disaster may strike.
text: Lab a paari buyopɔi, naaniŋ a te nuruba ale fi zɛ kaasuŋ kuui ale cheena tɛŋka zuk la.

ref: If you worry about the weather and don't plant seeds, you won't harvest a crop.
text: Waai meena ale nya viok a kan bori ba dega, baai mɛ ale a nya chiŋmaaŋa la a kan nya ŋandiinta.

ref: No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
text: Ase fi ale kan seba viok suik diila yaase nyiŋ ale a piilim dii ma popo la, ku ka dila mɛ ate fi kan miŋ Wen tuini, waai ale ka jaab meena nyeerɔ la.

ref: Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce. Youth and Old Age
text: Bori fi ŋanborintaŋa saluik, a tom ate ku paari junɔi ale fi zɛ ale ka di dii dek ale a niak la, ase ka di de yaase ka ndila yaase ŋa nɔi buyewa ale nye wayeŋŋa.

ref: Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun.
text: Bolim a nala kama ku abe le te numbinni ka masim ase bu nin nya wenbinni.

ref: Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
text: Ale ge bena yega nuru a baga a boro kama, basi ate wa dɛ ba meena masim. Alege basi ate wa teeri da ŋaai po ate wa jam bo legini po la. Ba jam piisi kama. Wari meena ale kali di jam la a ka kiri ya.

ref: Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
text: Ta suipeentik nuru paaliga, ase fi le diem paala la, abe fi te ate fi sui a peenti da ŋaai ate fi diem paala la po. Va fi suinummu yaalika ale dii meena ate fi nummu a nya la alege seba ayen wieŋa de meena nyiŋ Naawen ale bo fi buusa.

ref: Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
text: Dila nyiŋ zɛri wieŋa de fi suinum po a yeeri daanika de fi nyiŋka po ale paalim ale pagrim a ka kiri ya.

ref: Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
text: A teeri fi nyeerɔwa fi paalimu daaŋa po, ale ge jigi ate daanika daa a jam ate benaŋa a moata ate fi le weeni ayen, <<Mi an nya masim ŋa po.>>

ref: Someday the light of the sun and the moon and the stars will all seem dim to you. Rain clouds will remain over your head.
text: Ale ge ate wenbinni ale chiika ale chiŋmarisaŋa bolimu a nye birim la ate chiŋmaaŋa a ŋman va ŋmorukku;

ref: The noisy grinding of grain and the voices of singers will be shut out by your deaf ears, but even the song of a bird will keep you awake.
text: Ase suik duataŋa a dan lik ate numka nuemka a kpeglim, ase nuruba a nin wom nuinsa kumsa a yiti, alege si yiilaŋa meena a nueri.

ref: You will be afraid to climb up a hill or walk down a road. Your hair will turn as white as almond blossoms. You will feel lifeless and drag along like an old grasshopper. We each go to our eternal home, and the streets here are filled with those who mourn.
text: Ase nuruba a nin yɔgsa ale pimpitima jiga ale yɔgsa ale suik duata po chelim ase kanpoak a nin ta puuta ate nanchoŋ a vuuri ku dek a va ate koarisa masim a ŋman ka. Nuruwa ale kpi ate kumdɔma a bo suik duataŋa niŋ a cheŋ.

ref: So our bodies return to the earth, and the life-giving breath returns to God.
text: abe ni ŋman cheŋ tantaŋa po ni le nyini juijui la abe chiika a ŋmani cheŋ Wen jigi.

ref: Nothing makes sense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense. Respect and Obey God
text: Sagrɔwa weeni ayen, <<Ku ka kiri ya! Ku ka kiri ya! Wari meena a ka kiri ya!>>

ref: I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied.
text: Sagrɔwa a jam ka daa yam nyiini, alege wa jam sak nuruma ka dii ate wa seba la. Wa kpesi gisi nya a magsi wamagsima boari.

ref: Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
text: Sagrɔwa a nya wie maŋsa, dii ate wa jam ŋmarisi la jam ka chekki ale wensie.

ref: Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together.
text: Yam nyɔnɔ wieŋa a nye ase ka naapeerik doari la, wie ŋaai ate wa biisi la a nye ase ka peema ale feri jo paari diila, ka naapeerik ale biisi ŋa.

ref: My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these. There is no end to books, and too much study will wear you out.
text: Bi kpesi fidek m biiga ale sinsaga ŋa chaab. Nuruba a kasim a ŋmarisi gbaŋsa kama, zamsika yegayega ale nye ate fi jiak.

ref: Everything you were taught can be put into a few words: Respect and obey God! This is what life is all about.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de fi wom wari meena kama, wanni kpeglimka ale nna a chali Wen abe fi ta wa wieŋa ale ka nuru ale magsi wa a nye dii meena la ale nna.

ref: God will judge everything we do, even what is done in secret, whether good or bad.
text: Wen ale bo wari meena buusa ale wari dii meena ate fi suk nye la, di ka wamaŋ yaase wabiok yoo wa le bo di buusa.

ref: This is Solomon's most beautiful song. She Speaks:
text: Solomon yaalika yiilaŋa ale nna:

ref: Kiss me tenderly! Your love is better than wine,
text: Basi ate wa gbaari mu, diila wa yaalika a zunchoŋ daam kama.

ref: and you smell so sweet. All the young women adore you; the very mention of your name is like spreading perfume. *
text: Fi kpaataŋa nyummu a ta ka suipeentik. Fi yuenni a nye ase ka kpaam ale kpiiri la. Chichama a karo dii ale soa ate dɔkliema a yaali fu la.

ref: Hurry, my king! Let's hurry. Take me to your home. The Young Women Speak: We are happy for you! And we praise your love even more than wine. She Speaks: Young women of Jerusalem, it is only right that you should adore him.
text: Te ti m va fu a cheŋ, te ti nye mwuli. Basi ate naawa a ta mu jo diin goamaŋa po. Ti sue a peenti kama ale a naŋ fi nyiŋ, ti le pak fi yaalika a gaam daam. Ku magsi ba le puusi fu kama.

ref: My skin is dark and beautiful, like a tent in the desert or like Solomon's curtains.
text: Mi a sobla kama ale nala, Jerusalem liebaa, a sobla ase Kedar viita la, ase Solomon viuk garuk pala la.

ref: Don't stare at me just because the sun has darkened my skin. My brothers were angry with me; they made me work in the vineyard, and so I neglected my complexion.
text: Ka a nya mu di m le sobla la nyiŋŋa, dii nyiŋla ka wenbinni ale sob mu. Mi mawa nidoabilisaŋa sue ale jam a puuri ale mu a basi ate mi a nya kaduksaŋa zuk, mi banti mi dek kadukka a basi kama.

ref: My darling, I love you! Where do you feed your sheep and let them rest at noon? Don't let the other shepherds think badly of me. I'm not one of those women who shamelessly follow after shepherds. He Speaks:
text: Weeni mu, fi waai ate mi a yaali la, juijui ate fi piisaŋa a dɛ la ale juijui ate fi piisaŋa a vuusi kantueŋ suŋsuŋ la. Ka boa ale soa ate mi a nye ase nipok waai nina ale lik ale garuk nyaara nyaara la a bo fi doama piisaŋa gauŋ la?

ref: My dearest, if you don't know, just follow the path of the sheep. Then feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
text: Fi dan kan seba, nipok waai ale nala a gaam nipooba meena la, va piisaŋa naŋsa ate fi bua paalaŋa a dɛ piisaŋa viitaŋa gauŋ.

ref: You move as gracefully as the pony that leads the chariot of the king.
text: M nɔŋŋoa, mi pai fu a magsi chaab ale ka wusum sari ale basi ate Faaro torokoma wusum duataŋa nyiŋsa a zeenti diila.

ref: Earrings add to your beauty, and you wear a necklace of precious stones.
text: Fi tapayaasaŋa a nala kama ale tuikpana, fi ŋinni a nala ale ŋiri baŋsa.

ref: Let's make you some jewelry of gold, woven with silver. She Speaks:
text: Ti le nye ligmɔniŋ tuikpana a pai kpana a gobi te fu.

ref: My king, while you were on your couch, my aroma was a magic charm.
text: Naawa ale diem doa wa zukpaglika zuk la mi kpaamu nyummu yaa waaŋ jigini meena.

ref: you are flower blossoms from the gardens of En-Gedi. He Speaks:
text: Mi nɔŋku a nye ase ka pumɔnta ale busum nna tukki a bo En Gedi kaduksa po la.

ref: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— your eyes are those of a dove. She Speaks:
text: Nya fi le nala dii yaa, m dek nɔŋŋoa. Aao, fi le nala dii yaa. Fi ninaŋa a nyaksi ale ka yaalika.

ref: My love, you are handsome, truly handsome— the fresh green grass will be our wedding bed
text: Nya fi le ka duerɔ a nala dii yaa, m dek nɔŋŋoa. Aao, fi le a dari mi dii. Ate wusobluku ale chim ti gaduok.

ref: in the shade of cedar and cypress trees.
text: Ti yenni chibsaŋa ka nyunyoŋ, ti da chubintaŋa a chim damɔnta tiisa.

ref: I am merely a rose from the land of Sharon, a lily from the valley. He Speaks:
text: Mi a nye ase ka Saaron wupuuta, ase vaasa po wupuuta.

ref: My darling, when compared with other young women, you are a lily among thorns. She Speaks:
text: Nna ase wupuuta ale bo munsa po la, mi nɔŋku ka dila dɔklieba suŋsuŋ.

ref: And you, my love, are an apple tree among trees of the forest. Your shade brought me pleasure; your fruit was sweet.
text: Nna ase yɔna tiib ale bo gɔnni tiisa po la, mi nɔŋku ka dila nidoa paaluk suŋsuŋ. Mi a yaali ayen m kali ka wa yɔgsummu po, ate wa yɔnaŋa a masa a te mu.

ref: You led me to your banquet room and showered me with love.
text: Wa ta mi cheŋ ka ŋandiinta tigini dɔk labsuku, ate wa tiktiwa ale bo mi zuk la a chim yaalika.

ref: Refresh and strengthen me with raisins and apples. I am hungry for love!
text: Pai yɔn kosa a te mu pagrim, pai yɔna a yɔk m suinummu, diila yaalika a basi kama ate m cha.

ref: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
text: Mi kpagli ka wa gala nisaŋa, ate wa juga nisaŋa a gbaari mu.

ref: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles never to awaken love before it is ready. Winter Is Past She Speaks:
text: Puulim te mu, Jerusalem lieba, ni pɛ walik doataŋa ale walik saaŋa nyiŋ ayen ni kan kaasi ti yaalika.

ref: I hear the voice of the one I love, as he comes leaping over mountains and hills
text: Wom de! M nɔŋŋoa! Nya! Wa le nna cheena, a yɔk zi a gaam guutaŋa, a chali a va guutaŋa zuima.

ref: like a deer or a gazelle. Now he stands outside our wall, looking through the window
text: Mi nɔŋku a nye ase kab la yaase walik duok la. Nya! Wa le la a za ti parika ŋaaŋ, a va tuokpattaŋa a nya, a va nansuiŋku a chuiri a nya.

ref: and speaking to me. He Speaks: My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
text: Mi nɔŋku a jam biisi ale mi kama ayen, <<Yiti, m nɔŋŋoa, m sambuliyaa, jam va mu.

ref: Winter is past, the rain has stopped;
text: Nya! Ŋootaŋa a taam kama, ŋmottaŋa a basi nika ale taam.

ref: flowers cover the earth, it's time to sing. The cooing of doves is heard in our land.
text: Wupuuta yaa le na nyini tɛŋka, yiila yika daaŋa a jam kama, nangbaŋsa kumsa ate ti a wom ti tɛŋka po.

ref: Fig trees are bearing fruit, while blossoms on grapevines fill the air with perfume. My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
text: Kinkaŋka a boro a piilim kinkama yɔnika, ti sii ale a melim la busumka nyum masika a waaŋ jigi meena. Vaari yiti, jam, m nɔŋŋoa, m sambuliyaa, va mu jam.

ref: You are my dove hiding among the rocks on the side of a cliff. Let me see how lovely you are! Let me hear the sound of your melodious voice.
text: Mi nangbaŋka ale bo piuŋku zuk vɔrumu po la, a bo sukka jigi guutaŋa chiak la, sak mu fi nimbidiaka, basi ate m wom fi lueluku, ale ku masa kama, ate fi nimbidiaka a ta mariŋka.

ref: Our vineyards are in blossom; we must catch the little foxes that destroy the vineyards. She Speaks:
text: Yik suemkpattaŋa a te ti, suemkparuk bisaŋa ale a kaasi kaduksaŋa la, ti ti sii ale a nye puutaŋa la.

ref: My darling, I am yours, and you are mine, as you feed your sheep among the lilies.
text: Mi nɔŋku ka mi ate mi chim wa, wa bo ka wupuutaŋa po a dɛ.

ref: Pretend to be a young deer dancing on mountain slopes until daylight comes and shadows fade away.
text: Ate vanni a ga vienti ate yisuŋtaŋa a bɛ, viriŋ, m nɔŋŋoa a nye ase kab la yaase walik paalik ale bo gu tii ale churinti la zuk la.

ref: While in bed at night, I reached for the one I love with heart and soul. I looked for him, but he wasn't there.
text: Yɔkku meena mi gaduokku zuk mi a gisi ka waai ate mi suinummu a yaali la, mi gisi wa kama alege an nya wa.

ref: So I searched through the town for the one I love. I looked on every street, but he wasn't there.
text: Mi le yiti kama yɔgyɔgla de a cheŋ tɛŋka po, a va suitaŋa ale gugottaŋa, m le gisi waai ate m suinummu a yaali la. Dila mi yaa gisi wa alege an nya wa.

ref: I even asked the guards patrolling the town, “Have you seen the one I love so much?”
text: Limisidɔma a yaa nya mi ase ba le a gilim tɛŋka la. <<Nama nya waai ate mi suinummu a yaali la?>>

ref: Right after that, I found him. I held him and would not let go until I had taken him to the home of my mother.
text: Mi ale din ga basi ba la mi deri nya wa. Mi yaa yik wa a kan siak ayen wa cheŋ ate mi ga ta wa jam mi mawa yenni, dɔk kuui po ate mi mawa a yik mi lɔgni la.

ref: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles, never to awaken love before it is ready. The Groom and the Wedding Party Their Friends Speak:
text: Puulim te mu, Jerusalem lieba ni pɛ walik doataŋa ale walik saaŋa nyiŋ ayen ni kan daani ti yaalika.

ref: What do we see approaching from the desert like a cloud of smoke? With it comes the sweet smell of spices, including myrrh and frankincense.
text: Ka wana ale la a nyini gɔnni a cheena ase nyuisa ale a jueli wen nna dek dek la ate nyum a nye ase ŋan baai nyum ale masa la ate ba pai geruŋdɔ ŋanta a nye?

ref: It is King Solomon carried on a throne, surrounded by sixty of Israel's best soldiers.
text: Solomon ale cheena, a ji wa naam zukpaglika zuk, tugurik tɔŋdɔba pisiyuebi ale a vi wa ŋaaŋ, Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔ naliŋsa.

ref: Each of them wears a sword. They are experts at fighting, even in the dark.
text: Ba meena a yik ka gebisa, ba meena a sebi ka kpaliŋ nyeka, waai meena a su ka gebik wa gauŋ, a gomsi magsi yok ba nin siti ba.

ref: Its posts are silver, the back is gold, and the seat is covered with purple cloth. You women of Jerusalem have taken great care to furnish the inside.
text: Ka daataŋa wa nye ale ka kpana, naŋsaŋa kieŋa a chim ligmɔniŋ. Ka kalika jigini a pai garuk naliŋ a nye, ate Jerusalem lieba a yɔk.

ref: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— as you look through your veil, your eyes are those of a dove. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
text: Nya fi le nala dii yaa, m dek nɔŋŋoa! Aao, fi le nala dii yaa! Fi ninaŋa garuk nyaara nyaaraŋa po a nyaksi ale ka yaalika. Fi zuisaŋa a nye ase bua boari ale nyini Gilead Guuku zuk a siŋ la.

ref: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
text: Fi nyinaŋa a peenti ase ka piisa ate ba che ŋa kɔbta a sugri la. Kunyi an bɛ ya, ŋa meena a magsi ka chaab chappi.

ref: Your lips are crimson cords, your mouth is shapely; behind your veil are hidden beautiful rosy cheeks.
text: Fi nɔngbanvaataŋa a nye ase ka garucha mɔnuŋ la, ti le nala dii ase fi nin boro a biisi. Fi tapayaasaŋa a nyaksi kama garuk nyaara nyaaraŋa po.

ref: Your neck is more graceful than the tower of David, decorated with thousands of warriors' shields.
text: Fi ŋinni a nye ase ka Deevid kiani la a vili ale solisi, ale ŋiri baŋ ase ŋanchɔgsinta tusidi ale yik du a gilim la.

ref: Your breasts are perfect; they are twin deer feeding among lilies.
text: Fi biisaŋa a nye ase ka walisa la, kab yibsa ale za wupuuta po a dɛ la.

ref: I will hasten to those hills sprinkled with sweet perfume and stay there till sunrise.
text: Mi ale bo zauŋ kunuŋ guuku zuk, ŋan baai nyum ale masa la guuku zuk, ate saluik vayɔgsummu a ga fuk ate legini a muriŋ bɛ.

ref: My darling, you are lovely in every way.
text: Fi nala ka meena, m nɔŋŋoa. Kaasuŋ a ka fi jigi ya.

ref: My bride, together we will leave Lebanon! We will say goodbye to the peaks of Mount Amana, Senir, and Hermon, where lions and leopards live in the caves.
text: Va mu a nyini Lebanon, m pok fiaga, va mu a nyini Lebanon. Nyini Amana guuku zuk a siŋ, a nyini Senir guuku ale Yermon guuku zuk a siŋ, juijui ate gbeŋmaŋa ale yɔŋma a boro la.

ref: My bride, my very own, you have stolen my heart! With one glance from your eyes and the glow of your necklace, you have stolen my heart.
text: Fi zu mi suinummu kama, m dek tua, m pok fiaga. Fi zu mi suinummu kama ale fi ninaŋa ale chiak nya mi bunyi la, ale fi ŋinni baŋ yeŋ dekki.

ref: Your lips are a honeycomb; milk and honey flow from your tongue. Your dress has the aroma of cedar trees from Lebanon.
text: Fi nɔngbanvaataŋa a lɔnsi ka masim ase samparima la, m pok fiaga, biisim ale siita ale bo fi giŋgeluŋku tɛŋ. Fi gattaŋa nyummu a nye ase ka Lebanon la.

ref: My bride, my very own, you are a garden, a fountain closed off to all others.
text: Fi a nye ase ka kaduk kaai ale suk, m dek tua, m pok fiaga, fi ka bulik kaai ale ligi, vili dii ale ligi.

ref: Your arms are vines, covered with delicious fruits and all sorts of spices— henna, nard,
text: Fi tiisaŋa a nye ase yɔn gilima ti boari la, a yɔni yɔn maŋsa, ale a nye ase kpa buui nyum ale masa la,

ref: saffron, calamus, cinnamon, frankincense, myrrh, and aloes —all the finest spices.
text: yaase ŋan baai meena nyum ale masa la.

ref: You are a spring in the garden, a fountain of pure water, and a refreshing stream from Mount Lebanon. She Speaks:
text: Fi ka kaduk po bulik, vili dii ate nyiam a buli a nyini Lebanon a siŋ a jam.

ref: Let the north wind blow, the south wind too! Let them spread the aroma of my garden, so the one I love may enter and taste its delicious fruits.
text: Vaari yiti, wiiluk geŋ viowa, a jam, yeseok geŋ viowa. Fuk m kadukka zuk ate ka nyummu a waaŋ jigi meena. Basi ate m nɔŋku a jam jo wa kadukka po a lam ka yɔn maŋsaŋa.

ref: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
text: Mi jam jo ka m kadukka po, m dek tua, m pok fiaga. Mi tigsi m zaankuŋku ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la kama. Mi dɛ m samparimaŋa ale m siitaŋa kama, mi nyu m daamu ale m biisimu kama. Ni dɛ, m doaba, abe le nyu, ni nyu chak, m nɔŋta.

ref: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
text: Mi goa kama alege mi suinum po mi yiti kama. Wom, mi nɔŋku a nak kama. Lak te mu, m dek tua, m nɔŋŋoa, m nangbaŋŋa, m dek waai ale kan ta kaasuŋ la. Mi zukku a yɔk ale ka maglim, m zuisaŋa a mooŋ ale yokku pikka.

ref: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?
text: Mi yeeri m garukku kama. Ku a fɛ ayen m ŋman jo ku yaa? Mi sugri m naŋsaŋa kama. Ku a fɛ ayen m ŋman daŋ si yaa?

ref: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
text: Mi nɔŋku a pai ka wa nisa a yik tuoku, ate mi sui a peenti wa le moata la.

ref: When I rose to open the door, my hands and my fingers dripped with perfume.
text: Mi jam gomsi kama ayen m te ti wa jo. Mi nisaŋa a tiri zaankuŋ, mi nandubsaŋa a tiri zaankuŋ nyiam ase mi ale yik tuoku ja yigimu la.

ref: And I yearned for him while he spoke to me, but when I opened the door, my darling had disappeared. I searched and shouted, but I could not find him— there was no answer.
text: Mi yaa jam lak te m nɔŋku, alege mi nɔŋku a cheŋ, wa jam cheŋ. Mi suinum a daani wa le cheŋ la. Mi yaa jam gisi wa alege an nya wa. Mi jam wi wa alege wa an tulisi ya.

ref: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.
text: Limisidɔma yaa nya ase ba le jam a gilim tɛŋ nummu la. Ba nak mi, ba te mi mula, ba yeeri mi garukku ta cheŋ, parisaŋa limisidɔ bala.

ref: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:
text: Ni puulim te mu, Jerusalem lieba. Ni dan nya m nɔŋku, ni le weeni mu ayen ka boa? Ni weeni wa ayen yaalika a basi kama ate mi cha.

ref: Most beautiful of women, why is the one you love more special than others? Why do you ask us to tell him how you feel? She Speaks:
text: Fi le a yaali waai la a zunchoŋ mbala ka sɛ, fi nala a gaam ka nipooba meena? Fi le a yaali waai la a nye ka sɛ a zunchoŋ mbala, ate ti a te fu ti puulimka?

ref: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven.
text: Wa zukku a nye ase ka ligmɔniŋ weleŋ la, wa zuisaŋa a yuk, a sob ase tagaaruk la.

ref: His eyes are a pair of doves bathing in a stream flowing with milk.
text: Wa ninaŋa a nala kama ase nangbaŋsa ale bo beli naŋsa nyiam nɔi la, nangbaŋsa ale sugri si dek biisim po a za beli naŋ nɔi la.

ref: His face is a garden of sweet-smelling spices; his lips are lilies dripping with perfume.
text: Wa tapayaasaŋa a nye ase ŋan baai nyum ale masa la gaduata a ta nyum nyiini. Wa nɔngbanvaataŋa a nye ase ka wupuuta ate zaankuŋ a zi.

ref: His arms are branches of gold covered with jewels; his body is ivory decorated with sapphires.
text: Wa nisimaŋa ka ligmɔniŋ doa a nye ale tintain salima. Wa nyiŋka a nye ase ka yauk nyin ale salisi la a ŋmirisi ale tintain sobta.

ref: His legs are columns of marble on feet of gold. He stands there majestic like Mount Lebanon and its choice cedar trees.
text: Wa naŋsaŋa a nye ase ka tintain mɔnta zaŋŋa a za ligmɔniŋ weleŋ zuk la. Wadek a nye ase ka Lebanon nyunyoŋta ate ba luk yeeri la.

ref: His kisses are sweet. I desire him so much! Young women of Jerusalem, he is my lover and friend.
text: Wa nɔnni dek potim ka masim nyiini, wa wari meena mi a yaali kama. Mi nɔŋku ale nna, mi doawa de, Jerusalem liebaa.

text: Azaya waai ale jam ka Amoz nidoabili la, gɔdaasimaŋa ate wa jam nya a ta va Juda ale Jerusalem zuk la. Diipo ate Yuzaya a dɛ naam Juda tɛŋka po ale pa te Jotam ate wa mɛ a pai te Ayazi ate wa mɛ a pai te Azekaya la.

text: Dan kan daa ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale basi ate ti ba gela a vua, tama ate le nye ase ka Sodom ale Gomora la.

ref: You are no better than the leaders and people of Sodom and Gomorrah! So listen to the Lord God:
text: Ni wom Naawen wanni, nama Sodom niŋdeerɔma. Ni wom ti Wen sinsaŋŋa, nama Gomora nuruma.

text: Ni nyiem ale jam mi niŋ la, ka wana ale bek jaab a nyini ni jigi ya, ate ni basi ate ŋantaŋa de a nyiem mi yenni po?

ref: Your sacrifices are worthless, and your incense disgusting. I can't stand the evil you do on your New Moon Festivals or on your Sabbaths and other times of worship.
text: Ni basi tiirim tii ale kan ta kiri la ta jamka. Mi a kisi ni ŋan baai nyum ale masa ate ni ju a te mi la kama. Ni a kpesi Chi Paalisa tiŋŋa ale Vuusum Daaŋa ale chaab gumka tiŋŋa. Alege mi a kan baga a bo ale ni, dii nyiŋla biem ale bo ni suŋsuŋ.

ref: I hate your New Moon Festivals and all others as well. They are a heavy burden I am tired of carrying.
text: Mi a kisi ni Chi Paalisa tiŋŋa ale tiga ŋaai ate ni lueri la kama. Ŋa chim ka jibta a te mi. Mi jiak ale ŋa taka kama.

ref: Wash yourselves clean! I hate your filthy deeds. Stop doing wrong
text: Ni so nidek ate ni nala. Ni pai ni tuimbaataŋa a ta nyini mi niŋ. Ni basi tom kaasika nyeka.

ref: and learn to live right. See that justice is done. Defend widows and orphans and help the oppressed.” An Invitation from the Lord
text: Ni zamsi a nye dii ale nala. Ni gisi wensie abe ni a te baai ale a nam la nyiŋbiiri. Ni a maari baai ale kan ka koba la ale pukɔga ba wie po.

ref: I, the Lord, invite you to come and talk it over. Your sins are scarlet red, but they will be whiter than snow or wool.
text: <<Ni jam yɔgyɔgla de ate ti poli ale chaab.>> Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Ni wabaataŋa a dan muni, ti ale peenti nna tektek. Ti dan poom muni, ti ale peenti ase kɔb peeta la.

ref: If you willingly obey me, the best crops in the land will be yours.
text: Ase ni daa yaali ale a wom mi nɔi, ni ale dɛ ŋan maŋsa tɛŋka po.

ref: But if you turn against me, your enemies will kill you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
text: Alege nama a dan zɛri mi nɔi ale nye tukpari, ba ale ko ni ale gebik.>> Naawen ale pai wa nɔi a biisi.

ref: Jerusalem, you are like an unfaithful wife. Once your judges were honest and your people lived right; now you are a city full of murderers.
text: Ni nya wensie tɛŋ kpieŋka a yaa le chim taabuk la! Wa jam chim ka waai ale jam ta wensie. Wayɔrisima a jam bo wa po kama. Alege yɔgyɔgla de ba yaa ka nuru koorisa.

ref: Your silver is fake, and your wine is watered down.
text: Ni kpanaŋa a ka kiri ya. Ba pai ka nyiam a dam daam buui ate ni a yaali la.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the mighty ruler of Israel, and I make you a promise: You are now my enemy, and I will show my anger by taking revenge on you.
text: Dila nyiŋ Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Waai Ale Ka Izirali Tanjaŋini La ale a weeni ayen, <<Mi ale nya vuusum a nyini m dachaasaŋa jigi abe m namsi m dachaasaŋa.

ref: I will punish you terribly and burn away everything that makes you unfit to worship me.
text: Mi ale viriŋ a ta chaab ale ni. Mi ale yeeri ŋan baai ale kan ta kiri la ni po ale ni ŋan baai meena ale kan welema la.

ref: Jerusalem, you will be saved by showing justice; Zion's people who turn to me will be saved by doing right.
text: Zayon ale va nyemagsika nyiŋ a nya datuesika. Baai ale siak ba kaasuŋ la ale va wayɔrisima nyiŋ a nya datuesika.

ref: But those rebellious sinners who turn against me, the Lord, will all disappear.
text: Alege tukpari ale wabanyeerisa ale waaŋ chaab, baai ale zɛri Naawen la a za ba kpi kama.

ref: You will be made ashamed of those groves of trees where you worshiped idols.
text: <<Kiŋkaŋ peruk weleŋsaŋa ate ni ta suipeentik si nyiŋla, chivie ale yik ni. Tattaŋa ate ni lueri la nyiŋ, chivie ale yik ni.

ref: You will be like a grove of trees dying in a drought.
text: Ni za ni nye ase ka kinkaŋ peruk vaata ale kɔ la. Ni a nye ase ka talim buui ale kan ta nyiam la.

ref: Your strongest leaders will be like dry wood set on fire by their idols. No one will be able to help, as they all go up in flames.
text: Nuru pagrɔwa ale nye ase ka wukosik la, wa tuimaŋa mɛ a nye ase ka chesik la, ba meena bolim ale dɛ ba ate waai a kan boro a kpimsi bu.>>

ref: This is the message I was given about Judah and Jerusalem:
text: Amoz nidoabinni Azaya ale nya dii a ta va Juda ale Jerusalem zuk la ale nna.

ref: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills; every nation will rush to it.
text: Dai kpeglimaŋa po, Naawen yenni guuku ale zaani ase naab la guutaŋa po. Ku ale yiti ŋmai a gaam guutaŋa, ate tɛŋsa meena ale chuiri a cheŋ ku jigi.

ref: Many people will come and say, “Let's go to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
text: Nuru boari ale jam a weeni ayen, <<Ni jam ate ti jueli Naawen guuku, ti jueli Jekob Wen yenni. Wa ale sak ti Wa suitaŋa ate ti baga a cheŋ ti po.>> Wa sinsaŋŋa ale nyini Zayon a cheŋ. Ate Naawen wanni ale nyini Jerusalem.

ref: People of Israel, let's live by the light of the Lord. Following Sinful Customs
text: Jekob dɔkdemma abe jam ate ti cheŋ Naawen bolimu po.

ref: Our Lord, you have deserted your people, Israel, because they follow customs of nations from the east. They worship Philistine gods and are close friends of foreigners.
text: Fi zɛri fidek nuruma Jekob dɔkdemma kama. A nyini Kori geŋsa, ku kasim a sueri ale ka kperisa tuima. Ba a tom ka sampoporinni tuima ase Filistia demma la, ale a nak ba nisima ale baai ale kan seba Wen la.

ref: They have endless treasures of silver and gold; they have countless horses and war chariots.
text: Ba tɛŋka a sueri ale ka kpana ale ligmɔniŋ. Ba tuilum ŋantaŋa a ka kpeglimka. Ba torokoma a ka kpeglimka.

ref: And so, all of them will be ashamed and disgraced. Don't forgive them! A Day of Judgment
text: Dila Naawen ale te nuru siŋ tɛŋ ate nurubiik a zaab wadek. Kan vua a te ba.

ref: Every one of you, go hide among the rocks and in the ground, because the Lord is fearsome, marvelous, and glorious.
text: Ni cheŋ pinaŋa po, ni suk tɛŋka po a nyini Naawen kpazinagsuku po ale wa naamu nalimu po.

ref: When the Lord comes, everyone who is proud will be made humble, and the Lord alone will be honored.
text: Nuru waai ale a nya wadek nna se wa gaam nuruba la ale zaab wadek, ate kanjanta nyam ale siŋ tɛŋ. Ka Naawen nyiini ale za wa nya zakzaanika da dila danni.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful has chosen a day when those who are proud and conceited will be put down.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a lueri ka dai a magsi kanjanta nyam ale kayeruk nyam ale zak badek a zaani la, ba meena ale zaab badek.

ref: The tall and towering cedars of Lebanon will be destroyed. So will the oak trees of Bashan,
text: Wa lueri ka dai a magsi Lebanon nyunyoŋtaŋa meena ale woŋŋa ale ta kayeruk la ale Basan kinkaŋpettaŋa meena.

ref: all high mountains and hills,
text: Guuk woŋta ale guuk tii ale jueli la meena ale

ref: all the seagoing ships, and every beautiful boat.
text: Tarsis ŋaaruŋ meena ale ŋaaruŋ naluŋ meena.

ref: When that day comes, everyone who is proud will be put down. Only the Lord will be honored.
text: Nurubiik kanjantaŋa ale siŋ tɛŋ ate nurubisa ale zaab badek ale ba kanjantaŋa. Ka Naawen nyiini ale za wa soa zakzaanika da dila danni.

ref: Idols will be gone for good.
text: Ate bɔgta meena ale muriŋ bɛ.

ref: You had better hide in caves and holes— the Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth.
text: Nurubisa ale chali a jo pina vie ale tɛŋka vieŋa po, dii nyiŋla Naawen kpazinagsuk ale wa naamu nalimu nyiŋ. Wa ale yiti kama a choa tɛŋka.

ref: On that day everyone will throw to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold they made to worship.
text: Da dila danni nuruba ale yuk ba bɔgtaŋa tii ate ba pai kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a nye ayen ba a puusi la a te ŋooma ale kpinkpirinsa.

ref: The Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth— they will hide in caves and in the hills.
text: Ba ale yiti a jo vie pinaŋa po ale pina ŋaai ale yik wen a churinti la po, a nyini Naawen kpazinagsuk ale wa naamu nalimu nyiŋ, wa ale yiti kama a choa tɛŋka.

ref: Stop trusting the power of humans. They are all going to die, so how can they help?
text: Kan mariŋ nuru biiga, waai ale ta vuusum wa nyuevie po la, wa ka boa?

ref: The mighty Lord All-Powerful is going to take away from Jerusalem and Judah everything you need— your bread and water, *
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ni nya, Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, a za wa tuesi Jerusalem ale Juda jigi ŋan baai ate wa a te ale a maari la kama. Wa le basi ŋandiintaŋa ale nyiamu teka meena.

ref: soldiers and heroes, judges and prophets, leaders and army officers,
text: Nuru tuaka ale tugurik tɔŋdɔwa ale boteerɔwa ale biisiteerɔwa ale baanɔwa ale nisɔmawa,

ref: He will let children and babies become your rulers.
text: Mi ale basi ate nidoabilisa a chim ba kpaga. Bi fiisa ale nya ba zuk.

ref: You will each be cruel to friends and neighbors. Young people will insult their elders; no one will show respect to those who deserve it.
text: Nuruba ale namsi chaab, nidoa ale ta chaab ale wa choa, ate kali mɔtidɔ ale ta chaab ale wa choa. Bi paaluk ale yiti a ta chaab ale ŋankpagsa. Nuru baai ale kan ta zula la ale yiti a ta chaab ale baai ale ta zula la.

ref: Some of you will grab hold of a relative and say, “You still have a coat. Be our leader and rule this pile of ruins.”
text: Nuru ale yiti a yik wa suata po wanyi wa ko yeri po ayen. <<Fi ale ta garuk la nyiŋ, chim ti niŋdeerɔ. Be soa ŋan baai meena ale kaasi la zuk a nya.>>

ref: But the answer will be, “I can't do you any good. Don't make me your leader. There's no food or clothing left in my house.”
text: Alege da dila danni wa ale kaari a weeni ayen, <<Mi zɛ mi ale m nye diila. Mi ka ŋandiinta yaase gatta m yenni po, kan nye mu ate m chim nuruba niŋdeerɔ.>>

ref: Jerusalem and Judah, you rebelled against your glorious Lord— your words and your actions, made you stumble and fall.
text: Jerusalem a ja kama, Juda a lo kama. Ba wieŋa ale ba tuima a nye a kaasi ka Naawen ale a taŋ wa zulaŋa.

ref: The look on your faces shows that you are sinful as Sodom, and you don't try to hide it. You are in for trouble, and you have brought it all on yourselves. The Wrong Kind of Leaders
text: Fi dan nya ba ninaŋa po, ku ale sum a sak fu ayen ba sum nye kaasi kama. Ba a tigsi ba wabaataŋa ase ka Sodom tɛŋka demma la. Ba kan suk bu. Ku ale toa a te ba. Ba ta ka kaasuŋ a jam badek zuk.

ref: Tell those who obey God, “You're very fortunate— you will be rewarded for what you have done.”
text: Weeni wayɔrisima nyama ayen ku ale niak a te ba. Ba ale dɛ masim a ta va ba tuimaŋa ŋanta nyiŋ.

ref: Tell those who disobey, “You're in big trouble— what you did to others will come back to you.”
text: Ku ale toa a te gaasa nyam. Kaasuŋ ale jam ba zuk. Ba ale nya ba ale pai ba nisimaŋa a tom tuim ŋaai la tutuna.

ref: Though you are God's people, you are ruled and abused by women and children. You are confused by leaders who guide you down the wrong path.
text: Bi paalukku a namsi mi nuruma, ate nipooba mɛ ta pagrim a nya ba zuk. Mi nuru baai ale a dɛ ni niŋ la a ta ni a cheŋ a bɛ kama. Ba basi suiku kama.

ref: The Lord is ready to accuse and judge all nations.
text: Naawen a kali wa kalika jigini boteka yenni po kama. Wa abe yiti kama ayen wa bo nuruma buusa.

ref: He will even judge you rulers and leaders of his own nation. You destroyed his vineyard and filled your houses by robbing the poor.
text: Naawen abe boro ayen wa bo nisɔmma ale wa nuruma niŋdeerɔma buusa. <<Ka nama ale kaasi mi kadukka. Ale ŋman pai ŋanjaksaŋa ŋantaŋa a basi ni yeeŋa po.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful says, “You have crushed my people and rubbed in the dirt the faces of the poor.” The Women of Jerusalem
text: Boan nyiŋ ate ni a kaasi mi nuruma ale ŋman a num ŋanjaksaŋa nina?>> Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni dila.

ref: The Lord says: The women of Jerusalem are proud and strut around, winking shamelessly. They wear anklets that jingle and call attention to the way they walk.
text: Naawen ale weeni ayen, <<Zayon nipooma a ta ka kanjanta. Ba chelim po, ba a yeeri ka ba ŋieŋa a sak. Ba nyiem nya nidoaba kama a cheŋ koarisa chelim ale su baŋsa ba naŋsa po ate si a nak chaab a kum.

ref: But I, the Lord, will cover their heads with sores, and I will uncover their private parts.
text: Dila nyiŋla, Nyɔnɔwa ale basi ate nira a nye Zayon nipooma zuimaŋa. Naawen ale basi ate ba zuisa a kpa.>>

ref: In place of perfume, there will be a stink; in place of belts, there will be ropes; in place of fancy hairdos, they will have bald heads. Instead of expensive clothes, they will wear sackcloth; instead of beauty, they will have ugly scars.
text: Ku ale magsi ku chim nyum masik la ku le chim ka nyum biok, ku le magsi ku chim garuk pali la ku le chim ka miik, ku ale magsi ku chim zuisa la ku le chim ka zuk kpaauŋ. Ate garuk naluŋ ale chim boorik garuk, ku le magsi ku chim nalim la ku le chim ka chivie.

ref: The fighting men of Jerusalem will be killed in battle.
text: Gebik ale lɔnsi fi nidoama tɛŋ ate fi tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale kpi kpaliŋ po.

ref: The city will mourn and sit in the dirt, emptied of its people.
text: Zayon nansuiŋtaŋa ale fɔbili abe ba a kum. Wa za wa kali ka tɛŋka wa kan ta jaaboa.

ref: When this happens, seven women will grab the same man, and each of them will say, “I'll buy my own food and clothes! Just marry me and take away my disgrace.” The Lord Will Bless His People Who Survive
text: Dai dila danni, nipooba bayopɔi ale yik nidoa yeŋ a weeni wa ayen, <<Tama ale dɛ tidek ŋandiinta abe ti yaali tidek gatta a jɔ, fi tin siak ate ti a wi fu ayen ti chorɔ. Ate dila ale lik tama chivieŋa.>>

ref: The time is coming when the Lord will make his land fruitful and glorious again, and the people of Israel who survive will take great pride in what the land produces.
text: Dai dila danni, Naawen Tiib Naŋ ale ta nalim ale zula, ate tɛŋka yɔnaŋa ale chim baai ale vuuk la kanjanta ale zula Izirali tɛŋka po.

ref: after the Lord sends a fiery judgment to clean the city and its people of their violent deeds.
text: Nyɔnɔwa ale sugri Zayon nipooma daŋtaŋa a basi. Wa ale pai buusa boka chiik ale bolim chiik a duisi ziim buui ale maŋ Jerusalem la a basi.

ref: Then the Lord will cover the whole city and its meeting places with a thick cloud each day and with a flaming fire each night. God's own glory will be like a huge tent that covers everything.
text: Ate Naawen ale nye ate chiŋmari ale nyuisa a bo Zayon Guuku ale baai ale tigsi dula la zuk kantueŋ abe bolim ŋiak a bo ba zuk yok. Viuk ale ku bo zulaŋa meena zuk.

ref: It will provide shade from the heat of the sun and a place of shelter and protection from storms and rain.
text: Ku ale chim ka kusuŋ ale yɔgsum jigi ate kantueŋ kaa nak ba, ale varibasika ale sukka jigi ate vioku ale ŋmorukku kaa paari ba.

ref: I will sing a song about my friend's vineyard that was on the side of a fertile hill.
text: Mi ale yi yiili a te waai ate mi a yaali la. Wa kadukka wari yiili. Mi ale a yaali waai la a ta ka kaduk, ate ka poak a bo guuku geŋ.

ref: My friend dug the ground, removed the stones, and planted the best vines. He built a watchtower and dug a pit in rocky ground for pressing the grapes. He hoped they would be sweet, but bitter grapes were all it produced.
text: Wa tu tɛŋka kama a yeeri tana ŋaai ale boro la, alege a yaa vuk tiisa sii ate wa a yaali la. Wa sɛ ka yeri ate di woŋŋa kadukka po ale ŋman nye daam ŋmiaka jigi. Wa jam a gisi ka tiib sii ale ta yɔn maŋsa la, alege si meena a jam yɔni ka yɔn baata.

ref: Listen, people of Jerusalem and of Judah! You be the judge of me and my vineyard.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de, nama baai ale bo Jerusalem la ale nidoa baai ale bo Juda la, ni weeni dii ale bo mi ale m kadukka suŋsuŋ la.

ref: What more could I have done for my vineyard? I hoped for sweet grapes, but bitter grapes were all that grew.
text: Ka boa ate mi ale nye a te m kadukka a ŋman gaam mi ale nye diila? Mi ale a gisi yɔn ŋaai ale nala la, ka boan nyiŋ ate si yɔni yɔn baata?

ref: Now I will let you know what I am going to do. I will cut down the hedge and tear down the wall. My vineyard will be trampled and left in ruins.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de, mi ale weeni ni. Mi ale za m nye m kadukka diila. Mi ale yeeri ka geruku a basi ate ka kaasi. Mi ale nak ka siaka a lɔnsi tɛŋ, ate ba ale tabi ka zuk.

ref: It will turn into a desert, neither pruned nor hoed; it will be covered with thorns and briars. I will command the clouds not to send rain.
text: Mi ale nye ate tɛŋka a kan ta kiri ya, m kan ŋman yoarisi tiisaŋa naŋsaŋa yaase m kpa ka po. Mi ale basi ate ŋankayaata ale muŋsa a nyini tɛŋka zuk. Mi ale weeni chiŋmaaŋa ate ŋmoruk a kan ni ka po.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful! Israel is the vineyard, and Judah is the garden I tended with care. I had hoped for honesty and for justice, but dishonesty and cries for mercy were all I found. Isaiah Condemns Social Injustice
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La kadukka ka Izirali yenni ale Juda nidoama a chim kaduk ate wa mariŋ. Ate wa jam a gisi nyemagsika, alege wa taam goanti a nya ziim nyinika. Wa jam a yaali ka wayɔrisima alege wa goanti wom nyiŋdomma kumsa.

ref: You are in for trouble! You take over house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone else in all the land.
text: Ku ale toa a te ni, nama baai ale pai nuruba yie a gum yeeŋa po la ale pai tɛŋsa a gum tɛŋsa po la, ate ku ga paari diipo ate peelim an ŋman tali la, ate nidek ni nyiini bo tɛŋka po la.

ref: But the Lord All-Powerful has made this promise to me: Those large and beautiful homes will be left empty, with no one to take care of them.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a weeni kama ate mi a wom wa ayen, <<Chekki yie ŋaai ale zuak la ale kaasi, ate yie kpiema ŋaai ale nala tali la nuruba a kan bo ŋa po.

ref: None of them are tired. They don't sleep or get drowsy, and they run without stumbling. Their belts don't come loose; their sandal straps don't break.
text: Ba waai an poom jiak ya, yaase wa nak naŋŋa. Ba wanyi mɛ an goa a jɔgsi ya yaase wa poom a goa ya. Ba waai chiak gbaŋ an foli a nyini wa chiaka po. Ba waai nuensiri an poom a kaasi ya.

ref: You are in for trouble! The lies you tell are like ropes by which you drag along sin and evil.
text: Ku ale toa a te baai ale pai pimpaasima miik a dari wabiok la, ale baai mɛ ale pai miik a dari gaasa la.

ref: You are in for trouble! You get up early to start drinking, and you keep it up late into the night.
text: Ku ale toa ate nama baai ale a yiti saluik yokyok chali a vi daam la, ale nama baai nyiem ale bo daam nyuka po a ga paari yok diipo a buk la.

ref: At your drinking parties you have the music of stringed instruments, tambourines, and flutes. But you never even think about all the Lord has done,
text: Ba ta ka kpanta ale bagansa ale kayaksa ale paampuuŋta ale daam ba ŋandiinta tiŋŋa po, alege ba niŋ ka Naawen tuimaŋa po, ba ka zula a te wa nisa tuimaŋa.

ref: and so his people know nothing about him. That's why many of you will be dragged off to foreign lands. Your leaders will starve to death, and everyone else will suffer from thirst.
text: Dila nyiŋ, ba ale yik m nuruma a ta cheŋ tɛŋ yoŋ po, ba ale a silim miŋka la nyiŋ. Ba nuru baai ale ta kpaŋta la, ale kpi ale kom, ate nyanyuila ale ko ba nuru boanni.

ref: The world of the dead has opened its mouth wide and is eagerly waiting for the leaders of Jerusalem and for its noisy crowds, especially for those who take pride in that city.
text: Dila nyiŋla, vɔrumu a basi kama ate bu koarisaŋa a zuak ate bu lak bu nɔnni nna yegayega. Ba kpaŋŋa ale nuru boanni ale siŋ bu po ale ba wɔkwɔk nyama ale baai ale a dɛ masim la meena.

ref: Its citizens have been put down, and its proud people have been brought to shame.
text: Dila nyiŋ nuru meena ale siŋ tɛŋ ate nurubiik ale zaab wadek, ate kanjanta nyam ale zaab badek.

ref: But the holy Lord God All-Powerful is praised, because he has shown who he is by bringing justice.
text: Alege Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale nya zak zaanka wa nyemagsika nyiŋ, ate tuilum Wenni ale sak wa tuilummu a ta va wa wayɔrisimaŋa nyiŋ.

ref: His people will be like sheep grazing in their own pasture, and they will take off what was left by others.
text: Ate piisa ale ŋɔbi wuyɔgsuk ase ka ŋa dɛka jigi la. Ate pabisa ale dɛ jigsirɔma ŋan kaasuŋta po.

ref: And you say, “Let the holy God of Israel hurry up and do what he has promised, so we can see it for ourselves.”
text: A te baai ale a weeni ayen, <<Basi ate Wen a nye nwuli, basi ate wa tom wa tuini nwuli ate ti nya. Basi ate ku forisi a paari. Basi ate Waai Ale Welema A Bo Izirali La zɔŋŋa a jam, ate tama a seba.>>

ref: And you are great at drinking and mixing drinks. But you are in for trouble.
text: Ku ale toa a te nuru baai ale so ale daam la, ale baai ale kperi ale daam damka la,

ref: You accept bribes to let the guilty go free, and you cheat the innocent out of a fair trial.
text: baai ale a tuesi ŋanta a nyini baai ale tom kaasi la jigi a nyiem le basi ba la, alege a kan pai nyemagsika a te baai ale kan seba wari nɔi po la.

ref: You will go up in flames like straw and hay! You have rejected the teaching of the holy Lord God All-Powerful of Israel. Now your roots will rot, and your blossoms will turn to dust.
text: Dila nyiŋla, ase bolim ŋiak ale a dɛ kinkaa ale wukosik diila, dila tɛŋ naŋsaŋa ale poak, ate viok ale ji wupuutaŋa a ta cheŋ ase nyuŋ la. Dii nyiŋla, ba zɛri Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La sinsaŋŋa kama, ale ŋman zɛri Waai Ale Welema A Bo Izirali La wanni.

ref: You are the Lord's people, but you made him terribly angry, and he struck you with his mighty arm. Mountains shook, and dead bodies covered the streets like garbage. The Lord is still angry, and he is ready to strike you again. Foreign Nations Will Attack
text: Dila nyiŋla, Naawen sui ale a puuri ale wa nuruma. Wa zak ka wa nisaŋa wen a yaa a nak ba a lɔnsi. Guutaŋa a choa kama ate baai ale kpi la a nye ase yaata ale doa suitaŋa po diila. Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ meena, wa suipuurumu an basi ya, wa nisaŋa a diem bo ka ŋmai.

ref: The Lord has signaled for the foreign nations to come and attack you. He has already whistled, and they are coming as fast as they can.
text: Wa a zak ka tikti ayen tɛŋ sii ale yalima la a jam wa jigi, ale ŋman fiili fiiluk a wi baai ale bo tɛŋka kpeglimka la ayen ba jam. Ba abe sum jam kama, ba kpabi kama a jam nna a wuli.

ref: Their arrows are sharp, and their bows are ready. The hoofs of their horses are hard as flint; the wheels of their war chariots turn as fast as a whirlwind.
text: Ba timaŋa peemaŋa a choarisi kama, ate ba gbeeri ba timaŋa meena a magsi tɔŋka. Ba wusumaŋa naŋsabaŋa a pagra ase tintana la. Ba wusuma torokoma naŋsaŋa a nye ase ka va pagrik la.

ref: They roar and growl like fierce young lions as they grab their victims and drag them off where no one can rescue them.
text: Ba wuurika a nye ase ka gbeŋli la, ba a wuuri ase ka gbeŋ paala la. Ŋa a ŋuuni kama ase ŋa ale yik jaab ate nuru karo a vari wa a basi la.

ref: On the day they attack, they will roar like the ocean. And across the land you will see nothing but darkness and trouble, because the light of day will be covered by thick clouds.

text: Dii nyiŋla, wa weeni kama ayen, <<Mi dek nisa pagrim ate m pai a nye kude ale m dek yam, dii nyiŋla m le baga a miŋ wie kiri la nyiŋ. Mi a yeeri tɛŋ kpieŋsa bana ale kɔlim ba tuilum ŋanta. Ase pagrɔ la m nya pagrim ba nalimaŋa zuk.

ref: The mighty Lord All-Powerful will send a terrible disease to strike down your army, and you will burn with fever under your royal robes.
text: Dila nyiŋla, Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale basi ate nyiŋtuila a jam ba tugurik tɔŋdɔma zuk. Wa ale za wa pai jabuui a lɔnsi ba po la ale chɔgsi ase ka bolim ŋiak la a dɛ ba.

ref: The holy God, who is the light of Israel, will turn into a fire, and in one day you will go up in flames, just like a thornbush.
text: Naawen dii ale ka Izirali bolim buui ale nyaksi la ale chim ka bolim buui ale za bu a dɛ. Waai ale Welema a bo Izirali la ale nye ase ka bolim ŋiak. Wa ale pa ka dai yeŋ a ju wa muŋsaŋa ale muŋkangɔtisaŋa meena.

ref: The Lord will make your beautiful forests and fertile fields slowly rot.
text: Wa gɔnni nalimu ale laŋ sii ale ta poosuk la ale kaasi meena, ase yɔgnyieŋ ale kpeeri a bɛ diila.

ref: There will be so few trees that even a young child can count them. Only a Few Will Come Back
text: Ate wa ti sii ale tali gɔnni po la ale soa ka nna fii fiiga ate biik ale poom a ŋmarisi dueni.

ref: A time is coming when the survivors from Israel and Judah will completely depend on the holy Lord of Israel, instead of the nation that defeated them.
text: Dai dila danni Izirali dem baai ale tali la, Jekob dɔkdem baai ale vuuk la, a kan ŋman pai ba yiila a nyo waai ale jam a kaasi wa la po, alege ba ale ta siaka ale ka Naawen, Waai ale Welema a bo Izirali la.

ref: There were as many people as there are grains of sand along the seashore, but only a few will survive to come back to Israel's mighty God. This is because he has threatened to destroy their nation, just as they deserve.
text: Izirali nuruma a dan poom piisi ase tintain busuŋku ale bo nyakpiemu nɔi la, ku ale chim ka nuruba maga ale za ba ŋman pilim jam. Kaasuŋ a gomsi kama dua ale diirika ale nyemagsika.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful has promised that everyone on this earth will be punished.
text: Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale za wa basi ate kaasuŋku a paari tɛŋka meena.

ref: Now the Lord God All-Powerful says to his people in Jerusalem: The Assyrians will beat you with sticks and abuse you, just as the Egyptians did. But don't be afraid of them.
text: Dila nyiŋ, Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Mi nuruma baai ale bo Zayon la, ni kan chali Assiria demma yɔgsummoa, baai ale a nak ni ale tachek ale zak doari a ta chaab ale ni ase Ejipiti ale jam a nye ni diila.

ref: Soon I will stop being angry with you, and I will punish them for their crimes.
text: Ku a kan beni, m kan ŋman ta suipuurum ale ni, m suinni a yaa ale bo ale ka bala ate m za m kaasi ba.>>

ref: I will beat the Assyrians with a whip, as I did the people of Midian near the rock at Oreb. And I will show the same mighty power that I used when I made a path through the sea in Egypt.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale miiri ba kama ale fiŋ ase wa ale jam nak Midian ale bo Oreb piuŋku zuk la. Ate wa ale zak wa tachekka nyaataŋa zuk ase wa ale jam nye dii Ejipiti po la.

ref: Then they will no longer rule your nation. All will go well for you, and your burden will be lifted.
text: Da dila danni, ba jiptaŋa ale zak ni ŋmankpalaŋa zuk, ba niiga diokku ni ŋieŋa zuk. Niiga diokku ale wɛ dii nyiŋla ni biigi kama.

ref: Enemy troops have reached the town of Aiath. They have gone through Migron, and they stored their supplies at Michmash,
text: Ba jo Aiat tɛŋka po. Ba jam va Migron tɛŋka po a taam, a yaa pai ba ŋantaŋa a dueni Mikmas tɛŋka po.

ref: before crossing the valley and spending the night at Geba. The people of Ramah are terrified; everyone in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, has run away.
text: Ba va ka guutaŋa zuk a taam, ale a weeni ayen, <<Ti ale bo ka Geba yokku de.>> Ate Arama demma kpaziita a yaa a nak. Gibea ale ka Sɔɔl tɛŋ dem la a yiti chali.

ref: Loud crying can be heard in the towns of Gallim, Laishah, and sorrowful Anathoth.
text: Gallim liewa abe kaari ate kaarika a chim kaamka a te Laisa. Anatot demma ka niniga!

ref: No one is left in Madmenah or Gebim.
text: Madmena demma a yiti chali bɛ kama ate Gebim demma mɛ a chali suk.

ref: Today the enemy will camp at Nob and shake a threatening fist at Mount Zion in Jerusalem.
text: Danni de po ba ale bo ka Nob tɛŋka po. Ba ale gurum ka ba nisa a basi Zayon nuruma ale bo Jerusalem guuku zuk la.

ref: With an ax, the glorious Lord will destroy every tree in the forests of Lebanon.
text: Wa ale che gɔnni tikima ale liak a lɔnsi. Lebanon ale ti kpieŋsaŋa ale lo.

ref: Like a branch that sprouts from a stump, someone from David's family will someday be king.
text: Naŋ buli ale pusi nyini Jese kinni po. A nyini wa tɛŋ naŋsaŋa po Naŋ ale yɔn yɔna.

ref: The Spirit of the Lord will be with him to give him understanding, wisdom, and insight. He will be powerful, and he will know and honor the Lord.
text: Naawen Chiika ale bo wa zuk. Chiik kaai ale a te yam ale miŋka ale sinsaga ale pagrim ale sebika ale Naawen yɔgsum chalika.

ref: His greatest joy will be to obey the Lord. This king won't judge by appearances or listen to rumors.
text: Wa ale mariŋ Naawen yɔgsum chala. Wa kan bo buusa a va dii ate wa nya ale wa nina la, yaase dii ate wa wom ale wa tue la.

ref: The poor and the needy will be treated with fairness and with justice. His word will be law everywhere in the land, and criminals will be put to death.
text: Alege a ta nyini wayɔrisima po wa ale bo baai ale a silim ŋanta la buusa ale nyemagsika wa ale poli a magsi te tɛŋka ŋanjaksa. Wa ale pai wa nɔnni po tachekka a nak tɛŋka. Wa ale pai wa nɔngbanvaataŋa vuusumu a ko gaasa nyama.

ref: Leopards will lie down with young goats, and wolves will rest with lambs. Calves and lions will eat together and be cared for by little children.
text: Piuk ale posuk ale bo ale chaab, ate yɔŋni ale buuk ale duak jigi yeŋ ale chaab, ate naabiik ale gbeŋli ale duŋsaŋa bisa ale bo ale chaab. Ate bi fiik ale nya ŋa zuk.

ref: Cows and bears will share the same pasture; their young will rest side by side. Lions and oxen will both eat straw.
text: Naab ale gɔi biak ale dɛ ale chaab, ba bisaŋa ale duak ale chaab, ate gbeŋli ale ŋɔbi wuuk ase naab la.

ref: Little children will play near snake holes. They will stick their hands into dens of poisonous snakes and never be hurt.
text: Biluak ale diini jinkpaŋ vɔrup nɔi, ate bi fiik ale pai wa nisa a su waapiik duaka jigi.

ref: Nothing harmful will take place on the Lord's holy mountain. Just as water fills the sea, the land will be filled with people who know and honor the Lord. God's People Will Come Back Home
text: Ba a kan nye biemmoa yaase ba kaasi mi tuilum guuku zuwa, dii nyiŋla tɛŋka ale sueri ale ka Naawen sebika ase nyaata ale lik nyakpiemu diila.

ref: The time is coming when one of David's descendants will be the signal for the people of all nations to come together. They will follow his advice, and his own nation will become famous.
text: Dai dila danni Jese Ŋaaŋbiik ale zaani ase ka tikti a te nuruma, ate tɛŋsaŋa ale tigsi a jam wa jigi, ate wa vuusika jigini ale ta ka zula nna yegayega.

ref: When that day comes, the Lord will again reach out his mighty arm and bring home his people who have survived in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Ethiopia, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the land along the coast.
text: Dai dila danni Nyɔnɔwa ale ŋman pilim a teeri wa a nye buye a tuesi wa nuru baai ale tali a bo Assiria ale Ejipiti ale Patros ale Kus ale Iilam ale Sinar ale Yamat ale tɛŋ sii meena ale bo nyakpiemu jigini la.

ref: He will give a signal to the nations, and he will bring together the refugees from Judah and Israel, who have been scattered all over the earth.
text: Wa ale zak tikti a te tɛŋsaŋa, abe wa tigsi Izirali dem baai ate ba yik ta cheŋ tɛŋ yoŋsa la. Wa ale tigsi Juda dem baai ale waaŋ a bo tɛŋka meena la a ta jam jigi yeŋ.

ref: Israel will stop being jealous of Judah, and Judah will no longer be the enemy of Israel.
text: Ɛfraim nyunni ale bɛ, ate Juda dachaasaŋa kan ŋman boro. Ɛfraim a kan ŋman ta nyuri ale Juda, yaase Juda ale ŋman ta dachaani ale Ɛfraim.

ref: Instead, they will get together and attack the Philistines in the west. Then they will defeat the Edomites, the Moabites, and the Ammonites in the east. They will rule those people and take from them whatever they want.
text: Ba ale gum chaab a siŋ cheŋ Filistia demma ale bo yeniŋ la po. Ba ale ŋman cheŋ nuru baai ale bo konni po la a nak ba a vari ba ŋantaŋa. Ba ale nak dɛ Edom ale Moab demma ate Ammon demma ale siak te ba.

ref: The Lord will dry up the arm of the Red Sea near Egypt, and he will send a scorching wind to divide the Euphrates River into seven streams that anyone can step across.
text: Naawen ale basi ate Ejipiti demma nyakpiemu vuuku a kpeeri. Wa ale yuk nisa ate va tuilik fuk va Benni zuk. Wa ale gebi di beli naŋsa si siyopɔi ate nuruba a su nuensa a baga a cheŋ taam.

ref: Then for his people who survive, there will be a good road from Assyria, just as there was a good road for their ancestors when they left Egypt.
text: Suik duok ale boro ate wa nuru baai ale tali nyini Assiria tɛŋka cheena la a va, ase ku ale jam boro a te Izirali diipo ate ba jam nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka la.

ref: At that time you will say, “I thank you, Lord! You were angry with me, but you stopped being angry and gave me comfort.
text: Dai dila danni, ni ale weeni ayen, <<Naawen yaa, m le pak fu. Fi sui ate le jam puuri ale mi, alege fi basi fi suipuurumu kama alege a yaa yɔk m sui.

ref: I trust you to save me, Lord God, and I won't be afraid. My power and my strength come from you, and you have saved me.”
text: Wensie, Wen ale mi varibasika. M le ta sebchakka ale wa la nyiŋ, m kan chali yɔgsummoa. Naawen, Naawen dek ale mi pagrɔ ale m yiili. Wa chim ka m varibasika.>>

ref: With great joy, you people will get water from the well of victory.
text: Masim ale bo ni jigi ase ni ale a dari nyiam a nyini varibasika viliŋa po la.

ref: At that time you will say, “Our Lord, we are thankful, and we worship only you. We will tell the nations how glorious you are and what you have done.
text: Dai dila danni ni ale weeni ayen, <<Pai jiam a te Naawen, wi wa yuenni. Ni basi ate tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa demma a miŋ wa ale nye diila, abe ni mooli ayen wa yuenni a yiti ya.

ref: Because of your wonderful deeds we will sing your praises everywhere on earth.”
text: Ni yi yiila a pak Naawen, dii nyiŋla, wa nye ka wie naliŋsa. Ni basi ate tɛŋka demma meena a seba.

ref: Sing, people of Zion! Celebrate the greatness of the holy Lord of Israel. God is here to help you.
text: Zayon demma, ni nuem abe ni yi yiila ale masim, dii nyiŋla Waai ale Welema a bo Izirali la a zuak kama a bo ni suŋsuŋ.>>

ref: From high on a barren hill give a signal, shout the orders, and point the way to enter the gates of Babylon's proud rulers.
text: Zak tikti guuk kuui ate jaab a ka ku zuk la, nuem ate ba wom abe ni zak nisa, ate ba baga a va nuru kpientaŋa nansuiŋtaŋa a jo.

ref: The Lord has commanded his very best warriors and his proud heroes to show how angry he is.
text: M weeni m nuru weleŋsaŋa kama. M te m tugurik tɔŋdɔma ka nɔi ayen ba sak m suipuurumu. Baai nyiem ale a dɛ masim m nakdeka nyiŋla.

ref: Listen to the noisy crowds on the mountains! Kingdoms and nations are joining forces. The Lord All-Powerful is bringing together an army for battle.
text: Ni wom, nuemka ale bo guutaŋa zuk ase nuru boari la. Ni wom nalima tɛŋsa wɔkwɔk choa ka nna ase tɛŋ kpieŋsa dem ale tigsi jigi yeŋ la. Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a gomsi ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba a magsi kpaliŋ.

ref: From a distant land the Lord is coming fierce and furious— he brings his weapons to destroy the whole earth.
text: Ba a nyini tɛŋ sii ale yalima, ba nyini ka wenŋmazukku kpeglimka meena. Ka Naawen ale cheena ale wa suipuurumu kɔlimaŋa ayen wɛ kaasi tɛŋka meena.

ref: Cry and weep! The day is coming when the mighty Lord will bring destruction. *
text: Ni abe kum, dii nyiŋla Naawen danni a moata kama. Ku ale jam ase ka kaasuŋ la a nyini Waai Ale A Niak La jigi.

ref: All people will be terrified. Hands will grow limp; courage will melt away.
text: Dila nyiŋ, nisa meena ale wobsa, ate nuru meena ale ŋiak.

ref: Everyone will tremble with pain like a woman giving birth; they will stare at each other with horror on their faces. There Will Be No Mercy
text: Yɔgsum ale yik ba, nyiŋdomma ale daanika ale jam ba zuk. Ku ale toa a te ba ase ka nipok ale a dom lɔgi diila. Ku ale cha ba kama ase bolim ŋiak ale a nyaksi ba nina po diila.

ref: I, the Lord, will show no mercy or pity when that time comes. In my anger I will destroy the earth and every sinner who lives on it.
text: Ni nya, Naawen danni a cheena di abe ka nyeka tuem dai ale suipuurum nna yegayega ate wa ale kaasi tɛŋka ale wabaata nuru baai meena ale bo ka po la.

ref: Light will disappear from the stars in the sky; the dawning sun will turn dark, and the moon will lose its brightness.
text: Chiŋmarisaŋa ale ŋan baai meena ale bo wenŋmazukku la a kan nyaksi. Wenbinni ale sobri ate chiika a kan nya.

ref: I will punish this evil world and its people because of their sins. I will crush the horrible pride of those who are cruel.
text: Mi ale namsi tɛŋka nuruma ba biemu nyiŋ ale nuru baataŋa ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ. Mi ale basi ate kanjanta nyam ale ba kayerinni a kpeglim, abe m nye ate kanjanta nuruba ale baai ale kan ta jiirim la a siŋ tɛŋ.

ref: Everyone will run to their homelands, just as hunted deer run, and sheep scatter when they have no shepherd.
text: Ase sebik la, ase piisa ale kan ta naapeerik la, waai meena ale ŋman cheŋ wadek nuruba jigi, waai ale ŋman cheŋ wadek tɛŋ.

ref: They will see their children beaten against rocks, their homes robbed, and their wives abused.
text: Ba bisaŋa ale ŋɔriŋ ba nina po. Ba ale kɔlim ba ŋantaŋa a nyini ba yieŋa po abe ba fɛ a goa ale ba pooma.

ref: The Medes can't be bought off with silver or gold, and I'm sending them to attack Babylonia.
text: Ni nya, mi ale siti Miidi demma a basi ni nyiŋ, baai niŋ ale kan bo kpana ale ligmɔniŋ po la.

ref: Their arrows will slaughter the young men; no pity will be shown to babies and children. The Lord Will Destroy Babylon
text: Ba timaŋa ale lɔnsi nidoabili paalisaŋa tɛŋ. Ba a kan ta jiirim ale buluataŋa yaase bi fiisaŋa.

ref: The city of Babylon is glorious and powerful, the pride of the nation. But it will be like the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah after I, the Lord, destroyed them.
text: Babilon, tɛŋ kaai ale nala a gaam tɛŋsa meena la, Kaldiya demma zulaŋa ate ba a ta kanjanta ŋa nyiŋla, Naawen ale tuesi a nyini ba jigi ase Sodom ale Gomora tɛŋsaŋa ate wa jam a nye diila.

ref: Only desert creatures, hoot owls, and ostriches will live in its ruins, and goats will leap about.
text: Alege gɔi ŋanta ale duak dula, gɔi baasa ale sueri yieŋa po. Dula jigini viita ale boro, dula ate bua ŋaai ale waara la ale yɔk a zi.

ref: The Lord will have mercy on Israel and will let them be his chosen people once again. He will bring them back to their own land, and foreigners will join them as part of Israel.
text: Naawen ale ta jiirim ale Jekob dɔkdemma. Wa ale ŋman pilim lueri Izirali demma pai ba a kali badek tɛŋ po. Nicham ale gum chaab ale ba, ate ba nye nɔiyeŋ ale Jekob dɔkdemma.

ref: Other nations will lead them home, and Israel will make slaves of them in the land that belongs to the Lord. Israel will rule over those who once governed and mistreated them. Death to the King of Babylonia!
text: Satɛŋsa ale ta ba a ŋman jam badek jigini. Ate Izirali dɔkdemma ale soa tɛŋsaŋa ate ba nidoama ale nipooma ale chim ba yɔm a bo Naawen tɛŋka zuk. Baai ale a yik Izirali la, ba ale yik ba. Ate ba ale nya baai ale a namsi ba la zuk.

ref: The Lord will set you free from your sorrow, suffering, and slavery.
text: Dai dii dai ate Naawen a yeeri ni ta a nyini ninam ale butimka ale nyeka tuem yontidi po la,

ref: Then you will make fun of the King of Babylonia by singing this song: That cruel monster is done for! He won't attack us again.
text: ni le ni nye Babilon naawa a la diila ale nna: Nya namsidɔwa nuerika a paari ya. Nya wa suipuurumu a kpeglim ya.

ref: The Lord has crushed the power of those evil kings,
text: Naawen a wɛ nuru bioku tachekka, ale niŋdeerɔma tachekka mɛ.

ref: Now all the world is at peace; its people are celebrating with joyful songs.
text: Tɛŋsaŋa meena a bo ka vuusum ale suiyɔgni po. Ba a yi ka yiila.

ref: King of Babylonia, even the cypress trees and the cedars of Lebanon celebrate and say, “Since you were put down, no one comes along to chop us down.”
text: Ate damɔnta tiisa ale Lebanon nyunyoŋtaŋa a dɛ ka masim ni zuk ale a weeni ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla ate ni siŋ tɛŋ la, dacheerik karo ayen wa che ti a lɔnsi.>>

ref: Each one of them will say, “Now you are just as weak as any of us!
text: Ba meena ale tulisi, ba ale weeni ni ayen, <<Nama mɛ a yaa wobsa ase ka tama la. Ni a nye ase ka tama la.>>

ref: Your pride and your music have ended here in the world of the dead. Worms are your blanket, maggots are your bed.”
text: Ni nalimu meena a siŋ ka boosuku po ale ni kpanuŋku nakka. Ni doa ka nanzue zuk ate bobla a lik ni nyiŋsaŋa meena.

ref: You, the bright morning star, have fallen from the sky! You brought down other nations; now you are brought down.
text: Nya fi le nyini wenŋmazuk a lo dii ya, vari chiŋmariga ale varivientidi nidoabiligaa. Fi waai ale jam basi ate tɛŋsa a duak tɛŋ la.

ref: You said to yourself, “I'll climb to heaven and place my throne above the highest stars. I'll sit there with the gods far away in the north.
text: Fi weeni fi suinum po ayen, <<M le jueli wenŋmazuk. Mi ale nye ate m naamu zukpaglika a yiti a gaam Wen chiŋmarisaŋa. M le kali naam zukpaglika zuk a nya baai meena ale tigsi guuku zuk la ale baai ale bo guuk weleŋka zukparukku la.

ref: I'll be above the clouds, just like God Most High.”
text: Mi ale yiti a jueli chiŋmaaŋa zuk. Mi ale nye m dek ase Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La.>>

ref: But now you are deep in the world of the dead.
text: Alege ba ta fu siŋ ka vɔrumu po, a ta siŋ golukku tɛŋ.

ref: Those who see you will stare and wonder, “Is this the man who made the world tremble and shook up kingdoms?
text: Ku ale cha baai ale a nya la, ba ale poli fi ale jam ka diila abe ba ayen, <<Ka nuruwa de ale jam a choa tɛŋka la a basi ate tɛŋsa a yɔksa,

ref: Did he capture every city and make earth a desert? Is he the one who refused to let prisoners go home?”
text: nuru waai ale nye ate tɛŋka meena a chim gɔi la, waai ale nak yiak tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale kan basi ate baai ate wa yik la a kuli?>>

ref: When kings die, they are buried in glorious tombs.
text: Tɛŋsaŋa nalimaŋa meena a doa ka ba jiga waai meena a doa ka wadek vɔrup po.

ref: But you will be left unburied, just another dead body lying underfoot like a broken branch. You will be one of many killed in battle and gone down to the deep rocky pit.
text: Alege ba yeeri fi a ta nyini fi vɔrumu po kama ase tiib naŋ ate ba zɛri la. Baai ate ba ko la ale lik fu, baai ate ba chub ale gebik la, baai ale siŋ golukku tanaŋa po la. Fi a nye nna ase ka kpio ate ba tabi wa zuk la.

ref: You won't be buried with kings; you ruined your country and murdered your people. You evil monster! We hope that your family will be forgotten forever.
text: Ba a kan maa gu fu ale ba, dii nyiŋla fi kaasi fi tɛŋka kama ale ŋman ko fi nuruma. Ba a kan teeri nuru baataŋa bisa ŋmana.

ref: We will slaughter your sons to make them pay for the crimes of their ancestors. They won't take over the world or build cities anywhere on this earth.
text: Ni gomsi jigi a magsi wa nidoabilisaŋa tɔgrika. Ba kokpieŋsaŋa wabaataŋa nyiŋ. Ba kan ŋman yiti a tuesi tɛŋka abe ba lik tɛŋzuk de ale ba tɛŋsaŋa.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful has promised to attack Babylonia and destroy everyone there, so that none of them will ever be remembered again.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a weeni ayen, <<Mi ale yiti a nye kpaliŋ ale ba,>> Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Ni gebi Babilon yuenni ale baai ale vuuk la ale wa bisaŋa ale wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa.>>

ref: The Lord will sweep out the people, and the land will become a swamp for wild animals. Assyria Will Be Punished
text: Naawen Dii Ale A De Tugurik Tɔŋdɔba Niŋ La a weeni kama ayen, <<Mi ale nye ate wa tɛŋka a chim viita ale nyiam boka jigi. M le vaari wa ale kaasuŋ sie a basi.>>

ref: The Lord All-Powerful has made this promise: Everything I have planned will happen just as I said.
text: Ka Naawen dii ale ka Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋdeerɔ la ale pɛ ayen, <<Wensie, mi ale zɔk diila ku ale nye, ate mi ale poli diila ku ale zaani.

ref: I will wipe out every Assyrian in my country, and I will crush those on my mountains. I will free my people from slavery to the Assyrians.
text: Mi ale kaasi Assiria demma m dek tɛŋka po. M guuku zuk ate mi ale tabi ba a dueni tɛŋ. Wa niiga diokku a kan ŋman vi m nuruma zuwa, ate wa jibtaŋa a zak ba ŋmankpalaŋa zuk.>>

ref: I have planned this for the whole world, and my mighty arm controls every nation.
text: Mi ale poli dii a ta va tɛŋzuk de meena la ale nna. M be teeri ka nisa a basi tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa meena zuk.

ref: This message came from the Lord in the year King Ahaz died:
text: Naawen wanni de a jam mi jigi ka ben dii ate naab Ayazi a kpi la.

ref: Philistines, don't be happy just because the rod that punished you is broken. That rod will become a poisonous snake, and then a flying fiery dragon.
text: Nama Filistia demma ni kaa naŋ ayen tachek kaai ale nak ni la a wɛ ya. A nyini waab bula tɛŋ naŋka waab piik ale yiti, bu yoanni ale chim ka waab biok tintueta.

ref: The poor and needy will find pastures for their sheep and will live in safety. But I will starve some of you, and others will be killed.
text: Baai ale jaŋ a gaam ŋanjaksa meena la ale nya ba le a yaali diila, ate baai ale a silim la ale boro ale suiyɔgni. Alege mi ale kaasi fi buuni ale kɔm. Bu ale ko ni nuru baai ale vuuk la.

ref: Cry and weep in the gates of your towns, you Philistines! Smoke blows in from the north, and every soldier is ready.
text: Nansuiŋŋoa, kum! Tɛŋŋa, kaari ate ku jueli Filistia demma meena ale nyaliŋ bɛ! Chiŋmari ale nyuisa ale nyini wiiluk geŋ a jam, ba ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai ate jayɔgsuk a ka ba po.

ref: If a messenger comes from a distant nation, you must say: “The Lord built Zion. Even the poorest of his people will find safety there.”
text: Ka boan jaab tulisa ate ti le pai te tɛŋ kala tomtomdɔma? <<Naawen a sɛ Zayon a zaani kama, ate kala po wa nuru baai ale a nam la ale suk du.>>

ref: This is a message about Moab: The towns of Ar and Kir were destroyed in a night. Moab is left in ruins!
text: Naawen wa dii ale a magsi chaab ale Moab la. Ar ale bo Moab po la a kaasi kama, a kaasi kama yok yeŋ po. Kir ale bo Moab la a kaasi kama, a kaasi kama yok yeŋ po.

ref: Everyone in Dibon has gone up to the temple and the shrines to cry and weep. All of Moab is crying. Heads and beards are shaved because of what happened at Nebo and Medeba.
text: Dibon demma a cheŋ ka ba puusika yenni ŋmani ayen ba kum. Moab a kum Nebo ale Medeba nyiŋ. Ba chiiri zuima meena ale che teeŋsa meena a basi.

ref: From Heshbon and Elealeh, weeping is heard in Jahaz; Moab's warriors scream while trembling with fear. Pity Moab
text: Yesbon ale Elealeya demma a kaari kama ate ba luelutaŋa a nyini peelim ate Jayaz a wom ba. Dila nyiŋla, Moab tugurik tɔŋdɔma a kaari kama ate ba kpaziita poom a nak.

ref: I pity Moab! Its people are running to Zoar and to Eglath-Shelishiyah. They cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they tell of disasters.
text: Mi a kum a te Moab a nyini ka m suinum po Moab nuruma a chali a cheŋ ka Zoar, ate ba gela a chali a cheŋ Eglat Selisiya. Ba poom cheŋ jueli a paari ka Luyit ale diem kum a cheŋ. Baai ale va Yoronaim suiku la, a kum kama a magsi chaab ale ba kaasuŋku.

ref: The streams of Nimrim and the grasslands have dried up. Every plant is parched.
text: Nimrim nyaataŋa a kpeeri kama ate wuutaŋa a kɔ. Gɔnni ale tattaŋa po jaab a karo a sobri.

ref: The people of Moab are leaving, crossing over Willow Creek, taking everything they own and have worked for.
text: Dila nyiŋ ba ŋantaŋa ate ba paari a tigsi ba la, ba ji ta cheŋ ka Niak Tiisaŋa Vooliŋka.

ref: In the towns of Eglaim and of Beerelim and everywhere else in Moab mournful cries are heard.
text: Ba kumsaŋa a chɔgsi a paari Moab tɛŋka banaŋa. Ba kumsaŋa a paari Eglaim ale Beer Elim tɛŋsaŋa kama.

ref: The streams near Dimon are flowing with blood. But the Lord will bring even worse trouble to Dimon, because all in Moab who escape will be attacked by lions.
text: Dimon tɛŋka nyaataŋa ka ziim, alege mi ale diem a ta namsika yega a jam Dimon zuk. A ta gbeŋli a jam Moab nuru baai ale chali la zuk ale baai ale tali bo tɛŋka po la.

ref: Send lambs as gifts to the ruler of the land. Send them across the desert from Sela to Mount Zion.
text: Ni ta pabisa a cheŋ a ga te waai ale a nya tɛŋka zuk la ase ni lampoo la. Ni nyini Sela a gaam gɔnni a ga paari Jerusalem.

ref: The women of Moab crossing the Arnon River are like a flock of birds scattered from their nests.
text: Moab nipooma ale bo Arnon benni la a nye ase ka nuinsa ale yiti nyini si tukta po ale masim ale poom zɛ si ale a cheŋ juijui la.

ref: Moab's messengers say to the people of Judah, “Be kind and help us! Shade us from the heat of the noonday sun. Hide our refugees! Don't turn them away.
text: <<Sak ti dii ale magsi ayen ti nye la, te ti popola. Basi ate fi yisuŋku a lik ti kantueŋ pagrik po. Suk nuruma kan pai baai ale suk la a da.

ref: Let our people live in your country and find safety here.” Moab, your cruel enemies will disappear; they will no longer attack and destroy your land.
text: Basi ate Moab demma a bo ale fu. Chim ba ligrɔ a nyini kaasirɔwa jigi.>> Namsidɔwa ale jam kpeglimka ate kaasuŋ a kan ŋman boro. Dachiaka ale bɛ tɛŋka po.

ref: Then a kingdom of love will be set up, and someone from David's family will rule with fairness. He will do what is right and quickly bring justice. Moab's Pride Is Destroyed
text: Ŋmanteka po naam zukpaglik ale zaani. Wensie po nuru ale kali ka zuk, waai ale nyini ka Deevid yenni po la. Waai ale a bo buusa ale a gisi nyemagsika la ale kpabi ale wayɔrisima tuima.

ref: We have heard of Moab's pride. Its people strut and boast, but without reason.
text: Ti wom Moab demma kanjantaŋa yegayega ale ba ale a poli ayen ba gaam nuruba la wari kama. Ba kanjantaŋa ale ba kuulimka meena ka koruk.

ref: Tell everyone in Moab to mourn for their nation. Tell them to cry and weep for those fancy raisins of Kir-Hareseth.
text: Dila nyiŋ, Moab demma a gum ka chaab a boro kum a te ba tɛŋka. Ba kum a te ka dii ale nye Kir Yareset tɛŋka nidoama la.

ref: Vineyards near Heshbon and Sibmah have turned brown. The rulers of nations used to get drunk on wine from those vineyards that spread to Jazer, then across the desert and beyond the sea.
text: Yesbon tattaŋa a kɔ kama. Sibma tiisaŋa mɛ a kɔ. Tɛŋsaŋa niŋdeerɔma a tabi si a kaasi kama. Ba tiisaŋa nyiem ale jam a teeri a paari Jazer a cheŋ gɔnni po la. Si naŋbuli teeri nyini a cheŋ paari nyakpiemu.

ref: or joyful and happy times, while bringing in the crops. Singing and shouting are gone from the vineyards. There are no joyful shouts where grapes were pressed. God has silenced them all.
text: Masim ale suipeentik a ŋman ka tiisaŋa tɛŋka po. Waai a kan yi yiila a nuem kaduksaŋa po. Waai a kan ŋmiak daam jigini diila mi kpeglim nuemka kama.

ref: It's useless for Moab's people to wear themselves out by going to their altars to worship and pray.
text: Moab demma a dan cheŋ ba guuku zuk, ku a kan te ba maarika. Ba abe dan cheŋ ba puusika jigini, ku a kan ta wamaŋ a te ba.

ref: The Lord has already said all of this about Moab.
text: Wanni de ate Naawen a poom ŋaam a dɛ niŋ a weeni a magsi chaab ale Moab.

ref: Now he says, “The contract of a hired worker is good for three years, but Moab's glory and greatness won't last any longer than that. Only a few of its people will survive, and they will be left helpless.”
