text: Alege yɔgyɔgla de Naawen ale a weeni diila ale nna. <<Bena ŋata po, ba ale nye ase ka tomteerɔba ale bo ba kpagi nisima po diila. Ba nalimu ale ba nuruma a kan ŋman boro, ate baai ale za ba vuuk la a kan soa diiya, ate ba ale wobsa mɛ.>>

ref: This is a message about Damascus: Damascus is doomed! It will end up in ruins.
text: Naawen wa dii ale a magsi chaab ale Damasikus la. <<Nya, Damasikus a kan ŋman chim tɛŋ kpieŋa, alege ka za ka chim ka guuk.

ref: The villages around Aroer will be deserted, with only sheep living there and no one to bother them.
text: Aroer tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale kaasi, ate piisa ale za ŋa a duak dula, ate nuru a kan boro ale nye ate ŋa kpaziita a nagi.

ref: Israel will lose its fortresses. The kingdom of Damascus will be destroyed; its survivors will suffer the same fate as Israel. The Lord All-Powerful has promised this. Sin and Suffering
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋ kaai ale pagra la ale bɛ nyini Ɛfraim, naam pagrim ale nyini Damasikus. Baai ale za ba tali a bo Araam la ale nye ase ka Izirali demma zulaŋa la, >> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a weeni.

ref: When that time comes, the glorious nation of Israel will be brought down; its prosperous people will be skin and bones.
text: <<Da dila danni Jekob zulaŋa ale muriŋ bɛ. Wa nyiŋka ale buk.

ref: It will be like an olive tree beaten with a stick, leaving two or three olives or maybe four or five on the highest or most fruitful branches. The Lord God of Israel has promised this.
text: Dila meena ŋaaŋnyiŋ, yiisika ale tali, ase kpaam tiib ate ba gbesi la ale basi yɔna ŋaye yaase ŋata ŋmazuk naŋsaŋa nyiŋla, yaase yɔna ŋanaansi yaase ŋanu naŋ kpieŋsaŋa nyiŋla.>> Naawen ale ka Izirali Wenni la ale weeni dila.

ref: At that time the people will turn and trust their Creator, the holy God of Israel.
text: Dai dila danni po, nuruba ale zak a nya ba Nyeerɔwa abe ba viriŋ ba nina a te Waai ale Welema a bo Izirali la.

ref: They have built altars and places for burning incense to their goddess Asherah, and they have set up sacred poles for her. But they will stop worshiping at these places.
text: Ba a kan zak a nya kuŋkuŋtaŋa ale ba nisa tuimaŋa, ba niŋ kan bo Asera zaŋŋa po ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la kuŋkuŋtaŋa ate ba nye la.

ref: Israel captured powerful cities and chased out the people who lived there. But these cities will lie in ruins, covered over with weeds and underbrush.
text: Dai dila danni po, ba tɛŋ pagrisaŋa, ate ba jam a basi si Izirali demma nyiŋla ale chim ka juijui ate nuruba ale zɛri ate jiŋŋa ale chim tiisa ale wuuta jigi. Ate jaab meena ale kaasi.

ref: Israel, you have forgotten the God who saves you, the one who is the mighty rock where you find protection. You plant the finest flowers to honor a foreign god.
text: Ni baŋ Naawen ni Varibasidɔwa kama. Ni an teeri Piuŋku, ni pagrɔwa. Dila nyiŋ, ni a vuk ti maŋsa, ale a vuk tiisa ate ni ta nyini tɛŋ yonsa a jam la,

ref: The plants may sprout and blossom that very same morning, but it will do you no good, because you will suffer endless agony. God Defends His People
text: dai dii dai ate ni vuk si la, ni nye kama ate si a chim, saluik kuui po ate ni vuk si la, ni nye kama ate si pusi. Alege dila meena kpesika ale chim ka kinla, dai dila danni ale chim ka nyiŋtuila ale nyiŋdomma ŋaai ale kan ta tebika.

ref: But even if they roar like a fearsome flood, God will give the command to turn them back. They will be like dust, or like a tumbleweed blowing across the hills in a windstorm.
text: Nuruma wuurika a poom a nye ase ka nyakpiem wuurika la, wa dan toariŋ ba, ba yiti a cheŋ ka nna niŋniŋa, nna se viok ale a ji vɔtta guuta zuk la, ate ku ale ŋman a nye ase va pagrik ale ji paasuk a gilim diila.

ref: In the evening their attack is fierce, but by morning they are destroyed. This is what happens to those who raid and rob us.
text: Junɔi ba nye kama ate yɔgsum kpiem a boro alege ta cheen saluik ba cheŋ. Waai meena ale a kɔlim ti tɛŋka la charuk ale la.

ref: Downstream from Ethiopia lies the country of Egypt, swarming with insects.
text: Ku ale toa a te tɛŋ kaai ale bo Kus belaŋa nɔi ate ka kiŋkaŋŋa a fuk la

ref: Egypt sends messengers up the Nile River on ships made of reeds. Send them fast to Ethiopia, whose people are tall and have smooth skin. Their land is divided by rivers; they are strong and brutal, feared all over the world.
text: ate ka tom baai ate ba va ŋaaruŋ tii ate ba pai bimbena a nye la. Ni cheŋ mwuli tomtomdɔba, ni cheŋ nuru baai ale woŋŋa ate ba nyiŋ gbaŋ saala la jigi, nuru baai ate tɛŋka meena a chali ba la jigi, tɛŋ kaai nyeka ale toa ale ta bichaŋ ate bela a poori tɛŋka la.

ref: Everyone on this earth, listen with care! A signal will be given on the mountains, and you will hear a trumpet.
text: Nama tɛŋka nuruma meena, baai ale bo tɛŋka zuk la, tikti a dan zak guutaŋa zuk, ni le nya, ate damuniŋ a dan peeri, ni le wom.

ref: The Lord said to me, “I will calmly look down from my home above— as calmly as the sun at noon or clouds in the heat of harvest season.”
text: Naawen ale weeni mi diila ale nna. <<M le nye diki abe m bo m boka jigini a nya, nna ase wenliuk wulum kantueŋ la, nna se chiŋmari maglim cheka wen la.>>

ref: Ethiopians will be food for mountain vultures during the summer and for wild animals during the winter.
text: Ba le basi ba meena a te guutaŋa nuinsaŋa ale gɔi duŋsaŋa. Nuinsaŋa ale dɛ ba yoenni meena, ate gɔi duŋsaŋa ale dɛ ba wenkarika meena.

ref: Those Ethiopians are tall and their skin is smooth. They are feared all over the world, because they are strong and brutal. But at that time they will come from their land divided by rivers, and they will bring gifts to the Lord All-Powerful, who is worshiped on Mount Zion.
text: Ba ale ta tiirita a jam a te Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La. Tiiritaŋa ale nyini ka nuru baai ale woŋŋa ate ba nyiŋ gbaŋsaŋa a saala la jigi, nuru baai ate tɛŋka meena a chali ba la jigi, tɛŋ kaai nyeka ale toa ale ta bichaŋ la ate bela a poori ka la. Ba ale ta tiiritaŋa a jam Zayon Guuku zuk, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La Yuenni jigini.

ref: This is a message about Egypt: The Lord comes to Egypt, riding swiftly on a cloud. The people are weak from fear. Their idols tremble as he approaches and says,
text: Naawen wa dii ale magsi chaab ale Ejipiti la ale nna: Nya, Naawen a do ka chiŋmari a cheena Ejipiti demma po. Ejipiti bɔgtaŋa kpaziita a nak wa niŋ, ate Ejipiti demma a ŋiak.

ref: “Egypt will be discouraged when I confuse their plans. They will try to get advice from their idols, from the spirits of the dead, and from fortunetellers.
text: Ejipiti demma ale jɔk nyiŋbiiri, mi ale basi ate ba le ta popola ŋaai meena la, ale chim kinla. Ba le ga kpesi nyini bɔgta ale kpilima ale sampoporisa ale chichirik wiirisa jigi.

ref: I will put the Egyptians under the power of a cruel, heartless king. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have promised this.” Trouble along the Nile
text: M le pai Ejipiti demma a nyo ka kpagi dii nyeka ale toa la nisima po, ate naab waai nyeka ale toa la ate wa a nya ba zuk.>> Ka Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: The Nile River will dry up and become parched land.
text: Benni nyaataŋa ale kpeeri, ate benni tɛŋka ale toliŋ a ko.

ref: Its streams will stink, Egypt will have no water, and the reeds and tall grass will dry up.
text: Nyiam vuutaŋa ale kasim a nyuŋ kama ate Ejipiti beli naŋsaŋa ale si abe ŋa kpeeri. Bimbenaŋa ale wobini ale kpi,

ref: None of the cloth makers will know what to do, and they will turn pale.
text: baai ale pai gungunta a tom tuima la ale jɔk yiila, baai mɛ ale a yɔk garuk naliŋsa la ale jɔk yiila,

ref: Weavers will be confused; paid workers will cry and mourn. Egypt's Helpless Leaders
text: baai ale a tom gatta tuima la sue a kan peenti, baai mɛ ale a tuesi tutuna la sue ale kaasi.

ref: The king's officials in Zoan are foolish themselves and give stupid advice. How can they say to him, “We are very wise, and our families go back to kings of long ago?”
text: Zoan kpaŋŋa daa ŋanta alege ka betta. Faaro yam sagrɔma a kan te yam sinsaga. Fi ale nye ka sɛ a weeni Faaro ayen, <<Mi ka yam nuruma po wanyi, ale dipo nalimaŋa ŋaaŋviirɔ?>>

ref: The royal officials in Zoan and in Memphis are foolish and deceived. The leaders in every state have given bad advice to the nation.
text: Zoan tɛŋka kpaŋŋa a chim ka betta, ate ba a paasi Memfis tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma. Ka nuruma gugottaŋa tintanaŋa a ta Ejipiti nuruma a cheŋ bɛ kama.

ref: The Lord has confused Egypt; its leaders have made it stagger and vomit like a drunkard.
text: Naawen a pai ka nimbigilugsuk chiik a te ba. Ba nye ate Ejipiti demma a ja ba wie meena nyeka po ase danyuirik ale a ja wa chichiita po diila.

ref: No one in Egypt can do a thing, no matter who they are.
text: Ejipiti demma an baga badek wari a nye, zuk yaase jiuk, yaase kpinkparuk yaase binbein.

ref: When the Lord All-Powerful punishes Egypt with his mighty arm, the Egyptians will become terribly weak and will tremble with fear.
text: Da dila danni, Ejipiti demma ale nye ase ka nipooba la. Ba nyiŋsa ale gɔk ate ba kpaziita nak ase Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a nin zak wa nisa a ta chaab ale ba.

ref: They will be so terrified of Judah that they will be frightened by the very mention of its name. This will happen because of what the Lord All-Powerful is planning against Egypt. The Lord Will Bless Egypt, Assyria, and Israel
text: Ate Juda tɛŋka ale ta yɔgsum a jam Ejipiti demma zuk. Tɛŋ sii meena ale a wom Juda wari la yɔgsum ale yik ba, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale zɔk dii a ta chaab ale ba la nyiŋ.

ref: The time is coming when Hebrew will be spoken in five Egyptian cities, and their people will become followers of the Lord. One of these cities will be called City of the Sun.
text: Dai dila danni tɛŋ kpieŋsa Ejipiti po ale biisi Keenan biika abe ba pɛ siak te Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La. Ba ale wi tɛŋsaŋa kanyi ayen Kaasuŋ Tɛŋ.

ref: In the heart of Egypt an altar will be set up for the Lord; at its border a shrine will be built to honor him.
text: Dai dila danni, Naawen ale ta ka kaabka kuŋkuŋ Ejipiti tɛŋka suŋsuŋ. Ale ŋan mɛɛnta a te Naawen tɛŋka banni.

ref: These will remind the Egyptians that the Lord All-Powerful is with them. And when they are in trouble and ask for help, he will send someone to rescue them from their enemies.
text: Ku ale chim ka daana ale seerɔ a te Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La Ejipiti tɛŋka po. Ba dan kum a te Naawen baai ale a namsi ba la niŋ, wa le tom varibasidɔ ale maarɔ ba jigi ate wa vari ba a basi.

ref: The Lord will show the Egyptians who he is, and they will know and worship the Lord. They will bring him sacrifices and offerings, and they will keep their promises to him.
text: Ate Naawen ale basi ate Ejipiti demma a miŋ wa, ate dai dila danni ba ale siak a te Naawen. Ba ale puusi wa ale kaabsa ale ŋandiinta tiirita. Ba ale puulim a te Naawen, abe ba ta pumpuulimaŋa.

ref: After the Lord has punished Egypt, the people will turn to him. Then he will answer their prayers, and the Egyptians will be healed.
text: Naawen ale namsi Ejipiti ale nyiŋtuila abe wa ŋman tebi ba. Ba le ŋmani Naawen jigi ate wa tulisi ba funfɔblaŋa abe wa tebi ba.

ref: At that time a good road will run from Egypt to Assyria. The Egyptians and the Assyrians will travel back and forth from Egypt to Assyria, and they will worship together.
text: Dai dila danni, suik duok ale nyini Ejipiti a cheŋ Assiria. Assiria demma ale cheŋ Ejipiti ate Ejipiti demma ale cheŋ Assiria. Ba ale gum chaab a puusi Naawen.

ref: Israel will join with these two countries. They will be a blessing to everyone on earth,
text: Dai dila danni, Izirali ale saari buta a gum chaab ale Ejipiti ale Assiria a chim niauŋ tɛŋka zuk.

ref: then the Lord All-Powerful will bless them by saying, “The Egyptians are my people. I created the Assyrians and chose the Israelites.”
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale niak ba abe wa a weeni ayen, <<Niauŋ a bo Ejipiti demma mi nuruma jigi, niauŋ a bo Assiria demma mi nisima tuimaŋa jigi ale Izirali demma mi nitalimu jigi.>>

ref: King Sargon of Assyria gave orders for his army commander to capture the city of Ashdod.
text: Bein dii po ate Naab Sargon Assiria naawa a tom wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni ate wa ga siti a nak yiak Asdod tɛŋka la.

ref: About this same time the Lord had told me, “Isaiah, take off everything, including your sandals!” I did this and went around naked and barefoot
text: Va ŋala po, Naawen a jam biisi ale Amoz nidoabinni Azaya ayen, <<Yeeri fi boorik garukku fi nyiŋka po ale fi nuesaŋa fi naŋsaŋa po.>> Ate wa nye dila, a gilim chaboala ale naŋta bie.

ref: for three years. Then the Lord said: What Isaiah has done is a warning to Egypt and Ethiopia.
text: Naawen yaa weeni ayen, <<Ase mi tomteerɔwa Azaya ale cheŋ chaboala ale naŋta bie bena ŋata la ase daana ale wa dii ale sak chum po wari la a ta chaab ale Ejipiti ale Kus tɛŋsaŋa.

ref: Everyone in these two countries will be led away naked and barefoot by the king of Assyria. Young or old, they will be taken prisoner, and Egypt will be disgraced.
text: Dila Assiria naawa ale yik baai Ejipiti ale Kus la, bi paaluk ale ŋankpagsa, wa le ta ba cheŋ nyiŋbolinni ale naŋta bie ate ba butagkolaŋa a nya ate ku ta chivie a jam Ejipiti jigi.

ref: They will be confused and frustrated, because they depended on Ethiopia and bragged about Egypt.
text: Baai ale ta sebchakka ale Kus ale baai ale a kuulim Ejipiti nyiŋla, yɔgsum ale yik ba ate ba jo chivie po.

ref: When this happens, the people who live along the coast will say, “Look what happened to them! We ran to them for safety, hoping they would protect us from the king of Assyria. But now, there is no escape for us.”
text: Dai dila danni, nuru baai ale bo nyakpiemu nɔi la ale weeni ayen, <Nya dii ale jam baai ate ti ta yiila ale ba ayen ba ale maari ti abe ba vari ti a basi a nyini Assiria naawa nisa po la. Ti ale nye ka sɛ a chali be?> >>

ref: This is a message about a desert beside the sea: Enemies from a hostile nation attack like a whirlwind from the Southern Desert.
text: Wen wa dii ale magsi chaab ale Gɔnni ale moata Nyakpiemu la. Ase va pagrisa ale fuk va yeseoku geŋsa la, fɛ juerɔ ale nyini gɔnni po a jam, a nyini kpazinagsuk tɛŋ a jam.

ref: What a horrible vision was shown to me— a vision of betrayal and destruction. Tell Elam and Media to surround and attack the Babylonians. The Lord has sworn to end the suffering they caused.
text: Kaasuŋ wie ate Naawen a pai sak mi. Bumbobrɔwa a bobri, varidɔwa mɛ a vari. Iilam demma a siti, Miidi demma a jam gilimka. Mi ale ta ŋuuni kaai meena ate ba nye la a jam kpeglimka jigi.

ref: In Babylon the high officials were having a feast. They were eating and drinking, when someone shouted, “Officers, take your places! Grab your shields.”
text: Ba gomsi ŋandiinta jazaanim, pai jaab a pati du, ba yaa dɛ ale nyu, nama kpaŋŋa ni yiti, ni nyo kpaam ŋanchɔgsintaŋa po.

ref: The Lord said to me, “Send guards to find out what's going on.
text: Nyɔnɔwa ale weeni mi diila ale nna, <<Te ate nuru a za nansuiŋku a nya abe wa weeni wa ale nya diila.

ref: When they see cavalry troops and columns of soldiers on donkeys and camels, tell them to be ready!”
text: Diipo meena wa dan nya torokoba ale wusuma beŋsa bon duerɔba, yaase laalaakomi duerɔba, wa abe kpesi wadek, a kpesi wadek a paari.>>

ref: Then a guard said, “I have stood day and night on this watchtower, Lord.
text: Ate waai ale a nya la a na ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, dai meena mi za a limisi gboŋku zuk kama, yok meena mi za ka dula.

ref: Now I see column after column of cavalry troops.” At once someone shouted, “Babylon has fallen! Every idol in the city lies broken on the ground.”
text: Nya nuru ale nna a bo toroko po a cheena ale wusuma beŋsa. Ate wa tulisika a ŋman te ayen, <<Babilon a lo ya, ka lo ya. Wa bɔgtaŋa ate ba mɛ a zaani la a lo paari ka tɛŋ munamuna.>>

ref: Then I said, “My people, you have suffered terribly, but I have a message for you from the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel.” How Much Longer?
text: M nuruma, ba a fɔbi ni ase ka zaa la, alege mi ale weeni ni dii ate mi a wom a nyini Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni jigi la.

ref: This is a message about Dumah: From the country of Seir, someone shouts to me, “Guard, how much longer before daylight?”
text: Naawen wa dii ale magsi chaab ale Duma la ale nna. A waai ale wi mi a nyini Seir ayen, <<Limisidɔ, yokku a tali soa ka sɛ? Limisidɔ, yokku a tali soa ka sɛ?>>

ref: From my guard post, I answered, “Morning will soon be here, but night will return. If you want to know more, come back later.”
text: Limisidɔwa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Saluik a cheena, alege yok mɛ a cheena. Fi abe daa a bek be bek abe fi ŋman jam.>>

ref: This is a message for Arabs who live in the barren desert in the region of Dedan: You must order your caravans
text: Naawen wa dii ale magsi chaab ale Arabia la ale nna. Nama Dedan nyiemdɔma ale ga bo Arabia tiisaŋa po la,

ref: to bring water for those who are thirsty. You people of Tema must bring food for the hungry refugees.
text: ni ta nyiam a jam te baai ate nyanyuila a ta ba la. Nama baai ale bo Tema tɛŋka la, ni ta ŋandiinta a jam te baai ale a chali ba be la.

ref: They are worn out and weary from being chased by enemies with swords and arrows.
text: Ba chali a be ka gebika, gebik kaai ate ba dari yeeri la, ale tom buui ale gbeeri la, a nyini kpaliŋka po.

ref: The Lord said to me: A year from now the glory of the people of Kedar will all come to an end, just as a worker's contract ends after a year.
text: Nyɔnɔwa ale weeni mi diila ale nna, <<Bein yeŋ po, ase tuimtomdɔ ale a nye nɔiyeŋ ale tuini diila, Kedar ŋan baai ate ba pai a nye kpaliŋsa la ale kpeglim.

ref: Only a few of their warriors will be left with bows and arrows. This is a promise that I, the Lord God of Israel, have made.
text: Tɔŋdɔ baai ale vuuk la, Kedar tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale fiisa.>> Ka Naawen Dii Ale ka Izirali Wenni la ale biisi.

ref: This is a message about Vision Valley: Why are you celebrating on the flat roofs of your houses?
text: Naawen wa dii ale magsi chaab ale pa sakka viaka la ale nna: Ka boa ale a daani ni yɔgyɔgla de, ate ni meena a jueli gbirima zuima,

ref: Your city is filled with noisy shouts. Those who lie drunk in your streets were not killed in battle.
text: tɛŋ kaai ate daanika a sueri ka la, tɛŋ kpieŋ kaai ate nuemka ale masim dɛka a sueri ka la? Ni nuruma daa gebik ate ba pai ko ba yaase ba kpi kpaliŋ po.

ref: Your leaders ran away, but they were captured without a fight. No matter how far they ran, they were found and caught.
text: Ni niŋdeerɔma meena maa chaab a yiti chali kama. Ba dachaasaŋa a yik ba kama ale an pai tom a tɔŋ ya. Nama baai ale a chali alege ate ni dachaasaŋa a bo niŋ la, ba a yik ni meena a lik kama.

ref: Then I said, “Leave me alone! Let me cry bitter tears. My people have been destroyed, so don't try to comfort me.”
text: Dila nyiŋ mi yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni basi mi abe ni cheŋ. Basi mu ate m kum ale sui kaasuŋ. Ni kan yɔk m sui m nuruma kaasuŋku nyiŋŋa.>>

ref: The Lord All-Powerful had chosen a time for noisy shouts and confusion to fill Vision Valley, and for everyone to beg the mountains for help.
text: Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a ta ka nuemka ale tabika kpazinagsuk dai pa sakka viaka po, parisa chub lɔnsika ale guuta kum teka dai.

ref: The people of Elam and Kir attacked with chariots and carried shields.
text: Iilam demma a pai ba peema pakka ale ba toroko duerɔma ale wusuma. Kir demma a gomsi ba kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsintaŋa a magsi.

ref: Your most beautiful valleys were covered with chariots; your cities were surrounded by cavalry troops.
text: Viak kaai ate ni lueri la, a sueri ale ka wusuma torokoba, ate wusum duerisa a za tɛŋ kpieŋka nansuiŋtaŋa.

ref: Judah was left defenseless. At that time you trusted in the weapons you had stored in Forest Palace.
text: Ba yeeri baai ale a maari Juda la pagrimu kama. Ate dai dila danni ba a nya kpaliŋ kɔlima Tiisa Naam Yenni po.

ref: You saw the holes in the outer wall of Jerusalem, and you brought water from the lower pool.
text: Fi nya kama ayen Deevid Tɛŋka parisaŋa a ta ka muulisa nna yegayega. Fi nyo nyiam Beli dii ale bo Tɛŋ la po.

ref: You counted the houses in Jerusalem and tore down some of them, so you could get stones to repair the city wall.
text: Fi chiini Jerusalem yeeŋa kama a yaa nak ŋa gela a lɔnsi ayen fi nye ate parika a pagra.

ref: Then you built a large tank between the walls to store the water. But you refused to trust the God who planned this long ago and made it happen. A Time To Weep
text: Fi se ka nyiam nyoka jigi parisa siyewa suŋsuŋ a magsi Beli Kpakka nyiamu, alege fi an gisi a nya Waai ale nye dila la, yaase fi niŋ a bo Waai ale poli di wie dipo la.

ref: When all of this happened, the Lord All-Powerful told you to weep and mourn, to shave your heads, and wear sackcloth.
text: Ka Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale wi fu dai dila ayen fi kum abe fi kaari, abe fi dari fi zuisaŋa a vɔssi abe fi jo boorisa garuk.

ref: But instead, you celebrated by feasting on beef and lamb and by drinking wine, because you said, “Let's eat and drink today! Tomorrow we may die.”
text: Alege ni nya, suipeentik ale masim dɛka ale boro, niiga tɔgrika ale piisa koka, lanta ŋɔbika ale daam nyuka, <<Ni weeni kama ayen basi ate ti de abe ti a nyu ale chum ti baga a kpi kama.>>

ref: The Lord All-Powerful has spoken to me this solemn promise: “I won't forgive them for this, not as long as they live.” Selfish Officials Are Doomed
text: Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale pai wanni de a sak mi ate m wom ayen, <<Kan daa ni kummu danni biemu de a kan nya duisi basika ka Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful is sending me with this message for Shebna, the prime minister:
text: Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni ayen, <<Cheŋ ga weeni Sebna nyaarɔwa ale a nya naab yenni zuk la ayen.

ref: Shebna, what gives you the right to have a tomb carved out of rock in this burial place of royalty? None of your relatives are buried here.
text: Ka boa ate fi bo dela a nye, ka wana ale te fi suik ayen fi keri boosuk a te fidek dela, a keri fi boosuku ŋmazukku dela ale a keri fi vuusumu jigini piuŋku po?

ref: You may be powerful, but the Lord is about to snatch you up and throw you away.
text: <<Be seba, Naawen a za wa yik fu kama giŋgiŋ yuk fu a basi, Fi nuru kpioŋku.

ref: He will roll you into a ball and throw you into a wide open country, where you will die and your chariots will be destroyed. You're a disgrace to those you serve.
text: Wa ale kpamsi fu kama nna ŋmapi ase gbeli la a yuk fu basi tɛŋ kpieŋ po. Ate fi ale kpi dula ate fi wusuma toroko naliŋsaŋa ale wari du. Fi ka chivie a te fi kpagni yenni.

ref: The Lord is going to take away your job!
text: Mi ale yeeri fi kpaŋtaŋa po, ate fi jɔk kpaŋtaŋa.

ref: He will give your official robes and your authority to his servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah. Eliakim will be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the royal family of Judah.
text: M le pai ka fi naam garukku a jo wa, abe m pai fi garuk panni bobi wa, a yaa pai fi pagrimu a te wa. Wa ale chim ka baai ale bo Jerusalem ale Juda yenni la koa.

ref: The Lord will put him in charge of the key that belongs to King David's family. No one will be able to unlock what he locks, and no one will be able to lock what he unlocks.
text: M le pai ka Deevid yenni saafiika a vi wa ŋmankpala. Ate wa ale a lak jabuui la, waai an baga a kpari, ate wa ale a kpari jabuui la waai an baga a lagi.

ref: The Lord will make him as firm in his position as a tent peg hammered in the ground, and Eliakim will bring honor to his family.
text: M le feri wa ase kpaasiri ate ba nak a feri diila, Wa ale ta zula a jam wa kowa yenni po.

ref: His children and relatives will be supported by him, like pans hanging from a peg on the wall.
text: Wa dɔkdemma zulaŋa meena ale bo ka wa jigi, wa bisa ale wa ŋaaŋbisa meena ale wa yenni ŋantomta meena.

ref: That peg is fastened firmly now, but someday it will be shaken loose and fall down. Then everything that was hanging on it will be destroyed. This is what the Lord All-Powerful has promised.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni ayen, <<Kpaasini ale feri tɛŋ kaai la ale baliŋ, ate kpaasini a voori, ate ŋan baai meena ale yik di nyiŋla a gebi lo.>> Ka Naawen ale biisi.

ref: Mourn in silence, you shop owners of Sidon, you people on the coast. Your sailors crossed oceans, making your city rich.
text: Ni nye diki nama baai ale bo tɛŋ kaai ate nyiam a gilim ka la ale nama Saidon geruŋdɔma, ate baai ale a nyiem nyiam po a jigsi ba la.

ref: Your merchants sailed the seas, making you wealthy by trading with nation after nation. They brought back grain that grew along the Nile.
text: Siyor a nya ba ŋan bieŋa a nyini ka nyakpientaŋa po. Taaya a nya ba ligraŋa a nyini ka ba ale a che ŋan baai Nile benni la, ate ka yaa chim satɛŋsa yaba.

ref: Sidon, you are a mighty fortress built along the sea. But you will be disgraced like a married woman who never had children.
text: Saidon tɛŋ demma, Chivie a yik ni, ale nama nyakpiemu ŋan pagrisaŋa, Ka nyakpiemu ale weeni ayen, <<Mi puuk an dom ya yaase m biak ya, mi an wuuk nidoabilisa yaase lieba.>>

ref: When Egypt hears about Tyre, it will tremble.
text: Ase wari a dan nyini Taaya a jam Ejipiti demma jigi ku le daani ba popola.

ref: All of you along the coast had better cry and sail far across the ocean.
text: Ni lo a jueli Tarsis tɛŋka. Nama tɛŋ kaai ate nyiam a gilim ka la demma.

ref: Can this be the happy city that has stood for centuries? Its people have spread to distant lands;
text: Ka ni tɛŋ kaai ate ni a dɛ masim ka nyiŋla ale nna, tɛŋ kpakka, tɛŋ kaai naŋsa ale ta ka a cheŋ niŋniŋ tɛŋsa la?

ref: The Lord All-Powerful planned it to bring shame and disgrace to those who are honored by everyone on earth.
text: Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale zɔk, ayen wa ta zula nyam baai meena ale ta kanjanta la a siŋ tɛŋ ate baai meena ale ta yue tɛŋzuk de la a zaab badek.

ref: People of Tyre, your harbor is destroyed! You will have to become farmers just like the Egyptians. Tyre Will Be Forgotten
text: Nama Tarsis demma ni ga kpa maŋ Nile benni, diila ni ŋman ka ŋaaruŋta zaanka jigi ya.

ref: The Lord's hand has reached across the sea, upsetting the nations. He has given a command to destroy fortresses in the land of Canaan.
text: Naawen a teeri ka wa nisa nyakpiemu zuk a nye ate bu naataŋa a choa. Wa a te ka nɔi a magsi chaab ale Keenan ayen ka yie pagrisaŋa ba kaasi.

ref: The Lord has said to the people of Sidon, “Your celebrating is over— you are crushed. Even if you escape to Cyprus, you won't find peace.”
text: Wa weeni ayen, <<Fi masimu dɛka a ŋman karo Saidon tɛŋka a yaa kaasi kama.>> Yiti a lo jueli Kittim dula jigini vuusum a poom ka.>>

ref: Look what the Assyrians have done to Babylonia! They have attacked, destroying every palace in the land. Now wild animals live among the ruins.
text: Nya Kaldiya demma tɛŋka, nuruma de ŋman ka magsa. Assiria demma a basi kama ate ka chim gɔi ŋanta boka jigi. Assiria demma a sɛ ka yie woŋta a gilim, alege Assiria demma a yeeri ka ŋan pagrisaŋa a tulim ka ate ka chim tɛŋ kaasuŋ.

ref: Not a fortress will be left standing, so tell all the seagoing ships to mourn.
text: Tarsis demma baai ale ta ŋaaruŋta la abe kum. Dii nyiŋla ba yie pagrisaŋa a kaasi kama.

ref: You're gone and forgotten, you evil woman! So strut through the town, singing and playing your favorite tune to be remembered again.
text: <<Pai kpanuŋ, a cheŋ va tɛŋka po, ba baŋ taabuka wari, nak kpanuŋku nalimnyiini, lenni yiila yega, ate dila basi ate ba teeri fi wari.>>

ref: but none of what is earned will be kept in the city. That money will belong to the Lord, and it will be used to buy more than enough food and good clothes for those who worship the Lord.
text: Alege wa ale a nya diila ale wa nyuentaŋa meena wa be le gaari a te ka Naawen. Ba kan pai nyo jaab po a zaani yaase ba pai suk. Wa nyuentaŋa ale cheŋ baai ale bo ale Naawen la jigi, a magsi ŋandiinta yegayega ale garuk naliŋsa.

ref: The Lord is going to twist the earth out of shape and turn it into a desert. Everyone will be scattered,
text: Ni nya, Naawen a za wa te tɛŋzuk de a duak ka koruk abe wa kaasi ka. Wa ale kaasi jaab meena ale bo ka po la abe wa kati ka nuruma a waaŋ.

ref: including ordinary people and priests, slaves and slave owners, buyers and sellers, lenders and borrowers, the rich and the poor.
text: Ku ale nye kaabteerɔ ka dila dekdega ase nuruma la, a nye kpagi ase tomteerɔ la, a nye nipok ase pɔkdɔklie la, a nye dateerɔ ase daarɔ la, a nye peemdɔ ase peemteerɔ la, a nye pamideerɔ ase pamiteerɔ la.

ref: The earth will be stripped bare and left that way. This is what the Lord has promised.
text: Tɛŋka meena ale duak koruk, abe ba koaliŋ ka meena, ka Naawen ale biisi wanni de.

ref: The earth is polluted because its people disobeyed the laws of God, breaking their agreement that was to last forever.
text: Tɛŋka nuruma a taŋ ka kama, ba nye ka tuikpari ale sinsaŋŋa, ale tom kaasi wieŋa, nɔiyeŋ kaai ale kan ta kpeglimka la ba kaasi ka.

ref: The earth is under a curse; its people are dying out because of their sins.
text: Dila nyiŋ kikaasa ale kaasi tɛŋka. Ka nuruma dek ale magsi ba siak ba kaasuŋku. Dila nyiŋ bolim ale dɛ tɛŋka demma ate maga dek a tali.

ref: Grapevines have dried up: wine is almost gone— mournful sounds are heard instead of joyful shouts.
text: Da paalika a kpieri kama ate tiisaŋa a kpi. Baai meena ale a de masim la a bo ka ŋuunika po.

ref: No one plays tambourines or stringed instruments; all noisy celebrating has come to an end.
text: Kayaksaŋa masimu a nye diki, baai ale a dɛ masim la nuemka a basi ya, kpanuŋku masimu a nye chorr.

ref: They no longer sing as they drink their wine, and it tastes sour.
text: Ba kan ŋman nak yiila a nyu daamoa. Daam toa kama a te bu nyuiriba.

ref: Towns are crushed and in chaos; houses are locked tight.
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋka a kaasi kama a doa koruk. Yeri meena nansuiŋ a lik kama.

ref: Happy times have disappeared from the earth, and people shout in the streets, “We're out of wine!”
text: Ba a kum a yaali ka daam suitaŋa po. Masim meena a labri chim ka niniga. Masim a ŋman ka tɛŋka zuwa.

ref: Cities are destroyed; their gates are torn down.
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋka a kaasi kama, ba nak ka tuataŋa a kaasi ka nna bunabuna.

ref: Nations will be stripped bare, like olive trees or vineyards after the harvest season. Praise the God of Justice
text: Ku be le nye ka dila tɛŋka zuk ale tɛŋ kpieŋsa, ase ba le fɔbi kpaam tiib diila, yaase ba ale gbesi ŋanta ale tali ate ba a yiisi diila.

ref: People in the west shout; they joyfully praise the majesty of the Lord.
text: Ba lak ba lueluta, ale a nuem ale masim. A nyini yeniŋka, ba weeni Naawen zuaka ale ka diila.

ref: And so, everyone in the east and those on the islands should praise the Lord, the God of Israel.
text: Dila nyiŋ, a nyini konni po, ni pai zula a te Naawen. Ni zak Naawen yuenni a zaani, waai ale ka Izirali demma Wen la, a bo tɛŋ sii ate nyiam a gilim la.

ref: From all over the world songs of praise are heard for the God of justice. But I feel awful, terribly miserable. Can anyone be trusted? So many are treacherous! There's No Escape
text: A nyini tɛŋka kpeglimka tama wom yiila lennika ayen, <<Zula a paari Waai ale ka Wayɔrisima Nyɔnɔ la.>> Alege mi a yaa weeni ayen, mi bɛ ya, mi bɛ ya. Ku le toa a te mu. Velimvendika a bobri ya. Velimvendika ale wa ventaŋa a bobri.>>

ref: Terror, traps, and pits are waiting for everyone.
text: Yɔgsum, ale goluk ale baruk ale a limisi ni tɛŋzuk demma.

ref: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; if you crawl out of the pit, you will get caught in a trap. The sky has split apart like a window thrown open. The foundations of the earth have been shaken;
text: Waai ale za wa yiti a chali yɔgsum nyiŋla, ale lo ka goluk po. Waai ale za wa nyini golukku po a nyini la, baruk ale yik wa. Wenŋmazuk tuataŋa a lagri, ate tɛŋka nyubaŋa a choa.

ref: the earth is shattered, ripped to pieces.
text: Tɛŋka a na lagri, tɛŋka gaari buye, tɛŋka a choa.

ref: It staggers and shakes like a drunkard or a hut in a windstorm. It is burdened down with sin; the earth will fall, never again to get up.
text: Tɛŋka a ja kama ase danyuirik la, ka a zaŋ ase ka viok ale a fuk kusuŋ diila. Dila dobrim buui ale bo ka zuk la ale ka biemu ate ka yaa lo ka kan ŋman yiti.

ref: On that day the Lord will punish the powers in the heavens and the kings of the earth.
text: Dai dila danni, Naawen ale namsi pagritaŋa ale bo wenŋmazuk la ale nalimaŋa ale bo tɛŋzuk de la.

ref: He will put them in a pit and keep them prisoner. Then later on, he will punish them.
text: Ba ale gum ba chaab ase ligrɔba ale bo likka dɔk po la. Wa le lik ba a namsi ba da boari.

ref: Both the moon and sun will be embarrassed and ashamed. The Lord All-Powerful will rule on Mount Zion in Jerusalem, where he will show its rulers his wonderful glory.
text: Chiika ale nye ŋoomaa ate chivie a yik wenbinni. Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale dɛ naam Zayon Guuku zuk ale Jerusalem po ale nisɔmma niŋ ale zula.

ref: You, Lord, are my God! I will praise you for doing the wonderful things you had planned and promised since ancient times.
text: Naawen yaa, fi ale mi Wen. M le zak fu zaani abe m pak fi yuenni, dii nyiŋla fi va ka wensie maŋsa po a tom tuim kpien ŋaai ate fi gomsi ŋa a nyini dipo la.

ref: You have destroyed the fortress of our enemies, leaving their city in ruins. Nothing in that foreign city will ever be rebuilt.
text: Fi nye kama ate tɛŋ kpieŋka a chim guuk, ate tɛŋ kaai ale pagra la a kaasi, nichamma pagrimu jigini tɛŋ a ŋman ka, ba kan ŋman sɛ ka.

ref: Now strong and cruel nations will fear and honor you.
text: Dila nyiŋ nuru pagrisa ale zuli fu. Tɛŋ kpieŋ sii ale kan ta jiirim la ale zuli fu.

ref: You have been a place of safety for the poor and needy in times of trouble. Brutal enemies pounded us like a heavy rain or the heat of the sun at noon, but you were our shelter.
text: Fi chim ka ŋanjaksa sukka jigi a chim sukka jigi a te waai ale a silim la wa daanika po, a chim kusuŋ a lik viok ale yɔgsum a lik kantueŋ. Diila baai ale kan ta jiirim la vuusumu a nye ase ka viok ale a fuk parik diila

ref: Those wild foreigners struck like scorching desert heat. But you were like a cloud, protecting us from the sun. You kept our enemies from singing songs of victory. The Lord Has Saved Us
text: ale a nye ase tɛŋ kosik tuiluk la. Fi basi ate nicham baai ale a nye wɔkwɔk la a nye diki, ase chiŋmari yɔgsum ale a baliŋ tuiluk diila, dila baai ale kan ta jiirim la ale basi ba yiini.

ref: On this mountain the Lord All-Powerful will prepare for all nations a feast of the finest foods. Choice wines and the best meats will be served.
text: Guuku de zuk ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a gomsi ŋan dii maŋsa tigi a te nuru meena, ale daam tigi a magsi baai ale pak la, lam maŋsa ale da maŋsa tigi.

ref: Here the Lord will strip away the burial clothes that cover the nations.
text: Guuku de zuk ate wa ale kaasi jabuui ale a lik nuruba meena la, garuk kuui ale a lik tɛŋsaŋa meena la.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful will destroy the power of death and wipe away all tears. No longer will his people be insulted everywhere. The Lord has spoken!
text: Wa ale nɛ kum ate bu a kan ŋman boro. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale duisi waai meena ninyaata a basi. Wa ale yeeri wa nuruma ale bo tɛŋka zuk la chivieŋa a basi. Ka Naawen ale biisi dila.

ref: At that time, people will say, “The Lord has saved us! Let's celebrate. We waited and hoped— now our God is here.”
text: Da dila danni ba ale weeni ayen, <Wensie ti Wenni ale la. Ti mariŋ wa kama ate wa vari ti a basi. Naawen ale nna, ti mariŋ wa kama. Ni basi ate ti dɛ masim abe ti sue a peenti ale wa varibasika.>>

ref: The powerful arm of the Lord will protect this mountain. The Moabites will be put down and trampled on like straw in a pit of manure.
text: Naawen nisa ale bo guuku de zuk. Alege wa ale tabi Moab kama ase kinkaa ate ba tigsi ŋa tabi ŋa ate ŋa chim bibaam diila.

ref: They will struggle to get out, but God will humiliate them no matter how hard they try.
text: Ba ale teeri ba nisa ku po, ase nyapuŋdoa ale a teeri nisa a de diila. Wen ale ta ba kanjantaŋa a siŋ tɛŋ ba ale ba nisaŋa kperika meena.

ref: The walls of their fortresses will be knocked down and scattered in the dirt.
text: Wa ale basi ate ni parik woŋsaŋa a lo a duak tɛŋ, wa le ta si siŋ dueni tɛŋ tantaŋa dek po.

ref: The time is coming when the people of Judah will sing this song: “Our city is protected. The Lord is our fortress, and he gives us victory.
text: Dai dila danni ba le yi yiini de Juda tɛŋka po ayen, ti ta ka tɛŋ pagrik. Wen a basi kama ate varibasika a chim ka parisa ale ka bimbima.

ref: Open the city gates for a law-abiding nation that is faithful to God.
text: Lak tuataŋa ate wayɔrisima tɛŋka a jo, tɛŋ kaai ale ta siaka la.

ref: The Lord gives perfect peace to those whose faith is firm.
text: Fi ale yik waai popola ale bo jigi yeŋ la ale suiyɔgni, dii nyiŋla wa ta sebchakka ale fu kama.

ref: So always trust the Lord because he is forever our mighty rock.
text: Kasim ta sebchakka ale Naawen, diila Naawen, Naawen ka Piuŋ taam wuu.

ref: God has put down our enemies in their mountain city and rubbed it in the dirt.
text: Wa nye ate kanjanta nyam a siŋ tɛŋ, ale kaasi ba tɛŋka. Wa palinti ka a magsi chaab ale tɛŋka a yuk ka a basi tantaŋa po.

ref: Now the poor and abused trample all over that city.” The Lord Can Be Trusted
text: Naŋtaata ale tabi ka a lɔnsi, baai ate ba a namsi ba la naŋtaataŋa, ŋanjaksaŋa naŋtaataŋa.

ref: Our Lord, you always do right, and you make the path smooth for those who obey you.
text: Gola a ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ suiku po. Fi Waai ale kan ta kaasuŋ la, a nye kama ate wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ suiku a nala.

ref: You are the one we trust to bring about justice; above all else we want your name to be honored.
text: Wensie, Naawen yaa, ti ale a cheŋ fi buusa suiku po la, ti le limisi fu. Ti suiniimaŋa a yaali ka fi yuenni ale a yiti diila.

ref: Throughout the night, my heart searches for you, because your decisions show everyone on this earth how to live right.
text: Mi chiika a yeenti a yaali fu kama yok, ate m chiika a zeenti a yaali fu saluiku. Fi buusaŋa a dan jam tɛŋka zuk, nuruma ale bo ka po la a zamsi ka wayɔrisima.

ref: Even when the wicked are treated with mercy in this land of justice, they do wrong and are blind to your glory, our Lord.
text: Niaka a dan poom jam gaasa nuruba jigi, ba kan zamsi wayɔrisima wie. Dan poom ka tɛŋ kaai ale nye a magsi la po ba ale diem a nye biem, ate ba poom a kan pa zula a te Naawen zuaka ale ka diila.

ref: Your hand is raised and ready to punish them, but they don't see it. Put them to shame! Show how much you care for us and throw them into the fire intended for your enemies.
text: Naawen yaa, fi nisaŋa a zak ka wen alege ba kan nya. Basi ate ba nya fi popola ale bo fi nuruma zuk diila ate chivie a yik ba. Basi ate fi ale tali bolim buui a magsi fi dachaasaŋa la a de ba.

ref: You will give us peace, Lord, because everything we have done was by your power.
text: Naawen yaa, fi ale te ti suiyɔgni. Ti ale baga a nye dii meena la, ka fi ale tom a te ti.

ref: Others have ruled over us besides you, our Lord God, but we obey only you.
text: Naawen yaa, ti Wenni, kpaga yona a nya ti zuk a nya kama, alege ka fi yuenni nyiini ate tama a zuli.

ref: Those enemies are now dead and can never live again. You have punished them— they are destroyed, completely forgotten.
text: Ba yaa kpi kama, ba ŋman karo. Chiik sii ale cheŋ la an yiti ya. Fi namsi ba kama ale ta ba jam kaasuŋ jigi. Fi ko ba kama ate waai a kan teeri ba.

ref: Our nation has grown because of you, our Lord. We have more land than before, and you are honored. The Lord Gives Life to the Dead
text: Naawen yaa, fi nye kama ate tɛŋ kpieŋka a lagri. Fi ale sum nye ate ka lagri nna yegayega. Fi nya zula kama a te fidek. Fi nye kama ate tɛŋka banaŋa a lagri.

ref: When you punished our people, they turned and prayed to you, our Lord.
text: Naawen yaa, ba jam fi jigi kama ale ba daanika. Ase fi ale dari ba tue la, ate ba waasi a puusi fu.

ref: Because of what you did to us, we suffered like a woman about to give birth.
text: Ase nipok ale ta lɔgi a dom ayen wa biak a kaari diila, dila ate tama a nye a bo fi niŋ, Naawen yaa.

ref: But instead of having a child, our terrible pain produced only wind. We have won no victories, and we have no descendants to take over the earth.
text: Ti jam ta ka puuk, ate ka a dom, alege ti biaka viok. Ti an ta varibasika a jam tɛŋka zuwa. Ti an biak nuruba a basi tɛŋka zuwa.

ref: Your people will rise to life! Tell them to leave their graves and celebrate with shouts. You refresh the earth like morning dew; you give life to the dead.
text: Alege ni kpiema ale boro. Ba nyiŋsaŋa ale yiti. Nama baai ale bo tanta po la, ni yiti a nuem ale masim. Ni maglimu a nye ase ka saluik maglim la. Tɛŋka ale ŋman biak ka kpiema.

ref: Go inside and lock the doors, my people. Hide there for a little while, until the Lord is no longer angry. The Earth and the Sea Will Be Punished
text: Mi nuruma, ni cheŋ, a ga jo ni diinaŋa po, abe ni lik nidek a basi ni diinaŋa po. Ni suk nidek maga ate wa suipuurumu a taam.

ref: The Lord will come out to punish everyone on earth for their sins. And when he does, those who did violent crimes will be known and punished.
text: Nya, Naawen a nyini ka wa boka jigini a cheena ayen wa namsi nuru baai ale tom wabaata la. Tɛŋka ale dak baai ale suk a ko nuruba ka zuk la. Tɛŋka a kan ŋman suk baai ate ba ko ba la.

ref: On that day, Leviathan, the sea monster, will squirm and try to escape, but the Lord will kill him with a cruel, sharp sword. Protection and Forgiveness The Lord said:
text: Dai dila danni, Naawen ale pai ka wa gebika ale wa nyinyigsaŋa ale gebik kaai ale zuak ale ta pagrim la, a namsi Jabuui ale a nye ase waab la, Jabuui ale a vili ase waab la. Wa le ko nyakpiemu po jachichimini.

ref: At that time you must sing about a fruitful vineyard.
text: Dai dila danni, <<Ni pai kaduk kaai ale ta yɔna la a lenni yiili.

ref: I, the Lord, will protect it and always keep it watered. I will guard it day and night to keep it from harm.
text: Mi, Naawen, a nya ka zuk kama. M kasim a zaŋti ka kama. Mi a nya ka zuk yok ale kantueŋ, ate waai a kan baga a daani ka.

ref: I am no longer angry. But if it produces thorns, I will go to war against it and burn it to the ground.
text: Mi sui a kan puuri. Ka kpiluŋbaoŋ ale muŋsa nyiini a nin tu chaab ale mu. Mi le gɔk santiri a ta chaab ale ba kpaliŋ po. Mi ale ju ba bolim.

ref: Yet if the vineyard depends on me for protection, it will become my friend and be at peace with me.
text: Yaase m basi ate ba jam a suk mi jigi. Basi ate ba ta suiyɔgni ale mi. Mm, basi ate ba ta suiyɔgni ale mi.>>

ref: Someday Israel will take root like a vine. It will blossom and bear fruit that covers the earth.
text: Daa a cheena Jekob ale feri naŋsa, Izirali ale pusi vaata a busum, a sueri tɛŋka meena ale yɔna.

ref: I, the Lord, didn't punish and kill the people of Israel as fiercely as I punished and killed their enemies.
text: Naawen an namsi Izirali demma yegayega ase ba dachaasaŋa la, yaase ba jɔk nuruba yega.

ref: I carefully measured out Israel's punishment and sent the scorching heat to chase them far away.
text: Wa pai ka kpaliŋ ale yik ta cheŋka a nye le ba, ale wa nyinyigsa nakka wa yiak ba ate ba nyini, ase dai dii dai ate kori vioku a fuk la.

ref: There's only one way that Israel's sin and guilt can be completely forgiven: They must crush the stones of every pagan altar and place of worship. The Lord Will Bring His People Together
text: Kude nyiŋ, ate Jekob foolaawa ale duisi basi, ate dila ale sak ayen biem a ŋman ka wa jigi ya. Ase wa dan nak juka kuŋkuŋku tanaŋa a buksi, ate Asera zaŋŋa ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la kuŋkuŋtaŋa an ŋman za.

ref: Fortress cities are left like a desert where no one lives. Cattle walk through the ruins, stripping the trees bare.
text: Tɛŋ kaai ale pagra la a doa ka koruk, a zɛri ba kalika jigini, a zɛri ase gɔi la. Dula ate naabisa a dɛ, dula ate si a duak, ale passi naŋsaŋa a zaani jassi.

ref: When broken branches fall to the ground, women pick them up to feed the fire. But these people are so stupid that the God who created them will show them no mercy.
text: Ase bu naŋsaŋa a dan ko si nyiem wɛ a lo kama ate nipooba a jam a yaali a ga cheem bolim. Dii nyiŋla, nuruma de a kan miŋ biik kiriya. Ate ba Nyeerɔwa a ka jiirim ale ba, wa poom kan ŋmani a te ba.

ref: The time is coming when the Lord will shake the land between the Euphrates River and the border of Egypt, and one by one he will bring all of his people together.
text: Dai dila danni, Naawen ale fɔbi a nyini Yufiretis Benni ale chali a taam la, ga paari Ejipiti Buboalika, ate nama Izirali demma ale tigsi wanyi wanyi.

ref: A loud trumpet will be heard. Then the people of Israel who were dragged away to Assyria and Egypt will return to worship the Lord on his holy mountain in Jerusalem.
text: Ate da dila danni, damuniŋ kpieŋ ale peeri. Ate baai ale jam a kpi Assiria tɛŋka po la, ale baai ate ba ta cheŋ Ejipiti la ale jam puusi Naawen tuilum guuku zuk Jerusalem po.

ref: The city of Samaria above a fertile valley is in for trouble! Its leaders are drunkards, who stuff themselves with food and wine. But they will be like flowers that dry up and wilt.
text: Ku le toa a te wuuta puuta tulika, Ɛfraim danyuirisa kanjantaŋa, nalim buui ale a nyini la, wa zula nalimu, a doa viak poosuk zuk la, tɛŋ kala jigi baai kanjanta ate daam a basi ate ba siŋ tɛŋ la.

ref: Only the Lord is strong and powerful! His mighty hand will strike them down with the force of a hailstorm or a mighty whirlwind or an overwhelming flood.
text: Nya, Nyɔnɔwa a ta ka waai ale pagra. Nna ase ŋmoruk tana ale kaasuŋ viok la, nna ase ŋmoruk niuŋ ale a fɔbi la ale ŋmoruk kuui ale chuiri a chali la, wa le yuk ka ale pagrim a lɔnsi tɛŋ.

ref: Every drunkard in Ephraim takes pride in Samaria, but it will be crushed.
text: Wuuta puuta tulika de, Ɛfraim danyuirisaŋa kanjantaŋa, ba le tabi ba ale naŋsa.

ref: Samaria above a fertile valley will quickly lose its glory. It will be gobbled up like the first ripe fig at harvest season.
text: Nalim buui ale nyini la, zula nalimu, a doa viak poosuku po la, ale nye ase ka kiŋkama ale muni a magsi gbesika diila, nuru a dan ga nya a gbesi nyo nisa po, wa a dɛ kama.

ref: When this time comes, the Lord All-Powerful will be a glorious crown for his people who survive.
text: Dai dila danni, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, ale chim ka zula naam zutɔk, wuuta puuta tulik kaai ale nala a te wa nuru baai ale tali la.

ref: He will see that justice rules and that his people are able to defend their cities. Corrupt Leaders Will Be Punished
text: Wa le ta nyemagsika popola a te waai ale a bo buusa la, abe wa te baai ale ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba a za nansuiŋku nɔi la pagrim.

ref: Their tables are covered, completely covered, with their stinking vomit.
text: Ŋan zaanitaŋa meena a lik ale ka chichiita ate jigi a karo an daŋ ya.

ref: So, the Lord will speak to his people in strange sounds and foreign languages.
text: Ku yaa be nala, Wen ale pai bi chaŋ a biisi a te nuruma de,

ref: You rulers of Jerusalem do nothing but sneer; now you must listen to what the Lord says.
text: Dila nyiŋla, ni wom Naawen wanni, nama baai ale nye nuruba a la, nama baai ale a nya Jerusalem nuruma zuk la.

ref: Do you think you have an agreement with death and the world of the dead? Why do you trust in your lies to keep you safe from danger and the mighty flood?
text: Ni a kuulim kama ayen, <<Ti nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale kum, ale nye nɔiyeŋ ale boosuku. Ate kaasuŋ a dan poom cheena, ku a kan paari ti. Dii nyiŋla, ti te ate ka venta a chim ti varibasika, ate venta wie a chim ti sukka jigi.>>

ref: And so the Lord says, “I'm laying a firm foundation for the city of Zion. It's a valuable cornerstone proven to be trustworthy; no one who trusts it will ever be disappointed.
text: Dila Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, <<Nya mi dueni ka tintain Zayon po, chamsi nyaka tintain, tintain dii ale ta yuei ale magsi nyubini, waai ale ta siaka la sui a kan kaasi.

ref: Justice and fairness will be the measuring lines that help me build.” Hailstones and floods will destroy and wash away your shelter of lies.
text: Mi ale pai nyemagsika a chim magsika miik abe wayɔrisima a chim ja magsim. Ŋmoruk tana ale chuiri ni varibasika jigini a ta cheŋ ale ni ventaŋa nyama, ate nyiam ale mobi a sueri ni sukka jigini.

ref: Your agreement with death and the world of the dead will be broken. Then angry, roaring waves will sweep over you.
text: Ni nɔiyeŋka ate ni nye ale kum la ale kaasi. Ni nɔiyeŋka ate ni nye ale boosuku la a kan ŋman boro. Ase kaasuŋ kuui ale a taam la a dan jam ku le nak ni a dueni.

ref: Morning, noon, and night an overwhelming flood will wash you away. The terrible things that happen will teach you this lesson:
text: Ku a dan ga jam, ku a ta ni a taam kama. Dan poom ale saluita yaase danni po, yaase yok po, ku a ta ni a taam kama. Biika de kiri miŋka ale ta yɔgsum a jam ni jigi.>>

ref: The Lord will fiercely attack as he did at Mount Perazim and in Gibeon Valley. But this time the Lord will do something surprising, not what you expect.
text: Naawen ale yiti ŋmai ase wa ale jam nye dii Perazim Guuku zuk la, Wadek ale yiti ase wa ale jam nye dii Gibeon Viaka po la ayen wa tom wa tuini la, wa tuin chaŋka, abe wa tom wa ale magsi ayen wa tom diila, wa tuin chaŋ kaai ale magsi wa tom la.

ref: So you had better stop sneering or you will be in worse shape than ever before. I heard the Lord All-Powerful threaten the whole country with destruction. All Wisdom Comes from the Lord
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ni basi ni nye laka dan kan daa di ni chɔrimaŋa ale dobra. Ka Nyɔnɔwa Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni mi kaasuŋku ate wa ta chaab ale tɛŋka meena la.

ref: Pay close attention to what I am saying.
text: Wom, abe fi wom m lueluku, kpesi a wom dii ate mi a weeni la.

ref: When a field is ready, they scatter the seeds of dill and cumin; they plant the seeds of wheat and barley in the proper places and sow other grains around the edges.
text: Wa a dan chalisi bu a magsi chaab wa kan bori ŋan baai nyum ale masa la bieŋa ale bie ŋaai nyum ale masa la? Wa kan bori daa ŋanbie kadukka po ale ŋan yona laŋka po?

ref: They learn this from their God.
text: Wa Wenni ale dak wa abe wa sak wa suik maŋka.

ref: Wheat and barley are pounded, but not beaten to pulp; they are run over with a wagon, but not ground to dust.
text: Ku a fɛ ate ba num ŋan bie a nye maasa, dila waai a kan fɔbi ŋa taam wuu. Wa dan poom ta wa toroko wiilima a tabi ŋa zuk, wa wusumaŋa a kan num ŋa.

ref: This wonderful knowledge comes from the Lord All-Powerful, who has such great wisdom.
text: Kude meena mɛ a nyini ka Naawen Dii Ale A De Tugurik Tɔŋdɔba Niŋ La jigi, dii ale kperi ale sakka ale zuak ale yam la.

ref: Jerusalem, city of David, the place of my altar, you are in for trouble! Celebrate your festivals year after year.
text: Ku ale toa a te Ariel, tɛŋ kaai ate Deevid a kali ka po la. Ben meena ni kasim a nye ni kaabka kama. Ale a de ni tiŋŋa.

ref: I will still make you suffer, and your people will cry when I make an altar of you.
text: Dila meena mi ale basi ate ba gilim Ariel tɛŋka. Wa le kum, abe wa nye ase juka kuŋkuŋ la a te mi.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will come to your rescue with a thundering earthquake and a fiery whirlwind.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale jam ale ka nanpansa ale tɛŋ choaka ale nuemka nna yegayega ale viok pagrik ale bolim ŋiak kaai ale a dɛ ŋanta.

ref: Every brutal nation that attacks Jerusalem and makes it suffer will disappear like a dream when night is over.
text: Ate tɛŋsaŋa meena dachaasaŋa ale kpaliŋ ale Ariel ale siti ka ale ka yie pagrisaŋa ale gilim ka la ale nye ase ka gɔdaasima ale pa sakka yok po la.

ref: Be shocked and stunned, you prophets! Refuse to see. Get drunk and stagger, but not from wine.
text: Ni baŋ nidek ate ku cha ni, abe ni yi ate ni kaa nya. Ni buk, alege ku a kan chim daam nyuka. Ni a ja alege ku kan chim daam nyuka.

ref: The Lord has made you drowsy; he put you into a deep sleep and covered your head.
text: Naawen a nye kama ate goom a jam ni jigi. Wa a lik wa biisiteerɔma nina kama. Wa ŋman lik wa biisiteerɔma zuimaŋa.

ref: Now his message is like a sealed letter to you. Some of you say, “We can't read it, because it's sealed.”
text: Fi jigi pa sakka de meena ka kinla alege ka wie nyiini a lik bo gbaŋka po. Ate fi dan weeni waai ale baga a karim ayen, <<Wa karim kude, >> Wa ale tulisi ayen, <<Mi an baga. Ba lik ka kama.>>

ref: Others say, “We can't read it, because we don't know how to read.”
text: Yaase fi dan pai te waai ale kan baga a karim la, ayen <<Wa karim kude.>> Wa ale tulisi ayen, <<Mi zɛ karimka.>>

ref: The Lord has said: “These people praise me with their words, but they never really think about me. They worship me by repeating rules made up by humans.
text: Nyɔnɔwa a weeni kama ayen, <<Nuruma de a jam a moata mi ale ka ba noaŋa ale a zuli mi ale ba nɔngbanvaataŋa, alege ba suiniimaŋa a yalima ale mi kama. Ka nuruba ale sak ba wie ate ba pai wa ŋala nyiini a puusi mi.

ref: So once again I will do things that shock and amaze them, and I will destroy the wisdom of those who claim to know and understand.”
text: Dila nyiŋla, mi ale ŋman cha nuruma de ale wakinkagla. Yam nyam yam ale be, sebrɔba sebika ale muriŋ bɛ.>>

ref: You are in for trouble, if you try to hide your plans from the Lord! Or if you think what you do in the dark can't be seen.
text: Ku ale toa a te baai ale a siŋ liuŋ po nna niŋniŋa a suk Naawen a nye ba wie la, ale baai ale a nye ba wie legi po ale a poli ayen, <<Ka wana ale nya ti? Ka wana ale seba?>>

ref: You have it all backwards. A clay dish doesn't say to the potter, “You didn't make me. You don't even know how.” Hope for the Future
text: Ni yik ka wie a tulim a basi tɛŋ, nna se mɛɛrɔwa ale tulim chim yak diila. Jaab ale weeni waai ale nye wa la ayen <<Wa an nye mi?>> Samɔniŋka ale baga a weeni mɛɛrɔwa ayen, <<Wa zɛ jaaboa?>>

ref: Soon the forest of Lebanon will become a field with crops, thick as a forest.
text: Ku a kan beni, ate Lebanon labri a chim tɛŋ poosukwa, ate tɛŋ poosuku a nye ase gɔi la?

ref: The deaf will be able to hear whatever is read to them; the blind will be freed from a life of darkness.
text: Dai dila danni, baai tue ale ka a wom la ale wom gbaŋka wieŋa ate legi po yeoba nina ale nya.

ref: The poor and the needy will celebrate and shout because of the Lord, the holy God of Israel.
text: Baai ale yik badek la ale ŋman nya masim Naawen nyiŋ. Ate baai ale a silim ŋanta la ale de masim Waai ale Welema a bo Izirali la nyiŋ.

ref: The Lord who rescued Abraham has this to say about Jacob's descendants: “They will no longer be ashamed and disgraced.
text: Dila nyiŋla, Naawen dii ale vari Abrayam a basi la, ale a weeni dii a te Jekob dɔkdemma la ale nna: <<Chivie a kan ŋman yik Jekob, chivie a kan ŋman bo ba nina po.

ref: When they see how great I have made their nation, they will praise and honor me, the holy God of Israel.
text: Ba dan nya mi nisimaŋa tuima ba bisaŋa po, ba ale ta mi yuenni ale weleŋsa. Ba ale siak Jekob Weleŋsa Nyɔnɔwa weleŋsaŋa, abe ba zaani a pai zula a te Izirali Wenni.

ref: Everyone who is confused will understand, and all who have complained will obey my teaching.”
text: Baai tue ale kpari la ale miŋ biik kiri. Ate baai ale a fɔbili la ale siak sinsaga.>>

ref: This is the Lord's message for his rebellious people: “You follow your own plans instead of mine; you make treaties without asking me, and you keep on sinning.
text: Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Ku ale toa a te bi sii tue ale kpari la, ate baai ale a pai zɔk ŋaai ale kan daa mi zɔga la, ale a nye nɔiyeŋ alege an nyini mi Chiika jigi la, a pai wabaata a vi chaab zuk la,

ref: You trust Egypt for protection. So you refuse my advice and send messengers to Egypt to beg their king for help.
text: a cheŋ siŋ Ejipiti alege an bek mi, baai ale gisi maarika a nyini Faaro jigi la, Ejipiti yɔgsum ayen ba suk la.

ref: “You will be disappointed, completely disgraced for trusting Egypt.
text: Alege Faaro likka ale te ni ka chivie, ate Ejipiti yɔgsummu ale ta chivie a jam ni jigi.

ref: The king's power reaches from the city of Zoan as far south as Hanes.
text: Ba dan poom ta kpaga ate ŋa bo Zoan, ate ba tomtomdɔma a paari Yanes,

ref: This is a message about the animals of the Southern Desert: “You people carry treasures on donkeys and camels. You travel to a feeble nation through a troublesome desert filled with lions and flying fiery dragons.
text: Naawen wa dii ale magsi chaab ale Negev duŋsaŋa la ale nna. Tɛŋ kaai ale pagra ate daanika ale gbeŋma ale gbeŋ niima ale waapiisa ale nakpaasa, tuimtomdɔma a pai ba jigsika a vi bonsa zuk, ba tuilum ŋantaŋa a vi laalaakomiba boataŋa zuk, a cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ale kan ta nyuenta la,

ref: Egypt can't help you! That's why I call that nation a helpless monster.” Israel Refuses To Listen
text: a cheŋ Ejipiti, kaai maarika ale bola kan ta kiri ya. Dila nyiŋla mi a wi wa ayen ka Arayab a Ka Tuintuini.

ref: The Lord told me to write down his message for his people, so that it would be there forever.
text: Cheŋ yɔgyɔgla de, a ga ŋmarisi a dueni tintain paglak nyiŋ a te ba, abe fi ŋman ŋmarisi a nyo gbaŋ po, ayen da ŋaai ale cheen la ku baga a chim taam wuu seerɔ kama.

ref: They have turned against the Lord and can't be trusted. They have refused his teaching
text: Ba ka nuru baai ale a zɛri wie, ba ka bi sii ale a velim ale bi sii ale kaa a yaali ayen ba wom Naawen ale a weeni diila.

ref: and have said to his messengers and prophets: Don't tell us what God has shown you and don't preach the truth. Just say what we want to hear, even if it's false.
text: Ba a weeni baai ale a nya wie la ayen, <<Ni kan ŋman a nya wie!>> ale a weeni biisiteerɔma ayen, <<Ni kan ŋman pai wamaŋsa wie a te ti! Ni weeni ti wamasisa, ni mooli pimpaasima wie.

ref: Stop telling us what God has said! We don't want to hear any more about the holy One of Israel.
text: Ni basi suiku de, ni nyini suiku po a nyini, abe ni kan ŋman ta Waai ale Welema Izirali po la wie a paari ti!>>

ref: Now this is the answer of the holy One of Israel: “You rejected my message, and you trust in violence and lies.
text: Dila nyiŋ, Waai ale Welema Izirali po la ale a weeni diila ale nna: <<Ni ale zɛri wanni de la nyiŋ, ale pa ni sebchakka a basi namsika zuk la ale pimpaasima zuk la,

ref: This sin is like a crack that makes a high wall quickly crumble
text: biemu de ale za bu jam ni zuk ase parik woŋ ale na a moata lueta, a yaa deri lo mwuli.

ref: and shatter like a crushed bowl. There's not a piece left big enough to carry hot coals or to dip out water.” Trust the Lord
text: Ka le wɛ ka nna bunabuna ase samɔniŋ la, a lo ate jiirim karo ate takabaŋa po takabi karo a pai bolim kaali daanika po yaase a kuuri nyiam samɔniŋ po.>>

ref: The holy Lord God of Israel had told all of you, “I will keep you safe if you turn back to me and calm down. I will make you strong if you quietly trust me.” Then you stubbornly
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen dii ale Welema a bo Izirali la ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Laŋ nyeka ale vuusum po ale fi ta varibasika, sinika ale mariŋka po ale fi ta pagrim, alege fi kan ta bade waai ya.

ref: As few as five of them, or even one, will be enough to chase a thousand of you. Finally, all that will be left will be a few survivors as lonely as a flag pole on a barren hill. The Lord Will Show Mercy
text: Nuru yeŋ nyigsika ale basi ate tusidi a chali, ate nuruba banu nyigsika ni meena ale chali, ate ba ga tali ni ase tikti la guuku zuk, ase tikti la pina zuk.>>

ref: The Lord God is waiting to show how kind he is and to have pity on you. The Lord always does right; he blesses those who trust him.
text: Alege Naawen a yaali kama ayen wa chim suipeentik a te ni. Wa yiti kama ayen wa sak jiirim. Dii nyiŋla Naawen ka nyemagsika Wen. Baai meena ale a limisi wa la ale nya niaka.

ref: People of Jerusalem, you don't need to cry anymore. The Lord is kind, and as soon as he hears your cries for help, he will come.
text: Zayon nuru baai ale bo Jerusalem po la, ni kan ŋman kum. Ni dan kum a yaali maarika wa jigi wa ale chim niauŋ a te ni. Wa dan ga wom wa le tulisi ni.

ref: The Lord has given you trouble and sorrow as your food and drink. But now you will again see the Lord, your teacher, and he will guide you.
text: Nyɔnɔwa a te ni ka dachaani ŋandiinta ale namsika nyiam, ni sagrɔma a kan ŋman suk, ni le pai nidek nina a nya ba.

ref: Whether you turn to the right or to the left, you will hear a voice saying, “This is the road! Now follow it.”
text: Ni dan poom cheem juga yaase gala, ni tueŋa ale wom lueluk ni ŋaaŋ, a weeni ayen, <<Suiku ale nna, ni cheŋ ku po.>>

ref: Then you will treat your idols of silver and gold like garbage; you will throw them away like filthy rags.
text: Ate ni le kaasi ni bɔgtaŋa ate ni pai kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a taari ŋa la. Ni le yuk ŋa a basi ase garuk daŋtik la a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni cheŋ du.>>

ref: The Lord will send rain to water the seeds you have planted—your fields will produce more crops than you need, and your cattle will graze in open pastures.
text: Wa ale basi ate ŋmoruk a ni a basi ni ŋan borintaŋa po, ate ni ale a nya ŋandiin tii tɛŋka zuk la ale nala abe ti piisi. Dai dila danni, ni niiŋa ale nya wuuk yɔksuk yegayega a ŋɔbi.

ref: Even the oxen and donkeys that plow your fields will be fed the finest grain.
text: Lalisaŋa ale bonsaŋa ale a kpa la ale ŋɔbi kinkaa ale wukosik ate ba pai ŋanta a kati a waaŋ la.

ref: On that day people will be slaughtered and towers destroyed, but streams of water will flow from high hills and towering mountains.
text: Dai dii dai ate ni dachaasaŋa a za ba kpi la ate ba yie woŋtaŋa a za ŋa lo la, beli naŋsa nyaata ale nyini guuta, meena zuk a siŋ.

ref: Then the Lord will bandage his people's injuries and heal the wounds he has caused. The moon will shine as bright as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter than usual. It will be like the light of seven days all at once. Assyria Will Be Punished
text: Chiika ale nyaksi ase wenbinni la, ate wenbinni nyaksika ale nye ka nna cheri ku naŋtuok nɔi buyopɔi, ase da puma ŋayopɔi bolim la, Naawen ale pɔbi wa nuruma mulaŋa abe wa tebi wa ale kɔni baai la.

ref: The Lord is coming from far away with his fiery anger and thick clouds of smoke. His angry words flame up like a destructive fire;
text: Ni nya, Naawen Yue a nyini ka niŋ a cheena ale suipuurum buui ale a dɛ la ale nyuisa chiŋma. Wa nɔngbanvaataŋa a sueri ale ka suipuurum, ate wa giŋgeluŋku a chim bolim buui ale a dɛ.

ref: he breathes out a flood that comes up to the neck. He sifts the nations and destroys them. Then he puts a bridle in every foreigner's mouth and leads them to doom.
text: Wa vuusumu a nye ase ka nyiam ale a wuuri la, a yiri jueli a paari ŋiri. Wa pai kaasuŋ yeliŋka a yeliŋ tɛŋsaŋa. Wa pa ka nɔi baŋsa a su ba noaŋa a ta ba a cheŋ bɛ.

ref: The Lord's people will sing as they do when they celebrate a religious festival at night. The Lord is Israel's mighty rock, and his people will be as happy as they are when they follow the sound of flutes to the mountain where he is worshiped.
text: Ate ni ale lenni yiila ase yok po tigi weleŋ ate ni a de la. Ni suiniima ale de masim ase nuruba ale ta paampuuŋta a jueli Naawen guuku, Izirali Piuŋku zuk la.

ref: The Lord will get furious. His fearsome voice will be heard, his arm will be seen ready to strike, and his anger will be like a destructive fire, followed by thunderstorms and hailstones.
text: Naawen ale basi ate nuruba a wom wa lueluk pagrika, abe wa basi ate ba nya wa nisaŋa ale a siŋ tɛŋ ale suipuurum ale bolim buui ale a dɛ la ale nyiam chiŋma, ale ŋmoruk viok ale ŋmoruk tana.

ref: When the Assyrians hear the Lord's voice and see him striking with his iron rod, they will be terrified.
text: Naawen lueluku ale kaasi Assiria. Wa ale pai wa dachekka a nak ba a lɔnsi tɛŋ.

ref: He will attack them in battle, and each time he strikes them, it will be to the music of tambourines and harps.
text: Nakka meena ate Naawen a pa wa namsika doani a nak la ale chim ka kayaksa ale kpanta yiili, ase wa le pai nigua a kpaliŋ ale ba kpaliŋka po la.

ref: Long ago the Lord got a place ready for burning the body of the dead king. The place for the fire is deep and wide, the wood is piled high, and the Lord will start the fire by breathing out flaming sulfur.
text: Ba gomsi Tofet ate ku beni ya. Ku gomsi a magsi naawa. Bolim golukku a limisa kama ale lagri, ale bolim yega ale daata. Naawen vuusumu a nye ase ka benaŋ ate bolim ŋiak a nyini du a de la.

ref: You are in for trouble if you go to Egypt for help, or if you depend on an army of chariots or a powerful cavalry. Instead you should depend on and trust the holy Lord God of Israel.
text: Ku ale toa a te baai ale a cheŋ Ejipiti a yaali maarika la, baai ale pai ba sebchakka a basi wusuma zuima la, baai ale ta sebchakka ale toroko boanni la, ale ba wusum duerɔma pagrimu la, alege a kan gisi Waai ale Welema a bo Izirali la, yaase ba gisi maarika a nyini Naawen jigi la.

ref: The Lord isn't stupid! He does what he promises, and he can bring doom. If you are cruel yourself, or help those who are evil, you will be destroyed.
text: Wala abe ale ta yam a baga a ta kaasuŋ a jam. Wa dan weeni wari, wa kan lugsi wa wieŋa. Wa ale yiti ŋmai a kpaliŋ ale ja bioku yenni ale baai ale a maari nuru baata ate ba a tom biem la.

ref: The Egyptians are mere humans. They aren't God. Their horses are made of flesh; they can't live forever. When the Lord shows his power, he will destroy the Egyptians and all who depend on them. Together they will fall.
text: Alege Ejipiti demma ka nurubisa ba daa Wen ya. Ba wusumaŋa a ta ka nyiŋlam ŋa ka chiisa. Dai dii dai ate Naawen a teeri wa nisaŋa la, waai ale a maari wa la ale nak naŋ a lo. Ate waai ate ba a maari la ale lo. Ba nɔi bayewa ale maa chaab a kpi.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful said to me, “I will roar and attack like a fearless lion not frightened by the shouts of shepherds trying to protect their sheep. That's how I will come down and fight on Mount Zion.
text: Nya kude ate Naawen a weeni mi ayen, <<Ase kom ale ta gbeŋli ate di yik jaab a boro a ŋɔbi ate naapeerisa a tigsi chaab ayen ba nyigsi di ale ba nakka yaase ba daani di ale ba kaarik la alege di an yɔgsa ale ba kaarika. Dila Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale siŋ a nye kpaliŋ Zayon Guuku ale ku zukparukku.

ref: People of Israel, come back! You have completely turned from the Lord.
text: Ni ŋman jam wa jigi ale ni tom a kaasi wa kama. Nama Izirali demma.

ref: The time is coming when you will throw away your idols of silver and gold, made by your sinful hands.
text: Ate da dila danni, ni waai meena ale zɛri kpana ale ligmɔniŋ bɔgtaŋa ate ni nisim baataŋa a nye la.

ref: The Assyrians will be killed, but not by the swords of humans. Their young men will try to escape, but they will be captured and forced into slavery.
text: Assiria demma ale lo ale gebik kaai ale kan daa saalɔ gebiga. Gebik kaai ale za ka kaasi ba la daa nurubiik ale nye ka. Gebik ka de nyiŋ, ba le chali a bɛ gebika. Ate ba bi paalukku ba fɛ ba ate ba tom tuim pagra.

ref: Their fortress will fall when terror strikes; their army officers will be frightened and run from the battle. This is what the Lord has said, the Lord whose fiery furnace is built on Mount Zion.
text: Ba pagrimu jigini ale lo tɛŋ yɔgsum nyiŋ. Ba kpaŋŋa a dan nya kpaliŋka tiktiwa ba kpaziita ale nak.>> Naawen ale weeni diila ale la, waai bolimu ale bo Zayon la, waai bolim dɔkku ale bo Jerusalem la.

ref: A king and his leaders will rule with justice.
text: Ni nya, naab ale dɛ naam ale wayɔrisima, ate kpaga ale dɛ naam ale nyemagsika.

ref: They will be a place of safety from stormy winds, a stream in the desert, and a rock that gives shade from the heat of the sun.
text: Nuru meena ale nye ase ka yɔgsum la a lik vioku ate ku kan paari fu ale sukka jigi ate ŋmoruk vioku a kan paari fu, ale benaŋsa ale bo gɔi po la, ale piuŋ kpioŋ yisuŋ ale bo tɛŋ kosik po la.

ref: Then everyone who has eyes will open them and see, and those who have ears will pay attention.
text: Dila baai nina ale a nya la a kan ŋman ligi, baai tue ale a wom la ale wom.

ref: All who are impatient will take time to think; everyone who stutters will talk clearly.
text: Waai ale a poli mwuli la ale seba abe wa miŋ chak, waai ale biisi a gagli la ale biisi nyaanti.

ref: Fools will no longer be highly respected, and crooks won't be given positions of honor.
text: Ba kan ŋman wi beruk ayen zula nyɔnɔ yaase paasidɔ ayen zula nyɔnɔ.

ref: Fools talk foolishness. They always make plans to do sinful things, to lie about the Lord, to let the hungry starve, and to keep water from those who are thirsty.
text: Beruk a biisi ka berinni, ate wa popolaŋa a kasim ta biem nyiini. Wa a nye ka wie ŋaai ate Naawen a kisa la, ale a nye wie a kaasi Naawen. Wa kan te kom ale ta baai la ŋandiinta ale a mini baai ate nyanyuila a ta la nyiam.

ref: Cruel people tell lies— they do evil things, and make cruel plans to destroy the poor and needy, even when they beg for justice.
text: Paasidɔwa nyeelaŋa ka gaasa nyiini, wa a nye ka biem wie ayen wa kaasi jajakka ale venta, jajakka wanni a dan poom ta wensie, wa bo a mini wa.

ref: But helpful people can always be trusted to make helpful plans. Punishment for the Women of Jerusalem
text: Alege zula nyɔnɔ a zɔk ka zula zɔga, wa zulaŋa nyiŋ wa a zaani kama.

ref: You may not have worries now, but in about a year, the grape harvest will fail, and you will tremble.
text: Ku dan gaam bein maga dega nama baai ale a poli ayen ni bo ka boka dek jigi la ale lo, tii sii ale a yɔni yɔna la a kan ŋman yɔni.

ref: Slap your breasts in sorrow because of what happened to the fruitful fields and vineyards,
text: Ni a nak kuusidi laŋ maŋsaŋa ale yɔna tiisaŋa

ref: The palace will be deserted, the crowded city empty. Fortresses and towers will forever become playgrounds for wild donkeys and pastures for sheep. God's Spirit Makes the Difference
text: Yie pagrisaŋa ba le banti ŋa, nuemka tɛŋka a doa koruk, guuta ale gboŋ woŋku ale chim tɛŋ kaai ale kan ta kiri la taam wuu, bonsa boka jigi ale duŋsa dɛka jigi,

ref: When the Spirit is given to us from heaven, deserts will become orchards thick as fertile forests.
text: ate ku paari diipo ate Naawen Chiika ale nyini ŋmazuk a siŋ ti zuk la, ate gɔnni ale chim laŋ poosuk abe laŋ poosuku a nye ase sagi la.

ref: even if hailstones flatten forests and cities.
text: Ŋmoruk tana a dan lo gɔnni po ate tɛŋ kpieŋka a ŋɔriŋ meena,

ref: You will have God's blessing, as you plant your crops beside streams, while your donkeys and cattle roam freely about.
text: nya ku le chim suipeentik dii a te ni, ate ni a bori ni ŋantaŋa buboalisa nɔi meena ale basi ate ni niiŋa ale ni bonsaŋa a dɛ nna fasiyaa.

ref: You defeated my people. Now you're in for trouble! You've never been destroyed, but you will be destroyed; you've never been betrayed, but you will be betrayed. When you have finished destroying and betraying, you will be destroyed and betrayed in return.
text: Ku le toa a te fi kaasirɔwa, fi waai ate ba an kaasi la. Ku le toa a te fu bumbobrɔwa, fi waai ate ba an bobri fi wari la. Ase fi a dan basi kaasika, ba ale kaasi fu, ase fi a dan basi bobrika, ba ale bobri fi wie.

ref: Please, Lord, be kind to us! We depend on you. Make us strong each morning, and come to save us when we are in trouble.
text: Naawen yaa, ta ŋmantiik ale ti. Ti kasim a gisi fu kama. Chim ti pagrɔ saluik meena, abe fi chim ti varibasidɔ diipo ate ti bo daanika po la.

ref: Nations scatter when you roar and show your greatness.
text: Fi lueluku a dan na nuruma a chali, fi dan vaari yiti tɛŋsaŋa meena a waaŋ ka chaab.

ref: You, Lord, are above all others, and you live in the heavens. You have brought justice and fairness to Jerusalem;
text: Naawen a nya ka pimpauk diila wa bo ka wen. Wa le basi ate nyemagsika ale wayɔrisima a sueri Zayon.

ref: you are the foundation on which we stand today. You always save us and give true wisdom and knowledge. Nothing means more to us than obeying you. The Lord Will Do Something
text: Wa ale chim nyubi dek a magsi ni vaaŋa po, tigi a magsi varibasika ale yam ale sebika. Naawen yɔgsum chalika ka saari fiik a magsi jigini de.

ref: Listen! Our bravest soldiers are running through the streets, screaming for help. Our messengers hoped for peace, but came home crying.
text: Nya, ba nidoa tuasaŋa a kaari ate ku a jueli kama suitaŋa po, suiyɔgni nyama a kum kama tuotuowa.

ref: No one travels anymore; every road is empty. Treaties are broken, and no respect is shown to any who keep promises.
text: Ba banti suik doataŋa kama, nyeendɔba a ka suitaŋa po. Nɔiyeŋka a kaasi ya, baai ale za ka ŋaaŋ la a waaŋ ya, ba waai a ka zula.

ref: Fields are dry and barren; Mount Lebanon wilts with shame. Sharon Valley is a desert; the forests of Bashan and Carmel have lost their leaves.
text: Tɛŋka a kum kama ale kpeeri a bɛ, chivie a ta Lebanon ate ka kpi. Saaron a nye ase ka Araba la, ate Basan ale Karmel vaataŋa a wiiri a lo.

ref: But the Lord says, “Now I will do something and be greatly praised.
text: Naawen ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de m le vaari yiti, yɔgyɔgla de m le nya pimpauk, yɔgyɔgla de m le nya zak zaanika.

ref: Your deeds are straw that will be set on fire by your very own breath.
text: Ni yik ka yaata puuk, ni biak kinkaa, Ni vuusumu ka bolim a dɛ ni.

ref: You will be burned to ashes like thorns in a fire.
text: Nuruma ale dɛ a chim buntuem, ase munsa ate ba che basi la, ba ale chɔgsi bolim.>>

ref: Everyone, both far and near, come look at what I have done. See my mighty power!” Punishment and Rewards
text: Nama baai ale yalima la, a wom dii ate mi nye la, nama baai ale moata la ni miŋ m pagrimu.

ref: But there will be rewards for those who live right and tell the truth, for those who refuse to take money by force or accept bribes, for all who hate murder and violent crimes.
text: Ka waai ale a cheŋ wayɔrisima po ale a biisi dii ale magsi, waai ale a zɛri nyuenta a nyini varidɔba jigi la ate wa nisa kan tuesi ŋan baai ate ba pai a da wa la, waai ale kaa wom nuru koorisa wie a kan chamu biem wie la.

ref: They will live in a fortress high on a rocky cliff, where they will have food and plenty of water. The Lord Is Our King
text: Nuruwa de ale wa bo ŋmai, waai sukka jigi ale ku chim guuku yie pagrisaŋa la. Wa le nya ŋandiinta, wa be kan silim nyiamoa.

ref: With your own eyes you will see the glorious King; you will see his kingdom reaching far and wide.
text: Fi ninaŋa ale nya naawa wa nalimu po, abe fi nya tɛŋ kaai ale tati a cheŋ niŋ la.

ref: Then you will ask yourself, “Where are those officials who terrified us and forced us to pay such heavy taxes?”
text: Fi popola po fi ale poli yikaasidɔ kpakka wari ayen, <<Kpagi kpienni a bo ka bɛ? Waai ale a tuesi ligraŋa la a bo ka bɛ? Waai ale a nya yie woŋtaŋa zuk la a bo ka bɛ?>>

ref: You will never again have to see the proud people who spoke a strange and foreign language you could not understand.
text: Fi a kan ŋman nya kayerinni nuruma de, nuru baai ale a biisi bichaŋ la, ate ba pai ba giŋgeluŋta a biisi bi chaŋsa ate si miŋka a toa la.

ref: Look to Mount Zion where we celebrate our religious festivals. You will see Jerusalem, secure as a tent with pegs that cannot be pulled up and fastened with ropes that can never be broken.
text: Ni zak nya Zayon, ni tiŋŋa tɛŋka, ni nina ale nya Jerusalem, suiyɔgni boka jigi, viuk kuui ale kaa yeeri la, ku kpaasaŋa a kan voori yaase ku miisaŋa kanyi mɛ la a gebi.

ref: Our wonderful Lord will be with us! There will be deep rivers and wide streams safe from enemy ships. The Lord Is Our Judge
text: Dula Naawen ale chim ti Tanjaŋini. Ku ale nye ase ka benaŋsa ale buboalisa jigi la. Ŋaaruŋ kpioŋ an baga a cheŋ ŋa zuwa yaase ku baga a zaani ŋa zuwa yaase ku baga a zaani ŋa nɔi ya.

ref: The Lord is our judge and our ruler; the Lord is our king and will keep us safe.
text: Naawen ale tama boteerɔ. Naawen ale a te tama sinsaga. Naawen ale ti naab. Ka wala ale wa vari ti a basi.

ref: But your nation is a ship with its rigging loose, its mast shaky, and its sail not spread. Someday even you that are lame will take everything you want from your enemies.
text: Ni miisaŋa a baliŋ kama. Chimmu a ŋman ka pagrimoa, ate ŋaaruŋku a kan damu a cheŋ niŋŋa. Ate ni ale nye kpaliŋsa a nya ŋan baai a nyini du la, ba ale lab ŋa a te chaab ate gbansa mɛ ale nya ba nitalim.

ref: The Lord will forgive your sins, and none of you will say, “I feel sick.”
text: Waai a kan bo Zayon po a weeni ayen, <<Mi a yuak kama.>> Ate baai ale bo dula la biemu a nya vɔŋteka.

ref: Their dead bodies will be left to rot and stink; their blood will flow down the mountains.
text: Ba ale yuk nuru baai ate ba ko la a basi, ba kpiema ale kasim a nyuŋ, ba ziitaŋa ale tagli guutaŋa zuima meena.

ref: Each star will disappear— the sky will roll up like a scroll. Everything in the sky will dry up and wilt like leaves on a vine or fruit on a tree. Trouble for Edom
text: Chiŋmarisaŋa meena ale bo wenzukku la ale nyaliŋ, ate wenzuk a kpamsi ase duŋ gbaŋ la. Chiŋmarisaŋa meena ale wiiri lo ase tiib vaata la, ase moota ale nyini kiŋkaŋ zuk a lo diila.

ref: After the sword of the Lord has done what it wants to the skies above, it will come down on Edom, the nation that the Lord has doomed for destruction.
text: M gebika a nyu chak kama wenŋmazuk. Ni nya, ka siŋ cheen ka Edom zuk ale buusa, ba ka nuru baai ate mi a poom ŋaam a kaasi ba la.

ref: The sword of the Lord is covered with blood from lambs and goats, together with fat from kidneys of rams. This is because the Lord will slaughter many people and make a sacrifice of them in the city of Bozrah and everywhere else in Edom.
text: Naawen gebika a so ale ka ziim. Kpaam ale lik ka ale pa bisa ale bua ziita ale kpaam a nyini padaasa yiima po. Diila Naawen a ta ka kaabka a bo Bozra ale tɔgrik kpieŋ a bo Edom.

ref: Edom's leaders are wild oxen. They are powerful bulls, but they will die with the others. Their country will be soaked with their own blood, and its soil made fertile with their own fat.
text: Ate lalik jeeŋ kaai ale waara la ale lalikbilisa ale lalik kpieŋsa ale lɔ tɛŋ ale ba. Ziim ale tagli ba tɛŋka zuk, ate kpaam ale mooŋ nyuŋku.

ref: The Lord has chosen the year and the day, when he will take revenge and come to Zion's defense.
text: Diila Naawen a ta ka dai ayen wa tuni baai ale nye biem la. Ku ale chim ka namsika ben, ayen wa pai a nye a maari Zayon.

ref: Edom's streams will turn into tar and its soil into sulfur— then the whole country will go up in flames.
text: Edom beli naŋsaŋa ale chim kotaali, ate nyuŋku ale chim bolim kaala, ate wa tɛŋka ale chim kotaali bolim.

ref: It will burn night and day and never stop smoking. Edom will be a desert, generation after generation; no one will ever travel through that land.
text: Bu a kan kpi yok yaase kantueŋŋa. Bu nyuisaŋa ale kasim a yiti kama taam wuu. Gaŋsa tɔgatɔga ale jam taam, ka ale diem chim ka tɛŋ lɔri a dua. Nuru a kan ŋman va ka po a taam.

ref: Owls, hawks, and wild animals will make it their home. God will leave it in ruins, merely a pile of rocks. The End of Edom
text: Kpaluŋ ale viuk ale tuesi ka. Viuk kpioŋ ale tagaaruk ale yɔk tukta dula. Wen ale teeri butimka magsika miika ale kaasuŋ magsika jaamu a basi Edom zuk.
