text: Diila fi ale teeri cheŋ juga ale gala. Fi ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale tuesi tɛŋsa a kali si tɛŋ kottaŋa po.

ref: Don't be afraid or ashamed and don't be discouraged. You won't be disappointed. Forget how sinful you were when you were young; stop feeling ashamed for being left a widow.
text: <<Kan chali yɔgsummoa. Chivie a kan yik fu. Kanpiinta a kan yik fu, fi a kan chim ja valiŋŋa. Fi ale baŋ fi paalimu po chivieŋa, fi kan ŋman teeri fi pukɔgini po niniŋŋa.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful, the Holy God of Israel, rules all the earth. He is your Creator and husband, and he will rescue you.
text: Diila fi Nyeerɔwa ale fi chorɔ. Wa yuenni ale Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ la, Waai Ale Welema Izirali po la ale fi Da Tuesirɔwa. Ba a wi wa ayen ka tɛŋzuk de meena Wen.

ref: You were like a young wife, brokenhearted and crying because her husband had divorced her. But the Lord your God says, “I am taking you back!
text: Naawen ale ŋman wi fu ase nipok waai ate ba zɛri ate ku a daani wa chiika po la, nipok waai ale yali wa paalim po ate ba zɛri wa la, >> Ka fi Wenni ale weeni.

ref: I rejected you for a while, but with love and tenderness I will embrace you again.
text: <<Ku an beni ya ate mi a banti fu basi, alege jiirim nyiŋ m le ŋman ta fu a jam.

ref: For a while, I turned away in furious anger. Now I will have mercy and love you forever! I, your protector and Lord, make this promise.” The Lord Promises Lasting Peace
text: Suipuurum nyiŋ ate mi jam suk m nimbidiaka a nyini fi jigi maga dega, alege ŋmanteka nyiŋ, m le ta jiirim ale fu,>> Ka Naawen fi Da Tuesirɔwa ale weeni.

ref: I once promised Noah that I would never again destroy the earth by a flood. Now I have promised that I will never again get angry and punish you.
text: <<Mi jigi kude a nye ase ka Nowa daaŋa po la, ase mi ale jam pɛ ayen Nowa nyaataŋa a kan lik tɛŋzuk de ŋmana la. Dila yɔgyɔgla de mi pɛ kama ayen m sui a kan ŋman puuri ale fu, m be kan ŋman toariŋ fu diipo.

ref: Every mountain and hill may disappear. But I will always be kind and merciful to you; I won't break my agreement to give your nation peace. The New Jerusalem
text: Guutaŋa a dan poom a choa ate pinaŋa a voori, mi ŋmanteka a kan choa yaase m suiyɔgni nɔiyeŋka a yeeri,>> Ka Naawen dii ale ta jiirim ale fu la ale weeni.

ref: Jerusalem, you are sad and discouraged, tossed around in a storm. But I, the Lord, will rebuild your city with precious stones; for your foundation I will use blue sapphires.
text: <<Tɛŋ kaai ate ku jo ka nyiŋla, ate ŋmoruk viok a kuri ka alege daa sui yɔkka la, m le pai tintain ŋmiŋmirita a sɛ fu, fi nyubini m pai tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase gunungoona la a dueni.

ref: I will teach your children and make them successful.
text: Naawen ale sak fi nidoabilisaŋa meena, ate fi bisaŋa suiyɔgni ale zuak nna yegayega.

ref: You will be built on fairness with no fears of injustice; every one of your worries will be taken far from you.
text: Wayɔrisima po fi ale zaani paari. Namsika ale yalima ale fu. Fi kan chali yɔgsum ale jaaboa. Yɔgsum ale nyini fi po a cheŋ. Bu kan jam a moata fu.

ref: I will never send anyone to attack your city, and you will make prisoners of those who do attack.
text: Waai a dan ta chaab ale fu, daa mi ale nye ya. Waai ale a ta chaab ale fu la, wa le siak a te fu.

ref: Don't forget that I created metalworkers who make weapons over burning coals. I also created armies that can bring destruction.
text: <<Nya, ka mi ale waai ale nye choabiika la, waai ale fuk kaalaŋa ate ŋa toati bolim ŋiak, a nye kpaliŋ jaab a magsi tuini. Ku be ka mi ale nye kaasirɔwa ate wa a ta butimka a jam.

ref: Weapons made to attack you won't be successful; words spoken against you won't hurt at all. My servants, Jerusalem is yours! I, the Lord, promise to bless you with victory.
text: Kpaliŋ jabuui ale a tu chaab ale fi la a kan baga nye fu wari ya, ate fi ale zɛri waai ale biisi a ŋma fu la. Naawen tomteerɔma nitalim ale la. Maarika de ate ba nya a nyini mi jigi,>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: If you are thirsty, come and drink water! If you don't have any money, come, eat what you want! Drink wine and milk without paying a cent.
text: <<Jam, nama baai meena ate nyanyuila a ta la, ni jam nyiamu jigini, nama baai ale kan ta ligra la, ni jam a da abe ni dɛ! Ni jam da daam ale biisim, daa ligri ate ni pai a da yaase jaaboa.

ref: Why waste your money on what really isn't food? Why work hard for something that doesn't satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and you will enjoy the very best foods.
text: Ka boa ate ni pai ligra a kaasi jabuui ale kan daa ŋandiinta la zuk ale a nam jabuui ale kaa chak ni la zuwa? Wom, wom mi, a dɛ jabuui ale nala la, ate ni nya masim a nyini ŋandiin maŋsa po.

ref: Pay close attention! Come to me and live. I will promise you the eternal love and loyalty that I promised David.
text: Lak tue a wom a jam mi jigi. Wom mi, ate ni chiisaŋa a baga a boro. Mi ale nye nɔiyeŋ kaai ale kaa taam la ale ni, m ŋmanteka ate m sak ale Deevid la.

ref: I made him the leader and ruler of the nations; he was my witness to them.
text: Nya, m nye kama ate wa chim seerɔ a te nuruma, ate wa chim niŋdeerɔ ale kpagi nuruma zuk.

ref: You will call out to nations you have never known. And they have never known you, but they will come running because I am the Lord, the holy God of Israel, and I have honored you. God's Words Are Powerful
text: Chekki ni ale wi tɛŋ sii ate ni zɛ la, ate tɛŋ sii ale kan seba ni la ale kpabi a wom ayen Naawen ni Wenni nyiŋ, Waai Ale Welema Izirali po la, diila wa te ni ka nalim.

ref: Turn to the Lord! He can still be found. Call out to God! He is near.
text: Gisi Naawen ale ni diem baga a nya wa. Wi wa ale wa diem moata ni.

ref: Give up your evil ways and your evil thoughts. Return to the Lord our God. He will be merciful and forgive your sins.
text: Te ate gaasa nyɔnɔwa a basi wa nyeka ate nuru bioku a basi wa popolaŋa. Te ate wa cheŋ Naawen ti Wenni jigi, wa le ta jiirim ale wa a vɔŋ te nna fasiyaa.

ref: The Lord says: “My thoughts and my ways are not like yours.
text: <<Mi ale a poli diila daa ni ale a poli diila yaase ni suitaŋa ka mi suitaŋa,>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Just as the heavens are higher than the earth, my thoughts and my ways are higher than yours.
text: <<Ase wenŋmazukku ale jueli a gaam tɛŋzuk de diila, dila mɛ ate m suitaŋa a jueli a gaam ni suitaŋa, ate m popolaŋa a gaam ni popolaŋa.

ref: “Rain and snow fall from the sky. But they don't return without watering the earth that produces seeds to plant and grain to eat.
text: Ase ŋmorukku ale ŋmoruk tanaŋa ale nyini wenzukku a siŋ ale kan ŋmani la, a kan zaŋti tɛŋzuk de a yɔgi ate ŋanta a pusi la, ate ŋa a nye bie a te bodɔwa ale ŋandiinta a te dɛɛrɔwa la,

ref: That's how it is with my words. They don't return to me without doing everything I send them to do.” God's People Will Celebrate
text: dila mɛ ate m wanni ale nyini mi nɔnni po a nyini. Di kan ŋman jam m jigi kinla, alege di le nye mi ale a yaali diila abe di tom dii ate m tom di la.

ref: When you are set free, you will celebrate and travel home in peace. Mountains and hills will sing as you pass by, and trees will clap.
text: Ni ale nyini peelim ale masim abe suiyɔgni a de ni niŋ. Guutaŋa ale pinaŋa ale lenni yiila ni niŋ, ate tiisaŋa meena ale bo kaduksaŋa po la ale nak si nisaŋa.

ref: Cypress and myrtle trees will grow in fields once covered by thorns. And then those trees will stand as a lasting witness to the glory of the Lord.
text: Ku le magsi ku chim munsa la, ku le tagri chim ka dapeelita tiisa, ku le magsi ku chim muŋkangɔtisa la, ku le tagri chim ka puuta tiisa a nyini du. Kude ale ta ka yuei a jam te Naawen ate ku chim daana ŋaai ale ŋa boro taam wuu la, ŋaai ale kaa kaasi.>>

ref: The Lord said: Be honest and fair! Soon I will come to save you; my saving power will be seen everywhere on earth.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Kasim ta nyemagsika nyeela abe fi nye dii ale magsi la, diila m varibasika a moata kama ate m wayɔrisimaŋa a kan beni ale peelim nyinika.

ref: Foreigners who worship me must not say, “The Lord won't let us be part of his people.” Men who are unable to become fathers must no longer say, “We are dried-up trees.”
text: Kan basi ate nichaanɔ ale pai wadek a te Naawen la a weeni ayen, <<Naawen ale gaari mi a nyini wa nuruma po.>> Abe fi kan basi ate ba le jɛ waai la a fɔbili ayen, <<Mi ka tiib kosik nyiini.>>

ref: Then you will be like monuments in my temple with your names written on them. This will be much better than having children, because these monuments will stand there forever.
text: bala m yenni ale parisaŋa po m le te ba ka teerika ale yuei ate di gaam nidoabilisa ale lieba. Mi ale te ba yuei dii ale boro taam wuu ate di kan bɛ.

ref: Foreigners will follow me. They will love me and worship in my name; they will respect the Sabbath and keep our agreement.
text: Ate nicham baai ale pai badek a te Naawen ayen ba tom a te wa, abe ba yaali Naawen yuenni abe ba a puusi wa la, baai meena ale ta Vuusumu Danni ale kan kaasi di, ale baai ale ta m nɔiyeŋka giŋgiŋ la,

ref: I will bring them to my holy mountain, where they will celebrate in my house of worship. Their sacrifices and offerings will always be welcome on my altar. Then my house will be known as a house of worship for all nations.
text: bade ale m ta a jam m tuilum guuku zuk a te ba masim m puusa yenni po. M le tuesi ba juka tiiritaŋa ale ba kaabka m kuŋkuŋku zuk, diila mi yenni yuei ale puusa yeri a te tɛŋsa meena.

ref: I, the Lord, promise to bring together my people who were taken away, and let them join the others. God Promises To Punish Israel's Leaders
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen a weeni kama ayen, wa ale waai ale tigsi Izirali demma ale bo yɔntini po la. <<Mi ale diem tigsi ba chaab a gum du a te ba, baai ale poom ŋaam tigsi la ba tɔga.>>

ref: Come from the forest, you wild animals! Attack and gobble up your victims.
text: Ni jam, nama duŋ sii meena ale bo gɔnni po la, ni jam nɛ, nama duŋ sii meena ale bo gɔnni po la.

ref: You leaders of Israel should be watchdogs, protecting my people. But you can't see a thing, and you never warn them. Dozing and daydreaming are all you ever do.
text: Izirali limisidɔma ka yeoba, ba meena a silim ka yam. Ba ka bagaanta, ba kan wosi. Ba doa kama a gilim a gɔdaasim, ba kasim a yaali ka goom.

ref: You stupid leaders are a pack of hungry and greedy dogs that never get enough. You are shepherds who mistreat your own sheep for selfish gain.
text: Ba ka ba sii ale ta koarisa nna yegayega, jaab kan paari ba. Ba ka naapeerik sii ale a silim miŋka. Ba meena a va ka badek suik, wanyi meena a gisi wadek paaruŋ.

ref: You say to each other, “Let's drink till we're drunk! Tomorrow we'll do it again. We'll really enjoy ourselves.”
text: Waai meena a kum a weeni kama ayen, <<Jam, te m nya daam! Basi ate ti nyu daam a chak! Ale chum ale nye ase jinla la yaase ku poom a gaam dila.>>

ref: but in death they find peace for obeying God. The Lord Condemns Idolatry
text: Baai ale a cheŋ yɔrr la a jo ka suiyɔgni po. Ba dan kpi doa ba a nya ka vuusum.

ref: You people are unfaithful! You go to fortunetellers, and you worship idols. Now pay close attention!
text: Alege ni jam de, nama chichirik wiirisa nidoabilisa, nama kaboŋ nyeerisa ale taabuksa bisa!

ref: Who are you making fun of? Who are you sneering at? Look how your sins have made fools of you.
text: Ka wana ate ni koosi a la? Ka wana ate ni yik nimbie a kaasi ale a yeeri ni giŋgeluŋta? Ni daa tukpari ale venta nyam bisa?

ref: All you think about is sex under those green trees where idols are worshiped. You sacrifice your children on altars built in valleys under rocky slopes.
text: Koarisa ale a dɛ ni kinkaŋpettaŋa ale ti sii meena ale a teeri la po. Ni pai ni bisaŋa a nye ka kaabka vooliŋsaŋa ale pinaŋa ale zuli wen la muulisaŋa po.

ref: You have chosen to worship idols made of stone; you have given them offerings of wine and grain. Should I be pleased?
text: Bɔgtaŋa ale bo vooliŋsaŋa tintain saalisaŋa po la ka nama ale soa. Mm, ti ka ni ŋanta, ti zuk ni kpiiri ka nyuka tiirita ale te ti ŋandiinta tiirita. Ŋade meena po, ku a magsi ayen m sui peenti?

ref: You have spread out your beds on the tops of high mountains, where you sacrifice to idols.
text: Fi nye fi gaduokku ka guuk ale jueli wen ale nala la zuk. Dula jigini fi ga nye ka kaabka.

ref: Even in your homes you have placed pagan symbols all around your huge beds. Yes, you have rejected me, sold yourselves to your lovers, and gone to bed with them.
text: Fi tuataŋa ŋaaŋ ale fi tuataŋa zuk fi pai fi bɔgluk ŋantaŋa a yik du kama. Fi banti mi kama ale lak fi gaduokku a basi, fi jueli ka ku zuk ale lak ku nna jassi. Fi nyeka nɔiyeŋ ale baai gaduata ate fi a yaali la ale nya ba chaboalaŋa.

ref: You smear on olive oil and all kinds of perfume to worship the god Molech. You even seek advice from spirits of the dead.
text: Fi ta ka kpaam a cheŋ Molek ale nye ate fi ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a piisi. Fi yiak baai ale tagri za fi naŋkula po la a basi ka nna niŋniŋŋa. Fi siŋka boosuku dek po!

ref: Though you tired yourself out by running after idols, you refused to stop. Your desires were so strong that they kept you going.
text: Fi jam jiak kama fi suitaŋa po meena, alege fi an jam a weeni ayen, <<Yiila karo>>, Fi ŋman jam nya fi pagrimu kama, ate dila basi ate fi an cha vuusummoa.

ref: Did you forget about me and become unfaithful because you were more afraid of someone else? Have I been silent so long that you no longer fear me?
text: <<Ka wana ate fi yɔgsa ale wa ate ku a daani fu, ate fi chim venta nyɔnɔ a te mi yaase fi an poom teeri m wari yaase fi poom a poli kude fi suinum po? Ku be ka mi ale nye chim ate ku beni la nyiŋ ale soa ate fi kan chali mu?

ref: You think you're so good, but I'll point out the truth.
text: M le ta fi wayɔrisimaŋa ale fi tuimaŋa a nyini peelim, ate ŋa kan te fu nyuenta.

ref: Ask your idols to save you when you are in trouble. Be careful though— it takes only a faint breath to blow them over. But if you come to me for protection, this land and my holy mountain will always belong to you. The Lord Helps the Helpless
text: Ase fi dan kaari a yaali maarika, fi basi ate fi bɔgtaŋa ate fi tigsi gum chaab la a vari fu basi, viok ale ji ba meena a cheŋ, vuusum nyiini ale ji ba a ta cheŋ. Alege nuru waai ale pai mi a chim wa sukka jigi la ale tuesi tɛŋka abe wa soa m tuilum guuku.>>

ref: Our holy God lives forever in the highest heavens, and this is what he says: Though I live high above in the holy place, I am here to help those who are humble and depend only on me.
text: Ka nnala ate waai ale bo ŋmai ale nala la, waai ale boro taam wuu la, waai yuenni ale ka weleŋsa la, ale weeni ayen, <<Mi bo ka ŋmai ale weleŋsa jigi, ale ŋman boro ale waai ale nya kaasuŋ ate ku a daani wa chiik po la, a ta tagruŋ a jam chiik kaai ale yik ka dek la ale a tagri chiik kaai suinum po la ale a yik ka dek la.

ref: My people, I won't stay angry and keep on accusing you. After all, I am your Creator. I don't want you to give up in complete despair.
text: Mi a kan kaasim a ŋma ni taam wuu, yaase m sui a kasim a puuri ale ni, dila ale te ate nurubiik chiika a kasim a cha m niŋ ale nuru vuusum ate m nye la.

ref: Your greed made me furious. That's why I punished you and refused to be found, while you kept returning to your old sinful ways.
text: M sui ale jam puuri ale wa ale a yaali biem nyeka la nyiŋ. Mi jam a namsi wa kama ale suk m nimbidiaka a nyini wa jigi ale suipuurum alege wa kasim a nye ka wa ale a yaali diila.

ref: I know what you are like! But I will heal you, lead you, and give you comfort, until those who are mourning
text: Mi nya wa suitaŋa kama, alege m le tebi wa. M le cheŋ ale wa abe m ŋman yɔk wa sui,

ref: start singing my praises. No matter where you are, I, the Lord, will heal you and give you peace.
text: abe maa nye ate pimpauk a bo Izirali baai ale a kum la nɔi po. Suiyɔgni, suiyɔgni a cheŋ baai ale yalima ale baai ale moata la jigi,>> Naawen ale weeni ayen, <<Mi ale tebi ba.>>

ref: But I, the Lord, have promised that none who are evil will live in peace.
text: Mi Wenni ale weeni ayen, <<Suiyɔgni a karo a te gaasa nyɔnɔwa.>>

ref: Shout the message! Don't hold back. Say to my people Israel: You've sinned! You've turned against the Lord.
text: <<Na ate ku jueli kan sina. Te fi lueluku a jueli ase damuniŋ la. Weeni m nuruma ba tukpanni ale Jekob yenni ba wabaataŋa.

ref: Day after day, you worship him and seem eager to learn his teachings. You act like a nation that wants to do right by obeying his laws. You ask him about justice, and say you enjoy worshiping the Lord.
text: Daa meena ba a gisi mi. Ba nyiŋsa a zak kama ayen ba miŋ m suitaŋa, nna se ba ka tɛŋ kaai ale a nye dii ale yoarisi la ale an zɛri Wenni wieŋa la. Ba a bek mi a yaali popola ŋaai ale chim wensie ale a nya nna se ba ka baai nyiŋsa ale a zak a yaali ayen Wen jam moata ba la.

ref: You wonder why the Lord pays no attention when you go without eating and act humble. But on those same days that you give up eating, you think only of yourselves and abuse your workers.
text: Ba a weeni kama ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate ti a bobi noa, alege ate fi an nya ku? Ka boan nyiŋ ate ti zɛri tidek, alege ate fi an miŋ ya? <<Ni nɔi bobika danni ni nye ka nidek ale a yaali diila ale pai ni tuimtomdɔma meena nyiŋ a nya nyuenta.

ref: Do you think the Lord wants you to give up eating and to act as humble as a bent-over bush? Or to dress in sackcloth and sit in ashes? Is this really what he wants on a day of worship?
text: Ka nɔi bobika de choa ate mi a lueri, ayen nuru a pai dai yeŋ nyiini a zɛri wadega? Ku ka fi su fi zuk tɛŋ nyiini ase wobi la, abe fi doa boorisa garuk zuk ale buntuem po? Ka dii ate ni a wi ayen nɔi bobika la, dai dii ate Naawen a siak la?

ref: I'll tell you what it really means to worship the Lord. Remove the chains of prisoners who are bound unjustly. Free those who are abused!
text: Daa nɔi bobika de choa ate mi lueri ayen m gebi venta chɔrima abe m yeeri niiga diokku a basi, abe m tuesi baai ate ba a namsi la a basi, abe m wɛ niiga diok meena?

ref: Share your food with everyone who is hungry; share your home with the poor and homeless. Give clothes to those in need; don't turn away your relatives.
text: Daa fi nye ŋandiinta a te waai ate kɔm a ta wa la, abe fi te jajak kaai ale nyiem a tuinti la goom jigi ya, fi dan nya chaboala nyɔnɔ te wa garuk, abe fi kan basi waai ate fi ale wa a chim ziim yem la?

ref: Then your light will shine like the dawning sun, and you will quickly be healed. Your honesty will protect you as you advance, and the glory of the Lord will defend you from behind.
text: Ate fi bolimu ale na nyini ase varivientidi la, ate fi ale kpabi a nya fi tebika. Ate fi wayɔrisimaŋa ale de fi niŋ a cheŋ, Ate Naawen zulaŋa ale sum chim fi limisidɔ.

ref: When you beg the Lord for help, he will answer, “Here I am!” Don't mistreat others or falsely accuse them or say something cruel.
text: Ate fi ale wi ate Naawen ale tulisi. Fi ale kaari a yaali maarika, ate wa ale weeni ayen, Mi bo ka dela. <<Fi a dan pai ŋiri namsika diokku a basi ale nisa dakka ale gaasa wie weenika,

ref: Give your food to the hungry and care for the homeless. Then your light will shine in the dark; your darkest hour will be like the noonday sun.
text: ale te baai ate kɔm a ta ba la ale pai baai ale a nam la ale a yaali ŋan baai la a te ba, dila ale te ate fi bolimu a toati legini po, ate fi yokku ale chim kantueŋ.

ref: The Lord will always guide you and provide good things to eat when you are in the desert. He will make you healthy. You will be like a garden that has plenty of water or like a stream that never runs dry.
text: Naawen ale kasim a gani fu. Wa ale te fu fi ale silim ŋan baai la kantueŋ bolim tɛŋka po, abe wa te fi kobaŋa pagrim. Fi ale nye ase ka kaduk kaai ale zaŋti nalimnyiini la, ale nye ase bulik kaai nyiam ale kaa a kpeeri la.

ref: You will rebuild those houses left in ruins for years; you will be known as a builder and repairer of city walls and streets.
text: Fi nuruma ale ŋman sɛ ŋiaka guuraŋa, abe ba zak nyubi kpagsaŋa a zaani. Ba ale wi fu ayen Waai ale a Tebi Parik Lueŋsa la, ale Waai ale Ŋman Yik Suik Tii Ate Nuruba A Bo Ti Po La a nye a magsi.

ref: Then you will truly enjoy knowing the Lord. He will let you rule from the highest mountains and bless you with the land of your ancestor Jacob. The Lord has spoken!
text: dila fi ale nya masim Naawen po, ate m le nye ate fi kali tɛŋka kab tii ale jueli la zuk, abe fi dɛ fi kowa Jekob nitalimu.>> Ka Naawen nɔi ale biisi.

ref: The Lord hasn't lost his powerful strength; he can still hear and answer prayers.
text: Chekki Naawen nisa an gela ayen si an baga vari a basi, yaase wa tueŋa a kpari ayen wa kan wom.

ref: Your sins are the roadblock between you and your God. That's why he doesn't answer your prayers or let you see his face.
text: Alege ka ni biemu ale gaari ni ale ni Wenni. Ni wabaataŋa a nye kama ate wa suk wa nimbidiaka a nyini ni jigi, ate wa kan wom ni.

ref: Your talk is filled with lies and plans for violence; every finger on your hands is covered with blood.
text: Dii nyiŋla ni nisaŋa a tiri ka ziim ate bu kan sugri a nyini, ate ni nandubsaŋa a nye kaasi. Ni nɔngbanvaataŋa a biisi ka venta, ate ni giŋgeluŋtaŋa a lerigi gaasa wie.

ref: You falsely accuse others and tell lies in court; sin and trouble are the names of your children.
text: Waai karo a biisi a wi nyemagsika wie. Waai a karo a yaali wensie. Ba pai ba sebchakka a basi ka nanpaga kɔta ale venta biisa po. Ba yik ka daanika puuk a yaa biak biem.

ref: You eat the deadly eggs of poisonous snakes, and more snakes crawl out from the eggs left to hatch. You weave spider webs,
text: Ba a wɔgri ka waapiisa jena ale a yɔk nari batta. Waai a dan ŋɔbi ŋa jenaŋa wa a kpi kama, ate jenni dinyi a dan mobi, di a wɔgri ka waapiik.

ref: You hurry off to do wrong or murder innocent victims. All you think about is sin; you leave ruin and destruction wherever you go.
text: Ba a cheŋ ka nna nwuli a ga a nye wabiok. Ba yeenti kama ale nuru baai ale kan nye wari a kaasi la kɔka. Ba popolaŋa ka popola baata. Juijui meena ate ba a cheŋ la kaasuŋ a sak ba suitaŋa.

ref: You don't know how to live in peace or to be fair with others. The roads you make are crooked; your followers cannot find peace. The People Confess Their Sins
text: Ba zɛ suiyɔgni suiku. Nyemagsika a ka ba suitaŋa po. Ba labri ti kama ate ti chim suik goliŋta. Waai karo a va ti po a seba suiyɔgni.

ref: No one has come to defend us or to bring about justice. We hoped for a day of sunshine, but all we found was a dark, gloomy night.
text: Dila nyiŋ nyemagsika wie a yalima ale ti kama, ate wayɔrisima a kan paari ti. Ti a gisi ka bolim, alege ka legi nyiini ale gilim ti. Ti a yaali kama ayen ku peela a te ti, alege ti a cheŋ ka yisuŋ kpienta po.

ref: We feel our way along, as if we were blind; we stumble at noon, as if it were night. We can see no better than someone dead.
text: Ase yioba la, ti a ta kama a gilim parika, a bo suiku po a nye ase nuru baai ale kan ta nina la. Kantueŋ ti a cheŋ a nak ka naŋsa ase tɛŋ sob paalik la. Baai ale pagra la suŋsuŋ ti a nye ase ka kpieba la.

ref: We growl like bears and mourn like doves. We hope for justice and victory, but they escape us.
text: Ti meena a ŋuuni ase ka piina la. Ti a kum kama se nangbaŋsa la. Ti a gisi ka nyemagsika, alege ti an nya ya. Ti a yaali ka varibasika alege ka a yalima ale ti.

ref: How often have we sinned and turned against you, the Lord God? Our sins condemn us! We have done wrong.
text: Dii nyiŋla ti kaasuŋku a piisi kama fi nina po, ate ti wabaataŋa a sum a sak ti le ka diila. Ti nye kaasuŋku a kasim bo ale ti kama, ate ti miŋ ti biemu.

ref: We have rebelled and refused to follow you. Our hearts were deceitful, and so we lied; we planned to abuse others and turn our backs on you.
text: Ti nye ka tukpari ale zɛri Naawen ale cheem ti ŋaaŋsa a te ti Wenni ale ta namsika ale wɔkwɔk ale a velim ti suiniimaŋa ale ta diila.

ref: Injustice is everywhere; justice seems far away. Truth is chased out of court; honesty is shoved aside.
text: Ate nyemagsika a forisi ga ŋaaŋ, ate wayɔrisima a za nna niŋniŋa, ate wensie a nak naŋ suitaŋa po, ate wensie nyeka an baga a jɔ.

ref: Everyone tells lies; those who turn from crime end up ruined. The Lord Will Rescue His People When the Lord noticed that justice had disappeared, he became very displeased.
text: Jigi a karo ate wensie a boro, ate waai ale a yeeri wa nina a nyini biem po la a chim ka waai ate ba a gisi ayen ba ko ŋɔbi. Naawen a nya kama ate ku daani wa nyemagsika ale kan boro la nyiŋ.

ref: It disgusted him even more to learn that no one would do a thing about it. So with his own powerful arm, he won victories for truth.
text: Wa nya kama ayen waai karo, ku jam a cha wa kama ayen waai karo a jo wanni po. Ate wadek nisaŋa a tom varibasika tuima a te wa, ate wadek wayɔrisimaŋa a maari wa.

ref: He will attack like a flood in a mighty windstorm. Nations in the west and the east will then honor and praise his wonderful name.
text: Nuruba ale chali Naawen yuenni a nyini yeniŋ, a nyini wenbinni pusika jigini ba le mariŋ wa zulaŋa. Diila wa ale jam ase ka nyiam ale mobi a jueli diila ate Naawen vuusumu a ta bu a cheŋ la.

ref: The Lord has promised to rescue the city of Zion and Jacob's descendants who turn from sin.
text: Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Da Tuesirɔwa ale jam Zayon, baai ale bo Jekob po a tagri a nyini ba wabaata po la.>>

ref: Jerusalem, stand up! Shine! Your new day is dawning. The glory of the Lord shines brightly on you.
text: <<Yiti, a nyaksi ale fi bolimu a jam kama ate Naawen zulaŋa a yiti bo fi zuk.

ref: The earth and its people are covered with darkness, but the glory of the Lord is shining upon you.
text: Nya, legi ale lik tɛŋzuk de, ate leg kpienni a bo nuruma zuk, alege Naawen a yiti bo fi zuk, ate wa zulaŋa a jam fi zuk.

ref: Nations and kings will come to the light of your dawning day. Crowds Are Coming to Jerusalem The Lord said:
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale jam fi bolimu jigi, ate nalima ale nya fi saluiku nyaksika a jam.

ref: Open your eyes! Look around! Crowds are coming. Your sons are on their way from distant lands; your daughters are being carried like little children.
text: <<Lak fi ninaŋa a nya gilim fidek. Ba meena a tigsi kama a jam fi jigi. Fi nidoabilisaŋa a nyini ka niŋniŋ, ate ba pai fi liema ale nisima.

ref: When you see this, your faces will glow; your hearts will pound and swell with pride. Treasures from across the sea and the wealth of nations will be brought to you.
text: Ate fi ale zak nya ate fi ale nyaksi, ate fi suinummu ale nya masim. Nyakpientaŋa jigsika ba ale ta jam a te fu. Tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa jigsika ale jam fi jigi.

ref: Your country will be covered with caravans of young camels from Midian and Ephah. The people of Sheba will bring gold and spices in praise of me, the Lord.
text: Laalaakomi boari ale taari lik fi tɛŋka, Midian ale Efa laalaakomi paalisa. Ate baai meena ale bo Siiba jam a ta ligmɔniŋ ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a jam a mooli Naawen pimpaukku.

ref: Every sheep of Kedar will come to you; rams from Nebaioth will be yours as well. I will accept them as offerings and bring honor to my temple.
text: Kedar piisaŋa meena ale tigsi a jam fi jigi, ate Nebaiot padaasaŋa ale tom a te fu. M le tuesi ŋa ase tiirita la m kuŋkuŋku zuk, abe m gomsi m zula yenni.

ref: What is that sailing by like clouds or like doves flying home?
text: <<Bade ka bana a yiri ase chiŋmaaŋa la ale a nye ase nangbaŋsa ale a cheŋ si tukta po la?

ref: On those distant islands your people are waiting for me, the Lord. Seagoing ships lead the way to bring them home with their silver and gold. I, the holy Lord God of Israel, do this to honor your people, so they will honor me. Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt The Lord said:
text: Chekki tɛŋ sii ate nyiam a gilim si la a nya ka mi. Tarsis ŋaaruŋtaŋa a de ka niŋ, a ta fi nidoabilisaŋa ale bo niŋ la a cheena ale ba kpana ale ba ligmɔniŋ ate ku a te Naawen fi Wenni zula, Waai Ale Welema A Bo Izirali la, diila wa pai ka nalim a basi fi nyiŋ.

ref: Jerusalem, your city walls will be rebuilt by foreigners; their rulers will become your slaves. I punished you in my anger; now I will be kind and treat you with mercy.
text: <<Nicham ale ŋman sɛ fi parisaŋa, ate ba nalimaŋa ale tom a te fu. Ku jam va ka suipuurum nyiŋ ate m nak fu, m ŋmanteka nyiŋ m le sak jiirim ale fu.

ref: Your gates will be open day and night to let the rulers of nations lead their people to you with all their treasures.
text: Fi nansuiŋtaŋa ale kasim a lak za, ba kan lik ti kantueŋ yaase yowa, ate nuru a baga a ta tɛŋsaŋa paaruŋku a jam te fu, ate ba nalimaŋa ale tom chaab ale nak dɛka.

ref: Any nation or kingdom that refuses to serve you will be wiped out.
text: Ate tɛŋ kpieŋ kaai yaase naam buui ale kan tom a te fu la ale kpi. Tɛŋka ale kaasi meena.

ref: Wood from Lebanon's best trees will be brought to you— the pines, the firs, and the cypress trees. It will be used in my temple to make beautiful the place where I rest my feet.
text: Lebanon zulaŋa ale jam fi jigi, dapeelita ale kinkaŋ peruk ale damɔnta ale gum chaab a gomsi juijui ate m boro la. Ate m le nye ate m naŋsaŋa jigini a nya zula.

ref: The descendants of enemies who hated and mistreated you will kneel at your feet. They will say, “You are Zion, the city of the Lord, the holy One of Israel.”
text: Fi namsidɔma nidoabilisaŋa ale jam kpi duna fi niŋ. Baai ale kan pai fu a chim nuru la meena ale kpi duna fi naŋtaata po, ate ba ale wi fu ayen Naawen Tɛŋ Nummu, Waai Ale Welema A Bo Izirali la Zionwa.

ref: You were hated and deserted, rejected by everyone. But I will make you beautiful, a city to be proud of for all time to come.
text: <<Ba zɛri fu kama ale ŋman kisi fu ate waai a kan va fi tɛŋka po a taamu. M le nye ate fi kanjantaŋa a boro taam wuu, abe masim a boro a te gaŋsa meena.

ref: You will drain the wealth of kings and foreign nations. You will know that I, the mighty Lord God of Israel, have saved and rescued you.
text: Fi le nyu tɛŋ kpieŋsa biisim, abe fi ŋoosi naab yeri po. Ate fi yaa le seba ayen mi Naawen m ka fi Varibasidɔ ale fi Da Tuesirɔ Waai Ale Ka Jekob Pagrim Nyɔnɔwa La.

ref: I will bring bronze and iron in place of wood and stone; in place of bronze and iron, I will bring gold and silver. I will appoint peace and justice as your rulers and leaders.
text: Ku le magsi ku chim kutuk mɔnuŋ la m le te fu ligmɔniŋ. Ku le magsi ku chim kutuk la m le te fu kpana. Ku le magsi ku chim diok la m le te fu kutuk mɔnuŋ, abe m pai kutuk a tagri tana. Ate m le nye ate suiyɔgni a chim fi kpagi ate wayɔrisima a chim fi niŋdeerɔ.

ref: Violence, destruction, and ruin will never again be heard of within your borders. “Victory” will be the name you give to your walls; “Praise” will be the name you give to your gates.
text: Ba kan ŋman wom wɔkwɔk ni tɛŋka po, yaase kaasuŋ mɛ la a bo ni banaŋa po, alege ni ale wi ni parisaŋa ayen Varibasika abe ni wi ni nansuiŋtaŋa ayen Pimpauk.

ref: You won't need the light of the sun or the moon. I, the Lord your God, will be your eternal light and bring you honor.
text: Wenbinni a kan ŋman chim ni bolim kantueŋ po, yaase chiika nyaksika a bo ni zuwa, diila Naawen ale chim ka ni taam wuu bolim, abe ni Wenni a chim ni zula.

ref: Your sun will never set or your moon go down. I, the Lord, will be your everlasting light, and your days of sorrow will come to an end.
text: Ni wenbinni a kan siŋ nya, ni chiika a kan ŋman bugi. Naawen ale chim ni taam wuu bolim, ate ni niniga daaŋa ale kpeglim.

ref: Your people will live right and always own the land; they are the trees I planted to bring praise to me.
text: Ate ni nuruma meena ale chim wayɔrisima nyam, ate ba ale jam soa tɛŋka taam wuu. Bala ale ŋanbulaŋa ate mi a vuk, ba ka mi nisima tuima, diila ba a sakka m nalimu.

ref: Even the smallest family will be a powerful nation. I am the Lord, and when the time comes, I will quickly do all this.
text: Baai ale fiisa ni po la ale chim tusidi, ate baai ale pɔsima la ale chim tɛŋ kpieŋ. Ka Mi ale Naawen. Ku danni po m le nye kude nwuli.

ref: The Spirit of the Lord God has taken control of me! The Lord has chosen and sent me to tell the oppressed the good news, to heal the brokenhearted, and to announce freedom for prisoners and captives.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen Chiika a bo ale mu kama, dii nyiŋla, wa lueri mu kama ayen m pai Naawen wapaalaŋa a sak baai ale ka ŋanjaksa la. Wa tom mu mɛ kama ayen m ga tebi baai suiniima ale kaasi la, abe m mooli fasiyaa wie a te baai ate ba yik la abe m yeeri ligrɔba legi po a basi.

ref: This is the year when the Lord God will show kindness to us and punish our enemies. The Lord has sent me to comfort those who mourn,
text: Abe m mooli Naawen benni ŋmanteka ale ti Wenni tutunaŋa danni, a yɔk baai ale a kum la sue,

ref: especially in Jerusalem. He sent me to give them flowers in place of their sorrow, olive oil in place of tears, and joyous praise in place of broken hearts. They will be called “Trees of Justice,” planted by the Lord to honor his name.
text: abe baai ale bo Zayon a kum la, wa le te ba ŋan baai ate ba a yaali la. Abe m pai nalim naam zutɔk a vuk ba alege daa buntuemmoa, suipeentik kpaam alege daa kumsa, ale pimpauk garuk alege daa sui kaasuŋ chiiga. Ba le wi ba ayen wayɔrisima dapagrisa tiisa, ate Naawen a vuk ayen wa sak wa nalimu.

ref: They will hire foreigners to take care of their sheep and their vineyards.
text: Nicham ale nya ni duŋ buulimu zuk. Ba ale tom ni laŋsaŋa ale ni kaduksaŋa po.

ref: But they themselves will be priests and servants of the Lord our God. The treasures of the nations will belong to them, and they will be famous.
text: Ate ba ale wi ni ayen Naawen kaabteerɔba, ba le wi ni ayen ti Wenni tuimtomdɔba. Ni ale dɛ tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa jigsika masim, ate ba jigsika po ate ni ale nak kuusidi.

ref: I, the Lord, love justice! But I hate robbery and injustice. My people, I solemnly promise to reward you with an eternal agreement.
text: <<Dila mi, Naawen, a yaali ka nyemagsika. Mi kisi varuk ale biem kama. M wensieŋa nyiŋ m le tuni ba, abe m nye taam wuu nɔiyeŋ ale ba.

ref: Your descendants will be known in every nation. All who see them will realize that they have been blessed, by me, the Lord. Celebrate and Shout
text: Ba le seba ba ŋaaŋbisaŋa tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po ale ba bisaŋa nuruba suŋsuŋ. Baai meena ale a nya ba la ale miŋ ayen ba ka nuru baai ate Naawen a niak la.>>

ref: I celebrate and shout because of my Lord God. His saving power and justice are the very clothes I wear. They are more beautiful than the jewelry worn by a bride or groom.
text: Mi sui a peenti ka nna yegayega ale Naawen. M chiika a dɛ ka masim ale m Wenni. Diila wa pai ka varibasika gatta a jɔ mu ale gomsi mu ale wayɔrisima garuk woŋ, ase duerɔ ale gomsi wa zuk ase kaabteerɔ la ale ŋman nye ase pok fiak ale gomsi wadek ale ŋiri chɔrima la.

ref: Jerusalem, I will speak up for your good. I will never be silent till you are safe and secure, sparkling like a flame.
text: Zayon ale Jerusalem nyiŋ, m kan sina ate ku paari diipo ate wa wayɔrisimaŋa a nyaksi ase varivientidi la, ate wa varibasika a nye ase bolim ŋiak la.

ref: Your great victory will be seen by every nation and king; the Lord will even give you a new name.
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale nya fi wayɔrisimaŋa, abe nalima meena a nya fi zulaŋa. Ba le wi fu yuei paali, dii ate Naawen ale wi fu la.

ref: You will be a glorious crown, a royal headband for the Lord your God.
text: Fi ale chim ka naam zutɔk naliŋ Naawen nisa po ale naam zutɔk a bo fi Wenni nisa po.

ref: Your name will no longer be “Deserted and Childless,” but “Happily Married.” You will please the Lord; your country will be his bride.
text: Ba a kan ŋman wi fu ayen Abazerimi yaase ba wi fi tɛŋka ayen Atɛŋkoruwa. Alege ba ale wi fu ayen Yefziba, abe ba wi fi tɛŋka ayen Beula. Diila Naawen sui ale peenti ale fu, ate fi tɛŋka ale yali.

ref: Your people will take the land, just as a young man takes a bride. The Lord will be pleased because of you, just as a husband is pleased with his bride.
text: Ase nidoabili ale a faari nipokbili diila dila ate fi nidoabilisaŋa ale faari fu. Ase duerɔ ale a dɛ masim wa nipok fiak zuk diila, dila ate Wen ale dɛ masim fi zuk.

ref: Jerusalem, on your walls I have stationed guards, whose duty it is to speak out day and night, without resting. They must remind the Lord
text: Jerusalem, m basi kama ate nuruba a nya fi parisaŋa zuk. Ku dan poom ka kantueŋ yaase yok ba kan sina. Nama baai ale a wi Naawen la ni kan te nidek vuusummoa

ref: and not let him rest till he makes Jerusalem strong and famous everywhere.
text: abe ni kan te wa vuusum ate wa ga yik Jerusalem a zaani, abe wa nye ate wa chim pimpauk tɛŋzuk de.

ref: The Lord has given his word and made this promise: “Never again will I give to your enemies the grain and grapes for which you struggled.
text: Naawen a pɛ kama ale wa juga nisaŋa ale wa ni pagrisaŋa ayen, <<M kan ŋman pai fi ŋan bieŋa ase ŋandiinta la a te fi dachaasaŋa, ate nicham a kan ŋman nyu da paalika ate fi nam bu nyiŋla,

ref: As surely as you harvest your grain and grapes, you will eat your bread with thankful hearts, and you will drink your wine in my temple.”
text: alege baai ale a che la ale dɛ abe ba pak Naawen, ate baai ale a tigsi yɔnaŋa la ale nyu bu m dɔkku dabaasaŋa po.>>

ref: People of Jerusalem, open your gates! Repair the road to the city and clear it of stones; raise a banner to help the nations find their way.
text: Ni va taam, ni va nansuiŋtaŋa a taam. Ni gomsi suiku a te nuruma. Ni gomsi, ni gomsi suik duoku. Ni pai tanaŋa a nyini suiku po. Ni zagri tikti a te tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa.

ref: Here is what the Lord has said for all the earth to hear: “Soon I will come to save the city of Zion and to reward you.
text: Naawen a mooli kama a te tɛŋzuk de kpeglimka ayen, <<Weeni sak Zayon Liewa ayen, Nya fi Varibasidɔwa a cheena. Nya wa tutunaŋa a bo ale wa, ate wa tutunaŋa a va wa.>>

ref: Then you will be called, ‘The Lord's Own People, The Ones He Rescued!’ Your city will be known as a good place to live and a city full of people.”
text: Ba le wi ba ayen, Tuilum Nuruba ale Naawen ale Da Tuesi Baai La. Ate ba ale wi fu ayen Agisi ale Tɛŋ Kaai Ate Ba Kan Ŋman Zɛri Ka.

ref: Who is this coming from Bozrah in Edom with clothes stained red? Who is this hero marching in his glorious uniform? “It's me, the Lord! I have won the battle, and I can save you!”
text: Ka wana ale nna a nyini Edom a cheena, a nyini Bozra ale wa garuk ate ŋan mɔnta a tiri ku? Ka wana ale nna a jɔ garuk woŋ naliŋ a nyini cheena ale zuaka ale pagrimoa? <<Ku ka mi ale a biisi wayɔrisima po, a zuak a vari a basi.>>

ref: What are those red spots? Your clothes look stained from trampling on grapes.
text: Ka boa ate fi gattaŋa a muni, ase daŋmiadɔ la?

ref: I did this because I wanted to take revenge— the time had come to rescue my people.
text: Tunika danni a jam bo ka m suinum po, m da tuesika benni a jam.

ref: No one was there to help me or to give support; my mighty arm won the battle, strengthened by my anger.
text: Mi nya kama, alege waai karo a maari mu. Ku cha mi kama ase nuru ale kan boro a te mu maarika la. Ate mi dek nisaŋa a tom varibasika a te mi, ate mi dek suipuurumu a maari mu.

ref: In my fury I trampled on nations and made them drunk; their blood poured out everywhere on earth.” The Lord's Goodness to His People
text: Mi tabi tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa kama ale m suipuurumu. M pai ka m suipuurumu a nye ate ba nyu dam a buk ale kpiiri ba ziimu a basi tɛŋka zuk.>>

ref: I will tell about the kind deeds the Lord has done. They deserve praise! The Lord has shown mercy to the people of Israel; he has been kind and good.
text: M le weeni Naawen ŋmanteka ate wa nye la ale tuim ŋaai ate wa nye a magsi ayen ti pak wa a magsi chaab ale wie ŋaai meena ate Naawen a nye te ti la. Wensie, wie maŋsa nna yegayega ate wa nye a te Izirali yenni, a magsi chaab ale wa jiirimu ale wa ŋmanteka.

ref: The Lord rescued his people, and said, “They are mine. They won't betray me.”
text: Wa jam weeni ayen, <<Ba sum ka mi nuruba, nidoabili sii ale za ba kan chim venta a te mi la.>> Ate m yaa chim ba Varibasidɔ.

ref: It troubled the Lord to see them in trouble, and his angel saved them. The Lord was truly merciful, so he rescued his people. He took them in his arms and carried them all those years.
text: Ba daanika meena po, ku jam maari a daani wa kama, ate maarɔwa ale jam boro la, a jam vari ba a basi. Wa va wa yaalika ale wa jiirimu nyiŋ a da ba tuesi. A nyini dila po, wa zak ba kama a zaani ale pai ba tara.

ref: Then the Lord's people turned against him and made his Holy Spirit sad. So he became their enemy and attacked them.
text: Alege ba jam zɛri wa kama ale nye ate Naawen Chiika sui a puuri. Ate wa yaa labri a chim ba dachiak, a nye kpaliŋ ale ba.

ref: But his people remembered what had happened during the time of Moses. Didn't the Lord bring them and their leaders safely through the sea? Didn't he give them his Holy Spirit?
text: Ate wa nuruma jam teeri dila po wa, Moosis ale wa nuruma daaŋa. Wa waai ale jam ta ba va nyakpiemu po a taam ase naapeerik ale wa piisa la a bo ka bɛ? Waai ale te ate Naawen Chiika a bo ale ba la a bo ka be,

ref: The glorious power of the Lord marched beside Moses. The Lord will be praised forever for dividing the sea.
text: Ka wana ale tom wa zula nisim pagrisaŋa ayen si bo ale Moosis juga nisaŋa, ka wana ale lab nyaataŋa ba niŋŋa ayen wa kasim chim wa tɔga taam wuu,

ref: His Spirit gave them rest, just as cattle find rest when led into a valley. The name of the Lord was praised for doing these things. A Prayer for Mercy and Help
text: Ase niiga ale siŋ bo viak po la. Naawen Chiika a te ba vuusum kama. Fi ale gani fi nuruma diila ale nna, ayen fi nye zula yuei a te fidek.

ref: Please, Lord, look down from your holy and glorious home in the heavens and see what's going on. Have you lost interest? Where is your power? Show that you care about us and have mercy!
text: Nyini wenŋmazuk a nya nyini fi weleŋsa ale fi zula naam zukpaglika zuk. Fi ninmunaŋa ale fi zuaka a bo ka bɛ? Fi yik fi yaalika ale fi jiirimu a nyini ti jigi kama.

ref: Our ancestors Abraham and Jacob have both rejected us. But you are still our Father; you have been our protector since ancient times.
text: Alege fi ka ti ko, Abrayam a zɛ ti yaase Izirali a miŋ ti. Naawen yaa, fi ale ti Ko ale ti Da Tuesirɔ a nyini dipo ale fi yuenni.

ref: Why did you make us turn away from you, our Lord? Why did you make us want to disobey you? Please change your mind! We are your servants, your very own people.
text: Ka boa, Naawen yaa, ate fi nye ate ti a tuinti a nyini fi suitaŋa ale nye ate ti suiniima a pagra ate ti kan zuli fu? Fi tomteerɔma ale fi dɔkdemma ate fi soa la nyiŋ ŋman pilim jam.

ref: For a little while, your temple belonged to us; and now our enemies have torn it down.
text: Ku an beni ya fi nuruma a tuesi fi jigi weleŋka, alege yɔgyɔgla de ti dachaasaŋa a jam tabi fi boka jigini kama a dueni tɛŋ.

ref: We act as though you had never ruled us or called us your people.
text: Fi ale soa ti a nyini dila po. Alege fi an nya ti zuwa, fi an pai fi yuenni a wi ti.

ref: Rip the heavens apart! Come down, Lord; make the mountains tremble.
text: Mi a yaali kama ayen fi lagri wenŋmazukku a siŋ jam tɛŋ ate guutaŋa ale choa fi niŋ!

ref: Be a spark that starts a fire causing water to boil. Then your enemies will know who you are; all nations will tremble because you are nearby.
text: Ase bolim ale toati daata tiye a nye ate nyiam a vaasi diila, be siŋ jam ate fi dachaasa a seba fi yuenni, abe fi nye ate tɛŋ kpieŋsa a choa fi niŋ!

ref: Your fearsome deeds have completely amazed us; even the mountains shake when you come down.
text: Ate fi jam nye wakperikaliisa ate tama a jam ka yiila ale ŋa. Fi siŋ jam kama ate guutaŋa a choa fi niŋ.

ref: You help all who gladly obey and do what you want, but sin makes you angry. Only by your help can we ever be saved.
text: Fi a maari baai ale nye a magsi ale popeentik la kama baai ale a teeri fi suitaŋa la. Alege tama ale jam nye a kaasi ba la, fi sui a jam puuri kama. Tama abe le nye ka sɛ a nya varibasika?

ref: We are unfit to worship you; each of our good deeds is merely a filthy rag. We dry up like leaves; our sins are storm winds sweeping us away.
text: Ti meena nye ase ka baai ale daŋ la, ate ti wayɔrisimaŋa a nye ase ka garuk cha daŋtisa la. Ti meena kɔ kama ase vaata la, ate ti wabaataŋa a nye ase viok la a ji ti a basi.

ref: No one worships in your name or remains faithful. You have turned your back on us and let our sins melt us away.
text: Nuru waai karo a wi fi yuenni, yaase waai a nye ayen wa paari a yik fu. Diila fi suk ka fidek a nyini ti jigi, ale nye ate tama a ka kiri ya ti wabaataŋa nyiŋ.

ref: You, Lord, are our Father. We are nothing but clay, but you are the potter who molded us.
text: Alege Naawen yaa, fi ale ti ko. Tama ale yakka, ate fi a chim mɛɛrɔwa. Ti meena ka fi nisa tuima.

ref: Don't be so furious or keep our sins in your thoughts forever! Remember that all of us are your people.
text: Naawen yaa, kan te fi sui a puuri ale ti a gaam taam. Kan teeri ti wabaataŋa taam wuu. Ti a puusi kama ayen fi zak a nya ti, dii nyiŋla ti meena ka fi nuruba.

ref: Every one of your towns has turned into a desert, especially Jerusalem.
text: Fi tuilum tɛŋsaŋa a jam chim ka gɔi. Zayon mɛ a jam chim gɔi. Jerusalem a jam ka tɛŋ koruk.

ref: Zion's glorious and holy temple where our ancestors praised you has been destroyed by fire. Our beautiful buildings are now a pile of ruins.
text: Ti tuilum ale zula Wen yenni juijui ate ti koma a jam a pak fu la, bolim ale jam dɛ di, ate nitalim buui meena ate ti pai basi du la a kaasi.

ref: When you see these things, how can you just sit there and make us suffer more?
text: Naawen yaa, kude meena ŋaaŋnyiŋ, fi diem za kama? Fi ale nye ka chim abe fi namsi ti a gaam taam mu?

ref: I, the Lord, was ready to answer even those who were not asking and to be found by those who were not searching. To a nation that refused to worship me, I said, “Here I am!”
text: <<Mi pai ka m dek a sak baai ale kan bek m wari la. Baai ale kaa gisi mi la a nya mi kama. Tɛŋ kpieŋ kaai ale kaa wi mi yuenni la, mi weeni kama ayen, <Mi ale nna, mi ale nna.>

ref: All day long I have reached out to stubborn and sinful people going their own way.
text: Danni po meena mi laari mi nisaŋa a tuesi tukpari nyam, baai ale kan va suik maŋsa po ale a nye badek ale a yaali diila,

ref: They keep making me angry by sneering at me, while offering sacrifices to idols in gardens and burning incense to them on bricks.
text: nuru baai ale kasim nye ate m sui a puuri m dek nina po la, a nye kaabsa tatta po ale a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la tanta peela kuŋkuŋta zuima.

ref: They spend their nights hiding in burial caves; they eat the meat of pigs, cooked in sauces made of stuff unfit to eat.
text: Ba ka baai ale a kali boosita po ale a zɔk wasusuga yokku po. Ba ka baai ale a ŋɔbi die lanta, ate ba binbili sii ate jenta ale lan tii ale kan nye cheri la a sueri la.

ref: And then they say to others, “Don't come near us! We're dedicated to God.” Such people are like smoke, irritating my nose all day.
text: Baai ale weeni ayen, <Zaani nakpiak, kan jam moata mi, diila mi ŋmasi ta tuilum kama a te fu. Nuru bala ka nyuisa m nyuevieŋa po ale bolim buui ale kasim a dɛ danni meena.

ref: I have written this down; I won't keep silent. I'll pay them back just as their sins deserve.
text: <<Nya, ku poom ŋmarisi doa ka m niŋ. M kan sina alege m le nye ba a tuni. M le tuni ku a basi ba naŋsa zuk,

ref: I, the Lord, will make them pay for their sins and for those of their ancestors— they have disgraced me by burning incense on mountains.
text: fi ale fi koma wabaataŋa.>> Naawen ale weeni ayen, <<Ba ju kaabka guutaŋa zuk ale nak nanpaga ale mi pinaŋa zuk, m le magsi ba kɔsutaŋa zuk a tuni meena a magsi chaab ale ba nyeela kpaksaŋa.>>

ref: Here is what the Lord says: A cluster of grapes that produces wine is worth keeping! So, because of my servants, I won't destroy everyone.
text: Nya kude ate Naawen a weeni, <<Ase nyiam nyiem ale diem bo yɔnsaga nyiŋ diila, ate nuruba a weeni ayen, <Kan yik kaasi, wamaŋ a diem bo ŋa po kama,> M za m nye ka dila m tomteerɔma nyiŋ. M kan kaasi ba meena.

ref: I have chosen the people of Israel and Judah, and I will bless them with many descendants. They will settle here in this land of mountains, and it will be theirs.
text: M le ta ŋaaŋsa a nyini Jekob ale Juda a jam, baai ale ba soa m guutaŋa la. M dek nuruma ate m lueri la ale tuesi dula, ate dula ate m tomteerɔma ale boro.

ref: My people will worship me. Then the coastlands of Sharon and the land as far as Achor Valley will turn into pastureland where cattle and sheep will feed and rest.
text: Saaron ale chim wuyɔgsuk jigi a te piisa, ate Achor Viaka ale chim vuusum jigi a te duŋsa, a te m nuru baai ale a gisi mu la.

ref: What will I, the Lord, do if any of you reject me and my holy mountain? What will happen to you for offering food and wine to the gods you call “Good Luck” and “Fate”?
text: <<Alege nama baai ale zɛri Naawen ale baŋ m tuilum guuku la, baai ale a gomsi jazaanim a magsi ba wena la ale dam daam a sueri taasa a magsi chum po la.

ref: Your luck will end! I will see to it that you are slaughtered with swords. You refused to answer when I called out; you paid no attention to my instructions. Instead, you did what I hated, knowing it was wrong.
text: M le gomsi ni a magsi gebika, ate ni meena ale koori a te togridɔwa. Diila mi wi kama alege ni an tulisi ya ale biisi alege ni an wom ya. Ni nye biem mi nina po ale lueri dii ale kan a peenti mi sui la.>>

ref: I, the Lord God, will give food and drink to my servants, and they will celebrate. But all of you sinners will go hungry and thirsty, overcome with disgrace.
text: Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, <<M tomteerɔma ale dɛ, alege kom ale yik ni. M tomteerɔma ale nyu, alege nyanyuila ale yik ni. M tomteerɔma ale dɛ masim, alege ni ale jo chivie po.

ref: My servants will laugh and sing, but you will be sad and cry out in pain.
text: M tomteerɔma ale yi yiila ale masim a nyini ba suiniima po, alege ku le daani ni suiniima po ate ni kaari abe ni a wooli ale sui kaasuŋ.

ref: I, the Lord God, promise to see that you are killed and that my chosen servants use your names as curse words. But I will give new names to my servants.
text: Fi ale basi fi yuenni a te m nuruma ate fi lueri la ase kikaasa la. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale ko fu. Alege wa ale te wa tomteerɔma yuei yoŋ.

ref: I am God! I can be trusted. Your past troubles are gone; I no longer think of them. When you pray for someone to receive a blessing, or when you make a promise, you must do it in my name. I alone am the God who can be trusted. The Lord's New Creation
text: Waai ale a bek niauŋ tɛŋka po la ale nye dila ka wensie Wenni nyiŋ. Waai ale a pɛ tɛŋka po la, a pɛ ka wensie Wenni nyiŋ. Diila m le baŋ daani kpagsaŋa wie abe ŋa suk ate mi a kan nya ŋa.

ref: I am creating new heavens and a new earth; everything of the past will be forgotten.
text: <<Nya, m le nye wenŋmazuk paalik ale tɛŋ paalik. M kan teeri wakpagsa yaase ŋa poom jam m popola po.

ref: I will celebrate with Jerusalem and all its people; there will be no more crying or sorrow in that city.
text: M le naŋ Jerusalem nyiŋ abe m ta suipeentik ale m nuruma. Ba kan ŋman wom kumsa ale kaarik ka po diipo diipo.

ref: No child will die in infancy; everyone will live a very long life. Anyone a hundred years old will be considered young, and to die younger than that will be considered a curse.
text: <<Biluak a kan bo ka po alege wa daa an soa dii ya yaase nisɔmma a boro alege an paari wa bena. Waai ale ta bena kook ale a kpi la ba le nya ase ka bi paalik ale kpi la. Waai ale kan paari bena kook la, ale nya ase ka kikaasa ale ko wa la.

ref: My people will live in the houses they build; they will enjoy grapes from their own vineyards.
text: Ba ale sɛ yie a bo ŋa po. Ba le vuk tiisa ba kaduksaŋa po a dɛ si yɔnaŋa

ref: No one will take away their homes or vineyards. My chosen people will live to be as old as trees, and they will enjoy what they have earned.
text: Ba kan ŋman sɛ yie ate nuru yoŋta a bo ŋa po, yaase ba vuk tiisa ate nuru yoŋta a dɛ. Ase tiib daa ale a soa diila, mi nuruma daaŋa ale soa ka dila. M nuru baai ate m lueri la ale dɛ masim ate ku beni a nyini ba nisa tuima po.

ref: Their work won't be wasted, and their children won't die of dreadful diseases. I will bless their children and their grandchildren.
text: Ba kan nam kinla, yaase ba biak bisa ate ba ta zu baata. Diila ba le chim ka nuru baai ate Naawen a niak ba ale ba ŋaaŋbisa.

ref: Wolves and lambs will graze together; lions and oxen will feed on straw. Snakes will eat only dirt! They won't bite or harm anyone on my holy mountain. I, the Lord, have spoken!
text: Piuk ale pabiik ale dɛ ale chaab, ate gbeŋli ale ŋɔbi kinkaa ase lalik la, alege tanta ale chim waamu ŋandiinta. Ba kan nye biemmoa yaase ba yik kaasi mi tuilum guuku meena zuwa.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The Lord said: Heaven is my throne; the earth is my footstool. What kind of house could you build for me? In what place will I rest?
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Wenŋmazuk ale mi naam zukpaglika, ate tɛŋzuk de a chim m naŋsa tabika jigi. Yenni ate fi ale sɛ a te mi la a bo ka bɛ? M vuusumu jigini a bo ka bɛ?

ref: I have made everything; that's how it all came to be. I, the Lord, have spoken. The people I treasure most are the humble— they depend only on me and tremble when I speak.
text: Daa mi nisa ale nye ŋantaŋa de meena ate ba boro?>> Naawen ale weeni. <<Waai ate mi a yaali la ale nna: waai ale a zaab wadek ale a siak wa kaasuŋ ate wa nyiŋ a gɔk ale m wanni la.

ref: You sacrifice oxen to me, and you commit murder; you sacrifice lambs to me and dogs to other gods; you offer grain to me and pigs' blood to idols; you burn incense to me and praise your idols. You have made your own choice to do these disgusting things that you enjoy so much.
text: Alege waai ale a nye lalik kaabka la a nye ase ka waai ale ko nuru la, waai mɛ ale a nye pabiik kaabka la, a nye ase ka waai ale wɛ biak ŋiri la. Waai ale a nye ŋandiinta tiirim la a nye ase ka waai ale pai deri ziim te la, waai ale a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa ase teerika la, a nye ase ka waai ale a kaabi bɔgluk la. Ba lueri ka badek suita, ate ba chiisaŋa a mariŋ ba kisita wie.

ref: You refused to answer when I called out; you paid no attention to my instructions. Instead, you did what I hated, knowing it was wrong. Now I will punish you in a way you dread the most. The Lord Will Help Jerusalem
text: Dila mi mɛ lueri nyeka tuem ayen m tebi ba, abe m ta dii ate ba a chali yɔgsum la a jam ba zuk. Mi ale jam wi la, waai an tulisi ya, mi ale biisi la, waai an wom ya. Ba nye ka biem mi nina po ale lueri dii ale kaa peenti mi sui la.>>

ref: If you tremble when the Lord speaks, listen to what he says: “Some of your own people hate and reject you because of me. They make fun and say, ‘Let the Lord show his power! Let us see him make you truly happy.’ But those who say these things will be terribly ashamed.”
text: Wom Naawen wanni, nama baai nyiŋsa ale a gɔk ale wa wanni la, <<Ni suataŋa baai ale kisi ni ale gaari ni mi yuenni nyiŋla, a weeni kama ayen, <Te Naawen a nya zula, ate tama nya ni masimu. Alege ba ale jo chivie po.

ref: Do you hear that noise in the city and those shouts coming from the temple? It is the Lord shouting as he punishes his enemies.
text: Wom kaarika tɛŋ nummu po, wom nuemka ale nyini Naawen yenni po la, Ku nyini ka Naawen jigi a tuni wa dachaasaŋa dii ale magsi ba la.

ref: Have you ever heard of a woman who gave birth to a child before having labor pains?
text: <<Ate wa piilim wa puuka domka la ale wa poom biak kama. Ate nyiŋdomma a jam wa nyiŋka po la ale wa poom biak ka nidoabili.

ref: Who ever heard of such a thing or imagined it could happen? Can a nation be born in a day or come to life in a second? Jerusalem is like a mother who gave birth to her children as soon as she was in labor.
text: Ka wana ale maa wom wieŋa de chaaba? Ka wana ale maa nya wieŋa de chaaba? Ba ale baga a biak tɛŋ kpieŋ dai yeŋ po yaase ba biak tɛŋ kpieŋ nna kadi? Alege Zayon ale biak wa bisaŋa kama ale an poom dom ya.

ref: The Lord is the one who makes birth possible. And he will see that Zion has many more children. The Lord has spoken.
text: Naawen ale weeni ayen, <<Mi ale ta biam jam ale kan basi ate ba a biagi?>> Fi Wenni a weeni kama ayen, <<Mi a dan ta biam jam, mi a lik biam luikku kama?>>

ref: If you love Jerusalem, celebrate and shout! If you were in sorrow because of the city, you can now be glad.
text: <<Dɛ masim ale Jerusalem abe fi sui a peenti wa nyiŋ, nama baai meena ale a yaali wa la. Dɛ masim yegayega ale wa, nama baai meena ale a kum wa nyiŋla.

ref: She will nurse and comfort you, just like your own mother, until you are satisfied. You will fully enjoy her wonderful glory.
text: Diila wa le nya ni zuk ate ni chak abe ni sue yɔk ale wa biisaŋa ŋoosika. Ni le nyu chak abe ni sue peenti ale wa ŋantaŋa.>>

ref: The Lord has promised: “I will flood Jerusalem with the wealth of nations and make the city prosper. Zion will nurse you at her breast, carry you in her arms, and hold you in her lap.
text: Dila nya kude ate Naawen a weeni ayen: <<M le te suiyɔgni a teeri paari wa ase benaŋ la ale tɛŋ kpieŋsa jigsika ase nyiam ale sueri benaŋ a waaŋ la. Wa le nya ni zuk abe wa pai ni ale wa nisa a yuk a kali wa naŋsaŋa zuk.

ref: I will comfort you there like a mother comforting her child.”
text: Ase ma ale a yɔk wa biik sui diila, mi mɛ ale yɔk ni sue. Ate ni sue ale yɔk Jerusalem nyiŋ.>>

ref: When you see this happen, you will celebrate; your strength will return faster than grass can sprout. Then everyone will know that the Lord provides help for his servants, but he is angry with his enemies.
text: Ni dan nya kude, ni sue ale peenti ate ni le busum ase wuuk la. Naawen tomteerɔma ale miŋ wa nisaŋa, alege wa ale sak wa suipuurumu ale wa dachaasaŋa.

ref: The Lord will come down like a whirlwind with his flaming chariots. He will be furiously angry and punish his enemies with fire.
text: Nya, Naawen a cheen kama ale bolim ate wa wusuma torokoma a nye ase va pagrik la. Wa siŋ cheen kama ale wa suipuurumu ale wa toariŋka ale bolim ŋaasa.

ref: The Lord's fiery sword will bring justice everywhere on this earth and execute many people. A Threat and a Promise
text: Naawen a ta ka bolim ale wa gebi woŋka ayen wa pai sak wa buusaŋa nuru meena zuk, nuruba yega ate Naawen a za wa ko.

ref: Some of you get yourselves ready and go to a garden to worship a foreign goddess. You eat the meat of pigs, lizards, and mice. But I, the Lord, will destroy you for this.
text: <<Baai ale gaari badek a te ale sugri badek ayen ba jo kaduksaŋa po la ale va waai ale bo ale baai ale a ŋɔbi die lanta ale dawuita ale kisita ŋanta la, ba ale tu ba kpeglimka.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: I know everything you do and think! The time has now come to bring together the people of every language and nation and to show them my glory
text: <<Ba nyeelaŋa ale ba popolaŋa nyiŋ, ate mi za m tigsi tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale buura meena ate ba jam nya mi zulaŋa.

ref: by proving what I can do. I will send the survivors to Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Meshech, Tubal, Javan, and to the distant islands. I will send them to announce my wonderful glory to nations that have never heard about me.
text: <M le nye wari ba po ate ba nya, ate m le tom baai ale vuuk la ate ba cheŋ tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa de, Tarsis ale Libia ale Liidiya, baai ale ta yuei ase tɔŋdɔba la ale Tubal ale Girik tɛŋka ale tɛŋ sii ate nyiam a gilim si ate si yalima la, sii ale kan wom mi yuei yaase si nya m zulaŋa la. Ba le mooli m zulaŋa wie tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po.

ref: They will bring your relatives from the nations as an offering to me, the Lord. They will come to Jerusalem, my holy mountain, on horses, chariots, wagons, mules, and camels. It will be like the people of Israel bringing the right offering to my temple.
text: Ate ba ale ta ni suataŋa meena a nyini tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa meena po a jam m tuilum guuku Jerusalem po ase tiirim la a te Naawen wusuma ale wusuma torokoba ale wusum bonsa ale laalaakomiba zuk: Naawen weeni kama ayen, <<Ba ale ta ba jam ase ka Izirali demma ale ta ba ŋanbie tiiritaŋa a jam Wen yenni po la ate ba pai nyo ŋan naliŋsaŋa ate ba ta tom tuima la po.

ref: I promise that some of them will be priests and others will be helpers in my temple. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Ate m le lueri ba gela ate ba chim kaabteerɔba ale Livaiba. >> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: I also promise that you will always have descendants and will never be forgotten, just as the new heavens and the new earth that I create will last forever.
text: <<Ase wenŋmazuk paalukku ale tɛŋ paalika ate m za m nye ate ka bo m niŋ la, fi yuenni ale fi ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale boro ka dila mɛ.

ref: On the first day of each month and on each Sabbath, everyone will worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: A nyini Chiik Paalik a ga paari ka choa ale Vuusum Dai ga paari di choa, saalɔ meena ale jam koori mi niŋ,>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: My people will go out and look at the dead bodies of those who turned against me. The worms there never die, the fire never stops burning, and the sight of those bodies will be disgusting to everyone.
text: <<Ate ba ale nyini peelim a nya baai ale nye tukpari ale mi a kpi la nyiŋsaŋa, ba nanzueŋa a kan kpi yaase ba bolimu a kpi, ate saalɔ a kan yaali ba.

ref: My name is Jeremiah. I am a priest, and my father Hilkiah and everyone else in my family are from Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. This book contains the things that the Lord told me to say.
text: Wieŋa de ka kaabteerɔma wanyi ate ba a wi ayen Yilkia ate wa nyini Anatot ate ka bo Benjamin po la nidoabinni Jeremaya ale weeni.

ref: The Lord first spoke to me in the thirteenth year that Josiah was king of Judah,
text: Naawen wanni yaa jam wa jigi bena pi ale ŋatawa po ate Amon nidoabinni Josia a dɛ naam Juda la,

ref: and he continued to speak to me during the rule of Josiah's son Jehoiakim. The last time the Lord spoke to me was in the fifth month of the eleventh year that Josiah's son Zedekiah was king. That was also when the people of Jerusalem were taken away as prisoners. The Lord Chooses Jeremiah
text: a ta ga paari Josia nidoabinni Jeyoiakim Juda naawa a ŋman ga paari bena pi ale dinyiwa chiisa sinuwa po ate Josia nidoabinni Zedekia a chim Juda naab la, ate ba yik Jerusalem nuruma ta cheŋ.

ref: “Jeremiah, I am your Creator, and before you were born, I chose you to speak for me to the nations.”
text: <<Alege ate m daani fu bisa luikku po la ale mi seba fu kama, alege ate ba biak fu ale mi poori fu kama fi tɔga. Mi lueri fu ase biisiteerɔ la a te tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa.>>

ref: I replied, “I'm not a good speaker, Lord, and I'm too young.”
text: Mi yaa weeni ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔwa Naawen mi zɛ biiga. Mi ka biik.>>

ref: “Don't say you're too young,” the Lord answered. “If I tell you to go and speak to someone, then go! And when I tell you what to say, don't leave out a word!
text: Alege Naawen a weeni mi ayen, <<Kan weeni ayen, <Mi ka biiga.> Ku a fɛ ate fi cheŋ waai meena jigi ate mi a tom fu la abe fi weeni dii meena ate mi a weeni fu la.

ref: I promise to be with you and keep you safe, so don't be afraid.”
text: Kan chali ba yɔgsummoa, diila mi a bo ale fu kama m be le vari fu a basi.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The Lord reached out his hand, then he touched my mouth and said, “I am giving you the words to say,
text: Ate Naawen yaa laari nisa a tiri mi nɔnni ale weeni mi ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de m pai m wieŋa a nyo fi nɔnni po.

ref: and I am sending you with authority to speak to the nations for me. You will tell them of doom and destruction, and of rising and rebuilding again.”
text: Nya, jinla m lueri fu kama ayen fi a nya tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale naata zuk fi dari voori abe fi cheeri lɔnsi, fi kaasi abe fi yuk basi, fi sɛ abe fi vuk.>>

ref: The Lord showed me something in a vision. Then he asked, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I answered, “A branch of almonds that ripen early.”
text: Naawen wanni a jam mi jigi ayen, <<Fi nya ka boa, Jeremaya?>> Mi yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi nya ka almond tiib naŋ.>>

ref: “That's right,” the Lord replied, “and I always rise early to keep a promise.”
text: Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Fi nya kama chekki, diila mi a kpesi kama ayen m nya m wanni nyeka.>>

ref: Then the Lord showed me something else and asked, “What do you see now?” I answered, “I see a pot of boiling water in the north, and it's about to spill out toward us.”
text: Naawen wanni a ŋman jam mi jigi ayen, <<Fi nya ka boa?>> Mi yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi nya ka samɔniŋ ale a vaasi, a gbeliŋ a nyini wiilukku.>>

ref: The Lord said: I will pour out destruction all over the land.
text: Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<A nyini wiilukku kaasuŋ ale jam waai meena ale bo tɛŋka zuk la zuk.

ref: Just watch while I send for the kings of the north. They will attack and capture Jerusalem and other towns, then set up their thrones at the gates of Jerusalem.
text: M boro a yaali ayen m wi ka na tii meena ale bo wiiluk geŋka la nuruma.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni. <<Ba nalimaŋa ale jam zaani ba naam zukpagliksaŋa Jerusalem nansuiŋtaŋa po, ba le jam ta chaab ale parik sii meena ale gilim la ale Juda tɛŋsaŋa meena.

ref: Jeremiah, get ready! Go and tell the people what I command you to say. Don't be frightened by them, or I will make you terrified while they watch.
text: <<Gomsi fidek a magsi. Yiti zaani ate fi weeni ba dii meena ate mi a weeni fu la. Kan chali yɔgsum ale ba, kan daa di mi ale basi ate yɔgsum a yik fu ba niŋ.

ref: My power will make you strong like a fortress or a column of iron or a wall of bronze. You will oppose all of Judah, including its kings and leaders, its priests and people.
text: Jinla mi a nye fu ka tɛŋ parik, kutuk zaŋi ale kutuk mɔnuŋ parik ayen fi zaani a ta chaab ale tɛŋka meena, a ta chaab ale Juda nalimaŋa, ka kpaŋŋa, ka kaabteerɔma ale tɛŋka nuruma.

ref: They will fight back, but they won't win. I, the Lord, give my word— I won't let them harm you.
text: Ba le nye kpaliŋ ale fu alege ba kan nya pagrim fi zuwa, diila mi a bo ale fu kama m be le vari fu a basi.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The Lord told me
text: Naawen wanni a jam mi jigi ayen,

ref: to go to Jerusalem and tell everyone that he had said: When you were my young bride, you loved me and followed me through the barren desert.
text: <<Cheŋ a ga mooli ate Jerusalem demma a wom. <Mi a teeri ni bi paalukku pa teka kama, nama le jam yaali mi dii ase nipok fiak la ale va mi vuri gɔnni po, a va tɛŋ kaai ale kan bori po.

ref: You belonged to me alone, like the first part of the harvest, and I severely punished those who mistreated you.
text: Izirali jam ta tuilum kama a te Naawen, baai ale chim wa cheka niŋ yɔna. Baai meena ale kaasi ba la a nye ka foola ate kaasuŋ a laari pai ba.> >> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: and I, the Lord, will speak. I was never unfair to your ancestors, but they left me and became worthless by following worthless idols.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Ka boan kaasuŋ ate ni koma a nya mi jigi ya, ate ba cheŋ bɛ a yalima ale mi? Ba va bɔgluk kayaata a yaa chim ŋan kayaata badek.

ref: Your ancestors refused to ask for my help, though I had rescued them from Egypt and led them through a treacherous, barren desert, where no one lives or dares to travel.
text: Ba an bek ayen, <Naawen a bo ka bɛ, waai ale ta tama a nyini Ejipiti a jam la ale ta tama a va gɔi koroku po la, a va tɛŋ kosik ale vaasa po, tɛŋ kaai ale koi ale nye legi, tɛŋ kaai ate nuru an nyiem ka po ate nuru an bo ka po?>

ref: I brought you here to my land, where food is abundant, but you made my land filthy with your sins.
text: Mi ta ni jam ka tɛŋ kaai ale poak la po ayen ni dɛ ka yɔnaŋa ale ka ŋandiin maŋsaŋa ate ka ta la. Alege ni jam taŋ mi tɛŋka ale nye ate mi nitalimu a chim kisuk ŋanta.

ref: The priests who teach my laws don't care to know me. Your leaders rebel against me; your prophets give messages from Baal and worship false gods. The Lord Accuses His People
text: Kaabteerɔma an begi ayen, <Naawen a bo ka bɛ?> Baai ale a nye ale wanni la a zɛ mi. Niŋdeerɔma a zɛri ka mi nɔi. Biisiteerɔma a va ka Baal a mooli, ba va ka bɔgluk kayaata.

ref: of a crime that no nation has ever committed before. Just ask anyone, anywhere, from the eastern deserts to the islands in the west.
text: Gaam taam Kittim nyiamu geŋsa a nya, te tomtomiŋ Kedar a kpesi nya paari. Nya ase wari a boro ase nnala la.

ref: You will find that no nation has ever abandoned its gods even though they were false. I am the true and glorious God, but you have rejected me to worship idols.
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋ a diem tagri ka wenaŋa? Alege ŋa daa wena bola. Alege mi nuruma a pai ba zulaŋa a tagri bɔgluk kayaata.

ref: You, my people, have sinned in two ways— you have rejected me, the source of life-giving water, and you've tried to collect water in cracked and leaking pits dug in the ground.
text: <<Mi nuruma a nye ka wabaata tiye: Ba zɛri mi, nyuvuri nyiam bulika, ale tu badek vila. Vili ŋaai ale wɛ a kan yik nyiam a tara.

ref: People of Israel, you weren't born slaves; you were captured in war.
text: Izirali ka tomteerɔ, ka yɔma ate ba biagi? Be ka boa ate wa chim jakoalimoa?

ref: Enemies roared like lions and destroyed your land; towns lie burned and empty.
text: Gbeŋma a ŋuuni a na, ŋa a ŋuuni wa. Ŋa basi ate wa tɛŋka a doa kinla, a ju wa tɛŋsaŋa ale zɛri si.

ref: Soldiers from the Egyptian towns of Memphis and Tahpanhes have cracked your skulls.
text: Memfis ale Tayapanes nidoama mɛ a chiiri fi zukku zuisaŋa.

ref: It's all your own fault! You stopped following me, the Lord your God,
text: Ni an ta kude a jam daa nidek zuwa ni ale zɛri Naawen ni Wenni wa le dɛ ni niŋ suiku po la?

ref: Your own sins will punish you, because it was a bitter mistake for you to reject me without fear of punishment. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
text: Ni gaasaŋa ale namsi ni, ni pilim ŋmanika ale toariŋ ni. Ni poli abe ni miŋ ku le bie ale tua dii a te ni ase ni a nin zɛri Naawen ni Wenni ale ka yɔgsum chalika ale mi.>> Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: Long ago you left me and broke all ties between us, refusing to be my servant. Now you worship other gods by having sex on hilltops or in the shade of large trees.
text: <<Dila powa ni wɛ niiga diokku kama ale gebi ni chɔrimaŋa. Ni weeni ayen, <Ti kan tom a te fu!> Chekki guuk meena zuk ale tiib buui meena ale teeri tɛŋ ni doa kama ase taabuksa la.

ref: You were a choice grapevine, but you have become a wild, useless vine. Israel Is Stained with Guilt
text: Mi jam vuk fu kama ase tiib maŋ la. Fi nye ka sɛ a tulim a ta chaab ale mi, a chim tiib poosukwa?

ref: The Lord said: People of Israel, you are stained with guilt, and no soap or bleach can wash it away.
text: Fi dan poom sugri fidek ale chiuk kuui ale ta nɔi la, m le diem nya fi foolaawa ale maŋ fu la.>> Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: You deny your sins and say, “We aren't unclean. We haven't worshiped Baal.” But think about what you do in Hinnom Valley. You run back and forth like young camels, as you rush to worship one idol after another.
text: <<Fi le nye ka sɛ weeni ayen, <Mi an taŋ ya. Mi an chali vi Baal bɔgtaŋa?> Nya fi ale nye dii viaka po la. Poli fi le nye diila. Fi a nye ase ka gɔi laalaakomi la a chali dɛ ale dɛ,

ref: Your shoes are worn out, and your throat is parched from running here and there to worship foreign gods. “Stop!” I shouted, but you replied, “No! I love those gods too much.”
text: Kan chali ate fi naŋtaata a ga toariŋi, yaase fi basi ate fi tutɔk a ga ko. Alege fi weeni ayen, <Ku ka kiri. Mi a yaali ka bɔgluk chaŋsa, ku be a fɛ ate m va ti.>

ref: You and your leaders are more disgraceful than thieves— you and your kings, your priests and prophets
text: <<Ase ba dan yik zue chivie ale a ta wa diila, dila dek ate chivie a ta Izirali. Badek ale ba nalimaŋa ale ba kpaŋŋa ale ba kaabteerɔma ale ba biisiteerɔma.

ref: worship stone idols and sacred poles as if they had created you and had given you life. You have rejected me, but when you're in trouble, you cry to me for help.
text: Ba a weeni diok ayen, <Fi ka m ko,> ale a weeni tintain ayen, <Fi ale biak mu.> Ba cheem ba ŋaaŋsa a te mi alege daa ba nina, alege ba daanika po, ba weeni ayen, <Jam a vari ti a basi.>>

ref: Go cry to the gods you made! There should be enough of them to save you, because Judah has as many gods as it has towns. Israel Rebels against the Lord
text: Bɔgluk tii ate ni nye a te nidek la abe bo ka bɛ? Ni basi ate ba jam ase ba nin baga a vari ni a basi ase ni a nin bo daanika po. Juda, ni ta bɔgta piisi ase ka ni ale ta tɛŋsa a piisi diila.

ref: The Lord said to Israel: You accuse me of not saving you, but I say you have rebelled.
text: <<Ka boa ate ni a ta ŋmiŋmaasa a jam ta chaab ale mi? Ni meena a zɛri mi nɔi kama,>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: I tried punishing you, but you refused to come back to me, and like fierce lions you killed my prophets.
text: <<Mi namsi ni nuruma ka kinla nyiŋ, ba an siak mi sinsaŋŋa. Ni gebika a ko mi biisiteerɔma kama ase kɔm gbeŋli la.

ref: Now listen to what I say! Did I abandon you in the desert or surround you with darkness? You are my people, yet you have told me, “We'll do what we want, and we refuse to worship you!”
text: <<Nama gaŋka de, ni poli Naawen wanni. Mi chim ka gɔi a te Izirali yaase tɛŋ kaai ale chim legi kpitɔ? Ka boa ate mi nuruma a weeni ayen, <Ti ta fasiyaa kama a nyiemu, ti kan ŋman jam fi jigi diipo diipo?>

ref: A bride could not forget to wear her jewelry to her wedding, but you have forgotten me day after day.
text: Nipok kaliak ale baŋ wa nifelima ale baŋsa yaase nipok fiak a baŋ wa gatta? Alege mi nuruma a baŋ mi wari da boari a ka chiina.

ref: You are so clever at finding lovers that you could give lessons to a prostitute.
text: Fi seba nɔŋta chali vi yaalika kama. Nipok baai ale ŋmasi bie a baga a zamsi fi suitaŋa kama.

ref: You killed innocent people for no reason at all. And even though their blood can be seen on your clothes,
text: Fi gattaŋa nyiŋ nidoaba a nya ŋanjak sii ale kan kaasi wari la ziim, alege fi an poom yik ba ale ba wɛ a jo. Alege kude meena

ref: you claim to be innocent, and you want me to stop being angry with you. So I'll take you to court, and we'll see who is right.
text: fi a weeni ayen, <Mi an kaasi wari ya, wa sui kan puuri ale mu.> Alege mi ale bo fi buusa dii nyiŋla fi a weeni ayen, <Mi an nye wabiowa.>

ref: When Assyria let you down, you quickly ran to Egypt, but you'll find no help there,
text: Ka boa ate fi a cheŋ nna yegayega a tagri fi suitaŋa? Ejipiti ale piinti fu ase Assiria ale jam piinti fu diila.

ref: and you will leave in great sadness. I won't let you find help from those you trust.
text: Fi mɛ ale basi dula a pai nisa a ji zuk, diila Naawen a zɛri baai ate fi mariŋ la kama, ba kan maari ba.

ref: The Lord said to the people of Israel: If a divorced woman marries, can her first husband ever marry her again? No, because this would pollute the land. But you have more gods than a prostitute has lovers. Why should I take you back?
text: <<Ase nuru a dan zɛri wa pok ate wa basi wa ale yali nidoa yoŋ, wa le ŋman tuesi nipowa? Dila a kan taŋ tɛŋka? Alege fi jam ta ka nɔŋta nna yegayega. Fi le ŋmani mi jigi ya?>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Just try to find one hilltop where you haven't gone to worship other gods by having sex. You sat beside the road like a robber in ambush, except you offered yourself to every passerby. Your sins of unfaithfulness have polluted the land.
text: <<Zak a nya guuta zuima. Jigi a boro ate fi an nye ase taabuk ale nye fu la? Fi jam kali suiku niŋ a limisi nɔŋta, ase Arab denɔ ale gu doa a limisi nuruba gɔnni po la. Fi taŋ tɛŋka kama ale fi taabugni ale fi gaasaŋa.

ref: So I, the Lord, refused to let the spring rains fall. But just like a prostitute, you still have no shame for what you have done.
text: Dila ale soa ate ŋmottaŋa a kan ni, ate tɛŋ sim ŋmorukku an jam ya. Fi a nye ase taabuk la, fi ka chivie.

ref: You call me your father or your long-lost friend;
text: Fi an wi mi ayen, <M Ko, m doa a nyini m bimbain po,

ref: you beg me to stop being angry, but you won't stop sinning. The Lord Asks Israel To Come Back to Him
text: fi sui ale kasim a puuri? Fi suipuurumu ale kasim boro dila taam wuu?> Fi ale a biisi diila ale nna, alege a nye biem buui meena ate fi baga la.>>

ref: When Josiah was king, the Lord said: Jeremiah, the kingdom of Israel was like an unfaithful wife who became a prostitute on the hilltops and in the shade of large trees.
text: Naab Josia naamu dɛka vaaŋa po, Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Fi nya Izirali ale kan ta siaka a nye diila? Wa jueli ka guuk meena zuk ale tiib buui meena ale teeri naŋsa la tɛŋ a nye kaboŋ dula jigini.

ref: I knew that the kingdom of Israel had been unfaithful and committed many sins, yet I still hoped she might come back to me. But she didn't, so I divorced her and sent her away. Her sister, the kingdom of Judah, saw what happened, but she wasn't worried in the least, and I watched her become unfaithful like her sister.
text: Mi jam te Izirali le kan siaka la wa basika gbaŋka a basi ate wa cheŋ wa kaboŋsaŋa meena nyiŋ. Alege mi nya wa suoku Juda ate wa ka wensie la a kan chali yɔgsum, wa mɛ nyini a ga nye kaboŋ.

ref: The kingdom of Judah wasn't sorry for being a prostitute, and she didn't care that she had made both herself and the land unclean by worshiping idols of stone and wood.
text: Dii nyiŋla Izirali daŋta wieŋa daa wari a te wa, wa yaa jam taŋ tɛŋka ale nye kaboŋ ale tintain ale diok.

ref: And worst of all, the people of Judah pretended to come back to me.
text: Ale dila meena wa suoku Juda ate wa ka wensie an ŋmani mi jigi ale wa suinum meena, alege ka pimpaasima nyiini.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Jeremiah, shout toward the north: Israel, I am your Lord— come back to me! You were unfaithful and made me furious, but I am merciful, and so I will forgive you.
text: Cheŋ ga mooli wanni de a te wiiluk geŋ demma ayen, <Ŋmani, Izirali waai ale kan ta siaka la.> Ka Naawen ale weeni. <M kan ŋman kaasi nina ale fu, diila mi ta ka jiirim,> Naawen ale weeni. <M sui kan ŋman puuri diipo diipo.

ref: You are unfaithful children, but you belong to me. Come home! I'll take one or two of you from each town and clan and bring you to Zion.
text: <<Ni ŋmani, nama nuru baai ale kan ta siaka la.>> Naawen ale weeni. <<Diila mi ka ni chorɔ. M le lueri ni, wanyi a nyini tɛŋ num wanyi mɛ a nyini yezuk a yaa ta ni jam Zayon.
