text: alege basi ate waai ale a kuulim la a kuulim nna: Ayen wa a miŋ ale seba mi, ayen Mi ale Naawen, waai ale a sak ŋmanteka ale nyemagsika ale wayɔrisima tɛŋzuk de, diila mi mariŋ ka ŋade.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Someday I will punish the nations of Egypt, Edom, Ammon, and Moab, and the tribes of the desert. The men of these nations are circumcised, but they don't worship me. And it's the same with you people of Judah. Your bodies are circumcised, but your hearts are unchanged.
text: Ejipiti ale Juda ale Edom ale Ammon ale Moab ale baai meena ale bo gɔnni po niŋniŋ jiga la. Diila tɛŋsaŋa de meena an sum gebi ya, ate Izirali yenni meena an poom gebi ba suiniima po.>>

ref: The Lord said: Listen to me, you people of Israel. Don't follow the customs of those nations who become frightened when they see something strange happen in the sky.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Ni kan zamsi tɛŋsaŋa wieŋa yaase ni kpaziim a nak ale daani ŋaai ale bo wenzukku la, tɛŋsaŋa kpaziim a poom a nak ale ba kama.

ref: Their religion is worthless! They chop down a tree, carve the wood into an idol,
text: Nuruma korom wieŋa a ka kiriya. Ba gebi ka tiib tiisaŋa po ate peesirɔ a peesi ale liak.

ref: cover it with silver and gold, and then nail it down so it won't fall over.
text: Ba gobi ku ale kpana ale ligmɔniŋ. Ba pai piema ale janakferim a nak yik chaab dila ate ku kan kpeeri.

ref: An idol is no better than a scarecrow. It can't speak, and it has to be carried, because it can't walk. Why worship an idol that can't help or harm you? Jeremiah Praises the Lord
text: Ase jaab ate ba ti zaani ŋan kpaanta po a yiak nuinsa, ba ka bɔgluk tii ale kaa biisi, ku a fɛ ayen ba ji a ta cheŋ dii nyiŋla ti an baga a cheŋ. Ni kan chali ti. Ti an baga a nye biem yaase ti nye wamaŋŋa.>>

ref: You are King of the nations. Everyone should worship you. No human anywhere on earth is wiser than you.
text: Ka wana ale kan wa chali fu, tɛŋsa Naaba? Ka fi ale magsi diila ale la. Yam nyama meena ale bo tɛŋsaŋa po la ale ba naataŋa meena po la, waai karo ase fi la.

ref: Idols are worthless, and anyone who worships them is a fool!
text: Ba meena a ka yammoa ale chim betta. Daata bɔgluk tii ale kan ta kiri la ale sak ba.

ref: Idols are made by humans. A carver shapes the wood. A metalworker hammers out a covering of gold from Uphaz or of silver from Tarshish. Then the idol is dressed in blue and purple clothes.
text: Kpana ŋaai ate ba kuri la a nyini ka Tarsis ate ligmɔniŋka a nyini Ufaz. Peesirɔwa ale choakudɔwa ale nye jabuui la ba jo wa ale ka garuk sobluk ale garuk mɔnuŋ. Ba meena ka baai ale seba ŋanta nyeka la ale nye.

ref: You, Lord, are the only true and living God. You will rule for all time. When you are angry the earth shakes, and nations are destroyed.
text: Alege Naawen ale wensie Wenni, wa ale Wen dii ale vua la, taam wuu Naawa. Wa sui a dan puuri, tɛŋka a kpiŋsi kama. Tɛŋsaŋa an baga a pik wa suipuurumu.

ref: You told me to say that idols did not create the heavens and the earth, and that you, the Lord, will destroy every idol.
text: <<Weeni ba nna: <Wenaŋa de, ŋaai ale kan nye wenzukku ale tɛŋka la ale bɛ tɛŋzuk ale tɛŋka meena.> >>

ref: With your wisdom and power you created the earth and spread out the heavens.
text: Alege Wen ale nye tɛŋka ale wa pagrim, wa dueni tɛŋka ale wa yam ale dari wenŋmazukku ale wa miŋka.

ref: The waters in the heavens roar at your command. You make clouds appear— you send the winds from your storehouse and make lightning flash in the rain.
text: Wa dan na nanpaniŋ, nyaataŋa ale bo wenŋmazukku la a wuuri kama, wa basi ate chiŋma a yiti tɛŋka kpeglimka jiga. Wa a tom nyaksika ale ŋmoruk ale ta viok a nyini wa kɔlima yeeŋa po a nyini.

ref: People who make idols are so stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods are not alive.
text: Waai meena a kan poli ale zɛ jaaboa, ligmɔniŋ kuridɔ meena chivie ale ta wa ale wa bɔgtaŋa. Wa ŋan mɛɛntaŋa ka varuk. Ba ka vuusum ba po.

ref: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
text: Ba ka kiri ya, ŋan baai ale ka ŋan laanta. Ba buusaŋa a dan jam, ba le kpi.

ref: But you, Israel's God, created all things, and you chose Israel to be your very own. Your name is the Lord All-Powerful. Judah Will Be Thrown from Its Land
text: Jekob Wenni daa nna, diila wa ale jaab meena Nyeerɔ, a maa gum Izirali du, wa nitalim buuni. Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale wa yuenni.

ref: I said to the people of Judah, “Gather your things; you are surrounded.
text: Ni tigsi ŋan baai ate ni soa la a basi tɛŋka, nama baai ate ba lik ni a ta la.

ref: The Lord said these troubles will lead to your capture, and he will throw you from this land like a rock from a sling.”
text: Diila Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Nnala nna Naawen ale yuk baai ale bo tɛŋka de po la a basi. M le ta daanika a jam ba jigi ate dila ba yik ba.>>

ref: The people answered, “We are wounded and doomed to die. Why did we say we could stand the pain?
text: Ku ale tua a te mu m kɔnika nyiŋ. M le kɔni diila a ka tebika. Alege mi weeni mi dek ayen, <<M nyiŋtuilaŋa ale nna, ate ku a fɛ ayen m pik.>>

ref: Our homes are destroyed; our children are dead. No one is left to help us find shelter.”
text: Mi viuku a kaasi kama. Ku miisaŋa meena ba chiak kama. M nidoabilisaŋa a cheŋ alege mu ba ŋman ka. Waai an ŋman tali ayen wa ti m viuku yaase wa ti m kusuŋku.

ref: But I told them, “Our leaders were stupid failures, because they refused to listen to the Lord. And so we've been scattered like sheep.
text: Naapeerisaŋa a kan poli, ba abe kan kpesi a nyini Naawen jigi ya, dila nyiŋ ba kan nya ba dega ate ba piisaŋa meena a waaŋ.

ref: “Sounds of destruction rumble from the north like distant thunder. Soon our towns will be ruins where only jackals live.” Jeremiah Prays
text: Ni wom, tontomiŋka cheena, butimka yega ale nyini wiiluk geŋka tɛŋka a cheena. Ku le nye ate Juda tɛŋ ninaŋa a doa koruta, suemkpatta boka jigi.

ref: I know, Lord, that we humans are not in control of our own lives.
text: Naawen yaa, mi seba ayen nurubiik nyuvuri daa wadek ale soa. Daa nurubiik dek ale a dak wa chelimu.

ref: Correct me, as I deserve, but not in your anger, or I will be dead.
text: Sak mu, Naawen yaa, alege nye ale nyemagsika daa suipuurummoa, kan daa di fi le nye ate m chim jaab kama.

ref: Our enemies refuse to admit that you are God or to worship you. They have wiped out our people and left our nation lying in ruins. So get angry and sweep them away!
text: Kpiiri fi suipuurumu a basi tɛŋsaŋa zuk sii ale kan siak a te fu la, baai ale kaa wi fi yuenni la. Diila ba ko Jekob kama. Ba ko wa ka chessi a kaasi wa tɛŋka meena.

ref: The Lord God told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord, am warning you that I will put a curse on anyone who doesn't keep the agreement I made with Israel. So pay attention to what it says.
text: Weeni ba ayen dii ate Naawen, Izirali Wenni a weeni la ale nna: <Kikaasa a bo nuru waai ale kaa va nɔiyeŋka nyemagsika de la,

ref: My commands haven't changed since I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, a nation that seemed like a blazing furnace where iron ore is melted. I told your ancestors that if they obeyed my commands, I would be their God, and they would be my people.
text: nye magsi kaai ate mi weeni ni kokpieŋsaŋa diipo ate mi ta ba nyini Ejipiti a nyini la, a nyini kuta nyaliŋka bolimu po a nyini la.> Mi jam weeni kama ayen, <Ni a zuli mu abe ni a nye dii meena ate m weeni la, ate ni chim m nuruba ate mi chim ni Wen.

ref: Then I did what I had promised and gave them this wonderful land, where you now live. “Yes, Lord,” I replied, “that's true.”
text: Ate mi yaa nye dii ate mi a pɛ ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa, ayen m le te ba tɛŋ ate biisim ale siita a chali ka po la,> tɛŋ kaai ate ni soa jinla la.>> Mi yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ku be nye dila, Naawen yaa.>>

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to everyone on the streets of Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah: Pay attention to the commands in my agreement with you.
text: Naawen a weeni mi ayen, <<Mooli wieŋa de Juda tɛŋsaŋa ale Jerusalem suitaŋa po. <Wom nɔiyeŋka nyemagsika de a va ŋa.

ref: Ever since I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I have been telling your people to obey me. But you and your ancestors
text: A nyini diipo ate mi ta ni kokpieŋsaŋa a nyini Ejipiti a jam paari jinla la, mi kaam ba kama a tulim ayen, <<Ni zuli mu.>>

ref: have always been stubborn. You have refused to listen, and instead you have done whatever your sinful hearts have desired. You have not kept the agreement we made, so I will make you suffer every curse that goes with it.
text: Alege ba an wom ya yaase ba popola a boro. Alege ba goanti va ka ba tuikpanni ale ba suiniim baataŋa ale a yaali diila. Dila mi yaa ta nɔiyeŋka kikaasaŋa meena a jam ba zuk mi ale weeni ba ayen ba va nɔiyeŋka alege ba an va la.> >>

ref: The Lord said to me: Jeremiah, the people of Judah and Jerusalem are plotting against me.
text: Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Biem zɔga ale bo Juda nuruma ale baai ale bo Jerusalem la suŋsuŋ.

ref: They have sinned in the same way their ancestors did, by turning from me and worshiping other gods. The northern kingdom of Israel broke the agreement I made with your ancestors, and now the southern kingdom of Judah has done the same.
text: Ba pilim ŋmani ka ba kokpieŋsaŋa wabaataŋa po, baai ale jam zɛri an wom mi wieŋa. Ba va ka wen yona a tom a te ŋa. Izirali yenni ale Juda yenni meena a kaasi nɔiyeŋka ate mi a nye ale ba kokpieŋsaŋa la kama.

ref: Here is what I've decided to do. I will bring suffering on the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and no one will escape. They will beg me to help, but I won't listen to their prayers.
text: Dila nyiŋ Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <M le ta kaasuŋ a jam ba zuk ate ba kan bɛ. Ba le kaari a wi mi m kan wom ba.

ref: Then they will offer sacrifices to their other gods and ask them for help. After all, the people of Judah have more gods than towns, and more shameful altars for Baal than there are streets in Jerusalem. But those gods won't be able to rescue the people of Judah from disaster.
text: Juda demma, ni ta wena ka nna yega ase ni ale ta tɛŋsaŋa diila ale ni kuŋkuŋtaŋa ate ni sɛ a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te chivie wenni Baal la a piisi ase ka Jerusalem suitaŋa la.>

ref: Jeremiah, don't pray for these people or beg me to rescue them. If you do, I won't listen, and I certainly won't listen if they pray!
text: <<Kan puusi a te nuruma de yaase fi saalimu yaase juisi te ba, dii nyiŋla ba dan wi mu a nyini ba ninammu po m kan wom ba.

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah: You are my chosen people, but you have no right to be here in my temple, doing such evil things. The sacrifices you offer me won't protect you from disaster, so stop celebrating.
text: <<Nuru baai ate mi a yaali la a nye ka biem wie. Ka boa ale soa ate ba a jo mi yenni po? Ba a poli kama ayen pumpuulima nyeka ale kaabka tiirita ale kasi ba kaasuŋ po. Ba kaa naŋi.>>

ref: Once you were like an olive tree covered with fruit. But soon I will send a noisy mob to break off your branches and set you on fire.
text: Naawen a jam a wi ni ayen ka kpaam tiib buui ale ta va yɔgsa a ta yɔn naliŋsa, alege yɔgyɔgla wuurika ase nanpansa la ale ju bu vaataŋa ale bolim abe bu naŋsaŋa a wɛ.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful. You people of Judah were like a tree that I had planted, but you have made me angry by offering sacrifices to Baal, just as the northern kingdom did. And now I'm going to pull you up by the roots. The Plot To Kill Jeremiah *
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale vuk ni la, ale dueni kaasuŋ a magsi ni dii nyiŋla Izirali yenni ale Juda yenni a nye ka biem ale nye ate mi sui a puuri ba le ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te Baal la.

ref: Some people plotted to kill me. And like a lamb being led to the butcher, I knew nothing about their plans.
text: Naawen ale pai ba biem zɔŋŋa a sak mi la nyiŋ, mi jam seba kama, diila dila po wa sak mi kama dii ate ba jam boro a nye la.

ref: I prayed, “Lord All-Powerful, you always do what is right, and you know every thought. So I trust you to help me and to take revenge.”
text: Alege Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, fi waai ale a bo buusa a yɔrisi la ale a chamsi suinum ale popola, basi ate mi a nya fi tutuna ba zuk, diila fi ate mi pai m wanni a te.

ref: Then the Lord said: Jeremiah, some men from Anathoth say they will kill you, if you keep on speaking for me.
text: <<Dila nyiŋ Naawen ale weeni dii a magsi chaab ale Anatot nuruma baai ale a gisi ba ko fu la ale a weeni ayen, <Kan mooli Naawen yuenni nyiŋŋa kan daa di ti le ko fu.>

ref: But I will punish them. Their young men will die in battle, and their children will starve to death.
text: Dila nyiŋ Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna: <M le namsi ba. Gebik ale ko ba nidoa paalukku, kom ale ko ba nidoabilisaŋa ale ba liema.

ref: And when I am finished, no one from their families will be left alive.
text: Nuruba magadek mɛ la a kan poom tali a te ba, dii nyiŋla m le ta kaasuŋ a jam Anatot nuruma zuk ba namsika benni.> >>

ref: Whenever I complain to you, Lord, you are always fair. But now I have questions about your justice. Why is life easy for sinners? Why are they successful?
text: Naawen yaa, fi kasim ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ, ase m nin ta biik a jam fi jigi. Alege m le biisi fi nyemagsika wari. Ka boa ale soa ate wabanyeerik wari a nye a niagi? Ka boa ale soa ate baai ale kan ta siaka la a boro ale suiyɔgni?

ref: You plant them like trees; you let them prosper and produce fruit. Yet even when they praise you, they don't mean it.
text: Fi ale vuk ba, ate ba feri naŋsa, ate ba chim a yɔni yɔna. Fi kasim bo ka ba nɔngbanvaataŋa alege yalima ale ba suiniimaŋa.

ref: But you know, Lord, how faithful I've always been, even in my thoughts. So drag my enemies away and butcher them like sheep!
text: Alege fi seba mi, Naawen yaa. Fi a nya mi kama a chamsi mi popolaŋa ale fu ale ka diila. Dari ba ta cheŋ ase piisa la ate ba che ba. Gaari ba a magsi da dii dai ate ba a tɔgri la.

ref: How long will the ground be dry and the pasturelands parched? The birds and animals are dead and gone. And all of this happened because the people are so sinful. They even brag, “God can't see the sins we commit.” The Lord Answers Jeremiah
text: Tɛŋka ale ko beni soa ka sɛ ate wuuku ale bo laŋ meena po la a kpi. Dila meena, nuruma a weeni kama ayen, <<Wa kan nya dii ale di nye ti la.>>

ref: Jeremiah, if you get tired in a race against people, how can you possibly run against horses? If you fall in open fields, what will happen in the forest along the Jordan River?
text: <<Fi daa chali chala ale nuruma naŋta ate ba nye ate fi jiak fi le nye ka sɛ a nak nanpaga ale wusuma? Fi dan nak naŋ a lo tɛŋ kaai ate wari a kan nye fu, fi le nye ka sɛ a maari fidek Jodan Benni tiisaŋa po?

ref: Even your own family has turned against you. They act friendly, but don't trust them. They're out to get you, and so is everyone else. The Lord Is Furious with His People
text: Fi suataŋa, fidek dɔkdemma a poom a pa fu a da kama, ba kaari kama ate ku jueli a ta chaab ale fu. Kan mariŋ ba, ba le poom a biisi fi wamaŋsa la mɛ.

ref: I loved my people and chose them as my very own. But now I will reject them and hand them over to their enemies.
text: <<M le zɛri m yenni, a banti m nitalimu. M le pai waai ate mi a yaali la a nyo wa dachaasaŋa nisima po.

ref: My people have turned against me and roar at me like lions. That's why I hate them.
text: Mi nitalimu a yaa nye mi nna ase ka gbeŋli ale bo tiisa po la. Wa a na mi, dila nyiŋ mi kisi wa kama.

ref: My people are like a hawk surrounded and attacked by other hawks. Tell the wild animals to come and eat their fill.
text: Mi nitalimu a nye mi jigi nna ase piina ale nuin sii ale a dɛ lanta la ale gilim a dɛ mi nuruma ate mi lueri a te m dek la. Ga tigsi gɔi duŋsaŋa meena, a ta si jam ate si dɛ.

ref: My beautiful land is ruined like a field or a vineyard trampled by shepherds and stripped bare by their flocks.
text: Naapeerisa yega ale kaasi m kadukka a tabi m laŋka. Ba le tulim m laŋka ate m sui peenti ale ka la ate ka chim laŋ koruk kinla.

ref: A destroying army marches along desert roads and attacks everywhere. They are my deadly sword; no one is safe from them.
text: Guutaŋa meena zuk gɔnni po kaasirɔba ale tigsi diila Naawen gebika ale ko a nyini tɛŋka kpeglim kinka a ga paari m kala, waai a kan vuugi.

ref: My people, you planted wheat, but because I was furious, I let only weeds grow. You wore yourselves out and gained only shame! The Lord Will Have Pity on Other Nations
text: Ba le bori ŋanbie alege ŋari munsa. Ba le jiak badek alege kan nya jaaboa. Dila ni ta ni cheka chivieŋa Naawen suipuurumu nyiŋ.>>

ref: The Lord said: I gave this land to my people Israel, but enemies around it have attacked and robbed it. So I will uproot them from their own countries just as I will uproot Judah from its land.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Mi gaasa gilagila nyama ale vari nitalimu ate mi te Izirali demma la, m le dari ba a voori ba tɛŋsaŋa po abe m voori Juda yenni ba suŋsuŋ.

ref: But later, I will have pity on these nations and bring them back to their own lands.
text: Alege m dan voori ba ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ, m le ta jiirim ale ba abe m ta waai meena a ŋman jam wadek nitalim jigi ale wadek tɛŋ po.

ref: They once taught my people to worship Baal. But if they admit I am the only true God, and if they let my people teach them how to worship me, these nations will also become my people.
text: Ate ba dan zamsi nalimnyiini mi nuruma suitaŋa ale pɛ mi yuenni nyiŋ ayen, <Chekki Naawen ale vua la nyiŋ,> alege ba poom jam sak mi nuruma ayen ba a pɛ Baal nyiŋla ba yaa le kali paari mi nuruma po.

ref: However, if they don't listen to me, I will uproot them from their lands and completely destroy them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Alege tɛŋ kaai a dan kan wom ya, m le dari ka a voori a kaasi ka chessi.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The Lord told me, “Go and buy a pair of linen shorts. Wear them for a while, but don't wash them.”
text: Naawen ale weeni mi diila ale nna: <<Cheŋ a ga da chiak gbain naliŋ a bobi fi chiaka, alege kan te di tiri nyiamoa.>>

ref: So I bought a pair of shorts and put them on.
text: Dila mi yaa jam da chiak gbain, ase Naawen ale dak diila, a pai bobi mi chiaka.

ref: “Take off the shorts. Go to Parah and hide the shorts in a crack between some large rocks.”
text: <<Pai chiak gbain dii ate fi da a bobi fi chiaka la a cheŋ Perat yɔgyɔgla a suk di dula pinaŋa vie po.>>

ref: Some time later the Lord said, “Go back and get the shorts.”
text: Daa yega ale taam la Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Cheŋ Perat yɔgyɔgla a ga pai gbanni ate mi weeni ate fi suk la.>>

ref: I went back and dug the shorts out of their hiding place, but the cloth had rotted, and the shorts were ruined.
text: Dila mi yaa cheŋ Perat a tu yeeri gbanni juijui ate mi a pai di a suk la, alege yɔgyɔgla de di kaasi a ŋman ka kiri ya.

ref: Then the Lord said:
text: Naawen wanni yaa jam mi jigi ayen,

text: <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <M le kaasi Juda kanjantaŋa ale Jerusalem kanjauŋ kpientaŋa ka dila dek.

text: Wabaata nyama de, ale zɛri an wom mi wieŋa, ale va ba tuikpanni yaalika a va wen yona a tom a te ŋa ale a puusi ŋa la ale nye ase ka chiak gbanni de la a ka kiri ya.

ref: These shorts were tight around your waist, and that's how tightly I held onto the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. I wanted them to be my people. I wanted to make them famous, so that other nations would praise and honor me, but they refused to obey me. Wine Jars The Lord said:

ref: Jeremiah, tell the people of Judah, “The Lord God of Israel orders you to fill your wine jars with wine.” They will answer, “Of course we fill our wine jars with wine! Why are you telling us something we already know?”
text: <<Weeni ba ayen, <Naawen, Izirali Wenni a weeni ayen, daam bunlɔk meena a sueri ale daam.> Ate ba dan weeni fu ayen, <Tama zɛ ayen daam bunlɔk meena a magsi ku sueri ale daamoa?>

ref: Then say to them: I am the Lord, and what I'm going to do will make everyone in Judah and Jerusalem appear to be full of wine. And the worst ones will be the kings of David's family and the priests and the prophets.
text: Yaa weeni ba ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Mi a yaali ayen m buk waai meena ale bo tɛŋka de po la a gum nalima ŋaai ale kali Deevid naam zukpaglika zuk la, ale kaabteerɔma ale biisiteerɔba ale baai meena ale bo Jerusalem la.

ref: Then I will smash them against each other like jars. I will have no pity on the young or the old, and they will all be destroyed. I, the Lord, have spoken. The People of Judah Will Be Taken Away
text: M le ŋɔriŋ ba a gum chaab, koba ale bisa wayeŋ. Naawen ale weeni. M kan te ate ŋmanteka yaase jiirimmoa yaase vɔŋteka a kasi mu ate m kan kaasi ba.> >>

ref: People of Judah, don't be too proud to listen to what the Lord has said.
text: Chiib kpesi abe ni wom ni kan ta kanjanta, diila Naawen a biisi kama.

ref: You hope for light, but God is sending darkness. Evening shadows already deepen in the hills. So return to God and confess your sins to him before you trip and fall.
text: Ni pai zula a te Naawen ni Wenni alege ate wa ta legi a jam, alege ate ni a nak naŋsa guutaŋa zuk legini po. Ni yiili a yaali ka bolim alege wa le tulim ate bu chim legi nna kpitɔ a tagri ate ku nye birim.

ref: If you are too proud to listen, I will weep alone. Tears will stream from my eyes when the Lord's people are taken away as prisoners.
text: Alege ni dan kan wom ya, m le kum digdig ni kanjantaŋa nyiŋ. Mi nina ale kum tuotuowa ate ninyaata a chali, dii nyiŋla Naawen piisaŋa ba le yik ŋa.

ref: The Lord told me to tell you that your king and his mother must surrender their thrones and remove their crowns.
text: Weeni naawa ale naab mawa ayen, <<Ni nyini ni naam zukpagliksaŋa zuk a siŋ diila ni zula naam zutɔksaŋa a lak ni zuimaŋa a lo kama.>>

ref: The cities in the Southern Desert are surrounded; no one can get in or out. Everyone in Judah will be taken away.
text: Tɛŋ nina ŋaai ale bo Negev la a lik kama, waai abe kan boro a lak si. Juda meena ba le ji ba a ta cheŋ tɛŋ yoŋ, ba ji a ta cheŋ ferr.

ref: Jerusalem, you were so proud of ruling the people of Judah. But where are they now? Look north, and you will see your enemies approaching.
text: Ni zak zuima a nya baai ale nyini wiilukku geŋ a cheena la. Pa ŋaai ate ba jam pai te fu la, a bo ka be, pa ŋaai ate fi kuulim ŋa wie la?

ref: You once trusted them to help, but now I'll let them rule you. What do you say about that? You will be in pain like a woman giving birth.
text: Ni le weeni ayen ka boa ase nuru baai ate nama poli ayen ba jam ka ni doaba la a nin nak de ni a nya ni zuwa? Ni nyiŋsa ale dom ase nipok puuk ale a dom ayen wa biak la.

ref: Do you know why your clothes were torn off and you were abused? It was because of your terrible sins.
text: Ate fi dan bek fidek ayen, <<Ka boa ate kude nye mi?>> Ka fi waba boanni nyiŋ ale soa ate fi mankutaŋa a cheeri ale fɛ a goa ale fu.

ref: Can you ever change and do what's right? Can people change the color of their skin, or can a leopard remove its spots? If so, then maybe you can change and learn to do right.
text: Kus denɔ a baga a tagri wa nyiŋ gbaŋka yaase yɔŋni di soblaŋa? Ni be an baga a nye wamaŋsa mɛ ni ale malim ale biem nyeka diila.

ref: I will scatter you, just as the desert wind blows husks from grain tossed in the air.
text: <<M le kati ni waaŋ ase vɔtta ate tɛŋ kosik viok a ji la.

ref: I won't change my mind. I, the Lord, have spoken. You rejected me and worshiped false gods. *
text: Ni charuku ale nna, charuk kuui ate mi gomsi dueni ni la, dii nyiŋla ni baŋ mi kama ale ta sebchakka ale venta wena. Naawen ale weeni.

ref: You were married to me, but you were unfaithful. You even became a prostitute by worshiping disgusting gods on hilltops and in fields.
text: <<M le dari ni mankutaŋa a ta jueli ni ninaŋa ate ba nya ni chivie

ref: So I'll rip off your clothes and leave you naked and ashamed for everyone to see. You are doomed! Will you ever be worthy to worship me again?
text: ale ni kaboŋsaŋa ale kɔrisaŋa ale a kan chali chivie taabugni. Mi nya ni nyeela ŋaai ate mi a kisa la kama guutaŋa zuk ale laŋsaŋa po. Kikaasa a bo ni zuk Jerusalem demma! Ni le daŋ a paari ka dimpo?>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: When there had been no rain for a long time, the Lord told me to say to the people:
text: Naawen wanni ale nna a jam Jeremaya jigi a magsi chaab ale tɛŋ kosikka:

ref: Rulers send their servants to the storage pits for water. But there's none to be found; they return in despair with their jars still empty.
text: Nuru kpientaŋa a tom ba tomteerɔma ayen ba ta nyiam jam te ba. Ba cheŋ viliŋa alege an nya nyiamoa. Ba ŋmani ale samɔn koruta, ba jɔk nyiŋbiiri ale tuim, a yaa lik ba nimbieŋa.

ref: There has been no rain, and farmers feel sick as they watch cracks appear in the dry ground.
text: Tɛŋka a na ka mulisa dii nyiŋla ŋmoruk an ni tɛŋka zuwa, kpaarɔma a jɔk nyiŋbiiri a lik ba nimbieŋa.

ref: A deer gives birth in a field, then abandons her newborn fawn and leaves in search of grass.
text: Laŋka po walik nubini a basi di biika dii nyiŋla wuuk a karo.

ref: Wild donkeys go blind from starvation. So they stand on barren hilltops and sniff the air, hoping to smell green grass. The Lord's People Pray
text: Bon waarisa a za guutaŋa zuima a vuusi a kpeeri ase suemkpatta la, si nina a kan ŋmaa nya wuuk ale kan boro la nyiŋ.>>

ref: We rejected you and did evil, so we deserve to be punished. But if you rescue us, Lord, everyone will see how great you are.
text: Ti wabaataŋa a poom a bo seerɔ a mini ti kama, Naawen yaa, nye wari fi yuenni nyiŋ. Diila ti pilim ŋmanika a zuak kama. Ti tom a kaasi fu kama.

ref: You're our only hope; you alone can save us now. You help us one day, but you're gone the next.
text: Fi nyiini ale Izirali Yiila, ka Varibasidɔ ninam po, ka boa ate fi a nye ase nichaanɔ la tɛŋka po, ase nyeendɔ ale a goa jigi yok yeŋ la?

ref: Did this disaster take you by surprise? Are you a warrior with your hands tied? You have chosen us, and your temple is here. Don't abandon us! The Lord's Answer
text: Ka boa ate fi a nye ase nuru ate ku diiri wa la, ase tugurik tɔŋdɔ wobsik ale kan baga a vari a basi la? Fi bo ka tama po, Naawen yaa, tama abe ta ka fi yuenni, kan zɛri ti.

ref: My people, you love to wander away; you don't even try to stay close to me. So now I will reject you and punish you for your sins. I, the Lord, have spoken. Lying Prophets
text: Naawen ale weeni nuruma de wie diila ale nna: <<Ba a yaali tuintika ka nna yegayega. Ba kan yik badek ale ba chelimu. Dila Naawen a kan siak ba. Yɔgyɔgla de wa le teeri ba gaasaŋa a namsi ba ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ.>>

ref: The Lord said, “Jeremiah, don't ask me to help these people.
text: Ate Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Kan puusi a yaali nuruma de nye niaka.

ref: They may even go without eating and offer sacrifices to please me and to give thanks. But when they cry out for my help, I won't listen, and I won't accept their sacrifices. Instead, I'll send war, starvation, and disease to wipe them out.”
text: Ba a bobi ka nɔi, m kan wom ba kumsa, ba a te juka tiirita ale ŋanbie tiirita, m kan siak ba. M le goanti a ko ba ale gebika ale kɔm ale nyiŋtuila.>>

ref: I replied, “The other prophets keep telling everyone that you won't send starvation or war, and that you're going to give us peace.”
text: Alege mi weeni ayen, <<Nyɔnɔ Naawen yaa, biisiteerɔma kasim a weeni ba kama ayen, ba kan nya gebika yaase ba nam ale kɔmmoa. <Chekki, m le te fu suiyɔgni dii ale di beni dela jigini.> >>

ref: The Lord answered: They claim to speak for me, but they're lying! I didn't even speak to them, much less choose them to be my prophets. Their messages come from worthless dreams, useless fortunetelling, and their own imaginations.
text: Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Biisiteerɔma a mooli ka venta ale mi yuenni. Mi an tom ba yaase m lueri ba yaase m biisi ale ba. Ba a mooli ka venta gɔdaasima wie ale venta sampoporinni ale venta bɔgta wie ale badek popola wie.

ref: Those lying prophets say there will be peace and plenty of food. But I say that those same prophets will die from war and hunger.
text: Dila la, Naawen ale weeni dii a magsi chaab ale biisiteerɔ baai ale a mooli mi yuenni nyiŋla ale nna: Mi an tom ba, alege ba a weeni ayen, <Gebik yaase kɔm a kan tiri tɛŋka de.> Biisiteerɔ bala dek ale kpi ale gebika ale kɔm.

ref: And everyone who listens to them will be killed, just as they deserve. Their dead bodies will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem, because their families will also be dead, and no one will be left to bury them.
text: Ate nuru baai ate ba mooli a te la ba le yuk ba a basi Jerusalem suitaŋa po kɔmmu ale gebika nyiŋ. Waai a kan boro a gu ba yaase ba pooma ale ba nidoabilisaŋa ale ba liema. M pai kaasuŋ kuui ale magsi ba la a basi ba zuk.

ref: Jeremiah, go and tell the people how you feel about all this. So I told them: “Tears will flood my eyes both day and night, because my nation suffers from a deadly wound.
text: <<Biisi wanni de a te ba ayen, <Basi ate m ninaŋa ninyaata sueri a chali yok ale kantueŋ a kan gebiri a te m liewa kaliaka. M nuruma a nam kama ale kɔni biok, niguri dii ale a ŋɔriŋ.

ref: In the fields I see the bodies of those killed in battle. And in the towns I see crowds dying of hunger. But the prophets and priests go about their business, without understanding what has happened.” Jeremiah Prays to the Lord
text: M dan jo tɛŋ kpieŋka po, mi a nya baai ate gebika a ko ba la, m dan jo tɛŋ nummu po, mi a nya kɔmmu ale a viiri nuruba diila. Biisiteerɔ ale kaabteerɔ meena a cheŋ ka tɛŋ kaai ate ba zɛ la.> >>

ref: Have you rejected Judah, Lord? Do you hate Jerusalem? Why did you strike down Judah with a fatal wound? We had hoped for peace and a time of healing, but all we got was terror.
text: Fi zɛri Juda ka chessi? Fi banti Zayon kama? Ka boa ate fi kɔni ti ate ti kan baga a nya tebika. Ti yiili kama a yaali suiyɔgni alege wamaŋ an jam ya, diipo ale magsi tebika alege ka nyinyigsa nyiini.

ref: We and our ancestors are guilty of rebelling against you.
text: Naawen yaa, ti siak ti wabaataŋa ale ti koma foolaawa kama, ti sum a tom kaasi fu kama.

ref: If you save us, it will show how great you are. Don't let our enemies disgrace your temple, your beautiful throne. Don't forget that you promised to rescue us.
text: Fi yuenni nyiŋ kan zɛri ti a basi, kan te fi zula yuenni chivie. Teeri fi nɔiyeŋka ale ti abe fi kan yik a kaasi.

ref: Idols can't send rain, and showers don't fall by themselves. Only you control the rain, so we put our trust in you, the Lord our God.
text: Tɛŋsaŋa bɔgluk tii ale kan ta kiri la a ta ŋmoruk a jam? Wenŋmazuimaŋa dek a te ŋmoruk bie a jam? Aaya, ka fi Naawen ti Wen yaa. Dila nyiŋ ti yiilaŋa a bo ka fi jigi, diila ka fi ale a nye kude meena.

ref: The Lord said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel were here, praying with you, I wouldn't change my mind. So send the people of Judah away.
text: Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Moosis ale Samuel a dan poom za mi niŋ, m suinum a kan bo nuruma de jigi ya. Te ti ba cheŋ mi niŋ. Basi ate ba cheŋ.

ref: And when they ask where they are going, tell them that I, the Lord, have said: Some of you are going to die of horrible diseases. Others are going to die in war or from starvation. The rest will be led away to a foreign country.
text: Ate ba dan bek fu ayen, <Ti cheŋ bɛ?> Weeni ba ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Baai ale magsi kum la ba kpi, baai ale magsi gebika la gebika a ko ba, baai ale magsi viirika a viiri, baai ale magsi yik ta cheŋka la, ba yik ta cheŋ.>

ref: I will punish you in four different ways: You will be killed in war and your bodies dragged off by dogs, your flesh will be eaten by birds, and your bones will be chewed on by wild animals.
text: Naawen ale weeni ayen, <<M le tom kaasirɔba tɔgatɔga banaansi ate ba ta chaab ale ba, gebika a ko ba ate baasaŋa a dari ta cheŋ, ate wenzuk nuinsaŋa ale tɛŋzuk duŋsaŋa a kaasi abe si ŋɔbi.

ref: This punishment will happen because of the horrible things your King Manasseh did. And you will be disgusting to all nations on earth.
text: M le nye ate tɛŋzuk naataŋa a kisi ba Azekaya nidoabinni Manasa waai ale ka Juda naab la ale nye dii Jerusalem po la nyiŋ.>>

ref: People of Jerusalem, who will feel sorry for you? Will anyone bother to ask if you are well?
text: <<Ka wana ale wa ŋmani te ni, Jerusalem demma? Ka wana ale wa kum ni nyiŋŋa? Ka wana ale wa baga a puusi ni?

ref: My people, you abandoned me and walked away. I am tired of showing mercy; that's why I'll destroy you
text: Ni zɛri mi kama,>> Naawen ale weeni. <<Ni kasim pai mi vaka a basi. Dila m le pai nisa a yik ni a kaasi ni. M kan ŋman baga a sak jiirimmoa.

ref: by scattering you like straw blown by the wind. I will punish you with sorrow and death, because you refuse to change your ways.
text: M le yali ni ale jayalim buui ale ta nyina la tɛŋka nansuiŋtaŋa nɔi. M le basi ate ku ko ba abe m kaasi m nuruma diila ba an tagri ba suitaŋa.

ref: There will be more widows in Judah than grains of sand on a beach. A surprise attack at noon! And the mothers in Jerusalem mourn for their children.
text: M le basi ate ba pukɔŋŋa a piisi ase nyakpiemu tintain busuŋku la. Kantueŋ suŋsuŋ m le ta kaasirɔ a jam ate wa ta chaab ale ba bi paalukku mama. M le ta sui kaasuŋ ale kpazinagsuk a jam ba zuk nna mwuli.

ref: A mother is in deep despair and struggles for breath. Her daylight has turned to darkness— she has suffered the loss of her seven sons. I will kill anyone who survives. I, the Lord, have spoken. Jeremiah Complains
text: Bisa bayopɔi ma ale cha abe wa vuusi wa vuusum buui ale a kpegli. Wa wenbinni ale siŋ ale ku diem ka kantueŋ. Wa le nya chivie ale valiŋsa. Baai ale vuugi la m le ko ba ale gebik ba dachaasaŋa niŋ.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: I wish I had never been born! I'm always in trouble with everyone in Judah. I never lend or borrow money, but everyone curses me just the same.
text: Mi daa suipeentik nuru. Mi zɛ dii ate mi mawa a biak mi a basi tɛŋka po la. Mi nye ka kpaliŋsa ale nak nanpaga ale waai meena tɛŋka po. Mi an piem waai ligra yaase m piem ligra a te waai ya, alege waai meena a ka a te mi.

ref: Then the Lord replied, “I promise to protect you, and when disaster comes, even your enemies will beg you for help.” The Enemy Cannot Be Defeated The Lord told me to say:
text: Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Chekki m le vari fu a basi wamaŋ nyiŋ. Wensie m le basi ate fi dachaasaŋa a saalim fu kaasuŋ ale ninam daaŋa po.

ref: People of Judah, just as you can't break iron mixed with bronze, you can't defeat the enemies that will attack from the north.
text: <<Nuru a baga a wɛ kutuwa. Kutuk kuui ale nyini wiiluk geŋ ŋa yaase kutuk mɔnuŋŋoa?

ref: I will give them everything you own, because you have sinned everywhere in your country.
text: Ni jigsika ale ni tuilum ŋantaŋa m le basi ate ba koalim a ta cheŋ ni wabaataŋa tɛŋka po meena nyiŋ.

ref: My anger is a fire that cannot be put out, so I will make you slaves of your enemies in a foreign land. Jeremiah Complains Again
text: M le basi ate ni chim ni dachaasaŋa yɔm tɛŋ kaai po ate ni zɛ, diila mi suipuurumu ale fuk bolim toati buui ale bu de ni.>>

ref: You can see how I suffer insult after insult, all because of you, Lord. Don't be so patient with my enemies; take revenge on them before they kill me.
text: Naawen yaa, fi a miŋ wie kama, teeri m wie abe fi nya m zuk. Tuni m dachaasaŋa a te mu. Fi ka waai ale a duŋ sui, kan ta mu a cheŋŋi. Poli m le nam ale lieta fi nyiŋ diila.

ref: When you spoke to me, I was glad to obey, because I belong to you, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Fi wieŋa ale jam la, mi dɛ ŋa kama. Ŋa jam ka mi masim ale suinum mariŋka, diila mi ta ka fi yuenni, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Wen yaa.

ref: I don't go to parties and have a good time. Instead, I keep to myself, because you have filled me with your anger.
text: Mi an maa kali nuruba suŋsuŋ a la ale a dɛ masim ale ba, mi kali ka m dek m nyiini dii nyiŋla fi nisa ale jam bo mi zuk ate fi sueri mi ale suipuurum.

ref: I am badly injured and in constant pain. Are you going to disappoint me, like a stream that goes dry in the heat of summer? The Lord Replies
text: Ka boa ate mi domka a kan kpeglim ate mi kɔnika a bie a ka tebika? Fi le chim ka pimpaasima beli a te mi, ase bulik kaai ale kpeeri ya?

ref: Then the Lord told me: Stop talking like a fool! If you turn back to me and speak my message, I will let you be my prophet once again. I hope the people of Judah will accept what you say. But you can ignore their threats, *
text: Dila nyiŋ Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Fi dan laŋ nyeka, m le ta fu ŋmani ate fi tom a te mu. Ase fi a nin biisi wamaŋsa alege daa wakayaata, fi le chim m biisiteerɔ. Basi ate nuruma de a tulim jam fi jigi, alege ku a fɛ ate fi a kan tulim cheŋ ba jigi ya.

ref: I will be there to rescue you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: <<M le vari fu gaasa nyama nisa po a basi abe m yeeri fu gaasa nyama bobika po a ta nyini.>>

ref: The Lord said to me:
text: Ate Naawen wanni a jam mi jigi ayen,

ref: Jeremiah, don't get married and have children—Judah is no place to raise a family.
text: <<Ku a fɛ ate fi kan faari nipok a biak nidoabilisa ale lieba dela jigini.>>

ref: They will die of horrible diseases and of war and starvation. No one will give them a funeral or bury them, and their bodies will be food for the birds and wild animals. And what's left will lie on the ground like manure.
text: <<Ba le kpi ale nyiŋtui baata. Ba kan kum ba yaase ba gu ba alege ba le chim ka yaata a doa tɛŋka. Ba le kpi ale gebik ale kɔm, ate ba nyiŋsaŋa a chim ŋandiinta a te wenzuk nuinsaŋa ale tɛŋzuk duŋsaŋa.>>

ref: When someone dies, don't visit the family or show any sorrow. I will no longer love or bless or have any pity on the people of Judah.
text: Dila Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Kan jo yeri diipo ate kuub ŋandiinta a boro la, kan cheŋ ga kum yaase fi sak jiirim ale ba, dii nyiŋla mi yeeri m niauŋku ale m ŋmanteka ale m yaalika m nuruma jigi kama.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Rich and poor alike will die and be left unburied. No one will mourn and show their sorrow by cutting themselves or shaving their heads.
text: <<Baai ale fiisa ale baai ale zuak ale kpi tɛŋka po. Ba kan gu ba yaase ba kum ba, ate waai a kan gebi wadek yaase wa chiiri wa zuk a te ba.

ref: No one will bring food and wine to help comfort those who are mourning the death of their father or mother.
text: Waai a kan te baai ale a kum kpiewa la ŋandiinta ayen wa yɔk ba sue, dan poom ka wa ma yaase wa ko ale kpi wa kan te daam ayen wa yɔk ba sue.

ref: Don't even set foot in a house where there is eating and drinking and celebrating.
text: <<Kan jo yeri po ate ŋandiinta tigi a boro yaase fi kali a de ale nyu.

ref: They will ask, “Why has the Lord our God threatened us with so many disasters? Have we done something wrong or sinned against him?”
text: <<Fi dan weeni nuruma de kude meena ate ba bek fu ayen, <Ka boa ate Naawen a te ti kaasuŋ kpioŋku de choa? Ti nye ka boan kaasi? Ka boan wabiok ate tama nye kaasi Naawen ti Wenni?>

ref: Then tell them I have said: People of Judah, your ancestors turned away from me; they rejected my laws and teachings and started worshiping other gods.
text: Yaa weeni ba ayen, <Ka ni koma ale zɛri mu la nyiŋ ale va wen yona la ale tom te ŋa ale puusi ŋa. Ba zɛri mi kama ale an ta mi sinsaŋŋa. Naawen ale weeni.

ref: And you have done even worse! You are stubborn, and instead of obeying me, you do whatever evil comes to your mind.
text: Alege ni nye gaasa nyeka kama a gaam ni koma. Nya ni waai meena ale va wadek tuikpari suinum yaalika ale goanti an va mi.

ref: So I will throw you into a land that you and your ancestors know nothing about, a place where you will have to worship other gods both day and night. And I won't feel the least bit sorry for you.
text: M le ta ni nyini tɛŋka de po a cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ate nama yaase ni koma a zɛ, ate dula ni tom a te wen yona yok ale kantueŋ, diila m kan sak ni ŋmanteka.> >>

ref: A time will come when you will again worship me. But you will no longer call me the Living Lord who rescued Israel from Egypt.
text: Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Alege daaŋa a cheena ate nuruba a kan ŋman weeni ayen, <Ase Naawen ale sum vua la, waai ale ta Izirali demma a nyini Ejipiti a nyini la,>

ref: Instead, you will call me the Living Lord who rescued you from that country in the north and from the other countries where I had forced you to go. Someday I will bring you back to this land that I gave your ancestors.
text: alege ba le weeni ayen, <Ase Naawen ale sum vua la, waai ale ta Izirali demma a nyini wiiluk geŋka tɛŋka ale tɛŋ sii ate wa jam yiak ba la.> Diila m le ta ba a jam tɛŋ kaai ate m pai te ba kokpieŋsaŋa la.

ref: But for now, I am sending enemies who will catch you like fish and hunt you down like wild animals in the hills and the caves.
text: Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Alege m le tom a yaali jum yigrɔ boari ate ba yik ba. Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ m le tom a yaali yaalɔ boari, ate ba yaalim a nak ba dueni guuk meena ale piuŋ meena zuk ale pina vie po.

ref: I can see everything you are doing, even if you try to hide your sins from me.
text: Mi nina a bo ba suitaŋa meena po kama, ba an suk ale mi, yaase ba wabiokku a suk mi nina po.

ref: I will punish you double for your sins, because you have polluted my own land. You have filled it with lifeless idols that remind me of dead bodies. The Lord Gives Strength I prayed to the Lord:
text: Mi tuni ba ku nɔi buye ba gaasaŋa ale ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ diila ba taŋ mi tɛŋka kama ale ba ŋanmɛɛn tii ale kan ta vum la nyeelaŋa ale sueri mi nitalimu ale ba bɔgluk tii ate mi kisa la.>>

ref: Our Lord, you are the one who gives me strength and protects me like a fortress when I am in trouble. People will come to you from distant nations and say, “Our ancestors worshiped false and useless gods,
text: Naawen yaa, m pagrim ale m ligrɔ, m sukka jigi daanika po, fi jigi ate tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale nyini tɛŋka kpeglimka meena jigi a jam weeni ayen, <<Ti koma a jam ka jaaboa alege ka venta wena ŋaai ale kan nye wamaŋ a te ba.

ref: worthless idols made by human hands.”
text: <<Nuruba a nye badek wena? Ba a nye alege ŋa daa wena.>>

ref: Then the Lord replied, “That's why I will teach them about my power, and they will know that I truly am the Lord.”
text: <<Dila nyiŋ, m le sak ba. Yɔgyɔgla de m le sak ba m pagrimu ale zuaka. Ba yaa le seba ayen mi yuenni ale Naawen.

ref: People of Judah, your sins cannot be erased. They are written on your hearts like words chiseled in stone or carved on the corners of your altars. *
text: <<Juda wabiokku a ŋmarisi ale ka kutuk jaŋmarisim ale kerisi ale janoachɔrik ba suiniimaŋa nyiŋ ale ba kuŋkuŋtaŋa nyiilaŋa zuk.

ref: One generation after another has set up pagan altars and worshiped the goddess Asherah everywhere in your country— on hills and mountains, and under large trees.
text: Ba bisaŋa a poom a teeri ba kuŋkuŋtaŋa ale Asera zaŋŋa ale za ti sii meena ale ta va sobta la ale gu wɔŋtaŋa zuk.

ref: So I'll take everything you own, including your altars, and give it all to your enemies.
text: Mi guuku ale bo tɛŋka po la ale ni nitalimu ale ni tuilum ŋantaŋa m le pai te ate ba koalim ale ni tangbanaŋa meena ni wabaataŋa tɛŋka po meena nyiŋ.

ref: You will lose the land that I gave you, and I will make you slaves in a foreign country, because you have made my anger blaze up like a fire that won't stop burning. Trust the Lord
text: Nidek nye beka nyiŋ ni le jɔk nitalim buui ate m pai te ni. M le basi ate ni chim ni dachaasaŋa yɔm tɛŋ kaai po ate ni zɛ. Diila ni zuk m suinni po kama ate di ale de taam wuu.>>

ref: I, the Lord, have put a curse on those who turn from me and trust in human strength.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Kikaasa a bo waai ale ta sebchakka ale nurubiik la. Waai yiila ale bo nyiŋlam jigi a yaali pagrim ale waai suinum ale tulim a basi Naawen.

ref: But I will bless those who trust me, the Lord.
text: <<Alege niauŋ a bo ka waai ale ta sebchakka ale Naawen la, waai sebchakka ale bo ale wa la.

ref: They will be like trees growing beside a stream— trees with roots that reach down to the water, and with leaves that are always green. They bear fruit every year and are never worried by a lack of rain.
text: Wa le nye ase ka tiib ate ba vuk nyiam nɔi la buui tɛŋ naŋsa ale teeri a siŋ benni po. Bu niŋ ka tuiluk po ase ku nin jam, bu vaataŋa kasim sobi kama. Ku kan daani bu ase ben dii ŋmoruk a nin kan ni ya ale kan kpeeri yɔna yɔnika.>>

ref: You people of Judah are so deceitful that you even fool yourselves, and you can't change.
text: Suinummu a ta pimpaasima a gaam ŋanta meena kama a ka tebika. Ka wana ale baga a miŋ bu?

ref: But I know your deeds and your thoughts, and I will make sure you get what you deserve.
text: <<Mi Naawen ale a gisi suinum ale a kpesi popolaŋa, a tuni nuru a magsi chaab ale wa nyeelaŋa, a magsi chaab ale wa tuimaŋa ale magsi diila.>>

ref: You cheated others, but everything you gained will fly away, like birds hatched from stolen eggs. Then you will discover what fools you are. Jeremiah Prays to the Lord
text: Ase yeŋ ale a wɔgri jena ŋaai ate ka an lobi la ku ka dila dek ale nuru waai ale pai venta suik a paari ŋanta. Wa dan ga pak maga wa le jɔk ba ate ku kpeglimka wa chim beruk.

ref: Our Lord, your temple is a glorious throne that has stood on a mountain from the beginning.
text: Ti Wen yenni a nye ase ka zula naam zukpaglik la, a za gu woŋ zuk a nyini piilimka po.

ref: You are a spring of water giving Israel life and hope. But if the people reject what you have told me, they will be swept away like words written in dust.
text: Naawen yaa, Izirali yiila, baai meena ale zɛri fu la ale jo chivie po. Ba le muriŋ bɛ ase yue ale ŋmarisi tanta po la dii nyiŋla ba zɛri Naawen kama, nyuvuri nyiam bulika.

ref: You, Lord, are the one I praise. So heal me and rescue me! Then I will be completely well and perfectly safe.
text: Tebi mu, Naawen yaa, ate m nya tebika, vari mu basi ate m nya varibasika, diila ka fi ale waai ate mi a pak.

ref: The people of Judah say to me, “Jeremiah, you claimed to tell us what the Lord has said. So why hasn't it come true?”
text: Ba kasim a weeni mi kama ayen, <<Naawen wanni a bo ka bɛ? Basi ate ku nye yɔgyɔgla de.>>

ref: Our Lord, you chose me to care for your people, and that's what I have done. You know everything I have said, and I have never once asked you to punish them.
text: Mi an chali a bɛ ya ale m le chim fi naapeerik la. Fi seba ayen mi an yaali daanika danni: Wa dii ale a nyini mi nɔi po la fi seba kama.

ref: I trust you for protection in times of trouble, so don't frighten me.
text: Kan chim nyinyigsa nyɔnɔ a te mu, fi jigi ate mi a suk kaasuŋ danni.

ref: Keep me from failure and disgrace, but make my enemies fail and be disgraced. Send destruction to make their worst fears come true. Resting on the Sabbath
text: Basi ate baai ale a namsi mu la chivie a yik ba, alege kasi mu chivie po, basi ate yɔgsum yik ba, alege kasi mu nyinyigsa po. Ta kaasuŋ danni a jam ba zuk, kaasi ba ale kaasuŋ ku nɔi buye.

ref: The Lord said: Jeremiah, stand at each city gate in Jerusalem, including the one the king uses, and speak to him and everyone else. Tell them I have said: I am the Lord, so pay attention.
text: Weeni ba ayen, <Wom Naawen wanni, Juda nalima ale Juda nuruma meena ale waai meena ale bo Jerusalem a va nansuiŋtaŋa de a jam la.

ref: If you value your lives, don't do any work on the Sabbath. Don't carry anything through the city gates or through the door of your house, or anywhere else. Keep the Sabbath day sacred! I gave this command to your ancestors, but they were stubborn and refused to obey or to be corrected. But if you obey,
text: << <Alege ni dan kpesi a wom mi nɔi, Naawen ale weeni, an ta jiboa a va tɛŋka nansuiŋtaŋa a jo Vuusum Danni, alege basi ate Vuusum Danni a chim tuilum dai an tom tuini,

ref: then Judah and Jerusalem will always be ruled by kings from David's family. The king and his officials will ride through these gates on horses or in chariots, and the people of Judah and Jerusalem will be with them. There will always be people living in Jerusalem,
text: nalima ŋaai ale a kali Deevid zukpaglika zuk la ale va tɛŋka de nansuiŋtaŋa a jo ale ba kpaŋŋa. Ba ale ba kpaŋŋa ale do wusuma ale torokoba, ate Juda nuruba ale baai ale bo Jerusalem la a bani ba, ate tɛŋka de nuruba a bo ka po taam wuu.

ref: and others will come here from the nearby villages, from the towns of Judah and Benjamin, from the hill country and the foothills to the west, and from the Southern Desert. They will bring sacrifices to please me and to give me thanks, as well as offerings of grain and incense.
text: Nuruba ale nyini Juda tɛŋsaŋa ale tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale gilim Jerusalem, ba le nyini Benjamin tɛŋbanni po ale yeniŋ guutaŋa, ale tɛŋ kaai ale ta guutaŋa la ale Negev a ta juka tiirita ale kaabsa ale ŋanbie tiirita ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa ale jiam teka tiirita a jam Naawen yenni po.

ref: But if you keep on carrying things through the city gates on the Sabbath and keep treating it as any other day, I will set fire to these gates and burn down the whole city, including the fortresses.
text: << <Alege ni dan kan wom mi nɔi ya a basi ate Vuusum Danni a ta tuilum an ji jibta a va Jerusalem nansuiŋtaŋa Vuusum Danni m yaa le fuk bolim buui ale kaa kpimsi Jerusalem nansuiŋtaŋa ate bu dɛ ka ŋan pagraŋa.> >>

ref: I went there and saw the potter making clay pots on his pottery wheel.
text: Dila mi yaa cheŋ siŋ mɛɛrɔwa yenni, ate mi nya ale wa a mɛ a gilim.

ref: And whenever the clay would not take the shape he wanted, he would change his mind and form it into some other shape.
text: Alege samɔniŋka ate wa a mɛ ale yakka la yaa kaasi wa nisa po, dila mɛɛrɔwa yaa yik tulim a nye ka choa, a tagri a nye dii ale nala a te wadek la.

ref: Then the Lord told me to say:
text: Naawen wanni yaa jam mi jigi ayen,

ref: People of Israel, I, the Lord, have power over you, just as a potter has power over clay.
text: <<Izirali yeri yaa, mi an baga a nye fu ase mɛɛrɔwa de ale a nye diila?>> Naawen ale weeni. <<Ase yak ale bo mɛɛrɔwa nisa po diila, ni ka dila mi nisa po, Izirali yeri yaa.

ref: If I threaten to uproot and shatter an evil nation,
text: Ase diipo meena m dan mooli ayen tɛŋ yaase naam a yeeri abe bu lo waaŋ abe bu kaasi,

ref: If I promise to make a nation strong,
text: Ate diipo ŋmana m dan mooli ayen tɛŋ ba sɛ ka yaase naam a zaani,

ref: but its people start disobeying me and doing evil, then I will change my mind and not help them at all.
text: ate ka nye biem mi nina po ale an wom mi nɔi ya, m le zimsi ale mi ale jam a poli ayen m nye wamaŋ kaai la.

ref: So listen to me, people of Judah and Jerusalem! I have decided to strike you with disaster, and I won't change my mind unless you stop sinning and start living right.
text: <<Dila nyiŋ yɔgyɔgla de weeni Juda nuruma ale baai ale bo Jerusalem ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Nya! Mi a gomsi ka kaasuŋ a magsi ni ale poli zɔga ayen m ta chaab ale fu. Dila ni basi ni biem suitaŋa, waai meena wanyi wanyi a tagri ni suitaŋa ale ni nyeelaŋa.>

ref: But I know you won't listen. You might as well answer, “We don't care what you say. We have made plans to sin, and we are going to be stubborn and do as we please!”
text: Alege ba le tulisi ayen, <Ku ka kiri. Ti le ta ka tidek zɔga. Ti meena ale va ka tidek tuikpari ale biem popolaŋa.> >> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: So I, the Lord, command you to ask the nations, and find out if they have ever heard of such a horrible sin as what you have done.
text: Dila la Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Kpesi nya tɛŋsaŋa meena po: Ka wana ale wom wanni de choa? Wa dii ale bie la ate Izirali demma a nye.

ref: The snow on Lebanon's mountains never melts away, and the streams there never run dry.
text: Lebanon ŋmoruk tanaŋa a nyaliŋ a bɛ pina ŋaai ale churinti la zuwa? Ka nya yɔgsisa ale nyini niŋniŋ la a basi chalika kama?

ref: But you, my people, have turned from me to burn incense to worthless idols. You have left the ancient road to follow an unknown path where you stumble over idols.
text: Alege mi nuruma a baŋ mi, ba ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te bɔgluk tii ale kan ta kiri ya, tii ale basi ate ba a nak naŋsa ba suita po ale dipo suitaŋa po. Ba basi ate ba a cheŋ sui tii ale kaa nya po ale manpala ŋaai ale kan kpa ya.

ref: Your land will be ruined, and every passerby will look at it with horror and make insulting remarks.
text: Ba tɛŋka ale doa kinla, jabuui ale kasim chim jalaam taam wuu, baai meena ale a taam la ku le cha ba ate ba a girinti zuima.

ref: When your enemies attack, I will scatter you like dust blown by an eastern wind. Then, on that day of disaster, I will turn my back on you. The Plot against Jeremiah
text: Ase viok ale nyini konni po, m le kati ba waaŋ ba dachaasaŋa niŋ. M le sak ba m ŋaaŋka alege daa m nina ba kaasuŋku danni.>>

ref: Some of the people said, “Let's get rid of Jeremiah! We will always have priests to teach us God's laws, as well as wise people to give us advice, and prophets to speak the Lord's messages. So, instead of listening to Jeremiah any longer, let's accuse him of a crime.” Jeremiah Prays about His Enemies
text: Ba weeni ayen, <<Ni jam, ni basi ate ti zɔk a ta chaab ale Jeremaya, diila kaabteerɔba ale diem boro a sak ti, ate yam nyam a kaam ti, ale biisiteerɔba ate ba a mooli Naawen wanni. Dila ni jam ate ti siti wa ale ti noaŋa abe ti kan wom wa le a weeni diila.>>

ref: Please, Lord, answer my prayer. Make my enemies stop accusing me of evil.
text: Wom mi, Naawen yaa, wom baai ale a ŋma mu la ale a weeni diila.

ref: I tried to help them, but they are paying me back by digging a pit to trap me. I even begged you not to punish them.
text: Ba pai biem a tuni nalimmoa? Alege ba tu goluk a magsi mi. Teeri ayen mi jam zaani ka fi niŋ a biisi a te ba ayen m tulim fi suipuurumu ba jigi a basi.

ref: But now I am asking you to let their children starve or be killed in war. Let women lose their husbands and sons to disease and violence.
text: Dila pai ba bisaŋa a te kɔm. Pai ba a te gebika pagrimu. Basi ate ba pooma a kan ta bisa abe ba chim pukɔga. Basi ate ba nidoama ba ko ba, ba nidoa paalukku ba ko ba ale gebik kpaliŋ po.

ref: These people have dug pits and set traps for me, Lord. Make them scream in fear when you send enemy troops to attack their homes.
text: Basi ate ba wom kaarik ba yeeŋa po ase fi nin ta nuruba a jam diiri ayen ba koalim ba, diila ba tu ka goluk ayen ba yik mi ale suk batta a magsi mi naŋsaŋa.

ref: The Lord said: Jeremiah, go to the pottery shop and buy a clay jar. Then take along some of the city officials and leading priests
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Cheŋ a ga da yak samɔniŋ mɛɛrɔ jigi. Basi ate nuruma nisɔmma ale kaabteerɔma a va fu

ref: and go to Hinnom Valley, just outside Potsherd Gate. Tell the people that I have said:
text: a cheŋ Ben Yinnom Viaka, ale moata Takabi Nansuiŋku la. Dula jigi mooli wa ŋaai ate mi a weeni fu la,

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and you kings of Judah and you people of Jerusalem had better pay attention. I am going to bring so much trouble on this valley that everyone who hears about it will be shocked.
text: a weeni ayen, <Wom Naawen wanni, Juda nalima ale Jerusalem nuruba. Dii ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni la: Ni wom, mi ale ta kaasuŋ a jam dela ate waai meena tue ale a wom la ku le cha wa.

ref: The people of Judah stopped worshiping me and made this valley into a place of worship for Baal and other gods that have never helped them or their ancestors or their kings. And they have committed murder here, burning their young, innocent children as sacrifices to Baal. I have never even thought of telling you to do that.
text: Ba sɛ Baal tangbana ayen ba ju ba nidoabilisa bolim po ase tiirita la a te Baal, wa dii ate mi an sak ba yaase m wi di yuei ya yaase di jo m popola po.

ref: So watch out! Someday this place will no longer be called Topheth or Hinnom Valley. It will be called Slaughter Valley!
text: Dila ni seba, daaŋa a cheena, Naawen ale weeni, ate nuruba a kan ŋman wi dela ayen Tofet yaase Ben Yinnom Viaka, alege ka Tɔgrika Viak.

ref: You people of Judah and Jerusalem may have big plans, but here in this valley I'll ruin those plans. I'll let your enemies kill you, and I'll tell the birds and wild animals to eat your dead bodies.
text: << <Dela jigini m le kaasi Juda ale Jerusalem zɔŋŋa. M le te ate ba ko ba dueni ale gebik ba dachaasaŋa niŋ. Baai ale a gisi ba nyuvooŋa la ale ba ko ba, ate ba pai ba nyiŋsaŋa a te ase ŋandiinta la a te wenzuk nuinsaŋa ale tɛŋka zuk duŋsaŋa.

ref: I will turn Jerusalem into a pile of rubble, and every passerby will be shocked and horrified and will make insulting remarks.
text: M le kaasi tɛŋka a basi ate waai a kan yaali ka, baai meena ale a taam la ku le cha ba kaasuŋku nyiŋ.

ref: And while your enemies are trying to break through your city walls to kill you, the food supply will run out. You will become so hungry that you will eat the flesh of your friends and even of your own children.
text: M le basi ate ba ŋɔbi ba nidoabilisaŋa ale ba liema, ba le ŋɔbi chaab diipo ate ba dacha sii ale a gisi ba nyuvooŋa la ale gilim ba a lik ba ta ate ku jo ba nyiŋla.>

ref: Jeremiah, as soon as you have said this, smash the jar while the people are watching.
text: <<Yaa mobi samɔniŋka alege ate baai ale va fu la a nya,

ref: Then tell them that I have also said: I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warn you that I will shatter Judah and Jerusalem just like this jar that is broken beyond repair. You will bury your dead here in Topheth, but so many of you will die that there won't be enough room.
text: a weeni ba ayen, <Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna: M le ŋɔriŋ tɛŋ kpieŋ de ale tɛŋ num de ase ka mɛɛrɔwa samɔniŋka ale ŋɔriŋ a ka tebika la. Ba le gu kpiema Tofet ate jigi a kan boro.

ref: I will make Jerusalem as unclean as Topheth, by filling the city with your dead bodies. I will do this because you and your kings have gone up to the roofs of your houses and burned incense to the stars in the sky, as though they were gods. And you have given sacrifices of wine to foreign gods. Jeremiah Speaks in the Temple Courtyard
text: Jerusalem yeeŋa ale Juda nalimaŋa yeeŋa ale yie ŋaai meena zuk ate ba ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te chiŋmarisa ale kpiiri daam ase tiirim a te wen yona, ŋa meena taŋ kama ase Tofet la.> >>

ref: I went to Topheth, where I told the people what the Lord had said. Then I went to the temple courtyard and shouted to the people,
text: Jeremaya yaa ŋman cheŋ Tofet, juijui ate Naawen jam tom wa ayen wa mooli la, ate wa zaani Naawen yenni dabiaka po a weeni nuruma meena ayen,

ref: “Listen, everyone! Some time ago, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, warned you that he would bring disaster on Jerusalem and all nearby villages. But you were stubborn and refused to listen. Now the Lord is going to bring the disaster he promised.”
text: <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <Ni wom, m za m ta ka kaasuŋ meena ate mi a mooli la a jam tɛŋ nummu de ale tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale gilim ka la zuk, dii nyiŋla ba ka tuikpari nyam a kan wom mi wieŋa.> >>

ref: Pashhur son of Immer was a priest and the chief of temple security. He heard what I had said,
text: Immer nidoabinni Pasur waai ale jam ka kaabteerɔ ale chim kpagi kpienni Naawen yenni po la, ale wom Jeremaya a mooli wieŋa de la,

ref: and so he hit me. Then he had me arrested and put in chains at the Benjamin Gate in the Lord's temple.
text: wa yaa basi ate ba nak biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya ale su wa chɔrima Benjamin Nansuiŋku Guuku Zuk Naawen yenni jigini.

ref: The next day, when Pashhur let me go free, I told him that the Lord had said: No longer will I call you Pashhur. Instead, I will call you Afraid-of-Everything.
text: Da dii ale pai saŋ la, ate Pasur a yeeri chɔrimaŋa ale basi wa la, Jeremaya yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen ale te fu yuei diila daa Pasur, alege ka Magor Missabib.

ref: You will be afraid, and you will bring fear to your friends as well. You will see enemies kill them in battle. Then I will let the king of Babylonia take everyone in Judah prisoner, killing some and dragging the rest away to Babylonia.
text: Dila Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <M le basi ate fi chim nyinyigsa nyɔnɔ a te fidek ale fi doama meena. Ale fidek nina fi le nya ba dachaasaŋa ale ko ba ale gebik a lɔnsi. M le pai Juda meena a te Babilon naawa, waai ale wa ji ba a ta cheŋ Babilon yaase wa ko ba.

ref: Pashhur, you are guilty of telling lies and claiming they were messages from me. That's why I will let the Babylonians take you, your family, and your friends as prisoners to Babylonia, where you will all die and be buried. Jeremiah Complains to the Lord
text: Ale fi, Pasur ale baai meena ale bo fi yenni po la ba le ta ni cheŋ Babilon. Dula ni le kpi ate ba gu ni, nama ale ni doama ate fi mooli ventaŋa a te la.> >>

ref: You tricked me, Lord, and I was really fooled. You are stronger than I am, and you have defeated me. People never stop sneering and insulting me.
text: Naawen yaa, fi paasi mu, ate mi nya paasika. Fi ta pagrim a gaam mi kama, a nya pagrim mi zuk. Waai meena a nye mi ka siak, ba a la mi kama danni meena.

ref: You have let me announce only injustice and death. Your message has brought me nothing but insults and trouble.
text: Diipo meena mi dan biisi, see m kaari ate ku nyini abe m na ayen, wɔkwɔk ale kaasuŋ. Dila Naawen wanni a ta ka leeta ale ŋmiŋmasim a jam mi jigi danni meena.

ref: Sometimes I tell myself not to think about you, Lord, or even mention your name. But your message burns in my heart and bones, and I cannot keep silent.
text: Alege mi weeni ayen, <<Mi kan weeni wa wari ya yaase m wi wa yuei ya,>> wa wanni a bo ka m suinummu po ase bolim la, bolim buui ale lik bo m kobaŋa po. M jiak kama ale di pik taka. Chekki mi an baga.

ref: I heard the crowds whisper, “Everyone is afraid. Now's our chance to accuse Jeremiah!” All of my so-called friends are just waiting for me to make a mistake. They say, “Maybe Jeremiah can be tricked. Then we can overpower him and get even at last.”
text: Mi a wom waai meena a waasi kama ayen, <<Nyinyigsa ale bo jigi meena. Dila ni te ti weeni wa wie a te pagrɔma.>> Baai ale poom moata mi a chim mi doaba la a limisi mi lueta kama. Da dii dai ba le paasi wa. Ba le weeni ayen, <Ti yaa baga a yik wa kama a tuni.>>

ref: But you, Lord, are a mighty soldier, standing at my side. Those troublemakers will fall down and fail— terribly embarrassed, forever ashamed.
text: Alege Naawen a bo le mi kama ase tugurik tɔŋdɔ pagrik la, dila baai ale a namsi mu la ale nak naŋsa a lo ba kan nya pagrimoa. Ba le nye kpeeri abe ba nya chivie, ba valiŋsaŋa ba kan maa baŋ.

ref: Lord All-Powerful, you test those who do right, and you know every heart and mind. I have told you my complaints, so let me watch you take revenge on my enemies.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, fi waai ale a kpesi a nya wayɔrisima nyama ale seba dii ale bo ba suiniima ale ba popola po, basi ate mi nya ale fi tuni ba a te mu, diila m pai m wanni a te ka fi.

ref: I sing praises to you, Lord. You rescue the oppressed from the wicked.
text: Leni yiila a te Naawen. Pai pimpauk a te Naawen. Wa a vari baai ale a silim la gaasa nyama nisa po a basi.

ref: Put a curse on the day I was born! Don't bless that day.
text: Kikaasa a cheŋ dai dii danni ate ba biak mi la. Dai dii ate mi mawa a biak mi la a kan nya niauŋŋoa.

ref: Put a curse on the man who told my father, “Good news! You have a son.”
text: Kikaasa a cheŋ waai ale ta wapaalaŋa a jam mi kowa jigi, waai ale basi ate wa sui a peenti, a weeni ayen, <<Ba biak biik a te fu, nidoabili.>>

ref: May that man be like the towns you destroyed without pity. Let him hear shouts of alarm in the morning and battle cries at noon.
text: Nuru wala abe nye ase tɛŋ sii ate Naawen a yuk yiak ale an sak jiirim la. Wa be wom kaarik saluiku, kpaliŋ kaarik kantueŋka.

ref: He deserves to die for not killing me before I was born. Then my mother's body would have been my grave.
text: Diila wa an jam ko mi luikku po, ate mi mawa a chim mi boosukwa, wa luikku a lagri kama taam wuu.

ref: Why did I have to be born? Was it just to suffer and die in shame?
text: Ka boa ate mi poom maa nyini luikku po a nyini a nya daanika ale suipuurummoa a za ayen m kpeglim daaŋa ale chivie?

ref: King Zedekiah of Judah sent for Pashhur son of Malchiah and for a priest named Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. Then he told them, “Talk with Jeremiah for me.” So they came to me and said,
text: Naawen wanni yaa jam Jeremaya jigi diipo ate naab Zedekia a tom Malkija nidoabinni Pasur ale Maaseiya nidoabinni Zefania ale jam ka kaabteerɔ la wa jigi. Ba weeni ayen,

ref: “King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked Judah. Please ask the Lord to work miracles for our people, as he has done in the past, so that Nebuchadnezzar will leave us alone.”
text: Kpesi yɔgyɔgla de Naawen a te ti dii nyiŋla Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar a siti ti kama. Dai dii dai Naawen ale tom wakinkagla a te ti ase dipo la ate wa basi ti.

ref: Then I told them that the Lord had said: People of Jerusalem, I, the Lord, give you the choice of life or death.
text: A ŋman gum du, weeni nuruma ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Nya, mi a dueni ka nyuvuri suik ale kum suik ni niŋ.

ref: The Babylonian army has surrounded Jerusalem, so if you want to live, you must go out and surrender to them. But if you want to die because of hunger, disease, or war, then stay here in the city.
text: Waai dek ale a bo tɛŋka de po la ale kpi ale gebik ale kɔm ale nyiŋtuila. Alege waai ale a nyini peelim a siak a te Kaldiya demma ale gilim a lik ni ta la ale vuuk.

ref: I have decided not to rescue Jerusalem. Instead, I am going to let the king of Babylonia burn it to the ground. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Warns the King of Judah *
text: Mi piika nyiŋ ayen m nye tɛŋka de biem alege daa nalimmoa, Naawen ale weeni. M le pai nyo Babilon naawa nisa po ate wa kaasi ka ale bolim.

ref: Pay attention, you that belong to the royal family.
text: Diem a weeni Juda naam yenni ayen, <Ni wom Naawen wanni.

ref: Each new day, make sure that justice is done, and rescue those who are being robbed. Or else my anger will flame up like a fire that never goes out.
text: Deevid yeri yaa, Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Ni nye a magsi saluik meena, ni vari waai ate ba vari wa la namsidɔwa nisa po a basi kan daa di m suipuurumu ale na pusi a dɛ ase bolim la ni le nye biem buui la nyiŋ, bu le dɛ ate waai a kan boro a kpimsi.

ref: and I will punish you as you deserve. I'll set your palace on fire, and everything around you will go up in smoke.

ref: and I will punish you as you deserve. I'll set your palace on fire, and everything around you will go up in smoke.

ref: But all you think about is how to cheat or abuse or murder some innocent victim.

ref: You will be given a burial fit for a donkey; your body will be dragged outside the city gates and tossed in the dirt. I, the Lord, have spoken. King Jehoiachin and the People of Jerusalem The Lord told me to say:

ref: People of Jerusalem, the nations you trusted have been crushed. Go to Lebanon and weep; cry in the land of Bashan and in Moab.

ref: Now you will be disgraced because of your sins. Your leaders will be swept away by the wind, and the nations you trusted will be captured and dragged to a foreign country.

ref: King Jehoiachin, son of Jehoiakim, even if you were the ring I wear as the sign of my royal power, I would still pull you from my finger.

ref: You leaders of my people are like shepherds that kill and scatter the sheep.
text: <<Ku le bie a te naapeerik sii ale a kaasi ale a waaŋ mi piisaŋa la.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: You were supposed to take care of my people, but instead you chased them away. So now I'll punish you severely and make you pay for your crimes!

ref: Someday I will appoint an honest king from the family of David, a king who will be wise and rule with justice.

ref: As long as he is king, Israel will have peace, and Judah will be safe. The name of this king will be “The Lord Gives Justice.”

text: Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Ku daaŋa a cheena ate nuruba a kan ŋman pɛ mi nyiŋ ase Naawen dii ale vua la ale jam ta Izirali demma a nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka po a nyini.

ref: Instead, you will call me the Living God who rescued you from the land in the north and from all the other countries where I had forced you to go. And you will once again live in your own land. Jeremiah Thinks about Unfaithful Prophets
text: Ba le goanti a pɛ ka mi nyiŋ ase Naawen dii ale vua la ale jam ta Izirali demma a nyini wiiluk geŋka tɛŋka ale tɛŋ sinsila meena ate mi kati ba waaŋ ate ba cheŋ si la po a nyini. Ate ba yaa bo badek tɛŋ po.>>

ref: When I think of the prophets, I am shocked, and I tremble like someone drunk, because of the Lord and his sacred words.
text: A magsi chaab ale biisiteerɔma: M suinummu a kaasi kama, m kobaŋa a choa kama. Mi a nye ase ka dabugrik la, a nye ase nuru ate daam baga wa la, Naawen ale wa tuilum wieŋa nyiŋ.

ref: Those unfaithful prophets misuse their power all over the country. So God turned the pasturelands into scorching deserts. The Lord Will Punish Unfaithful Prophets

ref: The Lord told me to say: You prophets and priests think so little of me, the Lord, that you even sin in my own temple!
text: <<Biisiteerɔ ale kaabteerɔ meena a ka wen ya, mi poom a nya ba gaasaŋa ka m yenni po.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Now I will punish you with disaster, and you will slip and fall in the darkness. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: <<Dila nyiŋ ba suik a za ku a sati kama, m le yiak ba a basi legi po ate dula ba lo. M le ta kaasuŋ a jam ba zuk ba namsika benni.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The prophets in Samaria were repulsive to me, because they preached in the name of Baal and led my people astray.

text: Jerusalem biisiteerɔma suŋsuŋ mi nya ka wa dii ale bie: Ba nye ka kaboŋsa ale a velim, ba a te ka baai ale a nye biem la nyiŋbiiri, ate waai a kan basi wa gaasa. Ba meena a nye ase ka Sodom la a te mi, Jerusalem demma a nye ase ka Gomora la.>>

ref: You prophets in Jerusalem have spread evil everywhere. That's why I, the Lord, promise to give you bitter poison to eat and drink. The Lord Gives a Warning The Lord said:

ref: Don't listen to the lies of these false prophets, you people of Judah! The message they preach is something they imagined; it did not come from me, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Ni kan wom biisiteerɔma ale mooli dii a te ni la, ba pai ka venta yiila a sueri ni popola. Ba biisi ka gɔdaasima wie a nyini badek popola po, daa Naawen nɔi po wie.

ref: These prophets go to people who refuse to respect me and who are stubborn and do whatever they please. The prophets tell them, “The Lord has promised everything will be fine.”
text: Ba kasim a weeni baai ale a zɛri mi la kama ayen, <Naawen a weeni ayen ni le ta suiyɔgni.> Ale baai meena ale a va ba tuikpari yaalika la ayen, <Biem a kan jam ni jigi ya.>

ref: But I, the Lord, tell you that these prophets have never attended a meeting of my council in heaven or heard me speak.
text: Alege ka ba wana ale zaani Naawen tigsuŋ po a nya yaase wa wom wa wanni? Ka wana ale kpesi wom wa wanni?

ref: They are evil! So in my anger I will strike them like a violent storm.

ref: I won't calm down, until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday you will understand exactly what I mean.

ref: I did not send these prophets or speak to them, but they ran to find you and to preach their message.
text: Mi an tom biisiteerɔma de alege ba chali cheŋ ale ba biika, mi an biisi ale ba alege ba mooli.

ref: If they had been in a meeting of my council in heaven, they would have told you people of Judah to give up your sins and come back to me.

ref: in heaven and on earth. There are no secret places where you can hide from me.
text: <<Nuru waai a baga a suk jigi susugi ate mi a kan seba?>> Naawen ale weeni. <<Mi an sueri daa wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk wa?>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: These unfaithful prophets claim that I have given them a dream or a vision, and then they tell lies in my name.

ref: But everything they say comes from their own twisted minds. How long can this go on?
text: Kude ale kasim nye beni ka sɛ venta biisiteerɔma de suiniimaŋa po, baai ale a mooli badek nyebeka popolaŋa de la?

ref: They tell each other their dreams and try to get my people to reject me, just as their ancestors left me and worshiped Baal.
text: Ba a poli kama ayen gɔdaasimaŋa ate ba weeni a sak chaab la ale basi ate mi nuruma a baŋ mi yuenni, ase ba koma ale baŋ mi yuenni Baal puusika nyiŋla.

ref: Their dreams and my truth are as different as straw and wheat. But when prophets speak for me, they must say only what I have told them.
text: Basi ate biisiteerɔ waai ale ta gɔdaasima la a weeni wa gɔdaasimaŋa, alege ate waai ale ta mi wanni la a biisi di ale wensie. Kinkari a ta ka boan wari a nye ale za biri ya?>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: My words are a powerful fire; they are a hammer that shatters rocks.
text: <<Mi wanni a kan nye ase daa bolim la ale a nye ase guri la a nak piuŋ a mobi yisayisa?>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: These unfaithful prophets claim I give them their dreams, but it isn't true. I didn't choose them to be my prophets, and yet they babble on and on, speaking in my name, while stealing words from each other. And when my people hear these liars, they are led astray instead of being helped. So I warn you that I am now the enemy of these prophets. I, the Lord, have spoken. News and Nuisance The Lord said to me:
text: Ni wom mi Naawen ale a weeni diila. <<Mi ta ka chaab ale biisiteerɔ baai ale a weeni ba gɔdaasima ate venta a boro la. text: Alege ku a fɛ ate ni kan wi <Naawen tontomiŋka wari> ŋmana, dii nyiŋla nuru meena wari a yaa chim ka tomtomiŋ ate dila ni yaa yik Wen vukku, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ti Wenni wanni a labri.

ref: If you go to a prophet, it's all right to ask, “What answer did the Lord give to my question?” or “What has the Lord said?”

text: M le ta taam wuu chivie a jam ni zuk, taam wuu kanpiin tii ate ni kan baŋ.>>

ref: The Lord spoke to me in a vision after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had come to Judah and taken King Jehoiachin, his officials, and all the skilled workers back to Babylonia. In this vision I saw two baskets of figs in front of the Lord's temple.
text: Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar a yaa jam ta Jeyoiakim nidoabinni Jekonaya ale jam ka Juda naab la a nyini Jerusalem a cheŋ Babilon ase ligrɔ la, a maa gum Juda niŋdeerɔma ale gobrɔma ale baai ale seba tuima la. ref: One basket was full of very good figs that ripened early, and the other was full of rotten figs that were not fit to eat.
text: Busik kanyi a jam ta ka kinkama ŋaai ale nala, ase ŋaai ale kpabi a muni la, m kala a jam ta kinkama ŋaai ale kan nala, an nala a baga a dɛ.

ref: “Jeremiah,” the Lord asked, “what do you see?” “Figs,” I said. “Some are very good, but the others are too rotten to eat.”
text: Naawen yaa bek mi ayen, <<Jeremaya, ka boa ate fi a nya?>> Mi yaa tulisi ayen, <<Kinkama. Kinkama naliŋsaŋa a nala ka yega, alege ŋaai ale kan nala la an bola nala a magsi dɛka.>>

ref: Then the Lord told me to say:
text: Naawen wanni yaa ŋman jam mi jigi:

text: <<Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <Baai ate mi basi ate ba yik ba Juda a ta cheŋ Kaldiya demma tɛŋka la a nye ase ka kinkam naliŋsaŋa la.

ref: where I am watching over them. Then someday I will bring them back to this land. I will plant them, instead of uprooting them, and I will build them up, rather than tearing them down.

ref: I will give them a desire to know me and to be my people. They will want me to be their God, and they will turn back to me with all their heart.
text: M le te ba suinum buui ate ba seba mu la, ayen ka Mi ale Naawen. Ba le chim mi nuruba, ate mi ale chim ba Wen, diila ba le ŋmani mi jigi ale ba suinum meena.

ref: The rotten figs stand for King Zedekiah of Judah, his officials, and all the others who were not taken away to Babylonia, whether they stayed here in Judah or went to live in Egypt.
text: <<Naawen a weeni ayen, <Alege Juda naawa Zedekia ale wa nuruma ale a nye ase kinkama ŋaai ale kan nala la, ŋaai ale ŋmasi bie a ka dɛka la, m le nye ale Zedekia ale wa kpaŋŋa ale Jerusalem nuru baai ale vuuk la, ba wari tɛŋka de po yaase ba bo Ejipiti.

text: <<Yaa weeni ba ayen, <Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni ayen. Nyu, nyu buk abe fi chiiri, a lo abe fi kan ŋman yiti diipo dii nyiŋla gebik ale cheena ni po.>

ref: The Lord's people are his flock, and you leaders were the shepherds. But now it's your turn to be butchered like sheep. You'll shatter like fine pottery dropped on the floor. So roll on the ground, crying and mourning.
text: Nama naapeerisaŋa, ni a kum abe ni a wooli, ni a bilim tantaŋa po, nama piisaŋa niŋdeerɔma. Diila ni tɔgrika daaŋa a paari kama, ni ale lo a mobi ka yisayisa ase samɔn naliŋ la.

text: <<Dii ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La Izirali Wenni a weeni la ale nna: <M le wɛ Babilon niiga diokku.
