text: Ate biisiteerɔwa Yanania yaa yeeri niiga diokku biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya ŋinni po a wɛ ku,

ref: Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.” I left the temple,
text: ale weeni nuruma meena niŋ ayen, <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar niiga diokku ale bo tɛŋsaŋa meena nuruma ŋie po la m le wɛ bena ŋaye po.> >> Biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya yaa cheŋ.

ref: to go back and say to Hananiah: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You smashed a wooden yoke, but I will replace it with one made of iron. I will put iron yokes on all the nations, and they will have to do what King Nebuchadnezzar commands. I will even let him rule the wild animals.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: M pai kuta niiga diokku a su tɛŋsaŋa de demma meena ŋie ate ba tom a te Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar, m le poom te wa pagrim duŋ waarisa zuk.> >>

ref: Hananiah, I have never sent you to speak for me. And yet you have talked my people into believing your lies and rebelling against me. So now I will send you—I'll send you right off the face of the earth! You will die before this year is over.
text: Dila nyiŋ Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <M za m yeeri fu kama tɛŋka zuk. Benni de dek fi za fi kpi kama, dii nyiŋla fi mooli ka tuikpari a ta chaab ale Naawen.> >>

ref: Two months later, Hananiah died.
text: Ben dila dek chiisa siyopɔiwa po biisiteerɔwa Yanania yaa kpi.

ref: I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote
text: Wa jam pai gbaŋka a nyo ka Safan nidoabinni Elasa ale Yilkia nidoabinni Gemaria ate Juda naawa Zedekia a tom Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar jigi la nisima po. Ka weeni ayen,

ref: that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. Now I tell you
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni, ale weeni dii a te baai meena ate mi ji a ta nyini Jerusalem a cheŋ Babilon la ale nna:

ref: to settle there and build houses. Plant gardens and eat what you grow in them.
text: <<Ni sɛ yie a kali a kpa kaduksa a de ŋan baai ale a nye la.

ref: Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
text: Ni faari nipooba a biak nidoabilisa ale lieba. Ni gisi pooba a te ni nidoabilisaŋa abe ni pai ni liema a yalisi, ate ba mɛ a nya nidoabilisa ale lieba. Ni piisi dula ni kan muuri.

ref: Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
text: Ni a juisi ayen tɛŋ kaai ate mi ta ni cheŋ la suiyɔgni a bo ka po abe ka nya ka dek. Ni puusi a te Naawen dila nyiŋ, diila ka dan nya ka dek, nama mɛ ale nya nidek.>>

ref: You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers.
text: Ate ni yaa le wi mi abe ni jam puusi a te mu, ate m wom ni.

ref: You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you
text: Ni le gisi mu a nya mu ase ni a nin gisi mu ale ni suinum meena.

ref: You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
text: Dai dii dai ni le weeni ayen, <<Naawen a te ti biisiteerɔba kama Babilon tɛŋka po,>>

ref: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now.
text: Dila la, ni wom Naawen wanni, nama baai meena ate ba yik ate mi a basi ate ni nyini Jerusalem a cheŋ Babilon la.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
text: <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni ayen, fi jam tom ka gbaŋsa fidek yuei nyiŋ a te nuruma meena ale bo Jerusalem la ale Maaseiya nidoabinni Zefania kaabteerɔwa ale kaabteerɔ mbala meena. Fi jam weeni Zefania ayen,

ref: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars.
text: <Naawen a lueri ka fi ase kaabteerɔ la a tagri Jeyoiada ayen fi a nya Naawen yenni zuk. Ku magsi fi nya ku zuk ate yesiŋ kaai meena ale potim a nye ase biisiteerɔ la ba su wa chɔrima abe kutuk gilinni a su wa ŋiri.

ref: Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him?
text: Ka boa ale soa ate fi an nye Anatot denɔwa Jeremaya nna, waai ale a biisi ase biisiteerɔ a te nuruma la.

ref: He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
text: Wa te ti tomtomiŋ ka de ka Babilon po. Ku le beni kama. Dila nyiŋ ni sɛ yie a kali abe ni vuk tiisa a de si le a yɔni ŋan baai la.> >>

ref: When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me.
text: Alege kaabteerɔwa Zefania a yaa jam kariŋ gbaŋka a te biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya.

ref: Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter
text: Naawen wanni yaa jam Jeremaya jigi.

ref: to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said: I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name.
text: <<Te tomtomiŋ ka de a paari baai meena ate ba yik ta cheŋ la: <Naawen ale weeni dii a magsi chaab ale Neyela denɔwa Sɛmaiya la ale nna: Sɛmaiya ale mooli te ni alege mi an tom wa a basi ate ni ta sebchakka ale ventaŋa la nyiŋ,

ref: He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: M le sum namsi Neyela denɔwa Sɛmaiya ale wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa. Wa kan ta waai ate wa tali nuruma de po yaase wa nya wamaŋ sii ate mi ale nye a te mi nuruma la, dii nyiŋla wa mooli ka tuikpari wie a ta chaab ale mi.> >> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you.
text: <<Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <Ŋmarisi wie ŋaai meena ate mi weeni fu la a nyo gbaŋ po.>

ref: Someday I will let my people from both Israel and Judah return to the land I gave their ancestors.”
text: Naawen ale weeni. <Daaŋa cheena ate m le ta m nuruma Izirali demma ale Juda demma a nyini ba yɔntini po a jam tɛŋ kaai ate mi pai te ba kokpieŋsaŋa ayen ba ta la.> Naawen ale weeni.>>

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah: Screams of terror are heard, with no word of peace.
text: <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <Yɔgsum kaarisa ate ba wom, ka kpazinagsuk daa suiyɔgni.

ref: Can men give birth? Then why do I see them looking so pale and clutching their stomachs like women in labor?
text: Bek a nya: Nidoa a baga a biak bisa? Ka boa yaa be le soa ate nidoa pagrik meena a pai nisima a ji wa lɔgi ase nipok ale a dom la, ate nimbidiaka meena a peenti?

ref: My people, soon you will suffer worse than ever before, but I will save you.
text: Dai dila danni ale bie chekki. Dai a kan nye ase di la. Ku le chim ka daanika dai a te Jekob, alege wa le nyini ka po a nyini.>

ref: Now you are slaves of other nations, but I will break the chains and smash the yokes that keep you in slavery.
text: <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni ayen, <Dai dila danni m le wɛ niiga daataŋa ba ŋieŋa po, abe m gebi ba chɔrimaŋa, ba kan ŋman chim nicham yɔmma.

ref: Then you will be my servants, and I will choose a king for you from the family of David. *
text: Ba le goanti a tom a te Naawen ba Wenni ale ba naawa Deevid, waai ate mi ale basi ate wa yiti a chim ba naab la.

ref: Israel, you belong to me, so don't be afraid. You deserved to be punished; that's why I scattered you in distant nations. But I am with you, and someday I will destroy those nations.
text: << <Mi dek tomteerɔwa Jekob, kan chali yɔgsummoa, Izirali, kan te ku daani.> Naawen ale weeni. <M le sum vari fu a ta nyini niŋniŋka jigini, fi ŋaaŋbisaŋa a ta nyini ba le yik ba a ta cheŋ juijui la. Jekob ale ŋman ta suiyɔgni ale likka ate waai a kan basi ate wa chali yɔgsummoa.

ref: Then I will bring you and your descendants back to your land, where I will protect you and give you peace. Then your fears will be gone. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
text: M bo ale fu kama m be le vari fu a basi.> Naawen ale weeni. <Mi a dan poom kaasi tɛŋ sii meena ate mi basi ate ni waaŋ si po la chessi, mi kan kaasi ni chessi. M le te ni waalika alege mi a nye ale ka nyemagsika. M kan basi dila ale kan namsi ni.>

ref: The Lord said: My people, you are wounded and near death.
text: <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <Fi kɔnika a ka tebika, fi munni a gaam tebika.

ref: You are accused of a crime with no one to defend you, and you are covered with sores that no medicine can cure. *
text: Waai karo a biisi a te fu, tiim ka a tebi fi noruku, tebika a ka a te fu.

ref: Your friends have forgotten you; they don't care anymore. Even I have acted like an enemy. And because your sins are horrible and countless, I will be cruel as I punish you.
text: Fi maarɔma meena a baŋ fi wari, ba ka kinla a te fu. Mi nak fu ase ka dachiak ate le wa nye diila ale namsi fu ase nyeka tuem nyɔnɔ ate le wa nye diila, dii nyiŋla fi foolaawa a zuak ka yega ate fi wabaataŋa a piisi.

ref: But if your enemies try to rob or destroy you, I will rob and destroy them, and they will be led as captives to foreign lands.
text: << <Alege baai meena ale a kaasi fu la m le kaasi ba. Fi dachaasaŋa meena ba le yik ba ta cheŋ tɛŋ yoŋ. Baai ale a koalim fu la ba le koalim ba. Baai meena ale a pai ni ŋanta la ba le pai ba ŋanta.

ref: No one wants you as a friend or cares what happens to you. But I will heal your injuries, and you will get well. The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
text: Alege m le te ni ŋman nya nyiŋyɔgsa abe m tebi ni kɔnika, dii nyiŋla ba a wi ni ayen ka yiak basidɔba waai niŋ a ka Zayon po.> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The Lord said: Israel, I will be kind to you and let you come home. Jerusalem now lies in ruins, but you will rebuild it, complete with a new palace.
text: <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna. <M le ŋman ta m nuruma a cheŋ ba tɛŋka abe m ta jiirim ale dɔkdem meena. Tɛŋka ba le ŋman sɛ ka ka guuraŋa zuk ate naab yenni ŋman zaani di jigi maŋka.

ref: Other nations will respect and honor you. Your homes will be filled with children, and you will celebrate, singing praises to me.
text: Nuru baai ale bo ka po la ale siak pimpauk yiila, ba le nuem ale suipeentik. Mi niauŋku nyiŋ ba le piisi. Mi niauŋku ale ta zula a jam ba jigi.

ref: It will be just like old times. Your nation will worship me, and I will punish anyone who abuses you.
text: Ba bisaŋa ale nye ase ka dipo daaŋa la, ate ba gilagilawa a kali paari mi nina po. M le namsi baai meena ale a namsi ba la.

ref: One of your own people will become your ruler. And when I invite him to come near me at the place of worship, he will do so. No one would dare to come near without being invited.
text: Ba niŋdeerɔwa ale chim ka badek po wanyi, ba kpagni ale yiti ka badek po. M le ta wa jam moata ate wa jam moata mi, ka wana ale wa siak ayen wa jam moata mi alege mi an wi wa?> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: You will be my people, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: << <Dila ni ale chim ka mi nuruba, ate mi a chim ni Wen.> >>

ref: I am furious! And like a violent storm I will strike those who do wrong.
text: Nya, Naawen vamuniŋka ale na nyini ale suipuurum, va pagrik ale vigsi a siŋ gaasa nyama zuk.

ref: I won't calm down until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday, you will understand what I mean.
text: Naawen suipuurumu a kan ŋman ŋaaŋ ŋa ate wa ga nye wa suinummu ale a yaali diila. Daa a cheena ni le miŋ kude.

ref: The Lord said: Israel, I promise that someday all your tribes will again be my people, and I will be your God.
text: Naawen ale weeni, <<Va ŋala po mi le chim Izirali yezuimaŋa meena Wen ate ba chim mi nuruba.>>

ref: In the desert I was kind to those who escaped death. I gave them peace, and when the time is right, I'll do the same for you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Rebuild Israel
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Nuru baai ale vuugi ate ba an ko ba ale gebik la ale nya ŋmanteka gɔnni po, m le jam te Izirali vuusum.>>

ref: Some time ago, the Lord appeared to me and told me to say: Israel, I will always love you; that's why I've been so patient and kind.
text: Naawen a jam pai wadek a sak ti kama dipowa a weeni ayen, <<Mi jam yaali ni ale ka yaali kaai ale kaa nueri la. Mi dari ni kama a ta jam ale ŋmanteka.

ref: You are precious to me, and so I will rebuild your nation. Once again you will dance for joy and play your tambourines.
text: M le ŋman yik ni zaani abe ni ŋman sɛ, Izirali demma. Ni le ŋman pai ni kayaksaŋa a nyini gɔk ale suipeentik.

ref: You will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria and enjoy the grapes.
text: Ni le ŋman kpa kaduksa Samaria guutaŋa zuima. Kpaarɔma ale vuk tiisa a de yɔnaŋa masim.

ref: Someday those who guard the hill country of Ephraim will shout, “Let's go to Zion and worship the Lord our God.” Israel Will Return to Its Own Land
text: Dai ale boro ate limisidɔba ale kaari Ɛfraim guutaŋa zuk ayen, <Ni jam ate ti jueli Zayon, Naawen ti Wenni jigi.> >>

ref: The Lord says: Celebrate and sing for Israel, the greatest of nations. Offer praises and shout, “Come and rescue your people, Lord! Save what's left of Israel.”
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Siak yiila ale suipeentik a te Jekob, nuem a te tɛŋ kaai ale gaam tɛŋsaŋa meena la. Basi ate ba wom pimpaukku, a weeni ayen, <Naawen yaa, vari fi nuruma a basi, Izirali dem baai ale tali la.>

ref: I, the Lord, will bring my people back from Babylonia and everywhere else on earth. The blind and the lame will be there. Expectant mothers and women about to give birth will come and be part of that great crowd.
text: Nya, m le ta ba nyini wiiluk geŋka tɛŋka a jam a tigsi ba a ta nyini tɛŋka kpeglisa jigi. Ba po ale chim ka yeoba ale gbansa, nipok puusa ale baai ale moata biam, ba chim ka tɛŋ pagrik a ŋmani.

ref: They will weep and pray as I bring them home. I will lead them to streams of water. They will walk on a level road and not stumble. I am a father to Israel, my favorite children.
text: Ba le ŋmani ale ka kumsa, ba le puusi ase m le ta ba ŋman cheen la. M le de ba niŋ a ta ba sali va beli naŋ sii ale ta nyiam ale suik kuui ale doa magsi chaab ate ba kan nak naŋsa, dii nyiŋla mi ka Izirali ko, ate Ɛfraim a chim m nidoabili kpagi.

ref: Listen to me, you nations nearby or across the sea. I scattered the people of Israel, but I will gather them again. I will protect them like a shepherd guarding a flock;
text: <<Tɛŋsa, wom Naawen wanni, mooli di tɛŋ sii ale yalima a bo nyiam nɔi la. <Waai ale waaŋ Izirali la ale tigsi ba abe wa nya wa piisaŋa zuk ase naapeerik la.>

ref: I will rescue them from enemies who could overpower them.
text: Naawen ale da tuesi Jekob abe wa da tuesi ba baai ale pagra a gaam ba la jigi a basi.

ref: My people will come to Mount Zion and celebrate; their faces will glow because of my blessings. I'll give them grain, grapes, and olive oil, as well as sheep and cattle. Israel will be prosperous and grow like a garden with plenty of water.
text: Ba le jam nuem ale suipeentik Zayon guutaŋa zuk, ba le naŋ ale Naawen tiiritaŋa, ŋanbieŋa ale dapaalika ale kpaamu ale pabisaŋa ale naabisaŋa nyiŋ. Ba le nye ase ka nyiam ale zaŋti kaduk nalimnyiini la ate ba sue kan ŋman kaasi.

ref: Young women and young men, together with the elderly, will celebrate and dance, because I will comfort them and turn their sorrow into happiness.
text: Dɔklieba yaa le gɔk abe ba sue a peenti, nidoa paaluk ale ŋankpagsa meena. M le tulim ba kumsaŋa ate si chim suipeentik. M le te ba suiyɔgni ale masim alege daa suipuurummoa.

ref: I will bless my people with more food than they need, and the priests will enjoy the choice cuts of meat. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Offers Hope
text: M le basi ate kaabteerɔma a ta yegayega abe m nuruma a nya ba ŋan silimta meena.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: In Ramah a voice is heard, crying and weeping loudly. Rachel mourns for her children and refuses to be comforted, because they are dead. *
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Nuemka ate ba wom Arama tɛŋka po, kumsa ale a kum nna yegayega, Arekel ale a kum wa bisa nyiŋ ale zɛri kan yaali suiyɔgni dii nyiŋla wa bisaŋa a karo.>>

ref: But I, the Lord, say to dry your tears. Someday your children will come home from the enemy's land. Then all you have done for them will be greatly rewarded.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Basi fi kumsaŋa abe fi duisi fi ninyaataŋa. Dii meena ate fi nye te fi bisaŋa la fi le nya ku tutuna, ba le nyini dachiaka tɛŋka a ŋmani.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: So don't lose hope. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: <<Dila yiila a boro a magsi chum. Fi bisaŋa ale ŋmani badek tɛŋka.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The people of Israel moan and say to me, “We were like wild bulls, but you, Lord, broke us, and we learned to obey. You are our God— please let us come home.
text: <<Mi sum wom Ɛfraim funfɔblaŋa kama: <Fi waali mi ase ka duŋ kaai ale kan baliŋ la ate mi a nya waalika. Tuesi mu ate m pilim a ŋmani, dii nyiŋla fi ka Naawen mi Wenni.

ref: When we were young, we strayed and sinned, but then we realized what we had done. We are ashamed and disgraced and want to return to you.”
text: Mi le cheŋ bɛ la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, mi laŋ ka nyeka. Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ mi le miŋ la, mi nak ka mi kuusidi. Chivie ale jam ta mi ate mi nya kanpiinta dii nyiŋla mi ta ka m bimbain chivie.>

ref: People of Israel, you are my own dear children. Don't I love you best of all? Though I often make threats, I want you to be near me, so I will have mercy on you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Ɛfraim daa mi dek nidoabili ya, biik kaai ate m mariŋ? Mi nyiem biisi kama a ta chaab ale wa, m diem a teeri wa kama. Dila nyiŋ mi suinum a bo ale wa kama. M ta ka jiirim yega ale wa.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: With rock piles and signposts, mark the road well, my dear people. The road by which you left by will now lead you home.
text: <<Ni ti daana ŋanta suiku niŋ, ni daani suiku. Ni kpesi suik duoku, suik kuui ate ni a va la. Izirali demma ni pilim ŋmani, ni ŋman cheŋ ni tɛŋsaŋa.

ref: Will you ever decide to be faithful? I will make sure that someday things will be different, as different as a woman protecting a man. The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
text: Fi le tuinti a beni a soa ka sɛ, lie waai ale kan ta wensie la? Naawen ale nye wa paali tɛŋzuk de, nipok ale lik nidoa.>>

ref: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said: I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say, “We pray that the Lord will bless his home, the sacred hill in Jerusalem where his temple stands.”
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <<M dan ta ba a nyini yɔntidi po a ŋman jam nuruma ale bo Juda ale ka tɛŋsaŋa po la ale ŋman weeni wieŋa de: <Naawen a niak wayɔrisima boka jigini ale tuilum guuku.>

ref: The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds.
text: Nuruba ale bo ale chaab Juda ale ka tɛŋsaŋa, kpaarɔba ale baai ale a gilim ale ba piisa la.

ref: Those who feel tired and worn out will find new life and energy,
text: M le basi ate baai ale jiak la nyiŋsa yɔk abe baai ate kɔm basi ate ba wobsa la a chak.>>

ref: and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
text: Kude yaa basi ate mi yiti a nya gilim. Mi goomu a jam masa te mi kama.

ref: Someday, Israel and Judah will be my field where my people and their livestock will grow.
text: Naawen ale a weeni ayen, <<Daaŋa a cheena ate m le basi ate nuruba ale duŋsa a sueri Izirali ale Juda.

ref: In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow.
text: Ase mi ale a limisi ba ayen ba dari voori abe ba dari lɔnsi abe ba yuk yiak abe ba ta kaasuŋ a jam la, ku ka dila ate m le basi ate ba sɛ abe ba vuk.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: No longer will anyone go around saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
text: <<Da ŋala po nuruba a kan ŋman weeni ayen, <Koba a de yɔn miisinsa, ate bisa nyina a miigi.>

ref: When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death. The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
text: Waai meena ale goanti a kpi ka wadek biem nyiŋ, waai ale a de yɔn miisinsa la wadek nyina ale a miik.

ref: The Lord said: The time will surely come when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah.
text: Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Daaŋa a cheena, ate m le nye nɔiyeŋ paalik ale Izirali yenni ale Juda yenni.

ref: It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
text: Ka kan nye ase nɔiyeŋ kaai ate mi jam nye ale ba kokpieŋsaŋa la m le jam yik ba nisa a de ba niŋ a ta nyini Ejipiti nyini, dii nyiŋla ba kaasi m nɔiyeŋka mi le jam diem chim chorɔ a te ba la.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Here is the new agreement that I, the Lord, will make with the people of Israel: “I will write my laws on their hearts and minds. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
text: Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Nɔiyeŋ kaai ate mi za m nye ale Izirali yenni va ŋala po la ale nna: M le pai m sinsaŋŋa a nyo ba popolaŋa po abe m ŋmarisi ŋa ba suiniimaŋa po. M le chim ba Wen, ate ba le chim m nuruba.

ref: “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
text: Naawen a weeni ayen, waai a kan ŋman sak wa vaanchoa, yaase nuru waai a sak wa suok wa a weeni ayen, <Seba Naawen,> dii nyiŋla ba meena ale seba mu, a zaani waai ale pɔsima a ga paari waai ale zuak, diila mi ale vɔŋ ba gaasaŋa a te ba m kan ŋman teeri ba wabaataŋa wie.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
text: Alege yɔgyɔgla de ni ŋman cheem kaasi mi yuenni, waai meena a ŋman tuesi wa yɔma nipok ale nidoa ate ni basi ayen ba cheŋ juijui ate ba a yaali la. Ni fɛ ba kama ate ba ŋman chim ni yɔm.

ref: You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
text: <<Dila la, Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Ni an wom mi nɔiya, ni an mooli fasiyaa a te ni tɛŋ demma. Dila mi yɔgyɔgla de a mooli ka <fasiyaa> a te ni, Naawen ale weeni, <fasiyaa> ayen gebika ale nyiŋtuila ale kɔm ale jam ni jigi. M le basi ate tɛŋsa a kisi ni.

ref: You asked me to be a witness when you made the agreement to set your slaves free. And as part of the ceremony you cut a calf into two parts, then walked between the parts. But you people of Jerusalem have broken that agreement as well as my agreement with Israel. So I will do to you what you did to that calf.
text: Nuru baai ale zɛri mi nɔiyeŋka alege an nye nɔiyeŋka wie ate ba nye mi niŋ la, m le nye ba ase ka naabiika ate ba gebi ka buye a cheŋ va suŋsuŋka po a taam diila.

ref: I will let your enemies take all of you prisoner, including the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the royal officials, the priests, and everyone else who walked between the two parts of the calf. These enemies will kill you and leave your bodies lying on the ground as food for birds and wild animals.
text: m le pai ba a te ba dacha sii ale a gisi ba nyuvooŋa la. Ba nyiŋsaŋa ale chim ka ŋandiinta a te wenzuk nuinsaŋa ale tɛŋzuk duŋsaŋa.

ref: These enemies are King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia and his army. They have stopped attacking Jerusalem, but they want to kill King Zedekiah and his high officials. So I will command them to return and attack again. This time they will conquer the city and burn it down, and they will capture Zedekiah and his officials. I will also let them destroy the towns of Judah, so that no one can live there any longer.
text: M boro ayen m te ka suik, Naawen ale weeni, abe m ta ba a ŋman jam tɛŋka de. Ba le kpaliŋ ale ka, a yik ka ale ju ka basi. Ate m yaa basi ate Juda tɛŋsaŋa a doa koruk nuru a kan baga a boro.>>

ref: “Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
text: <<Cheŋ Arekab dɔkdemma jigi a wi ba ate ba jam Naawen yenni nakpiak diinaŋa kunyi po a te ba daam ate ba nyu.>>

ref: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
text: Mi yaa cheŋ ayen m yik Jeremaya nidoabinni Jaazania ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Yabazzinia ale wa suataŋa ale wa nidoabilisaŋa meena, Arekab dɔkdemma meena.

ref: I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
text: Mi yaa ta ba jam Naawen yenni Igdalia Wen nuruwa nidoabinni Yanan nidoabilisaŋa dɔkku po. Ku jam pai saŋ ka kpaŋŋa dɔkku, kuui ale jam bo Sallum nidoabinni Maaseiya waai ale a nya nansuiŋku zuk la dɔkku ŋmai.

ref: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
text: Mi yaa pai taasa a zaani ate daam a sueri ale beerisa Arekab dɔkdemma nidoama niŋ a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni nyu daam.>>

ref: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
text: Alege ba a tulisi ayen, <<Tama a kan nyu daamoa, dii nyiŋla tama kokpieŋka Arekab nidoabinni Jonadab a te ti ka sinsaŋŋa de: <Ku a fɛ ate nama yaase ni ŋaaŋbisa a kan nyu daamoa.

ref: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
text: Ku a fɛ mɛ ate ni kan sɛ yie, ni bori abe ni vuk tiisa, ni kan maa ta ŋantaŋa de alege ku a fɛ ate ni bo viita po. Ni yaa le goa tɛŋka zuk beni juijui ate ni chim nicham la.>

ref: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
text: Alege Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar ale jo tuesi tɛŋka de la, tama weeni kama ayen, <Ni jam, ku a fɛ ate ti cheŋ Jerusalem ate ti bɛ ale Kaldiya tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale Araam tugurik tɔŋdɔma.> Dila tama yaa wari bo Jerusalem.>>

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson
text: <<Dii ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni la ale nna: Cheŋ a ga weeni Juda nuruma ale Jerusalem demma ayen, <Nama a kan zamsi wari a va mi wieŋa?> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
text: <Arekab nidoabinni Jonadab a weeni wa nidoabilisaŋa kama ayen ba kan nyu daamoa ate ba ta wanni de. A ta jam paari jinla ba an nyu daamoa, dii nyiŋla ba va ka ba kokpieŋka wanni. Alege mi biisi ale ni kama a tulim tulim, alege ni an wom mi nɔiya.

ref: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
text: Mi tom mi tomteerɔma biisiteerɔma kama a tulim tulim ni jigi. Ba weeni ayen, <<Waai meena a cheem basi wa gaasa suita abe wa tagri nyeela, ni kan va wen yona a tom te ŋa. Ate ni yaa le bo tɛŋ kaai po ate mi pai te ni ale ni koma la.>> Alege ni popola a ka mi jigi yaase ni wom mi.

ref: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
text: Arekab nidoabinni Jonadab ŋaaŋbisaŋa a ta ba kokpieŋka wanni ate wa te ba la kama, alege nuruma de an wom m nɔiya.>

ref: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
text: <<Dila, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni ayen, <Ni wom. Mi za ayen m ta ka kaasuŋ meena ate mi a mooli la a jam Juda ale waai meena ale bo Jerusalem la zuk. Mi jam biisi le ba kama alege ba an wom ya, a wi ba alege ba an tulisi ya.> >>

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
text: Jeremaya yaa weeni Arekab dɔkdemma ayen, <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <Ni wom ka ni kokpieŋka Jonadab ale weeni diila ale va wa sinsaŋŋa meena ale nye dii meena ate wa weeni la.>

ref: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
text: Josia nidoabinni Jeyoiakim Juda naawa naamu bena ŋanaansiwa po wanni de yaa nyini Naawen jigi a jam Jeremaya jigi:

ref: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
text: <<Pai gbaŋ a ŋmarisi wie ŋaai meena ate mi biisi a te fu a magsi chaab ale Izirali ale Juda ale tɛŋ yonsaŋa meena a zaani diipo ate mi piilim a biisi a te fu Josia naamu daaŋa po a jam paari yɔgyɔgla la a nyo ka po.

ref: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
text: Dai dii dai Juda nuruma a dan wom kaasuŋ meena ate mi zɔk ayen m ta jam ba zuk la, ba wanyi meena ale basi wa gaasa suiku, ate m vɔŋ ba gaasaŋa ale ba wabaataŋa a te ba.>>

ref: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
text: Dila Jeremaya a yaa wi Neria nidoabinni Baruk ate Jeremaya ale a biisi wie ŋaai meena ate Naawen a biisi a te wa la ate Baruk a ŋmarisi a nyo gbaŋ po.

ref: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
text: Jeremaya yaa jam weeni Baruk ayen, <<Ba kasi mi kama, mi an baga a cheŋ Naawen yenni.

ref: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
text: Dila cheŋ Naawen yenni nɔi bobika dai a kariŋ Naawen wieŋa gbaŋ po ate mi a biisi ate fi ŋmarisi la a te nuruma. Karim a te Juda nuruma meena ale nyini ba tɛŋsaŋa a jam la.

ref: The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
text: Dai dii dai ba le puusi a te Naawen ate ba waai meena a basi wa gaasa suik, diila Naawen ale mooli ale suipuurum buui a basi nuruma zuk la a zuak ka yega.>>

ref: Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said.
text: Gemaria nidoabinni Mikaiya ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Safan la ale wom Naawen wieŋa gbaŋka po la,

ref: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
text: wa deri siŋ gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa dɔkku po naawa yenni po, juijui ate kpaŋŋa meena a kala la, Elisama gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa ale Sɛmaiya nidoabinni Delaiya ale Achbor nidoabinni Elnatan ale Safan nidoabinni Gemaria ale Yanania nidoabinni Zedekia ale kpaga m ŋala meena.

ref: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
text: Mikaiya ale weeni dii meena ate wa wom Baruk ale kariŋ a te nuruma gbaŋka po la,

ref: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
text: Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Kali tɛŋ, ti a saalim kariŋ a te ti.>> Baruk yaa kariŋ a te ba.

ref: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
text: Ba le wom wieŋa de meena la, ba yaa nya chaab ale yɔgsum a weeni Baruk ayen, <<Ku a fɛ ate ti weeni wieŋa de meena a sak naawa.>>

ref: “Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
text: Baruk yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mm, wa le biisi wieŋa de meena a te mi, ate mi a ŋmarisi gbaŋka po.>>

ref: The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
text: Kpaŋŋa yaa weeni Baruk ayen, <<Fi ale Jeremaya, ni ga suk. Ni kan basi ate waai a seba ni ale bo juijui la.>>

ref: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
text: Naawa a goanti a te ka Jerameel naawa nidoabili ale Azriel nidoabinni Seraiya ale Abdeel nidoabinni Selemia suik ayen ba yik ŋmarisidoawa Baruk ale biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya. Alege Naawen a pai ba a suk.

ref: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
text: Naawa ale ju gbaŋka ate Jeremaya a biisi ate Baruk a ŋmarisi ka wieŋa la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Naawen wanni yaa jam Jeremaya jigi ayen,

ref: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
text: <<Pai gbaŋ ka choa a ŋmarisi ka po wie ŋaai meena ale liŋ bo niŋ gbaŋka ate Juda naawa Jeyoiakim a ju la.

ref: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
text: Weeni Juda naawa Jeyoiakim mɛ ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Fi ju gbaŋ kala kama ale weeni ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate fi ŋmarisi ayen Babilon naawa ale sum jam kaasi tɛŋka de abe wa gebi nuruba ale duŋsa a ta nyini ka po?>>

ref: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
text: Dila la Naawen ale weeni dii a magsi chaab ale Juda naawa Jeyoiakim la ale nna: Wa kan ta waai ate wa kali Deevid naam zukpaglika zuwa, ba le yuk wa nyiŋka a basi ate ka bo kantueŋka tuilukku po ale yokku maglimu po.

ref: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
text: M le namsi wa ale wa bisaŋa ale baai ale tom a te wa la ba gaasaŋa nyiŋ, m le ta kaasuŋ kuui meena ate mi a mooli la a jam ba zuk ale baai ale bo Jerusalem la ale Juda nuruma zuk, dii nyiŋla ba an wom ya.> >>

ref: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
text: Jeremaya yaa pai gbaŋ ka choa a te ŋmarisidoawa Neria nidoabinni Baruk, ate Jeremaya ale a biisi la Baruk a ŋmarisi ka po wa ŋaai dek ale jam bo kaai po ate Juda naawa Jeyoiakim a ju ale bolimu la. Ate wa ŋala chaab dek a maa gum du.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
text: Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar yaa bobi Josia nidoabinni Zedekia Juda naab a tagri Jeyoiakim nidoabinni Konia.

ref: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
text: Alege Zedekia yaase baai ale tom a te wa la yaase tɛŋka nuruma niŋ a bo wie ŋaai ate Naawen a biisi a ta va biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya jigi la.

ref: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
text: <<Dii ate Naawen, Izirali Wenni a weeni la ale nna: Weeni Juda naawa waai ale tom fu ayen fi bek mi la ayen, <Faaro tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale gɔk santinni a nyini ayen ba maari ni la ale pilim ŋmani badek tɛŋka Ejipiti.

ref: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
text: Kaldiya demma ale ŋman jam a siti tɛŋka de a yik ka a ju basi.>

ref: Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before.
text: <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Ni kan paasi nidega, a poli ayen, <Kaldiya demma a za ba sum basi ti kama.> Ba kan basi ni.

ref: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
text: Babilon tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai meena ale a siti la ba nuru baai ale kɔni la a dan poom tali bo ba viitaŋa po ba le nyini a ju tɛŋka de a basi.>>

ref: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
text: Babilon tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale basi Jerusalem Faaro tugurik tɔŋdɔma la ŋaaŋnyiŋ,

ref: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
text: Jeremaya yaa piilim a basi tɛŋka a cheŋ Benjamin tɛŋka ayen wa tuesi wa charuku nuruma jigi dula.

ref: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
text: Alege wa le paari Benjamin nansuiŋku la, limisidɔwa kpagni, ate wa yuei a chim Irija la Selemia nidoabinni ate wa kokpieŋ a chim Yanania la a yik wa ale weeni ayen, <<Fi basi kama ale a cheŋ Kaldiya demma jigi?>>

ref: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
text: Jeremaya yaa weeni ayen, <<Kula daa wensie. Mi an basi ale a cheŋ Kaldiya demma jigi ya.>> Alege Irija a kan wom wa, wa goanti yik Jeremaya kama a ta wa jam kpaŋŋa jigi.

ref: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
text: Naab Zedekia yaa tom ate ba ta wa jam naab yenni, juijui ate wa bek wadek wa nyiini ayen, <<Wari boro a nyini Naawen jigi ya?>> Jeremaya yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mm, ba le pai fu a te Babilon naawa.>>

ref: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
text: Jeremaya yaa weeni naab Zedekia ayen, <<Boan biem ate m tom a kaasi fu yaase fi kpaŋŋa yaase nuruma de, ate fi lik mu?

ref: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
text: Fi biisiteerɔma a bo ka bɛ? Baai ale mooli a te fu ayen, <Babilon naawa a kan siti fu yaase tɛŋka de la?>

ref: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
text: Alege yɔgyɔgla de, m nyɔnɔ naaba, mi a saalim wom de. Basi ate m saalim fu: Kan te ate m ŋman cheŋ gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Jonatan yenni dan kan daa di m le kpi dula.>>

ref: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
text: Naab Zedekia yaa te suik ate ba pai Jeremaya a basi limisidɔma dabiaka po ale a te wa boroborok a nyini seerɔma jigi ate boroborok tɛŋka po meena a nueri. Dila Jeremaya yaa jam wari ka limisidɔma dabiaka po.

ref: that the Lord had said, “If you stay here in Jerusalem, you will die in battle or from disease or hunger, and the Babylonian army will capture the city anyway. But if you surrender to the Babylonians, they will let you live.”
text: Naawen abe le weeni diila ale nna: <Tɛŋka de m le sum pai te Babilon naawa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ate ba yik ka.> >>

ref: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
text: Kpaŋŋa yaa weeni naawa ayen, <<Nuruwa de a magsi ka koka. Wa basi ate ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai ale tali bo tɛŋka po la a jɔk nyiŋbiiri ale nuruma meena ale wa le weeni wie ŋaai a te ba la. Nuruwa de a kan gisi nuruma de nalimmoa alege ka ba kaasuŋ.>>

ref: Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
text: Naab Zedekia yaa tulisi ayen, <<Wa bo ni nisima po. Naawa an baga a kasi ni.>>

ref: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
text: Dila ba yaa pai Jeremaya a nyo naawa nidoabinni Malkija vili po, dii ale jam bo limisidɔma dabiaka po la. Ba jam pai ka miisa a bobi wa a basi ate wa siŋ vinni po. Nyiam a jam ka di po, ka bagta nyiini, ate Jeremaya a siŋ bagtaŋa po.

ref: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
text: <<M nyɔnɔ naaba, nuruma de a tom ka gaasa tuima ale ba le nye biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya dii meena la. Ba le pai wa basi vinni po la ale basi kama ate wa viiri a kpi ase ŋandiinta a nin kan ŋman bo tɛŋka po.>>

ref: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
text: Dila Ebed Melek a yaali nidoama ate ba cheŋ dɔk ate ba a dueni ŋanta du naab yenni po la. Wa yaa pai garucha kpagsa ale garuk tii ale bugi a yaa basi ate ti siŋ Jeremaya jigi vinni po ale miisa.

ref: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
text: Kus denɔwa Ebed Melek a yaa weeni Jeremaya ayen, <<Pai garucha kpagsaŋa de ale garuk tii ale bugi la a su fi nisimaŋa de ate miisaŋa a kan te fu tuemoa.>> Ate Jeremaya a nye dila,

ref: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
text: ate ba dari wa ale miisaŋa a ta nyini vinni po a jueli. Ate Jeremaya a jam wari bo limisidɔwa dabiaka po.

ref: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
text: Naab Zedekia yaa tom ate ba ta biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya a jam nansuiŋ kuui ale saari buta wa a jo Naawen yenni po la. Naawa yaa weeni Jeremaya ayen, <<Mi a yaali ayen m bek fu ka wari. Kan suk wari ale mu.>>

ref: “Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
text: Jeremaya yaa weeni Zedekia ayen, <<M dan tulisi fu fi kan ko mu? M dan poom sak fu fi kan wom mu.>>

ref: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
text: Alege Zedekia a suk pɛ ale Jeremaya ayen, <<Naawen ale sum boro la nyiŋ, waai ale basi ate ti a vuusi la, m kan ko fu yaase m pai fu a te baai ale a gisi fi nyuvunni la.>>

ref: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
text: Jeremaya yaa weeni Zedekia ayen, <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni ayen, <Fi dan siak a te Babilon naawa kpaŋŋa, fi le nyini vum nyiŋ ate ba kan ju tɛŋka de, ate fi ale fi dɔkdemma ale boro.

ref: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
text: Alege fi dan kan siak a te Babilon naawa kpaŋŋa tɛŋka de, ale jo Kaldiya demma nisa po ate ba ju ka basi, fidek a kan yuli bɛ ba nisima po.> >>

ref: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
text: Naab Zedekia a weeni Jeremaya ayen, <<Mi a chali ka yɔgsum ale Juuma baai ale cheŋ Kaldiya demma jigi la, Kaldiya demma ale pai mu a te ba ate ba nye mu gaasa.>>

ref: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.

ref: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
text: Dila nyiŋ mi suipuurum yega wa mi yaa kpiiri ate bu de Juda tɛŋsaŋa ale Jerusalem suitaŋa a basi ate si doa guura. Si ka dila jinla.

ref: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
text: Ka boa ate ni nye ate m sui a puuri ale ni nisima ale nye ŋan baai la, a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te wen yona Ejipiti po, juijui ate ni jam boro la? Ni le kaasi nidek abe ba nye ni a la abe ba pai ni yuenni a nye kikaasa tɛŋsa meena po.

ref: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
text: Ni baŋ ni koma ale nye biem buui la kama ale nalimaŋa ale naab nipooma ale nye diila kama ale waba tii ate nama ale ni pooma a nye Juda tɛŋka po ale Jerusalem suitaŋa po la?

ref: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
text: A ta jam paari jinla ba an zaab ba dega yaase ba sak zula, yaase ba va m sinsaŋŋa ale m ŋmarisika ate mi a pai dueni nama ale ni koma niŋ la.

ref: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
text: M le pai Juda baai ale tali a pii nyiŋ ayen ba cheŋ Ejipiti a ga kali dula la a ta cheŋ. Ba meena ale kpi Ejipiti. Ba le ko ba ale gebik abe kɔm a ko ba. A zaani nuru fiisa a ga paari nuru kpienta gebik yaase kɔm ale ko ba. Ba le nye ba a la kama, abe ku cha nuruba ba le ka diila abe ba yuenni a chim kikaasa.

ref: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
text: M le namsi baai ale bo Ejipiti la ale gebik ale kɔm ale nyiŋtuila ase m le namsi Jerusalem diila.

ref: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
text: Juda baai ale tali a cheŋ Ejipiti ayen ba boro la waai a kan bɛ yaase wa vuuk a ŋmani Juda tɛŋka kaai ate ba a yaali ayen ba ŋmani a ga boro la, waai a kan ŋmani ka magdega.>>

ref: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
text: Nidoama meena baai ale jam seba ayen ba pooma a jam a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te wen yona ale nipok baai meena ale jam boro, tigsuŋ kpioŋ ale nuruma meena ale bo Ejipiti tɛŋka la Patros tɛŋka a weeni Jeremaya ayen,

ref: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
text: <<Ti kan wom bi kaai ate fi biisi te ti Naawen yuenni nyiŋla.

ref: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
text: Ti le sum nye dii meena ate ti weeni ayen ti le nye la: Ti le ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a te Wenŋmazuk Nipok Naawa abe ti kpiiri daam tiirita a te wa ase tama ale ti koma ale ti nalimaŋa ale ti kpaŋŋa ale nye dii Juda tɛŋsaŋa po ale Jerusalem suitaŋa po la. Dila po ti jam ta ka ŋandiinta yega a nya tidek an ŋman nam ya.

ref: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
text: Alege ti le din basi ŋan baai nyum ale masa Wenŋmazuk Nipok Naawa ju teka la ale daam tiirita kpiiri teka la, ti an nya jaaboa alege a kpi ale gebik ale kɔm.>>

ref: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
text: Nipooma a gum du ayen, <<Tama ale jam ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te Wenŋmazuk Nipok Naawa la ale kpiiri daam tiirita a te wa la, ti chorɔma a jam zɛ ayen ti jaa a nye ka maasa ase wadek la ale a kpiiri daam tiirita a te wa?>>

ref: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
text: <<Naawen an jam teeri ale poli ni koma ale ni nalimaŋa ale ni kpaŋŋa ale tɛŋka nuruma ale jam a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la Juda tɛŋsaŋa po ale Jerusalem suitaŋa po wari ya?

ref: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
text: Naawen ale kan ŋman baga a pik ni gaasa nyeelaŋa ale kisuk wieŋa ate ni nye la ate ni tɛŋka a chim kikaasa jaab ale doa kinla ate jaab a ka ka po ase jinla la.

ref: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
text: Ni le ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa ale tom kaasi Naawen la ale an wom wa nɔiya yaase ni va wa sinsaŋŋa yaase wa ŋmarisika yaase wa kaamka la nyiŋ kaasuŋku de a jam ni zuk ase ni ale a nya yɔgyɔgla de la.>>

ref: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: Nama ale ni pooma a sak ni nyeelaŋa po kama ni le puulim weeni dii ayen, <Ti le puulim dii ayen ti le ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa abe ti kpiiri daam tiirita a te Wenŋmazuk Nipok Naawa la ti le nye.> Ni nye a cheŋ, ni nye ni le puulim diila. Ni ta ni pumpuulimaŋa.

ref: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
text: Alege ni wom Naawen wanni, Juuma meena ale bo Ejipiti la: <Mi pɛ m yuei kpienni nyiŋ, Naawen ale weeni, ayen waai a ka Juda a bo Ejipiti juijui ya ale wi mi yuenni yaase wa pɛ, <<Ase Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale boro la.>>

ref: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
text: Mi a kpesi a nya ba kama biem nyiŋ daa nalimmoa, Juuma ale bo Ejipiti la ale kpi ale gebik ale kɔm ate ba meena a ga kpi nueri.

ref: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
text: Baai ale ba chali bɛ a nyini Ejipiti ŋmani Juda la a kan soa dii ya. Ate Juda baai ale tali la ale seba ase mi wanni ale di zaani yaase ka ba.

ref: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
text: << <Kude ale ku chim magsa a sak ayen m le namsi ni dela jigini,> Naawen ale weeni, <Ate ni seba ayen mi nyigsi ayen m nye ni biem la ale zaani.>

ref: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <M le pai Ejipiti naawa Faaro Yofra a te wa dachaasaŋa ale a gisi wa nyuvunni la, ase m le pai Juda naawa Zedekia a te Nebukadnezzar Babilon naawa, dacha kaai ale jam a gisi wa nyuvunni diila.> >>

ref: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
text: Biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya ale jam weeni Neria nidoabinni Baruk dii ate Josia nidoabinni Jeyoiakim Juda naawa bena ŋanaansiwa po ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate Jeremaya a weeni wieŋa ate Baruk a ŋmarisi nyo gbaŋka po la ale nna:

ref: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
text: <<Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale a weeni dii a te fi Baruk la ale nna:

ref: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
text: Fi weeni ayen, <Ku le tua a te mi! Naawen a gum ka suipuurum mi nyiŋdomma po, mi jiak kama ale ŋuunika a kan nya vuusummoa.> >>

ref: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
text: Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Weeni wa nna: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<M le yuk yiak mi ale sɛ jabuui la abe m voori mi ale vuk jabuui la tɛŋka meena.

ref: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Ni magsi ni gisi wakpiema a te ni dega? Ni kaa a gisi. M le ta kaasuŋ a jam nuruba meena zuk, alege juijui meena ate ni a cheŋ la ni le nyini vum nyiŋ. Naawen ale weeni.> >>

ref: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
text: Naawen wanni ale nna a jam biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya jigi a magsi chaab ale tɛŋsaŋa:

ref: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
text: A magsi chaab ale Ejipiti: Wa dii ate Naawen a ta chaab ale Ejipiti naawa Faaro Neko tugurik tɔŋdɔma baai ate Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar a jam nak ba de Karchemis po Yufiretis Benni zuk Josia nidoabinni Jeyoiakim Juda naawa bena ŋanaansiwa po la ale nna:

ref: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
text: <<Ni gomsi ni ŋanchɔgsintaŋa, ŋan fiisa ale ŋan kpienta a gɔk santiri a nyini kpaliŋ.

ref: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
text: Ni gomsi ni wusumaŋa abe ni do ŋa. Ni zaani ni zaana jigi abe ni vuk ni zuk chinaŋa. Ni soa ni gbattaŋa, abe ni jo ni kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa.

ref: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
text: <<Baai ale a nye mwuli la an baga a chali yaase pagrɔma a chali bɛ. Wiiluk geŋka Yufiretis Benni nɔi ba nak naŋsa a lo.

ref: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
text: <<Ka wana ale yiti a jueli nna ase Nile benni la, nna ase bela, ŋaai nyaata ale waaŋ a cheŋ la.

ref: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
text: Ejipiti a yiti a jueli ase Nile benni la, nna ase bela nyaata ale waaŋ a cheŋ la. Wa weeni ayen, <M le yiti a lik tɛŋzuk, m le kaasi tɛŋsa ale si nuruba.>

ref: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
text: Wusuma, ni te ni nyiŋsa a nyaanti. Damdɔba, ni dam ale suipuurum. Tugurik tɔŋdɔba, Kus ale Put nidoaba ale ji ŋanchɔgsintaŋa la, Liidiya nidoa baai ale yeeri ba tima la a gɔk santiri a cheŋ.

ref: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
text: Alege dai dila danni ka Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale soa tutuna dai, tutuna wa dachaasaŋa zuk. Gebika ale ko kama ate ka ga chak, ate ka ga ko ka nyanyuila kommu ale ziim. Dila Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale te kaabka wiiluk geŋka tɛŋka Yufiretis Benni nɔi.

ref: Egypt, no medicine can heal you, not even the soothing lotion from Gilead.
text: <<Ejipiti demma, ni cheŋ Gilead a ga yaali tiim. Ni tiitaŋa meena an sak jaaboa, jaab karo a tebi ni.

ref: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
text: Tɛŋsa a wom ni chivieŋa wari kama, waai meena a wom ni kumsa kama. Tugurik tɔŋdɔ m wa a nak naŋ a va m wa zuk, ba meena ale maa chaab a lo.>>

ref: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
text: <<Mooli kude Ejipiti po, abe fi mooli Migdol po, mooli ku mɛ Memfis ale Tayapanes po: <Ni zaani ni zaana jigi a gomsi magsi, diila gebika a ko ka baai ale gilim fu la.>

ref: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
text: Ka boa ate ni tugurik tɔŋdɔma a lo? Ba an baga a zaani, diila Naawen ale tusi ba lɔnsi.

ref: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
text: Ba le nak naŋsa a tulim, ba le lo chaab zuk. Ba le weeni ayen, <Yiti ni te ti ŋmani a cheŋ tidek nuruma jigi ale tidek tɛŋsaŋa, ate ti yalima ale namsidɔwa gebika.>

ref: Give the king of Egypt this new name, “Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
text: Dula jigini ba le weeni ayen, <Ejipiti naawa Faaro ka nuemka nyiini, wa jɔk wa suik kama.>

ref: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
text: Naawa ale weeni waai yuei ale Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ayen, <<Ase mi ale sum boro la waai ale jam a nye ase Tabor la guutaŋa suŋsuŋ, a nye ase Karmel guuku la nyakpiemu nɔi.

ref: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
text: Ni pai ni ŋantaŋa a magsi tɛŋ yoŋ chelim, nama baai ale bo Ejipiti la, diila Memfis ale doa kinla ale guura ate waai a kan boro.

ref: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
text: <<Ejipiti a nye ase ka naab buui ale nala la ate nanjuŋ kaai ale a dom la a nyini wiilukku geŋ a cheena ayen ka siti bu.

ref: The foreign soldiers you hired will turn and run. But they are doomed, like well-fed calves being led to the butcher. *
text: Ba tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai ate ba da la a nye ase ka naabi biitita la. Ba mɛ ale cheem a chali ale chaab, ba kan baga a chiib a zaani, diila kaasuŋku danni a cheen ka ba zuk, diipo ale magsi ba namsi ba.

ref: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
text: Ejipiti ale fuusi ase ka waab ale a chali la ase dachiaka ale a jueli ba zuk ale pagrim la, ba le jam ta chaab ale ka ale laasa, ase nidoaba ale a gebi tiisaŋa a lɔnsi la.

ref: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
text: Ba le gebi tiisaŋa a lɔnsi tɛŋ, ale si ale lik chaab la meena.>> Naawen ale weeni. Ba piisi kama a gaam tintue, ba ka chiina.

ref: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
text: <<Ejipiti demma ale jo chivie po, ba le pai ba a te wiiluk geŋ nuruma.>>

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni ayen, <<M za m ta ka namsika a jam Amon wenni zuk Tebes po ale Faaro ale Ejipiti ale ka wenaŋa ale ka nalimaŋa ale baai sebchakka ale bo Faaro zuk la.

ref: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
text: M le pai ba a te baai ale a gisi ba nyuvooŋa la, a te Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar ale wa kpaŋŋa. Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ nuruba ale kali Ejipiti ase ku nyiem ale ka diila.>> Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
text: <<Jekob m tomteerɔwa, kan chali yɔgsummoa, Izirali kan te ku a daani fu. M le vari fu niŋniŋ jigini a basi, fi ŋaaŋbisaŋa a nyini tɛŋ kaai ate ba yik ba ta cheŋ la. Jekob ale ŋman nya suiyɔgni ale ganika, ate waai a kan nye ate wa a chali yɔgsum.

ref: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Jekob mi tomteerɔwa, ka a chali yɔgsummoa, diila m bo le fu kama,>> Naawen ale weeni. <<M kaasi tɛŋ sii ate ni waaŋ bo si po la ka chessi, m kan kaasi nama chessi. M le waali ni alege mi a nye ale ka nyemagsika. M kan basi ni dila ale kan waali ni.>>

ref: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
text: Naawen wanni ale nna a jam biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya jigi a magsi chaab ale Filistia demma alege ate Faaro a siti Gaza.

ref: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
text: ase ba nin wom naŋsabaŋa ale a zi a kum la, dachaasaŋa torokoma ale wiilima nuemka. Koba a kan cheem maari ba bisa, ba nisima ale kpi ka nna limalima a yiga.

ref: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
text: Danni a jam kama ayen ba kaasi Filistia demma meena abe ba gebi baai meena ale vuuk a baga a maari Taaya ale Saidon la. Naawen a boro ayen wa kaasi Filistia demma kama, baai ale tali a bo Kaftor nyiamu nɔi la.

ref: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
text: Gaza ale chiiri wa zukku abe wa a kum, Askelon ale nye diki. Baai ale tali a bo peelimmu po la, ni le gebi nidek a basi a paari ka dimpo?

ref: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
text: << <Naawen gebiga,> fi a kaari kama. <Fi le ko a paari ka dimpo? Pilim jo fi fooku po, bo dula a vuusi.>

ref: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
text: Alege ka ka nye ka sɛ a vuusi, mi ale te ka tuima ayen ka tom la? Mi ale weeni ka ayen ka siti Askelon ale nuru baai ale bo nyiamu nɔi la.>>

ref: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
text: A magsi chaab ale Moab: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Ku le toa a te Nebo, diila ka le kaasi. Chivie ale yik Kiriataim abe ba yik ka, ka jigi pagrika ale kaasi ate chivie a yik ka.

ref: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
text: Moab kan ŋman nya pimpauk wa, Yesbon po nuruba ale zɔk ka lueta: <Ni jam ate ti kpeglim tɛŋ kala.> Fi mɛ, Madmen tɛŋka ale nye diki, gebika ale vi fu.

ref: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
text: Wom kumsaŋa a nyini Yoronaim, kaasuŋ ale biem kumsa.

ref: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
text: Moab ale wɛ, wa bisaŋa ale kaari.

ref: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
text: Ba cheŋ va ka suiku a jueli Luyit, a kum nna tuotuowa a cheŋ, suiku po a siŋ Yoronaim ka sui kaasuŋ kumsa kaasuŋ nyiŋ ate ba wom.

ref: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
text: <<Chali! Ni chali ni nyuvooŋa nyiŋ. Ni chali ase gɔi po bon waarik la.

ref: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
text: Ni le toalim ta sebchakka ale ka ni tuima ale ni jigsika la, nama mɛ ba le yik ni, ate Chemos wenni a cheŋ tɛŋ yoŋ ale ka kaabteerɔma ale kpaŋŋa.

ref: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
text: Kaasirɔwa ale jam ta chaab ale tɛŋ meena, ate tɛŋ yeŋ mɛ la a kan yuli bɛ. Viaka ale kaasi ate peelimmu a kaasi dii nyiŋla Naawen ale biisi.

ref: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
text: Pai yesa a nyo Moab zuk, diila ka le doa kinla, ka tɛŋsaŋa ale doa koruk ate waai a kan bo si po.

ref: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
text: <<Kikaasa a bo waai ale kaa yaali ayen wa tom a te Naawen la zuk. Kikaasa a bo waai ale a peri wa gebik ayen ka kan te ziim a nyini la zuk.

ref: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
text: Chivie ale yik Moab Chemos wenni nyiŋ ase Izirali yenni ate chivie a jam yik ba ba le mariŋ Betel la.

ref: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
text: <<Ni le nye ka sɛ ayen, <Tama ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba, nuru tuasa kpaliŋ po?>

ref: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
text: Moab ale kaasi ate ka tɛŋsaŋa ba tuesi, ka nidoa paaluk naliŋsaŋa ale cheŋ tɔgrika jigi.>> Naawa ale weeni waai yuei ale Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La.

ref: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
text: <<Moab luetaŋa a moata kama, ka kaasuŋku ale jam mwuli.

ref: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
text: Kum te ka, baai meena ale gilim ka la, baai meena ale seba wa yuenni la, weeni ayen, <Tachek kpieŋka ale wɛ dii, zula tachekka ale wɛ dii!>

ref: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
text: <<Nyini fi zulaŋa jigini a siŋ a kali tɛŋ kosik tuilikka po, nama Dibon demma, diila waai ale a kaasi Moab la ale jam ta chaab ale ni a kaasi ni tɛŋ pagrisaŋa.

ref: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
