ref: After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month,
text: Chiisa sinaansiwa po, daa neokku po, kɔmmu a jam pagra kama tɛŋ nummu po nna yegayega ate ŋandiinta karo ate nuruma a dɛ.

ref: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the Jordan River valley,
text: Ba yaa wɛ tɛŋ nummu parika a jo ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena a yiri chali. Ba jam basi tɛŋ nummu ka yokku a va nansuiŋku parisa siyewa suŋsuŋ a moata naawa kadukka, Babilon demma ale gilim tɛŋ nummu la po a nyini. Ba jam chali kama a duŋ Araba,

ref: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
text: ate ba jam yik wa. Ba jam ta wa cheŋ ka Babilon naawa jigi Aribla ale bo Yamat tɛŋka la, ate ba mooli ba le ba nye wa diila.

ref: Zedekiah's sons and the officials of Judah were killed while he watched,
text: Aribla po ate Babilon naawa a tɔgri Zedekia nidoabilisaŋa wa nimbie. Wa jam ko Juda kpaŋŋa mɛ kama.

ref: Jerusalem was captured during Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king of Babylonia. About a month later, Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guards arrived in Jerusalem. His name was Nebuzaradan,
text: Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar naamu bena pi ale neokku po chiisa sinuwa po ka daa piika danni Nebuzaradan tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni waai ale tom a te Babilon naawa la, yaa jam Jerusalem.

ref: and he burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses.
text: Wa yaa jam ju Naawen yenni ale naawa yenni ale Jerusalem yieŋa meena. Tuilum yeri meena wa jam ju basi kama.

ref: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
text: Babilon tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena ate kpagni Nebuzaradan a jam a nya ba zuk la a jam wɛ parisaŋa meena ale gilim Jerusalem la kama.

ref: He led away the people left in the city, including everyone who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar, the rest of the skilled workers, and even some of the poor people of Judah.
text: Kpagni Nebuzaradan a jam ji ŋanjaksaŋa gela kama ale baai ale tali tɛŋ nummu po la, a maa gum baai ale ka yɔgdɔba la ale baai ale dɛ niŋ a cheŋ Babilon naawa jigi la.

ref: Only the very poorest were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
text: Alege kpagni Nebuzaradan a jam basi ka ŋanjaksaŋa gela ŋaaŋ ayen ba a tom kaduksaŋa ale tattaŋa po.

ref: Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
text: Wa yaa jam biisi jiirim biik ale wa ale te wa zula zukpaglik a gaam nalima m ŋala ale jam bo le wa Babilon la.

ref: Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day.
text: Dila Jeyoiachin yaa yeeri wa likka gattaŋa a dueni nakpiak alege ate wa boka po meena wa a dɛ ale naawa.

ref: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
text: Daa meena Babilon naawa a jam a tuni Jeyoiachin kama wa boka po ga paari wa kum dai.

ref: Jerusalem, once so crowded, lies deserted and lonely. This city that was known all over the world is now like a widow. This queen of the nations has been made a slave.
text: Jerusalem tɛŋka jam ka nuruba nyiini, alege yɔgyɔgla de ka ka tɛŋ koruk. Ka jam ka tɛŋ kpieŋ tɛŋsaŋa meena po, alege yɔgyɔgla de ka a nye ase ka pukɔgi la. Ka jam a nye ase ka tɛŋsaŋa meena nipok naab la, alege yɔgyɔgla de ka ka yɔma.

ref: Each night, bitter tears flood her cheeks. None of her former lovers are there to offer comfort; her friends have betrayed her and are now her enemies.
text: Ka kasim a kaari yok kama ate ku a jueli ate ninyaata a kpiiri a siŋ. Waai karo a basi ate ka sui a yɔgi, baai meena ale a yaali ka a cheŋ ferr. Ka doama meena a cheem kisi ka, a chim ka dachaasa.

ref: The people of Judah are slaves, suffering in a foreign land, with no rest from sorrow. Their enemies captured them and were terribly cruel.
text: Juda a jo ka yɔntidi po, a yaa nam ale a tom nna yegayega. Ka yaa bo ka tɛŋ yonsa po, alege kan nya vuusummoa. Baai ale a vi ka la a yikka kama ka le jam bo daanika po la.

ref: The roads to Zion mourn because no one travels there to celebrate the festivals. The city gates are deserted; priests are weeping. Young women are raped; Zion is in sorrow!
text: Sui tii ale a cheŋ Zayon la a doa ka nna dikdik, diila nuru an cheen tiŋŋa. Waai an va tuataŋa a jo. Ka kaabteerɔma a nam, nipok paalisaŋa a nam ate Jerusalem kasim a nam nna yegayega.

ref: Enemies now rule the city and live as they please. The Lord has punished Jerusalem because of her awful sins; he has let her people be dragged away.
text: Ka dachaasaŋa a yaa chim ka ka kpaga. Ka dachaasaŋa yaa a dɛ ka masim ale jigsika. Naawen ale a namsi ka, ka wabaataŋa ale piisi la nyiŋ. Ka bisaŋa a yaa cheŋ kama ase dachaasa yɔm la.

ref: Zion's glory has disappeared. Her leaders are like deer that cannot find pasture; they are hunted down till their strength is gone.
text: Zayon nalimu a muriŋ bɛ kama. Ka kpaŋŋa a nye ase ka kabsa ale kan nya ŋandiinta la. Ba wobsa kama a yaa chali bɛ alege yaalɔma.

ref: Her people recall the good life that once was theirs; now they suffer and are scattered. No one was there to protect them from their enemies who sneered when their city was taken.
text: Jerusalem kasim a nam kama a ka goom jigi ya. Ka yaa teeri nyiemwa ŋanmaŋsaŋa meena. Alege dachaasaŋa a nak dɛ ka nuruma meena, ate waai karo a maari ka. Ka dachaasaŋa ale nye ka la, ba yaa la kaasuŋ kuui meena ale nye la.

ref: Jerusalem's horrible sins have made the city a joke. Those who once admired her now hate her instead— she has been disgraced; she groans and turns away.
text: Jerusalem demma a tom kaasi ka yega, a yaa daŋ badek. Baai ale jam a zuli ba la, yaa kisi ba kama, diila ba nya ba chaboala kama. Ka yaa kaari a chali bɛ.

ref: Her sins had made her filthy, but she wasn't worried about what could happen. And when Jerusalem fell, it was so tragic. No one gave her comfort when she cried out, “Help! I'm in trouble, Lord! The enemy has won.”
text: Ka daŋ kadek kama ale ka wabaataŋa alege an poli dii ale di nye ka la. Ba le nak yik ka la a cha ka kama, waai be karo a nye ate ka sui a yɔgi. Ka yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen yaa, nya ti le a nam diila, dii nyiŋla dachaasaŋa a nak dɛ kama.>>

ref: Zion's treasures were stolen. Jerusalem saw foreigners enter her place of worship, though the Lord had forbidden them to belong to his people.
text: Dachaasaŋa a pai ka ŋanmaŋsaŋa meena. Ka nya nicham mɛ a jo ka puusaŋa yenni po. Naawen ale weeni ayen nicham kan maara jo ka nuruma tuka jigini.

ref: Everyone in the city groans while searching for food; they trade their valuables for barely enough scraps to stay alive. Jerusalem Speaks: Jerusalem shouts to the Lord, “Please look and see how miserable I am!”
text: Jerusalem nuruma meena a yaa kaari a gisi ŋandiinta. A pai ba ŋanmaŋsa meena a gerim a yaali ŋandiinta ate ba baga nyini vum nyiŋ. Tɛŋka yaa weeni ayen, <<Nya, Naawen yaa, nya. Ba kisi ti kama.>>

ref: No passerby even cares. Why doesn't someone notice my terrible sufferings? You were fiercely angry, Lord, and you punished me worst of all.
text: <<Nama ale va suiku a taam niŋ karo. Ni jam nya mi. Nyiŋdomma boro a nye ase tama nyiŋdommaŋa la? Ninam boro a magsi buui ate Naawen a basi ate bu jam tama jigi la? Naawen a namsi tama kama wa suipuurumu danni.

ref: From heaven you sent a fire that burned in my bones; you set a trap for my feet and made me turn back. All day long you leave me in shock from constant pain.
text: Wa basi ate ka bolim a nyini wenŋmazuk a siŋ jam jo m kobaŋa po. Wa pati ka ŋmiak a yik m naŋsaŋa, a yaa yik mu viriŋ ŋaaŋnyiŋ. Wa basi kama ate m sui kaasi ate m wobsa danni meena.

ref: You have tied my sins around my neck, and they weigh so heavily that my strength is gone. You have put me in the power of enemies too strong for me.
text: Wa miŋ m wabaataŋa kama, ti bobi maŋ ka wa nisimaŋa nyiŋ, ti yik ka m ŋiri po. Wa basi kama ate m pagrimu a chim wobsim. Nyɔnɔwa a pai mu kama a te baai ale pagra a gaam mu.

ref: You, Lord, have turned back my warriors and crushed my young heroes. Judah was a woman untouched, but you let her be trampled like grapes in a wine pit.
text: Nyɔnɔwa a zɛri mi nuru pagrisaŋa meena ate parisaŋa a gilim ba la kama. Wa ta ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba jam mi po ayen ba kaasi mi nidoa paalukku. Nyɔnɔwa a kaasi Juda tɛŋ kpieŋka kama ase ba ale a ŋmiak yɔna a nye daam diila.

ref: Because of this, I mourn, and tears flood my eyes. No one is here to comfort or to encourage me; we have lost the war— my people are suffering. The Prophet Speaks:
text: Ate mi kum wieŋa de nyiŋ ate ninyaata sueri m ninaŋa a siŋ. Waai karo moata a basi ate m sui a yɔgi. Waai karo a te mu pagrim ŋmana. A basi m bisaŋa ate ba sue kaasi ate ba nye nna diki dii nyiŋla dachaasaŋa a nak dɛ kama.

ref: Zion reaches out her hands, but no one offers comfort. The Lord has turned the neighboring nations against Jacob's descendants. Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag to her neighbors. Jerusalem Speaks:
text: Zayon a yaa laari nisa alege waai karo basi ate wa sui a yɔgi. Naawen yaa te suik ayen Jekob ale wa nuruma dachaasa a gilim ba. Jerusalem yɔgyɔgla de yaa daŋ kama baai ale gilim ba la jigi.

ref: The Lord was right, but I refused to obey him. Now I ask all of you to look at my sufferings— even my young people have been dragged away.
text: <<Naawen a ta wensie, alege tama zɛri an wom wa nɔiya. Ni meena wom abe ni nya ti ninammu. Ti nipok paalukku ale nidoama a jo yɔntidi po.

ref: I called out to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and my leaders died while searching the city for scraps of food.
text: Ti kaari wi ti doama alege ba zɛri. Ti kaabteerɔma ale nisɔmma ale boro a gisi ŋandiinta yen ba nyini vum nyiŋla a kpi kama tɛŋka po.

ref: Won't you look and see how upset I am, our Lord? My stomach is in knots, and my heart is broken because I betrayed you. In the streets and at home, my people are slaughtered.
text: <<Naawen yaa, nya ti geŋ. Ti sueŋa kaasi kama. Ti suiniimaŋa a daani ti, dii nyiŋla ti tueŋa a kpari kama. Suitaŋa niŋ ba a ko nuruma ale gebisaŋa ka dila. Yieŋa po kummu kasim a vaasi ka dila.

ref: Everyone heard my groaning, but no one offered comfort. My enemies know of the trouble that you have brought on me, and it makes them glad. Hurry and punish them, as you have promised.
text: Nuruba a wom ti kumsa kama, alege waai karo a yɔk ti sue. Ti dachaasaŋa meena a wom ti daanika kama, alege ba sue peenti fi le nye ti dila la nyiŋ. Yɔgyɔgla de da dii ate fi mooli weeni di wari la, basi ate di jam ate ti dachaasaŋa a nye ase tama mɛ la.

ref: Don't let their evil deeds escape your sight. Punish them as much as you have punished me because of my sins. I never stop groaning— I've lost all hope!
text: <<Bi nya ba biemu. Fi le nye tama dii ti wabaataŋa nyiŋla, nye ba mɛ dila dek. M ninammu zuak kama, ate yɔgsum yaa ta mu.>>

ref: The Lord was angry! So he disgraced Zion though it was Israel's pride and his own place of rest. In his anger he threw Zion down from heaven to earth.
text: Nya Nyɔnɔwa ale wa suipuurumu ale basi ate Jerusalem a jo chivie po diila! Wa pai Izirali ale ba zuaka meena a zaani ka Wenzuk a yuk basi tɛŋ, wa an teeri wa Yenni ale ka wa naŋsa tabika jigi la wari ya.

ref: The Lord had no mercy! He destroyed the homes of Jacob's descendants. In his anger he tore down every walled city in Judah; he toppled the nation together with its leaders, leaving them in shame.
text: Nyɔnɔwa a kaasi Jekob nuruma yeeŋa meena alege an sak jiirimmoa. Wa kaasi Juda jigi pagrisaŋa meena ale suipuurum. Wa yuk ba tɛŋka ale ka nalimaŋa a lɔnsi tɛŋ ate ba an nya zula.

ref: The Lord was so furiously angry that he wiped out the whole army of Israel by not supporting them when the enemy attacked. He was like a raging fire that swallowed up the descendants of Jacob.
text: Wa yeeri Izirali pagrimu meena ale suipuurum. Wa yeeri Izirali pagrimu diipo ate ba dachaasaŋa a jam la. Wa dɛ Jekob nuruma nna se bolim ŋiak ale dɛ jaabuuri meena ale gilim bu diila.

ref: He attacked like an enemy with a bow and arrows, killing our loved ones. He has burned to the ground the homes on Mount Zion.
text: Ase dachiak la, wa gomsi kama ayen wa tɔŋ wa Penni, ale zak wa nisa ayen wa nye le ti. Ase dachiak la, Wa ko nuru naliŋsaŋa meena, ale kpiiri wa suipuurumu ase bolim la a basi Jerusalem yeeŋa zuk.

ref: The Lord was like an enemy! He left Israel in ruins with its palaces and fortresses destroyed, and with everyone in Judah moaning and weeping.
text: Nyɔnɔwa a jam a nye ase ka dachiak la, a kaasi Izirali. Wa kaasi nalimaŋa yeeŋa meena ale kaasi jigi pagrisaŋa meena. Wa basi ate Juda a kasim a fɔbili ale a kum nna yegayega.

ref: He shattered his temple like a hut in a garden; he completely wiped out his meeting place, and did away with festivals and Sabbaths in the city of Zion. In his fierce anger he rejected our king and priests.
text: Nyɔnɔwa kaasi wa Yenni pari pagrisaŋa nna chaalima ale kaasi tuka jigini mɛ. Naawen a basi kama ate Zayon a baŋ ba tiŋŋa ale ba Vuusum daaŋa wie. Wa zɛri naawa ale kaabteerɔwa ale suipuurum.

ref: The Lord abandoned his altar and his temple; he let Zion's enemies capture her fortresses. Noisy shouts were heard from the temple, as if it were a time of celebration.
text: Nyɔnɔwa a zɛri wa kuŋkuŋku ale basi wa Yenni. Wa pai Jerusalem parisaŋa ale naamu yeeŋa a te dachaasaŋa. Ba nuemka Naawen Yenni po a nye ase ka tigi dai la.

ref: The Lord had decided to tear down the walls of Zion stone by stone. So he started destroying and did not stop until walls and fortresses mourned and trembled.
text: Naawen yaa gomsi ayen wa kaasi parika ale gilim Zayon Liewa la. Wa magsi parika kama alege an basi ka kaasi ka. A basi ate niniga a yik parisaŋa ale ŋan kasintaŋa ate ba meena a lo tɛŋ.

ref: Zion's gates have fallen facedown on the ground; the bars that locked the gates are smashed to pieces. Her king and royal family are prisoners in foreign lands. Her priests don't teach, and her prophets don't have a message from the Lord.
text: Jerusalem nansuiŋtaŋa a lo ka tɛŋ. Wa kaasi nansuiŋtaŋa da kpientaŋa. Ka naawa le wa bisaŋa maa bo ka tɛŋ yonsa po. Ba basi Naawen wieŋa sakka, ate biisiteerɔma a kan ŋmaa nya wie Naawen jigi ya.

ref: Zion's leaders are silent. They just sit on the ground, tossing dirt on their heads and wearing sackcloth. Her young women can do nothing but stare at the ground.
text: Zayon kpaŋŋa nisɔmma a kali ka tɛŋ nna diki. Ba vaari ka tanta basi ba zuima ayen ba sak ba sue ale kaasi la. Jerusalem nipok paalukku a pai ka ba zuima su tɛŋ ale suipuurum.

ref: My eyes are red from crying, my stomach is in knots, and I feel sick all over. My people are being wiped out, and children lie helpless in the streets of the city.
text: Mi nina ŋman ka ninyiam ate m poi mɛ yɔk ate maa yuak. Ku a nye m jigi ase m ka nuru koruk la, dii nyiŋla ba kaasi m nuruma ka meena. Bisa ale buluata a cha tɛŋka suitaŋa niŋ.

ref: A child begs its mother for food and drink, then blacks out like a wounded soldier lying in the street. The child slowly dies in its mother's arms.
text: Ate ba a bek ba mama, <<Ŋandiintaŋa ale daamu bie?>> Ba kasim a cha kama ase tugurik tɔŋdɔba ale nya tuem tɛŋka suita niŋ la, a kpi ba mama nisa po.

ref: Zion, how can I comfort you? How great is your pain? Lovely city of Jerusalem, how can I heal your wounds, gaping as wide as the sea?
text: M le biisi Jerusalem wie ayen ka boa? Jerusalem Liewa, m le pai ni magsi ka boa? M le weeni ayen ni a nye ase ka boan la? M le nye ka sɛ ate ni sue yɔgi, Zayon Liewa? Ni kaasuŋku a limisa ase ka nyakpiemu la. Waai an baga a tebi ni.

ref: Your prophets deceived you with false visions and lying messages— they should have warned you to leave your sins and be saved from disaster.
text: Ni biisiteerɔma a nya wie kama, alege ŋa ka venta wie a ka kiri ya. Ba an weeni ni wabaataŋa a sak ni ate ba kan baga a yik ni. Ba mooli ka venta wie a basi ate ni cheŋ bɛ.

ref: Those who pass by shake their heads and sneer as they make fun and shout, “What a lovely city you were, the happiest on earth, but look at you now!”
text: Baai meena ale va suiku a taam la a nak nichaala, a nye Jerusalem Liewa a la ale a girinti ba zuima. Ba a bek ayen, <<Ka tɛŋ kaai ate nuruba a wi ayen tɛŋ naliŋ la ale nna, juijui ale ka suipeentik jigi tɛŋzuk la?>>

ref: Zion, your enemies curse you and snarl like wild animals, while shouting, “This is the day we've waited for! At last, we've got you!”
text: Ni dachaasaŋa meena a lak ka nɔi a biisi a kaasi ni. Ba nye ni a la ale a ŋɔbi nyina ale suipuurum. Ba a weeni ayen, Ba kaasi ni meena. Ti daam ale a limisi da diila ale nna. Ti nya ku nye ka kama.

ref: The Lord has done everything that he had planned and threatened long ago. He destroyed you without mercy and let your enemies boast about their powerful forces.
text: Naawen a nye dii ate wa gomsi ayen wa nye la kama. Wa dii ate wa puulim dipo la wa ta di kama. Wa kaasi ni alege an sak jiirimmoa, ale basi ate ni dachaasaŋa a la ni. Wa te ni dachaasaŋa pagrim.

ref: Zion, deep in your heart you cried out to the Lord. Now let your tears overflow your walls day and night. Don't ever lose hope or let your tears stop.
text: Nuruma kaari weeni Nyɔnɔwa, Zayon parika, basi ate fi ninyaataŋa a chali a siŋ ase beli nyiam la yok ale kantueŋ. Kan basi kumsa yaase fi ninyiamu gebiri.

ref: Get up and pray for help all through the night. Pour out your feelings to the Lord, as you would pour water out of a jug. Beg him to save your people, who are starving to death at every street crossing. Jerusalem Speaks:
text: Yiti ŋmai, a kum yokku, ale ku le diem a piilim sobika la. Lak fi suinummu a kpiiri ni puusaŋa ase nyiam la a te Nyɔnɔwa. Zak nisa a puusi a te wa ni bisaŋa nyuvooŋa nyiŋ. Kommu a viiri ba kama suitaŋa meena gugorutaŋa po.

ref: Think about it, Lord! Have you ever been this cruel to anyone before? Is it right for mothers to eat their children, or for priests and prophets to be killed in your temple?
text: <<Naawen yaa, nya baai ate fi nye ba nna la. Nipooba a ŋɔbi biik sii ate ba nam nya ba zuk la. Ba a ko kaabteerɔ ale biisiteerɔ Nyɔnɔwa yenni po?

ref: My people, both young and old, lie dead in the streets. Because you were angry, my young men and women were brutally slaughtered.
text: Nuruba, bisa ale ŋankpagsa a doa ka tɛŋ peelim. Ba ko nipok paalukku ale nidoa paalukku ale gebisa. Fi ko ba kama fi suipuurumu danni alege m bola sak jiirimmoa.

ref: When you were angry, Lord, you invited my enemies like guests for a party. No one survived that day; enemies killed my children, my own little ones.
text: Fi wi ka dachaasa ayen ba nyini jigi meena a jam nye ale ti ase fi wi ba ayen ba jam ka tigi. Nuru waai an chali bɛ ya, yaase waai tali vua Naawen suipuurumu danni. Ti dachaasaŋa a ko baai ate ti nya ba ate ba pak la.

ref: He chased me into a dark place, where no light could enter.
text: Wa ta mu jo legi po, daa juijui ale a nya.

ref: I am the only one he punishes over and over again, without ever stopping.
text: Wa teeri ka nisa a kasim ta chaab ale mu daa meena.

ref: God caused my skin and flesh to waste away, and he crushed my bones.
text: Wa basi kama ate m nyiŋka buk ate m koba a nye nna ase ŋa wɛ la.

ref: He attacked and surrounded me with hardships and trouble;
text: Wa wi mu kama ale sui kaasuŋ a ta chaab ale mu ale suipuurum.

ref: he forced me to sit in the dark like someone long dead.
text: Naawen basi kama ate m kali legi po ase baai ale kpi dipo dipo la.

ref: God built a fence around me that I cannot climb over, and he chained me down.
text: Wa lik mu kama tapi ate mi an baga a nyini, ale pai chɔrin kpiema a vi m zuk.

ref: Even when I shouted and prayed for help, he refused to listen.
text: Ate mi a kaari a saalim a yaali maarika, alege wa zɛri m puusaŋa.

ref: God put big rocks in my way and made me follow a crooked path.
text: Wa lik m suiku ale ka tintana parik ate m va suik kuui ale kan magsi la.

ref: God was like a bear or a lion waiting in ambush for me;
text: Naawen a nye ase ka piuk ale gomsi ku yik mu la, nna ase gbeŋli ale suk doa a limisi mu la.

ref: he dragged me from the road, then tore me to shreds.
text: Wa ta mu va ka suik kaasuŋku ate m bɛ ate wa yaa basi mu m ka maarɔ.

ref: God took careful aim and shot his arrows
text: Wa gomsi kama ayen wa tɔŋ wa tommu. Wa tuk wa peeŋa ka m nyiŋ.

ref: I am a joke to everyone— no one ever stops making fun of me.
text: Mi yaa chim laata a te nuruma. Ate ba a yi yiila a nye mu a la daaŋa meena.

ref: He made me eat gravel and rubbed me in the dirt.
text: Wa voori m nyina ale ziŋa ale tabi mu a feri daŋta po.

ref: I tell myself, “I am finished! I can't count on the Lord to do anything for me.”
text: Mi yaa weeni ayen, <<M pagrimu a cheŋ ya, ate m ŋman ka yiila ale Naawen.>>

ref: Just thinking of my troubles and my lonely wandering makes me miserable.
text: Mi a teeri m ninammu ale m niniŋŋa ale m suipuurumu ale daanika.

ref: That's all I ever think about, and I am depressed.
text: Mi a saalim teeri m wie abe fi poli m wie.

ref: Then I remember something that fills me with hope.
text: Alege m ta yiila kama ase m nin poli nna.

ref: The Lord's kindness never fails! If he had not been merciful, we would have been destroyed.
text: Naawen ŋmanteka kan kpegli, wa jiirimu mɛ kan kpegli.

ref: The Lord can always be trusted to show mercy each morning.
text: Ŋa ka wa paala saluik meena. Fi wensieŋa zuak ka yega.

ref: Deep in my heart I say, “The Lord is all I need; I can depend on him!”
text: Mi yaa weeni m dek ayen, <<Naawen ka mi ale soa, m ta yiila ale wa.

ref: The Lord is kind to everyone who trusts and obeys him.
text: Naawen a nala te baai yiila ale bo ale wa ale a gisi wa la.

ref: It is good to wait patiently for the Lord to save us.
text: Ku nala kama ale fi le nye nna chim a limisi ate Naawen a vari fu basi.

ref: When we are young, it is good to struggle hard
text: Ku nala kama ate nuru a dan diem paala wa a tom nalimnyiini.

ref: and to sit silently alone, if this is what the Lord intends.
text: Wa kali tɛŋ nna chim, Naawen a te wa ka tuim pagra ayen wa tom.

ref: Being rubbed in the dirt can teach us a lesson;
text: Wa koori tɛŋ, da di dai yiila diem boro.

ref: we can also learn from insults and hard knocks.
text: Wa basi ate waai a fɔbi wa tapiaka. Wa basi ate chivie yik wa.

ref: The Lord won't always reject us!
text: Nyɔnɔwa a kan zɛri wa nuruma taam wuu.

ref: He causes a lot of suffering, but he also has pity because of his great love.
text: Wa dan poom ta suipuurum jam ni jigi, wa ta jiirim ale ŋmanteka kama.

ref: The Lord doesn't enjoy sending grief or pain.
text: Wa kan yaali nuruba namsika yaase wa nye ate ba sue a kaasi.

ref: or cheat anyone out of what is rightfully theirs. God Most High sees everything,
text: Wa a nya kama ase ba nin kan nye waai a magsi wa Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La niŋŋa.

ref: and he knows when you refuse to give someone a fair trial.
text: Nyɔnɔwa a nya kama ase waai a nin ta wensie alege ate ba bo mini wa biisa dɔkku.

ref: No one can do anything without the Lord's approval.
text: Nuru karo a biisi ate wari a nye se ka Nyɔnɔwa a nin te suik.

ref: Good and bad each happen at the command of God Most High.
text: Wabaata ale wamaŋsa meena ka Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La ale te suik ate ŋa a jam.

ref: We're still alive! We shouldn't complain when we are being punished for our sins.
text: Wa dan namsi waai wa wabaata nyiŋ wa kan fɔbili.

ref: Instead, we should think about the way we are living, and turn back to the Lord.
text: Ni basi ate ti kpesi nya ti le tom diila abe ti ŋman jam Naawen jigi.

ref: When we lift our hands in prayer to God in heaven, we should offer him our hearts and say,
text: Ni te ti zak nisa wen a puusi a nyini ti suiniima po a te Wen dii ale bo wenŋmazuk la.

ref: “We've sinned! We've rebelled against you, and you haven't forgiven us!
text: Ti tom ka wabaata ale kisi fu ate fi an vɔŋ a te ti.

ref: Anger is written all over you, as you pursue and slaughter us without showing pity.
text: Fi din lik fidek ale ka suipuurum a vi ti. A ko ti alege an sak jiirim ale ti.

ref: You are behind a wall of clouds that blocks out our prayers.
text: Fi din lik fidek ale ka chiŋmari ate ti puusa an baga a paari fu.

ref: You allowed nations to treat us like garbage;
text: Fi nye kama ate tama ŋman ka kiri tɛŋ yonsa po.

ref: We are terrified and trapped, caught and crushed.”
text: Yɔgsum yaa le yik ti, kaasuŋ yega a paari ti.

ref: My people are destroyed! Tears flood my eyes,
text: M ninyaata kasim a siŋ, dii nyiŋla fi kaasi m nuruma kama.

ref: until the Lord looks down from heaven and helps.
text: se ka Naawen wenŋmazuk po a nin chui nya.

ref: I am horrified when I see what enemies have done to the young women of our city.
text: M sui kaasi ka yega m ni nya dii ale nye tɛŋka nipok paalukku la.

ref: No one had reason to hate me, but I was hunted down like a bird.
text: Baai ale ka mi dachaasa alege daa wari nyiŋla a va mu kama ase nuim la.

ref: Then they tried to kill me by tossing me into a pit and throwing stones at me.
text: Ba pai mu nyo goluk po a pai tana a lɔnsi m zuk.

ref: Water covered my head— I thought I was gone.
text: Ate nyiam chali va mi zuk, ti mi yen mi za m kpi kama!

ref: From the bottom of the pit, I prayed to you, Lord.
text: Naawen yaa, mi kaari wi fu golukku po.

ref: I begged you to listen. “Help!” I shouted. “Save me!” You answered my prayer
text: Fi wom mi le a wi la. Kan lik fi tueŋa abe fi zɛri m kaari wi ka.

ref: and came when I was in need. You told me, “Don't worry!”
text: Fi jam moata m le wi la, ate fi yaa weeni ayen, <<Kaa chali yɔgsummoa.>>

ref: You rescued me and saved my life.
text: Nyɔnɔ, fi nya m wanni zuk kama, fi da tuesi m nyuvunni kama.

ref: You know every plot they have made against me.
text: Fi nya m dachaasaŋa ale zɔk dii dueni a te mu la kama.

ref: Yes, you know their insults and their evil plans.
text: Naawen yaa, fi wom ba leetaŋa ale ba le zɔk biem buui a te mu la kama.

ref: All day long they attack with words and whispers.
text: M dachaasaŋa a kasim za ka mi ka zaka ale ba wie ale ba popola.

ref: No matter what they are doing, they keep on mocking me.
text: Nya, wari meena ti ba a nye la, ba a yi ka yiila a nye mu a la.

ref: Pay them back for everything they have done, Lord!
text: Biem buui meena ate ba tom la. Naawen yaa, tuni ba.

ref: Put your curse on them and make them suffer.
text: Basi ate ba ta tukpari abe fi yaa ka basi ba zuk.

ref: Get angry and go after them until not a trace is left under the heavens.
text: Naawen yaa, pai fi suipuurumu a vi ba a kaasi ba meena tɛŋzuk de.

ref: The purest gold is ruined and has lost its shine; jewels from the temple lie scattered in the streets.
text: Nya ligmɔniŋka le kan ŋmaa nyaksi diila. Ligmɔniŋ maŋka dek an ŋmaa nyaksi. Naawen yenni tanaŋa a waaŋ ka tɛŋka po meena.

ref: These are Zion's people, worth more than purest gold; yet they are counted worthless like dishes of clay.
text: Zayon bi paalukku meena a jam gaam ligmɔniŋ kama, alege yɔgyɔgla de ba yaa nye nna se samɔnsa ate mɛɛrɔ a mɛ la.

ref: Babies are so thirsty that their tongues are stuck to the roof of the mouth. Children go begging for food, but no one gives them any.
text: Nyanyuila ale a ko buluataŋa ate ba giŋgeluŋtaŋa a maŋ ba laŋtisaŋa. Bimbaansa a juisi ŋandiinta alege waai kan te ba.

ref: All who ate expensive foods lie starving in the streets; those who grew up in luxury now sit on trash heaps.
text: Baai ale jam a dɛ ŋandiin maŋsa la yaa juisi. Ka suitaŋa niŋ ayen ba tin nya jaab. Nuru baai ale jam yiti a jo garuk naliŋsa la a yaa gisi ka yaata kpiirika jigi ba dan nya jaab ba pai.

ref: My nation was punished worse than the people of Sodom, whose city was destroyed in a flash without the help of human hands.
text: Mi nuruma ninammu a gaam Sodom ale jam nam diila kama. Sodom tɛŋka a jam kaasi kama alege ba an nya maarika.

ref: The leaders of Jerusalem were purer than snow and whiter than milk; their bodies were healthy and glowed like jewels.
text: Nabisaŋa jam a nyaksi ase ka ŋmoruk tana la, a peenti gaam biisim. Ba nyiŋsaŋa a jam muni kama gaam tintain munta, a nye ase tintain sobta la.

ref: Now they are blacker than tar, and no one recognizes them; their skin clings to their bones and is drier than firewood.
text: Alege yɔgyɔgla ba sobi gaam kaala ate waai an ŋman nya ba a miŋ suitaŋa niŋŋa. Ba nyiŋsaŋa a yaa maŋ ka ba kobaŋa, si yaa ko ka nna chekchek ase daata la.

ref: Life in the city is so bad that loving mothers have boiled and eaten their own children.
text: Nipok baai ale ta jiirim a pai badek bisa a dik ŋɔbi ayen ba jɔk vuugi.

ref: The Lord was so fiercely angry that he burned the city of Zion to the ground.
text: Naawen a jɔk wa suinni ate di kasim a dom ate wa moak bolim a ju Zayon ate bu dɛ jaab meena a ga paari wa kiri.

ref: Not a king on this earth or the people of any nation believed enemies could break through her gates.
text: Nalima ale tɛŋzuk nuruba meena a kan jam a siak ayen dachaasa ale baga a jo Jerusalem po.

ref: Jerusalem was punished because her prophets and her priests had sinned and caused the death of innocent victims.
text: Ku nye dila kama dii nyiŋla biisiteerɔma ale wa kaabteerɔma a jam tom ka biem. Ba jam ko baai ale a tom wamaŋsa la.

ref: Yes, her prophets and priests were covered with blood; no one would come near them, as they wandered from street to street.
text: Ba jam nyiem a tuinti kama ase yioba la nuruma ziimu a jam daŋ ba kama ate waai kan yaali wa tiri ba gattaŋa.

ref: Instead, everyone shouted, “Go away! Don't touch us! You're filthy and unfit to belong to God's people!” So they had to leave and become refugees. But foreign nations told them, “You can't stay here!”
text: Nuruba yaa na ba, <<Ni cheŋ du, ni daŋ kama.>> <<Ni cheŋ du! Ni cheŋ du! Ni kan tiri tama!>> Ate ba yaa chali bɛ a tuinti a cheŋ. Tɛŋ yonsa a weeni ba ayen, <<Ba kan bo ni ba.>>

ref: The Lord is the one who sent them scattering, and he has forgotten them. No respect or kindness will be shown to the priests or leaders.
text: Naawen dek ale yiak ti waaŋ chaab an ŋmaa nya ti zuwa. Nuru kan ŋmaa zuli kaabteerɔma yaase niŋdeerɔma.

ref: Our eyes became weary, hopelessly looking for help from a nation that could not save us.
text: Ti kasim za ka ti gbirimaŋa zuk a nya ase tɛŋ kaai ale vari ti basi ya, alege ti nya ti nina ga feligi maarika kan jam.

ref: Enemies hunted us down on every public street. Our time was up; our doom was near.
text: Ti dachaasaŋa a vi ti, ti an baga a cheŋ suitaŋa po. Ti kpeglimka a moata. Ti daaŋa a paari ya. Ti kpeglimka a jam ya.

ref: They swooped down faster than eagles from the sky. They hunted for us in the hills and set traps to catch us out in the desert.
text: Baai ale a vi ti la a kpabi a gaam jiiritaŋa ale bo wenzuk la. Ba vi ti ti ga jo guutaŋa po ate ba gu doa gɔnni po a limisi ti.

ref: The Lord's chosen leader was our hope for survival! We thought he would keep us safe somewhere among the nations, but even he was caught in one of their traps.
text: Naawen ale lueri naab waai ate wa jam ka tama dek nyuvuri la, ba bari yik wa. Ti jam weeni wa wie kama ayen, wa le wa a lik ti ate tɛŋ yonsa kan nya ti pagrimoa.

ref: You people of Edom can celebrate now! But your time will come to suffer and stagger around naked.
text: Edom Liewa ale bo Uz tɛŋka la, ni sue peenti kama ate ni a naŋŋi. Naawen suipuurum beerika ale sueri a jam ni jigi ate ni nyu buk a cheŋ chaboala.

ref: The people of Zion have paid for their sins, and the Lord will soon let them return home. But, people of Edom, you will be punished, and your sins exposed.
text: Zayon Liewa ni ninammu a kpegli ya. Wa kan ŋman te ni jo ninam po. Alege Edom Liewa, ni ninammu diem a piilim kama. Wa le lak ni wabaataŋa.

ref: Our Lord, don't forget how we have suffered and been disgraced.
text: Naawen yaa, teeri dii meena ale nye ti la abe fi nya chivie ŋaai ale a dɛ ti la.

ref: Foreigners and strangers have taken our land and our homes.
text: Ti tɛŋka nicham yaa le soa, ti yeeŋa mɛ nicham yaa le tuesi.

ref: The water we drink and the wood we burn cost far too much.
text: Nya buui ate ti a nyu la se ti da, abe ti da daata mɛ.

ref: We are terribly mistreated; we are worn out and can find no rest.
text: Baai ale a vi la a yaali ayen ba yik ka ti ŋeeŋa. Ti jiak kama yɔgla a kan nya vuusum.

ref: We had to surrender to Egypt and Assyria because we were hungry.
text: Ti nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale Ejipiti ale Assiria ayen ti nya ŋandiinta jɔk vuuk.

ref: Our ancestors sinned, but they are dead, and we are left to pay for their sins.
text: Ti kokpieŋsaŋa a tom kaasi fu kama, alege ba ŋman ka. Yɔgyɔgla de tama a nam ka ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ.

ref: Slaves are now our rulers, and there is no one to set us free.
text: Yɔm yaa le chim tama kpaga, nuru be karo a vari ti ba nisa po a basi.

ref: We are in danger from brutal desert tribes; we must risk our lives just to bring in our crops.
text: Ti bola nya ka kum ale a jo bu po a gisi ŋandiinta. Ti kasim a tu ka kum gɔnni po.

ref: Our skin is scorched from fever and hunger.
text: Ti nyiŋ gbaŋsaŋa yaa toliŋ kama ase boroborok seka dɔk la kom le a ko ti.

ref: On Zion and everywhere in Judah our wives and daughters are being raped.
text: Dachaasaŋa yik Zayon nipooma ale nipokbilisaŋa ale bo Juda tɛŋsaŋa po la.

ref: Our rulers are strung up by their arms, and our nation's advisors are treated shamefully.
text: Ba bobi nabisa nisima a yik ate nisɔm kan ŋmaa nya zula.

ref: Young men are forced to do the work of slaves; boys must carry heavy loads of wood.
text: Ba yik nidoa paalukku ate ba a num zueta alege ate nidoabilisa ji da dobrita a cheŋ a ja.

ref: Our leaders are not allowed to decide cases in court, and young people no longer play music.
text: Nisɔmma an ŋmaa kali nansuiŋtaŋa noa, nidoa paalukku mɛ an ŋmaa yi yiila.

ref: Our hearts are sad; instead of dancing, we mourn.
text: Ti ŋman ka suipeentiga. Ti gɔgtaŋa yaa tulim chim ka kumsa.

ref: Zion's glory has disappeared! And we are doomed because of our sins.
text: Naam zutɔgsaŋa yaa lak ti zuimaŋa po. Ku yaa bie ti jigi ka nna yegayega ti le tom kaasi la nyiŋ.

ref: We feel sick all over and can't even see straight;
text: Kude nyiŋ ti ka yiila. Ti nina kan ŋmaa nya.

ref: our city is in ruins, overrun by wild dogs.
text: Zayon Guuku yaa doa ka koruk ate gɔi baasa yaa boro nyiem cheŋ a gilim.

ref: You will rule forever, Lord! You are King for all time.
text: Naawen yaa, a dɛ naam taam wuu. Fi le chim ti naab yɔgyɔgla de a cheŋ.

ref: Why have you forgotten us for so long?
text: Ka boa ate fi baŋ ti wie ate ku beni nna? Fi basi ti kama?

ref: Bring us back to you! Give us a fresh start.
text: Naawen yaa, ta ti ŋman, ti ŋman jam. Basi ate ti daaŋa ŋmaa nye ase ŋa le jam ka diila,

ref: Or do you despise us so much that you don't want us?
text: yaa fi din chiib zɛri ti kama? Fi sui ale daa puuri ale ti?

ref: I saw a windstorm blowing in from the north. Lightning flashed from a huge cloud and lit up the whole sky with a dazzling brightness. The fiery center of the cloud was as shiny as polished metal,
text: Mi yaa nya ale vamuniŋ a nyini wiiluk geŋka a cheena. A nya chiŋmari mɛ ate nyaksi ka a gilim di ate bolim mɛ nyaksi nyini di po a nyini. Jaab mɛ a nye nna ase kutuk mɔnuŋ la a nyaksi di suŋsuŋ.

ref: and in that center I saw what looked like four living creatures. They were somewhat like humans,
text: Chiŋmanni suŋsuŋ ku jam a nye nna ase ka ŋanvuta ale bo du la. Ba jam a nye nna mɛ ase nuru bisa la,

ref: except that each one had four faces and four wings.
text: alege ba wanyi a jam ta ka nimbidaasa sinaansi ale kiŋkaŋŋa ŋanaansi.

ref: Their legs were straight, but their feet looked like the hoofs of calves and sparkled like bronze.
text: Ba naŋsaŋa jam yɔrisi kama. Ba naŋtaataŋa a nye ase naabiik naŋsaba la ale a nyaksi ase kutuk ate ba soa ti ku a nyaksi la.

ref: Under each of their wings, these creatures had a human hand.
text: Ŋanvutaŋa de jam ta ka nurubiik nisima ba kiŋkaŋŋa suŋsuŋ kabta tinaansiwa. Banaansiwa meena jam ta ka nimbidaasa ale kiŋkaŋŋa,

ref: The four creatures were standing back to back with the tips of their wings touching. They moved together in every direction, without turning their bodies.
text: ate ba kiŋkaŋŋa a tiri chaab. Ba dan jam a cheŋ, ba kan cheemu alege ba yɔmisi kama a cheŋ.

ref: Each creature had the face of a human in front, the face of a lion on the right side, the face of a bull on the left, and the face of an eagle in back.
text: Ba nimbidaasaŋa ale jam ka diila ale nna. Ba wanyi meena a jam ta ka nurubiik nimbidiak ale gbeŋli nimbidiak juga geŋ ale naab nimbidiak gala geŋ. Ba wanyi meena mɛ a ta ka jiiruk nimbidiak.

ref: Two wings of each creature were spread out and touched the wings of the creatures on either side. The other two wings of each creature were folded against its body.
text: Ba nimbidaasaŋa ale jam ka diila ale la. Ba kiŋkaŋŋa a lak kama a nyini a jueli. Ba wanyi meena a ta ka kiŋkaŋŋa ŋaye ate ŋa a tiri mbala ate kiŋkaŋŋa ŋaye a lik wa nyiŋka.

ref: The four living creatures went wherever the Spirit led them, and they moved together without turning their bodies, because each creature faced straight ahead.
text: Ba wanyi meena yɔmisi ka niŋ a cheŋ. Wen Chiika ale a cheŋ juijui la ŋanvutaŋa mɛ a cheŋ ka dula alege kan cheen ŋaaŋŋa.

ref: The creatures were glowing like hot coals, and I saw something like a flaming torch moving back and forth among them. Lightning flashed from the torch every time its flame blazed up.
text: Ŋanvutaŋa de a nye ase ka bolim kaala ale a dɛ la. Bolim ale kasim a cheŋ niŋ ale ŋaaŋ ba suŋsuŋ. Ku jam a nyaksi kama alege a nya nna cheri.

ref: The creatures themselves moved as quickly as sparks jumping from a fire.
text: Ba kasim a chali a ga ka niŋ ale ŋaaŋ nna yilibi yilibi ase bolim ale a nyaksi la.

ref: I then noticed that on the ground beside each of the four living creatures was a wheel,
text: Yɔgyɔgla de mi yaa le a nya ŋanvutaŋa la, mi yaa nya wiili a za ba wanyi meena ale ta nimbidaasa sinaansi la tɛŋ.

ref: shining like chrysolite. Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it,
text: Ba le nye wiilima diila ale nna. Ba jam a nyaksi kama ase tintain salima la. Wiiliba banaansiwa meena jam a neesi ka chaab, a nye nna ase ba bari jo chaab la.

ref: so that they could move in any direction without turning.
text: Ba daa cheŋ ba a va jiga bunaansiwa kama alege kan viriŋ.

ref: The rims of the wheels were large and frightening, and they had eyes all the way around them.
text: Wiilima noawaaŋa a jueli kama alege ta nina a gilim a nak kpaziim.

ref: The creatures controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the four creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels were beside them.
text: Ŋanvuta a dan cheŋ, wiilima mɛ cheŋ. Ba dan zaani wiilima mɛ zaani. Ba dan yiti wiilima mɛ yiti, dii nyiŋla chiika bo wiilima mɛ po kama.

ref: Above the living creatures, I saw something that was sparkling like ice, and it reminded me of a dome. Each creature had two of its wings stretched out toward the creatures on either side, with the other two wings folded against its body.
text: Jagigiluku tɛŋ ba yaa teeri ba kiŋkaŋŋa a tuk chaab. Ba wanyi meena a ta ka kiŋkaŋŋa ŋaye a lik wa nyiŋka.

ref: Whenever the creatures flew, their wings roared like an ocean or a large army or even the voice of God All-Powerful. And whenever the creatures stopped, they folded their wings against their bodies.
text: Ba le a cheŋ la mi yaa wom nuemka nna ase nyakpiemu ale a wuuri la. Nuemka nna ase Wen Dii Ale A Niak La, a wuuri mɛ ase tugurik tɔŋdɔba ale a nuem la. Ba le ga zaani la, ba basi ate ba kiŋkaŋŋa a siŋ tɛŋ.

ref: When the creatures stopped flapping their wings, I heard a sound coming from above the dome.
text: Lueluk yaa nyini ba zuimaŋa jagigiluku po. Ba dan ga zaani, ba te ti ba kiŋkaŋŋa a siŋ tɛŋ.

ref: I then saw what looked like a throne made of sapphire, and sitting on the throne was a figure in the shape of a human.
text: Jagigiluku ale bo ba zuima la jaab ale a nye nna ase naam zukpaglik la. Ate ka a nyaksi ase tintain sobta la. Zukpaglika zuk a nye ase nuru ale kali du la.

ref: From the waist up, it was glowing like metal in a hot furnace, and from the waist down it looked like the flames of a fire. The figure was surrounded by a bright light,
text: Mi ya nya wa chiaka ta jueli a nye nna ase kutuk ate bolim boro la. Zaani wa chiaka a siŋ a nye nna ase bolim la ate nyaksika a gilim bolimu.

ref: as colorful as a rainbow that appears after a storm. I realized I was seeing the brightness of the Lord's glory! So I bowed with my face to the ground, and just then I heard a voice speaking to me.
text: Wa gilagilawa a nye nna ase ŋmoruk nika dai nagoritom la. Ku a nye nna ase Naawen zula ale wa nalimu la. Mi ale nya la, mi yaa lo poi nyiŋ a wom lueluk ale a biisi ale mi.

ref: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, I want you to stand up and listen.”
text: Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, yiti zaani fi naŋsa zuk ate m biisi ale fu.>>

ref: After he said this, his Spirit took control of me and lifted me to my feet. Then the Lord said:
text: Wa le a biisi ale mi la, Wen Chiika a yaa jo mi a zak mi zaani mi naŋsa zuk. Ate mi yaa wom ale Naawen a biisi ale mi.

ref: Ezekiel, I am sending you to the people of Israel. They are just like their ancestors who rebelled against me and refused to stop.
text: Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, maa tom fu ka Izirali demma jigi. Ba zɛri mi kama ale basi mu. Ba le ba kokpieŋsaŋa a tom kaasi mi kama a jam paari jinla danni.

ref: They are stubborn and hardheaded. But I, the Lord God, have chosen you to tell them what I say.
text: Maa tom fu ka nuru baai tue ale kpari ale kan zuli mɛ la jigi. Fi le weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna.>

ref: Those rebels may not even listen, but at least they will know that a prophet has come to them.
text: Dai di dai ba le wom yaa ba poom kan wom, ba tɔlim ka tukpari nuruba. Alege ba le seba ayen biisiteerɔ a bo ba suŋsuŋ.

ref: and preach my message to them, whether they choose to listen or not.
text: Alege biisi m wieŋa a te ba. Ba le wom yaa ba kan wom diila ba basi mu kama.

ref: Ezekiel, don't rebel against me, as they have done. Instead, listen to everything I tell you. And now, Ezekiel, open your mouth and eat what I am going to give you.
text: Alege fi saalɔ biiga wom mi le a weeni fu diila. Kan basi mu ase nuruma de ale basi mu diila. Lak fi nɔnni a dɛ jabuui ate m pai a te fu la.>>

ref: Just then, I saw a hand stretched out toward me. And in it was a scroll.
text: Mi yaa nya nisa ale teeri a tuk mi nyiŋ, ate gbaŋ a bo si po.

ref: The hand opened the scroll, and both sides of it were filled with words of sadness, mourning, and grief.
text: Wa yaa a lak gbaŋka mi niŋ. Kuuna yiila, ale niniga ŋmarisika, ale daanika wie a ŋmarisi doa ka niŋ ale ka ŋaaŋ.

ref: He handed me the scroll and said, “Eat this and fill up on it.” So I ate the scroll, and it tasted sweet as honey.
text: Wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, ŋɔbi gbaŋka de ate m pai a te fu la a sueri fi ponni.>> Ate mi ya ŋɔbi ate ka masa nna se siita la mi nɔnni po.

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, I am sending you to your own people.
text: Wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, cheŋ Izirali demma jigi a ga biisi m wieŋa a te ba.

ref: They are Israelites, not some strangers who speak a foreign language you can't understand. If I were to send you to foreign nations, they would listen to you.
text: M kan tom fu ka tɛŋ sii biik ate fi kan wom yaase ka pagra ate fi kan miŋ wieŋa la jigi ya. M dan tom fu ka ba de jigi ba le wom fu.

ref: But the people of Israel will refuse to listen, because they have refused to listen to me. All of them are stubborn and hardheaded,
text: Alege Izirali demma a kan siak wom fu dii nyiŋla ba an poom a yaali ayen ba wom mi. Mm Izirali demma meena tue kpari kama a kan wom mi nɔi ya.

ref: so I will make you as stubborn as they are.
text: Nya, yɔgyɔgla m basi kama ate fi tuiri kpari ale pagra ase ba la.

ref: Then go to the people who were brought here to Babylonia with you and tell them you have a message from me, the Lord God. Do this, whether they listen to you or not.
text: Abe fi cheŋ ligrɔma jigi fidek nuruma a weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna.> Ba le wom yoo ba kan wom yoo tin weeni ba.>>

ref: The Spirit lifted me up, and as the glory of the Lord started to leave, I heard a loud, thundering noise behind me.

text: Saluiku ate Naawen biisi wa wanni te mi ayen,

text: Naawa ale pai wa ŋantaŋa a vi ŋmankpala a nyini legini po a cheŋ. Nuruma ale keri vɔrup siaka po a ta wa nyini. Wa le lik wa ninaŋa ate wa kaa nya tɛŋka.

ref: The Lord will spread out a net and trap him as he leaves Jerusalem. He will then be led away to the city of Babylon, but will never see that place, even though he will die there.
text: Alege m le yuk m ŋmiaka a vi wa zuk a yik wa. M yaa le ta wa jam Babilon, Kaldiya demma tɛŋka. Wa kan nya tɛŋ kala, alege wa za wa kpi ka dula.

ref: His own officials and troops will scatter in every direction, and the Lord will track them down and put them to death.
text: Baai meena ale gilim naawa la, wa maarima ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena, m le basi ate ba waaŋ jigi meena a yaa ko ba ale m gebika.

ref: The Lord will force the rest of the people in Jerusalem to live in foreign nations, where they will realize that he has done all these things.
text: M dan basi ate ba waaŋ tɛŋsaŋa meena po ba le seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Some of them will survive the war, the starvation, and the deadly diseases. That way, they will be able to tell foreigners how disgusting their sins were, and that it was the Lord who punished them in this way. A Sign of Fear
text: Alege m le vari ba maga a basi, m kan ko ba ale gebika, yaase m basi ate kɔm ko ba, yaase m basi ate nyiŋtuila a ko ba. Ba yaa le weeni sak tɛŋ sii meena ba cheŋ la gaasa wie ŋaai meena ba nye la. Ate ba yaa seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, shake with fear when you eat, and tremble when you drink.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, fi daa dɛ ŋandiinta basi ate fi nyiŋka a gɔk, fi be daa nyu nyiam basi ate fi nyiŋka a gɔk ale yɔgsum.

ref: Tell the people of Israel that I, the Lord, say that someday everyone in Jerusalem will shake when they eat and tremble when they drink. Their country will be destroyed and left empty, because they have been cruel and violent.
text: Abe fi yaa weeni tɛŋka demma ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni dii a magsi chaab ale nuru baai ale bo Jerusalem, Izirali tɛŋka po la. Ba le dɛ ŋandiinta ale yɔgsum abe ba nyu nyiam ale chichama, dii nyiŋla ba tɛŋka kan ŋman ta jaaboa nuruma gaasaŋa ale nyeka tuemu nyiŋ.

ref: Every town will lie in ruins, and the land will be a barren desert. Then they will know that I am the Lord. The Words of the Lord Will Come True
text: Tɛŋ sii ate nuruba a boro la ale kaasi doa. Tɛŋka ale chim tɛŋ koruk. Ate ni seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.> >>

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, you've heard people in Israel use the saying, “Time passes, and prophets are proved wrong.”
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, ka boan biik ate ni ta Izirali tɛŋka po nna: <Daaŋa jam a taam ka di alege dii ate Naawen pai sak la kan nye jaaboa>?

ref: Now tell the people that I, the Lord, am going to prove that saying wrong. No one will ever be able to use it again in Israel, because very soon everything I have said will come true!
text: Dila nyiŋ weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, M le te ba basi nna wa weeni ka. Waai be kan bo Izirali a ŋman weeni wanni de.> Alege weeni ba ayen, <Ku moata ate dii meena m pai sak la a chim wensie.

ref: The people will hear no more useless warnings and false messages.
text: Venta wie nyaasim ale bi sii ale a peenti nuruba sui Izirali tɛŋka po la a kan boro.

ref: I will give them my message, and what I say will certainly happen. Warn those rebels that the time has come for them to be punished. I, the Lord, make this promise.
text: Alege Mi Naawen ale biisi. Mi ale a weeni diila ale nye ku kan beni. Ni zɛri mi zula teka kama ale ni daaŋa po m le biisi abe m nye. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>

ref: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are also saying that your visions and messages are only about things in the future.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, Izirali demma weeni kama ayen, <Ezekiel ale nya diila ka chum po wie nyiini. Wa a biisi ka chum po wie.>

ref: So tell them that my words will soon come true, just as I have warned. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Dila be weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Wa wieŋa ŋa ŋaai mɛ la kan beni. M le weeni diila m le nye. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the prophets of Israel who say they speak in my name, but who preach messages that come from their own imagination. Tell them it's time to hear my message.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, mooli a kaam Izirali biisiteerɔma. Weeni baai ale poli a weeni badek wie la ayen ba wom Naawen wanni.

ref: I, the Lord God, say those lying prophets are doomed! They don't see visions—they make up their own messages!
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ku le bie te biisiteerɔ bettaŋa ale a va badek popola alege an nya wari mi jigi la.

ref: Israel's prophets are no better than jackals that hunt for food among the ruins of a city.
text: Izirali demma, ni biisiteerɔma a nye ase ka gɔi baasa ale a gisi ŋanta ayen si ko abe si dɛ yie luema po la.

ref: Those prophets lie by claiming they speak for me, but I have not even chosen them to be my prophets. And they still think their words will come true.
text: Ni biisiteerɔma a nya ka venta wie ale a biisi venta mɛ. Ba a weeni kama ayen, <<Naawen wari ale nna,>> alege Naawen an poom tom ba. Alege ba a poli ayen ba le weeni diila ale chim wensie.

ref: They say they're preaching my messages, but they are full of lies—I did not speak to them!
text: Ni nyiem weeni kama ayen, <<Naawen wari ale nna,>> alege ka venta wie ni nya. Ni wieŋa ka venta, dii nyiŋla mi an biisi wari ya.

ref: I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. They will not be allowed to call themselves Israelites or even to set foot in Israel. Then they will realize that I am the Lord God.
text: Mi ale namsi biisiteerɔ baai ale a nya venta wie ale a velim wie la. Ba kan jigi mi nuruma po. Ba yue kan maa ŋmarisi bo Izirali demma wieŋa po, ba be kan jo Izirali tɛŋka. Dila ni le seba ayen ka Mi ale Nyɔnɔwa Naawen la.

ref: Those prophets refuse to be honest. They tell my people there will be peace, even though there's no peace to be found. They are like workers who think they can fix a shaky wall by covering it with paint.
text: Dii ate mi a nye dila la ba te ti m nuruma a cheŋ a bɛ ale a weeni ayen, <<Suiyɔgni a boro.>> alege suiyɔgni a ka. Nuruma a dan se parik kaai ale kan pagra biisiteerɔma a sa siaka ale peeluk ase parik pagrik la.

ref: People will then ask the workers why the paint didn't hold it up.
text: Siaka a dan lo nuruba ale bek fu ayen, <<Peelukku ate fi pai sa siaka la a bo be?>>

ref: That wall is the city of Jerusalem. And I, the Lord God, am so angry that I will send strong winds, rainstorms, and hailstones to destroy it.
text: << <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, M le wɛ siaka ale va pagrik. M suinni ale a puuri la nyiŋ m le basi ate ŋmoruk a ni yega abe tintain tuila a kaasi parika.

ref: The lying prophets have tried to cover up the evil in Jerusalem, but I will tear down the city, all the way to its foundations. And when it collapses, those prophets will be killed, and everyone will know that I have done these things.
text: M le kabri parik kaai ate ni nye ka peelukku la. Ka le paari tɛŋ ate nuruba nya ka nyubini. Parisaŋa a dan lo, nama dek ale kpi si kiri la. Ate ni seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: The city of Jerusalem and its lying prophets will feel my fierce anger. Then I will announce that the city has fallen and that the lying prophets are dead,
text: M sui le puuri ale parika ale baai ale pai peelukku a sa ka la. Abe m weeni ni ayen, parika a cheŋ ale baai ale pai peelukku a sa ka la.

ref: because they promised my people peace, when there was no peace. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Women Who Wear Magic Charms The Lord said:
text: Izirali biisiteerɔma ale mooli a te Jerusalem la ale baai ale nya ayen suiyɔgni a bo tɛŋka po alege suiyɔgni a ka la ale taam meena. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.>> >

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, now condemn the women of Israel who preach messages that come from their own imagination.
text: <<Yɔgyɔgla de, Saalɔ biiga nya nipooma ale bo nuruma po la a poli badek wieŋa a weeni la. Biisi te ba.

ref: Tell them they're doomed! They wear magic charms on their wrists and scarves on their heads, then trick others into believing they can predict the future. They won't get away with telling those lies.
text: Weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ku le bie a te nipok baai ale a baali ŋan kperisa a su ba nisa ale a nye ŋan nyaara a pai vi ba zuima ayen ba bari yik nuruba la. Ni kaasi mi nuruma nyuvooŋa kama ale ayen ni vari nidek nyuvooŋa.

ref: They charge my people a few handfuls of barley and a couple pieces of bread, and then give messages that are insulting to me. They use lies to sentence the innocent to death and to help the guilty go free. And my people believe them!
text: <Barli> nisa nɔi ale boroborok maga nyiŋ ate ni an zuli mi m nuruma suŋsuŋŋa. Ni velim te mi nuru baai ale a wom venta la. Ni ko baai ale kan magsi ba kpi ale basi baai ale magsi ba kpi la.

ref: I hate the magic charms they use to trick people into believing their lies. I will rip those charms from their wrists and set free the people they have trapped like birds.
text: << <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, wa kan yaali kperisa wie ŋaai ate ba nye a bari a yik nuruba ase nuinsa la. Ayen wa le gebi kperisa ŋantaŋa ba nisaŋa po a vari baai ate ba bari yik ase nuinsa la a basi.

ref: I will tear the scarves from their heads and rescue my people from their power once and for all. Then they will know that I am the Lord God.
text: M le cheeri ba ŋan nyaaraŋa abe m vari m nuruma ni nisa po. Ni kan ŋman bari yik ba ale ni pagrimu. Ate ni seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: They do things I would never do. They lie to good people and encourage them to do wrong, and they convince the wicked to ruin their own lives by not turning from sin.
text: Ba a nye ka wie ate mi a kan nye ŋa. Ba velim kama a te nuru maŋsa ale a te ba nyiŋbiiri ate ba nye a kaasi, ale a paasi wabaata nyama ate ba kasim a nye biem a kaasi ba nyuvooŋa.

ref: I will no longer let these women give false messages and use magic, and I will free my people from their control. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
text: Mi kan basi ate ba ŋman nya venta wie abe ba porisi, ate m vari m nuruma ba nisa po a basi. Ate ba seba ayen, Mi Naawen ale nye wieŋa de.> >>

ref: One day, some of Israel's leaders came to me and asked for a message from the Lord.
text: Izirali niŋdeerɔ kpagsaŋa gela yaa jam kali mi niŋ.

ref: While they were there, the Lord said:
text: Naawen yaa biisi ale mi a weeni ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, these men have started worshiping idols, though they know it will cause them to sin even more. So I refuse to give them a message!
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, nuruma de a yaali ayen ba kaab ka bɔgta. Ba ta ka biem wie ŋaai ale nye ate nuruba a tom biem la. M be te ba suik ate ba bek maarika?

ref: Tell the people of Israel that if they sin by worshiping idols and then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will give them the answer their sins deserve.
text: Dila nyiŋ, biisi weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Izirali nuruma baai ale a yaali ba kaab bɔgta abe ba ta biem wie ŋaai ale nye ate nuruba a nye biem alege a jam biisiteerɔwa jigi la, Mi, Naawen dek ale tulisi ba ba bɔgtaŋa kaabka nyiŋ.

ref: When they hear my message, maybe they will see that they need to turn back to me and stop worshiping those idols.
text: Ate m ŋman nya m nuruma Izirali demma, baai ale basi mu ba bɔgtaŋa nyiŋla.>

ref: Now, Ezekiel, tell everyone in Israel: I am the Lord God. Stop worshiping those idols I hate so much and come back to me.
text: <<Dila nyiŋ weeni Izirali demma ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ni tagri ni nyeka ale ni suiniimaŋa abe ni basi bɔgta kaabka. Ni basi wie ŋaai meena ate mi kisi la nyeka.

ref: Suppose one of you Israelites or a foreigner living in Israel rejects me and starts worshiping idols. If you then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will answer
text: << <Izirali demma baai ale nichamma baai ale bo Izirali tɛŋka po la a daa yaali ba poori badek mi jigi a kaab bɔgta abe ba ta, nye kaai ale a basi ate nuruba a nye biem la. Ba yaa dan jam biisiteerɔwa jigi ayen ba bek mu bega, Mi Naawen ale tulisi ba m dek.

ref: by turning against you. I will make you a warning to anyone who might think of doing the same thing, and you will no longer belong to my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord and that you have sinned against me.
text: M le zɛri ba, M le yeeri ba m nuruma po ate ba a nya ba. Dila ni le seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.

ref: If a prophet gives a false message, I am the one who caused that prophet to lie. But I will still reject him and cut him off from my people,
text: << <Alege, ba dan paasi biisiteerɔwa ate wa biisi wari ka mi Naawen ale paasi wa ate wa biisi. Dila mi yaa le pai m pagrimu a kaasi wa Izirali demma suŋsuŋ.

ref: and anyone who goes to that prophet for a message will be punished in the same way.
text: Biisiteerɔwa ale nye bɛ kama ase waai ale bek a yaali maarika la. Ba nɔi bayewa ale nam ba biemu nyiŋ.

ref: I will do this, so that you will come back to me and stop destroying yourselves with these disgusting sins. So turn back to me! Then I will be your God, and you will be my people. I, the Lord God, make this promise. Judgment on a Sinful Nation
text: Ate Izirali tɛŋka kan ŋman basi mi yaase ba daŋ badek ale ba wabaataŋa. Ba le chim m nuruba ate mi mɛ a chim ba Wen. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>

ref: The Lord God said:
text: Naawen yaa biisi ale mi a weeni ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, suppose an entire nation sins against me, and I punish it by destroying the crops and letting its people and livestock starve to death.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, tɛŋ kaai nuruba a dan tom kaasi mi a kan zuli mi, m le tu chaab ale ba ale pagrim. M le kaasi ŋandiintaŋa abe m basi ate kɔm jam ate nuruba ale duŋsa meena a kpi.

ref: Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living in that nation, their faithfulness would not save anyone but themselves.
text: Nuruma de batawa Nowa ale Daniel ale Job a dan poom bo tɛŋ kala po ba tuim maŋsaŋa ale vari ka badek ba nyiini a basi. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen la ale weeni.

ref: Or suppose I punish a nation by sending wild animals to eat people and scare away every passerby, so that the land becomes a barren desert.
text: <<Yaase m basi ate gɔi duŋsa a jo tɛŋka po ate tɛŋka a doa koruk, biik a kan boro. Ate nuru a kan va ka po a taamu duŋsaŋa nyiŋ.

ref: As surely as I live, I promise that even if these three men lived in that nation, their own children would not be spared. The three men would live, but the land would be an empty desert.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale a weeni ayen, Mi le ka waai ale vua la, Nowa ale Daniel ale Job a dan poom bo tɛŋka po ba kan baga a vari badek bisa ale ba lieba a basi, ba le vari ka badek a basi. Ba le vari ka badek a basi alege tɛŋ kala ale doa koruk.

ref: Or suppose I send an enemy to attack a sinful nation and kill its people and livestock.
text: <<Yaase m ta kpaliŋ jam tɛŋka po. Da dii dai m le weeni ayen, <Kpaliŋ siti tɛŋka po,> a ko nuruma ale duŋsaŋa.

ref: If these three men were in that nation when I punished it, not even their children would be spared. Only the three men would live.
text: Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale a weeni ayen, Mi ale vua la, nuru bala batawa a dan poom bo tɛŋ kala po ba kan baga a vari ba bisa ale ba lieba a basi. Ba le vari ka badek a basi.

ref: And suppose I am so angry that I send a deadly disease to wipe out the people and livestock of a sinful nation.
text: <<Yaase m basi ate tuem a waaŋ tɛŋka meena. M sui ale puuri nna yegayega ale ba ate m kaasi abe m ko nuruma ale duŋsa.

ref: Again, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living there, I, the Lord, promise that the children of these faithful men would also die. Only the three of them would be spared.
text: Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni ayen mi ale sum vua la, Nowa ale Daniel ale Job a dan poom bo tɛŋka po ba kan baga vari ba biik yaa ba lie a basi. Ba te vari ka badek a basi ba wamaŋsaŋa nyiŋ.

ref: I am the Lord God, and I promise to punish Jerusalem severely. I will send war, starvation, wild animals, and deadly disease to slaughter its people and livestock.
text: <<Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ayen m le zɔk dii a magsi Jerusalem la a bie ka yega. M le te ninam tɔgatɔga bunaansi jam ba jigi. Kpaliŋ, kɔm, gɔi duŋsa ale tuem. A ko nuruma ale duŋsaŋa.

ref: And those who survive will be taken from their country and led here to Babylonia. Ezekiel, when you see how sinful they are, you will know why I did all these things to Jerusalem.
text: Alege nuruba gela ale nyin du nyin, bisa ale lieba ale nyini. Ba le nyini jam ni jigi ate ni nya ba nyeka ate sui yaa yɔk ale mi ale ta kaasuŋ kuui a jam Jerusalem la.

ref: You will be convinced that I, the Lord God, was right in doing what I did.
text: Ni dan nya ba nyeka ni sue le yɔk ate ni seba ayen mi an nye basi du alege ka wari nyiŋ. Ka Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Some time later, the Lord said:
text: Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, what happens to the wood of a grapevine after the grapes have been picked? It isn't like other trees in the forest,
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, tunuk dabi a gaam ti sii meena ale bo gɔnni po la daataŋa?

ref: because the wood of a grapevine can't be used to make anything, not even a small peg to hang things on.
text: Fi baga a pai tunuk dabi a nye jaaboa? Fi baga a pai a nye kpaasiri a yik jaab du?

ref: It can only be used as firewood. But after its ends are burnt and its middle is charred, it can't be used for anything.
text: Ase ba dan pai tunuk dabi a yuk basi bolim po ate bu dɛ kaabta buyewa jam suŋsuŋka po a dɛ, fi baga a pai a nye jaaboa.

ref: The wood is useless before it is burned, and afterwards, it is completely worthless.
text: Diokku ale chim pumi la, ba an baga a pai nye jaaboa. Bolim abe dan dɛ ku meena ba kan baga a pai ku a nye jaaboa.

ref: I will punish the people of Jerusalem with fire. Some of them have escaped one destruction, but soon they will be completely burned. And when that happens, you, Ezekiel, will know that I am the Lord.
text: abe tulim ta chaab ale ba. Ba va ka bolim yeŋ po nyini alege bolim ale diem dɛ ba kaasi, m dan tulim ta chaab ale ba, ni le seba ayen mi ka Naawen.

ref: I will make their country an empty wasteland, because they have not been loyal to me. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: M le basi ate tɛŋka doa koruk dii nyiŋla ba ka siaka. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.>>

ref: The Lord said:
text: Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, remind the people of Jerusalem of their disgusting sins
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, weeni Jerusalem demma ale ba nye bioku.

ref: and tell them that I, the Lord God, am saying: Jerusalem, you were born in the country where Canaanites lived. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.
text: Weeni ayen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni Jerusalem dii la ale nna: Ba jam biak ni ka Keenan demma tɛŋka: Ni kowa jam ka Amori demma denɔ, ate ni mawa a chim Yit demma denɔ.

ref: When you were born, no one cut you loose from your mother or washed your body. No one rubbed your skin with salt and olive oil, and wrapped you in warm blankets.
text: Dai dii dai ate ba biak fu la, ba an so fi nyiŋka, ba an gebi fi suiku. Ba an pai yesa a sa fu yaa ba pai gatta a pobi fu.

ref: Not one person loved you enough to do any of these things, and no one even felt sorry for you. You were despised, thrown into a field, and forgotten.
text: Fi jiirim an dari waai ayen wa nye wieŋa de dii a te fu. Ba pai fu kama a yuk basi peelim, dii nyiŋla ba jam kisi fu kama da dii danni ate ba biak fu la,

ref: I saw you lying there, rolling around in your own blood, and I couldn't let you die.
text: <<Mi ale a taam la, mi yaa nya fu dua ziimu po a tɔŋ, ate mi yaa weeni fu ayen, <Vuuk.>

ref: I took care of you, like someone caring for a tender, young plant. You grew up to be a beautiful young woman with mature breasts and hair, but you were still naked.
text: Mi basi kama ate fi chim ase viok la. Ate fi chim a waaŋ a nyaksi. Ate fi nyini biisa ate fi zuisaŋa a chim, alege fi ta chaboala a ka gatta.

ref: When I saw you again, you were old enough to have sex. So I covered your naked body with my own robe. Then I solemnly promised that you would belong to me and that I, the Lord God, would take care of you.
text: <<Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate mi a taam a nya fu ale fi pak a magsi yaalika. Mi yaa pai m garukku a lik fi chaboalaŋa Ate mi puulim alege ate ti nye nɔiyeŋ ate m soa fu. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: I washed the blood off you and rubbed your skin with olive oil.
text: Ate mi so fu ale nyiam ale sugri fi ziimu a sa fu ale kpaam.

ref: I gave you bracelets, a necklace,
text: A pai kpana a su fi ŋiri ale fi nisima,

ref: a ring for your nose, some earrings, and a beautiful crown.
text: baŋ a su fi nyori, a pai tukpana a su fi tue, a pai naam zutɔk a vuk fi zuk.

ref: Your jewelry was gold and silver, and your clothes were made of only the finest material and embroidered linen. Your bread was baked from fine flour, and you ate honey and olive oil. You were as beautiful as a queen,
text: Fi yaa jo ligmɔniŋ ale kpana. Fi gattaŋa a jam a nyaksi kama alege a sati ale yɔk ale garuk pein. Fi jam a dɛ ka zom maŋ ale siita ale kpaam. Fi jam kasim nala kama ale chim nipok naab.

ref: and everyone on earth knew it. I, the Lord God, had helped you become a lovely young woman.
text: Ate fi yuei yiti tɛŋsaŋa po, dii nyiŋla fi nala ka nna yegayega. Fi nalimu jam ka chekki, dii nyiŋla zuli ŋaai ate mi te fu la. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: You learned that you were attractive enough to have any man you wanted, so you offered yourself to every passerby.
text: <<Alege fi ta sebchakka ale fi nalimu. A yaa chim ja kaasuŋ, fi yuenni ale yiti la nyiŋ. Waai a daa taam fi deri goa ale wa.

ref: You made shrines for yourself and decorated them with some of your clothes. That's where you took your visitors to have sex with them. These things should never have happened!
text: A pai fi gattaŋa gela a nye ate kaabka jigini a nye nna ŋmiriŋmiri. Dula jigini fi yaa tom kaasuŋ tuimaŋa. Wieŋa de m magsi ŋa a nye, ŋa poom kan boro.

ref: You made idols out of the gold and silver jewelry I gave you, then you sinned by worshiping those idols.
text: Mi ligmɔniŋka ale kpanaŋa ate m pai te fu ate fi nye ŋan naluŋ sii la fi ŋman pai nye ka bɔgta nidoaba a tom fi kaasuŋ tuimaŋa ale ti.

ref: You dressed them in the clothes you got from me, and you offered them the olive oil and incense I gave you.
text: Ate fi pai fi garuk naliŋsaŋa ate ba pai garuk peinni a yɔk la a lik bɔgtaŋa. A pai m kpaamu ale ŋan baai nyummu ale masa la a te bɔgtaŋa.

ref: I supplied you with fine flour, olive oil, and honey, but you sacrificed it all as offerings to please those idols. I, the Lord God, watched this happen.
text: Boroboroku, zommu, kpaamu ale siitaŋa ate mi pai a te fu ayen fi a dɛ la fi pai ba mɛ a kaab bɔgta. Dii ale nye la ale nna. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: But you did something even worse than that—you sacrificed your own children to those idols!
text: <<Alege fi le a goa ale nidoama an diem magsi fu ate fi pai bisaŋa ale liema baai ale ka mi bisa la a kaab bɔgta.

text: Fi ko m bisaŋa a pai ba ju bolim a te bɔgtaŋa.

text: <<Ku le bie! Ku le bie a te fu, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni. Fi le nye biemu de meena la ŋaaŋnyiŋ,

text: fi se ka jigi ayen fi a kaab bɔgta. Fi nye tɛŋ meena po kama bɔgta kaabka jigi.

text: Dila nyiŋ fi ka fi tɔga ale nipok kaasuŋta. Waai an weeni fu ayen fi chim ja kaasuŋoa ate fi tuni ligra a te alege ba kan tuni a te fi. Fi ka fi tɔga.

text: <<Dila nipok kaasuŋoa, wom Naawen ale a weeni la.

text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Fi pai fi chaboalaŋa a sak tɛŋ yonsa. Fi an suk fidek ale fi nɔŋtaŋa goomu ale bɔgtaŋa ate mi kisi la kaabka. Fi ko fi bisaŋa a pai ba ziimu a kaab bɔgta.

ref: I will find you guilty of being an unfaithful wife and a murderer, and in my fierce anger I will sentence you to a violent death!
text: M le namsi fu ase nipooba ale nye kaboŋsa ate ba a namsi ba yaase nuru koorisa ate ba a namsi diila. M le ko fu dii nyiŋla m sui ale a puuri ale a dɛ nyuri.

text: M le pai fu a te fi nɔŋtaŋa. Ba le kaasi fi kaabka jiŋŋa abe ba kaasi juijui meena ate fi a kaab bɔgta la. Ba le cheeri fi gattaŋa a yeeri fi ŋan baai fi su la alege basi fu chaboala.

ref: Your lovers and an angry mob will stone you to death; they will cut your dead body into pieces
text: Ba le ta nuru boari jam ate ba siti fu a yuk fu ale tana abe ba gebi fu gela gela ale gebi kpieŋsa.

ref: and burn down your houses. Other women will watch these terrible things happen to you. I promise to stop you from being a prostitute and paying your lovers for sex.
text: Ba le ju fu yeeŋa abe ba namsi fu nipok boari niŋ. M le kpegli fi nidoama bobi goomu ate fi kan ŋman tuni baai ate fi a yaali la.

ref: Only then will I calm down and stop being angry and jealous.
text: Ate m yaa vuusi ale m suinni abe m kan ŋma a dɛ nyuri ya. M le nye diki m sui kan ŋman puuri.

ref: You made me furious by doing all these disgusting things and by forgetting how I took care of you when you were young. Then you made things worse by acting like a prostitute. You must be punished! I, the Lord God, have spoken. Jerusalem's Two Sisters The Lord said:
text: <<Fi kan teeri diipo ate fi jam ka biik alege basi ate m sui a puuri ale nyeka de meena la, m le tuni fu fi le nye diila. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni. Fi an pai nidoaba bobi goom a gum fi wa yɔnaŋa ate m kisi la po?

ref: People will use this saying about you, Jerusalem: “If the mother is bad, so is her daughter.”
text: <<Nuru waai ale a biisi yam wie la ale biisi nna a te fu. <Liewa a nye ase ka wa mawa la.>

ref: You are just like your mother, who hated her husband and her own children. You are also like your sisters, who hated their husbands and children. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.
text: Fi a nye ase ka fi mawa ale kisi wa chorɔwa ale wa bisaŋa la. Fi a nye ase ka fi suataŋa ale kisi ba chorɔma ale ba bisaŋa la. Fi mawa jam ka Yit denɔ, fi kowa jam ka Amori denɔ.

ref: Your older sister was Samaria, that city to your north with her nearby villages. Your younger sister was Sodom, that city to your south with her nearby villages.
text: Fi soa kpagni ka Samaria denɔ a kali wiilukku geŋka ale wa liema, alege baaŋka Sodom denɔ a kali yeseoku geŋka ale wa liema.

ref: You followed their way of life and their wicked customs, and soon you were more repulsive than they were.
text: Daa yen fi le va ba nyeka ate mi kisa la nyiini alege fi nye kama a gaam ba le a nye diila.

ref: As surely as I am the living Lord God, the people of Sodom and its nearby villages were never as sinful as you.
text: Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen la ale a weeni ayen mi ka waai ale vua. Kude ka wensie. Fi suoku Sodom ale wa liema a jam tom dii ate fi ale fi liema a tom la.

ref: They thought they were better than everyone else, and they did things I hate. And so I destroyed them.
text: Dila Sodom ale wa liema a jam ta ka kanjanta ale nye wie mi niŋ ate mi kisi la. Mi le nya ba ale nye diila mi deri gebi ba wie basi.

ref: You people of Jerusalem have sinned twice as much as the people of Samaria. In fact, your evil ways have made both Sodom and Samaria look innocent.
text: Samaria an jam nye waba tii ate fi nye la geli ya. Fi nye wie ŋaai ate mi kisi la a gaam ba kama. Fi basi kama ate fi suataŋa ale ba biemu a diem a nye nna ase nuru maŋsa la.

ref: So their punishment will seem light compared to yours. You will be disgraced and put to shame because of your disgusting sins. Jerusalem Will Be Ashamed The Lord said to Jerusalem:
text: Fi le dɛ chivie, dii nyiŋla fi te fi suataŋa ka suik. Ba zunchoŋ fu kama. Fi wabaataŋa jam bie gaam ba kama. Te chivie yik fu, dii nyiŋla fi nye ate fi suataŋa a poli ba ka nuru maŋsa.

ref: Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you.
text: Ate fi dɛ chivie a magsi chaab ale fi le nye dii meena la. Fi suataŋa ale ba biemu meena fi basi kama ate ba sue yɔk.

ref: When that day comes, you and Sodom and Samaria will once again be well-off, and all nearby villages will be restored.
text: Fi suataŋa Sodom ale wa liema ale Samaria ale wa liema ale pilim ŋmani ba daam kuuni. Fi mɛ ale fi liema ale pilim ŋmani ka ni daam kuuni.

ref: Jerusalem, you were so arrogant that you sneered at Sodom.
text: Fi an poom teeri fi suoku mɛ fi kanjantaŋa danni,

ref: You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem The Lord said:
text: Fi ninammu ale nna dii nyiŋla fi wabaataŋa ale fi nyeka ate m kisi la. Naawen ale weeni.

ref: But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever.
text: Alege m le teeri nɔiyeŋ kaai ate mi jam nye ale fu diipo ate fu diem paala la, abe m ŋman nye nɔiyeŋ kaai ale ka boro a cheŋ la,

text: Ate fi teeri dii ate fi jam nye la ate chivie yik fu fi le jam tuesi fi suataŋa kpaŋŋa ale baansaŋa la. M le pai ba a te fu ase lieba la, alege da ayen ba maa bo ka nɔiyeŋka po.

ref: I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord.
text: M le nye m nɔiyeŋka ale fu ate fi seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.

text: Fi le teeri fi le nye diila ate chivie yik fu. Fi kan ŋman lak nɔiya chivieŋa nyiŋ ate m ni vɔŋ dii meena ate fi nye la a te fu. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The Lord said:
text: Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story,
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, yaali wamagsini a magsi te Izirali demma.

ref: so they will understand what I am saying to them: A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree,
text: Weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ayen jiiruk tanjaŋi ale kiŋkaŋ kpiema ale kɔbta nna ŋmiriŋmiri ale jam Lebanon a yaa yik nyunyoŋ ŋmai naŋsa.

ref: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
text: Bu yaa teeri ase tunuŋ la a lik tɛŋka. Vaataŋa yaa tulim tuk jiirukku nyiŋ, alege bu tɛŋka naŋsaŋa a bo jiirukku naŋsa tɛŋ. Ate binni yaa chim ase tunuŋ la ate naŋsaŋa a chim a ta vaata.

ref: There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil.

ref: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
text: <<Weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Tiimu a kan kasim a chimu. Niŋ jiirukku ale dari bu naŋsaŋa a voori a cheri bu yɔnaŋa. Ate tiimu ale bu va paalitaŋa a jak a kpi. Ku kan pai daa ni pagrisa yaase nuruba yegayega ate ba dari bu naŋsaŋa a voori.

ref: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
text: Ba dan poom ŋman vuk bu, bu kan kasim a chim. Bu le jak kama a kpi meena ase kori geŋ vioku a nin fuk bu kauk kuui ate bu chim la.> >>

ref: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
text: <<Yɔgyɔgla de weeni nuru baai ale zɛri a kan zuli mi la ayen, <Ni sebi wieŋa de kiriya?> Weeni ayen, <Babilon naawa a jam ka Jerusalem a yik ba naawa ale ba nuru kpientaŋa a ta jam Babilon.

text: << <Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen a weeni ayen: Mi ale vua la, fi le kpi Babilon tɛŋka po, tɛŋ kaai naab ale basi ate fi chim Juda naab la. Juda naawa a kisi pumpuulimaŋa ŋaai ate wa nye ale Babilon naawa la kama yaa yik nɔiyeŋka a kaasi.

text: << <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, wa ale vua la wa le tuni Juda naawa wa le kisi wa pumpuulimaŋa alege kaasi ba nɔiyeŋka la.

text: Wa kan nye waai gaasa alege wa le puulim a peem jabuui la wa a te kama. Wa kan vari waai ya, alege a te baai ate kɔm ta ba la ŋandiinta, ale baai ale ta chaboala la gatta.

text: <<Alege da dii dai nuruwa de a dan ta biik kaai nyeka ale toa ate wa a ko nuruba ale a nye wieŋa de gela.

ref: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.

text: M le baŋ ba wabaataŋa. Dii nyiŋla ba nye ka dii ale magsi la, ba be kan kpi.

text: <<Alege nuru maŋsa a dan basi wamaŋsa nyeka ale a nye wie ŋaai ate mi kisa ate wabaata nyam a nye la, ba le boro? Ba wamaŋsaŋa meena m le baŋ, dii nyiŋla ba ŋman ka siaka. Ba nyeka wabaata, dila nyiŋ ba le kpi ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ.

text: Nuru maŋsa a dan basi wamaŋsa nyeka ale a nye biem, ba le kpi ku nyiŋ. Ba le kpi, dii nyiŋla ba nye ka wabaata.

text: Dii nyiŋla ba poli kama a pai biemu nyeka a basi. Ba kan kpi, ba le boro.

ref: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
text: Alege Izirali demma a diem a weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa ale a nye diila an nala.> Izirali demma, mi ale a nye diila a nala kama. Ka nama ale a nye diila ale kan nala.

ref: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
text: Ni basi waba tii meena ate ni tom la abe ni ta suiniim paala ale popola paala. Ka boa ale soa ate ni a yaali ayen ni kpi, Izirali demma?

text: Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni ayen m kan yaali ayen waai kpi, dila nyiŋ ni tagri ni suiniimaŋa ale ni nyeka ate ni boro.

ref: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
text: <<Leni kuun yiili a te Izirali niŋdeerɔma.

text: Leni ayen, ni mawa a nye ase ka gbeŋ nubi la. A doa gbeŋ bisaŋa suŋsuŋ. Di ta ka bisa yegayega.

text: Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale a weeni ayen mi ale toalim vua la, m le pai m pagrim kpiemu ale suipuurumu a basi ni zuk.

text: M le ta ni jam tɛŋsaŋa gɔnni po ate dula ti le tu chaab. Dula jigini m le bo ni buusa.

text: Mi le nye ale ni m yuenni nyiŋ, daa yen ka ni biemu yaase daŋta wieŋa nyiŋŋa. Izirali demma ate ni seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.>>

text: Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ba le yik ti diipo la bena neokku po, chiik kaai ale saari piika la, ka daa pi dai. Wa weeni ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem.
