text: <<Saalɔ biiga, ŋmarisi jinla danni a dueni, jinla danni dek. Babilon naawa ale wa nuruma gilim Jerusalem jinla kama.

ref: Throw in the legs and shoulders of your finest sheep and put in the juicy bones.
text: Pa lam gelaŋa a nyo du, tii ale nala, naŋsaŋa ale bɔŋŋa. Pa kobi maŋsaŋa a sueri.

ref: Pile wood underneath the pot, and let the meat and bones boil until they are done.”
text: Yeeri pai naluŋ, abe fi pai daata a fak samɔniŋka kiri. Basi ate lammu a vaasi ate kobaŋa a ga bɛ.

ref: These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it.
text: << <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, ku le bie ale tɛŋ kaai ale ta nuru koorisa la. Ku le bie ale samɔniŋ kaai ale muni ate ka munuku kan nyini la. Yeeri lammu ka po, bunyi bunyi. Kan luk yeeri buui ya.

ref: The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground.
text: << <Wa le ko baai la ziimu a diem bo tɛŋka po kama. Wa Kpiiri ziimu kama a dueni piuŋku zuk. Wa an kpiiri a basi tɛŋŋa ayen tanta ligi.

ref: But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
text: Mi yaa basi ayen ziim buui ate wa kpiiri a dueni piuŋku zuk la a kan ligi ate suinni a damu ate a ta chaab ale wa.

ref: I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood,
text: << <Dila nyiŋ Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ku le bie a te tɛŋ kaai ale ta nuru koorisa la. Mi dek ale fak daataŋa a jueli a magsi dɛka.

ref: so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch.
text: Fak daataŋa a cheem bolimu. Dik lammu nueri, a pai ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a dam du, a basi ate kobaŋa a dɛ.

ref: Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust.
text: Pa samɔniŋ koroku a dik kaalaŋa po ate ka toliŋ ate ka ganaŋa a muni gbaŋ gbaŋ. Daŋ tii ale maŋ du la ale nyaliŋ ate munuku nyini.

ref: Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it.
text: << <Fi wabaata a basi ate fi daŋ kama. Mi a yaali ayen M duisi alege fi diem daŋ. M kan duisi ka m suinni a nin yɔk a basi.

ref: That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Ezekiel's Wife Dies
text: << <Mi Naawen ale biisi. Ku yaa paari ka diipo ale magsi ayen m nye wari. M kan basi namsika yaase m ŋman te yaase m tagri m popola. M le bo ni buusa a magsi chaab ale ni nyeka. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>

ref: “Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, mi a yaali ayen m tuesi fi powa kama fi jigi. Nipok waai ate fi kasim a nya a yaali nna yegayega la. Wa le kpi ku kan benni, alege kan te fi sui kaasi, yaase fi kum ate ku jueli ate ninyaata nyini.

ref: Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
text: Kum dikdik. Kan kum ate ku jueli a te kpiewa. Pa jaab a vili fi zukku abe fi su fi nuesaŋa. Kan lik fi teeŋkuruku, abe fi kan dɛ ŋandiin tii ate nuruba a dɛ ase ba nuruba a nin kan ka ate ba sue dan kaasi ba a dɛ la.>>

ref: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
text: Mi yaa le biisi ale nuruma saluik ate junɔi jam a paari la ate mi powa deri kpi. Vari ale veenti la mi yaa nye va chaab ale Naawen ale weeni la.

ref: and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
text: Nuruma yaa bek mi ayen, <<Fi kan weeni ti wieŋa de ale ta jabuui wari a nye ale tama la?>>

ref: I answered: The Lord God says
text: Mi yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Naawen weeni mi kama ayen,

ref: he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed.
text: Weeni Izirali demma ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi ale banti m yenni a basi kama, pagrim jigi dii ate ni ta kanjanta, juijui ate ni nina a sueri la, ni mariŋka jigini. Ni nidoabilisaŋa ale ni liema ale tali la, ba le ko ba ale gebik.

ref: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
text: Ku dan jam nye dila, nye m le weeni diila. Ni kan lik ni teeŋkutaŋa. Ni be kan dɛ ŋandiin tii ate nuruba a dan jɔk ba nuru ba a dɛ la.

ref: You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
text: Ni le pai ŋan baai vili ni zuimaŋa la a bo du abe ni nuesaŋa a bo ni naŋsaŋa po. Ni kan kum ate ku jueli. Ni basi ni wabaataŋa abe ni a fɔbili ale chaab.

ref: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
text: Dila la Ezekiel ale wa nye ate ni nya. Wa le a nye diila, nama mɛ maa nye dila dek. Kude meena a dan nye ni le seba ayen ka Mi ale Nyɔnɔwa Naawen.>

ref: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
text: Dila po waai ale wa vuuk la ale jam fi jigi ale wie ate fi wom.

ref: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
text: Dila po wa fi nɔnni ale lagri. Fi le biisi fi kan ŋman sina. Fi ale fi chim waai ate ba a nya a tomsi la, ate ba seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.>>

ref: The Lord God said:
text: Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, nya Ammon demma geŋ a mooli a te ba.

ref: and tell them: You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners.
text: Weeni ba ayen, ba wom Nyɔnɔwa Naawen wanni. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Ni sue jam peenti kama ba le kan zuli mi yenni la, ale Izirali ale kaasi la, ale Juda ba le yik ba ta cheŋ la.

ref: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
text: Dila nyiŋ, mi za m pai ni te ka kori geŋ ka nuruma ate ba soa ni. Ba le ti ba viitaŋa ni suŋsuŋ a goa ale ni. Ba le dɛ ni yɔnaŋa abe ba nyu ni biisimu.

ref: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
text: M le basi ate Arabba tɛŋka a chim laalaakomiba dɛ ka jigi. Ammon tɛŋka ale chim piisa vuusum jigi. Ate ni yaa seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.

ref: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
text: M le pai m pagrimu a nye ale ni. M le pai ni a te tɛŋsaŋa ase tuilum ŋanta ate ba kɔlim kpaliŋ po la. Mi le duisi ni basi ate ni kan ŋman chim tɛŋŋa. M le kaasi ni ate ni seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.>>

ref: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
text: <<Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, ayen Moab ale Edom a weeni kama ayen Juda demma a nye ase ka tɛŋ sinsila la.

ref: So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim.
text: Dila nyiŋ mi a yaali m yeeri ka tɛŋ sii ale a lik Moab banaŋa la, tɛŋ maŋsaŋa ale bo ka po la. Si le Bet Jesimot ale Baal Meon ale Kiriataim.

ref: The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever,
text: Ate si yaa pai Moab ale Ammon demma meena a te kori geŋka nuruma ate ba soa ba. Moab a kan ŋman chim tɛŋŋa ale Ammon demma meena.

ref: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
text: Dila nyiŋ m le namsi Moab demma ate ba seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.>>

ref: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. <Edom a tuni Juda nuruma. Edom nye kama kaasi dila nyiŋ.

ref: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
text: Dila la, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, M le pai m pagrimu a nye ale Edom. M le ko nurubiik meena ale duŋsaŋa ale boro la. M le kaasi Edom a zaani Teman a ga paari Dedan. Ba le kpi kpaliŋka po.

ref: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
text: Mi le pai m nuruma Izirali a tuni Edom. Izirali demma ale nye Edom demma dii ate mi suinni a yaali la. Ate Edom demma a seba m le a tuni ba le diila. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>

ref: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
text: <<Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, <Filistia demma a pai ka kisika a tuni Juda. Ba kisika nyiŋ ba nye ka nyiŋbiiri ayen ba kaasi Juda.

ref: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
text: Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. M le pai m pagrimu a nye ale Filistia demma. M le ko Keret demma abe m ko baai ale bo nyakpiemu nɔi la.

ref: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
text: M le namsi ba ale m suipuurumu abe m nye wie kpiema a tuni ba. Ate ba seba ayen Mi ale Naawen a nye ba dila.>>

ref: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
text: Bena pi ale dinyi wa po, chiik kaai ale a piilim la piilimka dai, Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, Taaya tɛŋka demma a biisi a kaasi Jerusalem kama. Ayen tɛŋ kaai ale jam a gerim ale tɛŋsa la a kaasi ya. Yɔgyɔgla de tama tɛŋka a baga a chim geruŋku num jigi kama. Jerusalem ale tɔlim kaasi la, ti baga a nya ligra kama.

ref: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
text: Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Mi ta ka chaab ale nama Taaya demma. M le basi ate tɛŋsa yega a siti ni ase nyakpiemu ale yiti a nak tɛŋka kunkɔŋni diila.

ref: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
text: Ba le kaasi Taaya parisaŋa abe ba nak ba yie woŋtaŋa a lɔnsi. M le chuiri ba ŋan kaasimaŋa a basi abe m ge ba jassi ase puŋ la.

ref: where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed
text: Taaya ale chim ka tɛŋ kaai ale bo nyiam suŋsuŋ la ate jum yigrisa a danni ba ŋmaasa. Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni. Tɛŋsaŋa ale zu ŋan maŋsa Taaya po.

ref: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Taaya tɛŋ fiisaŋa ale bo nyiamu nɔi la, ale kaasi kpaliŋka po. Ate ni seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
text: <<Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. M le ta naab a nyini wiilukku geŋ a jam ate wa siti Taaya. Wala ale Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar. Wa ka nalima naab wusuma ale torokoba ale wusum duerisa ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba boari.

ref: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
text: Wa le nye kpaliŋ a kaasi ni tɛŋ fiisaŋa ale bo nyiamu po bu nɔi la. Wa le zɔk zɔga a siti ni. Wa le pai tanta a dueni bimbimi a jueli parisaŋa ŋmai. Wa le pai peema ŋanchɔgsinta a siti ni.

ref: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
text: Wa le ta da biga a jam chubi ni tɛŋka parisaŋa, abe wa wɛ ni yie woŋtaŋa ale kuta.

ref: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
text: Wa wusumaŋa ale piisi dii nna yegayega la ŋa nyuŋku ale lik ni. Wusum duerisaŋa, torokoma nuemka ale basi ate ni parisaŋa a choa. Babilon naawa ale jo ni tɛŋka po ase nuruba ale va parisa lo ka jigi a jo tɛŋ po diila.

ref: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
text: Wa wusumaŋa naŋsabaŋa ale tabi va ni suitaŋa. Wa le ko ni tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale gebik. Ni ŋan pagri ŋaai meena ale yik ni yeeŋa ta la ale lo tɛŋ.

ref: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
text: Wa nuruma mɛ ale pai ni le jigsi ale ŋan baai la a ta cheŋ abe wa zu ŋan baai ni a da la. Ba le wɛ ni parisaŋa abe ba kaasi ni yie naliŋsaŋa. Ba le yuk ni tanaŋa, ale ni daataŋa, ale ni ŋan baai ale kan ta kiri la a basi nyakpiemu po.

ref: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
text: M kan te ni ŋman lenni yiila. Ni kpantaŋa yiilaŋa ni kan ŋman wom diipo diipo.

ref: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
text: M le basi ni ka nna jassi ase puŋ ale dua la, ate ni chim juijui ate ba a danni ŋmaasa du la. Ba kan ŋman se ka, dii nyiŋla, mi Naawen ale biisi. Ka Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni dila.

ref: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
text: Ate niŋdeerɔma meena ale bo nyiamu nɔi la ale basi ba naamu zukpagliksaŋa. Ba le yeeri ba garuk naliŋsaŋa ate ba yɔk la, ate yɔgsum ale ta ba. Ba le kali tɛŋ ate ba nyiŋsa a kasim a gɔk. Ba dan nya fu ku le cha ba.

ref: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
text: Yɔgyɔgla de nuru baai ale bo nyiamu nɔi la nyiŋsa ale a gɔk, Yɔgyɔgla de fi yaa lo ya. Nyiamu po tɛŋsaŋa kpaziim ale a nak dii nyiŋla ba nak dɛ fu kama.>

ref: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
text: Dila po m le basi ate ni siŋ kpiluŋ a ga gum baai ale kpi dipodipo la po. M le basi ate ni bo kpiluŋ ale kpiema ase jigsi ŋaai ale kaasi la. Ni kan ŋman nyini dula jamu yaase ni nya jigi tɛŋzuk a bo ale nuru vuuta ŋmana.

ref: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Nuru yonta kpaziim ale nak ale dii ale nye ni la, ate ku yaa kpeglim ale ni. Nuruba ale gisi ni alege ba kan ŋman nya ni diipo. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The Lord said:
text: Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, Pa Taaya tɛŋka a lenni kuun yiili.

ref: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
text: Weeni Taaya ale ta ŋaaruŋta zaana jigi a te nyakpiemu la, ayen ka le chim geruŋ jigi a te tɛŋsa yega ale nyiamu nɔi nuruma. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. <Taaya fi weeni kama ayen, <<Mi a nye ase ŋaaruŋ naluŋ la.>>

ref: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
text: Fi jam bo ka yeri nya kpientaŋa zuk. Fi seerɔma a basi ate fi nalimu a nye chekki.

ref: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
text: Fi tapaŋŋa ba pai ka dapeelita tiisa ale bo Yermon guuku zuk la a nye. Ba pai ka Lebanon nyunyoŋ a nye ŋaaruŋku da woŋtaŋa ale ti wen la a te fu.

ref: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
text: Gat tii ate ba baali ale ŋmirisi la ate ba pai maa nye ŋaaruŋtaŋa la a nyini ka Ejipiti, a yaa chim tikti a te ni. Garuk kuui ale lik ŋaaruŋku tɛŋka a te yɔgsum la, ka sobluk ale mɔnuŋ a nyini Saipurus ale bo nyiamu suŋsuŋ la.

ref: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
text: << <Persia dem, ale Liidiya dem, ale Put dem meena a jam bo ka nama nyiam po tugurik tɔŋdɔma po, a pai ba peema ŋanchɔgsintaŋa ale zuk chinaŋa a yik ni gauŋ. Ba jam basi kama ate ni nala.

ref: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
text: Arvad dem ale Yelek dem ale jam gilim ni tɛŋka parisaŋa a limisi. Gammad dem ale jam za ni gbirimaŋa zuima a pai ba peema ŋanchɔgsintaŋa a yik saasaŋa nyiŋ. A yaa basi ate ni nalimu a chiib boro chekki.

ref: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
text: << <Tarsis demma a jam a gerim kama ale ni, ni ale jigsi la nyiŋ. Ba pai ka kpana ale kuta tɔgatɔga a tagri ni ŋantaŋa.

ref: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
text: << <Javan dem ale Mesek dem ale Tubal dem a jam a gerim kama ale ni. Ba jam pai ka yɔm ale kuta a tagri ni ŋantaŋa.

ref: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
text: << <Dedan demma a jam a gerim kama ale ni. Tɛŋ sii ale bo nyaata nɔi la a jam ka nama yaba, ate ba ta yauk nyina ale da gaab daata a jam a tuni ni.

ref: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
text: << <Juda ale Izirali demma a gerim kama ale ni. Ba pai ka Minnit tɛŋka ŋanbie ale ŋanmasisa ale siita ale kpaam ale kpa buui ale ka tiim la a tagri ni ŋantaŋa.

ref: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
text: << <Damasikus demma a jam a gerim kama ale ni dii nyiŋla ni ta ka ŋanta yegayega ale jigsi. Ba pai ka Yelbon daam ale piisa kɔbta a nyini Zayar tɛŋka a tagri ni ŋantaŋa.

ref: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
text: << <Siiba ale Araamaya geruŋdɔma a jam a gerim kama ale ni. Ba jam pai ka ŋan baai nyum ale masa, ale tintain naliŋsa ale ligmɔniŋ a tagri ni ŋantaŋa.

ref: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
text: << <Yaran ale Kanne ale Eden nuruma, ale Siiba ale Assur ale Kilmad geruŋdɔma a jam a gerim kama ale ni.

ref: and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope.
text: Ba jam pai ka garuk maŋsa, garuk sobta, garuk tii ate ba yɔk a ŋmirisi, diina tɛŋ ŋanpatinta ale miik pagrisa a tagri ni ŋantaŋa.

ref: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
text: << <Tarsis ŋaaruŋ tii ale jam a gerim la ale a ji ni ŋantaŋa ate ni a da la. Ni jam a nye ase ka ŋaaruŋ ate ŋan dobra a sueri a bo nyiamu suŋsuŋ la.

ref: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
text: Nuru baai ale bo kunkɔŋni la nyiŋsa a gɔk kama, ba le wom baai ale bo ŋaaruŋku po kaarik la.

ref: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
text: Baai meena ale a damu la a basi ba ŋaaruŋtaŋa. Nyiam nuruma ale baai meena ale bo ŋaaruŋ yonta po la a za kunkɔŋni.

ref: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
text: Ba yaa kaari ate ku a jueli ni nyiŋ. A kaari nna yegayega. A yuk tanta a basi ba zuima po ale a bilim buntuem po a sak ba sue ale kaasi diila.

ref: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
text: Ba le kaari ate ku a jueli la, ba yaa yi kuun yiili ayen, Ba an kaasi waai ase Taaya ate nyakpiemu a gilim ka diila.

ref: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
text: Alege nyakpiemu a wɛ fi ŋaaruŋku ate ku siŋ paari tɛŋ. Fi ŋantaŋa ale nuruma meena a siŋ tɛŋ ale ku.

ref: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
text: Baai meena ale bo kunkɔŋni la ku cha ba dii meena ale nye fu la. Ba nalimaŋa kasim a chali yɔgsum. Ba nyaasimu abe le a sak ba yɔgsummu.

ref: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
text: Geruŋdɔma ale bo tɛŋsaŋa po la a yaa yeesi fu. Fi yaa nueri fi niŋ. Fi cheŋ kama feritete.> >>

ref: The Lord God said:
text: Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, weeni Taaya niŋdeerɔwa ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Ayen fi kanjantaŋa nyiŋ fi a weeni ayen fi ka wen. Mi kali kan wen naam zuk nyakpientaŋa suŋsuŋ. Fi a poli ayen fi ta ka yam ase wen la, alege fi ka saalɔbiik, daa wen ya.

ref: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
text: Fi va fi yammu ale fi wie miŋka nyiŋ a jigsi kama. A nya ligmɔniŋ ale kpana a yaa pai dueni fi ŋanta diinaŋa po.

ref: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
text: Fi le seba geruŋ la nyiŋ fi jigsi ka nna yegayega. Fi ta ka kanjanta fi jigsika nyiŋ.

ref: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
text: << <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Fi a poli ayen fi ta ka yam ase wen la,

ref: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
text: Ba le ko fu. Fi kummu ale nye ase ka baai ate ba ko a nyakpiem po la.

ref: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
text: Ba dan boro a ko fu, fi kan ŋman baga a weeni ayen fi ka wen ya. Fi ya le chim ka nurubiik daa wen ya ase ba nin boro a ko fu.

ref: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
text: Fi le kpi ase ka daŋta nyɔnɔ la. Nicham ale ba ko fu. Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi.

ref: The Lord said:
text: Naawen a biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, yi kuun yiili a te Taaya naawa. Weeni ayen Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Fi ale jam a sak wa nalimu meena ate nuruba a nya. Fi jam ta ka yam ale nalim maŋ.

ref: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
text: Mi yaa lueri javuk ayen wa a limisi fu. A pai fu basi Naawen tuilum guuku zuk. Ate fi a cheŋ tintanaŋa ŋaai ale a nyaksi ase bolim la po.

ref: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
text: Fi boka a jam nala kama ale yɔrisi fi nyeka danni ate biem a yaa jo fu ŋaaŋnyiŋ.

ref: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
text: Fi le a gerim ale niŋniŋ tɛŋsa la nyiŋ fi yaa zamsi ba nyeka tuemu a tom kaasi. Mi yaa pai fu Naawen guuku zuk a yuk basi ate fi nya chivie. Ate javuk kuui ale a nya fu zuk la a yaa fɛ yeeri fu tintana ŋaai ale a nyaksi la po.

ref: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
text: Fi ta ka kanjanta nna yegayega fi nalimu nyiŋ. Fi kaasi fi yammu kama fi zulaŋa nyiŋ. Mi yaa pai fu yuk basi tɛŋ, ate ku sak nalim yonta yam.

ref: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
text: Fi an zuli fi puusaŋa jigini fi wabaataŋa yegayega ale fi venta geruŋku nyiŋ. Ate mi yaa ju juijui ate fi boro la ate bolimu a dɛ meena. Ate mi basi ate fi chim buntuem tɛŋka ate waai meena a nya.

ref: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
text: Tɛŋ sii meena ale sebi fu la, ku cha ba. Fi namsika a bie ka yega, ate fi cheŋ nna feritete.> >>

ref: The Lord said:
text: Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, zak nya Saidon tɛŋka a mooli te ka.

ref: and tell its people: I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy.
text: Weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ayen, mi ta ka chaab ale Saidon, m be le sak m zulaŋa ni suŋsuŋ. M dan namsi Saidon, nuruba le seba ayen Mi ale Naawen. M le namisi ba abe m sak ba ayen mi welema kama.

ref: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
text: M le te nyiŋtuila a jam Saidon, ate ziim a chali ka suitaŋa niŋ. Baai ale nya tueta Saidon po la ale kpi abe ba siti ba jiŋŋa meena. Ate ba yaa seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.

ref: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
text: << <Tɛŋ sii ale moata la a kan ŋman chim munsa yaase ŋan baai ale kpari a maŋŋa ate ba namsi Izirali. Ate ba seba ayen Mi ale Nyɔnɔwa Naawen.

ref: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
text: << <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Izirali demma ale waaŋ bo tɛŋsaŋa la, m le tigsi ba. M le sak m tuilummu ase tɛŋsaŋa a nin nya mi ale nye dii a te m nuruma la. Ate ba yaa bo badek tɛŋka po, tɛŋ kaai ate mi a pai te m tomteerɔwa Jekob la.

ref: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
text: Ba le boro ale nyiŋyɔgsa abe ba sɛ yie abe ba vuk tiisa. Ba le boro ale nyiŋyɔgsa tɛŋsaŋa namsika ŋaaŋnyiŋ. Tɛŋ sii meena ale kisi ba a gilim ba la. Ate ba seba ayen Mi ale Naawen ba Wen.> >>

ref: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
text: Ba le yik tama a ta cheŋ la ben dii ale nye tama bena pi la, chiisa piwa po ka daa pi ale ŋaye dai ate Naawen a biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, zak nya Faaro Ejipiti naawa a mooli te wa le Ejipiti meena.

ref: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
text: Weeni wa ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Mi ta ka chaab ale fi Faaro Ejipiti naawa. Fi a nye ase ka ŋauk tanjaŋini ale bo Nile benni po la. Fi weeni ayen Nile benni ka mi ale soa mi nye di a te ka m dek.

ref: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
text: Alege m le pai gɔtik a nyo fi chikpeeŋa po, ate m basi ate jumaŋa ale bo Nile benni po la a maŋ fi ganaŋa. M le dari fu yeeri fi belaŋa po ale juma ŋaai meena ale maŋ fi ganaŋa la.

ref: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
text: M le pai fu basi gɔnni po, fi ale fi jumaŋa meena ale bo fi belaŋa po la. Ni le bo kunkoŋŋa, ba kan pai ni ba be kan gu ni. M pai ni te ka gɔi duŋsaŋa ale wenzuk nuinsaŋa ayen si dɛ ni.

ref: Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord. You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick.
text: Ate nuruma meena ale bo Ejipiti la a seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen. Izirali a nye ka nyiŋbiiri a maŋ ni ayen ba nya maarika alege ni a nye ase ka kinkari dagbiok la.

ref: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
text: Ba le yik fi ale nisa la, fi wɛ kama a chub ba ŋmankpalaŋa a cheeri. Ba le sali fu la, fi wɛ kama ate ba ŋaaŋsaŋa a vuri.

ref: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
text: << <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. M le basi ate dachaasa a siti fu a ko fi nuruma ale fi duŋsaŋa.

ref: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
text: Ejipiti ale chim ka tɛŋ koruk a doa. Ate ba yaa seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen. Dii nyiŋla fi weeni kama ayen, <<Nile benni ka mi ale soa, mi abe le nye di.

ref: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
text: Mi ta ka chaab ale fu ale fi belaŋa. M le kaasi Ejipiti tɛŋka abe m basi ate ka chim tɛŋ koruk a nyini Migdol ale bo wiiluk geŋ la a ga paari Aswan ale bo yeseok geŋ la, a ta ga paari Kus tɛŋ banni.

ref: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
text: Nuru yaase duŋ a kan cheŋ va du a taamu, waai abe kan bo Ejipiti tɛŋka po a ga paari bena pisinaansi.

ref: They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom
text: M le ta Ejipiti demma ba yik la a ŋmani. M le te ba ŋmani Patros ba le nyini juijui la. Ba yaa le chim tɛŋ wobsik.

ref: and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past.
text: Ka le chim tɛŋ wobsik, ka kan ŋman ta pagrim tɛŋ yonsa zuwa. M le basi ate ka ŋmasi wobsa ka kan ta pagrim a ŋma nya tɛŋ yonsa zuwa.

ref: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
text: Izirali demma a kan ŋma nya Ejipiti a yaali maarika. Ejipiti demma ninammu ale teeri Izirali ba biemu ba le jam cheemu a nya Ejipiti a yaali maarika la. Ate ba yaa seba ayen Mi ale Nyɔnɔwa Naawen.> >>

ref: Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
text: Ba le jam yik ti ta cheŋ la, bena pisiye ale ŋayopɔiwa po, piilimka chiika ka piilimka dai, Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma a chiib kpaliŋ kama ale Taaya. Tugurik tɔŋdɔ meena zuk a jam kpa kama ate ŋmankpala meena a muli. Alege Nebukadnezzar ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma an nya jaab jaab ba le kpaliŋ ale Taaya.

ref: So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops.
text: Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Mi le pai Ejipiti tɛŋka a te Nebukadnezzar Babilon naawa. Mi le ta Ejipiti nuruma a cheŋ ate wa le jigsi ale ŋan baai meena a chim tugurik tɔŋdɔma tutuna la.

ref: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Nebukadnezzar ale tom nna yegayega a te mu la nyiŋ m le pai Ejipiti tɛŋka a te wa ase tutuna la. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
text: <<Dila powa m le ŋman basi ate Izirali nya pagrim, ate m yaa te fi Ezekiel a biisi a te ba. Ate ba seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.>>

ref: The Lord said:
text: Naawen a biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, mooli a weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Kaari a weeni ayen, Da beoku danni a cheena.

ref: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
text: Danni a moata, Naawen buusa danni a moata. Di za di chim ka buusa dai ale diipo ate wa le bo tɛŋsaŋa buusa la.

ref: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
text: Dachiak ale siti Ejipiti, ate Kus nyiŋ a gɔk ale yɔgsum. Koka a dan piilim Ejipiti, wa le jigsi ale ŋan baai la ba le pai ta cheŋ, ate wa nyubaŋa meena a wɛ lo.

ref: Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle.
text: Kus ale Put ale Liidiya ale Arabia meena ale Kub ale mi nuruma ale nye nɔiyeŋka la ale kpi kpaliŋka po ale Ejipiti.

ref: All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: << <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, Baai ale kpaliŋ a maari Ejipiti la ale kpi. Pagrim buui ate wa ta kanjantaŋa ale bu la ale bɛ. Nuruma ale bo Ejipiti la ale kpi kpaliŋka po a nyini Migdol ale bo wiiluk geŋka la a ga paari Aswan ale bo yeseok geŋka la. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
text: << <Si le chim tɛŋ sii ate ba je si basi. Ejipiti tɛŋsa ale kaasi kama a bie a doa.

ref: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Ate ba yaa seba ayen Mi ale Naawen ase m nin ju Ejipiti ale bolim ate tɛŋ sii meena ale a maari ba la a kaasi.

ref: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
text: << <Dila po m le tom nuruba ale ŋaaruŋta ate ba nyigsi Kus ale a poli ayen wari a kan daani ba la. M dan boro a namsi Ejipiti, Kus nuruma nyiŋsa ale gɔk ate yɔgsum yik ba. Da dila danni abe za di jam kama.

ref: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
text: << <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. M le ko nuruba yega Ejipiti po ale Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar pagrim.

ref: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
text: M le basi ate Nile beli naŋsaŋa meena a kpeeri a ko, ate mi yaa pai tɛŋka a da te nuru baata. M le basi ate nicham pai ba pagrim a kaasi tɛŋka ale jaab meena ale bo ka po la. Mi Naawen ale biisi.

ref: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
text: << <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. M le kaasi bɔgtaŋa abe m pai wenaŋa ŋanmɛɛntaŋa Memfis tɛŋka po a ta cheŋ. Niŋdeerɔ a kan ŋman bo Ejipiti tɛŋka po. M le basi a te yɔgsum a bo Ejipiti tɛŋka meena po.

ref: The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed!
text: M le basi ate tɛŋka Patros a doa koruk abe m ju bolim Zoan abe m namsi Tebes.

ref: The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
text: M le kpiiri m suipuurumu a basi Sin zuk. Dula ale chim Ejipiti jigi pagrik. M le basi ate nuruba yegayega Tebes po a kpi.

ref: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
text: M le ju Ejipiti ale bolim Sin ale bo ka nyiŋ doma po. Tebes parisaŋa ale wɛ lo. Memfis ale kasim ta ka daanika daa meena.

ref: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
text: On ale Pi Beset bi paalukku ale kpi kpaliŋ po abe ba yik ba gela a ta cheŋ.

ref: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
text: Dai dii dai ate mi a wɛ Ejipiti pagrimu la Tayapanes po ku le chim legi. Ate wa kan ŋman ta kanjanta ale wa pagrimu. Chiŋmari ale lik Ejipiti ate ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ba yik ta cheŋ.

ref: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
text: Dila la m le namsi Ejipiti ate ba seba ayen mi ka Naawen.> >>

ref: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
text: Ba le jam yik ti ta cheŋ la, bena pi ale dinyi wa po, chiik kaai ale a piilim la ka daa ŋayopɔi dai ate Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, mi wɛ Ejipiti naawa Faaro nisaŋa ale pagra la kama. Ban pobi si dila nyiŋ si kan tomu. Ba an vili si ale garuk pali ya, dila nyiŋ si kan pagra a yik gebik kpaliŋ po.

ref: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
text: Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi ta ka chaab ale Ejipiti naawa Faaro. M le wɛ wa nisimaŋa. M le wɛ sii le pagra la ale sii ale wɛ la meena. Abe m basi ate gebika nyini wa nisaŋa po lo tɛŋ.

ref: and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
text: M le basi ate Ejipiti demma a waaŋ tɛŋsaŋa po meena. Ba le waaŋ bo tɛŋsa tɔgatɔga po.

ref: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
text: Dila la m le basi ate Babilon naawa nisaŋa a pagra alege Faaro nisaŋa kan pagra. M dan pai gebika a nyo Babilon naawa nisa po ate wa siti Ejipiti naawa nuruba ale seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
text: Ate m yaa basi ate Ejipiti demma a waaŋ a bo tɛŋsa tɔgatɔga po. Ate ba seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
text: Ba le jam yik ti ta cheŋ la bena pi ale dinyi wa po chiisa sitawa po ka piilimka dai ate Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, weeni sak Ejipiti naawa Faaro ale wa nuruma ayen, <Nuru karo a magsi chaab ale fu ale fi naamu.

ref: There was once a cedar tree in Lebanon with large, strong branches reaching to the sky.
text: Assiria jam a nye ase ka Lebanon nyunyoŋ la. Ate bu naŋsaŋa a nala a te gɔnni yɔgsum. Bu jam wɔŋa kama, a jueli a bo chiŋmaaŋa po.

ref: This tree had plenty of water to help it grow tall, and nearby streams watered the other trees in the forest.
text: Nyiam yegayega ale jam basi ate tiimu a chim. Nya tii ale nyini tɛŋ a jueli a basi ate bu naŋsa a te ti sinsila ale bo tɛŋka nakpaasaŋa la.

ref: But this tree towered over those other trees, and its branches grew long and thick.
text: Dila nyiŋ tiimu jam wɔŋa kama a gaam nakpaasaŋa tiisaŋa meena. Bu suŋsuŋ naŋsaŋa a wɔŋa kama ale biga nyiamu yegayekka nyiŋ.

ref: Birds built nests in its branches, and animals were born beneath it. People from all nations lived in the shade of this strong tree.
text: Wenzuk nuinsaŋa meena yaa yɔk si tugta tiimu suŋsuŋ naŋsa zuk. Gɔi duŋsaŋa meena a jam bu tɛŋ a biak. Tɛŋ kpieŋsa meena a jam bo ka tiimu yɔgsummu po.

ref: It had beautiful, long branches, and its roots found water deep in the soil.
text: Tiimu jam zuak kama ale nala ale bu naŋ woŋsaŋa, dii nyiŋla bu tɛŋ naŋsaŋa a siŋ paari ka tɛŋ a nya nyiam yegayega.

ref: None of the cedar trees in my garden of Eden were as beautiful as this tree; no tree of any kind had such long branches.
text: Nyunyoŋta tiisaŋa ale jam bo Naawen talimu po la an jam soa ase tiimu dɛ ale soa diila. Damɔnta tiisaŋa a jam ka suŋsuŋ naŋ kpieŋsa dila. Dapeelita tiisaŋa a jam ka naŋ sila chaaba. Tiib a jam ka Naawen tiisaŋa po a nala ase tiimu dɛ la.

ref: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
text: Mi basi kama ate bu nala ale naŋsa yega, ate Eden tiisaŋa ale bo Naawen tiisaŋa po la a yaali ayen si nye ase bu la.

ref: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
text: << <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Tiimu chim kama wɔŋa. Ate bu ŋmanni paari chiŋmaaŋa. Ate bu yaa ta kanjanta bu woglimmu nyiŋ.

ref: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
text: Mi yaa pai bu te tɛŋsaŋa kpagi kpienni ayen wa namsi bu. Bu le bie la nyiŋ, mi yaa yeeri bu.

ref: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
text: Tɛŋ kaai nyeka ale tua la po yaa che bu lɔnsi a basi bu ate bu doa. Tiimu naŋsaŋa a yaa lo guutaŋa zuima ale vaasaŋa po meena, ate bu suŋsuŋ naŋsaŋa ale wɛ la a bo tɛŋka va sii ale limisa la po meena. Tɛŋsaŋa meena deri basi bu yɔgsummu.

ref: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
text: Wenzukku nuinsaŋa a yaa bo tiimu ale lo la zuk. Gɔi duŋsaŋa a bo tiimu naŋsaŋa ale lo la po.

ref: Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
text: Dila nyiŋ ti sii ale za nyiamu nɔi a chim la a kan ta kanjanta ayen si ale wɔŋa. Si ŋmaaŋa a kan paari chiŋmaaŋa. Ti sii buuni ale a nya nyiam la a kan chim a wɔŋa dila, dii nyiŋla si meena a magsi ka si kpi a siŋ tɛŋ. Si meena ale bo ale ka nuru baai ale kpi a cheŋ kpiluŋ la.

ref: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
text: << <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Da dii danni ate tiimu a cheŋ kpiluŋ la, mi basi kama ate bulisaŋa meena a kaari ate ku a jueli. Mi lik si kama alege yik belaŋa nyaataŋa ate nyaataŋa a kan chali. Mi yaa jo Lebanon ale garuk sobluk ayen ku sak wa sui ale kaasi ale tiib kpiemu la. Tiisaŋa meena ale bo nakpaasaŋa la sui a kaasi dila nyiŋ.

ref: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
text: Tɛŋsaŋa ale wom mi ale basi ate tiimu a lo a cheŋ kpiluŋ la, yɔgsum yaa yik si ate si a choa. Bu cheŋ a ga gum ka baai ale siŋ kpiluŋ la po. Ate Eden tiisaŋa meena ale Lebanon tiib maŋsaŋa meena, ale ti sii meena ale a nya nyiam nalimnyiini la sui a yɔk kpiluŋ ale bo tɛŋ la.

ref: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
text: Tiisaŋa de meena a maa siŋ ka kpiluŋ ale tiib kpiemu. Ba gum ka baai ate ba ko kpaliŋ po la ale baai ale bo tɛŋsaŋa po a jam bo tiib kpiemu de yɔgsummu po la.

ref: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: << <Dila la tiib a ka Eden a magsi chaab ale fu. Ejipiti fi le fi zuaka ale fi zulaŋa meena fi siŋ kpiluŋ a gum Eden tiisaŋa po. Fi le duak ale nuru daŋtisa ate ba ko ba kpaliŋ po la. Faaro wie ale nna. Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>

ref: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
text: Ba le yik tama ta cheŋ la, bena pi ale ŋayewa chiisa pi ale siyewa piilimka danni ate Naawen yaa biisi ale mi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying: You act like a lion roaming the earth; but you are nothing more than a crocodile in a river, churning up muddy water with your feet.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, pai Ejipiti naawa Faaro a siak kuun yiili. Weeni wa ayen, <Fi a nye ase ka gbeŋli biik la tɛŋsaŋa po. Fi a nye ase ka ŋauk la nyakpientaŋa po. Fi kasim a fɔbi ka nanpansa belaŋa po, ale a damu nyiamu ale fi naŋsaŋa. A basi ate belaŋa a chim bagta.

ref: King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore.
text: << <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, ayen m le yuk m ŋmiaka a vi fi zuk, a yaa basi ate nuru boari a dari fu ale ŋmiaka a ta jueli.

ref: I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh.
text: Ate m yaa yuk fu ate fi jueli lo kunkɔŋni. M le basi ate wenzuk nuinsaŋa a vuusi fi zuk abe tɛŋzuk duŋsaŋa a dɛ fu a ga chak.

ref: I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys,
text: M le zarinti fi nyiŋ lammu guutaŋa zuima abe kab tii ale tali m pai sueri vaasaŋa.

ref: and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams.
text: M le basi ate fi ziimu a nyini a chali yɔk tɛŋka ale guutaŋa meena, ate va sii ale limisi la fi nyiŋ lammu a sueri.

ref: I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining.
text: Mi dan basi ate fi muriŋ bɛ, m yaa le lik wenni abe m basi ate chiŋmarisaŋa a lik. M le lik wenbinni ale chiŋmanni ate chiika a kan ŋma nyaksi.

ref: The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: M le lik ŋan baai meena ale bo wenzukku a nyaksi la. A basi ate legi a jam tɛŋka zuk. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you.
text: M dan basi ate ba yik ni ta cheŋ tɛŋ yonsa sii ate ni zɛ si la yɔgsum ale yik nuruba yega.

ref: They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
text: M le basi ate ni wie a cha nuruba. Nama nyiŋ ba nalimaŋa nyiŋsa ale kasim a gɔk ase m nin yuk m gebika ba niŋ. Da dii dai ate fi a lo la, ba nyiŋsa ale kasim a gɔk kama. Naab meena ale kasim a chali ka yɔgsum wadek nyuvuri nyiŋ.

ref: The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt!
text: << <Dila Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Babilon naawa ale siti ni ale wa gebika.

ref: Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed.
text: M le basi ate tugurik tɔŋdɔ pagrisa a ko fi nuruma ale gebisa a dueni. Wa dii ale di bie tɛŋka po. Ba le kaasi Ejipiti kanjantaŋa ale ka nuruma meena.

ref: I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water.
text: M le ko Ejipiti niiŋa meena ale bo nyiam yegayega nɔi la. Nurubiik naŋ a kan damu nyiamu, naab mɛ naŋsabi a kan pɔti nyiamu ŋmana.

ref: The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Dila la m le basi ate Ejipiti demma nyiamu a nye cheri. M le basi ate ba nyiamu a chali nalimnyiini ale kpaam. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi.

ref: Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
text: M dan basi ate Ejipiti a chim tɛŋ koruk alege pai jaab meena ale bo tɛŋka po la, ale ko baai meena ale bo Ejipiti la, ba yaa le seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.>

ref: This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. A Sad Ending for Egypt
text: <<Kuun yi dii ate nuruba ale yi te Ejipiti la ale nna. Tɛŋsaŋa nipooma ale ba yi di. Ba le yi kuun yiili a te Ejipiti ale ka nuruma. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.>>

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, kum a te Ejipiti nuruma. Ta Ejipiti a jam ale tɛŋ pagrisaŋa nipooma meena. Ta ba siŋ jam kpiluŋ ate ba gum kpiema po.

ref: Say to them: You may be more beautiful than the people of other nations, but you will also die and join the godless in the world below.
text: Weeni ba ayen, <Nama a nala a gaam nuru yonta kama? Ni le cheŋ kpiluŋ a ga duak gum baai ale kan seba Naawen la po.>

ref: You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you.
text: Ejipiti demma ale lo a gum baai ate ba ko kpaliŋka po la. Gebik ale gomsi magsi ayen ka ko ba.

ref: The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
text: ate ba boositaŋa a bo kpiluŋ kauk kuui ale limisa la. Ka tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena a kpi kama kpaliŋka po ate ba boositaŋa a gilim ka boosuku. Ba le bo tɛŋzuk la, ba nyigsi nuruba, alege yɔgyɔgla de ba ko ba meena kpaliŋka po.

ref: The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
text: Iilam a dua kama ale baai meena ate ba ko kpaliŋ ka po la. Ka tugurik tɔŋdɔma boositaŋa meena a gilim ka kama. Iilam nuruma a daŋ kama, ate ba ko ba. Ba jam nyigsi nuruba ba le diem jam bo tɛŋzuk la. Alege yɔgyɔgla de ba le cheŋ kpiluŋ ale chivie. Ba boositaŋa a bo le ka baai ate ba jam ko la.

ref: The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle.
text: <<Mesek ale Tubal a bo ka dula ate ka tugurik tɔŋdɔma boositaŋa a gilim ka. Ba meena a daŋ kama ate ba ko ba kpaliŋka po. Ba mɛ jam nyigsi nuruba ba le jam bo tɛŋzuk de la.

ref: They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
text: Alege ba an gu ba ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba baai ate ba jam ko kpaliŋka po dipodipo la. Ba la jam cheŋ ka kpiluŋ ale ba kpiluŋ kɔlimaŋa. Tugurik tɔŋdɔma dɛ nyiem kpagli ba gebisaŋa alege pai ŋan baai ate ba ta a chɔgsi peema la a vi pai zuk. Tugurik tɔŋdɔba pagrisaŋa de ale jam bo tɛŋzuk la jam a nyigsi ka nuruba.

ref: You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
text: <<Fi Faaro ba le kaasi fu ate fi dua ale biem nyam baai ate ba ko ba kpaliŋ po la.

ref: The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
text: <<Edom mɛ bo ka dula ale ka nalimaŋa ale niŋdeerɔma meena. Ba jam pagra kama alege yɔgyɔgla de ba kpi kama dua ale baai ate ba ko kpaliŋka po la, baai ale ka biem nyam, baai ale cheŋ kpiluŋ.

ref: The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
text: <<Wiiluk geŋka kpaŋŋa meena ale Saidon demma a bo ka dula. Ba pagrimu a nyigsi ka nuruba alege ba cheŋ ale baai ate ba ko la ale chivie. Ba ka biem nyam, a dua ale baai ate ba ko kpaliŋka po la. Ba ta ba chivieŋa a cheŋ ale baai ale siŋ kpiluŋ la.

ref: The Lord God says: When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering.
text: <<Ejipiti naawa Faaro ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale nya baai ate ba ko kpaliŋka po la. Ate wa sui yaa yɔk ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena ate ba ko kpaliŋka po la. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Mi basi kama ate nuruba a chali Ejipiti naawa yɔgsum wa le diem bo tɛŋzuk la. Alege wa ale wa nuruma meena ale duak gum biem nyama po, baai ate ba ko ba kpaliŋka po la. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming.
text: ate wa nya gebika a cheen ka ta chaab ale tɛŋka ate wa peeri damuniŋ a kaam nuruma,

ref: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
text: Ba le yik tama a ta cheŋ la bena pi ale ŋayewa po, chiisa piika po ka daa ŋanu danni nuru yaa vari nyini Jerusalem a jam mi jigi a weeni ayen, <<Tɛŋka a lo kama.>>

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying: Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, biisi a te fi tɛŋka demma a weeni ba ayen, <M dan ta gebika jam ta chaab ale tɛŋ, ate tɛŋka demma a lueri ba nidoama wanyi ate wa chim limisidɔ,

ref: If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
text: Wa le toalim wom damuniŋka kumsa alege an siak kaamka la, wa ziimu ale bo ka wadek zuk. Wa dan siak kaamka kama, wa ti vari wadek a basi kama.

ref: But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
text: Alege limisidɔwa a dan nya gebika a cheena alege an peeri damuniŋka a kaam nuruma ate gebika a jam pa ba wanyi nyuvuri, nuru wala ba pa wa ta cheŋ ka wa biemu nyiŋ, alege mi le yik limisidɔwa a bek nuruwa ziimu nyiŋ.>

ref: Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, mi nye fu ka limisidɔ a te Izirali yenni. Dila nyiŋ wom wa dii ate mi a biisi la a pa kaamka mi jigi a te ba.

ref: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death.
text: Mi a dan weeni gaasa nyɔnɔwa ayen, <Gaasa nyɔnɔ, fi le sum kpi,> ate fi an biisi ate ku nyini a yeeri wa wa suitaŋa po, gaasa nyɔnɔ wala ale kpi wa biemu nyiŋ, ate m yik fu a bek wa ziimu nyiŋ.

ref: If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent. The Lord Is Always Fair (Ezekiel
text: Alege fi dan kaam gaasa nuruwa ayen wa basi wa suitaŋa ate wa an nye ya, wa le kpi wa biemu nyiŋ, ale fi vari dek a poom basi kama.

ref: If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned.
text: Wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ a dan basi wa wayɔrisimaŋa ale nye biem wa le kpi bu nyiŋ.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.”
text: <<Alege fi saalɔ biiga, fi tɛŋka demma a biisi ale ka chaab fi wie parisaŋa kie ale yeeŋa tuataŋa nɔi, a weeni chaab ayen, <Ni jam wom biika ale nyini Naawen jigi a jam la.>

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, weeni Izirali yenni, ayen fi ale a weeni diila ale nna. <Ti nye kaasika ale ti biemu a duŋ ti a basi ka tɛŋ, ate ti muriŋ a bɛ ti nyiŋ. Ti be ti nye ka sɛ a boro?>

ref: Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
text: Weeni ba ayen, <Mi ale sum boro la, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale a weeni, Mi an mariŋ gaasa nyɔnɔ kummoa, alege ka ba goanti basi ba biemu suitaŋa a boro. Ni tulim, ni tulim a basi ni biemu suitaŋa. Ka boan le soa ate ni a kpi, Izirali yeri demma?>

ref: Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
text: <<Dila nyiŋ, saalɔ biiga, weeni fi tɛŋka demma ayen, <Wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa wayɔrisimaŋa a kan vari wa a basi ase wa nin zɛri mi nɔiya. Biem nyɔnɔwa biemu abe kan basi ate wa lo ase wa nin basi wa biemu wayɔrisima nyiŋŋa.>

ref: Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
text: M dan weeni wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa ayen wa le sum boro, alege ate wa ta sebchakka ale wa wayɔrisimaŋa a nye biem wayɔrisimaŋa dinyi mɛ la m kan teeri, wa le kpi biem buui ate wa nye la nyiŋ.

ref: Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right.
text: Mi be dan weeni gaasa nyɔnɔwa ayen, <Fi le sum kpi,> alege ate wa basi wa biemu ale nye dii ale wensie ale magsi la,

ref: For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live.
text: ale pa jabuui ate wa puulim a piem la a te, a pa jabuui ate wa zu la a te, a va sinsak ŋaai ale a te nyuvuri la, a kan nye biemmoa, wa kan sum kpi.

ref: Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair.
text: <<Alege fi tɛŋka demma a weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa suiku daa wensie.> Alege ka ba suiku ale kan daa wensie.

ref: And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
text: Gaasa nyɔnɔ a dan basi wa gaasaŋa ale nye dii ale wensie ale magsi, wa le boro dila nyeka nyiŋ.

ref: But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done. The News of Jerusalem's Fall
text: Alege, Izirali yeri demma, ni a weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa suiku daa wensie.> Alege, mi le bo ni wanyi, wanyi buusa a va wadek suitaŋa.>>

ref: The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak. What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
text: Yɔgyɔgla de junɔi ale taam alege ate nuruwa a paari la, Naawen nisa yaa jam bo mi zuk, ate wa lak mi nɔnni alege ate nuruwa a jam mi jigi saluiku. Dila nyiŋ mi nɔnni yaa lagri mi ŋman sina.

ref: Then the Lord said:
text: Naawen wanni yaa jam mi jigi ayen,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, nuruma ale bo yie luemaŋa po Izirali tɛŋka po la a weeni kama ayen, <Abrayam jam ka nuru yeŋ alege wa ta tɛŋka. Alege tama piisi kama, chekki wa pa tɛŋka a te ti kama ase nitalim la.>

ref: So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying: How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder
text: Dila nyiŋla weeni ba ayen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Ni le a ŋɔbi lam ate ziim a diem bo bu po la, ale zak a nya ni bɔgtaŋa a basi ate ziim a nyini la ni le tuesi tɛŋka a ta?

ref: and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
text: Ni yiila a bo ka ni gebika zuk, ni a nye ka wie ŋaai ale a kisi la, alege ate waai meena a taŋ vaanchoa pok. Ni be le tuesi tɛŋka a ta?>

ref: As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases.
text: <<Weeni kude a te ba, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Mi ale sum boro la, baai ale tali bo yie luemaŋa po la ale kpi ale gebika, baai ale bo tɛŋka peelim la m le pa ba a tɛŋ gɔi duŋsa ate si ŋɔbi ba, abe baai ale bo yie pagrisa po ale pina vie po la a kpi ale nyiŋtuila.

ref: I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them.
text: M le basi ate tɛŋka a doa kinla, ate ka kanjanta pagrim a jam kpeglimka jigi, ate Izirali guuta a doa koruk ate waai a kan va ti po taamu.

ref: I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord. The People Listen, but Don't Change The Lord said:
text: Ate ba yaa seba ayen Mi ale Naawen, m le basi ate tɛŋka a doa koruk ale kinla dii nyiŋla ba le nye wie ŋaai ale a kisi la.>

ref: So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money.
text: Mi nuruma a jam fi jigi kama, ase ba nyiem ale a nye diila, a kali fi niŋ a wom fi wieŋa, alege ba kan pa ŋa a tom tuima. Ba pa ba noaŋa kama a biisi ba le pa badek a te diila, alege ba suiniimaŋa ka butuem ale sueri a yaali venta nyuenta.

ref: They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
text: Ba jigi fi daa jaab a gaam waai ale a yi yeŋka yiila ale lueluk masiga ale a nak ŋannaŋta nalimnyiini, diila ba a wom fi wieŋa kama ale kan pa ŋa a tom tuima.

ref: Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
text: <<Kude meena a dan jam chim wensie, ku be le chim mɛ, ba yaa le seba ayen biisiteerɔ a bo ba suŋsuŋ.>>

ref: The Lord God said:
text: Naawen wanni a yaa jam mi jigi.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them: I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, mooli a ta chaab ale Izirali naapeerisaŋa, mooli a weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Kikaasa a bo Izirali naapeerisaŋa zuk baai ale a nya ka badek zuk la. Naapeerisa an magsi ba a nya ka piisaŋa zuwa?

ref: You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock!
text: Ni a de naabiisim goamu, a lik nidek ale ŋa kɔbtaŋa ale a lueri duŋ sii ate a yaali la a tɔgri, alege kan nya piisaŋa zuwa.

ref: You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep.
text: Ni an te baai ale wobsa la pagrim yaase ni tebi baai ale a yuak la yaase ni pob baai ale kɔni la nira. Ni an ta baai ale cheŋ tuiri la ŋmani ya yaase ni gisi baai ale be la. Ni nya ba zuk ka nna vakvak ale gaasa.

ref: They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals.
text: Dila ba yaa waaŋ dii nyiŋla ba ka naapeeriga, ba be le waaŋ la ba yaa chim ŋandiinta a te gɔi duŋsaŋa

ref: So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
text: Mi piisaŋa yaa cheŋ bɛ guutaŋa meena zuk ale gu didek meena zuk. Ba waaŋ kama tɛŋka meena zuk ate waai an gisi ya yaase wa nya ba boka jigi ya.

ref: Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep.
text: Mi ale sum boro la, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni, mi piisaŋa ale kan ta naapeerik la nyiŋ ate ba vari ŋa, ate ŋa chim ŋandiinta a te gɔi duŋsa la, ate mi naapeerisaŋa an gisi ŋa alege nya badek zuk alege daa piisaŋa la,

ref: So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi ta ka chaab ale naapeerisaŋa m be le yik ba bek m piisaŋa wari. M le yeeri ba ate ba kaa nya ŋa zuwa ate naapeerisaŋa a kan baga a nya badek zuwa. M le vari m piisaŋa ba noaŋa po a basi ate ŋa kan ŋman chim ŋandiinta a te ba.

ref: The Lord God then said: I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself,
text: << <Dila Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi dek ale gisi m piisaŋa abe m nya ase ŋa bo ka be.

ref: just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them
text: Ase naapeerik ale a nya wa pa ŋaai ale waaŋ la zuk ase wa nin bo le ŋa diila, mi le nya m piisaŋa zuk ka dila. M le vari ŋa a ta nyini juijui meena ate ŋa jam waaŋ boro chiŋmaaŋa ale legini danni la.

ref: and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields.
text: M le ta ba nyini tɛŋsaŋa po a nyini abe m tigsi ba a nyini tɛŋka po. M le nya ŋa zuk ate ŋa a dɛ Izirali guutaŋa zuk ale vaasaŋa po ale kalisaŋa jiŋŋa tɛŋka po.

ref: I promise to take care of them and keep them safe,
text: Mi dek ale nya m piisaŋa zuk abe m basi ate ŋa duak. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right. Judgment on the Strong Sheep
text: M le gisi ŋaai ale bɛ la abe m ta ŋaai ale cheŋ tuiri la a ŋmani. M le pob ŋaai ale kɔni la, abe m basi ate ŋaai ale wobsa la a nya pagrim, alege ŋaai ale jigsi ale pagra la m le kaasi ŋa. M le nya piisaŋa zuk ale wensie.

ref: The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel: I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak.
text: << <Alege nama, mi piisaŋa, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. M le bo posuk m ku ale m ku buusa, ale padaasa ale bua buusa.

ref: Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy.
text: Ku an zuak ale ni le a dɛ wuuk maŋŋa? Ku a fɛ kama ayen ni tabi ni wuuk tintila ale ni naŋsa? Ku an zuak ale ni le nyu nya naliŋŋa? Ku a fɛ kama ayen ni pɔti nya tintila ale ni naŋsaŋa.

ref: So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak.
text: << <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Nya, mi dek ale bo pa biitita ale pa kpiilinsa buusa.

ref: You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak,
text: Ni le a peŋ ale a chub pa wobsisaŋa ale ni nyiilaŋa ate ni ga yiak ŋa a basi la nyiŋ,

ref: but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
text: M le vari m piisaŋa a basi ate ni kan ŋman vari ŋa. M le bo posuk m ku ale m ku buusa.

ref: After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you.
text: M le basi ate naapeerik yeŋ a nya ba zuk, m yɔmawa Deevid, ale wa a kasi ba, wa le wa a kasi ba abe wa chim ba naapeerik.

ref: He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep The Lord God said:
text: Mi Naawen ale chim ba Wen, ate m yɔmawa Deevid a chim nabiik ba suŋsuŋ. Mi Naawen ale biisi.

ref: The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid.
text: << <M le nye suiyɔgni nɔiyeŋ ale ba abe m yeeri gɔi duŋsa tɛŋka po ate ba bo gɔnni po abe ba a goa tiisaŋa po ate jaab kan daani ba.

ref: They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain
text: M le niak ba ale jigi ŋaai ale gilim mi guuku la. M le basi ate ŋmoruk ale boro.

ref: to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
text: Laŋsaŋa po tiisaŋa ale yɔni yɔna ate tɛŋka ŋandiintaŋa ale be nalimnyiini, nuruma ale soa badek tɛŋka po. Ba ale seba ayen Mi ale Naawen ase m nin wɛ ba baai ale a nye ba yɔntidi la nisima po a basi.

ref: Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear.
text: Tɛŋsa a kan ŋman a vari ba, yaase gɔi duŋsa a yik ba. Ba le boro ate wari a kan daani ba, ate waai a kan basi ate yɔgsum yik ba.

ref: I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners.
text: M le te ba tɛŋ ate ba seba ka ŋandiinta nɔi po, ate ba kan ŋman chim kɔm nuruba tɛŋka po yaase ba chim laata a te tɛŋsa.

ref: Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise.
text: Ba yaa le seba ayen Mi Naawen ale ba Wen, Mi bo le ba kama, Izirali yenni demma, ka Mi nuruba, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
text: Nama mi piisaŋa, ka pa ŋaai ate mi a nya ŋa zuk la, ka nuruba, ate mi chim ni Wen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, pa fi nina a tuk Seir guuku nyiŋ, mooli a ta chaab ale ku

ref: and say to them: I, the Lord God, am now your enemy! And I will turn your nation into an empty wasteland,
text: a weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi ta ka chaab ale Seir guuku, m be le teeri nisa a ta chaab ale fu abe m basi ate fi kaasi a dua kinla.

ref: leaving your towns in ruins. Your land will be a desert, and then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: M le tulim ni tɛŋsaŋa ate si chim guura ate waai a kan boro. Ni yaa ni seba ayen mi ka Naawen.

ref: People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins.
text: << <Ni le ta dipo dachaani ni suiniimaŋa po a pa Izirali demma a te gebika ba kaasuŋku daaŋa po la, diipo ate ba namsika a paari ku paariŋa la,

ref: And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death.
text: dila nyiŋ mi ale sum boro, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni m le pa ni a te ziim ate bu va ni. Ni le kan jam kisi ziim nyini ka la, ziim nyinika ale va ni.

ref: and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
text: M le basi ate ni chim kinla ta cheŋ, ni tɛŋsaŋa waai kan boro, Ni yaa le seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.

ref: You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God,
text: << <Ni le weeni dii ayen, <<Tɛŋsaŋa de siyewa ka tama ale soa ti be le tuesi si ta la nyiŋ,>> ale mi Naawen a boro kama.

ref: and as surely as I live, I will punish you for treating my people with anger and hatred. Then they will know that I, the Lord, am punishing you!
text: Dila nyiŋ mi ale boro la, Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale a biisi, m le nye ni a magsi chaab ale suipuurum buui ale nyuri dii ate nama sak ni le jam ta suipuurum ale ba diila. M le basi ate ba seba mu ba suŋsuŋ ase m nin boro a bo ni buusa.

ref: And you will finally realize that I heard you laugh at their destruction and say their land was yours to take.
text: Ni yaa ni seba ayen mi Naawen a wom wa kayaa tii meena ate ni biisi a magsi chaab ale Izirali guutaŋa la kama. Ni weeni ayen ti dua ka kinla, ba be pa te ti kama ayen ti ŋɔbi ba.

ref: You even insulted me, but I heard it all.
text: Ni ta chaab ale mi ni kunkuulima ale ni biik po ale kan zimsi, ate mi wom.

ref: just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
text: Nama ale jam a naŋ alege ate Izirali yenni nitalimu a jam dua kinla la nyiŋ, mi le nye ni ka dila dek. Ni le dua kinla, Seir Guuku ale Edom meena. Ate ni yaa seba ayen ka mi le Naawen.> >>

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, mooli a te Izirali guutaŋa a weeni ayen, <Izirali guuta, wom Naawen wanni.

ref: that I, the Lord God, am saying: Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Dachiaka daa weeni ni wie ayen, <<Ŋiak ŋanwoŋtaŋa meena ka tama ale soa.>> >

ref: So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you.
text: Izirali guuta, wom Nyɔnɔwa Naawen wanni. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale a biisi a te guuta ale guwoŋtaŋa ale Vooliŋsaŋa ale vaasaŋa ale kab tii ale chim guura a dua kinla ale tɛŋ sii ate ba zɛri si a basi tɛŋ yonsaŋa a vari ni ale nye ni a la,

ref: But in my fierce anger, I will turn against those nations, and especially the Edomites, because they laughed at you the loudest and took over your pasturelands.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi biisi kama ale nyiŋ zeentika a ta chaab ale tɛŋ yonsaŋa ale Edom meena, diila biem nyeka masim ale naŋka ale bo ba suiniimaŋa po ate ba yaa nye mi tɛŋka kaai ate ba soa ate ba vari ka wumaŋka tɛŋka.>

ref: Trees will grow on you mountains of Israel and produce fruit for my people, because they will soon come home.
text: << <Alege nama, Izirali guutaŋa, ni le tom naŋsa a yɔni yɔna a te mi nuruma Izirali demma, diila ku kan beni ba le jam yeri.

ref: I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes.
text: Mi niŋ a bo ni po kama m le nya ni zuk ale ŋmanteka, ba le kpa ni abe ba bori ni.

ref: The people of Israel will return and rebuild your ruined towns and live in them.
text: M le basi ate nuruba dii ale boro la a piisi, poom ka Izirali yenni meena tɛŋsaŋa ba le bo si po ate ŋanluemaŋa a ŋman sɛ.

ref: Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: M le basi ate nidoama ale duŋsa a piisi ni zuk, abe ba a biak a chim ŋanbɔri, M le basi ate nuruba a kali ni zuk ase nyiem wala ate m basi ate ni jigsi a gaam ni nyiem ale ka diila. Ate ni yaa seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.

ref: I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve.
text: M le basi ate nuruba, mi nuruma Izirali demma, a cheŋ ni zuk. Ba le soa ni, ate ni chim be nitalim, ni kan ŋman kasi ba bisa taka diipo diipo.

ref: It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve.
text: << <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Nuruba a biisi a te ni kama ayen, <<Ni ŋɔbi nidoaba ale a kasi ni tɛŋka ale bisa taka,>>

ref: But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord Will Be Honored
text: Ni kan ŋman wom tɛŋsaŋa nye laka diipo diipo, ni be kan ŋman nam ale nuruma nye laka yaase ba nye ate ni tɛŋka a lo. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>
