ref: Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean.
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, Izirali demma ale jam bo badek tɛŋka po la ba jam taŋ ka kama ale ba nyeelaŋa. Ba nyeelaŋa a jam a nye ase ka nipok chiik po chiak loka daŋta la mi nina po.

ref: They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people
text: Mi yaa basi ate mi suipuurumu jam ba zuk dii nyiŋla ba basi ate ka ziim a nyini tɛŋka zuk diila ba taŋ ka kama ale ba bɔgtaŋa.

ref: Wherever they went, my name was disgraced, because foreigners insulted my people by saying I had forced them out of their own land.
text: <Juijui meena ate ba cheŋ tɛŋsaŋa po la ba kaasi mi tuilum yuenni kama, diila ba jam biisi ba wie kama ayen, Naawen nuruba ale nna alege ate ba basi wa tɛŋka.>

ref: so tell the Israelites that I am saying: You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name
text: <<Dila nyiŋ weeni Izirali yenni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Daa nama nyiŋŋa, Izirali yeri ya, ate mi a za ayen m nye wieŋa de, alege ka mi tuilum yuenni ate ni kaasi tɛŋsa po juijui ate ni cheŋ la.

ref: I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols.
text: M le pa nya naliŋ a misi ni ate ni nala. M le sugri ni a ta nyini ni daŋtaŋa po ale ni bɔgtaŋa meena po.

ref: I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts,
text: M le te ni suinum paalik abe m pa chi paalik a nyo ni po. M le yeeri suinum pagrika ase tain la abe m te ni suinum baasuŋ.

ref: because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings.
text: M le pa m Chiika a nyo ni po abe m basi ate ni va m ŋmarisika abe ni kpesi a ta m buusaŋa.

ref: You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
text: Ni le bo tɛŋ kaai po ate mi a te ni kokpieŋsaŋa la. Ni le chim mi nuruba ate mi ale chim ni Wen.

ref: I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve.
text: M le vari ni ni daŋtaŋa meena po a basi. M le wi ŋandiinta, ŋan bie ate ba jam a basi ate ŋa piisi abe m kan ta kɔm a jam ni zuwa.

ref: Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food.
text: M le basi ate tiisaŋa yɔnaŋa ale laŋsaŋa ŋandiintaŋa a zuak ate ni kan ŋman dɛ chivie tɛŋsaŋa po kɔm nyiŋŋa.

ref: You will remember your evil ways and hate yourselves for what you've done.
text: Ate ni yaa teeri ni biem suitaŋa ale ni gaasa nyeelaŋa, ate ni kisi nidek ni wabaataŋa ale nyeela ŋaai ate mi kisa la nyiŋ.

ref: People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Mi a yaali kama ayen ni seba ayen mi a nye kude ka mi yuenni nyiŋ, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni. Ni chali chivie ni nyeelaŋa nyiŋ, Izirali yeri demma.

ref: After I have made you clean, I will let you rebuild your ruined towns and let you live in them.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Dai dii dai ate mi a sugri ni wabaataŋa la, m le basi ate ni ŋman kali ni tɛŋsaŋa, ate ŋanluemaŋa ni ŋman sɛ.

ref: Your land will be plowed again, and nobody will be able to see that it was once barren.
text: Tɛŋ kaai ale dua kinla la ni le kpa ka ate ka kan dua kinla ate baai meena ale va ka po a taam la a nya.

ref: Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people.
text: Ba le weeni ayen, <<Tɛŋka de ale jam dua kinla la a yaa nye ase ka Eden tiisaŋa la, tɛŋ sii ale jam lo a chim guura la, a kaasi a dua kinla la a yaa sɛ ka yie pagrisa ate nuruba a boro.

ref: Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
text: Ate tɛŋ sii ale tali gilim ni la ale seba ayen ka mi Naawen ale sɛ ŋan baai ale jam kaasi la ale ŋman bori ŋan baai ale jam dua kinla la. Mi Naawen ale biisi, m be le nye.

ref: I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi le pilim siak Izirali yenni saalimka a nye ku a te ba. M le basi ate ba nuruma a piisi ase piisa la.

ref: The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Ba le piisi ase piisa ale magsi tiirita Jerusalem tɛŋka po tiga daa po la. Dila tɛŋ sii ale lo la ale sueri ale nuruba ase piisa. Ate ba yaa seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.

ref: Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones.
text: Naawen nisa yaa jam bo mi zuk, ate wa basi ate Naawen Chiika a ta mi nyini zaani viak suŋsuŋ. Ka jam sueri ale ka koba.

ref: The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out.
text: Wa yaa dɛ mi niŋ a ta mi a cheŋ ŋaaŋ ale niŋ ŋa po, ate mi yaa nya koba piisi nna yegayega tɛŋka viaka po, Koba ŋaai ale koi nna chechea.

ref: He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?” I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
text: Wa yaa bek mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga koba ŋade a baga a nya nyuvuri ya? Mi yaa weeni ayen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen yaa, fi nyiini ale seba.

ref: He then told me to say: Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you,
text: Wa yaa weeni mi ayen, mooli a te kobaŋa de a weeni ŋa ayen, koba kosa, wom Naawen wanni.

ref: “I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale a weeni kobaŋa de diila ale nna. M le basi ate vuusum a jo ni ate ni nya nyuvuri.

ref: I will wrap you with muscles and skin and breathe life into you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.”
text: M le basi ate jiina a maŋ ni a basi ate nyiŋ lam a lik ni ale nyiŋ gbaŋ. M le pa vuusum a nyo ni po ate ni nya nyuvuri. Ate ni yaa seba ayen Mi Ka Naawen.> >>

ref: I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together!
text: Mi yaa mooli ase wa le weeni mi la. Ase mi ale a mooli la nuemka ale jam boro, choaka nuemka, ate kobaŋa a jam jigi yeŋ, kobi meena a cheŋ di choa jigi.

ref: I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
text: Mi nya ale jiina ale nyiŋlam a jam ŋa zuk ate nyiŋ gbaŋ a lik ŋa, alege vuusum a ka ŋa po.

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
text: Wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Mooli a te vuusumu, mooli, saalɔ biiga a weeni bu ayen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Nyini vaata tinaansiwa jigi a jam, vuusummoa, jam vuusi basi bade ale kpi dua la po, ate ba nya nyuvuri.

ref: As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
text: Mi yaa mooli ase wa le weeni mi diila, ate vuusum a jo ba. Ba yaa nya nyuvuri a yiti zaani ba naŋsa zuk tugurik tɔŋdɔba boari.> >>

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future.
text: Wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, kobaŋa de ka Izirali yenni meena. Ba a weeni ayen, Tama kobaŋa a ko kama ate yiila a karo, ba gebi tama a basi kama.

ref: So tell them, “I, the Lord God, promise to open your graves and set you free. I will bring you back to Israel,
text: Dila nyiŋ mooli a weeni ba ayen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi nuruma, mi a yaali ayen m lagri ni boositaŋa kama a yeeri ni ti po. M le ta ba ŋman jam Izirali tɛŋka.

ref: and when that happens, you will realize that I am the Lord.
text: Ate nama mi nuruma, ale seba ayen Mi ale Naawen, ase m nin lak ni boositaŋa a ta ni nyini ti po a nyini.

ref: My Spirit will give you breath, and you will live again. I will bring you home, and you will know that I have kept my promise. I, the Lord, have spoken.” Judah and Israel Together Again
text: M le pa m Chiika a nyo ni po ate ni vuuk ate m pa ni a kali nidek tɛŋka po. Ate ni seba ayen Mi Naawen ale biisi, m nye kama. Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.”
text: Saalɔ biiga, pa diok a ŋmarisi ku nyiŋ ayen, <<Juda ale soa ate Izirali demma a gum du. Yaa ŋman pa diok ku choa, a ŋmarisi ku nyiŋ ayen, Ɛfraim duoku, ate Josefi a soa la, ate Izirali yenni meena a gum wa po.

ref: Hold these two sticks end to end, so they look like one stick.
text: Pa ti a tom tom chaab ate ti chim diok yeoŋ ate ti yaa chim kunyi fi nisaŋa po.

ref: And when your people ask you what this means,
text: Fi tɛŋka demma a dan bek fu ayen, kude kiri ale boa?

ref: tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
text: Weeni ba ayen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi a yaali ayen m pa ka Josefi duoku ale bo Ɛfraim nisa po la ale Izirali diinaŋa ale gum wa po la, a tom Juda diok, ate ti chim diok yeoŋ, ate ti chim kunyi m nisaŋa po.

ref: Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone
text: Yik daataŋa ate fi ŋmarisi ti zuk ba nimbie po,

ref: and then say: I, the Lord God, will gather the people of Israel and bring them home from the foreign nations where they now live.
text: a weeni ba ayen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. M le yeeri Izirali demma tɛŋsaŋa po ate ba cheŋ la. M le tigsi ba jigi meena a ta ba ŋman jam badek tɛŋka.

ref: I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations.
text: M le basi ate ba chim tɛŋ yeŋ tɛŋka zuk, Izirali guutaŋa zuk. Na yeŋ ale wa a nya ba meena zuk ate ba kan ŋman chim tɛŋsa siye yaase ba poori naata buye.

ref: They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
text: Ba kan ŋman taŋ badek ale ba bɔgtaŋa ale ba ŋanmɛɛntaŋa yaase ba nye kaasika diila m le vari ba biem po pilim ŋman ka a basi, abe m sugri ba. Ba le chim m nuruba ate mi ale chim ba Wen.

ref: Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did.
text: Ba le bo tɛŋ kaai po ate mi a pa te mi yɔma Jekob la, tɛŋ kaai ate ni koma a jam boro la. Ba ale ba bisaŋa ale ba bisaŋa bisa ale bo dula taam wuu, ate Deevid mi yɔmawa a chim ba nabiik taam wuu.

ref: I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time,
text: Mi le nye suiyɔgni nɔiyeŋ ale ba. Ka le chim nɔiyeŋ kaai ale ka boro taam wuu. M le yik ba kali abe m basi ate ba piisi a gum du, abe m pa m yenni a zaani ba suŋsuŋ taam wuu.

ref: and I will live among my people and be their God.
text: Mi boka jigi ale bo ale ba, m le chim ba Wen, ate ba chim m nuruba.

ref: Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
text: Ate tɛŋsaŋa ale seba ayen mi Naawen ale basi ate Izirali welema, ase m yenni a nin bo ba suŋsuŋ taam wuu.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:
text: <<Saalɔ biiga, pa fi nina tuk Gɔg nyiŋ, ate ka bo Megɔg tɛŋka la, Mesek nabi kpioŋku ale Tubal. Mooli a ta chaab ale wa,

ref: and I will make you powerless! I will put a hook in your jaw and drag away both you and your large army. You command cavalry troops that wear heavy armor and carry shields and swords.
text: Mi le yik a viriŋ, a pa gɔtisa a yik fi chikpeeŋa a ta fu a nyini ale fi tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena, ale wusumaŋa ale wusum duerisaŋa ale bobi kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa la, ale nuru boari a ta piema ŋanchɔgsin kpienta ale ŋan fiisa, ba meena a yuk ba gebisaŋa a basi.

ref: Your army includes soldiers from Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya,
text: Persia ale Kus ale Put ale bo ale ba, ba meena ta peema ŋanchɔgsinta ale kuta zuk china.

ref: as well as from Gomer and Beth-Togarmah in the north. Your army is enormous!
text: Gomer mɛ ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔba, ale Bet Togarma ale nyini niŋ wiiluk geŋ la ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔba tɛŋ boanni yega ale fu.

ref: because in a few years, I will command you to invade Israel, a country that was ruined by war. It was deserted for a long time, but its people have returned from the foreign nations where they once lived. The Israelites now live in peace in the mountains of their own land.
text: Bena yega a dan taam ba le wi fu ate fi pa kpaliŋ kɔlima. Bena ale cheen chum po la fi le tuesi tɛŋ kaai ale diem nyini kpaliŋ po a nyini, kaai nuruba ale jam tigsi nyini tɛŋsa yega a cheŋ Izirali guutaŋa zuk tii ale jam dua kinla ate ku beni. Ba jam ta ba nyini ka tɛŋsaŋa po a nyini ate yɔgyɔgla de ba meena boro sɔŋsɔŋŋoa,

ref: But you and your army will attack them like a fierce thunderstorm and surround them like a cloud.
text: Nama ale ni tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale tɛŋsaŋa yekka ale bo ale ni la ale jueli, a duŋ niŋ ase viok la, ni le nye ase ka chiŋmari ale lik tɛŋka la.

ref: When that day comes, I know that you will have an evil plan
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Da dila danni popola ale jam ni zuimaŋa po ate ni yaali popoli baata yam.

ref: to take advantage of Israel, that weak and peaceful country where people live safely inside towns that have no walls or gates or locks.
text: Ni le weeni ayen, <<M le tuesi tɛŋ kaai ate ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa an sɛ parisa. Mi le siti ka suiyɔgni ale baai ale kaa poli ayen wari ale nye la nyam, baai ale boro alege ka parisa ale nansuiŋta ale kutuk biga.

ref: You will rob the people in towns that were once a pile of rubble. These people lived as prisoners in foreign nations, but they have returned to Israel, the most important place in the world, and they own livestock and property.
text: M le vari ba abe m zu ba abe m cheem ta chaab ale ŋanluemaŋa ate ba ŋman sɛ la ale nuruma ale tigsi a nyini tɛŋsaŋa po la, a jigsi ale duŋsa ale kɔlima a bo tɛŋka suŋsuŋka la.

ref: The people of Sheba and Dedan, along with merchants from villages in southern Spain, will be your allies. They will want some of the silver and gold, as well as the livestock and property that your army takes from Israel.
text: Siiba ale Dedan ale Tarsis geruŋdɔma ale ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa meena ale weeni fu ayen, << Fi jam ayen fi vari kama? Fi tigsi nuru boanni ayen fi zu, abe fi ji kpana ale ligmɔniŋka fi ji duŋsa ale kɔlima a ta cheŋ abe fi tuesi ŋan baai fi vari yega la?

ref: You will attack my people like a storm-cloud that covers their land. I will let you invade my country Israel, so that every nation on earth will know that I, the Lord, am holy. Judgment on Gog
text: Ni le cheŋ a duŋ mi nuruma Izirali nyiŋ a ta chaab ale ba ase chiŋmari ale lik tɛŋka la. Daa a cheena, Gɔg, m le ta fi jam ate fi ta chaab ale mi tɛŋka, ate tɛŋsaŋa a seba mu ase m nin va fi nyiŋ a sak m dek tuilummu ba nimbie po.

ref: The Lord said to Gog: Long ago, I ordered my prophets to warn the people of Israel that someday I would send an enemy to attack them. You, Gog, are that enemy, and that day is coming.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Daa fi ate mi va m yɔmawa Izirali biisiteerɔma a biisi fi wie dipo daaŋa la. Dila po ba mooli kama ate ku paari bena ayen mi ale ta fu jam ta chaab ale ba.

ref: and in my anger I will send a terrible earthquake to shake Israel.
text: Mi nyiŋka ale a zeenti ate m suinni a dɛ la mi weeni kama ayen dila po tɛŋ choaka yegayega ale bo Izirali tɛŋka po.

ref: Every living thing on earth will tremble in fear of me—every fish and bird, every wild animal and reptile, and every human. Mountains will crumble, cliffs will fall, and cities will collapse.
text: Nyakpiemu jumaŋa, ale wenzuk nuinsaŋa, ale duŋsaŋa ale bo tɛŋka po la, ale jaab meena ale cheŋ tɛŋka zuk la, ale nuruma ale bo tɛŋka zuk la, mi dan jam ba nyiŋsa ale gɔk. Guutaŋa ale tulim a kpib ate pinaŋa a kabri ate parik meena a lo tɛŋ.

ref: I, the Lord, will make the mountains of Israel turn against you. Your troops will be so terrified that they will attack each other.
text: Mi le wi gebik ate ka jam ta chaab ale Gɔg mi guutaŋa meena zuk. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni. Nidoa meena gebik ale ta ka chaab ale wa suok.

ref: I will strike you with diseases and punish you with death. You and your army will be pounded with rainstorms, hailstones, and burning sulfur.
text: M le ta buusa jam wa zuk ale nyiŋtuila ale ziim nyinika. Mi le basi ate ŋmoruk pagrik a siŋ, ale ŋmoruk tana ale tintain tuila a siŋ wa zuk ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale tɛŋ sii meena ale bo ale wa la.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog and tell him: You are the ruler of Meshech and Tubal, but I, the Lord, am your enemy!
text: Saalɔ biiga, mooli a ta chaab ale Gɔg abe fi weeni ayen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Mi ta ka chaab ale fu, Gɔg ale Mesek ale Tubal nabi kpioŋku.

ref: I will turn you around and drag you from the north until you reach the mountains of Israel.
text: M le yik fu viriŋ abe m vuuri fu ta cheŋ. M le ta fu nyini wiiluk geŋka niŋniŋ a ta fu cheŋ ate fi ta chaab ale Izirali guutaŋa.

ref: I will knock the bow out of your left hand and the arrows out of your right hand,
text: M le che fi tommu ale bo fi gala nisaŋa po la abe m basi ate fi peemaŋa nyini fi juga nisaŋa po a lo.

ref: and you and your army will die on those mountains. Then birds and wild animals will eat the flesh
text: Izirali guutaŋa zuk fi ale fi tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale tɛŋ sii ale bo ale fu la ale lo ti zuk. M le pa ni ase ŋandiinta la a te nuinsa ale gɔi duŋsa.

ref: of your dead bodies left lying in open fields. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Ni le lo dua peelim jassi, diila ka mi ale biisi, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: I will set fire to the land of Magog and to those nations along the seacoast that think they are so secure, and they will know that I am the Lord.
text: M le te bolim jam Megɔg zuk ale baai ale bo nyiamu nɔi ate wari kan daani ba la, ate ba seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.

ref: My people Israel will know me, and they will no longer disgrace my holy name. Everyone on earth will know that I am the holy Lord God of Israel.
text: M le basi ate ba seba m tuilum yuenni m nuruma Izirali demma suŋsuŋ. M kan ŋman siak ate m tuilum yuenni kaasi, ate tɛŋsaŋa a seba ayen mi Naawen ale Weleŋsa nyɔnɔwa Izirali po.

ref: The day is coming when these things will happen, just as I have promised.
text: Ku cheena. Ku be le sum nye. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni. Dai dii dai ate m biisi la ale nna.

ref: When that day comes, the people in the towns of Israel will collect the weapons of their dead enemies. They will use these shields, bows and arrows, spears, and clubs as firewood, and there will be enough to last for seven years.
text: Ate baai ale bo Izirali tɛŋsaŋa po la ale nyini a pa kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa ase bolim daata la a ju ba, peema ŋanchɔgsin fiisa ale ŋan kpienta, ale tima ale peema, ale kpaliŋ dua ale gbatta. Ba le pa ba a chim bolim daata bena ŋayopɔi meena.

ref: They will burn these weapons instead of gathering sticks or chopping down trees. That's how the Israelites will take revenge on those who robbed and abused them. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Burial of Gog The Lord said:
text: Ba kan ŋman yaali ayen ba tigsi daata laŋsa po yaase ba che ti gɔi po, diila ba le pai kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa a chim bolim daata la. Ate ba yaa vari baai ale vari ba la abe ba zu baai ale zu ba la. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: After Gog has been destroyed, I will bury him and his army in Israel, in Travelers' Valley, east of the Dead Sea. That graveyard will be so large that it will block the way of anyone who tries to walk through the valley, which will then be known as “The Valley of Gog's Army.”
text: Da dila danni mi le te Gɔg guka jigi Izirali po, viaka po ate baai a nyiem va du a cheŋ kori geŋ nyakpiemu geŋsaŋa la. Ku le kasi nyeendɔba suik, dii nyiŋla Gɔg ale wa nuruma ba le gu ba ka dula. Ba le wi dula jigini ayen Yamon Gɔg Viak.

ref: The Israelites will spend seven months burying dead bodies and cleaning up their land.
text: Izirali yenni demma ale kasim a gu ba kama ate ku paari chiisa siyopɔi ate tɛŋka vaamu a nyini.

ref: Everyone will help with the burial, and they will be honored for this on the day the brightness of my glory is seen.
text: Tɛŋka nuruma meena ale gu ba, ate da dii dai mi a nya zula la ale chim ba teerika dai. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi.

ref: After those seven months, the people will appoint a group of men to look for any dead bodies left unburied. This must be done for seven months to make sure that the land is no longer unclean.
text: Ba le pa nuruba ate ba a sugri tɛŋka daa meena, baai ale a gum ba po la ale baai ale ba a gu baai ale tali dua tɛŋka la. Chiisa siyopɔiwa nuerika ba le piilim ba gisika.

ref: Whenever they find a human bone, they will set up a marker next to it. Then the gravediggers will bury it in “The Valley of Gog's Army”
text: Ba le a cheŋ tɛŋka po la, ba wanyi a dan nya nurubiik kobi, wa le pa jaab a nye daana di tɛŋ ate baai ale a tu vieŋa la a gu Yamon Gɔg Viaka po.

ref: near the town of “Gog's Army.” After that, the land will be pure again.
text: Tɛŋ mɛ ate ba a wi ayen Yamona. Ka le bo du. Ate dila nyiŋ ba sugri tɛŋka.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to hold a feast on Israel's mountains and offer sacrifices there. So invite all the birds and wild animals to come from every direction and eat the meat of sacrifices and drink the blood. The birds and animals
text: Saalɔ biiga, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Wi nuim buuri meena ale gɔi duŋsaŋa meena. Si tigsi a jam jigi yeŋ a gilim magsi kaabka ate mi gomsi a magsi ni la, kaabi kpioŋ Izirali guutaŋa zuk. Dula ni le ŋɔbi lanta abe ni nyu ziim.

ref: will feast on the bodies of warriors and foreign rulers that I will sacrifice like sheep, goats, and bulls.
text: Ni le ŋɔbi nuru kpienta lanta abe ni nyu tɛŋka nabisa ziim ase ba ka padaasa ale pabisa ale bua ale lalisa la. Ŋa meena duŋ biitita a nyini Basan.

ref: I want the birds and animals to eat until they are full and drink until they are drunk.
text: Kaabka jigini mi gomsi a magsi ni kama. Ni le ŋɔbi kpaam a ga chak gaam taam abe ni nyu ziim a ga buk.

ref: They will come to my table and stuff themselves with the flesh of horses and warriors of every kind. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Israel Will Be Restored The Lord said:
text: Jazaanimu jigini ni ŋɔbi wusuma ale ŋa duerɔba, ale nuru kpienta ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba tɔgatɔga. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: When I punish the nations of the earth, they will see the brightness of my glory.
text: M le sak m zulaŋa tɛŋsaŋa po, ate tɛŋsaŋa meena a nya ninam buui ate mi a te ba la ale nisa ate mi a vi ba zuk la.

ref: The people of Israel will know from then on that I am the Lord their God.
text: A zaani da dila danni a cheŋ Izirali yenni ale seba ayen Mi ale Naawen ba Wen.

ref: Foreign nations will realize that the Israelites were forced to leave their own land because they sinned against me. I turned my back on my people and let enemies attack and kill them.
text: Ate tɛŋsaŋa a seba ayen Izirali a ga bo tɛŋ yoŋ ka ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ, dii nyiŋla ba jam ka siaka ale mi. Dila mi yaa cheem m nina a basi nakpiak ale pa ba a te ba dachaasaŋa ate ba ko ba meena ale gebik.

ref: Their lives were wicked and corrupt, and they deserved to be punished.
text: Mi nye le ba kama a magsi chaab ale ba daŋtaŋa ale nye kaasika, ate mi yaa cheem m nina a basi nakpiak,

ref: Now I will show mercy to the people of Israel and bring them back from the nations where they are living. They are Jacob's descendants, so I will bless them and show that I am holy.
text: Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. M le ta Jekob nyini wa yik taka jigini a jam abe m ta jiirim ale Izirali demma meena, abe m mariŋka a bo m tuilum yuenni po.

ref: They will live safely in their own land, but will be ashamed when they remember their evil ways and how they disgraced me.
text: Ba le baŋ ba chivieŋa ale ba le kan pa siaka a sak mi la ase ba yaa nin boro ate wari kan daani ba, ba tɛŋka po ate waai a kan nye ate ba kpaziim a nak.

ref: Foreign nations will watch as I take the Israelites from enemy lands and bring them back home, and those nations will see that I am holy.
text: M dan ta ba ŋman nyini tɛŋsaŋa po a jam ale tigsi ba a ta nyini ba dachaasaŋa tɛŋsaŋa a jam, m le va ba nyiŋ sak ayen m dek ta tuilum kama tɛŋsa yega nimbie po.

ref: My people will realize that I, the Lord their God, sent them away as prisoners and now will bring them back to their own land.
text: Ba yaa le seba ayen Mi ale Naawen ba Wenni. M ta ba kama a cheŋ tɛŋ yonsa ate ba boro, m le tigsi ba a ta cheŋ badek tɛŋka. M kan tali waai a basi ŋaaŋ ŋa.

ref: Never again will I turn my back on the people of Israel, and my Spirit will live in them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Mi kan ŋman cheem m nina a basi nakpiak abe m ge ba, M le basi ate m chiika a jam Izirali yenni zuk. Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: Twenty-five years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, and
text: Naawen wie gɔdaasima po wa yaa ta mi cheŋ Izirali tɛŋka a pa mi zaani gu woŋ zuk. Guuku yeseok geŋka yie ale a nye nna ase tɛŋ kpieŋ la.

ref: He measured the entrance room at the far end of the passageway, and it was ten meters wide.
text: Wa magsi parisaŋa ale ji chaab la a gilim nansuiŋku ponni po ate ku chim anamagib kook ale pinaanuŋ. Magsika a paari vataamka vuuku ale a tuk dabiaka la kama.

ref: In my vision the Lord took me closer, and I saw a man who was sparkling like polished bronze. He was standing near one of the gates and was holding a tape measure in one hand and a measuring stick in the other.
text: Wa ta mi a cheŋ dula, ate mi nya nuru ate wa a nye nna ase kutuk mɔnuŋ la. Wa za ka nansuiŋku nɔi ale garuk miik naluŋ ale magsika diok wa nisa po.

ref: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay close attention to everything I'm going to show you—that's why you've been brought here. Listen carefully, because you must tell the people of Israel what you see.” The East Gate
text: Nuruwa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, nya ale fi ninaŋa abe fi wom ale fi tueŋa abe fi kpesi a pa fi popola basi dii meena ate mi a sak fu la, diila dila nyiŋ ate m ta fu a jam dela. Weeni Izirali yenni dii meena ate fi nya la.

ref: Then he went to the east gate, where he walked up steps that led to a long passageway. On each side of this passageway were three guardrooms, which were three meters square, and they were separated by walls two and a half meters thick. The man measured the distance between the opening of the gate and the first guardroom, and it was three meters, the thickness of the outer wall. At the far end of this passageway, I saw an entrance room that faced the courtyard of the temple itself. There was also a distance of three meters between the last guardroom and the entrance room
text: Diin fisaŋa ate limisidɔma a boro la woglimmu jam ka diokku meena woglimmu, ŋa labsimu a nye ase diokku meena la. Parik sii ale jam yik diin fiisaŋa la biglimu jam ka anamagib pi. Ate nansuiŋku tɛŋka ale pa a saŋ vataamka vuuku ale tuk Naawen Yenni la a limisa ase ka diokku meena la.

ref: at the end of the passageway. The man measured this room: It was four meters from the doorway to the opposite wall, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one meter.
text: Ku jam limisa ase ka anamagib pi ale naaniŋ la ate ku nakpaasaŋa daataŋa bigla ase anamagib bunaansi. Nansuiŋku vataamka vuuku jam tuk ka Naawen Yenni.

ref: The three guardrooms on each side of the passageway were the same size, and the walls that separated them were the same thickness.
text: Nansuiŋ kuui ale tuk kori geŋ ka la jam ta ka diin fiisa ŋata kauk meena ate ŋantawa magsika a chim bunyi. Diin fiisaŋa parisaŋa ale tuk chaab la, ale yik chaab la magsika jam ka bunyi.

ref: Next, the man measured the width of the passageway, and it was six and a half meters, but the two doors of the gate were only five meters wide.
text: Wa yaa magsi va jo ka jigini a ta cheŋ nansuiŋku labsimu ate ku chim anamagib pisita ate woglimmu a chim anamagib pisita ale neok.

ref: The man measured the distance from the back wall of one of these rooms to the same spot in the room directly across the passageway, and it was twelve and a half meters.
text: Ate wa magsi nansuiŋku a zaani dɔk fiika parika kanyi a ta ga paari m kala, ate woglimmu a chim anamagib pisiyopɔi ale bunu a zaani ŋmazukku lakka a ga paari m kala.

ref: Finally, he measured the total length of the passageway, from the outer wall to the entrance room, and it was
text: Nansuiŋku va jo ka a ga paari ku diin fiisaŋa woglimmu jam ka anamagib kook ale pisinu.

ref: The three walls in the guardrooms had small windows in them, just like the ones in the entrance room. The walls along the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. The Outer Courtyard
text: Diin fiisaŋa ale parik sii ale ji chaab nansuiŋku ponni po a jam bo ka parik gelisa ŋmai ate parik a yaa boro a gilim ase dɔk fiika la, paaŋa meena ale gilim la a tuk ka chaab ponni po. Parisaŋa ale ji chaab ale tuk chaab la ba jam ŋmirisi ale ka kpinkpatta tiisa.

ref: The man then led me through the passageway and into the outer courtyard of the temple, where I saw
text: Ate wa yaa ta mi a jam peelim dabiaka po. Dula mi yaa nya diina ale piisika a gilim dabiaka meena. Diina pisita ale gani piisika zuk.

ref: In fact, everything along the passageway was also the same size, including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, the entrance room at the far end, and the windows. This gate, like the others, was

text: Ka nabiika dek wa nyiini ale waai ale wa kali ponni po nansuiŋku nɔi a de Naawen niŋ. Wa va nansuiŋku vataamka vuuku a jo a va dula dek a nyini.

ref: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
text: Nuruwa yaa ta mi a va wiiluk geŋka nansuiŋku a jo jam Naawen yenni niŋka. Mi yaa nya Naawen zulaŋa a sueri Naawen yenni ate mi a lo poi nyiŋ.

ref: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not.
text: Naawen a weeni mi ayen, Saalɔ biiga, kpesi nya, chiib wom abe fi popola a bo ŋmarisika meena po ate mi a weeni fu a va chaab ale Naawen yenni la a magsi chaab ale di sinsaŋŋa meena. Pa fi popola a basi yenni nansuiŋku ale puusika jigini va nyinika jiŋŋa zuk.

ref: Tell those rebellious people of Israel: I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways!
text: Weeni tuikpari Izirali yenni ayen, Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Izirali yeri ya ni nye kaai ate mi a kisi la a zuak kama.

ref: My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement.
text: A gum ni wa yonaŋa nyeka ate mi a kisi la ale ni ta ka nicham ate ba suiniima ale ba nyiŋlam po ba an gebi ba yua ate ba jo mi puusika jigini a taŋ mi yenni alege pa ŋandiinta ale kpaam ale ziim a te mi ale kaasi mi nɔiyeŋka.

ref: Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
text: Ni le magsi ayen ni tom ni tuimaŋa a va mi tuilum ŋantaŋa la, ni basi ate ka nuru yonta a nya mi boka jigini.

ref: And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel. The Levites Are Punished The Lord said:
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Nichaanɔ waai ale kan gebi wa yoari wa suinum ale wa nyiŋ lam po la a kan jo mi jigini daa nicham baai ale poom bo Izirali demma suŋsuŋ la mɛ.

ref: Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished!
text: Livaima ale basi mi a cheŋ niŋ diipo ate Izirali a cheŋ bɛ la, baai ale basi mi ale cheŋ bɛ a va ba bɔgtaŋa la ale nam ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ.

ref: They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers.
text: Ba baga a tom mi boka jigini kama, a nya yenni nansuiŋtaŋa zuk abe ba a tom di po. Ba baga a tɔgri juka tiiritaŋa kama ale kaabka tiirita a te nuruma abe ba zaani a te nuruma a tom a te ba.

ref: But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning,
text: Alege ba le tom te ba ba bɔgta niŋ la a basi ate Izirali yenni a lo biem po la, dila nyiŋ mi zak ka nisa wen a pɛ ayen ba le nam ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins.
text: Ba kan jam moata ayen ba tom a te mi ase kaabteerɔba la, yaase ba jam moata mi tuilum ŋantaŋa, yaase mi tiiritaŋa ale ŋmasi ta tuilum la. Ku a fɛ ate ba ta wie ŋaai ate mi kisa ate ba nye la chivieŋa.

ref: They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple. Rules for Priests The Lord said:
text: Alege mi le basi ate ba a nya yenni tuimaŋa ale tuim ŋaai meena ate ba le tom la.

ref: The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices.
text: Alege kaabteerɔma, baai ale ka Livaiba a chim Zadok ŋaaŋbisa a jam tom mi boka jigini tuimaŋa ale siaka diipo ate Izirali demma basi mi niŋ. Ba zaani mi niŋ a pa kpaam ale ziim a kaab te mi. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
text: Ba nyiini ale a jo mi boka jigini. Ba nyiini mɛ ale jam a moata mi jazaanimu a tom mi niŋ ale a tom m tuimaŋa.

ref: When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple.
text: Ba daa jo ponni po dabiaka nansuiŋtaŋa, ba jo garuk naliŋsa, ba kan jo kɔbta gatta ase ba nin boro a tom ponni po dabiaka nansuiŋtaŋa yaase yenni ponni po.

ref: Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work.
text: Ba pa garuk naluŋ zutɔksa a vuk ba zuimaŋa abe tɛŋ garuk naliŋsa a bobi ba chaasaŋa. Ba kan jo jabuui ale basi ate wulum a nyini ba.

ref: And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
text: Ba dan nyini peelim dabiaka po juijui ate nuruma a boro la, ba yeeri ba garuk tii ate ba jo a tom la a basi ti tuilum diinaŋa po, abe ba jo garuk yonta, ate ba kan gaari nuruma a te ase tuilum nyam la ale ba gattaŋa.

ref: Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long.
text: Ba kan chiiri ba zuimaŋa yaase ba basi ate ba zuisaŋa a chim woŋŋa alege ba kasim a zamsi zuisaŋa ba zuimaŋa po.

ref: They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
text: Kaabteerɔ waai a kan nyu daam a jo ponni dabiaka po.

ref: A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
text: Ba kan faari pukɔga yaase nipok baai ale ba chorɔba ale basi chaaba. Ba baga a faari ka baai ale kan seba nidoaba ale nyini Izirali buuni po nyiini yaase kaabteerɔba pukɔga.

ref: Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean.
text: Ba sak mi nuruma ate ba seba tuilum ŋanta ale ŋankoa a gaari abe ba sak ba ate ba a gaari ŋan naliŋsa ale ŋan daŋtisa.

ref: They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
text: Nuruba a dan ta chaab, kaabteerɔma a tom ase boteerɔba la a abe ba poli ku zuk a va chaab ale mi buusaŋa. Se ba ta mi sinsaŋŋa ale mi ŋmarisika a magsi mi tiŋŋa ate mi a lueri la. Abe ba ta m Vuusum Daaŋa ate ŋa welema.

ref: Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister.
text: Kaabteerɔ a kan cheŋ a moata kpio ate wa taŋ wa dega, alege waai ale kpi la a dan ka wa ko yaase wa ma, wa nidoabili yaase lie, suok yaase tua waai ale kan yali ya, wa baga a taŋ wadek kama.

ref: If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later,
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa dan sugri wadek ku a fɛ ate wa limisi daa ŋayopɔi.

ref: he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Dai dii dai ate wa a jo mi boka jigini ponni po dabiaka ayen wa tom la, wa te biem tiirim a magsi wadek. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own.
text: Mi nyiini ale kaabteerɔma nitalim. Ni kan pa jaab Izirali a te ba ate ba ta. Mi le chim waai ate ba ta la.

ref: Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me.
text: Ba a dɛ ŋandiinta tiirimu ale biem tiirimu ale nyemagsika tiirimu ale jaab meena ate Izirali a pa a te Naawen la ba le soa.

ref: The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
text: Yɔn maŋ sii meena ale a dɛ niŋ la ale tiirim yonta ka kaabteerɔma ale soa. Ni tɛŋka ale dɛ niŋ a bɛ ŋan baai la ni pa te ba ate niauŋ a jam ni yenni zuk.

ref: Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
text: Kaabteerɔma kan ŋɔbi jaaboa, nuim yaase duŋŋa ale ka kpi doa yaase gɔi duŋsa a ko ka.

ref: So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures.
text: Ni pa ŋanmagsin maŋsa, taasi kpien maŋ ale samɔniŋ maŋ.

ref: The temple will be on a piece of land
text: Mi jigini ni gebi tɛŋ ate kabta bunaansiwa kauk meena a chim anamagib tusidi ale kobsinu (

ref: The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
text: Tigini daa ŋayopɔiwa po, dii ale a piilim chiisa siyopɔiwa po ka daa pi ale ŋanu danni la, wa gomsi yaali dila degadega a magsi biem tiiritaŋa, juka tiiritaŋa, ŋandiinta tiiritaŋa ale kpaam.

ref: kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem. Land for Israel's Ruler The Lord said:
text: Tuilum tɛŋka ate ni gebi a te mi la ni magsi woglimmu anamagib tusa pisiyopɔi ale bunu (

ref: Next to my sacred land will be an area
text: Magsi tɛŋka labsimu anamagib tusa pi ale bunu (

ref: The Lord God said: You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Ni cheŋ niŋ ka yega, Izirali nabisa. Ni pa ni wɔkwɔkka ale ni namsika a basi abe ni a nye dii ale ka wensie ale magsi la. Ni basi m nuruma taka. Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

ref: The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
text: Taasi kpienni ale samɔniŋka a magsi ba chim ka bunyi. Taasi kpienni a soa se ka kuruba kpioŋ la ate samɔniŋka a soa se kuruba kpioŋ, kuruba kpioŋku ale chim ja magsim a te buyewa.

ref: The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
text: Se fi nye dila dek daa ŋayopɔiwa danni chiika po a te waai ale kan potim tom kaasi ya yaase wa zɛ ale tom kaasi. Se fi nye biem duisi basika a te yenni.

ref: They will also bring one percent of their olive oil. These things will be measured according to the bath, and ten baths is the same as one homer or one cor.
text: Wa le te kpaamu magsaŋa la, ate ba pa samɔniŋ a magsi la, ka samɔniŋka piika po a nyini kuruba ba pi meena po. Ku meena a nye ase ka samɔniŋsa pi a magsi chaab ale kuruba ba pi la.

ref: The people of Israel will bring you these offerings.
text: Izirali demma meena ale nye tiirimu de a magsi Izirali nabisaŋa nyeka.

ref: But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people. The Festivals (Exodus
text: Ku ka nabisaŋa tuini ayen ba te juka tiiritaŋa ale ŋandiinta tiiritaŋa ale daam tiiritaŋa tiŋŋa jigini. Chi Paalika ale Vuusum Daaŋa tiŋŋa, Izirali yenni tiga ŋaai meena ate wa lueri la. Wa le te biem tiirimu, ŋandiinta tiirimu, juka tiirimu ale suiyɔgni tiirita a nye biem duisi basika a te Izirali yenni.

ref: Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
text: Dai meena Tigini daa ŋayopɔiwa po wa yaali lalisa siyopɔi ale padaasa siyopɔi ale kan ta jomi ya ase juka tiirim la a te Naawen ale buduk ase biem tiirim la.

ref: The Lord God said: On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Chi kaai ale a piilim la ka dai yeŋ dai ni pa lalik paalik kaai ale kan ta jomi ya a sugri mi boka jigini.

ref: The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
text: Kaabteerɔwa a pa biem tiirimu ziimu gela a nyo yenni tuataŋa nyiŋ ale kuŋkuŋku ŋmazuk noawanni gugotta tinaansiwa ale ponni po dabiaka tuataŋa nyiŋ.

ref: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast.
text: Piilimka chiika ka daa pi ale ŋanaansi dai ni kpesi Gaambasika Tigini, tigi dii ale di dɛ daa ŋayopɔi, diipo ate ni le ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ale kan ta dabinta la.

ref: On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people.
text: Dai dila danni nabiika a yaali lalik ase biem tiirim la a magsi wadek ale tɛŋka nuruma meena.

ref: He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
text: Wa magsi wa yaali ŋandiinta tiirim, taasi kpien nɔi a magsi lalik meena ale taasi kpien nɔi a magsi padiak meena, ale kpaam kolini nɔi a magsi taasi kpien.

ref: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Ponni po dabiaka nansuiŋka ale a tuk kori geŋ la, lik ku tuima daa ŋayuebiwa meena, alege Vuusumu Danni ale Chi Paalika Danni ku lagri.

ref: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
text: Nabiika a va peelimmu a jo a va vataamka vuuku ale bo nansuiŋku po a zaani nansuiŋku nɔi. Kaabteerɔma a kaabi wa juka tiirimu ale wa suiyɔgni tiiritaŋa. Wa puusi nansuiŋku dek nɔi abe wa nyini, alege tuoku a kan ligi a ga a paari junɔi.

ref: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
text: Vuusumu Daaŋa ale Chi Paalisaŋa Daaŋa tɛŋka demma a puusi Naawen niŋ nansuiŋku va joka jigini.

ref: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
text: Juka tiirimu ate nabiika a ta jam a te Naawen Vuusum Danni la ka padabilisa siyuebi ale padiak, si meena kan ta jomi ya.

ref: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
text: Ŋandiinta tiirimu ale a te ale padiaka a chim ka taasi kpien nɔi, ate ŋandiinta tiirim buui ale a te ale pabisaŋa a chim dii meena ate wa a yaali la. Kpaam kolini ale a magsi taasi kpien meena a maara boro.

ref: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
text: Chi Paalika tigini danni wa a te ka lalik paalik, pabisa siyuebi ale padiak, ba waai a kan ta jomi ya.

ref: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
text: Wa te ŋandiinta tiirim taasi kpienni ale lalik, taasi kpienni ale padiak, wa te dii ate wa a yaali la ale pabisaŋa. Wa maa te kpaam kolini a magsi taasi kpienni meena.

ref: The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
text: Nabiika a daa jo, wa va nansuiŋku vataamka vuuku a ŋman va dula dek a nyini.

ref: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
text: Tɛŋka nuruma a dan jam Naawen niŋ tiŋŋa daaŋa, waai ale va wiiluk geŋka nansuiŋku a jo wa puusi la a va yeseoku nansuiŋku a nyini, waai abe le va yeseoku nansuiŋku a jo la a va wiilukku nansuiŋku a nyini waai a kan va nansuiŋ kuui ate wa va jo la a nyini, alege waai meena a va m kula a nyini.

ref: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
text: Nabiika a maa bo ba po, a va jo ase ba le a jo abe wa va nyini ase ba le a nyini.

ref: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
text: Tiŋŋa ale tiga ŋaai ate wa lueri la daaŋa, ŋandiinta tiirimu a chim taasi kpien nɔi ale lalik, taasi kpien nɔi ale padiak ale dii meena ate wa a yaali la ale pabisaŋa, ale kpaam kolini a magsi taasi kpien meena.

ref: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
text: Nabiika a dan pa wadek yaalika tiirimu a te Naawen, juka tiirim yaase suiyɔgni tiirita, nansuiŋ kuui ale tuk kori la a lagri te wa. Wa te wa juka tiirimu yaase suiyɔgni tiiritaŋa ase wa le a nye dii Vuusum danni la. Wa yaa nyini. Wa dan nyini ŋaaŋnyiŋ ku lik.

ref: Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me.
text: Daa meena se fi te bein yeŋ pabiik kaai ale kan ta jomi ya a magsi juka tiirim a te Naawen. Saluik meena se fi te ka.

ref: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
text: Se saluik meena fi te pabiika ale ŋandiinta tiirim, taasi kpien nɔi a nin poori buyuebi, ku bunyi ale kpaam kolini a nin poori buta, ku bunyi fi te ale pabiika a dam zommu. Ŋan bieŋa de Naawen teka ka ŋmarisi kaai ale ka beni.

ref: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna. Nabiika a dan pa tiirim wa nitalimu po a te wa nidoabilisaŋa, ka wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa mɛ ale soa. Ka ba nitalim ŋanta ate ba soa.

ref: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
text: Wa be dan pa tiirim wa nitalimu po a te wa tomteerɔ wanyi, tomteerɔwa a baga a ta kama a ga paari varibasika benni, ate tiirimu a ŋman cheŋ nabiika jigi. Wa nitalimu ka wa nidoabilisaŋa ale soa. Ka ba ŋanta.

ref: The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him. The Sacred Kitchens
text: Nabiika kan pa nuruma nitalimu jaajaaboa a yiak ba alege ba nitalimu. Wa te wa nidoabilisaŋa ba nitalimu a nyini wadek ŋantaŋa po, ate mi nuruma waai a kan poori wadek wa ŋanta po.

ref: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
text: Nuruwa yaa ta mi va vajoka jigini ale bo nansuiŋku geŋka ale tuak tuilum diinaŋa ale tuk wiiluk geŋka ate kaabteerɔma a soa la a jo, a sak mi jigi ale bo yeniŋ geŋka kpeglimka.

ref: We went back to the outer courtyard and walked past the four corners.
text: Wa yaa ta mi nyini peelim dabiaka po a ta mi gilim gugotta tinaansiwa, ate mi nya gugoruk meena po dabiak ka choa.

ref: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
text: Dabaasa sinaansiwa kanyi meena ponni po a gilim kinni ka tintain ate bolim jiga a sɛ gilim kinni tɛŋka.

ref: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
text: Wa yaa weeni mi ayen, gbanlontaŋa ale nna ate baai ale a tom yenni po la a dik nuruma kaabka tiiritaŋa.

ref: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
text: Nuruwa a ta mi a ŋman jam Naawen yenni nansuiŋku ate mi nya a nyini tuoku tɛŋka a nyini a cheŋ kori geŋka, yenni a tuk ka kori geŋ. Nyiamu a nyini ka yeseok geŋka a siŋ a jam, kuŋkuŋku yeseok geŋ ale la.

ref: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
text: Wa yaa ta mi va wiiluk geŋka tuoku a nyini, a ta mi gilim peelimmu a ga paari peelim tuoku ale tuk kori la, ate nyiam a chali a nyini yeseok geŋka.

ref: Then he measured another
text: Wa ŋman magsi anamagib tusa ŋata (

ref: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
text: Wa bek mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, fi nya kude? Wa yaa ŋman ta mi a cheŋ kunkɔŋni.

ref: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
text: Mi ale paari du la, mi yaa nya ti boari benni kabta buyewa.

ref: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
text: Wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Nyiamu de a chali a cheŋ ka kori geŋka a taam a siŋ Araba po, juijui ate bu a jo Yesa Nyakpiemu po la. Bu dan nyini meena a jo Yesa Nyakpiemu po, bu le chim nya naliŋ.

ref: Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea.

text: Naawa a weeni ba ayen, ba magsi ayen ba ta nyiŋyɔgsa, ba nala, ba korisi, ba ta yam, ba seba gbaŋ, ba magsi ba a tom naab yenni po. Sak ba ate ba a biisi abe ba a ŋmarisi ti tɛŋka biika,

text: Ba po biik paali sii ate ba jam lueri la ale, Daniel ale Yanania ale Misael ale Azariya, ba meena a nyini ka Juda buuni po.

text: Alege Naawa yenni kpaŋŋa a te ba ka yue paala. Daniel yuei jam le Beltesazzar, Yanania jam le Sadrak, Misael jam le Mesak, ate Azariya a chim Abednego.

ref: Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace.
text: Daniel yaa nye wa popolaŋa ayen wa kan taŋ wadek ale naab yeri ŋandiintaŋa ale daamu. Ate wa yaa weeni Naawa yenni kpaŋŋa ayen ba kan te wa ŋandiinta ale da buui ate ba a chari naawa yenni po la.

ref: God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel.
text: Wen ale nye ate kpagni a ta yaalika ale jiirim ale Daniel.

ref: But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”

ref: “For the next ten days, let us have only vegetables and water at mealtime.
text: Daa pi, te tama nyiam ale jenvaata nyiini ase ku nin paari diipo ale magsi ayen ti dɛ la.

ref: When the ten days are up, compare how we look with the other young men, and decide what to do with us.”
text: Daa piwa a dan paari, pai tama a magsi chaab ale nuru paalukku baai ale a dɛ naab yeri ŋandiintaŋa la a nya abe fi yaa nye ti dii ate fi a yaali la.>>

ref: The guard agreed to do what Daniel had asked.
text: Wa yaa siak a nye dii ate Daniel a weeni wa la.

ref: Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace.
text: Daa piwa ale paari la, Daniel ale wa doama a yaa jam pagra ale zunchoŋŋa nuru paalukku baai ale jam a dɛ ŋandiintaŋa naawa yenni po la.

ref: After this, the guard let them eat vegetables instead of the rich food and wine.
text: Kude ŋaaŋnyiŋ limisidɔwa an ŋman jam a te ba ŋandiinta ale daamoa. Ba jam a dɛ ka jenvaata nyiini.

ref: God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
text: Nuru paalisa banaansiwa dɛ, Wen a yaa te ba yam ale sebika ase ba ale jam a kariŋ gbaŋsa nna yegayega la. Daniel mɛ jam a weeni gɔdaasima kiri kama.

ref: At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him.
text: Bena ŋatawa ate Naab Nebukadnezzar a jam te la a yaa paari, wa yenni kpagni a yaa ta nuru paalukku meena a jam wa jigi.

ref: The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court.

text: Alege ni dan weeni gɔdaasimaŋa ale ŋa kiri ale ka diila a sak mu, mi ale te ni tiirim buui ale zuak la ale zula. Yɔgyɔgla de ni weeni gɔdaasimaŋa ale ŋa kiri a sak mu.>>

ref: “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
text: Ba yaa tulisi ayen basi ate Naawa a weeni wa tomteerɔma wa gɔdaasimaŋa ate tama ale weeni wa ŋa kiri.

text: Ni dan kan baga a weeni mu gɔdaasimaŋa, wa yeŋ dekki ate mi a yaali ayen m nye ni. Nama ka velimvendisa. Nama a poli ayen wie ale tagri. Ni weeni mu gɔdaasimaŋa ate kula ale sak ayen ni baga a miŋ wie.

text: Naawa ale bek diila a melima kama. Waai karo a weeni a sak Naawa ka wenaŋa, ŋa be an bo ale nuruma mɛ.

text: Kaamka yaa jam ayen ba ko yam nyama meena. Ba yaa jam boro a gisi Daniel ale wa doama ayen ba ko ba.

ref: In a vision one night, Daniel was shown the dream and its meaning. Then he praised the God who rules from heaven:

text: <<Naaba ase fi ale nya jameemmu ale wa za fi niŋ a zuak ale a nyaksi la.

text: Fi ka Nalima Naab. Wenŋmazuk Wenni ate fu ka pagrim ale zuaka ale zula.

text: Mi gɔdaasimaŋa po ase mi ale diem doa m gaduokku zuk la, mi yaa nya maarɔ waai ale welema la ale wa nyini wenŋmazuk a cheen tɛŋzuk de.
