text: Naab Belsazzar yaa ŋmasi jam yɔgsa ate wa ninaŋa mɛ a ŋmasi a tagri a gum du. Ku jam cha wa nuruma kama.

ref: When the queen heard the king and his officials talking, she came in and said: Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! Don't be afraid or look so pale.
text: Naawa mawa ale wom naawa ale wa nuruma luelutaŋa tigini dɔkku po la, wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Naaba, boro taam wuu, kaa chali yɔgsummoa, yaase fi kaasi nina!

ref: In your kingdom there is a man who has been given special powers by the holy gods. When your father Nebuchadnezzar was king, this man was known to be as smart, intelligent, and wise as the gods themselves. Your father put him in charge of all who claimed they could talk with the spirits or understand the meanings in the stars or tell about the future.
text: Nuru ale bo fi tɛŋka po wala a ta wen weleŋsaŋa chiika wa po, fi kowa daaŋa po wala ate ba nya ate wa seba ale ta yam ase wenaŋa la. Ate fi kowa Naab Nebukadnezzar, fi kowa Naawa yaa basi ate wa chim sampoporisa ale baai ale a nya chiŋmarisa wie la ale baanɔba meena naab.

ref: He also changed the man's name from Daniel to Belteshazzar. Not only is he wise and intelligent, but he can explain dreams and riddles and solve difficult problems. Send for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means.
text: Daniel wa de, waai ate Naawa a wi ayen Beltesazzar la, wala ale ba jam nya ate wa ta popola ale miŋ chakka a baga a weeni gɔdaasima ale wakperikaliisa kiri. Wi Daniel ate wa ale weeni fu ŋmarisika kiri ale ka diila.>>

ref: When Daniel was brought in, the king said: So you are Daniel, one of the captives my father brought back from Judah!
text: Daniel yaa jam naawa niŋ ate naawa a weeni wa ayen, <<Ka fi ale Daniel baai wanyi ate m kowa naawa a ta nyini Juda po a jam la?

ref: I was told that the gods have given you special powers and that you are intelligent and very wise.
text: M wom kama ayen wenaŋa chiika a bo ale fu kama ate fi ta popola ale yam.

ref: Neither my advisors nor the men who talk with the spirits of the dead could read this writing or tell me what it means.
text: Yam nyama ale chichirik wiirisaŋa ale baai ale a zamsi chiŋmarisa wie la ale sampoporisaŋa meena a jam kama alege ba an weeni mu ŋa kiri ya.

ref: But I have been told that you understand everything and that you can solve difficult problems. Now then, if you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. You will wear royal purple robes and have a gold chain around your neck.
text: Yɔgyɔgla mi wom kama ayen fi baga a weeni mu ŋa kiri ale baga a yik wa pagrisa a niak. Fi a dan baga a kariŋ ŋmarisika ale a weeni mu ku kiri, m le pai naam garuk ŋmiŋmirita a jo fu abe m pai ligmɔniŋ chɔrinni a su fi ŋinni po. Fi ale chim buta nyɔnɔwa a pai va mi ŋaaŋ tɛŋka po.

ref: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, I will read the writing and tell you what it means. But you may keep your gifts or give them to someone else.
text: Daniel yaa tulisi Naawa, ayen, <<Fi baga a ta fi tiirimu kama yaase fi pai a te nuru yoŋ. Alege m le kariŋ ŋmarisika a te fu abe m weeni fu ku kiri.

ref: Sir, the Most High God made your father a great and powerful man and brought him much honor and glory.
text: <<Naaba, Wen Kpienni a basi ate fi kowa Nebukadnezzar a zuak kama ale chim nuru waai ale ta pagrim ale zula ale pimpauk.

ref: But when he became proud and stubborn, his glorious kingdom was taken from him.
text: Alege wa ale jam nye tukpari ale kanjanta la wa jam jɔk wa naamu ale wa zulaŋa kama.

ref: His mind became like that of an animal, and he was forced to stay away from people and live with wild donkeys. Your father ate grass like an ox, and he slept outside where his body was soaked with dew. He was forced to do this until he learned that the Most High God rules all kingdoms on earth and chooses their kings.
text: Wa popolaŋa a jam nye ase ka duŋ la, wa jam bo ale ka bon sii ale waara la ale a dɛ wuuk ase naab la. Maglim mɛ a jam kasim a lo wa ase duŋ la a ta ga paari diipo ate wa ale miŋ ayen Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La ale soa naata tɛŋzuk de meena a baga a pai a te waai ate wa a yaali la.

ref: King Belshazzar, you knew all of this, but you still refused to honor the Lord who rules from heaven.
text: <<Alege fi wa nidoabinni, Belsazzar fi a seba wieŋa de meena kama alege an ta fidek a siŋ tɛŋa.

ref: Instead, you turned against him and ordered the cups from his temple to be brought here, so that you and your wives and officials could drink wine from them. You praised idols made of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, even though they cannot see or hear or think. You refused to worship the God who gives you breath and controls everything you do.
text: Fi yaa zak fidek a zaani wenŋmazuk Nyɔnɔwa niŋ, fi weeni ayen ba ta wa yenni beerisaŋa a jam te fi ale fi nuruma ale fi pooma ale baai ale tom a te fu la a pai si a nyu daam. Fi a pak kpana ale ligmɔniŋ ale kutuk mɔnuŋ ale kuta ale daata ale tintana wenaŋa ŋaai ale ka a nya yaase ŋa a wom yaase a miŋi wie la, alege fi an zuli Wen dii ale ta fi nyuvunni wa nisima po la.

ref: That's why he sent the hand to write this message on the wall.
text: Dila nyiŋ ate wa tom nisaŋa ate si ŋmarisi siaka nyiŋla.

ref: Belshazzar gave a command for Daniel to be made the third most powerful man in his kingdom and to be given a purple robe and a gold chain.
text: Belsazzar a weeni ate ba pai naam garuk ŋmiŋmirita a jo Daniel ale pai ligmɔniŋ chɔrinni a su wa ŋiri ate wa saari buta nyɔnɔwa waai ale pai a vi wa ŋaaŋ naamu po la.

ref: That same night, the king was killed.
text: Yok kula dek Kaldiya Naawa Belsazzar ba ko wa kama.

ref: In order to make sure that his government was run properly, Darius put three other officials in charge of the governors. One of these officials was Daniel.
text: Ale nuruba bata ayen ba a nya ba zuk. Ba wanyi a jam le Daniel. Nuruma de a jam maari wa kama ale basi ate naawa a kan namu.

ref: And he did his work so much better than the other governors and officials that the king decided to let him govern the whole kingdom.
text: Wa ale a tom nalimnyiini a gaam mbala meena la ale soa ate naawa a lueri wa ayen wa a nya tɛŋsa zuk.

ref: The other men tried to find something wrong with the way Daniel did his work for the king. But they could not accuse him of anything wrong, because he was honest and faithful and did everything he was supposed to do.
text: Mbala a yaa jam a gisi suik ayen ba velim a te naawa ayen wa kan tom wa tuimaŋa a magsi. Alege ba an jam nya suiwa. Dii nyiŋla wa tom kama nalimnyiini. Dii ale magsi ayen wa nye la wa jam nye kama.

ref: Finally, they said to one another, “We will never be able to bring any charge against Daniel, unless it has to do with his religion.”
text: Kpeglim ka po, ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Tama a kan baga a velim a te Daniel. Ka ti nin ta va Daniel Wenni sinsaŋŋa.>>

ref: They all went to the king and said: “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
text: Ba meena a yaa cheŋ naawa jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Naab Darius, boro taam wuu.

ref: All of your officials, leaders, advisors, and governors agree that you should make a law forbidding anyone to pray to any god or human except you for the next
text: Tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma, baai ale a sak naawa wie la ale kpaŋŋa la a nye ka nɔiyeŋ ba nye kisuk ayen waai a kan puusi wen yoŋŋoa yaase nuru yoŋ a gum chaab ale naawa bɔglukku.

ref: Order this to be written and then sign it, so it cannot be changed, just as no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed.”
text: Naaba basi ate ku nye abe fi ŋmarisi ku a ta va chaab ale Miidi ale Persia wieŋa ale ka diila ate ba kan baga a tagri.>>

ref: So King Darius made the law and had it written down.
text: Naab Darius mɛ yaa ŋmarisi kaamka.

ref: Daniel heard about the law, but when he returned home, he went upstairs and prayed in front of the window that faced Jerusalem. In the same way that he had always done, he knelt down in prayer three times a day, giving thanks to God.
text: Ase Daniel ale wom dii ate ba weeni la, wa yaa kuli yeri a jueli gboŋ wa dɔkku po a lak tuokpattaŋa a basi Jerusalem geŋka a kpi duna tɛŋ a puusi a te wa Wenni jiam ase wa nyiem ale jam a nye diila.

ref: The men who had spoken to the king watched Daniel and saw him praying to his God for help.
text: Nuruma de yaa tigsi chaab a yaa nya ale Daniel a puusi a bek Wen ayen wa maari wa.

ref: The men then told the king, “That Jew named Daniel, who was brought here as a captive, refuses to obey you or the law that you ordered to be written. And he still prays to his god three times a day.”
text: Ba yaa weeni Naawa ayen, <<Juuwa ate ba a wi wa ayen Daniel la, waai ale bo dela ase yɔma la, a zɛri kama wa an va fi ale weeni dii ate fi a ŋmarisi la. Wa diem a puusi ka wa Wenni buta dai yeŋ.>>

ref: The king was really upset to hear about this, and for the rest of the day he tried to think how he could save Daniel.
text: Ase Naawa ale wom dila la, ku yaa daani wa. Wa jam kasim a gisi ka suik ayen wa vari Daniel a basi.

ref: At sunset the men returned and said, “Your Majesty, remember that no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed, not even by the king.”
text: Nuruma yaa tigsi chaab a cheŋ Naawa jigi a yaa weeni wa ayen Naaba a teeri ayen Miidi ale Persia tɛŋka wieŋa ale weeni diila Naawa a kan baga a tagri ŋa.

ref: So Darius ordered Daniel to be brought out and thrown into a pit of lions. But he said to Daniel, “You have been faithful to your God, and I pray that he will rescue you.”
text: Darius yaa weeni ayen ba ta Daniel a jam yuk basi gbeŋmaŋa dɔkku po. Naawa a weeni Daniel ayen, <<Fi Wenni dii ate fi a va la ale vari fu a basi.>>

ref: A stone was rolled over the pit, and it was sealed. Then Darius and his officials stamped the seal to show that no one should let Daniel out.
text: Tintain ate ba jam pai lik gbeŋmaŋa dɔkku nɔnni. Darius ale wa nuruma a yaa ŋmarisi ba yueŋa ate ku a sak ayen gbaŋka an baga a tagri Daniel ale nye diila.

ref: All night long the king could not sleep. He did not eat anything, and he would not let anyone come in to entertain him.
text: Yok kula meena Darius an daliŋ ale waai ya wa bi an goa ya.

ref: At daybreak the king got up and ran to the pit.
text: Vari ale veenti la, Naawa a yiti saluik a cheŋ gbeŋmaŋa dɔkku.

ref: He was anxious and shouted, “Daniel, you were faithful and served your God. Was he able to save you from the lions?”
text: Ase wa ale moata dɔkku la wa yaa kaari wi Daniel nna tuotuowa ayen, <<Daniel Wen dii ale vua la tomteerɔwa, fi Wen dii ate fi a va la an gomsi ayen wa vari fu a ta nyini gbeŋmaŋa jigi a basi?>>

ref: Daniel answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever!
text: Daniel yaa tulisi ayen, <<Naaba boro taam wuu.

ref: My God knew that I was innocent, and he sent an angel to keep the lions from eating me. Your Majesty, I have never done anything to hurt you.”
text: Mi Wenni a tom ka maarɔ ate wa lik gbeŋmaŋa noaŋa ŋa an baga a nye mu wari ya, dii nyiŋla mi an nye wari a kaasi fu Naaba.

ref: The king was relieved to hear Daniel's voice, and he gave orders for him to be taken out of the pit. Daniel's faith in his God had kept him from being harmed.
text: Naawa sui yaa peenti ate wa weeni ayen ba lak Daniel ate wa nyini gbeŋmaŋa dɔkku po a nyini. Ba ale lak wa la ba an nya lauŋ wa nyiŋka dii nyiŋla wa ta sebchakka ale wa Wenni kama.

ref: And the king ordered the men who had brought charges against Daniel to be thrown into the pit, together with their wives and children. But before they even reached the bottom, the lions ripped them to pieces.
text: Naawa a weeni ate ba pai baai ale velim a te Daniel la ale ba pooma ale ba bisaŋa a nyo gbeŋmaŋa dɔkku po. Alege jigi ate ba paari dɔkku tɛŋka la gbeŋmaŋa a poom labi ba ka gela gela.

ref: King Darius then sent this message to all people of every nation and race in the world: “Greetings to all of you!
text: Naab Darius a tom ayen ba weeni nuru meena ale tɛŋ meena ale buuri meena ayen ka wa ale a puusi ba.

ref: I command everyone in my kingdom to worship and honor the God of Daniel. He is the living God, the one who lives forever. His power and his kingdom will never end.
text: Mi weeni kama ayen waai meena m tɛŋka po, ku a magsi kama ayen ni a chali abe ni a zuli Daniel Wenni. Dii nyiŋla wa ka Wen vuk ale boro taam wuu. Wa naamu a kan maara a taamu wa pagrimu mɛ a ka kpeglimka.

ref: He rescues people and sets them free by working great miracles. Daniel's God has rescued him from the power of the lions.”
text: Wa ale vari a basi wa a tom wakperikaliisa wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk de. Wa vari Daniel a ta nyini gbeŋmaŋa jigi a basi.

ref: All went well for Daniel while Darius was king, and even when Cyrus the Persian ruled.
text: Daniel a jam nya ka niaka diipo ate Darius ale Sairus Persia demma a jam chim nalima la.

ref: Daniel wrote: In the first year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had some dreams and visions while I was asleep one night, and I wrote them down. The four winds were stirring up the mighty sea,
text: Daniel weeni ayen, <<Yɔkku ate mi gɔdaasim la, mi nya ale ka kinkaŋŋa ŋanaansi ale nyini wenŋmazuk a yaa a dam nyakpiemu.

ref: when suddenly four powerful beasts came out of the sea. Each beast was different.
text: Ate duŋ kpieŋsa sinaansi a nyini nyakpiemu po a jueli kunkɔŋni si jam kan neesi chaaba.

ref: The first was like a lion with the wings of an eagle. As I watched, its wings were pulled off. Then it was lifted to an upright position and made to stand on two feet, just like a human, and it was given a human mind.
text: Kaai ale dɛ niŋka la a nye ase ka gbeŋli la, alege a ta jiiruk kinkaŋŋa. Mi yaa kasim a jam a nya ka. Ase mi ale a nya ka la, kinkaŋŋa a yaa vɔssi. Ka yaa jam yiti zaani naŋsa siye zuk ase nurubiik la ale ta nurubiik suinum.

ref: The second beast looked like a bear standing on its hind legs. It held three ribs in its teeth, and it was told, “Attack! Eat all the flesh you want.”
text: M yaa ŋman nya ka choa a saari siye. Kala mɛ a nye nna ase ka goabiak la. Ka yaa yiti zaani kauk yeŋ nyiŋ ale ta nyapik koba ŋata ka nɔnni po nyinaŋa suŋsuŋka po. Ate jaab yaa weeni ayen, <Yiti a ŋɔbi lam chak!>

ref: The third beast was like a leopard—except that it had four wings and four heads. It was given authority to rule.
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ mi yaa nya duŋ ka choa kala a nye ase ka yɔŋni la, ka ta ka kinkaŋŋa ŋanaansi ka ŋaaŋka a nye ase nuim la. Duŋ ka de a jam taka zuima ŋanaansi ale ta pagrim a dɛ naam.

ref: The fourth beast was stronger and more terrifying than the others. Its huge teeth were made of iron, and what it didn't grind with its teeth, it smashed with its feet. It was different from the others, and it had horns on its head—ten of them.
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ m gɔdaasimaŋa po, m nya ka duŋ ka choa ale saari sinaansi, kala wie a toa kama a nyigsi ale pagra. Kala a jam taka kuta nyin kpiema. Ka jam a ŋɔriŋ kama ale a nɛ ka ale a yik ŋan baai la, ale a tabi ŋan baai ale tali la. Kala ka ka tɔga ale nsila meena. Ka jam taka nyiila pi.

ref: Just as I was thinking about these horns, a smaller horn appeared, and three of the other horns were pulled up by the roots to make room for it. This horn had the eyes of a human and a mouth that spoke with great arrogance. Judgment Daniel wrote:
text: Ase mi ale a poli nyiilaŋa wie la, nyiili di choa mɛ a ŋman nyini nna fiifiiga a gum chaab ale m ŋala. Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ m ŋala ŋata a yaa voori, nyiini de a jam ta ka nina ase nurubiik nina la ate wa nɔnni a biisi kanjanta wie.

ref: Thrones were set up while I was watching, and the Eternal God took his place. His clothing and his hair were white as snow. His throne was a blazing fire with fiery wheels,
text: Ase mi ale a nya la, wenŋmazuk naamu zukpagliksaŋa a yaa zaani magsi ate Dila Po Nuruwa a yaa kali. Wa garukku a jam peenti kama nna tektek. Wa zuisaŋa mɛ a peenti ase ŋmoruk tana la. Wa zukpaglika mɛ a jam a nyaksi ase ka bolim la, ka naŋsaŋa mɛ a nyaksi.

ref: I watched closely to see what would happen to this smaller horn because of the arrogant things it was saying. Then before my very eyes, the fourth beast was killed and its body destroyed by fire.
text: Mi yaa kpesi a wom dii nyiŋla kanjanta wie ate nyiini de a jam a biisi. Mi jam kasim a nya ka dila a ta ga paari diipo ate ba ko duŋka de ale ju ka nyiŋka ale bolim la.

ref: The other three beasts had their authority taken from them, but they were allowed to live a while longer.
text: Duŋ sinsila a yaa jɔk si pagrimu ale diem vua a boro magadega.

ref: As I continued to watch the vision that night, I saw what looked like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven, and he was presented to the Eternal God.
text: <<Mi gɔdaasimaŋa po yok kula, mi yaa nya ale waai ale a nye nna ase nurubiik la a nyini chiŋmaaŋa po a cheena. Wa yaa jam Dila Po Denɔwa jigi ate wala a dɛ wa niŋ.

ref: He was crowned king and given power and glory, so that all people of every nation and race would serve him. He will rule forever, and his kingdom is eternal, never to be destroyed. The Meaning of Daniel's Vision
text: Wa yaa ta pagrim ale zula. Nuru meena, tɛŋ meena ale waai meena a nyini biik buuri meena po a yaa puusi wa. Wa pagrimu ale boro ka dila taam wuu. Ate wa naamu a kan maa kaasi.

ref: Daniel wrote: I was terrified by these visions, and I didn't know what to think.
text: <<Ku yaa kasim jam a daani mi Daniel kama m ni gɔdaasim diila nyiŋ.

ref: “The four beasts are four earthly kingdoms.
text: <Duŋ kpieŋsa sinaansiwa de ka naata tinaansi ale za ti yiti tɛŋzuk de.

ref: But God Most High will give his kingdom to his chosen ones, and it will be theirs forever and ever.”
text: Alege Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La bisaŋa ale za ba tuesi tɛŋka a nya ka zuk taam wuu.>

ref: I wanted to know more about the fourth beast, because it was so different and much more terrifying than the others. What was the meaning of its iron teeth and bronze claws and of its feet that smashed what the teeth and claws had not ground and crushed?
text: <<Dila nyiŋla mi a yaali ayen m seba ka wensieŋa dek chekki a ta va duŋ kaai ale saari sinaansiwa la. Kaai ale nye ka tɔgawa ale nsila meena la. Ka kutuk nyinaŋa ale ka kutuk mɔnuŋ nampiemaŋa, duŋ kaai ale ŋɔriŋ ale nɛ ŋan baai ate ka yik ale a tabi ŋan baai ale tali la zuk.

ref: I also wanted to know more about all ten of those horns on its head. I especially wanted to know more about the one that took the place of three of the others—the horn that had eyes and spoke with arrogance and seemed greater than the others.
text: M ŋman a yaali ayen m seba nyiila piwa ale bo ka zukku po la kiri. Poom daa nyii fiika ale tagri m ŋala ŋata wa la. Dii ale zak di dek a zaani ale ta nina ale nɔi dii ale a biisi kanjanta wie la.

ref: While I was looking, this horn attacked God's chosen ones and was winning the battle.
text: Mi ale a nya la, nyiini de yaa boro a nye kpaliŋ ale Wen bisaŋa a nya pagrim ba zuk.

ref: Then God Most High, the Eternal God, came and judged in favor of his chosen ones, because the time had arrived for them to be given the kingdom.
text: Ate Dila Powa Denɔwa a jam bo a te Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La bisaŋa dii nyiŋla ku paari ka diipo ale magsi ayen ba soa naamu la.

ref: Then I was told by the one standing there: “The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom to appear on earth. It will be different from all the others— it will trample the earth and crush it to pieces.
text: Wa yaa weeni mu ku kiri ayen, <<Duŋ kaai ale saari sinaansiwa la kiri ale naam ale saari naata tinaansi a yiti tɛŋka zuk. Bu ale chim ka bu tɔga ale naam tintila, ate bula ale bu a nya tɛŋ sinsila meena tɛŋka zuk abe ka tabi si zuk a taam.

ref: All ten of those horns are kings who will come from this kingdom, and one more will follow. This horn will be different from the others, and it will conquer three other kings.
text: Nyiila piwa ka nalima pi baai ale ba nyini wa naamu po. Bala ŋaaŋnyiŋ Naab wa choa ale jam, wala ale nye ka wa tɔga ale mbala. Wa ale ta mbala batawa a siŋ tɛŋ.

ref: “This king will speak evil of God Most High, and he will be cruel to God's chosen ones. He will try to change God's Law and the sacred seasons. And he will be able to do this for a time, two times, and half a time.
text: Wa yaa ale biisi Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La a kaasi abe wa namsi wa bisaŋa abe wa dan baga wa tagri tiŋŋa ale wa wieŋa. Wa bisaŋa ale bo wa nisima po a paari bena ŋata ale geli.

ref: But he will finally be judged, and his kingdom completely destroyed.
text: Alege buusa boka danni ale paari ate wa ale jɔk wa pagrimu.

ref: “Then the greatest kingdom of all will be given to the chosen ones of God Most High. His kingdom will be eternal, and all others will serve and obey him.”
text: Ate tɛŋ kpieŋ kaai ale zuak la a yaa le bo Wen bisaŋa nisima po, Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La nuruma ale la. Wa naamu ale boro ka dila taam wuu ate kpaga meena ale kasim a puusi wa.

ref: That was what I saw and heard. I turned pale with fear and kept it all to myself.
text: Wanni kpeglimka jigi ale nna. Mi Daniel, ku jam kasim a daani mu kama m popolaŋa po ate mi ninaŋa a tagri alege m jam ta wanni kama m dek m nyiini.

ref: Daniel wrote: In the third year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had a second vision
text: Naab Belsazzar ale dɛ wa naamu a paari bena ŋatawa po la, mi Daniel jam gɔdaasim kama ŋmana. Mi ale liŋ gɔdaasim la ŋaaŋnyiŋ ale la.

ref: when I looked up and saw a ram standing there with two horns on its head—both of them were long, but the second one was longer than the first.
text: Mi a yaa zak nya ŋmai ale padiak a za mi niŋ ale ka nyiila ŋaye a za benni nɔi. Nyiilaŋa a jam wɔŋa kama alege dinyi a jam chim a gaam m dila.

ref: The ram went charging toward the west, the north, and the south. No other animals were strong enough to oppose him, and nothing could save them from his power. So he did as he pleased and became even more powerful.
text: Mi yaa nya padiaka a kpa tuak yeniŋ geŋsa ale wiilukku geŋsa ale yeseoku geŋsa. Alege duŋ ka choa karo a pagra a nye kpaliŋ ale ka, duŋ mɛ abe karo a pagra ase kala la ate ka yaa kasim a nye dii ate ka a yaali la ale pagra a gum du.

ref: I kept on watching and saw a goat come from the west and charge across the entire earth, without even touching the ground. Between his eyes was a powerful horn,
text: Mi ale diem a poli la, ku an beni ya buuk ale ta nyiili ku ninaŋa suŋsuŋ a nyini yeniŋ geŋsa a gilim tɛŋka meena alege kan tabi tɛŋka.

ref: and with tremendous anger the goat started toward the ram that I had seen beside the river.
text: Ku yaa jam padiaka jigi kaai ate mi nya ale ka za nyiam vuuku nɔi ale nyiila ŋayewa la jigi ale suipuurum.

ref: The goat was so fierce that its attack broke both horns of the ram, leaving him powerless. Then the goat trampled on the ram, and no one could do anything to help.
text: Ku yaa nye kpaliŋ ale padiaka a wɛ ka nyiila ŋayewa padiaka a jam wobsa kama ka an jam baga a zaani ale ku. Buuku a nak ka a lɔnsi ka tɛŋ ale tabi ka zuk alege jaab a karo a vari padiaka a ta nyini ku jigi a basi.

ref: After this, the goat became even more powerful. But at the peak of his power, his mighty horn was broken, and four other mighty horns took its place—one pointing to the north and one to the east, one to the south and one to the west.
text: Buuku a yaa zuak alege pagrim buui ate ku ta la, ku nyii dii ale zuak la a yaa wɛ alege ate nyii pagrisa ŋanaansi a nyini dula kuuni a jueli jiga bunaansi.

ref: A little horn came from one of these, and its power reached to the south, the east, and even to the holy land.
text: Ŋatawa po nyiili di choa nna fii fiiga alege chim ale pagrim a nyini yeseok geŋsa a ta ga paari kori geŋ a ta moata Tɛŋ Kaai Ale Nala La geŋ.

ref: It became so strong that it attacked the stars in the sky, which were heaven's army. Then it threw some of them down to the earth and trampled on them.
text: Di chim kama a jueli moata wenŋmazuk. Di yaa nye kpaliŋ ale chiŋmarisaŋa gela ale zak si a yuk basi tɛŋzuk alege a tabi si zuk.

ref: Then one of the holy angels asked another, “When will the daily sacrifices be offered again? What about this horrible rebellion? When will the temple and heaven's army no longer be trampled in the dust?”
text: Ate mi wom ale nuru weleŋ a biisi, ate nuru weleŋ wa choa a weeni wa ayen, <<Ka disa po ate gɔdaasimaŋa dɛ ale nye a ta va danni po kaabka, tukpari nyeka a ta ka kaasuŋ a jam Wen dɔkku ate ba ale tabi tama zuwa?>>

ref: evenings and mornings before the temple is dedicated and in use again.” Gabriel Interprets the Vision
text: ) alege ate ba ŋman nye ate Wen dɔkku a nye cheri.>>

ref: Daniel wrote: I was trying to figure out the meaning of the vision, when someone suddenly appeared there beside me.
text: Mi Daniel ale diem a poli gɔdaasimaŋa kiri la ayen m dan baga m miŋ ŋa kiri la, m yaa ŋman nya waai m niŋ ase nuru la.

ref: And from beside the Ulai River, a voice like that of a human said, “Gabriel, help him understand the vision.”
text: Mi yaa wom nuru lueluk a nyini Ulai Nyiam Vuuku a wi Gabriel, ayen weeni nuruwa de gɔdaasimaŋa kiri.

ref: Gabriel came over, and I fell to the ground in fear. Then he said, “You are merely a human, but you need to understand that this vision is about the end of time.”
text: Ase wa ale forisi moata mi ale za kauk kuui la mi nyiŋka a yaa deri a gɔk ate mi a lo tɛŋ ase m cha la wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, bi seba ayen gɔdaasimaŋa a weeni ka da kpeglimaŋa wie.>>

ref: While he was speaking, I fell facedown in a deep sleep. But he lifted me to my feet
text: Wa ale diem boro a biisi ale mi la, mi jam pai mi ninaŋa a vuk ka tɛŋ a goa. Wa yaa tiri mi ale zak mu a zaani.

ref: and said: Listen, and I will tell you what will happen at the end of time, when God has chosen to show his anger.
text: Wa weeni ayen, <<Mi a yaali ayen m weeni fu ka dii ale za ku nye suipuurum daaŋa po la, dii nyiŋla gɔdaasimaŋa a weeni ka da kpeglimaŋa po wie.

ref: The two horns of the ram are the kings of Media and Persia,
text: Padiaka ate fi a nya ale nyiila ŋayewa la ka Miidi ale Persia nalima.

ref: the goat is the kingdom of Greece, and the powerful horn between his eyes is the first of its kings.
text: Budukku mɛ a magsi chaab ale ka Girik naawa, alege nyii kpien dii ale bo ninaŋa suŋsuŋ la mɛ a magsi chaab ale ka naab waai ale wa dɛ niŋ la.

ref: After this horn is broken, four other kingdoms will appear, but they won't be as strong.
text: Nyiila ŋanaansiwa, ŋaai ale tagri dii ale wɛ la kiri ale wa naamu ale lab bunaansi alege si pagrimu a kan chim bunyi.

ref: When these rulers have become as evil as possible, their power will end, and then a king who is dangerous and cannot be trusted will appear.
text: Ba dan dɛ ba naamu a ta ga moata nueri ka, gaasa tuima ale kasim boro, Naab ale jam ate wa nyeka ale toa.

ref: He will gain strength, but not on his own, and he will cause terrible destruction. He will wipe out powerful leaders and God's people as well.
text: Wa ale kasim pagra kama alege daa wadek pagrimoa. Wa ale kasim a kaasi tuima abe wa nya suik a nye dii meena ate wa a yaali la. Wa ale kaasi niŋdeerɔma baai ale ta pagrim la ale Wen nuruma.

ref: His deceitful lies will make him so successful, that he will think he is really great. Suddenly he will kill many people, and he will even attack God, the Supreme Ruler. But God will crush him!
text: Wa ale paasi nuruba a jigsi. Wa ale pai wadek a chim nuru dek, ate ba daa a poli ayen ba boro ka boka dek, wa ale ko nuruba yegayega, ate ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa ale kpaliŋ ale nabisa meena Nabiika. Alege ba ale nak yik wa alege daa nurubiik pagrimoa.

ref: This vision about the evenings and mornings is true, but these things won't happen for a long time, so don't tell it to others.
text: Junoaŋa ale saluitaŋa gɔdaasimaŋa ate fi a nya la ka wensie. Ta kude fidek fi nyiini ale gɔdaasimaŋa ka chum po wie.

ref: After this, I was so worn out and weak that it was several days before I could get out of bed and go about my duties for the king. I was disturbed by this vision that made no sense to me.
text: Mi Daniel a jam jiak kama ale a yuak a paari da boari. Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate mi a baga a yiti a tom naawa tuini. Gɔdaasimaŋa a jam cha mu kama ate mi an miŋ ŋa kiri ya.

ref: Daniel wrote: Some years later, Darius the Mede, who was the son of Xerxes, had become king of Babylonia. And during his first year as king, I found out from studying the writings of the prophets that the Lord had said to Jeremiah, “Jerusalem will lie in ruins for
text: Bein dii ate wa piilim dɛ naamu la, mi Daniel a miŋ chak kama ayen Naawen wanni ate wa pai a te biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya ayen Jerusalem tɛŋka ale duak a paari bena pisiyopɔi.

ref: Then, to show my sorrow, I went without eating and dressed in sackcloth and sat in ashes. I confessed my sins and earnestly prayed to the Lord my God: Our Lord, you are a great and fearsome God, and you faithfully keep your agreement with those who love and obey you.
text: M yaa puusi a te Naawen, m Wenni a juisi vɔŋteka ayen, <<Nyɔnɔwa, Wen dii ale zuak la, ale waai ate ba a chali wa la ale waai ale kasim ta wa nɔiyeŋka ale ŋmanteka ale waai meena ale a yaali wa la ale a zuli wa sinsaŋŋa la.

ref: But we have sinned terribly by rebelling against you and rejecting your laws and teachings.
text: Ti nyeka biem ale tom kaasi. Ti ka gaasa nyam ale zɛri fi nɔi, ti basi fi wieŋa ale fi buusaŋa kama.

ref: We have ignored the message your servants the prophets spoke to our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and everyone else.
text: Tama an wom fi biisiteerɔma baai ale biisi fi yuenni a te ti nalimaŋa ale ti nabisaŋa ale ti nuruma meena tɛŋka po la.

ref: Lord God, you are merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against you
text: Tama a zɛri wa kama ale ge ti Nyɔnɔwa Wen a ta jiirim kama ale diem a vɔŋ a te ti.

ref: and rejected your teachings that came to us from your servants the prophets.
text: Tama zɛri Naawen ti Wenni kama ale an va wa sinsaŋŋa ate wa te ti a ta va wa tomteerɔma biisiteerɔma la.

ref: Everyone in Israel has stubbornly refused to obey your laws, and so those curses written by your servant Moses have fallen upon us.
text: Izirali demma meena a nye kaasi sinsaŋŋa kama ale zɛri ba an va fu, <<Dila nyiŋla kikaasa ale ŋmarisi Moosis Wen biisiteerɔwa gbaŋka po la a yaa jam ti jigi dii nyiŋla ti tom a kaasi fi kama.

ref: You warned us and our leaders that Jerusalem would suffer the worst disaster in human history, and you did exactly as you had threatened.
text: Fi a nye dii ate fi weeni a ta va chaab ale tama ale ti niŋdeerɔma la kama a ta kaasuŋ a jam ti jigi. Fi a namsi tama Jerusalem demma a gaam tɛŋ meena kama.

ref: We have not escaped any of the terrible curses written by Moses, and yet we have refused to beg you for mercy and to remind ourselves of how faithful you have always been.
text: Ase ku ale ŋmarisi dii Moosis sinsaŋŋa po la, kaasuŋku de meena a jam tama jigi kama, alege tama an diem gisi Naawen ti Wenni jiirimu a basi ti biemu ale va wensieŋa.

ref: And when you finally punished us with this horrible disaster, that was also the right thing to do, because we deserved it so much.
text: Naawen an beni du ale namsi ti, tama Naawen ti Wen a kasim a nye ka dii ale nala la alege tama an diem a va wa.

ref: Our Lord God, with your own mighty arm you rescued us from Egypt and made yourself famous to this very day, but we have sinned terribly.
text: <<Nyɔnɔ ti Wen yaa, fi sak fi pagrimu kama a ta fi nuruma a nyini Ejipiti po a nyini ti kan baŋ fi pagrimu wari ya. Tama nyeka biem, tama a nye kaasi kama.

ref: In the past, you treated us with such kindness, that we now beg you to stop being so terribly angry with Jerusalem. After all, it is your chosen city built on your holy mountain, even though it has suffered public disgrace because of our sins and those of our ancestors.
text: Nyɔnɔ, ti le ta fi wayɔrisima nyeelaŋa meena la, basi fi suipuurumu ale Jerusalem, fi tɛŋka, fi tuilum guuku. Tama wabaataŋa ale ti koma tuimbaataŋa a basi kama ate Jerusalem ale fi nuruma a chim baai ate baai meena ale gilim ti la a la ti.

ref: I am your servant, Lord God, and I beg you to answer my prayers and bring honor to yourself by having pity on your temple that lies in ruins.
text: <<Wen yaa, be wom m puusaŋa ale m saalimka. Pilim sɛ fi yenni, dii ale kaasi la pilim a sɛ di ate waai meena ale seba ayen fi ka Nyɔnɔwa.

ref: Forgive us! Hurry and do something, not only for your city and your chosen people, but to bring honor to yourself. The Seventy Weeks Daniel wrote:
text: Nyɔnɔ wom ti. Nyɔnɔ vɔŋ a te ti. Nyɔnɔ wom ti abe fi tom ate ti dii ale ku nye ate waai meena ale seba ayen fi ka Wen. Kan beni. Tɛŋka ale nuruma ka fi ale soa ba.>>

ref: I was still confessing my sins and those of all Israel to the Lord my God, and I was praying for the good of his holy mountain,
text: Ase mi ale diem boro a puusi a juisi mi biemu ale Izirali m nuruma biemu vɔŋteka ale Naawen m Wenni ayen wa pilim a sɛ wa yenni la,

ref: when Gabriel suddenly came flying in at the time of the evening sacrifice. This was the same Gabriel I had seen in my vision,
text: ase mi ale diem a puusi la, Gabriel nuru waai ate mi a poom liŋ nya m gɔdaasimaŋa po la, a yaa jam mi jigi nna mwuli diipo ate ba nye junɔinni kaabka la.

ref: and he explained: Daniel, I am here to help you understand the vision.
text: Wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Daniel mi jam kama ayen m maari fu ate fi miŋ wanni kiri.

ref: God thinks highly of you, and at the very moment you started praying, I was sent to give you the answer.
text: A nyini dai dii danni ate fi a piilim a puusi Wen la. Wa tulisi fu kama. Wa a yaali fu kama, dila nyiŋla mi jam kama ayen m tulisi fu. Be ŋmasi a wom chak.

ref: For one week this foreigner will make a firm agreement with many people, and halfway through this week, he will end all sacrifices and offerings. Then the “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction will be put there. And it will stay there until the time God has decided to destroy this one who destroys.
text: Niŋdeerɔ wala ale nye nɔiyeŋ ale nuruba yegayega bena ŋayopɔi, bena ŋata ale geli a dan taam, kaabka ale jiam teka a kan ŋman boro. Wabiok kuui ale ku jam a basi ate nuruba a nam la ale jam bo Wen yenni po kama. Ku ale boro ka dila a ta ga paari diipo ate waai ale basi ate ku boro la a jam paari ku da kpeglimaŋa po ase Wen ale gomsi a magsi wa diila.>>

ref: In the third year of Cyrus the king of Persia, a message came to Daniel from God, and it was explained in a vision. The message was about a dreadful war, and it was true.
text: Persia Naawa Sairus ale jam dɛ wa naamu a paari bena ŋatawa la, Daniel, waai ate ba jam a wi wa ayen Beltesazzar la, a yaa jam gɔdaasim a nya wasusugi. Wanni a jam ka wensie a ta va chaab ale kpaliŋ. Wa jam miŋ wanni kiri ka wa gɔdaasima po.

ref: Daniel wrote: For three weeks I was in sorrow.
text: Dila po mi, Daniel a jam a kum kama a ti ku ga paari daa pisiye ale dinyi.

ref: I ate no fancy food or meat, I drank no wine, and I put no olive oil on my face or hair.
text: Mi an dɛ ŋandiinta, m be an ŋɔbi lammoa yaase daam a tiri m nɔngbanvaataŋa yaase mi sa kpaammoa, ate daa pisiye ale dinyiwa meena a ga taamu.

ref: Then, on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing on the banks of the great Tigris River,
text: Chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la ka daa pisiye ale ŋanaansiwa danni, ase mi ale jam za beli kpienni ate ba a wi di ayen Tigris kuŋkuŋku zuk la,

ref: when I looked up and saw someone dressed in linen and wearing a solid gold belt.
text: mi yaa zak nya ŋmai ale ka nuru ale za mi niŋ a jo garuk ate ku a nyaksi ale pai ligmɔniŋ gbain a bobi wa chiaka.

ref: His body was like a precious stone, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming fires, his arms and legs like polished bronze, and his voice like the roar of a crowd.
text: Wa nyiŋka jam a nye ase ka tintain salima la. Wa nimbidiaka mɛ a nye nna se bolim la wa ninaŋa mɛ a nyaksi ase bolim ŋaasa la wa nisimaŋa ale wa naŋsaŋa mɛ a jam maari a nyaksi kama alege ate wa lueluku a nye ase nuru boari lueluta la.

ref: Although the people who were with me did not see the vision, they became so frightened that they scattered and hid.
text: Mi Daniel, nyiini ale waai ale jam nya wanni de, nuru baai ale jam bo dula ale mi la an jam nya wanni de. Kude a jam nye kama ate yɔgsum a yik ba ate ba yaa chali a suk.

ref: and at the sound of his voice, I fell facedown in a deep sleep.
text: Mi a yaa wom ale wa a biisi. Ase mi ale a wom wa la, mi yaa deri doa po nyiŋ a goa.

ref: and then said, “Daniel, your God thinks highly of you, and he has sent me. So stand up and pay close attention.” I stood trembling, while the angel said:
text: Ate wa weeni mi ayen Daniel Wen a yaali fu kama zaani nalimnyiini a wom dii ate mi a yaali ayen m weeni sak fu la, ba tom mu kama fi jigi. Ase wa ale weeni dii ale mi la, mi yaa yiti zaani ate m nyiŋka a gɔk.

ref: Daniel, don't be afraid! God has listened to your prayers since the first day you humbly asked for understanding, and he has sent me here.
text: Wa ŋman weeni mi Daniel ayen m ka a chali yɔgsummoa a zaani dai dii danni ate fi piilim a zɛri fidek ale a puusi ayen fi miŋ wanni kiri la, Wen a wom fi puusaŋa kama m jam kama ayen m tulisi fu puusaŋa.

ref: I will tell you what is written in The Book of Truth. But first, you must realize that no one except Michael, the guardian angel of Israel, is on my side.
text: Alege dii ale dɛ niŋ la mi a yaali m weeni ka dii ale ŋmarisi Wensie Gbaŋka po la. Waai an jam maari mi ate mi a kpaliŋ ale ba, ka Maakil waai ale a nya Izirali zuk la.

ref: While this angel was speaking to me, I stared at the ground, speechless.
text: Ase wa ale boro a weeni mi wanni de la, mi yaa koori a pai m ninaŋa a vuk tɛŋ chorototo.

ref: Then he appeared in human form and touched my lips. I said, “Sir, this vision has brought me great pain and has drained my strength.
text: Ate waai ale a nye ase nidoa la yaa tiri mi nɔngbanvaataŋa ate mi a jam lak m nɔnni a yaa piilim a biisi. Mi yaa weeni waai ale za m niŋ la ayen, <<Gɔdaasimaŋa de a basi kama ate m nyiŋka a kasim a gɔk.>>

ref: I am merely your servant. How can I possibly speak with someone so powerful, when I am almost too weak to get my breath?”
text: Mi fi tomteerɔwa, mi a yaa m nye ka sɛ a biisi ale fu m nyɔnɔ? M ŋman ka pagrimoa mi an baga a vuusi.>>

ref: Then the angel said: Now do you understand why I have come? Soon I must leave to fight against the guardian angel of Persia. Then after I have defeated him, the guardian angel of Greece will attack me.
text: Ate wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi seba dii nyiŋ ate mi a jam fi jigi la? Ku kan beni m le pilim ŋmani a ga kpaliŋ ale maarɔ waai ale a nya Persia tɛŋka zuk la, ase m dan ga cheŋ nueri maarɔ waai ale a nya Girik tɛŋka zuk la mɛ ale jam.

ref: You also need to know that I protected and helped Darius the Mede in his first year as king. The Angel's Message to Daniel Part One: The Four Kings and Their Successors
text: Bein dii ate Miidi denɔwa Darius a dɛ wa naamu la mi zaani kama a te wa nyiŋbiiri.

ref: What I am going to tell you is certain to happen. Four kings will rule Persia, one after the other, but the fourth one will become much richer than the others. In fact, his wealth will make him so powerful that he will turn everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
text: <<Yɔgyɔgla de, mi a weeni fu ka wensie nuruba bata ale za ba yiti a dɛ naam Persia tɛŋka po ate waai ale wa saari banaansiwa la ale jigsi a gaam mbala. Wa yaa dan nya pagrim wa jigsika nyiŋ, wa ale nye ate waai meena a nye kpaliŋ ale Girik tɛŋka.

ref: Then a mighty king will come to power and will be able to do whatever he pleases.
text: Naab kpioŋ ale jam waai ale wa a nya ni zuk ale pagrim abe wa nye dii ale a yɔk wa suinni la.

ref: But suddenly his kingdom will be crushed and scattered to the four corners of the earth, where four more kingdoms will rise. But these won't be ruled by his descendants or be as powerful as his kingdom.
text: Wa dan jam a ga nueri wa tɛŋka ale poori bunaansi. Nalima ŋaai ale kan nyini wa buuni po la ale jam tuesi wa tɛŋka alege bala a kan ta pagrim ase wa ale jam ka diila.

ref: The king of the south will grow powerful. Then one of his generals will rebel and will rule an even larger kingdom.
text: Ejipiti Naawa ale jam ta pagrim alege wa ŋaaŋviirɔma wanyi ale ta pagrim a gaam wadek a yaa a nya wa mɛ dek tɛŋka zuk.

ref: Years later the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom will make a treaty, and the daughter of the king of the south will marry the king of the north. But she will lose her power. Then she, her husband, their child, and the servants who came with her will all be killed. After this,
text: Bena maga dega a dan ga taam Ejipiti naawa ale nye nɔiyeŋ ale Siriya naawa a pai wa lie a yalisi wa alege ba nɔiyeŋka a kan beni ate wa chorɔwa ale wa biika ale wa tomteerɔma baai meena ale va wa a cheŋ la, ba ale ko ba meena kama.

ref: one of her relatives will become the ruler of the southern kingdom. He will attack the army of the northern kingdom and capture its fortresses.
text: Ku kan beni nipowa buuni po nuru ale jam chim naab. Wala ale nye kpaliŋ ale Siriya naawa tugurik tɔŋdɔma a jo ba tɛŋka po a nak yik ba.

ref: Then he will carry their idols to Egypt, together with their precious treasures of silver and gold, but it will be a long time before he attacks the northern kingdom again. Some years later
text: Wa ale tuesi ba bɔgtaŋa ale ba ŋan baai ate ba pai kuta a nye ba la ale ba kpana ale ligmɔniŋka a ta ba a cheŋ Ejipiti tɛŋka. Bena maga dega a dan taam wa le basi Siriya naawa.

ref: the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom, but he will be forced back to his own country.
text: Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ Siriya naawa ale jo Ejipiti tɛŋka po a tuesi ka ate ba pilim yik wa ate wa ŋmani a kuli wadek tɛŋka.

ref: The sons of the king of the north will gather a huge army that will sweep down like a roaring flood, reaching all the way to the fortress of the southern kingdom.
text: Siriya Naawa bisaŋa ale gomsi badek ayen ba nye kpaliŋ. Ba le tigsi tugurik tɔŋdɔba ate ba piisi a magsi dila.

ref: But this will make the king of the south angry, and he will defeat this large army from the north.
text: <<Ate Ejipiti Naawa yaa le tu suik ale suipuurum a nye kpaliŋ ale Siriya Naawa, waai ale ta tugurik tɔŋdɔba a piisi la a nak yik ba.

ref: The king of the south will feel proud because of the many thousands he has killed. But his victories won't last long,
text: Ase ba dan yik ba a ta cheŋ Ejipiti Naawa ale ta kanjanta ate dila ale basi ate wa togri nuruba a paari tusa alege wa kan nya nakdeka.

ref: because the king of the north will gather a larger and more powerful army than ever before. Then in a few years, he will start invading other countries.
text: Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ Siriya Naawa ŋman yaali tugurik tɔŋdɔba ate bala ale piisi a gaam piilimka ate bena yega ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa le kasim a duŋ ale kpaliŋ nyeerɔ boari ale kpaliŋ kɔlima.

ref: At this time many of your own people will try to make this vision come true by rebelling against the king of the south, but their rebellion will fail.
text: Da ŋala po nuruba yegayega a kan siak a te Ejipiti Naawa. Gaasa nuruba ale nyini fi Daniel dek nuruma po a nye si fi gɔdaasimaŋa ale weeni diila alege ba kan nya suik a nye dila.

ref: Then the army from the north will surround and capture a fortress in the south, and not even the most experienced troops of the southern kingdom will be able to make them retreat.
text: Ate Siriya naawa a yaa le jam a nye kpaliŋ a tuesi tɛŋ maŋsaŋa gela. Ejipiti tugurik tɔŋdɔma a kan baga a nye kpaliŋ ale ba. Baai dek ate ba a poli ayen ba ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba dek la a kan poom ŋman ta pagrim ale magadek mɛ la.

ref: The king who invaded from the north will do as he pleases, and he will even capture and destroy the holy land.
text: Siriya demma a yaa le kasim a nye ka dii ale a yɔk ba sueŋa la ate waai a kan bola a zaani ale wa. Wa yaa le jo ka tɛŋka dek po a ta pagrim ka zuk.

ref: In fact, he will decide to invade the south with his entire army. Then he will attempt to make peace by giving the king of the south a bride from the northern kingdom, but this won't be successful.
text: Siriya naawa ale gomsi kama nalimnyiini a pai wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena a tom tuima, dii le ku basi ate wa baga a nya pagrim wa dachaasaŋa zuk. Wa ale nye nɔiyeŋ ale wa a pai wa liewa a yalisi wa a yaali ayen wa va dila nye a nya pagrim ba zuk ale dila meena wa kan diem a nya suik a nye wa ale a yaali diila.

ref: Afterwards, this proud king of the north will invade and conquer many of the nations along the coast, but a military leader will defeat him and make him lose his pride.
text: Dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa yaa le nye ka kpaliŋ ale tɛŋ sii ale kala a moata nyiamu nɔi la a nya pagrim si yega zuk. Alege ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ tɛŋ yoŋ nuru ale jam a nak yik wa ate wa kanjantaŋa ale nueri dula jigini.

ref: He will retreat to his fortresses in his own country, but on the way he will be defeated and never again be seen.
text: Kula meena ŋaaŋnyiŋ naawa a yaa le pilim ŋmani kama ayen wa cheŋ wadek tɛŋka, ate ba yaa le yik wa dula jigini ate wa naamu mɛ a nueri dula.

ref: The next king of the north will try to collect taxes for the glory of his kingdom. However, he will come to a sudden end in some mysterious way, instead of in battle or because of someone's anger. Part Two: The Evil King from the North
text: Naab waai ale nak a yik wa la ale basi kama ate lampoo cheesirɔ a va wa ga cheesi ligra ate dila a nye ate naab paalika tɛŋka mɛ a jigsi. Dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ ku kan beni ba ale ko wa kama ate waai a kan nya.

ref: The successor of this king of the north will be a worthless nobody, who doesn't even come from a royal family. He will suddenly appear and gain control of the kingdom by treachery.
text: Maarɔwa a yaa weeni ayen, <<Siriya naab waai ale kala wa dɛ naamu la ale chim ka nuru biok waai ale kan magsi ayen wa chim naaba, alege wa ale chim naab a diiri ni kama.

ref: He will make a treaty, but he will be deceitful and break it, even though he has only a few followers.
text: Ase wa dan nye nɔiyeŋka ale ba wa le paasi ba, wa le nuruba maga ale yiti nya pagrim.
