text: Ba dan jueli Karmel guuku, mi ale yik ba meena a ta ba siŋ tɛŋ. Ba dan suk badek nyakpiemu tɛŋ dula mi ale basi ate waab a dom ba.

ref: I'll send a sword to kill them, wherever their enemies drag them off as captives. I'm determined to hurt them, not to help them.” His Name Is the Lord
text: Ba dachaasaŋa ale yik ba ta ga basi badek tɛŋ po ate m le te ba ko ba. M kan maari ba. M za m kaasi ba kama. M le pai biem nina a nya ba alege daa nalimmoa.>>

ref: When the Lord God All-Powerful touches the earth, it melts, and its people mourn. God makes the earth rise and then fall, just like the Nile River.
text: Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, waai ale a tiri tɛŋka ate ka a nyaliŋ la, ate baai meena ale bo ka po la a kum. Tɛŋka meena a yiti kama ase Nile benni la, a yaa siŋ ase Ejipiti benni la.

ref: He built his palace in the heavens and let its foundations rest on the earth. He scoops up the ocean and empties it on the earth. His name is the Lord. The Lord Is God
text: Naawen dii ale sɛ wa yenni wenŋmazuk la ale nye di nyubini tɛŋka zuk la, waai ale basi ate nyakpiemu nyaataŋa a tagli tɛŋka meena la. Wa yuei ale Naawen.

ref: Israel, I am the Lord God, and the Ethiopians are no less important to me than you are. I brought you out of Egypt, but I also brought the Philistines from Crete and the Arameans from Kir.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Izirali demma, nama ale tɛŋ yoŋ dem, ase Kus demma daa bunyi? Mi a yeeri Izirali demma a nyini yontidi po Ejipiti tɛŋka po, Filistia demma nyini Kaftor po ate Araam demma nyini Kir tɛŋka po?

ref: My eyes have seen what a sinful nation you are, and I'll wipe you out. But I will leave a few of Jacob's descendants. I, the Lord, have spoken!
text: <<Chekki Nyɔnɔwa Naawen a nya Izirali tɛŋka demma wabaataŋa kama m be za m kaasi ba kama a ta nyini tɛŋka zuk. Alege m kan kaasi Jekob ŋaaŋsaŋa meena.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: At my command, all of you will be sifted like grain. Israelites who remain faithful will be scattered among the nations. And the others will be trapped like trash in a sifter.
text: <<Mi ale te ka nɔi, ayen tɛŋ yonsa demma a nye Izirali demma ase ba ale a yɛliŋ zom diila a yeeri baai ale kan ta kiri la a basi.

ref: Some of you are evil, and you deny that you will ever get caught. But you will be killed. The Lord's Promise to Israel
text: Wabaata nyama ale maa pulim nuruma po la meena a za ba kpi kama kpaliŋ po, ale baai mɛ ale weeni ayen kaasuŋ a kan paari ba la mɛ la meena.>>

ref: In the future, I will rebuild David's fallen kingdom. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again, just as it used to be.
text: Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Dai ale jam ate mi ale ŋman pilim pai Izirali demma pagrimu a te ni ase diipo ate Deevid a jam ka naab la. Ba yie ŋaai ale lo la, mi ale pilim a sɛ ŋa ate ŋa pilim a nye ase ŋa nyiem ale jam ka diila.

ref: Then you will capture Edom and the other nations that are mine. I, the Lord, have spoken, and my words will come true.
text: Ate ba pilim a nak tuesi Edom demma ale bo tɛŋ sii po la meena ale tɛŋ sii meena ale ta mi yuenni la.>> Ka Naawen dii ale wa nye wieŋa de la ale weeni.

ref: You will have such a harvest that you won't be able to bring in all of your wheat before plowing time. You will have grapes left over from season to season; your fruitful vineyards will cover the mountains.
text: Naawen ale weeni ayen, <<Daaŋa a cheena ate naa kpaarɔwa ale gaam cheerɔwa a taam. Ate yɔn pisidɔwa a gaam vukdɔwa a taam. Da paalik ale nyini pinaŋa po a tagli guutaŋa meena zuk.

ref: I'll plant your roots deep in the land I have given you, and you won't ever be uprooted again. I, the Lord God, have spoken!
text: Mi ale te Izirali demma a kali ba tɛŋka po waai a kan ŋman yiak ba a nyini tɛŋ kaai ate mi a pai a te ba la.>> Ka Naawen fi Wenni ale weeni.

ref: The Lord God gave Obadiah a message about Edom, and this is what we heard: “I, the Lord, have sent a messenger with orders for the nations to attack Edom.”
text: Obadia ale jam gɔdaasim diila ale nna. Nya kude ate Nyɔnɔwa Naawen a weeni a magsi chaab ale Edom. Ti wom ka wari a nyini Naawen jigi ayen, Waai ale ba tom ayen wa cheŋ tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po a ga weeni ayen, <<Yiti, ate ti cheŋ a ga siti tugurik ale wa.>>

ref: The Lord said to Edom: I will make you the weakest and most despised nation.
text: <<Nya, m le nye ate fi fiisa tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po. Ba ale valiŋ fu.

ref: You live in a mountain fortress, because your pride makes you feel safe from attack, but you are mistaken.
text: Fi suinummu kanjantaŋa a paasi fu kama, fi waai ale bo pinaŋa po ale sɛ fi yenni ŋmai la, fi weeni ka fidek ayen, <Ka wana ale wa ta mi a siŋ tɛŋŋa?>

ref: I will still bring you down, even if you fly higher than an eagle or nest among the stars. I, the Lord, have spoken!
text: Fi poom a yiri wen ase ka jiiruk la ale a yɔk fi tukku chiŋmarisaŋa po, dula ate m le ta fu a siŋ tɛŋ,>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

ref: If thieves break in at night, they steal only what they want. And people who harvest grapes always leave some unpicked. But, Edom, you are doomed!
text: <<Ase zueba nin jam fi jigi, ate varidɔba a jam fi jigi yok. Ka boa kaasuŋ choa ate fi za fi tu. Ba kan zu koalim daa jaab buuri meena ate ba a yaali la? Yɔn pisidɔba a dan jam fi jigi, ba kan pisi abe ba tali gela a basi?

ref: Everything you treasure most will be taken from you.
text: Alege nya ba ale vari Iisɔ dii yaa, ba koalim wa nitalimu ate wa pai suk la kama.

ref: Your allies can't be trusted. They will force you out of your own country. And your best friends will trick and trap you, even before you know it.
text: Fi sɔmma meena ale fɛ fu a ta cheŋ tɛŋka banni. Fi doama ale paasi fu a nya pagrim fi zuk. Baai ale a dɛ fi ŋandiintaŋa la ale bari fu alege fi kan miŋ ku.

ref: Warriors from the city of Teman will be terrified, and you descendants of Esau will be wiped out. The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
text: Teman, fi tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaziita ale nak, ate waai meena ale bo Iisɔ guutaŋa po la ale kpi tugurik po.

ref: You were cruel to your relatives, the descendants of Jacob. Now you will be destroyed, disgraced forever.
text: Wɔkwɔkka ate fi jam nye ale fi suoku Jekob la nyiŋ, chivie ale lik fu. Fi ale kaasi kama taam wuu.

ref: You stood there and watched as foreigners entered Jerusalem and took what they wanted. In fact, you were no better than those foreigners.
text: Fi jam nye ase ka ba la la, dai dila danni fi jam za a nya kama ate nicham a ji ba jigsika ŋantaŋa, ate nicham a va ba nansuiŋtaŋa a jo a nak gbaŋ Jerusalem nyiŋ.

ref: Why did you celebrate when such a dreadful disaster struck your relatives? Why were you so pleased when everyone in Judah was suffering?
text: Ku an magsi ayen fi valiŋ fi suoku dai dii danni ate wa bo daanika po la, yaase fi dɛ masim dai dii danni ate Juda demma a bo kaasuŋ po la, yaase fi kuulim nna yegayega ba daanika danni po.

ref: In their time of torment, you ambushed refugees and handed them over to their attackers. The Lord Will Judge the Nations
text: Ku an magsi ayen fi za suimagsa po a yik baai ale chali a bɛ la, yaase fi pai baai ale vuuk la a nyo ba nisa po.

ref: The day is coming when I, the Lord, will judge the nations. And, Edom, you will pay in full for what you have done.
text: <<Naawen danni a moata kama a te tɛŋ kpieŋsa meena. Ase fi ale nye diila, ba ale nye fi mɛ dila. Fi tuimaŋa ale ŋman pilim siŋ fidek zuk po.

ref: I forced the people of Judah to drink the wine of my anger on my sacred mountain. Soon the neighboring nations must drink their fill— then vanish without a trace. Victory for Israel
text: Ase fi ale jam nyu daam m tuilum guuku zuk diila, dila mɛ ate tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa meena ale kasim a nyu daam. Ba ale kasim a nyu kama ate ku ale nye ba jigi nna se ba an poom nyu daam a nya la.

ref: The Lord's people who escape will go to Mount Zion, and it will be holy. Then Jacob's descendants will capture the land of those who took their land.
text: Alege varibasika ale bo Zayon Guuku zuk. Ka ale ta tuilum ate Jekob yenni ale soa ka nitalimu.

ref: The people of Israel who live in the Southern Desert will take the land of Edom. Those who live in the hills will capture Philistia, Ephraim, and Samaria. And the tribe of Benjamin will conquer Gilead.
text: Nuru baai ale nyini Negev la ale bo Iisɔ guutaŋa, ate nuru baai ale nyini guutaŋa tɛŋsa la ale soa Filistia demma tɛŋka. Ba ale tuesi Ɛfraim ale Samaria kaduksaŋa, abe Benjamin a soa Gilead.

ref: Those who return from captivity will control Phoenicia as far as Zarephath. Captives from Jerusalem who were taken to Sepharad will capture the towns of the Southern Desert.
text: Izirali dem baai ale bo Keenan la ale soa tɛŋka a ga paari Zarefat. Nuru baai ale nyini Jerusalem ale ga bo Sefarad la ale soa Negev tɛŋ fiisaŋa.

ref: Those the Lord has saved will live on Mount Zion and rule over Edom. Then the kingdom will belong to the Lord.
text: Varibasidɔba le cheŋ jueli Zayon Guuku zuk a nya Iisɔ guutaŋa zuk. Ate Naawen ale soa naamu.

ref: One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai,
text: Naawen a yaa biisi ale Amittai nidoabinni Jona ayen,

ref: to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
text: <<Cheŋ tɛŋ kpieŋka Niineve a ga biisi ale ka nuruma, dii nyiŋla ka nuruma biemu a zuak kama m niŋ.>>

ref: Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
text: Alege Jona a yiti chali a bɛ Naawen niŋ. Wa jam chali a cheŋ ka Tarsis tɛŋka. Wa abe liŋ jam cheŋ ka Jopa tɛŋka a yaa nya ŋaaruŋ ale ku a cheŋ Tarsis. Wa yaa tuni ale ge jueli ate ku ta wa a cheŋ Tarsis ayen wa chali bɛ Naawen.

ref: But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces.
text: Naawen a yaa basi ate va pagrik a fuk nyiamu ate ŋaaruŋku a tali maga ate ku mobi kabakaba.

ref: The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
text: Nuru waai ale chim kpagi a nya ŋaaruŋku zuk la, a yaa cheŋ wa jigi a ga weeni wa ayen, <<Ka boan nyiŋ ate fi doa goa? Yiti ŋmai a wi fi wenni. Fi wenni ale naam chali ti jiirim a vari ti a basi ate ti kan kpi.>>

ref: Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
text: Ŋaaruŋku damdɔma a yaa wi chaab a weeni chaab ayen, <<Ni jam ate ti nak gbaŋ ate ti nya ase ka wana ale soa ate wapagni de a paari ti.>> Ba yaa nak gbaŋka ate ka za lɔ Jona zuk.

ref: They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
text: Ba yaa bek wa ayen, a weeni, <<Ka wana ale soa ate ninammu de a jam tama zuwa? Fi nye ka boa? Fi nyini ka be? Fi nyini ka tɛŋ kana? Fi ka boan buuri?>>

ref: Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
text: Wa yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Mi ka Yiburu denɔ, a puusi Naawen, Wen dii ale soa wenŋmazuk la, waai ale nye nyakpiemu ale tɛŋka la.>>

ref: When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
text: Jona tulisaŋa a yaa nak ba kpaziim ate ba yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi nye?>> Ba poom jam seba kama ayen Jona a chali a bɛ kama Naawen niŋ dii nyiŋla wa ŋaam jam weeni ba kama.

ref: The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
text: Ŋaaruŋku damdɔma ale a biisi ale Jona la, nyiamu choaka a ŋman ŋmasi a gaam di. Ba yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ti be ti nye fu ka sɛ ate nyiamu a baliŋ a te ti?>>

ref: Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
text: Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni koati mu a lɔnsi nyiamu po dila ale bu baliŋ. Mi seba ayen ka mi nyiŋ ale soa ate daanika de a paari ni.>>

ref: The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute.
text: Jona ale biisi nnala a nueri la, ŋaaruŋku damdɔma a diem pii ka nyiŋ ayen ba dam ŋaaruŋku a ta ŋmani jueli kunkɔŋi alege ba an jam baga dii nyiŋla nyiamu choaka a jam pagra ka nna yegayega a gaam bu nyiem ale ka dii la.

ref: So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.”
text: Ba yaa kum te Naawen weeni ayen, <<Naawen yaa, kan ko ti ase tama a nin ko nuruwa de. Kan te ti pamiya ase tama a nin ko nuru waai ale kan kaasi tuini la, dii nyiŋla ka fi Naawen yaa, ale tom fidek ale a yaali diila.>>

ref: Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down.
text: Ba yaa koati Jona a lɔnsi nyiamu po ate nyiamu ale a dɛ bu tuemu la a yaa deri baliŋ.

ref: The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
text: Damdɔma ale nya ale nyiamu a baliŋ la, ba yaa chali yɔgsum ale Naawen ate ba nye kaabka a te Naawen ale puulim ayen ba le kasim a zuli wa.

ref: The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
text: Alege Naawen a gomsi jum kpioŋ ate bu nɛ Jona. Jona jam bo jummu poni po ka daa ŋata.

ref: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
text: Jona yaa duak jummu poni po a puusi te Naawen wa Wenni.

ref: When I was in trouble, Lord, I prayed to you, and you listened to me. From deep in the world of the dead, I begged for your help, and you answered my prayer.
text: Wa weeni ayen, <<M ninammu po m wi Naawen Yuei ate wa tulisi mu. M le bo vɔrumu po la, m wi wa a bek maarika, ate fi wom m kumsa.

ref: You threw me down to the bottom of the sea. The water was churning all around; I was completely covered by your mighty waves.
text: Fi yuk mu a basi nyakpiemu po juijui ate nyiamu ale nya miisaŋa a gilim mu.

ref: I thought I was swept away from your sight, never again to see your holy temple.
text: <<M weeni ayen, <Fi zɛri mu kama, alege m diem za ayen m cheŋ fi yenni po kama a puusi fu.>

ref: I was almost drowned by the swirling waters that surrounded me. Seaweed had wrapped around my head.
text: Nya buui ale a lim a gilim mu la a paari ka m ŋiri, liuŋku a gilim mu kama, beni wuutaŋa a bobi m zukku mɛ.

ref: I had sunk down deep below the mountains beneath the sea. I knew that forever, I would be a prisoner there. But, you, Lord God, rescued me from that pit.
text: M siŋ paari ka nyiamu niŋniŋa ase gu kpioŋ chiak ate m za la juijui ate ba lik tɛŋka tuataŋa diipo meena wuu. Naawen m Wen yaa, alege fi dari mu yeeri vɔrumu po a pilim te mu vum.

ref: When my life was slipping away, I remembered you— and in your holy temple you heard my prayer.
text: M daam le boro a jɔk m nyuvunni la, Naawen yaa, m teeri fi wari, a yaa jo fi yenni po a puusi a te fu.

ref: All who worship worthless idols turn from the God who offers them mercy.
text: Baai ale pai badek a seeri bɔgta la a yeeri badek Naawen jigi kama a kan nya wa jiirimu.

ref: But with shouts of praise, I will offer a sacrifice to you, my Lord. I will keep my promise, because you are the one with power to save.
text: Alege mi, ale pai ka yiila a nye kaabka a te fu. M le puulim ayen mi le nye diila, mi le nye ate ku nala. Varibasika a nyini ka Naawen jigi.>>

ref: The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
text: Jona ale puusi nnala a nueri jummu poni po la, Naawen a yaa weeni jummu ate bu ta Jona jueli kunkɔŋi a chiiri wa dueni vuta.

ref: Once again the Lord told Jonah
text: Naawen a yaa ŋman biisi ale Jona ku naŋtuok nɔi buye.

ref: to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
text: <<Cheŋ Niineve tɛŋ kpieŋka a weeni ba wa dii ate m pai te fu ayen fi weeni ba la.>>

ref: Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it.
text: Jona a yaa siak Naawen nɔi a yaa cheŋ Niineve. Niineve jam ka tɛŋ kpieŋ. Ba pai ka daa ŋata a cheŋ a paari ka.

ref: After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
text: Jona ale cheŋ paari Niineve wa pai ka dai a cheŋ mooli Naawen ale weeni wa diila ayen, <<Da pisinaansi ale tali ate Naawen yik Niineve nuruma ale ka jaab meena kaasi.>>

ref: They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
text: Jona ale biisi nnala a nueri la, Niineve nuruma a yaa siak Naawen lueluku. Ba yaa nya chaab a zɛri ŋandiinta dɛka. A zaani ba ŋankpagsa ta ga paari ba bimbaansa meena a yaa pai boorisa gatta a jo ayen ku sak ayen ba sue a kaasi ale ba wabaataŋa kama.

ref: When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust.
text: Ba le weeni ate ku paari Niineve naawa, Naawen ale weeni diila, wa yaa yeeri wa naamu gattaŋa ale yaali boorisa gatta a jo a yiri wa naamu zaŋgɔŋka zuk a siŋ kala tantaŋa po.

ref: When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
text: Wen ale nya ba le nye diila, ale ba le pai ba biemu nyeka a basi la, Wen jiirim a yaa dari ba ate wa an ŋman ta kaasika jam ba jigi ya ase wa le poom piilim poli ayen wa kaasi ba diila.

ref: So he prayed: Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
text: Wa yaa puusi a te Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Naawen yaa, daa m ni poom bo yeri a weeni diila ale la? Ka fi nye ka de nyiŋ ale soa ate mi din banti ale chali a cheŋ Tarsis la. Mi seba kama ayen fi ka jiirim kpiem nyɔnɔ ate fi sui yirika a toa ate fi ŋmanteka mɛ a ka bain ya, fi ka Wen dii ale ka a daliŋ fi vɔŋ te la.

ref: The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
text: Alege Naawen a ya tulisi wa ayen, <<Ka din dek nyiŋ ale soa ate fi basi ate fi sui a puuri?>>

ref: Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
text: Jona yaa nyini tɛŋka po a nyini a taam ka kori geŋ a ti viuk a yaa jo kali ku po a limisi ase Naawen ale kaasi tɛŋka ya.

ref: The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine,
text: Naawen dii ale ka Wen la yaa basi ate tunuŋ a nyini chim yɔgsum a liŋ Jona zukku ate wa yaa kala. Jona sui jam peenti ka nna yegayega ale tunuku yɔgsummu.

ref: but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up.
text: Vari ale veenti la, saluik yokyokwa Wen a yaa basi nanzuiri ate di dɛ tunuku kinni ate ku kpi.

ref: During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
text: Wenbinni ale pusi la, Wen a yaa basi ate kantueŋ wuluk a ŋari nyini koni po a nak Jona zukku ate wa buk nna zana. Wa jaa yaa ka kum nyiini. Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<M dan jɔk kpi a zunchoŋ m le vua la kama.>>

ref: But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?” “Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
text: Naawen a yaa bek Jona ayen, <<Fi ta suik a basi ate fi sui a puuri ale tunuku ale kpi la nyiŋŋa?>> Jona yaa tulisi ayen, M ta suik kama. M suinni ale puuri diila m yaa a yaali ka kum nyiini.>>

ref: But the Lord said: You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next.
text: Naawen yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Tunuku ale nyini la, fi a kpa gilim ku, fi a nyo bibaam ku tɛŋa. Ku pai ka yok yeŋ a nyini, a ŋman pai yok yeŋ a kpi, alege fi basi ate fi sui a puuri ale ku kum.

ref: In that city of Nineveh there are more than
text: Alege Niineve a ta ka nuruba ate ba piisi gaam tusa kook ale pisiye (

ref: people who cannot tell right from wrong, and many cattle are also there. Don't you think I should be concerned about that big city?
text: ) ate ba zɛ ba juga ale ba gala. Ba bi ta niiga mɛ kama a piisi. Ku a magsi ayen m basi ate m jiirim a dari tɛŋ kpieŋ ka dɛ?>>

ref: I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah. Judgment on Samaria
text: Naawen wa dii ale jan jam Maika ale nyini Moreset la jigi. Di jam ka va ŋaai po ate Jotam dɛ naam ate Ayazi a jam dɛ ate Azekaya mɛ a jam dɛ Juda la. Wa le jam nya wa dii a magsi chaab ale Samaria ale Jerusalem la ale nna:

ref: Listen, all of you! Earth and everything on it, pay close attention. The Lord God accuses you from his holy temple.
text: Nuruba, ni wom, ni meena abe wom, tɛŋzuk de ale baai meena ale bo ka po la, ayen Nyɔnɔwa Naawen a nya ni ale nye dii a kaasi la kama. Nyɔnɔwa a nyini ka wa yenni po.

ref: And he will come down to crush underfoot every pagan altar.
text: Nya! Naawen a nyini ka wa bo ka jigini a cheena. Wa siŋ cheen kama ayen wa tabi tɛŋzuk de guutaŋa zuk.

ref: Mountains will melt beneath his feet like wax beside a fire. Valleys will vanish like water rushing down a ravine.
text: Guutaŋa a nyaliŋ kama wa naŋtaata po, ate vaasaŋa a lab ase bolim ale paari zirima diila ase nyiam ale va churintika jigi a siŋ diila.

ref: This will happen because of the terrible sins of Israel, the descendants of Jacob. Samaria has led Israel to sin, and pagan altars at Jerusalem have made Judah sin.
text: Nya kude meena ka Jekob nye kaasuŋku ale Izirali wabaataŋa nyiŋ. Ka boa ale Jekob nye kaasuŋku? Ku daa Samaria? Ka boa ale Juda puusika jigini? Daa Jerusalem?

ref: So the Lord will leave Samaria in ruins— merely an empty field where vineyards are planted. He will scatter its stones and destroy its foundations.
text: <<Dila nyiŋ m le nye ate Samaria a chim guura, a chim kaduk ate ba a bori ŋanta ka po. M le kpiiri ka tanaŋa a basi viaka po ate ka nyubaŋa a doa jassi.

ref: Samaria's idols will be smashed, and the wages of temple prostitutes will be destroyed by fire. Silver and gold from those idols will then be used by foreigners as payment for prostitutes. Judah Is Doomed
text: Ka bɔgtaŋa meena ale ŋɔriŋ nna bunabuna. Ka yenni tiiritaŋa meena ale dɛ bolim. M le kaasi ka ŋanmɛɛntaŋa meena. Ka ale toalim a tigsi ka tiiritaŋa a nyini ka taabuksa tutuna jigi la, ase taabuksa tutuna la ate ba ale ŋman pai ŋa a tom.>>

ref: Because of this tragedy, I go barefoot and naked. My crying and weeping sound like howling wolves or ostriches.
text: Nya kude nyiŋ m le kum abe m wooli. M le cheŋ naŋta bie ale chaboala. M le wooli ase gɔi biak la, abe m siŋti ase viuk la.

ref: The nation is fatally wounded. Judah is doomed. Jerusalem will fall.
text: Diila wa niraŋa a kan nueri. Ku cheŋ paarika Juda. Ku paarika m nuruma Jerusalem dek nansuiŋku nɔi.

ref: Don't tell it in Gath! Don't even cry. Instead, roll in the dust at Beth-Leaphrah.
text: Kan weeni ku Gat po. Kan poom kum. Bilim fidek Bet Ofra paasuku po.

ref: Depart naked and ashamed, you people of Shaphir. The town of Bethezel mourns because no one from Zaanan went out to help.
text: Nama baai ale bo Safir po la, ni cheŋ chaboala ale chivie. Baai ale bo Zaanan po la a kan nyini peelim. Bet Ezel a bo ka kumsa po. Ba pai jabuui ale a nya ba zuk la kama ta cheŋ.

ref: Everyone in Maroth hoped for the best, but the Lord sent disaster down on Jerusalem.
text: Baai ale bo Marot la a viriŋ ale ka nyiŋdomma a limisi nyiŋyɔgsa, dii nyiŋla kaasuŋ a nyini ka Naawen jigi a jam, a poom ga paari Jerusalem nansuiŋku nɔi.

ref: Get the war chariots ready, you people of Lachish. You led Jerusalem into sin, just as Israel did.
text: Nama baai ale bo Lachis la, ni bobi wusumaŋa a maŋ torokowa. Nama ale piilim a nye Zayon Liewa biem. Dii nyiŋla ba nya Izirali wabaataŋa ka fi po.

ref: Now you will have to give a going-away gift to Moresheth. Israel's kings will discover that they cannot trust the town of Achzib.
text: Dila nyiŋ ni ale te Moreset Gat basika tiirita. Akzib tɛŋka ale paasi Izirali nalimaŋa.

ref: People of Mareshah, the Lord will send someone to capture your town. Then Israel's glorious king will be forced to hide in Adullam Cave.
text: M le basi ate nakdeerɔ a jam nama baai ale bo Maresa po la zuk. Waai ale ka Izirali zula la ale jam Adullam.

ref: Judah, shave your head as bald as a vulture and start mourning. Your precious children will be dragged off to a foreign country.
text: Ni poni ni zuimaŋa abe ni a kum ni bisaŋa ate ni ta suipeentik ba nyiŋla. Ni nye ate ni zuimaŋa a kpa ase duiŋ la, diila bisaŋa ale nyini ni jigi kama a cheŋ tɛŋ yoŋ po.

ref: Doomed! You're doomed! At night you lie in bed, making evil plans. And when morning comes, you do what you've planned because you have the power.
text: Ku ale toa a te baai ale a zɔk wabaata ale baai ale a zɔk biem ba gaduata zuk la! Saluiku po ba nyiem yaa ji kama a ta nyini dii nyiŋla ba ta pagrim kama a nye di.

ref: You grab any field or house that you want; you cheat families out of homes and land.
text: Ba nina a muni ale nuruba kaduksa ale a vari ba yieŋa. Ba a vari nuru wa yeri po ale a vari wa vaanchoa nitalim.

ref: But here is what the Lord says: “I am planning trouble for you. Your necks will be caught in a noose, and you will be disgraced in this time of disaster.”
text: Dila nyiŋ, Naawen a weeni kama ayen, <<M boro a zɔk ka kaasuŋ nuruma de zuk ate ba kan baga a vari badek a basi. Ni kan ŋman cheŋ kanjanta po, diila va ŋala ale chim ka kaasuŋ.

ref: When that happens, this sorrowful song will be sung about you: “Ruined! Completely ruined! The Lord has taken our land and given it to traitors.”
text: Dai dila danni nidoaba ale nye fu a la. Ba ale nye ate ni sue a puuri ale kumsa yiini de ayen, <Ti kaasi kama. Ba lab m nuruma ŋantaŋa a te ka chaab. Wa pai a nyini m jigi! Wa pai ti kaduksaŋa te bumbobrɔba.>>

ref: And so you will never again own property among the Lord's people.
text: Dila nyiŋ fi kan nya waai Naawen nuruma po ate wa nak gbaŋ a lab tɛŋka.

ref: “Enough of your preaching!” That's what you tell me. “We won't be disgraced, so stop preaching!”
text: Ba biisiteerɔma a weeni kama ayen, <<Ni kan biisi. Ni kan biisi ŋantaŋa de wie. Chivie a kan bag ti.>>

ref: Descendants of Jacob, is it right for you to claim that the Lord did what he did because he was angry? Doesn't he always bless those who do right?
text: Jekob yenni ale weeni ayen, <<Naawen Chiika sui a puuri kama? Wa a nye ŋade chaab kama? Mi wieŋa kan nye nalim a te waai suita ale nala la?

ref: My people, you have turned against one another! You have even stolen clothes right off the backs of innocent neighbors who pass by in peace.
text: Mi nuruma a yiti ka yɔgyɔgla de ase dachiak la. Ni vari jigsika garukku a nyini baai ale va suiku a taam la ate ni niŋ a poom ka ba po nna se nidoaba ale nyini kpaliŋ po a cheena la.

ref: You take over lovely homes that belong to the women of my nation. Then you cheat their children out of the inheritance that comes from the Lord.
text: Ni yiak m nuruma nipooma a nyini ba yie naliŋsaŋa po. Ni pai m niauŋku a nyini ba bisaŋa jigi taam wuu.

ref: Get out of here, you crooks! You'll find no rest here. You're not fit to belong to the Lord's people, and you will be destroyed.
text: Ni yiti zaani, cheŋ niŋ! Diila dela daa ni vuusum jigi ya, dii nyiŋla ka daŋ kama. Ka kaasi kama ate jaab karo a yik ka nye a magsi.

ref: The only prophet you want is a liar who will say, “Drink and get drunk!” A Promise of Hope
text: Ase velimvendik ale pimpaasirɔ a dan jam weeni ayen, <Mi le mooli ate daam ale buui ale a buk la a jam ni jigi.> Wa le chim ka biisiteerɔ waai ate nuruma de a yaali la!

ref: I, the Lord, promise to bring together the people of Israel who have survived. I will gather them, just as a shepherd brings sheep together, and there will be many.
text: <<Jekob, m le sum a tigsi ni meena. M le sum a ta Izirali dem baai ale tali la a jam jigi yeŋ. M le ta ba a jam jigi yeŋ ase piisa ale bo zɔŋ po diila. Ba ale bo jigi yeŋ ase piisa ale bo wuyɔgsuk po diila. Nuruba ale sueri jigini.

ref: Listen to me, you rulers of Israel! You know right from wrong,
text: Ate mi yaa weeni ayen, <<Nama Jekob niŋdeerɔma ale Izirali yenni kpaŋŋa ni wom. Ni kan seba nyemagsika,

ref: but you prefer to do evil instead of what is right. You skin my people alive. You strip off their flesh,
text: nama baai ale kisa nalim ale a yaali biem la. Nama baai ale a puli nyiŋ gbaŋ a nyini m nuruma jigi ale ba nyiŋ lammu a nyini ba kobaŋa po la.

ref: Someday you will beg the Lord to help you, but he will turn away because of your sins.
text: Ate ba yaa le kaari a te Naawen, alege wa a kan wom ba. Dila po wa ale suk wa nimbidiaka a nyini ba jigi, dii nyiŋla biemu ate ba nye la nyiŋ.

ref: You lying prophets promise security for anyone who gives you food, but disaster for anyone who refuses to feed you. Here is what the Lord says to you prophets:
text: Nya kude ate Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Dan ka biisiteerɔ baai ale ta mi nuruma a cheŋ a bɛ la, ase ba wanyi a dan te ba ŋandiinta, ba a mooli ka suiyɔgni. Ate wa dan kan nye ya, ba a gomsi kama ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale wa.

ref: “You will live in the dark, far from the sight of the sun, with no message from me.
text: Dila nyiŋ yok ale jam fi zuk, ate fi kan nya, ate legi ale nye ate fi kan baga a porisi. Wenbinni ale siŋ biisiteerɔma zuk, ate danni ale chim legi a te ba.

ref: You prophets and fortunetellers will all be disgraced, with no message from me.”
text: Chivie ale yik biisiteerɔma ate kanpiinta ale dɛ sampoporisaŋa. Ba meena ale lik ba nimbidaasaŋa dii nyiŋla tulisika a kan nyini Wen jigi ya.>>

ref: But the Lord has filled me with power and his Spirit. I have been given the courage to speak about justice and to tell you people of Israel that you have sinned.
text: Alege dan ka mi, mi sueri ale ka pagrim ale Naawen Chiika ale nyemagsika ale zuaka ayen m weeni Jekob nye kaasuŋku ale Izirali wa biemu.

ref: So listen to my message, you rulers of Israel! You hate justice and twist the truth.
text: Wom de, Jekob yenni niŋdeerɔma ale Izirali yenni kpaŋŋa baai ale a zɛri nyemagsika ale yik dii meena ale magsi a tagri la.

ref: You make cruelty and murder a way of life in Jerusalem.
text: Baai ale a ko nuruba a sɛ Zayon ale ziim ale a sɛ Jerusalem ale gaasa la.

ref: You leaders accept bribes for dishonest decisions. You priests and prophets teach and preach, but only for money. Then you say, “The Lord is on our side. No harm will come to us.”
text: Wa niŋdeerɔma a tuesi ŋanta nuruba jigi alege a bo buusa, ate wa kaabteerɔma a tuesi ŋanta alege a sak, ate wa biisiteerɔma a tuesi ligra alege a porisi. Alege ba a sali ka Naawen ale a weeni ayen, <<Naawen an bo ale ti? Kaasuŋ a kan jam ti zuwa.>>

ref: And so, because of you, Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.
text: Dila nyiŋ nama nyiŋ, ba ale kpa Zayon ase ka laŋ la. Jerusalem ale nye ase ka guura la, Naawen yenni a chim guuk ate tiisa a chim lik.

ref: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills, and every nation will rush to it.
text: Dai kpeglimaŋa po, Naawen yenni guuku ale zaani ase naab la guutaŋa po. Ku ale zak ŋmai a gaam guutaŋa, ate tɛŋsa meena ale chuiri a cheŋ ku jigi.

ref: People of many nations will come and say, “Let's go up to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋsa yega ale jam a weeni ayen, <<Ni jam ate ti jueli Naawen guuku, ti jueli Jekob Wen yenni. Wa ale sak ti Wa suitaŋa ate ti baga a cheŋ ti po.>> Wa sinsaŋŋa ale nyini Zayon a cheŋ. Ate Naawen wanni ale nyini Jerusalem.

ref: He will settle arguments between distant and powerful nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never again make war or attack one another.
text: Wa ale bo nuru boari buusa. Wa le yik tɛŋ pagrisa wie a yomsi. Ba ale kuri ba gebisaŋa a nye niiga kua. Ba gbattaŋa ale labri a chim gebisa ate ba pai a yoarisi tiisa. Tɛŋ a kan pai gebik a ta chaab ale tɛŋ ka choa, yaase ba ŋman sak badek a magsi kpaliŋ diipo diipo.

ref: Everyone will find rest beneath their own fig trees or grape vines, and they will live in peace. This is a solemn promise of the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Nuru meena ale kali wadek yɔna tiib tɛŋ ale wadek kiŋkaŋ tɛŋ, ate waai a kan nye ate ba kpaziim kasim a nak, dii nyiŋla ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: Others may follow their gods, but we will always follow the Lord our God. The Lord Will Lead His People Home
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa meena ale cheŋ ba wenaŋa yuenni nyiŋ, alege tama ale cheŋ ka Naawen ti Wenni yuenni nyiŋ taam wuu.

ref: The Lord said: At that time I will gather my people— the lame and the outcasts, and all others into whose lives I have brought sorrow.
text: Naawen ti Wenni a weeni kama ayen, <<Dai dila danni m le tigsi gbansa, abe m tigsi baai ale basi ba tɛŋsa la ale baai ate m daani ba la.

ref: Then the lame and the outcasts will belong to my people and become a strong nation. I, the Lord, will rule them from Mount Zion forever.
text: M le basi ate gbansaŋa a tali, abe baai ate ba yiak basi la tɛŋ pagrik. Naawen ale nya ba zuk Zayon po a nyini dai dila danni a taa cheŋ.

ref: Mount Zion in Jerusalem, guardian of my people, you will rule again.
text: Dan ka fi, piisaŋa yewɔŋku, Zayon liewa pagrimu, fi a ŋman nya fi pagrim kpakka. Naam ale jam Jerusalem Liewa jigi.

ref: Jerusalem, why are you crying? Don't you have a king? Have your advisors gone? Are you suffering like a woman in childbirth?
text: Boan nyiŋ ate fi a kaari? Fi a ka naabaa? Fi sagrɔwa a bɛ kama? Nyiŋ dommaŋa de a nye fi ase ka nipok waai ale boro a biak la?

ref: Keep on groaning with pain, you people of Jerusalem! If you escape from your city to the countryside, you will still be taken as prisoners to Babylonia. But later I will rescue you from your enemies.
text: Zayon Liewa, a bilim tɛŋka ale nyiŋdomma, ase nipok ale boro a biak diila. Diila yɔgyɔgla de fi magsi fi basi tɛŋka kama a ga kali peelim. Fi ale cheŋ Babilon, ate fi ale nya varibasika dula. Naawen ale da fu a tuesi dula a nyini fi dachaasaŋa nisa po.

ref: Zion, because of your sins you are surrounded by many nations who say, “We can hardly wait to see you disgraced.”
text: Alege yɔgyɔgla de tɛŋ kpieŋsa yega a nya ka chaab ayen si nye kpaliŋ ale fu. Ba a weeni kama ayen, <<Basi ate wa taŋ, basi ate ti ninaŋa a naŋ Zayon zuk.

ref: But they don't know that I, the Lord, have gathered them here to grind them like grain.
text: Alege ba zɛ Naawen popola. Ba kan miŋ wa zɔŋŋa. Ka wala ale a tigsi ba ase boba la a taa cheŋ fɔbika jigini.

ref: Smash them to pieces, Zion! I'll let you be like a bull with iron horns and bronze hoofs. Crush those nations and bring their wealth to me, the Lord of the earth.
text: Zayon Liewa, yiti a fɔbi, diila m le te fu ka kutuk nyiila ale kutuk mɔnuŋ naŋsaba, ate fi ale kaasi tɛŋ kpieŋsa nna yegayega.>> Ni ale pai ba nyuentaŋa ate ni nak vari la a te Naawen ale ba jigsika ŋantaŋa a te tɛŋzuk de meena Nyɔnɔwa.

ref: Jerusalem, enemy troops have surrounded you; they have struck Israel's ruler in the face with a stick.
text: Tigsi fi tugurik tɔŋdɔma, tugurik tɔŋdɔba tɛŋ nummoa, diila ba gilim kama a ta chaab ale ti. Ba le fɔbi Izirali niŋdeerɔwa tapiak ale doari.

ref: Bethlehem Ephrath, you are one of the smallest towns in the nation of Judah. But the Lord will choose one of your people to rule the nation— someone whose family goes back to ancient times.
text: <<Alege fi Betiliyem Efrata, Juda buuni po fi ale pɔsima, a nyini fi po ate niŋdeerɔ ale nya Izirali zuk a te mi. Waai kiri ale nyini ŋiak po.>>

ref: The Lord will abandon Israel only until this ruler is born, and the rest of his family returns to Israel.
text: Dila nyiŋ ba za ba zɛri Izirali kama ate ku ga paari diipo ate nipok waai ale a dom la a ga biak, ate wa soa tii ale tali la a pilim ŋmani a ga gum Izirali demma po.

ref: Like a shepherd taking care of his sheep, this ruler will lead and care for his people by the power and glorious name of the Lord his God. His people will live securely, and the whole earth will know his true greatness,
text: Wa ale zaani a kasi wa piisaŋa Naawen pagrimu nyiŋ ale Naawen wa Wenni zula yuenni nyiŋ. Ate ba ale bo sukka dek jigi, ate wa zuaka ale paari tɛŋka kpeglimka.

ref: because he will bring peace. Assyria Will Be Defeated Let Assyria attack our country and our palaces. We will counterattack, led by a number of rulers
text: Ate wala ale chim ba suiyɔgni. Ase Assiria demma nin wɛ jɔ ti tɛŋka po a gɔk santiri a gilim ti yie pagrisaŋa, ti ale siti ka naapeerisa bayopɔi dan poom ka nidoaba naaniŋ a basi ba zuk.

ref: whose strong army will defeat the nation of Assyria. Yes, our leaders will rescue us, if those Assyrians dare to invade our land. The Survivors Will Be Safe
text: Ba ale pai gebika a nya Assiria tɛŋka zuk, abe ba dari gebik a yeeri fook po a nya Nimrod tɛŋka zuk. Wa ale vari ti a nyini Assiria demma nisa po a basi ase ba nin wɛ jo ti tɛŋka po a gɔk santiri va ti tɛŋ banaŋa po.

ref: A few of Jacob's descendants survived and are scattered among the nations. But the Lord will let them cover the earth like dew and rain that refreshes the soil.
text: Jekob nuru baai ale tali la ale bo nuru boari po ase maglim ale nyini Naawen jigi diila, abe ba ŋman nye ase ŋmoruk ale ni a basi wuuk zuk diila, ale kan limisi nuru yaase nurubiik zuk nyaka la.

ref: At present they are scattered, but later they will attack, as though they were fierce lions pouncing on sheep. Their enemies will be torn to shreds, with no one to save them;
text: Jekob nuru baai ale a tali la ale bo ka tɛŋsaŋa po, nuru boari suŋsuŋ po ase gbeŋli ale bo gɔi po ale duŋsa diila, abe ba ŋman nye ase gbeŋ paali ale bo ale piisa a na ale dari a ŋasi nna bunabuna ate waai karo ale vari ŋa a basi la.

ref: they will be helpless, completely destroyed. Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
text: Fi ale zagri fi nisaŋa ŋmai nakdeka po fi dachaasaŋa zuk, ate fi dachaasaŋa meena ale kaasi.

ref: The Lord said: At that time I will wipe out your cavalry and chariots,
text: Naawen ale a weeni ayen, <<Dai dila danni m le kaasi ni wusumaŋa ni suŋsuŋ, abe m ŋɔriŋ ni torokoma.

ref: I will stop you from telling fortunes and practicing witchcraft.
text: M le kaasi ni sakpaŋni ate ni kan ŋman baga a tom sampoporinni.

ref: You will no longer worship the idols or stone images you have made— I will destroy them,
text: M le kaasi ni bɔgtaŋa ale ni tuilum tanaŋa ni suŋsuŋ. Ni kan ŋman koori tɛŋ a te ni nisa tuima.

ref: together with the sacred poles and even your towns.
text: M le voori Asera zaŋŋa ni suŋsuŋ abe m kaasi ni tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa.

ref: I will become furious and take revenge on the nations that refuse to obey me.
text: Suipuurum po ate m le nye tuni tɛŋ kpieŋ sii meena ale kan wom mi la.>>

ref: The Lord said to his people: Come and present your case to the hills and mountains.
text: Wom Naawen ale a weeni diila. <<Ni yiti zaani, ni weeni ni wanni ate guutaŋa wom. Ni basi ate pinaŋa a wom ni ale a yaali ayen ni weeni diila.

ref: My people, have I wronged you in any way at all? Please tell me.
text: <<M nuruba, ka boan wari ate m pai nye ni? M te ni ka boan jiboa? Ni tulisi mu.

ref: I rescued you from Egypt, where you were slaves. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to be your leaders.
text: M ta ni nyini Ejipiti ale ŋman da tuesi ni a nyini yɔntidi tɛŋ po. Mi jam tom Moosis ate wa dɛ ni niŋ, a ŋman tom Aaron ale Miriam.

ref: Don't forget the evil plans of King Balak of Moab or what Balaam son of Beor said to him. Remember how I, the Lord, saved you many times on your way from Acacia to Gilgal. True Obedience
text: M nuruba, ni teeri Moab naawa Belak ale jam zɔk dii ayen wa nye la, ate Biio nidoabinni Balaam a jam tulisi diila. Ni teeri ni suiku chelimu a nyini Sittim a ga paari Gilgal ate ni baga a miŋ Naawen wayɔrisima tuimaŋa ale ka dii la.>>

ref: What offering should I bring when I bow down to worship the Lord God Most High? Should I try to please him by sacrificing calves a year old?
text: Ka boa ate m le ta jam Naawen niŋ abe m koori wenŋmazukku Wenni niŋŋa? M jam wa niŋ ale ben yeŋ naabisa juka tiirita?

ref: The Lord God has told us what is right and what he demands: “See that justice is done, let mercy be your first concern, and humbly obey your God.” Cheating and Violence
text: Nuru, wa sak fu ka dii ale nala la. Be ka boa ate Naawen a yaali a nyini fi jigi yaa? Fi nye a magsi abe fi a yaali jiirim abe fi yik fidek a cheŋ ale fi Wenni.

ref: I am the Lord, and you are wise to respect my power to punish. So listen to my message for the city of Jerusalem:
text: Ni wom! Naawen a wi ka tɛŋ nummu, ate fi daa chali wa yuenni yɔgsum ka yam. <<Ni zuli tachekka ale waai ale lueri ka la.

ref: But I, the Lord, will punish you for cheating with weights and with measures.
text: M siak a te nuru waai ale ta venta ŋanmagsinta ale venta boorik kaai dobrim ale kan daa wensie la ayen ku magsi yaa?

ref: You rich people are violent, and everyone tells lies.
text: Wa nuru baai ale jigsi la ka wɔkwɔk nuruba. Wa nuruma ka velimvendisa ale a paasi nuruba.

ref: Because of your sins, I will wound you and leave you ruined and defenseless.
text: Dila nyiŋ m piilim kama ayen m kaasi fu, fi wabaataŋa nyiŋ.

ref: You will eat, but still be hungry; you will store up goods, but lose everything— I, the Lord, will let it all be captured in war.
text: Fi ale dɛ alege fi kan chagi. Fi puuka ale chim ka pu koruk. Fi ale dueni ŋanta alege jaab a kan boro a te fu, dii nyiŋla fi ale a dueni ŋan baai la m le pai ŋa a te kpaliŋ po.

ref: You won't harvest what you plant or use the oil from your olive trees or drink the wine from grapes you grow.
text: Fi ale bori alege fi kan nya che. Fi ale ŋmiak kpaam alege fi kan pai bu a tom tuini. Fi ale ŋmiak yɔna alege fi kan nyu ŋa daamoa.

ref: Jerusalem, this will happen because you followed the sinful example of kings Omri and Ahab. Now I will destroy you and your property. Then the people of every nation will make fun and insult you.
text: Fi va ka Omri ŋmarisika ale Ayab yenni ale a nye dii meena la ale va ba ŋiak wieŋa. Dila nyiŋ m le kaasi ni, ate fi nuruma ale chim nuru valiŋsa. Tɛŋ kpieŋsa meena ale nye ni a la.>>

ref: I feel so empty inside— like someone starving for grapes or figs, after the vines and trees have all been picked clean.
text: Niniga nuru ale mi! Mi a nye ase ka waai ale a yiisi yɔna kaduk po wenkarik diila. Yɔn saga a karo ate m le dɛ. Kinkama ŋaai ale kpabi a yɔni ate m ta koarisa ale ŋa la mɛ karo.

ref: No one is loyal to God; no one does right. Everyone is brutal and eager to deceive everyone else.
text: Wensie nuruba a ka tɛŋka zuwa. Wanyi mɛ la an tali ya. Nuru meena kali kama a yaali kpaliŋ a pai ŋmiak a yik wa suok.

ref: The most honest of them is worse than a thorn patch. Your doom has come! Lookouts sound the warning, and everyone panics.
text: Waai ale nala ba po la a nye ase ka wobi la, ate nuru maŋka ba po a gaam muŋ. Fi limisidɔma danni a paari ya, di danni ate Wen ale jam fi jigi la. Yɔgyɔgla de ale ba butimka dai.

ref: Don't trust anyone, not even your best friend, and be careful what you say to the one you love.
text: Kan ta mariŋka ale waai ale kali moata fu. Kan ta sebchakka ale fi doa. Poom le waai ale a duak fi nigoruk po. Be kpesi fi wieŋa a paari abe fi ge a biisi.

ref: Sons refuse to respect their own fathers, daughters rebel against their own mothers, and daughters-in-law despise their mothers-in-law. Your family is now your enemy.
text: Diila nidoabili a kan zuli wa ko, ate lie ale yiti a ta chaab ale wa ma, ate sampok ale yiti a ta chaab ale wa ŋiak nipok. Nuru dachiak a nyini ka wadek yeri po.

ref: But I trust the Lord God to save me, and I will wait for him to answer my prayer. The Nation Turns to God
text: Alege dan ka mi, m yiilaŋa a bo ka Naawen jigi. Mi a limisi ka Wen m varibasidɔwa. M Wenni ale wom mu.

ref: My enemies, don't be glad because of my troubles! I may have fallen, but I will get up; I may be sitting in the dark, but the Lord is my light.
text: M dachiagaa, kan te fi sui a peenti ale m lueta. M dan poom lo, m le ŋman yiti. M dan poom kala legi po, Naawen ale chim m bolim.

ref: I have sinned against the Lord. And so I must endure his anger, until he comes to my defense. But I know that I will see him making things right for me and leading me to the light.
text: Dii nyiŋla m tom kaasi wa kama, ate ku magsi ayen m tu chaab ale wa suipuurumu, ate ku ga paari diipo ate wa le biisi te mu a ŋman nye mu a magsi la. Wa ale ta mu a nyini peelim ale bolim. M le nya wa wayɔrisimaŋa.

ref: You, my enemies, said, “The Lord God is helpless.” Now each of you will be disgraced and put to shame. I will see you trampled like mud in the street. A Bright Future
text: Ate m dachiaka ale nya ate chivie a yik wa, ate waai ale jam weeni mi ayen, <<Naawen fi Wenni a boka be la?>> M ninaŋa ale nya wa lueta. Ba poom ŋaam tabi wa kama ase tantaŋa ale doa suiku po diila.

ref: Towns of Judah, the day is coming when your walls will be rebuilt, and your boundaries enlarged.
text: Fi parisaŋa sɛka danni ale paari. Fi tɛŋ banaŋa lagrika danni a cheena.

ref: Those nations will suffer disaster because of what they did. Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
text: Tɛŋzuk de a doa koruk ka nuruma tuimaŋa nyiŋ.

ref: Lead your people, Lord! Come and be our shepherd. Grasslands surround us, but we live in a forest. So lead us to Bashan and Gilead, and let us find pasture as we did long ago.
text: Pai fi tachekka a kasi fi nuruma. Duŋsaŋa ale fi nitalim ate si dek a bo gɔi tɛŋ maŋka ate wuyɔgsuk a boro la. Basi ate si a dɛ Basan ale Gilead ase dila po wa la.

ref: I, the Lord, will work miracles just as I did when I led you out of Egypt.
text: <<M le sak ni m wakinkaglaŋa ase diipo ate ni jam nyini Ejipiti a jam la.>>

ref: Nations will see this and be ashamed because of their helpless armies. They will be in shock, unable to speak or hear,
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale nya ate chivie a yik ba, ate ba pagrimu ale yalima ale ba. Ba ale pai ba nisa a vi ba noaŋa zuk ate ba tueŋa ale kpari.

ref: because of their fear of me, your Lord and God. Then they will come trembling, crawling out of their fortresses like insects or snakes, lapping up the dust. No One Is Like God The people said:
text: Ba ale leeli tanta ase waab la, abe ba kuuk tɛŋ ase duŋsaŋa la. Ba le nyini ba diinaŋa po ale kpazinagsuk. Ba ale viriŋ cheŋ Naawen ti Wenni jigi ale kpazinagsuk ate ba ale chali fu.

ref: Our God, no one is like you. We are all that is left of your chosen people, and you freely forgive our sin and guilt. You don't stay angry forever; you're glad to have pity
text: Wen dina ale a nye ase fi la, ate fi a vɔŋ fi nuru baai ale tali boro la wabaata ale ba nye kaasuŋ a te ba? Fi sui a kan puuri gaam a taam, dii nyiŋ la fi kasim a yaali ŋmanteka kama.

ref: and pleased to be merciful. You will trample on our sins and throw them in the sea.
text: Fi ale ŋman ta jiirim ale ti. Fi ale tabi ti wabaataŋa zuk abe fi yuk ti biemu meena a basi nyakpiemu liuŋku po.

ref: You will keep your word and be faithful to Jacob and to Abraham, as you promised our ancestors many years ago.
text: Fi ale ta wensie ale Jekob, abe fi sak ŋmanteka ale Abrayam ase fi ale jam puulim a te ti koma dipo diila.

ref: I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh. The Fierce Anger of the Lord
text: Nayum ale nyini Elkos tɛŋka la ale nya wanni de a magsi chaab ale Niineve tɛŋka.

ref: The Lord is powerful, yet patient; he makes sure that the guilty are always punished. He can be seen in storms and in whirlwinds; clouds are the dust from his feet.
text: Naawen sui a kan kpabi a puuri, alege ta pagrim a kan basi baai ale nye kaasi la namsika. Juijui ate Naawen a cheŋ la, va pagrik ale a yiti. Chiŋmaaŋa ka nyuŋ a yiti wa naŋsa po.

ref: At the Lord's command, oceans and rivers dry up. Bashan, Mount Carmel, and Lebanon wither, and their flowers fade.
text: Wa dan na biisi nyakpiemu a kpeeri kama. Wa basi kama ate belaŋa a kpeeri. Basan tɛŋsaŋa ale Karmel guuku a ko ka chekchek ale Lebanon wuutaŋa ale ti puutaŋa a kpi meena.

ref: At the sight of the Lord, mountains and hills tremble and melt; the earth and its people shudder and shake.
text: Guuta a choa Naawen niŋ. Gu tii meena ale jueli a nyaliŋ Naawen niŋ. Naawen a dan na nyini tɛŋka a choa kama ate tɛŋka meena nuruma nyiŋsa a gɔk.

ref: Who can stand the heat of his furious anger? It flashes out like fire and shatters stones. The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
text: Wa sui a dan puuri ka wana le wa vuugi? Ka wana le wa lati ale wa suipuurumu nna? Wa suinni kasim a yiti ase ka bolim ŋiak la, ate pina a mobi wa niŋ.

ref: The Lord is good. He protects those who trust him in times of trouble.
text: Naawen a nala ale a lik wa nuruma daanika po. Baai ale pilim a jam wa jigi la wa a nya ba zuk kama.

ref: But like a roaring flood, the Lord chases his enemies into dark places and destroys them.
text: Wa nyiem deri kaasi wa dachaasaŋa kama ase nyiam ale tagli jigi meena a pai nna pilim pilim la. Wa le vi wa dachaasaŋa a ga ko ba meena.

ref: So don't plot against the Lord! He wipes out his enemies, and they never revive.
text: Ka boa ate ni a zɔk ayen ni tu chaab ale Naawen yaa? Wa le kaasi ni. Nuru karo a daani wa a saari buye.

ref: They are like drunkards overcome by wine, or like twisted thornbushes burning in a fire.
text: Wa le ju ni ase munsa ale wukosik la.

ref: Assyria, one of your rulers has made evil plans against the Lord.
text: Nuru ale nyini Niineve ale popola baata a kisi Naawen ale ta gaasa sinsaga.

ref: But the Lord says, “Assyria, no matter how strong you are, you will be cut down! My people Judah, I have troubled you before, but I won't do it again.
text: Naawen ale weeni dii a te Juda demma la ale nna, <<Assiria demma a dan poom pagra ale piisi m le kaasi ba ate ba muriŋ bɛ. Nama mi dek nuruma m namsi ni kama alege m kan nye di ŋmana.

ref: I'll snap your chains and set you free from the Assyrians.”
text: Assiria ale ta pagrim buui ni zuk la, m le kpeglim bu abe m gebi chɔrima ŋaai ale bobi ni la.

ref: Assyria, this is what else the Lord says to you: “Your name will be forgotten. I will destroy every idol in your temple, and I will send you to the grave, because you are worthless.”
text: Naawen ale weeni dii dueni a magsi Niineve la ale nna, <<Ba kan nya ŋaaŋsa ate ba diem ta ba yuenni. M le kaasi ba bɔgtaŋa ale bo ni wenaŋa yenni po la. M boro a gomsi ka vɔrup a magsi Assiria demma. Ba an magsi boka.>>

ref: Look toward the mountains, people of Judah! Here comes a messenger with good news of peace. Celebrate your festivals. Keep your promises to God. Your evil enemies are destroyed and will never again invade your country.
text: A nya, nuru ale nyini guutaŋa zuk a cheena ale wa paala. Wa bo ka suik cheena ayen wa mooli nak dɛka. Juda demma, ni a dɛ ni tiŋŋa abe ni pai jabuui ate ni puulim ayen ni te wa la a te. Nye ka tuem nyama a kan ŋman tuesi ni tɛŋka. M kaasi ba ka meena.

ref: Nineveh, someone is coming to attack and scatter you. Guard your fortresses! Watch the road! Be brave! Prepare for battle!
text: Nama Niineve demma kaasirɔwa cheena ayen wa siti ni. Pagrim buui ale bu kaasi ni la a jam ya. Ni lik ŋan kasintaŋa. Ni kasi suiku. Ni gomsi magsi kpaliŋ.

ref: Judah and Israel are like trees with branches broken by their enemies. But the Lord is going to restore their power and glory. *
text: Naawen a yaali wa ŋman te Izirali zulaŋa kama ase ba le jam ka dii alege ate ba dachaasaŋa a yik ba la.

ref: An officer gives a command. But his soldiers stumble, as they hasten to build a shelter to protect themselves against rocks thrown down from the city wall.
text: Ba wi ba kpaŋŋa kama ate baa cheŋ niŋ geŋ ale a nak naŋsa a lo. Tugurik tɔŋdɔma a chali ga parika jigini ayen ba kasi ŋan baai ba a yuk la.

ref: The river gates fly open, and panic floods the palace.
text: Nansuiŋ tii ale bo benni jigini la a lagri Naawa yenni po niniga nyiini ale sueri.

ref: Nineveh is disgraced. The queen is dragged off. Her servant women mourn; they moan like doves, and they beat their breasts in sorrow.
text: Nipok naawa ba yik ate wa yɔmma a kum ase nangbaŋsa la a nak ba kuusa ale niniga.

ref: Nineveh is like a pond with leaking water. Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!” can be heard everywhere. But everyone is leaving.
text: Niineve demma a daa chali kama ase mɔgi ale ŋɔsi la. Ba yaa kaari ayen, basi basi, alege waai an viriŋ ŋaaŋŋa.

ref: Enemy soldiers shout, “The city is full of treasure and all kinds of wealth. Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
text: Ni vari kpanaŋa. Ni vari ligmɔniŋka. Tɛŋka jigsi kama ale ŋanta.

ref: Nineveh is doomed! Destroyed! Her people tremble with fear; their faces turn pale.
text: Niineve a kaasi kama a dua. Ate nuruma nyiŋsa a gɔk ate ba duna a nak chaab, pagrim a bɛ. Ate nimbidaasa a peenti.

ref: What happened to this city? They were safer there than powerful lions in a den, with no one to disturb them.
text: Tɛŋ kaai ale jam a nye ase gbeŋma boka jigi la a boka be yɔgla, juijui ate gbeŋma bisa a dɛ ŋandiinta la, juijui ate gbeŋduata ale gbeŋniima a cheŋ ate jaab a kan nye ŋa bisaŋa wari la?

ref: These are the same lions that ferociously attacked their victims, then dragged away the flesh to feed their young.
text: Gbeŋli a ko ka lanta yega a te di bisaŋa ale di vaanchoawa, ale sueri di boka jigini ale lanta.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful is against you, Nineveh. God will burn your chariots and send an army to kill those young lions of yours. You will never again make victims of others or send messengers to threaten everyone on this earth.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi ka ni dachiak. M le ju ni torokoma. Ba le ko ni tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaliŋ po abe m tuesi jaab meena ate ni tuesi nuru yonta jigi la. Ba kan ŋman wom baai ate ni a tom la luelita.>>

ref: here is your fate— cracking whips, churning wheels; galloping horses, roaring chariots;
text: A wom finsaŋa miirika ale torokoma naŋsaŋa nuemka. Wom wusumaŋa ale yɔk a tabi la ale torokoma ale dari a nuem la.

ref: You were nothing more than a prostitute using your magical charms and witchcraft to attract and trap nations.
text: Tɛŋka a nye ka nna ase nipok kaasuŋ la. A yaali porisika ale a nye nuruba ale tiita. A pai ka kaasuŋ nyeka ale sakpaŋni a basi ate tɛŋsa a chim ka yɔm.

ref: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, am now your enemy. I will pull up your skirt and let nations and kingdoms stare at your nakedness.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni ayen, <<Mi ta ka chaab ale ni, nama Niineve demma. M le nye ni gattaŋa a ta jueli lik ni ninaŋa a pai ni chaboalaŋa a sak tɛŋsaŋa ate si nya ni chivieŋa.

ref: I will cover you with garbage, treat you like trash, and rub you in the dirt.
text: M le nye ni m kan sak zula abe m lik ni ale daŋta ate nuruba kasim a nya ni.

ref: Everyone who sees you will turn away and shout, “Nineveh is done for! Is anyone willing to mourn or to give her comfort?” Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
text: Waai meena a dan nya ni ba le yiti a chali abe ba a weeni ayen, <Niineve a kaasi ya.> Ka wana le wa kum ka nyiŋŋa? Niineve demma, mi ale nya ka wana ate wa nye ate ni sue yɔk.>>

ref: Nineveh, do you feel safer than the city of Thebes? The Nile River was its wall of defense.
text: Ni an zunchoŋ Tebes tɛŋka ale moata Nile benni ate nyiam gilim ka la. Nyiamu, ale jam kasi ka. Nyiamu jam a nye ase ka parik la gilim ka.

ref: Thebes trusted the mighty power of Ethiopia and Egypt; the nations of Put and Libya were her allies.
text: Kus ale Ejipiti a te ba pagrim buui ale kaa nueri. Put ale Libia mɛ a maa maari ka.

ref: But she was captured and taken to a foreign country. Her children were murdered at every street corner. The members of her royal family were auctioned off, and her high officials were bound in chains.
text: Alege ba yik Tebes demma ate ba ga bo tɛŋ yoŋ. Ba bimbaan fiisaŋa ba nak ba ko dueni suitaŋa niŋsa. Ba niŋdeerɔma ba yik ba ale chɔrima a ta cheŋ.

ref: Nineveh, now it's your turn! You will get drunk and try to hide from your enemy.
text: Niineve demma ni le nyu daam buk. Ni le suk. Ni le gisi yaali jigi ayen dachaasaŋa kan nya ni.

ref: Your fortresses are fig trees with ripe figs. Merely shake the trees, and fruit will fall into every open mouth.
text: Ni ŋan kasintaŋa meena a nye ase kinkaŋsa ale ta moota la. Ba dan zaŋ tiimu, yɔnaŋa deri lo dɛɛrɔwa nɔi po.

ref: Your army is weak. Fire has destroyed the crossbars on your city gates; now they stand wide open to your enemy.
text: Ni nya ni tugurik tɔŋdɔma. Ba meena ka nipooba. Ni tɛŋka tuataŋa a lak kama a magsi ayen dachaasaŋa a jo. Bolim a dɛ ni tuataŋa daataŋa.

ref: Your city is under attack. Haul in extra water! Strengthen your defenses! Start making bricks! Stir the mortar!
text: Ni ŋari nyiam zuak alege ti kpaliŋ le za ka beni la piilim. Ni basi ate ni ŋan kasintaŋa a pagra. Ni yaali yak a dam ni tanta a nak peela.

ref: You will still go up in flames and be cut down by swords that will wipe you out like a field attacked by grasshoppers. So, go ahead and increase like a swarm of locusts!
text: Dula jigini bolimu ale dɛ ni. Gebika ale ko ni. Kpaliŋka ale ko ni ka meena ase nanchoŋta ale dɛ ŋanta vaata diila. Ni be piisi yega ase nanchoŋta ale yɔk a cheŋ. Ni piisi yega ase tintue la.

ref: More merchants are in your city than there are stars in the sky— but they are like locusts that eat everything, then fly away.
text: Ni geruŋdɔma a piisi a gaam chiŋmarisaŋa ale bo wenzukku la kama, alege a nye ase tintue la, a dɛ jaab meena ale yiti cheŋ.

ref: Your guards and your officials are swarms of locusts. On a chilly day they settle on a fence, but when the sun comes out, they take off to who-knows-where.
text: Ni limisidɔma a nye ase ka tintue la a bo saasaŋa nyiŋ da di dai ate ku yɔk la. Alege kantueŋka a dan jam ŋa yiti cheŋ ate waai zɛ ŋa le ga juijui la.

ref: King of Assyria, your officials and leaders are sound asleep, while your people are scattered in the mountains. Yes, your people are sheep without a shepherd.
text: Assiria naaba, fi kpaŋŋa kpi kama ate fi nuru baai ale ta zula la a goa takakaka. Fi nuruma a waaŋ bo guutaŋa zuima ate waai karo a ta ba a jam yeri ŋmana.

ref: You're fatally wounded. There's no hope for you. But everyone claps when they hear this news, because your constant cruelty has caused them pain.
text: Ni le kɔni ale nya tueta la tebika karo ate ni a nya nyiŋyɔgsa. Baai meena le wom ni tɛŋka kaasika la a nak ka nichaala a naŋ diila waai meena ku jo wa nyiŋ kama ale ni nyeka tuemu ale kaa nueri la.

ref: I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me. Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
text: Wa dii ate Naawen a pai sak wa biisiteerɔwa Yabakkuk la,

ref: Our Lord, how long must I beg for your help before you listen? How long before you save us from all this violence?
text: Naawen, mi ale saalim fi soa ka sɛ a weeni ayen fi maari ti alege ate fi yaa wom? Ku le beni ka sɛ alege ate fi vari ti gaasaŋa dɛ po basi?

ref: Why do you make me watch such terrible injustice? Why do you allow violence, lawlessness, crime, and cruelty to spread everywhere?
text: Ka boa ale soa ate fi basi ate mi a nya daanika de meena? Ka boa ale soa ate fi a nya nye kaasika de meena? Kaasuŋ ale gaasa ale kasim gilim mu, ate kpaliŋ ale nanpaga kasim bo jigi meena.

ref: Laws cannot be enforced; justice is always the loser; criminals crowd out honest people and twist the laws around. The Lord Answers Habakkuk
text: Sinsaŋŋa ŋman ka kiriya, ŋa kan ŋma tomu, wensie tuima ka. Nuru baataŋa a goanti a nya badek alege nuru maŋsaŋa a lo ate boteerɔma kan bo buusa a magsi.

ref: Look and be amazed at what's happening among the nations! Even if you were told, you would never believe what's taking place now.
text: Ate Naawen yaa weeni wa nuruma ayen, <<Ni a nya tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale gilim ni la. Ni le a nya diila le cha ni. M le za m nye diila ni kan siagi ase ni nin poom wom.

ref: I am sending the Babylonians. They are fierce and cruel— marching across the land, conquering cities and towns.
text: Kaldiya demma baai nyeka ale toa nna yegayega la, m le te ba pagrim. Ba gɔk ka santiri a diak a nak tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale tɛŋ fiisa a cheŋ.

ref: How fearsome and frightening. Their only laws and rules are the ones they make up.
text: Ba kasim a nyigsi ka nuruba. Ba a nyeka ba le a yaali diila. Ba le ba kanjantaŋa ba chim nuru maŋsa te ka badek.

ref: Their cavalry troops are faster than leopards, more ferocious than wolves hunting at sunset, and swifter than hungry eagles suddenly swooping down.
text: Ba wusumaŋa a korisi gaam yɔŋma ate ŋa nyeka mɛ toa ase kom ale ta piina la. Ba wusum duerisaŋa nyiem deri jam diiri kama. Ba nyini ka niŋniŋŋa. Ba nyiem jam diiri kama ase jiiruk ale diiri jaab diila.

ref: They are eager to destroy, and they gather captives like handfuls of sand.
text: Ba meena jam ka kpaliŋ. Jaab karo a kasi ba. Ba ligrɔma a piisi ase ka tintain busuŋ la.

ref: Then suddenly they disappear like a gust of wind— those sinful people who worship their own strength. Habakkuk Complains Again
text: Ate ba yaa boro ase viok la a cheŋ. Nuru ba tii ale a zuli badek pagrim la.>>

ref: Holy Lord God, mighty rock, you are eternal, and we are safe from death. You are using those Babylonians to judge and punish others.
text: Naawen yaa, fi ka Naawen a nyini piilimka po meena. Fi ka m Wen, a Welema ale ka kpeglimka. Ti kan kpi. Naawen yaa m ligrɔ, fi ale lueri Kaldiya demma a te ba pagrim ayen ba namsi ti.

ref: The people you put on this earth are like fish or reptiles without a leader.
text: Fi a nye nuruba nna se ka jumaŋa ale bo nyiamu po la, nna se ŋan baai ale bo nyiam po a ka niŋdeerɔ la.

ref: Then an enemy comes along and takes them captive with hooks and nets. It makes him so happy
text: Kaldiya demma a yik nuruba ale ka goatisa ase juma la. A yaa dari ale ba ŋmaasaŋa ale a kaari ale suipeentik ba le yik la.

ref: that he offers sacrifices to his fishing nets, because they make him rich and provide choice foods.
text: Ba poom a zuli ba ŋmaasaŋa kama ale a kaab si, si ale a te ba dii meena ate ba a yaali la.

ref: Will he keep hauling in his nets and destroying nations without showing mercy?
text: Ba le kasim pai ba gebisaŋa a kaasi tɛŋsaŋa kama a cheŋ alege kan sak jiirimmoa?

ref: While standing guard on the watchtower, I waited for the Lord's answer, before explaining the reason for my complaint.
text: Mi ale jueli ka gboŋ a za ase limisidɔ la a limisi ate m nya Naawen ale wa weeni mu diila ale wa le wa tulisi m funfɔblaŋa diila.

ref: Then the Lord told me: “I will give you my message in the form of a vision. Write it clearly enough to be read at a glance.
text: Naawen yaa tulisi mi a weeni ayen, <<Ŋmarisi dii ate fi nya la dueni. Ŋmarisi cheri a dueni tintain paglak nyiŋ ate waai dek ale a karim la a chali ga weeni ba gela.

ref: At the time I have decided, my words will come true. You can trust what I say about the future. It may take a long time, but keep on waiting— it will happen!
text: Ku an diem paari diipo ate wanni ale chim wensie la, alege ku cheena ate wanni a chim wensie. Ku a nye ase ku a beni kama la, alege yik fidek a limisi, dii nyiŋla ku le sum jam, ku kan beni.

ref: “I, the Lord, refuse to accept anyone who is proud. Only those who live by faith are acceptable to me.” Trouble for Evil People
text: <<Kanjanta nyɔnɔ nyeelaŋa an nala alege wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa a vuuk kama wa siaka nyiŋ.

ref: Wine is treacherous, and arrogant people are never satisfied. They are no less greedy than death itself— they open their mouths as wide as the world of the dead and swallow everyone.
text: Daam ale baga a paasi nuru la, wabaata nyama a kan benni, diila ba a yaali ŋanta ase ka vɔrup ale a yaali kum diila, kum abe kasim a yaali ka kpieba yega. Ba tigsi tɛŋsaŋa meena nuruma a ta jam jigi yeŋ a ta ba.

ref: You robbed cities and nations everywhere on earth and murdered their people. Now those who survived will be as cruel to you.
text: Ni be le zu tɛŋsa yegayega la, baai ale tali la ale tuesi yegayega ni jigi. Dii nyiŋla ni ko nuruba yega a kaasi tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale nuru baai meena ale bo si po la.

ref: You're doomed! You made your family rich at the expense of others. You even said to yourself, “I'm above the law.”
text: <<Ku le ku bie dii ale tɛŋ kaai ale va biem nyiŋ a jigsi la, ale a poli ayen ba le bo kauk kuui ate ba nyini biem po la.

ref: But you will bring shame on your family and ruin to yourself for what you did to others.
text: Ni be le a zɔk ayen ni ko nuruba yega la ni nye kama ate chivie a yik nidek dɔkdemma. Dila nyiŋ ni le jɔk ni nyuvooŋa.

ref: The very stones and wood in your home will testify against you.
text: Saasaŋa tintanaŋa ale kaari a weeni ayen ni an nye magsi ya, da pilintaŋa ale siak ayen ni nye kaasi kama.

ref: But the Lord All-Powerful sends up in flames what nations and people work so hard to gain.
text: Naawen dii ale ka Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋdeerɔ ale basi ate bolim jam kaasi ba le se ŋan baai meena la, ate ba tuimaŋa meena a chim kinla.

ref: Just as water fills the sea, the land will be filled with people who know and honor the Lord.
text: Ate nya kpiem ale taari lik dua ate ba a nya diila, nuruba ale bo jigi meena la ale nya Naawen zulaŋa ale wa nalimu.

ref: Now you will be disgraced instead of praised. The Lord will make you drunk, and when others see you naked, you will lose their respect.
text: Nama Kaldiya demma chivie ale yik ni chekki, ni kan nya zula. Ku tulim jam kama ayen nama mɛ nyu buk lo tɛŋ ase da bugrik la. Suipuurum beerika ale bo Naawen juga nisa po la cheen ni jigi. Ni le tuesi chivie, daa zula.

ref: What is an idol worth? It's merely a false god. Why trust a speechless image made from wood or metal by human hands?
text: <<Bɔgluk a kan nye wamaŋa, diila nurubiik ale nye ku, ku ka jameem buui ale a sak venta. Waai ale nye ku la a ta sebchakka kama ayen wadek tuini maari wa, alege wa a nye ka bɔgluk tii ale kan poom a biisi.

ref: Let all the world be silent— the Lord is present in his holy temple.
text: Naawen a bo ka wa yenni po, tɛŋka nuruma meena nye diki wa niŋ.>>

ref: I know your reputation, Lord, and I am amazed at what you have done. Please turn from your anger and be merciful; do for us what you did for our ancestors.

text: Wa a nye ase ka bolim la nna cha. Bolim ale a nyaksi wa nisa po nna ziriziri, ate wa yaa suk wa pagrimu dula.

text: Suipuurum nyiŋ ate fi tabi tɛŋka zuk a taam, suipuurum nyiŋ ate fi namsi tɛŋsaŋa.

text: <<Nama Kus demma mɛ mi gebika ale basi ate ni nye diki.>>

text: Ase ni ale jam boro a dɛ ale a nyu la, ni a jam a nye daa nidek masim nyiŋŋa?

ref: I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.

ref: and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.

ref: Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
text: Piilimka po tutuna a jam karo a te nuru yaase duŋŋa. Waai an jam baga a tom wa tuima ale nalim wa dachaasa nyiŋŋa, diila m basi kama ate nuru meena a ta chaab ale wa vaanchoa.

ref: My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before.

ref: Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky.

text: <<Dila nyiŋ, yɔgyɔgla de m ŋman poli kama ayen m ŋman nye wamaŋsa a te Jerusalem ale Juda. Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa.

ref: But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace.
text: Ni magsi kama ayen ni nye nna: Ni a biisi wensie ale chaab abe ni a bo wensie buusa ni buusa yieŋa po.

ref: Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things. A Time of Celebration
text: Kan poli ayen fi nye fi vaanchoa biemmoa, kan yaali venta pɛka. Mi a kisi wieŋa de kama,>> Naawen ale weeni diila.

No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
text: Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna. <<Chiisa sinaansiwa po ale sinuwa po ale siyopɔiwa po ale piika po ate ni nyiem a bobi nɔi la a za ku chim ka suipeentik tigi a te Juda. Dila nyiŋla ni be yaali wensie ale suiyɔgni.>>

ref: Many people from strong nations will come to Jerusalem to worship me and to ask me to treat them with kindness.

text: Mi ale tuesi wusum torokoma Ɛfraim jigi ale kpaliŋ wusumaŋa Jerusalem jigi, abe m wɛ kpaliŋka tommu. Wa ale mooli suiyɔgni a te tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa. Wa naamu dɛka ale nyini nyakpiem a cheŋ nyakpiem, a ŋman nyini Benni a ga paari tɛŋzuk de kpeglimka.

ref: You can't believe idols and fortunetellers, or depend on the hope you receive from witchcraft and interpreters of dreams. But you have tried all of these, and now you are like sheep without a shepherd.

ref: I will strengthen the kingdoms of Judah and Israel. And I will show mercy because I am the Lord, their God. I will answer their prayers and bring them home. Then it will seem as though I had never rejected them.

ref: Israel will be like a tribe of warriors celebrating with wine. When their children see this, they will also be happy because of me, the Lord.

text: Ate Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Yuk ŋa a te ligtaarɔwa.>> Da magsika ate ba dak mi la a magsi kama. Ate mi yaa pai kpana ligbie pisitawa a yuk basi Naawen yenni po a te ligtaarɔwa.
