ref: Next, the Lord said to me, “Act like a shepherd again—this time a worthless shepherd.
text: Ate Naawen yaa ŋman jam weeni mi ayen, <<Ŋman tuesi naapeerik beruku kɔlimaŋa.

ref: Once more I am going to let a worthless nobody rule the land—one who won't care for the strays or search for the young or heal the sick or feed the healthy. He will just dine on the fattest sheep, leaving nothing but a few bones.”
text: Diila m za m te ate ka naapeerik a bo tɛŋka zuk ate wa niŋ a kan bo ŋaai ale koani la po, yaase wa te ŋaai ale ta nyiŋyɔgsa la ŋandiinta, alege wa ale yik ka pa ŋaai ale nala naŋsabaŋa a dari fɔgri abe wa ŋɔbi ŋa lanta.

ref: This is a message from the Lord about Israel: I am the Lord! I stretched out the heavens; I put the earth on its foundations and gave breath to humans.
text: Naawen wari ale nna a ta va Izirali nyiŋ. Naawen dii ale nye wenzuk, ale ŋman dueni tɛŋzuk de nyubini la, ate ku nyini wadek po ate wa nye nurubiik chiik la, waai meena abe seba dila kama. Wa ale a weeni diila ale nna:

ref: I have decided that Jerusalem will become a bowl of wine that makes the neighboring nations drunk. And when Jerusalem is attacked, Judah will also be attacked.
text: <<Mi ale nye Jerusalem ase ka daam ale bo beerik po la: tɛŋ sii ale moata ka la a dan nyu, ba ale nyiem a ja kama ase danyuirisa la. Ba le gilim Juda ale Jerusalem a siti ba.

ref: But I will turn Jerusalem into a heavy stone that crushes anyone who tries to lift it. When all nations on earth surround Jerusalem,
text: Dai dila danni, tɛŋsaŋa meena ale ta ka chaab ale Jerusalem. Mi ale nye Jerusalem ase ka piuŋjaaliŋ kuui ale kaa choa la a te tɛŋsaŋa meena. Baai ale za ba voori ku la za ba kɔni ka badek.

ref: I will blind every horse and make them panic, and every rider will be confused. But at the same time, I will watch over Judah.
text: Dai dila danni mi ale nye kama ate wusuma kpaziita a nak ate baai ale ba dɔ ŋa la ale chim yesiŋsa.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni dila. <<Mi nina ale kasim a nya Juda demma zuk kama, alege mi ale nye ate tɛŋsaŋa meena wusumaŋa ninaŋa a yi.

ref: Then every clan in Judah will realize that I, the Lord All-Powerful, am their God, and that I am the source of their strength.
text: Kula nyiŋ Juda niŋdeerɔma ale weeni ba suiniima po ayen, <Jerusalem demma a ta pagrim la, dii nyiŋla Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale ka ba Wen la nyiŋ.>

ref: At that time I will let the clans of Judah be like a ball of fire in a wood pile or a fiery torch in a hay stack. Then Judah will send the surrounding nations up in smoke. And once again the city of Jerusalem will be filled with people.
text: <<Dai dila danni mi ale nye Juda ase ka bolim ale bo daata po a dɛ diila, ate ba ŋman a nye ase bolim ŋiak ale chogsi ŋan kosa a dɛ diila. Bu za bu kasim a dɛ ka nuruma a gala ale a juga meena alege jaab a kan maa nye Jerusalem demma ale ba tɛŋka.

ref: But I will first give victory to Judah, so the kingdom of David and the city of Jerusalem in all of their glory won't be thought of more highly than Judah itself.
text: <<Naawen ale dɛ ka niŋ a vari Juda demma a basi, ate Deevid ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale Jerusalem demma zula ŋaai ate ba za ba nya la a kan gaam Juda demma.

ref: I, the Lord God, will protect Jerusalem. Even the weakest person there will be as strong as David, and David's kingdom will rule as though my very own angel were its leader.
text: Dai dila danni Naawen ale lik baai ale bo Jerusalem la kama, ate nuru baai ale wobsa a maa bo ba po la ale nya pagrim ase Deevid la, ate Deevid yenni ale dɛ ba niŋ ase Naawen Maarɔ la.

ref: I am determined to wipe out every nation that attacks Jerusalem. Mourning for the One Pierced with a Spear
text: Dai dila danni, mi ale kaasi tɛŋ kpieŋ sii meena ale ta chaab ale Jerusalem la kama.

ref: I, the Lord, will make the descendants of David and the people of Jerusalem feel deep sorrow and pray when they see the one they pierced with a spear. They will mourn and weep for him, as parents weep over the death of their only child or their first-born.
text: <<Ate mi ale pai chiik a basi Deevid yenni ale Jerusalem demma zuk, ka ale chim ka niauŋ ale puusa chiik. Ba ale nya mi, mi waai ate ba jam pai gbaluku a chub la, ate ba ale kum ase waai ale a kum wa biik yeŋ nyiŋ diila, ate ba ale kum ka nna yegayega nna se waai ale a kum wa biik kpagi nyiŋ diila.

ref: On that day the people of Jerusalem will mourn as much as everyone did for Hadad Rimmon on the flatlands near Megiddo.
text: Dai dila danni Jerusalem demma a za ba a kum ka nna yegayega. Kumsaŋa de za ŋa pagra kama ase Yadad Arimmon ale bo Megiddo peelimmu po la.

ref: Everyone of each family in the land will mourn, and the men will mourn separately from the women. This includes those from the family of David, and the families of Nathan,
text: Tɛŋka dɔkdemma wanyi wanyi ale ba pooba za ba kum kama: Deevid dɔkdemma ale ba pooba ale kum Natan dɔkdemma ale ba pooba mɛ ale kum.

ref: In the future there will be a fountain, where David's descendants and the people of Jerusalem can wash away their sin and guilt.
text: <<Dai dila danni, mi ale lagri nyiam a te Deevid ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale Jerusalem demma, ate nya bula ale sugri ba biem ale daŋta tuima a basi.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful says: When that time comes, I will get rid of every idol in the country, and they will be forgotten forever. I will also do away with their prophets and those evil spirits that control them.
text: <<Dai dila danni, mi le yeeri bɔgtaŋa yueŋa tɛŋka zuk, ate ba a kan ŋman teeri ti wari ya.>> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni. Wa ŋman weeni kama ayen, <M le yeeri biisiteerɔma ale baai ale ta chiik daŋtisa la tɛŋka zuk.>>

ref: If any such prophets ever appear again, their own parents must warn them that they will die for telling lies in my name—the name of the Lord. If those prophets don't stop speaking, their parents must then kill them with a sword.
text: Ate waai dan diem a weeni chum po wie, kula choa nyɔnɔwa ko ale wa ma ale weeni wa ayen ba ko wa dii nyiŋla wa pai ka Naawen yuenni a weeni venta wie. Wa dan weeni chum po wie, wadek nyam ale chub wa ale gebik a ko.

ref: Those prophets will be ashamed of their so-called visions, and they won't deceive anyone by dressing like a true prophet.
text: <<Dai dila danni, biisiteerɔ meena za wa ta ka chivie ale wa gɔdaasini. Wa a kan jo garuk kuui ale ta kɔbta ayen wa paasi nuruba.

ref: Instead, they will say, “I'm no prophet. I've been a farmer all my life.”
text: Wa ale weeni ayen mi daa biisiteerɔ, mi ka kpaarɔ! A zaani m paalim po ate m kasim kpa a dɛ.

ref: And if any of them are asked why they are wounded, they will answer, “It happened at the house of some friends.” A Wounded Shepherd and Scattered Sheep
text: Waai a dan bek wa ayen, <Mulaŋa de a nye ka sɛ a bo fi nyiŋka? Wa ale tulisi kama ayen, <Mi nya mulaŋa de a nyini ka mi doaba yie po.>

ref: The Lord All-Powerful said: My sword, wake up! Attack my shepherd and friend. Strike down the shepherd! Scatter the little sheep, and I will destroy them.
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni ayen, <<Gebik woŋka abe ta chaab ale m naapeerika ale nuru waai ale moata mu la! Siti naapeerika ate piisaŋa ale waaŋ chaab, ate m le pai m nisa a nye kpaliŋ ale bisaŋa.

ref: Nowhere in the land will more than a third of them be left alive.
text: Tɛŋka meena, fi dan lab ka po buta, ka po buye ale za ba kpi, ate ka bunyiwa ale boro.>> Naawen ale weeni dila.

ref: Then I will purify them and put them to the test, just as gold and silver are purified and tested. They will pray in my name, and I will answer them. I will say, “You are my people,” and they will reply, “You, Lord, are our God!”
text: <<Nya kude ale butawa po bunyi ate mi ale ta jam bolimu po. M le soti ba ase kpana la, abe m chamsi ba a nya ase ligmɔniŋ la. Ba ale wi m yuenni ate m le tulisi ba. M le weeni ayen, <Ba ka mi nuruba>, ate ba ale weeni ayen, <Naawen ka tama Wen.> >>

ref: The Lord will have his day. And when it comes, everything that was ever taken from Jerusalem will be returned and divided among its people.
text: Naawen danni a cheena ate ni ale jam koalim ŋan baai la, ba ale lab ŋa a te ni.

ref: But first, he will bring many nations to attack Jerusalem—homes will be robbed, women raped, and half of the population dragged off, though the others will be allowed to remain.
text: Mi ale tigsi tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa mɛ ate ba cheŋ a ga kpaliŋ ale Jerusalem, ba ale nak ba tɛŋ kpieŋka a vari ba ale ŋman tuesi ba yeeŋa, ba ale fɛ a goa ale ba pooma. Tɛŋka demma geli po ale cheŋ a ga bo tɛŋ yoŋ po, alege baai ale za ba tali la ale boro.

ref: The Lord will attack those nations like a warrior fighting in battle.
text: Naawen yaa ale nyini a kpaliŋ ale tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa de, ase wa ale a kpaliŋ dai diila.

ref: He will take his stand on the Mount of Olives east of Jerusalem, and the mountain will split in half, forming a wide valley that runs from east to west.
text: Dai dila danni wa naŋsaŋa a za si tabi ka Olivi Guuku zuk, ku ale chim ka Jerusalem kori geŋ, ate Olivi Guuku ale lab buye a ta nyini kori a cheŋ yeniŋ a dueni va kpieŋ ate ku geli mɛ a cheŋ wiilukku ate ku geli mɛ a cheŋ yeseoku.

ref: Then you people will escape from the Lord's mountain, through this valley, which reaches to Azal. You will run in all directions, just as everyone did when the earthquake struck in the time of King Uzziah of Judah. Afterwards, the Lord my God will appear with his holy angels.
text: Ni le chali va mi guuku viaka tɛŋ diila ku le teeri a paari Azel. Ni le chali ase ni le jam chali nyini tɛŋka choaka po diipo ate Yuzaya a jam ka Juda naab la. Ate Naawen mi Wenni ale baai meena ale welema la ale jam ale wa.

ref: It will be a bright day that won't turn cloudy or cold.
text: Dai dila danni bolim a kan boro, ŋoota yaase pik a kan boro.

ref: In both summer and winter, life-giving streams will flow from Jerusalem, half of them to the Dead Sea in the east and half to the Mediterranean Sea in the west.
text: Dai dila danni nyuvuri nyiam ale nyini Jerusalem, bu geli ale cheŋ nyakpiemu kori geŋsa, ate bu geli a cheŋ nyakpiemu yeniŋka geŋsa wenkarik ale yoei po.

ref: Then there will be only one Lord who rules as King and whose name is worshiped everywhere on earth.
text: Naawen ale chim ka naab tɛŋka meena zuk. Dai dila danni, ku ale chim ka Naawen nyiini, wa yuenni nyiini ale yuei.

ref: Here is what the Lord will do to those who attack Jerusalem: While they are standing there, he will make their flesh rot and their eyes fall from their sockets and their tongues drop out.
text: Nyiŋtuilaŋa de ale Naawen a za wa pai a nye tɛŋ kpieŋ sii meena ale jam ta chaab ale Jerusalem la: Ba nyiŋsaŋa ale yuati ale ba diem za ba naŋsa zuk, ba ninaŋa ale poak, ba num kunkooŋa po, ate ba giŋgeluŋtaŋa ale poak ba noaŋa po.

ref: The Lord will make them go into a frenzy and start attacking each other,
text: Dai dila danni Naawen a za wa nye kama ate nuruba kpaziita a nak. Ate waai meena a cheem a ta chaab ale wa choa.

ref: until even the people of Judah turn against those in Jerusalem. This same terrible disaster will also strike every animal nearby, including horses, mules, camels, and donkeys. Finally, everything of value in the surrounding nations will be collected and brought to Jerusalem—gold, silver, and piles of clothing.
text: Namsika de dekdek ale za ku jam wusumaŋa ale wusumbonsaŋa ale laalaakomima ale bonsaŋa ale duŋ sii meena ale bo tigsuŋtaŋa de la zuk.

ref: Afterwards, the survivors from those nations that attacked Jerusalem will go there each year to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful, and to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
text: Ate baai ale vuuk a nyini tɛŋsa meena po a jam siti Jerusalem la, ale cheŋ jueli ben meena po a ga puusi Naawa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a ga dɛ Viitaŋa Tigini.

ref: No rain will fall on the land of anyone in any country who refuses to go to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Nuruma waai a dan kan cheŋ a ga puusi Naawa ya, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ŋmoruk a kan ni ba tɛŋka zuk a te ba.

ref: This horrible disaster will strike the Egyptians and everyone else who refuses to go there for the celebration.
text: Nya kude ale chim ka namsika a te Ejipiti ale tɛŋ sii meena ale kan cheŋ a ga maa dɛ Viitaŋa Tigini la.

ref: At that time the words “Dedicated to the Lord” will be engraved on the bells worn by horses. In fact, every ordinary cooking pot in Jerusalem will be just as sacred to the Lord All-Powerful as the bowls used at the altar. Any one of them will be acceptable for boiling the meat of sacrificed animals, and there will no longer be a need to sell special pots and bowls.
text: Samɔnsa meena ale bo Jerusalem ale Juda la a za si ta tuilum kama a te Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale baai meena ale jam a nye kaabka la ale pai si kama a dik ba ŋandiintaŋa. Ate dai dila danni Keenan denɔ a kan ŋman bo Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La yenni po.

ref: I am Malachi. And this is the message that the Lord gave me for Israel. The Lord's Love for Israel
text: Wanni de ka wa dii ate Naawen a pai te Malakai ayen wa biisi a te Izirali demma.

ref: Israel, I, the Lord, have loved you. And yet you ask in what way have I loved you. Don't forget that Esau was the brother of your ancestor Jacob, but I chose Jacob
text: Naawen weeni ayen, <<Mi a yaali ni kama.>> Alege ni yaa bek ayen, <<Fi ti a yaali ti ka sɛ?>> Naawen yaa weeni ayen, Iisɔ ale Jekob jam daa suata? Mi jam a yaali Jekob kama,

ref: instead of Esau. And I turned Esau's hill country into a barren desert where jackals roam.
text: alege kisi Iisɔ. Mi jam kaasi wa tɛŋka ale ka guutaŋa jigini kama ate gɔi duŋsa yaa boro.

ref: Esau's descendants may say, “Although our nation Edom is in ruins, we will rebuild it.” But I, the Lord All-Powerful, promise to tear down whatever they build. Then everyone will know that I will never stop being angry with them as long as they are so sinful.
text: Edom nuruma ale weeni ayen, ti tɛŋka kaasi kama alege ti ŋman cheŋ a ga sɛ ŋan baai ale kaasi la. Alege Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a yaa weeni ayen, ba dan ŋman sɛ, m le kaasi ba ŋmana. Nuruma ale weeni ayen, Edom ka tɛŋ kaai nyeka ale toa. Naawen sui kasim a puuri ale Edom demma kama.

ref: Israel, when you see this, you will shout, “The Lord's great reputation reaches beyond our borders.” Judgment against Priests
text: Ni le nya wieŋa de ale nidek nina. Ate ni weeni ayen, <Naawen a zuaya a nyini Izirali a ga paari jigi meena.> >>

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something to say to you priests. Children respect their fathers, and servants respect their masters. I am your father and your master, so why don't you respect me? You priests have insulted me, and now you ask, “How did we insult you?”
text: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a weeni ayen, <<Biik a zuli wa ko kama, yɔma mɛ a zuli wa kpagi. Mi ka ko, alege ka boa ale soa ate ni kan zuli mi? Mi ka kpagi, ka boa ate ni kan zuli mi? Nama kaabteerɔma a kan zuli mi. Alege ni bek ayen, <Tama nye ka sɛ a kan zuli fu?>

ref: You embarrass me by offering worthless food on my altar. Then you ask, “How have we embarrassed you?” You have done it by saying, “What's so great about the Lord's altar?”
text: <<Dii ale a sak ayen ni kan zuli mi la, ni ta ka ŋandiin tii ale kan nala a jam a te mi. Ni ŋman bek ayen, boan le nye ate ŋantaŋa an nala? Ŋa an nala dii nyiŋla ni kan zuli mi kuŋkuŋku.

ref: But isn't it wrong to offer animals that are blind, lame, or sick? Just try giving those animals to your governor. That certainly wouldn't please him or make him want to help you.
text: Ni dan ta duŋ yioba a jam nye kaabka, ku an nala. Ni dan ta duŋ gbaŋsa ale duŋ yɔgnyieŋsa a jam a nye kaabka, ku an nala. Ni be pai bala a te ni tɛŋka kpagni, wa sui ale peenti ale ni? Wa ale siagi? Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a weeni.

ref: I am the Lord God All-Powerful, and you had better try to please me. You have sinned. Now see if I will have mercy on any of you.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ni weeni ate Wen a ta jiirim ale ni, alege wa kan siak tuesi ni tiirimu. Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: I wish someone would lock the doors of my temple, so you would stop wasting time building fires on my altar. I am not pleased with you priests, and I refuse to accept any more of your offerings.
text: <<Ni wanyi a dan poom lik Wen Yenni tuataŋa ate ni kan tɔti bolim tii ale kan ta kiri la mi kuŋkuŋku zuwa. Mi sui an peenti ale ni. M kan tuesi ni tiiritaŋa.>> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: From dawn until dusk my name is praised by every nation on this earth, as they burn incense and offer the proper sacrifices to me.
text: <<A zaani kori a ga paari yeri niŋ tɛŋsa meena ale zuli mi. Jigi meena ba le ta ŋan baai nyum ale masa ale tiirim maŋsa a jam te mi. Dii nyiŋla tɛŋsaŋa ale zuli mu.>> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: But even you priests insult me by saying, “There's nothing special about the Lord's altar, and these sacrifices are worthless.”
text: <<Alege ni kan zuli mu. Ni weeni ayen Nyɔnɔwa jazaanimu an nala, dila la ŋandiintaŋa mɛ a ka kiri ya.

ref: You get so disgusted that you even make vulgar signs at me. And for an offering, you bring stolen animals or those that are lame or sick. Should I accept these?
text: Ni weeni ayen, nama a jiak kama ale dila meena nyeka, ate ni yaa zɛri ale kisika. Ate ni yaa pai duŋ sii ale kɔni, ale duŋ gbansa, ale duŋ sii ale a yuak a te mi ayen ni tiirim. Ni ta jam kama ase tiirim la alege mi kan tuesi.>> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: Instead of offering the acceptable animals you have promised, you bring me those that are unhealthy. I will punish you for this, because I am the great King, the Lord All-Powerful, and I am worshiped by nations everywhere.
text: <<Nuru waai ale a vari la ale nya kikaasa. Wa ta duŋ diok kama wa duŋsaŋa po a nyiem yaa puulim ayen wa pai te mi. Wa ŋman pai duŋ kaai ale ta wari la a te. Mi ka naab kpioŋ.>> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni. <<Tɛŋsa meena abe a chali mu kama.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something else to say to you priests.
text: <<Nama kaabteerɔma, mi a kaam ni kama.

ref: You had better take seriously the need to honor my name. Otherwise, when you give a blessing, I will turn it into a curse. In fact, I have already done this, because you haven't taken to heart your duties as priests.
text: Ni wom. Ni kpesi wom mi ale a weeni diila. Ni a zuli m yuenni.>> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni. <<Ni dan kan wom ya, m le ka basi ni zuk abe m ka a kaasi ni niauŋku meena. M poom ka kama a basi ni zuk, dii nyiŋla ni an kpesi a wom mi ale a weeni diila.>>

ref: I will punish your descendants and rub your faces in the manure from your animal sacrifices, and then be done with you.
text: <<M le namsi ni ŋaaŋbisaŋa. M le pai ni duŋsaŋa puusaŋa po ŋantaŋa a taari ni ninaŋa a yaa pai ni ale ŋan bala a yuk a basi.

ref: I am telling you this, so I can continue to keep my agreement with your ancestor Levi.
text: Ate ni seba ayen mi ale a te ni kaamka dɛ ayen, Mi ale Livai nɔiyeŋka a kasim boro.>> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: I blessed him with a full life, as I had promised, and he kept his part of the agreement by honoring me and respecting my name.
text: <<Mi nɔiyeŋka ale Livai. Mi puulim kama ayen m le te ba nyuvuri ale suiyɔgni ate ba a zuli mu. Ba be zuli mi kama, ale a chali mi yɔgsum.

ref: He taught the truth and never told lies, and he led a lot of people to turn from sin, because he obeyed me and lived right.
text: Ba sak wensie sinsaŋŋa kama alege an biisi venta. Ba nye mi ale weeni ayen ba nye dila kama ale suiyɔgni ale wensie. Ba ŋman kasi nuruba yega biem nyeka.

ref: You priests should be eager to spread knowledge, and everyone should come to you for instruction, because you speak for me, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Kaabteerɔ a magsi wa sak wa le sebi diila, ate nuruba zamsi nyini wa jigi, dii nyiŋla, wa ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La tuimtomdɔ.

ref: But you have turned your backs on me. Your teachings have led others to do sinful things, and you have broken the agreement I made with your ancestor Levi.
text: Alege nama kaabteerɔma a deri basi mi zula teka. Ni sinsaŋŋa a basi ate ka nuruba yega a tom wabaata. Ni yik mi ale Livai buuni nɔiyeŋka kaasi kama.>> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.

ref: So I caused everyone to hate and despise you, because you disobeyed me and failed to treat all people alike. A Broken Agreement
text: <<Ni an kpesi nye dii ate mi weeni ayen ni nye la, Ni niŋ goanti boka nuruba biisa buusa boka. Mi yaa basi ayen nuruba kisi ni abe chivie yik ni nuru meena niŋ.>>

ref: Don't you know that we all have God as our Father? Didn't the one God create each of us? Then why do you cheat each other by breaking the agreement God made with your ancestors?
text: Ti meena ta ka ko yeŋ. Wen yeŋ ale nye ti. Dila la ka boa ale soa ate nuruba a nyiem nye nɔiyeŋ a ŋman yik kaasi, a kan zuli ti koma ale Naawen ale jam nye nɔiyeŋ kaai la.

ref: You people in Judah and Jerusalem have been unfaithful to the Lord. You have disgraced the temple that he loves, and you have committed the disgusting sin of marrying the worshipers of other gods.
text: Juda demma a yik mi dɔkku kaasi kama. Ba nye ka wa dii ate Naawen a kisi Izirali ale Jerusalem po la. Juda demma a kan zuli Wen yenni Naawen ate wa a yaali la. Juda demma a faari ka nipok baai ale a kaab tɛŋ yonsa bɔgta.

ref: I pray that the Lord will no longer let those who are guilty belong to his people, even if they eagerly decide to offer the Lord a gift.
text: Nuru ale a nye nnala a baga ta tiirim kama a jam Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La jigi alege Naawen ale gebi kula nyɔnɔwa a basi ate wa kan maa bo Izirali demma po.

ref: And what else are you doing? You cry noisily and flood the Lord's altar with your tears, because he isn't pleased with your offerings and refuses to accept them.
text: Wa di choa ale nna ni a nye. Ni a lik Naawen kuŋkuŋku ale ninyaata. Ni a kum kama dii nyiŋla, wa kan tuesi ni tiiritaŋa, wa sui abe kan peenti ale ni ale ta ŋan baai a jam la.

ref: And why isn't God pleased? It's because he knows that each of you men has been unfaithful to the wife you married when you were young. You promised that she would be your partner, but now you have broken that promise.
text: Ni bek ayen ka boa? Dii nyiŋla Naawen a chim ka fi ale fi bimbain po powa seerɔ, ate fi a chiib a nye wa a kaasi. Wa abe ka fi bandɔ ate fi ale wa a jam nye nɔiyeŋ.

ref: Didn't God create you and your wife to become like one person? And why did he do this? It was so you would have children, and then lead them to become God's people. Don't ever be unfaithful to your wife.

ref: One night he went to Jesus and said, “Rabbi, we know that God has sent you to teach us. You could not work these miracles, unless God were with you.”
text: Yɔk kunyi po ate nuruwa de yaa cheŋ Yeezu jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<M Sagrɔ, tama seba fi ka sagrɔ waai ate Wen a tom fu. Nuru an baga a nye wakperikaliik sii ate fi a tom ase daana la, ka Wen a nin bo ale wa.>>

ref: Jesus replied, “I tell you for certain that you must be born from above before you can see God's kingdom!”
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Wensie ate mi a weeni fu ayen nuru an baga a jo Wen naamu po, ka ba nin pilim biak wa.>>

ref: Jesus answered: I tell you for certain that before you can get into God's kingdom, you must be born not only by water, but by the Spirit.
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Wensie ate mi a weeni fu ayen nuru an baga a jo Wen naamu po, ka ba nin biak wa ale nyiam ale pilim biak wa ale Wen Chiika.

ref: Humans give life to their children. Yet only God's Spirit can change you into a child of God.
text: Waai ate ba biak nyiŋ lammu po la, ka nyiŋ lam, waai ate ba biak Chiika po la ka chiik.

ref: Don't be surprised when I say that you must be born from above.
text: Kan te ku cha fu mi ale weeni fu ayen, <Ka ba nin pilim biak fu la.>

ref: Only God's Spirit gives new life. The Spirit is like the wind that blows wherever it wants to. You can hear the wind, but you don't know where it comes from or where it is going.
text: Vioku a fuk a cheŋ ka juijui meena ate ku a yaali la, ate fi mɛ a wom ku fukka, alege fi zɛ ku le nyini juijui la yaase ku ale a cheŋ juijui la. Ku abe ka dila ale waai meena ate Wen Chiika a biak la.>>

ref: Jesus replied: How can you be a teacher of Israel and not know these things?
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi ka sagrɔ kpioŋ a bo Izirali tɛŋka alege an baga a miŋ mi ale weeni fu diila kiri ya?

ref: I tell you for certain we know what we are talking about because we have seen it ourselves. But none of you will accept what we say.
text: Wensie ate mi a weeni fu ayen ti a biisi ka wie ŋaai ate ti seba ŋa la, ale a weeni wie ŋaai ate ti nya ŋa la, alege ni waai a kan siak tama wieŋa.

ref: If you don't believe when I talk to you about things on earth, how can you possibly believe if I talk to you about things in heaven?
text: Ni ka siaka ale mi ase m nin weeni tɛŋka de zuk wie, ni abe ni nye ka sɛ a ta siaka ale mi ase m nin weeni wenŋmazuk wie?

ref: No one has gone up to heaven except the Son of Man, who came down from there.
text: Nuru karo a jueli wenŋmazuwa ka Mi Saalɔbiika ale nyini wenŋmazuk a jam tɛŋzuk de.

ref: And the Son of Man must be lifted up, just as the metal snake was lifted up by Moses in the desert.
text: Ase Moosis ale jam mɛ waamu a yik diok woŋku nyiŋ a zak zaani sagni po la, dila dek ate ba le yik Mi Saalɔbiika a kpi jabarimu nyiŋ a zak zaani.

ref: Then everyone who has faith in the Son of Man will have eternal life.
text: Ate waai meena ale a ta siaka ale mi la ale nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka.

ref: God loved the people of this world so much that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who has faith in him will have eternal life and never really die.
text: <<Wen a yaali tɛŋzuk de demma ka nna yegayega ate wa tom wa bi yeŋka ba jigi, ayen baai ale ta siaka ale wa la a kan kpi alege ba le nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la.

ref: God did not send his Son into the world to condemn its people. He sent him to save them!
text: Wen an tom wa Nidoabinni ayen wa jam kaasi tɛŋzuk de demma, alege wa jam kama ayen wa vari ba a basi.

ref: No one who has faith in God's Son will be condemned. But everyone who doesn't have faith in him has already been condemned for not having faith in God's only Son.
text: Baai ale ta siaka ale Wen Nidoabinni la, Wen a kan bo ba buusa. Baai ale kan ta siaka ale wa Nidoabinni la, Wen a poom bo ba buusa kama, dii nyiŋla ba an ta siaka ale wa bi yeŋka.

ref: The light has come into the world, and people who do evil things are judged guilty because they love the dark more than the light.
text: Buusaŋa abe le nna, ayen Bolimu a jam tɛŋzuk de kama, ate nurubiik a yaali legini a gaam Bolimu, dii la ba nyeelaŋa jam ka biem nyeela.

ref: People who do evil hate the light and won't come to the light, because it clearly shows what they have done.
text: Ba seba ayen ba dan bo Bolimu nyaka jigini a tom ba wabaataŋa, waai meena ale nya dii ate ba a nye la kama. Ka dila ale soa ate ba kan yaali ayen ba moata Bolimu jigini.

ref: But everyone who lives by the truth will come to the light, because they want others to know that God is really the one doing what they do. Jesus and John the Baptist
text: Alege baai ale a tom dii ale ka wensie la, bala a kan chali bolimu jigini boka. Ba a tom ba tuimaŋa ate ŋa a sak kama ayen ba a tom ka dii ate Wen a yaali la.>>

ref: Later, Jesus and his disciples went to Judea, where he stayed with them for a while and was baptizing people.
text: Kude ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa basi dula jigini ale ge cheŋ Judia. Ba jam bo dula ka daa maga dega a te nuruba soka.

ref: John's followers got into an argument with a Jewish man about a ceremony of washing.
text: Dai yeŋ po ate Juuma wanyi a yaa jam Jɔɔn ŋaaŋviirɔma jigi a ta nanpaga ale ba soka teka nyiŋ.

ref: They went to John and said, “Rabbi, you spoke about a man when you were with him east of the Jordan. He is now baptizing people, and everyone is going to him.”
text: Ba yaa jam Jɔɔn jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Ti Sagrɔ, nuru waai ale poom a bo ale ti Jodan Benni kauk kunkula ale dii ate fi poom a weeni wa wie a sak ti la, yɔgyɔgla de wa yaa a te ka nuruba soka ate waai meena a cheŋ wa jigi.>>

ref: John replied: No one can do anything unless God in heaven allows it.
text: Jɔɔn yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nuru an baga a lueri wari wa dega, ka Wen a nin te wa.

ref: You surely remember how I told you that I am not the Messiah. I am only the one sent ahead of him.
text: Nama teeri ayen mi a poom weeni ni ayen, <Daa mi ale Kirisitawa.> Wen a tom mi ate mi dɛ wa niŋ a jam ayen m gomsi suiku a magsi a te Wa.

ref: Jesus must become more important, while I become less important. The One Who Comes from Heaven
text: Ku magsi kama ayen wala a jueli ŋmai abe mi a bo tɛŋ.>>

ref: God's Son comes from heaven and is above all others. Everyone who comes from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks about earthly things. The one who comes from heaven is above all others.
text: Waai ale nyini wenŋmazuk la a gaam waai meena kama. Waai ale nyini tɛŋzuk de la, ka tɛŋzuk de nuru ale a biisi tɛŋzuk de wie, alege waai ale nyini wenŋmazuk la a gaam waai meena kama.

ref: He speaks about what he has seen and heard, and yet no one believes him.
text: Wa a weeni ka wie ŋaai ate wa nya ale wom la alege waai a ka siaka ale ŋa.

ref: But everyone who does believe him has shown that God is truthful.
text: Alege waai ale ta siaka ale wa wieŋa la a sak kama ayen Wen ka wensie nyɔnɔ.

ref: The Son was sent to speak God's message, and he has been given the full power of God's Spirit.
text: Waai ate Wen tom la a biisi ka Wen wieŋa, dii nyiŋla Wen a basi ate wa Chiika a bo ale wa kama.

ref: The Father loves the Son and has given him everything.
text: Kowa a yaali wa Nidoabinni kama ate wa pai jaabuuri meena pagrim a te wa.

ref: Everyone who has faith in the Son has eternal life. But no one who rejects him will ever share in that life, and God will be angry with them forever.
text: Waai meena ale ta siaka ale wa Nidoabinni la a nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la kama. Waai meena mɛ ale kan ta siaka ale wa ale kan va wa nɔi la, a kan nya nyuvuri dila, alege Wen suipuurumu ale jam wa zuk.>>

ref: But Jesus' disciples were really the ones doing the baptizing, and not Jesus himself. Jesus and the Samaritan Woman
text: daa Yeezu dek ale jam a te nuruma soka, alege ka wa ŋaaŋviirɔma.

ref: Jesus left Judea and started for Galilee again.
text: Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita jam basi Judia ale ŋmani a cheŋ Galili.

ref: This time he had to go through Samaria,
text: Yeezu a jam va ka Samaria a cheŋ Galili.

ref: “You are a Jew,” she replied, “and I am a Samaritan woman. How can you ask me for a drink of water when Jews and Samaritans won't have anything to do with each other?”
text: Nipowa a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi ka Juu alege mi a chim Samaria tɛŋka nipok. Ka boa ate fi a juisi nyiam mi jigi ya?>>

ref: “Sir,” the woman said, “you don't even have a bucket, and the well is deep. Where are you going to get this life-giving water?
text: Nipowa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, fi ka jaŋarimmoa alege vinni mɛ limisa. Fi ale nya, nya bula ka be a te mi?

ref: Our ancestor Jacob dug this well for us, and his family and animals got water from it. Are you greater than Jacob?”
text: Tama kokpieŋka, Jekob, ale tu vinni de dipo, ayen wa ale wa dɔkdemma ale wa duŋsaŋa a nya nyiam a nyu di po. Fi abe zuak a gaam ti kokpieŋka Jekob kama?>>

ref: But no one who drinks the water I give will ever be thirsty again. The water I give will become in that person a flowing fountain that gives eternal life.”
text: Waai meena ale a nyu nya buui ate mi a te wa la, nyanyuila a kan ŋman yik wa diipo diipo. Mi ale m te nya buui la ale kasim a buli kama a te wa nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la.>>

ref: The woman replied, “Sir, please give me a drink of that water! Then I won't get thirsty and have to come to this well again.”
text: Nipowa yaa le ga wom dii ate Yeezu a weeni la, wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, be te mu fi nyiamu de ate nyanyuila a kan ŋman yik mu ate m ŋman jam dela a ŋari nyiamoa.>>

ref: Jesus told her, “Go and bring your husband.”
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Cheŋ a ga wi fi chorɔwa ate ni jam.>>

ref: The woman answered, “I don't have a husband.” “That's right,” Jesus replied, “you're telling the truth. You don't have a husband. You have already been married five times, and the man you are now living with isn't your husband.”
text: Fi yali ka nidoaba banu. Nidoa waai ate fi boro ale wa jinla la wala ka fi nɔŋ. Fi ale weeni mu diila ka wensie.>>

ref: My ancestors worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say Jerusalem is the only place to worship.”
text: Nya guuk kpioŋku de kuui ale za dela la. Ti kokpieŋsaŋa a puusi a te Wen ka kula zuk alege nama Juuma a weeni ti ayen ka Jerusalem tɛŋka ale Wen puusi teka jigi.>>

ref: Jesus said to her: Believe me, the time is coming when you won't worship the Father either on this mountain or in Jerusalem.
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nipowa, ta siaka ale mi ku danni a cheena ate nuruba a kan ŋman puusi Kowa guuku de zuk yaase Jerusalem tɛŋka po.

ref: You Samaritans don't really know the one you worship. But we Jews do know the God we worship, and by using us, God will save the world.
text: Nama Samaria demma, ni sum zɛ waai dek ate ni puusi a te la. Tama Juuma a seba waai dek ate ti puusi a te la kama. Dii la varibasika a nyini ka Juuma jigi.

ref: But a time is coming, and it is already here! Even now the true worshipers are being led by the Spirit to worship the Father according to the truth. These are the ones the Father is seeking to worship him.
text: Dai a cheena, di abe poom jam kama ayen, baai ale sum a puusi Wen la a puusi Kowa chiika po ale wensie, ka bala ale Kowa a gisi ayen ba a puusi wa.

ref: God is Spirit, and those who worship God must be led by the Spirit to worship him according to the truth.
text: Wen ka chiik, baai ale a puusi wa la ku a fɛ ate ba puusi wa chiika po ale wensie.>>

ref: The woman said, “I know that the Messiah will come. He is the one we call Christ. When he comes, he will explain everything to us.”
text: Nipowa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M seba ayen Waai Ate Wen A Lueri La a cheena kama waai ate ba a wi ayen Kirisitawa la. Wa dan jam, wa le sak ti wie meena.>>

ref: “I am that one,” Jesus told her, “and I am speaking to you now.”
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Mi ka wala waai ale a biisi ale fu la.>>

ref: The disciples returned about this time and were surprised to find Jesus talking with a woman. But none of them asked him what he wanted or why he was talking with her.
text: Wa le diem boro a biisi la, wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa deri ŋman jam. Ba le nya Yeezu ale nipowa a za a biisi la, ku yaa deri cha ba, alege ba waai an jam bek wa ayen ka boa ate fi a biisi ale wa yaase jabuui wari ate ba a biisi la.

ref: The woman left her water jar and ran back into town, where she said to the people,
text: Dula jigini nipowa yaa basi wa nyiamu liikka ale ŋmani cheŋ tɛŋka po a ga weeni nidoama ayen,

ref: “Come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done! Could he be the Messiah?”
text: <<Ni jam nya nuru ale weeni mi wie ŋaai meena ate mi nye la. Wala ale baga a chim Kirisitawa?>>

ref: Everyone in town went out to see Jesus.
text: Ba le wom dii ate wa weeni la, ba yaa deri nyini a cheŋ Yeezu jigi.

ref: While this was happening, Jesus' disciples were saying to him, “Teacher, please eat something.”
text: Ase nipowa ale jam bo suiku po a kuli la, Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa saalim wa ayen, <<Ti Sagrɔ, ti a saalim fu ayen fi ŋoa ŋandiintaŋa a dɛ.>>

ref: But Jesus told them, “I have food you don't know anything about.”
text: Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Mi ta ka ŋandiinta m dɛ tii ate nama a zɛ la.>>

ref: His disciples started asking each other, “Has someone brought him something to eat?”
text: Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa bek chaab ayen, <<Ka nuru yaa be le ta ŋandiinta a jam a te wa ale ge tama a zɛ yaa?>>

ref: Jesus said: My food is to do what God wants! He is the one who sent me, and I must finish the work that he gave me to do.
text: Yeezu yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Mi ŋandiintaŋa ale m nye waai ale tom mu la yaalika abe m nueri wa tuini.

ref: You may say there are still four months until harvest time. But I tell you to look, and you will see that the fields are ripe and ready to harvest.
text: Nama a kan weeni kama ayen, <Ku diem tali ka chiisa sinaansi ate ti che?> Mi a weeni ni, ni lak ni ninaŋa a zak nya talimu po ŋantaŋa a bɛ magsi ka cheka.

ref: Even now the harvest workers are receiving their reward by gathering a harvest that brings eternal life. Then everyone who planted the seed and everyone who harvests the crop will celebrate together.
text: Nuru waai ale a che ŋantaŋa la a tuesi tutuna kama. Wa ale a tigsi ŋanbieŋa la a nye ase ka nuruba la, ate nuru bala a nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la. Dila nyiŋ boridɔwa ale cheerɔwa sue ale peenti ale chaab.

ref: So the saying proves true, “Some plant the seed, and others harvest the crop.”
text: Juuma kpaŋŋa a nyiem ale kasim a weeni dii ayen, <Nuru wanyi ale a bori ate wanyi mɛ a che la,> ka wensie.

ref: I am sending you to harvest crops in fields where others have done all the hard work.
text: Ka mi ale tom ni ayen ni cheŋ a ga che ŋantaŋa kadukka po. Nuru yonta ale bori ate nama ayen ni nya ba tuimaŋa nyuenta.>>

ref: A lot of Samaritans in that town put their faith in Jesus because the woman had said, “This man told me everything I have ever done.”
text: Samaria tɛŋka nipowa ale ga weeni wa tɛŋka demma ayen ba jam nya nuru waai ale weeni wie ŋaai meena ate wa nye la, ba yegayega yaa jam ta siaka ale Yeezu.

ref: They came and asked him to stay in their town, and he stayed on for two days.
text: Ba yaa jam wa jigi a saalim wa ayen wa jam a bo ale ba. Yeezu yaa siak a wari ba jigi daa ŋaye.

ref: They told the woman, “We no longer have faith in Jesus just because of what you told us. We have heard him ourselves, and we are certain that he is the Savior of the world!” Jesus Heals an Official's Son (Matthew
text: Ba yaa weeni nipowa ayen, <<Tama an ta siaka ale wa ka fi ale weeni ti diila nyiini nyiŋŋa, alege ka wa sakka nyiŋ ale soa ate ti ta siaka ale wa. Ti seba ayen ka wa a sum le tɛŋzuk de meena Varibasidɔwa.>>

ref: Jesus had said, “Prophets are honored everywhere, except in their own country.” Then two days later he left
text: Wadek a poom weeni kama ayen Wen biisiteerɔ dek tɛŋka demma a kan te wa zula.

ref: and went to Galilee. The people there welcomed him, because they had gone to the festival in Jerusalem and had seen everything he had done.
text: Ba ale paari Galili la nuruma a jam te wa tia kama dii nyiŋla ba cheŋ ga dɛ Gaambasika Tigini Jerusalem kama ale nya wie ŋaai meena ate wa tom la.

ref: While Jesus was in Galilee, he returned to the village of Cana, where he had turned the water into wine. There was an official in Capernaum whose son was sick.
text: Yeezu yaa ŋman cheŋ Kena tɛŋka ate ka bo Galili la. Ka dula jigini ate wa nye ate nyiamu a tagri a chim daamu la. Kpagi dinyi ale jam bo Kapernaum ate wa nidoabili a yuak.

ref: And when the man heard that Jesus had come from Judea, he went and begged him to keep his son from dying.
text: Wa le wom ayen Yeezu a basi Judia ale ŋman jam Galili la, wa yaa jam Yeezu jigi ayen wa saalim wa ate wa ga tebi wa nidoabinni waai ale moata kum la.

ref: Jesus told the official, “You won't have faith unless you see miracles and wonders!”
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nuruba a kan ta siaka ale mi, ka mi a nin tom wakperikaliisa ale daana ate ba nya.>>

ref: The man replied, “Lord, please come before my son dies!”
text: Kpagni yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔ, fi dan kan va mu a kuli nwuli, m biika ale kpi.>>

ref: Jesus then said, “Your son will live. Go on home to him.” The man believed Jesus and started back home.
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Kuli yeri a ga nya fi nidoabinni ale wa ta nyiŋyɔgsa kama.>> Kpagni yaa deri ta siaka ale Yeezu ale weeni diila a yaa kuli.

ref: Some of the official's servants met him along the road and told him, “Your son is better!”
text: Wa le jam bo suiku po a kuli la, wa tomteerɔma gela yaa tu wa suiku niŋ a weeni wa ayen, <<Fi nidoabinni a ta nyiŋyɔgsa kama.>>

ref: He asked them when the boy got better, and they answered, “The fever left him yesterday at one o'clock.”
text: Wa yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ka dimpo ate wa nya nyiŋyɔgsa?>> Ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ka deemwa baŋ bunyi wentueŋ ate kazangbarimaŋa a basi wa.>>

ref: The boy's father realized that at one o'clock the day before, Jesus had told him, “Your son will live!” So the man and everyone in his family put their faith in Jesus.
text: Biika kowa yaa deri teeri ayen ka diipo ate Yeezu a weeni wa ayen wa nidoabinni a nya nyiŋyɔgsa kama la. Wa yaa ga paari yeri a nya ale dii ate wa tomteerɔma a weeni wa la sum ka wensie. Wa le wa dɔkdemma meena a yaa ta siaka ale Yeezu dii ate wa nye la nyiŋ.

ref: This was the second miracle that Jesus worked after he left Judea and went to Galilee.
text: Wakperikaliika de ase daana la ate Yeezu a tom saari buye wa le nyini Judia a jam Galili la.

ref: In the city near the sheep gate was a pool with five porches, and its name in Hebrew was Bethzatha.
text: Beli gilini ale jam bo dula a moata tɛŋka nansuiŋtaŋa kunyi ate ba a wi ayen Piisa Nansuiŋ. Juuma a wi dula jigini ale badek tɛŋka biika ayen ka Betezata. Kusuŋta tinu ale jam gilim benni nɔnni.

ref: Beside the pool was a man who had been sick for
text: Nuru wanyi a yaa maa boro ate yuammu a ta wa paari bena pisita ale naaniŋ.

ref: You have not believed his message, because you refused to have faith in the one he sent.
text: Wa tom mi ka nama jigi, alege ni ka siaka ale mi. Ka dila ale soa ate wa sinsaŋŋa a ka ni suiniimaŋa po la.

ref: When Jesus saw the man and realized that he had been crippled for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be healed?”
text: Yeezu ale nya wa la wa seba ayen tuemu a yik wa ate ku beni kama ate wa bek wa ayen, <<Fi a yaali fi nya nyiŋyɔgsa?>>

ref: The man answered, “Sir, I don't have anyone to put me in the pool when the water is stirred up. I try to get in, but someone else always gets there first.”
text: Yuarɔwa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, nyiamu a nyiem dan choa, m ka nuru ate wa pai mu a ta ga a nyo bu po nwuli. M nyiem dan pii nyiŋ a yaali ayen m forisi a paari bu, nuru yoŋ a nyiem ale dɛ niŋ a paari du ale ge mu.>>

ref: Jesus told him, “Pick up your mat and walk!”
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Yiti a zaani abe fi kpamsi fi tiaka a cheŋ.>>

ref: Right then the man was healed. He picked up his mat and started walking around. The day on which this happened was a Sabbath.
text: Nuruwa yaa deri nya nyiŋyɔgsa a yiti zaani ale kpamsi wa tiaka a cheŋ. Dai dii danni ate nya kude a nye la a jam ka Juuma Vuusum Dai.

ref: When the Jewish leaders saw the man carrying his mat, they said to him, “This is the Sabbath! No one is allowed to carry a mat on the Sabbath.”
text: Juuma yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ku a kisi kama ate fi ji fi tiaka tama Vuusum Danni po.>>

ref: But he replied, “The man who healed me told me to pick up my mat and walk.”
text: Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nuru waai ale tebi mu la ale weeni mu ayen m pai tiaka a cheŋ.>>

ref: They asked him, “Who is this man that told you to pick up your mat and walk?”
text: Ba yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka wana ale weeni fu ayen fi nye kude?>>

ref: But he did not know who Jesus was, and Jesus had left because of the crowd.
text: Nuru waai ale nya nyiŋyɔgsaŋa la a jam zɛ Yeezu ale ka waai la, dii nyiŋla nuru boari ale jam bo dula ate Yeezu a moali nyini.

ref: Later, Jesus met the man in the temple and told him, “You are now well. But don't sin anymore or something worse might happen to you.”
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ Yeezu yaa ŋman nya wa Wen yenni po a weeni wa ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de fi yaa ta nyiŋyɔgsa kama. Be kan ŋman a tom tuimbaata. Fi dan ŋman tom tuimbaata, fi le nam a gaam ku le jam ka diila.>>

ref: The man left and told the leaders that Jesus was the one who had healed him.
text: Nuruwa yaa deri nyini a ga weeni Juuma ayen ka Yeezu ale tebi wa.

ref: They started making a lot of trouble for Jesus because he did things like this on the Sabbath.
text: Kude nyiŋ Juma yaa namsi Yeezu, diila wa nye kude ka Vuusum Danni.

ref: But Jesus said, “My Father has never stopped working, and this is why I keep on working.”
text: Alege Yeezu yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<M Kowa a diema tom kama ate mi mɛ a tom.>>

ref: Now the leaders wanted to kill Jesus for two reasons. First, he had broken the law of the Sabbath. But even worse, he had said God was his Father, which made him equal with God. The Son's Authority
text: Kude nyiŋ ate Juuma a jaa gisi ba ko wa la, dii nyiŋla daa Vuusum Danni nyiini ate wa kaasi alege wa jam a wi Wen ayen ka wadek Ko, a pai wadek a magsi chaab ale Wen.

ref: Jesus told the people: I tell you for certain the Son cannot do anything on his own. He can do only what he sees the Father doing, and he does exactly what he sees the Father do.
text: Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Wensie ate mi a weeni ni ayen Nidoabinni an baga a nye wadek wari ya. Dii meena ate m Kowa a tom la, mi mɛ a tom ka dila dekdega.

ref: The Father loves the Son and has shown him everything he does. The Father will show him even greater things, and you will be amazed.

text: alege mi ale seba wa. Mi ale wa a jam bo ka jigi yeŋ ale ge ate wa tom mi ni jigi.>>

ref: But Jesus told them, “I will be with you a little while longer, and then I will return to the one who sent me.

text: Farisiima yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Wa sum a maa paasi nama mɛ kama?

ref: The people asked, “Does he intend to kill himself? Is that what he means by saying we cannot go where he is going?”

ref: Jesus replied: I tell you for certain that anyone who sins is a slave of sin!

text: Mi a biisi ka mi ale nya dii m kowa jigi la alege nama a biisi ni kowa ale weeni diila.>>

ref: The people said to Jesus, “Abraham is our father!” Jesus replied, “If you were Abraham's children, you would do what Abraham did.

ref: Jesus answered: If God were your Father, you would love me, because I came from God and now I am here. He sent me. I did not come on my own.

text: Ni ka ni kowa jabioku bisa ate ni a yaali ayen ni a va wa yaalika. A nyini piilimka po wa ka nuru koorik. Wa an maa va wensie siuwa dii nyiŋla wensie ka wa jigi ya. Wa daa velim wa a nye dila kama diila venta a piilim ka wa jigi ale chim venta ko.

ref: Anyone who belongs to God will listen to his message. But you refuse to listen, because you don't belong to God. Jesus and Abraham
text: Baai ale ka Wen bisa la a wom wa ale a weeni ba diila kama. Nama ale kan a yaali ayen ni wom Wen wieŋa diila a sak kama ayen ni daa wa bisa.>>

ref: Are you greater than our father Abraham? He died, and so did the prophets. Who do you think you are?”
text: Ti kokpieŋka Abrayam kpi kama. Fi a poli ayen fi zuak a gaam wa kama. Wen biisiteerɔma mɛ a kpi, fi a poli ayen fi ka wana?>>

text: Wensie ate mi a weeni ni. Yɔma a kan zuak a gaam wa nyɔnɔ. Tomteerɔ mɛ an baga a zuak a gaam waai ale tom wa la.

ref: I am not talking about all of you. I know the ones I have chosen. But what the Scriptures say must come true. And they say, “The man who ate with me has turned against me!”
text: Daa ni meena ate mi a weeni, alege ka baai nyiini ate m lueri a te m dek la. Ba ŋmarisi Wen Gbaŋka po ayen, <Waai ale wa ta mu a ga bobri sak la, wala ate mi ale wa a dɛ ŋandiintaŋa ale chaab.> (Yiila

ref: I am telling you this before it all happens. Then when it does happen, you will believe who I am.
text: Dila nyiŋla, m liŋ a weeni ni kama, ayen ku dan jam boro a nye, ni ta siaka ale mi ale weeni ayen m ka waai la.

ref: So the disciple leaned toward Jesus and asked, “Lord, which one of us are you talking about?”
text: Waai ate Yeezu a jam a yaali nna yegayega la, a yaa forisi paari a bek wa ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, ka wana dega?>>

ref: After Jesus had said these things, he was deeply troubled and told his disciples, “I tell you for certain that one of you will betray me.”
text: Yeezu ale biisi a nueri la, ku yaa daani wa, wa suinum po nna yegayega. Wa yaa weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen, <<Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, ni po wanyi ale wa ta mu a ga bobri sak.>>

ref: Jesus' favorite disciple was sitting next to him at the meal,
text: Waai ate Yeezu a jam a yaali ba po nna yegayega la a jam kala kama a moata wa.

ref: and Simon motioned for this disciple to find out which one Jesus meant.
text: Simon Piita yaa magsi a weeni wa ayen wa bek Yeezu a miŋ waai dek ale wa nye wa dila la.

ref: But because Judas was in charge of the money, some of them thought that Jesus had told him to buy something they needed for the festival. Others thought that Jesus had told him to give some money to the poor.
text: Judas a jam ale waai ale a nya ba ligraŋa zuk la. Dila nyiŋla, ba jam a poli kama ayen Yeezu a tom wa kama ayen wa cheŋ a ga da ŋanta a magsi tigini, yaase wa te niwomma ligra.

ref: Judas took the piece of bread and went out. It was already night. The New Command
text: Judas ale ga tuesi boroboroku la, wa yaa deri yiti a nyini a cheŋ. Ku jam ka yok ate wa nyini la.

ref: Then, after God is given glory because of him, God will bring glory to him, and God will do it very soon.
text: Ase Wen a dan nya pimpauk, Wen mɛ ale pak wa wadek nyiŋ.

ref: My children, I will be with you for only a little while longer. Then you will look for me, but you won't find me. I tell you just as I told the people, “You cannot go where I am going.”
text: M bisa, mi a kan bo ale ni ate ku beni. M dan cheŋ, ni le nyiem a gisi m boka jigini. Ni teeri diipo ate m weeni Juuma kpaŋŋa ayen ba kan baga a va mu a cheŋ juijui ate mi a cheŋ la. Dila nama mɛ a kan baga a cheŋ juijui ate mi a cheŋ la.

ref: “Would you really die for me?” Jesus asked. “I tell you for certain before a rooster crows, you will say three times that you don't even know me.”
text: Yeezu yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi sum gomsi a magsi ayen fi kpi mi nyiŋŋa? Wensie ate mi a weeni fu. Fi le weeni nuruba ku nɔi buta yokku de ayen fi zɛ mi abe vari kpadiaka a kum.>>

ref: Jesus said to his disciples, “Don't be worried! Have faith in God and have faith in me.
text: Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni kan basi ate ni sue a kaasi, ni ta siaka ale Wen abe ni ta siaka ale mi mɛ.

ref: There are many rooms in my Father's house. I wouldn't tell you this, unless it was true. I am going there to prepare a place for each of you.
text: Mi Kowa yenni po ka diin bori. Mi abe pilim a cheŋ ku jigini kama, ayen m gomsi jigi a te ni. Ase ku dan kan daa dila, m te kan weeni ni.

ref: After I have done this, I will come back and take you with me. Then we will be together.
text: M dan gomsi ŋa a nueri, m le ŋman jam a ta ni a cheŋ ku jigini ate nama ale mi a maa chaab a bo jigi yeŋ.

ref: You know the way to where I am going.”
text: Ni seba mi ale a cheŋ juijui la kama ale suik kuui ale a cheŋ ku jigini la.>>

ref: “I am the way, the truth, and the life!” Jesus answered. “Without me, no one can go to the Father.
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Mi ale suiku ale wensieŋa ale nyuvunni, waai a kan baga a jam Kowa jigi ya alege ka wa nin va mi jigi.

ref: If you had really known me, you would have known the Father. But from now on, you do know him, and you have seen him.”
text: <<Nama ale seba mi ale ka waai yɔgyɔgla de la, kula le basi ate ni seba m Kowa ale ka waai la mɛ. A nyini jinla a ta a cheŋ ni yaa nya wa kama ale seba wa.>>

ref: Philip said, “Lord, show us the Father. That is all we need.”
text: Filip yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, tama ale a yaali dii nyiini la ale fi basi ate ti nya fi Kowa.>>

ref: Jesus replied: Philip, I have been with you for a long time. Don't you know who I am? If you have seen me, you have seen the Father. How can you ask me to show you the Father?
text: Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Tama a bo le chaab ate ku beni kama alege fi a zɛ mi? Waai meena ale nya mi la, a nya m Kowa kama. Ka boa ale soa ate fi weeni ayen m dak m Kowa a sak ni?

ref: Don't you believe that I am one with the Father and that the Father is one with me? What I say isn't said on my own. The Father who lives in me does these things.
text: Fi ka siaka ayen mi a bo ale m Kowa ate m Kowa mɛ a bo ale mu? Mi ale sak ni wie ŋaai meena la an nyini daa mi dek jigi ya. M Kowa waai ale bo ale mu la, ale a tom wa tuimaŋa.>>

ref: Have faith in me when I say that the Father is one with me and that I am one with the Father. Or else have faith in me simply because of the things I do.
text: Yeezu yaa cheem a weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma meena ayen, <<Ni ta siaka ayen m Kowa a bo ale mu kama ate mi mɛ a bo ale wa. Be dan kan daa di ni be ta siaka ale m tuimkperikaliik sii ate ni nya ale maa tom la nyiŋ.

ref: I tell you for certain that if you have faith in me, you will do the same things I am doing. You will do even greater things, now that I am going back to the Father.
text: Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, baai ale ta siaka ale mi la ale ba a tom dii ate mi a tom la. Bala dek ale tom tuimkperikaliisa a gaam dii ate mi a tom la, dii nyiŋla mi ale ŋmani a cheŋ m Kowa jigi la.

ref: Ask me, and I will do whatever you ask. This way the Son will bring honor to the Father.
text: Ni dan juisi jaabuuri meena mi yuenni nyiŋ m le nye a te ni, ate Kowa ale nya zula Nidoabinni nyiŋ.

ref: I will do whatever you ask me to do. The Holy Spirit Is Promised
text: Jaabuuri meena ate ni a juisi mi yuenni nyiŋla, m le nye.

ref: Jesus said to his disciples: If you love me, you will do as I command.
text: <<Ni dan a yaali mu, ni le nye dii ate mi a weeni ni la.

ref: Then I will ask the Father to send you the Holy Spirit who will help you and always be with you.
text: <<Mi le saalim m Kowa ate wa te ni Sagrɔ wa choa ate wa kasim a bo ale ni taam wuu.

ref: The Spirit will show you what is true. The people of this world cannot accept the Spirit, because they don't see or know him. But you know the Spirit, who is with you and will keep on living in you.
text: Wa ka wensie Chiik, waai ate tɛŋzuk de demma an tuesi wa la, dii nyiŋla ba an nya wa yaase ba seba wa, nama abe seba wa kama, diila wa bo ale ni kama, wa be le bo ni po.

ref: I won't leave you like orphans. I will come back to you.
text: <<M kan basi ni, nidek ni nyiini ase kpinsa la. M le ŋman jam ni jigi.

ref: In a little while the people of this world won't be able to see me, but you will see me. And because I live, you will live.
text: Dai dii danni ate tɛŋzuk de meena demma a kan ŋman nya mu la a moata kama, alege nama ale ŋman nya mu kama. Mi abe nin kasim a boro la nama mɛ ale kasim boro.

ref: Then you will know I am one with the Father. You will know you are one with me, and I am one with you.
text: Dai dila danni a dan paari, ni le seba ayen mi bo ale ka m Kowa ate nama a bo ale mi ale ge ate mi mɛ a bo ale nama.

ref: If you love me, you will do what I have said, and my Father will love you. I will also love you and show you what I am like.
text: Baai ale a wom mi wieŋa ale a va ŋa la a sak kama ayen ba a yaali mu. Mi mɛ ale pai m dek a sak ba abe mi a yaali ba. Ba le a yaali mu la nyiŋ, m Kowa mɛ ale yaali ba.>>

ref: The other Judas, not Judas Iscariot, then spoke up and asked, “Lord, what do you mean by saying that you will show us what you are like, but you will not show the people of this world?”
text: Judas wa choawa, daa Judas Iskariot waai ale ta Yeezu a ga bobri sak la, yaa weeni Yeezu ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, fi le nye ka sɛ a pai fidek a sak tama nyiini alege daa tɛŋka meena demma?>>

ref: Jesus replied: If anyone loves me, they will obey me. Then my Father will love them, and we will come to them and live in them.
text: Yeezu yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Baai ale a yaali mi la a va ka m sinsaŋŋa. Bala mɛ ate m Kowa a yaali ate mi ale wa a jam bo ba suiniimaŋa po.

ref: But anyone who doesn't love me, won't obey me. What they have heard me say doesn't really come from me, but from the Father who sent me.
text: Baai ale kan a yaali mi la a kan va m wieŋa. Mi ale a sak ni diila an nyini daa mi dek jigiya, alege ka m Kowa ale tom mu la jigi.

ref: I have told you these things while I am still with you.
text: <<Mi ale diem bo ale ni la, ale soa ate mi a weeni ni wieŋa de.

ref: But the Holy Spirit will come and help you, because the Father will send the Spirit to take my place. The Spirit will teach you everything and will remind you of what I said while I was with you.
text: Alege Sagrɔwa, Wen Chiika, waai ate Kowa ale tom mi yuenni nyiŋ la, wa le sak ni wie meena abe wa basi ate ni teeri dii meena ate m weeni ni la.

ref: I give you peace, the kind of peace only I can give. It isn't like the peace this world can give. So don't be worried or afraid.
text: Mi ale basi ate ni ta suiyɔgni. Suiyɔgni dii ate mi ayen m te ni la ka di tɔga ale tɛŋka meena demma suiyɔgni. Ni kan a yiili abe ni a chali yɔgsummoa.

ref: You have already heard me say I am going and I will also come back to you. If you really love me, you should be glad I am going back to the Father, because he is greater than I am.
text: Mi poom a liŋ weeni ni kama ayen m le cheŋ m Kowa jigi abe m ŋman pilim jam. Ase ni dan sum a yaali mu, ni sue ale peenti, ale m ale a cheŋ m Kowa jigi la diila m Kowa a zuak kama a gaam mi.

ref: I am telling you this before I leave, so when it does happen, you will have faith in me.
text: Mi a weeni ni wieŋa de kama alege ŋa an diem nye ya, ate ŋa dan jam a nye abe ni ta siaka ale mu.

ref: I cannot speak with you much longer, because the ruler of this world is coming. But he has no power over me.
text: Mi kan yaali ayen m biisi wa boari ale ni, dii nyiŋla Sitaana waai ale soa tɛŋzuk de meena demma la, a cheena kama. Wa ka pagrim mi zuwa.

ref: I obey my Father, so everyone in the world might know that I love him. It is time for us to go now.
text: Alege tɛŋka meena demma ale seba ayen mi a yaali m Kowa kama, dila mɛ abe ni soa ate mi a tom wa dii meena ate wa a weeni mu la. Ni basi ate ti yiti a cheŋ jigi yoŋ.

ref: Jesus said to his disciples: I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener.
text: <<Mi a nye se ka tiib la. Mi Kowa mɛ ale a nya tiimu zuk la.

ref: He cuts away every branch of mine that doesn't produce fruit. But he trims clean every branch that does produce fruit, so that it will produce even more fruit.
text: Wa nyiem a kasim a gebi naŋ sii ale kan a yɔni la a basi kama ale a gebi sii ale a yɔni la a magsi chaab ate si a yɔni yɔna yega.

ref: You are already clean because of what I have said to you.
text: Wen a poom liŋ sugri ni suiniimaŋa kama ale wie ŋaai ate mi a sak ni la.

ref: Stay joined to me, and I will stay joined to you. Just as a branch cannot produce fruit unless it stays joined to the vine, you cannot produce fruit unless you stay joined to me.
text: Ni be kasim a bo ale mi ate mi mɛ a bo ale ni. Naŋ a kan baga yɔni yɔna ka dega, ka naŋka a nin bo kinni nyiŋ ale ka baga a yɔni. Ni dan kan bo ale mi ni kan baga a nye wari ya.

ref: I am the vine, and you are the branches. If you stay joined to me, and I stay joined to you, then you will produce lots of fruit. But you cannot do anything without me.
text: Mi ale kinni alege nama a chim naŋsaŋa. Waai ale bo ale mi ate mi mɛ a bo ale wa la ale yɔni yɔna yega. Ni kan baga a nye wari ya ka mi nin bo ale ni.

ref: If you don't stay joined to me, you will be thrown away. You will be like dry branches that are gathered up and burned in a fire.
text: Waai ale kan bo ale mi la m Kowa ale gebi wa a basi ase tiib naŋsa la, naŋ sila a dan ko ba tigsi si kama a nyo bolim po a ju.

ref: Stay joined to me and let my teachings become part of you. Then you can pray for whatever you want, and your prayer will be answered.
text: Ni dan bo ale mi ate m wieŋa a bo ale ni, ni dan juisi jabuui ate ni a yaali la Wen ale te ni.

ref: When you become fruitful disciples of mine, my Father will be honored.
text: Ni dan a yɔni yɔna kula ale sak ayen ni ka mi ŋaaŋviirɔba ate m Kowa a nya zula.

ref: I have loved you, just as my Father has loved me. So remain faithful to my love for you.
text: Mi a yaali ni ase ka m Kowa ale a yaali mu diila. Ni kasim a ta yaalika ale mu.

ref: If you obey me, I will keep loving you, just as my Father keeps loving me, because I have obeyed him.
text: Ni dan ta m wieŋa, ni le bo m yaalika po ase m le ta m Kowa wieŋa abe m bo wa yaalika po.

ref: I have told you this to make you as completely happy as I am.
text: Wieŋa de meena mi a biisi ale ni kama ayen m suipeentika a bo ni po, ate ni suipeentika a zuak.

ref: Now I tell you to love each other, as I have loved you.
text: <<Sinsak paali ate mi a yaali ayen ni va di. Ni a yaali chaab ase mi a ale yaali ni diila.

ref: The greatest way to show love for friends is to die for them.
text: Nuru ka yaali kpieŋ a gaam ka de, ate waai a zaani wa doaba naŋkula po a kpi a te ba.

ref: And you are my friends, if you obey me.
text: Ni dan a va dii ate mi a sak ni la, ni ka mi doaba.

ref: Servants don't know what their master is doing, and so I don't speak to you as my servants. I speak to you as my friends, and I have told you everything my Father has told me.
text: Wie ŋaai meena ate m Kowa a weeni mu la, ŋala ale mi a pai weeni ale ni. Ka dila ale soa ate mi a weeni ayen ni ka m doaba la. Mi kan yaali ayen m ŋman weeni ayen ni ka mi yɔm, dii nyiŋla yɔma a zɛ wa nyɔnɔ ale ta diila.

ref: You did not choose me. I chose you and sent you out to produce fruit, the kind of fruit that will last. Then my Father will give you whatever you ask for in my name.
text: Daa nama ale lueri mi, alege ka mi ale lueri nama ayen ni a yɔni yɔna ate yɔnaŋa a boro ate dii meena ate ni a bek Kowa mi yuenni nyiŋ la, wa le te ni.

ref: So I command you to love each other. The World's Hatred
text: Dii ate mi a weeni ni la ale ni a yaali chaab nalimnyiini.

ref: If the people of this world hate you, just remember that they hated me first.
text: <<Ase tɛŋka meena demma a dan kisi ni, ni be teeri ayen ka mi ate ba jam a liŋ kisa.

ref: Remember how I told you that servants are not greater than their master. So if people mistreat me, they will mistreat you. If they do what I say, they will do what you say.
text: Ni teeri dii ate m weeni ni ayen tomteerɔ an baga a zuak a gaam wa nyɔnɔ la. Ba jam a daani mi ka nna yegayega. Dila dek dek ate ba a yaali ayen ba daani nama mɛ. Ba dan wom mi wanni kama, ba te le wom nama wieŋa mɛ.

ref: People will do to you exactly what they did to me. They will do it because you belong to me, and they don't know the one who sent me.
text: Ba le daani ni dii nyiŋla ba zɛ waai ale tom mi la. Ba le ŋman a daani ni, ni ale a va mi la nyiŋ.

ref: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. But now they have no excuse for their sin.
text: M jam kama ayen m weeni ba ate ba basi ba wabaataŋa suiku vaka, alege ba zɛri. Dila nyiŋ Wen a dan bo ba buusa ayen ba lo ya, ba an ŋman baga a weeni wari ale wa.

ref: Everyone who hates me also hates my Father.
text: Waai ale kisi mi la, a kisi m Kowa mɛ kama.

ref: I have done things no one else has ever done. If they had not seen me do these things, they would not be guilty. But they did see me do these things, and they still hate me and my Father too.
text: Mi tom ka tuimkperikaliik sii ate waai an baga a tom la, ba nimbie po. Dila nyiŋ Wen ale weeni ba ayen ba nye kaasiya. Badek a nya ŋaai meena ate mi a nye la kama ale ba nimbie alege ba diem kisi mi ale m Kowa.

ref: This is why the Scriptures are true when they say, “People hated me for no reason.”
text: Ba kisi mu nna la kama ayen dii ate ba ŋmarisi Wen Gbaŋka po la a chim wensie. Ba ŋmarisi ayen, <Ba kisi mu kama kinla nyiŋ.> (Yiila

ref: I will send you the Spirit who comes from the Father and shows what is true. The Spirit will help you and will tell you about me.
text: <<Mi poom a liŋ weeni ni kama ayen Sagrɔwa waai ale ka Wen Chiika la ale pai Wen wensie wieŋa a sak ni, wa abe le nyini ka m Kowa jigi. M le tom wa ate wa nyini m Kowa jigi a jam a biisi mi wie.

ref: Then you will also tell others about me, because you have been with me from the beginning.
text: Ate nama mɛ a baga a biisi mi wie dii nyiŋla ni bo ale mu kama a nyini piilimka.

ref: I am telling you these things, so that you will not turn away.
text: <<Mi a weeni nama wieŋa de kama, ate ni kan jɔk siaka ale mi.

ref: You will be chased out of the synagogues. And the time will come when people will kill you and think they are doing God a favor.
text: Juuma ale yiak ni ba tuka diinaŋa po a basi. Ku danni mɛ dek ale jam paari ate baai ale ba ko ni la a poli ayen ba a tom ka dii ate Wen a yaali la.

ref: They will do these things because they don't know either the Father or me.
text: Ba le nye ni nyaŋa de meena, dii nyiŋla ba zɛ mi yaase m Kowa.

ref: I am saying this to you now, so that when the time comes, you will remember what I have said. The Work of the Holy Spirit I was with you at the first, and so I didn't tell you these things.
text: Mi a weeni ni wieŋa de kama ate da ŋala, dan paari ate ba boro a nye ni dila abe ni teeri mi ale weeni ni diila. Mi an weeni ni wieŋa de piilimka po, diila m le jam bo ale ni la.

ref: But now I am going back to the Father who sent me, and none of you asks me where I am going.
text: <<Yɔgyɔgla de m ŋmani a cheŋ ka Waai ale tom mu la jigi, alege ni waai an bek mi m le a cheŋ juijui la.

ref: You are very sad from hearing all of this.
text: Mi ale weeni ni wieŋa de meena la a nye kama ate ni sue a kaasi nna yegayega.

ref: But I tell you I am going to do what is best for you. This is why I am going away. The Holy Spirit cannot come to help you until I leave. But after I am gone, I will send the Spirit to you.
text: Alege wensie ate mi a weeni ni, ku ale zunchoŋ ni jigi ase m nin cheŋ m Kowa jigi, dii nyiŋla m dan kan cheŋ ya, Sagrɔwa a kan jam ni jigi ya. Alege m dan cheŋ m le tom wa ate wa jam a maari ni.

ref: The Spirit will come and show the people of this world the truth about sin and God's justice and the judgment.
text: Ase wa dan jam wa le basi ate tɛŋka demma a seba wensieŋa a magsi chaab ale tuimbaata ale wayɔrisima ale buusa boka.

ref: The Spirit will show them that they are wrong about sin, because they didn't have faith in me.
text: A magsi chaab ale tuimbaata, dii nyiŋla ba ka siaka ale mi.

ref: They are wrong about God's justice, because I am going to the Father, and you won't see me again.
text: A magsi chaab ale wayɔrisima, dii nyiŋla mi a cheŋ ka Kowa jigi ate ni kan ŋman nya mu.

ref: And they are wrong about the judgment, because God has already judged the ruler of this world.
text: A magsi chaab ale buusa boka, dii nyiŋla waai ale soa tɛŋka a nya la ba bo wa buusa kama.

ref: I have much more to say to you, but right now it would be more than you could understand.
text: <<Mi ta ka wie nna yegayega ayen m weeni a sak ni a gum du, alege ŋa zuak kama a gaam ni womka.

ref: The Spirit shows what is true and will come and guide you into the full truth. The Spirit doesn't speak on his own. He will tell you only what he has heard from me, and he will let you know what is going to happen.
text: Wen Chiika kaai ale ka wensie nyɔnɔ la, ale jam a bo ni suiniimaŋa po, ka le dɛ ni niŋ a sak ni wensie suiku. Ka le ka sak ni diila a kan nyini daa ka dek jigi ya. Wie ŋaai ate mi ale m Kowa a weeni ka la, ŋala ale ka pai a sak ni. Ka le sak ni mɛ wie ŋaai ale diem cheena ayen ŋa nye la wie.

ref: The Spirit will bring glory to me by taking my message and telling it to you.
text: Ka le te mi zula yegayega, dii nyiŋla ka le wom mi wie ŋaai ate mi a weeni ka la abe ka pai a sak ni.

ref: Everything the Father has is mine. This is why I have said that the Spirit takes my message and tells it to you. Sorrow Will Turn into Joy
text: Jaabuuri meena ate m Kowa a ta la ka mi ale soa. Ka dila ale soa ate mi a weeni ni ayen Wen Chiika ale wom dii ate mi a weeni ka la abe ka pai a sak ni.

ref: Jesus told his disciples, “For a little while you won't see me, but after a while you will see me.”
text: <<Mi a kan bo ale ni a beni abe m ge cheŋ m Kowa jigi ya. Mi a dan cheŋ wa jigi ku kan beni ate ni ŋman nya mu.>>

ref: They said to each other, “What does Jesus mean by saying that for a little while we won't see him, but after a while we will see him? What does he mean by saying he is going to the Father?
text: Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma gela yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Wa a weeni ka tama ayen wa kan bo ale ti a beni abe wa ge a cheŋ wa kowa jigi ya. Wa ŋman a weeni ti kama ayen wa dan cheŋ ku kan beni ate ti ŋman nya wa. Nya kude meena ate wa biisi la, kiri ale boa?>>

ref: What is this ‘little while’ that he is talking about? We don't know what he means.”
text: Ba weeni ayen, <<Ku kan beni kiri ale boa? Tama zɛ wa le a weeni dii la kiriya?>>

ref: Jesus knew they had some questions, so he said: You are wondering what I meant when I said that for a little while you won't see me, but after a while you will see me.
text: Yeezu a jam seba kama ayen ba a yaali ayen ba bek wa kama. Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ku kan beni ate ni kan ŋman nya mu, ku be kan beni ate ni ŋman nya mu. Ka kude ate ni a bek chaaba?

ref: I tell you for certain that you will cry and be sad, but the world will be happy. You will be sad, but later you will be happy.
text: Wensie ate mi a weeni ni le kum abe ni a fɔbili alege ate tɛŋzuk de demma sue peenti, niniga ale paari ni alege niniŋŋa ale tulim chim suipeentik.

ref: When a woman is about to give birth, she is in great pain. But after it is all over, she forgets the pain and is happy, because she has brought a child into the world.
text: Nipok a dan boro a dom wa puuk, wa sui a nyiem kaasi kama. Wa dan biak nueri, wa a baŋ sui kaasuŋku kama, ale ta suipeentik wa biika nyiŋ.

ref: You are now very sad. But later I will see you, and you will be so happy that no one will be able to change the way you feel.

ref: And you gave him power over all people, so he would give eternal life to everyone you give him.
