text: Jigaŋa de meena, ba kasim jam a deŋsi ka ŋaaŋviirɔma kpa, a weeni ba ayen ba kasim ta siaka ale Yeezu. Ba jam maa sak ba ayen, <<Ku a fɛ kama ayen ti nya ninam yegayega abe ti ge jo Wen naamu po.>>

ref: Paul and Barnabas chose some leaders for each of the churches. Then they went without eating and prayed that the Lord would take good care of these leaders who had trusted in the Lord.
text: Pɔɔl ale Banabas ale Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la yaa maa chaab a bobi nɔi a puusi lueri kpaga a ta nyini Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab tɔgatɔga la po. Pɔɔl ale Banabas yaa pai ba nyo Naawen dii ate ba ta siaka ale wa nalimnyiini la nisima po.

ref: Paul and Barnabas went on through Pisidia to Pamphylia,
text: Ba yaa jam va Pisidiya tɛŋka po a taam cheŋ Pamfiliya tɛŋka.

ref: where they preached in the town of Perga. Then they went down to Attalia
text: Dula jigini ba jam sak wapaala maŋsaŋa Periga mɛ po ale ge a cheŋ Ataliya tɛŋka.

ref: and sailed to Antioch in Syria. It was there that they had been placed in God's care for the work they had now completed.
text: Ba yaa zaani dula a jueli ŋaaruŋ a pilim ŋman Antiok juijui ate Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la a liŋ pai ba a nyo Wen nisima po ayen wa maari ba ate ba baga tom wa tuim ŋaai ate ba yaa tom nueri nna la.

ref: After arriving in Antioch, they called the church together. They told the people what God had helped them do and how he had made it possible for the Gentiles to believe.
text: Ba ale jam paari Antiok la, ba yaa tigsi Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la meena a nyo jigi yeŋ a weeni sak Wen ale pai ba a tom dii meena la. Ba weeni a sak ba wa ale lak suik ate baai ale kan daa Juuba la a maa ta siaka la.

ref: Then they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
text: Pɔɔl ale Banabas a jam goa dula jigini kama ale ŋaaŋviirɔma meena ate ku beni nna yegayega.

ref: Some people came from Judea and started teaching the Lord's followers that they could not be saved, unless they were circumcised as Moses had taught.
text: Nuruba ale jam nyini Judia a jam Antiok tɛŋka a deri piilim a sak baai ale ta siaka ale Yeezu la sinsaga ayen, <<Nuru karo a baga nya varibasika see ka kula nyɔnɔwa a nin gebi wa yoanni ase Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a sak diila.>>

ref: This caused trouble, and Paul and Barnabas argued with them about this teaching. So it was decided to send Paul and Barnabas and a few others to Jerusalem to discuss this problem with the apostles and the church leaders. The Church Leaders Meet in Jerusalem
text: Dila nyiŋla Pɔɔl ale Banabas yaa jam ta nanpaga nna yegayega ale ba. Baai ale ta siaka la yaa lueri Pɔɔl ale Banabas ale baai ale ta siaka la gela a bo Antiok la ayen ba cheŋ Jerusalem a ga nya tuimtomdɔma ale kpaŋŋa wanni de zuk.

ref: When the men arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, including the apostles and the leaders. They told them everything God had helped them do.
text: Ba ale jam paari Jerusalem la, Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la ale ba kpaŋŋa ale tuimtomdɔma a jam maa chaab a nye ba tia kama ate ba weeni a sak ba meena Wen ale pai ba a tom tuima diila.

ref: But some Pharisees had become followers of the Lord. They stood up and said, “Gentiles who have faith in the Lord must be circumcised and told to obey the Law of Moses.”
text: Baai ale ta siaka la, baai ale ka Farisiima po nuruba la, yaa yiti zaani ŋmai a weeni ayen, <<Ku a fɛ kama ayen baai ale kan daa Juuba la a gebi ba yoaŋa. Ku a fɛ kama mɛ ayen, ba kaam ba ayen ba a zuli Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila.>>

ref: The apostles and church leaders met to discuss this problem about Gentiles.
text: Tuimtomdɔma ale nisɔmma yaa tu chaab ayen ba biisi wanni de.

ref: They had talked it over for a long time, when Peter got up and said: My friends, you know that God decided long ago to let me be the one from your group to preach the good news to the Gentiles. God did this so they would hear and obey him.
text: Ba ale nak nanpaga di nyiŋ ate ku beni la, Piita yaa zaani a biisi ayen, <<M suata, nama dek seba ayen a ta nyini dipo, Wen ale jam lueri mi a ta nyini nama po a nyini ayen m ga sak baai ale kan daa Juuba la, wapaala maŋsaŋa ate ba wom abe ba ta siaka ale ŋa.

ref: He knows what is in everyone's heart. And he showed he had chosen the Gentiles, when he gave them the Holy Spirit, just as he had given his Spirit to us.
text: Wen dii abe ale seba nurubiik meena popola ale ka diila, a te Wen Chiika baai ale kan daa Juuba la kama ase wa ale te tama mɛ diila ayen ku sak ayen wa ta yaalika ale ba kama ase wa ale ta yaalika ale tama mɛ diila.

ref: Now why are you trying to make God angry by placing a heavy burden on these followers? This burden was too heavy for us or our ancestors.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de, ka boa ale soa ate nama a yaali ayen ni pai jib kpiemu de buui ate ti kokpieŋsaŋa a yaase tama dek an baga ji bu la ayen ŋaaŋviirɔma ji? Ni dan a nye nna, ni a nye ka Wen a nya.

ref: After they had finished speaking, James said: My friends, listen to me!
text: Ba ale ga biisi nueri la, Jeemsi yaa tulisi ayen, <<M suata, ni meena a wom mi.

ref: Simon Peter has told how God first came to the Gentiles and made some of them his own people.
text: Ni wom Simon Piita ale tɔk Wen ale liŋ nye dii a sak baai ale kan daa Juuba la a yaa piilim lueri ba wa yuenni nyiŋ dii la.

ref: “I, the Lord, will return and rebuild David's fallen house. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again.
text: <Nya kude ŋaaŋnyiŋ, m le pilim jam a nye ate Deevid yenni ale lo la a ŋman zaani. M le ŋman pilim sɛ di juijui ale lo la, abe m nye ate di ŋman pagra.

ref: Then other nations will turn to me and be my chosen ones. I, the Lord, say this.
text: Ate nurubiik meena ale gisi Naawen. Baai meena ale kan daa Juuba ate mi wi ba ayen m nuruba la. (Amos

ref: And so, my friends, I don't think we should place burdens on the Gentiles who are turning to God.
text: Jeemsi yaa ŋman biisi a cheŋ a weeni ayen, <<Dila nyiŋ mi a poli kama ayen ti kan daani baai ale kan daa Juuba a tagri va Wen la.

ref: We should simply write and tell them not to eat anything that has been offered to idols. They should be told not to eat the meat of any animal that has been strangled or that still has blood in it. They must also not commit any terrible sexual sins.
text: Ku magsi ka ti ŋmarisi gbaŋ a te ba ayen, ba kan dɛ bɔgta ŋandiinta dii nyiŋla, ŋandiin tila an welema. Ti weeni ba mɛ ayen ba kan bobi nipok baai ale kan daa ba pooba la a goa, abe ba kan a ŋɔbi jabuui ate ba an tɔgri la lammoa abe ba kan a dɛ ziimoa.

ref: We must remember that the Law of Moses has been preached in city after city for many years, and every Sabbath it is read in our synagogues. A Letter to Gentiles Who Had Faith in the Lord
text: Baai ale kan daa Juuba la, le deri siak nyaŋa de kama, boan nyiŋŋa ba seba kama ayen Juuma baai ale bo juijui meena ale ba la, ba sak Moosis Sinsaŋŋa de kama ate ku beni yegayega. Ba be wom ale karim ŋa kama ba tuka diinaŋa po ba Vuusum Daaŋa meena po.>>

ref: They wrote a letter that said: We apostles and leaders send friendly greetings to all of you Gentiles who are followers of the Lord in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
text: Ba ale jam ŋmarisi gbaŋka a weeni diila ale nna ayen, <<Tama ni suataŋa tuimtomdɔma ale kpaŋŋa a maa chaab a puusi ti suataŋa baai ale potim kan daa Juuba a nyini biam po ate ba bo Antiok ale Siriya ale Silisiya tɛŋsaŋa la.

ref: So we met together and decided to choose some men and to send them to you along with our good friends Barnabas and Paul.
text: Dila nyiŋ ate tama meena a nye tuka a yaa poli ate ti yaa siak a lueri nuruba ayen ba va Pɔɔl ale Banabas ti sua tii ate ti mariŋ la a jam ni jigi.

ref: These men have risked their lives for our Lord Jesus Christ.
text: Pɔɔl ale Banabas ka nuru baai ale pai ba nyuvoa a da ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋla.

ref: We are also sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things that we are writing.
text: Dila nyiŋ ate ti yaa tom Judas ale Silas ni jigi. Ba ale poom weeni a sak ni dii meena wuu ate ti ŋmarisi gbaŋka de po la.

ref: But you should not eat anything offered to idols. You should not eat any meat that still has the blood in it or any meat of any animal that has been strangled. You must also not commit any terrible sexual sins. If you follow these instructions, you will do well. We send our best wishes.
text: Wieŋa de ale, Ni kan a dɛ bɔgta ŋandiinta, ni kan a dɛ ziimoa, ni kan a ŋɔbi jabuui ate ba an tɔgri la lammoa, ni kan a bobi nipok baai ale kan daa ni pooba la a goa. Ku a le nala kama ase ni nin kaa nye wieŋa de. <<Ni boro nalimnyiini.>>

ref: The four men left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. Then they called the church members together and gave them the letter.
text: Ba yaa basi Jerusalem ale cheŋ Antiok, a tigsi baai ale ta siaka la a te ba gbaŋka.

ref: When the letter was read, everyone was pleased and greatly encouraged.
text: Ba ale ga karim ka la, gbaŋka wieŋa yaa ta suipeentik a jam ba jigi.

ref: Judas and Silas were prophets, and they spoke a long time, encouraging and helping the Lord's followers.
text: Judas ale Silas dek ale jam ka biisiteerɔba la, ba yaa deŋsi ba kpa ale wie yega ayen ba nya pagrim.

ref: The men from Jerusalem stayed on in Antioch for a while. And when they left to return to the ones who had sent them, the followers wished them well.
text: Ba ale ga daliŋ maga dega la, Antiok demma yaa te Judas ale Silas suik ale suiyɔgni ate ba pilim cheŋ baai ale tom ba la jigi.

ref: But Paul and Barnabas stayed on in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached about the Lord. Paul and Barnabas Go Their Separate Ways
text: Alege Pɔɔl ale Banabas a jam wari ka Antiok, a sak ale a mooli ale nuruba ba chaab mɛ, Naawen wanni.

ref: Sometime later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let's go back and visit the Lord's followers in the cities where we preached his message. Then we will know how they are doing.”
text: Ku ale ga beni maga dega la, Pɔɔl yaa weeni Banabas ayen, <<Basi ate ti pilim ŋmani cheŋ jigi ŋaai meena ate ti sak Naawen wanni la a ga nya ase Kirisita bisaŋa a nye ka sɛ.>>

ref: Barnabas wanted to take along John, whose other name was Mark.
text: Banabas a jam a yaali kama ayen Jɔɔn Maak a maa va ba a cheŋ.

ref: Paul and Barnabas argued, then each of them went his own way. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus,
text: Nanpaga yaa deri jam ba suŋsuŋ ate ba poori chaab. Banabas yaa yik Maak ate ba jueli ŋaaruŋ a cheŋ Saipurus tɛŋka

ref: but Paul took Silas and left after the followers had placed them in God's care.
text: alege Pɔɔl a jam lueri ka Silas ate ba cheŋ. Siarɔma ale bo Antiok la yaa pai Pɔɔl a nyo Naawen ŋmanteka po,

ref: Paul and Silas went back to Derbe and Lystra, where there was a follower named Timothy. His mother was also a follower. She was Jewish, and his father was Greek.
text: Pɔɔl yaa nyini Siriya ale Silisiya tɛŋsaŋa a cheŋ Daabe ale Lisitira. Kirisita bisaŋa wanyi ale jam bo Lisitira. Wa yuei jam ale Timoti. Wa mawa jam ka Juu a ta siaka ale ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita. Alege Timoti kowa jam ka Girik denɔ.

ref: The Lord's followers in Lystra and Iconium said good things about Timothy,
text: Kirisita bisaŋa meena ale jam bo Lisitira ale Ikoonium la, a kasim jam a pak Timoti kama.

ref: and Paul wanted him to go with them. But Paul first had him circumcised, because all the Jewish people around there knew that Timothy's father was Greek.
text: Pɔɔl yaa jam a yaali ayen wa maa va a cheŋ. Pɔɔl yaa gebi wa yoanni dii nyiŋla, Juuma meena ale jam bo dula jigini meena la, a jam seba ayen Timoti kowa ka Girik denɔ.

ref: As Paul and the others went from city to city, they told the followers what the apostles and leaders in Jerusalem had decided, and they urged them to follow these instructions.
text: Ba ale jam va tɛŋsaŋa po a taam la, ba jam weeni sinsaŋŋa meena ate tuimtomdɔma ale niŋdeerɔma a te ba Jerusalem tɛŋka la a sak baai ale ta siaka la kama. Ba weeni ba mɛ ayen ba chiib a va sinsaŋŋa.

ref: The churches became stronger in their faith, and each day more people put their faith in the Lord. Paul's Vision in Troas
text: Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la siaka a yaa ŋmasi pagra a gum du ate ba jam a piisi daa meena a gum du.

ref: Paul and his friends went through Phrygia and Galatia, but the Holy Spirit would not let them preach in Asia.
text: Ba yaa jam cheŋ a va Firijiya ale Galatia tɛŋsaŋa dii nyiŋla, Wen Chiika an jam te ba suik ate ba sak wapaala maŋsaŋa Asia tɛŋka po.

ref: After they arrived in Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not let them.
text: Ba ale jam paari Misiya tɛŋ banni la, ba jam poli kama ayen ba cheŋ Bitiniya tɛŋka alege Yeezu jam tom ka Naawen Chiika ayen wa weeni ba ayen ba kan cheŋ.

ref: So they went on through Mysia until they came to Troas.
text: Ba yaa va Misiya tɛŋka a taam siŋ Torowas tɛŋka.

ref: During the night, Paul had a vision of someone from Macedonia who was standing there and begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
text: Ku yaa nye Pɔɔl jigi yokku ase wa goa daasim kama la ate wa nya Masidoniya denɔ a za wa tɛŋ a saalim wa ayen, <<Taam jam Masidoniya a maari ti.>>

ref: After Paul had seen the vision, we began looking for a way to go to Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news there. Lydia Becomes a Follower of the Lord
text: Ase wa le nya gɔdaasini la, ti yaa yiti a gomsi ayen ti cheŋ Masidoniya, a poli ayen Wen weeni ti ayen ti cheŋ ka Masidoniya a ga mooli wapaala maŋsaŋa a te ba.

ref: We sailed straight from Troas to Samothrace, and the next day we arrived in Neapolis.
text: Ti yaa jueli ŋaaruŋ a zaani Torowas a gaam taam cheŋ Samotiras. Vari ale veenti la, ti yaa ŋman cheŋ Niyapolis.

ref: From there we went to Philippi, which is a Roman colony in the first district of Macedonia. We spent several days in Philippi.
text: Ti yaa zaani dula a basi ŋaaruŋku ale ge cheŋ Filipai, ka Masidoniya tɛŋsaŋa po tɛŋ kpieŋ ale la. Aroom demma ale ba kpaga ale jam bo tɛŋka de po a nya ba zuk. Ti jam bo tɛŋ kala ate ku beni ka maga.

ref: Then on the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a place by the river, where we thought there would be a Jewish meeting place for prayer. We sat down and talked with the women who came.
text: Vuusum Danni ti yaa nyini tɛŋka po nyini a cheŋ benaŋka geŋsa, juijui ate ti a poli ayen ti le nya jigi a puusi la. Ti yaa kali tɛŋ a biisi ale nipok baai ale jam bo dula la.

ref: One of them was Lydia, who was from the city of Thyatira and sold expensive purple cloth. She was a worshiper of the Lord God, and he made her willing to accept what Paul was saying.
text: Ti ale jam boro a biisi la, nipok ate ba a wi wa ayen Liidiya ale jam a wom dii ate ti a biisi la. Wa jam nyini ka Tayatira. Wa jam ta ka garuk ŋmiŋmirita a gerim. Wa jam a puusi Wen nna yegayega. Dila nyiŋla, Naawen yaa lagri wa popolaŋa ate wa wom Pɔɔl ale jam a weeni diila.

ref: Then after she and her family were baptized, she kept on begging us, “If you think I really do have faith in the Lord, come stay in my home.” Finally, we accepted her invitation. Paul and Silas Are Put in Jail
text: Wa ale wa dɔkdemma ale ga tuesi soka a nueri la, wa yaa wi tama a weeni ayen, <<Nama a dan sum siak kama ayen mi ta siaka ale Naawen, ni be jam mi yenni a goa.>> Wa le jam weeni dila la, ti yaa va wa a cheŋ.

ref: One day on our way to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl. She had a spirit in her that gave her the power to tell the future. By doing this she made a lot of money for her owners.
text: Ase ti le jam a cheŋ juijui ate ti a puusi la, ti yaa nya nipokbili tomteerɔ yaa jam tu ti, wa jam ka sampoporik, wa jam a nya ka ligra nna yegayega a te wa nyama.

ref: The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she kept yelling, “These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how to be saved.”
text: Wa jam va Pɔɔl ale tama a kaari a weeni ayen, <<Nuruma de ka Wen Dii Ale Bo Wenŋmazuk La tomteerɔba. Ba a mooli a sak ni ka ni ale ni nye dii ate ni nya varibasika la.>>

ref: This went on for several days. Finally, Paul got so upset that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I order you to leave this girl alone!” At once the evil spirit left her.
text: Wa jam nye dila a paari ka daa dii choa ate ku yaa puuri Pɔɔl sui nna yegayega ate dai dila danni Pɔɔl yaa virim a weeni chichirik bioku ayen, <<Yeezu Kirisita yuenni nyiŋ ate mi a weeni fu nyini wa po a nyini.>> Chichirik bioku yaa deri nyini dula kuuni.

ref: When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court.
text: Nipokbilika nyama ale ga miŋ ayen ba kan ŋman a nya ligra la, ba yaa yik Pɔɔl ale Silas a vuuri ta cheŋ kpaŋŋa jigi yaba peelimmu po,

ref: The crowd joined in the attack on Paul and Silas. Then the officials tore the clothes off the two men and ordered them to be beaten with a whip.
text: Nuru boanni yaa gum ba po a tu chaab ale Pɔɔl ale Silas. Ate kpaŋŋa a yaa yik Pɔɔl ale Silas gattaŋa a dari cheeri ale weeni ate ba nak ba ale doa.

ref: After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully.
text: Ba ale nak ba a te ba tueta la, ba yaa ta ba a ga lik ale weeni likka dɔkku limisidɔwa ayen wa ŋmasi lik ba nalimnyiini.

ref: The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
text: Limisidɔwa ale ga wom nna la, wa yaa ta ba taam niŋniŋ dɔkku a lik, a pai diok kpioŋ ate ba keri vie, ku dobra nna zaŋzaŋ a pai ba naŋsaŋa a su du.

ref: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing praises to God, while the other prisoners listened.
text: Alege goota suŋsuŋ ale ga paari la, Pɔɔl ale Silas yaa jam boro a puusi ale a yi yiila a pak Wen, ate ligrɔma a jam wom ba.

ref: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
text: Tɛŋka yaa deri choa, ate likka dɔkku nyubini mɛ a choa, ku an beni ya tuataŋa meena yaa deri lak, ate choarimaŋa a gebi.

ref: When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself.
text: Likka yenni limisidɔwa yaa yiti nya ale likka yenni noaŋa a lagri ya. Wa yaa yeeri gebik woŋ ayen wa ko wadek dii nyiŋla, wa jam a poli kama ayen nuruma a nyini chali bɛ kama.

ref: But Paul shouted, “Don't harm yourself! No one has escaped.”
text: Pɔɔl yaa nya a kaari ate ku jueli ayen, <<Kan te fidek tuemoa, ti meena bo ka dela.>>

ref: The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas.
text: Limisidɔwa yaa wi ayen ba ta bolim a jam ale chali jo yenni po ate yɔgsum yik wa ate wa nyiŋka yaa a gɔk nna pampam a lo Pɔɔl ale Silas niŋ

ref: After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
text: a ta Pɔɔl ale Silas a nyini peelim weeni ba ayen, <<M koba, ku a fɛ ayen m nye ka sɛ ate m nya varibasika?>>

ref: They replied, “Have faith in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved! This is also true for everyone who lives in your home.”
text: Ba yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ta siaka ale Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, ate fi le nya varibasika, fi ale fi dɔkdemma meena.>>

ref: Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord.
text: Ba yaa sak wa ale baai meena ale bo wa yenni po la Naawen wanni.

ref: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
text: Dila powa dekdega yok kula ate nuruwa a yaa yik ba a sugri ba niraŋa ate ba deri te wa ale wa dɔkdemma soka.

ref: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
text: Wa yaa ta ba jo wa dɔkku a nye ŋandiinta a te ba. Wa dɔkdemma meena sue a yaa jam peenti nna yegayega dii nyiŋla, ba ta siaka ale Wen kama.

ref: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
text: Vari ale ga veenti la, Aroom tɛŋka buusa boorɔma a yaa tom limisidɔba ale tuntomiŋ ka de ayen, <<Ni basi ate nuru bala cheŋ.>>

ref: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
text: Limisidɔwa yaa weeni Pɔɔl ayen, <<Aroom tɛŋka buusa boorɔma a tom weeni kama ayen m lak fi ale Silas a basi. Dila nyiŋ yɔgyɔgla de, ni nyini cheŋ ale suiyɔgni.>>

ref: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
text: Alege Pɔɔl yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Ba nak tama kama ate waai meena nya ale an bek ti wari ya, tama mɛ abe ka Aroom tɛŋbisa, ate ba yik ti a lik. Yɔgyɔgla de ba a yaali ayen ba suk a yiak ti kama. Aaya, ni basi ate badek a jam lak ti basi.>>

ref: When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid.
text: Limisidɔwa ale ga weeni buusa boorɔwa Pɔɔl ale weeni dii ayen ba ka Aroom tɛŋbisa la, ba yaa jam yɔgsa.

ref: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
text: Dila ba yaa ga weeni ba ayen ba kaasi ale ge lak ba ate ba nyini a saalim ba ayen ba basi tɛŋka.

ref: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
text: Pɔɔl ale Silas a yaa basi likka dɔkku ale ge cheŋ Liidiya yenni. Dula jigini, ba yaa tu chaab ale Kirisita bisinsila a biisi wie a deŋsi ba kpa ale ge yaa basi ba ale cheŋ.

ref: After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city.
text: Pɔɔl ale Silas yaa ŋman va Amfipolise ale Apoloniya tɛŋsaŋa po a taam cheŋ Tesalonika tɛŋka. Juuma tuka yeri dinyi ale jam bo dula.

ref: So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures
text: Pɔɔl yaa ga jo ase wa nyiem ale a nye diila. Wa jam bo dula ka Vuusum Daa ŋata a sak ba a nyini Wen Gbaŋka po,

ref: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
text: tɔgi Gbaŋka wieŋa kie a sak ba ayen ku sak ba ayen ku jam a fɛ kama ayen Kirisitawa ale nam abe wa ŋman yiti kum po, <<Yeezuwa de ate mi a mooli a te ni la ale Kirisitawa.>>

text: Baai ale jam ka tinansa nyam la yaa ta ba gbaŋsaŋa a jam jigi yeŋ a ju si waai meena niŋ, ba le jam ŋmɛ ligraŋa a gum chaab la jam ka ligbie tusa pisinu (

ref: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
text: Dila Wen wanni a kasim jam a tagli tɛŋka meena ale pagrim.

ref: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
text: Wieŋa de meena ale ga nye la ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate Pɔɔl yaa poli ayen wa le va ka Masidoniya ale Akaaya ŋaaŋnyiŋ a taam cheŋ Jerusalem. Wa yaa weeni wadek ayen, <<M dan cheŋ dula, ku a fɛ kama ayen m basi dula abe m cheŋ Aroom tɛŋka.>>

ref: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
text: Dila nyiŋ wa yaa tom baai ale a maari wa la po baye, Timoti ale Erasitus ayen ba cheŋ Masidoniya ale ge ate wadek a diem wari Asia tɛŋka ate ku beni maga.

ref: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
text: Ku jam ka dila powa dek ate daani kpieŋ a jan jam Efisos tɛŋka ti Wenni Suiku wieŋa nyiŋ.

ref: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
text: Nuru ale jam boro wa yuei ale Dimetirus, wa jam ka choabiik, wa jam mɛ ka jaab ate wa nye ase nipok bɔglukku Atimis la. Baai ale jam a tom tuini de la a jam ka ligra.

ref: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
text: Wa yaa jam wi nuruma de chaab ale baai ale a tom ale ba la ate ba jam jigi yeŋ ate ba nye tuka. Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<M doaba, nama dek seba ayen ti jigsika meena a nyini ka tuini de po.

ref: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
text: Nama dek abe nya kama ale wom nuruwa de Pɔɔl ale a nye diila. Wa a weeni kama ayen bɔgluk tii ate nuruba pai ba nisima nye la, a ka pagrim fiik fiik mɛ la. Wa biisi dila a paasi nuruba yegayega kama. Efisos ale Asia tɛŋka meena po ba siak wa ale a biisi diila kama.

ref: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
text: Mi abe a chali ka yɔgsum ayen ti tuimaŋa de ale nya ka yuei kaasuŋ. Daa dila nyiini, mi a chali yɔgsum mɛ ayen bɔgluk kpioŋku Atimis yenni kan ta kiri ya. Bɔglukku dek mɛ le jɔk yuei, ku kan ŋman nya zula. Waai meena Asia tɛŋka po ale tɛŋka meena ale doa a ga saari la abe a te zula bɔglukku de kama.>>

ref: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
text: Nuru boanni ale ga wom wieŋa de la, ku yaa puuri ba sue ate ba yaa deri a kaari a weeni ate ku a jueli wein a tulisi chaab ayen, <<Efisos bɔglukku Atimis ka bɔgluk kpioŋ.>>

ref: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
text: Nuem ka de yaa jam deri basi ate Efisos tɛŋka po meena a nye nna ŋaglam. Nuru boanni de yaa maa chaab a yik Masidoniya demma bayewa ate ba a wi ba ayen Gayus ale Arisitaakus la. Ba jam va ka Pɔɔl a cheŋ ate ba yaa yik ba nɔi bayewa a ta ba chali cheŋ juijui ate tɛŋka nuruma a nyiem tigsi chaab a nye tuka la.

ref: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
text: Pɔɔl dek a jam a yaali kama ayen wa zaani nuru boanni niŋ a biisi alege Kirisita bisaŋa an jam siak ate wa nye dila.

ref: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
text: Tɛŋka meena kpaŋŋa gela baai ale jam ka Pɔɔl doaba la, ba mɛ a jam maa te Pɔɔl tuntomiŋ a saalim wa ayen wa kan pai naŋ a tabi tuka jigini.

ref: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
text: Ba gela a weeni wayeŋ, ba gela mɛ a na a weeni wa di choa, dii nyiŋla, ba yegayega jam poom zɛ ba ale jam ayen ba nye tuka ale dii nyiŋla, ba jam butim kama.

ref: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
text: Juuma yaa weeni Alezanda ate wa taam niŋ ate nuru boanni ba gela yaa kaari ate ku jueli a weeni a sak wa, wa le wa weeni diila. Alezanda yaa zak nisima ayen ba goori ate wa biisi a tuesi Juuma basi.

ref: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
text: Alege ba ale ga miŋ ayen wa ka Juu la, ba meena yaa kasim a nuem a na ale nɔiyeŋ ate ku a jueli a ayen, <<Efisos bɔglukku, Atimis ka bɔgluk kpioŋ.>> Ba kasim jam a weeni ka nna ate ku ga beni nna yegayega.

ref: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
text: Kpaŋŋa dinyi waai ale ta pagrim a nya nuru boari zuk la yaa weeni ate nuru boanni a goori. Wa weeni ba ayen, <<M mabisa, Efisos demma waai meena seba kama ayen ka Efisos tɛŋka ale a nya bɔgluk kpioŋku Atimis yenni zuk. Ka maara nya ka tintain weleŋ kaai ale nyini wenŋmazuk a jam lo la zuk.

ref: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
text: Ni ale ta nuruma de a jam dela nna, ba be an zu jaab jaaboa Atimis yenni po, yaase ba lɛ ku.

ref: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
text: Alege ku dan ka wari dii ate ni ŋman ta bega ŋa chaab, ku a fɛ kama ayen ti biisi nya kude ti tuka dai a nueri.

ref: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
text: Mi a weeni kude kama dii nyiŋla, nuruba gela ale nya daanika jinla ayen tama ta ka wɔkwɔk cheena, te kan bag biisi ate ba miŋi dii nyiŋla ti potim ka wari a zaani di zuwa.>>

ref: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
text: Tɛŋka kpagni ale biisi wieŋa de la ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa yaa weeni nuruma ayen ba kuli yeri.

ref: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
text: Wɔkwɔkka de ale ga nueri la, Pɔɔl yaa wi Kirisita bisaŋa jigi yeŋ a biisi deŋsi ba kpa ale ge a banti ba ale a cheŋ Masidoniya.

ref: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
text: Wa ale nyiem gilim Masidoniya tɛŋka meena a biisi deŋsi ba kpa la, wa yaa cheŋ Girik tɛŋka.

ref: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
text: Dula jigini, wa jam goa ka chiisa sita. Wa ale jam boro a gomsi ayen wa jueli ŋaaruŋ a cheŋ Siriya tɛŋka la, wa yaa miŋ ayen Juuma a jam a poli ka wa sitika. Wa yaa tagri wa popolaŋa a pilim ŋmani va Masidoniya a taam cheŋ Siriya.

ref: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
text: Bade a jam dɛka niŋ cheŋ ga bo Torowas a limisi tama.

ref: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
text: Alege tama a basi Filipai tɛŋka a lo benni a jueli ba le jam de tigi dii ate ba kan nyo dabinta di ŋandiintaŋa po la ŋaaŋnyiŋ. Daa ŋanu dai ti yaa paari ba Torowas tɛŋka po, ti jam bo dula ka daa ŋayopɔi.

ref: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
text: Bakoanni piilimka dai, ti meena yaa tu chaab ti de ŋandiinta ate Pɔɔl yaa biisi te tigsuŋku. Dii nyiŋla wa jam a poli kama ayen dai dii ale paasaŋ la wa basi dula jigini. Wa jam kasim a biisi kama ate ku paari yok suŋsuŋ.

ref: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
text: Zeuŋta yegayega ate ba jam toati zaani ŋmazuk kiari po ate tama jam tigsi kala.

ref: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
text: Nidoabili wanyi ale jam maa kala dɔkku tuokparuku zuk diipo ate Pɔɔl jam boro a biisi la. Nuruwa de yuei ale Yutikus. Goom yaa jam yik wa ate wa goa a baŋ wadek a yaa nyini kiari dii ale saari butawa la zuk a jam lo tɛŋ. Ba ale jam zak wa la, ba ga a nya ale wa kpi kama.

ref: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
text: Pɔɔl yaa siŋ tɛŋ a kpi duna tɛŋ gbaari wa ale ge weeni ayen, <<Ni kan basi ate ku daani ni, wa vua kama.>>

ref: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
text: Ba yaa ta nidoabinni a kuli yeri ale suipeentik. Wa an jam kpi ya.

ref: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
text: Ti yaa cheŋ ga jo ŋaaruŋku po a cheŋ Asos tɛŋka. Pɔɔl jam nye wa popola kama wa va suik a cheŋ Asos ate ti yaa jam paari wa dula jigini ate ti cheŋ.

ref: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
text: Wa yaa ale jam paari tama Asos tɛŋka la, ti yaa pai wa a nyo ŋaaruŋku po a cheŋ Mitiliini.

ref: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
text: Ti yaa jueli ŋaaruŋku a cheŋ dila veenti vari a va Kiyos tɛŋka a taam paari Samos tɛŋka. Vari ale ga veenti la, ti yaa paari Militus.

ref: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
text: Ti jam gaam Efisos kama dii nyiŋla wa kan jam a yaali ayen wa beni Asia tɛŋka. Dii nyiŋ ate wa jam a kpabi la, wa jam a yaali kama ayen wa paari Jerusalem ate wa dan baga abe wa paari Daa Pisinu Tigini.

ref: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
text: Pɔɔl yaa zaani Militus a tom tuntomiŋ a te Efisos a weeni Efisos Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la kpaŋŋa ayen ba tu wa Militus.

ref: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
text: Ba ale jam tu wa la, wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nama dek seba mi boka ale ka diila kama a zaani da dii danni ate mi jam Asia tɛŋka meena po dela la.

ref: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
text: Nama dek abe seba mɛ ayen diipo ate m jam nyini peelim ale maa jo ni yeeŋa po a sak ni la, mi an zɛri ni sakka wa dii ale di te ni maarika la.

ref: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ka Wen Chiika ale weeni mu ayen m cheŋ Jerusalem ate m siak alege m zɛ dii ale di nye mu dula la.

ref: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
text: Alege m seba kama ayen Wen Chiika ale kaam mu ayen m seba ale jigi meena ate mi a cheŋ la, ba le yik mu a lik, daanika mɛ le jam m jigi.

ref: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
text: Alege mi dek nyuvunni, mi kan nya di ase di ka jaab mi jigi la. Mi a yaali kama ayen m tom tuin dii ate Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu a te mu la a nueri. Tuini de ale m weeni a sak nuruba wapaala wamaŋsaŋa a magsi chaab ale wamaŋ sii ate wa nye a te nuruba ŋmanteka nyiŋla.

ref: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
text: <<M nyiem nama meena po kama a sak Wen naamu wie. Yɔgyɔgla de, m be seba kama ayen ni wanyi la kan ŋman nya mu.

ref: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
text: Dila nyiŋla, mi a weeni ni kama ayen ni wanyi abe dan bɛ kula daa mi niŋ ale la.

ref: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
text: Dii nyiŋla, mi an tali wari a magsi chaab ale Wen ale a poli ayen wa nye diila.

ref: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
text: Dila nyiŋla, ni be ŋmasi a nya nidek ale nuru baai ate Wen Chiika a pai te ni la zuk nalimnyiini. Wen pai ka wadek biika ziimu a da Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la. Ni be a nya ba zuk ase naapeerik ale a nya wa piisa zuk diila.

ref: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
text: M seba a chak kama ayen mi dan basi ni ale cheŋ, nuruba ale jam jo ni suŋsuŋ. Ba a nye ase ka piina ale jo piisa suŋsuŋ a kaasi ŋa diila.

ref: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
text: Dila nyiŋla, ni be kpesi nidek abe ni a teeri diipo yok ale kantueŋ ate m kasim a kum ale a kaam ni wanyi wanyi ate ku ga paari bena ŋata la.

ref: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
text: <<Yɔgyɔgla de, m pai ni a nyo Wen nisima po ale wa ŋmanteka wanni, dii ale di basi ate ni zaani paari abe wa te ni nitalimu a nyini baai meena ale nye cheri la po.

ref: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
text: Mi an jam vari ni waai ligra yaase wa gatta.

ref: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
text: Nama dek abe seba ayen mi pai ka m dek nisimaŋa dɛ a tom tuima a nya jaab meena ate mi ale m vaanchaama a jam a yaali la.

ref: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
text: Wari meena po, mi sak ni kama ayen, ku a fɛ kama ayen ti a maari niwoba abe ni a teeri, Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu wieŋa, wa weeni ayen, <Niauŋ yega a bo teka po a gaam tuesika kama.> >>

ref: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
text: Pɔɔl ale ga biisi nueri la, wa yaa kpi duna tɛŋ a puusi ale ba meena.

ref: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
text: Ba meena yaa jam a kum ale gbaari wa.

ref: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
text: Dii ale potim jam kaasi ba sue la ale Pɔɔl ale weeni ba dii ayen ba kan ŋman nya wa diipo diipo la. Ba yaa bani wa a ta cheŋ ŋaaruŋku jigini ayen wa jueli cheŋ.

ref: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
text: Ti ale ga banti ba nueri la, ti yaa jueli ŋaaruŋku a cheŋ yɔrr a jam paari Kosi tɛŋka. Vari ale veenti la, ti yaa paari Aroodisi tɛŋka a zaani dula a taam paari Pataara tɛŋka.

ref: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
text: Dula jigini, ti yaa nya ŋaaruŋ ale ku a cheŋ Fonisia tɛŋka. Ti yaa jueli ŋaaruŋ kula a maa va cheŋ.

ref: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
text: Ŋaaruŋku yaa le paari jigi ate ti jam baga nya Saipurus tɛŋka la, a yaa dam va tɛŋ kala yeniŋ a juga geŋ a ga paari Siriya tɛŋka. Ti ale jam paari Taaya la, ti yaa siŋ dii nyiŋla ka dula jigini ate ŋaaruŋku nyama a jam a yaali ayen ba yeeri ba kɔlimaŋa.

ref: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
text: Ti ale jam boro ale ba ate ti danni jam paari ayen ti basi ba la, ti yaa banti ba ale ŋman lo ti chelimu po. Ti ale jam banti ba ale ge ayen ti cheŋ la, ba meena ale ba pooba ale ba bisa ale jam ta ti a nyini tɛŋka po a ta ti jam paari nyakpiemu nɔi. Dula jigini ti meena yaa maa chaab a kpi duna tɛŋ a puusi

ref: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
text: ale ge banti chaab ate tama mɛ jueli ŋaaruŋku a cheŋ ale ge ate ba ŋman a kuli.

ref: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
text: Ti yaa ŋman lo ti chelimu po a zaani Taaya a jueli ŋaaruŋ a cheŋ Tolomayas tɛŋka. Dula jigini ti yaa puusi Kirisita bisaŋa ale ge goa dai yeŋ.

ref: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
text: Vari ale ga veenti la, ti yaa basi dula ale ŋman cheŋ Siizariya. Dula jigini, ti yaa jam boro ale Filip waai ale ka Naawen wieŋa moolidɔwa la. Wa jam ka bayopɔiwa po wanyi baai ate Kirisita bisaŋa a lueri ayen ba a nya ligraŋa zuk la.

ref: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
text: Ti ale jam goa dula ate ku beni maga la, Wen biisiteerɔ wanyi yaa jam nyini Judia a jam tama jigi. Wa yuei ale Agabus.

ref: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
text: Wa yaa jam pai Pɔɔl chiak gbanni a bobi wadek naŋsa ale wa nisima ale weeni tama ayen, <<Wen Chiika ale weeni diila, ale nna, ayen, Juuma Jerusalem tɛŋka po ale yik ka di nyɔnɔwa a bobi ase nna la a yaa pai wa a te baai ale kan daa Juuba la.>>

ref: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
text: Ti ale wom nna la, tama ale mbala ale jam maa bo dula la, yaa maa chaab a saalim Pɔɔl ayen wa kan cheŋ Jerusalem.

ref: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
text: Alege wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ka boa ate nama a nye dila, a nye ate m popola a kaasi? Mi poom gomsi magsi kama ayen ba kan bobi mu bobika nyiini Jerusalem, alege m poom gomsi magsi kama ayen m kpi dula jigini Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu yuenni nyiŋ.>>

ref: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
text: Ti an jam baga fɛ wa ate wa wari ya. Ti yaa pai dila basi ale weeni wa ayen, <<Ti a saalim Naawen ayen ku meena abe nye magsi ale wadek ale a yaali diila.>>

ref: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
text: Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma baai ale jam nyini Siizariya la gela yaa ta ti cheŋ nuru waai yenni ate ti jam a poli ayen ti goa la. Nuruwa yuei ale Minaason. Wa nyini ka Saipurus. A ta nyini diipo ate Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la a piilim boro la ale nuruwa a chim ka Kirisita biik.

ref: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
text: Ti ale jam paari Jerusalem la, ti suataŋa Kirisita bisaŋa a jam nye ti tia ka nalimnyiini ale suipeentik.

ref: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
text: Vari ale veenti la Pɔɔl yaa maa va ti a cheŋ ayen wa nya Jeemsi. Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la nisɔmma meena a jam maa boro kama.

ref: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
text: Ba ale wom wa a nueri la, ba meena yaa te Wen pimpauk. Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Ti suowa, fi nya Juuma ale piisi dii chim Kirisita bisa la kama. Fidek be nya ba ale kasim a yaali ayen nuruba a va sinsaŋŋa la kama.

ref: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
text: Nuruba weeni ba kama ayen ka fi ale a sak Juuma meena baai ale bo tɛŋ sii ale kan daa Juuba tɛŋsa la, ayen ba kan a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa abe ba kan a gebi ba bisaŋa yoaŋa yaase ba kan a va Juuma kisitaŋa.

ref: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ti ale nye ka sɛ? Ku a fɛ kama ayen ba wom ayen fi jam ya.

ref: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
text: Tama ale a yaali ayen fi nye diila ale nna. Nuruba banaansi ale bo dela jigini a puulim ale Wen.

ref: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
text: Alege baai ale kan daa Juuba a yaa chim Kirisita bisa la, gbaŋ kaai ate tama ŋmarisi ayen fi ta ga te ba la, ti weeni ba kama ayen, ba kan a dɛ bɔgta ŋandiinta, ba kan a dɛ ziim ba a kan ŋɔbi jabuui ate ba an tɔgri la lammoa, abe ba kan a bobi nipok baai ale kan daa ba pooba la a goa.>>

ref: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
text: Vari ale veenti la, Pɔɔl yaa dɛ nuruma niŋ ate ba cheŋ a ga nye dii ale dii ale di basi ate ba chim cheri nuruba. Pɔɔl yaa jo Wen yenni po a weeni ku a le pai daa ŋaai ate cheri nyaka tigini de a nueri abe ku ge ate ba yaa nya suik ate ba nye kaabka a te ba wanyi wanyi la.

ref: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
text: Ku jam pai ka daa ŋayopɔi ate weleŋsa nyaka tigini de a taam. Alege ku ale jam tali maga ate ŋa nueri la, Juuma gela baai ale jam nyini Asia la yaa nya Pɔɔl Wen yenni po. Ba yaa choa nuru boanni meena a yik Pɔɔl ale pagrim,

ref: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
text: a yaa nuem ate ku a jueli ayen, <<Izirali demma, ni maari ti, nuruwa de ale a nyiem jigi meena a sak ayen Moosis Sinsaŋŋa daa sinsak maŋsa ale biisi a kaasi ti nuruma ale Wen yenni. Wa ta ka baai ale kan daa Juuba la a jam Wen yenni po ale nye ate jigi weleŋka a taŋ.>>

ref: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
text: Ba jam weeni kude kama dii nyiŋla, ba jam nya ka Torofimus waai ale nyini Efisos la ale wa va ka Pɔɔl a nyiem tɛŋka po ate ba yaa deri poli ayen da dii dai Pɔɔl a ta wa jam jo ka Wen yenni po.

ref: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
text: Nuruma meena Jerusalem po sue yaa jam puuri. Ba yaa gum chaab chali ga yik Pɔɔl a vuuri wa a ta nyini Wen yenni po a nyini ale lik di tuataŋa.

ref: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
text: Ba ale jam boro a poli ayen ba ko Pɔɔl la, tuntomiŋ yaa jam paari Aroom tɛŋka tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni ayen wa nya Jerusalem tɛŋka meena demma boro a nye ka kpaliŋ nna ŋaglam.

ref: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
text: Kpagi kpienni yaa deri yik kpaga fiisaŋa gela ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba ate ba yaa chali siŋ nuru boanni jigi. Nuru boanni ale nya wa ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma la, ba yaa basi Pɔɔl nagta.

ref: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
text: Kpagi kpienni yaa taam cheŋ Pɔɔl jigi a yik wa ale pagrim a yaa weeni ayen tugurik tɔŋdɔma pai chɔrima ŋaye a bobi wa. Wa yaa bek ayen, <<Ka be denɔ ale nna? Wa nye ka sɛ?>>

ref: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
text: Nuru boanni yaa deri a nuem ate ku a jueli. Ba gela a nuem a weeni wari di choa, ba gela mɛ a nuem a weeni di choa. Juuma yaa nye nna ŋaglam ate kpagi kpienni an jam baga miŋ wari dii ate Pɔɔl nye la. Wa yaa weeni wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen ba ta Pɔɔl cheŋ juijui ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma boro la.

ref: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
text: Ba ale jam ta wa a jueli dɔkku tiilaŋa zuk la, nuru boanni sue yaa ŋman ŋmasi jam a puuri nna yegayega. Dila nyiŋ ku yaa jam fɛ tugurik tɔŋdɔma ate ba koati Pɔɔl a ji.

ref: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
text: Nuru boanni a kasim jam a vi wa kama ale a kaari a weeni ayen, <<Ko wa.>>

ref: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale jam tali maga ate ba ta wa jo yenni po la, Pɔɔl yaa weeni kpagi kpienni ayen, <<Mi a saalim, m weeni wari a sak fu?>> Kpagni yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi a wom Girik biika kama?

text: ) a nyini sagni po a nyini la?>>

ref: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
text: Ba ale wom ale wa a biisi ale badek biika Yiburu la, ba yaa ŋmasi goori nna chorototo ale ge ate Pɔɔl a biisi a cheŋ a weeni ayen,

ref: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
text: <<Mi ka Juu. Ba biak mu ka Taasus tɛŋka kaai ale bo Silisiya po la. Mi jam tom a te Wen ale ka nimmuna, ase nama baai ale bo dela jinla de la.

ref: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
text: Mi namsi baai ale a va Yeezu la ka nna yegayega a poom jam a bobi ba gela nidoaba ale nipooba ta ba ga a lik, ale ko ba gela mɛ.

ref: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
text: Ni dan bek Wen yenni kpagi kpienni ale kpaŋŋa meena, ba le siak ayen mi ale a biisi diila ka wensie. ref: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
text: <<Ase mi ale jam bo suiku po a cheŋ moata Damasikus tɛŋka la, wenbinni jam bo ka wein zuk suŋsuŋ ate wenŋmazuk a deri nyaksi a gilim mu.

ref: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
text: Mi yaa lo tɛŋ a wom ale lueluk a weeni mi ayen, <Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, ka boa ate fi a namsi mu nna?>

ref: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
text: Ate mi yaa bek wa ayen, <Ka wana, m Nyɔnɔ?> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <Ka mi, Yeezu, Nazaret denɔwa ate fi a namsi dila.>

ref: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
text: Nidoa baai ale jam maa va mi a cheŋ la, a jam nya nyaksika kama alege ba an jam wom lueluku ale jam a biisi dii ale mi la.

ref: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
text: Mi yaa bek ayen, <Mi le nye ka sɛ m Naawen yaa?> ate ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita yaa weeni ayen, <Yiti cheŋ Damasikus. Dula jigini fi le wom dii meena ate mi a poli ayen fi nye la.>

ref: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
text: Nyaksi kaai ale jam nyaksi la, a jam basi kama ate m deri yi. M vaanchaama baai ale jam maa va mu la, a yaa yik m nisima a ta mu cheŋ Damasikus.

ref: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
text: <<Dula jigini, nuru wanyi, wa yuei jam le Ananaiyas. Wa jam ka wensuik nyɔnɔ. Wa jam a zuli Moosis Sinsaŋŋa kama. Juuma meena ale jam bo dula la a jam a te wa zula kama.

ref: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
text: Wala yaa jam mi jigi a zaani m tɛŋ a yaa weeni mu ayen, <M suok Sɔɔl, lak fi ninaŋa.> Mi yaa deri lagri ŋa a yaa nya wa

ref: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
text: ate wa deri weeni mi ayen, <Ti kokpieŋsaŋa Wenni ale lueri fu ayen fi seba wa ale a yaali diila, abe fi nya wayɔrisima Tomteerɔwa, abe fi wom wadek lueluku.

ref: You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard.
text: Fi ale chim wa seerɔ a weeni waai meena fi ale nya ale wom diila.

ref: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
text: Fi be ŋman a limisi ka boa jaab yɔgyɔgla de? Yiti, a tuesi soka abe fi puusi a wi wa yuenni ate wa sugri fi wabaataŋa a basi.>

ref: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
text: <<Mi ale ŋmani Jerusalem la, mi yaa bo Wen yenni po a puusi, ku yaa nye mi jigi nna ase gɔdaasima la

ref: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
text: ate mi nya ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ate wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <Nye nwuli basi Jerusalem yɔgyɔgla de dii nyiŋla nuruma dela jigini a kan siak fi ale a biisi dii a magsi chaab ale mi la.>

ref: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.

ref: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
text: Ba ale jam yik Sitiven a ko ayen wa ale jam a sak nuruba fi wieŋa la nyiŋ, ka mi dek abe ale jam maa boro a siak ayen ba ko wa. Be ka mi ale jam a nya baai ale ko wa la kasaautaŋa zuk.>

ref: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
text: Ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita yaa weeni mi ayen, <M le basi ate fi cheŋ nna niŋniŋa baai ale kan daa Juuma la jigi.> >>

ref: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
text: Nuru boanni a jam a wom Pɔɔl kama ate wa ga biisi nna la. Ba yaa piilim a na ayen, <<Ni ko wa, ni yeeri wa tɛŋzuk de a basi, ni kan basi ate wa vua.>>

ref: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
text: Ba yaa jam a kaari a yik ba gattaŋa a kpaanti ale ŋari tintanta a yuk a basi wenzuk.

ref: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
text: Aroom tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni yaa weeni wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen ba ta Pɔɔl a ga jo tugurik tɔŋdɔma yenni po, a miiri wa ate wa weeni a sak ba jabuui nyiŋ ale soa ate Juuma a kaari ayen ba kan yaali wa la.

ref: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
text: Ase tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale chamsi wa a nya a gomsi ba miiri wa la, Pɔɔl yaa weeni kpagi dinyi ale jam moata wa la ayen, <<Fi ta suik a nak Aroom tɛŋka denɔ waai ale kan kaasi wari yaa?>>

ref: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni ale wom nna la, wa yaa ga bek Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni ayen, <<Fi a nye ka boan dila? Fi zɛ ayen nuruwa dɛ ka Aroom denɔ?>>

ref: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
text: Kpagi kpienni yaa cheŋ Pɔɔl jigi a ga bek wa ayen, <<Weeni a sak mu, fi ka Aroom denɔ?>> Pɔɔl mɛ yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mm.>>

ref: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
text: Kpagi kpienni yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi tuni ka ligra nna yegayega ale ge a chim Aroom denɔ.>> Pɔɔl yaa tulisi ayen, <<Alege a nyini mi biam po mi ka Aroom denɔ.>>

ref: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
text: Nuru baai ale jam gomsi ayen ba miiri Pɔɔl la ale wom nna la, yaa pilim ŋmani ŋaaŋ ale ge basi Pɔɔl. Yɔgsum yaa yik kpagi kpienni dii nyiŋla wa ale jam miŋ ayen Pɔɔl ka Aroom denɔ alege bobi wa ayen ba nak wa la.

ref: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
text: Wa jam a yaali kama ayen wa seba a chak dii nyiŋ ale soa ate Juuma a ŋma Pɔɔl la. Dila nyiŋ vari ale ga veenti la, wa yaa foli Pɔɔl chɔrimaŋa ale ge a wi kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma tɛŋka kpaŋŋa ayen ba nye tuka. Wa yaa ta Pɔɔl a cheŋ ga zaani ba niŋ.

ref: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
text: Pɔɔl yaa nya tigsuŋku po a weeni ba ayen, <<M mabisa, Izirali demma, mi seba chak kama nalimnyiini ayen a zaani diipo ate mi kasim boro a jam paari jinla la, Wen jigi mi ka wari ya.>>

ref: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
text: Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Ananaiyas yaa weeni baai ale jam za moata Pɔɔl la ayen, ba fɔbi wa nɔnni.

text: Pɔɔl yaa weeni Ananaiyas ayen, <<Wen ale fɔbi fi mɛ. Fi ka pimpaasirɔ. Fi kala ka dula a pai Moosis Sinsaŋŋa a bo mi buusa alege fi zɛ ayen fi a kaasi ka Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale fi ale a weeni ayen ba fɔbi mi nɔnni la?>>

ref: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
text: Nuru baai ale jam za moata Pɔɔl la a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi kan baga a lɛ Wen kaabteerɔ kpioŋku dila?>>

ref: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
text: Pɔɔl yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<M mabisa, mi poom zɛ ayen wa ka kaabteerɔ kpioŋŋoa. Dii nyiŋla, Wen Gbaŋka a weeni ayen, <Ku a fɛ kama ayen nuru waai kan biisi kpagi dii ale a nya ba zuk la a kaasi.> >>

ref: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
text: Pɔɔl ale ga nya ale nuruma gela ka Sajusiiba, ba gela mɛ Farisiiba la, wa yaa biisi ate ku jueli a weeni kpaŋŋa ayen, <<M mabisa, mi ka Farisii, mi be ka Farisii biik. ref: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
text: Wa ale weeni dila a magsi chaab ale kpieba le ba ŋman yiti a vua la, Farisiima ale Sajusiiba a yaa deri piilim ta chaab ate dila yaa nye ate ba poori chaab.

ref: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
text: Sajusiiba a weeni kama ayen nuruba a kan ŋman yiti kum po a vua, ba a weeni kama mɛ ayen Wen Maarɔba ale chichirisa karo. Alege Farisiima ta siaka kama ayen nuruba le yiti kum po kama, Wen Maarɔba ale chichirisa boro kama.

ref: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
text: Nuemka yaa jam a jueli nna yegayega ate Sinsak sagrɔma gela baai ale jam maa ka Farisiima la yaa yiti weeni ale pagrim ayen, <<Tama an nya wari dii ate nuruwa de kaasi la. Da dii dai ku ka wensie ayen chichirik yaase Wen maarɔ ale sum jam biisi ale wa.>>

ref: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
