ref: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
text: Gomina yaa karim gbaŋka ale ge yaa bek Pɔɔl ayen, <<Fi nyini ka tɛŋ boa?>> Gominawa ale miŋ ayen Pɔɔl nyini ka Silisiya la, wa yaa weeni Pɔɔl ayen,

ref: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
text: <<Mi le wom dii ate fi ta la ase baai ale a toariŋ fu la a nin jam.>> Gominawa yaa weeni tugurik tɔŋdɔba ayen ba basi Pɔɔl yenni po abe ba nya wa zuk nalimnyiini. Ye kpienni de jam ka Naawa Ayerod ale se di.

ref: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
text: Daa ŋanu ale jam taam la, kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Ananaiyas ale tɛŋka nisɔmma gela yaa va chaab a cheŋ Siizariya. Ba jam ta ka Tetuulos cheŋ ayen wa biisi te ba. Ba yaa jam Gominawa Feliksi jigi a jam zaani wa niŋ a weeni dii nyiŋ ale soa ate ba a toariŋ Pɔɔl la.

ref: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
text: Ba yaa wi ate Pɔɔl jo ate Tetuulos yaa deri piilim a ŋma wa ayen, <<Feliksi, fi yam buui ate fi pai a nya ti zuk la a basi kama ate ti boro ale suiyɔgni a ta nyini dipo. Ti be seba kama mɛ ayen ka fi yammu nyiŋ ate tagrika kasim a jam ti tɛŋka po ate ti boro ale suiyɔgni.

ref: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
text: Diipo meena wuu ale jiga meena wuu ti kasim a nye ka fi jiam ŋa nyiŋ.

ref: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
text: M be kan yaali ayen m beni fu, alege mi a saalim fu ayen fi le te ti zula a lak tue a wom ti biik gelika de.

ref: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
text: Tama nya kama ale nuruwa de ka nuru biok a ta daanika a jam ti tɛŋka po. Wa a deŋsi ka Juuma ale bo tɛŋzuk de meena la kpa ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale Aroom demma. Wa be ka nuru baai ate ba a wi ayen Nazaretba la kpagi.

ref: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
text: Fi dek a dan bek wa bega, fi yaa le miŋ ase ŋade meena ka wensie ya.>>

ref: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
text: Juuma yaa jam pai badek a gum ba po ate ba meena a weeni ayen dii meena ate ba a weeni la ka wensie.

ref: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
text: Gominawa yaa te Pɔɔl suik ayen wa biisi. Pɔɔl yaa piilim ayen, <<M seba ayen fi chim boteerɔ tɛŋka de ate ku beni ka nna yegayega. Dila nyiŋla, ku te mu suipeentik ate m zaani fi niŋ a biisi vari m dek a basi.

ref: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ase fidek a dan bek nuruba wieŋa de fi le wom ayen ka ku da pi ale ŋaye nyiini ale jinla ate mi daam yiti a cheŋ Jerusalem ayen m puusi.

ref: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
text: Diipo ate mi jam jo Wen yenni po la, yaase ba tuka diinaŋa po la, yaase tɛŋka po la, Juuma an nya ale mi a nak nanpaga ale nuru yaase m nye wari dii ale basi ate nuruba tigsi chaab jigi yeŋ la.

ref: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
text: Ba an baga ale sak fu ayen wieŋa de meena ate ba a toariŋ mi la ka wensie.

ref: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
text: Alege mi a weeni nya kude a sak fu kama ayen mi a va ka Kirisita bisaŋa suik kuui ate nuruma de a weeni ayen ku ka venta la, a puusi ti kokpieŋsaŋa Wenni. M be maa ta siaka kama ale Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni dii meena la kama. Wen biisiteerɔma mɛ ale ŋmarisi ba gbaŋsaŋa a weeni ŋaai meena la, m ta siaka kama mɛ ale ŋa.

ref: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
text: Mi be ta yiila kama ase nuruma de dek ale ta yiila diila ayen, waai meena, nuru maŋsa ale nuru baata le yiti kum po kama.

ref: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
text: Dila nyiŋla, mi nyiem kasim a pii ka nyiŋ m boka meena po ale m popola po ayen m nye dii ale ka wamaŋ Wen ale nurubiik niŋ la.

ref: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
text: <<Mi ale ga basi Jerusalem ate ku beni maga la, m jam cheŋ kama ayen m te m Kirisita bisa vaanchaama ligra abe m te Wen tiirim.

ref: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
text: Diipo ate mi jam bo Wen yenni po a nye dila la ate Juuma yaa nya mi du. Dila powa ale mi nye weleŋsa nyeka tuini a nueri kama. Dila powa mɛ, nuru boari yaase daanika a jam karo.

ref: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
text: Alege Juuma gela ale jam nyini Asia tɛŋka a jam maa boro. Ku a fɛ kama ayen bala dek a dan ta wari ayen ba toariŋ mu di nyiŋ ba be jam zaani fi niŋ a weeni wa dii ate mi nye kaasi la.

ref: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
text: Yaase fi basi ate nuruma ale za dela la a weeni sak fu diipo ate mi jam zaani kpagi kpiemaŋa niŋ ate ba nya mu la m nin nye wari kaasi.

ref: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
text: Kan daa ka wari dinyi dekki ate mi jam weeni dipo ayen, <Jinla ate mi za nama niŋ ate ni a bek mu beŋŋa de mi ale weeni ayen baai ale kpi la a le yiti kum po kama a ŋman vua la nyiŋ.> >>

ref: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
text: Alege Feliksi a jam seba Yeezu suiku kama, a yaa dak da yoŋ ayen ba biisi biika ale ge a weeni ba ayen, <<Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni Lisiyas a dan jam, abe m yaa poli nya dii ate m le weeni la.>>

ref: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
text: Feliksi yaa weeni tugurik tɔŋdɔ waai ale a nya Pɔɔl zuk la ayen wa ŋmasi nya Pɔɔl zuk nalimnyiini abe wa basi wa nna fasiyaa yenni po, abe wa basi mɛ ate wa doama a te wa jaabuuri meena ate wa a yaali la.

ref: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
text: Daa maga ale taam la, Feliksi yaa jam ale wa powa Durusila, wa jam ka Juu, a yaa weeni ayen ba ta Pɔɔl a jam wa jigi. Wa jam wom kama ale Pɔɔl a weeni kama ayen ba ta siaka ale Yeezu Kirisitawa.

ref: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
text: Alege Pɔɔl ale a biisi nyemagsika ale seba fidek yikka ale buusa boka la, yɔgsum yaa yik Feliksi ate wa yaa weeni Pɔɔl ayen, <<Fi baga cheŋ yɔgyɔgla de kama. M le ŋman wi fu ate fi jam ase m nin nya suik.>>

ref: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
text: Feliksi ale jam weeni dila la, wa jam a poli mɛ kama ayen da dii dai Pɔɔl ale te wa ligra. Dila nyiŋ wa yaa kasim jam a tom a wi Pɔɔl maga maga a daliŋ ale wa.

ref: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
text: Alege bena ŋaye ale taam la, Gominawa choa yaa jam tagri Feliksi zuk. Gominawa de yuei a jam le Poosiyos Fesitos. Dila powa Feliksi a jam a yaali kama ayen wa nye wari ate Juuma suipeentik. Dila nyiŋ, wa yaa basi ate Pɔɔl bo tugurik tɔŋdɔma nisima po.

ref: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
text: Fesitos ale ga dɛ wa naamu a yaa soa tɛŋka la, ku daa ŋata dai ate wa basi Siizariya ale ge cheŋ Jerusalem.

ref: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
text: Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku ale Juuma kpaŋŋa a yaa jam wa jigi a weeni wa wie ŋaai meena ate Pɔɔl kaasi la. Ba meena jam a saalim Fesitos ayen,

ref: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
text: wa maa maari ba ate ba ta Pɔɔl a jam Jerusalem. Ba jam weeni dila kama a poli ayen ba le basi kama ate nuruba suk suiku niŋ ate wa dan jam a taam abe ba ko wa.

ref: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
text: Fesitos yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Ba yik Pɔɔl a lik ka Siizariya. Mi dek abe le cheŋ dula ka yɔgyɔgla de.

ref: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
text: Ni basi ate ni kpaŋŋa a va mu cheŋ Siizariya ate ni ga ŋma wa dula jigini ase wa nin kaasi wari.>>

ref: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
text: Fesitos a ŋman goa ale ba daa naaniŋ yaase daa pi a gum du ale ge cheŋ Siizariya. Wa ale ga paari Siizariya ate vari veenti la, wa yaa jo biisaŋa dɔkku po a kali wa zukpaglika zuk a weeni wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen ba ta Pɔɔl jam.

ref: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
text: Pɔɔl ale ga jam la, Juuma baai ale jam maa nyini Jerusalem a jam la, a yaa jam za gilim Pɔɔl a weeni ayen wa kaasi ka wie nna yegayega alege ba an jam baga sak ayen ŋaai ate ba a weeni a magsi chaab ale Pɔɔl la ka wensie.

ref: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
text: Pɔɔl yaa biisi ayen wa vari wadek a basi, wa weeni ayen, <<Mi an kaasi Juuma Sinsaŋŋa yaase Wen yenni yaase m biisi naab kpioŋku Siiza a kaasi ya.>>

ref: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
text: Alege Fesitos ale jam a yaali ayen wa nye wari ate Juuma suipeentik la, wa yaa bek Pɔɔl ayen, <<Fi ale siak a cheŋ Jerusalem ate m bek fu a wom ba ale a biisi ŋaai meena a te fu la?>>

ref: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
text: Pɔɔl yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi za ka waai ale tagri naab kpioŋku Siiza la niŋ, ale wadek buusa boka dɔkku po juijui ale magsi ayen wa bo mi buusa la. Fidek abe seba chak kama ayen mi an nye Juuma wari a kaasi ya.

ref: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
text: M be dan kaasi ka wari ate dila nyiŋ ku magsi ayen m kpi, m kan weeni ayen m kan kpi. Alege wensie abe dan kan boro ale ba ale a ŋma mu la, nuru karo a baga pai mi a nyo ba nisima po. Mi a yaali kama ayen ti cheŋ naab kpioŋku Siiza jigi ate wala bo mi buusa.>>

ref: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
text: Fesitos yaa nya chaab ale wa nuruma baai ale bo ale wa a sak wa a magsi chaab ale wa tuimaŋa la a nueri ale ge a weeni Pɔɔl ayen, <<Fi weeni kama ayen fi yaali ayen fi cheŋ ka naab kpioŋku Siiza jigi, fi abe le cheŋ ka wa jigi.>>

ref: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
text: Ku ale ga beni maga la, Naab Agiripa ale wa toawa Beniis yaa cheŋ Siizariya ayen ba puusi Fesitos abe ba nye wa tia.

ref: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
text: Ba ale bo dula ate ku paari da boari la, Fesitos ya tɔk Pɔɔl wanni kiri a sak Naab Agiripa ayen, <<Nuru ale bo dela ate Feliksi jam yik wa lik.

ref: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
text: Mi ale cheŋ Jerusalem la, kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma nisɔmma ale jam a ŋma nuruwa de ayen wa nye wie kaasi ate ba yaa jam mi jigi ayen m bo wa buusa.

ref: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
text: Mi mɛ yaa tulisi ba ayen tama Aroom demma sinsaŋŋa a weeni kama ayen nuru waai ate nuru a ŋma wa ayen wa kaasi wari la, bala bayewa a tu chaab a nya chaab ate waai ate ba a ŋma la a biisi vari wadek a basi ale ge ate ti yaa bo ba buusa.

ref: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
text: Nuruma de ale va mi a jam Siizariya ayen ti chamsi wa nya la, mi an beni du. Dai dii ale pasaŋ la mi yaa kali buusa zukpaglika zuk a weeni ayen ba ta nuruwa a jam.

ref: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
text: Wa dachaasaŋa ale ga yiti zaani ayen ba biisi la, ba an poom biisi wakaasima ŋaai ate mi jam a poli ayen ba ale biisi a magsi chaab ale wa la.

ref: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
text: Ba ale jam a biisi dii meena la ale nanpaga nakka a magsi chaab ale badek wensuik vaka wie ale nuru wanyi ate ba a wi wa ayen Yeezu ate wa kpi alege Pɔɔl a weeni ayen wa vua kama.

ref: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
text: Mi ale kan jam seba mi ale m tulisi beŋŋa dii la, mi yaa bek Pɔɔl, <Fi a yaali fi cheŋ Jerusalem ate ba bo fi buusaŋa dula?>

ref: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
text: Alege Pɔɔl a jam weeni kama ayen wa a yaali kama ayen wa wari dela ate Naab Kpioŋku a poli nya wa ale wa nye wanni de diila. Dila nyiŋ ate mi yaa weeni ayen ba a limisi wa ate m yaa tom ate wa cheŋ naab kpioŋku Siiza jigi.>>

ref: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
text: Agiripa yaa weeni Fesitos ayen, <<Mi a yaali kama ayen midek a wom nuruwa de biik.>> Fesitos mɛ yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Chum fi be le wom wa.>>

ref: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
text: Vari ale ga veenti la, Agiripa ale Beniis yaa va chaab a jam ate nuruba nna yegayega a vi ba ŋaaŋ a te ba zula. Bala meena yaa va chaab ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpiemaŋa ale tɛŋka nisɔm kpientaŋa yaa maa jo dɔk kpioŋ kuui ate nuru boari a jo ku po a nye tuka la. Fesitos yaa weeni ate ba ta Pɔɔl a jo jam.

ref: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
text: Alege mi abe nya kama ale wari karo a magsi nuruwa kummoa. Alege wadek ale weeni ayen wa a yaali ayen wa cheŋ Naab Kpioŋku jigi la, ate mi yaa poli ayen m basi ate wa cheŋ Aroom.

ref: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
text: Alege mi potim ka wari ayen m ŋmarisi a magsi chaab ale wa a te Naab Kpioŋku. Dila nyiŋ ate m ta wa jam nama meena jigi a potim jam fi jigi Naab Agiripa ayen fi dan bek wa wanni a wom, abe mi yaa ta wari a ŋmarisi.

ref: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
text: Mi jigi, yam ka ku po ate m tom ligrɔ ale ge kan weeni ate ku a lagri dii dek chekki ate nuruba a weeni ayen wa kaasi la.>>

ref: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
text: <<Naab Agiripa, mi a poli ayen mi ta ka wein ate jinla mi zaani fi niŋ ayen mi biisi a vari m dek a basi ale Juuma ale a ŋma mu ayen mi kaasi la.

ref: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
text: Fidek abe seba Juuma ŋiak wieŋa ale ba beŋŋa a magsi chaab ale ba wensuiku vaka a chak kama. Dila nyiŋ ate mi a saalim fu ayen fi wom mi ale suduŋni.

ref: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
text: Ba seba mu ate ku beni kama. Ba daa yaali ba le weeni fu ayen mi jam ka Farisii. Farisiima abe a zuli mi tɛŋka sinsaŋŋa kama chekki a gaam tigsuŋ meena.

ref: Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de m be za ka dela ayen ni bo mu buusa dii nyiŋla, mi ta yiila kama ale Wen ale jam puulim dii ale ti kokpieŋsaŋa la.

ref: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
text: Pumpuulimaŋa de abe le tama nuruma diina pi ale buyewa a yiili ba nya ase ba le tom a te Wen danni po ale yok la. Naabaa, ba ŋma mu ka m ni ta yiilaŋa de dek la nyiŋ.

ref: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
text: Ka boa abe ale soa ate nama ayen ku daa moali ate Wen nak kpilima a yiti kum po?

ref: I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth.
text: <<Mi dek abe jam poli kama ayen m nye dii meena ale di kaasi Yeezu Nazaret denɔwa yuei la.

ref: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
text: M be ale jam nye dii Jerusalem tɛŋka la ale la. M jam tuesi ka suik kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa jigi a yik Kirisita bisaŋa yegayega a lik. Daa likka nyiini alege, ti ale jam poli ayen ku ka wamaŋ ate ti ko ba la, mi mɛ abe ale jam siak ayen ba ko ba.

ref: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
text: Daa dila nyiini, mi jam te ba waalika ti tuka diinaŋa po ate ku paari ka diichoa, a kasim a nye dila ayen ba lɛ Yeezu. M suinni kasim ŋmasi jam a de ka nna yegayega ale ba ate mi nyiem poom jam cheŋ satɛŋ yonsa juijui ate ba boro la a te ba waalika.

ref: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
text: Mi jam tuesi ka suik ale pagrim kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa jigi ayen m cheŋ Damasikus tɛŋka.

ref: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
text: Mi ale bo suiku po a cheŋ dula la, wentueŋ suŋsuŋ, mi yaa nya ku nyagsi a nyini wenŋmazuk. Ku jam nyagsi a gaam wenbinni kama a nyagsi a gilim mi ale baai meena ale jam va mi a cheŋ la.

ref: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
text: Ate ti meena yaa lo tɛŋ ate mi wom ale lueluk a weeni mi ale Juuma biika Yiburu ayen, <Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, ka boa ate fi a namsi mu nna? Fi a namsi ka fidek dila.>

ref: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
text: Mi yaa bek ayen, <Fi ka wana Nyɔnɔ?> Ate ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita yaa tulisi ayen, <Ka mi Yeezu ate fi a namsi.

ref: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
text: Alege, yiti zaani ŋmai. M pai m dek a sak fu kama yɔgyɔgla de ayen ku sak ayen m lueri fu kama ale tom fu mɛ ayen fi chim m tomteerɔ. Ku a fɛ kama ayen fi weeni a sak nuruba ba chaab dii ate fi nya a magsi chaab ale mi jinla la ale m nin m sak fu dii chum diipo la.

ref: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
text: M le vari fu fidek nuruma Juuma nisima po a basi ale baai mɛ ale kan daa Juuba ate mi le tom fu ba jigi la nisima po mɛ a basi.

ref: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
text: M dan tom fu, mi le basi ate fi lagri ba ninaŋa ate ba tagri nyini legini po a nyini jam peelim niŋ. Ba ale tagri nyini Sitaana nisima po a nyini a jam Wen nisima po ate ba ta siaka ale mu ate ba nya wabaataŋa vɔŋteka ate ba yaa maa bo nuru baai ate Wen lueri la po.>

ref: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
text: Mi yaa piilim Damasikus ale Jerusalem tɛŋsaŋa po ale ge yaa paari Judia tɛŋka meena ale baai mɛ ale kan daa Juuba la, a sak ba ayen ku a fɛ kama ate ba basi ba wabaataŋa tomka abe ba pai badek a te Naawen abe ba a tom tuim ŋaai ale a sak ayen ba tagri kama la.

ref: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
text: Ku be jam ka sinsaŋŋa de nyiŋ ate Juuma a jam yik mi diipo ate mi jam bo Wen yenni po la a pii nyiŋ ayen ba ko mu.

ref: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
text: Alege zaani dipo a jam paari jinla, ka Wen ale jam a maari mi. Ka dila nyiŋ ate mi za dela ayen m biisi wensie a sak waai meena, nuru fiik yaase nuru kpioŋ. Mi ale a biisi diila ale dila dekdega ate Wen biisiteerɔma ale Moosis a jam weeni ayen ku le nye la,

ref: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
text: ayen Kirisitawa ale kpi, ase wa ale waai ale wa dɛ niŋ a yiti kum po la, wa le ta bolim a jam te nuru meena.>>

ref: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
text: Ase Pɔɔl ale a biisi wieŋa de wa vari wadek a basi la, Fesitos yaa weeni ate ku jueli ayen, <<Pɔɔl fi zukku karo, zamsika yegayega a basi kama ate fi a yesim.>>

ref: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
text: Pɔɔl yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<M koa, mi kan yesimu. Wie ŋaai ate mi a biisi la ka wensie ale yam.

ref: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
text: Mi baga a nyini ka peelim a biisi ale fi Naab Agiripa dii nyiŋla fidek seba wieŋa de nɔi po kama. M seba chak kama ayen fi ŋmasi kpesi wieŋa de dinyi dinyi kama, dii nyiŋla, wanni de an suk nye ka gugoruk po.

ref: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
text: Naab Agiripa, fi ta siaka ale Wen biisiteerɔma ale a biisi diila? M seba ayen fi ta siaka kama.>>

ref: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
text: Agiripa yaa bek Pɔɔl ayen, <<Ku an diem bula beniya ale ge fi a poli ayen fi nye kama ate mi chim Kirisita biik, yaa boa?>>

ref: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
text: Pɔɔl yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ku beni yaa ku an beniya, mi a puusi a te ka Wen ayen fi ale baai meena ale kali dela jigini a wom mi jinla danni la, nama ale chim ase mi ale ka nuru waai jinla la. Alege m kan poli ayen ni le ta chɔrima ase mi ale ta diila.>>

ref: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
text: Naawa ale Gominawa ale Beniis ale mbala meena a yaa yiti nyini.

ref: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
text: Ba ale nyini nueri la, ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Nuruwa an nye wari a magsi wa kpi yaase ba yik wa a ligi.>>

ref: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
text: Agiripa yaa weeni Fesitos ayen, <<Nuruwa de a poom magsi ka ti basi wa ase wa nin poom kan weeni ayen wa a yaali ayen ka wa cheŋ Siiza jigiya.>>

ref: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
text: Gominawa ale jam poli ayen ti jueli ŋaaruŋ a cheŋ Itali la, ba yaa pai Pɔɔl ale ligrɔba ba chaab a nyo Juliyos nisima po. Juliyos jam ka Aroom tɛŋka tugurik tɔŋdɔma beŋ kanyi kpagi.

ref: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
text: Ti jam zaani ka Siizariya tɛŋka a jueli ŋaaruŋ. Ku jam nyini ka Adiramitiyom. Ŋaaruŋku a jam gomsi magsi ayen ku cheŋ ka jigi ŋaai meena ate ŋaaruŋta a zaani Asia tɛŋka la. Nuru ale jam maa va ti a cheŋ, wa yuei ale Arisitaakus wa jam ka Tesalonika denɔ.

ref: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
text: Vari ale veenti la, ti yaa paari Saidon. Juliyos a jam ta zula ale Pɔɔl a yaa siak ayen Pɔɔl ga nya wa doama ate ba te wa jabuui ate wa a yaali la.

ref: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
text: Ti yaa basi ale lo jueli moata Saipurus tɛŋka diila viok ale jam a fɔb ti.

ref: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
text: Ti yaa lo Silisiya nyakpiemu jueli cheŋ Pamfiliya a ga paari Mira tɛŋ kpieŋka ale bo Lisia po la.

ref: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
text: Dula jigini ate tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni a yaa nya ŋaaruŋ ale ku nyini Alezandiria a taam a cheŋ Itali. Wa yaa pai ti nyo ku po.

ref: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
text: Ŋaaruŋ kula po, ti kasim jam a cheŋ ka nna maga maga ate daaŋa jam paari da boari ate ti nam ale ge yaa paari Kinides tɛŋka. Ka an jam yalima ale ti. Vioku a jam pagra ka nna yegayega ate ti an ŋman jam baga a va suik kuui ate ti jam va la, ate ti yaa ŋmeriŋ va Kariti tɛŋka juijui ate vioku an jam pagra la a jam va jigi di choa ate ba a wi ayen Salomoni.

ref: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
text: Ti le jam sali va kunkɔŋni a cheŋ la, ku jam tua kama a te ti ate ti yaa jam paari jigi ate ba a wi ayen Ŋaaruŋta Zaani Maŋ jigi a moata Lasia tɛŋka.

ref: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
text: <<M doaba, mi nya kama ale ti chelimu a zaani dela a cheŋ a kan nala. Kɔlimaŋa ale ŋaaruŋku le kaasi kama, kum mɛ abe le jam ti jigi.>>

ref: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
text: Ba jam weeni ayen juijui ate ba jam za la, an jam nala a magsi ba wari dula ŋoota wenni. Dila nyiŋla, nuruma yegayega a jam a yaali kama ayen ku dan siak a nye ba dam a paari Foniksi tɛŋka ate ba wari dula ŋoota wenni a vuusi. Foniksi bo ka Kariti tɛŋka juijui ate ŋaaruŋta a nyiem zaani a vuusi la. Jigini de a tuk ka yeniŋ geŋ.

ref: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
text: Viok yaa nyini yeniŋ a gala geŋ a fuk nna balibali ate ba yaa poli ayen nya kude ale deri basi kama ate ba nye ba ale poom a yaali dii ayen ba cheŋ la. Ba yaa pai kutuk kpioŋ kuui ate ba nyiem pai a yik ŋaaruŋku a zaani la a yeeri ku a ta nyini nyiamu po a jueli. Ba yaa jam cheŋ va kunkɔŋni nɔi nna farafara a moata Kariti tɛŋka.

ref: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
text: Alege ku an bula beniya ate viok kpioŋ a yaa nyini a gala geŋ kori nummu po kunkɔŋni a jam

ref: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
text: fɔbi ŋaaruŋku. Ku be ale jam pagra nna yegayega ate ti an jam baga dam la, ti yaa basi ate ku ji ŋaaruŋku a ta a cheŋ.

ref: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
text: Ti ale jam paari tɛŋ fiik kanyi ate ba a wi ayen Kɔda ate nyiam a gilim ka la ate vioku an jam pagra, ti yaa nam nna yegayega ale ge baga a yaa yik ŋaaruŋku ŋaaruŋ fiika a zaani.

ref: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
text: Ba yaa dari ate ku jueli ŋaaruŋ kpioŋku zuk. Ba yaa pai mi pagrisa a bobi gilim ŋaaruŋ kpioŋku. Yɔgsum ale jam ta ba ayen dai dii dai ba ŋaaruŋku a nin zaan a chali ga feri tintain tii ale vi chaab a jueli dua nyiamu tɛŋ a moata Libia nyiamu kunkɔŋni nɔi la. Dila nyiŋ, ba yaa jam a cheŋ maga maga ale basi ate vioku a tusi ŋaaruŋku a ta a cheŋ.

ref: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
text: Daa ŋatawa danni ba yaa pai nisima a pai ŋan baai ate ti ta a nye ate ŋaaruŋku a zaani ale a cheŋ la gela a yuk basi nyiamu po.

ref: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
text: Daaŋa a jam piisi ka nna yegayega alege ti an jam baga a pai nimbiri tu wenbinni yaase chiŋmarisa. Vioku mɛ abe kasim jam a fɔbi ka dila. Ti ŋman jam ka yiila ayen ti le vuugi.

ref: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
text: Ba ale ga cheŋ ate ku beni alege ba an dɛ ŋandiinta la, Pɔɔl yaa yiti zaani ba niŋ a weeni ba ayen, <<Nidoaba, ku poom magsi ka ni ti wom mi ate ti kan poom ŋman zaani Kariti a dam cheŋ. Nna po de ti ti poom kan nya kaasuŋku de ale ŋantaŋa de ate ti jɔk la.

ref: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
text: Alege yɔgyɔgla de, ni yik nidek. Ni wanyi mɛ a kan kpi. Ka ŋaaruŋku nyiini ale ku kaasi.

ref: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
text: Deemwa yokku Wen maarɔ ale nyini Wen dii ale soa mi ate mi a puusi wa la a jam mi jigi

ref: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
text: a weeni mi ayen, <Pɔɔl, kan chali yɔgsum, ku a fɛ kama ate fi zaani Siiza niŋ. Wen abe tulisi fi puusaŋa kama ayen nuruma de wanyi mɛ la a kan kpi.> >>

ref: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
text: Alege ti cheŋ paari tɛŋ kanyi ate nyiam gilim ka la.>>

ref: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
text: Ba yaa gebi kuta tii ale jam yik ŋaaruŋku a zaani la miisaŋa yaa basi ate ti a cheŋ nyiamu po. Diipo ate ba boro a gebi kutaŋa miisaŋa la, ba jam maa foli dakpien tii ale bobi maŋ ŋaaruŋku ŋaaŋka ate nuruba pai a dam ku la ayen ba yaa pai tila a dam ku. Ba yaa zak garuk kuui ale bobi yiga ŋaaruŋku niŋka la ale ge ayen vioku fuk ku a basi niŋ. Ba yaa nye dila a deri a cheŋ kunkɔŋni.

ref: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
text: Baai ale a tom ŋaaruŋku po la, a jam pii ka nyiŋ ayen ba chali bɛ. Ba yaa foli ŋaaruŋ fiika a basi nyiamu po ale ge yaa velim ayen ba boro a foli ka kuta dobrita ti chaab ŋaaruŋku niŋ.

ref: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
text: Damdɔma a jam yɔgsa kama ayen ti le nak ka pinaŋa, dila ba yaa pai kutuk dobrita tinaansi a bobi basi nyiamu po ale a puusi ayen vari veenti.

ref: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
text: Alege Pɔɔl yaa weeni tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen, <<Ŋaaruŋku tuimtomdɔma de a dan kan bo ŋaaruŋku po, ni kan vuugi.>>

ref: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa gebi mi sii ale yik ŋaaruŋ fiika a ta la a basi nyiamu po.

ref: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
text: Dila nyiŋ ate mi a weeni ni ayen ni dɛ ŋandiinta. Ku a fɛ kama ayen ni dɛ ate ni vuuk. Wen weeni mi kama ayen ni zuimaŋa zuisaŋa kanyi la a kan bɛ.>>

ref: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
text: Pɔɔl ale ga weeni nna a nueri la, wa yaa pai boroborok puusi a te Wen a nye wa jiam ba meena niŋ, a yaa wɛ boroboroku a piilim ŋɔbika.

ref: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
text: Ba yaa yik badek meena a dɛ ŋandiinta.

ref: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
text: Waai meena ale dɛ chak la, ba yaa kɔlim ŋanbieŋa meena a yuk basi nyiamu po ale ge ayen ŋaaruŋku a valima maga.

ref: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
text: Vari ale veenti la, ŋaaruŋku tuimtomdɔma yaa nya kunkɔŋni dinyi alege ba an jam miŋ ale ka juijui kunkɔŋi la. Ba jam nya ka nyakpiemu gugoruk kunyi ale tintain busuŋ a dua jueli maga ate ba yaa poli ayen ba dan baga abe ba dam ŋaaruŋku a ga zaani dula.

ref: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
text: Alege ŋaaruŋku yaa nak kuŋkutinni ate ku niŋka yaa feri kuŋkutinni an ŋman baga cheŋ. Ku ale nye dila la, nyamiisaŋa mɛ a kasim jam a fɔbi ku ŋaaŋka ate ku a wɛ nna bunabuna a lo nyiamu po.

ref: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa nye ba popola ayen ba ko ligrɔma meena ate ba waai a kan nya suik a puŋ nyiamu a chali bɛ.

ref: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
text: Alege tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni a kan jam a yaali ayen wa ko Pɔɔl. Wa yaa weeni ba ayen ba kan nye dila. Wa jam weeni ba kama ayen waai meena ale baga a dɛ nyiam la, ba yɔk a zi nyiamu po a dɛ jueli kunkɔŋni

ref: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
text: ale ge ate mbala meena a yik ŋaaruŋku daataŋa yaase ku ŋan baai ale kasi a lo la a jueli. Ti meena ale jam nye dii a vuuk a paari kunkɔŋni la ale la.

ref: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
text: Ti ale jam paari kunkɔŋni nalimnyiini la, tɛŋ kala demma jam weeni ti kama ayen tɛŋ kala yuei ale Malita.

ref: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
text: Tɛŋ kala demma a jam tuesi ti kama a te ti zula. Ŋmoruk yaa deri a ni ate ŋoota boro ate ba yaa jam cheem bolim a te ti.

ref: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
text: Pɔɔl yaa tigsi daata ayen wa nyo bolimu po. Wa ale pai boro a nyoro la, bolim wuluku yaa nye ate waab a nyini ti po a chali nyini a meli wa nisa a dom wa.

ref: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
text: Tɛŋ kala demma ale nya ale waamu meli Pɔɔl nisimaŋa la, ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Nuruwa de ku a fɛ kama ayen wa ka nuru koorik. Wa baga nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini kama alege tama bɔglukku a kan nya ase ku magsi ayen wa vuuk la.>>

ref: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
text: Alege waamu ale meli Pɔɔl nisimaŋa la, wa yaa misi si ate waamu lo bolimu po alege wari an nye wa.

ref: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
text: Nuruma yaa jam a limisi ale a poli ayen ba nya ale wa nyiŋka fuusi yaase wa deri kpi dua. Alege ba ale jam a limisi ale a poli ate ku beni alege wari an nye wa la, ba yaa tagri ba popolaŋa ale ge weeni ayen, <<Wa ka wen.>>

ref: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
text: Tɛŋka naawa yuei a jam le Pubiliyosi. Naawa de kaduksa ale jam dua moata juijui ate ti jam kala la. Wa yaa jam nye ti tia. Daa ŋata meena ti kasim jam bo ka wala yenni ate wa a nya ti zuk nalimnyiini.

ref: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
text: Ŋoota ale poiyɔgsik ale jam ta wa kowa ate wa jam dua dɔk po. Pɔɔl yaa jo ayen wa nya wa a pai wa nisima a vi wa zuk a puusi te wa ate wa nya nyiŋyɔgsa.

ref: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
text: Wanni de ale ga nye la, yɔgnyieŋsa meena ale jam bo tɛŋ kala la, a jan jam kama a nya nyiŋyɔgsa.

ref: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
text: Ti jam goa Malita ka chiisa sita ale ge yaa cheŋ Aroom. Ŋaaruŋku de ate ti jam jueli la yuei ale <<Wen Yibsa.>> Ku jam ka Alezandiria ŋaaruŋ. Ku be jam ka ŋoota wein ate ku jam wari Malita ayen ŋootaŋa taamu.

ref: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
text: Ti yaa jam paari Sirakusi tɛŋka goa dula daa ŋata.

ref: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
text: A zaani dula a ŋman paari tɛŋ ka choa ate ba a wi ayen Arigiyum. Vari ale ga veenti la, viok yaa nyini yeniŋ a gala geŋ a fuk. Daa ŋaye dai ate ti yaa ŋman paari Putiyooli tɛŋka.

ref: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
text: Dula jigini ate ti jam nya Kirisita bisa ate ba weeni ti ayen ti daa yaali ti goa daa ŋayopɔi ale ba. Ti yaa siak a goa daa ŋayopɔiwa ale ba ale ge yaa yiti cheŋ Aroom.

ref: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
text: Ti Kirisita bisa suataŋa ale bo Aroom, ale wom ayen ti cheena la, ba yaa nyini cheŋ paari Apiyas Yabaŋa ale Vuusum Yie Ŋatawa, a jam tu ti. Pɔɔl ale ga nya ba ale ba cheena la, ku yaa te wa nyiŋ pagra ate wa te Wen jiam.

ref: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
text: Ti ale jam paari Aroom la, ba jam basi ate Pɔɔl a boro ka wadek wa nyiini, ale tugurik tɔŋdɔ waai ale a limisi wa la.

ref: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
text: Daa ŋata ale jam taam la, Pɔɔl yaa wi Juuma kpaŋŋa Aroom tɛŋka po ate ba jam ayen wa nye tuka ale ba. Ba ale jam tigsi chaab jigi yeŋ la, Pɔɔl yaa weeni ba ayen, <<M mabisa mi an kaasi tama nuruma wari ya yaase kisi tii ate ti tuesi ti kokpieŋsaŋa jigi la, alege ba yik mu a lik ka Jerusalem tɛŋka a pai mu nyo Aroom demma nisima po.

ref: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
text: Ba ale bek mu bega a piisi la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, ba an nya wari a magsi ba ko mu. Ba yaa a yaali ba basi mu ate m cheŋ fasiyaa,

ref: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
text: Dila nyiŋ ate mi wi ni ayen m nya ni abe m weeni a sak ni. Mi be ta chɔrinni de kama dii nyiŋla mi ta yiila ŋaai mɛ ate Izirali demma meena mɛ a ta la.>>

ref: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
text: Ba yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Tama an tuesi gbaŋ ate ka nyini Judia a biisi fi wari ya. Ti mabisaŋa wanyi mɛ la abe an nyini dula a jam weeni fi wari a sak ti yaase wa biisi wabiok a magsi chaab ale fi.

ref: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
text: Alege tama a yaali kama ayen ti wom fi mɛ popola ale ka diila, dii nyiŋla, jigi meena nuruba kasim a weeni kama ayen ba kan yaali nuru baai ate fi maa bo ba po la.>>

ref: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
text: Ba yaa dak dai yoŋ ayen ba ŋman nye tuka ale Pɔɔl. Dila danni ale jam paari la, ba yaa piisi a tigsi chaab juijui ate Pɔɔl a goa la. A ta nyini saluik a jam paari junɔi Pɔɔl kasim jam a biisi a magsi chaab ale ka Wen naamu wie. Wa kasim jam pii ka nyiŋ a biisi a ta a nyini Moosis Sinsaŋŋa gbaŋka po ale Wen Biisiteerɔma ale ŋmarisi dii la po ayen ku sak ayen wa ale a biisi diila ka wensie a magsi chaab ale Yeezu.

ref: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
text: Pɔɔl yaa weeni wa dinyi ayen, <<Wen Chiika ale jam basi ate Wen biisiteerɔwa Azaya a biisi dii a te ni kokpieŋsaŋa la sum ka wensie.

ref: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
text: Wen Chiika ale jam biisi dii a te wa ayen wa weeni a sak ni la ale nna ayen, <Cheŋ ga weeni sak nuruma ayen, Nama le wom, a wom alege ni kan miŋ chagi. Nama le nya, a nya alege ni kan zamsi ŋa.

ref: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
text: Dii nyiŋla, nuruma de ka tukpari nyam. Ba kan wom, ba abe mum ba ninaŋa kama, kan daa di, ba ti sum miŋ a chak kama. Dii ate ba nya ale ba ninaŋa la ale a wom ale ba tueŋa la. Ba ti sum miŋ chak kama ale ba popolaŋa a ŋmani jam mi jigi a nya nyiŋyɔgsa.>

ref: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
text: Pɔɔl ale weeni nna nueri la, Juuma yaa nak nanpaga ale chaab a yaa waaŋ chaab.

ref: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
text: Wa nyiem jam nyini ka peelim a kan chali yɔgsum a sak nuruba Wen naamu wie ale a sak ba mɛ Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita wie. Nuru an jam nye ate wa an baga sak wieŋa de.

ref: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
text: Mi Pɔɔl waai ale ka Yeezu Kirisita tomteerɔ la ale a ŋmarisi gbaŋka de. Wen dek ale lueri mu a potim gaari mu ayen m chim wa tuimtomdɔ abe m weeni wa wamaŋsaŋa a sak nuruba.

ref: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
text: Wamaŋsaŋa de ka ŋaai ate wa puulim a biisi ŋa dipo ate wa biisiteerɔma a ŋmarisi nyo Wen gbaŋka po la.

ref: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
text: A ta va Weleŋsa Chiika a mooli ale pagrim ayen wa ka Wen Nidoabili wa le yiti kum po la nyiŋ, wala ale Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa.

ref: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
text: Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ ale Wa Yuenni nyiŋ ate Wen a te mu suiku de ate m chim wa tuimtomdɔ ayen m baga a weeni wa wie a sak tɛŋsa meena nuruba ate ba ta siaka ale wa abe ba a va wa nɔi.

ref: You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
text: Wen wi nama mɛ kama ayen Yeezu Kirisita soa ni.

ref: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
text: Mi a puusi nama meena baai ate Wen ta yaalika ale ni a lueri ni a te wadek Aroom tɛŋka po la. Ti Kowa Wen ale ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita le niak ni abe wa te ni suiyɔgni.

ref: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
text: Mi a yaali ayen m va ka Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ a nye Wen jiam a te ni meena, dii nyiŋla, jigi meena nuruba a biisi ni wie kama ni ale ta siaka ale Yeezu Kirisita la.

ref: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
text: Wen dii ate m tom a te ale m suinum meena a sak nuruba Wa Nidoabinni wamaŋsaŋa wie la, ka wala ale mi seerɔ ate mi kasim a puusi a te nama daa meena. M maara puusi mɛ ayen,

ref: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
text: ku dan ka wa yaalika wa le te mu suik ate m jam ni jigi yɔgyɔgla.

ref: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
text: Mi a yaali ka nna yegayega ayen m nya ni ate m te ni Chiika tiirim ate ni ta pagrim.

ref: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
text: M suata, mi a yaali ayen m weeni a sak ni kama ayen m kasim a yaali ayen m jam ni jigi kama, alege mi an baga a jam ya. Mi a yaali ayen ka m dan jam m nye ate nuruba ni po a pai badek a te Wen ase m le nye dii ale ni vaanchaab baai meena ale kan daa Juuba la.

ref: It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome. The Power of the Good News
text: Dila ale soa ate m pii nyiŋ a yaali ayen m sak nama baai mɛ ale bo Aroom tɛŋka po la Wen wamaŋsaŋa.

ref: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
text: Dii nyiŋla, Wen wamaŋsaŋa a dak sak ti kama suik kuui ate Wen a nye ate ti a chim wayɔrisima nyam wa niŋ la. Wanni de abe ka siaka nyiini a ta nyini di piilimka po a ta ga paari di kpeglimka. Ase ba ale ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po dipo ayen, <<Nuru waai abe le ta siaka a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ Wen niŋ la, wala a nya nyuvuri kama.>>

ref: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
text: Nuruba ale boro a ta gaasa nna yegayega a kan siak ayen wensieŋa a nyini peelim. Wen abe a sak ti kama ayen wa sui ale a puuri ale baai ale kaa va wa suiku la ale ba gaasa tuimaŋa.

ref: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
text: Ba jam seba Wen kama, alege ba an jam a siak ayen ba a nye wa jiam yaase ba a te wa zula. Ba popolaŋa ka betta popola, ŋa daa popola yɔrisima.

ref: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
text: Ba a poli ayen ba ka yam nyam, alege ba chim ka betta,

ref: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
text: a yaa zuli ŋan baai ale a neensi nuruba ale nuinsa ale duŋsa ale ŋan baai meena ale a cheŋ ba lɔga nyiŋsa la, alege kan zuli Wen dii ale kasim boro taam wuu la.

ref: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
text: Ba ale a nye dila la ale soa ate Wen yaa pai ba basi ayen ba va badek sui po ale mariŋ diila ate ba yaa pai badek nyiŋsaŋa a tom daŋta tuim ŋaai ale kan magsi ba pai ba nyiŋsaŋa a tom la ale chaab.

ref: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
text: Ba yaa pai Wen wensieŋa a tagri chim venta ale a puusi ale tom a te ŋan nyeentaŋa ale basi nyeerɔwa, waai ale ta niauŋ taam wuu la. Ku be nye dila.

ref: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
text: Kude nyiŋ, Wen pai ba basi kama ayen ba va badek sui po ale mariŋ dii le di basi ate ba nya chivie la. Ba nipooma mɛ dek a kan yaali ayen ba a goa ale nidoaba. Ba a yaali ayen ka ba a bobi nipooba ba chaab a goa.

ref: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
text: Nidoama mɛ kan yaali ayen ba a goa ale nipooba. Ba kasim a yaali kama ale ba koarisa meena ayen ba a bobi nidoaba ba chaab a goa. Nidoama de ale a nye nna la a magsi ka chivie yik ba alege ba kan chali chivie. Nya kude abe basi kama ate waali kaai ale magsi ba nya la a jam ba jigi.

ref: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
text: Ba jam a poli kama ayen ku an magsi ate ba ta wensie popola maŋsa a magsi chaab ale Wen ya. Wen yaa pai ba basi ate ba ta popola kaasima ate ba a tom tuim ŋaai ale kan magsi ba a tom la.

ref: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
text: Ba suiniimaŋa kasim sueri ale ka gaasa meena wuu, ate ba a yaali chaab ŋanta ale a kisi chaab ale a de nyuri ale chaab ale a ko nuruba ale a nye kpaliŋsa ale chaab ale a paasi chaab ale a poli kaasuŋ nyiini a te nuruba ale a zu chaab ŋaaŋ

ref: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
text: ale a kaasi chaab yue ale kisi Wen mɛ. Ba ka nuru leerisa mɛ ale kanjanta nyam ale a yaali yue a te badek ale a gisi ayen ba nya su paalita ate ba a tom tuimbaata. Ba kan wom ba koba ale ba maba noa.

ref: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
text: Ba be seba ayen Wen weeni kama ayen ku magsi ka nuru baai meena ale a tom nna la, kpi, alege ba diem a tom ka dila ale poom a weeni mɛ ayen baai ale a tom tuim ŋala chaab la, a tom ka tuimaŋsa.

ref: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
text: Dila nyiŋla, ni wanyi ka suik ate fi suok a dan nye wari a kaasi, fi bo wa buusa. Fi dan nye dila, fi ta ka kaasuŋ a jam fidek jigi dii nyiŋla, wie ŋaai ate fi ayen wa nye a kaasi la, fidek a tom ka ŋala dekdega.

ref: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
text: Tama abe seba kama ayen ku sum magsi ka Wen ta kaasuŋ a jam baai meena ale a tom dila la jigi.

ref: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
text: Alege fi dan bo baai ale a nye nyaŋa de la buusa alege fidek a tom ŋa, fi a poli ayen fi le baga chali be ate Wen kan nya fu a bo buusa?

ref: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
text: Yaa fi zɛri Wen nye maŋ kaai ale suiduŋ dii ale wa ale ŋman ta chichiiba ale fi diila kama, fi a poli ayen wa le kasim a nye ka dila a ta a cheŋ. Fi zɛ ayen Wen nye maŋka fi jigi a sak fu kama ayen fi basi fi tuimbaataŋa tomka?

ref: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
text: Ni tue kan wom. Ni sue be kan kaasi ale ni tuimbaataŋa. Ni a tom tuimbaata kama alege jaab kan daani ni, alege Wen suipuurumu ale wa wensie buusaŋa danni a dan paari ate wa ayen wa bo wensie buusa ale ni, wa sui le puuri ka nna yegayega ale ni ate wa te ni waalika.

ref: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
text: Da dila danni, Wen le tuni waai meena a magsi chaab ale ka ti wanyi wanyi ale tom diila.

ref: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
text: Baai meena ale ta chichiiba a tom tuimaŋsa a gisi zula ale nalim ale nyuvuri Wen jigi la, wa le te ba ka nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la.

ref: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
text: Alege baai ale a yaali badek nyaka mwuli ale a zɛri wensie suiku vaka ale kasim a tom tuimbaata daa meena la, Wen le basi ate wa suipuurumu a jam ba zuk.

ref: This proves that the conscience is like a law written in the human heart. And it will show whether we are forgiven or condemned,
text: Ba nyeka a sak kama ayen Wen ŋmarisi wa Sinsaŋŋa a nyo ka ba suiniima po. Ba popolaŋa mɛ ale a bo ba buusa a weeni a sak ba ase ba kaasi yaa ba an kaasiya.

ref: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
text: Nama dek abe seba Wen ale a yaali ayen ni a tom tuimaŋsa diila kama, dii nyiŋla ni zamsi Sinsaŋŋa po ayen fi lueri dii ale nala la a tom.

ref: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
text: Fi seba chak ayen, fi baga a chim nuru waai ale cheŋ be Wen suiku po la kpagi kama. Fi a nye ase ka bolim la a te baai ale bo legini po la.

ref: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
text: Fi a weeni ayen fi baga nuru baai ale ka betta ale bi paaluk la a sak kama. Fi be seba fi popo a chak ayen, fi ale ta Wen Sinsaŋŋa la, fi ta yam meena ale wensie meena kama.

ref: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
text: Nyaŋa de meena abe dan ka wensie ale fi waai ale a sak nuruba la, ka boa ate fi kan sak fi dega? Ti a sak nuruba a weeni ayen, <<Kan zu>>, alege fidek a zu?

ref: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
text: Fi ta zupagruk kama ale Wen Sinsaŋŋa, alege a kaasi ŋa. Kaasika de a basi ate Wen a nya chivie yaa wa kan nya?>>

ref: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
text: Ba be ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po kama ayen, << Baai ale kan daa Juuba la, a kaasi Wen yuei kama nama Juuma nyiŋ.>>

ref: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
text: Nama Juuma dan gebi ni yoaŋa ale a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa, ni yoaŋa gebika ta kiri kama. Alege ni dan a kaasi wa Sinsaŋŋa ni a nye ase ni an gebi ni yoaŋa kama la.

ref: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
text: Juuma ta nyuenta kama wie yegayega po a gaam baai ale kan daa Juuba la. Ni basi ate m liŋ weeni a sak ni ayen Wen jam pai wa wieŋa a nyo ka Juuma nisima po.

ref: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People

ref: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
text: Alege yɔgyɔgla de Wen a pai sak wa le wa nye dii ate nuruba a chim wayɔrisima nyam la kama. Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale Wen biisiteerɔma a biisi dila wari kama, alege ku ka wari a nye ale Moosis Sinsaŋŋa.

ref: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
text: Nurubiik meena abe tom kaasi kama, a yaa yalima ale Wen zulaŋa.

ref: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
text: Alege Wen tiirim niaka nyiŋ ate ti nya da tuesika a yaa chim wayɔrisima nyam Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ.

ref: God sent Christ to be our sacrifice. Christ offered his life's blood, so by faith in him we could come to God. And God did this to show that in the past he was right to be patient and forgive sinners. This also shows that God is right when he accepts people who have faith in Jesus.
text: Alege yɔgyɔgla de, Yeezu kummu nyiŋ ate Wen yaa nya nurubiik wabaataŋa zuk ayen ku sak ayen Wen ka nyemagsika nyɔnɔ. Ku be a sak kama ayen wa ka nyemagsika nyɔnɔ ate baai meena ale ta siaka ale Yeezu la, wa basi kama ate ba chim nyemagsika nyam.

ref: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.

ref: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!

ref: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.

text: Gebika de abe jam a sak kama ayen ka wa siaka ale Wen nyiŋ ale soa ate wa wi wa ayen wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ ale ge ate wa yaa gebi wa yoanni. Dila abe ale soa ate baai meena ale ta siaka ale Wen alege an gebi ba yoaŋa, ate Wen nye ate ba chim wayɔrisima nyam la, a baga a wi Abrayam ayen ba ko.

ref: This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised. The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
text: Baai mɛ ale gebi ba yoaŋa la a wi Abrayam ayen ba ko ase ba a nin ta siaka ale Wen ase Abrayam la, alege ate wa yaa gebi wa yoanni la.

ref: God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable.
text: Wen jam puulim kama ayen Abrayam ale wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa le jam soa ka tɛŋka meena. Ku be jam daa Abrayam ale jam va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa la nyiŋŋa. Ku jam ka Abrayam ale ta siaka ale Wen ate wa nye ate wa chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ la nyiŋ ale soa ate wa jam puulim dila.

ref: If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
text: Ku be dan ka nuru baai ale a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa la le ba soa tɛŋka, nurubiik siaka ale Wen ka kiri ya ate Wen puulim ka a chim kinla nyiŋ.

ref: Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all.
text: Ka boan ale soa ate Wen le nye ate ti chim wayɔrisima nyam ti siaka nyiŋŋa? Dii nyiŋ ale soa ate wa le nye dila la ale wa ale puulim ayen wa le niak ti wa niaka nyiŋla.
