ref: Your husband or wife who isn't a follower is made holy by having you as a partner. This also makes your children holy and keeps them from being unclean in God's sight.
text: Diila chorɔwa waai ale kan daa Kirisita biik la a welema kama wa ale bo ale wa powa la nyiŋ. Powa mɛ waai ale kan daa Kirisita biik la a welema kama wa ale bo ale wa chorɔwa la nyiŋ. Dan kan daa di bisaŋa a kan chim bi weleŋsa, alege ku ale ka diila ba ka bi weleŋsa.

ref: If your husband or wife isn't a follower of the Lord and decides to divorce you, then you should agree to it. You are no longer bound to that person. After all, God chose you and wants you to live at peace.
text: Alege ba waai dek ale kan daa Kirisita biik la a daa yaali ayen wa basi m wala, wa baga a basi kama. Kude po chorɔwa yaase powa baga a lueri kama, Wen a wi ni kama ayen ni boro ale suiyɔgni.

ref: And besides, how do you know if you will be able to save your husband or wife who isn't a follower? Obeying the Lord at All Times
text: Nama zɛ ayen powa nyiŋ wa chorɔwa ale baga a nya varibasika, yaase chorɔwa nyiŋ wa powa ale baga a nya varibasika.

ref: In every church I tell the people to stay as they were when the Lord Jesus chose them and God called them to be his own. Now I say the same thing to you.
text: Nuru meena abe boro a magsi chaab ale Wen ale te wa tiirim buui la, ale wa ale jam ka dii alege ate Wen a wi wa la. Juijui meena ate Kirisita bisa a tu la mi ale a sak ba diila ale la.

ref: If you are already circumcised, don't try to change it. If you are not circumcised, don't get circumcised.
text: Nuru waai a dan gebi wa yoari alege a chim Kirisita biik wa kan weeni ayen wa duisi a basi, waai abe dan kan gebi ya wa kan weeni ayen wa gebi.

ref: Being circumcised or uncircumcised isn't really what matters. The important thing is to obey God's commands.
text: Nuru a gebi wa yoari yaase wa an gebi ya ku daa wari ya, dii ale nye wari yegayega la ale fi a zuli Wen sinsaŋŋa.

ref: So don't try to change what you were when God chose you.
text: Waai meena abe ale jam ka dii alege ate Wen a wi fu la, be kan tagri.

ref: Are you a slave? Don't let that bother you. But if you can win your freedom, you should.
text: Fi jam ka yɔma alege ate Wen a wi fu la? Kan te ate ku a daani fu. Fi abe dan baga a nya suik a kan ŋma chim yɔma be pai suik kula a tom.

ref: When the Lord chooses slaves, they become his free people. And when he chooses free people, they become slaves of Christ.
text: Waai ale ka yɔma ate Naawen a wi wa la a ŋman daa yɔma, suik kula po waai mɛ ale kan daa yɔma ate Naawen a wi wa la a yaa chim ka Naawen yɔma.

ref: God paid a great price for you. So don't become slaves of anyone else.
text: Wen a da ni kama a tuni, dila nyiŋla ni ŋman daa nurubisa yɔmma.

ref: Stay what you were when God chose you. Unmarried People
text: M suata, waai meena a be va Wen ase wa le jam ka dii alege ate wa wi wa la.

ref: I don't know of anything the Lord said about people who have never been married. But I will tell you what I think. And you can trust me, because the Lord has treated me with kindness.
text: M ka sinsaga a nyini Naawen jigi a magsi chaab ale gbaŋ kaai ate ni ŋmarisi a te mu baai ale kan ta nipooba la wari ya, alege mi a yaali ayen m weeni ni ale m dek popola. M be ka waai ate Naawen a ta jiirim ale mu ale mariŋ mu.

ref: We are now going through hard times, and I think it is best for you to stay as you are.
text: Ti dan nya ku yaa le kasim tua dii nna yegayega la, mi a poli ayen nuru a dan deri boro dila ku le zunchoŋŋa.

ref: If you are married, stay married. If you are not married, don't try to get married.
text: Fi ta nipowa? Be kan yiak wa. Yaa fi ka nipowa? Be kan ŋman faari.

ref: It isn't wrong to marry, even if you have never been married before. But those who marry will have a lot of trouble, and I want to protect you from this.
text: Alege fi dan faari nipok, fi an nye wabiowa, nipok waai mɛ ale kan yali la a dan yali wa an nye wabiowa. Alege baai ale ta nipooba yaa chorɔba la a ta ka daanika nna yegayega. Mi abe a yaali ayen m kasi ni ka daanika de po.

ref: My friends, what I mean is that the Lord will soon come, and it won't matter if you are married or not.
text: M suata, mi a weeni ni kude kama dii nyiŋla ti yaa le bo da ŋaai po la an soa dii ya. A ta nyini yɔgyɔgla de a cheŋ baai ale ta nipooba abe boro nna se ba an poom faari nipooba la.

ref: It won't make any difference how much good you are getting from this world or how much you like it. This world as we know it is now passing away.
text: Baai mɛ abe le ta tɛŋka de zuk ŋanta la abe a nye nna se ba ka jaab la. Ale tɛŋka de ale ka dii yɔgyɔgla de nna, a za ka taam kama.

ref: I want all of you to be free from worry. An unmarried man worries about how to please the Lord.
text: M kan yaali ayen kude a daani ni. Nuru waai ale kan ta nipok la niŋ a bo ka Naawen tuimaŋa jigi, dii nyiŋla wa a yaali ayen wa a nye ate ka Naawen sui a peenti.

ref: But a married man has more worries. He must worry about the things of this world, because he wants to please his wife.
text: Alege nuru waai ale ta nipok la niŋ a bo ka tɛŋka de zuk wie jigi, dii nyiŋla wa a yaali ayen wa a nye ate ka wa powa sui a peenti,

ref: So he is pulled in two directions. Unmarried women and women who have never been married worry only about pleasing the Lord, and they keep their bodies and minds pure. But a married woman worries about the things of this world, because she wants to please her husband.
text: ale ta popola buye. Nipok waai yaase nipokbili dii ale kan yali la niŋ a bo ka Naawen tuimaŋa jigi, dii nyiŋla wa pai wadek meena a te Wen kama, alege nipok waai ale yali la niŋ bo ka tɛŋka de zuk wie jigi, dii nyiŋ la wa a yaali ayen wa a nye ate ka wa chorɔwa sui a peenti.

ref: What I am saying is for your own good—it isn't to limit your freedom. I want to help you to live right and to love the Lord above all else.
text: Mi a yaali ayen m maari ni kama, dila ale soa ate mi a weeni wieŋa de. Mi a kan yaali ayen m fɛ ni kama ale wieŋa de, alege mi a yaali ayen ni va ka Naawen nalimnyiini abe ni pai nidek meena a te wa.

ref: But suppose you are engaged to someone old enough to be married, and you want her so much that all you can think about is getting married. Then go ahead and marry. There is nothing wrong with that.
text: Baai ale ta nɔŋta a gomsi ayen ba yali chaab ale ŋman poli ayen ba basi chaab la, ka nidoawa a daa nye wa ase wa kɔrisa pagra la ate wa ŋma a poli ayen wa faari wa wa abe faari. Wabiok a ka kude po.

ref: But it is better to have self-control and to make up your mind not to marry.
text: Alege nuru waai ate ba kan fɛ wa alege ate ka wadek popola po a weeni ayen wa kan faari wa la, wa abe kan faari nipokbinni.

ref: It is perfectly all right to marry, but it is better not to get married at all.
text: Dila la waai ale faari la a nye ka wamaŋ alege waai ale kan faari la a zunchoŋ kama.

ref: A wife should stay married to her husband until he dies. Then she is free to marry again, but only to a man who is a follower of the Lord.
text: Nipok waai ale yali la a ka suik a ŋma yali ase wa chora ale tɔlim boro la, alege wa chorɔwa a dan kpi wa ta suik kama a yali ase nidoawa a nin ka Kirisita biik.

ref: However, I think I am obeying God's Spirit when I say she would be happier to stay single.
text: Mi jigi wa ta suipeentik kama ase wa a nin kan yali ya. Mi ale ta popola ŋaai la ale la, mi abe a poli ayen ka Wen Chiika ale a sak mu.

ref: In fact, people who think they know so much don't know anything at all.
text: Nuru waai abe ale a poli ayen wa seba wie la a zɛ jaaboa ase wadek ale a poli diila.

ref: But God has no doubts about who loves him.
text: Alege Wen a seba ka nuru waai ale a yaali wa la.

ref: Even though food is offered to idols, we know that none of the idols in this world are alive. After all, there is only one God.
text: Dila la ni ale bek ase ŋandiin tii ate ba pai a kaab bɔgta la, ni baga a dɛ ya la, ti meena seba ayen bɔgluk dek daa jaab waai ale vua alege tama seba ayen ka Wen yeŋ dekki ale boro.

ref: Many things in heaven and on earth are called gods and lords, but none of them really are gods or lords.
text: Bɔgta abe dan poom bo wenŋmazuk yaase tɛŋzuk de ate wena ale bɔgta a piisi a boro,

ref: We have only one God, and he is the Father. He created everything, and we live for him. Jesus Christ is our only Lord. Everything was made by him, and by him life was given to us.
text: alege ka Wen yeŋ dekki ale boro, wala abe le tama Ko. Wala abe ale jaab meena nyeerɔ, wala nyiŋ abe le tama boro. Yeezu Kirisita nyiini abe ale tama Naawen ate wa lala nyiŋ ate Wen a nye jaab meena. Wa lala nyiŋ abe le tama boro.

ref: Not everyone knows these things. In fact, many people have grown up with the belief that idols have life in them. So when they eat meat offered to idols, they are bothered by a weak conscience.
text: Alege daa waai meena ale seba wensieŋa de. Nuruba gela a malim bɔgta ka nna yegayega, a ta jam paari jinla ba dan dɛ ŋandiin tila chaab, ba a poli ayen bɔglukku ale soa ŋandiintaŋa. Ate ba popolaŋa a yaa daani ba. Ba nyiem yaa poli ayen ba ka nuru daŋtisa.

ref: But food doesn't bring us any closer to God. We are no worse off if we don't eat, and we are no better off if we do.
text: Ŋandiinta dɛka a kan basi ate ti a chim nuruba dek Wen jigiya, ti abe dan kan dɛ ya ti kan chim nuru kayaata.

ref: Don't cause problems for someone with a weak conscience, just because you have the right to eat anything.
text: Ni be kpesi nidek ate baai siaka ale pagra la nyeka a kan basi ate baai siaka ale kan pagra la a tom wabaata.

ref: You know all this, and so it doesn't bother you to eat in the temple of an idol. But suppose a person with a weak conscience sees you and decides to eat food that has been offered to idols.
text: Ase nuru waai popola ale a daani wa ale wieŋa de chaab la, a dan nya fi waai popola ale ka a daani fu ale bɔgta ŋanta dɛka la ale fi boro a dɛ bɔgta ŋandiinta ku kan te wa nyiŋbiiri ate wa maari a dɛ?

ref: When you sin by hurting a follower with a weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
text: Waai abe dan nye kaasi wa Kirisita biik choa, a kaasi wa popola mɛ, wa nye kaasi ka Kirisita dila.

ref: So if I hurt one of the Lord's followers by what I eat, I will never eat meat as long as I live.
text: Dila la mi a dan dɛ bɔgta ŋandiinta ate m suok a va dila nyiŋ a nye a kaasi Naawen, mi kan ŋma a dɛ bɔgta ŋandiinta, dii nyiŋla mi a kan yaali ayen wa nye wabiowa.

ref: I am free. I am an apostle. I have seen the Lord Jesus and have led you to have faith in him.
text: Mi nya varibasika kama, mi ŋman daa wabaata yɔma. Mi ka Yeezu tuimtomdɔ. Ni abe seba ayen Yeezu ti Naawenni a pai wadek a sak mi kama. Mi abe le mooli Wen wieŋa a sak ni ate ni nya varibasika.

ref: Others may think that I am not an apostle, but you are proof that I am an apostle to you.
text: Nuruba a dan poom a weeni ayen mi daa Yeezu tuimtomdɔ alege nama ale siak ayen mi ka wa tuimtomdɔ, ni ale ka Kirisita bisa la nyiŋ.

ref: that Barnabas and I have the right to our food and drink.
text: ) Wen niŋ abe bo ale ka niiga?

ref: We each have the right to marry one of the Lord's followers and to take her along with us, just as the other apostles and the Lord's brothers and Peter do.
text: Mi mɛ a ta suik a yaali nipok a ta wa nyiem ase Yeezu tuimtomdɔba mbala, ale Yeezu ti Naawenni suataŋa ale Sifas ale ta ba pooma a nyiem diila.

ref: Are we the only ones who have to support ourselves by working at another job?
text: Daa mi ale Banabas ale magsi ayen ti tom tidek a dɛ.

ref: Do soldiers pay their own salaries? Don't people who raise grapes eat some of what they grow? Don't shepherds get milk from their own goats?
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔba waai karo a tuni wa dega. Nuru waai mɛ abe le a kpa la a dɛ ka wa kpanni ŋanta. Naapeerik kaai ale a kasi niiga la a ta suik a dɛ ŋa biisim kama.

ref: I am not saying this on my own authority. The Law of Moses tells us not to muzzle an ox when it is grinding grain. But was God concerned only about an ox?
text: Ku be ŋmarisi a bo Moosis Sinsaŋŋa po kama ayen, <<Ni dan yik niiga a boro a fɔbi za ni kan bobi ŋa noaŋa.>> (Teerika

ref: No, he wasn't! He was talking about us. This was written in the Scriptures so that all who plow and all who grind the grain will look forward to sharing in the harvest.
text: Daa tama nyiŋ ate wa weeni dila? Wa abe ŋmarisi a te ka tama. Nuru waai abe le a kpa ale waai ale a che la a ta yiila kama ayen ba ale nya ba kpanni ŋanta.

ref: When we told the message to you, it was like planting spiritual seed. So we have the right to accept material things as our harvest from you.
text: Ti abe bori ka ŋan maŋsa ni suiniimaŋa po. Tama abe dan weeni ayen ni a te ti ŋanta ale ka tama mɛ nyuenta ale la, ku gaam ni te ka kama?

ref: If others have the right to do this, we have an even greater right. But we haven't used this right of ours. We are willing to put up with anything to keep from causing trouble for the message about Christ.
text: Nuruba ba chaab dan ta suik a yiili ŋanta ni jigi, tama a ta suik a gaam dila kama. Tama a ta suik kama a yiili ŋanta ni jigi alege tama an nye di, ti chiibi wie meena kama ayen ti kan nye wari ate di kaasi nuruba ate ba kan baga a mooli Kirisita Wamaŋsaŋa.

ref: Don't you know that people who work in the temple make their living from what is brought to the temple? Don't you know that a person who serves at the altar is given part of what is offered?
text: Ni seba ayen baai ale a tom Wen yenni po la a nya ba ŋandiintaŋa ka dula. Baai mɛ ale nye kaabka a te Wen la a nya ba charuku ka dula.

ref: In the same way, the Lord wants everyone who preaches the good news to make a living from preaching this message.
text: Suik kula po, Naawen a sak kama ayen baai ale a mooli Wen wieŋa la ba a tuni ba ba tuimaŋa nyiŋ.

ref: But I have never used these privileges of mine, and I am not writing this because I want to start now. I would rather die than have someone rob me of the right to take pride in this.
text: Alege mi an pai suik kude a yiili ŋanta ni jigi yaase mi a ŋmarisi gbaŋka de a pai suik kude a te mi dega. M dan kpi a zunchoŋ m le a nye kude. Mi a kan te nuru pai kude nyiŋ a valiŋ mi.

ref: I don't have any reason to brag about preaching the good news. Preaching is something God told me to do, and if I don't do it, I am doomed.
text: M ka suik a nak suinum mi ale a mooli Wen wamaŋsaŋa la nyiŋ ŋa. Ka Wen ale weeni ayen mu a tom. Ku abe le bie m jigi ka nna yegayega ase m nin kan mooli wa wamaŋsaŋa.

ref: If I preach because I want to, I will be paid. But even if I don't want to, it is still something God has sent me to do.
text: Ase dan ka mi dek ale lueri tuini a tom m ta suik kama ayen ba a tuni mu. Alege ku ka fifiok ayen m tom dii nyiŋla Wen ale te mu tuini de.

ref: What pay am I given? It is the chance to preach the good news free of charge and not to use the privileges that are mine because I am a preacher.
text: Boan tutuna abe le mi a nya? M tutunaŋa meena ale m baga a mooli Wen wamaŋsaŋa abe m kan weeni ayen ba tuni mu m tuimaŋa nyiŋ ŋa. M daa nye kude m kan pai suik kuui meena ate mi deri ta la ayen m ka waai ale a mooli Wen wamaŋsaŋa la.

ref: I am not anyone's slave. But I have become a slave to everyone, so I can win as many people as possible.
text: Mi daa nuru waai yɔma alege mi a pai m dek kama a chim waai meena yɔma ayen m baga a mooli Wen wamaŋsaŋa ate nuruba yegayega a nya varibasika.

ref: When I am with the Jews, I live like a Jew to win Jews. They are ruled by the Law of Moses, and I am not. But I live by the Law to win them.
text: Mi a dan boro a mooli Wen wamaŋsaŋa a te Juuma, mi a nye m dek ase ka Juu la, ate ba baga a nya varibasika. Ku daa fifiowa ayen m va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa, alege m dan boro a mooli a te baai ale a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa la, mi a nye m dek ase m ka waai ale a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa la, ate ba baga a nya varibasika.

ref: And when I am with people who are not ruled by the Law, I forget about the Law to win them. Of course, I never really forget about the law of God. In fact, I am ruled by the law of Christ.
text: M dan boro a mooli a te baai ale kan daa Juuba la, mi a nye m dek ka nna ase m daa Juu la ate ba baga a nya varibasika. Kude a kan sak kama ayen m kan va Wen sinsaŋŋa, mi a va Kirisita sinsaŋŋa kama.

ref: I do all this for the good news, because I want to share in its blessings. A Race and a Fight
text: Wieŋa de meena mi a nye ka Wen wamaŋsaŋa nyiŋ ayen m baga a nya niauŋ ku po.

ref: You know that many runners enter a race, and only one of them wins the prize. So run to win!
text: Nuru baai ale a chali la meena a chali kama alege wanyi ale a tuesi deerɔwa jaamu. Ni abe basi ate ni wensuiku po boka a nala ase chalaŋa ale ka diila ate nama mɛ a tuesi jaab dila nyiŋ.

ref: I don't run without a goal. And I don't box by beating my fists in the air.
text: Dila ale soa ate mi a kasim a chali yɔrr ayen m nueri la. Dila mɛ ale soa ate mi a kan chubi a basi du la.

ref: I keep my body under control and make it my slave, so I won't lose out after telling the good news to others.
text: Mi a nak m nyiŋka kama ayen ka girigi ate m baga a yik ka ŋmapi, ate m dan mooli Wen wamaŋsaŋa a te nuruba abe ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ Wen kan zɛri mi dega.

ref: All of them also ate the same spiritual food
text: Ba meena a jam dɛ ka wenzuk ŋandiinta

ref: and drank the same spiritual drink, which flowed from the spiritual rock that followed them. That rock was Christ.
text: ale nyu nyiam piuŋ kuui ate Wen a jam te ba la po. Piuŋ kula abe jam ka Yeezu dek.

ref: But most of them did not please God. So they died, and their bodies were scattered all over the desert.
text: Alege dila meena Wen sui an jam peenti ale ba. Ba meena a jam kpi wari ka gɔnni po.

ref: They worshiped idols, just as the Scriptures say, “The people sat down to eat and drink. Then they got up to dance around.” So don't worship idols.
text: yaase ti a kaab bɔgta ase ba ale jam a nye diila. Ase ku le ŋmarisi ayen, <<Nuruma a jam kali ale ka chaab a dɛ ale a nyu ale yiti a boro a gɔk.>> (Nyinika

ref: Some of you say, “We can do whatever we want to!” But I tell you not everything may be good or helpful.
text: Nuruba a weeni kama, ayen ti baga a nye dii meena kama. Ku ka wensie, alege daa wieŋa meena ale nala. Ti baga a nye dii meena kama, alege daa wieŋa meena ale a maari ti.

ref: And don't try to test Christ, as some of them did and were later bitten by poisonous snakes.
text: Ti be kan nye Naawen a nya ase ba gela ale jam a nye dii ate Naawen a jam basi ate wiiŋa a dom ba a ko la.

ref: Don't even grumble, as some of them did and were killed by the destroying angel.
text: Ti be kaa fɔbili ase ba ale jam a fɔbili dii ate Wen a basi ate wa maarɔwa a ko ba la.

ref: These things happened to them as a warning to us. All this was written in the Scriptures to teach us who live in these last days.
text: Wieŋa de meena abe nye kama ayen ŋa sak ti, nuruba abe ŋmarisi kama mɛ ayen ŋa a kaam ti. Yɔgyɔgla de ate ti boro la tɛŋka a yaa moata ka kpeglimka.

ref: Even if you think you can stand up to temptation, be careful not to fall.
text: Nuru waai abe le a poli ayen wa siaka a pagra la, a kpesi wadek ate wa kan lo.

ref: You are tempted in the same way that everyone else is tempted. But God can be trusted not to let you be tempted too much, and he will show you how to escape from your temptations.
text: Nyenya kaai meena ate ni a tu la, mɛ dek a jam nuruba jigi kama. Alege a magsi chaab ale Wen ale puulim la, wa kan basi ate nyenya kaai ate ni kan baga a pik la a jam ni jigiya. Diipo ate ni a tu nyenyaka la, wa ale te ni pagrim ate ni baga a pik, abe wa te suik ate ni nyini nyenyaka po a nyini.

ref: My friends, you must keep away from idols.
text: Dila nyiŋ, m doaba, ni kan ta wari a nye ale bɔgta kaab ka.

ref: I am speaking to you as people who have enough sense to know what I am talking about.
text: Mi biisi a te ka yam nyam, ni bo mi ale weeni diila buusa.

ref: When we drink from the cup we ask God to bless, isn't that sharing in the blood of Christ? When we eat the bread we break, isn't that sharing in the body of Christ?
text: Kirisitawa ŋandiintaŋa ate ti nyiem a pai beerika a te Wen jiam la, ti dan nyu ku a nye ase ti maari ka chaab a nyu wa ziimu la. Boroboroku ate ti yik a ŋmari la ti dan ŋɔbi, ku a nye ase ti maari ka chaab a ŋɔbi wa nyiŋka la.

ref: By sharing in the same loaf of bread, we become one body, even though there are many of us.
text: Dii nyiŋla boroboroku ka kunyi, ti meena abe dan poom piisi diidii ya ti ka bunyi ase nyiŋ yeŋ la, diila ti meena a ŋɔbi ka boroborok yeŋ.

ref: Aren't the people of Israel sharing in the worship when they gather around the altar and eat the sacrifices offered there?
text: Ni abe nya Izirali demma ate baai a jam maari chaab a dɛ ŋan baai ate ba pai kaab te Wen la ka bunyi.

ref: Am I saying that either the idols or the food sacrificed to them is anything at all?
text: Mi abe a weeni kama ayen bɔgluk yaase ŋandiin tii ate ba pai kaab bɔgluk la daa ŋanta dega?

ref: No, I am not! This food is really sacrificed to demons and not to God. I don't want you to have anything to do with demons.
text: Aaya, mi a weeni kama ayen ŋan baai ate ba pai a kaab bɔgta la, ba kaab a te ka chichirisa daa Wen ya. Mi abe kan yaali ayen nama ale chichirisa a ta wari a nye ale chaaba.

ref: You cannot drink from the cup of demons and still drink from the Lord's cup. You cannot eat at the table of demons and still eat at the Lord's table.
text: Ku an magsi ni a nyu Naawen beerik po ale ŋmaa nyu chichirisa beerik po, ni an magsi ni kali a dɛ Naawen ŋandiinta ale ŋman kali a dɛ chichirisa ŋandiinta.

ref: We would make the Lord jealous if we did this. And we are not stronger than the Lord. Always Honor God
text: Yaa ti a yaali ayen ti basi ate Naawen a ta ka nyuri ya? Ti abe seba kama ayen ti an pagra a gaam wa.

ref: However, when you buy meat in the market, go ahead and eat it. Keep your conscience clear by not asking where the meat came from.
text: Ni baga a da ŋandiin tii meena ale bo yaba la kama a dɛ ale kan begi. Ŋandiin tila chaab dɛka an magsi ku a daani ni popola.

ref: The Scriptures say, “The earth and everything in it belong to the Lord.”
text: <<Naawen ale soa tɛŋka ale ka jaab meena.>> (Yiila

ref: If an unbeliever invites you to dinner, and you want to go, then go. Eat whatever you are served. Don't cause a problem for someone's conscience by asking where the food came from.
text: Ase baai ale kan daa Kirisita bisa la a dan wi fu ayen fi jam dɛ ŋandiinta ale ba, ŋandiin tii ate ba pai a zaani fi niŋ la kan begi, popola daani ka nyiŋ.

ref: But if you are told it has been sacrificed to idols, don't cause a problem by eating it. I don't mean a problem for yourself, but for the one who told you. Why should my freedom be limited by someone else's conscience?
text: daa fidek popola alege nwala popola nyiŋ. Ase nuru waai ale bek ayen ka boa ale soa ate mi ale ta suik a nye diila waai siaka ale kan pagra la a baga a kasi mi ate mi a kan nye.

ref: If I give thanks for what I eat, why should anyone accuse me of doing wrong?
text: Nuru waai abe ka suik a bo a mini mi ŋandiin tii ate mi a te Wen jiam ti nyiŋla.

ref: When you eat or drink or do anything else, always do it to honor God.
text: Dila la, wa dii meena ate fi a nye, fi a dɛ yaase fi a nyu, be a nye ate ku te Wen zula.

ref: Don't cause problems for Jews or Greeks or anyone else who belongs to God's church.
text: Ni kan basi ate ni nyeka a basi ate Juuba yaase baai ale kan daa Juuba la yaase Kirisita bisaŋa a tom wabiowa.

ref: You must follow my example, as I follow the example of Christ. Rules for Worship
text: Ni abe a tomsi mi ale a nye diila, ase mi ale a tomsi Kirisita diila.

ref: I am proud of you, because you always remember me and obey the teachings I gave you.
text: Mi a pak ni kama, dii nyiŋla ni ale kasim a teeri m wie la ale a va sinsak ŋaai ate m sak ni la.

ref: Now I want you to know that Christ is the head of all men, and a man is the head of a woman. But God is the head of Christ.
text: Alege mi a yaali kama ayen ni miŋ ayen Kirisita a ta pagrim kama nuru meena zuk, ate chora a ta pagrim wa pok zuk, ate Wen a ta pagrim Kirisita zuk.

ref: This means that any man who prays or prophesies with something on his head brings shame to his head.
text: Dila nidoa waai a dan boro a puusi yaase wa a tuesi biik Wen jigi a biisi a te nuru boari suŋsuŋ ale vuk zutɔk, ku a te Yeezu Kirisita ka chivie.

ref: But any woman who prays or prophesies without something on her head brings shame to her head. In fact, she may as well shave her head.
text: Nipok waai mɛ a dan boro a puusi yaase wa a tuesi biik Wen jigi a biisi a te, nuru boari suŋsuŋ alege an bobi bobik ku a te wa chorɔwa ka chivie, wa ale nipok waai ale chiiri wa zuk la ka bunyi.

ref: A woman should wear something on her head. It is a disgrace for a woman to shave her head or cut her hair. But if she refuses to wear something on her head, let her cut off her hair.
text: Nipowa abe dan kan bobi zuk bobiga, wa baga a che wa zuisaŋa kama. Ku abe ale ka chivie ate nipok a che wa zuisa yaase wa chiiri si la, wa kasim pai bobik a bobi wa zukku.

ref: Men were created to be like God and to bring honor to God. This means a man should not wear anything on his head. Women were created to bring honor to men.
text: Nidoa an magsi wa bobi wa zuwa dii nyiŋla Wen a nye wa ase ka wadek la ate wa a sak Wen zulaŋa. Alege nipok a sak ka nidoa zulaŋa,

ref: It was the woman who was made from a man, and not the man who was made from a woman.
text: Daa nipok nyipik kobi ate Wen a pai nye nidoa, alege ka nidoa nyipik kobi ate Wen a pai nye nipok.

ref: He wasn't created for her. She was created for him.
text: Wen an nye nidoa ka nipok nyiŋŋa, alege wa nye nipok ka nidoa nyiŋ.

ref: And so, because of this, and also because of the angels, a woman ought to wear something on her head, as a sign of her authority.
text: Dila ale soa ate nipok a magsi ayen wa pai bobik a bobi wa zukku ate ku sak ayen wa ta suik a puusi ale a tuesi biik Wen jigi a biisi a te, ate Wen maarɔma a nya ayen wa ta suik.

ref: As far as the Lord is concerned, men and women need each other.
text: Naawen nyiŋ nipok an soa wa dega ate nidoa mɛ an soa wa dega.

ref: It is true that the first woman came from a man, but all other men have been given birth by women. Yet God is the one who created everything.
text: Wen abe le pai nidoa nyipik kobi a nye nipok la, ku ka dila ate nipok a yaa biak nidoa. Wen abe le nye jaabuuri meena a basi tɛŋka zuk.

ref: Ask yourselves if it is proper for a woman to pray without something on her head.
text: Nama dek a poli nya ase ku magsi ayen nipok a puusi a te Wen nuru boari suŋsuŋ ate jaab an lik wa zukku?

ref: But long hair is a beautiful way for a woman to cover her head.
text: alege nipok jigi ku ka nalim. Wen a te wa zuwɔŋsaŋa kama ayen si a lik wa zukku.

ref: This is how things are done in all of God's churches, and this is why none of you should argue about what I have said. Rules for the Lord's Supper
text: Alege waai a dan ka a siak mi ale weeni diila, mi ale ta dii ayen m weeni la ale tama yaase Wen nuruma tigsuŋku a ŋman ka nyeela ŋa chaab a magsi chaab ale Wen puusika.

ref: Your worship services do you more harm than good. I am certainly not going to praise you for this.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ate mi a yaali ayen m weeni diila, m kan ŋman pak ni, dii nyiŋla ni ale a tu chaab la a kan niak ni alege a kaasi ni kama.

ref: I am told you can't get along with each other when you worship, and I am sure that some of what I have heard is true.
text: Nuruba abe weeni mu kama ayen ni a poori ka chaab a tu. Mi abe seba ayen wensie a bo ku po kama.

ref: You are bound to argue with each other, but it is easy to see which of you have God's approval.
text: Ku be daa chichama, poorika a bo ni suŋsuŋ kama ayen ku basi ate ba seba baai ale sum ta siaka la.

ref: You even start eating before everyone gets to the meeting, and some of you go hungry, while others get drunk.
text: Ni dan boro a yaali ayen ni dɛ, m ba ale deri a kpabi a dɛ ale a nyu ale kan limisi m ba, ate baai a chak alege baai kom a ta ba.

ref: The Lord meant that when you eat this bread and drink from this cup, you tell about his death until he comes.
text: Kude kiri abe le diipo meena ni dan boro a ŋɔbi boroboroku de ale a nyu beerika de po, ni kasim a mooli Yeezu ti Naawenni kummu wie ate wa taam ga jam.

ref: If you fail to understand that you are the body of the Lord, you will condemn yourselves by the way you eat and drink.
text: Ate waai a dan kan miŋ Naawen nyiŋka kiriya ale ŋɔbi boroboroku, a nyu beerika po wa ta ka buusa boka a jam wadek jigi.

ref: After the meal, Jesus took a cup of wine in his hands and said, “This is my blood, and with it God makes his new agreement with you. Drink this and remember me.”
text: Ba ale nueri junɔi ŋandiinta la, Yeezu yaa pai beerik, a weeni ayen, beerika de ka mi nɔiyeŋ paalika ziimu. Diipo meena ni dan boro a nyu, ni be a teeri m wari.

ref: I have already told you what the Lord Jesus did on the night he was betrayed. And it came from the Lord himself. He took some bread in his hands.
text: Sinsak ŋaai ate mi a sak ni nna ka Naawen sinsaga, ayen yok kuui ate Judas a bobri a pai Yeezu ti Naawenni da la, yok kula dek ate Yeezu a yaa pai boroborok,

ref: Then after he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is given for you. Eat this and remember me.”
text: a yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi nyiŋka ale nna ate mi a pai kaab a te ni. Ni be kasim a nye nna a teeri m wari.>>

ref: But if you eat the bread and drink the wine in a way that isn't worthy of the Lord, you sin against his body and blood.
text: Ku be ale ka diila nuru waai a dan ŋɔbi Naawen boroboroku ale nyu wa beerika po ale biem ku kan te Naawen zula. Dila wa be nye ka wabiok a kaasi Yeezu ti Naawenni nyiŋka ale wa ziimu.

ref: This is why you must examine the way you eat and drink.
text: Dila nyiŋla waai meena nyiem be kpesi nya wadek a magsi abe wa ge ŋɔbi boroboroku abe wa nyu beerika po.

ref: This is why many of you are sick and weak and why a lot of others have died.
text: Dila nyiŋ abe le ni ba yega a yuak ale wobsa ate yega mɛ va dila nyiŋ a kpi.

ref: If we carefully judge ourselves, we won't be punished.
text: Ti nyiem abe dan dɛ niŋ a kpesi tidek a magsi Wen a kan bo ti buusa.

ref: But when the Lord judges and punishes us, he does it to keep us from being condemned with the rest of the world.
text: Alege Naawen a bo ti buusa kama ale a namsi ti ate kula kan basi ate wa kaasi tɛŋka meena a maa gum ti du.

ref: My dear friends, you should wait until everyone gets there before you start eating.
text: Dila la, m suata, ni nyiem a dan tu chaab ayen ni dɛ Naawen ŋandiintaŋa, ni be limisi chaab.

ref: If you really are hungry, you can eat at home. Then you won't condemn yourselves when you meet together. After I arrive, I will instruct you about the other matters.
text: Kom abe dan ta waai wa dɛ yeri abe wa ge jam. Ate ni ale tu chaab a nye diila, Wen kan bo ni buusa. M dan jam ni jigi, wa yonaŋa buuni m ni nye ŋa a magsi.

ref: I want you to remember that before you became followers of the Lord, you were led in all the wrong ways by idols that cannot even talk.
text: Nama abe zɛ ayen ni ale jam kan ta siaka ale Wen la, ni jam bɛ suiku kama ale ni ale a kaab bɔgta ate ti ka nyuvuri la.

ref: Now I want you to know that if you are led by God's Spirit, you will say that Jesus is Lord, and you will never curse Jesus.
text: Mi a yaali ayen ni seba ayen nuru waai ate Wen Chiika a bo ale wa la an baga a ka a te Yeezu. Nuru waai abe m baga a weeni ayen Yeezu ka Naawen ya, ka Wen Chiika a nin te wa suik.

ref: There are different kinds of spiritual gifts, but they all come from the same Spirit.
text: Chiika tiiritaŋa ka nna tɔgatɔga, alege ka Chiik yeŋka ale a te.

ref: and we can each do different things. Yet the same God works in all of us and helps us in everything we do.
text: Sebika ka tɔgatɔga ate nuruba a tom a te Naawen alege ka Naawen ale a te sebi kala waai meena ate ba a tom a te wa.

ref: Some of us can speak with wisdom, while others can speak with knowledge, but these gifts come from the same Spirit.
text: Wen Chiika a te waai yam. Chiik yeŋka mɛ a te waai sebika.

ref: To others the Spirit has given great faith or the power to heal the sick
text: Chiik yeŋka la mɛ ale te waai siaka. Ale a te waai mɛ tebika.

ref: or the power to work mighty miracles. Some of us are prophets, and some of us recognize when God's Spirit is present. Others can speak different kinds of languages, and still others can tell what these languages mean.
text: Chiika a te waai mɛ wakperikaliisa pagrim. A basi ate waai a tuesi biik Wen jigi a biisi a te. A basi ate waai mɛ a gaari chiisa tɔgatɔga. A basi ate waai mɛ a baga a biisi bichaŋsa, a basi ate waai mɛ a weeni bichaŋsa kie.

ref: But it is the Spirit who does all this and decides which gifts to give to each of us. One Body with Many Parts
text: Alege ka chiik yeŋ kala dek ale a tom dila meena, ka ale a yaali diila. Ka a te waai meena tiirimu ka tɔgatɔga.

ref: The body of Christ has many different parts, just as any other body does.
text: Yeezu Kirisita a nye ase ka nurubiik nyiŋ ale ka diila alege ta kabta tɔgatɔga. Ka ta ka kabta tɔgatɔga alege be ka nyiŋ yeŋ ka la.

ref: Some of us are Jews, and others are Gentiles. Some of us are slaves, and others are free. But God's Spirit baptized each of us and made us part of the body of Christ. Now we each drink from that same Spirit.
text: Ku be ka dila tama jigi, ti ka Juuba yoo, ti daa Juuba yoo, yɔm yaase daa yɔm yoo ti maa chaab tuesi ka so yeŋ ale chiik yeŋka. Wen abe basi ate ka chiik kala a bo ti suiniimaŋa po.

ref: Our bodies don't have just one part. They have many parts.
text: Diila nyiŋka dek daa kauk yeoŋŋoa alege ka kabta yegayega.

ref: Suppose a foot says, “I'm not a hand, and so I'm not part of the body.” Wouldn't the foot still belong to the body?
text: Ase naŋtuoku dan weeni ayen ku ale kan daa nisa la nyiŋ, ku maa daa nyiŋka po, kula a kan basi ate ku kan maara chim nyiŋka po.

ref: Or suppose an ear says, “I'm not an eye, and so I'm not part of the body.” Wouldn't the ear still belong to the body?
text: Ase tuini a dan weeni, ayen, di ale kan daa num la, di maa daa nyiŋka po, kula a kan basi ate di kan maara chim nyiŋka po.

ref: If our bodies were only an eye, we couldn't hear a thing. And if they were only an ear, we couldn't smell a thing.
text: Ase nyiŋka meena daam dan ka num, bu le nye ka sɛ a wom? Ka daam abe dan ka tuiri, di nye ka sɛ a wom nyummoa?

ref: But God has put all parts of our body together in the way that he decided is best.
text: Ku be le ka diila, Wen a nye nyiŋka kama ate ka ta kabta tɔgatɔga ase wadek ale a yaali diila.

ref: A body isn't really a body, unless there is more than one part.
text: Dila la, nyiŋ be ti karo ase ka a nin ka kauk yeoŋ nyiini.

ref: It takes many parts to make a single body.
text: Ku be le ka diila, kabtaŋa a piisi kama alege ka nyiŋ yeŋka la.

ref: That's why the eyes cannot say they don't need the hands. That's also why the head cannot say it doesn't need the feet.
text: Dila nyiŋla, nummu a kan baga a weeni nisaŋa, ayen bu kan yaali si. Yaase zukku a baga a weeni naŋsaŋa ayen ku kan yaali si.

ref: In fact, we cannot get along without the parts of the body that seem to be the weakest.
text: Nyiŋka kab tii ate tama a poli ayen kab tila a wobsa la a dan kan karo ti kan baga a nye wari ya.

ref: but we don't have to be modest about other parts. God put our bodies together in such a way that even the parts that seem the least important are valuable.
text: Kab tila mɛ, kab tii ale nala la a kan yaali. Wen dek abe le nye nyiŋka diila, wa nye kama ayen tama ale a poli ayen kab tii ka tuilum la a nya zula.

ref: He did this to make all parts of the body work together smoothly, with each part caring about the others.
text: Wen abe nye kude kama ayen nyiŋka kabta tɔgatɔga a kan poori chaaba alege a nye magsi a boro.

ref: If one part of our body hurts, we hurt all over. If one part of our body is honored, the whole body will be happy.
text: Ase nyiŋ kauk kunyi a daa nam, kab yontaŋa mɛ a maara a nam kama. Kauk kunyi a dan nya zula kab yontaŋa mɛ maara nya ka masim.

ref: Together you are the body of Christ. Each one of you is part of his body.
text: Ni meena abe a nye ase ka Yeezu nyiŋka la, ni meena wanyi wanyi abe ka wa nyiŋka kabta.

ref: First, God chose some people to be apostles and prophets and teachers for the church. But he also chose some to work miracles or heal the sick or help others or be leaders or speak different kinds of languages.
text: Kirisita bisaŋa po Wen a te waai meena wa tomka jigi kama. Wa piilim ale ka tuimtomdɔba, a pai saŋ biisiteerɔba, butawa sagrɔba. A yaa pai saŋ wakperikaliisa, a pai saŋ tebika tiirita, a pai saŋ maarɔba, a pai saŋ niŋdeerɔba, a pai saŋ baai ale a biisi bichaŋsa la.

ref: Not everyone is an apostle. Not everyone is a prophet. Not everyone is a teacher. Not everyone can work miracles.
text: Ba meena daa tuimtomdɔba yaase biisiteerɔba yaase sagrɔba yaase baai ale a tom wakperikaliisa.

ref: Not everyone can heal the sick. Not everyone can speak different kinds of languages. Not everyone can tell what these languages mean.
text: Ba meena ka tebika tiirita yaase ba a biisi bichaŋsa yaase ba a weeni bi chaŋsa kie.

ref: I want you to desire the best gifts. So I will show you a much better way.
text: Ni be pii nyiŋ ate ni nya tiirim tii ale ta tuilum la. M be le sak ni suimaŋka dek ni ale ni nye diila.

ref: What if I could speak all languages of humans and even of angels? If I did not love others, I would be nothing more than a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal.
text: Mi dan poom baga a biisi tɛŋzuk de ale wenŋmazuk biisaŋa meena ale kan yaali nuruba ku a nye ase m biisi a nuem kama nna ase lɔŋi la yaase guŋgoŋ la.

ref: What if I could prophesy and understand all mysteries and all knowledge? And what if I had faith that moved mountains? I would be nothing, unless I loved others.
text: M be dan poom baga mɛ a mooli Wen wanni nalimnyiini, ale seba, a baga a miŋ Wen wa wasusuŋŋa meena, ale ta siaka yegayega a baga a weeni guuta ayen ti voori a yiti ga duak jigi yoŋ, alege ka yaalika ale nuruba m ka kiriya.

ref: What if I gave away all that I owned and let myself be burned alive? I would gain nothing, unless I loved others.
text: M dan pai m ŋanta meena a chari nuruba ale basi ate ba ju mu ale bolim alege ka yaalika ale nuruba ku kan maari mu.

ref: rude. Love isn't selfish or quick tempered. It doesn't keep a record of wrongs that others do.
text: fi dan a yaali nuruba fi kan ta tukpariya yaase butuemmoa yaase suipuurummoa, fi dan a yaali nuruba fi kan kasim a teeri ba ale nye fu kaasi dii ya.

ref: Love never fails! Everyone who prophesies will stop, and unknown languages will no longer be spoken. All that we know will be forgotten.
text: Ku be le ka diila, yaalika a kan kpegli. Ba dan poom a mooli Wen wanni di kan beni, a biisi bi chaŋsa ku le kpeglim, ba ale seba nna yegayega alege seba kala ale taam.

ref: We don't know everything, and our prophecies are not complete.
text: Diila te seba ka gela ale a mooli gela,

ref: But what is perfect will someday appear, and what isn't perfect will then disappear.
text: alege wamaŋka a dan jam, dii ale kan daa wamaŋ la ale muriŋ be.

ref: When we were children, we thought and reasoned as children do. But when we grew up, we quit our childish ways.
text: Diipo ate mi a jam ka biik la, mi jam ta ka bimbain biik ale bimbain popola alege yɔgyɔgla de ate mi a pak la, mi yaa basi bimbain nyeka kama.

ref: Now all we can see of God is like a cloudy picture in a mirror. Later we will see him face to face. We don't know everything, but then we will, just as God completely understands us.
text: Dii ate ti a nya yɔgyɔgla de nna a nye ase ka nyaasuŋ po ate ti a nya la. Ti be kan nya a chagi. Alege ku le jam diipo ate ti seba Wen chak abe ti miŋ wie meena.

ref: For now there are faith, hope, and love. But of these three, the greatest is love.
text: Ku abe le ka dii nna, wie ŋata ale tali. Wa ŋala abe le siaka ale yiila ale yaalika alege wieŋa de ŋatawa dii ale gaam la ale yaalika.

ref: Love should be your guide. Be eager to have the gifts that come from the Holy Spirit, especially the gift of prophecy.
text: Yaalika ka tiirim kpiem, alege mi an ŋma a biisi bula wie. Alege ku nala a magsi kama ayen ni ta Chiika tiiritaŋa. Tiiritaŋa de po buui ale nye wari nna yegayega ale buui ate fi baga a mooli Wen biika la.

ref: If you speak languages that others don't know, God will understand what you are saying, though no one else will know what you mean. You will be talking about mysteries that only the Spirit understands.
text: Nuru waai ale a biisi bichaŋ la, a kan biisi a te nuruba, wa biisi a te ka Wen, dii nyiŋla waai kan miŋ ka kiriya. Ka wensie wa susuga ate wa va Wen Chiika pagrim nyiŋ a biisi.

ref: But when you prophesy, you will be understood, and others will be helped. They will be encouraged and made to feel better.
text: Alege waai ale a mooli Wen biika la a biisi a te ka nuruba ale a maari ba, ale a te ba nyiŋbiiri ale a te ba suiyɔgni.

ref: By speaking languages that others don't know, you help only yourself. But by prophesying you help everyone in the church.
text: Nuru waai abe le a biisi bichaŋ ka la a maari ka wadek, alege waai ale a mooli Wen biik a te nuruma la a maari ka Kirisita bisaŋa meena.

ref: I am glad for you to speak unknown languages, although I prefer that you would prophesy. In fact, prophesying does much more good than speaking unknown languages, unless someone can help the church by explaining what you mean.
text: Mi a yaali ayen ni meena ate a biisi ka bi chaŋsa ale ŋman goanti a yaali ayen ni ta ka tiirim buui ate ni baga a mooli Wen biika la. Diila waai ale a mooli Wen biika la a gaam waai ale a biisi bi chaŋsa la kama. Be nin ka waai a nin weeni dii ate wa biisi la kiri ate ku maari Kirisita bisaŋa meena.

ref: My friends, what good would it do, if I came and spoke unknown languages to you and didn't explain what I meant? How would I help you, unless I told you what God had shown me or gave you some knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
text: M suata, mi abe dan jam ni jigi a biisi bichaŋ a te ni, ni kan nya nyuenta ku po. Ka Wen a nin pai wari a sak mu ayen m weeni ni yaase wa pai sebika a te mu ayen m pai sak ni yaase biik a nyini wa jigi ayen m biisi a te ni yaase sinsaga ate m sak ni.

ref: If all musical instruments sounded alike, how would you know the difference between a flute and a harp?
text: Ase paampuuŋ yaase kpanuŋ nna, nuruba dan ka a peeri yaase ba a nak nalimnyiini, baai ale a wom la ale nye ka sɛ a seba ba ale a keri yi diila.

ref: This is how it is when you speak unknown languages. If no one can understand what you are talking about, you will only be talking to the wind.
text: Ku abe ka dila dekdega, nuruba a kan miŋ fi ale a biisi diila kiriya ase fi ale a biisi bichaŋ ŋa. Dila fi a biisi a basi ka vioku po.

ref: When we speak languages that others don't know, we should pray for the power to explain what we mean.
text: Nuru waai ale a biisi bichaŋ la abe a puusi a te Wen ate wa te wa tiirim buui ate wa ale baga a biisi wa ale weeni diila kiri.

ref: For example, if I use an unknown language in my prayers, my spirit prays but my mind is useless.
text: Ase m dan puusi a biisi bichaŋ m chiika mɛ a puusi kama alege ku kan maari m popolaŋa.

ref: Then what should I do? There are times when I should pray with my spirit, and times when I should pray with my mind. Sometimes I should sing with my spirit, and at other times I should sing with my mind.
text: Ku abe dan ka dila, mi m nye ka sɛ? Mi ale kasim a puusi ale ka m chiika ale m popolaŋa, abe mi a yi yiila mɛ ale m chiika ale m popolaŋa.

ref: Suppose some strangers are in your worship service, when you are praising God with your spirit. If they don't understand you, how will they know to say, “Amen”?
text: Ase waai a dan boro a puusi a te Wen jiam ale chiika nyiini nuru waai a dan maa bo tuka po wa ale nye ka sɛ a weeni ayen, <<Ku be nye dila?>> Suik karo ate wa baga a miŋ wa ale a weeni diila.

ref: You may be worshiping God in a wonderful way, but no one else will be helped.
text: Wen jiamu teka a dan poom magsi, nuru m wala a kan bola a nya maarika.

ref: I thank God that I speak unknown languages more than any of you.
text: Mi a nye Wen jiam kama diila mi a biisi bichaŋka a gaam ni meena kama.

ref: But words that make sense can help the church. This is why in church I would rather speak five words that make sense than to speak
text: Alege Kirisita bisa tigsuŋku po mi a dan biisi wie ŋanu a sak nuruba ate ba miŋ a zunchoŋ m le biisi bichaŋka wie tusidi.

ref: My friends, stop thinking like children. Think like mature people and be as innocent as tiny babies.
text: M suata ni kan ta bimbain popola, ni a poli ase baai ale pak la. Alege biem jigi ni a nye ase buluata la ate ba zɛ biem diema la.

ref: In the Scriptures the Lord says, “I will use strangers who speak unknown languages to talk to my people. They will speak to them in foreign languages, but still my people won't listen to me.”
text: Ku ŋmarisi Sinsaŋŋa po ayen, Wen a weeni ayen, <<M le basi ate nuru baai ale a biisi bichaŋsa la ate ba biisi a te m nuruma. M le basi ate nicham pai ba noa a biisi a te ba, alege m nuruma a kan wom.>> (Azaya

ref: Languages others don't know may mean something to unbelievers, but not to the Lord's followers. Prophecy, on the other hand, is for followers, not for unbelievers.
text: Dila la tiirim buui ate fi baga a biisi bichaŋ ka la a sak ka daana waai ale kan daa Kirisita biik la jigi, alege tiirim buui ate fi baga a chɔgsi a biisi Wen biik a te la a sak ka daana Kirisita bisaŋa jigi.

ref: Suppose everyone in your worship service started speaking unknown languages, and some outsiders or some unbelievers come in. Won't they think you are crazy?
text: Kirisita bisaŋa abe dan tu ate waai meena a biisi bichaŋ ate Kirisita bi sii ate ba an diem a sak ba la yaase baai ale kan daa Kirisita bisa la a jam jo, ba kan weeni ayen ni meena ka yesiŋsa?

ref: But suppose all of you are prophesying when those unbelievers and outsiders come in. They will realize that they are sinners, and they will want to change their ways because of what you are saying.
text: Alege waai meena a dan chɔgsi a biisi Wen biika a te ate waai ale kan daa Kirisita biik la yaase Kirisita biik kaai ate ba an diem sak wa la a jam jo a wom ba ale a biisi diila wa le siak wa tom kaasika. Wie ŋaai ate wa a wom la ale bo wa buusa,

ref: They will tell what is hidden in their hearts. Then they will kneel down and say to God, “We are certain that you are with these people.” Worship Must Be Orderly
text: wa susuga popolaŋa meena ale lak a sak, ate wa koori tɛŋ zuli Wen a siak wa kaasuŋku abe wa weeni ayen, <<Wensie Wen a bo ni suŋsuŋ dela kama.>>

ref: My friends, when you meet to worship, you must do everything for the good of everyone there. That's how it should be when someone sings or teaches or tells what God has said or speaks an unknown language or explains what the language means.
text: M suata mi ale a weeni diila kiri ale nna, ase ni dan tu chaab ayen ni puusi Wen, nuru ale ta yiili a yi ate wa choa a sak ate wa choa a biisi Wen ale lak dii a sak wa la ate wa choa a biisi bichaŋ ate wa choa a biisi bichaŋ ka kiri a sak nuruma. Ni abe a nye wari meena ate ku a maari Kirisita bisaŋa ate ba siaka a pagra.

ref: No more than two or three of you should speak unknown languages during the meeting. You must take turns, and someone should always be there to explain what you mean.
text: Ase nuru waai a dan poom ayen wa biisi bichaŋ, ba chim nuruba baye yaase bata, ba kan gaam dila, ate m wa a dan biisi nueri abe nwala mɛ a ŋman biisi ate nuru wa choa a biisi dii ate ba weeni la kiri.

ref: If no one can explain, you must keep silent in church and speak only to yourself and to God.
text: Alege waai a dan kan boro a biisi ku kiri ya, nuru waai ale a biisi bichaŋ ka la abe goori abe wa a biisi wa popo a te wadek ale Wen.

ref: Two or three persons may prophesy, and everyone else must listen carefully.
text: Wen a dan te nuruba baye yaase bata biik, ba abe biisi ate mbala kpesi bɛ kaai ate ba a biisi la a nya.

ref: If someone sitting there receives a message from God, the speaker must stop and let the other person speak.
text: Alege nuru waai a dan kali tuka po ate Wen a te wa biik, waai ale liŋ boro a biisi la abe basi ate nwala a biisi.

ref: Let only one person speak at a time, then all of you will learn something and be encouraged.
text: Ni meena a tuesi biik Wen jigi a biisi wanyi wanyi ate waai meena a baga a zamsi a nya nyiŋbiiri.

ref: A prophet should be willing to stop and let someone else speak.
text: Nuru waai ale baga a tuesi biik Wen jigi a biisi la abe kpesi yik wadek nalimnyiini.

ref: God wants everything to be done peacefully and in order. When God's people meet in church,
text: Dii nyiŋla Wen a kan yaali butimka tuima alege wa yaali ka nɔiyeŋ ale suiyɔgni. Wie ŋaai abe le a nye Wen nuruma tuka po la ale la.

ref: the women must not be allowed to speak. They must keep quiet and listen, as the Law of Moses teaches.
text: Nipooma a nyiem abe a nye diki ba tuka po. Ba an magsi ba a biisi a magsi chaab ale Sinsaŋŋa ale weeni diila, ayen nipooma kan chim niŋdeerɔba.

ref: If there is something they want to know, they can ask their husbands when they get home. It is disgraceful for women to speak in church.
text: Ba a dan a yaali ayen ba bek a miŋ wari kiri, ba bek ba chorɔma ba yeeŋa Kirisita bisa a dan tu ate nipok a biisi wa a te ka wadek chivie.

ref: God's message did not start with you people, and you are not the only ones it has reached.
text: Yaa Wen wanni a nyini ka nama jigiya? Yaa di jam ka nama nyiini jigiya?

ref: If you think of yourself as a prophet or a spiritual person, you will know I am writing only what the Lord has commanded.
text: Nuru waai abe daa poli ayen wa ka Wen tomteerɔ yaase wa ta Chiika tiirimu, wa abe miŋ seba ayen mi ale ŋmarisi dii a te ni la a nyini ka Naawen jigi.

ref: So don't pay attention to anyone who ignores what I am writing.
text: Nuru waai ale a yaali ayen wa zɛri kude la abe zɛri ate wa nam ku nyiŋ.

ref: My friends, be eager to prophesy and don't stop anyone from speaking languages that others don't know.
text: Dila la, m suata, ni basi ate ni suiniima a bo Wen biika tuesi biik alege ni kan zɛri bi chaŋka biiga.

ref: But do everything properly and in order.
text: Ni bi nye wari meena a va abe le nye a magsi.

ref: I told you the most important part of the message exactly as it was told to me. This part is: Christ died for our sins, as the Scriptures say.
text: Ba a sak mi ka wa dii ale chim wari dek a gaam wie meena la ate mi me a pai sak ni. Wa dila ale Kirisita a kpi kama ti wabaataŋa nyiŋ, ase ba ale jam ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po diila.

ref: He was buried, and three days later he was raised to life, as the Scriptures say.
text: Wa abe le kpi la, ba gu wa kama ate ku daa ŋata danni wa yiti kum po ase ba ale jam ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po diila.

ref: After this, he appeared to more than five hundred other followers. Most of them are still alive, but some have died.
text: Wa a ŋman pilim pai wadek a sak wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ba chaab kobsinu. Ba gela a diem boro kama alege ba gela a kpi.

ref: He also appeared to James, then to all of the apostles.
text: ) alege Adam waai ale kpeglim la dek ale a te nuruba nyuvuri.

ref: I am the least important of all the apostles. In fact, I caused so much trouble for God's church that I don't even deserve to be called an apostle.
text: Diila mi ka wa tuimtomdɔma po ŋaaŋ denɔ. Mi an poom magsi ayen ba a wi mu ayen tuimtomdɔ, dii nyiŋla m namsi Wen nuruma ka yegayega.

ref: But God treated me with undeserved grace! He made me what I am, and his grace wasn't wasted. I worked much harder than any of the other apostles, although it was really God's grace at work and not me.
text: Alege Wen ŋmanteka nyiŋ jinla mi ale ka nuru waai choa nna, Wen ŋmanteka nyiŋ mi an nye kaasi ya. Mi abe tom kama a gaam Yeezu tuimtomdɔ mbala, alege daa mi dek nyiŋŋa ka Wen ŋmanteka nyiŋ ate m baga a tom.

ref: But it doesn't matter if I preached or if they preached. All of you believed the message just the same. God's People Will Be Raised to Life
text: Dila la dan ka mi ale mooli yaase tuimtomdɔ mbala ale mooli, wa dii ate ti meena a mooli la ale la, dila abe le ni ta siaka ale di.

ref: If we preach that Christ was raised from death, how can some of you say the dead will not be raised to life?
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ate nuruba a mooli ayen Kirisita a yiti kum po la, ni ba gela a weeni kama ayen baai ale kpi la a kan yiti kum po.

ref: So if the dead won't be raised to life, Christ wasn't raised to life.
text: Diila baai ale kpi la dan ka a yiti kum po dan ka di Kirisita abe m yiti kum po.

ref: Unless Christ was raised to life, your faith is useless, and you are still living in your sins.
text: Wen a dan kan basi ate Kirisita a yiti kum po, ni siaka ale wa ka kinla, ate ku a sak ase ni bo ka ni wabaataŋa po la.

ref: And those people who died after putting their faith in him are completely lost.
text: Ku abe ŋma a sak me ayen baai ale ta siaka ale Kirisita alege kpi la meena a bo ka ninam po.

ref: If our hope in Christ is good only for this life, we are worse off than anyone else.
text: Tama ale ta yiili ŋaai ale Kirisita la dan ka wa te ti tɛŋka de zuk nyuvunni nyiini, ti ka niniga nyam a gaam waai meena tɛŋka zuk.

ref: But Christ has been raised to life! And he makes us certain that others will also be raised to life.
text: Alege ku ka wensie ayen Wen a basi ate Kirisita a dɛ niŋ yiti kum po ate ku a sak ayen baai ale ta siaka ale wa alege kpi la, wa le basi ate ba yiti kum po.

ref: Just as we will die because of Adam, we will be raised to life because of Christ.
text: Nuru yeŋ nyiŋ abe le soa ate nuruba a kpi la, wanyi me nyiŋ ale soa ate nuruba a yiti kum po.

ref: But we must each wait our turn. Christ was the first to be raised to life, and his people will be raised to life when he returns.
text: Alege Wen ale basi ate waai meena a yiti kum po a magsi chaab ale wa ale yaali ku diila. Wen a basi ate ka Kirisita a dɛ niŋ a yiti. Kirisita yaa dan ŋman jam, baai ale jam ta siaka ale wa la yaa yiti.

ref: Then after Christ has destroyed all powers and forces, the end will come, and he will give the kingdom to God the Father.
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate tɛŋka yaa kpeglim. Kirisita yaa le nak a nya pagrim chichirik sii ale ta pagrim la zuk ate wa yaa pai naamu a te wa kowa Wen.

ref: and the last enemy he destroys will be death.
text: Dachiak kaai ate Wen za wa nak yiak a kpeglim la ale kum.

ref: When the Scriptures say he will put everything under his power, they don't include God. It was God who put everything under the power of Christ.
text: Wen gbaŋka po ku weeni ayen, <<Wen a basi kama ate Kirisita a nya pagrim ŋanta meena zuk ale tabi zuk.>> Ku be weeni a lagri kama, da ayen Wen dek a maa gum du kama. Wen dek ka waai ale wa basi ate Kirisita tabi ŋanta meena zuk.

ref: After everything is under the power of God's Son, he will put himself under the power of God, who put everything under his Son's power. Then God will mean everything to everyone.
text: Alege Wen a dan pai jaabuuri meena ate Kirisita a nya, Wen nidoabinni Kirisita yaa le pai wadek a te Wen dii ale pai jaabuuri meena a te wa la, ate Wen a yaa a nya jaabuuri meena zuk.

ref: If the dead are not going to be raised to life, what will people do who are being baptized for them? Why are they being baptized for those dead people?
text: Ni be te ti poli nya baai ale zaani kpieba naŋkula po ate ba te ba soka la. Ku abe dan ka wensie ase nuruba ale a weeni ayen kpieba a kan yiti kum po la, ka boa abe le soa ate ba a te nuru bala soka a magsi kpiema?

ref: And why do we always risk our lives
text: Ka boan jaab ale soa ate tama a chali a jo biem po,

ref: and face death every day? The pride that I have in you because of Christ Jesus our Lord is what makes me say this.
text: a tu kum daaŋa meena? Kanjauŋ tii ate mi ta ni nyiŋla ale basi ate mi a weeni kude. Be ka Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa me nyiŋ ate m ta kanjantaŋa.

ref: Be sensible and stop sinning. You should be embarrassed that some people still don't know about God. What Our Bodies Will Be Like
text: Ni te ate ni popola a ŋman jam abe ni basi wabaata nyeka. Ku magsi chivie ta ni kama ni ale kan seba Wen la nyiŋ.

ref: Some of you have asked, “How will the dead be raised to life? What kind of bodies will they have?”
text: Nuru waai ale bek ayen, baai ale kpi la ale nye ka sɛ a yiti kum po. Ba dan yiti ka boan nyiŋsa chaab ate ba le tara?

ref: Don't be foolish. A seed must die before it can sprout from the ground.
text: Betta beka ale la. Ase fi dan bori biri tɛŋ, di kan deri a nyini viowa, se di poak abe di yaa nyini.

ref: Wheat seeds and all other seeds look different from the sprouts that come up.
text: Jaabuui ate fi a bori la ka biri, da dii dai mum biri yaase jaab yoŋ biri, ku da ayen ka kinni ale vioku meena.

ref: People, animals, birds, and fish are each made of flesh, but none of them are alike.
text: Ŋanvuta ale bo tɛŋzuk de la nyiŋsaŋa a daa nyiŋ yeŋsa, nurubisa nyiŋsaŋa ka si tɔga, duŋsa nyiŋsaŋa si tɔga, nuinsa nyiŋsaŋa si tɔga ate juma me nyiŋsaŋa si tɔga.

ref: Everything in the heavens has a body, and so does everything on earth. But each one is very different from all the others.
text: Wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk ŋanta meena a ta nyiŋsa kama. Wenŋmazuk ŋantaŋa nyiŋsaŋa nalimu ka bu tɔga ale tɛŋzuk ŋantaŋa nyiŋsa nalimu.

ref: The sun isn't like the moon, the moon isn't like the stars, and each star is different.
text: Wenbinni a ta di me dek nalim kama, Chiika a ta ka dek nalim, chiŋmarisaŋa me a ta si dek nalim. Chiŋmarisaŋa nalimu a poom diem ka tɔgatɔga.

ref: As surely as there are physical bodies, there are spiritual bodies. And our physical bodies will be changed into spiritual bodies.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ate ti ta nyiŋ sii la a za si jam tagri a chim ka chiika po nyiŋsa. Dila la nyiŋ lam a boro ate Chiika po me nyiŋ a boro.

ref: The first man was named Adam, and the Scriptures tell us that he was a living person. But Jesus, who may be called the last Adam, is a life-giving spirit.
text: Ku ŋmarisi ayen, Wen ale jam liŋ nye nuru waai ate ba a wi ayen Adam la. Wa jam te wa ka nyuvuri (Piilimka

ref: We see that the one with a spiritual body did not come first. He came after the one who had a physical body.
text: Nuru waai ale jam ale nyiŋ lammu la ale dɛ niŋ ate waai ale jam ale chiika la a tagri.

ref: The first man was made from the dust of the earth, but the second man came from heaven.
text: Adam waai abe le dɛ niŋ la, Wen nye wa ka tɛŋzuk de alege Adam waai ale pai saŋ la a nyini ka wenŋmazuk.

ref: Everyone on earth has a body like the body of the one who was made from the dust of the earth. And everyone in heaven has a body like the body of the one who came from heaven.
text: Tɛŋka zuk demma a nye ase ka nuru waai ate Wen a nye wa tɛŋzuk de la, baai mɛ ale ba bo wenŋmazuk la a nye ase ka waai ale nyini wenŋmazuk la.

ref: Just as we are like the one who was made out of earth, we will be like the one who came from heaven.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ti a nye ase ka nuru waai ate Wen a nye wa tɛŋzuk de la alege ta cheena ti le nye ase ka nuru waai ale nyiini wenŋmazuk la.

ref: My friends, I want you to know that our bodies of flesh and blood will decay. This means they cannot share in God's kingdom, which lasts forever.
text: M suata, mi ale a yaali ayen ni seba diila ale tama ale ti nyiŋsa dɛ a kan baga a nya Wen naamu. Ti ta ka nyiŋ sii ate ti dan kpi si poak la.

ref: I will explain a mystery to you. Not every one of us will die, but we will all be changed.
text: M le weeni wasusugi ate ni wom. Ti meena a kan deri kpi alege ti dan wom damuniŋ ale ka peeri wenŋmazuk ti nyiŋsaŋa ale deri tagri ka nna yilibi.

ref: It will happen suddenly, quicker than the blink of an eye. At the sound of the last trumpet the dead will be raised. We will all be changed, so we will never die again.
text: Ba dan peeri damuniŋ Kirisita bi sii ale kpi la ale yiti kum po. Ba abe dan yiti ba kan ŋman kpi. Tama baai ale diem bo tɛŋzuk de la nyiŋsaŋa ale deri tagri.

ref: The bodies we now have are weak and can die. But they will be changed into bodies that are eternal. Then the Scriptures will come true, “Death has lost the battle!
text: Dila la kude a dan nye, ate jabuui ale a poak la a tagri a chim jabuui ale kaa poak la, dii ate ba a ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po la ale chim wensie. Ku ŋmarisi ayen, <<Kum pagrim a yaa taam kama.>> (Azaya

ref: Where is its victory? Where is its sting?”
text: <<Bu pagrimu a bo ka bɛ? Bu pagrimu a bo ka be a koani nuruba?>> (Yosea

ref: Sin is what gives death its sting, and the Law is the power behind sin.
text: Kum a nya bu pagrimu a nyini ka wabaata jigi ate wabaata a nya ti pagrimu Sinsaŋŋa jigi.

ref: But thank God for letting our Lord Jesus Christ give us the victory!
text: Alege ti a nye Wen jiam Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa nyiŋ ate wa a te ti pagrim la.

ref: My dear friends, stand firm and don't be shaken. Always keep busy working for the Lord. You know that everything you do for him is worthwhile.
text: Dila nyiŋ m suata, ni chiib a zaani nalimnyiini. Ni kasim a tom Naawen tuimaŋa ale ninmuna, ni ale tɔlim seba ayen dii meena ate ni tom a te Naawen la daa kinla nyiŋla.

ref: When you collect money for God's people, I want you to do exactly what I told the churches in Galatia to do.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de mi a yaali ayen m weeni ka ni ale ŋmarisi gbaŋka a weeni ligraŋa ate ni a cheesi la wari. M le weeni Galatia Kirisita bisaŋa ayen ba nye diila nama me a nye dila dekdega.

ref: That is, each Sunday each of you must put aside part of what you have earned. If you do this, you won't have to take up a collection when I come.
text: Laasidi dai meena waai meena a gaari ligra a magsi wa pagrim ale ka diila a dueni ate m dan jam abe ni kan ŋman weeni ayen ni cheesi ligra.

ref: Choose some followers to take the money to Jerusalem. I will send them on with the money and with letters which show that you approve of them.
text: M bɛ dan jam m le ŋmarisi gbaŋ a te nuru baai ate nama a mariŋ ba a lueri la ate ba ta ni tiirimu a cheŋ Jerusalem tɛŋka.

ref: If you think I should go along, they can go with me. Paul's Travel Plans
text: M bɛ dan ŋman nya ale ku magsi ayen m dek cheŋ abe ba va mu a cheŋ.

ref: After I have gone through Macedonia, I hope to see you
text: Mi a poli ayen m va ka Masidoniya. M dan va dula abe m deri jam ni jigi.

ref: and visit with you for a while. I may even stay all winter, so that you can help me on my way to wherever I will be going next.
text: M dan jam ni jigi m le goa a beni maga. M le bo ale ni ŋoota wen meena ate ni baga a maari mu ate m ŋman baga a cheŋ juijui meena ate mi a yaali ayen m cheŋ la.

ref: If the Lord lets me, I would rather come later for a longer visit than to stop off now for only a short visit.
text: M kan yaali ayen m nya ni ale ka m nimbie abe mi a taam mu. Mi a yaali kama ayen m goa ale ni a beni maga ase Naawen a nin te suik.

ref: because there is a wonderful opportunity for me to do some work here. But there are also many people who are against me.
text: Wen a lak ka suik a te m boro a tom tuima dek dela jigini alege nuruba a kisi mu a kan siagi.

ref: When Timothy arrives, give him a friendly welcome. He is doing the Lord's work, just as I am.
text: Timoti a dan jam ni jigi ni tuesi wa nalimnyiini ate ku nye wa masim ale wa a tom a te ka Naawen ase mi la.

ref: Don't let anyone mistreat him. I am looking for him to return to me together with the other followers. So when he leaves, send him off with your blessings.
text: Ni waai a kan pai wa a chim jaab valiŋŋa, ni maari wa ate wa jam m jigi ale suiyɔgni. Mi a limisi wa kama ale m tomteerɔ chaama.

ref: I have tried hard to get our friend Apollos to visit you with the other followers. He doesn't want to come just now, but he will come when he can. Personal Concerns and Greetings
text: Mi a kasim a te ti suoku Apolos nyiŋbiiri kama ayen wa jam ni jigi alege wa an yaali ayen wa jam yɔgyɔgla de. Wa dan nya suik wa ale jam.

ref: Show love in everything you do.
text: Ni a tom ni tuimaŋa meena ale yaalika.

ref: You know that Stephanas and his family were the first in Achaia to have faith in the Lord. They have done all they can for God's people. My friends, I ask you
text: Ni seba Sitifanus ale wa dɔkdemma ka baai ale liŋ dɛ niŋ tagri a chim Kirisita bisa Akaaya tɛŋka po. Ba ka baai ale tagri Kirisita bisa zuk a kasim a tom Wen tuimaŋa. Mi a saalim ni, m suata.

ref: to obey leaders like them and to do the same for all others who work hard with you.
text: Ni a zuli nuruma de chaab, ale waai meena ale a tom ale ba la.

ref: I was glad to see Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus. Having them here was like having you.
text: Mi sui a peenti ka nna yegayega ale Sitifanus ale Fortunatuse ale Akaikus, dii nyiŋla ba tagri ka nama zuk a cheena

ref: They made me feel much better, just as they made you feel better. You should appreciate people like them.
text: ate ku basi ate m popola a yɔk. Ni a zuli nuruma de chaab.

ref: Greetings from the churches in Asia. Aquila and Priscilla, together with the church that meets in their house, send greetings in the name of the Lord.
text: Kirisita bisaŋa meena ale a tu tɔgatɔga a bo Asia meena la a puusi ni. Akiila ale Pirisila ale Kirisita bi sii ale a tu ba yenni po la a puusi ni nalimnyiini.

ref: All the Lord's followers send their greetings. Give each other a warm greeting.
text: Ni Kirisita bi chaama ale bo dela la a puusi ni. Ni meena nyiem a dan yiti ni a puusi chaab.

ref: I am signing this letter myself: PAUL.
text: Mi Pɔɔl, ale a ŋmarisi puusaŋa dɛ ale m dek nisa.

ref: I pray that God will put a curse on everyone who doesn't love the Lord. And may the Lord come soon.
text: Nuru waai ale ka a yaali Naawen la, kikaasa ale bo kula nyɔnɔwa zuk. Ti Naawen yaa, be pilim jam.

ref: I pray the Lord Jesus will be kind to you.
text: Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa ŋmanteka a bo ale ni meena.

ref: I love everyone who belongs to Christ Jesus.
text: Mi yaalika a bo ale ni meena Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ. Ku be nye dila.

ref: From Paul, chosen by God to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, and from Timothy, who is also a follower. To God's church in Corinth and to all of God's people in Achaia.
text: Mi Pɔɔl, ka waai ate Wen a lueri ayen m chim wa tuimtomdɔ la. Ti suoku Timoti a puusi ni. Mi Pɔɔl, ale a ŋmarisi gbaŋka de a te nama Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab Korinti la, ale baai meena ale ka Wen nuruba bo Akaaya tɛŋka la.

ref: I pray that God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! Paul Gives Thanks
text: Mi a puusi a te Wen ti Kowa ale ka Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa la kama ayen wa te ni ŋmanteka abe wa te ni suiyɔgni.

ref: Praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! The Father is a merciful God, who always gives us comfort.
text: Ni basi ate ti pak Wen ale ka Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa Ko la. Wa ka jiirim Ko waai ate maarika meena a nyini wa jigi.

ref: He comforts us when we are in trouble, so that we can share this same comfort with others in trouble.
text: Wa kasim a maari ti kama daanika meena po, ate ti baga a maari ti suata daanika meena po. Ti be pai ka maari kaai ate tama dek a nya Wen jigi la a maari ba.

ref: We share in the terrible sufferings of Christ, but also in the wonderful comfort he gives.
text: Tama abe le maa tuesi Kirisita ninammu a nam la ti be le va wa nyiŋ a nya Wen maarika yegayega kama.

ref: We suffer in the hope that you will be comforted and saved. And because we are comforted, you will also be comforted, as you patiently endure suffering like ours.
text: Tama a daa a nam, ka nama maarika ale ni varibasika nyiŋ. Ti be dan nya maarika nama me a nya maarika kama ale pagrim ate ni baga a chiib ale ninam buui choawa ate tama me a chiibi la.

ref: You never disappoint us. You suffered as much as we did, and we know that you will be comforted as we were.
text: Ti seba chak kama ayen ni le ŋmasi chiibi ate ni kan lo. Tama mɛ be seba ayen nama ale tama ninammu ka bunyi. Ti maarika me ka bunyi.

ref: My friends, I want you to know what a hard time we had in Asia. Our sufferings were so horrible and so unbearable that death seemed certain.
text: M suata, mi a yaali ayen m teeri ni kama ate ni seba daani kaai ate ti nya Asia la. Va ŋala po, tama ninammu a jam zuak ka nna yegayega. Ti jam poom poli ayen ti le kpi kama.

ref: God saved us from the threat of death, and we are sure that he will do it again and again.
text: Va ŋala po Wen a jam vari ti kum po a basi kama. Ti ta yiila kama ayen wa le ŋman vari ti a basi kama.

ref: Please help us by praying for us. Then many people will give thanks for the blessings we receive in answer to all these prayers. Paul's Change of Plans
text: Ni be le a puusi nna yegayega a te ti la, Wen ale tulisi ni puusaŋa abe wa niak ti, ate nama a te wa jiam tama nyiŋ.

ref: We can be proud of our clear conscience. We have always lived honestly and sincerely, especially when we were with you. And we were guided by God's gift of undeserved grace instead of by the wisdom of this world.
text: Ti ta kanjanta kama diila tama dek popola po ti seba chak kama ayen ti boka tɛŋzuk de, ale tama ale ni ale ka diila ka Wen ale maari ti ate ti ta suinum weleŋsa ale popola maŋsa. Kude be ka Wen ŋmanteka nyiŋ daa nurubiik yammoa.

ref: I am not writing anything you cannot read and understand. I hope you will understand it completely,
text: M le a ŋmarisi a te ni diila, mi a poli ayen m le a weeni diila, an pagra ate ni kan baga miŋ.

ref: just as you already partly understand us. Then when our Lord Jesus returns, you can be as proud of us as we are of you.
text: Ni diem zɛ mu a chak ya, alege mi a yaali kama ayen ni seba mu nalimnyiini, ate ni ta kanjanta m nyiŋ ase Yeezu ti Naawenni a nin pilim jam.

ref: I was so sure of your pride in us that I had planned to visit you first of all. In this way you would have the blessing of two visits from me—
text: M le jam seba kude chak la nyiŋ, m yaa jam poli ayen m jam ni jigi ate m baga a niak ni a nye buye.

ref: once on my way to Macedonia and again on my return from there. Then you could send me on to Judea.
text: M poli kama ayen m jam ni jigi ase m nin pilim a ŋmani a cheŋ Masidoniya ate m yaa zaani Masidoniya a jam ni jigi, ate ni yaa basi ate m cheŋ Judia.

ref: God can be trusted, and so can I, when I say our answer to you has always been “Yes” and never “No.”
text: Wen ale mi seerɔ ayen m daa nuru wala choa. Mi ka nuru waai ale wensie nyɔnɔ la.

ref: This is because Jesus Christ the Son of God is always “Yes” and never “No.” And he is the one Silas, Timothy, and I told you about.
text: Diila Wen Nidoabinni, Yeezu Kirisita, waai ate mi ale Silas ale Timoti a mooli wa wie a te ni la jam daa ŋa le nye yaase ŋa kan nye alege ŋa nye kama wa nyiŋ.

ref: Christ says “Yes” to all God's promises. This is why we have Christ to say “Amen” for us to the glory of God.
text: Wen dan poom puulim zuak diiya ŋa a nye kama Kirisita nyiŋ. Ate wa nyiŋ tama ale a biisi ayen ku be nye dila la a te Wen zula.

ref: And so God makes it possible for you and us to stand firmly together with Christ. God is also the one who chose us
text: Wen dek ale lueri tama ale nama meena ate ti seba chak ayen ti ta nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la ti le Kirisita ale ka bunyi la nyiŋ.

ref: God is my witness that I stayed away from Corinth, just to keep from being hard on you.
text: Wen ale mi seerɔ a seba dii ale bo m suinum po la. Mi an ŋman pilim jam ayen m nya ni, dii nyiŋla, m dan poom jam, ni te jam wom ka m biik pagrika.

ref: We are not bosses who tell you what to believe. We are working with you to make you glad, because your faith is strong.
text: Tama kan yaali ayen ti jam sak ni a gum ni ale ta siaka ale Yeezu Kirisita diila. Ni poom ta siaka ale wa ka nalimnyiini. Ti a yaali ayen ti maari ni kama ate ni sue peenti.

ref: I have decided not to make my next visit with you so painful.
text: M kan yaali ayen m biisi bipagrik ate ku nye ate ni sue ŋman kaasi. Dila ale soa ate mi an jam ni jigi ya.

ref: If I make you feel bad, who would be left to cheer me up, except the people I had made to feel bad?
text: M daam dan poom jam ni jigi ate ni sue kaasi, ka wana ale wa boro a nye ate mi sui a peenti? Ka nama baai ate mi a nye ate ni sueŋa a kaasi la.

ref: The reason I want to be happy is to make you happy. I wrote as I did because I didn't want to visit you and be made to feel bad, when you should make me feel happy.
text: Dila ale soa ate m jam ŋmarisi gbaŋka a te ni. Dila mɛ be ale soa ate mi an ŋman pilim jam ayen m nya ni, dii nyiŋla, nama baai ale ni jam nye ate m sui peenti la, ni te jam nye kama ate di kaasi. Mi dek seba m suinum po ayen wie ŋaai ale bo m suinum po la, ŋa a nye ate nama mɛ sue a peenti kama.

ref: At the time I wrote, I was suffering terribly. My eyes were full of tears, and my heart was broken. But I didn't want to make you feel bad. I only wanted to let you know how much I cared for you. Forgiveness
text: M le jam ŋmarisi gbaŋka a te ni diipo la, m sui ale jam kaasi nna yegayega ni nyiŋ. M suinni a jam kaasi ka nna yegayega ate m ninyiam a zi m popo. Ni kan te ni sue kaasi, kude a sak ka mi yaalika ale ni.

ref: I don't want to be hard on you. But if one of you has made someone feel bad, I am not really the one who has been made to feel bad. Some of you are the ones.
text: Waai a dan basi ate sui kaasuŋ a boro, wa an basi ate daa mi nyiini sui a kaasi ya, ka ni meena sue ale kaasi. Mi kan yaali ayen m nyeka a toa ale wa.

ref: Most of you have already pointed out the wrong that person did, and this is punishment enough for what was done.
text: Ni yega ale namsi wa diila a zuak kama a te wa.

ref: When people sin, you should forgive and comfort them, so they won't give up in despair.
text: Ni vɔŋ a te wa abe ni a te wa nyiŋbiiri ate wa suipuurumu kan te ate wa basi ni.

ref: You should make them sure of your love for them.
text: Mi a saalim ni kama ayen ni weeni wa ayen ni a yaali wa kama nna yegayega.

ref: I will forgive anyone you forgive. Yes, for your sake and with Christ as my witness, I have forgiven whatever needed to be forgiven.
text: Ni dan vɔŋ a te nuru, mi mɛ vɔŋ a te wa kama. Mi a nye dila kama dii nyiŋla, mi a yaali ayen m maari ni kama. Ku a nye se Kirisita a nya m le a nye diila kama.

ref: I have done this to keep Satan from getting the better of us. We all know what goes on in his mind.
text: Ti seba Sitaana ale kasim a tom diila kama. Dila ale soa ate ku a fɛ ayen ni va suik kula ate wa kan baga a nak ni a yiagi.

ref: When I went to Troas to preach the good news about Christ, I found that the Lord had already prepared the way.
text: M le jam paari Torowas tɛŋka la, ti Naawenni a jam te mu ka suik nalimnyiini ayen m sak nuruba Kirisita wamaŋsaŋa.

ref: But I was worried when I didn't find my friend Titus there. So I left the other followers and went on to Macedonia.
text: Alege ku jam daani mu yegayega m le jam kan baga a nya m suoku Titus la. Dila ale soa ate mi an jam bo ale Torowas demma a beni ya ale ge cheŋ Masidoniya tɛŋka la.

ref: I am grateful that God always makes it possible for Christ to lead us to victory. God also helps us spread the knowledge about Christ everywhere, and this knowledge is like the smell of perfume.
text: Ni basi ate ti a te Wen jiam. Wa basi kama ate tama ale Kirisita a chim bunyi. Wa soa ti kama yɔgyɔgla. Wa kasim a basi ti kama ate ti a nyiem a sak nuruba ate ba nya suik a seba Kirisita.

ref: In fact, God thinks of us as a perfume that brings Christ to everyone. For people who are being saved, this perfume has a sweet smell and leads them to a better life. But for people who are lost, it has a bad smell and leads them to a horrible death. No one really has what it takes to do this work.
text: Jigi meena ate ti ga a paari la, ti a nyuŋ ka nna biokbiokwa baai ate Wen le basi ate ba kan ta kiri la nyue po. Alege ti a nyuŋ ka nna masimasiga baai ale nya varibasika la nyue po. Ka wana dek ale pagrɔ ate wa tom tuimaŋa dɛ a te Wen yaa?

ref: A lot of people try to get rich from preaching God's message. But we are God's sincere messengers, and by the power of Christ we speak our message with God as our witness.
text: Nuruba yegayega ale a sak nuruba Wen wamaŋsaŋa wie ale ba noa nyiini, ayen ba nya nyuenta a te badek. Tama kan nye se nuru bala chaaba. Wen a tom ti kama ayen ti a sak nuruba wa wie ale popola yena. Ku a nye se Wen a nya ti kama la.

ref: Are we once again bragging about ourselves? Do we need letters to you or from you to tell others about us? Some people do need letters telling about them.
text: Tama ŋman pak tidek nama niŋŋa? Ti a yaali ka gbaŋ nama jigi ayen ti seba ni wamaŋsa yaase nama a yaali gbaŋ tama jigi ayen ni seba tama wamaŋsa.

ref: But you are our letter, and you are in our hearts for everyone to read and understand.
text: Nama dek a nye se ka gbaŋsa a ŋmarisi ti suiniimaŋa nyiŋ ate waai meena a karim la.

ref: You are like a letter written by Christ and delivered by us. But you are not written with pen and ink or on tablets made of stone. You are written in our hearts by the Spirit of the living God.
text: Wen dii ale vua la, a pai wa chiika a nyo ka mi suinum po. Dila ale soa ate ni a nye se Kirisita gbaŋ kaai ate ti ŋmarisi la. Wen ale nye diila a basi kama ate ni gaam wa le jam ŋmarisi wa sinsaŋŋa a dueni tintain paglaksa zuk la.

ref: We are sure about all this. Christ makes us sure in the very presence of God.
text: Ka Kirisita nyiŋ ate ti ta siaka ale Wen. Dila ale soa ate ti a weeni nna a sak ni.

ref: We don't have the right to claim that we have done anything on our own. God gives us what it takes to do all we do.
text: Tama an baga pai tidek pagrim a tom a te Wen yaa. Wa a pai ka wa pagrimu a te ti ayen ti a tom tuima a te wa.

ref: So won't the agreement the Spirit brings to us be even more wonderful?
text: alege Wen a pai wa zulaŋa a nyo wa Chiika po waai ale a basi ate nuruba a nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la.

ref: In fact, the new agreement is so wonderful that the Law is no longer glorious at all.
text: Zula ŋaai ale wa nalim buui ate Wen a pai te wa Chiika la ale basi ate zula ŋaai ale nalim buui ate wa jam pai te wa sinsaŋŋa dila po la a taam.

ref: The Law was given with a glory that faded away. But the glory of the new agreement is much greater, because it will never fade away.
text: Wen sinsaŋŋa ŋaai ale soa wa zulaŋa la an jam beni ya. Wa Chiika a boro kama taam wuu. Dila ale soa ate wa zulaŋa a gaam Wen sinsaŋŋa zulaŋa la.

ref: We are not like Moses. His face was shining, but he covered it to keep the people of Israel from seeing the brightness fade away.
text: Tama kan nye a se Moosis waai ale jam pai garuk a lik wa nimbidiaka ayen Izirali demma a kan baga a nya Wen zulaŋa ale ŋa le a basi wa nimbidiaka diila.

ref: The people were stubborn, and something still keeps them from seeing the truth when the Law is read. Only Christ can take away the covering that keeps them from seeing.
text: Dila la ba popolaŋa a jam lik kama. A ta jam paari jinla ba popolaŋa a nye se ka garuk ale lik ŋa la ase ba nin boro a karim Nɔiyeŋ Kpakka. Alege waai ale a siak Kirisita la garukku a zagri kama.

ref: When the Law of Moses is read, they have their minds covered over
text: Alege jinla ba dan a karim Moosis Sinsaŋŋa garukku a diem a lik ba popolaŋa kama.

ref: with a covering that is removed only for those who turn to the Lord.
text: Alege nuru a dan ŋmani Naawen jigi garukku a zagri kama.
