ref: Use clean language that no one can criticize. Do this, and your enemies will be too ashamed to say anything against you.
text: Sak ba sinsak ŋaai le ŋa basi ate nuru kan baga a nya suik a biisi a gaam fu la. Fi dan a biisi wieŋa de ale wensie, chivie le yik ti dachaasaŋa kama ate ba kan nya suik a biisi tama wari ya.

ref: or steal from them. They must be completely honest and trustworthy. Then everyone will show great respect for what is taught about God our Savior. God's Kindness and the New Life
text: Yaase ba a zu ba ŋanta. Ku a fɛ kama ayen ba lak ba suiniima meena ale ba popola wie meena po daa meena a tom a te ba nyama, ate Wen ti Varibasidɔwa sinsaŋŋa a nya yue maŋ.

ref: He gave himself to rescue us from everything evil and to make our hearts pure. He wanted us to be his own people and to be eager to do right.
text: Wa jam kpi kama ayen wa da tuesi ti ti tuimbaataŋa po a basi abe wa sugri ti suiniimaŋa, abe wa soa ti ate ti chim wadek nuruba, abe ti nina muni ale tuimaŋsa tomka.

ref: Remind your people to obey the rulers and authorities and not to be rebellious. They must always be ready to do something helpful
text: Teeri fi nuruma ayen ba a zuli ba tɛŋka nalimaŋa ale ba tɛŋka kpaŋŋa abe ba a va ba noa, abe ba gomsi badek a tom tuimaŋsa.

ref: God our Savior showed us how good and kind he is.
text: Alege Wen ti Varibasidɔwa a pai wa jiirimu ale wa yaalika a sak ti kama

ref: He saved us because of his mercy, and not because of any good things we have done. God washed us by the power of the Holy Spirit. He gave us new birth and a fresh beginning.
text: a yaa vari ti ti tuimbaataŋa po a basi. Wa an jam nye dila ka tama dek tuimaŋsa nyiŋŋa, alege ka wa jiirimu nyiŋ ate wa nye dila. Ka Wen Chiika ale sugri ti suiniimaŋa a yaa te ti biam paalik ale nyuvuri paalik.

ref: God sent Jesus Christ our Savior to give us his Spirit.
text: Wen va ka Yeezu Kirisita ti Varibasidɔwa nyiŋ a sueri ti suiniimaŋa ale Wen Chiika nna yegayega.

ref: Jesus treated us much better than we deserve. He made us acceptable to God and gave us the hope of eternal life.
text: Wen ŋmanteka nyiŋ ate Wen Chiika a nye ate ti chim weleŋsa nyam Wen jigi, a yaa basi ate ti ta yiila ayen ti le nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la.

ref: This message is certainly true. These teachings are useful and helpful for everyone. I want you to insist that the people follow them, so that all who have faith in God will be sure to do good deeds.
text: Nya kude ate m weeni la abe ka wensie ate nuruba weeni. Mi a yaali kama ayen daa meena fi a sak nuruma wieŋa de ale sebchakka ate bala baai ale ta siaka ale Wen la, nina muni ate ba a tom tuimaŋsa ŋaai ale nala a te nuruba la.

ref: But don't have anything to do with stupid arguments about ancestors. And stay away from disagreements and quarrels about the Law of Moses. Such arguments are useless and senseless.
text: Alege kan a nak betta nanpaga, abe fi kan a wom baai ale a sak ba kokpieŋsa yue wie la. Kan a nye kpaliŋsa ale nuruba Moosis Sinsaŋŋa nyiŋŋa, dii nyiŋla, nyaŋa de meena kan niak nuru ale magadek mɛ la, ŋa ka wakayaata.

ref: You know their minds are twisted, and their own sins show how guilty they are. Personal Instructions and Greetings
text: Fidek seba ayen nuru wala choa ka popola baata nyɔnɔ. Wa tuimbaataŋa abe a sak waai meena wa ale ka nuru waai choa la kama.

ref: I plan to send Artemas or Tychicus to you. After he arrives, please try your best to meet me at Nicopolis. I have decided to spend the winter there.
text: M le tom Atemas yaase Tikikus fi jigi. Ba wanyi a dan jam fi jigi fi mɛ pii nyiŋ ate fi jam m jigi Nikopolis tɛŋka po. Mi a yaali ayen m goa ka dula ate ŋoota wein ga taam.

ref: When Zenas the lawyer and Apollos get ready to leave, help them as much as you can, so they won't have need of anything.
text: Fidek pii nyiŋ a maari Zenas waai ale a biisi buusa wie la, abe fi maa maari Apolos ate ba noa bayewa a baga gomsi ba chelimu. Pai jaabuuri meena ate ba a yaali la a te ba.

ref: Greetings to you from everyone here. Greet all of our friends who share in our faith. I pray that the Lord will be kind to all of you!
text: Baai meena ale bo ale mi la, a puusi fu. Puusi baai ale a va Yeezu ale ta yaalika ale tama mɛ la, a te ti. Wen ŋmanteka le bo ale ni meena.

ref: From Paul, who is in jail for serving Christ Jesus, and from Timothy, who is like a brother because of our faith. Philemon, you work with us and are very dear to us. This letter is to you
text: Mi Pɔɔl, waai ate ba yik lik Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋla ale ti suoku Timoti a puusi ni. Mi Pɔɔl, ale a ŋmarisi gbaŋka de a te ti suoku ale ti tomteerɔ choawa, Failemon

ref: and to the church that meets in your home. It is also to our dear friend Apphia and to Archippus, who serves the Lord as we do.
text: ale Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab fi yenni po la ale ti toawa Afia ale ti tugurik tɔŋdɔ choawa Akipus.

ref: I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! Philemon's Love and Faith
text: Wen ti Kowa ale ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita le te ni ŋmanteka ate ni boro ale suiyɔgni.

ref: I hear about your faith in our Lord Jesus and about your love for all God's people.
text: Dii nyiŋla, m wom fi ale ta yaalika soa dii ale Wen nuruma meena la kama. M wom fi siaka ale ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ale soa dii mɛ la kama.

ref: My friend, your love has made me happy and has greatly encouraged me. It has also cheered the hearts of God's people. Paul Speaks to Philemon about Onesimus
text: Fi yaalika ate fi ta la, m dek suowa, a ta ka masim nna yegayega ale nyiŋbiiri a jam m jigi. Fi nye kama ate Wen nuruma meena sue peenti.

ref: I beg you to help Onesimus! He is like a son to me because I led him to Christ here in jail.
text: M be tagri ka Onesimos waai ale ka m biik Yeezu Kirisita yuenni nyiŋla. Mi ale diem bo likka dɔk nna la m chim ka wa ko Yeezu yuenni nyiŋ.

ref: Before this, he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
text: Dila po wa jam ka tuintuini a te fu, alege yɔgyɔgla de, wa ta tuilum kama mi ale fi jigi.

ref: Sending Onesimus back to you makes me very sad.
text: M basi wa kama ale m suinum meena ayen wa pilim jam fi jigi.

ref: I would like to keep him here with me, where he could take your place in helping me while I am here in prison for preaching the good news.
text: Mi a yaali kama ayen m le diem bo likka dɔk la, wa diem maa boro ale mu Wen wamaŋsaŋa tomka nyiŋ ate wa tagri fi zuk a maari mu.

ref: But I won't do anything unless you agree to it first. I want your act of kindness to come from your heart, and not be something you feel forced to do.
text: Alege, m kan fɛ fu kama ayen fi nye wanni de, alege mi a yaali kama ayen fi siak ale fidek yaalika ate m kan nye wari nin ka fi a nin siak ayen m nye.

ref: Perhaps Onesimus was taken from you for a little while so you could have him back for good,
text: Ku baga a nye kama ate Onesimos ale kan bo fi jigi ate ku beni magadek la, ate fi a yaali ayen wa pilim jam fi jigi a boro taam wuu.

ref: If he has cheated you or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
text: Wa dan kaasi ka fi wari yaase wa ta ka fi pami, basi ate mi tuni dila.

ref: My dear friend and follower of Christ our Lord, please cheer me up by doing this for me.
text: Dila nyiŋ, m suowa, mi a saalim kama ayen ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ fi nye wanni de a te mu. Ase m Kirisita biik choa la, basi ate m poi peenti.

ref: Epaphras is also here in jail for being a follower of Christ Jesus. He sends his greetings,
text: Epafiras, waai ate ba maa yik wa a lik Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ la, a puusi ni.

ref: and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, who work together with me.
text: M tuimtomdɔ chaama mɛ Maak ale Arisitaakus ale Diimas ale Luuk a puusi fu.

ref: I pray that the Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you!
text: M be ŋman a saalim ayen ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ŋmanteka a bo ale ni meena.

ref: God has never said to any of the angels, “You are my Son, because today I have become your Father!” Neither has God said to any of them, “I will be his Father, and he will be my Son!”
text: Dii abe ale a sak ayen nya kude a sum ka wensie la ale, Wen an diem weeni wa maarɔma waai ya ayen, <<Fi ka M Nidoabili ya. Jinla mi chim ka fi Ko.>> (Yiila

ref: When God brings his first-born Son into the world, he commands all of his angels to worship him.
text: Wen ale liŋ biak wa nidoabinni a basi tɛŋzuk de la, wa weeni ayen, <<Ku a fɛ kama ayen Wen maarɔma meena a te Nidoabinni zula.>> (Yiila

ref: And when God speaks about the angels, he says, “I change my angels into wind and my servants into flaming fire.”
text: Wen ale weeni dii a magsi chaab ale maarɔma la ale nna ayen, <<Wa nye wa maarɔma kama ate ba a nye ase viok ale bolim ŋiak la.>> (Yiila

ref: But God says about his Son, “You are God, and you will rule as King forever! Your royal power brings about justice.
text: Alege wa ale ŋman biisi Wa Nidoabinni wari diila ale nna ayen, <<Naawen, fi le soa fi naamu ka dila taam wuu. Fi a nya fi nuruma zuk kama ale wensie.

ref: You loved justice and hated evil, and so I, your God, have chosen you. I appointed you and made you happier than any of your friends.”
text: Fi a yaali ka wari dii ale ka wensie la. Fi kisi wa dii ale ka wa kaasuŋ la kama. Dila ale soa ate Naawen, fi Naawen lueri fu a te fu zula, a yaa te fu suipeentik nna yegayega a gaam fi chaama.>>

ref: The Scriptures also say, “In the beginning, Lord, you were the one who laid the foundation of the earth and created the heavens.
text: Ale, <<Ka fi, ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ale nye tɛŋka a ta nyini ku piilimka po. Be ka fidek nisima ate fi pai nye wenŋmazuk ale jaabuuri meena ale bo ku po la.

ref: They will all disappear and wear out like clothes, but you will last forever.
text: Bala meena ale tɛŋzuk de meena le muriŋ bɛ kama. Alege fi kasim boro kama taam wuu. Ba le kaasi kama ase garuk la.

ref: You will roll them up like a robe and change them like a garment. But you are always the same, and you will live forever.”
text: Ase nuru ale a yeeri wa garuk kpak a yuk a basi ale ge a pai garuk paaluk a jo la. Suik kula po, ŋanta bala meena le tagri ka dila. Alege fi kasim boro ka dila kan maari a tagri. Fi le kasim boro ka dila taam wuu.>> (Yiila

ref: God never said to any of the angels, “Sit at my right side until I make your enemies into a footstool for you!”
text: Ka dimpo ate Wen diem weeni wa maarɔma wanyi ayen, <<Kali mi juga geŋ ate m ga basi ate fi dachaasaŋa a chim fi naŋsa tabika jaab.>> (Yiila

ref: Angels are merely spirits sent to serve people who are going to be saved.
text: Wen maarɔma ka wa tomteerɔba. Waai an baga a nya ba ale nina. Wen tom ba kama ayen ba jam maari baai le ba nya varibasika la.

ref: So if we refuse this great way of being saved, how can we hope to escape? The Lord himself was the first to tell about it, and people who heard the message proved to us that it was true.
text: Ku be dan ka dila, ate Wen a te ti varibasika a soa nna yegayega, ti le nye ka sɛ ate ti kan nya waalika ase ti nin zɛri ka? Be ka ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita dek, daa maarɔba, ale liŋ weeni nya kude ate nuruba wom; baai abe ale wom ŋa wa jigi la, ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate bala weeni sak tama.

ref: Somewhere in the Scriptures someone says to God, “What makes you care about us humans? Why are you concerned for weaklings such as we?
text: ) Yɔgyɔgla de wa be ale nye dila la, wa an weeni ayen ŋanta ba gela a kan zuli wa nɔiya. Ku be ale ka dii yɔgyɔgla de la, ti an baga a nya waai ya ale wa soa ŋanta meena zuk a nya la.

ref: What we do see is Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels. Because of God's gift of undeserved grace, Jesus died for everyone. And now that Jesus has suffered and died, he is crowned with glory and honor!
text: Alege ti nya ka Yeezu nyiini ale soa ŋanta meena a nya. Wen nye kama ate wa pɔsima maga dega a gaam maarɔma alege ku an beni gaam taam ya. Dila powa, nuruba le jam basi ate wa nam a kpi ayen Wen ŋmanteka nyiŋ wa tagri waai meena zuk a kpi te ba. Yɔgyɔgla de ti be a nya wa ase wa ka naab la, ate nuruba yaa te wa pimpauk ale zula.

ref: Everything belongs to God, and all things were created by his power. So God did the right thing when he made Jesus perfect by suffering, as Jesus led many of God's children to be saved and to share in his glory.
text: Wa le ta bisa yega a jam zula jigi la, ku magsi kama Wen jigi, diila ka wa nyiŋ ale ŋman va wa nyiŋ mɛ ate ŋanta meena a boro ale chim ba varibasika piilimka wa ninammu nyiŋ ate wari meena a nye chekki.

ref: Jesus and the people he makes holy all belong to the same family. This is why he isn't ashamed to call them his brothers and sisters.
text: Be ka wala ale a poori nuruba ale biem tɔgatɔga. Bala ale wa abe ka ko yeŋ. Dila abe ale soa ate yɔgsum yaase chivie ka Yeezu ate wa wi ba ayen wa suata

ref: He even said to God, “I will tell them your name and sing your praises when they come together to worship.”
text: weeni ayen, <<Mi le weeni m suataŋa fi ale nye diila. Mi le te fu pimpauk ba tuka po.>> (Yiila

ref: He also said, “I will trust God.” Then he said, “Here I am with the children God has given me.”
text: Ate Wa ŋman weeni mɛ ayen, <<Mi le ta siaka ale Wa.>> (Azaya

ref: Jesus clearly did not come to help angels, but he did come to help Abraham's descendants.
text: Waai meena abe baga a nya kama ayen ka nurubiik ate wa a maari, daa Naawen maarɔba. Maarika de potim a cheŋ ka Abrayam ŋaaŋbiika jigi.

ref: And now that Jesus has suffered and was tempted, he can help anyone else who is tempted.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de, wa yaa be baga a maari ba kama diipo meena ate Sitaana a ta nyenyaka a jam ba jigi la. Boan nyiŋŋa, wadek jam nya nyenyaka kama ale ninam.

ref: Of course, every house is built by someone, and God is really the one who built everything.
text: Nama dek seba ayen yeri meena ale boro la, ka nuru ale sɛ di. Alege ka Wen ale nye jaabuuri meena.

ref: But Christ is the Son in charge of God's people. And we are those people, if we keep on being brave and don't lose hope. A Rest for God's People
text: Alege Kirisita a ta siaka kama ase wa nidoabili la Wen yenni zuk. Tama be ka wa yenni ase ti nin yik ti sebchakka ale ti yiilaŋa a ta, ŋaai nyiŋ ate ti a kuulim la.

ref: “Then God got tired of them and said, ‘You people never show good sense, and you don't understand what I want you to do.’
text: Dila nyiŋ ate m sui yaa jam puuri ale ba ate m yaa weeni ayen, ba kasim a yaali ka bɔgta a gum mi po, ba be kan miŋ mi ale nye diila kiriya.

ref: In other words, a will doesn't go into effect as long as the one who made it is still alive.
text: Wa ale weeni diila, wa dan kan kpiya, wa ale biisi diila ka pagrimoa, see ka wa nin kpi.

ref: Moses told the people all the Law said they must do. Then he used red wool and a hyssop plant to sprinkle the people and the book of the Law with the blood of bulls and goats and with water.
text: Moosis ale jam mooli Wen Sinsaŋŋa meena a sak nuruma la, dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate wa yaa jam pai niiga ale bua ziita ale nyiam a gum chaab, a yaa pai pakɔbta tii ate ba muni la ale kpaliok, a yaa pai bala bayewa a lusi ziimu ale nyiamu po a pai a misi Sinsaŋŋa Gbaŋka ale nuruma ale ge

ref: He told the people, “With this blood God makes his agreement with you.”
text: a weeni ayen, <<Ziim buui ale a te nɔiyeŋ kaai ate Wen weeni ti ayen ti siak di nɔi la pagrimu ale nna.>> (Nyinika

ref: Moses also sprinkled blood on the tent and on everything else used in worship.
text: Wa yaa ŋman pai ziimu a misi viuku ale ŋan baai meena ate ba pai a tom la nyiŋ.

ref: The Law says that almost everything must be sprinkled with blood, and no sins can be forgiven unless blood is offered. Christ's Great Sacrifice
text: Wensie, Sinsaŋŋa abe ale a weeni diila ale nna ayen, ka ziim ale a lo tɛŋ ate jaab meena a chim jaweleŋ. Ziim abe dan kan lo tɛŋka, wabaata vɔŋteka karo.

ref: These things are only copies of what is in heaven, and so they had to be made holy by these ceremonies. But the real things in heaven must be made holy by something better.
text: Viuku ale ŋan baai ate Moosis pai ziimu a misi ba nyiŋla, ka ŋan baai ale bo wenŋmazuk la, yisuŋta. M be weeni ni kama ayen ka duŋsa ziita ale a lo tɛŋ ate ba a welema. Alege, ŋan baai ale bo wenŋmazuk la, ku a fɛ kama ayen kaab kaai ale gaam ziim tila la a nye ate ba welema.

ref: This is why Christ did not go into a tent made by humans and was only a copy of the real one. Instead, he went into heaven and is now there with God to help us.
text: Kirisita an jo daa Weleŋsa Yegayekka Jigi dii ate nurubiik sɛ la. Weleŋsa Yegayekka Jigi dila ka jigi dii ate ti an baga a nya la, yisuŋ. Wa jo ka wenŋmazuk dek juijui yɔgyɔgla de ate wa yaa tagri tama zuk a pai wadek a sak Wen la.

ref: Christ did not have to offer himself many times. He wasn't like a high priest who goes into the most holy place each year to offer the blood of an animal.
text: Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku a nyiem ta ka duŋsa ziim a jo Weleŋsa Yegayekka Jigini bena meena. Alege Kirisita an nye dila maga maga.

ref: If he had offered himself every year, he would have suffered many times since the creation of the world. But instead, near the end of time he offered himself once and for all, so he could be a sacrifice that does away with sin.
text: Wa dan jam pai wadek te ate ku paari ka diichoa nna po de, wa daam ti nam a paari ka diichoa a zaani diipo ate Wen nye tɛŋka la. Alege, ku ale ka dii yɔgyɔgla nna, ate wie meena tuak kpeglimka la, ale wa yaa pai wadek a sak bunyi dekki ayen wa pai wadek a nye kaabka ate biem kan ŋman boro.

ref: So Christ died only once to take away the sins of many people. But when he comes again, it will not be to take away sin. He will come to save everyone who is waiting for him.
text: Nurubiik abe ale a kpi ka bunyi dekki la, Kirisita mɛ abe kpi ka bunyi dekki a nye kaabka ayen wa duisi nuru boari wabaata basi. Wa be le ŋman pilim jam kama. Wa dan pilim jam, wa kan ŋman duisi ka nuruba wabaata a basi, alege wa le vari ka baai ale a limisi wa jamka la a basi.

ref: The Law of Moses is like a shadow of the good things to come. This shadow isn't the good things themselves, because it cannot free people from sin by the sacrifices offered year after year.
text: Sinsaŋŋa abe ka wie ŋaai le sum ŋa nye la, yisuŋta, daa ŋa dega. Sinsaŋŋa de a sak kama ayen ku a fɛ kama ayen nuruba a jam Wen jigi daa meena, ale bena meena a nye kaabka. Alege kaabka de meena ale kan baga a nye ate nuruba a welema la, Sinsaŋŋa, ŋaai ale va ka kaabka de meena a tom la, an baga a nye dila mɛ.

ref: When Christ came into the world, he said to God, “Sacrifices and offerings are not what you want, but you have given me my body.
text: Dila nyiŋ ale, soa ate Kirisita ale jan jam tɛŋzuk de la, wa weeni ayen, <<Fi kan yaali ayen ba a ko ŋanta a te fu yaase ba pai tiirita a te fu. Alege fi gomsi ka nyiŋ a te mu.

ref: Then Christ said, “And so, my God, I have come to do what you want, as the Scriptures say.”
text: Be nya mi ale nna, <Wen, ayen m tom fi ale a yaali diila, ase ba ale poom ŋmarisi mi wie Sinsaŋŋa Gbaŋka po diila.> >>

ref: Well, it was to do away with offerings and sacrifices and to replace them. This is what he meant by saying to God, “I have come to do what you want.”
text: Wa yaa ŋman weeni ayen, <<Be nya mi ale nna, Naawen ayen m tom fi ale a yaali diila.>> Dila nyiŋla, Wen yuk kaab kpagsaŋa a basi kama alege pai Yeezu Kirisita kaabka zaani kaab sila naŋkula po.

ref: The priests do their work each day, and they keep on offering sacrifices that can never take away sins.
text: Kaabteerɔma meena a tom kaabka tuimaŋa ka daa meena. Ba be a nye kaab kala dekdega a paari ka diichoa. Alege kaabka de kan duisi wabaata a basi.

ref: But Christ offered himself as a sacrifice that is good forever. Now he is sitting at God's right side,
text: Yeezu Kirisita be nye kaabka ka bunyi dekki wabaata nyiŋ. Kaabka de abe kasim ta pagrim a boro ka dila taam wuu. Wa ale ga nye dila nueri la, wa yaa kali Wen juga geŋ, zula jigini.

ref: and he will stay there until his enemies are put under his power.
text: Dula jigini, wa yaa limisi ka da dii dai ate wa dachaasaŋa le chim wa yɔm la.

ref: By his one sacrifice he has forever set free from sin the people he brings to God.
text: Wa ale nye kaabka bunyi dekki dila la, a basi kama ate nuru baai ate Wen soa la, a kan maa ta kaasuŋ taam wuu.

ref: The Holy Spirit also speaks of this by telling us that the Lord said,
text: Wen Chiika dek abe siak kama ayen nya kude a sum ka wensie ale Wen ale weeni dii ayen,

ref: “When the time comes, I will make an agreement with them. I will write my laws on their minds and hearts.
text: <<Nɔiyeŋ kaai ate mi le nye ale ba da ŋaai le cheena la, ale mi le pai m sinsaŋŋa a nyo ka ba suiniima po, abe m ŋmarisi ŋa ba zuima po.>>

ref: Then I will forget about their sins and no longer remember their evil deeds.”
text: Wa ŋman weeni gum du ayen, <<M abe kan ŋman teeri ba wabaataŋa ale ba wakaasimaŋa diipo diipo.>>

ref: When sins are forgiven, there is no more need to offer sacrifices. Encouragement and Warning
text: Dila nyiŋla, ba wabaataŋa a dan nya vɔŋteka, ku an poom ŋman magsi ayen ba nye kaabka a duisi ba wabaataŋa a basi.

ref: My friends, the blood of Jesus gives us courage to enter the most holy place
text: Dila nyiŋla, m suata Yeezu ziimu ale lo tɛŋ ate wa kpi la nyiŋ abe ale soa ate ti baga a jo <<Weleŋsa Yegayekka Jigini>> ale ge kan chali yɔgsum.

ref: by a new way that leads to life! And this way takes us through the curtain that is Christ himself.
text: Garuk panni ate ba jam pai lik dɔkku nɔnni la a yaa lak kama ate ti va ka suik kuui ale vua la a jo dula. Yeezu abe pai ka wadek nyiŋka tagri jigi dila a te tama.

ref: We have a great high priest who is in charge of God's house.
text: Ti be ta ka kaabteerɔ kpioŋ ate wa a nya Wen yenni zuk.

ref: We must hold tightly to the hope we say is ours. After all, we can trust the one who made the agreement with us.
text: Ni basi ate ti ŋmasi yik nalimnyiini ti yiila ŋaai ate ti ta la, dii nyiŋla, ti baga a ta siaka kama ayen Wen ale puulim ayen wa nye diila wa le nye kama.

ref: We should keep on encouraging each other to be thoughtful and to do helpful things.
text: Ni basi ate ti ta chaab wie, a maari chaab ate ku basi ate ti ta yaalika ale nuruba a tom tuimaŋsa.

ref: Some people have given up the habit of meeting for worship, but we must not do that. We should keep on encouraging each other, especially since you know that the day of the Lord's coming is getting closer.
text: Ni kan basi ate ti basi chaab tuka ase nuruba gela ale kasim a nye diila. Alege ni basi ate ti a deŋsi chaab kpa nalimnyiini a gum du, ase ni ale nya ale da dii danni ate ti Naawenni le jam la a moata kama la.

ref: No sacrifices can be made for people who decide to sin after they find out about the truth.
text: Dii nyiŋla, kaab ka choa a ŋman karo ayen ka duisi ti wabaataŋa a basi ase ti nin potim seba alege kasim a tom wabaata a cheŋ alege seba ayen ti wom wensieŋa kama.

ref: They are God's enemies, and all they can look forward to is a terrible judgment and a furious fire.
text: Alege baai ale kan siak Wen nɔi la, bala be a limisi ale yɔgsum, buusa ŋaai ale ŋa jam la, ale bolim ŋiak kaai le bu dɛ ba la.

ref: We know that God has said he will punish and take revenge. We also know that the Scriptures say the Lord will judge his people.
text: Tama dek be seba ayen Naawen ale weeni nna. Ti be seba wa ale ka diila kama, wa weeni ayen, <<Ku ka mi wari ate m nye wari tuni baai ale a tom biem tuima la. M be le nye kama.>> (Teerika

ref: It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
text: Ku le pagra ka nna yegayega ase Wen dii ale vua la a nin weeni ayen wa le te fu waalika.

ref: You were kind to people in jail. And you gladly let your possessions be taken away, because you knew you had something better, something that would last forever.
text: Ni maa jam ta jiirim ale nuru baai ate ba yik lik la kama. Nuruba be ale tuesi ni jaabuuri meena la, ni diem ta suipeentik kama a duŋ ni sue. Dii nyiŋla, ni jam seba kama ayen ni ta ŋanta kama ate ba gaam bala nalimnyiini. Ba be kasim boro ka dila taam wuu.

ref: Keep on being brave! It will bring you great rewards.
text: Dila nyiŋla, ni kan pai ni sebchakka a yuk basi, ku ta ka tutuna kpiema a cheena.

ref: Learn to be patient, so you will please God and be given what he has promised.
text: Ku a fɛ kama ayen ni ta chichiiba ate ni baga tom Wen ale a yaali diila ate ni nya wa ale puulim ayen wa le nye dii a te ni la.

ref: As the Scriptures say, “God is coming soon! It won't be very long.
text: <<Dila nyiŋ, ku kan beni gaam taam, ale ge ate waai le wa jam la a jamu, wa kan beni.

ref: The people God accepts will live because of their faith. But he isn't pleased with anyone who turns back.”
text: Mi wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa le ta siaka kama ate wa vuuk. Alege, ba wanyi a dan nyini mi ŋaaŋ a ŋmani, m sui kan peenti ale wa.>> (Yabakkuk

ref: We are not like those people who turn back and get destroyed. We will keep on having faith until we are saved.
text: Alege tama daa baai ale a ŋmani wa ŋaaŋ a yaa cheŋ a bɛ suiku po la. Ti ka baai ale ta siaka ale wa a yaa nya varibasika la.

ref: Faith makes us sure of what we hope for and gives us proof of what we cannot see.
text: Siaka ka wari dii ate nuru ta yiila ale seba chak mɛ ayen di sum ka wensie yaase di le sum nye alege, wa an baga a nya wanni diema la.

ref: It was their faith that made our ancestors pleasing to God.
text: Ku jam ka ba siaka nyiŋ ate Wen jam basi ate dila po demma seba ayen wa sui peenti ale ba kama.

ref: Because of our faith, we know that the world was made at God's command. We also know that what can be seen was made out of what cannot be seen.
text: Ka siaka ale soa ate ti seba ayen ka Wen ale biisi a yaa nye wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋ ale ŋan baai meena wuu ale bo ba po la. Dila nyiŋ ate ti baga a nya ŋan baai ale boro nna la. Ti be an baga a nya ŋan baai ate wa pai nye ŋantaŋa de meena la.

ref: Because Noah had faith, he was warned about something that had not yet happened. He obeyed and built a boat that saved him and his family. In this way the people of the world were judged, and Noah was given the blessings that come to everyone who pleases God.
text: Ku be jam ka siaka mɛ nyiŋ ale soa ate Nowa baga wom Wen ale jam kaam wa a magsi chaab ale wie ŋaai le ŋa nye chum diipo la. Wa siaka nyiŋ ale soa ate wa jam lak tue wom, a yaa nye ŋaaruŋ ayen wa vari wa ale wa dɔkdemma meena a basi. Wa siaka de nyiŋ abe ale soa ate nurubiik tɛŋzuk de a jam nya chivie, ale ge ate Wen wi wa ayen wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ.

ref: Abraham had faith and obeyed God. He was told to go to the land that God had said would be his, and he left for a country he had never seen.
text: Ku jam ka siaka nyiŋ ale soa ate Abrayam zuli Wen nɔi a nyini cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ate Wen jam puulim ayen wa le pai te wa la. Abrayam yaa basi wa tɛŋka a yaa nyini a cheŋ alege poom zɛ juijui dek chekki ate wa jam a cheŋ la.

ref: Because Abraham had faith, he lived as a stranger in the promised land. He lived there in a tent, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who were later given the same promise.
text: Siaka de nyiŋ ate wa jam bo tɛŋ kaai ate Wen puulim ayen wa le pai te wa la. Wa jam bo ka po ase ka nichaanɔ la. Wa ale wa dɔkdemma jam a goa ka viita po ase Aizik ale Jekob ate Wen jam puulim ale ba ate ba mɛ jam bo viita po diila.

ref: Abraham did this, because he was waiting for the eternal city God had planned and built.
text: Dii nyiŋla, Abrayam jam a limisi ayen wa jo ka wenŋmazuk yeri dii ate Wen sɛ te wa la. Yeeŋa de kan maari a lo.

ref: Every one of those people died. But they still had faith, even though they had not received what they had been promised. They were glad just to see these things from far away, and they agreed that they were only strangers and foreigners on this earth.
text: Nyaba de meena ate m biisi ba wie la kpi kama ale ba siaka alege ba an tuesi ŋan baai ate Wen puulim ayen wa le te ba la. Alege siaka nyiŋ ba nya kama ayen ŋanta dua ka jigi nna niŋniŋa ate ba jam a nye ase ba jam paari ku jigini kama la. Ba be jam siak kama ayen ba ka nicham tɛŋzuk de. Ba yenni dek abe bo ka jigi yoŋ.

ref: When people talk this way, it is clear they are looking for a place to call their own.
text: Nuru baai abe ale a poli ase nna la, bala chaab a sak kama ayen ba kasim a gisi ka badek tɛŋ ayen ba kali.

ref: If they had been talking about the land where they had once lived, they could have gone back at any time.
text: Ba be dan kasim a poli ka tɛŋ kaai ate ba pai basi ŋaaŋ la wie, ba ta suik kama a pilim a ŋmani?

ref: But they were looking forward to a better home in heaven. This is why God wasn't ashamed for them to call him their God. He even built a city for them.
text: Aaya, wanni ale, ba kasim a yaali ale ka ninmuna tɛŋ kaai ale gaam ba tɛŋka la. Daa jigi yoŋ tɛŋzuk de, ka wenŋmazuk ale la. Dila nyiŋla, chivie ka Wen ale ba ale wi wa ayen ba Wen yaa. Dii nyiŋla, Wensie wa sɛ ka yeri te ba.

ref: Abraham had been promised that Isaac, his only son, would continue his family. But when Abraham was tested, he had faith and was willing to sacrifice Isaac,
text: Wen jam weeni wa ayen, <<Ka Aizik nyiŋ ate fi le nya ŋaaŋ biik sii ate m puulim la. (Piilimka

ref: because he was sure that God could raise people to life. This was just like getting Isaac back from death.
text: Abrayam be jam ta siaka kama ayen Wen baga a nak nuruba kama a yiti kum po. Dila nyiŋla, daam dan ka ku wensieŋa jigini, ti baga a weeni kama ayen Abrayam ŋman tuesi Aizik ka kum nisima po.

ref: Isaac had faith, and he promised blessings to Jacob and Esau.
text: Ku jam ka siaka nyiŋ ale soa ate Aizik weeni ayen chum da dii dai, Jekob ale Iisɔ le nya niaka kama.

ref: Later, when Jacob was about to die, he leaned on his walking stick and worshiped. Then because of his faith he blessed each of Joseph's sons.
text: Ku jam ka siaka ale basi ate Jekob te Josefi nidoabilisaŋa wanyi wanyi niaka ale ge kpi. Wa jam pai ka wa tachekka a chɔgsi wadek a yiti kali wa gaduokku zuk a yaa puusi Wen a te ba niaka.

ref: And right before Joseph died, he had faith that God would lead the people of Israel out of Egypt. So he told them to take his bones with them.
text: Ku jam ka siaka nyiŋ ale soa ate diipo ate Josefi a jam moata kum la wa biisi magsi chaab ale diipo ate Izirali demma ale jam basi Ejipiti tɛŋka abe ba kuli la. Wa jam maa weeni ba le ba nye wa dii ase wa nin kpi ate Izirali demma basi Ejipiti a kuli la.

ref: Because Moses' parents had faith, they kept him hidden until he was three months old. They saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid to disobey the king's orders.
text: Ku jam ka siaka ale basi ate Moosis kowa ale wa mawa ale biak wa la, a pai wa suk ate ku paari chiisa sita. Ba ale jam nya ale biika ka bimaŋ la, yɔgsum jam ka ba ate ba zɛri Ejipiti Naawa sinsaŋŋa.

ref: Then after Moses grew up, his faith made him refuse to be called the king's grandson.
text: Ku be jam ka siaka ale soa ate biika Moosis ale ga chim nueri la, wa zɛri ayen wa daa Ejipiti Naawa lie biiga.

ref: He chose to be mistreated with God's people instead of having the good time that sin could bring for a little while.
text: Wa jam a yaali ayen ka wa dan maa nam ale Wen nuruma a zunchoŋ gaam wa nin dɛ masim ale biem alege ku kan beni.

ref: Moses knew that the treasures of Egypt were not as wonderful as what he would receive from suffering for the Messiah, and he looked forward to his reward.
text: Wa jam poli kama ayen fi dan nya chivie Kirisitawa nyiŋ, waai ate Wen le tom ate wa jam la nyiŋ, a zunchoŋ ka nna yegayega a gaam Ejipiti jigsika meena. Wa jam a poli dila kama dii nyiŋla, wa nina jam muni ale ka tiirim buui ate wa le nya la.

ref: Because of his faith, Moses left Egypt. Moses had seen the invisible God and wasn't afraid of the king's anger.
text: Ku jam ka siaka ale soa ate Moosis basi Ejipiti tɛŋka alege yɔgsum an jam yik wa ale naawa suipuurumu. Wa kasim jam ta popola ale siaka kama ale Wen, waai ate nurubiik an baga nya wa la.

ref: His faith also made him celebrate Passover. He sprinkled the blood of animals on the doorposts, so that the first-born sons of the people of Israel would not be killed by the destroying angel.
text: Ku jam ka siaka ale soa ate wa weeni nuruma ayen ba nye Gaambasika Tigini ŋandiintaŋa abe ba pai ziimu a misimisi diinaŋa noaŋa ate maarɔ, waai ale a ko nuruba la a dan jam, wa kan ko nidoabili sii ate Izirali demma liŋ biak la.

ref: God's people had faith, and when they had walked around the city of Jericho for seven days, its walls fell down.
text: Ku jam ka siaka ale soa ate Jeriko tɛŋka parika ate ba sɛ gilim ka la a lo. Izirali demma jam cheŋ gilim ka, ka daa ŋayopɔi ale ge ate ka lo.

ref: Their faith helped them conquer kingdoms, and because they did right, God made promises to them. They closed the jaws of lions
text: Be ka siaka nyiŋ ate nyaba de meena a nye kpaliŋsa ale tɛŋsa a nak dɛ, a fɛ ate wensie boro, a nya Wen ale puulim ale ba ayen ba le nya diila, a nye ate gbeŋma a baga lik ŋa noa,

ref: and put out raging fires and escaped from the swords of their enemies. Although they were weak, they were given the strength and power to chase foreign armies away.
text: a kpimsi bolim kpienta, a chali liisi gebik woŋ sii ate ba jam ayen ba pai ko ba la. Ba jam wobsa kama alege tulim nya pagrim. Ba jam ta pagrim ka nna yegayega tugurisa po a yaa nak satɛŋsa tugurik tɔŋdɔba dɛ.

ref: Some women received their loved ones back from death. Many of these people were tortured, but they refused to be released. They were sure they would get a better reward when the dead are raised to life.
text: Nipooba gela baai ale ta siaka la nyiŋ ale soa ate ba mabisa ba gela baai ale kpi la a yaa yiti kum po. Ba gela mɛ a jam zɛri kama ayen nuruba kan basi ba namsika alege siak ayen ba namsi ba a ko, ayen ku basi ate ba yiti kum po a ta nyuvuri maŋ.

ref: Others were made fun of and beaten with whips, and some were chained in jail.
text: Nuruba jam nye ba gela mɛ a la, a miiri ba, a pai chɔrima bobi ba a ta ba ga lik.

ref: Still others were stoned to death or sawed in two or killed with swords. Some had nothing but sheep skins or goat skins to wear. They were poor, mistreated, and tortured.
text: Ba gela mɛ, ba yuk ba ale tana, a pai gebisa a gebi ba buye, a pai gebik woŋsa a ko ba gela mɛ. Ba gela mɛ a jam a jo ka piisa ale bua gbaŋsa, ba gela mɛ a jam chim ka ŋanjaksa nna yegayega, nuruba namsi ba gela a te ba tuem.

ref: The world did not deserve these good people, who had to wander in deserts and on mountains and had to live in caves and holes in the ground.
text: Ku an poom ŋman magsi ayen tɛŋzuk de demma a ŋman ta nuruma de chaab ba suŋsuŋŋa. Ba kasim jam bo ka sagni po a nyiem cheŋ a basi du, nna ase nicham la. Ba jam maa bo ka guuta zuima, ale pina vie po, ale maari a goa vie po mɛ.

ref: All of them pleased God because of their faith! But still they died without being given what had been promised.
text: Nya bade meena siaka nyiŋ abe ale soa ate Wen jam weeni ayen wa sui peenti ale ba kama alege, ba an jam nya Wen ale jam puulim ayen ba le nya jabuui la.

ref: This was because God had something better in store for us. And he did not want them to reach the goal of their faith without us.
text: Dii nyiŋla, Wen daam poom poli ayen wa nye ka wamaŋ ate di gaam dila a te ti. Wa be poli kama ayen wa kan nye ate nuru bala kan ta kaasuŋŋoa, ase ka wa nin pai tama mɛ a gum chaab ale bala, ale wa yaa nye dila.

ref: None of you have yet been hurt in your battle against sin.
text: Boan nyiŋŋa, ni ale diem boro a nye kpaliŋka ale biem la, ni an diem kpaliŋ paari juijui ate ni le kpi la.

ref: But you have forgotten that the Scriptures say to God's children, “When the Lord punishes you, don't make light of it, and when he corrects you, don't be discouraged.
text: Nama baŋ Wen ale biisi dii ayen ku deŋsi ni kpa ni ale ka wa bisa nyiŋla? Wa weeni ayen, <<M nidoabili yaa, kan pai ku chim diinta ase fi nin nye wari kaasi ate Naawen sak fu yam maga dega. Yaase fi basi ate fi su kaasi ase wa ale a toariŋ fu.

ref: God corrects all his children, and if he doesn't correct you, then you don't really belong to him.
text: Ni be dan kan a nya waalika ase wa bisa meena la, ku a sak ase ni sum daa wa bisa la. Ku a sak ase ni poom zɛ waai dek ale ka ni ko la.

ref: Our human fathers correct us for a short time, and they do it as they think best. But God corrects us for our own good, because he wants us to be holy, as he is.
text: Tama koma be ka nurubisa. Ba be a te waalika kama a magsi chaab ale badek ale poli dii ayen ku magsi ti kaasuŋku la. Waalika de a nyiem be kan beni. Alege Wen a te ti waalika kama ayen ku ta nalim jam ti jigi ate ti maa ta weleŋsa ase wa ale ka diila.

ref: It is never fun to be corrected. In fact, at the time it is always painful. But if we learn to obey by being corrected, we will do right and live at peace.
text: Diipo ate ti nyiem nya waalika la, dila powa ti sue a kaasi kama, ŋa kan peenti. Alege ti dan siak a te wa, ku a nye ase ka tiib ale a yɔni yɔna la. Ase tiimu ale a yɔni yɔna la, waalika mɛ a te ti ka yɔna. Yɔnaŋa de abe ale masim boka ale wayɔrisima tuima.

ref: Try to live at peace with everyone! Live a clean life. If you don't, you will never see the Lord.
text: Ni pii nyiŋ ate ni ta nye masik ale waai meena, abe ni welema dii nyiŋla, waai ale kan welema la, an baga a boro ale Naawen ya.

ref: Make sure no one misses out on God's wonderful kindness. Don't let anyone become bitter and cause trouble for the rest of you.
text: Ni kpesi nidek ate ni wanyi mɛ la a kan jɔk Wen ŋmanteka abe ni wanyi mɛ la a kan chim tituak a pai bu yaamu chɔgsi tiib sinsila,

ref: You have not come to a place like Mount Sinai that can be seen and touched. There is no flaming fire or dark cloud or storm
text: Mi a weeni nyaŋa de meena kama boan nyiŋŋa, nama an jam ase Izirali demma ale jan jam diila. Ni an jam daa jaab waai ate nuru baga a tiri wa ase Sinai Guuku ale ku bolim ŋiaka ale a dɛ la, ale legini nna kpitɔ la, ale va pagrika,

ref: because they could not obey its commands. They were even told to kill any animal that touched the mountain.
text: dii nyiŋla weeni kaai ale jam weeni ayen, <<Duŋ a dan poom tiri guuku, ku a fɛ kama ayen ba pai tana a yuk ka ko la.>> (Nyinika

ref: You have now come to Mount Zion and to the heavenly Jerusalem. This is the city of the living God, where thousands and thousands of angels have come to celebrate.
text: Alege nama ate mi a weeni ayen ni nya, ni goanti jam ka Zayon Guuku ale Wen dii ale vua la tɛŋka wenŋmazuk Jerusalem ale maarɔ baai ale piisi nna yegayega la,

ref: Here you will find all of God's dearest children, whose names are written in heaven. And you will find God himself, who judges everyone. Here also are the spirits of those good people who have been made perfect.
text: ale Wen biik sii ate wa liŋ biak la tigsika po kaai ale ka suipeentik tigsika la jigi. Bisaŋa de yue ale ŋmarisi bo wenŋmazuk. Ni jam ka Wen dii ale a bo nurubiik meena buusa la jigi. Ni chiisaŋa jam gum chaab ale ka nuru baai ale kan ta kaasuŋ la, chiisa.

ref: And Jesus is here! He is the one who makes God's new agreement with us, and his sprinkled blood says much better things than the blood of Abel.
text: Yeezu jigi, wa ka nɔiyeŋ paalika sanyigmoa, ate ziim buui ale a misi la jigi bu zunchoŋ Abel ziimu kama.

ref: Make sure you obey the one who speaks to you. The people did not escape, when they refused to obey the one who spoke to them at Mount Sinai. Do you think you can possibly escape, if you refuse to obey the one who speaks to you from heaven?
text: Ni be kpesi nidek ate ni kan zɛri Wen ale a biisi diila womka. Baai ate wa jam kaam ba tɛŋzuk de ate ba zɛri la a dan kan baga a chali bɛ ya, tama be ale nye ka sɛ a baga chali bɛ waai ale a biisi ate ku nyini wenŋmazuk la jigi ase ti nin zɛri wa?

ref: When God spoke the first time, his voice shook only the earth. This time he has promised to shake the earth once again, and heaven too.
text: Dila powa wa ale biisi la, ku jam choa tɛŋka meena kama. Alege yɔgyɔgla de, wa puulim kama ayen, <<M le choa ka tɛŋka a ŋman gum du. Be daa tɛŋka nyiini ate m le choa, m le choa ka tɛŋka ale wenŋmazuk meena a maa gum du.>> (Aggai

ref: We should be grateful we were given a kingdom that cannot be shaken. And in this kingdom we please God by worshiping him and by showing him great honor and respect.
text: Ni be basi ate ti te Wen jiam dii nyiŋla, wa te ti ka tɛŋ kaai ate ti le chim nalima la. Tɛŋka de abe kan maa choa a voori. Dila nyiŋla, ni be basi ate ti nye wa jiam abe ti a te wa zula ŋaai le ŋa basi ate wa sui peenti la, abe ti a chali yɔgsum ale wa,

ref: Keep being concerned about each other as the Lord's followers should.
text: Ni kasim ta yaalika ale chaab ase Kirisita bisa la.

ref: Be sure to welcome strangers into your home. By doing this, some people have welcomed angels as guests, without even knowing it.
text: Ni a teeri ate ni siak a tuesi nicham ni yeeŋa. Nuruba gela jam nye dila kama a yaa maa tuesi Wen maarɔba alege zɛ ayen ba ka Wen maarɔba.

ref: Remember the Lord's people who are in jail and be concerned for them. Don't forget those who are suffering, but imagine you are there with them.
text: Ni a teeri baai mɛ ale bo likka diina po la wie, ase nama mɛ maa bo ka likka diinaŋa po ale ba la. Ni a teeri baai mɛ ale a nam la ase nama mɛ maari a nam kama la.

ref: Have respect for marriage. Always be faithful to your partner, because God will punish anyone who is immoral or unfaithful in marriage.
text: Waai meena a magsi wa a zuli faarika ale yalika. Ba kan taŋ ba gaduokku. Chorɔba ale pooba a magsi ba ta wensie ale chaab. Wen ale bo baai ale kan yali yaase ba faari ale bobi chaab a goa yaase kaboŋ nyeerisa buusa.

ref: Don't forget about your leaders who taught you God's message. Remember what kind of lives they lived and try to have faith like theirs.
text: Ni teeri ni kpaŋŋa baai ale biisi Wen wanni a sak ni la. Ni poli nya ba nyeboka ale jam ta dii a jam alege ate ba yaa kpi la, ate ni tomsi ba siaka ale jam ka diila.

ref: Jesus Christ never changes! He is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
text: Yeezu Kirisita ka dila a ta nyini diem ale jinla ale daaŋa meena wuu. Wa kan maari a tagri diipo diipo.

ref: Don't be fooled by any kind of strange teachings. It is better to receive strength from God's gift of undeserved grace than to depend on certain foods. After all, these foods don't really help the people who eat them.
text: Ni kan basi ate sinsak kperikaliisa meena tɔgatɔga a nye ate ni basi suik maŋka vaka. Ku nala kama ate ti tuesi Wen tiirim buui le bu basi ate ti suiniimaŋa pagra ŋmanteka nyiŋ la. Daa ti nin a va ŋandiinta kisita ale ti suiniimaŋa ta pagrimoa. Baai ale a va sinsaŋŋa de chaama la, an diem nya maarika ŋa po.

ref: But we have an altar where even the priests who serve in the place of worship have no right to eat.
text: Kaabteerɔma ale a tom viuku po la a ka suik a dɛ ŋan baai ale dua kuŋkuŋku zuk la.

ref: After the high priest offers the blood of animals as a sin offering, the bodies of those animals are burned outside the camp.
text: Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku a ta ka duŋsaŋa ziimu a jo jigi dii ale ta tuilum la a nye kaabka wabaata nyiŋ, alege duŋsaŋa ba a ju ka peelim.

ref: Jesus himself suffered outside the city gate, so his blood would make people holy.
text: Kude nyiŋ Yeezu yaa kpi tɛŋka peelim, ayen wa baga a soti nuruma biem po ale wadek ziimu.

ref: This is why we should go outside the camp to Jesus and share in his disgrace.
text: Dila nyiŋla, ni basi ate ti nyini nuruma boka jigini nakpiaka ase wa ale nye diila a maa nya chivie wa nyiŋ.

ref: On this earth we don't have a city that lasts forever, but we are waiting for such a city.
text: Dii nyiŋla, tɛŋzuk de daa tɛŋ kaai ate ti le boro taam wuu la, ti ta yiila a limisi ka tɛŋ kaai ate ti le nya chum diipo la.

ref: But don't forget to help others and to share your possessions with them. This too is like offering a sacrifice that pleases God.
text: Ni kan baŋ ate ni a tom wamaŋsa a te nuruba abe ni pai ŋan baai ate ni ta la a chari chaab, dii nyiŋla, wieŋa de a nye ase ka kaabka la a te Wen ate wa sui a peenti.

ref: Obey your leaders and do what they say. They are watching over you, and they must answer to God. So don't make them sad as they do their work. Make them happy. Otherwise, they won't be able to help you at all.
text: Ni a zuli ni kpaŋŋa noa ale dii meena wuu ate ba a weeni ni la. Ba kasim a nya ni zuk kama daa meena, dii nyiŋla, Wen le bek ba kama ase ba ale a nya ni zuk ate dii ale dii nye la. Ni be dan a te ba zula, ba a tom ba tuimaŋa ale ka suipeentik. Kan daa di, ba a tom ale ka sui kaasima. Dila be kan maari ni.

ref: I especially want you to pray that I can visit you again soon. Final Prayers and Greetings
text: M be a saalim ni ale ka ninmuna ayen, ni puusi Wen ate wa basi ate m pilim ŋman jam ni jigi yɔgyɔgla.

ref: God gives peace, and he raised our Lord Jesus Christ from death. Now Jesus is like a Great Shepherd whose blood was used to make God's eternal agreement with his flock.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de suiyɔgni Wenni waai ale nak piisaŋa Naapeerik Kpioŋku a yiti kum po nɔiyeŋ kaai ale kaa kpeglim la ziimu nyiŋ la, wala ka ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu,

ref: My friends, I have written only a short letter to encourage you, and I beg you to pay close attention to what I have said.
text: M suata, mi a saalim kama ayen ni lak tue nalimnyiini ale chichiiba a wom tuntomika de ate m weeni a deŋsi ni kpa la, dii nyiŋla, gbaŋka de ate m ŋmarisi a te ni la, an wɔŋa gaam taam ya.

ref: By now you surely must know that our friend Timothy is out of jail. If he gets here in time, I will bring him with me when I come to visit you.
text: Mi a yaali ayen m weeni a sak ni kama ayen ba lak ti suoku Timoti likka dɔk po a basi kama. Wa dan jam nwuli, ate m cheena, m le ta wa maa jam kama.

ref: Please give my greetings to your leaders and to the rest of the Lord's people. His followers from Italy send you their greetings.
text: Puusi ni kpaŋŋa meena ale Wen nuruma meena te ti. Ti suataŋa baai ale nyini Itali tɛŋka a maa bo ale ti la, a puusi ni.

ref: I pray that God will be kind to all of you!
text: Naawen ŋmanteka a bo ale ni meena.

ref: From James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ. Greetings to the twelve tribes scattered all over the world. Faith and Wisdom
text: Mi, Jeemsi, waai ale ka Wen ale ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita tomteerɔ la, a puusi nama Izirali diina pi ale buyewa ale waaŋ bo tɛŋka meena po la.

ref: My friends, be glad, even if you have a lot of trouble.
text: M suata, ni dan jam nya nyenyaka, ni basi ate ni sue a peenti yegayega.

ref: You know you learn to endure by having your faith tested.
text: Ni seba ayen ni siaka ale Yeezu a dan baga a zaani nyenyaka de po, ni le baga zaani nyenyaka meena kama.

ref: If any of you need wisdom, you should ask God, and it will be given to you. God is generous and won't correct you for asking.
text: Wen ta niaka yegayega. Wa kasim pai ka ŋanta nna yegayega a te baai ale a juisi wa la. Dila nyiŋla, yam a dan posim ni ba gela jigi, ni puusi a te Wen ale wa le pai yam a te ni.

ref: But when you ask for something, you must have faith and not doubt. Anyone who doubts is like an ocean wave tossed around in a storm.
text: Ni dan puusi te wa, ku a fɛ ate ni ta siaka ale wa abe ni kan ta chichama. Chichama nyɔnɔ a nye ase ka viok ale a fɔbi nyakpiemu ate bu a cheŋ niŋ ale ŋaaŋ diila.

ref: Any of God's people who are poor should be glad he thinks so highly of them.
text: Nama baai ale ka ŋanjaksa la, ku a fɛ kama ate ni ta suipeentik, dii nyiŋla, Wen pai ni zaani ka niŋ.

ref: scorched by the burning heat of the sun. The flowers lose their blossoms, and their beauty is destroyed. This is how the rich will disappear, as they go about their business. Trials and Temptations
text: Wenbinni a dan jueli ate kantueŋka a moak yegayega, puutaŋa a jak kama a yuiri ate ti nalimu mɛ a bɛ. Suiku la po jigsirɔma a dan bo ba tuimaŋa po a tom, ba mɛ a kpi kama.

ref: God will bless you, if you don't give up when your faith is being tested. He will reward you with a glorious life, just as he rewards everyone who loves him.
text: Suipeentik bo ka waai ale baga a zaani nyenyaka la jigi. Naawen be puulim kama ayen wa le te nuru wala choa tiirim. Tiirimu de ale wa nyuvuri dii ale kan ka kpeglimka la ate wa le pai te baai ale a yaali wa la.

ref: Don't blame God when you are tempted! God cannot be tempted by evil, and he doesn't use evil to tempt others.
text: Nyenyaka a dan jam, waai a kan weeni ayen ka, <<Wen ale nye mi a nya.>> Wen a kan pai biem a nye nuru a nya yaase wa nye waai a nya.

ref: We are tempted by our own desires that drag us off and trap us.
text: Alege ka tidek kɔrisa ale a dari ti ate ti a tom tuimbaata.

ref: Our desires make us sin, and when sin is finished with us, it leaves us dead.
text: Dila nyiŋ kɔrisa a dan yik lɔgi, si a biak ka wabaata ate wabaata yaa dan chim paari, ti yaa biak kum.

ref: Don't be fooled, my dear friends.
text: M dek suata, ni kan a paasi chaaba.

ref: Every good and perfect gift comes down from the Father who created all the lights in the heavens. He is always the same and never makes dark shadows by changing.
text: Jaabuuri meena ate ti ta ate ba nala la, a nyini ka Wen jigi. Wa nye chiŋmarisaŋa meena a pai si a nyo wenŋmazuk ayen si a nyaksi. Wa kan tagri diipo diipo ase yisuŋtaŋa ale a tagri diila.

ref: He wanted us to be his own special people, and so he sent the true message to give us new birth. Hearing and Obeying
text: Ku ka Wen dek yaalika ate wa biak ti a va wa wensie wanni, ate wa yaa basi ate ti dɛ jaabuuri meena ate wa nye la niŋ.

ref: If you are angry, you cannot do any of the good things God wants done.
text: dii nyiŋla, ti dan ta suipuurum ale nuruba, ti kan va Wen ale a yaali diila. Wa a yaali kama ayen ti a tom tuimaŋsa a te wa.

ref: Obey God's message! Don't fool yourselves by just listening to it.
text: Ni dan a wom ŋa ale kan va ŋa, ni a paasi ka nidek.

ref: If you hear the message and don't obey it, you are like people who stare at themselves in a mirror
text: Nuru dan a wom Wen wieŋa ale kan va ŋa, wa a nye ase ka nuru waai a nyiem ale a nya wadek nyaasuŋ po diila.

ref: and forget what they look like as soon as they leave.
text: Wa dan nya wadek nyaasuŋku po a nueri, ale basi dula, wa deri a baŋ wa le poom a neensi diila kama.

ref: But you must never stop looking at the perfect law that sets you free. God will bless you in everything you do, if you listen and obey, and don't just hear and forget.
text: Nuru wala choa a nye se ka waai ale wom Wen Sinsak maŋsaŋa ale deri baŋ la. Ku be a fɛ kama ayen ni kan a nye dila, dii nyiŋla, Wen Sinsak maŋsaŋa a vari ka nuruba a basi. Dila nyiŋ ku a fɛ kama ayen ni ŋmasi wom ŋa nalimnyiini abe ni a va ŋa. Ni dan a nye dila Wen le te ni niaka.

ref: If you think you are being religious, but can't control your tongue, you are fooling yourself, and your religion is useless.
text: Nuru waai a dan a poli ayen wa va ka Wen ale kan yik wadek wa biik po, wa a paasi ka wadek. Wa Wenni vaka ka kinla.

ref: Religion that pleases God the Father must be pure and spotless. You must help needy orphans and widows and not let this world make you evil.
text: Ti Kowa Wen a yaali kama ayen ti a va wa ale wensie. Dila nyiŋla ku a magsi ka ti a maari kpin sii ale pukɔga ŋaai ale a nam la, abe ti kan basi ate tɛŋka demma tuimbaataŋa a chɔgsi ti.

ref: My friends, if you have faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, you won't treat some people better than others.
text: M suata, nama baai ale ta siaka ale ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita waai ale ka zula meena nyɔnɔ la, ni kan luk a yaali nuruba gela abe ni basi ba gela.

ref: Suppose a rich person wearing fancy clothes and a gold ring comes to one of your meetings. And suppose a poor person dressed in worn-out clothes also comes.
text: Ni dan tigsi chaab ayen ni puusi a te Wen ate nuruba baye a jam jo ni tigsika jigini, ate ba wanyi a jo jigsirɔ gatta ale su ligra nifelima ate ŋa a nyaksi, alege nwala mɛ jo garuk tii ale kan nala,

ref: You must not give the best seat to the one in fancy clothes and tell the one who is poor to stand at the side or sit on the floor.
text: ni dan te jigsirɔwa zula nna yegayega a weeni wa ayen, <<Nya kali maŋ jigi ale nna,>> alege weeni jajakka ayen wa, <<Cheŋ ga zaani denna,>> yaase <<Kali tɛŋ,>>

ref: This is the same as saying that some people are better than others, and you would be acting like a crooked judge.
text: nya kude a sak kama ayen ni a bo ka nuruba buusa dii nyiŋla, ni popolaŋa ka popola baata, ku an nala ate ni a luk chaaba.

ref: My dear friends, pay attention. God has given a lot of faith to the poor people in this world. God has also promised them a share in his kingdom that he will give to everyone who loves him.
text: M dek suata, ni wom de. Wen lueri ka baai ate tɛŋzuk de nuruma a poli ayen ba ka ŋanjaksa la ayen ba jigsi ale ba siaka ale Wen, abe ba dɛ Wen naam buui ate wa puulim ayen wa pai a te baai ale a yaali wa la.

ref: Aren't they the ones who make fun of your Lord?
text: Bala ale biisi a kaasi yuei maŋ kaai ate Wen a te ni la.

ref: You will do all right, if you obey the most important law in the Scriptures. It is the law that commands us to love others as much as we love ourselves.
text: Ni dan a va Wen naamu sinsak ŋaai ate ba ŋmarisi Wen Gbaŋka po la nalimnyiini ayen, A yaali fi vaanchoa ase fi ale a yaali fidek diila. (Kaabka

ref: But if you treat some people better than others, you have done wrong, and the Scriptures teach that you have sinned.
text: Ni dan luk a yaali nuruba gela ale kan yaali ba gela, dila an nala. Kula nyɔnɔwa a tom ka wabiok. Wen Sinsaŋŋa abe le bek wa kama

ref: If you obey every law except one, you are still guilty of breaking them all.
text: dii nyiŋla, waai a dan va wa sinsaŋŋa meena alege jam kaasi dinyi wa kaasi ka ŋa meena.

ref: Do this, because on the day of judgment there will be no pity for those who have not had pity on others. But even in judgment, God is merciful! Faith and Works
text: Tama be dan kan basi ate ti boka a nye dila, Wen kan ta jiirim ale ti dii nyiŋla, ti an jam ta jiirim ale ti vaanchaaba. Jiirim nyɔnɔ kan chali yɔgsum ale Wen buusa boka.

ref: My friends, what good is it to say you have faith, when you don't do anything to show you really do have faith? Can this kind of faith save you?
text: M suata, nuru waai a dan weeni ayen wa ta siaka ale Yeezu alege kan tom tuimaŋsa wa siaka nyiini an baga vari wa a basi,

ref: you shouldn't just say, “I hope all goes well for you. I hope you will be warm and have plenty to eat.” What good is it to say this, unless you do something to help?
text: ate ni wanyi yaa nya wa a weeni wa ayen, <<Wen ale te fu garuk ale ŋandiinta,>> alege kan poom a poli nuruwa ale a yaali fi maarika diila,

ref: Suppose someone disagrees and says, “It is possible to have faith without doing kind deeds.” I would answer, “Prove that you have faith without doing kind deeds, and I will prove that I have faith by doing them.”
text: Alege waai ale weeni ayen, <<Nuru wanyi ale a ta siaka, ate wa choa a tom tuimaŋsa.>> Mi ale weeni wa ayen, <<Sak mu nuru waai ale ta siaka ale Yeezu alege kan tom tuimaŋsa la. Mi ale tom tuimaŋsa a sak nuruba ayen mi ta siaka ale Yeezu kama.>>

ref: You surely believe there is only one God. That's fine. Even demons believe this, and it makes them shake with fear.
text: Fi ta siaka ayen Wen ka dinyi dekki a boro? Kula ka wensie. Chichirik baataŋa mɛ a ta siaka kama ayen Wen ka dinyi dekki a boro. Si a chali wa yɔgsum mɛ kama.

ref: Now you see how Abraham's faith and deeds worked together. He proved his faith was real by what he did.
text: Abrayam siaka ale wa tuimaŋa a jam ka bunyi. Wa ale nye diila a sak ti kama ayen wa sum ta siaka ale Naawen kama.

ref: This is what the Scriptures mean by saying, “Abraham had faith in God, and God accepted him.” That's how Abraham became God's friend.
text: Wie ŋaai ate ba ŋmarisi gbaŋka po la, ka wensie. Ba ŋmarisi weeni ayen, Abrayam ta siaka kama ale Wen. Ka dila nyiŋ ale soa ate Wen a wi wa ayen wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ (Piilimka

ref: My friends, we should not all try to become teachers. In fact, teachers will be judged more strictly than others.
text: M suata, ni seba ayen Wen le jam a bo tama baai ale ka sagrɔba la buusa a gaam ti sua tintila. Ka dila ale soa ate ku a fɛ ayen ni kan piisi a chim sagrɔba.

ref: All of us do many wrong things. But if you can control your tongue, you are mature and able to control your whole body.
text: Ti meena a kasim a nye wie a kaasi kama. Nuru a dan kan nye wie a kaasi wa biik po, wa ka nuru maŋ nna yegayega ale baga wadek mɛ a yik nalimnyiini.

ref: By putting a bit into the mouth of a horse, we can turn the horse in different directions.
text: Nuruba nyiem a pai ka wusuma noabaŋsa a su ŋa noa po ate ŋa baga a siak ba noa a va ba a cheŋ juijui meena ate ba a yaali la.

ref: It takes strong winds to move a large sailing ship, but the captain uses only a small rudder to make it go in any direction.
text: Ni a poli ŋaaruŋ kpioŋ kuui ale bo nyiam po ate vioku a fɔbi ku ate ku a chali nyiam zuk nna yegayega la. Ŋaaruŋku damdɔma a baga a pai duok fiik kama a nye ate ŋaaruŋku a cheŋ juijui meena ate ba a yaali ayen ku cheŋ la.

ref: Our tongues are small too, and yet they brag about big things. It takes only a spark to start a forest fire!
text: Ku ka dila ale nurubiik giŋgeluŋ kuui ale kan soa dii alege a biisi kanjanta wie la. Ni be ŋman poli nya ase bolim magadega ale baga a dɛ sagi kpienni diila.

ref: The tongue is like a spark. It is an evil power that dirties the rest of the body and sets a person's entire life on fire with flames that come from hell itself.
text: Nuru giŋgeluŋ a nye se ka bolim la. Ku ka bolim buui ale nyini Sitaana jigi a baga ju tɛŋka meena la. Giŋgeluŋku de abe le baga kaasi ti nyuvunni ti nyeka meena po ale bolim buui ale a nyini bolim buui ale kan maara kpimsi la jigini.

ref: All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures can be tamed and have been tamed.
text: Nuruba baga a baliŋ duŋsa ale nuinsa ale wiiga ale nyiam po ŋanta alege

ref: But our tongues get out of control. They are restless and evil, and always spreading deadly poison.
text: waai karo a diem baga a baliŋ wa giŋgeluŋŋoa. Ti giŋgeluŋtaŋa ka ŋan baata nna yegayega ate ti an baga a yik ti. Ti a nye se ka choŋ pagrik la.

ref: My dear friends, with our tongues we speak both praises and curses. We praise our Lord and Father, and we curse people who were created to be like God, and this isn't right.
text: Ti pai ka noa ŋala a pak Wen ale ŋman pai noa ŋala dek a lɛ nuruba. M suata, dii ate ti a nye la an nala.

ref: Can clean water and dirty water both flow from the same spring?
text: Ni seba ayen vili yeŋ nyiam an baga a masa ale a tua.

ref: Can a fig tree produce olives or a grapevine produce figs? Does fresh water come from a well full of salt water? Wisdom from Above
text: M suata, nama diem nya kiŋkaŋ ale ka yɔni chaama yaase gaab ale bu yɔni kiŋkama yaase nya buui ale ta yesa la a baga a chim nyanyuimoa?

ref: Are any of you wise or sensible? Then show it by living right and by being humble and wise in everything you do.
text: Nuru wanyi a bo ni po a ta yammoa? Wa basi ate wa boka ale wa tuimaŋsaŋa a sak nuruba ayen wa ka yam nyɔnɔ, alege ka kanjanta mɛ.

ref: But if your heart is full of bitter jealousy and selfishness, don't brag or lie to cover up the truth.
text: Alege ni dan ta nyuri ale popo soblum ale chim butuem nyam, ni kan a nak kuusa a velim ayen ni ka wensie nyama.

ref: This kind of wisdom doesn't come from above. It is earthly and selfish and comes from the devil himself.
text: Yammu de choa an nyini Wen jigi ya, bu nyini ka nurubiik ale chichirik baata jigi.

ref: Whenever people are jealous or selfish, they cause trouble and do all sorts of cruel things.
text: Juijui meena ate nuruba a dan boro ate ba ta nyuri ale butuem ba nyiem kasim ta ka chaab ale a tom wabaata tuima meena nna tɔgatɔga.

ref: Why do you fight and argue with each other? Isn't it because you are full of selfish desires that fight to control your body?
text: Ka boa ale soa ate nama kasim a kpaliŋ chaab ale ta daanika ale chaaba? Ni a kpaliŋ chaab ka nidek ale a yaali diila nyiŋ.

ref: You want something you don't have, and you will do anything to get it. You will even kill! But you still cannot get what you want, and you won't get it by fighting and arguing. You should pray for it.
text: Ni ta kɔrisa ale ŋanta, alege ni kan nya ba. Ka dila ale soa ate ni a ko nuruba. Ni kasim a yaali ka ni vaanchaab ŋanta, alege ni an baga a nya ba. Ka dila ale soa ate ni sue kasim a kpaliŋ chaab la. Ni le kan puusi a bek Wen ayen wa pai te ni la nyiŋ ale soa ate ni kan nya ba.

ref: You people aren't faithful to God! Don't you know if you love the world, you are God's enemies? And if you decide to be a friend of the world, you make yourself an enemy of God.
text: Nama kaboŋ nyeerisaŋa nna, nama zɛ ayen doata ale tɛŋka po ka dachaani ale Naawen ya? Dila nyiŋ waai ale a yaali ayen wa chim tɛŋka po doa la a chim ka Naawen dachiak.

ref: Do you doubt the Scriptures that say, “God truly cares about the Spirit he has put in us”?
text: Ni kan a poli ayen ba le ŋmarisi dii Wen Gbaŋka po la, ka kinla. Ba ŋmarisi weeni ayen, <<Chiik kaai ate Wen a pai nyo ti nyiŋsaŋa po la, kasim a yaali ka ŋanta.>>

ref: In fact, God treats us with even greater kindness, just as the Scriptures say, “God opposes everyone who is proud, but he blesses all who are humble with undeserved grace.”
text: Alege ŋmante kaai ate Wen pai te ti la, a pagra gaam chiik kaai ate wa pai nyo ti po la kama. Ba ŋman ŋmarisi Wen Gbaŋka po a weeni ayen, <<Wa ŋmani a te baai ale kan ta kanjanta la kama alege kasim ta chaab ale baai ale a nak ba kuusa la.>> (Wamagsima

ref: Surrender to God! Resist the devil, and he will run from you.
text: Dila nyiŋla ni pai nidek meena a te Wen abe ni zɛri jabioku ate wa nyini ni jigi a chali bɛ.

ref: Come near to God, and he will come near to you. Clean up your lives, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you people who can't make up your mind.
text: Ni forisi paari Wen ate wa mɛ forisi paari ni. Nama baai ale ka tuimbaata nyam la, ni nari ni nisima ale waba tii ate ni a nye la. Nama baai ale ka popola buye nyam la, ni sugri ni popola tɔgatɔga ŋaai ale bo ni suiniima po la a basi.

ref: Be sad and sorry and weep. Stop laughing and start crying. Be gloomy instead of glad.
text: Ni basi ate ni sue kaasi abe ni a kum. Ni basi ate ni laataŋa mɛ a tagri chim kumsa, abe ni popeentika a chim sui kaasuŋ.

ref: Be humble in the Lord's presence, and he will honor you. Saying Cruel Things about Others
text: Ni yik nidek a zuli Naawen ate wa pai ni chim niŋdeerɔba.

ref: My friends, don't say cruel things about others! If you do, or if you condemn others, you are condemning God's Law. And if you condemn the Law, you put yourself above the Law and refuse to obey either it
text: M suata, ni kan a biisi wabaata wie a te chaaba. Baai ale a biisi wabaata wie a te chaab ale a bo chaab buusa la, bala chaab a biisi ka wabaata wie a te Wen Sinsaŋŋa ale a bu ŋa buusa. Nama dan a bu Wen Sinsaŋŋa buusa, ku a sak se ni kan va ŋa kama la.

ref: or God who gave it. God is our judge, and he can save or destroy us. What right do you have to condemn anyone? Warning against Bragging
text: Wen nyiini ale a te sinsaŋŋa ale a bo nuruba buusa mɛ. Wala nyiini le baga vari ti a basi, wala nyiini abe le baga a te ti waalika. Ni dan a bo ni suata buusa, nama a poli ayen ni ka bana?

ref: You should know better than to say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to the city. We will do business there for a year and make a lot of money!”
text: Ni ba gela kasim a weeni chaab kama ayen, <<Jinla yaase chum, ti le nyiem a cheŋ tɛŋ ka choa a ga bo dula ate ku paari ase ben la a gerim ate ti nya ligra.>>

ref: What do you know about tomorrow? How can you be so sure about your life? It is nothing more than mist that appears for only a little while before it disappears.
text: Ni be basi ate m weeni sak ni ayen ni zɛ chum ale ta dii cheen la. Ni a nye se ka pik la, ka dan boro saluiku, ku kan beni ale ge ate ka ŋman a bɛ.

ref: You should say, “If the Lord lets us live, we will do these things.”
text: Ku magsi ka ni a weeni ayen, <<Ku dan ka Naawen yaalika, ti le baga a tom ti tuimaŋa.>>

ref: Yet you are stupid enough to brag, and it is wrong to be so proud.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ni ta ka kanjanta ale a nak kuusa. Ni ale a weeni diila an nala.

ref: If you don't do what you know is right, you have sinned.
text: Nuru waai ale seba tuimaŋsa tomka, alege a zɛri ŋa tomka la, wa a nye ka wabiok.

ref: You rich people should cry and weep! Terrible things are going to happen to you.
text: Jigsirɔma, ni wom mi. Ni le jam a nam ka nna yegayega. Dila nyiŋ ku a fɛ kama ayen ni a yiili abe ni a kum.

ref: Your treasures have already rotted, and moths have eaten your clothes.
text: Ni ŋantaŋa yegayega ate ni ta la, a kaasi kama ate ni gattaŋa miari mɛ a boro a dɛ ti.

ref: Your money has rusted, and the rust will be evidence against you, as it burns your body like fire. Yet you keep on storing up wealth in these last days.
text: Ni ligmɔniŋka mɛ a muni kaasi kama. Munika de a sak kama ayen ni nye kaasi kama ate Wen yaa nya a te ni waalika. Tɛŋka meena kpeglimka a kan beni ale ge jam, alege nama kasim kpelisi ni ŋantaŋa yegayega meena a dueni.

ref: You refused to pay the people who worked in your fields, and now their unpaid wages are shouting out against you. The Lord All-Powerful has surely heard the cries of the workers who harvested your crops.
text: Ni an tuni nuru baai ale a tom ni tattaŋa po la. Ni be wom ba funfɔblaŋa. Baai ale a che ni ŋantaŋa ni tattaŋa po la kumsaŋa a paari Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La kama.

ref: While here on earth, you have thought only of filling your own stomachs and having a good time. But now you are like fat cattle on their way to be butchered.
text: Ni ta ŋanta meena kama a de masim ale naam. Niiga ale a dɛ a biigi ate ba yik ŋa ko diila, nama mɛ a dɛ kama a biigi a gomsi ni dek a magsi Wen buusaŋa.

ref: You have condemned and murdered innocent people, who couldn't even fight back. Be Patient and Kind
text: Nama a bo ka baai ale kan seba wari la buusa ale a ko ba mɛ, alege ba an baga a zɛri.

ref: My friends, be patient until the Lord returns. Think of farmers who wait patiently for the autumn and spring rains to make their valuable crops grow.
text: M suata, ni ta chichiiba a limisi ate ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita a ŋman pilim jam. Kpaarɔ a ta ka chichiiba a limisi borika ŋmorukku ale ŋmoruk kuui ale ŋman pai a saŋ la ate wa yaa nye wa ŋantaŋa a ta jo dɔk.

ref: Don't grumble about each other or you will be judged, and the judge is right outside the door.
text: M suata, ni kan ta funfɔbla ale chaaba ate Naawen a jam a bo ni buusa. Ku kan beni ale ge ate wa jam bo ni buusa.

ref: My friends, follow the example of the prophets who spoke for the Lord. They were patient, even when they had to suffer.
text: M suata, ni teeri Naawen biisiteerɔma baai ale jam boro dila po a biisi Naawen wieŋa la. Ni teeri ba le jam ta chichiiba ba ninammu po diila. Nama mɛ a be ta chichiiba ase bala la.

ref: In fact, we praise the ones who endured the most. You remember how patient Job was and how the Lord finally helped him. The Lord did this because he is so merciful and kind.
text: Ba ta suipeentik kama yɔgyɔgla, dii nyiŋla ba nya ba ninammu kama ale chichiiba. Ni teeri Job, wa mɛ jam nya wa ninammu ale ka chichiiba. Ni be nya Naawen ale jam basi ate wa nya masim ku kpeglimka po diila. Nya kude a be a sak kama ayen ti nya Naawen ale ta jiirim ale nuruba ninammu po diila.

ref: My friends, above all else, don't take an oath. You must not swear by heaven or by earth or by anything else. “Yes” or “No” is all you need to say. If you say anything more, you will be condemned.
text: M suata, dii ale gaam wie meena la ale nna, ku an nala ate ni a pɛ wenŋmazuk nyiŋŋa a yaase tɛŋzuk meena yaase jaab meena. Waai a dan nye wari ate nuru bek wa, ku magsi ka wa weeni ale wensie ayen, <<Mm,>> yaase wa weeni ale wensie ayen, <<Aaya.>> Waai kan pɛ ate Naawen a bo mini fu.

ref: If you are having trouble, you should pray. And if you are feeling good, you should sing praises.
text: Nuru a bo ni po a nya daanika? Kula nyɔnɔwa puusi a te Wen. Nuru a ŋman bo ni po mɛ ate wa sui a peenti? Nuru wala mɛ a yi yiila a pak Wen.

ref: If you are sick, ask the church leaders to come and pray for you. Ask them to put olive oil on you in the name of the Lord.
text: Nuru a bo ni po a yuagi? Kula nyɔnɔwa a wi Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la kpaŋŋa ate ba nye kpaam a kpiiri wa zuk ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita yuenni nyiŋ, abe ba puusi Wen a te wa.

ref: If you have faith when you pray for sick people, they will get well. The Lord will heal them, and if they have sinned, he will forgive them.
text: Ba dan puusi a te Wen ale siaka ayen Wen le nye ate yuarɔwa nya nyiŋyɔgsa, wa le sum basi ate wa nya nyiŋyɔgsa kama. Tuimba tii ate wa tom la, Naawen le vɔŋ a te wa.

ref: If you have sinned, you should tell each other what you have done. Then you can pray for one another and be healed. The prayer of an innocent person is powerful, and it can help a lot.
text: Nyaŋa de nyiŋ ni a weeni a sak chaab ni waba tii ate ni nye la abe ni a puusi Wen a te chaab, ate tuem a dan yik ni abe Wen tebi ni. Wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ a dan puusi te Wen, wa puusaŋa a pagra ka nna yegayega.

ref: Elijah was just as human as we are, and for three and a half years his prayers kept the rain from falling.
text: Dila po Wen biisiteerɔwa Elaja a jam ka nurubiik ase tama mɛ la. Wa jam puusi kama ale nin muna a te Wen ayen ŋmoruk kan ni. Dila nyiŋla, ku jam paari ka bena ŋata ale geli, ŋmoruk an jam ni ya.

ref: But when he did pray for rain, it fell from the skies and made the crops grow.
text: Bena ŋata ale geli, ale jam taam la, wa yaa ŋman puusi a te Wen ayen wa basi ate ŋmorukku ni. Ŋmorukku yaa jam ni nna yegayega ate jaabuuri meena a ŋman a chim.

ref: My friends, if any followers have wandered away from the truth, you should try to lead them back.
text: M suata, nama wanyi a dan a bɛ wensie suiku po ate ni wanyi a ŋman yik wa a ta nyini wa biem suiku po a ŋman jam,

ref: If you turn sinners from the wrong way, you will save them from death, and many of their sins will be forgiven.
text: kula nyɔnɔwa a vari ka tuimbaata nyɔnɔwa a ta nyini kum po a nyini. Wa be ŋman nye kama ate Wen le vɔŋ tuimbaata nyɔnɔwa tuimbaataŋa yegayega a te wa.

ref: From Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ. To God's people who are scattered like foreigners in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
text: Mi Piita, Yeezu Kirisita tuimtomdɔwa ale a ŋmarisi gbaŋka de a te nama baai ate Wen a lueri la ale ka nicham tɛŋzuk de, a waaŋ bo Pontus ale Galatia ale Kapadosia ale Asia ale Bitiniya la.

ref: Praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. God is so good, and by raising Jesus from death, he has given us new life and a hope that lives on.
text: Ni basi ate ti te Wen dii ale ka ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita Kowa la jiam. Dii nyiŋla, wa ta jiirim ka nna yegayega ale ti, dila nyiŋ a yaa nak Yeezu Kirisita yiti kum po a yaa te ti nyuvuri dii ale kan ka kpeglimka. Dila nyiŋ ate ti ta yiila, ayen ti le nya nyuvunni de.

ref: God has something stored up for you in heaven, where it will never decay or be ruined or disappear.
text: Ayen dai yeŋ ti le nya ŋan maŋ sii ate wa pai zaani wenŋmazuk la. Ba kan kaasi dula diipo diipo.

ref: You have faith in God, whose power will protect you until the last day. Then he will save you, just as he has always planned to do.
text: Wen pai wa pagrimu a nya ka nama baai ale ta siaka ale wa la zuk ayen wa vari ni nalimnyiini ni tuimbaata po a basi. Tɛŋka ale za ka kpeglim diipo la a dan paari, wa ale pai wa varibasika a sak ti.

ref: Your faith will be like gold that has been tested in a fire. And these trials will prove that your faith is worth much more than gold that can be destroyed. They will show that you will be given praise and honor and glory when Jesus Christ returns.
text: Nyenyaka de a sak kama ayen ni ta ka siak maŋ ale wa. Ba nyiem pai ligmɔniŋ kama a nyo bolim po a nye ate ŋa a nala, alege ŋa baga a kaasi. Nama siaka abe le gaam ligmɔniŋ la, ni ale tu ka nyenyaka ate ni baga ta chichiiba, ate Yeezu Kirisita dan ŋman pilim jam abe ni nya pimpauk ale nalim ale zula.

ref: you are to be saved. This is why you have faith.
text: Ni le ta siaka ale wa la nyiŋ, ate wa vari ni nalimnyiini ni tuimbaata po a basi.

ref: Some prophets told how God would treat you with undeserved grace, and they searched hard to find out more about the way you would be saved.
text: A magsi chaab ale varibasika de, biisiteerɔ baai ale mooli ŋmante kaai ale ka jam ni jigi la, a chiib gisi kama ale kpesika nna yegayega,

ref: The Spirit of Christ was in them and was telling them how Christ would suffer and would then be given great honor. So they searched to find out exactly who Christ would be and when this would happen.
text: a yaali ayen ba seba diipo ate wie ŋaai ate Kirisita Chiika ale bo ba po la jam a dak, wa le mooli Kirisita ninammu ale zula ŋaai ale ŋa pai saŋ la.

ref: But they were told that they were serving you and not themselves. They preached to you by the power of the Holy Spirit, who was sent from heaven. And their message was only for you, even though angels would like to know more about it. Chosen To Live a Holy Life
text: Wen Chiika mɛ a jam sak wa biisiteerɔma a weeni ba ayen ba an jam a tom a te ka ba dega, alege ba jam a tom a te ka nama. Wen jam tom wa Chiika ate wa nyini wenŋmazukku po a jam ayen wa pai ka wa pagrimu a te baai ale jam a sak ni Wen wamaŋsaŋa la. Wa biisiteerɔma a jam seba wa wamaŋsaŋa wie kama ale jam a yaali ayen nama mɛ seba ŋa. Wen maarɔma dek mɛ a jam a yaali ayen ba seba wamaŋsaŋa de kiri kama.

ref: Behave like obedient children. Don't let your lives be controlled by your desires, as they used to be.
text: Ni le liŋ jam kan seba Wen la, ni jam va ka nidek yaalika. Ni be kan ŋman a nye dila, ni a zuli wa nalimnyiini.

ref: Always live as God's holy people should, because God is the one who chose you, and he is holy.
text: Wa ka Weleŋsa Nyɔnɔ. Dila ale soa ate wa lueri ni ayen ni ta suinum weleŋsa ale ni tuim ŋaai meena ate ni a tom a te wa la po.

ref: That's why the Scriptures say, “I am the holy God, and you must be holy too.”
text: Ba ŋmarisi ayen, <<Ni abe welema, dii la Mi welema kama.>> (Kaabka

ref: You say that God is your Father, but God doesn't have favorites! He judges all people by what they do. So you must honor God while you live as strangers here on earth.
text: Ni nyiem daa puusi Wen, ni a wi wa ayen ka ni Ko. Wala ale a bo waai meena buusa alege kan luk la. Wa a bo waai meena buusa a ta va ka wa dii meena ate wa nye la. Dila nyiŋla, ni pai ni nyeboka meena tɛŋzuk de a te wa zula nalimnyiini.

ref: You were rescued from the useless way of life you learned from your ancestors. But you know you were not rescued by such things as silver or gold that don't last forever.
text: Ni baga a teeri diipo ate ni jam a va ni kokpieŋsaŋa suik kayiokku la kama. Mi be ŋman seba Wen ale nye dii a da tuesi ni suik kula po a basi la kama. Jaab waai ate wa be pai da tuesi ni a basi la an baga a kaasi ase kuta yaase ligmɔniŋ la.

ref: Christ was chosen even before the world was created, but because of you, he did not come until these last days.
text: Wen a liŋ jam lueri Kirisita kama ale ge nye tɛŋzuk ale wenŋmazuk ale jaabuuri meena, ale ge ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ a yaa basi ate waai meena tɛŋzuk de a nya wa. Wa be nye dila ka nama nyiŋ.

ref: And when he did come, it was to lead you to have faith in God, who raised him from death and honored him in a glorious way. This is why you have put your faith and hope in God.
text: Wen a jam nak Kirisita yiti kum po kama a yaa pai wa zulaŋa ale nalimu yegayega a te wa. Kirisita nyiŋ mɛ ate ni ta siaka ale yiila Wen jigi. Ni be va ka wala nyiŋ a ta siaka ale Wen.

ref: You obeyed the truth, and your souls were made pure. Now you sincerely love each other. But you must keep on loving with all your heart.
text: Yɔgyɔgla de ate ni wom Wen wensie wamaŋsaŋa la, ni sugri ni tuimbaataŋa kama ni suiniima po a basi alege va wa. Dila nyiŋ ate ni yaa ta yaalika nalimnyiini ale ni Kirisita bi chaama. Dila nyiŋla, ni be ŋmasi a yaali chaab dila ale ni suiniima meena.

ref: The Scriptures say, “Humans wither like grass, and their glory fades like wild flowers. Grass dries up, and flowers fall to the ground.
text: Dii nyiŋla, <<Nurubiik meena a nye se ka wuuta la. Ba be nala ase ka wuutaŋa puutaŋa la. Wuutaŋa a jak kpi kama. Puutaŋa mɛ a siiri a lo ka tɛŋ alege ate wuutaŋa mɛ dek a yaa a ko,

ref: But what the Lord has said will stand forever.” Our good news to you is what the Lord has said.
text: Alege Wen Wanni a kasim boro ka dila taam wuu.>> (Azaya

ref: Stop being hateful! Quit trying to fool people, and start being sincere. Don't be jealous or say cruel things about others.
text: Dila nyiŋ, ni pai wieŋa de meena basi, kisika meena ale pimpaasima meena ale sakpaŋ zula ale nyuiri ale nuruba wie biisi kaasika meena.

ref: Be like newborn babies who are thirsty for the pure spiritual milk that will help you grow and be saved.
text: Ni a nye ase buluata la, a kasim a yaali ni maba biisim. Wen wanni abe a nye ase ka biisim la, ate ni dan tuesi di ase buluata la, a nyu ni le chim a pak a nya varibasika

ref: You have already found out how good the Lord really is.
text: yɔgyɔgla de nama dek abe nya ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita jiirimu ale soa diila kama.

ref: And now you are living stones being used to build a spiritual house. You are also a group of holy priests, and with the help of Jesus Christ you will offer sacrifices that please God.
text: Nama abe a nye se ka tintain ŋaai ate Wen a lueri ayen wa sɛ wa yenni la. Yenni de po, ni a nye se ka baai ale jam ka Wen yenni kaabteerɔma la, a pai ni suiniimaŋa ale ni popolaŋa Yeezu Kirisita yuenni nyiŋ a nye kaabka a te Wen.

ref: You are followers of the Lord, and this stone is precious to you. But it isn't precious to those who refuse to follow him. They are the builders who tossed aside the stone that turned out to be the most important one of all.
text: Wa ka tintain maŋ nna yegayega a te baai ale ta siaka ale wa la. Alege baai ale kan ta siaka ale wa la, <<Tintain dii ate seerɔma a zɛri la a yaa chim ka tintain dek,>> (Yiila

ref: “Once you were nobody. Now you are God's people. At one time no one had mercy on you. Now God has treated you with kindness.” Live as God's Servants Should
text: Dila powa ni jam daa wa nuruba, alege yɔgyɔgla ni ka wa nuruba. Dila powa ni jam zɛ Wen jiirimu ale ka diila, alege yɔgyɔgla de ni yaa nya jiirimu de ale ka diila kama.

ref: Dear friends, you are foreigners and strangers on this earth. So I beg you not to surrender to those desires that fight against you.
text: M dek doaba, ni a nye ase ka nicham tɛŋka de zuk la, dila nyiŋ ate mi a saalim ni ayen, ni pai nidek ŋan yaalika a basi. Ti dek ŋan yaalika ale Wen ale a yaali ayen ti a va wa diila an moata chaaba.

ref: Always let others see you behaving properly, even though they may still accuse you of doing wrong. Then on the day of judgment, they will honor God by telling the good things they saw you do.
text: Ku a fɛ ate ni ta yuei maŋ ale baai ale kan seba Wen la jigi, ate ku sak ba ate ba kan baga a biisi a gaam ni ayen ni a tom ka tuimbaata. Ni basi ate ba a nya ni tuimaŋsaŋa nyiini ate Wen dan jam ayen wa bo tɛŋzuk nuruma buusa, wa nya pimpauk nama nyiŋ.

ref: The Lord wants you to obey all human authorities, especially the Emperor, who rules over everyone.
