ref: He lets us rule as kings and serve God his Father as priests. To him be glory and power forever and ever! Amen.
text: alege a bobi ti nalima ale lueri ti ayen ti chim kaabteerɔba ate ti a tom tuima a te wa Kowa Wen. Yeezu a ta zula ale nalim ale pagrim yegayega taam wuu. Ku be nye dila.

ref: Look! He is coming with the clouds. Everyone will see him, even the ones who stuck a sword through him. All people on earth will weep because of him. Yes, it will happen! Amen.
text: Ni ŋmasi a nya. Wa le nyini ka chiŋmaaŋa suŋsuŋ a nyini ate baai ale jam chubi wa gauŋku la, ale nuru meena a nya wa. Wa dan ŋman pilim jam, nuru meena tɔgatɔga ale bo tɛŋzuk la, le kum kama a te wa. Ku be nye dila.

ref: The Lord God says, “I am Alpha and Omega, the one who is and was and is coming. I am God All-Powerful!” A Vision of the Risen Lord
text: Naawen dii ale ka Wen la weeni ayen, <<Mi ale Piilimka. Mi be le Kpeglimka. Mi jam boro kama. Mi abe boro kama. Mi abe le boro diipo meena. Mi ka waai ale Ta Ŋanta Meena Pagrim.>>

ref: I am John, a follower together with all of you. We suffer because Jesus is our king, but he gives us the strength to endure. I was sent to Patmos Island, because I had preached God's message and had told about Jesus.
text: Mi, Jɔɔn, ka ni suok. Mi ale nama a namu kama Yeezu nyiŋ, alege wa a maari ti ate ti a siak a te ti ninammu ayen dai yeŋ ti le jo wa naamu po. ref: On the Lord's day the Spirit took control of me, and behind me I heard a loud voice that sounded like a trumpet.
text: Naawen danni ate Wen Chiika a jam nye ate mi nya ŋanta nna ase m jam goa a daasim kama la. M jam wom ka lueluk kpioŋ ase damuniŋ la,

text: a weeni mu ayen, <<Ŋmarisi jabuui ate fi nya la a nyo fi gbaŋka po a pai te Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab a bo satɛŋsa siyopɔiwa Asia po ate ba a wi ayen Efisos ale Sumana ale Peganum ale Tiatira ale Sardis ale Filadelfia ale Laodisia la.>>

ref: When I turned to see who was speaking to me, I saw seven gold lampstands.
text: Mi yaa virim ayen m nya si ka wana ale a biisi, ate mi yaa nya ale zeuŋta tiyopɔi a za, ba pai ka ligmɔniŋ a nye ti.

ref: There with the lampstands was someone who seemed to be the Son of Man. He was wearing a robe that reached down to his feet, and a gold cloth was wrapped around his chest.
text: Mi ŋman nya ale jaab a neensi saalɔbiik a za zeuŋtaŋa suŋsuŋ. Wa jam jo ka garuk woŋ ale pai garuk kuui ale a nyaksi nna ase ligmɔniŋ la a bobi gilim wa kuusidi.

ref: His head and his hair were white as wool or snow, and his eyes looked like flames of fire.
text: Wa zukku zuisaŋa a jam peenti ka nna tektek, alege ate wa ninaŋa a muni ase bolim ale a dɛ la.

ref: His feet were glowing like bronze being heated in a furnace, and his voice sounded like the roar of a waterfall.
text: Wa naŋtaataŋa a jam muni ase ka kuta ate ba pai se bolim po la, ale ge a nyaksi nna yegayega. Wa lueluku a jam a kum ase ka nyaata ale a wuuri diila.

ref: He held seven stars in his right hand, and a sharp double-edged sword was coming from his mouth. His face was shining as bright as the sun at noon.
text: Wa ta ka chiŋmarisa siyopɔi wa juga po ale gebik kaai noaŋa meena ale a dɛ la ate ka nyini wa nɔi po a nyini. Wa ninaŋa a nyaksi ase wenbiri ale jueli wenzuk suŋsuŋ a nyaksi diila.

ref: When I saw him, I fell at his feet like a dead person. But he put his right hand on me and said: Don't be afraid! I am the first, the last,
text: Mi le nya wa la, mi ya lo tɛŋ ase m kpi la. Wa yaa tiri mi ale wa juga nisaŋa alege weeni mi ayen, <<Kan chali yɔgsum. Mi ale piilimka. Mi be le kpeglimka.

ref: and the living one. I died, but now I am alive forever, and I have the keys to death and the world of the dead.
text: Mi ka waai ale vua la. M jam kpi kama, alege yɔgyɔgla m boro kama diipo meena. Mi le ta kum ale kpiluŋ safiisaŋa.

ref: Write what you have seen and what is and what will happen after these things.
text: Ŋmarisi wie ŋaai ate fi nya la a dueni. Ŋa gela ka jinla wie. Ŋa gela ale jam nye chum diipo.

text: Ni siak a te ni ninammu ale chichiiba ka mi nyiŋ, alege kan yaali ayen ni basi mi vaka.

text: << <Alege ni diem tali ka wari dinyi. Ni kan yaali mu ase ni ale liŋ a yaali mu diila.

ref: But there is one thing you are doing right. You hate what the Nicolaitans are doing, and so do I.
text: Ni kisi tuimbaata tii ate Nikolai demma a nye la kama, ase mi ale kisi ba diila.

ref: If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches. I will let everyone who wins the victory eat from the life-giving tree in God's wonderful garden. The Letter to Smyrna
text: << <Ni lak ni tueŋa a wom dii ate Wen Chiika a weeni a sak Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab a bo Asia la. Baai meena ale kaa basi mi va ka la, m le te ba suik ate ba dɛ Wen tiib buui ale a te nyuvuri la yɔnni.>

ref: This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Smyrna: I am the first and the last. I died, but now I am alive! Listen to what I say.

text: Ni lak ni tueŋa a wom dii ate Wen Chiika a weeni Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab a bo Asia la. Nuru baai ale ŋmasi yik ba siaka ate ku a paari ku kpeglimka po la, Wen a kan pai ba a gum chaab ale nuru baai ate wa le te ba waalika la po.>

ref: Wake up! You have only a little strength left, and it is almost gone. So try to become stronger. I have found that you are not completely obeying God.
text: Ni yiti zaani ale ninmuna a va mu nalimnyiini, mi nya ayen tuim ŋaai ate ni tom la an diem magsi Wen nina po.

ref: Remember the teaching you were given and heard. Hold firmly to it and turn from your sins. If you don't wake up, I will come when you least expect it, just as a thief does.
text: Ni teeri ba ale sak ni dii ale ni ale wom diila ate ni basi ni wabaataŋa abe ni a zuli wa. Ni dan kan yiti a zaani ya m le jam diiri ni ase zue la, ni kan seba diipo ate m le jam la.

ref: A few of you in Sardis have not dirtied your clothes with sin. You will walk with me in white clothes, because you are worthy.
text: Ni ba gela ale bo Sardis la an diem tom tuimbaata tii le ti nye ate ni suiniima a daŋ la. M le te ni garuk peelita ate ni jo a be m basi ate nama ale mi a cheŋ ale chaab diila ni magsi ka dila.

ref: Everyone who wins the victory will wear white clothes. Their names will not be erased from the book of life, and I will tell my Father and his angels that they are my followers.
text: M le basi ate nuru baai ale ŋmasi yik nalimnyiini ate ku ga a paari ku kpeglimka la a jo garuk peelita m be kan yeeri ba yueŋa nyuvuri dii ale kan ka kpeglimka la gbaŋka po. M le weeni a lagri m Kowa niŋ ayen m soa ba kama.

text: Ni lak ni tueŋa a wom dii ate Wen Chiika a weeni Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab a bo Asia la.>

ref: This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Philadelphia: I am the one who is holy and true, and I have the keys that belonged to David. When I open a door, no one can close it. And when I close a door, no one can open it. Listen to what I say.
text: <<Ŋmarisi wieŋa de a te Wen maarɔwa waai ale a nya Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab Filadelfia la zuk. Wieŋa de a nyini ka waai ale ka nuru weleŋ ale wensie nyɔnɔ ale ge ta Deevid safiika la. M dan pai ka a lak tuok nuru karo a baga a lik ku. M be dan pai ka a kpari, nuru karo a baga a lagri ku.

ref: I know everything you have done. And I have placed before you an open door no one can close. You were not very strong, but you obeyed my message and did not deny you are my followers.
text: <M seba ni ale a tom diila kama. M be seba ni ale ta pagrim magadek la kama. Ni va m sinsaŋŋa kama ale ta siaka ale mu. Mi be lak tuoku kama ni niŋ geŋ. Nuru kan lik ku.

ref: Now you will see what I will do with those people who belong to Satan's group. They claim to be God's people, but they are liars. I will make them come and kneel down at your feet. Then they will know that I love you.
text: Ni a wom. Baai ale a velim ayen ba ka Juuba la, Sitaana ale soa ba. M le basi ate ba jam a kpi duna ni niŋ a zuli ni, ate ba seba ayen mi a yaali ni kama.

ref: You obeyed my message and endured. So I will protect you from the time of testing everyone in all the world must go through.
text: Ni ale va mi sinsaŋŋa ale chichiiba la nyiŋ, mi mɛ ale lik nama mɛ a tara ate ninam buui ale cheena tɛŋzuk ayen bu choa nuruma a nya la a kan paari ni.

ref: I am coming soon. So hold firmly to what you have, and no one will take away the crown you will be given as your reward.
text: M cheena kama, ku kan beni. Ni be chiib ta ni nak dega tiirimu ate waai a kan vari ni jigiya.

ref: Everyone who wins the victory will be made into a pillar in the temple of my God, and they will stay there forever. I will write on each of them the name of my God and the name of his city. It is the new Jerusalem my God will send down from heaven. I will also write on them my own new name.
text: Baai ale baga a yik ku a ta paari ku kpeglimka la, m le basi ate ba a nye ase ka zaŋŋa la Wen yenni po taam wuu. M le ŋmarisi Wen yuenni ale wa tɛŋka yuenni a dueni ba nyiŋ. ref: This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Laodicea: I am the one called Amen! I am the faithful and true witness and the source of God's creation. Listen to what I say.
text: <<Ŋmarisi wieŋa de a te Wen maarɔwa waai ale a nya Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab Laodisia la zuk. Wieŋa de a nyini ka waai ale basi ate wie a nye ale ta wensie la ale chim wensie seerɔ la ale a nya Wen ŋan nyientaŋa zuk la ayen,

ref: But since you are lukewarm and neither cold nor hot, I will spit you out of my mouth.
text: Alege ni abe le bo suŋsuŋsaŋa po nna, ni an tuila, ni abe an yɔgsa la, m le chiiri ni kama m nɔnni po a basi.

ref: You claim to be rich and successful and to have everything you need. But you don't know how bad off you really are. You are pitiful, poor, blind, and naked.
text: Ni a weeni nidek kama ayen, <<Tama ka jigsirɔba, ti kan yaali jaab jaaboa.>> Alege ni zɛ ayen ni ka niniga nyama. Ni ka ŋanjaksa a cheŋ chaboala ale chim yeoba.

ref: Buy your gold from me. It has been refined in a fire, and it will make you rich. Buy white clothes from me. Wear them and you can cover up your shameful nakedness. Buy medicine for your eyes, so you will be able to see.
text: Ni da ligmɔniŋ mi jigi, ŋaai ale chim ligmɔniŋ dek la ate ni chim jigsirɔba. Ni da garuk peelita mɛ mi jigi a lik ni chivieŋa. Ni be da nina kpaam mɛ m jigi a nyo ni ninaŋa po ate ni a nya.

ref: Listen! I am standing and knocking at your door. If you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in and we will eat together.
text: Ni be wom, mi kasim za ka dɔkku nɔi a nak ale ge a wi. Baai ale a wom m lueluku ale ge a lak tuoku la, m le jo, ate ba ale mi a maari chaab a dɛ ŋandiinta.

ref: Everyone who wins the victory will sit with me on my throne, just as I won the victory and sat with my Father on his throne.
text: Baai ale ŋmasi yik di nalimnyiini ate di a paari kpeglimka la, m le te ba suik ate ba kali m tɛŋ m naamu jigini. Mi daam ŋmasi yik kama a ta di a paari di kpeglimka. Dila ale soa ate m Kowa basi ate mi kali dula.

ref: After this, I looked and saw a door that opened into heaven. Then the voice that had spoken to me at first and that sounded like a trumpet said, “Come up here! I will show you what must happen next.”
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate mi ŋman pilim wom ale nya jaab ase m goadaasim kama la. Wenŋmazuk mi yaa nya tuok ale ku lak, ate lueluk kuui ate m liŋ wom nna ase damuniŋ la weeni mu ayen, <<Jueli jam dela ate m weeni fu dii ale ku jam nye la.>>

ref: Right then the Spirit took control of me, and there in heaven I saw a throne and someone sitting on it.
text: Wen Chiika a deri de mi niŋ ate mi jueli ga a jo. Mi yaa nya Wenŋmazuk naam zukpaglik ale ka za ate nuru a kali ka zuk.

ref: The one who was sitting there sparkled like precious stones of jasper and carnelian. A rainbow that looked like an emerald surrounded the throne.
text: Wa ninaŋa a jam a nyaksi ase ka tintain mɔnta la, ale tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase kpabunyiam la ate nagoritom a nye ase gunungoona la a gilim wa.

ref: Twenty-four other thrones were in a circle around that throne. And on each of these thrones there was an elder dressed in white clothes and wearing a gold crown.
text: Kalisa jiga pisiye ale sinaansi ale jam gilim wa. Nisɔm pisiye ale banaansi ale jam kali si zuk. Ba meena a jam jo ka garuk peelita ale vuk ligmɔniŋ zutɔgsa.

ref: Flashes of lightning and roars of thunder came out from the throne in the center of the circle. Seven torches, which are the seven spirits of God, were burning in front of the throne.
text: Wenzukku a jam a nyaksi kama ale a na wenŋmazuk naamu zukpaglika jigini. Zeuŋta tiyopɔi ale jam toati a za wa niŋ. Ti jam ka Wen chiisa siyopɔiwa.

ref: Also in front of the throne was something that looked like a glass sea, clear as crystal. Around the throne in the center were four living creatures covered front and back with eyes.
text: Nyakpiemu ale jam a nyaksi ase nyaasuŋ la ale jam maa za wenŋmazuk zukpaglika niŋ. Ŋanvuta tinaansi ale jam maa za gilim gum du. Si ninaŋa a jam piisi kama a kali niŋ ale ŋaaŋ.

ref: The first creature was like a lion, the second one was like a bull, the third one had the face of a human, and the fourth was like a flying eagle.
text: Duŋsaŋa kanyi a jam a nye ase ka gbeŋli la, kanyi a jam a nye ase ka lalik la, kanyi zuk a jam a nye ase nuru zuk la, kanyi mɛ zuk a jam a nye nna ase jiiruk ale lak ku kiŋkaŋŋa a basi la.

ref: Each of the four living creatures had six wings, and their bodies were covered with eyes. Day and night they never stopped singing, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord, the all-powerful God, who was and is and is coming!”
text: Si meena a jam ta ka kiŋkaŋŋa ŋayuebi alege ate si ninaŋa a sueri si nyiŋsaŋa meena. Si meena a kasim jam a yi ka yiila yok ale kantueŋ alege kan vuusi. Si jam yi a weeni ayen, <<Weleŋsa, Weleŋsa, Weleŋsa ale Naawen dii ale ka Wen a ta pagrim la, waai ale jam boro, ale boro, ale boro diipo meena la.>>

ref: The living creatures kept praising, honoring, and thanking the one who sits on the throne and who lives forever and ever.
text: Duŋsaŋa sinaansiwa a jam yi si yiilaŋa a pak ka waai ale jam kali wenŋmazuk naamu zukpaglika zuk la, dii nyiŋla wa jam ta ka zula ale nalim alege boro diipo meena.

ref: “Our Lord and God, you are worthy to receive glory, honor, and power. You created all things, and by your decision they are and were created.”
text: <<Ti Naawen ale ti Wen yaa, fi ale nye ŋanta meena. Ka fidek yaalika ate fi basi ate ba boro. Dila ale soa ate ku magsi ayen ti a puusi fu, dii nyiŋla fi ta ka zula ale nalim ale pagrim.>>

ref: In the right hand of the one sitting on the throne I saw a scroll that had writing on the inside and on the outside. And it was sealed in seven places.
text: Mi ale nya waai ale wa kali wenŋmazuk naamu zukpaglika zuk la, wa jam ta ka gbaŋ wa juga po, ba jam ŋmarisi ka wie a dueni ka niŋ ale ka ŋaaŋ alege pai ŋanta a bobi buyopɔi a lik gbaŋka.

ref: I saw a mighty angel ask with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?”
text: Ate mi yaa nya maarɔ wanyi ate wa yaa mooli ale lueluk kpioŋ ayen, <<Ka wana ale baga a foli bobika buyopɔiwa alege a lak gbaŋka nna.>>

ref: No one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or look inside it.
text: Alege nuru jam ka wenŋmazuk yaase tɛŋzuk yaase kpiluŋ a baga a lak gbaŋka a nya ka po.

ref: I cried hard because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or look inside it.
text: Mi ale nya ale nuru karo a baga a lak gbaŋka a nya ka po la, mi yaa deri a kum.

ref: Then one of the elders said to me, “Stop crying and look! The one who is called both the ‘Lion from the Tribe of Judah’ and ‘King David's Great Descendant’ has won the victory. He will open the scroll and its seven seals.”
text: Nisɔmma wanyi a yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Kan fi a kum. Gbeŋli dii ale nyini Juda demma po la, wa ka Naawa Deevid ŋaaŋbiik. Wala ale nakdeerɔ. Wa le foli bobika buyopɔiwa a lak gbaŋka.>>

ref: Then I looked and saw a Lamb standing in the center of the throne surrounded by the four living creatures and the elders. The Lamb looked as if it had once been killed. It had seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God, sent out to all the earth.
text: Mi yaa nya ale ka Pabiik ale za du. Ka jam za moata ka wenŋmazuk naamu zukpaglika ate ŋanvuta tinaansiwa ale nisɔm pisiye ale banaansiwa a za gilim ka la. Ka jam a nye ase ba ko ka kama la. Pabiika a jam ta ka nyiila ŋayopɔi ale nina ŋayopɔi. Ka nina ŋayopɔiwa ale ka nyiila ŋayopɔiwa ka Wen chiisa siyopɔiwa sii ate Wen a tom a basi tɛŋka meena po la.

ref: The Lamb went over and took the scroll from the right hand of the one who sat on the throne.
text: Pabiika yaa cheŋ ga tuesi gbaŋka waai ale kali wenŋmazuk naamu zukpaglika zuk la juga nisaŋa po.

ref: Then they sang a new song, “You are worthy to receive the scroll and open its seals, because you were killed. And with your own blood you bought for God people from every tribe, language, nation, and race.
text: Ba yaa jam yi yipaali ayen, <<Fi ka nuru waai ale magsi gbaŋka pai ka abe fi foli bobika buyopɔiwa. Ba le ko fu la, fi jam pai ka fi ziimu a da tuesi nuru boari a basi Wen jigi. Fi ale lueri ba a ta nyini satɛŋsa meena ale nuruba meena po a nyini ate ba meena a biisi biisa tɔgatɔga.

ref: You let them become kings and serve God as priests, and they will rule on earth.”
text: Fi ale bobi ba nalima a lueri ba ayen ba chim kaabteerɔma abe ba a tom tuima a te ti Wenni. Ba ale soa tɛŋka meena nuruma.>>

ref: As I looked, I heard the voices of a large number of angels around the throne and the voices of the living creatures and of the elders. There were millions and millions of them,
text: Mi yaa ŋman pilim nya ale Wen maarɔma a bo dula. Ba jam piisi kama a paari tusa ale tusa, tusa piisa ale tusa piisa. Ba yaa gilim ŋanvuta tinaansiwa ale nisɔmma.

ref: and they were saying in a loud voice, “The Lamb who was killed is worthy to receive power, riches, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, and praise.”
text: Ate ba yaa a yi yiili ate ku jueli ayen, <<Pabiik kaai ate ba ko la ku magsi ka ti a zuli fu dii nyiŋla fi soa ka ŋanta meena ale ta yam ale pagrim ale zula ale nalim ale pimpauk.>>

ref: Then I heard all beings in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and in the sea offer praise. Together, all of them were saying, “Praise, honor, glory, and strength forever and ever to the one who sits on the throne and to the Lamb!”

ref: The four living creatures said “Amen,” while the elders knelt down and worshiped.

text: Kirisita ka Wen nidoabinni waai ale kpi la. Ka wala ate ti suataŋa a jam sak nuruba wa wie alege a jam gomsi badek mɛ ayen ba kpi wa nyiŋla. Wieŋa de meena ale jam soa ate ba nak yiak Sitaana.

ref: “The heavens should rejoice, together with everyone who lives there. But pity the earth and the sea, because the devil was thrown down to the earth. He knows his time is short, and he is very angry.”
text: Nama baai meena ale bo wenŋmazuk la basi ate ni sue a peenti. Alege ku le toa kama tɛŋzuk demma meena jigi, diila jabioku a siŋ jam ka nama jigi. Wa abe ta ka suipuurum dii nyiŋla wa daaŋa an soa dii ya.>>

ref: When the dragon realized it had been thrown down to the earth, it tried to make trouble for the woman who had given birth to a son.
text: Jakpioŋku ale nya ale ba yiak wa a basi tɛŋzuk la, wa yaa daani nipok waai ale jam biak nidoabinni la nna yegayega.

ref: But the woman was given two wings like those of a huge eagle, so she could fly into the desert. There she would escape from the snake and be taken care of for a time, two times, and half a time.
text: Ba yaa pai jiiruk kiŋkaŋŋi kpiema ŋaye a te nipowa ayen wa yiti cheŋ sagni po, ale ba le nya wa zuk a ga paari bena ŋata ale chiisa siyuebi ate jakpioŋku a kan nye wa wariya.

ref: The snake then spewed out water like a river to sweep the woman away.
text: Jakpioŋku yaa basi ate nyiam nna yegayega a nyini ka nɔnni po a nyini ase beli la, ayen nyiamu ji nipowa a ta cheŋ bɛ.

ref: But the earth helped her and swallowed the water that had come from the dragon's mouth.
text: Alege tɛŋka a jam nyu nyiamu meena ate bu an paari nipowa.

ref: This made the dragon terribly angry with the woman. So it started a war against the rest of her children. They are the people who obey God and are faithful to what Jesus did and taught.
text: Alege jakpioŋku ale jam nya dii ale nye la, ate ka sui yaa ŋman kaasi nna yegayega ale nipowa. Ka yaa ŋman pilim cheŋ ayen ka tu chaab a nye kpaliŋ ale baai meena ale a siak a te Wen sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni nuruba ayen Yeezu ale soa ba la. Bala chaama ka nipowa bisa.

ref: I looked and saw a beast coming up from the sea. This one had ten horns and seven heads, and a crown was on each of its ten horns. On each of its heads were names that were an insult to God.
text: Dila powa, jakpioŋku a jam za ka nyakpiemu nɔi. Ate mi yaa ŋman nya duŋ kperikaliik ka choa ale ka nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini. Kala a jam ta ka zuima ŋayopɔi ale nyiila pi. Ka jam vuk ka naam zutɔgsa ka nyiilaŋa meena zuk. Ka zuimaŋa meena nyiŋ yue ale jam doa ŋa nyiŋ a lɛ Wen.

ref: The beast I saw had the body of a leopard, the feet of a bear, and the mouth of a lion. The dragon handed over its own power and throne and great authority to this beast.
text: Duŋ ka de jam a neensi ka yɔŋni. Ka naŋsaŋa mɛ jam a neensi ka piuk naŋsa. Ka nɔnni mɛ a neensi gbeŋli nɔi. Jakpioŋ kuui ale a neensi waab la jam pai ka pagrimu ale ka naamu a te ka duŋ kperikaliika.

ref: and they worshiped the dragon who had given its authority to the beast. They also worshiped the beast and said, “No one is like this beast! No one can fight against it.”
text: Waai meena yaa jam a te jakpioŋ kuui ale a neensi waamu la zula nna yegayega dii nyiŋla, wa jam pai ka pagrimu a te duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale nyini nyiamu po a nyini la. Ba yaa a weeni chaab ayen, <<Ka wana ale a nye ase duŋ kperikaliika de a ta pagrim ayen wa nye kpaliŋ ale ka?>>

ref: The beast cursed God, and it cursed the name of God. It even cursed the place where God lives, as well as everyone who lives in heaven with God.
text: Ka yaa jam biisi a kaasi Wen ale wa yuenni ale wa viuku, ku kiri ale baai meena ale jam bo wenŋmazukku po la.

ref: It was allowed to fight against God's people and defeat them. It was also given authority over the people of every tribe, nation, language, and race.
text: Ba yaa ŋman te ka suik ayen ka tu chaab ale Wen nuruma a nye kpaliŋ a nak yiak ba. Ba te ka mɛ pagrim ayen ka soa buura meena ale nuruba meena ale biisa meena ale tɛŋsa meena.

ref: If you are doomed to be captured, you will be captured. If you are doomed to be killed by a sword, you will be killed by a sword. This means God's people must learn to endure and be faithful!
text: Ku ka Wen dek yaalika ayen ba le jam yik ni ba gela a lik dɔk po a pai gebik woŋta a ko ni gela. Nama baai ale ka Wen nuruba la, ku a fɛ ayen ni nam ale chichiiba a ŋmasi yik di ate ku ga paari ku kpeglimka. Wieŋa de ale sum nye kama.

ref: I now saw another beast. This one came out of the ground. It had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon.
text: Ate mi yaa ŋman nya duŋ kperikaliik ka choa ale nyini tɛŋka a jueli. Ka jam ta ka nyiila ŋaye ase padiak nyiila la, alege a biisi ase jakpioŋku ale a neensi waamu la.

ref: It worked for the beast whose fatal wound had been healed. And it used all its authority to force the earth and its people to worship that beast.
text: Ka jam pai ka duŋ kperikaliika pagrim a tom ka dek nimbie po. Ka jam fɛ tɛŋka nuruma kama ayen ba a puusi duŋ kperikaliika ale kɔni la.

ref: It worked mighty miracles, and while people watched, it even made fire come down from the sky.
text: Duŋ kaai ale ta nyiila ŋayewa la dɛ a tom ka wakperikaliisa nna yegayega. Ka jam nye kama ate bolim a nyiini wenŋmazuk a siŋ tɛŋzuk nuru meena niŋ.

ref: This second beast fooled people on earth by working miracles for the first one. Then it talked them into making an idol in the form of the beast that did not die after being wounded by a sword.
text: Ate ka paasi tɛŋzuk nuruma meena ale wakperikaliik sii ate ka tom duŋ kperikaliika niŋ la. Ka weeni ayen ba mɛ duŋ kperikaliik kaai ate ba kɔni ka ale gebi woŋku alege ate ka diem vua la ate ba a zuli ka.

ref: It was allowed to put breath into the idol, so it could speak. Everyone who refused to worship the idol of the beast was put to death.
text: Ba yaa te ka suik ayen ka vuusi a basi duŋ kperikaliika ate ba mɛ la nyiŋ ate ka ta nyuvuri ate wa baga a biisi abe wa a ko baai meena ale kan puusi a te wa la.

ref: All people were forced to put a mark on their right hand or forehead. Whether they were powerful or weak, rich or poor, free people or slaves,
text: Duŋ ka de a yaa fɛ nuruma meena, baai ale chim nuru kpienta ale baai ale kan daa nuru kpienta, baai ale ka jigsirɔba ale baai ale kan daa jigsirɔba, baai ale ka yɔm ale baai ale kan daa yɔmma ate ba ŋmarisi ba juga nisima nyiŋ yaase ba dee nyiŋ.

ref: they all had to have this mark, or else they could not buy or sell anything. This mark stood for the name of the beast and for the number of its name.
text: Nuru waai an baga jaab a da ka wa nin ta ŋmarisika de. Ŋmarisika de ale wa yuenni yaase dii ale a sak wa yuenni la.

ref: You need wisdom to understand the number of the beast! But if you are smart enough, you can figure this out. Its number is
text: Kude abe a sak ka yam. Nuru waai a dan ta yam wa ale seba dii ale a sak wa yuenni la kiri. Dii abe ale a sak wa yuenni la ka kobsiyuebi ale pisiyuebi ale buyuebi.

ref: who had been rescued from the earth.
text: ) nyiini ale nya da tuesika a nyini tɛŋzuk la.

ref: I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion! With him were
text: Ate mi yaa nya ale Pabiik ale nuruba tusa kook ale pisinaansi ale banaansi (

ref: And a new song was being sung in front of God's throne and in front of the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn that song, except the
text: Ate ba yaa jam yi yi paali wenŋmazuk naamu zukpaglika niŋ ale ŋanvuta tinaansiwa ale nisɔm pisiye ale banaansiwa niŋ, ate waai an jam baga a zamsi yiini ka nuruba tusa kook ale pisinaansi ale banaansiwa (

ref: All of these are pure virgins, and they follow the Lamb wherever he leads. They have been rescued to be presented to God and the Lamb as the most precious people on earth.
text: Ba de ale baai ale kan jam taŋ badek ale nipooba, diila ba jam yik badek ka cheri. Ba jam va Pabiika kama juijui meena ate ka a cheŋ la. Ba jam da ba kama nuruba po a pai ba a te Wen ale Pabiika ase yɔna ŋaai ale dɛ niŋ la.

ref: They never tell lies, and they are innocent. The Messages of the Three Angels
text: Nuru an jam baga a weeni ayen ba velim venta. Ba jam ka kaasuŋ ale kunyi mɛ la.

ref: I saw another angel. This one was flying across the sky and had the eternal good news to announce to the people of every race, tribe, language, and nation on earth.
text: Ate mi yaa ŋman nya maarɔ ale wa bo wenŋmazuk niŋniŋa a yaa yiri a cheŋ. Wa ta ka Wen wamaŋsaŋa ayen wa ta cheŋ ga a te tɛŋsa meena ale buura meena ale biisa meena ale nuruba meena.

ref: The angel shouted, “Worship and honor God! The time has come for him to judge everyone. Kneel down before the one who created heaven and earth, the oceans, and every stream.”
text: Wa yaa weeni ba ale lueluk kpioŋ, ayen, <<Ni a te Wen zula abe ni a pak wa, dii nyiŋla, wa ka pagrim nyɔnɔ. Diipo ate wa ayen wa bo nuru meena buusa la a paari kama. Wa nye wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋka ale nyakpiemu ale bulisa meena. Dila ale soa ate ku a fɛ ayen ni a puusi a te wa.>>

ref: A second angel followed and said, “The great city of Babylon has fallen! This is the city that made all nations drunk and immoral. Now God is angry, and Babylon has fallen.”
text: Wen maarɔ wa choa mɛ yaa yiri a vi maarɔwa ŋaaŋ ale a weeni ayen, <<Tɛŋ kpieŋka Babilon, a lo kama. Kaboŋsa tuim ŋaai ate ka nuruma a jam a tom la, a nye se ka da pagrik ate ka fɛ ba ate ba nyu la.>>

ref: Finally, a third angel came and shouted: Here is what will happen if you worship the beast and the idol and have the mark of the beast on your hand or forehead.
text: Wen maarɔ wa choa a yaa ŋman yiri a vi nwala ŋaaŋ ale a weeni ale lueluk kpioŋ ayen, <<Baai meena ale a puusi a te duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale jam nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini la, yaase baai meena ale basi ate ka bɔglukku a ŋmarisi ba nisa ale ba dee nyiŋ la.

ref: You will have to drink the wine that God gives to everyone who makes him angry. You will feel his mighty anger, and you will be tortured with fire and burning sulfur, while the holy angels and the Lamb look on.
text: Wen ta ka suipuurum ale ba ate wa ayen wa le te ba waalika. Wa suipuurumu a nye ase ka da pagrik la. Wa suipuurumu a nye ase ka da bula ate wa yaa fɛ ba ayen ba nyu la. Wa le basi ate ba pai ba a nyo ka bolim po ate ba nam nna yegayega Pabiika ale ka maarɔma baai ate ka lueri a te ka dek la niŋ.

ref: If you worship the beast and the idol and accept the mark of its name, you will be tortured day and night. The smoke from your torture will go up forever and ever, and you will never be able to rest.
text: Bolim buui ate ba le nam bu po la nyuisaŋa a kasim a jueli ka wenŋmazuk taam wuu. Baai ale jam puusi a te duŋ kperikaliika ale ka bɔglukku ale ŋman basi ate ku pai ku yuenni a ŋmarisi ba nyiŋ la, bala dek ale ba kasim a nam alege kan nya vuusum.>>

ref: God's people must learn to endure. They must also obey his commands and have faith in Jesus.
text: Dila ale soa ate Wen nuruma baai ale a siak a te Wen sinsaŋŋa alege kan zɛri Yeezu vaka la, ku a fɛ ayen ba va yɔgyɔgla ale chichiiba.

ref: Then I heard a voice from heaven say, “Put this in writing. From now on, the Lord will bless everyone who has faith in him when they die.” The Spirit answered, “Yes, they will rest from their hard work, and they will be rewarded for what they have done.” The Earth Is Harvested
text: Ate mi yaa ŋman wom lueluk ale ku nyini wenŋmazuk siŋ jam a yaa weeni ayen, <<Ŋmarisi dii ate m le weeni la a dueni. Baai ale a tom tuima a te Naawen alege a kpi yɔgyɔgla la, ba sue le peenti kama.>> Wen Chiika mɛ a maa weeni gum du ayen, <<Fi biisi ka wensie. Wen le tuni ba abe wa basi ate ba vuusi ale ba tuim pagrisa yegayega abe wa basi ate ba sue peenti.>>

ref: I looked and saw a bright cloud, and someone who seemed to be the Son of Man was sitting on the cloud. He wore a gold crown on his head and held a sharp sickle in his hand.
text: Mi ŋman gaa nya la ale waai ale a nye ase saalɔbiik la, ale wa kali chiŋma peeluk zuk. Wa jam vuk ka zutɔk kaai ale a nye ase ligmɔniŋ ate ba pai nye la. Wa jam ta ka gɔtuk kuui ale ta nɔi la wa nisa po.

ref: An angel came out of the temple and shouted, “Start cutting with your sickle! Harvest season is here, and all crops on earth are ripe.”
text: Wen maarɔ a yaa nyini Wen yenni po a nyini a biisi ale lueluk kpioŋ a yaa weeni ayen, <<Ku paari tɛŋka ŋantaŋa ŋarika kama. Pai fi gɔtuku a nyini.>>

ref: The one on the cloud swung his sickle and harvested the crops.
text: Ate waai ale jam kali chiŋmanni zuk la a yaa misi wa gɔtuku a ŋari tɛŋka ŋantaŋa.

ref: Another angel with a sharp sickle then came out of the temple in heaven.
text: Wen maarɔ wa choa mɛ yaa jam nyini Wen yenni dii ale bo wenŋmazukku la. Wa mɛ jam ta ka gɔtuk kuui ale ta nɔi la.

ref: After this, an angel with power over fire came from the altar and shouted to the angel who had the sickle. He said, “All grapes on earth are ripe! Harvest them with your sharp sickle.”
text: Wen maarɔ waai ale a nya bolimu zuk la, yaa nyini kuŋkuŋku jigini a weeni maarɔ waai ale ta gɔtuku la ayen pai fi gɔtuku a ŋari tiisaŋa diila yɔnaŋa a muni kama.

ref: The angel swung his sickle on earth and cut off its grapes. He threw them into a pit where they were trampled on as a sign of God's anger.
text: Maarɔwa yaa misi wa gɔtuku a ŋari tiisaŋa yɔnaŋa a lɔnsi tɛŋ a yaa tigsi ŋa a dueni juijui ate ba a ŋmiak ŋa nyiamu la. Dula jigini ale Wen suipuurumu ka bunyi.

ref: After this, I looked at the sky and saw something else that was strange and important. Seven angels were bringing the seven last terrible troubles. When these are ended, God will no longer be angry.
text: Ate mi ŋman nya jakperikaliik tanjaŋini wenŋmazuk ate ku cha mi nna yegayega. Maarɔba bayopɔi ale jam ta ninam tɔgatɔga buyopɔi a jam bo dula. Ba le jam basi ate ninammu a yik ka tɛŋzuk nuruma a kpeglim. Dii nyiŋla, Wen sui ale jam a puuri ale nuruba diila ate wa ayen wa te ba waalika la a nueri kama yɔgla.

ref: Then I saw something that looked like a glass sea mixed with fire, and people were standing on it. They were the ones who had defeated the beast and the idol and the number that tells the name of the beast. God had given them harps,
text: Mi yaa nya Naawen nuru baai ale jam kan puusi a te duŋ kperikaliika yaase ka bɔglukku, yaase ka pai ka yuenni ale kobsiyuebi ale pisiyuebi ale bayuebi a ŋmarisi ba nyiŋ. Mi jam, nya ba ale za moata ka nyakpiemu ate bu a nyaksi nna ase nyaasuŋ la. Bolim ale jam bo nyiamu po. Nuruma a jam ta ka ŋanta nna a se kpanta la ate Naawen a jam pai a te ba.

ref: and they were singing the song his servant Moses and the Lamb had sung. They were singing, “Lord God All-Powerful, you have done great and marvelous things. You are the ruler of all nations, and you do what is right and fair.
text: Ba yaa jam yi Moosis waai ale jam ka Naawen tomteerɔ la ale Pabiika yiili. Ba jam yi yiini ayen, <<Naawen dii ale ka Wen la, fi ka waai ale soa ŋanta meena pagrim la, ku chim ka wakperikaliik ti jigi, fi tuimaŋa nyiŋ. Fi ka waai ale ka tɛŋzuk meena nuruma Naab la. Tuim ŋaai meena ate fi a tom la, ŋa ka wensie. Ŋa daa wasusuga.

ref: After this, I noticed something else in heaven. The sacred tent used for a temple was open.
text: Ba le jam yi yiini a nueri la, mi yaa nya ale Wen yenni nɔnni a lak ate pumpuulima viuku a boro.

ref: And the seven angels who were bringing the terrible troubles were coming out of it. They were dressed in robes of pure white linen and wore belts made of pure gold.
text: Maarɔba bayopɔiwa ale jam ta ninam tɔgatɔga buyopɔiwa la a yaa nyini dula a nyini. Ba jam jo ka garuk peelita ate ti nala nna yegayega. Ba jam maa ta ka garuk pali fiik sii ale a nyaksi a neensi ligmɔniŋ la yaa bobi gilim ba kuusa.

ref: The temple quickly filled with smoke from the glory and power of God. No one could enter it until the seven angels had finished pouring out the seven last troubles.
text: Wen zulaŋa ale wa nalimu ale wa pagrimu yegayega a jam a nye ase ka nyuisa la a yaa sueri wa Yenni. Ase ka maarɔma a nin basi ate ninam tɔgatɔga buyopɔiwa a yik tɛŋzuk nuruma a nueri, nuru an jam baga a jo Wen yenni po.

ref: From the temple I heard a voice shout to the seven angels, “Go and empty the seven bowls of God's anger on the earth.”
text: Ate mi yaa wom ale lueluk kpioŋ a nyini Wen yenni a yaa weeni Maarɔba bayopɔiwa ayen, <<Ni pai Wen suipuurum yegayega ale bo chinaŋa po la a cheŋ ga kpiiri basi tɛŋka zuk.>>

ref: The first angel emptied his bowl on the earth. At once ugly and painful sores broke out on everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol.
text: Maarɔma wanyi a yaa dɛ niŋ nyini ga kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi tɛŋka zuk, ate niri kperikaliisa a yaa nye nuru baai ate duŋ kperikaliika a ŋmarisi ba nyiŋsa ate ba jam a kaab ka bɔglukku la ate ba jam a nam nna yegayega.

ref: The second angel emptied his bowl on the sea. At once the sea turned into blood like that of a dead person, and every living thing in the sea died.
text: Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari bayewa la jam kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi nyakpiemu po. Nyiamu a yaa jam muni nna ase kpio ziim la ate jaabuuri ale jam bo bu po la a yaa kpi.

ref: The third angel emptied his bowl into the rivers and streams. At once they turned to blood.
text: Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari batawa la mɛ yaa kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi belaŋa ale bulisaŋa po ate nyaataŋa a chim ziim.

ref: Then I heard the angel, who has power over water, say, “You have always been, and you always will be the holy God. You had the right to judge in this way.
text: Mi yaa wom ale maarɔwa a weeni ayen, <<Fi ka waai ale ka Weleŋsa Nyɔnɔ la. Fi ale piilimka, fi be boro kama taam wuu, fi ka Weleŋsa Nyɔnɔ, dii nyiŋ la fi buusaŋa ate fi bo la ka wensie.

ref: They poured out the blood of your people and your prophets. So you gave them blood to drink as they deserve!”
text: Ba jam ko fi nuruma ale biisiteerɔma ate ba ziimu a yaa nyini tɛŋ. Ku magsi kama ale fi ale pai ziimu ayen ba nyu yɔgyɔgla la.>>

ref: The fourth angel emptied his bowl on the sun, and it began to scorch people like fire.
text: Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari banaansiwa la yaa kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi wenbinni zuk ate di kantueŋka a yaa nya suik a dɛ nuruma.

ref: Everyone was scorched by its great heat, and all of them cursed the name of God who had power over these terrible troubles. But no one turned to God and praised him.
text: Kantueŋka ale jam dɛ ba la, ba yaa ka a te Wen, dii nyiŋ la, wa le basi ate ninammu a yik ba la. Alege ba an jam basi ba tuimbaataŋa tomka alege tagri ba popola a te Wen zula.

ref: The fifth angel emptied his bowl on the throne of the beast. At once darkness covered its kingdom, and its people began biting their tongues in pain.
text: Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari banuwa la a yaa kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi duŋ kperikaliika naamu jigini. Wa jigini ate wa jam boro la a yaa jam sobri ate wa ŋaaŋviirɔma sue a jam a puuri ate ba jam a dom ba giŋgeluŋta.

ref: And because of their painful sores, they cursed the God who rules in heaven. But still they did not stop doing evil things.
text: Ba yaa jam ka a te Wen dii ale bo wenŋmazuk la ba niraŋa ale ninammu nyiŋ, alege ba an jam basi ba tuimbaataŋa tomka.

ref: The sixth angel emptied his bowl on the great Euphrates River, and it completely dried up to make a road for the kings from the east.
text: Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari bayuebiwa la yaa jam kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi beli kpienni Yufiretis po. Nyiamu a yaa jam kpeeri alege ate nalima ŋaai ale nyini kori nummu po a cheena la a nya suik a taam jam.

ref: An evil spirit that looked like a frog came out of the mouth of the dragon. One also came out of the mouth of the beast, and another out of the mouth of the false prophet.
text: Ate mi yaa nya chichirik baata tita ale ti a neensi buntua. Chichirik baataŋa de a jam nyini ka jaab waai ale a neensi waamu a jam yiak nipowa ale duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale jam nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini la ale venta biisiteerɔwa nɔi po a nyini.

ref: These evil spirits had the power to work miracles. They went to every king on earth, to bring them together for a war against God All-Powerful. But that will be the day of God's great victory.
text: Chichirik baataŋa a jam ta ka pagrim a tom wakperikaliisa yegayega. Ba jam nyiem kama a yaa tigsi tɛŋzuk nuruma meena nalimaŋa ale ba nuruma a nyo jigi yeŋ ayen Wen Kpienni dai kpienni danni ate wa le jam a bo buusa la a dan paari, ba le tu chaab ale wa a nye kpaliŋ.

ref: Remember Christ says, “When I come, it will surprise you like a thief! But God will bless you, if you are awake and ready. Then you won't have to walk around naked and be ashamed.”
text: Ni wom ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ale a weeni ayen, <<Nya, m kan beni m le jam ase ka zue la. Niauŋ a bo le ka waai ale a limisi ale basi ate wa gattaŋa a bo le wa la, ate wa kan cheŋ chaboala ate ba nya wa chivie.>>

ref: Those armies came together in a place that in Hebrew is called Armagedon.
text: Ate chichirik baataŋa a dɛ nalimaŋa niŋ, a ta ba jam jigi ate ba a wi dula ale Juuma biika ayen Amagedon.

ref: As soon as the seventh angel emptied his bowl in the air, a loud voice from the throne in the temple shouted, “It's done!”
text: Ate maarɔ waai ale saari bayopɔiwa la a jam kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi wenŋmazuk. Mi yaa wom ale lueluk kpioŋ nyini wenŋmazuk naamu zukpaglika jigini Wen yenni po a siŋ a weeni ayen, <<Ku jam ya.>>

ref: The great city of Babylon split into three parts, and the cities of other nations fell. So God made Babylon drink from the wine cup filled with his anger.
text: Tɛŋ kpieŋka a jam poori ka buta ate tɛŋzuk tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa a kaasi meena. Wen yaa teeri Babilon wari a yaa basi ate ka nuruma a nyu wa suipuurumu wa beerika po ase daam la.

ref: One of the seven angels who had emptied the bowls came over and said to me, “Come on! I will show you how God will punish that shameless prostitute who sits on many oceans.
text: Ate maarɔba bayopɔiwa wanyi waai ale jam ta china ŋayopɔi la a yaa jam weeni mi ayen, <<Jam ate m sak fu nidoa yaalika ale wa nya ninam diila. Waai ale kali nya boari zuk la.

ref: Every king on earth has slept with her, and her shameless ways are like wine that has made everyone on earth drunk.”
text: Tɛŋka nuruma ale ba nalimaŋa ale wala a maa chaab a tom ka kabonsa tuima. Nuruma ale wala ale jam nye diila a nye se ka daam ate ba nyu buk la.>>

ref: With the help of the Spirit, the angel took me into a desert, where I saw a woman sitting on a red beast. The beast was covered with names that were an insult to God, and it had seven heads and ten horns.
text: Wen Chiika ale basi ate maarɔwa a pai mi a ta cheŋ sagni po la. Duŋ kpieŋ mɔnuŋ ale jam ta zuima ŋayopɔi ale nyiila pi a jam za du. Ba jam ŋmarisi ka leeta yue nna yegayega ŋaai ale jam a lɛ Wen la a dueni ka nyiŋ ate nidoa yaalika a yaa jam kali ka zuk.

ref: The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet robes, and she wore jewelry made of gold, precious stones, and pearls. In her hand she held a gold cup filled with the filthy and nasty things she had done.
text: Wa jam jo ka garuk sobluk ale garuk mɔnuŋ ale maa su ligmɔniŋ ale tintana ŋaai ale a nyaksi la ŋanta. Wa jam ta ka ligmɔniŋ beerik ate ŋan daŋtisa a sueri ka, kude a sak ka wa nidoa yaalik tuimaŋa.

ref: I could tell that the woman was drunk on the blood of God's people who had given their lives for Jesus. This surprising sight amazed me,
text: Mi yaa jam nya ale nipowa a jam nyu ka Wen nuruma ale nuru baai ale jam kan basi Yeezu vaka la ziimu. Mi le jam nya wa la, ku jam ka wakperikaliik yegayega mi jigi.

ref: and the angel said: Why are you so amazed? I will explain the mystery about this woman and about the beast she is sitting on, with its seven heads and ten horns.
text: Maarɔwa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Ka boan nyiŋ ate ku chim wakperikaliik fi jigiya? Nipowa ale duŋ kpieŋ kaai ale ta zuima ŋayopɔiwa ale nyiila piwa ate wa jam do ka la, wala ale duŋka a jam ta kiri kama ate di suk. M le weeni di kiri ale ka diila a sak fu.

ref: The beast you saw is one that used to be and no longer is. It will come back from the deep pit, but only to be destroyed. Everyone on earth whose names were not written in the book of life before the time of creation will be amazed. They will see this beast that used to be and no longer is, but will be once more.
text: Duŋ kala a jam boro kama alege a ŋman karo. Ka abe za ka nyini ka vɔrup buui ale kan ka kpeglimka la po a nyini ate ba a kaasi ka. Nuru baai wie ale kan ŋmarisi dua ŋanvuta gbaŋka po a nyini diipo ate ba an diem nye tɛŋka la, ku le cha ba ase ba nin nya ka. Ka jam boro kama alege yɔgyɔgla de ka ŋman karo, alege ka le pilim vuri nyini.

ref: Anyone with wisdom can figure this out. The seven heads that the woman is sitting on stand for seven hills. These heads are also seven kings.
text: <<Be ka yam ale miŋka ate waai a miŋ wieŋa de. Zuima ŋayopɔiwa ka guuta tiyopɔi ate nipowa a kali ti zuk.

ref: Five of the kings are dead. One is ruling now, and the other one has not yet come. But when he does, he will rule for only a little while.
text: Ŋa bɛ ka nalima ŋayopɔi. Nalima ŋanu ale jɔk ba naamu alege wanyi a dɛ wa naamu diema alege wanyi an diem jam ya, wa dan jam wa ale dɛ wa naamu ka maga.

ref: You also saw a beast that used to be and no longer is. That beast is one of the seven kings who will return as the eighth king, but only to be destroyed.
text: Duŋ kaai ale jam boro alege a ŋman karo la a yaa saari ka nalima naaniŋ. Wa abe ka ŋayopɔiwa po wanyi a za wa nyini ate ba kaasi wa.

ref: The ten horns you saw are ten more kings, who have not yet come into power, and they will rule with the beast for only a short time.
text: <<Nyiila piwa ate fi nya la, ka nalima pi baai ale kan diem piilim ba naamu dɛ ka, alege ba ale nya ka pagrim a dɛ ba naamu ase miita pisiyuebi la ale duŋka.

ref: They all think alike and will give their power and authority to the beast.
text: Nalima piwa de meena a ta ka popola yena. Ba abe pai ba pagrimu a te ka duŋka.

ref: These kings will go to war against the Lamb. But he will defeat them, because he is Lord over all lords and King over all kings. His followers are chosen and special and faithful.
text: Ba ale nye kpaliŋ ale Pabiika alege Pabiika ale baai ate ka lueri ate ba va ka ale siaka la ale nak dɛ ba meena dii nyiŋla ka ka nyama meena Nyɔnɔ ale nalima meena Naab.>>

ref: The oceans you saw the prostitute sitting on are crowds of people from all races and languages.
text: Maarɔwa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Nyaataŋa ate fi nya ate nidoa yaalika a kali du la, ka nuruba ale nuru boari ale tɛŋsa ale biisa.

ref: The ten horns and the beast will start hating the shameless woman. They will strip off her clothes and leave her naked. Then they will eat her flesh and throw the rest of her body into a fire.
text: Nyiila piwa ate fi nya la ale duŋka ale kisi nidoa yaalika kama ate ba yaa yik jaabuuri meena ate wa ta la a tuesi alege basi wa chaboala. Ba ale ŋɔbi wa nyiŋ lammu abe ba kaasi wa ale bolim.

ref: God is the one who made these kings all think alike and decide to give their power to the beast. And they will do this until what God has said comes true.
text: Wen dek ale te ba suik ayen ba a tom ale chaab ate wa ale poli ayen dii a nye la, abe di nye. Abe ba pai ba pagrimu a te duŋka ate ka soa naamu a nya ate Wen wieŋa a chim wensie.

ref: The woman you saw is the great city that rules over all kings on earth.
text: <<Nipowa ate fi nya la ale tɛŋ kpieŋ kaai ale a nya tɛŋzuk nalimaŋa la.>>

ref: I saw another angel come from heaven. This one had great power, and the earth was bright because of his glory.
text: Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ mi yaa nya Maarɔwa choa ale wa nyini wenŋmazuk a siŋ tɛŋ. Wa ta ka pagrim nna yegayega ale a nyaksi a nya tɛŋka meena.

ref: The angel shouted, “Fallen! Powerful Babylon has fallen and is now the home of demons. It is the den of every filthy spirit and of all unclean birds, and every dirty and hated animal.
text: Wa yaa kaari weeni ale lueluk kpioŋ ayen, <<Wa lo kama, tɛŋ kpieŋka Babilon a lo kama. Chichirik baata ale bo ka po ale nuim baata ale sii ale kisi nuruba ale sueri ka po.

ref: Babylon's evil and immoral wine has made all nations drunk. Every king on earth has slept with her, and every merchant on earth is rich because of her evil desires.”
text: Ka kaboŋsa tuimaŋa a nye ase ka daam la, ate tɛŋsa meena a nyu. Tɛŋka zuk nalimaŋa a zamsi kaboŋsa tuima ka kala jigi. Tɛŋka zuk geruŋdɔma a va ka ka kɔrisa tuimaŋa nyiŋ a jigsi.>>

ref: Then I heard another voice from heaven shout, “My people, you must escape from Babylon. Don't take part in her sins and share her punishment.
text: Mi yaa ŋman wom lueluk ku choa wenŋmazuk a weeni ayen, <<Mi nuruma ni nyini ka po a nyini. Ni kan maara a tom ka tuimbaataŋa, ni kan maa nam ninam buui ate ba a nam la.

ref: Her sins are piled as high as heaven. God has remembered the evil she has done.
text: Ka tuimbaataŋa a piisi ka nna yegayega, Wen abe teeri wa nyeka tuemu wie kama.

ref: Treat her as she has treated others. Make her pay double for what she has done. Make her drink twice as much of what she mixed for others.
text: Ni nye ka ase ka mɛ ale a nye nama diila, ka ale nye ni dii meena la, ni nye dila ku nɔi buye a tuni ka. Ka ale sueri beerika ale daamu a te nama la. Nama mɛ a sueri ku nɔi buye a te ka.

ref: That woman honored herself with a life of luxury. Reward her now with suffering and pain. “Deep in her heart Babylon said, ‘I am the queen! Never will I be a widow or know what it means to be sad.’
text: Ni te ka ninam yegayega ase ka ale pai nalim ale masim a te ka dek diila. Diila wa kasim a weeni wadek kama ayen, <Mi nipok naawa kali ka dela. Mi daa pukɔgi ya. Mi kan maa seba jabuui ate ba a weeni ayen ninam la.>

ref: And so, in a single day she will suffer the pain of sorrow, hunger, and death. Fire will destroy her dead body, because her judge is the powerful Lord God.”
text: Wieŋa de nyiŋ, dai yeŋ ninam tɔgatɔga ase nyiŋtuila ale kum ale suipuurum ale kom ale yik wa. Ate bolim a dɛ wa dii nyiŋla Naawen dii ale ka Wen dii ale a bo wa buusa la a zuak kama yegayega.>>

ref: Every king on earth who slept with her and shared in her luxury will mourn. They will weep, when they see the smoke from that fire.
text: Tɛŋzuk de nalimaŋa baai ale maa tom ka kaboŋsaŋa ale ka kɔrisa tuimaŋa la ale kum te ka ase ba nin nya bolimu ale a dɛ ka ate nyuisaŋa a yiti la.

ref: Her sufferings will frighten them, and they will stand at a distance and say, “Pity that great and powerful city! Pity Babylon! In a single hour her judgment has come.”
text: Ba za ka nna niŋniŋa a nya dii nyiŋla ba a chali ka yɔgsum ale ba nin maa nam. Ba za kama a weeni ayen nya ku ale bie dii nna yegayega. Tɛŋ kpieŋka de ate miita pisiyuebi po ka deri nya ninam.

ref: Every merchant on earth will mourn, because there is no one to buy their goods.
text: Tɛŋka geruŋdɔma meena a kum a te ka diila waai a kan da ba ŋantaŋa.

ref: No one will buy their cinnamon, spices, incense, myrrh, frankincense, wine, olive oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, slaves, and other humans.
text: ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la ale ti daamu ale ti kpaamu ale zeuŋtaŋa ale ŋanbieŋa ale ti niiŋa ale ti piisaŋa ale ti wusumaŋa ale ŋa torokoma ale ti yɔmma ale nurubisa chiisaŋa.

ref: Babylon, the things your heart desired have all escaped from you. Every luxury and all your glory will be lost forever. You will never get them back.
text: Ate geruŋdɔma yaa weeni wa ayen fi jɔk ŋan maŋsaŋa meena kama a jɔk fi nalimu mɛ. Fi be kan ŋman nya ba.

ref: The merchants had become rich because of her. But when they saw her sufferings, they were terrified. They stood at a distance, crying and mourning.
text: Geruŋdɔ baai meena ale gerim tɛŋ kala po a jigsi la ale za ka nna niŋniŋa, dii nyiŋla ba a chali ka yɔgsum ale ba ale maa nam ale wa. Ba le kasim kaari kama,

ref: Then they shouted, “Pity the great city of Babylon! She dressed in fine linen and wore purple and scarlet cloth. She had jewelry made of gold and precious stones and pearls.
text: a weeni ayen, <<Ku bie ka nna yegayega tɛŋ kpieŋka de jigi. Ni nyiem kasim a jo ka garuk peeta ale garuk sobta ale garuk mɔnta ale a su ŋan baai ate ba pai ligmɔniŋ ale tintain naliŋsa ale ŋan baai ale a nyaksi a nye ba la.

ref: Yet in a single hour her riches disappeared.” Every ship captain and passenger and sailor stood at a distance, together with everyone who does business by traveling on the sea.
text: Ate ba deri jɔk ba ŋantaŋa meena miita pisiyuebi po.>> Ŋaaruŋtaŋa kpaŋŋa ale baai ale baai ale va ŋaaruŋtaŋa a nyiem ale baai ale a dam ŋaaruŋtaŋa ale baai meena ale a tom nyakpiemu po a dɛ la a yaa za niŋniŋa.

ref: When they saw the smoke from her fire, they shouted, “This was the greatest city ever!”
text: A kaari dii nyiŋla ba ale nya bolimu ale a dɛ ba ate nyuisaŋa a yiti diila. Tɛŋ a jam karo a magsi chaab ale tɛŋka de.

ref: They cried loudly, and in their sorrow they threw dust on their heads, as they said, “Pity the great city of Babylon! Everyone who sailed the seas became rich from her treasures. But in a single hour the city was destroyed.
text: Ba jam kasim ŋari ka tanta a basi ba zuimaŋa po, ale a kaari a weeni ayen dii ale a nye tɛŋka de po la a bie ka yega. Ka ka tɛŋ kaai ate nuruba a jam ka ale ŋaaruŋta a gerim, a va ka ŋantaŋa nyiŋ a jigsi. Ate ka deri yiti dai yeŋ a jɔk jaab meena.

ref: A powerful angel then picked up a huge stone and threw it into the sea. The angel said, “This is how the great city of Babylon will be thrown down, never to rise again.
text: Ate maarɔ kpioŋ a yaa pai tintain ate di soa ase niri la a yuk basi nyakpiemu po, ale weeni ayen, Wen a za wa yuk tɛŋ kpieŋka Babilon ale pagrim a basi ka dila dekdega ate waai a kan ŋman nya ka.

ref: The music of harps and singers and of flutes and trumpets will no longer be heard. No workers will ever set up shop in that city, and the sound of grinding grain will be silenced forever.
text: Nuruba a kan ŋman wom nuruba luelita yaase kpanta nakka yaase paampuuŋta peerika yaase damunsa peerika. Nuru kan ŋman tom tuini tɛŋ kala po, waai abe kan wom niri num ka.

ref: Lamps will no longer shine anywhere in Babylon, and couples will never again say wedding vows there. Her merchants ruled the earth, and by her witchcraft she fooled all nations.
text: Waai a kan nya zeuŋ toati ka tɛŋ kala po yaase nipok faarik wari du. Tɛŋ kala geruŋdɔma ale jam pagra tɛŋka meena zuk ate ka nuruma a tom kperisa tuima a paasi tɛŋka zuk nuruma meena.

ref: On the streets of Babylon is found the blood of God's people and of his prophets, and everyone else.”
text: Babilon a nya ninam yegayega dii nyiŋla ba ale ko Wen biisiteerɔma ale Wen nuruma ale nuruba yegayega ate ba ziimu a nyini tɛŋka po la.

ref: After this, I heard what sounded like a lot of voices in heaven, and they were shouting, “Praise the Lord! To our God belongs the glorious power to save,
text: Kude ŋaaŋnyiŋ mi yaa wom nuemka nna ase nuru boari la wenŋmazuk a weeni ayen, <<Pak Wen, varibasika ale zula ale pagrim, ka tama Wenni ale soa.

ref: because his judgments are honest and fair. That filthy prostitute ruined the earth with shameful deeds. But God has judged her and made her pay the price for murdering his servants.”
text: Wa ka wensie nyɔnɔ ale a bo wensie buusa. Wen a bo mini nidoa yaalika wa ale kaasi tɛŋka ale wa kaboŋsa tuimaŋa la kama. Wen a namsi wa kama dii nyiŋla wa ale ko wa tomteerɔma la.>>

ref: Then the crowd shouted, “Praise the Lord! Smoke will never stop rising from her burning body.”
text: Ba yaa ŋman pilim kaari a weeni ayen, <<Pak Wen, bolimu ale a dɛ tɛŋ kpieŋka la nyuisaŋa a kasim a jueli ka wein taam wuu.>>

ref: Then I heard what seemed to be a large crowd that sounded like a roaring flood and loud thunder all mixed together. They were saying, “Praise the Lord! Our Lord God All-Powerful now rules as king.
text: Mi yaa ŋman wom nuru boari luelita ate ti jam a nye wai nna yegayega ase nyaata ale a chali la. Luelutaŋa mɛ a jam a na ase ka nanpansa ale a na la. Luelutaŋa a jam a weeni ayen, <<Ni basi ate ti a pak Wen. Wala ale soa ŋanta meena pagrim. Wa ka Naawen.

ref: So we will be glad and happy and give him praise. The wedding day of the Lamb is here, and his bride is ready.
text: Wa zuak a gaam ŋanta meena kama. Dila ale soa ate ku a fɛ ayen ti a pak wa ale suipeentik. Di danni a paari kama ayen Pabiika a faari nipok waai ale gomsi wadek a limisi wa la.

ref: She will be given a wedding dress made of pure and shining linen. This linen stands for the good things God's people have done.”
text: Ba te wa powa ka suik ayen wa jo garuk tii ale nala ale a nyaksi la.>> Garuk naliŋtaŋa de ka tuim naliŋ sii ate Wen nuruma a jam nye la.

ref: Then the angel told me, “Put this in writing. God will bless everyone who is invited to the wedding feast of the Lamb.” The angel also said, “These things God has said are true.”
text: Wen maarɔ wanyi a yaa jam weeni mi ayen, <<Ŋmarisi dii ate mi a weeni la a dueni. Baai ate ba le wi ba ayen ba jam maa dɛ ŋandiinta Pabiika nipowa faarika la, ba sue ale peenti.>> Wa le ga weeni nna a nueri la, wa ŋman pilim weeni maga a gum du ayen, <<Wieŋa de ka Wen wensie wie.>>

ref: I knelt at the feet of the angel and began to worship him. But the angel said, “Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you and everyone else who tells about Jesus. Don't worship anyone but God. Everyone who tells about Jesus does it by the power of the Spirit.” The Rider on the White Horse
text: Mi yaa kpi duna wa niŋ ayen m puusi wa, alege wa jam weeni mi ayen, <<Kan nye dila, dii nyiŋla mi ale fi ale fi suataŋa baai ale a weeni nuruba ayen Yeezu ale soa ba la, tama meena ka wa tomteerɔba. A puusi Wen nyiini.>> Wensieŋa ate Yeezu a pai sak la ale a basi ate biisiteerɔma a biisi.

ref: I looked and saw heaven was open, and a white horse was there. Its rider was called Faithful and True, and he is always fair when he judges or goes to war.
text: Ate mi yaa nya ale wenŋmazuk lak ate wusum peeluk a yaa jam za du. Ba jam a wi waai ale jam do bu la ayen ka, <<Wensie Nyɔnɔ.>> Wa yuei mɛ jam ale, <<Waai ale ta Siaka la.>> Daa meena wa kasim jam a cheŋ ka kpaliŋ po, ale a bo wa dachaasaŋa buusa ŋaai ale jam magsi wa boka la.

ref: He had eyes like flames of fire, and he was wearing a lot of crowns. His name was written on him, but he was the only one who knew what the name meant.
text: Wa ninaŋa a jam muni ase ka bolim la. Wa mɛ jam vuk ka zutɔk boari. Ba jam ŋmarisi ka yuei dii ate nuru a jam zɛ di kiri la a dueni wa nyiŋ. Wadek wa nyiini ale jam seba yuenni kiri.

ref: The rider wore a robe that was covered with blood, and he was known as “The Word of God.”
text: Wa jam jo ka kasaauk ate ziim a jam muni ku meena. Wa yuei jam ale <<Wen Wanni.>>

ref: He was followed by armies from heaven that rode on white horses and were dressed in pure white linen.
text: Tugurik tɔŋdɔba yegayega baai ale jam bo wenŋmazuk la a jam jo ka garuk naliŋta ale do wusum peeta a yaa jam a vi wa ŋaaŋ.

ref: From his mouth a sharp sword went out to attack the nations. He will rule them with an iron rod and will show the fierce anger of God All-Powerful by trampling the grapes in the pit where wine is made.
text: Waai ale do wusum peelukku la a jam ta ka gebik ate ka ta noa ŋaye a yaa jam nyini wa nɔi po a nyini. Wa jam weeni ayen wa le pai kama a nye kpaliŋ ale tɛŋzuk nuruma a nak ba dɛ. Wa le soa ba ale pagrim nalimnyiini abe wa ŋmiak yɔnaŋa daamu. Dula jigini ale a sak Wen suipuurumu.

ref: On the part of the robe that covered his thigh was written, “KING OF KINGS AND Lord OF LordS.”
text: Ba jam ŋmarisi ka yuei a dueni tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni kasaauku ale wa naŋsaŋa kanyi nyiŋ. Yuenni jam ale, <<Nalima Meena Naab Ale Nyama Meena Nyɔnɔ.>>

ref: I then saw an angel standing on the sun, and he shouted to all the birds flying in the sky, “Come and join in God's great feast!
text: Mi yaa nya maarɔ ale wa za wenbinni zuk. Wa yaa jam kaari ale lueluk pagrik yegayega a weeni nuin sii meena ale jam bo wenŋmazuk a yiri la ayen, <<Ni tigsi chaab a jam dɛ ŋandiin tii ate Wen le te ni yegayega la.

ref: I also saw the beast and all kings of the earth come together. They fought against the rider on the white horse and against his army.
text: Ate mi yaa nya duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale jam nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini la ale tɛŋzuk nalimaŋa ale ba tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale ba maa chaab a cheŋ ayen ba ga nye kpaliŋ ale nuru waai ale jam do wusum peelukku la ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma.

ref: But the beast was captured and so was the false prophet. This is the same prophet who had worked miracles for the beast, so he could fool everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol. The beast and the false prophet were thrown alive into a lake of burning sulfur.
text: Wenŋmazuk tugurik tɔŋdɔma a yaa jam nak yiak tɛŋzuk nuruma tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale ge yaa yik duŋ kperikaliika ale venta biisiteerɔwa. Wenŋmazuk tugurik tɔŋdɔma a yaa yik duŋ kperikaliika ale biisiteerɔwa a ta cheŋ ga yuk basi nyakpiemu po, juijui ate bolimu a kasim a dɛ la.

ref: But the rest of their army was killed by the sword that came from the mouth of the rider on the horse. Then birds stuffed themselves on the dead bodies.
text: Wenŋmazuk tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni waai ale jam do wusum peelukku la, a yaa yeeri gebik woŋ kaai ale jam ta noa ŋayewa la wa nɔnni po a yaa ko tɛŋzuk tugurik tɔŋdɔma baai ale jam tali la. Nuinsaŋa a yaa basi wenŋmazuk ale siŋ a dɛ ba chak ale tali.

ref: I saw thrones, and sitting on those thrones were the ones who had been given the right to judge. I also saw the souls of the people who had their heads cut off because they had told about Jesus and preached God's message. They were the same ones who had not worshiped the beast or the idol, and they had refused to let its mark be put on their foreheads or hands. They will come to life and rule with Christ for
text: Ate mi yaa ŋman nya ale zukpaglik si chaab a za dula. Ba yaa jam pai pagrim a te baai ale jam kali si zuk la ayen ba bo buusa. ref: These people are the first to be raised to life, and they are especially blessed and holy. The second death has no power over them. They will be priests for God and Christ and will rule with them for
text: Baai ate Kirisita a liŋ lueri a nye ate ba yiti kum po la, ba sue ale peenti kama. Ba le chim ka Wen ale Kirisita kaabteerɔba. Ba ale wa ale ba soa tɛŋka ate ku ga paari bena tusini la. Kum buui ale a saari buyewa la a kan nya pagrim ba zuwa.

ref: He will fool the countries of Gog and Magog, which are at the far ends of the earth, and their people will follow him into battle. They will have as many followers as there are grains of sand along the beach,

ref: and they will march all the way across the earth. They will surround the camp of God's people and the city God loves. But fire will come down from heaven and destroy the whole army.
text: Ba le nyini ka jigi meena a jam gilim Wen nuruma baai ale jam bo dula la. Wa mariŋ ba boka jigi ka yegayega. Wen ale basi ate bolim nyini wenŋmazuk a siŋ jam dɛ baai meena ale za gilim la.

ref: Then the devil who fooled them will be thrown into the lake of fire and burning sulfur. He will be there with the beast and the false prophet, and they will be in pain day and night forever and ever. The Judgment at the Great White Throne
text: Ba yaa le yik jabioku waai ale jam a nyiem a paasi nuruma la a yuk wa a gum duŋ kperikaliika ale venta biisiteerɔwa po ate bolim buui ale kasim jam a dɛ nyakpiemu po la a dɛ ba meena. Dula, wala ale duŋ kperikaliika ale venta biisiteerɔwa ale kasim a nam ka nna yegayega taam wuu.

ref: I saw a great white throne with someone sitting on it. Earth and heaven tried to run away, but there was no place for them to go.
text: Ate mi yaa ŋman nya zukpaglika wenŋmazuk. Ka jam ka zukpaglik kpieŋ peeluk ate nuru a jam kali ka zuk. Tɛŋka ale wenŋmazuk a jam muriŋ bɛ wa niŋ, jigi mɛ abe jam karo ayen ba sugi.

ref: I also saw all the dead people standing in front of that throne. Every one of them was there, no matter who they had once been. Several books were opened, and then the book of life was opened. The dead were judged by what those books said they had done.
text: Mi yaa nya tɛŋzuk nuruma baai ale jam ka nuru kpienta ale baai ale jam kan daa nuru kpienta ate Wen yaa nak ba yiti kum po la. Ba jam za ka wa zulaŋa zukpaglika niŋ. Ba yaa jam lak nyuvuri gbaŋka ale gbaŋsa si chaab. Wa jam bo ba buusa a magsi chaab ale ka dii ate ba nye la ale dii ale jam ŋmarisi a nyo gbaŋsaŋa po la.

ref: The sea gave up the dead people who were in it, and death and its kingdom also gave up their dead. Then everyone was judged by what they had done.
text: Baai ale jam kpi ate ba gu ba tɛŋka ale nyakpientaŋa po la, ale baai ale jam bo kpiluŋ tɛŋ la, nuruma de meena a jam za ka dula. Wen a jam bo ba buusa a magsi chaab ale ka tuim ŋaai ate ba jam tom la.

ref: Anyone whose name wasn't written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
text: Baai ate ba an ŋmarisi ba yueŋa a nyo nyuvuri gbaŋka po la, ba jam maa pai ba a yuk basi ka dula.

ref: I heard a loud voice shout from the throne: God's home is now with his people. He will live with them, and they will be his own. Yes, God will make his home among his people.
text: Mi yaa wom ale lueluk kpioŋ a nyini wenŋmazuk zukpaglika jigini a yaa a weeni ayen, <<Wom mi. Wen viuku a bo ka nuruba suŋsuŋ, wa ale bo ale ba, ate ba ale chim wa nuruba, ate Wen dek ale bo ale ba.

ref: He will wipe all tears from their eyes, and there will be no more death, suffering, crying, or pain. These things of the past are gone forever.
text: Wa le duisi ba ninyaata a basi. Kum ale ninam ale nyiŋdomma a kan ŋman boro. Ku le liŋ jam ka diila, ku kan ŋman nye dila diipo diipo.>>

ref: Then the one sitting on the throne said: I am making everything new. Write down what I have said. My words are true and can be trusted.
text: Waai ale jam kali Wen zulaŋa zukpaglika zuk la a yaa weeni ayen, <<M nye ŋanta meena ka ŋanpaala.>> Wa ŋman pilim weeni mi ayen, <<Ŋmarisi dii ate m le weeni fu a dueni, dii nyiŋla m wieŋa ka wensie wie ale magsi mɛ.

ref: Everything is finished! I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will freely give water from the life-giving fountain to everyone who is thirsty.
text: M tuimaŋa a nueri kama. M ka Piilimka, m be kasim boro kama taam wuu. M nyuvuri paalik kaai ate m pai a te nuruba la, a nye se ka nyiam la. Nyanyuila ale ta waai meena la, m le basi ate ba nyu bu ka tiirim.

ref: All who win the victory will be given these blessings. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
text: Waai ale ta pagrim wie meena zuk la ale wa tuesi ŋantaŋa de meena, mi ale chim wa Wen ate wa mɛ ale chim m nidoabili.

ref: But I will tell you what will happen to cowards and to everyone who is unfaithful or dirty-minded or who murders or is sexually immoral or uses witchcraft or worships idols or tells lies. They will be thrown into that lake of fire and burning sulfur. This is the second death. The New Jerusalem
text: Alege baai ale yɔgsa la, bumbobrɔma ale baai ale daŋ badek ale wabaata la ale nuru koorisa ale kaboŋ nyeerisa ale sampoporinni tuima ale baai ale a kaab bɔgta ale velimvendisaŋa, a za ba jo ka mɔgi diipo ate bolim a dɛ taam wuu. Ku la a nye ase ba a kpi a saari ka buye la.>>

ref: I saw one of the seven angels who had the bowls filled with the seven last terrible troubles. The angel came to me and said, “Come on! I will show you the one who will be the bride and wife of the Lamb.”
text: Wen maarɔ baai bayopɔiwa ale jam ta china ŋayopɔiwa ate ninammu a bo ŋa po la, wanyi a yaa weeni mi ayen, jam de ate m dak Pabiika powa a sak fu.

ref: Then with the help of the Spirit, he took me to the top of a very high mountain. There he showed me the holy city of Jerusalem coming down from God in heaven.
text: Wen Chiika yaa sak mi ate mi nya ale maarɔ a ji mi a ta jueli guuk zuk. Wa yaa sak mi Tɛŋ Weleŋka Jerusalem ale ka nyini wenŋmazuk Wen jigi a cheena ale

ref: The glory of God made the city bright. It was dazzling and crystal clear like a precious jasper stone.
text: a nyaksi ale Wen zulaŋa. Tɛŋka a kasim a nyaksi kama ase tintain mɔnta la, a nya nna cheri ase nyaasuŋ la.

ref: The city had a high and thick wall with twelve gates, and each one of them was guarded by an angel. On each of the gates was written the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
text: Ka jam ta ka parik kpieŋ nna woŋwoŋŋoa ale nansuiŋta pi ale tiye, ate maarɔba pi ale baye a limisi nansuiŋtaŋa. Nansuiŋtaŋa nɔi ba ŋmarisi ka Izirali bisaŋa pi ale bayewa yue a dueni du.

ref: Three of these gates were on the east, three were on the north, three more were on the south, and the other three were on the west.
text: Nansuiŋta tita ale jam bo kauk kunyi meena. Tita ale jam bo kori geŋ. Tita ale jam bo yeseoku geŋ. Tita ale jam bo wiilukku geŋ. Tita mɛ ale jam bo yeniŋ geŋ.

ref: The city was built on twelve foundation stones. On each of the stones was written the name of one of the Lamb's twelve apostles.
text: Ba pai ka tintana pi ale ŋaye a dueni nyubini ase parika ale ŋmarisi Pabiika tuimtomdɔma pi ale bayewa wie a dueni ŋa nyiŋ la.

ref: The angel who spoke to me had a gold measuring stick to measure the city and its gates and its walls.
text: Wen maarɔ waai ale biisi ale mi la, a jam ta ka tachek ate ba pai ligmɔniŋ a nye ka ayen wa magsi tɛŋka, ale nansuiŋtaŋa ale parisaŋa.

ref: The city was shaped like a cube, because it was just as high as it was wide. When the angel measured the city, it was about
text: Tɛŋka labsimu ale ka woglimmu a jam soa ase ka chaab la. Maarɔwa a jam pai ka wa tachekka a magsi. Ka woglimmu jam ka mɛɛla tusidi ale kobsinu (

ref: Then the angel measured the wall, and by our measurements it was about
text: Maarɔwa jam magsi ka parika ate ka biglimu a chim ka anamagib kobsiye ale pinaanuŋ ale naaniŋ, a va chaab ale nurubiik magsika.

ref: The wall was built of jasper, and the city was made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
text: Tɛŋka parika ba jam pai ka tintain mɔnta a nye ka alege tɛŋka po dek ligmɔniŋ a nye nna ase nyaasuŋ la.

ref: Each of the twelve foundations was a precious stone. The first was jasper, the second was sapphire, the third was agate, the fourth was emerald,
text: Ba pai ka tintain naliŋsa tɔgatɔga a ŋmirisi nyubini. Ba ale liŋ pai ka tintain mɔnta a dueni nyubini, buyewa po ka tintain sobta, butawa po ka tintain paasa, bunaansiwa po ka tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase gunungoona la,

ref: Each of the twelve gates was a solid pearl. The streets of the city were made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
text: Ba yaa jam pai ka ŋanta pi ale baye wa ate ba a nyaksi ase tintana la, a nye parika nansuiŋta pi ale tiyewa meena. Ba jam maa pai ka ligmɔniŋ mɛ a se nyaasuŋ la a piisi suik kpioŋku.

ref: I did not see a temple there. The Lord God All-Powerful and the Lamb were its temple.
text: Mi an jam nya Wen yenni tɛŋka po dii nyiŋla Yenni ale Naawen dii ale ka Wen Kpienni la dek ale wa Pabiika ka Yenni.

ref: And the city did not need the sun or the moon. The glory of God was shining on it, and the Lamb was its light.
text: Baai ale jam bo dula la, an jam a yaali wenbiri yaase chiika. Wen ale wa nalimu ale a nyaksi ate ba a nya. Pabiika mɛ ale ba bolim ate ba a nya.

ref: Nations will walk by the light of that city, and kings will bring their riches there.
text: Tɛŋzuk nuruma le ba nya bolimu dɛ a cheŋ. Ba nalimaŋa mɛ le pai ba zulaŋa a jam gum du.

ref: Its gates are always open during the day, and night never comes.
text: Ba kan lik siaka noaŋa. Ŋa le kasim a lak kama daa meena. Dii nyiŋla yok a kan bo du.

ref: The glorious treasures of nations will be brought into the city.
text: Tɛŋzuk nuruma mɛ le ba zula yegayega a jam gum tɛŋka po.

ref: But nothing unworthy will be allowed to enter. No one who is dirty-minded or who tells lies will be there. Only those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will be in the city.
text: Tuim baata nyama ale baai ale a nye kaboŋsa ale maara velim la, ba kan baga a maa jo dula. Baai ate ba ŋmarisi ba yueŋa a nyo Pabiika nyuvuri paalika gbaŋka po la, bala nyiini ale ba jo du.

ref: The angel showed me a river that was crystal clear, and its waters gave life. The river came from the throne where God and the Lamb were seated.
text: Maarɔwa yaa dak Wen nyuvuri benni nyiamu ale jam a nyaksi nna ase nyaasuŋ la. Di jam nyini ka Wen ale Pabiika jigi wenŋmazuk.

ref: Then it flowed down the middle of the city's main street. On each side of the river are trees that grow a different kind of fruit each month of the year. The fruit gives life, and the leaves are used as medicine to heal the nations.
text: Benni a jam chali va ka tɛŋka suik kpioŋku suŋsuŋ. Wen nyuvuri tiimu a jam za ka benni kabtaŋa meena a yɔn yɔna. Bu jam a yɔni ka pi ale buye ben yeŋ po. Si vaataŋa ale jam a basi ate tɛŋzuk nuruma a nya nyiŋyɔgsa.

ref: God's curse will no longer be on the people of that city. He and the Lamb will be seated there on their thrones, and its people will worship God
text: Ŋan baai ate Wen a ka te ba la, a kan maa bo tɛŋka po. Wen ale Pabiika zulaŋa zukpaglika a bo ka dula ate wa tomteerɔma puusi a te ba.

ref: and will see him face to face. God's name will be written on the foreheads of the people.
text: Ba le nya Wen nimbidiaka ate wa ŋmarisi wa yuenni a dueni ba dee nyiŋ.

ref: Never again will night appear, and no one who lives there will ever need a lamp or the sun. The Lord God will be their light, and they will rule forever. The Coming of Christ
text: Abe wa basi ate ba chim nalima taam wuu. Yɔk a kan bo dula, dii nyiŋla ba Naawen dii ale ka Wen la ale wa te ba kantueŋ. Ba kan ba a yaali kantueŋŋa yaase zeuŋta ayen ba a nya.

ref: Then I was told: These words are true and can be trusted. The Lord God controls the spirits of his prophets, and he is the one who sent his angel to show his servants what must happen very soon.
text: Ate maarɔwa a yaa weeni mi ayen, <<M le a yaali ayen m weeni fu diila a magsi kama ale ŋman chim wensie mɛ. Naawen dii ale ka Wen la waai ale pai wa Chiika a nyo wa biisiteerɔma suiniima po la, a tom ka mi wa maarɔwa ayen wa jam sak wa tomteerɔma dii ale di nye yɔgyɔgla la.>>

ref: My name is John, and I am the one who heard and saw these things. Then after I had heard and seen all this, I knelt down and began to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown it to me.
text: Mi, Jɔɔn, a nya kama ale wom wieŋa de meena. Mi le ga nya ale wom wieŋa de meena a nueri la, m jam kpi ka duna tɛŋ ayen m puusi maarɔwa waai ale dak wieŋa de meena a sak mu la.

ref: But the angel said, Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you. I am the same as a follower or a prophet or anyone else who obeys what is written in this book. God is the one you should worship.
text: Alege wa weeni mi ayen, <<Kan nye dila, dii nyiŋla mi ale fi ale fi suataŋa baai ale ka Wen biisiteerɔba ale a va gbaŋka de wieŋa la, tama meena ka Wen tomteerɔba. Puusi a te wala nyiini.>>

ref: Evil people will keep on being evil, and everyone who is dirty-minded will still be dirty-minded. But good people will keep on doing right, and God's people will always be holy.
text: Basi ate waai ale a tom tuimkaasima la a kasim tom tuimkaasima a cheŋ, basi ate waai ale a tom tuimdaŋtisa la a kasim tom tuimdaŋtisa a cheŋ, basi ate waai ale a tom tuimaŋsa la a kasim tom tuimaŋsa a cheŋ, a basi mɛ ate waai ale welema la a kasim welema a cheŋ.>>

ref: Then I was told: I am coming soon! And when I come, I will reward everyone for what they have done.
text: Yeezu a weeni ayen, <<Nya, m cheena ku kan beni. M ta m tutunaŋa kama, ate m le te waai meena a magsi chaab ale wa le tom diila.

ref: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
text: Mi ale Piilimka ale Kpeglimka, mi ale dɛ niŋ ale wari ŋaaŋ, mi ale piilim ale kpeglim.

ref: God will bless all who have washed their robes. They will each have the right to eat fruit from the tree that gives life, and they can enter the gates of the city.
text: Baai ale a sugri ba gattaŋa ayen daŋta a kan tiri ba ate ba nya suik a jo tɛŋka po a dɛ Wen nyuvuri tiimu yɔnni la, ba sue le peenti.

ref: I am Jesus! And I am the one who sent my angel to tell all of you these things for the churches. I am David's Great Descendant, and I am also the bright morning star.
text: <<Mi, Yeezu, ale tom m maarɔwa ayen wa jam mooli wieŋa de ate baai meena ale a va mi la wom ŋa. Mi ka Naawa Deevid ŋaaŋbiik. Mi a nyaksi ka nna yegayega ase vari chiŋmarika la.>>

ref: The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” Everyone who hears this should say, “Come!” If you are thirsty, come! If you want life-giving water, come and take it. It's free!
text: Wen Chiika ale Pabiika powa a maa chaab a weeni ni ayen, <<Ni jam.>> Baai meena ale a wom ba wieŋa la, ale maa weeni kama mɛ ayen, <<Ni jam.>> Nama meena baai ate nyanyuila a ta ni la, ni jam nyu Wen nyuvuri nyiamu tiirim.

ref: Here is my warning for everyone who hears the prophecies in this book: If you add anything to them, God will make you suffer all the terrible troubles written in this book.
text: Mi, Jɔɔn, a kaam baai meena ale wom gbaŋka de wieŋa la kama. Waai a dan pai wari di choa a gum mi wieŋa de po, Wen le pai ninam ate maarɔba bayopɔiwa a jam ta la a gum ku nyɔnɔ waali kaai ate wa le waali wa la po.

ref: If you take anything away from these prophecies, God will not let you have part in the life-giving tree and in the holy city described in this book.
text: Waai mɛ a be dan yeeri wari gbaŋka de po a basi, Wen a kan basi ate ku nyɔnɔ a jo wa tɛŋka po a maa dɛ wa nyuvuri tiimu yɔnaŋa, ŋaai ate m poom weeni ŋa wari gbaŋka de po la.

ref: I pray that the Lord Jesus will be kind to all of you.
text: M be ŋman a saalim ayen ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ŋmanteka a bo ale ni meena. Ku be nye dila.
